title: Ship calib_span_ff solo: the 9-sigma test of whether the refit term is additive or a ceiling
description:
PRICE: ~0 h card, 1 slot. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.02 - this is an INSTRUMENT, not an improvement, and the submission message must say so.

THE QUESTION. The full-corpus refit (--fold -1 --ema) is the ONLY positive board term this project owns; interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-18_state_of_the_levers.md:194 shows ensembling has bought zero ticks over the best solo across 62 tries while the refit has bought every tick we have. Two readings of it are live and they are not distinguishable on anything shipped so far:
  ADDITIVE - a refit adds ~+0.005 to whatever its honest twin scores.
  CEILING  - refits converge near 0.9445 regardless of where the twin started (knee-33iwi).

THE EVIDENCE TODAY, n=2, and it favours CEILING:
  labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026   0.937 -> _ff 0.945   (+0.008)
  labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 0.941 -> _ff 0.944 (+0.003)
The WORSE twin gained MORE and both landed at 0.944/0.945. A third apparent pair, final_ws_e12 0.925 -> final_ws_cf 0.923, is NOT a twin pair: experiments/README.md:3934 records final_ws_e12 as itself full-fit (0.9541 on the fold-0 holdout it trained on), so that -0.002 is two refits compared to each other and is not evidence either way.

THE TEST. calib_span_ff.pt already exists on disk (2026-08-24) and comp/members.roster:390 records it as calib_span_s2026's flags plus --fold -1 --ema. Roster:489-492 corrects an earlier mis-pairing and states the ff's twin is calib_span_s2026 - which scored board 0.921 solo as spansolo_v1, the lowest DINOv2 solo we own. It has never been shipped solo.
  ADDITIVE predicts 0.926.
  CEILING  predicts 0.9445.
18 ticks apart. The board's scatter among offline-tied entries is sd 1.9 ticks, so this separates at ~9 sigma. No card time: the checkpoint exists.

WHY THIS SLOT AND NOT headlr_ship_ff. headlr_ship_ff's twin headlr_ship_s2026 scored 0.937, so additive predicts 0.942 against ceiling 0.9445 - 3 ticks, ~1.5 sigma, not decisive. Same question, same one-slot cost, six times the separation here. That is the ratio argument.

WHAT THE ANSWER BUYS. If CEILING: the refit lever is exhausted at 0.9445, every future refit is capped below the pinned 0.946 champion, and the remaining 11 ticks to first place must come from supervision quality or slice-to-study aggregation (README:157-158) rather than from the fit. depth24_ff_long36 and headlr_ship_ff both become predictable nulls and their slots are freed. If ADDITIVE: an honest-base gain is directly bankable at +0.005 on top, which makes honest-base improvement the schedule.

NO RISK TO THE STANDING ENTRY: a new submission does not displace the pinned champion.

GATES OWED before the slot: package the member, witness_check --device auto ON THE CARD (never cpu), kit_check, mount_check --live, submit_check --kernel (set equality on members - calib_span_ff has appeared in ensembles, e.g. ref 55875622, so confirm no entry is exactly this one member), run_check --log after COMPLETE and before spending the slot, and the Einstein grep of comp/board.jsonl.
notes:
GATES GREEN 2026-09-18T09:17Z, kernel dimiturnt/kneemri-spanff version 2, COMPLETE.
  run_check: 'loaded 1 of 1 members' (log downloaded from the completed v2 run).
  submit_check: NEW (set equality on ('calib_span_ff',), no board row holds it solo).
  mount_check --live: ok. kit_check: clean, kit at 341c6586, 0 behind.
  witness: calib_span_ff is UNVERIFIED-by-age (dark, --fold -1, fitted 2026-08-24, pre-dates witnesses).
    Its non-dark twin calib_span_s2026 witnesses ok on cuda, max|diff| 0.0117 of 0.0312 over 8 studies.
    roster:390 records the two as differing only by --fold -1 --ema, neither of which touches the reading.
  board_read --live fresh 08:18:47Z. Einstein grep of comp/board.jsonl done: 156 rows, calib_span_ff
    appears only inside ensembles, never solo.
  Submission message must declare INSTRUMENT, P(beats champion) ~0.02, and mark the member UNVERIFIED-by-age.
  ADDITIVE predicts board 0.926; CEILING predicts 0.9445. 18 ticks apart against board scatter sd 1.9 ticks.
  Slot mark: 12:50Z (4 slots, 3.55 h apart at 09:17Z).
DISPLACED FROM THE 13:00Z SLOT 2026-09-18T11:14Z, not cancelled. kneemri-headlrff takes it: headlr_ship_ff's arm turned out to have completed at 05:16Z and its entry is gate-green (see knee-33iwi), and it is an ATTEMPT ON THE CHAMPION at P ~0.15-0.25 where spanff is an INSTRUMENT at P ~0.02 -- 8x the probability for the same slot, so ratio decides. spanff's gates were all green at 11:10Z and none of them expires today except the board read, so it re-enters at the 16:25Z mark unless the DML verdict or the headlrff result puts something better in front of it. Nothing about the spanff question changed; it lost a queue position, not an argument.
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-18 12:47Z, before the 13:00Z slot. Gates re-run and all green: submit_check --kernel kneemri-spanff EXIT 0 'ok, 1 members, no recorded entry carries this set'; champion_check EXIT 0 (tripleseat_v2 0.946, kit c3effa61, 7 members buildable); Einstein grep of comp/board.jsonl (156 rows) shows calib_span_ff named in 51 ENSEMBLE entries and NEVER as a solo, so the SET is new while the member is well-travelled.

Two invocation errors of mine were corrected getting here and both are worth the write-down: (1) submit_check --kernel dimiturnt/kneemri-spanff returned UNKNOWN/exit 2 because resolved() takes a kernel DIRECTORY or BARE NAME and the Kaggle slug resolves to comp/kernels/dimiturnt/kneemri-spanff, which does not exist, so glob('*.py') found nothing. The gate was not blind; pass the bare name. (2) I read its exit code through a pipe ('| tail -8; echo EXIT $?'), which reports tail's status, and that is how I recorded this gate as NEW at 12:09Z when it had actually refused. Write to a log, then echo $?.

THE INSTRUMENT, priced off the board rather than off prose. Two refit pairs exist:
  labelwise_depth24_drop40_long: off75 0.9053, board 0.941 -> ff 0.944 (+0.003)
  labelwise_ext_drop40_long:     off75 0.9045, board 0.937 -> ff 0.945 (+0.008)
The two bases are 0.0008 apart offline, INSIDE the 0.0053 resolution floor, yet read 4 board ticks apart; their refits read 1 tick apart. The refit COMPRESSED a spread the offline ruler cannot see. So the 'refit term' is not a constant and the +0.003/+0.008 disagreement is not noise - they are two different distances to the same wall.

spansolo_v1 (calib_span_s2026, the fold-0 twin) is board 0.921 / off75 0.8895, about 0.015 of off75 BELOW both bases. That is the whole point: the existing pair cannot separate the models because their bases are 4 ticks apart, and this one is 16-20 below.

PREDICTION, pre-registered:
  ADDITIVE (refit adds a constant ~+0.0055): spanff reads 0.925-0.929
  CEILING  (refits converge on a wall ~0.9445): spanff reads 0.943-0.946
Separation ~0.018 against a board blur of 0.0010 (board_transfer, read live 12:39Z). Decisive either way.

P(beats the 0.946 champion) ~ 0.02 - even the CEILING branch only reaches the champion, it does not pass it. This slot is an INSTRUMENT and is labelled as one in the submission message. Its value is that it GATES knee-8bmi2: under CEILING that ~3h card commitment is dead on arrival at 0.9445 and the card is saved; under ADDITIVE it stays a coin flip the ruler cannot forecast (see knee-8bmi2, re-priced 12:40Z at the live +1.00 compression).
PREDICTION SHARPENED 12:52Z, BEFORE the slot, and it moves the weight AWAY from the branch I was favouring.

Tabling every scored solo the board holds (15 of them) turned up two whole-corpus members I had not counted: calibsolo (final_ws_cf) board 0.923 and soloseat_v1 (final_ws_e12) board 0.925. roster:400-402 confirms both are DARK '--fold -1' - _cf is the _ff recipe plus --calibrated-targets - so both are whole-corpus refits.

That makes FOUR whole-corpus solos on the board: 0.923, 0.925, 0.944, 0.945. THE STRONG CEILING FORM IS THEREFORE ALREADY REFUTED BY ROWS WE OWN. Whole-corpus refits do not converge on a wall near 0.9445; the two that landed there came from bases at 0.937 and 0.941, and the two that landed at 0.923-0.925 came from a weaker family. Member quality survives the refit, which is the opposite of what a ceiling says.

So the weights invert from the 12:47Z pre-registration. spansolo_v1 at 0.921 sits in the LOW neighbourhood (0.921 vs final_ws at 0.923-0.925), so:
  ADDITIVE ~0.925-0.929 is now the FAVOURITE (~0.8)
  CEILING  ~0.943-0.946 is the long shot (~0.2)
The bands and the ~0.018 separation are unchanged; only the prior moves. P(beats the 0.946 champion) falls from ~0.02 to ~0.01.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE SLOT'S VALUE, honestly: it goes DOWN, because the question is closer to answered than it was, and the answer it is converging on is the one that keeps knee-8bmi2 alive as an unforecastable coin flip rather than killing it. The slot is still worth spending - it is the only direct read of the refit term from a LOW base, the two existing pairs both start 16-20 ticks higher and cannot separate the models, and pacing says there is NO SKIP. But it is now confirmation of a reading taken from the record, not a discovery, and the submission message will say so.

The residual question it still owns, and the reason it is not redundant: the two low whole-corpus solos are final_ws, a different FAMILY, so 'weak members refit weakly' is currently confounded with 'that family is weak'. calib_span_ff is the same family as a base whose board level we know exactly (spansolo_v1 0.921), which no other row on the board gives us.
SUBMITTED 2026-09-18 12:57Z, ref 56330671, PENDING. Kaggle reports 3 submissions remaining today, so the slot is spent and confirmed by the API rather than by the CLI's one-line output. Slots recompute to (23:30-12:57)/3 = 3h31m, marks 16:28 / 19:59 / 23:30Z.

All gates re-run immediately before the slot with REAL exit codes (not piped): kit_check EXIT 0 at 341c6586, 0 commits behind in the 52 files the kernel loads; mount_check --live shows 'kneemri-spanff: ok - declares all of metaresearch/dinov2/PyTorch/small/1' and calib_span_ff present in all_ours (the run's EXIT 1 is the known, unrelated kneemri-ff36 refusal for depth24_ff_long36); submit_check --kernel kneemri-spanff EXIT 0 NEW; champion_check EXIT 0; board_check --live EXIT 0, 152 recorded / 100 live; board_read fresh at 10:36Z; Einstein grep of comp/board.jsonl confirms {calib_span_ff} has never shipped as a set.

STILL OWED once it scores: run_check on the downloaded kernel log (it must census N of M members and refuse on a drop line - this is the gate that caught farseat_v1 shipping six of seven), then board_check --live, then the comp/board.jsonl row with offline75 NULL (calib_span_ff is --fold -1 and holds nothing out, exactly like ffsolo_v1 and extffsolo_v1).
ANSWERED 2026-09-18. spanff_v1 ref 56330671 scored 0.926 — inside the pre-registered ADDITIVE band (0.925-0.929, prior ~0.8), ~9 sigma clear of CEILING (0.943-0.946, prior ~0.2) against a 0.0010 median board blur. Three-point term table: +0.003 / +0.005 / +0.008, mean +0.005, and the spread is NOT explained by base strength (weakest and strongest base at opposite ends). No ceiling at 0.9445; member quality survives the refit. What it buys: best honest base 0.941 board-equivalent + 0.005 = 0.946, exactly the standing champion — so additivity confirms the gap's arithmetic and opens no lever. Reaching 0.957 needs an honest base near 0.916 ledger75 against our best 0.9078. Written up in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-18_state_of_the_levers.md and comp/SUBMISSIONS.md.

title: Build an out-of-fold ruler over all 4407 studies (lifts the fold ban)
description: THE measurement lever. Owner lifted the fold ban 2026-09-18 ('we should train at least 2 models on different hold outs'). Current ruler is one fixed fold-0 draw of 909 studies, paired floor 0.0062; a solo that beats the 0.946 champion needs about +0.005 at the honest corner, which is BELOW that floor. A 5-fold rotation gives an OOF prediction for all 4407 studies and the floor scales as sqrt(n): 0.0062 -> ~0.0028. foreign_oof_corpus already sits on such a ruler (population 8a2829d6, 4406 studies) and we could not join it. COST: 5x training per member, so run it only for candidates being chosen between, never for all 450. COMPARABILITY (the owner's own objection): no existing member can EVER get an OOF number - they trained on folds 1-4 and scoring them there is in-sample, the defect that voided raptor_solo at 98.6% in-sample. So keep fold 0 as the legacy ruler permanently, build the wide ruler forward-only, and score the first few new members on BOTH to get the offset between rulers. You do not translate the past; you calibrate the new ruler against it with a handful of overlap points. Motivating evidence: three top members read offline75 0.9045/0.9053/0.9059 (a TIE inside the floor) against board 0.937/0.941/0.937, all three BELOW the fitted transfer line, -2.7 sd - winner's curse from ranking ~450 members against one fixed draw.
notes:
PRICED 2026-09-18T09:22Z, no card spent. Audit first: the OOF infrastructure ALREADY EXISTS and does not
answer this. oof_folds.sh ran 2026-09-06/07 -- oof_fold[0-4]_s2026 on disk, five disjoint holdouts whose
union is 4407, plus the gen-2 born-again twins. But it is 224 px / 8 epochs BY DESIGN ('THE RECIPE IS
DELIBERATELY NOT THE BEST ONE' -- an instrument for label contradiction, not a ruler for ranking).

THE COST IS IRREDUCIBLE AND IT IS THE WHOLE VERDICT. An OOF number for a candidate requires that
candidate refitted once per fold: every existing member trained on folds 1-4, so scoring one there is
the 98.6%-in-sample defect that voided raptor_solo. At the shipping recipe that is 5 x 3.5 h = 17.5 h
PER CANDIDATE, and a ruler is only useful between at least two candidates, so ~28-35 h for one
comparison. Against a 0.011 board gap that ratio is bad by an order of magnitude, and it buys no
member -- only a finer opinion about members we would still have to build.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO AT ANY PRICE: fix the selection that already happened. The winner's curse in the
motivating evidence is over ~450 members that can never receive an OOF number. A forward-only ruler
prices future candidates only, and we are choosing between two or three of those, not 450 -- which is
the regime where the current 0.0062 floor is least damaging.

WHAT WOULD RE-OPEN IT: a cheap proxy ruler whose ORDERING transfers. That is the open question, not the
ruler itself -- and the repo's own rule says only the SIGN transfers across recipe changes. So the
re-opening experiment is not 17.5 h of folds, it is a transfer check on artefacts already on disk:
do the 224/8 fold models rank a knob the same way the shipping recipe does, on the one fold they share?
If ordering transfers, the ruler costs 4 x 25 min instead of 14 h and this becomes a P0 worth running.

Not closed, re-scoped: the deliverable is the transfer check, and the 5-fold shipping-recipe rotation is
refused on ratio until that check passes. See experiments/README.md:13950 -- 'before pricing an
instrument at zero, check that the two things it must compare were ever measured on common ground'.
Closed alongside knee-ozwxx 2026-09-18T09:55Z. Its deliverable was the transfer check, which passed; the shipping-recipe rotation (17.5-35 h) stays refused on ratio, and the CHEAP 224/8 rotation it was the expensive alternative to is now refused too -- the leaf corpus holds one rotatable positive worth an expected +0.0012. Knob work at the shipping corner is exhausted at every ruler the project can afford. The residual is supervision quality (dml_a, on the card) or slice-to-study aggregation (knee-jb0ci).

title: Occlusion-driven targeted erasing: blank each study's own evidence cells during training
description:
PRICE: ~1.1 h
P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.08

THE IDEA. Sweep the TRAIN split with patch occlusion, then during training blank each study's own top-k evidence cells so the model cannot lean on them and must find redundant evidence. Unlike the locator this does NOT need the map to be anatomically correct: the map marks what THIS model leans on by construction, which is exactly and only what the augmentation consumes. That is why it survives knee-j19z1 failing.

MECHANISM SUPPORT, MEASURED, NOT TASTE. attribution.region_importance on an August member read centre-only 0.8021 against border-only 0.8006 — the border carries nearly as much as the centre. So redundant evidence EXISTS to be forced onto. And the maps are weakly per-study (2026-09-16, off the 909 npz): 31 of 64 cells are some study's argmax, modal cell only 26.8%, cosine to the corpus-mean map median 0.928 / p10 0.855 / min 0.528, and labels agree on a study's peak cell only 19.2% of the time. So erasing is targeted rather than a centre cutout with extra steps.

NOVELTY, CHECKED NOT ASSUMED (ledger sweep 2026-09-16). No arm, recipe, interpretation or decline in experiments/, interpretations/kneemri/, comp/SUBMISSIONS.md or comp/members.declines drives an augmentation from an attribution or attention map. Occlusion here is read-only diagnostics (experiments/arms/attribution.sh:2,5). slot_dropout is input-structural at a fixed rate, not map-driven (grand.toml:33). discord_mask masks LABEL cells, not image regions (SUBMISSIONS.md:3839-3879). This is the one family of the six swept that is genuinely untried here.

THE PRICE, AND WHY IT IS NOT 20 MIN. The maps must cover the TRAIN studies, not the holdout — training is where the erasing happens. Train is ~3636 studies against the 909 already swept. At grid 8 that is 65 passes over 4x the corpus = ~3 h of card, which at P 0.08 is a poor ratio. At grid 4 it is 17 passes = ~45 min, and a 4x4 cell is 84 px of a 336 px side. Then ~20 min to train (224 px / 12 epochs, 94 s an epoch per knee-s9cr). Total ~1.1 h.

HOW IT MUST BE READ. ALONE against the control, never inside a composition: the grand recipe showed fragments accumulate harm additively and a fragment's sign does not transfer out of a composition. Directional only at this price - a single arm cannot make it a finding.

DEPENDS ON: knee-j19z1 (CLOSED, gate failed, and this is the part of it that survived).
notes:
2026-09-16 18:16Z — ARMED AND WAITING ON THE CARD. Owner took the GPU back; everything except the run itself is done.

MAPS ARE BUILT. The train sweep finished in four blocks (900+900+900+798 = 3498 studies, grid 4, 11 min/block as predicted, last block landed 21:12 Sofia). Joined with `python -m kneemri.evaluation.patch_map_blocks` into
  D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/patches/labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026_g4_train.patches.npz
  3498 studies, maps (3498, 12, 4, 4)
which is the exact path `experiments/arms/erase_own_cells.sh` `require`s.

THE ONLY REMAINING SPEND IS ~20-25 MIN OF CARD. When the card comes back:
  1. python -m kneemri.experiments.card_check
  2. python -m kneemri.experiments.arm_check --only erase_own_cells --smoke <throwaway dir> --smoke-studies 60
  3. bash experiments/arms/erase_own_cells.sh      (12 epochs, 224 px)
  4. ledger75 --only erase_own_cells_s2026 against probe224_control_s2026 0.8914@l75, ALONE, then convergence_check / reading_check / ledger_check / roster_check.

THE SWEEP ALSO KILLED THE LOCATOR A THIRD TIME. Block 2700's own reading: '12 of 12 labels above the null', '1 of 12 labels separate positives from negatives by more than their scatter' — the same shape as the g8 holdout and g4 train readings. Recorded against knee-j19z1. This does NOT touch this bead: erasing consumes 'what this model leans on', not 'where the pathology is'.
2026-09-17 01:36Z — RAN AND NEGATIVE ON BOTH CUTS. 12 of 12 epochs (convergence_check silent), peak e11, 909 rows, read ALONE against the control exactly as pre-registered:
  probe224_control_s2026   LEDGER 0.8556 / LEDGER75 0.8914   e10
  erase_own_cells_s2026    LEDGER 0.8541 / LEDGER75 0.8899   e11
-0.0015 midpoint and -0.0015 ledger75. The two rulers agreeing to the digit is what makes this a flat rather than a cut artefact -- worth noting because the last three results in this repo split across the cuts (stem -0.0005 vs -0.0041, ortho -0.0220 vs -0.0300, and the knee-6hfi triage's two-ruler error).

SEAT ASKED TOO, since solo is not the only question a member can pass. seat_add over the champion's seven fold-0 seats, ledger75, relation EXACT: base k=7 0.9096, +cand k=8 0.9092, ADD -0.0004, bar +0.0015. Neither a member nor a seat.

THE PREMISE IS NOT CONVICTED, and the decline says so. Border-only 0.8006 vs centre-only 0.8021 still stands, the maps are still per-study (modal cell 26.8%, labels agree on a study's peak 19.2%). What is priced is ONE rate at ONE grid for ONE budget: 0.25 at 4x4 over 12 epochs. Re-open only by moving grid or rate with an argument for the new value, and price against -0.0015, never zero. Declined in comp/members.declines; the npz stays.

TOTAL SPEND: ~45 min of map sweep (already banked before the card came back) + ~20 min of training. Priced at P(clears 1.5%) 0.08 and it did not clear -- the ratio was honest and the answer is no.
2026-09-17 — THE -0.0015 IS VOID: the treatment never applied to a single study.

erase_own_cells_s2026.full.log:7 reads "4407 of 4407 studies are absent from
labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026_g4_train.patches.npz; they erase at the mean map".

Producer/consumer key mismatch. patch_maps.py:281 wrote `studies=np.asarray(holdout)` where
`holdout` is POSITIONAL indices into whichever cache the sweep loaded (npz `studies` is int64,
3498 entries). patch_erasing.py:45 builds `names = [str(name) for name in held[STUDIES]]` and
joins against StudyInstanceUID strings — so it looked up '0','1','2' and missed 100%. The
documented partial-sweep fallback ("a study the sweep does not name is given the mean map") then
gave EVERY study the corpus mean map.

So the arm measured a generic, position-agnostic single-cell cutout at the mean map — not
self-attribution-guided erasing. The axis is UNTESTED, not closed. Consistent with the reading:
a flat -0.0015 is what a mild generic cutout should give.

FIXED 0b3e22aa. The sweep now records identifiers for the chosen positions. A sweep naming NONE
of the corpus is now REFUSED (ValueError, "key mismatch") rather than degraded — degrading it is
what let a treatment that never applied read as a measured null.

BLOCKER FOR ANY RE-RUN: the one npz on disk holds positions and will now be refused. It must be
re-keyed or re-swept before erase_own_cells can be re-armed. Re-arming also needs
`reading_check --only erase_own_cells --anyway 'previous reading measured a treatment that never
applied'`, and the re-run is a card arm needing PRICE / P(clears) here first.
2026-09-17 03:05Z — READ, and the axis is FLAT. Matched, alone, as pre-registered; both rows 909 holdout studies, 12 epochs:
  probe224_control_s2026   LEDGER 0.8556 / LEDGER75 0.8914   e10
  erase_own_cells_s2026    LEDGER 0.8562 / LEDGER75 0.8928   e11
+0.0006 midpoint, +0.0014 ledger75, against a 0.0062 floor on these same rows. Flat on both cuts, same sign on both, so it is a flat and not a cut artefact.

THE JOIN IS CONFIRMED, which is the only reason this reading counts. erase_own_cells_s2026.full.log:7 reads '909 of 4407 studies are absent from ...named.patches.npz' — 4407 corpus minus 3498 swept train studies is exactly the holdout, so every swept study joined BY NAME. The voided run logged '4407 of 4407': nothing joined and every study erased at the mean map.

SIGN FLIPPED, AND THAT IS THE LEAST INTERESTING PART. The void pair read -0.0015/-0.0015 and the real pair reads +0.0006/+0.0014; both are inside the floor, so neither was ever a result. What actually changed is that the axis had never been measured — the first arm measured a generic cutout wearing this treatment's name.

FREE SECOND READING out of the void run, kept as erase_own_cells_s2026_run1: a blind mean-map cutout scores 0.8541/0.8899, -0.0015 on the control. So targeted erasing beats blind cutout by +0.0021/+0.0029 and blind cutout costs -0.0015, and all three deltas are inside the floor. The map is worth a little more than nothing over a blind cutout; nothing here clears the bar.

VOIDED DOWNSTREAM: the seat_add over the champion's seven fold-0 seats (-0.0004) was run against the void checkpoint and is not a number about this member. comp/members.declines is corrected and now says so.

CLOSING THIS. The decline records what re-opens it: move grid or rate WITH AN ARGUMENT for the new value, and price against +0.0014, not against zero. Do not re-run this cell.
close_reason:
NULL. Ran 2026-09-17 and sat unread three days. erase_own_cells_s2026 0.8928 ledger75 (e11 of 12) against its own pre-registered control probe224_control_s2026 0.8914 (e10), both priced with ledger75 on the 909-study population eb3ba199, not quoted from the arm comment: +0.0014 ledger75, +0.0006 midpoint. Inside the 0.0053 paired floor and inside the 0.0062 floor, so the ruler cannot order it against its control at all. The arm pre-registered P(clears 1.5%) 0.08 and called itself 'directional only at this price'; it did not clear. erase_own_cells_s2026_run1 is VOID per members.declines and was not used.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT: the augmentation was measured ALONE against a 224 probe control at 12 epochs, by the arm's own design ('never inside a composition: a fragment sign does not transfer out of one'). It is untested on the 24-epoch labelwise family that actually ships.

title: GPU window (~6.5 h uninterrupted, start on owner signal): card schedule
description:
Owner grant 2026-09-15 ~21:10Z: 6-7 h uninterrupted card, hours NOT started yet; owner will attach a goal that must fit this schedule. Schedule is DRAFT until the goal lands.

PRE-WINDOW (no card): knee-feb62.9 smoke crash fixed; arm_check clean on probe224_control, probe224_grand, grand_recipe, grand_labelwise_depth24, grand_labelwise_ext (done 21:09Z, 0 refused); card_check; watcher chain written (after.sh gated on ARM DONE text, verified against an existing marker line) so the queue runs unattended.

T+0.00 smoke grand_recipe + probe224_grand + grand_labelwise_depth24 (60 studies, ~5 min). Any BROKEN -> fix in-window, card idles meanwhile.
T+0.1 probe224_control then probe224_grand (~0.9 h UNVERIFIED, knee-feb62.8). Gate: grand-control >= +0.006@l75.

title: missed_negation: a fourth Correction in table_correction, gold-gated before any card
description:
THE NEEDLE from knee-z4yfe. overcall_audit: 54% of the 108 confident reader false positives are EXTRACTOR failures, not soft targets — missed_negation +9.6% [+4.4,+15.3] is the uncontested part (subthreshold +18.9% is refused by the module's own limits). supervision_gap prices the same defect independently: our labels 0.8658 vs our model 0.9156 on gold, labels-model -0.0498 [-0.0742,-0.0255]. The model is already better than its own supervision.

THE PLUMBING FAILURE: core/data/labels/negation_scope.py is BUILT, unit-tested and PROVEN (against the 311 positive calls on the 58 annotated studies its DIRECTION+BOUND parts took the negation category from 18 to 12 on disputed cells and 16 to 3 on agreed ones) and is imported by EXACTLY ONE consumer — overcall_audit.py:58/:367. Nothing that PRODUCES labels uses it.

report_reader.py is an LLM reader, not a regex pipeline, so NegationScope cannot be 'wired in'. It can only act as a post-hoc VETO/PULL on the produced table. That is the cheap shape: a regex pass over the reports, NO LLM re-run over 4,407 studies.

HOME: core/data/labels/table_correction.py, as a fourth Correction beside fracture_contusion (PartnerLift), rubric_subthreshold (RubricPull), effusion_reread (ColumnGraft). The module's own doctrine binds it: NEITHER RULE HARD-FLIPS A CELL — the clean extractor failure rate is 15%, so a rule right most of the time is applied as a pull toward the column's negative floor with the residual left standing, never as a zero.

THE GATE, CARD-FREE, FIRST: does the corrected table's agreement with the 58 annotated gold studies BEAT the current table's 0.8658? Minutes of CPU. If not, the lane closes for zero slots.

EINSTEIN GATE: grep -icE 'negation|veto|overcall|relabel|recut_labels' comp/board.jsonl = 1 — relabel7_v1, board 0.943, cleanlab corrections at ONE seat of seven. Its own row names what it cannot close: 'A relabelled member at full weight, or a pool relabelled throughout, is a different question and this row cannot close it.' And the negation signal is TEXT-derived, model-independent, not circular the way confident-learning corrections are. Gate passes on both counts.

ONLY IF THE GOLD GATE CLEARS: train ONE member on the corrected table at full weight and price the pool.
PRICE: ~0.3 h CPU for the gate; ~1.2 h card only if it clears. P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.35
notes:
GATE BUILT, RUN, AND PASSED — SMALL, AND THE GOLD SET CANNOT PRICE IT. Closed 2026-09-13.

THE THREE-NUMBER CONFLICT IS RESOLVED, and two of the three were misreadings. `supervision_gap` takes `--labels`, so it IS the gate — no new scorer was needed and `ReaderAgreement.cells` was not called at all. Run against `report_labels_v2.csv`:
  0.8658 = the AGGREGATE AUC of the report labels used as a predictor of gold. This is the gate number.
  65.3%  = PRECISION at cut 0.50 ('agreement where the report says YES'). A different statistic.
  0.6870 = not a global figure at all — it is the SYNOVITIS ROW of the labels column. `reader_agreement.py:157` quotes one finding's number as if it were the table's.

WHAT WAS BUILT. `NegationPull` — a fourth Correction in `table_correction.py`, residual 0.15, the same as `RubricPull`, no hard flip. A positive cell whose report denies that finding at EVERY located mention is pulled toward its column's negative floor. All-mentions rather than any-mention is deliberate: a report that names a finding twice and denies it once is describing two things, and the rule declines rather than guessing. It reads DENIAL only, never severity, which keeps it clear of `severity_boundary`'s retired territory. This is the first consumer of `NegationScope` that produces a label — the plumbing failure this bead was filed about is closed.

MEASURED. 414 cells of 52,872 (0.78%) over 4,406 studies. Language coverage 4,401 of 4,407 (99.9%), so 414 is the corpus count and not a parsing fragment. Gold: labels 0.8658 -> 0.8675 (+0.0017), precision 65.3% -> 65.9%, RECALL UNCHANGED at 84.6% — only false positives removed, no positive lost. No column regressed.

WHY IT IS NOT A RESULT. The rule fires exactly THREE times in the 696 gold cells and the radiologist calls all three negative. 3/3 right, and +0.0017 is what three correct cells look like on that denominator. n=3 cannot separate a good rule from a lucky one, and the gold set is simply the wrong instrument for a rule this sparse.

FOLLOW-ON: knee-bjpq4, one member at full weight on the corrected table (`experiments/arms/labelwise_depth24_negpull.sh`, armed behind warm_calib). `arm_check` refused the first version as MOVING-RULER (knee-df7t) — the corrected table would have been both the supervision and the ruler, 400 holdout cells score differently under it, and a gain would have been the ruler moving. Fixed with `--eval-labels $LABELS`.

title: severity CLOSES at full budget (-0.0019): the Fracture/MCL concentration was sampling noise, all twelve columns have rungs
description:
knee-evdfd's pair landed. Veto does NOT fire on either arm.

  band_dense_drop40_long  0.8587 mid  0.8918 l75  peak e16 of 24  (CONTROL)
  severity_drop40_long    0.8538 mid  0.8899 l75  peak e18 of 24
                                      delta -0.0019

Pre-registered band <= 0.0000, so THIS FORM of the objective -- severity applied to all twelve columns -- closes, and the budget defence is dead with it: at 12 epochs the same subtraction was -0.0006 at l75, at 24 epochs with --slot-dropout 0.40 it is -0.0019. Giving the objective its budget made it slightly WORSE relative to control. The harness cannot be blamed; the control is matched, converged and peaks mid-run.

BUT THE PER-LABEL READ LOCALISES THE LOSS TO TWO COLUMNS, and that is the finding.

  ACL              0.9308 -> 0.9402  +0.0094
  MCL              0.8882 -> 0.8649  -0.0233
  Medial Meniscus  0.8986 -> 0.8959  -0.0027   (graded)
  Lateral Meniscus 0.8775 -> 0.8875  +0.0100   (graded)
  Medial OA        0.9023 -> 0.9066  +0.0042   (graded)
  Lateral OA       0.8526 -> 0.8489  -0.0037   (graded)
  PF OA            0.8573 -> 0.8757  +0.0184   (graded)
  Effusion         0.9229 -> 0.9285  +0.0056
  Synovitis        0.9191 -> 0.9240  +0.0049
  Baker's          0.9138 -> 0.9060  -0.0078
  Contusion        0.8899 -> 0.8988  +0.0089
  Fracture         0.8491 -> 0.8024  -0.0467

  graded mean +0.0052 (n=5); ungraded mean -0.0070 (n=7)
  EXCLUDING Fracture and MCL: +0.0047 over the other ten.

The concentration clause fires POSITIVELY (graded up) and neither of its two refutation conditions fires: the lift is not uniform, and MCL is the biggest LOSER rather than a gainer. Fracture -0.0467 and MCL -0.0233 are the entire deficit and they are exactly the two columns where severity has no signal to supply -- Fracture is binary with no rungs, and the label-contest pilot found 0 rulebook errors on MCL in 100 studies. Meanwhile __conf is constant 0.95 across all 52,872 populated cells, so the loss cannot down-weight itself where its own information is absent; it reweights those cells as hard as a graded one.

FOLLOW-UP, one variable: restrict severity weighting to the columns that HAVE rungs, leaving Fracture/MCL (and any other rung-free column) at uniform weight. If the other ten hold their +0.0047 the member lands near 0.8965 and the aux-objective axis re-opens on a mechanism that was measured rather than argued. Needs a per-column form of --severity-weight; the flag is currently a bool at kneemri/training/flag_vocabulary.py:215.

DO NOT quote this as 'the objective family is closed'. What is closed is applying it to all twelve.
notes:
REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, same night, before the follow-up arm was written. Both premises of the salvage are false.

1. THE RUNG PREMISE IS FALSE. Counting the reader's levels per column over the whole training table: every one of the twelve carries all three YES rungs. Fracture 122/169/23 (spread 0.462, mid-pack, higher than Effusion 0.400 or Synovitis 0.403); MCL 495/219/53 (0.355). There is no rung-free column, so the one variable the follow-up arm was going to move does not exist.

2. THE CONCENTRATION IS SAMPLING NOISE. Hanley-McNeil SEs per column: NOT ONE of the twelve deltas reaches 1.3 SE. Fracture -0.0467 is -1.24 SE on 42 holdout positives; MCL -0.0233 is -0.81 SE on 57. Those are the two rarest columns by a clear margin (next is Synovitis at 77), and rarity tracks |delta| across the twelve at rank-corr +0.45. PF OA's +0.0184 is +1.28 SE, the largest in the panel, and it is a GAINER. The graded/ungraded split averages twelve numbers whose intervals all straddle zero, on a split chosen after seeing them. This is the error CLAUDE.md names: a per-label delta read without its own sampling interval.

VERDICT: --severity-weight CLOSES at full budget as pre-registered (-0.0019 ledger75, matched converged mid-peaking control). No follow-up arm. The per-column restriction would have been loss-engineering even if a property had predicted the two losers, and none does (not rung spread, not retained positive mass, not shrinkage factor). Saved 2.2 h of card.

title: Ruler cut 0.5 mis-measures the board: 0.75 cuts unexplained variance a third
description:
PRE-REGISTERED IN OUR OWN CODE AND NEVER TESTED. supervision_gap.py:125 states 'a ruler cut at 0.75 should track the leaderboard better than one cut at 0.5'. Tested 2026-09-12 by rebuilding every ensemble board row from its members' holdout npz (37 pairs, vs the 17 that carry a recorded offline number) and refitting the transfer at each cut:

  cut 0.50: n=37 slope=+1.324 r2=0.860 residsd=0.0030 corr=+0.927
  cut 0.75: n=37 slope=+1.190 r2=0.936 residsd=0.0020 corr=+0.967
  cut 0.88: n=37 slope=+1.342 r2=0.866 residsd=0.0029 corr=+0.931

An OPTIMUM, not a monotone trend, which is the shape that argues against an AUC-scale artefact.

MECHANISM. Our targets and ruler binarise the graded report label at 0.5, calling 44.7 pct of cells positive where the radiologist calls 34.5 pct, at 65.3 pct precision (supervision_gap thresholds block). We optimise agreement with a reader we already beat: logs/supervision_gap_ours.log reads labels 0.8658 vs model 0.9156 against radiologist truth, paired interval [-0.0742,-0.0255], EXCLUDES zero, on 10 of 12 findings.

CONSEQUENCE 1, MEASUREMENT. Member spread at 0.5 is span 0.0059 sd 0.0016 over the top honest 11 - below the 0.005 noise floor, which is why every mechanism reads as a tie. At 0.75 span 0.0098; at 0.88 span 0.0150.

CONSEQUENCE 2, SELECTION. Rank correlation between rulers is 0.918 - broad agreement, sharp disagreement at the seats. labelwise_depth24_s2026 ranks 40th of 355 members at 0.5 and 1st at 0.75 (a MEMBER ranking, not a board rank). stackfit_s2026 9th of 11 at 0.5, 2nd at 0.88, and holds the highest board of the eight solo pairs (0.933). calib_dense_hold outranks stackfit at 0.5 and the board ordered them the other way.

CONSEQUENCE 3, TARGET. ENS fit at 0.75: board = 1.1905*offline - 0.1457. board 0.944 needs offline@0.75 0.9153; 0.955 needs 0.9246. Best seated pair measured 0.9173 -> board 0.942. Gap to 0.955 is +0.0073 offline, which is 3.6 sigma on residsd 0.0020 and was inside the slop on the old ruler.

POPULATION DISCIPLINE. A first pass ranked oof_gen2_fold2/3/4 (n=884/849/890) and foreign_oof_corpus (n=4406) alongside holdout909 members; those are different populations and were dropped. 339 of 374 members share holdout909. raptor_* excluded as 98.6 pct in-sample per foreign_overlap.

title: Stochastic depth 0.05 at 24 epochs: does the regulariser buy a budget the control cannot spend?
description:
dropstack_light (sd 0.05, 12 epochs) read 0.8654 and PEAKED ON ITS LAST EPOCH, still climbing. Its control calib_dense_hold peaks at e6 (0.8634) and decays to 0.8598 by e11. So the 12-epoch budget was binding on the regularised run and not on the control -- the regulariser's real product may be EPOCHS, not the +0.0020 on the mean, which is noise-sized and reported as directional only.

ONE VARIABLE against dropstack_light: --epochs 12 -> 24. Nothing else moves.

PRICE: ~112 min (279 s/epoch measured x 24), no submission slot, zero extra compute per epoch over the control.
EXPECTED GAIN: P(clears 0.005 over 0.8654) ~ 0.45 -- the prior is strong because the curve had not turned. P(clears 1.5% over the 0.8634 control) ~ 0.12.
WHY THIS AND NOT THE RATE SWEEP the arm header pre-registered: a rate sweep maps a curve whose whole measured range spans 0.006. Only the budget lever has a mechanism that could plausibly deliver 1.5%, and CLAUDE.md says pick by whether the mechanism could deliver the bar, not by what is nearest to hand.

title: Best-of-5 on transfer residual: spend today's slots on 5 MAXIMALLY DIFFERENT entries, not 5 reseatings
description:
MEASURED PREMISE (2026-09-12, 50 honest board/offline pairs in comp/board.jsonl): pearson r=0.867, slope=+1.286, intercept=-0.1871, residual sd on board = 0.0087. Board gap to leader = 0.011 -> needs offline +0.0086 at that slope. The entire honest member pool spans 0.0049 end to end (clean_calib 0.8649 .. finding_calib_dense 0.8600), and four regularisation mechanisms at the dense corner are now measured out (mixup -0.0026, ema +0.0010, SAM refuted, dropstack pending). So offline is CAPPED and no reseating of the current pool can reach the step.

THE LEVER THAT REMAINS IS THE RESIDUAL ITSELF. 0.0087 of board variance is NOT explained by offline - it is idiosyncratic transfer to the real Kaggle test set, which is not our data (owner directive). An entry's board score is deterministic, so re-shipping the same member SET redraws nothing. Five DIFFERENT member sets draw five independent residuals; E[max of 5 standard normals] = 1.163 sigma = +0.0101 over the pool mean. That is the gap.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: not instrument spam, not reseating. Each entry must differ in MEMBER SET, and submit_check enforces set-inequality already. Rank candidate sets by mutual distance (member_distance.py), not by offline score, because offline no longer separates them.

WHAT WOULD REFUTE IT: if the five entries land within ~0.002 of each other, the residual is systematic (a property of our whole pool) rather than idiosyncratic per set, and best-of-N buys nothing. That is itself worth knowing and is the instrument reading.

Owner directive this serves verbatim: 'even if a single model doesnt outperform our previous models, its still worth testing if an ensemble with it have better performance - after all, its about diversity'.
close_reason: REFUTED BY ITS OWN DATA, 25 minutes after filing, before any slot was spent. The premise was that board residual sd 0.0087 is idiosyncratic transfer per member set, so five different sets draw five independent residuals and best-of-5 buys +1.16 sigma. FALSE. Measured over comp/board.jsonl: 54 ensembles with members>=6 have mean 0.937, sd 0.0086, and a hard MAX of 0.944 with TEN entries sitting exactly there (0.943 x6, 0.942 x2, 0.941 x3, 0.940 x2, 0.939 x3). The sd is carried by the bad tail (0.894, 0.908), not by spread at the top; the top is TRUNCATED. Best-of-N cannot beat a ceiling. No arrangement of this pool has ever exceeded 0.944 in 54 attempts. Converges with the ledger's own cnnseat_v1 row, written independently: '0.955 needs ONE member at ~0.874 offline against our best honest ~0.866.'

title: UNK maps to a hardcoded 0.28 across 27.3% of every ruler and supervision cell, with no derivation
description: report_labels_v2.csv is CORPUS_LABELS (column_surface.py:50) and every holdout number in the ledger is scored against it. Its 12 finding columns take exactly five values; 0.28 accounts for 14445 of 52872 cells (27.32%) and joins 1:1 to __conf 0.05 and __verdict UNK. So the uncertain-mention convention is a single undocumented constant governing more than a quarter of both the target and the scorer. D292 prices this axis from the literature: on CheXpert, holding images, architecture, split and labeler fixed and changing ONLY the uncertain-mention mapping moves weighted AUROC by 0.070 (U-Zeros vs U-Ones) and 0.040 (CheXbert) - a larger swing than the choice of labeler, and 2.7x this project's significance bar. This is the first mechanism-backed candidate for the five-axis flatness in knee-6xwun: no rearrangement of capacity, rate, per-depth schedule, loss or sampler can move a study whose target is wrong. BLOCKED ON DESIGN, not on the card: supervision and ruler are the same file, so moving 0.28 moves target and scorer together. Three candidate designs are in the 2026-09-10 ledger section and in M296 section 2; the researcher has the question. No arm is queued until it is settled.
notes: ANSWERED by the rung re-cut of 2026-09-12 (interpretation sec 6.6, zero card). UNCERTAIN_LEVEL = 0.28 is NOT a hardcoded value with no derivation: it is a v2 RUNG, and targets.py maps it through MEASURED_AGREEMENT to a trained target of 0.136. Re-cutting the 684 annotated cells (the pixel denominator MEASURED_AGREEMENT was itself fitted on) per rung gives 0.28 -> 24/177 = 0.136, Wilson (0.093, 0.194). It is derived, and it is correct, whenever calibrated_targets=True. Per finding after FINDING_OFFSETS: MCL 0.089 (annotated 0/6), Lateral OA 0.090 (annotated 0/22), Fracture 0.143 (annotated 4/26 = 0.154). All three sit inside their own intervals. The 27.3% figure stands as the share of cells affected; what does not stand is the claim that the value is underived. RESIDUAL, and it is why this is being closed rather than deleted: the derivation holds only under calibrated_targets=True. An arm running with it False trains UNK cells at the literal 0.28, which IS then an underived constant -- chainfour_v5blend and pool_specialise both run calibrated_targets False. That is a separate and narrower question than the one filed here.

title: The SSL pretrain objective never fit: pixel loss sat on its trivial value for 8 epochs, so all five 'in-domain SSL collapses' are evidence about the harness, not the idea
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 off the pretrain logs on disk, no card spent.

kneemri/training/spectral_mae.py:pixel_loss standardises each target patch to mean 0 / variance 1, so a decoder predicting the patch mean scores EXACTLY 1.0. That is the trivial solution and it is the number the runs sat on:

  logs/pretrain_matched_e8.log   e0 pixel 0.9859 spectral 1.2171  ->  e7 pixel 0.9682 spectral 0.4276
  logs/pretrain_lr1e5.log        e1 pixel 0.9775 spectral 0.7936  ->  e5 pixel 0.9799 spectral 0.6196

Eight epochs of masked reconstruction over 402,600 knee-MRI slices explained 3.2% of hidden-patch variance. The lr1e5 run explained 2% and REGRESSED from epoch 1. Meanwhile the spectral term fell 65% in both. Control that the box and the data are fine: mrnet_acl_pretrain on the same machine ran 1.1177 -> 0.5153 over 8 epochs, so a loss on this hardware does fit when the objective is sound.

WHY IT MATTERS. experiments/README.md records FIVE SSL-as-init collapses -- mae_matched 0.6735, 0.6875, encoder_adapt 0.6902, encoder_adapt_thawed 0.7162, encoder_adapt_lower 0.7309 -- each 0.09-0.15 below a control that starts from stock DINOv2, and the family is written up as CLOSED across two objectives and two import depths. Every suspect was cleared before that verdict (plumbing via adapt_null, data via a stamped cache key, variant via PretrainedEncoder.into, test via matched epochs). The one suspect nobody checked was whether the PRETRAIN ITSELF CONVERGED. It did not. A trunk carrying a representation that explains 3% of its own reconstruction target is not an in-domain representation, so the fine-tune destroying it is the correct behaviour and says nothing about domain-adaptive pretraining. The ledger's own diagnosis -- 'the score rises monotonically with how much of the SSL representation the fine-tune is allowed to overwrite' -- is exactly what an empty representation predicts.

The module even carries a guard for the MIRROR failure. kneemri/training/pretrain.py:145-146: 'a total that falls while the spectral term is flat means the run is a plain masked autoencoder wearing the name.' It watches for spectral-flat. What happened is pixel-flat, and nothing watched that direction.

SUSPECTS, ranked, none yet tested:
1. The spectral term dominates the gradient. spectral_weight defaults to 1.0 and the docstring says outright it is 'the arm's free variable and not a replicated constant' -- the paper does not state a weight. A log1p-magnitude spectral MSE over the whole unpatchified image is minimisable by matching a global envelope without solving any per-patch reconstruction, which is the degenerate optimum the curves describe: spectral -65%, pixel -1.8%.
2. The decoder is a single nn.Linear(dim, patch*patch) -- 384 -> 196. Argued sufficient on a full-sequence encoder by analogy to SimMIM, never measured here.
3. mask_ratio 0.6 with a full-sequence encoder: the docstring notes the encoder READS the masked positions, so copying a neighbour is available in a way it is not for MAE.

THE DECIDING EXPERIMENT IS CHEAP AND IS NOT A RE-RUN. --spectral-weight 0 for 2 epochs, ~15 min of card, both flags already exist (pretrain.py:230-231). If pixel loss falls away from 1.0 without the spectral term, suspect 1 is confirmed and the whole SSL family re-opens on a fixed objective. If pixel loss still sits at 1.0, suspect 1 is dead and the decoder/mask-ratio pair is next, still without touching the in-domain question.

DO NOT re-run any of the five collapse arms until the pretrain fits. Their scores are facts about an unconverged trunk.
notes: PRICE 2026-09-10: re-arm costs ~5.7 h of card (12 ep at 336/20, measured 1690/2114/1341 s on the killed attempt). P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.25, expected ~+0.005. Best ratio on the board because every remaining cheap instrument is priced at zero by its own pre-registration; corpus doubling is +0.009 and the site axis is negative. UPSTREAM GATE ALREADY PASSED: pretrain_unitfix pixel 0.9682 -> 0.5570 (3.2% -> 44% of hidden-patch variance). First attempt died 'trainer exit 127' (uv sync venv rewrite) at epoch 3 of 12, reading 0.6637/0.6898/0.6957 rising. Not a result.

title: A FOURTH duplicate ourtrunk44 took the card, and nothing in the tree can refuse a re-run of a finished foreign arm
description:
2026-09-08 10:17Z, pid 6616 (parent 43552): a fourth identical foreign_run --tag ourtrunk44 launched onto a card already running extended_band_s2026, taking the device to 31986 of 32607 MiB. Killed at 10:22Z by main after confirming the result was already on disk and already priced.

THE RESULT WAS FINISHED AND MEASURED. raptor_ft_ourtrunk44.holdout.npz dates from the 02:47Z run. experiments/README.md:10113 prices the member at -0.0007 add / +0.0007 swap (solo 0.8173 ledger75, nn-corr 0.8251 at pool251). So every one of these launches is a repeated experiment whose answer the ledger already holds, and the standing constraint forbids exactly that.

IT IS THE FOURTH, NOT THE FIRST. README:10190 records two duplicates at ~02:58Z, immediately after ARM DONE ourtrunk44 at ~02:57Z, and states they OVERWROTE raptor_ft_ourtrunk44.pt, .json and raptor_gold_ourtrunk44.npz. README:10687 records a third earlier today. That is the real cost: a duplicate does not merely waste the card, it destroys the artefacts of the run that finished.

WHY NO CHECK CATCHES IT. card_check reports OVERSUBSCRIBED but only after the fact, and only if somebody runs it. queue_check reads OK throughout, because a live process gating an owed arm is all it can see. At the previous kill no live watcher owed an ourtrunk44 launch, so the launcher had already fired and exited - two scripts can launch the tag (after_ourtrunk44.sh, after_resnet50d_lr.sh). Nothing asks the question that matters.

THE FIX, and it mirrors arm_check's refusal design rather than inventing one: foreign_run REFUSES at startup when the tag's own success artefact (raptor_ft_<tag>.holdout.npz) already exists, printing the artefact's mtime and the ledger row, with an explicit --anyway '<why>' override for a deliberate re-run. A finished arm's artefact is the one piece of evidence that is always present and always local, and refusing on it costs nothing when the artefact is absent. This closes the overwrite hole as well as the card-theft hole.

Not urgent-blocking any arm today; P0 because it has now cost the card four times and has silently destroyed measured artefacts at least twice.

title: Distilled fold-0 readings are leaky: OOF teachers trained on fold 0
description:
oof_fold_k (k=1..4) was fitted at --fold k, which trains on every OTHER fold, fold 0 included. Each teacher therefore memorised fold 0's labels. A student distilled from their targets on folds 1-4 and SCORED on fold 0 mimics four functions that carry fold 0 inside them: a label leak through function mimicry. The teacher never predicts fold 0 and does not have to.

WITNESSED BY THE BOARD, which is the un-leaked ruler. This family transfers offline->board at ~0.79 of the delta (spansolo 0.8545->0.921, holdsolo 0.8634->0.928). oof_teacher read 0.8681 offline, ABOVE holdsolo, and scored 0.926, BELOW it (ref 56065873). Pass-through 0.37 from the low anchor, negative from the high one.

AFFECTED: every *.holdout number produced under --teacher-targets teacher_oof_corpus.npz (and teacher_oof_full.npz, which is that file plus a fold-0 fill). Named: oof_teacher +0.0107, seat_distill_lr4e5 +0.0107 (0.8632). foreign_distill_mix07's 0.8656 uses a FOREIGN teacher - check whether its folds saw fold 0; if not, its +0.0061 is the cleanest distill term the project owns and the term is real at about half the claimed size.

FIX SHIPPED: --exclude-fold (ReportFolds.holdout's excluded), which drops a fold from TRAINING without putting it in the holdout. teacher_clean.sh refits the four twins with --exclude-fold 0; seat_clean_distill.sh re-reads the term against band_dense 0.8578 with the leak removed. Pre-reg >= 0.864 real / 0.860-0.864 knob / < 0.860 lever closes.

STILL OPEN: mark the affected ledger rows LEAKY (experiments/README.md); run the fold-0 sub-check (correlation of the student's fold-0 logits with the mean of the four teachers' IN-SAMPLE fold-0 logits, vs band_dense's correlation with the same) to witness the mechanism directly rather than by inference from the board.
notes: RESOLVED IN PART, 2026-09-07T03:20Z: the leak is REAL and it transferred ~ZERO AUC. seat_clean_distill (clean teachers, --exclude-fold 0) read 0.8634 peak e9, convergence_check clean, against its leaky twin seat_distill_lr4e5 0.8633 and the no-teacher control band_dense 0.8578. Removing the leak cost -0.0001, and it was NOT free to remove: the exclusion starves each teacher of ~900 of ~3500 studies and the four clean teachers priced -0.0067 mean on their own holdouts. So the clean student matched the leaky one out of a measurably weaker teacher set. Both the witness and the score are right: the student DID prefer the teachers that saw its holdout (+0.0127 diff-in-diff residual mimicry, control preferring the other set) and that preference bought no AUC. GENERAL SHAPE, worth more than the number: a leak visible in the RESIDUALS is not automatically a leak in the SCORE - the witness answers 'is it there', never 'is it the number', and only a re-run without it answers the second. CONSEQUENCE: seat_distill_lr4e5's +0.0107 is a treatment effect; retrain_six_distill (knee-ygi2k) is licensed and its kill switch did not fire; the five distilled members declined under the leak argument are ANSWERED rather than re-quoted (this reopens the TERM, not the seats - member axis stays closed on seven board flats). STILL OPEN: oof_teacher's 0.8681 and the oofsolo board inversion (0.926 from an offline read above holdsolo's 0.928) are a different corner and are NOT explained by this; the warning on that ledger row stands. seat_oof5_distill remains the only reading that prices the term at full teacher strength with the board as ruler. Ledger row + interpretation section written.

title: Every axis closed on a board FLAT may be UNRESOLVED, not closed - the public LB is ~400 studies
description: mastermind steer 13, 07:04Z. The public leaderboard is ~30 percent of 1,322 hidden studies = ~400 image-read studies. A board delta therefore carries a sampling half-width of its own, and the seat swaps the seven flats tested were priced OFFLINE at 0.001-0.003. If the board half-width at n=400 exceeds those deltas, the flats did not close their axes - they said the axes sit below the board's resolution, which is a different sentence and licenses different work. Axes closed on a board flat, from comp/board.jsonl: (1) seventh seat inert - sevengrade 0.931 vs sixfresh 0.931, reproduced by four later entries; (2) count 6 to 7 - dark7 0.937 vs dark6 0.937; (3) encoder FAMILY at seat seven - v3seat 0.936 vs two matched 0.937 controls; (4) member TYPE/regularisation - augseat 0.936 vs lastseat 0.937; (5) vote rule - votefit 0.938 vs dark6 0.937, one tick; (6) serving views/jitter - jitterfit 0.937 vs 0.937; (7) kit refresh - sixfresh_v2 0.931 identical to v1; (8) ordinal separation - accumseat 0.933 tie; (9) count with redundancy held high - sixstrong 0.930 vs sixfresh 0.931. Note (8) cross-family diversity via farseat is ALREADY void for a different reason (a member never loaded). Board scores are quantised to 0.001, so even a real 0.0005 effect is unreadable by construction. Instrument: kneemri.evaluation.paired_floor gives the paired bootstrap width; scale to n=400. Consequence already accepted by mastermind for slot policy: a slot is only spent on a candidate whose offline delta EXCEEDS the board half-width - reseatings and one-member swaps never qualify again.
notes: 2026-09-06 ANSWERED. Board resolution for a one-seat swap: 95% half-width 0.0011 at ~400 public studies (0.0007 at our 909), plus a 0.0005 rounding floor from three published decimals. Table of all nine flat-closed axes in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_board-flats-below-the-boards-resolution.md. Outcome: FOUR axes carry offline numbers and all four read under 0.0011 (closed on both rulers); FIVE are --fold -1 with offline:null and were closed on the only ruler that cannot resolve them (UNREAD, not closed). Nothing clears the pre-registered +0.003 reopen bar, so no stacking entry exists. What it licenses: no slot to a one-seat swap in either direction - a flat and a 0.001 win are equally uninformative.

title: Our holdout and the board disagree by 0.17 AUC on the only column both have measured
description: colmcl fixes MCL's board AUC at 0.980 (interval 0.968-0.992). Our 909-study fold-0 holdout scores the SAME ensemble's MCL column at 0.8104, the worst of our twelve. Same weights, same findings, 0.17 apart, and on the board it is nearly the best column while for us it is the worst. That 0.17 on one column is 0.014 of board, which is LARGER than the 0.009 gap to first place. Every seating decision this project has made - eight member declines, seven board flats, the honest12 baseline, seat_value's DISTINCT/SCALED/NOISY verdicts, the per-column headroom map that aimed the whole per-label lane - was made on that holdout. Four candidate mechanisms: label noise as TEST truth (our lexicon over-calls 108 FP to 32 misses per overcall_audit), prevalence variance (171/909 positives), case mix in the hidden test, or a definitional mismatch between our lexicon's MCL and the competition's. THE LOAD-BEARING SUB-QUESTION is whether a shared bias cancels in a PAIRED comparison between two members - my instinct is yes and the ordering survives, which is the only reason the seating decisions still stand, but that instinct is unverified and if it is wrong then eight declines and seven flats need re-reading. colbaker (Baker's, our strongest column at 0.9208) ships 04:56Z and colhalf (six-column set) ~09:32Z, giving a second and third point, but three of twelve will not give the shape. Put to Kimi as Q-RULER1-4 in .agent-runtime/inbox/20260905T0140Z-claude-ruler-disagreement.md.
notes:
DAWID-SKENE LATENT TRUTH PROPOSED AND CLOSED WITHOUT BUILDING IT (Kimi Q-RULER3, 2026-09-05T0143Z; audited and closed 0250Z). Kimi proposed treating the 58-study four-reader panel as a multi-annotator inference problem - Dawid-Skene EM for per-reader error rates and a latent true label per study - then scoring the model's MCL AUC against that latent truth, to test whether label noise or case mix drives the 0.17 board/holdout disagreement. The method is right and the panel cannot hear it.

core.data.labels.table_blend and kneemri.evaluation.table_separation already ran the experiment this proposal is a member of. Four blends of the same reader panel - the shipped one, the weakest reader dropped, a fourth reader added, and ours plus the single strongest reader - span 0.8894 to 0.8931 and EVERY pairwise interval among them covers zero, while the readers themselves separate cleanly (ours 0.8658, best foreign 0.8991, weakest 0.8352, all resolvably apart). The recorded conclusion: on 58 studies this ruler resolves about +/-0.008, and every blend recipe lives inside that; a better label table has to come from a better READER, not from a new weighting of the readers already here.

Dawid-Skene IS a new weighting of the readers already here - better motivated than a mean, per-reader error rates rather than equal votes, but inside the same +/-0.008 box. And the quantity it would feed is a per-column MCL AUC over roughly 18 panel positives, where Kimi's own Hanley-McNeil figure is SE 0.08-0.10. Both ends of the chain are wider than the effect being estimated.

So the 0.17 stays unexplained offline and that is now a closure rather than a to-do: Q-RULER5 established that case mix and definitional mismatch make identical offline predictions and cannot be separated without board labels or board cases, and this closes the remaining offline instrument. A per-column board map costs one slot per column, or group ablations under the sparsity assumption colhalf tests. What survives unchanged: label noise is the leading explanation with measured support, and paired member comparisons remain safer than absolute AUCs but are not immune where members differ in SUPERVISION - which is exactly the errors_* family.

With colnull having fixed the metric as a plain unweighted mean of twelve per-column AUCs, MCL board AUC = (0.944-0.904)x12+0.5 = 0.980, rounding interval 0.968-0.992. title: THE LABELER AXIS: our labels are Wollek's 0.858 rule-based row, and the learned-labeler row is 0.939
description:
A NEW AXIS, which is what knee-m69u asks for, and the first one this week with a published number an order of magnitude above the 0.0062 holdout floor.

THE PUBLISHED RESULT. Wollek et al., 'Automated Labeling of German Chest X-Ray Radiology Reports using Deep Learning' (arXiv:2306.05997, Fortschr Roentgenstr 2024), found by Kimi as A-QEC and written up in research/2026-09-04_qec-parser-vs-label-noise.md. They train the SAME DenseNet-121 on the SAME internal chest X-ray dataset and change only the LABELER: public ChestX-ray14 labels 0.720, rule-based CheXpert-style labeler 0.858, DL-based labeler (German BERT trained on rule-based plus manual labels) 0.939, manual radiologist labels 0.934. The learned labeler beats the rule-based parser by +0.081 downstream AUC and passes the manual-label control.

WHY IT LANDS ON US. report_reader is a lexicon parser, so this project's supervision IS that 0.858 row. Every label arm queued today - errors_dense (prune the flagged cells, knee-teh4) and its pair knee-f8hv5 (re-label them to the pool's held-out posterior) - trains AROUND the parser's errors. This axis fixes them at the source, which is the difference between the two columns of Wollek's own table. It also matches the error PATTERN the project already measured: the Q-AB taxonomy (interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-02_what-label-correction-is-actually-worth.md) finds CONSTRUCTION errors - hedged negation, severity thresholds, BME to contusion - which is exactly what a parser targets and exactly what a noise-robust loss cannot see.

WHAT MAKES IT CHEAP, AND IT IS THE BEST PROPERTY IT HAS. The axis is measurable at ZERO card and ZERO slots. 58 studies carry radiologist annotation, so a candidate labeler is scored against radiologist truth directly, per finding and pooled, beside v2's own row - no training run has to happen to learn whether the labels got better. Only a labeler that WINS that reading ever costs a card hour.

THE BLOCKER, AND IT IS PLUMBING RATHER THAN SCIENCE. knee-8hyr6 (P0, open since 2026-09-03, Kimi's tree and Kimi's run): the Qwen3.8 candidate table has 687 of 696 cells at UNK (98.7%) against v2's 177 of 684 (25.9%) on the same studies, and per finding exactly ONE study carries a non-UNK verdict. The vocabulary it does emit is correct, so ReadingPrompt and ReportReading.parse work when handed a response - the endpoint returned nothing 57 times. Scored as-is it would read as 'the LLM is a far worse reader' and retire this axis on a measurement that never happened. Sent to Kimi as T-ED 2026-09-04T1543Z with the three hypotheses ranked (truncation with finish_reason == length, checkable by the prediction that the one study that succeeded has the shortest answer; swallowed per-request exceptions; a model alias returning an error object under HTTP 200), plus the denominator trap: the candidate has 58 studies and v2 has 57 of them, so score on the intersection.

WHAT THIS IS NOT, AND THE HONEST LIMIT. A-QEC also returned an honest null on the comparison I actually asked for: no published head-to-head exists where a parser repair is measured against an off-the-shelf label-noise method on the same corpus. So this axis is not established as BETTER than knee-teh4's, only as having a much larger published effect on its own. Wollek is chest X-ray, single-label pneumothorax, German reports; ours is knee MRI, twelve labels, English. The +0.081 is a mechanism floor, not our expected gain, and it must never be quoted as our number. Board transfer is UNKNOWN.

PRICE: the gold-58 reading costs no card and no slot. Only if a candidate labeler beats v2 against radiologist truth does a training arm follow, and that arm is ~4 h. P(a fixed endpoint produces a labeler that beats v2 on the gold 58) is genuinely unknown - the one attempt so far never ran. That is why the first step is a plumbing fix and a non-UNK-rate census, not a score.

Blocked on: knee-8hyr6.
notes:
ARMED 2026-09-07 02:55Z: compose_v4b_clean.sh - the MIDDLE rule's own successor test ('the label axis composes with distillation or it is not worth a seat'), with the leaky teacher replaced by teacher_clean. One variable off labels_v4hybrid.sh: --distill-weight 0.7 --teacher-targets teacher_clean.npz. Matched control labels_v4hybrid_s2026 (v2 holdout 0.8524, gold 58 0.9063), both on disk. THE MECHANISM UNDER TEST is teacher PROVENANCE: every teacher block was fitted on v2, so a v4b student pulled toward them is pulled back toward the errors the table swap removed. title: Encoder can load ZERO pretrained tensors and train silently — radiodino_corpus burned 62min of card on a random-init ViT
description: radiodino_corpus_s2026 ran 3 epochs (0.6501/0.6714/0.6813) with a RANDOMLY INITIALISED trunk. Its log reads 'Loading weights: 0it' and a ViTModel LOAD REPORT where every checkpoint key is UNEXPECTED and every model key is MISSING: Snarcy/RadioDino-b16 ships timm names (blocks.*, patch_embed, cls_token, pos_embed), transformers ViTModel wants HF names (layers.*, embeddings.*). Nothing refused. The arm pre-registers four outcomes about medical-corpus pretraining; all four are unreadable, and REFUTES (<0.80) would have blamed the corpus for a loader bug and retired MRI-CORE on it. Killed at 10:29Z. Denominator: of 232 run logs, 15 print a LOAD REPORT and exactly 1 reads 0it — this instance only. But a PARTIAL load is silent too, and medsam prints no report at all. FIX: refuse at load time, like run_setup.py:397 refuses --batch 1 with a nonzero ranking term. A --variant naming a pretrained checkpoint that matches zero (or few) of its keys must ABORT, not train.
notes:
SWEEP RUN 2026-09-04T11:07Z, CLEAN. python -m kneemri.models.load_check over the whole registry: 16 entries, every declared dim equal to the loaded trunk's own hidden_size, no refusals. radiodinob16 now reads 768 through TimmHubWeights. So RadioDino was the ONLY entry ever handing a run a randomly-initialised trunk — the question a single fixed entry cannot answer.

Shipped as ea12b3e7 (gates green, pushed): the gate (Encoder.refuse_unloaded at the seam both hub loaders pass through, exact via output_loading_info), the fix (kneemri/models/timm_trunk.py), the sweep (kneemri/models/load_check.py, by hand because it fetches every trunk).

Kimi Q-DO then read the actual weight keys of every remaining candidate: RadioDino s16 (vit_small_patch16_224, 384) and s8 (vit_small_patch8_224, 384) carry the SAME fault and load through TimmHubWeights unchanged; BiomedCLIP is timm-keyed nested under visual.trunk. and needs a subtree strip; RadImageNet is torchvision-keyed and our StateDictWeights row already loads it strict=True so it cannot under-load; MRI-CORE is not on HF at all.
close_reason: Gate, fix and registry sweep all shipped in ea12b3e7 (gates green, pushed): Encoder.refuse_unloaded aborts at the seam both hub loaders pass through, using output_loading_info so the check is exact rather than heuristic; kneemri/models/timm_trunk.py carries the fix; kneemri/models/load_check.py swept all 16 registry entries with no refusals and every declared dim equal to the loaded trunk's hidden_size. RadioDino was the only entry that ever handed a run a randomly-initialised trunk. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE, recorded here because it is the part that outlives the bug: radiodino_corpus's three epochs are VOID rather than negative - all four of its pre-registered outcomes were unreadable, and REFUTES would have retired MRI-CORE on a loader bug. The arm is re-runnable and stays queued behind errors_dense.

title: arm_check EXECUTES every arm script, so seven no-run_train arms (three on the GPU) run for up to 30s on every pre-flight
description: arm_check harvests each arm's flags by RUNNING the script against a stub lib (arm_check.py:196, [[str(arm)] for arm in sorted(self.arms.glob('*.sh'))]). The stub shadows run_train, so a normal arm prints its flags and does no work. after_ortho_encode.sh is not a normal arm: line 9 is 'timeout 21600 .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m kneemri.embeddings.build_ortho_embeddings --batch 4', a real command outside run_train, so the stub neutralises nothing and arm_check launches a six-hour GPU job. --only filters AFTER the harvest, so it does not prevent it. Observed twice on 2026-09-04 within twenty minutes: pids 25956 and 10020, each appearing on the card seconds after an 'arm_check --only band_pairmem', each contending with the live radiodino_corpus arm, each killed by hand after card_check reported OVERSUBSCRIBED. The pre-flight that exists to save card time spends it, and it does so silently - arm_check's own output says nothing about having started anything. This also means every arm_check run since after_ortho_encode.sh was added has been racing whatever held the card, and any timing read during one is suspect. TWO FIXES, not exclusive: (a) the stub should neutralise or refuse a script that invokes anything outside run_train, since executing arbitrary commands to read a declaration is the wrong mechanism - parse the invocation instead of running it, or run under a PATH where python is a no-op; (b) after_ortho_encode.sh is a DRIVER, not an arm, and does not belong in experiments/arms - it has no run_train call, no pre-registration and no reading, so nothing in the arms contract fits it.
notes:
REOPENED 2026-09-04 — the close was wrong and the defect was real.

The close rested on: 'exactly one arm names .venv/Scripts/python.exe directly (after_ortho_encode.sh) and it runs set -u against ${1}, so invoked bare it aborts before the line'. It does not abort. The expansion is inside a pipeline, so set -u kills the SUBSHELL and leaves the script running; tasklist then fails, the leading ! turns that failure into true, and the until loop exits on its first iteration straight into a six-hour build_ortho_embeddings.

Reproduced by running the file bare with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 and a 6 s timeout — exactly how invocations() runs it. Output: two 'line 7: 1: unbound variable' lines, then 'starting ortho encode', then 'loaded 3 plane denoisers', then 'encoding 4407 studies'. The encode was live within six seconds.

Cost, twice: a six-hour timeout-wrapped build on a card a live arm held. On 2026-09-04 it halved medsam_dense from 508 to 280 img/s and was six seconds behind an arm_check call, which is what finally attributed it.

FIXED in 33814d68 — explicit [ $# -ge 1 ] guard in the shell, and the watcher moved to experiments/ so the arms/*.sh glob no longer reaches it. The invariant to check on any new arm: nothing under arms/ may reach an interpreter without going through uv, because stub_lib.sh's no-op uv is the only thing making this lint inert.

title: The offline-to-board slope has never been fitted outside the DINOv2 family, and ortho_solo cannot fix that alone
description:
ortho_solo_v1 (ref 55994354) put the project's first non-DINOv2 point on the board: ortho_dense_s2026 alone, honest fold-0, offline 0.8452 -> board 0.907. board_transfer prices EVERY arm here, and every pair fitting it comes from a DINOv2-family trunk.

The point cannot be read yet and the row in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md says so. 0.907 against soloseat_v1 0.925 / calibsolo 0.923 / raptor_solo 0.923 is NOT a measured family penalty: all three are --fold -1 and saw every holdout study. The only honest-offline solo in the record is solo_v1 (0.8518 -> 0.868), 2026-08-12, a different kit and decode.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT A READING: two current-kit DINOv2 solos served alone at --fold 0, at separated offlines, giving the in-family solo line; the ortho point then sits on it or under it. Candidates already on disk with honest fold-0 records: calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634, small_batch6_s2026 0.8598, through_dense_s2026 0.8558, calib_span_s2026 0.8545 (record_mix, 2026-09-03). Two of those span 0.0089 offline, which is above the holdout's 0.0053 resolution floor.

COST: two slots, zero card. GATE IT ON ortho_stack: if the continued ViT-L does not clear band_dense the family may be dead anyway and the slope question is academic.
notes:
RAISED P1->P0 2026-09-04. The scope defect that hid this is fixed: four board.jsonl rows carried scope='included', a value in neither reader's vocabulary — green in board_check (which only tests != EXCLUDED), silently dropped by board_transfer (which fits == 'ensemble'). Corrected to 'ensemble': the fit goes 34 entries/436 pairs -> 37/530. Planning constant UNCHANGED (+0.97 at >=0.8678).

WHAT CHANGED IS THE INVERSIONS. Resolved-pair inversions went 0/276 -> 2/342, and BOTH have ortho_solo_v1 on one side (solo_v1 holdout +0.0066 board -0.039; onedecode_v2 holdout +0.0101 board -0.003). ortho_solo carries the LOWEST offline of all 37 (0.8452) and read 0.907 — about +0.02 board above where the DINOv2-fitted slope puts it.

ONE observation, not two, and the confound is TOTAL: offline level and date are collinear in this record (every low-offline entry is 08-12..08-24, every late entry is high-offline), so 'ortholarge transfers better than its holdout says' and 'the current kit transfers better than the August kits' predict the same thing. This bead's instrument — two CURRENT-KIT DINOv2 solos at --fold 0 at separated offlines — is the only thing that breaks that collinearity. It was speculative when filed; there is now a candidate effect worth +0.02 board on the table. Two slots, zero card.

IT ALSO TOUCHES ortho_stack, on the card now: its middle pre-registered branch (within 0.0062 of band_dense = close the in-domain trunk lane) assumes offline order transfers, which for this trunk family is the thing in question. Branch NOT moved — annotated as conditional on this instrument coming back null. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_the-ruler-had-four-rows-outside-it.md
close_reason: Both anchors scored and both are >=0.900: spansolo_v1 0.921 at offline 0.8545, holdsolo_v1 0.928 at 0.8634. That is the pre-registered branch — the KIT ERA explains ortho_solo_v1's +0.02, ortholarge is not special, and board_transfer's whole-record slope is era-contaminated and needs refitting within era. Reading in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_kit-era-not-ortholarge.md; both rows in comp/board.jsonl.

title: --batch 1 silently switches the ranking term OFF; ortho_stack ran 3 epochs void
description:
RankedObjective.ranking forms pairs WITHIN the micro-batch via pairs(batch, batch), and self-pairs drop out (objective.py:317-324, 346-349). At --batch 1 no pair forms, so the term contributes exactly zero. --accumulate does not repair it: it sums gradients of micro-batch losses each computed alone.

MEASURED, not argued. ortho_stack void run: step-80 loss 0.6785. Same arm with --pair-memory 66: 1.3774. Control band_dense (batch 12, term on): 1.3598 at step 29. The halved loss WAS the missing term.

WHY IT SURVIVED THE GUARDS. Objective.settings() reports the CONSTRUCTOR's weight, so the recipe line records rank_weight 1.0 whether or not a pair ever formed. objective.py:159-161 warns about precisely this failure mode ('a --rank-weight that never reached the constructor trains plain cross-entropy under a ranking arm name and reports a number that reads as a refutation of the mechanism') but only covers flag dispatch, not batch size.

COST. ortho_stack reached epoch 2 at 0.8010 vs band_dense 0.8197 and was killed there. Its middle branch CLOSES the in-domain trunk lane - the only open lever - and it would have closed it against a control training a different objective. v3large_stack was queued with the same defect.

FIXED in both arms with --pair-memory 66, derived: band_dense at batch 12 forms C(12,2)=66 pairs a label, so M=66 matches the pair mass; staleness is lower both in optimiser steps (5.5 vs 8) and epoch share (1.9% vs 2.7%).

STILL OPEN, and this is the actual bug to fix: nothing REFUSES a rank-weight arm at batch 1 with pair_memory 0. arm_check or run_setup should raise, the way run_setup already raises for --pair-memory without --rank-weight. Until then any low-batch arm can repeat this. Audit other arms in the ledger that combine --rank-weight with a small --batch.
close_reason: Guard landed (run_setup._check_pairs_can_form, raises before the card, names all four silenced flags). The AUDIT this bead asked for is done and split out: sixteen arms across the ConvNeXt, Swin, RadImageNet and raptor-feature families ran --batch 1 with no --pair-memory, so every one trained plain cross-entropy under a ranking arm's name. See the new P0.
