title: The 224 pixel group is a complete second one-decode roster, already built and never read as a group
description:
FOURTEEN fold-0 checkpoints sit at (12 slices, band 0.2-0.8, 224px): adjacent224, base224, blendhold, confident224, holdannot, labelwise224, mixup224, mixup224_long, mixup224_strong, native224, native224_long, nocycle224_long, normcount224, tissue224. They were fitted as a RESOLUTION family, one arm at a time, and every reading of them was a member-quality reading against a 336 control. Nobody has ever asked what they are worth AS A GROUP.

WHY THAT IS NOW THE QUESTION. trioseat_v1 scored 0.938 by seating three members that share one decode, +0.013 over a single seat for one decode's cost — the first evidence in this project that a pixel group holds several seats. If that holds, a group of fourteen is not fourteen members; it is one decode with up to fourteen seats behind it.

WHY THIS GROUP RATHER THAN ANY OTHER. Its decode is the cheapest we own: 94 s/epoch against 336's 290, a measured 3.1x, at a member cost of -0.0023 (native224 0.8502 vs the 336 control lr4e-5_ws 0.8525) which is INSIDE the 0.0062 holdout floor — flat, not worse, and knee-s9cr already corrected the record that this was untested. Both rival self-reported singles above ours (0.942, 0.938) are at 224.

So it is the one lever that moves all three of the things being asked for at once: a new pixel group is the decode axis knee-nas5 measured transferring at 2.4x (SCORE), the cheapest decode we own is the efficiency-prize entry (EFFICIENCY, where our row is stale at 0.925 while accuracy shows 0.943), and a 3.1x epoch is the budget every future arm is fitted in (EXPERIMENT SPEED).

COST TO FIND OUT: ZERO CARD. All fourteen checkpoints are on disk. Only base224_s2026 and blendhold_s2026 are packaged in dimiturnt/kneemri-members; the other twelve are a dataset push and no fit. experiments/arms/trio_seat_value.sh (knee-vfnr) now prices this pool TWICE — against trioseat_v1, asking whether two one-decode groups compose, and against the pinned champion, asking whether a cheap decode earns a seat in our best roster at all. It is queued behind merged_span_cf.

A positive against the champion is a SCORE result and outranks everything else queued. A positive against trioseat with a negative against the champion is an efficiency-only play, which is still a prize we are entered for. Both negative kills the group as a group and leaves 224 as what it already was: a cheap fit for future arms.
notes:
2026-08-29 10:05 UTC — THE WHOLE-DISK MAP, measured by a tool rather than by hand, and it corrected the hand numbers.

`python -m kneemri.kaggle.roster_reads` (new; groups raw checkpoints by `Member.decode_key`, the SAME
property `Ensemble.reads` serves under, so its answer cannot drift from what a submission does) over all
195 `.pt` under the processed root — 7 of which describe no reading and are teachers or partial saves:

  108 members at [224, 336, 448]  canonical / 12 slices / band 0.2-0.8 / centre image / crop 130mm
   58 members at [336]            canonical / 20 slices / band 0.1-0.9 / centre image / crop 130mm
    9 members at [336]            canonical / 12 slices / band 0.1-0.9
    3 members at [336]            canonical / 20 slices / band 0.2-0.8
    ... nine more reads of one or two members each
  188 seats on 13 decodes = 14.5 seats per decode

TWO LARGE READS, and they are NOT equivalent:

  read A — 20 slices, 0.1-0.9:  58 on disk, 27 packaged, 3 seated (trioseat_v1), 336 ONLY
  read B — 12 slices, 0.2-0.8: 108 on disk, 19 packaged, 1 seated (the champion's lr4e-5_ws_cf),
                               carrying 224 AND 336 AND 448

Read B is the bigger pool AND the only one holding several resolutions, so it offers treatment AND
resolution diversity for one decode — and it is the read seated ONCE. Read B is the better read and it
is the one we barely use.

WHAT IS BUILDABLE TODAY: 46 packaged members already ride those two reads, so an entry seating all of
them costs TWO decodes, no card time and no dataset push — a kernel edit and a slot. The pinned champion
spends about four decodes to seat seven.

The hand grouping this bead's earlier note used said 49 and ~30; both were wrong (really 58 and 108),
because the hand pass grouped a filtered subset. The tool is the correction, which is the argument for it.

It also found four members in trio_seat_value.sh's own GROUP2 candidate list that would each have cost a
SECOND read: tissue224_s2026 and centre_tissue_s2026 (centre tissue), crop80_tissue_s2026 (80mm),
adjacent224_s2026 (spacing adjacent). Dropped from that list; they belong to the decode-distance
question, not the free-seat one.

STILL A COST RESULT. Nothing here says a seat is worth taking; correlated members from one cell most
likely price at zero. trio_seat_value.sh is the gate, and the bar is the 0.0062 holdout floor alone,
since there is no decode budget left to trade against.

title: Treatment diversity is a SEAT axis, not a decode axis: trioseat bought +0.013 from one pixel group
description:
OPENED 2026-08-29 by trioseat_v1 reading 0.938 against a pre-registered 0.925-0.929.

THE MEASUREMENT. final_ws_cf, grade_ladder_cf and through_dense_cf are matched on slices (20), band (0.1-0.9), image size (336) and backbone (dinov2-small). They differ only in SUPERVISION TREATMENT: final weight-averaging, the grade ladder, the through-plane read. Served at 1/3 each through one decode they read 0.938, +0.013 over `soloseat_v1` 0.925 -- level with onepair_v1's +0.011, which bought its bonus by crossing an architecture boundary and paying for a second decode.

WHY THIS IS A P0. Every roster decision in this ledger for the last week has been priced off knee-nas5's pixel-group collapse (0.0059 offline arriving as 0.014 board) and off the architecture-monoculture interpretation, both of which were being read as 'seats in one pixel group are redundant'. They never measured that. What they measured is that PIXEL GROUPS collapse. Treatment does not travel with the pixel group, and on this board it is worth as much per seat as architecture distance while costing nothing at inference beyond a head.

WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, AND WHY IT SERVES BOTH PRIZES AT ONCE. A roster maximising treatment diversity inside a SMALL number of decodes is simultaneously the accuracy play (more seats that actually disagree) and the efficiency play (few decodes). The efficiency track's top 20 span 0.925-0.948 with median 0.935; trioseat already clears that median at one decode.

THE OPEN QUESTION THIS DOES NOT ANSWER. Whether treatment diversity and decode diversity ADD or substitute. raptorseat 0.943 holds ~4 decodes and 7 treatments and cannot separate them. The clean next instrument is a roster with MORE treatments at the SAME one decode -- a quadruple or a quintuple inside the (20, 0.1-0.9) cell -- read against trioseat 0.938. If the count keeps paying inside one group, the decode axis is a smaller share of the champion's bonus than the ledger currently assumes, and the cheap lane is much longer than one entry.

FIRST STEP COSTS NO CARD: the pool holds 131 arms. Enumerate every existing checkpoint that already sits at (20 slices, 0.1-0.9) and differs by treatment, and greedy them offline on the fold-0 holdout. Only then spend a slot.
notes:
2026-08-29 14:24Z — CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT ON THE WHOLE POOL, and the arm built for it is retired.

The question was 'how many treatment seats does one decode hold?' It is answered, and not on a sample:
198 checkpoints enumerate to 191 members on 13 reads (14.7 seats per decode). Read B — canonical / 12
slices / band 0.2-0.8 / centre image / 130 mm / tie first / spacing spread — holds 108 members across
[224, 336, 448]; read A holds 59 at 336 only. Resolution is not in Member.decode_key and neither pooling
is, so one read serves three sizes.

ALL 41 SCOREABLE READ-B CANDIDATES were priced against honest12 (108 minus five smoke/other-fold, minus
confident224_s2026 which RecordMix refuses under a different label table, minus every checkpoint with no
holdout record). Best marginal +0.0003 (merged_blend_s2026), second +0.0001 (blendlabels_s2026),
everything else 0 to -0.0005. seat_value's own verdict: 'best is +0.0003, inside +0.0015: this ruler
cannot tell it from the incumbent.' The earlier 24-candidate pricing read the same number to the fourth
decimal, so this is the same null at 3.7x the denominator, not a confirmation of a sample.

THE PATTERN AT 41 IS THE FINDING, not the value. Every one of the 41 shares ONE best move — swap out
honest12's dud mae_matched_s2026 (0.6735 solo). Not a single candidate is a marginal ADDITION. A free
seat on a saturated read buys nothing; the only value on that read is not being the worst member already
sitting on it.

THE CONTROL BIASES THIS UPWARD, so the null is stronger than it reads. honest12 is 0.006 weaker on the
board than the pinned champion, and a seat is easier to earn in a weaker roster. It is also FORCED, not
preferred: every member of raptorseat_v1 and trioseat_v1 is fold -1, has seen every holdout study, carries
no holdout record, and seat_value refuses both rosters by name.

WHAT SURVIVES. The COST half only, as an efficiency-track lens (knee-7lyz): 44 seats on 2 decodes against
the champion's 7 on ~4 is a real runtime argument even though it is not a score argument.
WHAT IS RETIRED. experiments/arms/trio_seat_value.sh and experiments/arms/packaged_seats.sh, their
watchers killed and their after.sh markers deleted; queue_check reads clean.
WHAT IT POINTS AT. Decode DISTANCE, the lane the nulls left open — experiments/arms/crop80_tissue_full.sh
(knee-17kn), queued behind ARM DONE raddino_dense. It is confounded today because every distant member we
own is also a weak one, and crop80_tissue's weakness has a recorded cause that is not the mechanism
(--epochs 8 against everyone else's 12).

title: The champion is an architecture MONOCULTURE, and that is the mechanical cause of the 0.937-0.941 plateau
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-28 by dumping all six calibsix member configs. Every member of comp/champion.json is facebook/dinov2-small (DIM 384, 22M) at img=336, whole_stack=True, the SAME six slots (SAG_FLUID_FS, COR_FLUID_FS, AX_FLUID_FS, SAG_FLUID_NOFS, COR_T1, SAG_T1), the SAME head (pool=cls_mean token pool -> slice_pooling=max -> slot_pooling=attend SlotHead), encoder_layer=-1, lora_rank=0, crop_mm=130.0, head_lr=1e-3, backbone_lr=4e-5, rank_weight=1.0.

THREE THINGS VARY ACROSS THE WHOLE CHAMPION: slices (12 vs 20), band ([0.1,0.9] vs [0.2,0.8]), and through_plane (True on through_dense_cf alone). That is RECIPE diversity, not architecture diversity, and it is the direct mechanical explanation for seven differently-seated entries landing in a 0.004 band (0.937-0.941) against a 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil floor: seven ways of reseating six copies of one lens.

THE ROSTER'S ONLY NON-DINOv2 MEMBER is lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026.pt at 0.8215, too weak to have ever earned a seat.

THE SINGLE-MODEL CEILING IS NOT DINOv2's FAULT. calibsolo scored 0.923 and the foreign raptor_v4_swa (coatnet_rmlp_2_rw_384 at 384 px, different corpus, different decode, different head) scored 0.923 the SAME DAY. title: RAD-DINO cold re-run: the only medical-pretrained trunk we own was killed on a run with the wrong normalization
description:

THE DEFECT THAT VOIDS THE OLD NUMBER. raddino_dense ran 2026-08-23 and entered the ledger at 0.8137, -0.0375 against base_dense 0.8512, and the owner's ban list has carried 'do NOT re-queue raddino_dense (refuted)' ever since. The normalization fix landed 2026-08-25 in commit 3b74685 — TWO DAYS AFTER the run. For its entire twelve epochs RAD-DINO was fed the ImageNet constants while its own preprocessor_config.json declares 0.5307/0.2583 (greyscale, repeated over three channels): inputs 0.20 std off its pretraining distribution with a 12.8 percent scale error. The CONTROL was correct, because DINOv2-base does declare the ImageNet constants. So the one preprocessing difference the arm header called shared was in fact DIFFERENTIAL and pointed AGAINST the arm being tested.

That is a faulty-PLUMBING kill, not a refutation, and it is the third defect on the same number: the run was also TRUNCATED at epoch 7 of 12 under one_cycle (so the anneal never ran and 0.8137 is a FLOOR), and its recipe was tuned across ~189 DINOv2 runs. Three defects, one number, and no claim about radiology pretraining survives any of them.

THE BAN IS NOT BROKEN. The standing ban is on the WARM start and the RATE refit. This is neither: it is a COLD re-run from the HuggingFace checkpoint. A warm start is in fact impossible — the 2026-08-23 checkpoint carries the wrong constants baked into its own state dict as persistent buffers, which is what makes the owner's ban correct twice over. The arm file experiments/arms/raddino_dense.sh was already rewritten on 2026-08-25 to say exactly this and has been sitting unarmed since.

WHY IT IS THE BIGGEST LEVER ON THE BOARD. The champion is six DINOv2-small at 336 px with one head, one slot scheme and one slot list; only slices (12/20), band and one through_plane flag vary. Seven differently-seated entries span 0.937-0.941 against a 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil floor — the seating lane is saturated. RAD-DINO is the most pixel-distant trunk in the pool and the greedy search already reached for it (greedy 54: 0.8670 +raddino_dense) on its BROKEN number.

PRE-REGISTRATION is in the arm header, unchanged and binding: >=0.866 radiology initialisation is the lever (licenses RadImageNet) / 0.856-0.865 directional, seat it if a seat is free, do not plan around it / 0.846-0.855 a tie, kills the chest-radiograph route at this domain distance / <=0.845 SUSPECT THE HARNESS FIRST. title: Matched 58-study read: our member is LEVEL with Raptor (0.9152 vs 0.9167), and knee-rh4t's 0.017 member gap was a two-ruler artefact
description:
Both sides hold out the same 58 radiologist-annotated studies (our *_hold members train with --hold-annotations; their corpus is 4349 = 4407-58), so their published per-label 'aucs' and our cached annotated_predictions are on ONE ruler for the first time.

Macro: calib_span_hold 0.9152 vs raptor_ft_coatnet_v4_full 0.9167, delta +0.0016 against a macro SE of ~0.012. A genuine null.

CONSEQUENCE for knee-rh4t: the ~0.017 member gap was built by comparing our BOARD single (soloseat 0.925) to rivals' FORUM claims (0.938-0.942). Those are different rulers on different studies. On a matched ruler there is no gap. knee-rh4t is not refuted -- the board numbers are what they are -- but its MECHANISM sentence ('their member is better') is now unsupported, and the residual has to be explained by something other than member quality.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: n=58. Hanley-McNeil SE per label runs 0.031-0.072, so no single per-label delta clears. The per-label complementarity pattern (they win Medial OA +0.0884, Lateral OA, Effusion, Bakers; we win PF OA -0.1017, Lateral Meniscus, ACL, Medial Meniscus) is a HYPOTHESIS. The per-label oracle reads +0.0188 over the better single, and max-of-two-noisy-draws at this SE manufactures ~0.023 by itself -- so the oracle is fully explained by selection noise and is NOT evidence.

NEXT: knee-9g28 scores their checkpoints on our 909-study fold-0 holdout, 15x the studies, which is the test that can actually settle the complementarity claim.
notes:
2026-08-28 00:47Z — THE RE-SCORE THIS BEAD ASKED FOR IS IN, AND SELECTION IS NOT THE EXPLANATION.

calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634 beats calib_span_hold_s2026 0.8565), read on the 58:

  calib_span_hold  (chosen ON the 58)  0.9152        +0.0016              -
  calib_dense_hold (named in advance)  0.9117        +0.0051           +0.0033
  macro SE ~0.012 either way — both are still nulls on 58 studies.

THE SELECTION TERM IS 0.0035, AND IT IS OVER SIX ARMS, NOT 105. The cache holds six *_hold members
(0.8932-0.9152), so this bead's own note overstated the search: max-over-6 at this SE, not max-over-105.
Measured, the maximum buys 0.9152 - 0.9117 = 0.0035.

CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE POINT. 0.0035 is a TENTH of the 58-vs-909 disagreement (+0.0016 against
-0.0350, a swing of 0.037). Removing the selection effect moves the 58 delta from +0.0016 to +0.0051 and
leaves the disagreement essentially intact. So the 58 and the 909 do not disagree because our member was
picked on the small set. They disagree because the SETS differ — the 58 flatter our member by 0.059 and
theirs by 0.025, and that asymmetry survives naming the member in advance.

A SECOND FACT, FREE FROM THE SAME READ: the two rulers ORDER our members differently.

(0.9117 < 0.9152). n=58 cannot order two members 0.0035 apart against a macro SE of 0.012, so this is

WHAT IS STILL OPEN. Why the 58 flatter our members so much more than theirs. The 58 are radiologist-

SOURCE (the 58 answer radiologists, the 909 answer report-derived labels our members were trained on —

description:

  raptor-knee-widedense    raptor_ft_coatnet_v4_full.pt        gold 0.9167   coatnet_rmlp_2_rw_384   res 384  ep 12

  raptor-knee-finespacing  raptor_ft_coatnet_v9_full.pt        gold 0.9031   same                    res 384  ep 12

                           raptor_ft_effv2l480.pt              gold 0.8716   tf_efficientnetv2_l     res 480  ep 12
Every checkpoint loads under torch.load(weights_only=True) - no untrusted pickle is executed - and SELF-DESCRIBES: timm arch string, resolution, epoch, per-label aucs, and gold_auc on the 58 annotated. 0.9167 matches the number their notebook claims, so the file is self-consistent with its own publication. PERMITTED. comp/README.md:165, settled from COMPETITION_RULES.txt: 2.6.a permits External Data 'publicly available and equally accessible to all Participants at no cost' and 2.6.b permits models 'unless specifically prohibited by the Host'. The Host has prohibited exactly one corpus, KneeCoT (topic 734109), and it is not this.

THE MEASUREMENT, AND IT SPENDS NO SLOT. Rebuild their RaptorClassifier (backbone + per-finding attention head; 486 tensors, clsW/clsb + backbone.* + att.*), run their five-slot 64-slice decode, and score all six on OUR fold-0 holdout beside our own members. That puts a rival member on OUR ruler for the first time, which is what every previous attempt to price this gap lacked.

WHAT IT DECIDES, pre-registered.
  * A Raptor checkpoint scores at or above our best member (calib_dense_hold_s2026, 0.8634 holdout). Then it is BOTH the best member and the most architecturally distant one we have - CoAtNet/EffV2/ConvNeXtV2 against our ResNet/DenseNet/DINOv2 family - and seating it is the largest single lever on the board. Spend a slot on it.
  * It lands mid-pack among our members. Then the 0.017 board gap is NOT carried by their backbone or recipe, and the honest reading is that board-vs-holdout compression is doing the work - which retires the member-gap panic and redirects the schedule.
  * It lands below our members. Then their published set is genuinely their 0.924 tier, their unreleased 0.936-0.938 is where the gap lives, and the lever is the recipe delta they have not published.
In all three branches the number is on our ruler and costs no submission. That is the best ratio available today.

WHAT HAS ALREADY BEEN RULED OUT as the source of the gap, by reading their notebook against our code and NOT by guessing:
  * SLICE SPAN. They take 6-94% of the stack and say cutting the ends cost them collateral-ligament and lateral-meniscus accuracy. We measured that axis with three trained points - 0.20-0.80 = 0.8525, 0.10-0.90 = 0.8565, 0.00-1.00 = 0.8427, an interior optimum - and every shipped member already passes --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9.   * mm-BASED CROP. They crop 140 mm by DICOM pixel spacing; we crop 130 mm the same way, with an 80 mm detail scale beside it.

title: Per-diagnosis slice attention: our own head says it is next, and a 0.924 rival says it matters more than anything else
description:
FOUND 2026-08-26 23:52Z by reading the competition forum, not our ledger. Kaggle user dreaddevelopment published BOTH halves of the model behind a 0.924 public inference notebook: kernels 'knee-mri-twelve-findings-from-a-single-model' (84 votes) and 'knee-mri-training-the-twelve-finding-model'. Both are pulled to external/raptor/. Five fine-tuned checkpoints are also public as datasets (raptor-knee-arms, raptor-knee-arms-x, raptor-cnn336) across three architectures we do not have — ConvNeXt-v2-B@336, CoAtNet@384, EfficientNetV2-L@480. The author states in forum topic 737696 that the same set unblended scores 0.936-0.938.

THE LEVER, AND WHY IT IS A P0 AND NOT A KNOB.

Their head is an attention-MIL pool with ONE ATTENTION CHANNEL PER FINDING:

    self.att   = Linear(F, 256) -> Tanh -> Dropout -> Linear(256, 12)
    a          = softmax(att(h), dim=windows)
    pooled     = einsum('bkn,bkf->bnf', a, h)     # (batch, 12, F) — a separate pooled vector per finding
    logits     = (pooled * clsW).sum(-1) + clsb   # clsW is (12, F), a per-finding readout

Their own words for it: 'the windows are then pooled by an attention layer that has separate weights for each of the twelve findings. THAT LAST PART MATTERS MORE THAN ANYTHING ELSE HERE. A cruciate tear may be visible on two slices while osteoarthritis spreads across many, and one shared pooling weight forces those to compete; giving each finding its own attention lets each draw on the slices that actually show it.'

Ours is the same operator with a SHARED query — kneemri/models/slice_attention.py, gate width 64, Linear(gate, 1). And its docstring already names this exact successor: 'DELIBERATELY TINY: one gate of width 64 and a single shared query... A per-diagnosis query over slices is the obvious next step and is deliberately not taken until a shared one earns it.'

So this is a mechanism converged on from two independent directions: our own architecture note wrote it down as next, and a rival at 0.924 rates it above every other choice in their design. It is also the mechanism that predicts OUR OWN deficit pattern — the labels where we still trail our teacher are MCL -0.0465, Lateral Meniscus -0.0149 and PF OA -0.0071, and the first two are precisely the focal, few-slice findings that a shared pooling weight makes compete with the diffuse ones.

WHY THE SHARED ONE HAS NOT EARNED IT AND THIS SHOULD RUN ANYWAY. The docstring's gate was 'until a shared one earns it', and attend beat max by only +0.0002. But that null is EVIDENCE FOR this arm, not against it: if the shared query is being pulled in twelve directions at once, it should land on approximately the mean, which is approximately the max, which is what +0.0002 says. The shared-query null is what a per-diagnosis lever PREDICTS.

PRICE: WALL-CLOCK ~20 min at 224 (the native224 cell, 94 s/epoch x 12) plus maybe 2 h to build and test the head. GAIN: the author ranks it their top design choice and it is the only untried mechanism that explains the per-label deficit; plausibly 1-2% absolute. P(clears +0.010) ~ 0.45, P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.3. Best ratio on the board — better than adjacent224, which is queued and cheaper but explains less.

FOUR MORE MECHANISMS IN THE SAME NOTEBOOK, filed here so the read is not thrown away:
  1. Windows of 3 PHYSICALLY-CONSECUTIVE slices as RGB, with the window CENTRES spread by linspace across the valid range. Local contiguity, global extent — BOTH. This bears directly on knee-e6sj: our new Adjacent takes ONE contiguous run of 12 and pays for continuity with extent, which is that arm's own risk branch 4. Their geometry buys both and is the shape to test next if adjacent224 reads flat. We already own the local half as slice_pooling 'channels'.
  2. Soft LLM targets — twelve PROBABILITIES per report, a hedged 'suspected tear' emitted as ~0.8 rather than 1. Confirms our label lane and our --calibrated-targets independently.
  3. The 58 gold studies held out for validation and NEVER trained on — our --hold-annotations, priced at -0.0005 to -0.0015.
  4. Weight averaging over the best three epochs, written as a second checkpoint. Free at inference, unlike prediction averaging. Near our --ema but not the same operator.

DO NOT quote the 0.924 as replicated. Our own standing rule from biohub: a claimed number in a notebook is not a number until we reproduce it.
notes: MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-08-27. labelwise224_s2026 = 0.8517 vs native224_s2026 0.8502, MEAN +0.0015, converged (convergence_check clean). Pre-registration asked >= +0.010 with MCL AND Lateral Meniscus among the movers; got +0.0015, MCL moved (+0.0126) and Lateral Meniscus did not (+0.0051). NO delta is marked significant - paired half-widths run to +/-0.0326. Lands squarely in the pre-registered 'within +/- 0.006' branch: per-diagnosis pooling is not the lever at 12 slices, and 58 image-read labels cannot supervise twelve separate attention channels. What DID hold is the mechanism's predicted signature - focal +0.0038 vs regional -0.0017, six model-bottlenecked findings +0.0037 - so the direction is right and the size is a fifteenth of what was asked. CAVEAT ON THE RIVAL: their 0.924 is a whole model (ConvNeXt-v2-B@336 / CoAtNet@384 / EffNetV2-L@480, five checkpoints, blended), not this head in isolation; nothing here says their number is wrong, only that the head alone does not carry it on our trunk. NOT DEAD AS A MEMBER: +0.0015 with a different internal structure is a diversity-seat profile and costs nothing to try in one. Follow-up it named (window geometry) ran as adjacent224 and came back -0.0040 - see knee-e6sj. Ledger: experiments/README.md '2026-08-27 - the per-diagnosis head and its own named follow-up, BOTH closed on one control'.

title: board_transfer is a whole-range fit and we are on the flat part: local slope 0.74-0.88, not 1.72 - every arm in the repo is priced at roughly double
description:
Measured 2026-08-26T16:58Z, CPU only, zero slots, from comp/board.jsonl as board_check now maintains it.

WHAT IS WRONG. kneemri/evaluation/board_transfer.py reports 'compression: median +1.72 board points per holdout point' as a single number over all 171 orderable ensemble pairs. That statistic mixes pairs spanning the whole history, from solo_v1 (offline 0.8518, board 0.868) to peak8_v1 (0.8731, 0.932). Transfer is not constant across that range - it saturates - and every arm we price today sits at the top.

THE MEASUREMENT, two independent estimators, and the whole-range setting reproduces the tool exactly (1.72), which makes the comparison like-for-like:

  regime                     estimator        value        interval (2000 bootstrap draws)
  all pairs, resolved gap    median ratio     1.72         [1.42, 1.89]   <- the pinned constant
  all ensembles              OLS              2.22         [1.21, 3.14]
  offline >= 0.860           OLS              1.45         [0.76, 2.10]
  offline >= 0.8648 (now)    OLS              0.83         [0.55, 1.47]
  offline >= 0.8648, any gap median ratio     0.88         [0.59, 1.11]
  offline >= 0.8648, resolved median ratio    0.74         [0.49, 0.85]

Both current-regime intervals EXCLUDE 1.72. Monotone decreasing across three nested regimes, on two estimators that do not share a functional form.

THE CAVEAT, and it is real. The top band spans only 0.0083 of offline while the offline noise floor is 0.0053-0.0062. Restriction of range plus errors-in-variables attenuates BOTH estimators toward zero, so the STRUCTURAL slope may well still be near 1.72 and the three regime intervals do overlap - saturation itself is NOT resolved. But the attenuated coefficient is the correct one for PREDICTION: we predict a board move from an OBSERVED offline reading that carries exactly that noise, and the regression of board on a noisy offline is what 0.74-0.88 estimates. For pricing arms, 0.8 is right whether or not saturation is real.

WHAT IT CHANGES. 0.939 -> 0.950 is +0.011 board.
  at 1.72 (what the repo assumes):  +0.0064 offline
  at 0.83:                          +0.0133 offline
  at 0.74:                          +0.0149 offline
  at the optimistic end 1.11:       +0.0099 offline
Our best offline ensemble ever recorded is peak8_v1 at 0.8731; gradeswap_v1 at 0.8694 reads 0.933. 0.950 wants an offline around 0.883-0.888. Nothing in the repo is within +0.010 of the best. The goal is roughly TWICE as far as every plan in this repo has been written to assume.

Every arm priced this session was priced at 1.72 and is overstated ~2x. knee-8yi5's blendhold-six (+0.008-0.010 board) becomes +0.004-0.005. calibsix's case halves. This also explains blendthree_v1 reading 0.939 dead flat at dose 3, and the ten-entry 0.936-0.939 band across every axis we have varied: small offline gains on the flat part of the curve read as nothing.

FIX. board_transfer.py should report the regime-local slope alongside the whole-range one, with its interval, and name the regime by the score being priced - the whole-range median is the wrong number to quote when pricing an arm against a 0.939 champion. The failure shape is the one CLAUDE.md already records twice: a constant quoted from prose while the instrument said otherwise.

Does NOT change: the ORDERING. 0/108 resolved pairs are inverted; the holdout still ranks correctly. Only the SCALE is wrong.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-27 08:24Z, zero card, zero slots. board_transfer now reports the regime-local slope WITH its interval alongside the whole-range one, and the priced line names the score it was asked about.

Three additions to BoardTransfer:
  ratios_above(floor)  -- the resolved pairs' ratios behind a regime median, so a thin cell is visibly thin
  spread(ratios)       -- a seeded percentile interval on the median (2000 draws, seed 2026, 2.5/97.5)
  regimes()            -- now (floor, pairs, median, interval), the interval per regime

The tool reproduces this bead's measurement exactly:

  compression: median +1.72 board points per holdout point over the WHOLE record -- the wrong number
  to price an arm with, see below
    among entries at or above 0.8661: 4 resolved pairs, median +0.74 [+0.49, +1.11]
    among entries at or above 0.8679: 0 resolved pairs, median +0.00 [+0.00, +0.00]
    PRICE AN ARM AT THIS ONE: at or above 0.8648 (asked for), 8 pairs, median +0.74 [+0.50, +0.85]

The interval is what stops the local number becoming the next 1.72: +0.74 [+0.50, +0.85] on 8 pairs is
a range, not a constant, and an arm priced at the upper end is priced at 0.85 rather than 1.72. Seeded,
because a gate that redraws its own answer is not a gate.

CONSEQUENCE UNCHANGED AND NOW MACHINE-READABLE: 0.939 -> 0.950 is +0.011 board = +0.0133 to +0.0149
offline at the local slope, not the +0.0064 the 1.72 constant implied. Ordering is unaffected (0/108
resolved pairs inverted), so this reprices arms and does not invalidate any seating decision.

Gates green (Session gates was successful in 3 minutes); mirror tests test_ratios_above and test_spread

title: Nothing has ever tested whether directional gains ADD - and the 0.950 plan assumes they do
description:
THE PLAN RESTS ON AN UNTESTED ASSUMPTION. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_what-0950-actually-costs.md prices first place at +0.010 offline on ONE member. Since raddino_dense ran and read -0.0371, the page names no single arm reaching that, and its own conclusion is that the route is a STACK of directional gains, quoting CLAUDE.md's 'increments below the bar still compose, and a chain of them that sums past it IS a result'. That sentence is a licence, not a measurement. In 110 arms this project has never once put two measured-positive flags in the same run. Every ledger row is one flag against a control, read alone.

THE ARM: experiments/arms/stackfit.sh. Dense corner (336 px, 20 slices, 0.1-0.9), --calibrated-targets AND --ema AND --hold-annotations.

THE TWO TERMS, both with singles landing in the same hours:
 - --calibrated-targets: knee-bs4l measured the matched pair at +0.0072 proxy / +0.0129 annotated, the largest unrefuted directional gain we hold. calib_dense_hold reads it at this exact corner and its header predicts our first member above 0.860.
 - --ema: knee-56w5 pre-registered >=0.8640 against band_dense's 0.8578. A competitor's single-variable ablation of the same flag reads +0.003 (research/2026-08-26_the-ablation-table-a-competitor-published.md), so the honest prior is half the floor and directional. ema_dense reads it at this corner.
Mechanically independent - one changes what the targets say, the other changes which weights are kept - which is the precondition for a sum rather than a substitution.

CONTROL IS calib_dense_hold, so the arm moves exactly one flag (--ema) and the additive prediction is a subtraction with no correction terms:
    predicted = calib_dense_hold + (ema_dense - band_dense)
ema_dense carries no --hold-annotations and neither does its control band_dense, so its delta is internally matched and portable; the hold price cancels out of the difference.

GATED. Do not run until BOTH singles have landed AND both are non-negative, and read them through convergence_check first - under one_cycle a truncated score is a FLOOR and gating on a floor is gating on nothing. If either term is negative this becomes a two-variable arm with a known-bad term and diagnoses nothing.

PRE-REGISTRATION (full ladder in the arm header): >= predicted+0.0062 super-additive, suspect it and demand a second seed. Within 0.0062 ADDITIVE - the result the page needs, and it licenses stacking as a METHOD. <= predicted-0.0062 SUBSTITUTES NOT COMPLEMENTS, the depth_regions_span shape, which KILLS the stack route. <= band_dense_hold, suspect the harness first.

PRICE: ~85 min of card at 336 px / 20 slices, ZERO submission slots, fold-0 holdout, and --hold-annotations buys the second ruler in the same run (knee-9198 satisfied without a rerun).
P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.05 alone. That is not the case for it. The case is that it is a DECISION arm: P(it settles whether the stack route exists) ~ 0.8, and the stack route is the whole remaining plan for reaching 0.950. An 85-minute arm that can kill or license the entire strategy is the best ratio on the board, and killing it early is worth as much as licensing it.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY: two points do not fit a composition rule. Additive here is evidence about THESE two terms, not a law about the next three; each further term still needs its own single before it is stacked.
notes:
GATE RE-READ 2026-08-27T16:04Z, AND THE ARM IS NOW UNINFORMATIVE. DO NOT QUEUE stackfit.

Both singles have landed and both are non-negative, so the bead text says GO. Reading the actual numbers says otherwise:

  band_dense_hold   0.8573   (control for the calib term)
  calib_dense_hold  0.8634   --calibrated-targets = +0.0061
  band_dense        0.8578   (control for the ema term)
  ema_dense         0.8588   --ema = +0.0010

convergence_check lists neither ema_dense nor calib_dense_hold as TRUNCATED, so these are the recipes numbers and not floors.

--ema MISSED ITS OWN PRE-REGISTRATION. knee-56w5 pre-registered >=0.8640 against band_dense 0.8578. It read 0.8588. That is a null at this corner, not a directional gain, and the competitors published ablation reading +0.003 for the same flag is now the upper end of what we can claim rather than the honest prior.

WHY THE ARM CANNOT ANSWER ITS QUESTION ANY MORE. predicted = calib_dense_hold + (ema_dense - band_dense) = 0.8634 + 0.0010 = 0.8644, against a control of 0.8634. The ladder in the bead calls anything within +/-0.0062 ADDITIVE - but the SUBSTITUTES branch (<= predicted-0.0062 = 0.8582) and the additive branch both contain the do-nothing outcome 0.8634. A discriminating arm needs the two hypotheses to predict different numbers; here they differ by 0.0010 against a 0.0062 floor. The decision value P(settles the stack route) ~ 0.8 was priced when the ema term was expected at +0.0062; at +0.0010 it is ~0.05.

85 minutes of card, saved. The stack-route question is NOT closed - it is still open and still the whole plan. It needs a second term that actually measured over the floor, and --ema is not it. The candidates that remain are the ones whose singles read over +0.004 in the ledger; pair the calib term with one of THOSE, not with the largest available null.

LEDGER READ 2026-08-27T22:19Z — ZERO CARD, ZERO SLOT. THE STACK ROUTE IS NOT AWAITING A BETTER SECOND
TERM. IT HAS BEEN TESTED SEVEN TIMES AGAINST THE SAME CONTROL AND HAS NEVER ONCE LANDED NON-NEGATIVE.

The bead's own framing — "find a second term whose single measured over the floor, pair it with the
calib term" — assumes the failures so far were bad candidates. Grepping every arm in experiments/README.md
that runs `calib_dense_hold` (0.8634) as its control says the failure is the ROUTE, not the candidate:

  second term added to the calib corner        arm              holdout   delta
  --ema                                        stackfit         0.8631   -0.0003
  --slice-pooling labelwise                    labelwise_dense  0.8613   -0.0021
  --finding-calibration                        (offsets arm)    0.8595   -0.0039
  warm start from a converged parent           warm_calib_dense 0.8562   -0.0072
  --contrast-weight 1.0                        contrast_dense   0.8547   -0.0087
  --through-plane + attend + --pool sided      fuse_attend      0.8509   -0.0125
  --auc-margin 1.0 --rank-weight 0             margin_calib     0.8235   -0.0399

SEVEN OF SEVEN BELOW THE CONTROL. Three are inside the 0.0062 paired floor and are FLAT rather than
negative-with-confidence — but the SIGN is what this counts. Under a null-additive model (a second
mechanism-sound term is as likely to sit above the control as below), seven of seven on one side is
p = 2^-7 = 0.008. That clears any bar this project applies to a single arm, and it was free.

AND THE ORDERING IS MONOTONE IN HOW MUCH THE SECOND TERM CHANGES. A weight-averaging trick costs
0.0003; a pooling swap 0.0021; an auxiliary loss 0.0087; three pooling changes at once 0.0125; a
competing objective 0.0399. That is the shape of a LOCAL OPTIMUM, not of seven unrelated bad bets.
`calib_dense_hold` is not a member with room above it that the right flag unlocks — it is the top of a
basin our recipe cannot be pushed out of by adding terms to it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It does not say gains never compose — `2026-08-27_aggregation-beats-input`
still holds that four aggregation flags agree on a SIGN, and the running total 0.8272 -> 0.8523 is a
real chain. It says composition has not survived a single test AT THIS CORNER, where the first term is
already `--calibrated-targets`. A stack built from a DIFFERENT base has never been tried and is not
addressed here.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE 0.950 PLAN. The remaining lane for a better solo is not another flag on our
recipe. It is a genuinely different representation, which is knee-9g28 (`foreign_member`, built and
gates-clean, never run) and knee-tlba behind it. This bead's arm stays cancelled; what changes is that
it is now cancelled by a MEASUREMENT of the route rather than by one term's null.

DO NOT re-derive this. The seven rows are in experiments/README.md; grep for the string 0.8634.
close_reason:
Answered by measurement, not abandoned. The stack route was tested seven times against the same control
(calib_dense_hold 0.8634) and landed below it seven times out of seven: --ema -0.0003, labelwise pooling
-0.0021, --finding-calibration -0.0039, warm start -0.0072, --contrast-weight -0.0087, through-plane +
attend + sided -0.0125, --auc-margin -0.0399. Three of those are inside the paired floor and are FLAT
rather than negative-with-confidence, but the SIGN is what is being counted, and 7/7 on one side under a
null-additive model is p = 2^-7 = 0.008. The ordering is also monotone in how much the second term
changes the recipe, which is the shape of a local optimum rather than of seven unrelated bad bets.

The bead's title claim ("nothing has ever tested whether directional gains ADD") is therefore no longer
true, and leaving it open at P0 points the queue at an arm that is cancelled.

title: TissueCentre is plumbed through six places and has NEVER been trained - the worst tenth of studies crop a clipped joint
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-26, from core/data/corpus/crop_centre.py and crop_coverage.py.

THE FACT. Our default crop takes 130 mm about (height//2, width//2) - the IMAGE centre, on the assumption
the joint was framed in the middle. Measured over 60 studies, the tissue centroid sits a median 7 mm, p90
18 mm, and up to 32 mm from that point against a 160 mm field of view. At 130 mm the margin is ~15 mm.
So the worst ~10% of studies are trained on a crop that CLIPS THE JOINT, and every member this project
owns was fitted that way.

`TissueCentre` is the strategy that fixes it. It exists, it is plumbed through six call sites, it is
opt-in - and nothing has ever been trained under it. The reason given in crop_centre.py is honest and
still holds: switching the default silently would invalidate ~99 GB of cached arrays and every member
fitted on them, with no fingerprint to catch it.

WHY IT IS A DATA LEVER AND NOT A KNOB. knee-rh4t priced the board deficit at ~0.017 on ONE member, and
the arithmetic in this session put the noise floor at 0.0062 offline / 0.0107 board once the +1.72
transfer is applied - so nothing that moves 0.001-0.004 can close it. Recovering anatomy for a tenth of
the corpus is a change to WHAT THE MODEL SEES on 10% of its training signal, which is the only class of
change sized right. The forum's own convergence agrees: topic 735826, a poster running controlled
experiments with a frozen CPU cache reports 'image geometry / slice selection + label quality > backbone
size', and names fixed-mm physical cropping as the next thing to isolate. We already do fixed-mm cropping.
We do not do tissue-centring.

WHAT GATES IT, AND IT COSTS NO GPU. crop_coverage answers 'which centre keeps more of the imaged tissue'
without a label and without the card. Its own docstring records that the question has never been answered.
Launched 2026-08-26 11:14Z, --sample 400 --workers 12, log at experiments/logs/crop_coverage_400.log.
Prediction from that module, written before the run: at 130 mm the two centres are near-indistinguishable;
at the 80 mm tight extent tissue-centring must keep materially more or the strategy is not worth a rebuild.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY, inherited from the tool: retained tissue is not retained JOINT - a crop drifting toward
the calf keeps tissue while losing the knee. It bounds the failure from one side only.

NEXT STEP IF COVERAGE FAVOURS TISSUE-CENTRING. Do NOT rebuild the 336 cache. Rebuild at 224, where
native224 (ledger 2026-08-25) measured 0.8502 against the 336 control's 0.8525 - flat, -0.0023 on a 0.0062
floor - at 94 s/epoch and 8.1 GB instead of 290 s/epoch and 18.0 GB. A tissue-centred 224 cache is the
cheap arm that tests the mechanism; if it lands, the 336 rebuild is then justified by a measurement rather
than by an offset distribution.
design:
PRICE: ~19 min of card (12 epochs at 94 s/epoch, 224 px), plus ZERO for the cache — it was built on CPU
beside raddino_dense and cost no card at all. Zero submission slots.

PLAUSIBLE GAIN ON THE MEAN: small, and stating that honestly is the point. The mechanism is a
SUBPOPULATION claim. The tissue centroid sits a median 7 mm from the image centre, p90 18 mm, max 32 mm,
against ~15 mm of margin at a 130 mm crop. So roughly the worst TENTH of studies clip and nine tenths are
untouched. Even a large gain on the clipped decile (+0.05 there) moves the corpus mean about +0.005 —
below the 1.5% bar by construction, and below the 0.0062 paired floor.

P(clears 1.5% on the mean) ~0.10.
P(directional AND concentrated in the high-offset decile) ~0.35.

WHY IT RUNS ANYWAY, argued as an INSTRUMENT rather than sold as an improvement: 19 minutes retires or
licenses the entire CROP-GEOMETRY axis. That axis is ranked first by the one poster in forum topic 735826
running frozen-cache controlled experiments ('image geometry / slice selection + label quality > backbone
size'), and it is the only lever class that reaches EVERY member at once rather than one corner. Land it
and the 336 rebuild follows and every member is refitted; miss it and we stop paying attention to a
strategy that has sat plumbed through six call sites and untested since knee-yrf.

HOW IT IS READ, and this decides the verdict more than the mean does: split the fold-0 holdout by each
study's centroid offset and compare the top decile against the rest. FLAT mean + gain concentrated in the
high-offset decile CONFIRMS the mechanism and licenses the 336 rebuild. Gain spread uniformly across all
offsets REFUTES the mechanism even if the mean reads as a win — that is the shape to distrust, because
nothing in the physics predicts a benefit for a study whose joint was already centred.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-08-26: FLAT, the pre-registered middle branch. tissue224 0.8491 (best e6, converged 12/12,
convergence_check clean) against native224 0.8502 — -0.0011, a sixth of the 0.0062 paired floor.

FLAGS VERIFIED BEFORE THE VERDICT, which the header demanded: the run's own recipe prints "centre":
"tissue" and "image_size": "224". Not a flag that failed to land.

THE TISSUE IS REAL AND DOES NOT CONVERT. crop_coverage measured tissue-image at +0.0294 [+0.0276,
+0.0312] retained coverage at 130 mm over 1,822 series. So ~3% more imaged anatomy reaches the network
and buys nothing measurable.

WHICH MECHANISM DIED, and the header pre-registered both:
  COMMON-MODE FRAMING - refuted. It predicted a UNIFORM corpus-wide gain (every study's joint off-centre
  in the same direction, two thirds of the 9-14 mm displacement shared per crop_alignment), which moves
  the mean by construction. The mean did not move.
  CLIPPING - untested, NOT refuted. A subpopulation claim confined to the worst tenth (p90 offset 18 mm
  against ~15 mm of margin) predicts a flat mean by construction and shows up only in an offset split.

THE SPLIT CANNOT BE BUILT TODAY. crop_alignment.dump() writes `spread` - between-slot disagreement - not
the centroid's offset MAGNITUDE from the image centre, so the decile the clipping claim needs is not on
disk. Filed as its own bead rather than left as a clause here.

CONSEQUENCE: the 99 GB 336-cache rebuild this arm existed to license is NOT licensed. The crop/centre
axis is closed on the mean at both extents - 80 mm -0.0099 (crop80_span), 130 mm -0.0011 (here). What
survives is a claim about 10% of the corpus worth at most a tenth of its own size on the mean, i.e. below
the floor even if true. Do not spend a card on it; it would need a per-decile read of an existing pair,
not a new fit.

STILL OWED: seat_value on tissue224. Deferred, not skipped - the card is held by band_dense_hold and
card_check blocks on two of ours. The diversity read is worth taking because a member of equal quality
with different crop GEOMETRY is a distinct disagreement axis, and seat_value must be run --against
gradeswap_v1 (blendseat has only 1 of 6 members carrying a holdout record, so it cannot price a marginal
contribution).

title: Rivals reach 0.938-0.942 on a SINGLE model at 224px - the gap is a member gap and neither resolution nor folds nor ensembling explains it
description:
Read 2026-08-26 0614z from forum topic 735304 ('Best single-model score', 17 votes, 22 replies), live, no slot spent. Ten self-reported single-model board scores:

  0.942  single, 224px, 'some tweaks' on a 0.934 @ 224px
  0.938  single model, SINGLE FOLD
  0.929  single, 5-fold, 224px, LLM output labels only
  0.926  single, 5-fold, 336px, LLM output labels only
  0.920  single, OOF AUC = LB AUC within noise
  0.915  single, DINOv2
  0.887  single, DINOv2 (the asker)

OURS: soloseat 0.925. So the board deficit is ~0.017 ON ONE MEMBER, and knee-urvf's law says that transfers to the ensemble roughly one-for-one.

WHAT THIS RULES OUT, which is most of what we have been spending card on:

RESOLUTION IS NOT THE LEVER. The 0.942 and the 0.938 are both at 224px, and the poster explicitly says the 0.942 stayed at 224 through the tweaks. Our 336/392 work (band_span, res392, crop80) was chasing an axis the leaders are not on. Note the two 5-fold entries invert it too: 224px scores 0.929 against 336px's 0.926.

FOLDS ARE NOT THE LEVER, and this is the strongest line in the thread. The two FIVE-FOLD singles (0.929, 0.926) are BELOW the two SINGLE-fold ones (0.942, 0.938). Independent confirmation of the owner's standing ban - folds are the same thing tried slightly differently, and here they are measurably worse than one good run.

ENSEMBLING IS NOT THE LEVER, said twice by people above us. 'Public notebooks just ensemble early to get a high LB score and exposure; waste of time IMO' and 'nine days into a competition is a very silly time to be wasting efforts refining ensemble models.' One poster points at the Efficiency LB as evidence: high-scoring submissions with short runtimes cannot be 20-model ensembles. Our board history is nine entries sitting in 0.936-0.939, every one a different seating / vote rule / count / TTA over near-identical members. That is the trap knee-urvf named, now corroborated from outside.

LABELS ARE NOT THE WHOLE STORY EITHER. Both 5-fold entries say 'LLM output labels only' and land 0.926-0.929, right on top of our 0.925 - so a plain LLM label table plus a competent single model already reaches where we are. Consistent with today's closure of the label axis (knee-1ww2, knee-uahl).

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is the whole schedule: the recipe/backbone/training of ONE member at 224px. We do not know what the 0.934 -> 0.942 'tweaks' were and the poster did not say.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CARD. blendsix members 4 and 5 land ~0920z, leaving ~14 hours before the last slot at ~2330z. Under knee-urvf the six-member blendall is predicted at 0.939-0.941 - a ~zero-expected-gain run against the 0.939 champion, because the bonus term is saturated and the members are near-identical. Spending that card on a SINGLE-member arm at 224px has the better ratio even at low odds, because it is the only axis that can move the ensemble by more than the bonus.

CAVEAT, and the owner has stated it as a standing rule: notebook and forum claims are not results. biohub spent weeks failing to replicate a claimed 0.913. These are self-reports with no verification, and 0.942 would sit near the live leader at 0.952. title: The ensemble tracks best-single + ~0.019 and the single has been flat at 0.925 for five days - member quality is the only free term
description:
MEASURED from comp/board.jsonl, 56 scored entries, 2026-08-26 05:27Z. Three dated single-member board reads exist, each with a best-ensemble-of-that-day beside it.

  date        best single      best ensemble       bonus
  2026-08-12  solo_v1  0.868   0.894               +0.026
  2026-08-17  solo_v4  0.914   vote_v2 0.919 (m2)  +0.005
  2026-08-26  soloseat 0.925   blendseat 0.939(m6) +0.014

SINGLE moved 0.868 -> 0.914 -> 0.925. ENSEMBLE moved 0.894 -> 0.919 -> 0.939. Member gains transfer to the ensemble at roughly ONE-FOR-ONE, and the BONUS the ensemble adds over its own best member has hovered 0.005-0.026 with no trend across fourteen days, while the pool grew from one member to seven and roughly thirty seat/vote/count/TTA entries were spent on it.

THE LAW, stated as a working model: board(ensemble) ~= board(best single) + 0.015, with the second term SATURATED. Nine entries sit inside 0.936-0.939 (augseat, allfit, lastseat, v3seat, dark6, dark7, farseat, votefit, jitterfit) and every one of them is a different seating, vote rule, count or TTA over near-identical members.

WHAT IT PREDICTS, and this is why it is P0. To reach the owner's 0.950 target the ensemble needs a best single at ~0.935. Ours is 0.925. Rivals self-report singles at 0.938-0.942 (topic 735304), which under this law would put their ensembles at ~0.953-0.957 - consistent with the live leader at 0.952. The target is not reachable by re-combining what we hold; it needs +0.010 on ONE member.

THE TRAP IT ALSO NAMES. 'Replace the other seats with the best member' is the WRONG reading. The +0.015 is a DIVERSITY term; seating copies of one member collapses the ensemble to that member and gives the term back. weakseven_v1 (0.908, -0.026 from one weak member) and peak8 (0.932 at eight members, below six) bound the other side: the pool cannot be improved by adding members that are weak, and cannot be improved by adding more of them. What raises the ensemble is raising the FLOOR of every member, or adding one that is strong AND unlike.

CAVEAT ON THE MEASUREMENT. Three points, no intervals, and the 08-17 pair is the weakest (its best ensemble was a two-member vote, so the bonus there is not measured at the same pool size as the other two). The one-for-one claim is a SLOPE read off three points; treat the +0.015 as an order of magnitude, not a constant. It is enough to rank the axes, which is all it is being used for.
notes:
2026-08-30 21:48Z: holdswap_v1 (ref 55900461, PENDING) is a direct test of this bead's 'member quality is the only free term'. It holds seat COUNT, vote rule, foreign weight and kit fixed and moves exactly one seat to a higher-quality member -- lr4e-5_ws_cf (fold-0 analogue 0.8525 solo, the weakest of the five priceable champion seats) out, calib_dense_hold_ff (analogue 0.8634, the best solo the project owns) in. If quality is the free term, this is the cheapest possible way to spend it, and the swap was named by a ten-of-ten unanimous offline proxy rather than by hand. A flat reading would say quality does not transfer through a seat either, which would leave the bead with no free term at all.
2026-09-01 07:40Z RECOMPUTE, from the COMPLETED board record (board_check filled 24 missing rows on 2026-08-25; 87 rows now, joined on the 'members' field, scope:excluded dropped). The title's two claims split.

WHAT SURVIVES: the bonus is still small and the single is still the lever. Best single is unchanged since 2026-08-26 at 0.925 (soloseat_v1); calibsolo 0.923 and raptor_solo 0.923 did not beat it, and raptor_solo's offline is void anyway (98.6% in-sample, board_check 2026-08-29).

WHAT DOES NOT: 'has not grown in fourteen days' is now false. Best ensemble moved 0.939 (blendseat, 08-26) -> 0.944 (holdswap_v1 08-30, stackseat_v1 08-31), with the best single flat at 0.925 throughout. So the bonus went +0.014 -> +0.019 over five days on a FIXED best single. The law should read board(ensemble) ~= board(best single) + 0.019, not + 0.015, and the second term is not frozen -- it moved by 0.005, which is about our offline resolution (knee-b6sn) but is four board rows wide and monotone.

WHAT THAT COSTS THE P0 ARGUMENT: it makes the target EASIER than this bead states, not harder. At bonus 0.019 the 0.950 ensemble needs a 0.931 single rather than a 0.935 one. It does not rescue the seat axis -- holdswap and stackseat are both sevens and both read 0.944, i.e. two different seatings landing on the same number, which is knee-xuj5's finding again.

Best-by-count over the same recompute (knee-macc): 1->0.925(n5) 2->0.936(n5) 3->0.938(n4) 4->0.937(n12) 5->0.931(n5) 6->0.943(n12) 7->0.944(n19) 8->0.943(n5) 11->0.941 12->0.937 25->0.894.
