title: Mixup: the label-space regulariser the overfit diagnosis asks for, and it has never been in this repo
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-25 22:13Z, card-free while knee-bs4l trains. Grepped experiments/README.md and kneemri/ core/ for mixup|cutmix|label_smooth|drop_path|stochastic_depth. ZERO hits in the ledger and ZERO hits in the code. This axis has never been run and is not implemented.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE. The repo's own numbers say the model is DATA-LIMITED, not compute- or architecture-limited, and every closed axis is closed for that one reason:
  - band_dense_long (24 epochs, single variable): peaked at epoch 6 (0.8587), slid to 0.8405 by epoch 23 while the training loss halved 0.85 -> 0.4536. A 0.0182 peak-to-finish decline, 2.9x the noise floor. That is memorisation, stated in the ledger in those words.
  - cnx at MATCHED TRAIN LOSS: 0.8371 vs 0.7927, a 0.044 generalisation gap at equal fit (knee-jk3).
  - Every quantity axis (slices, pixels, slots, epochs, members past six) reads inside the 0.0062 floor. A model that memorises at 12 epochs has no use for more of anything.

WHY THE ONE REGULARISER WE DID RUN DOES NOT COVER IT. aug_long is intensity_aug False->True and nothing else: gain, gamma, blur, contrast, noise, plus rigid jitter. Every one of those perturbs how a study LOOKS. None touches the study-to-label mapping, so a trunk can still memorise anatomy-to-finding, and the ledger's own summary of that arm is "the regulariser fired, the overfitting did not care". Mixup is categorically different: a convex combination of two studies carrying the convex combination of their targets makes a memorised study-to-label pair actively WRONG, which is why it is the standard remedy for exactly this curve shape.

THE SEAM IS FREE, audited in trainer.py:367-380. The pixel tensor (UInt8 b n g h w), the slot mask (b s), and the score/weight pair from targets.rows(batch) are all materialised in the same three lines before the autocast block. A permutation of the batch dimension plus a Beta(a,a) draw mixes all four. Our targets are ALREADY soft -- objective.py's docstring: "our targets are weighted confidences in [0, 1] rather than binary labels" -- so the cross-entropy term takes a mixed target unchanged, with no soft-label plumbing to add. The mask mixes as an elementwise maximum (a slot valid in either study stays valid).

PRICE. Dev ~45 min (a Mixup policy dataclass beside the other trainer policies, a flag, a Landed witness, the jaxtyping boundary, the mirror test). Card 40 min for one 12-epoch arm against a matched control we already own. Plausible gain 1-3% on an overfitting classifier; odds it clears the 1.5% bar ~1 in 3. That ratio beats every other open lever, and every rival is either closed on a measurement or blocked on an owner licence call.

PRE-REGISTRATION, against the matched control at the SAME recipe:
  - the peak RISES by 0.015 or more -> the memorisation reading is right and the axis is a design lever, not a knob; sweep alpha and build members on it.
  - the peak is flat but the DECLINE shrinks (peak-to-finish well under 0.0182) -> mixup regularises as intended and the bound is elsewhere; keep it as a free rider, do not spend a slot.
  - the peak FALLS -> mixing across studies destroys the focal, few-voxel findings this task turns on (a torn meniscus blended with an intact one is not a study), and the label-space axis closes with a mechanism rather than a shrug.
  - training diverges or the witness says the flag did not land -> harness, not idea. Fix and re-run before reading anything.
notes:
READ 2026-08-26 08:47Z, four hours after the run finished. mixup224_long (a=0.4, 24 ep) vs native224_long control: peak 0.8505 e12 vs 0.8490 e9 (+0.0015, a quarter of the floor — FLAT), finish 0.8417 vs 0.8325, decline 0.0088 vs 0.0165 — HALVED, and below the 0.0124 the control's own pre-registration set for DEFECT REAL. Final train loss 0.6646 vs 0.4670, peak three epochs later: the blend fired, plumbing is not a suspect.

PRE-REGISTERED BAND 2 verbatim: peak flat, decline shrinks -> regularises as intended, bound is elsewhere, keep as a free rider, do NOT spend a slot. No slot spent.

WHAT IT CLOSES. The label-space regularisation account of the ceiling. It also SEPARATES two things this repo had bundled: the slide is memorisation and is curable; the ceiling is not the slide (curing it returns +0.0015). Every axis that presents the SAME supervision to the SAME encoder differently now reads flat — schedule (nocycle224_long), example count (half_data), appearance aug (aug_long), label-space mixing (here). What is left is a different REPRESENTATION or different SUPERVISION: knee-jk3, knee-rh4t.

Ledger section appended 2026-08-26. Limits: 224 only, says nothing about the 336/dense cell where -0.0182 was measured; the dose was not swept at 24 epochs and a sweep is not priced.
close_reason: Ran and read null: mixup_dense peaked 0.8552 at e11 against band_dense 0.8578, -0.0026, inside the 0.0062 paired floor in the negative direction. Peak on the LAST epoch means UNDERTRAINED, not truncated — mixup slows fitting so 12 epochs buys the arm less than it buys its control, and the honest claim is 'at this budget mixup pays nothing', not 'mixup fails here'. Ledger entry in experiments/README.md. Not re-queued: +6 epochs is ~50 min against a flat mechanism and loses the ratio to knee-for6.

title: Which ruler does the BOARD use — report-derived labels or image-read annotations? It decides whether the label lane is small or large
description:
OPENED 2026-08-25 20:52Z by the supervision-gap measurement (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md).

THE QUESTION. Every number this project optimises is scored against REPORT-DERIVED labels, because that is the only ruler that covers the corpus. The hidden test set is scored against something we have never identified. If it is report-derived, then matching the report reader is exactly right and a model that beats it is spending capacity on the wrong truth. If it is image-read annotation -- which is what the hosts' comment in thread 735826 implies, 'those folks did not use the reports as a starting point' -- then our TRAINING TARGETS are the binding ceiling, and target correction is worth substantially more than blendlabels' +0.0034 prices it at.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. The supervision-gap measurement closed both halves of the supervision question as small: the label half at +0.0034/+0.0070 (blendlabels) and the model half at three findings (MCL -0.0465, Lateral Meniscus -0.0149, PF OA -0.0071). That conclusion is conditional on the ruler. This single fact is the only thing that could reopen the label lane as a 1.5%-sized lever, and it costs no slot and no card to investigate.

EVIDENCE ALREADY IN HAND, pointing at ANNOTATIONS. holdannot_s2026 -- one member, one set of predictions -- scores 0.8487 against report labels and 0.8932 against the radiologist on the 58 annotated studies. That is +0.045 from the RULER ALONE, controlled: same model, same weights, different truth. Our board sits at 0.938 against a holdout of ~0.85, a gap of ~0.088 in the same direction. Do NOT read that as confirmation: the board figure is a six-member ensemble with TTA and the holdout figure is a single member, so most of that gap is ensembling and study draw, not ruler. What the +0.045 does establish is that the ruler is worth a LOT on the same predictions, so identifying it is not a bookkeeping detail.

HOW TO ANSWER, cheapest first: (1) re-read the competition data description and host comments for how test ground truth was produced -- board_read/discussion_read already talk to Kaggle and spend no slot; (2) note that test.csv has no Report column (core/data/labels/targets.py:4), which is consistent with annotation-based truth but does not prove it; (3) check whether the published/top notebooks calibrate toward annotations or toward reports.

DO NOT spend a submission slot probing this. It is a documentation question.
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-08-25 20:54Z, twenty minutes after filing, by one forum read and no card. The board scores against IMAGE-READ RADIOLOGIST CONSENSUS, not against reports.

Competition overview, topic 733343, 'Courtesy of Dr. Jacob Kazam':
  'Models are evaluated on twelve binary labels ... The labels, and the criteria used by the ANNOTATING RADIOLOGISTS, are summarized below. In each case, ambiguous or borderline findings ("on the fence") were graded as NEGATIVE to favor specificity.'
  'Each study in the annotated reference set was independently labeled by two subspecialty-trained MSK radiologists, with disagreements adjudicated by a third radiologist to produce a single consensus ground truth.'

CONSEQUENCES, and they are large:
1. Every number this project has ever quoted -- every ledger row, every run_comparison, the 0.8502 control -- is measured against a PROXY (the report-derived table). The objective is the annotation ruler.
2. The two rulers are +0.045 apart on identical predictions: holdannot_s2026 scores 0.8487 against report labels and 0.8932 against the 58 annotation cells. Same weights, same studies, no ensembling, no TTA.
3. That is a documented mechanism for part of the standing board-vs-holdout gap (0.938 vs ~0.85), which had been carried as unexplained.
4. blendlabels' +0.0034 is its value on the PROXY. Its value on the objective was never computed. The label lane is UNMEASURED, not measured-small -- the 'both supervision levers are priced' conclusion written 20 minutes earlier is withdrawn.
5. 'On the fence -> negative, to favor specificity' matches a measurement we already have: our ruler calls 44.7% of the 696 cells positive at cut 0.50 where the adjudicated radiologist calls 34.5%. Our targets are systematically more generous than the ground truth is DEFINED to be. Supervision.calibrated_targets already implements the correction and was built before there was a reason to think it mattered.
6. supervision_gap is not a side instrument. It is the only direct measurement of the actual competition objective this project owns.

WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE. n = 58, and the annotated set is not a random sample of the corpus (ACL 41% there vs ~20% overall, topic 734106). The claim is documentary -- which ruler -- not a statistical result about any arm.

Follow-up filed separately: score label-side arms on BOTH rulers, which costs only --hold-annotations (holdannot priced that at -0.0015, nothing). See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md.
close_reason: ANSWERED and recorded. The board scores against image-read radiologist consensus, not reports — the competition overview and topic 733343 both say so in the host's own words, and holdannot_s2026 measures the size: 0.8487 against report labels, 0.8932 against the 58 annotation cells, same weights, same studies. +0.045 from the ruler alone. Written up in experiments/README.md and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md; the standing rule it produced is knee-9198, and the arm it produced is knee-bs4l (on the card now).

title: a kaggle dataset version can land with a file missing, and it refuses the WHOLE package on every kernel
description:
farseat (kernel version 2, 2026-08-25 01:47Z) died with:

  kneemri.inference.members.WeightsError: /kaggle/input/datasets/dimiturnt/kneemri-members holds a
  manifest listing 40 members but 1 of their files are absent (first 'small_accum_s2026.pt')

The local staging package is INTACT - 40 .pt files, a 40-row manifest, nothing missing locally. So the manifest and the file set were consistent when they were written and the LIVE VERSION lost a file during upload. Kaggle reported the push a success; the marker line 'Dataset version is being created' appeared and nothing said a file had been dropped.

BLAST RADIUS IS EVERY KERNEL, not just farseat. MemberPackage.__init__ refuses a package whose manifest names a file it cannot find, so one dropped .pt takes down every kernel that mounts the members dataset regardless of whether its own tuple names the missing member. farseat's tuple does NOT name small_accum_s2026 and farseat still died. That is the whole submission path on one file.

THE DETECTOR WAS RIGHT AND I OVERRODE IT. mount_check --live read REFUSED for 8 kernels naming small_accum_s2026 at 01:43Z. I discounted it because it had given three different answers in two minutes while a dataset version materialised, and because the file was present locally and had carried the 0.933 accumseat entry. Both of those were true and neither was relevant: a file present locally says nothing about the live package. A detector that flip-flops during a push is not a detector that is wrong, and the correct response was to re-read it AFTER the version settled rather than to file the disagreement as noise. It cost a kernel run and about 20 minutes on the critical path with two slots left.

FIX APPLIED: re-pushed the version from the intact local package (logs/push_members_fix.log).

WHAT TO BUILD, and it is small: the push is not verified by its own marker today - 'Dataset version is being created' is printed BEFORE the files are all there. The gate that closes this is a post-push readback: list the live files and diff them against the local manifest, and refuse to submit until they match. mount_check --live already does the comparison; what is missing is that nothing FORCES it after a push and before a kernel run. Wire it into the push path so a dropped file is caught by the pusher rather than by a spent kernel slot.
notes:
SHARPER, from the farseat post-mortem: mount_check --live did NOT catch this. It read 'kneemri-farseat: ok - declares all of ...' at 01:41Z and the run died anyway. unpushed() only compares the members a kernel NAMES against the live set, but MemberPackage.__init__ refuses a manifest whose files it cannot ALL find - so one dropped .pt takes down kernels that never name it. The per-kernel question is the wrong question for a package-level refusal, and the 8 REFUSED verdicts were a coincidence of which kernels happened to name the missing member.

FIXED: MountCheck.absent() compares the whole manifest against the live listing, checked BEFORE the per-kernel loop because a manifest the live dataset cannot satisfy invalidates every verdict that loop prints. Non-zero exit. Unit test test_absent covers the case the old test could not express: a member absent live and named by NO kernel.

Verified on the real defect - the new check printed 'live dataset does not hold 1 of the 40 members the manifest names (small_accum_s2026)' against the same package where the old code called farseat ok. Members dataset re-pushed; live package now complete.
2026-08-25 02:07Z — the DETECTOR half is fixed and pushed (04d3f8b): MountCheck.absent() asks the package-level question that unpushed() structurally could not, plus a unit test carrying the 2026-08-25 failure. main() runs it BEFORE the per-kernel loop and exits non-zero on it, because a manifest the live dataset cannot satisfy refuses MemberPackage for EVERY kernel, not only the ones naming the missing member. What is still open is the UPLOAD half: a kaggle dataset version can still land incomplete, and the only defence is running mount_check --live and polling until it reads LIVE PACKAGE COMPLETE before pushing any kernel. Also unresolved: --live gives different answers while a version is still materialising, so a single green read is not proof; poll it twice.
2026-08-25: upload half closed in caf1aca. MountCheck.settled polls the live listing until the manifest reads present twice running; --settle implies --live and refuses on it; comp/push.sh's dataset branch runs it after the push, gated on manifest.json, with an explicit status check because push.sh is set -u and not set -e. A never-settling poll reports the union of everything seen absent, not the last read, because the last read of a flip-flopping listing is the one answer known unreliable.

title: The seventh seat was never READ: dark6/dark7 are fold -1 (no offline delta), and the fold-0 analogue is +0.0005 against a 0.0011 board resolution
description:
dark6 (55756018) = six all-data (--fold -1) members and nothing else. It reads 0.937 — EXACTLY the champion plateau that allfit and lastseat read with a SEVENTH member added.

So the seventh seat contributes zero board points. Every entry that varied it was measuring a coordinate with no value:
- lastseat 0.937 (small_batch6 in seat four)
- augseat 0.936 (aug_long, a regularised member)
- v3seat PENDING (v3base_dense, a DINOv3-base trunk)
- farseat (never submitted, gated)

That is three slots, and a fourth pending, spent on a null coordinate. The pre-registrations were all written against 0.937 as 'the champion' when 0.937 was really 'what six dark members already read'. augseat's 0.936 and v3seat's expected 0.936-0.939 are not readings about regularisation or encoder family; they are readings about noise around an inert seat.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: it does not say members are worthless — weakseven read 0.908, so member quality does move the board. It says the MARGINAL seventh seat, filled by anything, is worth nothing on top of six all-data members.

WHAT IS NOW LOAD-BEARING: dark7 (55756369) is seven ALL-DATA members, the only entry that raises count without adding a fold-0 seat. Its reading against dark6 0.937 is now the whole count axis.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMAINING SLOTS: seat search is closed on a measurement. The axes never tested on the board are (a) the VOTE (offline flat at +0.0002, but the offline ruler is measured anti-correlated at the top: peak8 0.8731 -> 0.932), and (b) the serving/overlap path. votefit is the strongest written candidate left.
notes: 2026-09-06 board_floor (knee-6j8b4). dark6/dark7 both carry offline:null - every member is --fold -1 and has seen all 909, so the INERT verdict rests on a board delta of 0.000 whose 95% half-width at ~400 public studies is 0.0011. Fold-0 analogues of the same swap on honest members: six+small_batch6 vs six = +0.0005 [n=400: -0.0005,+0.0016]; six+grade_ladder vs six = +0.0002 (matches the ledger's sevengrade-vs-sixfresh +0.0002); six+v3base_dense vs six = -0.0004. All inside the resolution, so the axis is closed on the analogue - but it was closed originally on a ruler that could not read it. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_board-flats-below-the-boards-resolution.md
close_reason: SUPERSEDED: closed on fold-0 analogue per notes; 2026-09-06_board-flats-below-the-boards-resolution.md

title: The model fails the FOCAL findings and beats the reader on the DIFFUSE ones
description:
supervision_gap on report_labels_v2 (58 annotated studies, 696 cells, radiologist truth, held-out predictions) splits the twelve findings by physics, not by label noise.

MODEL BEATS ITS OWN LABELS (reader is the weak part): Effusion +0.1304, Contusion +0.0891, Synovitis +0.0508, Medial OA +0.0419, Baker's +0.0226, Fracture +0.0160.
MODEL FAILS ITS OWN LABELS (extraction is the weak part): Lateral Meniscus -0.1925 (labels 0.8422, model 0.6497), ACL -0.1225, MCL -0.0964, Medial Meniscus -0.0938, PF OA -0.0856, Lateral OA -0.0793.

The split is not arbitrary. Every finding we beat is DIFFUSE AND BRIGHT - fluid, edema, inflammation, effusion - signal that is large, low-frequency and survives both the downsample to 336 px (0.39 mm/px) and the max-pool across 12-20 slices. Every finding we fail is SMALL, FOCAL AND STRUCTURAL - menisci, cruciate and collateral ligaments, cartilage - a few millimetres of altered signal that a max-pool over twenty slices dilutes and a 0.39 mm/px grid barely resolves. That is a mechanism, and it predicts which arms can pay.

SIZE. The negative gaps sum to 0.670 across twelve labels. The metric is an unweighted mean of twelve AUCs, so closing a third of that is +0.019 and Lateral Meniscus ALONE is worth +0.016 - the first mechanism priced this week that clears the owner's 1.5% bar on its own rather than by composition.

DENOMINATOR, STATED: n=58 studies per finding, so each individual value carries a wide interval and no single number here is a result. The PATTERN - six negative, six positive, sorted cleanly by whether the finding is focal or diffuse - is the finding.

WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE. 'Higher resolution' is already refuted IN AGGREGATE: 392 px at the control's own encoder rate read 0.8459, +0.0002 (knee-a8x), and res392's +0.0066 was the RATE not the pixels. But that null is an average over twelve labels and this finding says six move each way, which is exactly the shape an aggregate erases (CLAUDE.md: 'a metric averaging the effect away'). The open question is therefore NOT 'does resolution help' but 'does resolution help THE SIX FOCAL LABELS while costing the six diffuse ones'. lr4e-5_ws_s2026 (336 px) and res392_ws_s2026 (392 px) are a matched pair differing only in pixels, both cached, so the test is a paired per-label bootstrap at ZERO GPU. Running as logs/perlabel_res.log.

PRICE: the per-label read is free. If the focal labels move with resolution, the arm is a focal specialist - tighter field at higher in-plane resolution, slice pooling that does not max away a five-pixel lesion - and it is ensembled in for the labels it owns rather than for its aggregate. P(the split is real given the mechanism and the clean sort) ~ 0.6; P(an arm built on it clears 1.5%) ~ 0.25.
notes:
THIRD REFUTATION, 2026-08-25, FROM THE LEDGER AND NOT FROM A RUN — the surviving lever in note (2) is not
untested, it was run and per-label gated nine days ago, and it FAILED ON THE FOCAL HALF.

Note (2) ends: 'a tighter field at the same pixel count (more pixels ON the structure rather than more
pixels overall) is a different mechanism and is untested.' That is precisely `crop80_tissue`: 80 mm about
the tissue centre at 336 px = 0.238 mm/px, against the control's 130 mm at 336 px = 0.39 mm/px. Same pixel
count, tighter field, 1.6x more pixels on the structure. It ran 2026-08-16.

AND ITS GATE WAS THE PER-LABEL READ THIS BEAD ASKS FOR, pre-registered two-sided in `crop80_tissue.sh`
exactly as here (small structures up, diffuse down) with the mean explicitly forbidden as the read. The
gate returned: the diffuse half landed as predicted (Baker's -0.028, Synovitis -0.019, Effusion -0.015)
and THE FOCAL HALF — the half the whole argument rests on — did not move. Medial Meniscus -0.012, ACL and
MCL at the floor, only Fracture up (+0.019, and the worst-agreement label in the corpus). So the trade the
mechanism predicts is not a trade: we pay the diffuse side and are not paid on the focal side.

`centre_tissue` closes the alternative reading: at the control's 130 mm extent, moving the crop's centre
to the tissue is a null (-0.0048, inside the floor). So `crop80_tissue`'s pattern is attributable to the
RESOLUTION change and not to the centring, which is what makes it a clean test of this note's mechanism
rather than a confounded one.

THREE ROUTES NOW AGREE AND THEY DO NOT SHARE A RULER: 392 px at constant field, null per label on 909
report-holdout studies (note 2); 80 mm at constant pixels, negative on the focal half at matched epoch 7;
and the same member refused by joint selection on cached probabilities (best-N containing crop80 sits
below best-N without it, at every N). Sampling density is not the focal lever at any operating point this
project has measured.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is now only this: the model's ABSOLUTE weakness on the focal structural labels is
real and independently confirmed (MCL 0.7927 on the 909-study holdout, its own worst). The finding stands;
every GEOMETRIC route to it is closed. The remaining candidates are supervision (knee-ombx, external data,
owner-blocked) and representation (knee-jk3, the 0.044 gap at matched train loss) — not pixels, not field,
not centring, not pooling depth.

METHOD NOTE ON MYSELF: this cost no GPU and no slot. It is the CLAUDE.md rule 'READ THE LEDGER BEFORE
FILING' paying out — the note that called the mechanism untested was written the day after the ledger
recorded it failing.
close_reason: Analysis complete, no action left IN THIS BEAD. Three independent routes (392px at constant field, crop80_tissue at constant pixels, joint selection on cached probabilities) agree that sampling density is not the focal lever at any operating point measured. The FINDING survives and is confirmed absolutely (MCL 0.7927, its own worst on the 909-study holdout), but every route it licensed is closed and the two that remain live elsewhere: supervision in knee-ombx (owner-blocked on Redivis tables) and representation in knee-jk3. Closing so bd ready stops offering a settled question as P0 work.

title: seat_value went dark when the champion moved to the all-data pool - every arm now prints a traceback instead of its seat
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-08-24: python -m kneemri.kaggle.seat_value --candidates distill_pairs_s2026.pt

  ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty
  member_distance.py:86 in spread(), via seat_value.py:140 MemberDistance(held, rest).report()

MECHANISM, and it is a fact about the RESULT rather than about the code. Champion.recorded() now reads allfit (0.937), six of whose seven members were fitted with --fold -1. SeatValue.scoreable() drops every one of those - they have seen fold 0, so they carry no honest holdout record - leaving a roster of ONE (band_dense_long_s2026). MemberDistance.spread() then asks each seated member for its nearest neighbour among the others, and with one member that iterable is empty.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TRACEBACK. Seat value is how a member is BOUGHT here; solo score has repeatedly failed to predict it. run_train calls seat_value automatically at the end of every arm, so from the moment allfit became the champion, EVERY finishing arm prints this traceback in place of its seat - distill_pairs and margin_smoke both did today. The ruler that decides whether a member ships is dark, and it went dark silently, as a side effect of a board entry improving.

TWO PARTS TO FIX, and the second is a design decision not a patch:
  1. MemberDistance.spread() - a roster of one has no nearest neighbour. Say so in a line; do not crash.
  2. SeatValue - refuse with a STATED DENOMINATOR when fewer than two champion members are scoreable, naming the reason (fold -1 members have seen the holdout), and let a member be priced against a named board entry whose members ARE scoreable (--against <entry-id>), so the seat number always carries the pool it was measured in.

DO NOT paper over part 1 alone: a spread line that prints for a roster of one would report a seat priced against a single member as though it were priced against the champion.

title: Train the metric: AUC-margin loss (Deep AUC Maximization) instead of BCE
description:
THE MECHANISM. The competition metric is the unweighted mean of twelve per-label ROC AUCs. We train binary cross-entropy (kneemri/training/objective.py:182). BCE is a calibration objective; AUC is a ranking one, and AUC is invariant to every monotone recalibration BCE spends capacity on. So a measurable fraction of every gradient step goes into a degree of freedom the scoreboard cannot see.

PRIOR ART, not an idea of mine. Deep AUC Maximization with the AUC-margin surrogate took 1st place in the Stanford CheXpert competition (2020), which is the closest published task shape to ours: multi-label, class-imbalanced, medical imaging, scored on mean AUROC. Yuan et al., 'Large-scale Robust Deep AUC Maximization: A New Surrogate Loss and Empirical Studies on Medical Image Classification' (arXiv 2012.03173, ICCV 2021). Reference implementation: LibAUC (Optimization-AI/LibAUC), which ships a multi-label AUROC example on CheXpert with DenseNet121. Reported to beat both cross-entropy and focal loss on large-scale medical multi-label.

WHY IT FITS THIS REPO WITHOUT A REWRITE. objective.py already has the strategy hierarchy: Objective (BCE) -> RankedObjective (adds a pairwise hinge term) -> DistilledObjective (adds teacher imitation). AUC-M is a fourth sibling, not a fork. The loss carries per-label learnable scalars (a, b) plus a margin dual alpha, optimised min-max; LibAUC uses PESG for the outer step, and whether our one-cycle AdamW is close enough to work is the first thing to find out.

THE ONE REAL DESIGN QUESTION. Our targets are FIVE DISCRETE LEVELS (0.08/0.28/0.68/0.82/0.94, core/data/labels/targets.py:34), and AUC-M is defined on binary labels. But the METRIC itself binarises, so the loss should be taken against the same binarisation the scorer uses, with the graded levels retained only in whatever auxiliary term rides alongside. Getting this wrong silently trains a different objective than the one being scored.

WHY IT IS NOT A KNOB. It changes what the network is asked to do, not how hard it is asked. That is the class of change the owner asked for ('better loss handling' rather than sharpening a subscore), and CheXpert-scale reports put it at roughly 0.01-0.02 mean AUROC over BCE — at or through the 1.5% bar rather than under it.

COST. One 12-epoch arm, ~76 min of card, control band_dense = 0.8578 already in the ledger. Zero submission slots. Read PER LABEL: the mechanism predicts the largest gains on the most imbalanced labels, since that is where BCE's calibration effort is most wasted and where the AUC margin bites hardest. A uniform lift is a weaker reading and a uniform lift matched by the rare labels lagging would refute the stated mechanism.

DEPENDENCY NOTE. LibAUC can be vendored-by-reference under external/ per the repo rule, or the AUC-margin loss reimplemented directly in objective.py — it is about thirty lines and reimplementing avoids a dependency for one term.
notes:
PRICE: ~80 min of card (12 epochs at ~400 s), 0 submission slots, no cache to build. Control band_dense = 0.8578 already exists, so no matched-control arm is owed.

GAIN the mechanism could plausibly deliver: the metric is twelve rank statistics and every member fitted here descends cross-entropy, which reads values. The published version of this substitution (Yuan et al., arXiv 2012.03173) took 1st on CheXpert 2020 — mean per-label AUC on multi-label medical images, this metric with a different organ. If the value/rank mismatch is costing anything here it is an OBJECTIVE-level defect, so its size is not knob-sized: 1-2% absolute is the honest ceiling.

P(clears the 1.5% bar) ~ 0.20. Two reasons it is not higher. (1) The recipe ALREADY carries a ranking term at 1.0, so part of the rank-vs-value gap is already paid for — this arm is the difference between a ranking term added to cross-entropy and a pure rank surrogate replacing it, not the difference between rank and no-rank. (2) The rare-label batch hole is pre-registered: Fracture is positive in ~7% of studies against a batch of twelve, so its term is skipped in roughly half of all steps. Expected value is still good at 80 min because a null here is INFORMATIVE — it retires the whole 'the loss is not the metric' axis, which currently licenses several unrun ideas.

Arm written: experiments/arms/margin_seat.sh. arm_check --only margin_seat: 0 refused. Smoke next.

title: Rank-distillation from the fold-0 ensemble: one student, three exits (owner design 2026-08-24)
description:
OWNER'S DESIGN, and the unification is his. I had split this into three bets - distil-and-replace (efficiency), soft-targets-as-denser-supervision, and distilled-student-as-a-diverse-member. He collapsed them correctly: A and C are the SAME ARTEFACT with two exits chosen by the measurement rather than in advance, and B is not a separate training at all, it is an extra LOSS TERM in that one run. So: one student, one arm, three outcomes.

  EXIT A - student reaches teacher parity: ship it alone. 7 forward passes become 1, ~1h -> ~9min on a T4. That is the Efficiency Prize, which we currently lose by construction.
  EXIT C - student short of parity but structurally distant: seat it as a member. The ledger's own rule is 'buy a seat on the AXIS, not on the count and not on the solo score', and an encoder-family-distant member is more distant than anything ever seated (twin 0.930, recipe-distant 0.931, objective-distant 0.931, pixel-distant 0.932).
  EXIT B is the loss, and it runs either way.

THE LOSS FORM IS DECIDED BY THE METRIC, NOT BY THE DISTILLATION LITERATURE. Standard KD is KL on softened probabilities. That is wrong here and the repo already says why: ensemble.py:6, 'Calibration is worth nothing, so no thresholding, no temperature, no Platt scaling.' The metric is twelve rank-based AUCs, so a KL spends student capacity matching probability VALUES the metric discards. The term should be PAIRWISE ORDER against the teacher, and RankedObjective.pairs(above, below) already computes exactly that mass - it is handed labels today and would be handed teacher scores instead. Same tested code, different supervision.

WHY THIS IS NEW SUPERVISION AND NOT A RESTATEMENT OF THE LABELS - the mechanism that makes it worth card time. Under binary labels a pair carries order information ONLY if it is a positive against a negative; same-class pairs are unordered and teach nothing. Under teacher scores EVERY pair is ordered, including positive-vs-positive and negative-vs-negative. Effusion is positive in ~60% of studies so labels order ~48% of its pairs; Fracture is ~7% so labels order ~13% of its pairs; the teacher orders 100% of both. That is genuinely more supervision on the SAME corpus, with no external data and no licence answer - which matters because knee-y3pv's audit closed with data volume as the only axis above the bar and knee-ombx blocked on an owner licence call.

PRE-REGISTERED, and it is a PER-LABEL clause rather than a mean: the gain must CONCENTRATE on the labels with the most skewed positive rate, because that is where binary pairs are scarcest and where the teacher adds the most orderings. Fracture (~7%) should gain most, Effusion (~60%) least. If the mean moves but the per-label pattern is flat or inverted, the mechanism claimed here is NOT what moved it and the arm is not read as a confirmation - the same discipline calib_span was read under.

TEACHER CONTAMINATION, and it decides which members teach. Six of the seven champion members trained on all 4,406 studies (--fold -1), so their predictions on training studies are MEMORISED, not generalised, and distilling on them would teach the student the teacher's memorisation. The teacher is therefore the FOLD-0 TWINS, all on disk: band_dense_s2026, calib_span_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, base_dense_s2026, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026. Weaker teacher (~0.869 joint offline against the champion's 0.937 board) in exchange for a holdout that is clean for teacher AND student, which is the only way this arm produces a number anyone can read.

COST-TIERED, because a v3 student confounds two variables at once - if it fails, that is distillation failing OR v3 failing and the arm cannot say which.
  ARM 1 (~45 min card): DINOv2-small student, same family as the teachers. Zero architecture confound. Answers only 'does rank-distillation transfer at all'.
  ARM 2, gated on arm 1: DINOv3 student. The diversity play, both exits live. Also rescues a dead investment - every v3 arm lost on hard labels (-0.0377, -0.0400, -0.0445) but README:313 records frozen-v3-plus-LoRA beating fine-tuned v3 by +0.0160, annotated 'recipe was damaging v3'. A weak-transfer architecture failing on sparse hard labels and recovering on dense soft ones is the textbook distillation case, and three failed arms are evidence about the RECIPE.
design:
PLUMBING, smallest change that fits the existing strategy pattern.
1. Teacher targets over the 3,526 fold-0 TRAIN studies. PredictionCache and HoldoutPredictions already do this for the 909-study holdout; extend the cache key/slab to the train split rather than writing a second path. ~6 members x ~6 min = ~36 min card, cached once and reused by every later arm.
2. DistilledObjective(RankedObjective) adding  in __call__, and reporting its weight through settings() so  can assert the flag LANDED in the checkpoint config - the repo has been bitten by a flag recorded in a config and read as a constant.
3. Teacher scores thread through Predicted alongside logits/scores/weights.
4. --distill-weight on TrainOptions, defaulting 0.0 so every existing arm is bit-identical.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS for arm 1, against teacher joint offline ~0.869, best solo member 0.8598, and the plain-recipe control:
  >= 0.869  student MATCHES the six-member teacher. Exit A live; efficiency prize becomes real. Extraordinary and would need a re-run before it is believed.
  0.860 - 0.869  beats every single member this project has trained. Seats almost certainly; measure seat value against the champion pool.
  0.850 - 0.860  distillation transfers but does not beat the best solo. Read the per-label clause; seat value decides.
  <= 0.8598 with the per-label clause FLAT  the term is adding nothing the labels did not already carry, and arm 2 is NOT licensed.
Refutation: student at or below its own no-distillation control means the term did not transfer at this operating point, and the v3 arm does not run.
close_reason: Duplicate of knee-1xsu, and the duplication is mine: the first create emitted shell syntax errors (backticks and parens in the description hit bash eval), I grepped its output for the wrong marker, read a partial success as a failure and filed the same bead twice. It also landed MANGLED - every backticked fragment was eaten, so its design section reads 'adding  in __call__' with the actual term missing. knee-1xsu carries the intact text plus the falsifier clause. Lesson is the one that already cost a duplicate this week: verify a bd create by its own success marker, not by the absence of something in the tail.

title: Price the external knee-MRI corpora - the only axis above the bar is unpriced past MRNet
description:
WHY THIS IS P0 AND WHY IT IS NOT A NEW IDEA. experiments/README.md:2066 ends the half_data arm with: 'The corpora that could carry a doubling are OAI and the combination of several; pricing them is the next question, not this arm's.' Nobody asked it. The knee-y3pv audit closed on 2026-08-24 with every in-model direction dead (test-time path, metric structure, capacity, decode, supervision, schedule, regularisation - all flat inside the 0.0062 floor), leaving data volume as the ONLY axis whose mechanism has ever delivered above the 1.5% bar: +0.019-0.023 per doubling, measured at 1,763 -> 3,526 studies.

THE PRICE THE DOOR NEEDS. 0.937 -> 0.950 is +0.013 board = +0.0068 offline at the +1.92 transfer slope = 0.34 of a doubling = ~+930 training studies. That is SMALLER than MRNet's 1,370. The goal is not out of reach of the data axis; it is out of reach of the corpora we have ASKED ABOUT.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS AND IS NOT. It is a PRICING task: for each candidate corpus, establish (a) study count against our 3,526 training studies, so the slope prices it, (b) LICENCE - specifically whether a Kaggle competition submission may be built on it, which is the axis that already blocked MRNet in knee-ombx, (c) LABEL OVERLAP with our twelve, since MRNet's coarser abnormal/ACL/meniscus table makes it an auxiliary or pretraining corpus rather than N more supervised studies, and (d) modality/sequence match - our members read sagittal stacks at 336px and a corpus of a different sequence is a different mechanism again. It is NOT a download, NOT a training arm, and it must not become one before the licence column is filled, because that is exactly the column that stopped MRNet.

CANDIDATES NAMED SO FAR: OAI (the ledger's own suggestion), MRNet (priced ~+0.0095, licence-blocked pending knee-ombx), and 'the combination of several' - which is the reading that matters, since the slope is on TOTAL corpus and several sub-doubling corpora compose where one does not.

COSTS NO CARD AND NO SLOT. It is readable work, and the card is biohub's until 14:00Z by their written claim, so it contends for nothing.
close_reason:
DUPLICATE of knee-ombx, filed 3 days earlier and more thorough than this framing. Its LICENCE SWEEP note (2026-08-21) already priced every candidate I named and several I did not: K2S (CC BY-NC-ND and no longer distributed), KMAR-50K (NC), KneeMRI Rijeka (primary host 404, mirror is not a licence), mridata (unreachable), fastMRI and OAI (approval/DUC-gated, fail 2.6a on access). Its conclusion is the one that matters and I would have re-derived it: the sweep did not unblock the axis, it CLOSED the escape hatch. 'The combination of several' - the ledger line I filed this on - is dead on ACCESS rather than on size, which is a stronger result than the pricing question I asked.

I filed this without reading knee-ombx first. Fifth time the read-the-ledger-first rule has paid this week, and the first time it caught me after the write rather than before it.

title: The per-label deficit axis is worth +0.0043 total — closed on a matched ruler
description:
New instrument kneemri/evaluation/weights_gap.py compares OUR weights against the twenty published CC0 members' on the SAME 909 fold-0 studies, same graded truth, same midpoint, same rank AUC — the comparison published_ruler's own docstring says belongs on the shared fold-0 holdout and which nothing had built.

Their five folds and our one were drawn independently so no single member covers our holdout; within one seed their five folds partition the corpus, so stacking a seed gives one held-out prediction per study from ONE model. Four seed columns. Members whose oof covers >40% of the corpus (their fold:-1 blocks) are refused.

RESULT — ours minus their average single member:
  MCL              -0.0346 (0.7423 vs 0.7769)   n_pos 171
  Fracture         -0.0167 (0.7827 vs 0.7994)   n_pos 68
  Medial OA        +0.0069 | Lateral OA +0.0082 | Synovitis +0.0141 | Effusion +0.0146
  Contusion        +0.0253 | ACL +0.0292 | Baker's +0.0319 | PF OA +0.0348
  Medial Meniscus  +0.0529 | Lateral Meniscus +0.0712
  MEAN             +0.0198 (0.8483 vs 0.8285); we also beat their 4-seed pool at 0.8369

WE WIN TEN OF TWELVE LABELS. The entire demonstrated per-label headroom is (0.0346+0.0167)/12 = +0.0043 on the mean — a quarter of the bar, and it is the CEILING of the weak-column programme, not an arm's estimate. Fracture's share is not real (68 positives, SE ~0.04; corpus ruler puts Fracture at 0.8923, our strongest). Purchasable: MCL alone, +0.0029.

CONSEQUENCES:
 - focus_mcl CANCELLED before running. 3.1 h of card for at most +0.0029. Arm file kept, header says why.
 - focus_latmen's kill is confirmed for a better reason: Lateral Meniscus is the label we beat their weights on by the LARGEST margin (+0.0712). The corpus ruler calling it weakest was a fact about THEIR model.
 - knee-gisc (MCL recipe-axis ceiling) downgraded: the measurement stands, the target never deserved arms.

DOES NOT RULE OUT: ensembling (their pool gains +0.0084 over their single member here, and that is the axis that carries a public entry from 0.83 to 0.899); the ruler transfer to the board (ruler_transfer/board_transfer not re-read against this table); a genuinely different encoder.

Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-23_the_per_label_axis_is_worth_0.004.md
close_reason: RESOLVED: axis closed on matched ruler per own title (+0.0043 total), weights_gap.py

title: The per-label denominator that matters is OURS, not the corpus ruler's
description:
Two rulers give opposite weak-label profiles because they measure different WEIGHTS, and the project has now made the denominator error in both directions.

CORPUS RULER (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_the-ruler-was-five-times-too-small.md): 4,407 studies, floor 0.0024, built from the twenty published CC0 members' out-of-fold predictions. Says Lateral Meniscus 0.7981 is the weakest label, MCL 0.8166, Fracture 0.8923 is the BEST. That document holds THEIR members and says so.

OUR RULER (band_dense_llrd_s2026 fold-0, 909 studies, floor 0.0053), against its own mean 0.8481 at e11: MCL 0.7422 (-0.1059), Fracture 0.7830 (-0.0650), Lateral OA 0.8089 (-0.0391), Lateral Meniscus 0.8423 (-0.0058), ACL 0.8782 (+0.0301), Medial Meniscus 0.8975, Baker's 0.9062.

WHICH GOVERNS. What ships is basedense_v1, five ALL-OURS members. The score is the unweighted mean of twelve of OUR columns, so our profile is the denominator. Consequences both ways:
 - focus_latmen was built off the corpus ruler's weakest label and was aimed at a deficit belonging to somebody else's encoder. Retired; arm file deleted.
 - experiments/README.md line 827 retires 'MCL and Fracture are targets' on the corpus ruler. That retirement is correct for Fracture and WRONG for MCL: on our weights MCL is the weakest column by a wide margin.

FRACTURE STAYS RETIRED, on label_power's argument rather than on the ruler swap: 313 corpus positives means ~65 in a 909-study fold and a standard error near 0.04; it read 0.784/0.903/0.864 across three folds of one recipe. A fold cannot measure it.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT SURVIVES: MCL 0.7422 and Lateral OA 0.8089 to ~0.85 is +0.0124 of the mean. Under the 1.5% bar alone; the largest clean piece of it.

EXISTENCE PROOF, and it is the load-bearing part: another model fitted on THIS corpus reads MCL 0.8166 +/- 0.0155, which is 0.04 above our typical (0.773 across 83 runs) and above our best-ever 0.8042. MCL is not an intrinsic ceiling of the data or the label. The ceiling is ours.
notes: 2026-08-23: SUPERSEDED by knee-q1pf. This issue was right that the denominator is OUR columns, not the corpus ruler's. Its arithmetic (MCL + Lateral OA worth +0.0124) is not: it priced the deficits against our own mean, which is a statement about our profile's SHAPE, not about reachable headroom. weights_gap prices them against weights that provably exist on the same studies — Lateral OA is a label we BEAT them on (+0.0082), so it carries no headroom at all. Total demonstrated per-label headroom is +0.0043.

title: MCL is our cheapest column and our members are unanimous on it - test whether jointness is what imposes the ceiling
description:
Annotation-ruler AUCs (58 image-read studies) against published knee-MRI work: Lateral Meniscus 0.6497 vs OrthoDiffusion 0.850 (-0.20, 3-4 SE); ACL 0.8640 vs 0.970/0.965/0.960 (-0.10, ~2 SE). Every other label is within 0.04 of the field or above it. Ceiling on the competition metric if both reach published level: (0.20+0.10)/12 = +0.025, which clears the 0.02 bar and exceeds the 0.018 gap to first place (0.952). Lateral Meniscus alone: +0.017.

Both labels sit in knee-dtk's model-bottlenecked half, derived independently from the same annotations on 2026-08-14. External ruler and internal partition agree.

This bead names WHERE, not WHY. Candidate mechanisms unranked: slice sampling density, plane coverage (the 0.924 public kernel reads 42 slices across 5 plane/fat-suppression slots including Axial; we read 20), physical-mm vs pixel crop, per-finding head structure, pretraining domain.

Caveats that must travel with any plan built on this: 58-study ruler, per-label SE 0.04-0.06; corpus/prevalence confound; MRNet and ELNet are ACL-specialist models on ACL-enriched data; this competition grades ambiguous findings NEGATIVE for specificity, which no cited paper does.

Source: research/2026-08-23_published-per-label-auc-vs-ours.md
notes:
PRICE 3.1 h of card (12 epochs, 20 slices, band_dense recipe). GAIN if the top band lands (MCL >= 0.843): licenses a specialist column per weak label (MCL, Fracture, Lateral OA) under the twelve-column contract, ~+0.018 on the metric. P(clears 0.843) ~ 0.15 — MCL never passed 0.8042 across 83 recorded runs and every recipe axis is refuted on it, but the OBJECTIVE axis has never been tested, which is what this arm is. Expected ~+0.0027 per 3.1 h on the improvement path alone.

RE-PRICED 2026-09-01, and the instrument value is now the larger half. residual_split plus the honest12 per-label AUC put MCL at -0.0555 below our ensemble mean (the biggest single column on our OWN ruler, which is the one the metric sums) AND at 24.4% unanimity, at the pooled floor. Cheap and unanimous together means the family is stuck there, not mis-seated -- so a family-level change is the only kind that can move it, and the objective is the one such change left untested. The pre-registered null (0.783-0.802) retires the loss axis outright and points the deficit at mm/px on the medial margin, which is worth the card on its own.
close_reason: Answered by a run already on disk. focus_mcl RAN (12 epochs); MCL peaks 0.7861 (e7) vs the control's 0.7931 = -0.0070, inside the pre-registered 0.783-0.802 band: jointness costs MCL nothing, at maximum tilt. The ledger had it as cancelled-before-it-ran in one place and as refuted at 0.5332 in another, the latter being the twelve-label mean the arm forbids reading. The null's follow-up (mm/px on the medial margin) is answered in the opposite direction by crop80 and band140 on disk: tighter crop is monotonically worse on MCL and the widest band holds our best-ever 0.8076. No card spent. interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-01_mcl_falls_to_every_axis_we_own.md

title: External data has never been tried in 107 runs, and MRNet is the one candidate whose licence may survive rule 2.6a
description:
Rule 2.6a permits External Data that is 'publicly available and equally accessible to use by all Participants ... at no cost'. Nothing in 107 recorded runs has ever trained on external data; the repo knows MRNet only as slice-aggregation literature, never as a data source.

Licence read (2026-08-21), not assumed:
- MRNet (Stanford, 1370 knee exams, sag PD / cor T1+T2FS / ax PD-FS, labels abnormal / ACL tear / meniscal tear extracted from clinical reports - the same derivation as ours): free, instant self-registration, Research Use Agreement. Free and open to any participant, so 'equally accessible at no cost' holds. BUT the RUA is non-commercial and forbids redistribution and link-sharing, and this competition pays 77k with a winner licence to the host. That conflict is an OWNER DECISION, not a measurement.
- fastMRI / fastMRI+ (22 knee pathology categories, 16154 expert boxes): approval-gated application with institutional affiliation -> fails 2.6a, not equally accessible.
- OAI (KL grades, maps to 3 of our 12): signed institutional Data Use Certification -> fails 2.6a, and OA-only.

MECHANISM. Not '+1370 studies of label supervision' - only 2-3 of our 12 labels map, and a generous per-label read of that gives about +0.006, under the bar. The mechanism that could plausibly deliver 1.5% is SUPERVISED PRETRAINING OF THE ENCODER ON KNEE PATHOLOGY, which attacks the 0.044-at-matched-train-loss generalisation gap directly (base_dense 0.8371 at loss 0.8456 vs cnx_dense 0.7927 at loss 0.8332). Every encoder tried was pretrained on natural images and the failure mode is generalising badly from a good fit - which is what a domain-matched initialisation is for. Same goal the SSL MAE chased and failed at three times, with the difference that 1370 labelled knee exams are far denser supervision than MAE on unlabelled volumes. External corroboration: MRNet reaches ~0.97 on ACL with AlexNet at 256 px, a smaller model at lower resolution than our 336, against our 0.874.

PRICE. ~2h download + preprocess into the existing cache format, then one 45-min arm at the shipped recipe with the encoder initialised from MRNet-pretrained weights instead of DINOv2. ~3h. Plausible gain 1.5-3% if the domain-gap diagnosis is right, 0 if the generalisation gap is about data QUANTITY at fine-tune time rather than about the initialisation. Odds of clearing the bar ~1 in 3 - the best ratio on the board, because everything else is priced at <=0.006 with higher confidence.

BLOCKED on the licence decision. The loader, cache writer and pretraining arm are ours to write and cost nothing to have ready, so prepare them meanwhile.

REFUTATION CLAUSE, pre-registered: if the arm clears +0.015 the 'data-limited not capacity-limited' diagnosis is confirmed and the encoder chapter re-reads as 'wrong pretraining corpus'. If it lands flat AND the 3D-stem instrument lands flat, the binding constraint is neither initialisation nor receptive field, and the only remaining reading is the label ceiling, which reader_agreement says we cannot cross because the board's labels come from the same reports.

Full argument: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-21_three-failures-one-mechanism.md
design:
LICENCE QUESTION IS SETTLED — FROM THE PRIMARY SOURCE, WHICH IS IN THIS REPO.

The earlier DESIGN text on this bead asserted "THE PRIMARY SOURCE COULD NOT BE READ FROM THIS SESSION".
That was false and cost a user turn. The rules are transcribed at comp/COMPETITION_RULES.txt, 515 lines,
committed 2026-08-12. Read them, not forum quotes.

Section 2.6(a), lines 143-148, verbatim shape: External Data must be EITHER "publicly available and
equally accessible to use by all Participants of the Competition for purposes of the competition at no
cost to the other Participants" OR "satisfies the Reasonableness criteria as outlined in Section 2.6.b".
It is a DISJUNCTION. The earlier reading treated it as a conjunction and blocked on the wrong branch.

Section 2.6(b), line 150: "The use of external data and models is acceptable unless specifically
prohibited by the Host." The default is PERMIT; 2.6.b's machinery is entirely about EXCESSIVE COST
excluding participants, not about a dataset's redistribution licence.

MRNet clears branch ONE outright and never needs branch two: free self-registration, no fee, the same
access for every participant. Its non-commercial RUA restricts what we may do with the data, not who may
obtain it, and 2.6(a) is an ACCESSIBILITY test.

Section 2.5, lines 128-130, closes the winner-obligation half: "In the event that input data or
pretrained models with an incompatible license are used to generate your winning solution, you do not
need to grant an open source license in the preceding Section for that data and/or model(s)." And the
winner licence being granted is CC-BY-NC 4.0 (line 120) — itself non-commercial, so MRNet's NC term is
not incompatible in the first place. Section 2.8 (lines 187-197) asks for training code, inference code,
model weights and a compute-environment description; none of that requires redistributing MRNet.

CONCLUSION: MRNet is PERMITTED. This bead is unblocked on the licence axis. What remains is the work
itself, not a permission question. fastMRI+ and OAI were declined earlier on 2.6(a) — that reading was
made under the conjunction error and should be RE-CHECKED against the disjunction before either is
called out of bounds, though neither is priced above MRNet.
notes:
MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-09-03. mrnet_warm_s2026 trained (0.8487 peak e6, converged, reproduced epoch-for-epoch by a second run). Rule 2.6 permits it. Its SEAT is worth 0.0000: vote_ceiling over twinfive's five 0.8706 -> 0.8705; seat_value --against twinfive_v1 -0.0000, band [-0.0010,+0.0009], best swap +0.0004 vs BOARD_RESOLVABLE 0.0040. Decorrelation is REAL and is not the reason - MemberDistance nearest 0.8892 (roster's own spread 0.8696-0.8972) and mean 0.8552, the most globally distant candidate the pool has been offered. Specialist rescue measured and failed: MRNet pretrains on ACL, mrnet leads the pool on ACL solo 0.8840 vs 0.8737, but per-label the pool moves at most 0.0027 and mean +0.0000 because the pool is already 0.9011 on ACL. Declined in writing at comp/members.declines. THE STANDING READING: corpus distance on the SAME lens buys nothing; only ARCHITECTURE distance is untested.
2026-09-20T01:40Z REOPENED. The close on 2026-09-03 was a licence block; the owner's 2026-09-14 ruling removed it (everything usable except KneeCoT; SKM-TEA/fastMRI/Rijeka instrument-only). MRNet is not on the excluded list. The bead sat available for six days.

STATE NOW, measured this session, not assumed:
- corpus on disk: D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/mrnet, 7.3 GB, extracted (axial/ coronal/ sagittal/ + the six <split>-<finding>.csv tables).
- two bugs on the EXTRACTED read path, both fixed here. (1) mrnet_labels.ArchiveLabels.table opened the path with zipfile directly, so an extracted corpus raised PermissionError [Errno 13] from zipfile/__init__.py:1367 - a message about the wrong thing. Now routed through MRNetSource.at(). (2) ExtractedSource.names() globbed only *.npy while ZippedSource.names() returned the whole namelist, against its own 'Every member' contract, so the label tables were invisible and the decode died on FileNotFoundError: train-acl.csv is not in this download.
