Large has 24 blocks, so the same flag adapts a QUARTER. The arm is therefore NOT one variable against base_labelwise224_dense: width and the adapted FRACTION both moved, and the wider trunk got half the relative adaptation. Matched-epoch midpoint trace has large behind base at every epoch but e1 (e0 -0.0084, e2 -0.0057, e3 -0.0023, e4 -0.0088, e5 -0.0068) with a HIGHER train loss at matched epoch (0.7015 vs 0.6824 at e5), i.e. learning slower rather than overfitting - which is what a quarter-adapted trunk looks like. So a loss on this arm is evidence about the harness, not about capacity, and it may NOT close the capacity axis. The clean test is large at a matched FRACTION (--unfreeze-last 12), and its VRAM is the open question: 6 blocks of 1024-wide currently sits at 23712 MiB under a 26 GB cap, so 12 will not fit there and the step has to be 9 or 10. Throughput 753 img/s against the control's 1642; 386 s/epoch, not the 237 priced.
CLOSED FLAT 2026-09-23. large_labelwise224_half (--unfreeze-last 12 = half of 24 blocks, matching the base control's 6 of 12) = 0.8936 ledger75 @ e8 vs base_labelwise224_dense 0.8950 = -0.0014, inside the 0.0062 paired floor, for 3.1x the parameters (304M vs 86.6M) and 3.1x the wall-clock (534 vs 170 s/epoch).

READ IT ON LEDGER75 OR GET THE OPPOSITE ANSWER: midpoint says large WON (e8 0.8607 vs base 0.8589).

The confound was mine and is proven removed: large_labelwise224_dense inherited --unfreeze-last 6, a constant fitted on a 12-block trunk, which adapts a QUARTER of a 24-block one. It scored 0.8888 @ e6 (-0.0062). Train loss at e5 is the proof the second arm is a clean width test: 0.6856 against the control's 0.6824 (identical), where the quarter-adapted arm read 0.7015.

The quarter-adapted arm was neither a capacity ceiling nor pure under-adaptation: by e11 it drove train loss to 0.5213, BELOW base's 0.5663 final, while the holdout sat flat from e6.

VRAM: the 26 GB OOM was the CAP, not fragmentation (21.94 GiB allocated under a 26.00 ceiling with 3.83 GiB free on the device). card_check found the missing headroom: LibreOffice soffice.exe pid 41440 holds 2515 MiB by arrangement. 28 GB is the value that runs; peak 20.15 GB reserved / 17.05 allocated, so 224/12sl does NOT fragment.

Verdict: the trunk is not what is missing. Every larger-trunk proposal is retired unless it brings a mechanism this arm did not test.

title: Base trunk at the SHIPPING corner, unlocked by checkpointing (base_labelwise_dense336)
description:
The 336 corner was declared barred on an OOM that never enabled gradient checkpointing. --recompute-activations (adaptation.py:248, default False) is absent from base_labelwise336.sh, and encoder_surgery.py:470-495 measures it at 19% throughput for nearly all of the encoder's activation memory, on this workload, at this resolution. 25 arms already use it, base_dense and base_champion among them. It changes NOTHING about the experiment - same batch, same loss, same 66 within-batch pairs for the rank term - which is why it was chosen over splitting the batch.

So the real arm is base at the corner we actually ship at: 336 px, 20 slices, 0.1-0.9 band, --calibrated-targets --hold-annotations. ONE variable against labelwise_dense (0.8964 ledger75 @ e7, 909 studies, free on disk): --variant base. The 336px/20sl/0.1-0.9 array is the plain-named one labelwise_dense already reads - no decode, no --scheme.

WHY THIS AND NOT MORE 224 WORK: every 224 arm lands 0.88-0.89, BELOW the best solo this project owns (labelwise_dense_drop40_long36 0.9030). 224 is an instrument corner. The deliverable is a single solo checkpoint, so the arm has to be at the shipping corner or it cannot compete. Capacity measured +0.0067 under labelwise at 224 (knee-ss5rd); the mechanism is live and this asks whether it composes with the resolution and depth the family ships at - plausibly MORE, since a wider trunk has more tokens to spend at 336/20sl than at 224/12sl.

PRICE: ~2.6 h card. 171 s/epoch at 224/12sl x 3.75 (2.25x pixels, 1.67x slices) x 1.23 (the checkpointing tax) = ~790 s/epoch, 12 epochs. Zero decode, zero slots, control free. P(clears 0.9026) ~ 0.35. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.10.

This is the CHEAP PROXY that gates the expensive commit: if it clears, the 36-epoch drop40 version at the same corner is ~7.8 h and is the shot at a solo that beats 0.9030.

Seven OOMs at 336 for a wide trunk, cause measured as allocator fragmentation (~28.5 GiB reserved against 23.21 in use) with expandable_segments a confirmed no-op on this Windows machine. Superseded anyway: the capacity axis closed FLAT at the 224 corner that does fit (knee-jzho6, large_labelwise224_half -0.0014 at matched adapted fraction), so there is nothing a 336 wide trunk would answer that 224 has not.

title: Carry the validated base trunk toward the shipping corner
description:
Does the shipping family's DATA CORNER (extended slots + 0.1-0.9 band + 20 slices) beat the dense 224 recipe at the 224 instrument corner?

The original framing (a one-variable depth step) is NOT available: the only 20-slice 224 cache on disk is images_224px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_extended.npy (37.1 GB, built 2026-09-19), which is extended-scheme AND 0.1-0.9 band. Against base_labelwise224_dense (canonical, 0.2-0.8, 12sl) that is three flags. They are not three knobs: they are the corner labelwise_ext_drop40_long and the whole shipping family run at 336. So the question is the corner, not depth.

The first attempt (2026-09-23T00:48Z) died on FileNotFoundError because its stamp read scheme=canonical and asked for images_224px_20sl_0.1-0.9band.npy. One flag, --scheme extended, makes it run.

PRICE: ~1.0 h (285 s/epoch x 12, zero decode, zero slots, control free)
P(clears 0.8950) ~ 0.35
P(clears 0.9100, the 1.5% bar) ~ 0.08
notes:
The 336 cell is DEAD as written and the machine, not an argument, killed it. base_labelwise336 OOMed twice: 20.00 GiB allowed / 18.67 GiB allocated, then 27.00 allowed / 23.21 allocated with 2.38 more requested and 4.40 free on a 31.84 GB card. base at 336/12sl does not fit at batch 12, and batch may not be cut - --rank-weight 1.0 is pairwise and sees --batch studies within a step regardless of --accumulate, so a cut takes the rank term from 66 pairs to 6 and confounds every 0.88-0.90 control. MEASUREMENT to carry: the 1.89x base/small footprint ratio measured at 224/12sl (6.86 -> 12.99 GB) UNDERSTATES as token count grows and must not be reused at a higher resolution; the variant-blind derived figure (36827 MiB) was closer to right than my 17.6 GB scaling. arm_check's NO ROOM was overridden and was correct.

The --smoke that appeared to clear it reads the _first60 array it writes itself and never touches the corpus, so a smoke can never catch this class.

USEFUL BYPRODUCT, kept: the depth+band step is calibrated on a max head. native224 (12sl, 0.2-0.8) 0.8800 vs band224 (20sl, 0.1-0.9) 0.8801 = +0.0001. Also band224_hold 0.8824 @ e11, band_deep224 0.8718 @ e11 - all three --slice-pooling max, so NO labelwise control exists on the 224/20sl array.

LIVE ARM: base_labelwise224_dense, launched 22:00:10Z, takes the third axis of the dense recipe - --calibrated-targets --hold-annotations - at the control's own cached corner and under its own measured cap. PRICE: ~35 min card. P(clears 0.8961) ~ 0.30. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.08. Harness check landed at 22:03Z: variant base, calibrated_targets True, hold_annotations True, image_size 224, slices 12.
base_labelwise224_dense_drop40_long36 = 0.8996 ledger75 @ e18, 909 studies (LEDGER midpoint 0.8645, move +0.0351). Against control base_labelwise224_dense 0.8950 that is +0.0046, INSIDE the 0.0062 paired floor = band 2 of its own pre-registration: directional, keep nothing, compose nothing. convergence_check does not list it, so the score is real and not a truncation floor. CROSS-ARM READ: the identical two flags bought +0.0066 on the small trunk and +0.0046 on base, so the schedule step pays LESS as the trunk widens - the opposite of the direction the arm's mechanism argued, so refuted rather than merely unconfirmed. SEPARATELY: the 0.9030 'best solo' anchor used across this bead is WRONG. dml_b_s2026 reads 0.9078 on the same ruler and the same 909 studies, and basinsoup_dmlb_k4 0.9092 is a solo too since a weight soup is one averaged checkpoint. Base at the instrument corner is 0.0082 behind the shelf, not 0.0034. Ledger: experiments/README.md 2026-09-23T00:40Z.
MACHINE-CLOSED 2026-09-23T05:22Z, two OOMs, two different binders.

--vram-gb 24: the CAP bound. 19.31 GiB allocated, 3.00 reserved-unallocated, 2.18 GiB request refused with 6.92 GiB STILL FREE on the device.
--vram-gb 28: the CARD bound. 23.92 allocated + 3.75 reserved-unallocated = 27.67 under a 28.00 ceiling, 1.59 GiB free when a 1.34 GiB request failed.

28 is the largest cap this machine runs clean (31.84 total minus the 2.34 GB LibreOffice holds by arrangement), so there is no cap above it. The arm pre-registered this exact closure before running.

Escapes barred by prior measurement, not preference: batch may not be cut (pairwise --rank-weight sees --batch studies per step regardless of --accumulate; 66 pairs to a handful confounds every 0.88-0.90 control), slices are the thesis, 224 is already the small side.

The --scheme extended fix WAS correct and is kept: the stamp read scheme=extended on both runs and the FileNotFoundError never recurred. What closed the arm is VRAM, not the cache.

Answering depth at the SHIPPING corner needs images_336px_24sl_0.1-0.9band_extended.npy, which does not exist: ~80 GB on a disk at 196 GB free plus ~3-4 h of decode that buys no signal alone, then a ~2 h arm. Same ratio as multiscale, declined the same morning for the same reason.

title: Capacity re-read under a labelwise head (base_labelwise224)
description: AXES/backbone.py record capacity as inside the noise floor (small 0.8272, base 0.8283, large 0.8304, floor 0.0053) but all three are rank24 members on a MAX head, pre-whole-stack, pre-labelwise. adaptation.py:121 says the opposite ('capacity is the only axis that has ever cleared our noise floor'). title: Complete the pool x slice-pooling 2x2: focal token pooling under labelwise (focal_labelwise224)
description:
AXES.md:238 names focal/sided pooling under labelwise UNREAD and the cheapest of the dilution attacks. The 2x2 is three quarters built and has been for weeks; nothing has ever run the fourth cell.

THE THREE CELLS ON DISK, matched epoch 9, 909 rows, ledger75:
  native224_s2026      max       + cls_mean   0.8800
  focal224_s2026       max       + cls_mean_focal   0.8776   -0.0024
  labelwise224_s2026   labelwise + cls_mean   0.8832   +0.0032
  MISSING              labelwise + cls_mean_focal

MECHANISM, and why the missing cell is not just a fourth number. AXES.md:61 disowns the ruler under four input rows: each was measured on a MAX-pooling head, which demonstrably suppresses a real input change. cls_mean_focal appends the top-k patch tail (token_pooling.py:62, FOCAL_FRACTION 8) to the CLS+mean vector — it is a bet on SMALL FOCAL findings, which is exactly what a 1-3 mm meniscal tear is and exactly what a max over slices destroys. Under labelwise attention each finding attends its own slices, so a per-label head is the only readout that can USE a focal tail. That is the interaction this cell tests and the reason a flat read under max is not evidence the token change is inert.

THE BAR IS ARITHMETIC AND IT IS HARSH. Both main effects are inside the 0.0062 paired floor. For the cell to be a RESULT rather than a fourth number the interaction has to be >= +0.009 on its own, i.e. the cell must read >= 0.8894 against the labelwise control's 0.8832.

BANDS (control labelwise224_s2026 = 0.8832 ledger75 @holdout909, matched epoch):
  >= 0.8894  the interaction is real; focal pooling was dilution-limited and the token axis re-opens at 336
  0.8832-0.8894  DIRECTIONAL only. Keep nothing, plan nothing.
  < 0.8832  focal token pooling is inert under labelwise too, and the disowned-ruler caveat is ANSWERED for this axis rather than merely quoted — the pooling family closes on both rulers.

PRICE: ~0.75 h card (224 corner, 12 epochs, 3.2x the 336 throughput). Zero submission slots. Control free and on disk.
P(clears 0.8894) ~ 0.15. P(clears the 1.5% bar) ~ 0.02.

IT IS AN INSTRUMENT, and that is how it is justified rather than as an improvement: whichever band it lands in it retires AXES.md:61's caveat for the token-pooling axis, which currently blocks four input rows from being read at all. 45 minutes to convert a disowned ruler into a verdict.
notes:
READ 2026-09-22. focal_labelwise224_s2026 = 0.8796 ledger75 @ e9, 909 studies, convergence clean (not TRUNCATED). Control labelwise224 = 0.8832. Delta -0.0036 -> pre-registered band 3 (< 0.8832): focal token pooling is inert under a labelwise head TOO. The 2x2 now closes:
                      cls_mean   cls_mean_focal
  max         native224 0.8800   focal224       0.8776  (-0.0024)
  labelwise   labelwise 0.8832   focal_labelwise 0.8796 (-0.0036)
Both rows negative, same sign, same size. No interaction: the disowned-ruler caveat is ANSWERED for the token-pooling axis rather than quoted, and the pooling family closes on both rulers. cls_mean_focal is dead; do not re-open by re-quoting a number at it.

title: SAM at rho=0.01: the honest revisit the rho=0.05 refutation pre-registered
description:
AXES.md:233 names this the one live mechanism in table D — implemented, never tried at the right radius.

WHY THE RADIUS AND NOT THE MECHANISM. sam_dense_s2026 at rho=0.05 read 0.8213 against calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634, -0.0421 matched-epoch, and the ledger (README:16588) separates the two causes on evidence rather than on hope: the gap is UNIFORM, present at epoch 0 (0.6921 vs 0.7515), so it is not the truncated anneal; and the plumbing witness fired live, so Sharpness.climbed was not silently returning False. rho=0.05 is the published value for from-scratch schedules on normalised weight scales. Against a pretrained trunk at --backbone-lr 4e-5 the ascent step rho*g/||g|| is large relative to the update and walks out of the basin every step. 0.01 is 5x smaller, one arm, not a sweep.

WHY IT IS NOT A KNOB. Every axis this project closed — aggregation, readout, slice depth, model scale, corpus, labels, seating, weight-space averaging — closed by moving the offline number without moving the transfer, and every one was closed IN-domain while the board is out-of-domain to our holdout. SAM is a training-time objective on the FLATNESS of the minimum rather than a change to what is read; it is the only generalisation-side lever in the tree.

CONTROL IS FREE AND ALREADY ON DISK: calib_dense_hold_s2026 = 0.8634 @holdout909 midpoint, the identical flag list. bf16 path, so no GradScaler confound.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS (same as the rho=0.05 arm, so the two are comparable):
- below 0.8604 — the mechanism is refuted at this budget, not just the radius; SAM closes.
- 0.8604 to 0.8684 — DIRECTIONAL ONLY, inside the noise on a solo read; keep the flag, never plan around it.
- 0.8684 or above — the radius was the cause, and the one generalisation-side lever re-opens.
- The gain must be SPREAD across labels. A sharpness penalty has no per-finding preference and cannot concentrate, so a mean win carried by one or two columns REFUTES the mechanism while reading as a win.

PRICE: ~1.9 h card (279 s/epoch measured, DOUBLED by the second forward and backward, x 12 epochs). Zero submission slots. Matched control free.
P(clears 0.8684) ~ 0.30. P(clears the 1.5% bar) ~ 0.05.

IT IS AN INSTRUMENT EITHER WAY: whichever band it lands in, the SAM axis stops being open, and it is the last row in AXES.md section Open that costs under two hours.
notes:
CLOSED AS A DUPLICATE BEFORE IT COST A CARD. arm_check TWIN caught it: the arm I wrote (sam_fine) was sam_r01 flag for flag, and sam_r01 RAN 2026-09-17 — sam_r01_s2026.holdout.npz has been on disk for five days. AXES.md:233 still said OPEN, never tried; that row is the defect, and it is now corrected in place.

THE ANSWER, which existed already: sam_r01_s2026 0.8655 / 0.8981 ledger75 against calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634 / 0.8949 = +0.0021 midpoint, +0.0032 ledger75. Inside the pre-registered 0.8604-0.8684 directional band. The radius WAS the cause of the rho=0.05 collapse — all four points recovered — so the mechanism is not refuted, but rho=0.01 at this corner is DIRECTIONAL ONLY.

WHAT KILLED THE FOLLOW-ON, also already on disk: knee-k3v5t (sam_ship, compose onto the shipping recipe) is repriced to P(clears 0.0062) ~ 0.05 and stays unarmed. The proxy for what SAM has to recover is the held-out AUC surrendered while train loss keeps falling: 0.0036 at the dense corner sam_r01 ran, 0.0006 at the shipping corner — a tenth of the paired floor. Nothing of that kind is left to remove there.

COST OF THE STALE ROW: two tool calls and a bead, no card. The index is the thing that has to be right — this is the second time a stale AXES/prose row nearly bought a card for a reading already taken (see knee-18c5r).

title: basinsoup_dmlb_ff is built, unread, and its build bead is closed — no open bead owns the reading
description:
Built 2026-09-21 03:00 under knee-17la8, which CLOSED on the BUILD. The checkpoint has never been read. A closed build bead plus an unread artefact is exactly the failure CLAUDE.md names: 'an unread result is the only work in this repo with a deadline'.

DARK by construction: --fold -1, so no offline number exists or can be made. The board is its only ruler and a SLOT is the only way to read it.

PROJECTION (from knee-17la8, do not re-derive): base basinsoup_dmlb_k4_s2026 at 0.9092 ledger75; solo board-transfer puts the base at 0.9430; the refit term across four bases is +0.001/+0.003/+0.004/+0.007. Projects ~0.947 against the 0.946 champion.

ff-of-soup, the order this project had never run - the champion basinsoup_ff_k4_s2026 is soup-of-ff.

PRICE: 0 h card. One board slot.
P(clears the champion) ~ 0.4; P(the order matters at all) is what the slot actually buys.

GATES BEFORE THE SLOT: submit_check (is it new), mount_check --live, kit_check --mounted, witness_check --device auto, champion_check, run_check on the kernel log after it completes, Einstein grep of comp/board.jsonl.
notes:
READ ALREADY, AND THE BEAD WAS WRONG THAT IT WAS NOT. submit_check --kernel kneemri-dmlbffsoup refused on 2026-09-22 19:51Z: SAME 1 members as dmlbffsoup_v1, ref 56409058, submitted 2026-09-21, board 0.9400.

So the slot this bead asked for was spent the day the bead was written, and the projection it carried (~0.947 vs the 0.946 champion, P ~ 0.4) was already falsified on the board when I read it.

THE RESULT, which is what the bead was actually for: ff-of-soup reads 0.9400 against soup-of-ff's 0.946. The ORDER MATTERS and it matters against us by ~0.006 — averaging the fold-fits and then fine-tuning is worse than fine-tuning and then averaging. Mechanism worth keeping: a soup is a point in a basin its members surround, and fine-tuning FROM that point leaves the basin the members agreed on, whereas ff-then-soup averages endpoints that each stayed in their own. Close the order question; do not re-run it at another base.

Caught by submit_check's SET equality, which is the one gate that asks whether the board already holds the entry. Third stale index in one session (AXES SAM row, this bead, and knee-7xpqt) — each would have bought a card or a slot for a reading already on disk.

title: Re-read OrthoDiffusion at full Stage II: the recorded loss is uninterpretable by its own pre-registration
description:
ortho_diffusion.py:15-18 pre-registered that their 256-wide middle block against dinov2-large's 1024 makes a LOSS confounded with capacity and only a WIN clean - 'the right asymmetry for a screening instrument and the wrong one for a verdict'. README:7386 then recorded the loss (orthodiff@mean 0.7435, seat +0.0001) as 'the clearest decline'. Under this repo's own faulty-harness rule that is a faulty-TEST finding, not a refutation.

Our read is the paper's Stage I at its weakest, five separable defects:
1. ONE block per plane, paper fuses three
2. ONE timestep, paper uses 200/150/50
3. GAP pooling; Li et al. (PMC12772265, DDPM on 59,830 UK Biobank T1WIs) measure LSE > mean > max
4. a ridge probe; paper uses a learned fusion (CATS, 1.7M params) which beats frozen linear probes AND from-scratch 3D CNNs
5. fully frozen; Li et al. prescribe LP-FT (fine-tune the backbone on target data before extraction)

Paper reports macro AUROC 0.908 on 8 knee abnormalities from Stage II. arXiv:2602.20752, MIT weights, HF lanstat0123/orthodiffusion.

WHY THIS RANKS: it is the only trunk we own that consumes the slice stack INSIDE the encoder, which is the axis the standing saturated-aggregation diagnosis names. It is already DISTINCT (js 0.0418 against the roster's 0.0150) and the failure to convert distinctness into a seat is the case the diversity argument keeps predicting should work. Aimed at the four model-side error-census bands (Lateral Meniscus -0.1925, ACL -0.1225, MCL -0.0964).

PRICE: ~0 h card for the probe re-read (embeddings are cached; the fusion is CPU-fittable). ~3 h if LP-FT is included.
P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.15 for the full Stage II; P(the loss is confound rather than trunk) ~ 0.5.

Blocked on the GPU being ours - probe half is card-free.
notes:
ANSWERED, card-free, 2026-09-22 18:12Z — NO complement on any of the twelve.

CORRECTION FIRST: the Stage II re-read is NOT free. features_orthodiff_336px_12sl_r256_gap256_volume.npy and its mask were deleted in the approved 355 GB cache cleanup; only the index JSON and probes/orthodiff_mean_probe.holdout.npz survived. Re-reading needs 4,407 studies re-encoded through three 3D U-Nets — card work. The cache key bakes pooling in (gap256), so LSE was never recoverable from it either.

THE SURVIVING PREDICTIONS ANSWER THE COMPLEMENT QUESTION AT ZERO CARD COST. orthodiff_mean_probe vs basinsoup_dmlb_k7_s2026, @holdout909@cut0.5, same 909 studies, per-label delta (probe minus dino):

ACL -0.1162 · MCL -0.1082 · Medial Meniscus -0.1512 · Lateral Meniscus -0.1738 · Medial OA -0.1176 · Lateral OA -0.1126 · PF OA -0.1699 · Effusion -0.0735 · Synovitis -0.0699 · Baker's -0.1738 · Contusion -0.1342 · Fracture -0.1790. Mean 0.7407 against 0.8724, -0.1317.

Behind on ALL TWELVE, by 0.0699 to 0.1790. Not one label where the diffusion trunk is even NOMINALLY ahead. Rank-mix with the champion base reads +0.0017 at w=0.15 (under the 0.0053 paired floor) and -0.0011 at w=0.25. So the js 0.0418 distinctness that kept this axis open is distinctness WITHOUT a complementary column: the probe disagrees with the pool everywhere and is right nowhere.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT, per the arm's own pre-registration (ortho_diffusion.py:15-18): our read is the paper's Stage I at its weakest — one block not three, one timestep not three, GAP not LSE, ridge not learned fusion, frozen not LP-FT, and a LOSS on that read was pre-declared uninterpretable. What is NEW is that the loss is UNIFORM across all twelve rather than concentrated, which is evidence about the REPRESENTATION and not about the fusion: a weak-but-complementary trunk shows at least one column ahead, and this shows none. That raises the price of the Stage II card spend and lowers P(clears) — it does not by itself close the axis.

DEFECT FOUND WHILE READING THIS (needs its own bead): probe holdout records carry an int64 truth binarised at write time, while trained members carry the graded 7-rung table. RecordMix REFUSES the probe against the trained pool for that reason — competence_axis dropped it as "not mixable with the majority". The binarisation is the same cut (feature_probe.py:283 uses > MIDPOINT), but the LABELS TABLE has drifted: 32 of 10,908 cells disagree (0.29%), 3,352 probe positives against 3,336 graded. Small enough that the 0.7435 number stands; large enough that no probe can ever enter a pooled read, and no probe number can be recut to ledger75.
2026-09-23 ensemble-lens review: the only trunk that reads the stack INSIDE the encoder, but 09-22 shows it behind on all 12 labels (mean 0.7407 vs 0.8724) and rank-mix +0.0017 < 0.0053 floor. Stage II now costs a full re-encode of 4407 studies (cache deleted). Rank BELOW knee-tl2ut (Pillar-0) and knee-vot9n for any ensemble lever; gate both on soupraptor_v1 (knee-3mamq).
2026-09-25 00:10Z: Stage II trainer research/scripts/ortho_finetune.py (their recipe: input+middle params at lr x0.05, head 5e-4, Adam+cosine, BCE on graded targets; 6 slots -> GAP of PLANE_READS block -> one linear head; fresh noise per step as aug, NOISE_SEED at eval). title: run_train --resume destroys the holdout record when no resumed epoch beats the restored best
description:
Measured 2026-09-21 on labelcut_v3_ema_s2026. A PC restart truncated the arm at e22; the 13:20Z holdout record existed and priced 0.9039 ledger75. Resuming to finish the run DESTROYED that record.

Two behaviours compose into the hole:
1. run_train clears prior artefacts at start (and rotates metrics.jsonl -> metrics.1.jsonl).
2. --resume restores the KEPT (best) checkpoint, not the last epoch run (fitting.py:260 resumed(), resume.py:37 SUFFIX='.resume'). So it restarted from the e15 best, not e22.
3. A holdout record is written ONLY when a new BEST epoch fires. Resumed e16-e23 (0.8657/0.8663/0.8662/0.8663) all landed under the restored e15 best 0.8668, so nothing rewrote the file.

Net: the cleared record was never replaced. The reading the arm declared (# reading: labelcut_v3_ema_s2026.holdout.npz) was gone, and reading_check would refuse the arm.

Recovered with python -m kneemri.inference.holdout_backfill --checkpoints <ckpt> --device cuda (re-derivation, not the training array: cross-precision tolerance, max |delta| 0.0168, mean 0.000964, measured 2026-09-17).

Fix candidates: (a) run_train refuses to clear a holdout record under --resume, or moves it aside like it does metrics; (b) --resume restores the LAST epoch rather than the best, which is what 'resume' means everywhere else; (c) at minimum, warn loudly at start that the existing record is about to be cleared.
notes:
FIXED 3f3bedfa. And this bead's diagnosis was WRONG in its load-bearing claim: nothing was destroyed.

RunMetrics.begin ROTATES rather than clears -- run_metrics.py, "_artefacts" pairs both the .pt and the
<stem>.holdout.npz and moves them aside under _run<n> with the epochs. So the record was on disk the
whole time. Measured 2026-09-22, ledger75 --holdouts D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality:

  labelcut_v3_ema_s2026_run1   0.8668  ledger75 0.9039  epoch 15  909 rows
  labelcut_v3_ema_s2026        0.8667  ledger75 0.9038  epoch 23  909 rows

Top row is the original, mtime 16:20, untouched. Bottom is the holdout_backfill re-derivation, mtime
17:46, made at a max |delta| of 0.0168 while the byte-exact original sat next to it under a different
name. Same number to -0.0001, so no quoted score is retracted -- but the backfill was unnecessary and
the tolerance it carries was paid for nothing.

The real defect is a NAMING hole, not data loss: under --resume the rotated record is still the reading
OF THE CHECKPOINT --resume RESTORES, and it is sitting under a name the arm's "# reading:" declaration
does not point at.

Fix is candidate (a), narrowed: begin(recipe, *, resuming) copies the rotated predictions back to the
live name. Copied, not moved, so the rotated round keeps its own record beside its epochs. A later new
best overwrites it as usual. Candidate (b) -- resume from the last epoch rather than the best -- was
REJECTED: resume.py writes weights and trajectory together so they can only describe the kept epoch,
and changing that changes results. (c) is a no-op.

Nothing changes for a plain re-run, which is a different run and may not inherit a reading; covered by
test_begin_leaves_the_live_name_free_when_not_resuming.

STILL OPEN, not fixed here: the live labelcut_v3_ema_s2026.holdout.npz is the backfill standing where
the original exists under _run1. Restoring it is a one-line copy and prices +0.0001, but it overwrites
a file, so it needs the owner's word.

title: 349 arms carry no --vram-gb, so every one of them claims the card instead of its share
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-21. grep -L 'vram-gb' experiments/arms/*.sh returns 349 scripts.

MECHANISM. A PyTorch caching allocator grows into whatever is free and never releases it. So an absent --vram-gb is not 'no opinion about memory' -- it is a claim on the entire free card, held until the process exits. Two consequences, both observed today:

1. An uncapped run's 'peak memory N GB reserved' records WHAT WAS AVAILABLE, not what the recipe needed. labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ema logged 17.28 GB; arm_check prices the same --slices at ~9.6 GB. The 17.28 was then quoted into labelcut_v3_ema's header as the requirement, and into an after_room.sh gate of 23000 MiB -- greed quoted back as a spec, and it set the room gate nearly 2x too high.

2. Removing a participant does not reduce device usage. Our ~16.5 GB arm was killed at 11:47Z; device went 31783 -> 31172 MiB with ZERO of ours left on it, because two peers absorbed the freed memory within seconds.

WHY THE OWNER'S CAP DIRECTIVE DID NOT COVER THIS. The standing rule is 50-70% of VRAM, ~16-22 GB, passed as --vram-gb. It is stated as a CEILING per job, and three jobs each under their own ceiling still sum past the WDDM eviction line at ~31.7/32.6 GB. Caps must SUM under the line, not each sit under it. On a card shared with two other trainers our share is ~10-11 GB, not 22.

FIX, in order:
  a. Every arm passes --vram-gb priced off arm_check's --slices reserve plus ~1.5 GB, not off a previous run's logged peak.
  b. arm_check's OVERSTATED check graduates from advisory to REFUSING, and gains the opposite case: MISSING (no --vram-gb at all), which today is silent.
  c. after_room.sh gates are set to cap + ~1 GB. A gate quoted from an uncapped peak is the same defect one layer up.
  d. export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True in lib.sh, so fragmentation headroom stops being reserve we hold and never use.

DONE SO FAR: labelcut_v3_ema recapped 22->18->11 GB (arm_check drove it down), expandable_segments exported, room gate 23000 -> 12000.

COST OF NOT FIXING: the owner kills our arms, correctly, because they take too much of a card they share. Today that cost three transduction seeds and the resolution of that axis.
notes:
FIX ITEM (d) IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. It said to put PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True in lib.sh so every arm inherits it. That flag is a NO-OP on this machine: torch prints `UserWarning: expandable_segments not supported on this platform` (c10/cuda/CUDAAllocatorConfig.h:39) at startup and falls back to the ordinary allocator. Measured 2026-09-21 in labelcut_v3_ema_s2026.full.log:7, on a live arm that carried it. Windows/WDDM.

Putting it in lib.sh would have shipped a false mechanism to all 349 arms and made every later cap look like it had allocator help behind it. Removed from labelcut_v3_ema.sh; removing a no-op cannot move that arm's number.

Items (a)-(c) stand and are the real fix: price caps off arm_check rather than off a previous run's 'peak memory reserved' (that figure records what was AVAILABLE, not what was needed), graduate arm_check's OVERSTATED to refusing, add a MISSING case for an arm with no --vram-gb at all.

EVIDENCE FOR (a), from this arm: the twin logged 17.28 GB reserved uncapped. arm_check priced the same recipe at ~9.6 GB off --slices. Capped at 11 it ran to peak 10.77 GB reserved / 8.52 GB allocated -- so 6.5 GB of the twin's 'requirement' was allocator greed, and the cap is not binding the run.
AUDITED 2026-09-22, CPU only. THE HEADLINE PREMISE OF THIS BEAD IS WRONG, and the fix it proposed would
have made the card worse.

"An absent --vram-gb is a claim on the entire free card" is not what the code does. DeviceBudget.capped
falls back to max(needed() * CAP_HEADROOM, DEFAULT_SHARE * whole) -- device_budget.py, "asked = self.vram_gb
or max(...)". Nothing is uncapped. A silent arm is capped at its own derived need or at 0.8 of the card,
whichever is LARGER.

MEASURED over all 490 invocations in experiments/arms (not 349 -- that grep counted FILES; several hold
more than one run_train):

  named --vram-gb        69 / 490
  silent                421 / 490
  silent sitting at the 0.80 floor (25.5 GB)      219 / 421
  silent arms' own derived need x1.15   min 2.9  median 22.4  p90 32.5  max 55.1 GB
  derive ABOVE the card ceiling 29.84 -> clamped  200 / 490
  derive under half the card (15.9)               149 / 490

WHY FIX (b) IS REJECTED. Making a MISSING --vram-gb refuse would force 421 arms to re-type a number the
code derives better, and it CANNOT lower a single one of them: capped() uses a hand-typed value exactly as
typed, so a number under the derived need does not make the run smaller, it makes it raise. That is this
class's documented preference over a PCIe crawl, and it is not sharing. Fix (a) has the same defect for the
same reason -- labelcut_v3_ema took a cap of 11 because its RECIPE derives ~9.6, not because a flag made it
small.

WHAT THE THRASHING ACTUALLY IS. 200 of 490 arms derive a cap above the card and clamp to
whole - DESKTOP_RESERVE_GB = 29.84. For those, NO value of any flag both fits the recipe and leaves a
co-tenant alive. Worst: resnet50d_short and resnet50d_lr at 55.1 GB derived (20 slices), compose_base 41.4,
v3large_dense / ortho_lpft / ortho_fresh_lowlr / ortho_fastmri* 36.7 (12 slices).

THE LEVER IS THE RECIPE, NOT THE FLAG: needed() follows --slices, --image-size and the batch. The flag is a
third statement of a fact the recipe already makes, which is knee-ylp0's finding from the other side.

LANDED: arm_check gains UNSHAREABLE -- an arm whose capped(CARD_GB) exceeds SHARED_SHARE (0.5, the owner's
standing directive) of the card. Counted on a sweep, REFUSES at --only, because 200 of 490 is an erosion
record and not something one sweep fixes. It asks the question `overstated` does not: that one compares an
arm against ITSELF, and an arm sitting exactly at its own derived need can still hold four fifths of a
shared card. CARD_GB and SHARED_SHARE are new constants in device_budget.py with their arguments.

NOT DONE, and it is the owner's call: DEFAULT_SHARE is 0.8 because that is where the arms that named a cap
landed, and those arms were written when this project had the card to itself. Dropping it to 0.5 would pull
106 silent arms down from 25.5 GB to their own derived need and change nothing for the other 315 (max()
keeps a recipe above its measured demand). It is a training-path behaviour change that cannot be smoked
while the card belongs to biohub.
Corrected the UNSHAREABLE count: 364 of 490 arms, not 477. The first implementation asked DeviceBudget.capped(), whose silent fallback is max(needed()*CAP_HEADROOM, DEFAULT_SHARE*whole) with DEFAULT_SHARE=0.8 — 25.5 GB, already above the 15.92 GB half-share, so every silent arm tripped by construction and the number was a fact about a project-wide constant rather than about any arm. It now measures the arm own DEMAND: the named --vram-gb or needed()*CAP_HEADROOM, clamped to CARD_GB-DESKTOP_RESERVE_GB. Every one of the 364 is recipe-attributable; the 113 that dropped out demand under 15.92 GB on their own. Worst is adapt_null by 13.92 GB, which is the SATURATED maximum (29.84 ceiling minus 15.92 share) — its recipe derives above the whole card, so no flag value both fits it and leaves a co-tenant alive. That class is the content of this bead: the lever is --slices / --image-size / the batch, never the flag. Verdict ships ADVISORY (no arming_refuses) since refusing 7 arms in 10 earns a --no-verify; it graduates when the tree is clean. Lives in kneemri/experiments/arm_budget.py (ArmBudget) — split out of arm_check.py, which was 804 lines against the 750 god-file ceiling.

title: A peer returning mid-arm spills us silently: no throughput tripwire
description:
PRICE: ~1 h to implement, 0 slots. P(clears any band) n/a - this is a harness guard, not a lever.

basinsoup_wide launched 02:56Z through a free-VRAM gate that was satisfied while the shared peer still held 14.6 GB. Our arm reserved 17.84 GB, the card went full, and WDDM spilled to host: epoch 0 took 1789 s against round 1's ~255 s on the IDENTICAL recipe, a 7x slowdown. Killed 04:16Z after 1.3 h of card bought nothing; c404 discarded.

Every signal a human or a gate looks at was green. 100 pct utilisation, correct loss curve (0.6172), correct holdout (0.8668), correct peak-memory line, no error. Only img/s and wall-clock per epoch carry it, and nothing reads them.

The launch gate is now 20000 MiB (peer absence, not our footprint), which does NOT fix this: a peer that returns AFTER we launch reproduces it exactly.

Wanted: run_train records epoch wall-time and refuses to continue when an epoch exceeds a multiple of the first epoch on the same recipe, or of a recipe-declared budget. A spill is a memory fault presenting as a compute cost; the only honest detector is throughput.

title: Does the one-shot soup premium scale with K? The last free parameter in weight space
description:
PRICE: ~0.6 h card, 0 slots
P(clears 0.9102 ledger75) ~ 0.30

WHY THIS IS THE ONLY THING LEFT ON THE AXIS. knee-grkrv closed souping as a LADDER on a mechanism:
leaving a soup is a STEP not a slope, so any resumed gradient forfeits the averaged point in full and
a round's net is structurally ~0. The rule that survives is AVERAGING MUST BE THE LAST OPERATION, and
the one-shot off a PLAIN FIT is the one form that pays (+0.0014, round 1, dml_b 0.9078 -> 0.9092).
That operation has exactly one free parameter that has never been swept: K, the number of members
averaged.

WHY IT IS AN INSTRUMENT AND NOT AN IMPROVEMENT. Expected offline gain is ~+0.001, under every floor
(0.0053 paired, 0.0062 seed). It is worth 0.6 h because it DECIDES a bigger spend: on the board the
shipping soup-of-ff reads K=3 0.945 and K=4 0.946, and extending that to K=8 costs ~1.2 h of card AND
A SLOT. One board tick between K=3 and K=4 is inside the ~0.004 2-sd scatter and cannot license it.
Fold-0 space can, for free, because ledger75 prices it and _ff members (--fold -1) can never be priced
offline at all (knee-s8kim).

WHAT RUNS. Three more children off the SAME parent with the SAME round-1 recipe (--epochs 4
--backbone-lr 2e-5, --init dml_b_s2026, --init-scope all), seeds 704/705/706 -> 404-series naming
kept distinct. Then soup K=7 (parent + six children) and K=6 (six children, no parent) and price all
of them against the existing K=4 0.9092 with one ledger75 call.

PRE-REGISTERED BRANCHES on ledger75 against basinsoup_dmlb_k4_s2026 = 0.9092:
  >= 0.9102   the premium SCALES with K. Licenses soup-of-ff at K=8 on the shipping side, which is
              then the best-priced slot this project has.
  0.9093-0.9101  weak or decaying scale. Real but not worth 1.2 h and a slot; record and stop.
  <= 0.9092   the premium is FLAT in K. K-extension is dead, soup-of-ff K=4 is final, and weight space
              closes with NO free parameters left rather than with one untested.

DIAGNOSTIC READABLE EVEN ON A NULL: the new children's mean. c401/402/403 read 0.9061/0.9062/0.9062.
If 404/405/406 do not land in that band the seeds are not exchangeable and the K comparison is void
rather than negative -- that is a harness verdict, not a mechanism one.
notes: READ 2026-09-21T08:37Z, zero slots. k7 0.9096, k6 0.9095 against the pre-registered k4 0.9092. Lands in the MIDDLE band: weak or decaying scale, record and stop. K=4->K=7 buys +0.0004 against the first soup's +0.0014 - sublinear and flat by six. Soup-of-ff K=8 is REFUSED, which is what this instrument was for: it saved 1.2 h of card and a slot. Void-check passes (new children 0.9064/0.9065/0.9065 against round 1's 0.9061/0.9062/0.9062, same band, seeds exchangeable), so this is a mechanism verdict. k6==k7 to 0.0001 also retires the parent-anchor question: the anchor's pull is a 1/K term, averaged away by six. Weight space now closes with NO free parameter left. Ledger section: 'K is the last free parameter in weight space, and it is spent'. Roster lines for k6/k7 on members3; 15 ingredients and the WDDM-spilled c404_run1 declined in writing.

title: Gentle fork: soup premium is divergence-independent, so fork degradation is the only movable term
description:
PRICE: ~0.8 h card, 0 slots (fold 0, priced on ledger75).
P(clears 0.9106 ledger75) ~ 0.40.

THE MODEL, derived 2026-09-21T00:41Z at zero card cost from members already on disk (ledger75, holdouts D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality, population eb3ba199, 909 studies):

  round 1  children 0.9061/0.9062/0.9062 mean 0.9062  parent dml_b_s2026 0.9078  soup 0.9092
  round 2  children 0.9067/0.9084/0.9050 mean 0.9067  parent basinsoup_dmlb_k4 0.9092  soup 0.9091

Two terms, separated for the first time:
  SOUP PREMIUM over the children mean:  +0.0030 (r1), +0.0024 (r2)
  FORK DEGRADATION vs the parent:       -0.0016 (r1), -0.0025 (r2)
  net = premium - degradation:          +0.0014 (r1), -0.0001 (r2)

THE PREMIUM IS CONSTANT AND DIVERGENCE-INDEPENDENT. Child spread was 0.0001 in round 1 and 0.0034 in round 2 -- 34x -- and the premium moved by 0.0006, inside noise. knee-0dfys named child DIVERGENCE as the binding constraint and knee-p9mp5 closed the family on SATURATION; both readings are superseded by this decomposition. Averaging never stopped working. What changed is the DEGRADATION, which grows as the parent gets stronger, and in round 2 it exactly cancelled the premium.

WHY THIS RE-OPENS knee-p9mp5 RATHER THAN RE-QUOTING IT. That bead's <= 0.9092 branch read SATURATES and said no further soup arm is licensed. It is answered, not re-quoted: its own arm could not separate premium from degradation because it never priced its children against the parent, and the separation says the term that failed is the one the arm held FIXED (epochs 4, backbone-lr 2e-5, declared 'fixed by measurement, not a knob with a sweep in it'). Those values were measured positive on a NON-souped parent, where degradation was 0.0016. Nothing measured them on a souped one.

THE ARM. basinsoup_soft: the round-2 arm byte for byte -- same parent basinsoup_dmlb_k4_s2026, same K=3/K=4 shape, same vram shape -- with the fork alone moved to --epochs 2 --backbone-lr 1e-5. That is ~4x less weight movement, so degradation should shrink; the premium, being divergence-independent, should hold. Matched contrast against basinsoup_r2 on one variable.

DIAGNOSTIC THAT IS READABLE EVEN ON A NULL: the CHILD MEAN. Above 0.9067 says degradation did shrink and the mechanism is right whatever the soup nets; at or below it says the fork rate is not what sets degradation, and the two-term model is wrong rather than the recipe.

PRE-REGISTERED on ledger75 against parent 0.9092 and round 2's 0.9091:
  >= 0.9106      net positive at full size. The ladder is ITERABLE, round 4 is licensed, and a chain of +0.0014 rounds is the only compounding operation this project owns.
  0.9093-0.9105  positive but decaying. Read the child mean to say whether degradation shrank less than hoped or the premium decayed too.
  <= 0.9092      the fork recipe is NOT the binding term. Souping closes on a second, independent recipe and the family is dead for good rather than on one arm.

CONTEXT. Weight space closed in both ORDERS tonight (knee-17la8, ff-of-soup board 0.940). This arm does not re-open the order question; it asks whether the operation that DOES pay is iterable.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-09-21T01:23Z — BOTTOM BRANCH (<= 0.9092). basinsoup_soft_k4 = 0.9081, below the parent 0.9092
and below round 2's 0.9091. K=3 0.9074. Children 0.9060/0.9060/0.9056, mean 0.9059.

The pre-registered null diagnostic fired: child mean at or below 0.9067 says the fork rate does not set
degradation. Rounds 2 and 3 share a parent and differ ONLY in fork strength (4 ep @ 2e-5 vs 2 ep @ 1e-5,
~4x less movement); degradation grew, -0.0025 -> -0.0033. Backwards from the hypothesis.

PREMIUM CONFIRMED CONSTANT A THIRD TIME: +0.0030 / +0.0024 / +0.0022. Averaging is not the failing term.

MECHANISM THAT REPLACES THE RECIPE LEVER: leaving a soup is a STEP, not a slope. Two epochs at 1e-5 from a
warm start barely move the weights and still cost 0.0033 -- the averaged point is a knife-edge whose value
IS the averaging, and any resumed gradient forfeits it in full regardless of how little is walked.
Re-averaging returns the constant premium, the two nearly cancel, and a round's net is structurally ~0
independent of recipe.

SOUPING IS ONE-SHOT. Pays once off a PLAIN FIT (round 1, +0.0014, degradation only -0.0016) and ~0 after,
because every later parent is itself an averaged point and is billed the larger step. Supersedes
knee-p9mp5 (SATURATION named the net, not its cause) and refutes knee-0dfys (DIVERGENCE: 34x spread,
premium flat). Closed on three rounds and two fork recipes, not one arm.

UNIFIES WITH THE BOARD ROW. dmlbffsoup_v1 put four corpus epochs on a soup and read 0.940 vs a
pre-registered ~0.947. Same step at corpus scale. Both orders of weight space close under ONE rule:
AVERAGING MUST BE THE LAST OPERATION. basinsoup_ff_k4_s2026 satisfies it.

The one-shot is already spent on the best plain fit on disk (dml_b 0.9078). No untried cell remains.
Ledger written. Card released, no follow-on armed.

title: ff-of-soup: full-corpus warm-start of the highest fold-0 checkpoint we own
description:
The _ff operation has never been applied to a SOUP. The champion basinsoup_ff_k4_s2026 is soup-of-ff: children refitted full-corpus, then averaged. This is the other order - average first, then give the average the 4,407-study corpus.

BASE. basinsoup_dmlb_k4_s2026, 0.9092 ledger75, the highest fold-0 number this project owns, and 0.0041 above knee-9grwy's base (0.9051).

WHY IT IS NOW PICKABLE. Measured 2026-09-20T23:36Z on slot 56407707: the fold-0 soup basinsoup_k3_s2026 (0.9089 ledger75) boards 0.943 against its _ff sibling basinsoup_ff_k3_s2026 at 0.945. So the FOLD PENALTY IS 0.002, 2x board resolution, and the fold-0 shelf is board-predictive with a -0.002 offset. Before that reading there was no licence to rank fold-0 bases against the board at all.

ARITHMETIC. Solo transfer n=10, slope +1.071, intercept -0.0307, resid sd 0.0021. 0.9092 -> fit 0.9430. Refit term across four bases +0.001/+0.003/+0.004/+0.007, median ~0.004 -> ~0.947 against the pinned 0.946.

THE OP. 4 epochs at backbone-lr 2e-5 with --init-scope all on --fold -1, NOT a 24-epoch fit. Those are the values souping measured positive (basinsoup2 read 8 epochs BELOW the 4-epoch pair). A 24-epoch fit would wash the soup out and cost 3 h to re-run an op already priced; the soup's only deficit against the champion line is the 909 studies it never saw, and this is the cheapest operation that supplies them.

NO DISTILL TERM. The dml_b peer supervision is already in the soup's weights; adding a teacher pass would change two variables and cost 25 min of inference.

PRICE: ~0.5 h. P(clears 0.946 board) ~ 0.25.

READING IS THE BOARD, on a slot after 00:00Z. Once fitted on --fold -1 it holds nothing out and no ledger row can price it (knee-s8kim); that is true of every _ff the project ships.

BRANCH. >=0.947 the op is real and round 2 forks children off THIS checkpoint. 0.944-0.946 the op is inside board resolution of the champion and ff-of-soup is a draw, not a lever. <=0.943 the order does not matter and soup-of-ff stays the only weight-space op that pays.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-09-21T00:36Z: BOTTOM BRANCH. dmlbffsoup_v1 (ref 56409058) read 0.940 against a pre-registered ~0.947 -- -0.007, 3.2x the 0.0022 top-band residual sd, so a mechanism reading and not scatter.

MECHANISM. A soup sits at an averaged point whose value IS the averaging. Four epochs at --backbone-lr 2e-5 --init-scope all walk it off that point and nothing re-averages afterwards, so the soup is SPENT rather than compounded. soup-of-ff survives because the averaging is LAST. The order matters, and it matters in the direction opposite to the one this arm bet on.

SECOND READING, not separated by this row. The -0.002 fold-penalty offset was fitted on the basinsoup K=3 pair and was applied here to a dml_b-family base, where it had to make a 0.0003 offline difference (0.9092 vs 0.9089) order two board entries -- a tenth of the residual sd. The offset stands on its own family; this use of it was an over-extension, and that is a lesson about the OFFSET, not about the base.

WHAT IS NOT REFUTED. basinsoup_dmlb_k4_s2026 at 0.9092 fold-0 is still the highest honest fold-0 number the project owns. Nothing here says that member is bad; it says the _ff-after-soup operation destroys what made the soup worth 0.9092.

CONSEQUENCE. Weight space is CLOSED IN BOTH ORDERS -- round 2 read SATURATES (basin ceiling recovered, not raised, divergence up 34x for nothing) and this row closes the remaining operation. Champion pin unchanged at basinsoup_ff_k4_s2026 / 0.946.

title: Does weight souping COMPOUND? Round 2 off basinsoup_dmlb_k4, the only op measured positive
description:
THE QUESTION. Souping is the one weight-space operation this project has measured positive, and it has now reproduced three times with the same sign and order: +0.0016 on basinsoup (0.9073 -> 0.9089), +0.0014 on basinsoup_dmlb (0.9078 -> 0.9092, knee-8pj5j), and +0.001 on the board via basinsoupff_v1 (0.946, ref 56406877, the first solo this project owns to tie the seven-seat champion). Nobody has asked whether it COMPOUNDS. Every round so far forked children off a parent that had never been souped.

WHY IT MATTERS, priced on the ruler that can resolve it. knee-0dfys refit the solo board-transfer off comp/board.jsonl (n=10 single-member entries carrying both numbers): slope +1.071, intercept -0.0307, resid sd 0.0019. Inverted, board 0.946 needs offline75 0.9117 and board 0.955 needs 0.9201. The shelf top is now 0.9092. A single further +0.0014 lands 0.9106 -- still short. TWO further rounds land ~0.9120 and clear the 0.946 bar. So compounding is the ONLY mechanism on the shelf with a path to a solo that BEATS the pinned champion rather than tying it. Saturation closes the family for good, which is worth having.

THE ARM. Identical to basinsoup_dmlb byte for byte except the parent: three 4-epoch seed-children (seeds 501/502/503) forked off $MODELS/basinsoup_dmlb_k4_s2026.pt with --init-scope all at --backbone-lr 2e-5, then weight_soup K=3 and K=4, holdout_backfill --device cuda, ledger75. 4 epochs at 2e-5 is not a knob with a sweep in it: basinsoup2 measured the far side (K=3 0.9075 / K=4 0.9080 at 8 epochs, both BELOW the 4-epoch pair), so the cycle length is fixed by measurement.

THE NAMED RISK, and it is the reason P is not higher. knee-0dfys names the binding constraint as child DIVERGENCE, not K: K=3 and K=4 have now read identical to four decimals on TWO bases, the direct measurement that the children never leave the parents point. A soup is by construction the CENTRE of its basin, so children forked off a centre may diverge even less than children forked off an ordinary fit, and the average of three points that did not move is the point itself. That is the mechanism by which this saturates rather than compounds.

PRE-REGISTERED, on ledger75 against basinsoup_dmlb_k4 at 0.9092 and the 0.0053 paired floor
  >= 0.9106  COMPOUNDS at full size. A round 3 is then licensed, and an _ff round-2 becomes a slot with
             a mechanism behind it rather than a reseating.
  0.9093-0.9105  partial. The op still pays but is decaying; read the K=3/K=4 gap and the child spread to
             say whether divergence or the op itself is the term that shrank.
  <= 0.9092  SATURATES. Souping is a ONE-SHOT operation, not an iterable one, and the family closes on
             its own stated bar. The shelf top stays 0.9092 and no further soup arm is licensed.

ZERO SLOTS. Fold 0, priced offline on ledger75, decisive in both directions without spending a submission.

PRICE: ~1.4 h card (3 children x 4 epochs x ~350 s = ~1.2 h, plus ~10 min to backfill and price the two soups). P(clears 0.9106) ~ 0.30. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.02 -- this is not a 1.5% lever on its own; it is the licence for the chain that could be one, and it is justified as that.
notes:
LICENCE, from knee-xjxdn's surviving half and not previously written here: to beat the champion by the _ff route a fold-0 ledger75 must CLEAR 0.9098 (>=0.0053, the paired floor, over labelwise_ext's 0.9045). The shelf topped out at 0.9089 when that bar was stated; basinsoup_dmlb_k4's 0.9092 is still 0.0006 short and is INSIDE the one cluster whose every _ff refit has boarded 0.943-0.945, never 0.946. So this arm's >=0.9106 branch clears the bar with room, its 0.9093-0.9105 partial branch mostly clears it, and its <=0.9092 branch leaves the project with no member that can. That is the reason round 2 is the right card tonight and not momentum off what was just built: it is the ONLY open path to a member the _ff route can ship above the cluster. FIRST DATA POINT 23:10Z: c501 = 0.9067 ledger75, -0.0025 under the 0.9092 parent. Round 1's children sat -0.0017 under theirs and the soup still landed +0.0014 over; a child below its parent is the expected shape and prices nothing. The soups are the reading.
MID-ARM, two of three children, 23:14Z. c501 0.9067, c502 0.9084 ledger75 against the 0.9092 parent. The number that matters here is not either score but their SPREAD: 0.0017 between two children. Round 1's three children read 0.9061/0.9062/0.9062 -- a spread of 0.0001. So children forked off a SOUP diverge roughly seventeen times more than children forked off an ordinary fine-tuned parent. This runs directly AGAINST the risk this arm pre-registered, which was that a soup is the centre of its basin and its children would therefore diverge even LESS, making the average of three points that did not move the point itself. That mechanism is not what is happening. Divergence is the term that makes weight averaging pay, so on the stated mechanism this is the favourable direction. It is NOT a verdict: the reading is the K=3 and K=4 soups, and two children cannot price an average of three. Recorded because it is the arm's own named risk being measured and answered mid-flight, and because if the soups land short despite this the shortfall belongs to the averaging op and not to divergence -- which is exactly the attribution the 0.9093-0.9105 partial branch asks for.
NEXT ARM PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE READING, 23:22Z, so the branch is not chosen after seeing the number. If the k3/k4 soups land >= 0.9106 (COMPOUNDS), the card goes to souping round 2 on the _ff LINE -- three 4-epoch seed-children forked off basinsoup_ff_k4_s2026, the checkpoint behind the standing 0.946 entry -- and NOT to a fold-0 round 3. Ratio is why: both cost ~1.4 h, but a fold-0 product cannot be shipped (every solo this project has boarded is --fold -1) so round 3 buys evidence only, while the _ff round 2 yields ONE full-data solo checkpoint that tomorrow's slots can spend, produced by the same operation that boarded 0.946. P(it beats 0.946) ~ 0.25. If the soups land <= 0.9092 (SATURATES) the _ff round 2 is NOT licensed and must not be launched on momentum: this arm's own bar closes the family, and the _ff line would be a second blind round of an operation just measured one-shot. The 0.9093-0.9105 partial branch calls for reading the K=3/K=4 gap and the child spread first, and the child spread is already in hand at 0.0017 against round 1's 0.0001 -- so on that branch the shortfall belongs to the averaging op rather than to divergence, and the _ff round 2 is likewise unlicensed.
VERDICT 23:36Z: SATURATES. r2 soups k4 0.9091 / k3 0.9088 vs parent basinsoup_dmlb_k4 0.9092 - both BELOW. Children c501 0.9067 / c502 0.9084 / c503 0.9050 (spread 0.0034, 34x round 1's 0.0001). Soup beat its children mean (0.9067) by +0.0024, same premium as round 1, but did NOT exceed the round-1 parent. So the soup RECOVERS its basin's ceiling and never raises it; divergence rose 34x and bought nothing, which refutes the arm's own premise that divergence is the limiting term. Basin ceiling ~0.909, 0.0006 under the 0.9098 that licenses a champion attempt. The _ff round-2 arm is NOT licensed and was not launched. Souping family CLOSED.

title: Basin-soup the highest honest fold-0 fit: the only route to the stated 0.9098 bar
description:
knee-xjxdn's surviving finding states the bar in one number: a solo _ff refit beats the pinned 0.946 champion only from a fold-0 ledger75 of >= 0.9098 (labelwise_ext's 0.9045 plus the 0.0053 paired floor). The whole shelf tops out at basinsoup_k3's 0.9089, and every _ff refit of the top cluster has boarded 0.943-0.945 with none reaching 0.946. So the route is not another recipe -- it is to put the best base the project owns ABOVE that bar on the ruler that can resolve it.

dml_b_s2026 reads 0.9078 ledger75, peak epoch 18 of 24, convergence clean -- the HIGHEST honest single fit on the shelf -- and it has never been basin-souped. Basin souping is the only weight-space operation this project has measured positive (+0.0016 ledger75, 0.9073 -> 0.9089), and basinsoup2 fixed 4 epochs at backbone-lr 2e-5 as its measured optimum rather than a knob with a sweep in it. The arithmetic is the whole argument: 0.9078 + 0.0016 = 0.9094 against a 0.9098 bar. That is SHORT by 0.0004 in expectation, and the +0.0016 carries its own spread, which is exactly why this is worth a free card -- it is the only construction on the shelf whose expected value lands within scatter of the bar instead of 0.002 below it.

This is an INSTRUMENT and it is decisive in both directions. It costs ZERO slots: fold 0, so it is priced offline on ledger75 and never on the board. Clearing 0.9098 licenses an _ff refit aimed at 0.946+ with a mechanism behind it. Missing it CLOSES the top-the-shelf route by the record's own stated bar, which is worth more than another entry inside the cluster.

PRICE: ~1.4 h card (3 children x 4 epochs x ~330 s, plus backfill and pricing of the two soups). P(clears 0.9098) ~ 0.30.
notes:
Armed 2026-09-20T21:36Z. experiments/arms/basinsoup_dmlb.sh, three children seeds 401/402/403 off dml_b_s2026.pt at --epochs 4 --backbone-lr 2e-5 --init-scope all, then weight_soup K=3 and K=4, then holdout_backfill + ledger75. arm_check EXIT 0 (0 refused; three OVERSTATED lines are knee-ylp0's advisory VRAM note, the arms reserve ~11.3 GB against a 22 declared). reading_check --only EXIT 0, no declared reading on disk. card_check EXIT 0, card held nothing of ours.

THE OPERATION REPRODUCES -- now on two fold-0 bases and on the _ff board line (basinsoupff_v1 0.946, ref 56406877), same sign and order every time, and it reproduces off a NON-EMA parent, which was the named risk. 0.9092 is the highest fold-0 number this project owns.
