title: Basin soup on the _ff line: the one weight-space op measured POSITIVE, applied to the shipping solo
description:
basinsoup is the only weight-space operation this project has ever measured positive: +0.0016 ledger75 (parent 0.9073 -> basinsoup_k3 0.9089), and basinsoup2 (2026-09-20 19:44Z) established WHY it pays and why it cannot be pushed -- every child of a converged EMA parent lands below it, so the average only ever interpolates toward worse points, and the +0.0016 is the reading of the LEAST travelled children available. Doubling the cycle bought real divergence (K3 0.9075 vs K4 0.9080, separated where basinsoup had them equal to 4dp) and the product fell. So the op is a narrow, near-no-op average, and the 4-epoch/2e-5 recipe is its measured optimum, not a knob to sweep.

STAGE 2, RE-PRICED. Souping the _ff line was shelved as stage 2 of knee-ted6u on a differential rule (board_gain = 0.826 * fold0_gain, pricing it 0.949); knee-xjxdn killed that rule and its retraction left no replacement price. The direct one: the parent labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff IS extffsolo_v1, board 0.945, and the ledger75 solo transfer is ~1:1 (slope +1.09/+1.10, resid sd 0.0017-0.0022). +0.0016 on 0.945 lands 0.9466, which reads 0.946 or 0.947 at the board's own 0.001 resolution. Beating the pinned 0.946 champion needs the upper tick.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE OTHER OPEN LEVERS. knee-9grwy (_ff refit of a tied member) is re-priced at P~0.06 after the +0.008 refit term turned out to be an EMA misattribution. knee-xjxdn establishes the top-4 recipes are ONE CLUSTER inside the 0.0053 paired floor whose _ff refits all board 0.943-0.945, so no NEW cluster member reaches 0.946. This arm is not a new cluster member: it is a measured +delta applied ON TOP of the 0.945 entry we already hold.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO. fold -1 means there is no holdout, so there is no offline read and no ledger75 row -- the read is the BOARD and nothing else. That is also why weight_soup refuses FULL_DATA_FOLD: a full-data member in the pot leaks the holdout into any number the soup is then read on. An ALL-full-data soup has no such number by construction, so the guard is released only for the all -1 case and only behind an explicit ship-only flag; a MIX stays refused, which is the case the guard was actually written for.

PRICE: ~1.4 h card, 1 slot of 4. P(clears 0.946, i.e. strictly beats the champion) ~ 0.30.

REFUTATION CLAUSE, pre-registered on the BOARD, since no offline ruler exists here:
  >= 0.947  the op transfers, we hold a new champion and the best solo the project owns.
  0.946     tie at board resolution. The op does not lose but cannot be shown to pay; keep the standing entry.
  <= 0.945  weight-space souping does not transfer to the full-data fit, and the family closes on its FOURTH and last explanation.
notes:
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-20T20:28Z, BEFORE the soups exist: if this arm earns a slot, the shipped product is K=4, not K=3.

WHY, DECIDED WITHOUT A RULER. Both products are full-data (--fold -1), so neither has an offline number and neither ever will; the choice cannot be made by measurement and must therefore be made by mechanism, in advance, or it becomes a choice made by looking.

K=4 contains the PARENT, which IS extffsolo_v1, board 0.945. It is therefore a 1/4-weight perturbation of a known-good point with bounded downside. K=3 is an average of three children only, and basinsoup2 established the mechanism that every child of a converged EMA parent lands BELOW it -- so K=3 averages three points all worse than the entry we already hold, and can only win on basin curvature.

The fold-0 evidence does not separate them: basinsoup read K3 ~= K4 to four decimals, and basinsoup2 (with real divergence bought) read K3 0.9075 against K4 0.9080 -- K=4 ahead, inside noise. Nothing anywhere favours K=3 except that the original +0.0016 happened to be measured on it.

So: one slot, ship K=4. K=3 is not shipped on this line unless K=4 scores >= 0.947 and a second slot is justified by that result.

CARD PRICE CORRECTED. The 5.8h re-price logged earlier today was WRONG -- it read a mid-epoch step counter as a whole-epoch rate. Measured epoch times for c301: 444s / 351s / 336s, ~25 min per child. c301 finished 20:23Z; three children plus both soups land ~21:15Z. The original ~1.2h header price was right.

title: foreign_readout slot_cost breaks 18x on the reference cache, after eleven clean rows
description:
GATE 1 FAILED. experiments/after_fieldwide.sh's header: 'READ slot_cost FIRST, ON EVERY ROW. It serves our own pixels through the SHIFTED code path and must land inside +/-0.0001. Anything else means the shifted path is broken and decode_cost is not about pixels at all -- the one failure that is otherwise invisible, since a broken slab still prints a plausible number.'

Run cluster_decode 2026-09-20, seven fold-0 members, log D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/experiments/cluster_decode.full.log:
  labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 (20 slices): native 0.8672 kept 0.8654 | slots -0.0018
  basinsoup_k3_s2026 (20 slices):              native 0.8712 kept 0.8696 | slots -0.0017
  labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 (24):    native 0.8679 kept 0.8680 | slots +0.0000

-0.0018 is 18x the tolerance. This is not a tolerance quibble: experiments/README.md records ELEVEN prior rows across four independent passes (lines 11798, 16044, 16187, 16238, 16314) and every one lands inside +/-0.0001 (+0.0001, -0.0000, +0.0000, -0.0001, +0.0001). Line 11798 states it as a property: 'Every slot_cost lands inside +/-0.0001, so the shifted path serves our own pixels back at our own score'.

WHAT IS DIFFERENT ABOUT THIS RUN. Every prior pass handed foreign_readout an all-20-slice checkpoint list, so MemberReadings held ONE cache. This list is mixed (20/24/24/20/20/12/20), so member_readings.py:64-73 loads several. The reference cache is keys[0] - the 20-slice one - and member_readings.py:65 gives it  directly, skipping the reload AND the order check every other cache gets at :68. BOTH failing rows are on that reference cache; the one clean row is the 24-slice member that loads its own.

NOT YET RULED OUT, and the run's remaining four rows are the free discriminator (two more 20s, one 24, one 12): if every 20 reads ~-0.0017 and the 12 and 24 read ~0, it is the reference-cache path. If the 12 also fails, it is depth-dependent and the reference story is wrong.

ALSO UNRULED-OUT: native comes from PredictionCache(..., refresh=False) at foreign_readout.py:294 while kept is computed on the card, so a stale entry in holdout_predictions would produce exactly this signature without the shifted path being broken at all. The 24-slice member logged 'read from the run's own holdout record, not the card' - a different native path - and it is the one that passes. Check the cache key before blaming the slab.

CONSEQUENCE NOW: no decode_cost from this run may be read, which is the question it was launched to answer (whether a second independent ruler can order the four-recipe cluster the offline ruler cannot resolve, knee-xjxdn). The reading is UNTAKEN, not negative.

PRICE: ~0.5 h to characterise once the four rows land, card-free. P(the pattern resolves to one of the two named suspects) ~ 0.8.
notes:
REPAIR: the sentence about member_readings.py:65 lost its clause to a backtick the shell executed. It reads: the reference cache is keys[0] - the 20-slice one - and member_readings.py:65 assigns held = corpus directly, skipping the reload AND the order check that every other cache gets at :68.
ALL SEVEN ROWS IN; THE SPLIT IS POSITIONAL, NOT A MEMBER PROPERTY. Fail: labelwise_ext_drop40_long -0.0018, basinsoup_k3 -0.0017 (rows 1-2). Pass at exactly +/-0.0000: labelwise_depth24_drop40_long, dml_b, labelwise_drop_drop40_long, band_dense_hold, calib_span (rows 3-7). Three candidate properties are ELIMINATED by the full table. DEPTH does not separate it: the cached window widths read 20 for both failing members AND for labelwise_drop_drop40_long and band_dense_hold, which pass; dml_b passes at 24 and calib_span at 12. SOUP-NESS does not separate it: basinsoup_k3 fails but band_dense_hold passes. CACHE FAMILY does not separate it: labelwise_ext is the only _extended reader and basinsoup_k3 is not one. A STALE PREDICTION CACHE is not it either: every one of the seven has at least one entry under processed/rsna_knee_abnormality/holdout_predictions, so a cache hit cannot be what only two of them got. What is left is ORDER. An exact +/-0.0000 means native and kept are the same computation; a nonzero means native was computed against a differently ordered corpus. member_readings.py slabs() sets held = corpus for keys[0] alone, skipping both the reload and the order check every other decode_key gets, so the members sitting on the FIRST decode key are served an unreloaded corpus whose study order need not match the cache the truth vector is aligned to. A mild misalignment is exactly the -0.0017 to -0.0018 shape, and its near-equality across two unrelated members is the signature of a shared plumbing fault rather than two coincident model effects. Suspect 1 confirmed, suspect 2 (foreign_readout.py refresh=False) eliminated. REPAIR: slabs() applies the same reload and order assertion to keys[0] as to every other key. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS RUN: the five passing rows decode_cost ARE readable -- depth24 -0.0223, dml_b -0.0223, labelwise_drop_drop40_long -0.0243, band_dense_hold -0.0360, calib_span -0.0280 -- and the two failing rows are not.
CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS NOTE (2026-09-20T19:23Z): IT SAID SUSPECT 1 CONFIRMED AND SUSPECT 2 ELIMINATED. BOTH HALVES ARE WRONG, AND THE DEFECT IS NOW UNEXPLAINED WITH BOTH SUSPECTS DEAD. What the previous note got right is the elimination of depth, soup-ness and cache family; what it got wrong is everything after.

SUSPECT 1 (member_readings.py slabs, keys[0] served an unchecked corpus) CANNOT PRODUCE THIS AND NEVER COULD. foreign_readout.py:280-282 takes identifiers straight out of readings.reference(), which IS keys[0] own order, and then passes it back in as the thing every other key is checked against. keys[0] agreeing with itself is a tautology, so there is no order mismatch available on that path at all. The note asserted a mechanism from the SHAPE of the code (one branch skips a check) without asking where the check compares TO. That is the error, and it is mine, not the code.

SUSPECT 2 (the refresh=False prediction cache) IS ELIMINATED PROPERLY THIS TIME, AND THE FIRST ELIMINATION WAS ALSO BAD REASONING. It was dismissed on every member having at least one cache entry, which is not the question: the key carries the studies hash, the window and the checkpoint mtime_ns and bytes, so having entries is not having a HIT. Tested directly instead. All seven have a sidecar at exactly their own window, starts [0], the same studies hash c8dc97625d3e and count 909, so a hit is available to each. Comparing the recorded mtime_ns and bytes against the checkpoints on disk: labelwise_ext HIT, basinsoup_k3 MISS, labelwise_depth24 MISS, dml_b HIT, labelwise_drop_drop40_long HIT, band_dense_hold HIT, calib_span HIT. The two FAILING rows are one HIT and one MISS, and the five PASSING rows are four HITs and one MISS. Hit-versus-miss does not separate the table on either side, so a stale cached native is not the cause.

WHAT SURVIVES. Only the positional pattern: rows 1 and 2 fail at -0.0018 and -0.0017, rows 3 through 7 pass at exactly +/-0.0000. An exact zero still means native and kept were the same computation and a nonzero still means they were not, so the fault is real. No mechanism is in hand. DO NOT re-walk depth, soup-ness, cache family or the prediction cache; all four are measured dead. The next cheap probe is to print the decode-key grouping and the per-key iteration order that slabs() actually yields, which is the one thing correlating with the split that has not been read off disk.

THE FIVE PASSING ROWS decode_cost READINGS STAND UNCHANGED -- they are gated by their own slot_cost at zero and do not depend on any of this.
CONCRETE LEAD, NOT YET A MECHANISM (2026-09-20T19:24Z). The run header reads: served 909 studies from D:\data\external\raptor\corpus at 44 SLICES, 336 px. The reference corpus is 44 slices deep, and slabs() serves held = that corpus to every member on keys[0] while every other key is loaded fresh at ITS OWN depth. foreign_readout.py:301 then computes window = member.window(held.slices, ...), so a member sitting on keys[0] has its window derived from 44 while a member on any other key has it derived from its own cache depth. native is read through that window and kept is read through the pair, which is the one place the two sides can diverge without either being wrong on its own terms. That is the asymmetry the bead title already named, arrived at properly this time rather than assumed. IT IS STILL NOT CONFIRMED: it predicts that exactly the members grouped onto keys[0] fail, and the grouping has not been printed. THE ONE REMAINING PROBE is to print member.cache(processed).key for the seven checkpoints in the arm order and check that labelwise_ext_drop40_long and basinsoup_k3 are the two on keys[0]. If they are, the repair is to derive the window from the members own cache depth rather than from whichever corpus happened to be loaded first. If they are not, this lead dies with the other two and the defect stays open.
THE GROUPING PROBE LANDED AND THE PREDICTION HELD EXACTLY (2026-09-20T19:24Z). MemberReadings over the seven checkpoints in arm order groups them:
  key 0  336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_extended   labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026, basinsoup_k3_s2026
  key 1  336px_24sl_0.1-0.9band            labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026, dml_b_s2026
  key 2  336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band            labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026, band_dense_hold_s2026
  key 3  336px_12sl_0.1-0.9band            calib_span_s2026
keys[0] holds EXACTLY the two failing members and nothing else; keys 1 through 3 hold exactly the five that pass. The split is total, with no member on the wrong side.

THIS ALSO CORRECTS A SECOND THING THE FIRST NOTE GOT WRONG. It eliminated CACHE FAMILY on the ground that basinsoup_k3 is not an _extended reader. It IS one -- it is a soup of _extended children and lands on the _extended key. So the family was never eliminated, and saying it was rested on an assumption about the soup rather than on a reading.

AND THE TWO SURVIVING HYPOTHESES ARE PERFECTLY CONFOUNDED IN THIS TABLE. Being keys[0] and being _extended are the same set of two members here, so nothing in these seven rows can tell them apart. POSITIONAL would mean slabs() serves keys[0] the caller corpus while reloading every other key, and foreign_readout.py:301 then takes window = member.window(held.slices): the run header records the reference corpus as 44 SLICES deep, so a 20-slice member on keys[0] gets a window derived from 44. FAMILY would mean the _extended cache is simply read differently and position is incidental.

DISCRIMINATOR LAUNCHED, NO SLOT, CARD WAS IDLE (pid 240429, log permuted_decode.full.log). Same readout over three members with the order PERMUTED so a plain 20-slice member sits first: labelwise_drop_drop40_long, then labelwise_ext_drop40_long, then basinsoup_k3. If the fault is POSITIONAL, labelwise_drop_drop40_long now fails its slot_cost and the two _extended members pass. If it is the FAMILY, labelwise_drop_drop40_long passes and the two _extended members fail exactly as before. The two outcomes are disjoint and one run reads it.

VERDICT, 2026-09-20T19:39Z: THE FAULT IS THE _extended CACHE FAMILY, NOT THE FIRST-KEY POSITION.
The permuted-order foreign_readout ran with a plain 20-slice member first, inverting the confound:

  labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026  (now keys[0])  native 0.8703 kept 0.8703  slots -0.0000  PASS
  labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026   (now second)   native 0.8672 kept 0.8654  slots -0.0018  FAIL

Against the branches written before the run: POSITIONAL predicted labelwise_drop fails and the
_extended members pass; FAMILY predicted the exact reverse. The reverse is what happened. Position
moved, the verdict did not, so being keys[0] causes nothing and membership of the
336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_extended cache family causes all of it. -0.0018 is 18x the +/-0.0001 gate, not
scatter, and labelwise_drop reading an exact -0.0000 in the seat that had been blamed is the positive
control the first pass never had.

MY EARLIER CLAIM ON THIS BEAD WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. I wrote
"suspect 1 confirmed" from the SHAPE of MemberReadings.slabs() -- one branch skips an order check --
without reading what that check compares against; foreign_readout.py:280-282 derives `identifiers`
from readings.reference(), which IS keys[0]'s own order, so that path is a tautology and can raise
nothing. The run has now refuted the mechanism I had already recorded as confirmed.

STILL OPEN: WHY the _extended family diverges. native uses PredictionCache while kept (SlotsKept) is
always fresh, so an _extended member's two sides are not running the same computation -- but four of
the five passing rows are cache HITS too, so hit/miss does not separate the table and the divergence
has to be in what the _extended corpus itself serves. The five gated decode_cost rows already
recorded on knee-fbo5e stand: none of them is an _extended row.

title: The champion decodes at full depth: Serving.group is unset on kneemri-tripleseat
description:
TWO LADDERS. efficiency_read --live 2026-09-20 19:59Z: accuracy rank 73 at 0.946 (4054 rows), efficiency rank 17 at 0.945 (3976 rows). Six teams rank above us on efficiency while scoring BELOW us - runtime alone. 52 teams within 0.002 of 0.945 hold efficiency ranks 4 to 3457, median 584: that span is runtime, not accuracy.

THE LEVER IS BUILT AND UNUSED. comp/kernels/kneemri-tripleseat/kneemri-tripleseat.py:175 reads Serving(vote=LogitAverage(), budget=left) - no group, so all seven members pay a full-depth decode. Serving.group: SharedRead exists (kneemri/inference/ensemble.py:130-202), goes through SlotReader.band_indices (slot_reader.py:416-422), preserves the [0.1,0.9] band and drops only sampling density. Eight other kernels already set it; the champion's is not among them.

PRICE: ~0.7 h of agent time, zero card to build, one slot to score - and that slot scores BOTH boards.
P(clears 1 efficiency decile) ~ 0.55. P(costs an accuracy tick) ~ 0.35.

THE RUNG IS 16, NOT 12. The measured ladder (20 native 0.8672 | 18 +0.0001 | 16 -0.0008 | 14 -0.0025 | 12 -0.0056 | 10 -0.0098) was taken with member_curve --slices, which windows an already-decoded slab and NARROWS the band to ~[0.18,0.82] at 16 - so every rung is an UPPER BOUND on what SharedRead costs. 12 slices is not free: the Serving.group docstring prices it -0.0022 and calls that 'under the 0.0045 board resolution', which is stale prose - the board reports at 0.001, so -0.0022 offline is ~-0.0024 board, 2.4x blur.

NOT A CHAMPION REPLACEMENT. The pin stays at tripleseat_v2 0.946; this ships as its own row so a tick lost costs nothing standing.
notes:
THE LEVER IS ALREADY BOARD-PRICED, AND THE PRICING CONFOUNDS TWO THINGS. onegroup_v1 (ref 56052777, 2026-09-06, comp/board.jsonl) served the champion six as ONE read group at 12 slices / band 0.1-0.9 and read 0.942 against rootmove_v1's 0.944 - members and LogitAverage identical, so the whole delta is the read change. Its offline twin predicted -0.0022 and the board paid -0.002: a 1:1 transfer, and the only validated proxy this project owns. Runtime 7.6h -> 2.15h.

But that entry moved BOTH halves at once. The GROUP COLLAPSE (3 decodes -> 1) is where the runtime lives; the DEPTH CHANGE (20/24 -> 12) is where the -0.002 lives. They are separable and nothing has separated them.

THE CHAMPION'S READ BILL, measured off the seven checkpoints' own option records: three distinct readings, all band 0.1-0.9 at 336 px - slices 20 (final_ws_cf, stack_increments_ff, through_dense_cf, labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026, labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026), 12 (calib_span_ff), 24 (labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026). 20+12+24 = 56 slice-reads a study.

SharedRead(20, (0.1,0.9)) drops that to 20 - 2.8x fewer DICOM reads - and leaves FIVE OF SEVEN members byte-identical, because 20 is already their fitted depth. Only calib_span_ff (12 -> 20, served deeper than fitted) and labelwise_depth24 (24 -> 20, one rung down) change function at all. onegroup moved five seats down eight slices and one down twelve for its 0.002; this moves two seats by one rung each.

REVISED PRICE: ~20 min card for the offline twin (SharedRead(20) against native on the fold-0 twins) plus one slot. P(costs <= 1 board tick) ~ 0.75, against onegroup's measured 2. The 16-slice rung in the description above is superseded: 20 is the rung that buys the collapse for free, and 16 would re-introduce the depth change this finding exists to avoid.

Pin stays at tripleseat_v2 0.946; this ships as its own row.
THE DEPTH LADDER WAS RE-MEASURED ON THE SHIPPED SEMANTICS TODAY, AND IT REMOVES THE CARD READ THIS BEAD ASKED FOR. experiments/README.md:17395 - holdout_backfill --served-slices on band_dense_s2026 (DINOv2-S, 336 px, native 20, band 0.10-0.90 held, same 909 studies, same epoch): served 24 reads 0.8888 ledger75 (+0.0011), served 20 is native 0.8877, served 12 reads 0.8859 (-0.0018). Depth is FLAT from 12 to 24 - the whole ladder spans 0.0029 ledger75, inside the 0.0053 paired floor, and the 12-slice cost sits below the 0.0022 top-band residual sd.

That is the shipped intervention measured directly, so SharedRead(20) on the champion seating needs no new offline twin: five of seven members are byte-identical at 20 and the two that move (calib_span_ff 12 -> 20, labelwise_depth24 24 -> 20) each move ONE rung on a ladder whose full 12-24 range is under the noise floor. Projected cost ~0 against onegroup_v1 measured 2 board ticks at 12 across all six seats.

24 IS RULED OUT, and not on cost. labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 - a champion seat - reads the _extended cache family, which exists on disk only at 20 slices, so no offline check of a 24-slice regroup of this seating is possible. 20 is the only depth at which the whole seating can be verified offline AND the only one where most seats do not move at all.

THE PICK: SharedRead(20, (0.1, 0.9)) on the tripleseat seating, shipped as its own board row. Decode 56 -> 20 slice-reads a study, 2.8x. Pin stays at tripleseat_v2 0.946.
RE-EXAMINED 2026-09-20 20:00Z, and the verdict FLIPS FROM CANDIDATE TO INSTRUMENT rather than reopening.

kneemri-leanseat is this bead built: tripleseat's seating with Serving(group=SharedRead(20, (0.1,0.9))), committed 7a091e9c, kit uploaded, mount_check and champion_check clean. It was killed before a slot at 19:2xZ on two grounds. The notes above REFUTE THE FIRST: onegroup_v1's -0.002 was charged to the read collapse, but onegroup moved depth AND grouping together, and the depth ladder re-measured on shipped semantics (README:17395) is FLAT from 12 to 24 -- 0.0029 total, inside the 0.0053 paired floor. So the expected accuracy cost of SharedRead(20) here is ~0, not -0.002, and P(ties 0.946) is ~0.75 rather than low.

THE SECOND GROUND STILL STANDS AND STILL KILLS IT AS A CANDIDATE. A tie at 0.946 does not beat the champion, and on the efficiency ladder extffsolo_v1 dominates it BY CONSTRUCTION: one member behind one decode read (peak 0.8 GB) against seven behind the same one read. Nothing about collapsing the reads can make seven trunks cheaper than one. So this cannot improve either board.

WHAT IT CAN DO IS THE THING THIS BEAD SAYS NOBODY HAS DONE: 'the GROUP COLLAPSE (3 decodes -> 1) is where the runtime lives; the DEPTH CHANGE (20/24 -> 12) is where the -0.002 lives. They are separable and nothing has separated them.' leanseat holds depth at 20 -- five of seven seats byte-identical, two moving one rung on a flat ladder -- and collapses 56 slice-reads a study to 20. Its board row is therefore the group-collapse cost ALONE, read against tripleseat_v2's 0.946 at identical members and identical LogitAverage. That retires a suspicion standing since 2026-09-06 and prices every future regroup, which is instrument value, not candidate value.

SCHEDULED for the 20:51Z mark as a DECLARED INSTRUMENT, with the instrument-or-candidate status stated in the submission message per the pacing rule. submit_check will refuse it on SET equality against tripleseat_v2 and needs --anyway carrying that why, which is the designed path for a deliberate re-ship.
DEEPSOLO'S BOARD ROW RE-PRICES THIS BEAD, 2026-09-20T21:45Z. deepsolo_v1 (ref 56405965) served extffsolo_v1's member at 32 against its fitted 20, band held, one constant moved, run_check clean: 0.941 against 0.945, MINUS FOUR TICKS. Two consequences here. FIRST, the flat-ladder argument this bead leans on is contradicted by the board. The re-measured served-slices ladder (README:17395, 0.0029 total across 12-24, inside the paired floor) projected +0.0024 at 32 and the board paid -0.004 -- so 'holdout_backfill --served-slices is flat, therefore SharedRead(20) costs ~0' rests on a ruler that has now called the SIGN wrong once at full size. That does not make leanseat's projection wrong, but it removes the evidence the projection was resting on. SECOND, and specific: leanseat moves calib_span_ff from its fitted 12 to 20, EIGHT SLICES DEEPER THAN FITTED. That is the same direction and two-thirds the magnitude of the move that just cost four ticks, and it is one of seven seats. The other mover (labelwise_depth24, 24 -> 20) goes shallower and is not implicated. So leanseat's instrument value is now CONFOUNDED in the branch that matters: a negative row can no longer be charged to the group collapse alone, because one seat is also being served past its fitted depth on an axis the board has just measured negative. To keep the group-collapse reading clean the regroup would have to be SharedRead at a depth no seat is served deeper than it was fitted at -- i.e. 12, which re-introduces the depth change, or a seating without calib_span_ff. Not scheduled tonight.

title: weight_soup carries its first member's WITNESS, so every soup is refused by witness_check
description: witness_check refused basinsoup_k3_s2026 (max|diff| 0.15 of 0.0312) and basinsoup_k4_s2026 (0.0969), both in the 0.05-0.5 band the check documents as every real reading defect. It is not a reading defect. WeightSoup.write shallow-copies payload[0] and drops only DROPPED = (fingerprint, fingerprint_config); the witness lives nested at config[witness] and is copied forward. Measured: the soup's witness predictions are byte-identical to basinsoup_c101's (max|diff| 0.0) and 0.2497 / 0.2776 from c102 / c103. So the check re-derives the AVERAGE's predictions and compares them against the FIRST CHILD's claim, and the distance it reports is the soup being a different network, which is what souping is for. The module's own docstring already makes this argument for the fingerprint - a witness of a specific set of tensors, copying it forward would let witness_check pass a checkpoint whose weights it never saw - and then forgets the field actually named witness. Fix: clear config[witness] in write, so a soup reports UNVERIFIED rather than REFUSED. UNVERIFIED is the honest state: a witness is recorded by TRAINING and a soup never trained, and one minted through the inference path would be self-consistent by construction and prove nothing. Ledger scores are unaffected - holdout_backfill ran the real averaged weights. No board entry seats a soup, so nothing shipped is affected. Existing soup checkpoints on disk carry the stale field and must be rebuilt after the fix. PRICE: ~0.4 h. P(clears gate) ~ 0.9 - it unblocks a stated pre-flight for the whole soup family, it is not itself a score lever.
notes:
FIXED and verified 2026-09-20T18:49Z. WITNESS constant added to weight_soup; write() now rebuilds config without it. Both soups rebuilt from the same children, re-backfilled on cuda, re-packaged into members_3. ledger75 reproduces basinsoup_k3_s2026 at 0.9089 EXACTLY (0.8712 midpoint), which is the proof the weights were never the problem; basinsoup_k4_s2026 also 0.9089, matching the roster note that k4 reads identical to k3. witness_check --root members_3 now reads 0 ok, 2 unverified, 0 refused.

ONE THING LEFT, SMALL AND DELIBERATE. The UNVERIFIED message names a wrong cause: it reads 'no witness (a published member, or fitted before 2026-08-24)' and a soup is a THIRD cause, younger than that date and not published. The check's own docstring legislates against exactly this - a wrong cause that reads as a known one is worse than no message, because it retires the question. The payload already carries a soup key naming its parts, so the member can say so without a new field. Not done now because it needs a Member surface for that key and the slot path was the deadline.

title: Transduction needs a --pseudo-fold flag: fold -1 is unpriceable and fold 0 excludes the target
description:
THE LAST OPEN AXIS, and it cannot be run without one code change. knee-tta1 measured naive self-training with a LINEAR head under ZERO shift: 40 cells, no cell clears +0.0005, and the shape (delta shrinks toward zero as the tail GROWS) is circularity measured — pseudo-labels read off a ridge lie along that ridge's own decision direction. transduction.py records this as NOT a closure and names two suspects: (1) the head is linear, (2) shift is zero by construction.

Suspect (1) IS simulatable — fine-tune a MEMBER rather than a ridge and see whether a nonlinear head escapes the circularity. Suspect (2) is not: our holdout is drawn from the same corpus, so the level will read ~0 whatever happens, and only the real test set has shift.

WHY IT CANNOT BE RUN TODAY, checked 2026-09-20T18:27Z before spending any card:
  --fold -1  : holdout_backfill.py:109 raises UnbackfillableError on fold == -1. The arm would be a
               DARK ARM, unpriceable by construction — the rampsix failure (4.2 h, knee-s8kim).
  --fold 0   : folds.holdout() selects assignments == fold, so the 909 are excluded from training.
               They are precisely the studies that must be trained on, with pseudo-labels.
No combination of existing flags expresses 'train on the holdout fold under invented labels, score it
under true ones'. --eval-labels supplies half of it (train on one table, score against another, and its
own docstring names this use) but not the split half.

THE DESIGN. A --pseudo-fold leaf that puts the holdout fold into TRAINING while leaving the holdout
derivation intact for scoring. folds.holdout() already carries the precedent: its  argument
drops a SECOND fold from training without putting it in the holdout, added for the out-of-fold teacher
case that '--fold alone cannot express'. This is the mirror of that argument and belongs beside it.
Scoring stays honest because the 909 are trained under INVENTED labels and scored under TRUE ones —
that is the definition of transduction, not a leak.

PRICE: ~2 h of work (split path + ConfigLeaf + test mirror + gates) + ~1 h card. EXPECTED DELTA ~0, by
construction — shift is zero in any simulation we can build. P(clears 1.5%) ~0.10. So it is an
INSTRUMENT, justified only as one: it retires suspect (1) and either closes the last open axis in this
repo or licenses a slot on the member-head version under the real test set's shift. It touches the
training split path every arm depends on, so it is NOT work to start in the last hours of a window
with a standing entry to protect.
notes:
REPAIR: the description above lost one word to bash backtick expansion at creation (the shell ran it as a command). The sentence should read: folds.holdout() already carries the precedent — its "excluded" argument drops a SECOND fold from training without putting it in the holdout, added for the out-of-fold teacher case that --fold alone cannot express. This is the mirror of that argument and belongs beside it.
ARMED 2026-09-21T09:12Z. The flag landed (folds.py:100, config_tree.py:80) and the label half is kneemri/training/pseudo_table.py -- base table + teacher .holdout.npz -> a table whose fold-0 rows carry the teacher's predictions at a declared --confidence, verdict PSEUDO. Built on dml_b_s2026: 909 of 909 teacher studies written, mean |pseudo - true| 0.1771.

RE-PRICED DOWN, and this is the part worth keeping. The arm is ~50 min of card, not ~1 h plus a fresh control, because THE CONTROL IS ALREADY ON DISK: the six basinsoup_dmlb_c40* children are this recipe with --pseudo-fold absent and nothing else changed (same parent, --init-scope all, 4 epochs, 2e-5, ema, batch 4 x 3). They read 0.9061/0.9062/0.9062/0.9064/0.9065/0.9065 ledger75 -- mean 0.9063, sd 0.00017. So a 4-epoch continuation off this parent COSTS -0.0015 against its 0.9078, and pricing a pseudo child against 0.9078 would have charged transduction that cost. The comparison is 0.9063, and +/-0.0010 is a ~6 sd band, which is why two seeds resolve it.

PRE-REGISTERED: >= +0.0010 a nonlinear head escapes the circularity, suspect (1) retired and the real-test version becomes a slot with a mechanism. -0.0010 to +0.0010 knee-tta1's null reproduces with a nonlinear head, suspect (1) retired the other way and the axis closes on its own instrument. <= -0.0010 same closure, harder.
KILLED 2026-09-21T09:16Z, 3 minutes in, at step 13 of 1101 of the first child. My error, not the arm's. card_check at 09:12Z read 19577 MiB of 32607 used by peers and reported 'OK: at most one of our jobs holds this card' -- which answers CONTENTION, not ROOM, and I launched a 22 GB cap into ~12.7 GB free as though it had answered both. Three peer jobs (two shipd, one NativeSpectrum) then grew into the remainder and the card went to 31639 MiB at 99% util with five compute processes. Owner called it: thrashing.

No checkpoint was written and none is on disk, so reading_check --only transduce_dmlb still refuses nothing and the arm is re-armable unchanged.

THE RULE THIS COSTS: card_check's OK is a statement about OUR job count and nothing else. Before launching, read FREE VRAM (nvidia-smi memory.used against memory.total) and require it to exceed the arm's actual reserve with headroom for peer growth -- peers on this card grow, they do not hold still. At 09:16Z the peers hold 28037 of 32607 MiB, 4.5 GB free, so this arm is not runnable now at any cap.
ARMED BEHIND A ROOM GATE, 2026-09-21T09:26Z. experiments/after_room.sh <free-mib> <arm> holds an arm until nvidia-smi reports the free figure for 3 consecutive minutes, then re-runs card_check, then launches. Armed at 17000 MiB: the arm's measured reserve is ~11.4 GB and the remaining 5.6 GB is headroom for PEER GROWTH, which is the term the killed launch omitted. card_check answers CONTENTION (how many of ours hold the card) and never ROOM; reading its OK as room is what put a 22 GB cap into 12.7 GB free and took the card to 31.6 GB at 99% util with five processes.

THE WATCHER ITSELF WAS INVISIBLE TO queue_check TWICE, and both holes are now closed in the script. (1) Named when_room.sh it matched neither the after_*.log glob nor the after*.sh argv probe, so a live watcher owing an arm read as 'OK: nothing is queued'. (2) Renamed and printing its header in prose, the marker '17000 MiB free x3' appeared in no argv, so the check matched log and process to each other not at all and printed STRANDED on a live queue -- which invites the relaunch that DOUBLE-QUEUES the arm. The marker is now the bare argv token. Both false readings were reproduced and then verified fixed; the duplicate watcher that the second reading actually created was killed by CommandLine through CIM, since MSYS ps shows no argv and a grep-and-kill over it matches nothing while appearing to work.
FIRST ARM READ, 2026-09-21T10:30Z. transduce_dmlb_c408 0.9080 (+0.0017), c407 0.9066 (+0.0003), against the six-control mean 0.9063. Both treated seeds sit above ALL SIX controls -- the sign is clean -- and the mean is +0.0010, landing exactly on the pre-registered escape edge. convergence_check flags neither child; reading_check now refuses re-arming this arm, correctly.

MY PRE-REGISTRATION WAS ARITHMETIC ON THE WRONG DENOMINATOR, and this is the correction. It said: six control seeds at sd 0.00017 make +/-0.0010 a ~6 sd band, so two seeds resolve it. That assumed the TREATED arm inherits the CONTROL arm variance. It does not. The two treated seeds spread 0.0014 -- eight times the control sd -- so the band was never ~6 sd of anything the treated arm could produce, and two seeds never resolved this. The +0.0010 is currently unresolvable, not confirmed.

FOLLOW-UP ARMED 2026-09-21T10:47Z: experiments/arms/transduce_dmlb_more.sh, seeds 409-412, every other flag byte for byte, taking treated to n=6 against control n=6. SE lands near 0.0004, the first design here that can separate +0.0010 from zero. PRICE: ~1.7 h card, zero slots. P(clears 1.5%) ~0.02 on its own -- it is an INSTRUMENT, justified only because transduction is the one lever whose offline number is a LOWER BOUND BY CONSTRUCTION (measured under zero shift, while the real test has nonzero shift), so it gates whether a multi-day transductive-inference build is worth opening at all.

Held behind after_room.sh at 22000 MiB, not the 17000 the first arm used: that figure came from a REMEMBERED ~11.4 GB reserve and the run then reported peak memory 16.57 GB reserved, leaving ~0.4 GB of margin where ~5.6 GB was intended. 22000 is the measured reserve plus real headroom.
READ 2026-09-21, n=3 not n=6 (three seeds lost when the arm was killed at 11:47Z; 410 died at step 23, 411/412 never ran).

treated  transduce_dmlb_c407/408/409 = 0.9066 / 0.9080 / 0.9067, mean 0.90710, sd 0.00078, se 0.00045
control  basinsoup_dmlb_c401-406      mean 0.90632, sd 0.00017, se 0.00007
delta +0.00078, se 0.00046 -> 1.7 sigma. All ledger75, fold 0, 909 studies.

VERDICT: inside the pre-registered null band (-0.0010 to +0.0010) but NOT resolved -- the CI reaches the +0.0010 edge at 0.5 sigma. n=3 cannot close this axis; that was what the lost seeds were for. Do not write it up as closed.

NOT FINISHING IT, and the reason is the point estimate: +0.00078 already sits below the arm's own action threshold, so the only outcome that would change a decision is the one the data points away from. ~1.5 h of card to move a number that is already on the wrong side of its gate is a bad ratio against a 0.011 board gap.

FREE FINDING, bigger than the arm's own question: the PARENT dml_b_s2026 reads 0.9078 -- above all NINE children, treated and control alike. Four more epochs from that parent DEGRADES it in both arms. So the treated-vs-control delta is not a gain, it is less degradation, and the axis to look at is why continuation hurts, not whether pseudo-labels help. That reframing cost nothing and survives the missing seeds.
2026-09-23 09:17Z: queue_check STRANDED after_room.sh = transduce_dmlb_more (logs/after_room_more.log ends at warm start, watcher died 2026-09-21). NOT re-armed: the three fold-0 transduce members read c407 0.9066 / c408 0.9080 / c409 0.9067 ledger75 vs parent dml_b 0.9078 — max +0.0002, inside the 0.0062 floor, so more transduction epochs price at ~0 gain for card hours. Members declined in comp/members.declines (e1cac723).

title: fold-0 ledger75 ANTI-correlates with _ff board: 3 of 3 monotone inverted
description: Three recipes have both a fold-0 ledger75 and an _ff refit shipped to the board. labelwise_ext_drop40_long 0.9045 -> extffsolo_v1 0.945; labelwise_depth24_drop40_long 0.9053 -> ffsolo_v1 0.944; dml_b 0.9078 -> dmlbff_v1 0.943. Offline rises monotonically, board falls monotonically, 3 for 3. dml_b_ff_long36 0.938 agrees on the same direction (more epochs, worse board). CONSEQUENCE: the differential rule board_gain = 0.826 * fold0_gain, used to price a souped _ff refit at 0.949 against the champion 0.946, has the WRONG SIGN on every point that tests it. Stage 2 of knee-ted6u (soup the _ff, ~2h card + 1 slot) loses its mechanism and is NOT to be run on that argument. basinsoup_k3 0.9089 is the highest fold-0 number the project owns, which on this evidence predicts the worst _ff ship of the four. BOUND: n=3, spread 0.002 = 2x board blur 0.0010 but inside the solo-line residual sd 0.0025, so this is no-positive-transfer-demonstrated plus an observed negative slope, NOT a proven negative. MECHANISM that fits all four points: fold-0 ledger75 rewards machinery that fits a held-out split harder (depth, epochs, a peer/distill term); _ff absorbs that holdout into training so the machinery has nothing left to buy while its optimisation cost remains. labelwise_ext is the plainest of the three and boards highest. Testable restatement: _ff board tracks recipe SIMPLICITY, not offline score. This was found card-free by grepping comp/board.jsonl, after the ledger75 sweep showed no member on the shelf reaches the 0.9120 bar.
notes:
RETRACTED AS AN INVERSION, 40 minutes after filing, by a fourth point this bead should have looked for before claiming three. calib_span_s2026 reads 0.8895 fold-0 ledger75 and its refit spanff_v1 boards 0.926. Full picture: 0.8895->0.926, 0.9045->0.945, 0.9053->0.944, 0.9078->0.943. Across the WIDE range the relation is strongly POSITIVE: +0.0150 offline buys +0.019 board, slope about +1.27. title: Basin soup: fork seed-children off a fine-tuned parent, the one re-open condition weight souping left
description:
PRICE: ~1.3 h card. P(clears 0.9128 ledger75) ~ 0.25.

THE ONE UNCLAIMED RE-OPEN CONDITION. Weight-space souping is closed on TWO explanations in the ledger: heterogeneity (killed by the K=2 sibling soup, within 0.0004 of the K-law) and the anneal point (killed by soup_anneal2_s2026, -0.0040 against its best parent at e17/e18 of 24). Its close names the only way back in: 'Re-open only with a mechanism that puts the members in a SHARED basin (a common fine-tune trunk, not a common init), which no arm in this ledger has ever produced.' Every member ever souped here shared only the facebook/dinov2-small ImageNet init - twenty recipes, twenty basins. That is the setting Wortsman's uniform soup is KNOWN to fail in, so the two closes are the literature reproducing, not a refutation of souping.

THE MECHANISM. Fork K children off a parent that is ALREADY corpus-fine-tuned, using --init <parent> --init-scope all (kneemri/training/adaptation.py:145, the LP-FT flag, used by eight arms). Children branched from a converged trunk share a basin by construction; seeds differ so data order and augmentation draws decorrelate them over the child epochs. Then average the PARAMETERS. Product is ONE checkpoint with ONE forward pass - the only class of change that has moved this board by more than noise, and the solo deliverable rather than an ensemble.

PARENT: labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ema_s2026, 0.9073 ledger75, ledger75 rank 2, fold 0, plain single-model recipe (dml_b at 0.9078 is 0.0005 ahead, inside the floor, but needs a peer). Children carry the parent's flag line byte for byte plus --init/--seed/--epochs, so the architecture tuple weight_soup refuses on is identical.

TWO READINGS FOR ONE CARD COST: soup(3 children) and soup(parent + 3 children) - both are weight_soup calls over checkpoints that already exist once the children land.

PRE-REGISTERED BRANCHES, on ledger75 @ holdout909:
  >= 0.9128  the basin mechanism CARRIES THE BAR (+0.0055 over the parent; 0.9128 is the offline75 a solo needs to beat the pinned 0.946). Licenses forking children off every top member - a programme, not a member.
  0.9073 .. 0.9128  positive but sub-bar. The basin fix is real and insufficient alone; directional only, no slot.
  < 0.9073  below the parent: the shared basin does NOT save weight souping. The axis closes on its THIRD explanation and is never re-opened.
  ~0.9003   the K-law reproducing (-0.0044 per doubling, K=3). Basin buys exactly nothing.

THE HONEST COUNTER, first: experiments/arms/weight_average.sh averaged ONE run across its own epochs (an EMA) and read +0.0003. That is a near-null for parameter averaging in this repo. It is not this: EMA averages consecutive, highly-correlated iterates, while seed-forked children diverge in data order and augmentation for four epochs. If that difference is not real, this arm reproduces the K-law and retires the axis.

RETIRES THE AXIS WHICHEVER WAY IT READS, which is why it is worth card at P 0.25.

TWO MORE RESULTS, same card-free sitting, both now in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-20_pool_exhaustion.md.

SELECTION IS HONEST FOR ONE CHOICE. Split-half over the 909 studies, 20 trials, choose on A and score on B: corr(macro_A, macro_B) across 389 members = 0.989; the winner's optimism (its A score minus its OWN B score) = -0.0025 +/- 0.0083; the A-winner falls +0.0041 +/- 0.0027 short of B's own best. PER-LABEL COMPLEMENTARITY IS 84% NOISE. title: Item 3 of knee-lm37v: do the AUGMENTED members drop less on foreign_readout? (pre-registered)
description:
PARENT: knee-lm37v (whose items 1-2 are done; this is the half never run).

WHY NOW. The cross-site toll is -0.0336 +/- 0.0038, flat across eleven members, and 3x the live board gap (0.011 at rank 70/4036, read 2026-09-20T10:58Z). foreign_readout is the only sighted ruler this project owns for it. It has been run on exactly FOUR members and the result is the strongest precedent we have that a TRAINING OPERATOR moves transfer:

  band_dense        (control)  decode -0.0361
  ghosting 0.040               decode -0.0304   vs control +0.0057
  slot_dropout 0.40            decode -0.0229   vs control +0.0132
  slot_dropout 0.55            decode -0.0214   vs control +0.0147

Slot dropout is CLOSED and saturated at 0.40 (knee-yotj8), so that +0.0132 is already banked in every shipped member and is not available again. The question is whether any OTHER operator is also a carrier.

THE MEMBERS. aug_long, intensity392_ws, mixup_dense, mixup224_strong, crop160_span -- FIVE, not the bead's six: tissue224_s2026 is excluded because images_224px_12sl_tissue.npy is deleted, so it cannot be re-scored offline (roster_check). All are _s2026, the same seed as the control, so cross-member drop comparisons do not carry a seed term.

CALIBRATION GATE. band_dense_s2026 must reproduce -0.0361 to the fourth decimal in the same pass, and slot_cost must read ~0.0000. Either one off means the shifted path is broken and decode_cost is not about pixels (foreign_readout's own docstring).

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS on (member decode_cost - control decode_cost), written before the card is spent:
  >= +0.0132   CARRIER, slot-dropout class -- licenses ONE combined arm (slot_dropout 0.40 + this operator)
  +0.0062..+0.0132  DIRECTIONAL -- no card alone; TWO independent members landing here license one arm
  <= +0.0062   NULL (one seed spread) -- knee-lm37v's branch fires: augmentation is NOT the carrier and no card is spent on it for transfer
  < 0.0000     HARMFUL -- the operator costs transfer; close the axis

PRICE: ~1.0-1.5 h card for five members, no training, no slot. Must wait for the card to empty (biohub resident until ~15:00-15:35Z); NEVER co-resident -- a 6 GB arm cost the neighbour 33% on 2026-09-20 (knee-67rgi).
P(any member lands CARRIER) ~ 0.20. P(this chain then clears +1.5% on the board) ~ 0.15 -- board transfers ledger75 at slope +1.09, so a +0.015 offline75 gain is ~+0.016 board, larger than the 0.011 gap.
notes:
2026-09-20 11:11Z — THE EXACT COMMAND, staged, so the card window is not spent discovering an argument.

The readout is NOT card-free despite this bead's parent being titled 'zero-card': five members x 909 studies x ~5 live slots x 24 slices x TWO shifted passes is not CPU-feasible. It waits for the card. foreign_readout does expose --device cpu, and that is the wrong tool for this size.

STAGE 1 — the calibration gate plus ONE candidate (~25 min). Do not commit the full set until this returns:

  UV_NO_SYNC=1 uv run python -m kneemri.evaluation.foreign_readout     --checkpoints D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/band_dense_s2026.pt                   D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/aug_long_s2026.pt     --labels D:/data/volumetric/mri/processed/rsna_knee_abnormality/labels/report_labels_v2.csv     --foreign D:/data/external/raptor/corpus     --per-study D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/augdrop_decode_stage1.npz --device cuda

  REFUSE TO READ ANY CANDIDATE unless band_dense returns decode -0.0361 to the fourth decimal and its
  slot_cost reads ~0.0000. Both are stated by foreign_readout's own docstring: a broken shifted path
  still produces a plausible number, and that is the one failure invisible without this gate.

STAGE 2 — the remaining four (aug_long already read), --per-study augdrop_decode.npz.
Always pass --per-study: the tool argues for it itself, because a later SUBSET reading (coverage,
vendor) is then arithmetic rather than another hour on the card.

GEOMETRY, checked 2026-09-20 before the spend rather than after it. All five candidates and the control
are DINOv2-small with slice_pooling max, so the trunk is held. Slice counts are NOT held: band_dense,
aug_long and mixup_dense are 20-slice; intensity392_ws, mixup224_strong and crop160_span are 12-slice.
What licenses mixing them is D205's positive control on this exact instrument — our own 20-slice decode
against our own 12-slice reads correlation 0.9999, so slice count is free HERE. Stated rather than
inherited in silence; if a 12-slice candidate lands anomalously it is the first thing to suspect.

CARD DISCIPLINE. biohub is resident until ~15:00-15:35Z. card_check first, and take any co-tenancy
sample AFTER two minutes, never inside them — an early sample measures warmup and inverts the sign
(+25% read at 2 min against -33% at steady state, knee-67rgi).
2026-09-20 12:38Z NULL BRANCH FIRED. Calibration gate passed exactly (band_dense decode -0.0361 to 4dp, slots +0.0000, three passes). aug_long -0.0034 HARMFUL; mixup_dense +0.0063 DIRECTIONAL by one thousandth; mixup224_strong +0.0020 NULL; crop160_span and intensity392_ws UNREADABLE (caches deleted in the 355GB purge). Set was 3 of 5. DIRECTIONAL needed two members and there is one. Not promoted on a mechanism check: stronger mixup transfers WORSE than weaker (+0.0020 vs +0.0063), where slot dropout is monotone in dose (0.40 +0.0132, 0.55 +0.0147). No second carrier. Parent knee-lm37v's branch fires: augmentation is not the carrier, no card on it for transfer. Cost was ~15 s a member, not the 1.0-1.5 h priced here. Write-up in experiments/README.md.

title: resnet50d under the modern recipe stack at 224/12sl
description:
PRICE: ~1.0 h (12 epochs, 224px, 12 slices, resnet50d 25.6M, batch 2 accumulate 4, contended share of the card with biohub resident).

P(clears 0.8527) ~ 0.55. P(clears 0.867, our best dino midpoint) ~ 0.15.

MECHANISM. resnet_224_short_s2026 read 0.8527 midpoint / 0.8842 ledger75 on the BASELINE recipe (12 epochs, backbone-lr 2e-4, max pooling, plain targets). DINOv2 at the same 224 read native224 0.8502 / base224 0.8509. So the CNN is TIED with the transformer at matched resolution, from a family with zero recipe tuning. Our modern stack (labelwise pooling, whole-stack window, calibrated targets, hold-annotations, slot-dropout 0.40, stochastic-depth) lifted DINOv2 from 0.8502 to 0.867 midpoint / 0.9073 ledger75, roughly +0.017. That stack has NEVER been applied to the CNN. cnnseat_v1's own note states the plateau arithmetic: 0.955 needs ONE member at ~0.874 offline against our best honest ~0.866.

WHAT IS HELD FIXED. 12 epochs, matching resnet_224_short exactly, so the contrast against 0.8527 isolates the stack rather than the schedule. backbone-lr stays 2e-4 (resnet's own rate), NOT the 4e-5 tuned on DINOv2 — an under-driven CNN trunk is the RAD-DINO failure and would be a recipe defect wearing a result's clothes.

SLICES. 20 -> 12 because images_224px_20sl_0.1-0.9band.npy is deleted and only the 12sl cache survives. The ledger prices the slice-count axis at -0.0001 (flat), so this is close to free and de-confounds.

CO-TENANCY. biohub holds the card by the owner's arrangement: 9.6 GB resident, SM 14-58 pct (mean ~36), memory-controller 5-29 pct (mean ~16). Owner granted ~30 pct. Derived need 5319 MiB; --vram-gb 6, zero slack, because device_budget records that over-commit on 2026-08-17 paged over PCIe and caused three nvlddmkm engine resets that took BOTH projects down. bf16 on (default is fp16; bf16 halves activations and removes loss-scaling risk on a 2e-4 whole-stack fit). torch.compile deliberately NOT used: it fuses into larger kernels, which is what breaks interleaving with a bursty neighbour. channels_last is absent from the codebase and is not taken.

PRE-REGISTERED BRANCHES, on the 909 at midpoint:
  >= 0.867  the stack transfers to the CNN family. Licenses the matched 20sl arm and a 336 run, and the CNN family becomes the lead lever.
  0.8527-0.867  partial transfer. Directional, licenses the matched 20sl arm only.
  < 0.8527  the stack does not transfer to a CNN trunk. The lane closes with a measurement rather than an assumption; do NOT read it as 'CNNs are weak' before checking that the BN batch shape and the printed recipe are right.

HARNESS CHECK BEFORE ANY NUMBER IS READ. Printed recipe must name variant resnet50d, image_size 224, slices 12, backbone_lr 0.0002, unfreeze_last 16. The log's 'train mode pins N frozen norm layer(s)' must read 3, not 36 — 36 means the default six-block window is still in force and the arm is fitting a frozen trunk, which answers a different question.
notes:
TRUNCATED BY THE CO-TENANCY THRASH GATE at epoch 5 of 12, 2026-09-20T10:29Z. NOT a verdict on the lane.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, and it is the reusable part. The arm ran 22 min at batch 2 / accumulate 4 / vram-gb 6 / compile ON, peak 5.70 GB reserved inside the 6 GB cap, ~150 s/epoch. Holdout climbed 0.754 -> 0.7968 (e4) -> 0.8122 (e5), a normal shape, and the recipe dump confirmed every field including the load-bearing one (train mode pins 3 frozen norm layers, so the trunk was OPEN -- 36 would have meant a frozen trunk answering a different question).

THE NEIGHBOUR PAID 33%. biohub's step rate, median it/s over matched windows: 10.0 pre-arm -> 6.7 with our arm resident (n=24, then n=13 over a clean 75 s window; its own printed rate read 7.0 steady) -> 9.1 within 90 s of the kill (n=11). The recovery is what makes this a MECHANISM rather than a coincidence: our arm was the cause, and the design premise in the arm header -- that biohub is bursty at SM mean ~36% so the headroom lives in the gaps -- is WRONG in practice. Many short kernels did not interleave into the gaps; they contended. An earlier post-launch sample read 12.5 it/s (+25%, i.e. FASTER) and that reading was warmup/compile, not steady state, so a co-tenancy sample taken inside the first two minutes is worthless.

WHY IT DIED ANYWAY WITH 13 MIN LEFT. The gate was pre-registered out loud ('degradation past ~10% and I kill ours, no debate') precisely so that being nearly-done could not buy an exception, and the owner's constraint is 'we dont want thrawing' against a grant of ~30% util. Both were breached. The arm being 7 epochs from a number is the strongest possible pressure to renegotiate and is not a reason.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT -- the lane is OPEN and this bead is not closed. 0.8122 at e5 under one_cycle is a FLOOR (the anneal never ran), so it sits below all three pre-registered branches for a reason that has nothing to do with the trunk. The question 'does our stack transfer to a convolutional trunk' is untouched. What is now PRICED is the venue: this arm cannot be re-run while biohub is resident. Re-arm it when the card is ours alone, or re-price it at a footprint measured to cost the neighbour <10% -- which this run gives no evidence exists, since 6 GB / batch 2 was already the small end.
CARD WINDOW PLAN, priced 2026-09-20T10:39Z. biohub holds the card until ~15:00-15:35Z (12 epochs / 216288 steps, ETA 5.32 h read at 10:16Z, and that ETA was measured while OUR arm was stealing 33% of it, so the true finish is earlier). Nothing of ours goes on the card before it is empty -- card_check first, and a biohub step-rate sample AFTER two minutes, never inside them.

RANKED, ratio said out loud, ~4.5 h available:
1. resnet_stack_224 re-run -- 0.5 h. Validated (arm_check 0 refused, cache warm). Resolves the lane either way.
2. labelwise_drop_drop40_long_ff (knee-9grwy) -- 1.1-1.4 h, P(clears 0.945) ~0.30. The only queued arm that can move the BOARD rather than an axis.

Resnet runs first on cost alone: a third the wall-clock, and its own truncation is why the axis is open.

P(TOP BAND) REVISED DOWN, and this is a correction to this bead's own pre-registration rather than a new claim. The truncated run reached 0.8122 at epoch 5. The top band (>=0.867 midpoint) therefore needs +0.055 over the remaining epochs, against a corpus of 12-epoch runs whose epoch3-to-peak gain is median +0.0210 / p90 +0.0380 / max +0.0529 (n=96, trajectory_check). +0.055 is past the MAXIMUM ever observed on that budget. So P(top band) ~0.10, not the even odds the three-branch framing implies, and the modal landing is 0.84-0.85 -- i.e. BELOW resnet_224_short's own 0.8527, which is the branch that CLOSES the lane.

That does not cancel the run, it changes what it is bought for: 30 min to close an open axis with a measurement is a good ratio, and closing it stops the lane being re-opened by argument later. It is a CLOSER, not a lottery ticket, and it must be written up as one whichever way it lands. Note the two terms that bias against it and are not matched to 0.8527 (12 slices at band 0.2-0.8 vs its 20 at 0.1-0.9), so a number that clears does so despite them -- and a number that MISSES cannot be read as a clean refutation of the trunk without that caveat attached.
STALE FACT CORRECTED 2026-09-20T11:58Z, read off the metrics file rather than the mid-flight sample. This bead says 'TRUNCATED ... at epoch 5 of 12, holdout 0.8122'. The metrics.jsonl holds NINE rows, e0-e7: e4 0.7968, e5 0.8122, e6 0.8268, e7 0.8239. The kill landed at e7 and the peak was e6, so the forfeited floor is 0.8268, not 0.8122 -- the 0.8122 was a sample taken two epochs before the process died and then written down as the ending.

That moves the pricing. The top band (>=0.867) needs +0.040 from e7, not +0.055 from e5, which is p90 rather than past-maximum on the 12-epoch corpus (median +0.0210 / p90 +0.0380 / max +0.0529, n=96). P(top band) is nearer 0.15 than 0.10. The modal landing is still 0.84-0.85, i.e. the branch that CLOSES the lane, so the run remains a CLOSER and is bought as one.

RE-ARMED COLD 2026-09-20T11:59Z, card empty (card_check: one process, soffice at 2068 MiB, not ours; biohub NOT resident, ~3 h earlier than the 15:00-15:35Z this bead projected). The thrash condition this arm died on does not hold, which is exactly the venue its own note requires.

WARM RESUME WAS AVAILABLE AND WAS DECLINED, deliberately. A .resume sat at e7 and --resume 'continues the trajectory beside --out instead of starting the schedule cold' (config_tree.py:155), which would have cost 4 epochs x 150 s = ~10 min instead of 30. It writes a STITCHED metrics.jsonl, and that is the corpus defect trajectory_check found on lora_r8_v3small_224 -- 16 rows against a 12-epoch recipe, gate and peak from different runs, reading +0.1350 and lifting the epoch-gain ceiling 2.5x. The trajectory corpus is what prices every future truncation decision, so 20 extra minutes on an idle card is cheap against poisoning it. The e7 artefacts are PRESERVED, not overwritten, at D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/truncated/resnet_stack_224_s2026.e7trunc.*

Gates before arming: arm_check 1 checked 0 refused 0 uncached; queue_check nothing queued; reading_check --only REFUSED on the e7 holdout npz and the re-take is deliberate (a forfeited floor, superseded by a full trajectory).
2026-09-20 12:24Z CLOSED, < 0.8527 branch. resnet_stack_224_s2026 = 0.8459 midpoint / 0.8821 ledger75, peak e9 of 12, convergence_check converged. Reference resnet_224_short_s2026 = 0.8527 / 0.8842. Miss 0.0068 mid (branch ruler), 0.0021 l75 (inside the 0.0053 paired floor). Both rulers negative, neither a gain. FINDING LARGER THAN THE BRANCH: the stack is worth +0.054 on DINOv2-S (0.8502 -> 0.9045) and 0.000 on resnet50d -- representation-specific, not a general recipe. Unmatched terms stated not used: 12sl (ledger prices that axis -0.0001 flat) and band 0.2-0.8 vs 0.1-0.9 (UNMEASURED). Member declined in comp/members.declines; write-up in experiments/README.md.
BAND CAVEAT CLOSED, for free, by knee-f8nwd's geometry table. This arm carried a stated bias: its 12sl/0.2-0.8 cache was a FALLBACK forced by a deleted 0.1-0.9 cache, and I recorded the narrower band as possibly ADVERSE to it. It was not. Peripheral-minus-central label gap across 315 band-stamped members: -0.0801 at band 0.2-0.8, -0.0827 at 0.1-0.9, -0.0884 at 0.0-1.0, corr(width, delta) = -0.081. The NARROWEST window has the SMALLEST gap, monotonically. So 0.2-0.8 was mildly FAVOURABLE, and the arm's miss against its 0.8527 midpoint branch cannot be blamed on the band -- the verdict stands unweakened, and stands for the right reason now.

title: Full-fit refit of the last unexploited top-6 member (labelwise_drop_drop40_long_ff)
description:
labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026 reads 0.9051 ledger75, fourth in the top-6 band, and is the ONLY member there with no _ff refit on disk (19 _ff checkpoints exist, none for it). Its +0.0006 over the shipping member (0.9045) is a tenth of the 0.0062 seed spread, so it starts statistically TIED with what we ship. The edge is not the mechanism.

The mechanism is that the _ff operation has 8x variance on this corner, measured on the board: extsolo_v1 0.937 -> extffsolo_v1 0.945 (+0.008) against headlrsolo_v1 0.937 -> headlrff_v1 0.938 (+0.001), same operation, same starting board score. Refitting a tied member is a draw from a distribution with a measured +0.008 upper tail. This is the last such draw available in the top band: every other top-6 member is already shipped, or is soup_anneal2 at -0.0029 below the ship.

ema-ON, because knee-0ed8f landed 2026-09-20T09:22Z: the first matched single-variable ema contrast on this corner reads ema-ON ahead by +0.0028 ledger75 (0.9073 vs 0.9045, same fold, same 909 studies, convergence clean). That is under the 0.0053 paired floor and is directional only, but it is the OPPOSITE SIGN to the +0.0049 ema-OFF that matched_axes reported cross-member, and every shipping _ff is already ema-on.

PRICE: ~1.4 h. P(clears 0.945 board, i.e. a new best solo) ~ 0.30.

Deliverable is a single solo checkpoint, not an ensemble seat. No offline comparison against the fold-0 twin is meaningful (the full-fold member has seen the 909 rows the twin is scored on); the read is the BOARD, on a later slot, and only if a cheaper signal does not refuse it first.
notes:
RE-PRICED DOWN a second time, 2026-09-20, by noemasolo_v1's board reading. The arm header's whole mechanism -- 'a measured +0.008 upper tail' from extsolo_v1 0.937 -> extffsolo_v1 0.945 -- is an EMA MISATTRIBUTION: that pair crosses the ema axis (extffsolo_v1 ema ON, extsolo_v1 ema OFF). The matched ema-ON fold-0 twin (knee-0ed8f, 0.9073 ledger75) prices at board 0.9413 through the solo transfer (n=10, slope +1.071, intercept -0.0307, resid sd 0.0021), leaving +0.004 for the refit, not +0.008. Term across four bases: +0.001 / +0.003 / +0.004 / +0.007.

This arm's base labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026 reads 0.9051 offline75 -> fit 0.9387 -> +0.004 = 0.9427. Beating the pinned 0.946 champion needs +0.0033 over fit = 1.6 sd. P(beats champion) ~0.06, revised from ~0.15 for the 0.945 band. dml_b_ff already ran this shape from a HIGHER base (0.9078) and landed 0.943, under even its fit.

Card is sunk so it runs to completion, but it SHIPS AS AN INSTRUMENT OR NOT AT ALL, and the instrument value is low because dml_b_ff already spent a slot on the same question. Ledger section: 'The +0.008 refit term was an EMA misattribution'.
RAN 2026-09-20T14:41Z; checkpoint labelwise_drop_drop40_long_ff.pt on disk. Discovered 2026-09-21T08:24Z by reading_check --only, which REFUSED a re-arm that was about to spend ~1.4 h re-taking a reading already on disk - the knee-18c5r failure, caught by the gate built for it. No offline read is possible or owed (--fold -1). SHELVED, not shipped: the bead's own revised P(beats champion) is ~0.06 and the instrument value is low because dml_b_ff already spent a slot on the same question and landed 0.943, under even its fit. Shipping it would be a reseating, which the pacing rule forbids. Closing as ran-and-shelved; the checkpoint stays on disk and the decline is the record.

title: Matched ema contrast on the shipping recipe: ema is confounded with fold across the whole drop40 corner
description:
PRICE: ~1.4 h card (24 epochs x 206 s, measured on the fold-0 twin). P(clears 0.0053) ~ 0.35.

THE CONFOUND, measured from the run stamps 2026-09-20. Every fold-0 member of the drop40 corner is ema False (labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026, labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026, labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026, band_dense_drop40_long_s2026, both long36 arms). Every _ff refit is ema True (labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff, labelwise_dense_drop40_long_ff, labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_ff). The only ema=True fold-0 members are the chainfour family, a DIFFERENT recipe. So on the shipping recipe ema-on exists only where --fold -1 holds nothing out and no ledger row can price it: the axis is perfectly confounded with the ruler.

WHY THAT MATTERS NOW. knee-f2mj3 ships labelwise_ext_drop40_long_noema_ff as a solo today against extffsolo_v1 (0.945), and its own pre-registration names flat-within-0.004 as a live outcome, because 2 sd of the top-band board residual is ~0.004 while the matched_axes estimate is +0.0049 -- i.e. the board slot is very likely to be unable to resolve the question it is being spent on. The offline ruler can: the paired holdout floor is 0.0053 and ledger75 residual sd is 0.0017.

THE ARM. experiments/arms/labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ema.sh -- the ship arm verbatim plus --ema, fold 0 (default). Control is labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026, 0.9045 ledger75 at e23, 909 rows, already on disk. One variable.

BRANCHES. delta = ema_on - ema_off, ledger75, population eb3ba199.
  <= -0.0053  ema costs the ship what the matched groups suggest; drop --ema from every future _ff refit and the noemasolo direction is confirmed offline.
  within 0.0053  MATCHED NULL. The +0.0049 from matched_axes does not survive a same-recipe contrast, and the axis is retired rather than left open -- which the pooled mean sitting under the 0.0062 seed spread already warned about.
  >= +0.0053  the average is load-bearing on this recipe; the noemasolo entry is the wrong direction and every _ff keeps --ema.

NOT A CHAMPION ATTEMPT. knee-fbo5e prices the gap to first at 0.011 offline and this axis at ~0.005 at best, so it cannot take first place. It is an INSTRUMENT, and it is run on an otherwise idle card.
notes:
2026-09-20T08:12Z — arm LIVE on card, epoch 1. Contention incident: witness_check --device auto put a SECOND of our jobs on the card at 08:02Z; throughput fell 3608 -> 956 img/s (3.8x) and VRAM hit 31974/32607 MiB before card_check caught it as OVERSUBSCRIBED. Killed at member 167/190 (all ok to there). Card back to OK, arm resumed. Lesson: --device auto resolves to cuda and is NOT card-safe while an arm runs; scope with --members and run it between arms.
ARM'S PURPOSE RESTATED 2026-09-20T08:26Z, after reading the sibling arm rather than trusting memory. labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff.sh:65 sets FIT='--fold -1 --ema'. So the SHIPPING member (extffsolo_v1, board 0.945) IS ALREADY EMA-ON, and labelwise_ext_drop40_long_noema_ff.sh:80 (FIT='--fold -1') is its ema-OFF challenger, built and sitting in kneemri-noemasolo awaiting a slot.

I had this arm written up as building toward a new ema_ff member. That was wrong — that member exists and is what we ship. What this arm actually is: the DECIDER for mark 2.
  ema helps at e23  -> the ship's configuration is already correct, noemasolo is predicted to LOSE, cancel it, SLOT SAVED.
  ema hurts >=0.0053 -> noema_ff is the better solo, spend mark 2 on it, predicted ~0.950 at the +1.07 transfer.
Worst case it hands a slot back rather than spending one on a question the board cannot resolve (effect ~0.005 vs 2sd board scatter ~0.004). Zero slots, card otherwise idle.

Transfer validity confirmed on knee-fbo5e the same hour: offline75 vs board over 10 non-excluded solo entries is r=+0.987, slope +1.07, so this arm's free offline delta is a sound board proxy.

Mid-flight: e5 read 0.8405 vs control 0.8385 (+0.0020) after the e2-e4 lead of +0.0070/+0.0172/+0.0201 collapsed, exactly as pre-registered — a mid-training EMA lead is near-universal smoothing and is not evidence. Only e23 decides, against the control's 0.9045 ledger75. Card at 3475-3550 img/s, baseline, single occupant.
ARM LANDED 2026-09-20T09:21Z, READ 11:45Z, THE MATCHED-NULL BRANCH WITH A POSITIVE SIGN.

  labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ema_s2026   0.8687 midpoint / 0.9073 ledger75, e23, 909 rows
  labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026       0.8672 midpoint / 0.9045 ledger75, e23, 909 rows

delta = +0.0028 for ema ON, population eb3ba199, both at the same peak epoch. Inside the +-0.0053 paired floor, so by the pre-registration this is the MATCHED NULL branch and the axis is RETIRED rather than left open. The control reproduced its stated 0.9045 exactly, so the pair is clean and the one variable is the one flag.

THE SIGN IS THE RESULT, and it is the opposite of what sent this arm to the card. matched_axes read ema False > True at +0.0049; the same-recipe contrast reads ema TRUE better by +0.0028. The pooled cross-member estimate was n=2, single-seed, under the 0.0062 seed spread, and drawn from a corner where ema is perfectly confounded with fold -- this bead's whole thesis, confirmed by inverting the number that motivated it.

CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY THE SAME MORNING. knee-f2mj3 spent mark 1 on the board version of this question: noemasolo_v1 0.944 against the ema-ON twin extffsolo_v1 0.945, -0.001 for ema OFF. Two rulers, one sign, and the board delta carried at the +1.071 solo slope (-0.0009 to -0.003) is consistent with +0.0028 offline.

DECISION IT WAS BUILT TO MAKE: ema helps-or-neutral, so the ship's configuration is correct and knee-f2mj3's noemasolo direction is refuted. It did not save the slot -- mark 1 fired at 10:52Z before this reading was taken, which is the unread-result rule biting: the arm landed 09:21Z and sat 2.4 h while the slot it was supposed to decide was spent.

NOT A NEW BEST MEMBER: 0.9073 is SECOND on the honest ledger75 behind dml_b_s2026 at 0.9078, and the top eight span 0.0033. Its --fold -1 refit already exists and already shipped -- it IS extffsolo_v1 -- so this opens no untried refit. Rostered at comp/members.roster:967. CLOSING.

title: Lever audit 2026-09-20: no open axis is priced at 1.5%; the 1:1 board transfer is why
description:
Searched every axis for a mechanism that could carry 1.5%. None survives. Recording so the next tick does not re-walk it.

CLOSED, each with the ledger line that closes it:
- RECIPE knobs: matched_axes over 264 recipe-carrying members; the shipping member already holds the favoured value on backbone_lr 4e-05, calibrated_targets, epochs 24, image_size 336, mixup 0.0, slice_pooling labelwise, hold_annotations, slot_dropout 0.40. Only ema sat wrong and is in flight (knee-f2mj3).
- TRUNK SCALING: --key variant reads ortholarge 0.8707 vs small 0.8684, base 0.8795 vs small 0.8800, v3base 0.8724 vs small 0.8895 (+0.0171 for small). Bigger is flat-to-worse.
- CORPUS / more data: README:14419. beta=0.22 predicts +0.0201 for a doubling, but caveat 2 was answered NULL 2026-09-16 -- KMAR-50K's 1,088 studies (1.247x, predicted +0.0068) read -0.0012 / -0.0006 / -0.0011 / -0.0063 on four matched denominators. beta is not transferable across SITES. In-distribution is exhausted: the champion is already a 4,407-study full refit.
- LABEL NOISE: README:7670. Corpus carries ~10,840 wrong cells (20.5% gold cell error rate); errors_relabel fixed ~850 = 7.8% and read -0.0056. Binding constraint is detector recall 0.129, and the replacement detector was BUILT -- neighbour_errors, SimiFeat-style kNN over six frozen 336px trunks, AUC 0.6830 all / 0.3588 misses vs cleanlab 0.7628 / 0.6903. Rank-average wins on false positives (0.8020 vs 0.7580) but lands precision 0.480 at budget, under the 0.5 break-even B(2p-1) needs. And there is no positive to scale even given a detector.
- WEIGHT SOUPING, DEPTH READ: closed on their own ladders earlier.

WHY THE GAP IS HARD, STATED AS ARITHMETIC. board_transfer at our operating point is ~1:1, not x1.55. So the 0.011 board gap to first needs ~0.011 OFFLINE, which is 1.8x the 0.0062 seed spread and about 2.6x the largest per-unit any open lever has ever measured (+0.0043 per site, itself now refuted). No stack of knobs reaches it; a knob chain summing past the bar is the only route the closed axes leave, and every knob in the chain is already at its favoured value.

WHAT IS GENUINELY UNMEASURED, and both are small claims rather than 1.5% levers:
- foreign_readout: no artefact exists on disk (2026-09-16 sweep). KMAR as a training corpus is spent, but KMAR read through a cross-site DECODE ruler has never been measured. holdout909 is blind to the decode toll by construction.
- the asymmetric-cost knob k on confident learning: assumed in every published family, measured in none (Q-K).

NEXT ACTION IS NOT AN AXIS SEARCH. knee-f2mj3 is on the card and lands ~07:10Z; it is the live experiment and its board row is the ruler.

I earlier priced this instrument as under-powered, on the grounds that its pre-registered modal delta (~0.003) sits below the ~0.004 that is 2 sd of board scatter. THAT IS THE WRONG RULER AND IT UNDERSELLS THE INSTRUMENT.

sd(board) = 0.0091 and the 0.004 two-sd figure are CROSS-ENTRY quantities: they describe how much two DIFFERENT members' board scores scatter around an offline->board fit. Sign is the thing in dispute -- cross-member matched_axes says ema-OFF +0.0049, the matched fold-0 arm says ema-ON +0.0028 -- so the instrument is aimed at exactly the quantity it can read.
