title: Knob space is EXHAUSTED: dml_b_s2026 already sits on the favoured side of every replicated recipe contrast (matched-pair sweep, 347 comparisons, zero card)
description:
Measured 2026-09-20T04:49Z entirely from disk. No card, no slot.

THE INSTRUMENT. Group every member carrying a recipe (397 of them, 347 priceable) on ALL recipe keys
except one, ignoring out/seed/labels/paths/eval_labels/config. Any group with >=2 distinct values of the
held-out key is a matched one-variable A/B that has ALREADY been run. Guard each group on
Ledger75Row.population (two rows with different populations answer different questions) and skip any
member marked void by comp/members.declines, and any member below 0.86 ledger75 (that is a dead run,
not an axis reading). Then pool per VALUE-PAIR.

POOLING PER AXIS IS WRONG AND I DID IT FIRST. Orienting groups by the axis's most common value mixes
contrasts that are not the same question, and it produced two false levers before the pairs were read:
  - stochastic_depth pooled '+0.0035 favouring 0.05, 2/0'. The two groups are 0.05-vs-0.1 (+0.0067) and
    0.05-vs-0.0 (+0.0003). The first says DO NOT OVERDO IT; only the second is the add-it-or-not
    question, and it is +0.0003. Dead.
  - epochs pooled '+0.0016, 3/3'. It was mixing 24-vs-12 with 12-vs-48. Split: 24>12 is +0.0035 (n=5,
    3/5); 12>48 is +0.0079 (n=1). Longer helps to 24 and HURTS by 48.
  - slice_pooling pooled '+0.0001, 4/2' because a moments_wide-vs-moments group was signed as though it
    were labelwise-vs-max. Split: labelwise>max is +0.0013 (n=5, 4/5).
Pool per (axis, value-a, value-b), never per axis.

THE REPLICATED CONTRASTS (n>=2 matched groups, ledger75):
  calibrated_targets  True > False    n=6  +0.0072  sd 0.0040  6/6
  ema                 False > True    n=2  +0.0049  sd 0.0017  2/2
  sample_alpha        0.0 > 1.0       n=2  +0.0035  sd 0.0014  2/2
  epochs              24 > 12         n=5  +0.0035  sd 0.0035  3/5
  image_size          336 > 224       n=2  +0.0031  sd 0.0032  1/2
  mixup               0.0 > 0.2       n=2  +0.0026  sd 0.0004  2/2
  slice_pooling       labelwise > max n=5  +0.0013  sd 0.0049  4/5
  hold_annotations    True > False    n=4  +0.0012  sd 0.0018  3/4
  slot_dropout        0.4 > 0.0       n=2  +0.0011  sd 0.0006  2/2
  scheme              mergedk > canon n=2  +0.0010  sd 0.0023  1/2
Only calibrated_targets clears the 0.0053 paired floor, and it is the one axis with both n>=4 and
perfect sign agreement (6/6 by chance is p=0.016).

THE RESULT. dml_b_s2026 (ledger75 0.9078, the project's best fold-0 solo) is ALREADY on the favoured
side of every one of these: calibrated_targets True, ema False, epochs 24, image_size 336, mixup 0.0,
slice_pooling labelwise, hold_annotations True, slot_dropout 0.4. The only two it does not match are
scheme (it is canonical against mergedk, which is +0.0010 at 1/2 agreement -- not replicated) and
sample_alpha, where it sits at 0.5 and BOTH existing pairs are 0.0-vs-1.0, so its own contrast has
never been run. Monotone extrapolation prices 0.5->0.0 at about +0.0018, under the floor.

CONSEQUENCE. There is no stacking route through knob space. Against knee-lskiu's bars -- a solo needs
+0.0034 offline75 to match the 0.946 champion and +0.0133 to take first -- the entire replicated knob
budget available to the best solo is under +0.002. This CLOSES 'stack the axis marginals' as a lever
with evidence rather than intuition, and it confirms knee-2s0gp's 'the next lever must be DESIGNED' on
a much firmer basis: it is not that the shortlist happens to be empty, it is that the axes the project
has matched evidence on are all already spent on the member that would ship.

Per the global rule that data and architecture outsize knobs, the next lever has to come from one of
those two, not from the recipe.

DOES NOT RULE OUT: an axis with no matched pair on disk (it is invisible to this instrument), an
INTERACTION (every reading here is a main effect), or sample_alpha 0.5->0.0, which is simply unmeasured.

TOOL DEBT: this ran from a scratchpad script. Repo rules forbid one-off scripts -- it needs to land as
a committed CLI with a mirror test before it is used again.
notes:
2026-09-20 05:00Z -- TOOL DEBT DISCHARGED. kneemri/evaluation/matched_axes.py + its mirror test are committed; gates green (Session gates was successful). Three corrections the CLI forced, none of which change the exhaustion verdict:

1. AN ELEVENTH CONTRAST, and it is the LARGEST the project owns: backbone_lr 4e-05 > 0.0001, n=2, +0.0151, sd 0.0065, 2/2. Two independent matched groups -- probe224_control_s2026 0.8914 vs ctl_fastbb_s2026 0.8699 (+0.0215), and lr4e-5_ws_s2026 0.8840 vs lr1e-4_ws_s2026 0.8754 (+0.0086). It is FAR above the 0.0053 paired floor. The scratchpad missed it because its axis-level pooling folded the three-value group into one oriented delta.

2. 4e-05 IS THE OPTIMUM, not merely better than 1e-4. The same groups read 2e-05 at 0.8904 vs 4e-05's 0.8914 (-0.0010) and 1e-05 at 0.8910 vs 0.8916 (-0.0006): both single-group, both far under the floor. So the axis is a plateau from 1e-05 to 4e-05 with a cliff at 1e-4, and dml_b_s2026 sits ON the plateau. NOTHING TO GAIN. The row is a finding about the shape of the axis, not a lever.

3. A POOLING BIAS FIXED IN THE TOOL ITSELF, found by listing the groups member by member. contrasts() had taken a group's BEST and WORST member as its contrast; min-minus-max over a group is the widest delta it contains BY CONSTRUCTION, so every pooled mean for an axis anybody ever ran a third arm on was inflated, and the middle value was discarded unread. It now emits every value-pair, on per-value MEANS so a seed twin averages rather than entering twice (MatchedAxes.readings). On the current pool the printed table is UNCHANGED -- only backbone_lr's group held three values, and its extra pairs each appear once and fall under MIN_GROUPS -- so no number in this bead moves. The fix removes a trap, it does not repair a reading.

The verdict stands and is now stronger: dml_b_s2026 is on the favoured side of ALL NINE replicated contrasts, backbone_lr included. Knob space is closed; the next lever must come from DATA or ARCHITECTURE.

title: holdout_backfill cannot re-derive our best honest solos: no recipe recorded
description:
PRICE: ~0.3 h to diagnose, unknown to fix. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.00 - it is a correctness/instrument gap, not a lever.

WHAT. 'python -m kneemri.inference.holdout_backfill --served-slices N --served-band L H' is the ONLY tool that prices a serving-time regroup on the object that actually ships (Serving(group=SharedRead(...))). On 2026-09-20T04:15Z it refused four of six members asked:

  skipped labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026: no recipe recorded in its metrics or its checkpoint, so its split cannot be reconstructed
  skipped labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026:     same
  skipped labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026:   same
  skipped labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026:    same

Worked: base_dense_s2026, labelwise_dense_s2026, labelwise_depth20_b10_s2026.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING FILE. The refused set is not arbitrary - it is the drop40_long corner, which is where the members we actually ship live. labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 is our best honest solo (off75 0.9053, board 0.941 as l75solo_v1 ref 56309162). labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 is the holdout twin of labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff, the member in the SHIPPED efficiency entry extffsolo_v1 (ref 56312235, board 0.945). So the two members whose serving cost we most need to price are exactly the two that cannot be priced, and any depth/band/resolution number for them has to be TRANSFERRED from a member that can - which must then be stated as an assumption rather than a reading.

This is the 'faulty test' box in CLAUDE.md, found before it cost anything: the honest depth price measured this session (knee-uy8z0) is on base_dense_s2026 and two labelwise members, none of them the ship target.

WHAT TO CHECK. Whether the recipe is genuinely absent from both the metrics json and the checkpoint for these four, or whether the reader looks in a place the drop40_long arms wrote differently. If it is genuinely absent, whether the split can be reconstructed from the arm script that produced them (experiments/arms/) plus the recorded seed, and whether backfill should accept an explicit --recipe override rather than refusing.
notes:
REFUTED on its own subject, 2026-09-20T05:19Z. 'holdout_backfill --checkpoints D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026.pt --served-slices 12 --served-band 0.1 0.9 --device cuda' returned 'labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026: 909 studies re-derived at epoch 18'. That member carries a full 93-key recipe stamp on the first row of its .metrics.jsonl, and so does labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026; Backfill.of returns OK for both. The recipe is NOT absent and the reader is not looking in the wrong place.

WHAT ACTUALLY REFUSES, and it is correct behaviour. labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff - the member in the SHIPPED extffsolo_v1 - is a 'fold -1' full fit. holdout_backfill.py raises UnbackfillableError('a full-data fit held nothing out') on int(recipe.get('fold', NO_HOLDOUT_FOLD)) == NO_HOLDOUT_FOLD. A run that held nothing out has no holdout to re-derive, by construction rather than by bug. There is nothing to fix and no --recipe override to add.

SECOND REFUSAL, a real constraint but not this one. labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 (the _ff member's fold-0 twin) carries scheme=extended, and the corpus cache suffix comes from THAT key, not from target_corpus (which reads 'canonical' even on an extended-scheme member). So it wants images_336px_12sl_0.1-0.9band_extended.npy, which is not on disk - only the 20sl extended one it trained on. That is a missing CACHE, priced as a full decode, not a missing recipe.

THE READING THE BEAD WAS FILED TO GET, taken anyway. labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 is scheme=canonical, so it reads straight off images_336px_12sl_0.1-0.9band.npy at no cache cost. ledger75, population eb3ba199, 909 studies, epoch 18 both sides: native 0.9053, at 12 slices 0.9038, cost -0.0015. That is a 24->12 cut, HARSHER than the shipping member's 20->12, on the drop40_long corner itself - and it is smaller than all three transferred readings (base_dense -0.0034, labelwise_dense -0.0039, labelwise_depth20_b10 +0.0004). title: Serving.slices: a serving-time depth cap, the one decode lever with an isolated price
description:
PRICE: ~0.7 h of my time, ZERO card, ZERO slots. P(clears 1.5% on ACCURACY) ~ 0.00 - this is not an accuracy lever and is not sold as one. It is an EFFICIENCY-track lever, where the ratio is what makes it worth building: -36% total runtime for -0.0065 board on a track that is ADDITIVE and cannot touch the standing 0.946.

WHY IT IS BUILDABLE AND WHY IT IS NOT BUILT. Serving already owns four knobs no member can answer (views, budget, precision, read_size, vote). read_size is the near-twin and it states its own limit: it 'buys FORWARD time and never decode time', because SlotReader.cropped stops before the resize and one decode serves every size. Slices are the opposite axis and the expensive one: Member.decode_key is pixel_group MINUS resolution, so slices ARE in the decode key, and slot_reader.py:365 decodes exactly len(band_indices(n, slices)) files. Depth is therefore the only serving-time knob that reduces DICOM reads at all, and decode is 'the I/O-bound half on a Kaggle host with four CPUs'.

THE PRICE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and it is the reading cheapdecode_v1 said did not exist. That entry read 0.925 and wrote its own confound down: 'It cannot be attributed to slices alone without an arm that holds the members fixed and moves only the decode, and no such arm exists.' It changed the corner AND the members AND the seat count at once - and it never capped slices at serving time at all, it NAMED three members trained at 224/12. member_curve --slices (fixed under knee-i31az) is that missing arm: one member, one seed, centred window, midpoint, only depth moves.   20 (native) 0.8672 | 18 +0.0001 | 16 -0.0008 | 14 -0.0025 | 12 -0.0056 | 10 -0.0098

So the cheap corner's 0.019 deficit against the accuracy champion splits about 0.0056 to DECODE and 0.016 to the MEMBERS, and the corner was abandoned for the wrong reason. 12 is the knee of the curve: 20->12 costs 0.0056 and the next two rungs alone cost 0.0042.

FLOORS, in the honest direction: every rung is test-time only on a 20-slice-TRAINED member, so each pays a domain shift on top of the information loss. A member trained at the capped depth should read better than this, never worse.

WORK: add slices: int | None to Serving beside read_size, with its docstring stating the decode/forward asymmetry that read_size's states in the other direction; thread it through the member read the way member_curve does it (dataclasses.replace on the frozen Member's config, capping the member's OWN depth and never the slab's available depth - capping available makes width == available and (available-width)//2 degenerates to 0, so every rung reads the FIRST n slices instead of the middle n; that bias was 3x at 12 slices, -0.0166 against the true -0.0056). Then a kernel naming the shipped solo with slices=12.

NOT YET LICENSED, and must not be stacked on: the 224 px half. Its flat reading (band224_hold_s2026 0.8516 vs 0.8573, under the 0.0062 floor) is a DIFFERENT member, and read_size buys no decode anyway, so it would add a domain shift for a forward-time saving only.

title: member_curve --slices is a dead flag: declared, never consumed
description: kneemri/evaluation/member_curve.py:636 declares --slices (default 12); the only consumer of a slice count is line 723, window = member.window(held.slices, ...), which is the MEMBER's own recorded reading. So --slices N silently returns the native reading and an operator reading the log sees a clean number for a rung that was never scored. This is the tool whose own comment says 'it is the tool that decides WHICH members to submit, so a wrong number here chooses the wrong ensemble'. Checked: the README's -0.0001/+0.0080 slice-count family numbers came from TRAINED arms, not this flag, so no recorded number is poisoned. The exposure is forward - knee-i6ii7 was about to be answered with it. Fix: either consume the flag (override the window) or delete it. PRICE: ~0.3 h. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.00 - this is a correctness fix, not a lever.

title: convergence_check reads --stop-after-epoch as TRUNCATED: a designed stop is labelled a crash
description:
convergence_check separates TRUNCATED (died early) from STOPPED (patience fired) from UNDERTRAINED, but it compares epochs-run against the recipe's --epochs and cannot see the --stop-after-epoch leaf. headlr_ship_ffp reads 'best e- of 18 run, 24 asked' -> TRUNCATED, exit non-zero. The stop is DELIBERATE (knee-yatne): --stop-after-epoch 18 ends the loop while keeping the 24-epoch anneal, so the keep lands on the twin's peak e17 and recovers 0.0027 that fitting.py:283-292 gives away on a --fold -1 refit (ranked==epoch index with no holdout, so the last epoch always wins).

COST: read 2026-09-20T03:01Z as evidence the owed instrument slot had degraded to a floor. It had not. CLAUDE.md already records this check over-reporting three patience stops as crashes, one of which (res392) would have re-opened a correctly-closed family; this is the same class on a different leaf.

FIX: read the stop-after-epoch leaf from the recipe and treat run==stop_after_epoch as STOPPED (a decision), not TRUNCATED. Only a run ending below BOTH --epochs and any stop leaf is truncated.
close_reason: asked() now returns min(epochs, stop_after_epoch) — Fitting's own budget; headlr_ship_ffp leaves the TRUNCATED list (431 runs: 28 truncated, 3 stopped)

title: mergedk at shipping geometry: second site on the champion solo recipe
description:
Corpus lever at the geometry that actually ships. 336px/24sl/0.1-0.9/labelwise/depth24/drop40/24ep -- the champion solo recipe -- with --scheme mergedk (our 4407 + KMAR-50K 1088 = 5495 studies, two sites).

WHY NOW. The only prior 336 reading (mergedk_labelwise_drop40_long_336, 0.8901 ledger75, -0.0147 vs home family) is CONFOUNDED: it ran 12sl/band 0.2-0.8 against a home family at 24sl/0.1-0.9, so corpus and geometry moved together. No home control at 336/12sl/0.2-0.8/labelwise exists on disk (census 2026-09-20). This arm removes the confound by moving ONLY the corpus flag off the champion recipe.

MECHANISM. Second site buys corpus AXES (our 4407 carry 17.5 effective dims; 0.09% have a near-twin). Measured positive at the 224 corner, matched, four cells: base224_control 0.8754 / mergedk_corpus 0.8787 / mergedk_drop40 0.8805 / mergedk_drop40_long 0.8853 (+0.0099). Learning curve beta=0.22, 1088 on 4407 = 0.32 doublings -> +0.0064 offline75 predicted. KMAR rows are pseudo-labelled by our own champions (mean agreement 0.6548), so this is distillation-on-new-pixels, not new human labels.

PRICE: ~8 h (0.5 h CPU cache build off-card + ~7 h card).
P(clears 0.0062) ~ 0.33

TARGET. Base labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 = 0.9053 ledger75. Predicted 0.9117. Board via ledger75 top-band slope +1.09: our best solo ffsolo_v1 0.944 -> ~0.951 vs the 0.946 champion. This is the only open lever whose mechanism can carry the +0.003 board a SOLO needs.

LICENCE. KMAR-50K CC BY 4.0 (Mendeley DOI 10.17632/xw7mrg7ntg.6), no data agreement, clean through competition rule 2.5. The only merge this project owns that is shippable.
notes:
KILLED BEFORE THE CARD, on arithmetic that was already in the ledger (experiments/README.md:16335-16369). Zero card spent; ~10 min CPU/disk.

TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS.

1. THE PRICE WAS WRONG BY 2x AND THE ERROR WAS MINE. I priced this arm on +0.0099, which is
   mergedk_drop40_long vs base224_control -- a stack of corpus + slot-dropout 0.40 + 24 epochs against a
   12-epoch no-dropout control. The ledger's own 2x2 ISOLATES the corpus term: mergedk_corpus 0.8787 vs
   base224_control 0.8754 = +0.0033 ledger75 (+0.0039 midpoint). The base this arm moves one flag off,
   labelwise_depth24_drop40_long, ALREADY carries drop40 and 24 epochs, so the only increment available
   to it is the corpus-alone term: +0.0033, barely half the 0.0062 paired floor. A run whose own
   pre-registration predicts a null. The site axis agrees from a second direction: merged3 priced the
   second site at +0.0043 under SPARSE HUMAN labels, mergedk at +0.0039 under DENSE DISTILLED ones --
   'the gain is the site, and the distillation bought nothing on top of it'.

2. THE OFFLINE HOLDOUT CANNOT PRICE IT ANYWAY. kmar_pseudo.csv's teachers are DARK (--fold -1), which
   pseudo_labels.py permits for a foreign corpus and then rules on explicitly: 'What it does NOT license
   is reading a score off the student on OUR holdout and calling the gain a generalisation result -- the
   student's teacher saw those 909 studies, so that number prices the distillation, not the new data.'
   So every offline reading of a mergedk member, INCLUDING the 224 corner this lever was ranked on,
   prices distillation and not the corpus. A clean offline reading would need kmar_pseudo regenerated
   from fold-0 (holdout-blind) teachers.

WHAT WAS BUILT AND KEPT. images_336px_24sl_0.1-0.9band_kmar.npy (13.7 GB) and
images_336px_24sl_0.1-0.9band_mergedk.npy (83.2 GB) now exist at SHIPPING geometry. Not deleted -- no
owner word, and they are the cache any future mergedk work at the champion's geometry needs. The
rebuilt label table is BYTE-IDENTICAL to mergedk_labels.csv (5495 rows), so every mergedk member on
disk stays reproducible.

THE INVOCATION, WHICH WAS RECORDED NOWHERE and had to be re-derived:
  python -m core.data.corpus.build_kmar --archive D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/kmar50k --scheme kmar     --image-size 336 --slices 24 --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9
  python -m core.data.corpus.build_merged --scheme canonical --extra-scheme kmar --merged-scheme mergedk     --image-size 336 --slices 24 --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9 --extra-labels labels/kmar_pseudo.csv
Note --extra-labels: it defaults to rijeka_acl.csv, which would write the WRONG table straight onto
mergedk_labels.csv. Both legs are disk/CPU only, ~10 min total on NVMe.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. Not the corpus axis as such -- it closes corpus-for-a-SOLO at shipping
geometry, on the ground that +0.0033 cannot clear the floor. A mergedk member remains a DIVERSITY
candidate for a pool (nobody else has seen those pixels), which is a seat question and was already
answered no once by seat_value --against cleanseat_v1. And regenerating kmar_pseudo from holdout-blind
teachers would make the axis measurable offline for the first time.

title: Weight souping: average the parameters of independently fitted fold-0 members into ONE checkpoint
description:
PRICE: ~0.3 h card (four inference passes, no training). P(clears 0.0062) ~0.45.

kneemri/models/weight_soup.py has been on disk, guarded and unit-tested, and has NEVER been fired. Every 'soup' in the ledger is a LOGIT average (N forward passes, cannot move a solo); weight_average.sh was an EMA over ONE run's own epochs (+0.0003). Nothing has ever averaged the PARAMETERS of two independently fitted runs.

Census found the pot: 20 mutually-compatible scored fold-0 members at the shipping corner (small/cls_mean/labelwise/attend/336px/20sl/whole-stack/unfreeze 6/band 0.1-0.9, ruler report_labels_v2.csv), 0.8641-0.8703. Wortsman et al. report +0.5-1.0 absolute over the best single member in exactly this setting.

Deliverable is a SINGLE solo checkpoint, which is what the standing directive asks for and what a logit average cannot produce.

Ladder built: soup336_k{2,3,5,8}_s2026.pt, uniform average of the top-k by holdout. Baseline to beat: 0.8703 (labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026).
notes:
CLOSED 2026-09-20 on its own ladder, ~6 min of card, no training. Uniform parameter souping LOSES here, monotone in k.

All on the fold-0 holdout, 909 studies, population eb3ba199, LEDGER (midpoint) / LEDGER75:
  labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026  0.8703 / 0.9051   best single
  soup336_k2                        0.8667 / 0.9015   -0.0036
  soup336_k3                        0.8618 / 0.8949   -0.0085
  soup336_k5                        0.8581 / 0.8916   -0.0122
  soup336_k8                        0.8527 / 0.8855   -0.0176
  soup336_trunk3 (heads NOT souped)  0.8680 / 0.9032  -0.0023

Monotone in k makes this a kill, not a tuning miss. It also closes GREEDY souping without running it: greedy adds a member only if it improves, and no k>1 improves, so greedy returns the best single.

MECHANISM VERIFIED BEFORE BELIEVING THE RESULT. The soup is the exact parameter mean: on head.prior the two members differ by 0.189 and the soup residual from their mean is 0.0e0; same on layer 11 query (members differ 0.0145). Layer 0 is identical across members because unfreeze_last=6 freezes it.

ONE HYPOTHESIS RAISED AND REFUTED BY ITS OWN TEST: slot pooling is 'attend' and slots are permutation-symmetric, so souping could have been averaging mismatched slots. Hungarian matching on head.slot_emb (6x256) returns the IDENTITY permutation, matched distance 0.8307 = identity distance 0.8307, ratio 1.000. Slots are not permuted; both runs stay near their shared init in order. Not the cause.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY CARRIED FORWARD, and it is a positive finding: averaging three TRUNKS costs only -0.0023 while the same three heads cost -0.0085. The unfrozen trunks of independently fitted members live in one linearly connected basin; the heads do not. That licenses a souped trunk as an INIT with a head refit on top (see follow-up), and it does not license a soup as a shipped checkpoint.

One member was refused by the shape guard and is a separate bug: labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 shares all twelve ARCHITECTURE keys but carries a wider head.slot_emb/head.prior.

title: colsyn2 must not ship: it aims at the per-column axis retired as a class by colhalf_v1
description: kneemri-colsyn2 is built, gated and was queued for a slot. It must not be spent. WHAT IT IS: the 0.946 champion's 8 seats with the Synovitis column overwritten after the blend. submit_check REFUSES it anyway (SAME 8 members as tripleseat_v2 ref 56232529 board 0.9460 and tripleseatclean_v1 ref 56259030 board 0.9460), so shipping it needs --anyway. Do not pass --anyway. AS AN IMPROVEMENT it is a reseating: one column of seven moved post-blend, plausible board move +0.001-0.002, inside the top-band residual sd 0.0022 and at the 0.001 board resolution. AS AN INSTRUMENT it is answering a CLOSED question, and that is the refusal that matters. comp/board.jsonl retires the per-column axis AS A CLASS on two independent routes. colbaker_v1 (ref 56023244, board 0.903): ablating our HIGHEST column (Bakers, offline 0.9208) against colmcl_v1 ablating our LOWEST (MCL, offline 0.8104) puts both at about 0.98 board with OVERLAPPING intervals (0.980-1.004 and 0.968-0.992), so a 0.110-wide offline spread does not exist on the board and the pair cannot resolve ordering. colhalf_v1 (ref 56037952, board 0.728): the six columns our 909-study pool scores worst, Synovitis 0.8717 AMONG THEM, average 0.932 against the strong six 0.956 - a 0.024 gap against that 0.110 offline spread, and MCL, the worst column in the ablated half, reads 0.980, ABOVE the strong halfs mean. Its own words: there is no weak lane to attack and no per-column shortcut exists, the ten remaining single-column ablations are cancelled, they were ten slots aimed at a spread that is not there. Synovitis is already priced inside that partition, so colsyn2 buys a seventh reading of a retired class. CONSEQUENCE TO CARRY, and it is the strategic one: colhalf forces the arithmetic that to gain the 0.010 separating this project from first place, EVERY one of the twelve columns has to move about 0.010 of AUC. The headroom is distributed, not pooled. No seating, column or ensemble surgery can deliver a uniform twelve-column lift - only a better single member can. This also retires the floor-column framing (Lateral OA 0.8226, MCL 0.8233, Fracture 0.8241 on dml_b_s2026) as a TARGET: those are our holdouts weak columns and the board does not agree they are weak.

title: [bug] D262 calls LN-affine TTA 'the open lever, never measured' — knee-2sqyb closed it over a 10000x budget range
description:
STALE CLAIM IN THE LEDGER, found 2026-09-20 01:17Z during a card-free axis audit.

experiments/README.md:12335 (D262) reads: 'What is open is adapting the LN affine parameters at test time: TENT (Wang et al., ICLR 2021)... this project has never measured any of it. It needs no architecture change and no new cache, it applies to every member on disk, and it attacks the flat -0.0336 decode toll.'

That is false as written, and the refutation sits 290 lines ABOVE it in the same file. knee-2sqyb (CLOSED 2026-09-09) swept the CARVE per-study adapt budget over lr x steps against fovjitter160_s2026 and read decode cost FLAT-to-WORSE: -0.0297 control -> -0.0309 (|dtheta| 2e-3) -> -0.0355 (1e-2) -> -0.0360 (2e-2). That is 0.0063 in the WRONG direction across a 10000x displacement range, while kept collapses 0.8504 -> 0.7570. Its close reason states the finding generically: 'there is no budget at which decode turns, so try smaller closes too. REPRESENTATION-BOUND with the model-side lever removed rather than untested - the norm affines are not where the missing information is.'

WHY THIS CLOSES TENT AND NOT MERELY CARVE. TENT adapts THE SAME PARAMETERS - the LayerNorm affines - and differs only in the objective that points the gradient (entropy minimisation vs CARVE Eq.9 cardinality-aware). knee-2sqyb's conclusion is about WHICH PARAMETERS CARRY THE INFORMATION, not about one gradient direction, and it was measured across four orders of magnitude of displacement. The honest residual: strictly the sweep moved the affines along CARVE's direction only, so a different objective is not literally excluded. It is strongly disfavoured, and it may NOT be described as unmeasured.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A TYPO. D262 is written as a RANKING - it names this the one open lever and attaches a -0.0336 toll to it, which is twice the +0.018 ledger75 that prices first place. A reader ranking levers off that paragraph arms a closed axis. That already happened once on a different axis: knee-18c5r was ranked first among every open lever and handed a night's card to re-take a reading that had been on disk for seven days.

FIX: amend D262 in place with a pointer to knee-2sqyb and the budget table, the way the mergedk re-rank was superseded in place at :14415 rather than deleted. The reasoning in D262 is worth keeping; the ranking it performs is not.

PRICE: ~0.2 h, CPU only, no card and no slot. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0 as a SCORE - this is ledger hygiene and is justified as preventing a wasted card, not sold as an improvement.
close_reason: Amended D262 in place: superseded header plus the knee-2sqyb budget table, the TENT-not-merely-CARVE argument, and the honest residual that the sweep moved the affines along CARVE's direction only. Paragraph kept, ranking marked superseded, matching how the mergedk re-rank was handled at :14415.

title: resnet_224_ext: ViT's labelwise/ext/calib/drop40 recipe on the resnet50d trunk
description: Audit 2026-09-19: at 224 px on the 909 holdout, resnet_224_short 0.8842 @ledger75 beats band224 (ViT-S) 0.8801. title: Column profile is architecture-invariant across five encoder families
description: Measured 2026-09-18 on the fold-0 909-study holdout, truth cut 0.75: sixteen members across DINOv2, DINOv3, ResNet50d (CNN), MedSAM and V-JEPA have the same per-column difficulty SHAPE (profile r +0.78 to +0.93 vs DINOv2, +0.92 to +0.99 among the foreign families) over a 0.078 macro span, and NOT ONE beats DINOv2 on any of the twelve columns. Scaling null ruled out: ratio sd 0.065-0.099, residual sd 0.026-0.040 with sign-consistent structure (all foreign worse than predicted on LatMen/MCL, better on Synovitis/Effusion) - but the gap narrows and never crosses. RETIRES the 'structurally different member that covers DINOv2's blind spots' search direction. New cheap gate on any candidate member: score per column on this holdout, require it to WIN a column outright. Write-up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-18_the-column-profile-is-architecture-invariant.md
notes:
RESOLVED the image-vs-label-ceiling branch on 2026-09-18 with no new measurement: correlating reader_disagreement's per-finding spread (4406 studies, 4 readers, from interpretations 2026-08-26) against this profile's per-column AUC reads r=+0.081, Spearman +0.147 - zero, and the faint sign runs the WRONG way for a label ceiling. Only 1 of the 5 weakest columns (Fracture) is among the 5 most-disputed. So the invariant profile is an IMAGE ceiling: the weak columns are unsolved, not capped. Both chains now point at the same surviving lane - supervision made FROM PIXELS (mrnet_acl.csv, rijeka_acl.csv on disk) and representation (knee-jk3). Caveat: neither MRNet nor Rijeka covers the compartment split (Lateral Meniscus, Lateral OA) that carries most of the weak half.
2026-09-18: positive count is the strongest predictor of the conserved profile found so far -- r(AUC, log n_pos) = +0.536, r(AUC, prevalence) = +0.438, against +0.081 for reader disagreement. Both matched anatomical pairs track it (MedMen 1779/0.9444 vs LatMen 706/0.8949; MedOA 1102/0.9215 vs LatOA 644/0.8755). Partial: r2 ~ 0.29.

BUT THE CORRECTION IS ALREADY CLOSED AT BOTH ENDS, so this is a predictor and not a lever. Objective: per_label_loss inverse-prevalence weighting reads 0.8414 vs 0.8457, -0.0043, and its pre-registered clause concentrates in the rare labels with the WRONG sign -- Fracture (314 pos, most up-weighted) at -0.022 while eleven labels sit inside -0.007 (experiments/README.md:570-602). Ensemble: member_curve's with-the-answers oracle bounds every per-label weighting scheme over these members at +0.0002 over the plain average (README:602-633). Sixth route closed on the conserved shape.

NOT closed by this: the loss-weight axis over STUDIES (severity_weight, README:2102, knee-t1ho) -- different mechanism, own evidence.
2026-09-18: SEVENTH route closed -- compartment localisation. The lateral deficit is compartment CONFUSION (lateral meniscus 0.9212 on medial-negative studies vs 0.8392 on medial-positive, replicated on three members with intervals excluding zero), which explains both side_dense's -0.0641 and the architecture-invariance itself: every family reads the same pooled volume, so every family inherits the same confusion. But the clean regime is the ceiling and it prices at <= +0.002 macro, so it is retired on arithmetic. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-18_the-lateral-deficit-is-compartment-confusion-and-it-is-knob-sized.md

title: Price the slice-count runtime lever on the labelwise family (efficiency track)
description:
EFFICIENCY IS THE BEST RATIO WE OWN AND SLICES ARE ITS ONLY KNOB.
Efficiency track has THREE prize places; the metric weights runtime hard. Owner swapped our efficiency
entry to extffsolo (board 0.945, 1 member) from a 0.939 multi-member entry - a 3-8x runtime cut plus
+0.006 accuracy in one move. Remaining knob on a 1-member whole-stack entry is the SLICE COUNT, which
cuts encode work roughly linearly. extffsolo's member labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff runs 20 slices.

THE RECORD DISAGREES WITH ITSELF AND OUR FAMILY IS UNMEASURED.
  slice_count_maxpool Q vs R (README:302)      max pooling      12->20 = -0.0001
  band_span_hold -> band_dense_hold (:4758)    max, holdout     12->20 = +0.0080
  band_span -> band_dense (:4758)              max              12->20 = +0.0013
README:4776 states the family disagreement is NOT resolvable (0.0067, 0.76 floors). README:5273 gives the
-0.0001 its mechanism - 'slice count under MAX pooling ... the head cannot spend the extra slices'. Our
member is LABELWISE pooling with per-label slots, which plausibly CAN spend them, so the flat reading was
taken on a different head than the one we ship. No slice-count measurement exists on the labelwise family.

THE READ IS CHEAP AND NEEDS NO TRAINING.
The member is --whole-stack, so its slot embedding is an elementwise max over slices; feeding fewer slices
at inference is a graceful degradation, not a broken contract. Score the EXISTING checkpoint at 12 slices
against its own 20 on the holdout twin labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 (the _ff twin fits --fold -1 and
holds nothing out, so it cannot be read). ~909 studies, minutes of card, zero training.

PRICE: ~10 min of card against a ~40% runtime cut on the shipped efficiency entry.
P(clears) ~ 0.45 that the accuracy cost is inside the 0.0062 paired floor.

BRANCH
  cost <= 0.0062 (inside the floor)  -> ship a 12-slice efficiency kernel; the runtime cut is bought for free.
  0.0062 < cost <= 0.0150            -> a real trade; price it against the efficiency metric's runtime weight
                                        before spending a slot, do NOT ship on the accuracy board.
  cost > 0.0150                      -> labelwise slots DO spend the slices; the -0.0001 does not transfer,
                                        slice count is closed as an efficiency knob, and the finding is that
                                        the two pooling families differ on it - which resolves README:4776's
                                        open disagreement in the direction of head capacity.
Blocked on the card until dml_b_ff finishes ~16:35Z. Never a second job of ours on the card.
notes:
ASKED BEFORE, AND THE PRIOR ANSWER IS BETTER (owner, 2026-09-18).
experiments/README.md:5921-5940 (2026-08-29) already made this argument with sharper numbers: 232 teams
outrank us on efficiency while scoring BELOW us; 18 teams within 0.002 of our accuracy span efficiency
ranks 4 to 2140; 'the entire main board spans 0.930-0.952 and buys 2600 ranks with score; this axis buys
2136 with runtime at score held flat.' It also records the trade owner reversed today - our efficiency row
moved soloseat (1 member, 0.925) -> a multi-decode entry at 0.941, 'we bought 0.016 of accuracy and paid
229 ranks for it.'

THE CARD IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT AND THIS BEAD ASKED FOR IT.
The original plan (re-score the checkpoint at 12 slices on our holdout, ~10 min of card) measures ACCURACY
cost and only GUESSES at the runtime saving. What ranks us is wall-clock on a real T4, and README:91 already
names the free tool for it: comp/kernels/kneemri-loadcheck 'loads, forwards and chunks every member on a
real T4, spends no submission, and answers what only the runtime knows.' No slot, no card.
README:5980 - 'There is no projected runtime in any log we hold, and there never was' - is the gap that
makes loadcheck the only honest source.

REVISED: run loadcheck on the shipped efficiency member at 20 slices and at 12, read the T4 wall-clock
delta, and ONLY THEN spend card on the accuracy cost if the runtime saving turns out to be worth buying.
Cost: zero slots, zero card. Ordering matters - measure the gain before pricing the cost.
RESOLVED 2026-09-20T03:51Z, zero card, zero slots — by fixing knee-i31az (member_curve --slices was declared and never consumed) and then a bias in my own first fix.

MATCHED WITHIN-MEMBER LADDER on labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 (the honest twin of extffsolo_v1's member; never the _ff, which is --fold -1 and in-sample). Centred window, MIDPOINT cut, single member, single seed:
  20 (native) 0.8672 | 18 0.8673 (+0.0001) | 16 0.8664 (-0.0008) | 14 0.8647 (-0.0025) | 12 0.8616 (-0.0056) | 10 0.8574 (-0.0098)
Against the 0.0053 paired floor: 16 = 0.15 floors, 14 = 0.47, 12 = 1.06, 10 = 1.85.

WHY THE README CALLED THIS NOT RESOLVABLE AND WHY IT NOW IS. experiments/README.md:4776 priced the slice-count gap at 0.0067 = 0.76 of a 0.0088 ruler, because it was a CROSS-FAMILY difference of differences, which carries 1.4x a single paired comparison's noise. A matched ladder inside ONE member does not pay that factor. The two routes AGREE on the size (-0.0056 here vs 0.0067 there) — this is a confirmation of that number, not a contradiction of it, and it is now resolvable because the ruler changed, not because the effect did.

THE TRADE. Measured runtime slopes (mastermind letter 20260906T0833Z): 336px = 2.37 s fixed + 0.29 s/member per study, so 89% of a ONE-member entry is decode, which is what slice count drives.
  16 slices: -20% decode -> ~2.19 s/study, ~18% total runtime cut, for -0.0008 offline — ONE board tick, under the board's own 0.001 resolution. FREE.
  14 slices: -30% decode -> ~1.95 s/study, ~27% total cut, for -0.0025.
  12 slices: ~36% cut for -0.0056, about one paired floor. Priced, not free.

CAVEAT, AND IT IS THE DIRECTION THAT HELPS. This is a TEST-TIME window change on a member fitted at 20, so every rung also pays a domain shift. These are FLOORS on retention; a member trained at that depth should do better, not worse. It does not license a claim about train-time depth.

THE MISTAKE THAT ALMOST SHIPPED. My first fix capped the window's AVAILABLE depth. The member is whole_stack, and window() centres by (available - width) // 2 — capping available makes width == available, so that arithmetic degenerates to 0 and every rung read the FIRST n slices, not the middle n. That confounds depth with offset and read 12 at -0.0166, 3x the true cost, i.e. a cliff that does not exist. The cap belongs on the MEMBER's own read depth (min(self.slices, available)), which is also what it means semantically. Anyone re-running this must confirm window().starts is non-zero for a capped rung.

NOT DONE: no slot spent, nothing shipped. The efficiency track is ADDITIVE (efficiency_read header: a cheap entry ADDS a candidate and never displaces the accurate one), so a 16-slice ship cannot touch the standing 0.946.
READ 2026-09-20T04:17Z. BRANCH 1 FIRES: cost is inside the paired floor on every member measured.

METHOD, and it is not the one this bead proposed. The bead said to use member_curve; knee-i31az shows that flag was dead, and this session found worse - member_curve --slices takes a CENTRED window of the cached slab, which NARROWS the band (0.1-0.9 -> about 0.26-0.74 at 12 slices) and so measures depth plus band together. slot_reader.py prices band 0.1-0.9 -> 0.2-0.8 at 0.0040, the same size as the effect being looked for, so that route was unusable. Measured instead with the object that SHIPS: holdout_backfill --served-slices 12 --served-band 0.1 0.9, which builds Serving(group=SharedRead(slices=12, band=(0.1,0.9))) and resamples 12 indices across the SAME band. Fixed corpus, fixed band, fixed pixels, fixed epoch, same population eb3ba199, 909 studies.

  member                           head        native l75   12sl l75   d l75    d midpoint
  base_dense_s2026                 dense         0.8812      0.8778   -0.0034     -0.0030
  labelwise_dense_s2026            labelwise     0.8964      0.8925   -0.0039     -0.0040
  labelwise_depth20_b10_s2026      labelwise     0.8970      0.8974   +0.0004     -0.0013

THE BEAD'S MECHANISM IS REFUTED, in the direction that helps. The premise was that the -0.0001 flat reading came from MAX pooling, whose head 'cannot spend the extra slices', and that our LABELWISE head with per-label slots plausibly CAN, so the flat number would not transfer. It transfers. Labelwise mean cost is -0.0018 l75 against dense's -0.0034 - labelwise is if anything LESS slice-hungry, not more. n=2 per head, so the ORDERING between heads is not a finding; what is established is that no head measured pays more than 0.0039 for 20 -> 12.

CORROBORATION, independent and pre-existing: kneemri/inference/read_groups.py records 0.8706 native against 0.8684 at 12 slices / band 0.1-0.9 on the champion's five fold-0 twins = 0.0022. Four readings now, two heads plus the champion's twins, all between 0.0000 and 0.0039.

WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, stated rather than glossed. None of these IS the shipped efficiency member. labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 (twin of the shipped labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff) and labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 both refuse to re-derive - no recipe recorded in metrics or checkpoint, filed as its own bug. So the 12-slice cost on the entry we would actually ship is TRANSFERRED from three other members, not read on it. The transfer is supported by the head result above and by the spread being 0.004 wide across every member and head tried, but it is an assumption and the submission message must say so.

DIRECTIONAL ONLY, do not build on: labelwise_depth20_b10 moves +0.0004 on ledger75 and -0.0013 on midpoint - the two rulers disagree in SIGN on that member. Both are far inside the floor; it means the member is flat, not that 12 slices help.

title: The -2.7 sd transfer failure is a midpoint-ruler artefact; the composition escape was closed on it
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-18 off comp/board.jsonl, n=48 rows carrying offline75 + board, scope!=excluded, 10 of them solos.

THE FIT REPRODUCES THE DOCUMENTED CONSTANTS, which is what licenses the rest: OLS board = -0.0603 + 1.104*offline75, residual sd 0.0017, against CLAUDE.md's recorded 'whole record +1.10 (resid sd 0.0017) ledger75'. Independent arithmetic, same numbers.

THE DEFECT. interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-18_state_of_the_levers.md says 'The three highest offline members read 0.9045 / 0.9053 / 0.9059 against board 0.937 / 0.941 / 0.937 -- all three BELOW the fitted transfer line at -2.7 sd.' Those offline values are LEDGER75. The -2.7 sd is a MIDPOINT residual, and it belongs to ONE entry, not three. Two rulers in one sentence.

WHAT EACH RULER ACTUALLY SAYS (solo entries, top 3 by offline):
  kneemri-headlrsolo  ledger75 -1.9 sd   midpoint +0.7 sd
  kneemri-l75solo     ledger75 +0.9 sd   midpoint -2.8 sd
  kneemri-extsolo     ledger75 -1.0 sd   midpoint +1.1 sd
Top-3 mean z on ledger75 = -0.68, combined = -1.17. NOT SIGNIFICANT, and one of the three is ABOVE the line. The midpoint fit's residual sd is 0.0089, 5x looser than ledger75's 0.0017 -- the ruler this repo has been burned by repeatedly (knee-f9aao).

WHAT SURVIVES. The audit closed the composition escape on two legs and only one dies. Still true: headlr_ship_s2026 IS the shipping recipe plus every directional-positive knob, and from the HIGHEST offline the project owns (0.9059) it read board 0.937, against l75solo's 0.941 from a LOWER offline (0.9053). The full knob stack did underperform its own base on the board. But that is n=1 at -1.9 sd -- a QUESTION, not a verdict, and it may not be quoted as a closed axis.

WHAT IT RE-PRICES. dml_b_ff (knee-8bmi2, running) refits labelwise_depth24_drop40_long -- l75solo itself, which sits +0.9 sd ABOVE the transfer line. Its 0.9485 prediction assumed that base transfers AT the line; historically it transfers above it. The prediction is conservative, not optimistic.

DO NOT read this as 'composition works'. It is a licence to re-ask, priced separately, not evidence of a gain.
notes: Sibling of knee-36xad (the offline75 column held two rulers). Same defect class, one layer up: there the COLUMN mixed rulers, here the CONCLUSION drawn from it did.

title: Refit dml_b's peer term at --fold -1: the blockage was teacher-file coverage, not a law
description:
Whole-corpus refit of dml_b_s2026, the highest ledger75 this project owns (0.9078). Arm: experiments/arms/dml_b_ff.sh.

PRICE: ~3.5 h  (~25 min teacher_readings --teach-all off dml_a_s2026, then ~3 h of 24-epoch --fold -1 --ema train)
P(clears 0.946) ~ 0.35

THE ANCHOR, which is the tightest in the project. ffsolo_v1 (board 0.944) is labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_ff,
the whole-corpus refit of a base at 0.9053 ledger75. dml_b_s2026 is that SAME recipe at 0.9078 -- the peer term
is the only difference -- so this arm is ffsolo_v1's exact line with one term added. At the in-band transfer
constant +1.00 (board_transfer, 102 resolved pairs at or above 0.8977, read 2026-09-18, never quoted from prose)
the +0.0025 base gain carries to 0.9465, +0.0005 over the champion.

WHY P IS ONLY 0.35 AND NOT HIGHER. The +0.0025 sits INSIDE the 0.0053 paired floor, so our own ruler cannot
order dml_b_s2026 against its base. Mutual supervision moved the partner -0.0015 the other way, equally
unresolved: the cohort result is null in both directions. The predicted margin is also under the 0.0010 median
board blur. So this is bought as a refit of the best offline member on disk, not as a confirmation of the peer
term, which no ruler this project owns can resolve.

WHAT IT IS NOT. Not a 1.5% lever. The 2026-09-18 audit (interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-18_state_of_the_levers.md)
closed coverage, supervision, the trunk and the composition escape, and states that no refit of an owned base
clears the champion. This is chosen as the best-ratio remaining knob that yields a shippable SOLO, with the
audit's verdict standing: at 0.946 against a 0.957 leader we are not one knob away.

WHY THE AUDIT'S -2.7 sd OBJECTION DOES NOT BITE. The three highest offline members read board 0.937/0.941/0.937,
below the fitted line -- all three are FOLD-0 shipping entries. The whole-corpus refits transferred at their
anchors, 0.944 and 0.945. The curse is on the honest-fit road, not this one.

BRANCH (board, and its reading costs a slot).
  >= 0.947  the refit road reopens on a better base; this seat ships and dml_b_ff joins the roster.
  0.944-0.946  a tie with ffsolo_v1 inside blur: the peer term buys nothing through a refit, park it.
  <= 0.943  the peer term costs through the refit; close the DML road and decline dml_b_ff in writing.
notes:
DE-RISKED 2026-09-18 12:26Z, before the card frees. The route is not merely open, it has a dedicated documented flag: --teach-all ('teach EVERY study, for a fold -1 student the board rules; voids the student's own holdout score'). main() DOES refuse --fold -1, and that refusal is what I misread as the route being shut — its own message names the correct spelling. teach() is called as teach(members, identifiers, folds, -1 if teach_all else fold), so --checkpoints on the FOLD-AWARE twin plus --teach-all gives positions over every study with a teacher that never saw the board. Exact step 1:

  python -m kneemri.inference.teacher_readings --checkpoints <dml_a fold-0 ckpt> --out <teacher>_all.npz --teach-all

No code change is needed for either step. The 3 h price stands and so does P(clears 0.946) ~ 0.25; this only removes the risk of discovering a blocker with the card already held.
RE-PRICED 2026-09-18 12:40Z, and the earlier price was built on a QUOTED constant. board_transfer read live gives compression +1.00 in our band (102 pairs at/above 0.8977, median +1.00 [+0.89,+1.04]; 19 pairs at/above 0.9014, +1.00 [+0.87,+1.13]), not the 1.104/-0.0603 line quoted from the interpretation.

It is a pairwise median with no intercept, so it applies differentially against a named anchor, and the anchors disagree by more than the gain: vs headlr_ship_s2026 (0.9059->0.937) dml_b predicts 0.939, refitted ~0.944; vs l75solo (0.9053->0.941) it predicts 0.9435, refitted ~0.9465. The champion (0.946) sits INSIDE that 0.0045 spread.

So P(clears 0.946) ~ 0.25 is not defensible in either direction — the correct statement is that this refit cannot be predicted to either side of the champion with the ruler we own. The gating on knee-uh1j5 (ADDITIVE vs CEILING) stands and is now the ONLY thing that would move it: under CEILING it is dead at 0.9445, under ADDITIVE it is a coin flip whose outcome the ruler cannot forecast.

Also recorded, and it is the load-bearing half of the read: ZERO inversions in the 696 pairs the holdout resolved (gap >= 0.0053). The ruler is trustworthy above its floor and useless below it, and dml_b's +0.0019 over our best is below it by construction.
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-18 14:37Z, before dml_b_ff lands (~15:22Z, epoch 13/24 done at this writing).

PRICE: 0 h of card - the arm is sunk, it has been running since before this pricing. Cost is ONE of three
remaining slots (marks 17:34 / 20:32 / 23:30Z).

THE EVIDENCE, and it is two matched pairs off comp/board.jsonl rather than a remembered slope. The
--fold -1 full-corpus refit has been put on a SOLO member twice and paid both times:

  labelwise_depth24_drop40_long : l75solo  0.941 (off75 0.9053) -> ffsolo    0.944   +0.003
  labelwise_ext_drop40_long     : extsolo  0.937 (off75 0.9045) -> extffsolo 0.945   +0.008

dml_b_ff is the --fold -1 refit of dml_b, whose fold-0 twin dml_b_s2026 reads off75 0.9078 (verified on
ledger75 this hour, 909 rows, epoch 18) - the best of the three twins.

WHY THE OFFLINE EDGE IS NOT EVIDENCE, stated before the outcome. +0.0025 over the ffsolo twin is INSIDE
the 0.0053 paired floor. Worse, offline rank has already INVERTED against the board on the one pair that
can test it: extsolo is offline-WORST of the three twins and its refit is board-BEST. That is knee-wbkwp
(both rulers retired as seat selectors) arriving on solo refits. So this arm is bought as a refit of a
strong recipe, NOT as a bid that dml_b's peer-distillation term transfers.

P(clears 0.945, the best solo) ~ 0.35.  P(clears 0.946, the pinned champion) ~ 0.25.
Modal band 0.944-0.946: tie-or-just-under the incumbent solo.

BANDS:
  0.948+        the distill term carries at member level and the refit stacks on it. Re-open peer
                distillation as a member axis; refit-and-distill becomes the default member recipe.
  0.9465-0.9479 beats champion AND best solo. Ship it as the accuracy entry and it takes the efficiency
                row too - one member at ~0.8 GB peak against tripleseat's 7.2 GB.

The first is a REGULARISER, the one failure class the epoch-ladder lookup named this morning (8-vs-24 flat only WITHOUT slot dropout; drop40 x long interact +0.0113), so the rotation cannot settle it. That leaves ONE rotatable positive. Re-price: 2.1 h, P(resolves positive) ~0.5, gain +0.0025 whose magnitude does not transfer, expected ~+0.0012, against a required +0.0065. Refused on ratio -- worse than the arm already on the card. Priced 09:24Z as 3-4 leaves / ~12 h / +0.006..+0.009; that pricing is RETRACTED. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-18_the_rotation_works_and_has_nothing_left_to_point_at.md. What re-opens it: a non-regulariser leaf tilting positive above ~0.002; none exists in the 22 priced leaves, and pricing one of the 48 unpriced costs the same 2.1 h as resolving it (knee-dry3h consequence 4).

title: card_check cannot see a job that dies: two of ours ran on one card and every gate read OK
description:
On 2026-09-18 slicecover36 died silently at 06:45Z while depth24_ff_long36 ran on the same card until 07:01Z. Two of ours shared the card and nothing refused.

WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT. card_check asks the DEVICE what computes on it, which is the right question and answers it correctly - at the moment it is asked. It is a PULL channel: it reports when invoked, and nothing invokes it between one arm's launch and another's. queue_check read OK throughout, because a live process gating an owed arm is all it can see and both processes were live.

THE COST IS THE READING, NOT THE CARD. This is the same shape as the two member_curve scans: contention does not fail a run, it stretches one, and a stretched epoch is recorded as a fact about the member rather than about the contention. A silent death on top of that means the arm that died left no marker anyone read.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT, and what would not. A seventeenth thing to remember to run is the same defect with more prose - CLAUDE.md already legislates that. The card is held by hold_card/release_card in experiments/lib.sh, which is a PUSH point that already runs on every arm on every path out. The question to answer before building anything: does hold_card refuse when the lock is already held by a live pid of ours, and if so how did two arms both get it - a stale lock left by a killed process, or a launcher that bypasses hold_card entirely (foreign_run does not go through run_train).

Read lib.sh hold_card first. Do not add a check.
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-09-18T08:11Z, by reading, zero card. The hypothesis in this bead (a stale lock cleared out from under a live holder, MSYS-vs-Windows pid) is WRONG, and so is 'a launcher that bypasses hold_card' — both foreign_run (lib.sh:515) and run_train (lib.sh:620) call it.

THE MECHANISM: the lock covers the TRAINER ONLY, not the arm. run_train calls release_card (lib.sh:641) the instant the tee|grep pipeline returns. Everything the ARM SCRIPT does after run_train returns — holdout scoring, seat pricing, teacher_readings, packaging — is GPU work outside the lock. So chain 1 can be on the card with no lock held while chain 2's mkdir succeeds on the first try.

THE EVIDENCE, and it is decisive because it is what is ABSENT: neither slicecover36_s2026.full.log nor depth24_ff_long36.full.log contains 'parked', 'took the card after Nm parked', or 'clearing a GPU lock held by dead process'. Both got the lock on the first mkdir. Nobody waited and nobody cleared: when the second one asked, the lock did not exist.

WHY wait_for_free_card did not save it: it gates on free VRAM against the recipe's derived need. A post-training reading pass holds far less than a trainer, so free stays above needs and the gate passes correctly — it was built to wait out a co-tenant TRAINER (its own comment says so), and an unlocked sibling reading pass is not that.

NOT a missing check. CLAUDE.md legislates that a seventeenth pull-channel is the same defect with more prose, and card_check is a pull channel: it reported OK because at the instant it was asked, one job held the lock and the other held only the card. The fix is the lock's SCOPE, not a new detector — release_card should fire when the ARM exits, not when the trainer returns, with the per-ARM release that makes chains possible preserved (the lib.sh:111 comment: 'ONE ARM AT A TIME, NOT ONE CHAIN AT A TIME' — that is still right, it is the definition of 'arm' that is wrong, currently 'trainer').

LIVE EXPOSURE, named rather than left to be discovered: experiments/arms/dml_cohort.sh (running now) calls read_peer four times, and read_peer is a bare 'uv run ... teacher_readings' that never goes through run_train. So it takes no lock. Four GPU inference passes of this arm are unlocked right now. Harmless only because nothing else is queued; it is the same hole, in code I wrote after this bead was filed.
THE HOLE IS REPO-WIDE, not one arm. Census 2026-09-18T08:13Z — 'uv run ... python -m kneemri' inside experiments/arms/ that is neither run_train nor foreign_run: 20 call sites across 19 arms (attribution, carve_adapt_read, carve_budget_sweep, depth_reserve, diversity_curve, dml_cohort, foreign_drop_pilot, foreign_drop_pool, foreign_oof, fovjitter160_read, fov_perstudy_read, hisrecipe_distill, hisrecipe_distill_full, ortho_probe x2, packaged_seats x3, readout_probe, small_feat_fit, swin_distill_fit, trio_seat_value, vjepa_probe). NOT ALL OF THESE ARE GPU WORK — roster_reads and his_labels_blend may be CPU-only and the list is unaudited on that axis; it is the population to audit, not a count of defects.

FIX LANDED, PARTIAL AND SAID SO. experiments/lib.sh gains run_gpu: hold_card, run, release_card, with '|| status=$?' so a failure still releases under set -e. It takes no recipe flags, so arm_needs_mib falls back to ARM_NEEDS_MIB — a gate that cannot measure does not become a gate that permits, which is that function's own stated rule. dml_cohort.sh's read_peer now goes through it.

STILL OPEN, and this bead stays open for it: (1) the other 19 call sites are unconverted and unaudited; (2) run_train is NOT re-expressed in terms of run_gpu — that unification is the right end state but refactoring the hot path while an arm is live and full gates cannot be run is a bad trade, so there are now two lock-taking paths; (3) the LIVE dml_cohort run is reading from its snapshot (logs/dml_cohort.running.sh, copied at launch by run_snapshot), so its four reading passes stay unlocked for this run — the edit reaches the next one only.

title: Deep mutual learning: two DINOv2s supervising each other during training
description:
Owner's idea 2026-09-18: take our two best models and have each supervise the other on its last layer. It is a named, published practice - Deep Mutual Learning (Zhang et al. 2018) and codistillation (Anil et al. 2018).

WHY IT IS NOT REFUTED BY WHAT WE HAVE MEASURED. Four ledger rows test distillation and all are null or negative: distill_pairs (our own fold-0 twins, seat +0.0016, under the floor), raptor_distill (foreign teacher, right sign, under the floor), foreign_distill (distance 0.0249 -> 0.0190, DESTROYS it), and the feature-distillation pair (flat, gives the trunk's solo score back and nothing more). Every one of those uses a CONVERGED teacher emitting FIXED targets. DML does not: both models train from scratch simultaneously, and the paper's own claimed mechanism is the high entropy of peer posteriors EARLY in training - a regulariser, not a knowledge transfer. That is a different lever from anything in the ledger.

WHY IT IS NOT QUEUED. PRICE: ~5-6 h (two models trained jointly, 36 epochs at our sizes, 2x card). P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.05. DML's own reported effect is +0.5-1 percent, and it should be discounted here because our members correlate at 0.83+ and distill_pairs already diagnosed the blocker as 'a rank average cannot pay for an ordering it already holds' - two DINOv2s share a trunk, so they share the ordering. Against that, the fold rotation is 7.8 h for a ruler 2.2x sharper that unblocks every subsequent decision, including whether this worked.

RE-OPEN by answering the entropy argument - does the early-training peer signal survive a shared trunk - never by re-quoting DML's ImageNet number.
notes:
RE-OPENED 2026-09-18 06:45Z on this bead's OWN stated condition, measured, no card.

The condition written here was 'does the early-training peer signal survive a shared trunk'. Measured
the peer term against the supervised term it would be added to, on five top members, 909 studies,
12 labels (scratchpad peer_disagreement.py, HoldoutRecord predictions):

  headlr_ship_s2026 vs labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026  |pa-pb| 0.0499  |pa-truth| 0.1758  ratio 0.284  corr 0.957
  headlr_ship_s2026 vs calib_span_s2026                     |pa-pb| 0.0681  |pa-truth| 0.1758  ratio 0.387  corr 0.921
  labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 vs calib_span_s2026   |pa-pb| 0.0719  |pa-truth| 0.1730  ratio 0.415  corr 0.916
  clean_calib_s2026 vs stackfit_s2026                       |pa-pb| 0.0536  |pa-truth| 0.1889  ratio 0.284  corr 0.961

Peer disagreement is 28-42 percent of the supervised residual. The shared trunk does NOT collapse it.
And this is the HARDEST place to find disagreement - converged members, held-out rows, one family - so
early-training training-set disagreement is larger, not smaller. The mutual gradient is a third the
magnitude of the label gradient, not a rounding error.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. Disagreement is NECESSARY, not SUFFICIENT. distill_pairs (+0.0016, under the
floor) was our own fold-0 twins and would show the same ratio; mutual training still did not extract it.
This licenses a run, it does not predict a gain.

OWNER'S EXTENSION 2026-09-18 (K=3-5, per-epoch, success-weighted layer supervision), answered:
  * K: buy K=2 first. 2 x 4.5 h = 9 h. Cohort size is a knob bought AFTER the mechanism shows signal.
    Zhang et al.'s K gains are on HETEROGENEOUS cohorts (ResNet32/MobileNet/WRN); ours are copies.
  * PER-EPOCH: yes, and it is what makes this runnable at all. Simultaneous K does not fit - an arm
    declares --vram-gb 22 on a 32 GB card, so a 3-way at the shipping corner would have to change batch
    or image size and would no longer price the corner we ship. Cycle K through the card one at a time,
    each epoch reading peers' logits cached from THEIR previous epoch. 1x VRAM, Kx wall-clock, never a
    second job of ours on the card. Anil et al. 2018 showed that staleness is tolerable.
  * SUCCESS-WEIGHTING: flip the sign or drop it. Per-epoch cohort score gaps sit inside the 0.0062
    paired floor, so the weights fit noise; and upweighting last epoch's winner is positive feedback
    that collapses the cohort toward one model, destroying the disagreement measured above. Inverse
    (hold the cohort apart) or flat. KDCL (CVPR 2020) weights by loss and hits this instability.

PRICE: ~9 h (K=2, 36 epochs, sequential). P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.08. Deliverable is ONE checkpoint - DML is
a training-time regulariser, not an ensemble, so it does not violate the one-solo mandate.
PLAN + PRE-REGISTRATION 2026-09-18 06:55Z.

PRICE CORRECTED. The 9 h quoted an hour ago scaled the full-corpus refit (4407 studies, ~450 s/epoch
wall at 36 epochs = 4.5 h). The mechanism test runs on the HONEST split, 3498 studies, ~355 s/epoch, and
24 epochs is enough to see a regulariser. So K=2 is 2 x 2.4 h = ~4.7 h, and K=3 is ~7.1 h.
PRICE: ~4.7 h. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.08. P(clears the 0.0062 paired floor) ~ 0.3.

DESIGN.
  * SEQUENTIAL, NEVER SIMULTANEOUS. One model on the card at a time, alternating epochs: A1 B1 A2 B2 ...
    An arm declares --vram-gb 22 on a 32 GB card, so a simultaneous cohort at the shipping corner would
    have to cut batch or image size and would stop pricing the corner we ship. Sequential is 1x VRAM,
    Kx wall-clock, and never a second job of ours on the card.
  * PEER LOGITS CACHED ON DISK. Each model writes its predictions over the TRAINING studies at the end of
    each of its epochs; the next model reads the peer's most recent cache. 3498 x 12 float32 = 168 KB per
    epoch per model, so storage is free. This is Anil et al. 2018's stale-peer trick and they showed the
    staleness is tolerable.
  * EPOCH 1 IS PURE SUPERVISED for both - there is no peer cache yet. DML warms the same way.
  * ATTACH AT THE OUTPUT, not at features, for the first point. Standard DML is a KL between output
    posteriors; feature-level is a second variable and kneemri.training.feature_distillation already
    read FLAT on its own. One variable.
  * LAMBDA = 1. Not a guess: the measured peer/supervised ratio is 0.284-0.415, so unit weight puts the
    mutual gradient at about a third of the label gradient, which is the regime DML reports its gains in.
  * COLD, NOT WARM. Both models train from scratch. Warm-starting from converged members reinstates the
    converged-teacher setting that all four null distillation rows already tested.
  * NO SUCCESS-WEIGHTING in the first point - see the note above on positive feedback and cohort collapse.

READING. Honest split, so a ledger row prices it. Control is the matched 24-epoch honest member; paired
floor 0.0062. Report at ledger75, not midpoint.

PRE-REGISTRATION (offline75 against the matched control).
  >= +0.0062  the mutual term carries; refit --fold -1 and spend a slot on the solo.
  +0.002 to +0.0062  directional only. Does NOT license K=3 - buy cohort size after the mechanism shows,
    never before (stage-gated rigor). It licenses one confirmation seed and nothing else.
  <= +0.002  the peer disagreement measured above is real but a mutual term does not extract it, which
    is the same verdict distill_pairs reached from the other direction. Close the family on MECHANISM
    (state what it does NOT rule out: feature-level attachment, heterogeneous cohorts) rather than on
    the number alone.

DELIVERABLE IS ONE CHECKPOINT. DML is a training-time regulariser; the cohort is scaffolding and is
discarded. This does not violate the one-solo mandate.

PRICE RE-PRICED AGAIN 2026-09-18 07:40Z, DOWNWARD, on a measured epoch rate.
The 4.7 h above assumed ~355 s/epoch. headlr_ship_s2026's own log measures ~222 s/epoch on the honest
split at the shipping corner. K=2 x 24 epochs = 48 epochs x 222 s = 2.96 h, plus 4 peer-reading passes
over the training split ~0.5 h.
PRICE: ~3.5 h. P(clears the 0.0062 paired floor) ~ 0.30. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.08.

AMENDMENT: THE PEER TERM IS THE ORDERING TERM, NOT A KL. This bead's DESIGN section says 'attach at the
output ... standard DML is a KL between output posteriors'. Audit contradicts it and the disagreement
decides how many variables the arm moves. teacher_targets.py states distill_weight is a pairwise
ORDERING term and argues explicitly against KL: 'Not the usual KL on softened probabilities, which
targets calibration the metric discards.' All four null distillation rows cited above used the ORDERING
term with a CONVERGED teacher. So DML-with-ordering moves exactly ONE variable against distill_pairs -
teacher liveness - where DML-with-KL moves two and could not be read against that row at all. It also
needs no new plumbing: --teacher-targets + --distill-weight already carry it.

CADENCE MECHANISM BUILT AND COMMITTED ae71f68b, zero card. --stop-after-epoch bounds the LOOP while
one_cycle stays built for the full --epochs (run_setup.py:571). Lowering --epochs instead COMPRESSES the
anneal into a different recipe, which patience.py already legislates verbatim and measured head to head
(8-epoch cycle leads at epoch 0, 0.7510 vs 0.7393, and trails at the end, 0.8429 vs 0.8457). So a round
is Patience's mechanism with a deterministic trigger, and the epochs either side of an exchange are the
epochs the arm was priced for.

RESUME-ACROSS-ROUNDS VERIFIED 2026-09-18 07:44Z, by reading rather than by running.
RunMetrics.begin() 'moves any PREVIOUS run's epochs AND ARTEFACTS aside', which looked like it would
delete what round 2 resumes from. _artefacts() moves exactly two files - the checkpoint .pt and the
.holdout.npz - and resume reads NEITHER: fitting.py:263 'the weights come from the .partial and the
trajectory from the .resume', both under destination.with_suffix(). Nothing rotates those. The rotation
is a gift rather than a risk: round 2 keeps round 1 as _run1.pt + .metrics.1.jsonl, round 3 as _run2, so
the cross-round trajectory keeps itself and the arm copies nothing aside.
WHAT THE CARD DOES WHEN THIS ARM FREES IT (~11:35Z), decided 2026-09-18T08:20Z BEFORE the result, so it is not decided late.

Context from our own audit (2026-09-18_state_of_the_levers.md, CORRECTION section): the OOF rotation is forbidden on ratio (~9 h for a ~1.1 sigma knob read), neither queued refit can win (ADDITIVE puts depth24_ff_long36 at 0.946 and headlr_ship_ff at 0.942, CEILING puts both at 0.9445, champion is 0.946), and the file's closing line is 'at 0.946 against a 0.957 leader, we are not one knob away'. Live board read 08:18:47Z: rank 67 of 3931, 0.946, leader 0.957, gap 0.011, closing -0.00016/day.

BRANCH A - this arm clears the 0.0062 floor. The card goes to the owner's own escalation, and it is premise-independent of the spanff instrument because it is a MECHANISM and not a knob: K=3 rather than 2, exchange after every epoch rather than every 8, peer weight set by each model's previous-epoch holdout. Do not write that arm before the read; the read sets which of the three variables moved.

BRANCH B - this arm reads at or below zero. The card HOLDS, it does not get a consolation arm. knee-uh1j5 (spanff, the ~9 sigma ADDITIVE-vs-CEILING instrument) is submitted at the ~12:00Z mark and decides whether ANY honest-base gain is bankable at +0.005 or whether the fit is exhausted at 0.9445. Launching a 3 h arm at 11:35Z spends the card on a premise that instrument may destroy ~90 minutes later. An idle card for ~1.5 h is the cheaper error, and it is an ERROR ONLY if the instrument comes back ADDITIVE.

BRANCH C - directional, under the floor and above zero. Same hold as B. A sub-floor delta does not license a follow-up arm on its own; if spanff then reads ADDITIVE, the directional read plus a bankable base is the argument to escalate.

SLOT PACING at the time of writing: 4 left, (23:30Z - 08:20Z) = 15.2 h / 4 = 3.79 h apart, marks ~12:00Z, ~15:47Z, ~19:34Z, ~23:21Z. spanff pre-flight is already GREEN: submit_check 'ok kneemri-spanff: 1 members, no recorded entry carries this set'.
HARNESS VERIFIED AGAINST THE CONTROL, 2026-09-18T08:22Z, and it is EXACT. Round 1 carries no peer term, so dml_a epochs 0-7 should be headlr_ship_s2026's own trajectory, and they are: loss 1.1897/1.0455/0.9887 against the control's 1.18967/1.04538/0.98865, auc 0.7238/0.7557/0.7851 against 0.7238/0.7557/0.7851. Bit-for-bit. This is a matched PAIRED trajectory rather than a re-run with scatter, so any divergence from epoch 8 is attributable to the peer term alone, with no control arm to run and no seed scatter to subtract.

THE CONTROL'S FULL SERIES (midpoint auc, from headlr_ship_s2026.metrics.jsonl), which is the ruler to read dml_a against epoch by epoch: e0 .7238, e1 .7557, e2 .7851, e3 .8114, e4 .8252, e5 .8310, e6 .8447, e7 .8363, e8 .8547, e9 .8583, e10 .8576, e11 .8636, e12 .8652, e13 .8588, e14 .8668, e15 .8667, e16 .8677, e17 .8702 (PEAK), e18 .8695, e19 .8674, e20 .8674, e21 .8676, e22 .8675, e23 .8676. Note the shape: it is FLAT from e14, peak e17, and the last five epochs move 0.0002. A peer term that is doing anything has to show it in e8-e15, because e16-e23 has no room in it.

EARLY DECISION POINT, which the price did not have before. Order is fit_a 8, fit_b 8, read x2, fit_a 16, fit_b 16, read x2, fit_a 24, fit_b 24. So dml_a's first peer-affected epochs (8-15) run roughly 09:40-10:25Z, and the arm does not finish until ~12:45Z. The mechanism is therefore readable ~2.3 h before the arm ends, against an EXACT control, and kneemri.experiments.trajectory_check is the tool licensed to truncate on it.

RE-PRICE, said out loud: epochs are landing at 264-346 s, not the 222 s the original price assumed. 48 epochs at ~315 s is 4.2 h plus 4 reading passes, so ~4.7 h and a ~12:45Z finish, against the ~3.5 h and ~11:35Z that were priced. The card is healthy - 493 W, 98 percent, 31863 MiB - so this is the recipe's true cost, not contention.

CHECKED AND NOT AVAILABLE: skipping round 1 by warm-starting the cohort off the two bases. Both .partial files exist (89 MB each) but neither .resume does, and resume needs both - fitting.py:263, weights from the .partial and the trajectory from the .resume. Worse, those partials hold the CONVERGED 24-epoch state, not an epoch-7 state, so resuming from them is warm-start DML between two converged peers, which attacks the weak form of the mechanism: Zhang et al.'s claimed carrier is high peer entropy EARLY, and converged peers have little. Recorded so the K=3 escalation does not re-derive it as a saving.
2026-09-18T10:55Z ROUND 2 DONE, ROUND 3 (epochs 16-24) RUNNING. Mid-schedule read, midpoint auc, dml_a against control headlr_ship_s2026: e8 -0.0017, e9 -0.0035, e10 -0.0006, e11 -0.0040, e12 -0.0022, e13 -0.0008, e14 -0.0015, e15 +0.0003. 7/8 negative, mean -0.0018. NOT a baseline offset: the pre-peer epochs e3-e7 read -0.0012/-0.0012/+0.0006/-0.0011/+0.0034, mean +0.0001, so the sign went near-unanimously negative exactly when the peer term switched on -- a shift of -0.0022. e15 is the first crossing. trajectory_check --target 0.8702 (the control's own peak midpoint, same ruler, strictly weaker than the pre-registered +0.0062 ledger75 clear) returns EXIT 0 'still open ... generous ceiling 0.9002', so NO truncation is licensed and the arm runs to e24 as designed. The verdict epoch is 24, not 15. Also: the two _run1 checkpoints this arm rotated aside were roster_check's 2 undocumented members -- now declined in writing as intermediates by construction (they are the same weights the base name held at the end of round 1, so they can never be a distinct seat).
2026-09-18T11:00Z CORRECTION AND A DISCRIMINATOR, both free, no card. (1) A and B differ by EXACTLY ONE flag -- A carries --head-lr 2e-4 and B is labelwise_depth24_drop40_long's line -- so B's matched control is labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 and NOT headlr_ship_s2026. Read against headlr_ship, B looked like -0.0019/5-of-8 and appeared to confirm A's deficit by symmetry; that was an unmatched control and the reading does not stand. (2) Against its OWN control B reads e7 -0.0069, e8 +0.0025, e9 -0.0041, e10 +0.0005, e11 +0.0027, e12 -0.0010, e13 -0.0004, e14 +0.0038, e15 +0.0034 -- n=9, mean +0.0001, 4 negative. FLAT. (3) So the two arms carry the IDENTICAL peer term at the IDENTICAL weight and only A is down. That rules out the loss-budget tax (0.3 of the objective spent on soft targets instead of gold), which is symmetric by construction and would have moved both. It also rules out 'the peer is no better than the student so the term is noise' for the same reason. What is left is either an interaction with the one flag that differs (--head-lr 2e-4: a faster head under a moving target) or nothing at all -- every delta on both arms is far inside the 0.0062 paired floor and a sign count on sub-floor deltas is close to a coin flip, which is this repo's own standing warning. (4) HONEST MID-SCHEDULE STATEMENT: at e15 neither arm shows an effect its ruler can see. The verdict epoch remains 24 and the pre-registered branches are unchanged.
VERDICT 2026-09-18T11:25Z — dml_a CLOSES mutual supervision for this family at w=0.3.

dml_a_s2026  0.9044 ledger75 (0.8687 midpoint, peak e18 of 24)
control headlr_ship_s2026  0.9059 ledger75 (0.8702 midpoint, peak e17 of 24)
delta -0.0015 ledger75, on 909 studies, population eb3ba199.

Fourth pre-registered branch (<= 0.0000): mutual supervision does not pay on this family at this
weight. The peak is e18 and not the last epoch, so this is a verdict and not a void reading.

The per-epoch curve agreed the whole way and never crossed: e16 -0.0024, e17 -0.0020, e18 -0.0008,
e20 -0.0014, e21 -0.0008, e22 -0.0009, e23 -0.0009. A deficit that narrows to -0.0008 and stays
there is not a late payer being cut off; it is a flat loss.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT (the asset is not dead, only this use). It kills w=0.3 pairwise mutual
supervision on the DINOv2 labelwise corner, measured against the best member we own. It says
nothing about a different weight, about supervision at a different layer, or about a teacher that is
not also a student. It does however make the owner's 3-4-5-model extension a WEAK bet rather than a
fresh one: the two-model case is the same mechanism with less of it, and it reads negative on the
strongest trunk we have. Answering this decline means answering that flat curve, not re-quoting a
number.

dml_b is still on the card (round 3, e16-23, ~12:00Z). Its control is the weaker trunk
labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 (0.8679 midpoint), so it can harden this closure to two trunks
but cannot overturn it for the deliverable, which is one solo getting better.

title: Force all 58 gold-annotated studies into the holdout fold
description: Measured 2026-09-18: the 58 radiologist-annotated studies split across folds {0:13, 1:8, 2:16, 3:11, 4:10}, so only 13 are in holdout fold 0. The other 45 can score a member ONLY if that member carried --hold-annotations, making the gold quality check a per-arm accident instead of a property of the ruler. Fix: assign all 58 to the holdout unconditionally in core/data/corpus/folds.py. Costs 45 of 4407 training studies (1.0%) and removes a forgettable flag. Owner directive 2026-09-18: 'the 58 studies should be there (quality test)'. Gold is a CHECK reported beside every number, never a selector - 58 studies cannot rank.
notes:
CLOSED ON RATIO, measured 2026-09-18T08:43Z, zero card. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-18_the_holdout_is_not_the_defect.md.

(1) A SEED CANNOT DO IT. Gold studies per fold {0:13, 1:8, 2:16, 3:11, 4:10}. ReportFolds assigns by sha1(seed:report_text)%folds, so a seed search for all 58 in one fold is (1/5)^58. This needs an EXPLICIT STUDY LIST, i.e. a change to ReportFolds' source of truth, not a re-draw.

(2) THE RULER WOULD NOT RESOLVE US EVEN THEN. Hanley-McNeil sd at AUC 0.85 over the 58: mean per-label 0.062; macro 0.018 independent, 0.046 at corr 0.5. Paired scales the 909-study floor by sqrt(909/58)=3.96 -> 0.0062 becomes ~0.025. (3) COST IT WOULD HAVE TAKEN: ~2.6 h card (control refit under a new split AND --hold-annotation-studies, since --hold-annotations does NOT withhold the rows - 45 of 58 train in fold 0, knee-x4muo) plus the explicit-list change.

(4) BALANCE, the other stated requirement, IS ALREADY SATISFIED: fold 0 vs corpus is inside 1.1 binomial sigma on all twelve findings (worst MCL +0.0141 at sd 0.0126). Nothing to correct.

RE-OPENS ON: more annotation, not a split. ~400 gold studies brings paired resolution under 0.01. That is an acquisition question.
