title: Slice coverage at the shipping corner: 36 slices with the labelwise aggregator already in place
description:
PRICE: ~2.4 h
P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.25

THE CELL. Slice coverage has been measured twice and both readings are facts about a 12-epoch wall, on a recipe that is not the one we ship. stack224_s2026 read all 36 slices of a 30-40 slice volume with --slice-pooling max and landed 0.8476 midpoint against native224's 0.8502. Its own header diagnosed that as an AGGREGATOR failure rather than a coverage failure: the expected maximum of a set of noisy per-slice scores grows with the SIZE of the set, so a max over 36 candidates carries a strictly higher noise floor than one over 20. The evidence for the diagnosis is the SHAPE, not the mean - a twelve-label mean of -0.0026 hides Lateral Meniscus -0.0263 and Fracture -0.0180 against a nine-label rise (Synovitis +0.0101, ACL +0.0041). cover_labelwise_s2026 then moved exactly one flag, the aggregator, and recovered +0.0044 over stack224 to 0.8495 - back to flat against native224, and no further.

WHY THE CELL IS STILL OPEN. Neither arm is the shipping recipe. Both peaked at epoch 9 with no regulariser, which is the harness knee-kiss9 measured to BIND (+0.0111 from --slot-dropout 0.40 plus --epochs 24 on a matched plain recipe), so both numbers are facts about a wall in the same way the aux-objective family's twelve were. And the shipping corner ALREADY pools labelwise, so the aggregator objection that sank stack224 is answered by construction here rather than by a repair.

THE MECHANISM, AND WHY IT IS NOT A KNOB. The two labels stack224 collapsed are the THIN findings - a lesion present on two slices of a volume. Slice count is an INPUT axis: at 24 of a 30-40 slice volume the pipeline discards anatomy it holds, and a thin finding is exactly what an incomplete sample misses. Fracture is the shipping solo's weakest column (0.8650 against its 0.9059 mean, 0.040 under), and Lateral Meniscus is mid-table. If coverage recovers half the stack224 collapse on those two columns the twelve-label mean gains ~0.005.

ARM: headlr_ship's recipe, one flag moved, --slices 24 -> 36.
CONTROL: headlr_ship_s2026, 0.9059 ledger75, already on disk. No control arm is bought.
CONFOUND, PRE-MEASURED: 36 slices at 224 px will not fit at --batch 10, so the batch drops. batch_teardown already ran the control's own recipe at batch 6 where 12 is affordable and read 0.8598 against 0.8578, +0.0020, inside the floor and on the positive side - the batch is not a lever at this operating point. So the batch change is a named, measured-null confound rather than an unmeasured one.

PRE-REGISTRATION (delta = the arm minus headlr_ship_s2026, ledger75):
  >= +0.0040  slice coverage is a lever at the shipping corner. The member is a ship candidate and the
              axis re-opens at 48.
  +0.000..+0.004  directional. Keep for the pool, spend no slot.
  <= 0.000    coverage is closed at the shipping corner too, on a harness that cannot be blamed, and
              the 36-slice cell is done at three readings.
  CONCENTRATION: the gain must concentrate on the THIN findings (Fracture, Lateral Meniscus, Medial
  Meniscus). A uniform lift across all twelve REFUTES the mechanism - it would be budget or batch, not
  coverage - and a lift concentrated in the thick findings (Synovitis, ACL, Effusion) refutes it too.

title: An arm cannot RESUME its own schedule, so a machine restart costs the whole run
description:
A session/OS restart at 21:15Z killed headlr_ship at epoch 14 of 24 (holdout 0.8659, climbing, anneal not yet run) and the arm had to be relaunched from epoch 0 — 96 minutes of card to recover 60 minutes of work. This is the general gap the owner named: 'the no warm start is something you have to work on in general'.

TWO DEFECTS, ONE COST.

(1) FIXED IN THIS COMMIT. Trainer.save_partial did temp-then-rename with no fsync. The rename is atomic against a dying PROCESS, not a dying MACHINE: NTFS journals the size while the data blocks sit in cache, so a restart leaves a file of exactly the right length whose tail is zeros and which has no zip central directory. Measured on the dead artefact — 89409675 bytes, valid PK header, tail_all_zero True, 35.7% zero bytes overall, and torch.load raises PytorchStreamReader failed reading zip archive. Its own docstring claimed 'a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated file behind either'. It can, and did. The fix flushes and fsyncs the temp handle before replace.

(2) STILL OPEN, AND THE LARGER HALF. Even an intact .partial cannot continue the run. The only re-entry the trainer has is WarmStart, which loads weights and starts a FRESH one_cycle — a different learning-rate trajectory, so an arm resumed that way is no longer the single-knob comparison it was armed as, and its number may not be compared to its control. That is why the relaunch was from scratch rather than from the 0.8659 weights.

DESIGN. save_partial's payload already carries weights, holdout and epoch (it was widened once already, for MemberPackage's fingerprint). Widen it once more to carry optimizer.state_dict(), the LR scheduler's state_dict() and the epoch index, and add a --resume <checkpoint> that restores all three and continues the SAME schedule from that epoch. The constraint that PROVES it: a run trained 24 epochs straight and a run killed at epoch 14 and resumed must agree on the holdout to within float noise, on a fixed seed. That equality is the whole feature — anything that does not satisfy it is WarmStart again under a new name.

The cost is bounded: optimizer state for this trunk is roughly the weight size again, so .partial goes from ~90 MB to ~250 MB, written once per improving epoch. Disk is not the constraint; an hour of card is.
notes:
PROVEN 2026-09-18T06:30Z. Defect (2) was already IMPLEMENTED — kneemri/training/resume.py exists, ResumeState is captured and written beside the weights on every keep (fitting.py:206), resumed() restores optimiser/schedule/scaler plus all four RNG streams, and epochs() starts at the restored epoch. The bead text saying it is 'STILL OPEN, AND THE LARGER HALF' was stale.

What was genuinely missing was this bead's OWN proving constraint. Unit tests covered capture/write/beside/restore mechanically; nothing asserted the end-to-end equality, and an unverified resume is the failure this module exists to prevent — it loads, logs 'continuing the same schedule', and is WarmStart under a new name.

tests/integration/interrupted_run_to_checkpoint.py now makes the claim: a run killed at epoch 2 and resumed to 4 lands within 1e-6 of the straight 4-epoch run, on identical epoch and holdout. A second test is the negative control — four epochs must differ from two by more than the tolerance, so the equality cannot pass by measuring nothing. Synthetic corpus, CPU, 31 s, no card and no real data. ruff/format/pyrefly clean.

Cost recovered: headlr_ship lost 96 min of card to a restart at epoch 14 of 24. Long arms now run at 36 epochs (~2.7 h), so the exposure was growing.

  0.939 .. 0.941   refit term +0.004 to +0.006. Agrees with pair 1 inside scatter. The term is a
                   CONSTANT near +0.004 and the champion path may multiply by it.
  >= 0.942         refit term <= +0.003, possibly zero. The premium is thinner than carried; a
                   headlr winner refits to ~0.948-0.949 rather than 0.951. Still over the champion,

  <= 0.938         refit term >= +0.007, over pair 1 by more than 2 sd. The term is MEMBER-SPECIFIC,

WHAT IT CANNOT DO. It cannot beat the champion — 0.940 predicted against 0.946 pinned. It is spent on the constant, not on the rank, and the submission message must say INSTRUMENT.

title: ledger75 --holdouts prices every npz against its own baked-in truth without checking consistency; rescore_t1_ruler over-refuses on soft targets
description:
THE DEFECT. `python -m kneemri.evaluation.ledger75 --holdouts <dir>` prices every npz on disk into ONE flat ranking and never checks that the members share a truth table. Each member's holdout npz carries its OWN truth array, baked in at training time from whatever --labels/--eval-labels the arm passed. A member whose arm passed a non-v2 table is scored against its own ruler and printed in the same column as everything else.

EVIDENCE, already on disk, no card and no slot. research/scripts/rescore_t2_deletions_ruler.out.txt:3 reads 'npz scanned: 448; kept: 391; excluded: 57' and names six members refused with 'truth array disagrees with reference after alignment':

  confident224_s2026
  oof_band_fold0_s2026
  ortholarge@focal-attend_mean_probe
  radnet121@focal-max_mean_probe
  recal_holdannot_s2026
  v3large@focal-attend_mean_probe

The rescore script refuses them. ledger75 --holdouts ranks them. RecordMix.per_member also refuses them ('Truth is checked against the first member's for every other member'), which is why an ENTRY built from such a member fails while a RANKING containing it passes.

WHAT IT ALREADY COST. recal_holdannot_s2026 ranks #1 of 430 on midpoint (0.8964) and #11 on ledger75 (0.9004) — it moves +0.0040 between the rulers where every other member moves +0.031 to +0.038, because its truth is not the one the move is defined against. comp/members.declines:84 states in capitals that its 0.8964 is a ruler artefact (--labels v3 with --eval-labels unset, so the holdout truth was binarised against the RE-MAPPED values and the ruler moved with the arm); its honest proxy on report_labels_v2 is 0.8515. It was one grep away from being picked as a slot instrument on the strength of that #1.

THE LIVE EXPOSURE. Five of the six are declined in writing and unshippable. oof_band_fold0_s2026 is ON comp/members.roster — shippable — and its roster line quotes '0.8522 midpoint on the 909' and compares it directly to res392_ws_s2026 0.8523 and extended_ws_s2026 0.8459. Those three numbers are not on one ruler. Never seated in a shipped entry (0 mentions in comp/board.jsonl), so no board row is wrong today; the roster line is what would put it in one.

THE FIX. ledger75 --holdouts adopts the check RecordMix and the rescore script already implement: align each npz's truth against a reference member and REFUSE the row, printing the member and the cell count that differs, rather than ranking it. A flag releases it for a deliberate cross-ruler read. Same family as the entry_offline scope-field bug — a tool that prints a number the record has ruled out will keep putting that number back.

PRICE: ~1 h CPU, no card, no slot. P(clears 0.0062) ~ 0.00 — it is an INSTRUMENT: it retires the class of wrong-ruler readings that has now produced a voided 0.8938 (raptor_solo), eleven of fifteen apparent ruler inversions, and this near-miss slot spend.
notes:
MECHANISM NAMED, for the one rostered member. oof_band_folds.sh:72 is `run_train oof_band_fold${fold} $RECIPE --fold $fold --epochs 8 ... --labels "$BAND_LABELS" --out ...` where BAND_LABELS=report_labels_v6band50.csv (line 65), and `--eval-labels` is NEVER PASSED. So the holdout truth is binarised against the band table. Identical to the recal_holdannot defect in comp/members.declines:84, produced by a different arm eight days apart, which is what makes it a TOOL defect rather than two mistakes: nothing between the arm and the roster asks whether --eval-labels was set when --labels was overridden.

CHEAPEST PARTIAL FIX, ahead of the ledger75 work: arm_check refuses an arm that passes --labels without --eval-labels. That is a string check on the flag line, it costs no card, and it closes the SOURCE while the ranking fix closes the READING. Both are needed — six members already on disk carry the bad truth and no future-facing gate retires them.

DONE 2026-09-17: comp/members.roster's oof_band_fold0 entry rewritten. It quoted 0.8522 midpoint and compared it to res392_ws_s2026 0.8523 and extended_ws_s2026 0.8459 — three numbers on two rulers. The line now states the constraint and marks the member unseatable until re-scored against v2. No board row was ever built from it (0 mentions in comp/board.jsonl), so nothing shipped is wrong.

STILL OPEN: the ledger75 --holdouts refusal, and the arm_check --eval-labels rule.
CORRECTION 2026-09-17T21:03Z — THE MECHANISM NAMED IN THIS BEAD WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS THE ROSTER LINE IT PRODUCED. Measured, not argued:

1. `Ruler(report_labels_v2.csv).moved_cells(Ruler(report_labels_v6band50.csv))` = 0. Both tables are 4406x12 over identical studies and identical columns. So `--labels v6band50` with `--eval-labels` unset CANNOT have moved this ruler, and the 'repeats across two arms eight days apart' reading collapses: there is one arm with a moved ruler (recal_holdannot), not two.

2. `arm_check` ALREADY HAS the rule I filed here as the cheapest partial fix — `arm_check.py:610-623`, landed 2026-08-30 (`1ae5e2e9`), built for knee-8wa0. It is keyed correctly (compares the named table to DEFAULT_LABELS and counts moved cells via `Ruler`), NOT on '--eval-labels absent'. It does not refuse `oof_band_folds` because `moved_cells` is 0 — correct behaviour, nothing to refuse. It does not refuse `headlr_floor` either (checked: 1 arm, 0 refused). NOTHING TO BUILD HERE. Do not re-file it.

3. THE REAL AXIS IS SOFT-TARGET CONSTRUCTION. The holdout npz `truth` stores the SOFT training target, not a binary label. Reference (`band_span_s2026`) grid: {0, 0.08, 0.28, 0.68, 0.82, 0.94}. Arms that change target softness (band smoothing, --calibrated-targets, confidence weighting) write a different array while the BINARY ruler may be untouched.

4. `rescore_t1_ruler.py:140` OVER-REFUSES. It tests `np.allclose` on the soft array, but `macro_auc` (:72-79) consumes only `>= 0.5`. Binarised against the reference:
     oof_band_fold0_s2026                soft 1318   BINARY     0  -> SAME RULER, false positive
     confident224_s2026                  soft 3161   BINARY  3161  -> real
     recal_holdannot_s2026               soft 10752  BINARY  1319  -> real
     ortholarge\@focal-attend_mean_probe  soft 10784  BINARY    32  -> real
     radnet121\@focal-max_mean_probe      soft 10784  BINARY    32  -> real
     v3large\@focal-attend_mean_probe     soft 10784  BINARY    32  -> real
   One of six exclusions is spurious, and it is the ONLY rostered one — i.e. the only live exposure this bead opened was not an exposure. FIX: binarise before comparing, or compare on `>= 0.5` and keep the soft array for provenance only.

5. ROSTER CORRECTED. The line now records 0.8522 as comparable with the binary evidence, and states that v6band50 is not the mechanism. The earlier line claimed the number 'MAY NOT be compared to res392_ws_s2026 0.8523' — false.

STILL TRUE AND STILL OPEN: `ledger75 --holdouts` prices every npz against its own baked-in truth and does not check truth-table consistency, while `RecordMix.per_member` does. That is the defect this bead is for. But its severity is lower than filed: the check that would catch a genuinely moved ruler exists on the arm side, and the one member it was supposed to have let through is clean.

LESSON: I named a mechanism from a flag line and a filename WITHOUT running the comparison the repo already had a class for (`Ruler.moved_cells`), then wrote it into a roster comment and committed it. The comparison cost one command.
OPEN HALF LANDED 2026-09-18T01:15Z — the ledger75 --holdouts refusal, built INTO `population` rather than beside it.

`LedgerSeventyFive.population` digested only the study ids. It now digests the truth alongside them, in one canonical study order. A population is the studies AND the table that graded them, so a member on a moved table falls into a population of its own — which `table` already refuses to interleave and `--only` already refuses to span. No new flag and no new branch; the machinery that stops a 4406-study record outranking the 909 now stops a moved ruler too. The --only message was rewritten because it read "spans 2 study populations ([909] studies)", which looks like a tool bug when both rows are 909.

VERIFIED: `--only recal_holdannot_s2026 headlr_ship_s2026` refuses; the default sweep gains a divider instead of a silent row; 980 unit tests pass; two new equivalence-class tests (moved table separates, record order does not).

THE EXPOSURE IS NOW BOUNDED BY MEASUREMENT, and it is SMALLER than this bead states. All 458 holdout records on disk were fingerprinted by their truth arrays: 451 carry the corpus rungs, 5 are the `oof_band` fold targets (continuous by construction, not a defect), and exactly TWO carry another table — `recal_holdannot_s2026` and `confident224_s2026`. The six members the rescore script named are not six moved rulers; that matches this bead's own CORRECTION (v6band50 moves 0 cells) and confirms README:10701 by measurement.

AND `confident224_s2026` IS NOT A WRONG-RULER READING. Re-scored on the corpus truth it moves EXACTLY 0.0000: its table only shifts a rung 0.28 -> 0.50, inside a gap the 0.75 cut cannot see. So ONE member in the whole pool is on a moved ruler. That is also the supervision-side arrival of `cut_sweep.py`'s three-ruler collapse — a rung move that crosses no cut is not a ruler move.

NEW NUMBER FOR recal_holdannot_s2026, which this bead and comp/members.declines:84 only carry at midpoint (0.8515 proxy / 0.8964 log): its honest LEDGER75 on the corpus truth is 0.8888 against the 0.9004 it was ranked at. +0.0116 of promotion, ~2x the paired floor and ~1.4x the board gap. Against `headlr_ship_s2026` on one ruler it loses ELEVEN of twelve columns; its only win is MCL +0.0221.

WHY IT STILL COST SOMETHING TODAY. `interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-17_member_candidates.md`, written one day ago, ranked that 0.9004 and named the member per-finding leader on SIX of twelve columns by +0.0073 to +0.0423 — with declines:84 stating the defect in capitals the whole time. An oracle ceiling computed off that table reads +0.0215 over our best member and is not real. The document is corrected at the source with a banner and the row marked. Third instance of the `entry_offline` scope-field pattern: a tool that prints a number the record has ruled out will keep putting it back, and prose cannot stop it — which is the argument for putting this in `population` rather than in a doc.

Evidence: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-18_the_cut_is_not_what_exhausted_our_ruler.md, final two sections.

title: headlr_floor: the third point on head_lr at the shipping corner
description:
THIRD POINT ON THE ONLY UNPRICED LEAF WITH A MEASURED GRADIENT. `head_lr` is 0.001 in 286 of 288 runs
in this project's corpus: it is a silent default, not a tuned value. The corpus holds exactly one
isolating pair, at the 224/max corner, 0.005 -> 0.0002 reading +0.0106 ledger75. Shipping sits INSIDE
that interval, so the local sign at the shipping corner is assumed, not measured.

`headlr_ship` (knee-xuarh) takes the second point at 2e-4. This takes the THIRD at 5e-5, which is what
turns two points into a SHAPE. That is the design that closed the depth axis today (4 -> 6 -> 7 blocks:
+0.0129 per block to six, then -0.0012 past it), and it is informative in BOTH branches:

  - if 2e-4 BEATS the 0.001 control, 5e-5 says whether the gradient continues or has turned over;
  - if 2e-4 LOSES, 5e-5 confirms the shipping corner is already at the optimum and CLOSES the axis.

A two-point read cannot distinguish "monotone down" from "0.001 is past a flat top", which is exactly
the error knee-dry3h caught on weight_decay: the +0.0106 there decomposed into 0.005->0.02 +0.0077 and
0.02->0.1 +0.0029, so the curve was BAD -> FLAT TOP -> FLAT and most of the headline was "0.005 is too
little". Without a third point head_lr is open to the same misreading.

CONTROL. `labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026` = 0.8679 midpoint / 0.9053 ledger75, peak e18 of 24.
Same control as `headlr_ship`, so the three points share one baseline.

THE FLAG LINE IS labelwise_depth24_drop40_long's BYTE FOR BYTE plus `--head-lr 5e-5`. --batch 10 and
--vram-gb 28 may not move: RECIPE carries --rank-weight 1.0, whose pairwise population IS the batch
(head_trial.py:231), so a batch trim makes this measure two knobs. If it OOMs, lower --slices.

PRICE: ~1.7 h
P(clears 0.0062) ~ 0.12
notes:
RESULT 2026-09-18 00:41Z — the head_lr axis has a SHAPE and 2e-4 is at its top. Three points, one variable, same recipe otherwise, all 909-study holdout:
  head_lr 1e-3  labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026  0.8679 midpoint / 0.9053 ledger75
  head_lr 2e-4  headlr_ship_s2026                    0.8702 / 0.9059  (peak e17 of 24)
  head_lr 5e-5  headlr_floor_s2026                   0.8652 / 0.9011  (peak e17 of 24, converged)
The floor is the WORST of the three by 0.0048 ledger75 against the top — still inside the 0.0062 paired
floor, so DIRECTIONAL, not a result. What it does establish is the SIGN of the second derivative: the
axis is not monotone, 2e-4 is not an edge, and there is nothing below it. Axis CLOSED — no further
head_lr arm is worth a card. It also cost nothing to learn: the arm was already queued.
The knob is board-invisible either way (headlr_ship's +0.0006 over the anchor compresses to ~+0.0007,
below the competition's own 0.001 resolution) — kneemri-headlrsolo read 0.937 and that was a reading
about the transfer LINE, never about this knob.

title: head_lr at the shipping corner: the head runs 25x the trunk and nobody has measured it there
description:
PRICE: ~1.5 h (222 s/epoch x 24, measured off labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026.full.log). P(clears 0.0062) ~ 0.25.

The shipping arm names neither --head-lr nor --weight-decay; both are silent defaults (0.001 and 0.02). head_lr has exactly one isolating pair in the whole corpus, at the 224/max corner: headlr224 0.005 -> headlr224_slow 0.0002 reads +0.0106 midpoint, CLEARS the 0.0062 paired floor. Shipping sits at 0.001, INSIDE that interval, so the local sign is assumed and not measured - that is the hypothesis this buys.

Mechanism, and why it should be stronger at the shipping corner than where it was measured: backbone_lr is pinned at 4e-5 while head_lr sits 25x above it. The 224 pair ran slice-pooling max, whose head is one shared projection. Shipping runs labelwise, whose head is twelve per-label projections - far more head parameters chasing the same twelve columns. A head moving 25x faster than its trunk fits those columns before the trunk has adapted, and the labelwise head has more capacity to do it with.

Chosen over the weight_decay candidate (same +0.0106, decay224_high 0.1 vs decay224_low 0.005) because weight_decay is a regulariser and three independent regularisers already read flat at this corner: slot_dropout 0.4 -> +0.0018 and +0.0005, stochastic_depth 0.05 -> +0.0003. A fourth into a saturated corner is the weaker bet. head_lr is a rate ratio, not regularisation.

Single flag on the shipping line: --head-lr 2e-4. Control is labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026, on disk, same line - no control run owed.
notes:
Composition audit finished 2026-09-17 ~19:47Z. The shipping corner is at corpus-best on every priced leaf but this one and weight_decay: intensity_aug=False, image_size=336, mixup=0.0, slices=24, epochs=24, backbone_lr=4e-5, calibrated_targets=True (4 clearing pairs, all agreeing), variant=small (base->small +0.0005, ortholarge->small inside floor), labels=v2 (wins its own eight-way axis by +0.0066, see interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-17_labels_axis_is_measured_and_v2_wins_it.md), slice_pooling=labelwise (beats max in 4 of 6), train_fraction=full. slot_dropout and stochastic_depth are saturated at this corner.

Aggregator axis closed while auditing: moments_wide had the highest in-family number (0.8946) and no cross-family pair, which looked like an unexploited structural lever. calib_dense_hold_s2026 IS moment_wide_s2026's flag line with --slice-pooling max in place of moments_wide, byte-for-byte otherwise, and reads 0.8949 — a -0.0003 flat that recipe_pairs simply failed to detect as isolating. moments_wide buys nothing over max.

TOOL FACT worth carrying: recipe_pairs prices on LEDGER75, not midpoint. confident_span prints 0.8785, which is its ledger75; its midpoint is 0.8449. Every delta cited in this bead is therefore ledger75.
=== BANDS PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-17T20:27Z, BEFORE THE ARM LANDED (~21:52Z) ===

Control: labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 = 0.8679 midpoint / 0.9053 ledger75, peak e18 of 24.
Read on LEDGER75 as the deciding ruler, midpoint reported beside it. Paired floor 0.0062.
Order of operations on landing, no number quoted before it: convergence_check --run <metrics path>
FIRST, then ledger75 --holdouts D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality --only headlr_ship_s2026
labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026, then reading_check, then a roster line or a written decline.

  CLEARS   ledger75 delta >= +0.0062  -- head_lr is a real lever at the shipping corner, not a silent
                                         default. headlr_floor (knee-h25fx) then locates the optimum,
                                         and a shipping refit becomes arguable on the third point.
  DIRECTIONAL  +0.0000 .. +0.0062     -- keep, do not plan around it, do not call it a finding.
                                         headlr_floor decides whether the gradient continues.
  CLOSED   <= 0.0000                  -- 0.001 is at or past the optimum; headlr_floor confirms from
                                         below and the axis closes in both directions, as depth did.

WHY A THIRD POINT IS OWED IN EVERY BRANCH, INCLUDING THE WIN. Two points give a sign, not a shape. The
corpus' one isolating pair on this key (0.005 -> 0.0002, +0.0106 ledger75, taken at the 224/max corner)
brackets shipping without measuring it, and knee-dry3h showed exactly how that misreads: weight_decay's
+0.0106 decomposed into 0.005->0.02 +0.0077 and 0.02->0.1 +0.0029, so the curve was BAD -> FLAT TOP ->
FLAT and the headline was mostly "0.005 is too little". head_lr is open to the same error until 5e-5 is
read. `experiments/after_headlr_ship.sh` is armed and gating on `ARM DONE headlr_ship`.

EARLY TRAJECTORY, informational only, not a band: e1 holdout mean AUC 0.7558 at 250 s/epoch, so 24
epochs lands ~21:52Z. An e1 number is not evidence about e18 and is recorded here only to date the run.
RESTARTED FROM EPOCH 0 AT 21:27Z. A machine restart at ~21:15Z killed the first run at epoch 14 of 24 — holdout 0.8659 and still climbing, with the one_cycle anneal not yet run, so that number is a FLOOR and not this arm's reading. The e14 artefacts are archived at $MODELS/dead/e14_headlr_ship_s2026.* and are NOT a result: the .partial among them is unreadable (valid PK header, tail all zero, no central directory), which is the unflushed-write defect now fixed in Trainer.save_partial and filed as knee-c317d.

The relaunch is byte-identical to the original arm — same script, no flags moved — and the recipe line in the new log confirms head_lr 0.0002 against backbone_lr 4e-05, epochs 24, fold 0, slice_pooling labelwise, slot_dropout 0.4. Launched 21:27Z at ~230 s/epoch uncontended, so it lands ~23:02Z. The pre-registered bands are unchanged: CLEARS at >= +0.0062 over the 0.8679 control, DIRECTIONAL in 0..+0.0062, CLOSED at <= 0.

Not warm-started deliberately: the only re-entry the trainer has is WarmStart, which begins a FRESH one_cycle, and an arm resumed on a different learning-rate trajectory is no longer the single-knob comparison this arm exists to be. That gap is knee-c317d.
READ 2026-09-17T23:08Z. headlr_ship_s2026 converged, peak e17 of 24: LEDGER 0.8702, LEDGER75 0.9059, 909 rows, population 66c6f231. Baseline labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 0.8679 / 0.9053. Delta +0.0023 midpoint, +0.0006 ledger75, against the pre-registered floor of 0.0062 -> DIRECTIONAL, band 0..+0.0062, NOT CLEARS. It is a knob (--head-lr 1e-3 -> 2e-4) and it landed where a knob lands. Compressed at the top band's ledger75 slope +1.09 the board delta would be ~+0.0007, below the competition's own 0.001 resolution, so it is unmeasurable on the board as an improvement and may not be shipped as one. KEPT: it is free, the mechanism (head no longer outrunning the trunk it reads) is sound, and it is now the highest ledger75 the project owns, so it is the top point of the solo ruler. Added to comp/members.roster and packaged (148 members). trajectory_check called it correctly while live: at e18 it read 0.8695 needing +0.0046 with a median remaining gain of +0.0014.
head_lr 2e-4 shipped as kneemri-headlrsolo (ref 56316099) 2026-09-18 and read board 0.937. The entry claimed nothing about the knob and the reading says nothing about it either: +0.0006 ledger75 is below the board's own 0.001 resolution by construction. The knob stays DIRECTIONAL and free. What the slot bought was the line, not the knob - see comp/SUBMISSIONS.md headlrsolo_v1.
ANSWERED AND CLOSED 2026-09-18T10:10Z. The arm landed 2026-09-17 ~21:52Z as headlr_ship_s2026: 0.9059 ledger75 against the control labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 at 0.9053. Delta +0.0006, well inside the 0.0062 paired floor -- DIRECTIONAL ONLY, not a finding, and not a lever. The hypothesis (head_lr 25x the trunk mis-fits the twelve labelwise projections, so 2e-4 should beat the silent 0.001 default) is not supported at this corner: the 224/max pair's +0.0106 did not reproduce, which is the magnitude non-transfer measured 2026-09-18 (a 224 delta carries its SIGN and never its size). The member is nonetheless the highest-offline75 checkpoint the project owns and has shipped (headlrsolo_v1, ref 56316099, board 0.937) -- so this bead's product is a member, not a knob reading. Consistent with knee-dry3h: knob work at the shipping corner is exhausted in every direction the corpus can price.

title: Unfreeze depth has only ever been tested DOWNWARD: 6->12 blocks is the one live single-flag axis left
description:
PRICE: ~2.2 h
P(clears +0.0062) ~ 0.30

THE AXIS IS LIVE AND THE CORPUS PROVES IT. `unfreeze_depth.sh` ran at BLOCKS=4 on 2026-08-19 and read 0.8320 midpoint against its declared 6-block control `band_dense` 0.8578 -- **-0.0258 midpoint, 4x the paired floor**, converged (peak e6, flat for five after), negative on eleven of twelve labels. (Its own header quotes -0.0137 against a STALER control, wsfold0_e6; the re-based control is band_dense and that is the number used here.) So moving fewer blocks costs a lot. Nobody has ever asked whether moving MORE blocks buys anything: `recipe_pairs` returns ZERO isolating pairs on `unfreeze_last` at any corner, the leaf's shipping value is the DEFAULT 6, and a defaulted leaf is invisible to every audit of the arms themselves (knee-5dx47's general defect).

WHY THIS IS NOT THE CAPACITY AXIS AGAIN. knee-5dx47 refuted WIDTH -- DINOv2-base over DINOv2-small, 4x the parameters, five isolating pairs, median 0.0000 -- and concluded the model is not representation-capacity-bound. Unfreeze depth is a different quantity: not how much trunk EXISTS but how much of it MOVES toward this domain. A wider frozen trunk of natural-image features buying nothing is entirely consistent with a deeper ADAPTATION of the trunk we have buying something, and the 4-block result is direct evidence that this axis has a steep gradient where the width axis has none.

THE ARM. `experiments/arms/unfreeze_full.sh`, single flag `--unfreeze-last 12` (all twelve blocks) on the EXACT corner the existing two points were measured at -- 12 epochs, max pooling, whole-stack, 4e-5, 20 slices, band 0.10-0.90 -- so the comparison needs no new control and the result lands as a THREE-POINT CURVE with two points already on disk: 4 -> 0.8320, 6 -> 0.8578, 12 -> ?

NOT at the shipping corner, deliberately. The shipping corner is 24 epochs with more slices and would cost 6-7 h at twelve unfrozen blocks. This corner is where the axis's other two points live, it is half the wall-clock, and a flat here retires the axis without spending the bigger run. A CLEAR here licenses the expensive corner arm, which is the only thing that would ship.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS, against band_dense 0.8578 midpoint (both points on the same ruler as the existing series):
  >= +0.0120   the axis is a real lever; queue `--unfreeze-last 12` at the shipping corner next
  +0.0062..+0.0119  clears the floor; directional, and still licenses the corner arm
  +0.0000..+0.0061  inside the floor; six blocks is already enough, axis retired
  <= 0.0000    deeper adaptation costs; the curve peaks at six and this axis is CLOSED in both directions

ESCALATION RULE, PRE-REGISTERED: if this arm peaks ON ITS LAST EPOCH the budget is binding at 12 and NO delta may be read -- a fuller unfreeze needs more epochs to anneal, and reading a truncated curve as an axis verdict is the defect `convergence_check` exists for.

MECHANISM, and why it could plausibly carry more than a knob: DINOv2 is pretrained on natural images and knee MRI is far out of that distribution. The standard move in the MRI literature is a full fine-tune; this project has never done one, it has adapted the last six blocks by default since the first arm and never questioned the default. If the generic early blocks are carrying features that do not transfer, six blocks cannot fix it and twelve can.

RISK: VRAM. Twelve unfrozen blocks hold roughly twice the backward state of six at the same batch. Smoke with `arm_check --only unfreeze_full --smoke` before queueing; if it OOMs, drop the batch rather than the block count, since the block count IS the question.
notes:
ARMED AT SEVEN BLOCKS, NOT TWELVE. The card refused both larger points, and the refusal is a
measurement: VRAM is LINEAR at ~1299 MiB per unfrozen block. Twelve asked 36727 MiB, nine asked
32830, both against 30991 MiB free of a 32607 MiB card (arm_check --smoke, 19:00Z and 19:03Z).
Seven asked 30232 and the launcher's gate confirms that figure exactly. LibreOffice holds the
missing ~1.6 GB and is shared by arrangement, not ours to reclaim.

WHY NOT JUST DROP --batch, WHICH THE ARM'S OWN HEADER ORIGINALLY SAID TO DO. RECIPE carries
--rank-weight 1.0, and that term's pairwise population IS the batch (head_trial.py:231, stated in
experiments/after_depth.sh:8). So a batch trim makes this arm measure two knobs at once. The
precedent is labelwise_depth24, which trimmed batch 12->10 to fit 24 slices and had to buy
labelwise_depth20_b10 as a matched control to absorb it. That doubles a 2.2 h arm for P ~ 0.30 and
the ratio does not survive it. The original header instruction is therefore WRONG and is corrected
in experiments/arms/unfreeze_deep.sh: lower the block count, never the batch.

THE STEP IS ONE BLOCK AND THE QUESTION SURVIVES IT, because the measured segment RISES. 4 blocks
0.8320, 6 blocks 0.8578, both midpoint at this corner: +0.0258 over two blocks, +0.0129 per block.
More unfrozen is BETTER in the measured range. The arm asks whether that gradient continues past
six. The step being small is what the fixed batch costs; it is not a weaker question, only a
smaller one.

BANDS, REVISED FOR A ONE-BLOCK STEP, against band_dense = 0.8578 MIDPOINT:
  >= +0.0129   the gradient is undiminished; a larger step is worth buying a batch-matched pair for
  +0.0062..+0.0128  clears the paired floor; gradient persists, attenuated
  +0.0000..+0.0061  inside the floor; the curve has flattened by seven and the axis is retired
  <= 0.0000    the curve peaks at six; axis CLOSED in both directions

ESCALATION RULE UNCHANGED: if this arm peaks ON ITS LAST EPOCH the budget is binding and NO delta
may be read. Run convergence_check BEFORE the delta, not after.

ARM RENAMED unfreeze_full -> unfreeze_deep; reading is unfreeze_deep_s2026.holdout.npz. Smoked
green at 60 studies, launched 19:06Z.
THE SEGMENT THE ARM RESTS ON IS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. The whole case for arming this is that 4 -> 6
blocks rises +0.0258, and that number joins a run from 2026-08-19 to one from 2026-09-03. Two runs
three days apart is exactly the join control_check was built for — adapt_null's famous -0.0338
against this same band_dense turned out to be budget plus eight keys that did not exist in the older
build.

Ran it. unfreeze_depth.sh declares `# control band_dense = 0.8578` and control_check DOES NOT FLAG
IT: clean on all four axes (budget, sourced, ruled, build), while 141 of 173 declared comparisons in
the corpus fail the build test and 11 fail on budget. So the 4-block point and the 6-block control
are the same trainer at the same schedule, and the +0.0129 per block is a segment rather than a
build artefact.

unfreeze_deep.sh now declares the same control line, so the 6 -> 7 point joins the curve under the
same audit instead of being trusted.
READ 2026-09-18T03:19Z, population eb3ba199, 909 studies. unfreeze_deep_s2026 0.8585 midpoint / 0.8865 ledger75, converged, peak epoch 9 of 12. Control band_dense_s2026 0.8578 / 0.8877. So +0.0007 midpoint and -0.0012 ledger75 — FLAT on both rulers, inside the 0.0062 paired floor, with the negative sign on the better ruler. The pre-registered branch was: a flat says the curve has peaked and the axis is closed. It is flat. The +0.0129-per-block gradient measured from 4 to 6 blocks does NOT extend past six, so --unfreeze-last 6 is at its optimum and the adaptation-depth axis is closed. This was also the last member roster_check counted as undocumented; it is now declined in writing.

title: Ship labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff SOLO to measure the full-corpus refit term at n=2
description:
The +0.003 that a --fold -1 --ema whole-corpus refit buys a LONE member is measured by exactly one matched pair (l75solo_v1 0.941 / ffsolo_v1 0.944, same recipe, differing only in whether the holdout fifth was trained on). That term is load-bearing: it sits in the inversion that prices every open arm (0.947 needs +0.0021 offline75, 0.955 needs +0.0089). n=1.

The ensemble dose series does NOT give a second measurement: tripleseat_v2/fullseat_v1/fullseat2_v1 read 0.946/0.946/0.946 over 0/1/2 refit seats, so the term is under 0.001 at a 1-of-8 share and says nothing about the solo end.

labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff is byte-identical to labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 (0.9045 ledger75, CONVERGED) apart from --fold -1 --ema and --out. Shipping it SOLO is the second matched pair.

PRICE: ~0 h card (checkpoint on disk, mounted). One slot.
P(clears 0.944) ~ 0.5 -- the term is unmeasured at n=1, which is the point.

PRE-REGISTRATION (fit: board = -0.1131 + 1.165*offline75, resid sd 0.0017):
  >= 0.944  refit term reproduces at n=2; +0.003 stays in the inversion.
  <= 0.941  term was n=1 scatter; it comes out, and a solo beat of the champion needs +0.0047 not +0.0021.
  0.942-0.943 ambiguous, leans small.

RE-OPENS the comp/members.declines entry for this checkpoint on that decline's own terms: it declined the member as a SEAT ('more data per seat', measured flat at two doses) and explicitly invites re-opening 'by naming a mechanism that is not more data per seat'. This is not a seat; it is the solo end, where the dose series is silent by construction.
notes:
GATE STATE 2026-09-17T17:41Z, all owed gates green for kneemri-extffsolo: submit_check (new member set), mount_check --live (0 refused of 161), kit_check --mounted (341c6586, 0 behind), champion_check, board_read --live (rank 66 of 3897, gap 0.011), and witness_check --members labelwise_ext_drop40_long_ff. It passed at max|diff| 0.00615 of the 0.0312 bound over 8 studies, batch 4, 7 of 12 labels carrying it - 5x inside. No second job went on the card.
READ 0.945 (ref 56312235), clearing the >=0.944 band. Predicted 0.9432 from the honest twin labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 at 0.9045 ledger75 over the solo transfer (0.9402) plus the +0.003 term under test; landed 0.0018 above, inside one residual sd. The refit term REPRODUCES at n=2 and reads slightly larger on this recipe (+0.0048 vs depth24's +0.003) - carry ~+0.004. The inversion stands: 0.947 needs +0.0021 offline75, 0.955 needs +0.0089.

Term = +0.008, against +0.003 on labelwise_depth24_drop40_long: 2.7x apart on two members, beside an ensemble dose series that reads flat (0.946/0.946/0.946) on a seat of this very member. title: A shared study-level aggregation failure is excluded: the residual is near-isotropic across the 12 labels
description:
PRICE: ~0 h (no card). P(clears 0.0062) ~ 0.00 -- INSTRUMENT. It refutes a fourth cause of the class-B per-column holes, and it retires my own focal/peripheral story before it cost a card.

MEASURED on labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026.holdout.npz, 909 studies x 12 labels,
truth cut 0.75, residual taken in RANK space so the labels share one scale despite
prevalence spread. Instrument: scratchpad/shared.py.

  cross-label residual correlation   mean +0.090  median +0.080  max +0.317
  leading PC variance                0.179  0.116  0.102  0.089   <- flat, near-isotropic
  worst  1% of studies carry          1.8% of total residual
  worst  5% of studies carry          8.1%
  worst 10% of studies carry         15.5%   (uniform would be 10%)
  worst 25% of studies carry         35.4%
  ORACLE macro, PC1 projected out    0.9340 (+0.0223 over 0.9117) -- USES TRUTH, upper bound only

A study-level failure -- the model reading the wrong part of the volume, so a study it
gets wrong is wrong on ALL its labels together -- predicts a DOMINANT PC1 and a
CONCENTRATED set of hard studies. Neither is present. The spectrum is flat and the
failure is spread almost uniformly across studies.

SO: a SHARED, STUDY-LEVEL aggregation failure is EXCLUDED. A PER-LABEL one is NOT.

WHY THIS MATTERS: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-11_seat_value_and_the_per_column_label_wall.md
records three refuted causes of the class-B holes -- rarity (Spearman -0.333, p=0.29),
external corpus coverage (MCL +4, Fracture +0, Lateral OA +0) and geometry (reversed).
This is a FOURTH refutation on an axis nobody had tested. Verified new: grep for
'principal component|cross-label correlation|residual correlation|isotropic|PC1' across
interpretations/kneemri/ and experiments/README.md returns nothing.

MY OWN STORY, KILLED BEFORE IT COST A CARD. My per-label table (my statistic, truth cut
0.75, macro 0.9117 -- NOT ledger75's 0.9053) reads:
  Fracture 0.8424, Lateral OA 0.8792, MCL 0.8830, Lateral Meniscus 0.8966 weakest;
  Baker's 0.9561, ACL 0.9458, Medial Meniscus 0.9430 strongest.
I read that as focal/peripheral structures scoring worse and central/diffuse ones better.
That is the GEOMETRY hypothesis, and it is already refuted with the sign REVERSED:
'Widening helps the CENTRAL columns twice as much as the peripheral ones -- the opposite
of the hypothesis', and 'MCL's best band is the NARROWEST' (0.7908 at 0.2-0.8, 0.7869 at
0.1-0.9, 0.7823 at full). Also 'the band acts through TRAINING, not through inference --
the outer slices carry nothing the model would use even if shown them'. DO NOT RE-OPEN IT.

WHAT DOES CONVERGE, and is worth carrying: three of my weak four -- Fracture, Lateral OA,
MCL -- are exactly the three class-B HOLES that note priced independently nine days
earlier on a different instrument (MCL +0.121, Lateral OA +0.121, Fracture +0.115 below a
perfect-truth ceiling), and it states 'MCL's +0.121 hole is real modelling headroom, and so
is Lateral OA's'. Two instruments, two rulers, same three columns.

WHAT IS NOT A LEVER: the fourth weak label, Lateral Meniscus, is class C -- WALLED. The
pool's best members already score at or above its perfect-truth ceiling (v2 contradicted on
89 of 89 dissent cells), so further measured gain there is learned label noise. That also
weakens the lateral-meniscus thread in 2026-08-20_pooling-is-closed-on-the-mean-but-not-on-
lateral-meniscus.md: the label it pre-registered and found moving is the one that is walled.

NOR is the per-label arithmetic a lever. Lifting the weak four to ~0.93 computes to +0.0182
macro. That is an ARITHMETIC IDENTITY, not a mechanism. The label lane is closed TWICE by
exhaustion (2026-08-26, 2026-09-03) and every label-correction arm is negative: confident_span
-0.0116, errors_dense -0.0158, v2_corrected -0.0173, matching knee-dry3h's 26/26 negative on
--label-errors. DO NOT RE-OPEN ON THIS ARITHMETIC.

WHERE THAT LEAVES IT: the class-B holes on MCL / Lateral OA / Fracture are real and now have
FOUR refuted causes (rarity, coverage, geometry, shared study-level aggregation) and one
closed one (supervision). No mechanism is identified. That is an open QUESTION, not a lever,
and it does not earn a card until something names a mechanism that could carry 1.5%.

HONEST LIMITS: one holdout, one split, one seed, one checkpoint. The oracle bound uses the
truth and is not achievable. Rank-space residual is a choice; a probability-space one might
show more shared structure. Per-label AUC noise here is wider than the 0.0062 mean floor and
no per-label interval was computed.
notes:
Interpretation written 2026-09-17: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-17_warm_starting_is_measured_flat_and_has_never_been_tried_at_the_corner.md. 26 arms carry --encoder-weights, ZERO at the shipping corner (labelwise/drop40/24ep). recipe_pairs --key encoder_weights over 284 priced recipes: 6 isolating pairs, 0 clearing the 0.0062 floor; the four warm-vs-cold pairs favour COLD in three of four (+0.0030, +0.0004, +0.0002 to cold; +0.0006 to warm), all taken at ledger75 0.8507-0.8619, i.e. 0.04-0.05 BELOW our 0.9053 corner and on swin/v3small trunks we do not ship. title: The shipping corner is at a local optimum on every defaulted leaf the corpus can price: 22 leaves, not one alternative beats it above the floor
description:
PRICE: ~0 h (card-free, a read of 368 arm scripts joined to holdout records). P(clears 0.0062) ~ 0.00 -- INSTRUMENT. It retires an axis rather than gaining on it.

Generalises knee-5dx47 (DINOv2-base buys nothing over small) from one knob to the whole blind half of the corpus. Instrument: scratchpad/blindspot.py -- joins the stamped recipe defaults onto every arm, so a leaf the corner leaves at its default becomes comparable. Multi-run_train scripts EXCLUDED (20 of 388): the flag parser merges flags across arms and manufactured one false pair before this guard existed.

368 single-arm scripts, 19 at the corner (--epochs 24 --slice-pooling labelwise --slot-dropout 0.40). The stamp holds 70 leaves the corner NEVER NAMES. 22 of them have at least one scored isolating A/B.

RESULT: in every one of the 22, the corner default WINS OR TIES at our band.

  --spacing        spread vs adjacent      5/5 negative,  -0.0076 .. -0.0001
  --label-errors   None vs FLAGS          26/26 negative, -0.028 .. -0.011
  --side-weight    0.0 vs 1.0             12/12 negative, -0.073 .. -0.059
  --contrast-weight 0.0 vs 1.0             9/12 negative, median -0.0013
  --grad-clip      0.0 vs 0.5/1.0          8/10 negative, median -0.0023
  --slot-pooling   attend vs mean          5/6 negative, median -0.0055
  --centre         image vs tissue         3/5 negative, median -0.0009
  --mixup          0.0 vs 0.2/0.4          6/11 negative, median -0.0005
  --train-fraction 1.0 vs 0.5/0.25        24/24 negative (sanity: the ruler is alive)

Only two leaves tilt positive at our band, both inside the 0.0062 floor:
  --weight-decay   0.02 -> 0.1    median +0.0029  (5 pairs, 4/5 positive)
  --warmup         0.15 -> 0.05   median +0.0025  (5 pairs, 4/5 positive)

TWO APPARENT BIG POSITIVES ARE NOT AT OUR CORNER and must not be quoted as levers:
  --rank-weight 1.0 -> 0 reads +0.0938, but the pair is radnet_family 0.6766 -> radnet_pinned
    0.7704, both far below our band, inside the foreign RadNet family.
  --encoder-adapt-depth 0 -> 6 reads +0.0357..+0.0512, but all three sides are 0.6958-0.7470,
    inside the broken encoder-adaptation family. Neither touches a shipping arm.

WHAT THIS RETIRES -- the weight-decay caveat on knee-e9f83, now MEASURED rather than suspected.
That interpretation recorded decay224_low 0.005 0.8714 -> decay224_high 0.1 0.8820 = +0.0106, and
flagged that the corner value 0.02 sits BETWEEN the endpoints so the pair could not price the step
from where the corner is. Supplying the default makes that step exist:
    0.005 -> 0.02 (corner)   median +0.0077   5 pairs, 5/5
    0.02  -> 0.1             median +0.0029   5 pairs, 4/5
So the curve is 0.005 BAD -> 0.02 FLAT TOP -> 0.1 FLAT, and most of +0.0106 was "0.005 is too
little decay", exactly as suspected. The same construction gives --weight-decay the THREE-POINT
CURVE that scratchpad/tri.py found nowhere in 407 arms -- tri.py could not see it because the
middle point is a default and is written in no arm script.

HONEST LIMITS. (1) One alt checkpoint per value, mostly: the many pairs per row share a single
alternative arm compared against many corner siblings, so they are NOT independent replications --
the same limit as knee-5dx47. (2) These are 12-epoch 224 arms; the corner is 24-epoch. A leaf flat
at 12 epochs is not proven flat at 24. (3) 48 of the 70 defaulted leaves have NO isolating pair at
all: unpriced, not flat.

CONSEQUENCES.
(1) lr8e5_ship stays first, now on a third independent ground: --backbone-lr is the only knob where
    the corner value is an ENDPOINT with 4/4 sign agreement upward, and every defaulted leaf the
    corpus can price is already at its optimum. The rate is the last un-probed direction at the corner.
(2) Do NOT spend a card on weight-decay or warmup. Both are inside the floor from where we are.
(3) MECHANISM, the 1.5% question. Third independent line agreeing the model is not capacity-bound
    and not knob-bound: (a) a 4x encoder buys nothing (knee-5dx47), (b) 22 defaulted knobs are all
    at their optimum (here), (c) the 24-epoch arm fits LESS than the 12-epoch one (knee-e9f83).
    The residual is downstream of the encoder and downstream of the optimiser: SUPERVISION QUALITY
    or SLICE-TO-STUDY AGGREGATION. A 1.5% lever has to live there, and knob work cannot reach it.
(4) OPEN: 48 defaulted leaves are unpriced. That is a list, not a lever -- do not spend card on it.
notes: SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-09-18T02:31Z — consequence (1) is now MEASURED and reads the other way. lr8e5_ship_s2026 (backbone-lr 4e-5 -> 8e-5, one flag off the control, 24 epochs, slot dropout 0.40) reads 0.9031 ledger75 against the control's 0.9053: -0.0022, inside the floor, negative. So the rate is not an endpoint to climb at THIS corner, and the 4/4 upward sign agreement in the corpus was an artefact of honest limit (2) — those pairs are 12-epoch 224 arms without slot dropout. The consequence to carry is therefore the STRONGER form of (3): 22 defaulted leaves at their optimum, a 4x encoder buying nothing, AND the rate reading down means knob work at the shipping corner is exhausted in every direction the corpus can price. The residual is downstream of the encoder and the optimiser -- supervision quality or slice-to-study aggregation -- and slicecover36 (knee-jb0ci) is now on the card as the input-side instrument for the second of those.

title: DINOv2-base buys nothing over DINOv2-small: five isolating pairs, median 0.0000, and the corner is right to default to small
description:
CAPACITY IS NOT THE BOTTLENECK. 2026-09-17, zero card, read off arm scripts joined to holdout records already on disk.

WHY THIS WAS ASKED. The directive is to prefer levers whose mechanism could carry 1.5 percent, and knobs are not that. The biggest structural lever nameable on a single DINOv2 is CAPACITY: the shipping corner stamps variant: small (~22M params) and DINOv2-base is ~86M, a 4x. Twenty-one arms in the corpus name --variant base. No arm at the shipping corner names --variant at all except base_champion, which is parked (knee-4zw4n).

WHY NO EXISTING AUDIT COULD SEE IT. small is the DEFAULT, so a small arm carries NO --variant flag. Every pair-finding instrument compares arms that BOTH write the flag, which is why a sweep over --variant returned twenty isolating pairs and not one of them compared base to small: they were all base-vs-foreign or ortholarge-vs-foreign. Supplying the stamped default for the missing side is what makes the comparison exist at all. That is a general defect in how this project audits itself -- A KNOB WHOSE SHIPPING VALUE IS A DEFAULT IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY AUDIT OF THE ARMS THEMSELVES, and --variant is not the only one.

THE READING, ledger75 @909, five isolating pairs (everything byte-identical but --variant):

  base224   base 0.8795  vs  ema224        small 0.8822   +0.0027
  base224   base 0.8795  vs  native224     small 0.8800   +0.0005   <- diff verified by hand
  base224   base 0.8795  vs  through224    small 0.8792   -0.0004
  base224   base 0.8795  vs  holdannot     small 0.8782   -0.0013
  base224   base 0.8795  vs  normcount224  small 0.8748   -0.0048

Sign split 3 up / 2 down, median -0.0004, full range -0.0048 to +0.0027. EVERY delta is inside the 0.0062 paired floor and the median is indistinguishable from zero. Four times the parameters buys nothing measurable.

HONEST LIMIT, stated because it is the weak point. This is FIVE COMPARISONS BUT ONE BASE CHECKPOINT -- base224 against five small siblings. It is not five independent base runs. A sixth pair (base_clean vs batch_teardown, which would have been a second base checkpoint) was DROPPED as a parser artefact, not a result: batch_teardown.sh holds TWO run_train calls and the flag parser splits on the first, merging flags across arms. 20 of 407 scripts are multi-arm; none of the other pairs quoted today or on knee-e9f83 come from one, checked individually.

UNPAIRED BUT CONSISTENT. The other base checkpoints are base_dense 0.8812 and base_clean 0.8887. The best SMALL arms in the corpus are stackfit 0.8962, batch_teardown 0.8895, severity_weight 0.8871, through_dense 0.8867 -- and the shipping small arm is 0.9053, above every base arm the project owns. Not matched comparisons, so not evidence on their own, but they do not contain a hidden base advantage either.

WHAT THIS MEANS MECHANICALLY, and it is the part worth carrying. If a 4x encoder buys zero, the model is NOT representation-capacity-bound, and no amount of trunk is the lever. That agrees with the train-loss reading on knee-e9f83 -- the shipping arm finishes 24 epochs at 0.5600 while a 12-epoch arm finishes at 0.5130, so it is regularisation-bound, not capacity-bound -- and the two arrive at it from independent directions. The bottleneck is downstream of the encoder: supervision quality, or the aggregation from slices to a study-level call. That is where a 1.5 percent mechanism would have to live.

CONSEQUENCES:
  1. The shipping corner should KEEP variant: small. It is not an accident to be fixed.
  2. base_champion (knee-4zw4n) stays parked, and now for a measured reason rather than by default.
  3. DO NOT spend a card on small -> base at the shipping corner. Five pairs at median zero is more
     replication than any other knob in this project has, and the ratio is terrible.
  4. OPEN: audit the other DEFAULTED leaves the same way. --variant was found only because the corner
     stamps it; the stamp holds 93 leaves and 40 are never named by any corner arm.

title: The shipping corner's learning rate was chosen at 12 epochs and never re-asked: 4e-5 loses to ~2x in every isolating pair
description:
PRICE: ~2.6 h of card (the matched cost of labelwise_depth24_drop40_long, knee-9bnkc). Zero submission slots.

P(clears the 0.0062 paired floor) ~ 0.20. P(clears the 1.5% bar) ~ 0.03.

THE HOLE. 18 of 406 arms sit at the shipping corner (--epochs 24 --slice-pooling labelwise --slot-dropout 0.40). Across those 18, labels varied (4 schemes), slices varied (12/20/24), band-low (0.1/0.2), band-high (0.8/0.9), batch (4/10), image-size (224/336), vram-gb (22/24/28) and scheme (4 values). FIXED across all 18: --backbone-lr 4e-5. Corpus-wide, 286 of 334 arms naming the flag use 4e-5, and EVERY arm carrying any other value runs 12 epochs. At 24 epochs the corpus is 36 arms at 4e-5 against exactly 1 at 1e-5, and that one (warm_hislabels) is a warm start whose low rate is by design. So the rate was picked at 12 epochs and carried into the 24-epoch labelwise corner for 41 arms without ever being varied there.

THE AXIS IS PRICED AND IT IS NOT PEAKED AT 4e-5. Sweeping all 333 arms that carry both --backbone-lr and --out for pairs whose every other flag is byte-identical gives 16 isolating pairs. The scored ones, ledger75 @holdout909:

  RAISING the rate, on OUR DINOv2 whole-stack recipe (both diffs verified to touch nothing but the rate):
    llrd224_flat      4e-5 0.8694  ->  llrd224            8.2e-5 0.8737   +0.0043  (2.05x)
    band_dense_llrd   4e-5 0.8765  ->  band_deep_matched  9.8e-5 0.8781   +0.0016  (2.45x)
  RAISING the rate, on Swin (same direction, larger):
    swin_calib_dense  4e-5 0.8479  ->  swin_wholetop        1e-4 0.8509   +0.0030
    swin_calib_dense  4e-5 0.8479  ->  swin_supervised      1e-4 0.8537   +0.0058
  LOWERING it 4x, fresh arms, costs an order of magnitude more than raising it gains:
    ortho_dense       4e-5 0.8748  ->  ortho_fresh_lowlr    1e-5 0.8526   -0.0222
    ortho_pool_read   4e-5 0.8760  ->  ortho_slow_trunk     1e-5 0.8540   -0.0220
    warm_calib_dense  4e-5 0.8916  ->  warm_calib_lowlr     1e-5 0.8910   -0.0006  (warm start, so the trunk is already placed)
  AND THE CEILING IS REAL, between 1e-4 and 4e-4:
    cnx_own_recipe    4e-4 0.8451  ->  cnx_top_rate       1.2e-3 0.8042   -0.0409
    mricore_corpus    4e-5 0.8658  ->  mricore_rate         4e-4 0.8034   -0.0624

FOUR FOR FOUR ON SIGN going up about 2x, two of them on our own stack, median about +0.0037. Each is individually under the 0.0062 paired floor and none is a finding on its own -- what is a finding is that the curve is ASYMMETRIC around 4e-5 and tilted upward, and that 4e-5 has never been the measured optimum of anything. It was inherited.

MECHANISM, AND WHY 24 EPOCHS SHOULD WANT MORE RATE THAN 12, NOT LESS. Every datum above is at 12 epochs and no slot-dropout. The shipping corner doubles the one-cycle schedule to 24 and adds --slot-dropout 0.40. A one-cycle doubled at fixed peak rate halves the average step size per unit of schedule, and 0.40 slot dropout is a large added regulariser -- both push the arm toward underfitting at a rate tuned where neither applied. THE TRAIN LOSS SAYS THAT IS WHAT HAPPENED: the shipping arm finishes at 0.5600 while calib_dense_hold, a 12-epoch arm at the same rate, finishes at 0.5130. The arm with twice the budget fits LESS. That is the signature of a schedule that is regularisation-bound, and it points the same direction as all four pairs.

THE ARM. experiments/arms/labelwise_depth24_drop40_long.sh with --backbone-lr 8e-5 and nothing else changed (2x, the size both of our own DINOv2 pairs measured; 1e-4 is Swin's value and sits closer to the collapse). Single variable against a control that already exists at 0.9053, so no matched control has to be paid for.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS, ledger75 @909 vs labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 = 0.9053:
  >= 0.9115  (+0.0062)  the rate carries at the shipping corner. This becomes the new best honest solo and
                        the escalation is 1.2e-4 plus a second seed -- NOT a submission on n=1.
  0.9053-0.9115         DIRECTIONAL. Keep 8e-5 as the corner's rate when a future arm is free to take it,
                        do not seat it, do not plan around it.
  0.8991-0.9053         flat-to-negative: the 12-epoch tilt does not survive the doubled schedule, which is
                        itself the answer to the mechanism argument above.
  <  0.8991  (-0.0062)  CLOSE THE AXIS at this corner. 4e-5 was inherited but it was also right.
Record the PEAK EPOCH and the peak-to-finish drop, as knee-fw1hc requires of any arm on this card: if the
higher rate peaks EARLIER than the control's e18 with a similar value, the schedule is what is binding and
the follow-up is budget, not rate.

EINSTEIN GATE: grep -nE 'backbone-lr' over all 406 arms returns no arm at any rate but 4e-5 with --epochs 24
except warm_calib_lowlr_drop40_long (1e-5, max pooling, 0.8994) and warm_hislabels (1e-5, warm start). No arm
at any rate above 4e-5 runs more than 12 epochs anywhere in the corpus. GATE PASSED.

Evidence: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-17_the_shipping_rate_was_never_asked.md
notes:
THE CORNER'S OTHER UNASKED KNOBS, 2026-09-17 14:40Z, zero card. Extending the audit from flags the corner FIXED to leaves it NEVER NAMED AT ALL -- those sit at the recipe default and no audit of the arms' own flags can see them, because they appear in none of them. The stamped recipe (93 leaves) is the only place every one is written. 40 leaves are never named by any of the corner's arms while some other arm in the corpus moved them. Dropping the teacher/distill/warm-start ones (they are the composition route, knee-0cm0k, not this single-model path), the ones with a single-flag isolating pair already on disk:

  --head-lr, corner runs 0.001:
    headlr224       5e-3   0.8670
    headlr224_slow  2e-4   0.8777    +0.0106
  --weight-decay, corner runs 0.02:
    decay224_low    0.005  0.8714
    decay224_high   0.1    0.8820    +0.0106
  --pool, corner runs cls_mean:
    focal224 / sided224        -0.0001
    focal_dense / sided_pool   +0.0022
  --unfreeze-last (corner 6, corpus has 12 in 6 arms) and --slice-regions (corner 1, corpus has 4 in 7
    arms): ZERO isolating pairs. Never A/B'd anywhere, at any corner. Unpriced, not flat.

BOTH OF THE +0.0106 READINGS ARE BIGGER THAN THE BACKBONE-LR EFFECT THIS BEAD WAS FILED ON, AND
NEITHER DISPLACES IT, FOR A REASON THAT IS ABOUT THE PAIRS AND NOT ABOUT THE SIZES. In both of those
pairs the corner's own value sits BETWEEN the two endpoints (0.001 between 2e-4 and 5e-3; 0.02 between
0.005 and 0.1), and both endpoints are deliberately extreme. So the pair prices the GRADIENT ACROSS A
20-25x SPAN and says nothing about the step from where the corner actually is -- most of a +0.0106 over
25x is plausibly just '5e-3 is a broken head rate'. The backbone-lr pairs are cleaner precisely because
4e-5 IS one endpoint in all four of them, and all four move the same way.

So the arm order is unchanged and lr8e5_ship stays the one that runs. head-lr 0.001 -> 2e-4 and
weight-decay 0.02 -> 0.1 are the next two single-flag arms IF it clears, each ~2.6 h, and they are not
being queued now: three arms on one axis before the first reads is the pile-up, not the plan.

AND ONE HONEST TENSION WITH THIS BEAD'S OWN MECHANISM. The description argues the corner is
REGULARISATION-BOUND (train loss 0.5600 at 24 epochs against 0.5130 at 12) and that this is why a
higher backbone rate should pay. But MORE weight decay wins by +0.0106 and a SLOWER head wins by
+0.0106, and both of those are more regularisation, not less. The two are not strictly contradictory --
trunk rate, head rate and decay are different axes, and a trunk that steps too slowly under a head that
steps too fast is a coherent picture that all three readings fit -- but the underfitting story is
weaker than the description states, and it is quoted there as one argument among four pairs rather than
as the finding. If lr8e5_ship lands flat, this tension is the first thing to read, not the last.
CAN THE CORPUS READ THE SHAPE OF ANY OF THESE KNOBS? NO -- 407 ARMS AND NOT ONE THREE-POINT CURVE. 2026-09-17 14:46Z, zero card. The previous note said the +0.0106 readings price a gradient across a 20-25x span while the corner's own value sits in the interior, so the obvious next question is whether some third arm already sits inside that span with every other flag identical. Grouped all arms into equivalence classes on every flag but the knob, then counted DISTINCT values per class:

  --head-lr        corpus ever used 5e-3 (2 arms) and 2e-4 (4). Classes: four at 1 value, ONE at 2.
                   THE CORNER'S 0.001 HAS NEVER BEEN RUN AGAINST AN ISOLATING PARTNER AT ALL.
  --weight-decay   corpus used 0.1 (1), 0.005 (1), 0.05 (3). Classes: three at 1 value, ONE at 2.
                   The three 0.05 arms never share a class with either endpoint, so they add nothing.
  --pool           cls_mean_focal (3), sided (5), mean (3). Six classes at 1 value, two at 2.
  --unfreeze-last  FOUR values in the corpus (12x6, 0x2, 4x1, and one passing $BLOCKS) and TEN classes,
                   every one of them at a single value. Four values, zero comparisons.
  --slice-regions  ONE value ever named (4, in 7 arms). There is no A/B to find; this is not a gap in
                   the pairing, it is a knob nothing has ever varied.
  --backbone-lr    17 values, 249 classes at 1 value, TWELVE at 2, and ONE at 3 -- the only three-point
                   class in the corpus, and its interior point has no reading:
                     swin_calib_dense   4e-5   0.8479
                     swin_toprate       3e-5   NO RECORD
                     swin_wholetop      1e-4   0.8509
                     swin_supervised    1e-4   0.8537

THIS IS WHY lr8e5_ship STAYS FIRST, and the reason is no longer just that its endpoint is the corner's
own value. BACKBONE-LR IS THE ONLY KNOB IN THIS PROJECT WITH ANY REPLICATION AT ALL: twelve classes hold
a comparison, four of them scored and all four tilting the same way. Every other knob above is carried by
a SINGLE class -- head-lr and weight-decay are each literally one pair, n=1, and no arrangement of the
existing corpus can make them more than that. So their +0.0106 is not a bigger effect than the rate's
+0.0037; it is a WIDER SPAN read once, against a median of four reads across a narrow one.

TWO THINGS THIS PUTS ON THE BOARD, neither of them costing a card:
  1. swin_toprate at 3e-5 would COMPLETE the corpus's only three-point rate curve and it has no reading.
     Check whether the checkpoint exists unpriced before assuming it never ran -- reading_check's
     declared-and-missing rule is the tool, and an unpriced checkpoint is a free point on a curve.
  2. --slice-regions is not 'flat', it is UNASKED: one value, seven arms, no comparison anywhere. Any
     future claim about it has to start by saying that.
2026-09-17 14:55Z THE WEIGHT-DECAY CAVEAT IS RETIRED BY MEASUREMENT, not by argument. See the new bead on the defaulted-leaf audit.

This bead recorded decay224_low 0.005 0.8714 -> decay224_high 0.1 0.8820 = +0.0106, and argued it
must not displace the rate arm because the corner value 0.02 sits BETWEEN two deliberately extreme
endpoints, so the pair prices a gradient across a 20x span and says nothing about the step from the
corner. That was a structural suspicion. It is now a measurement: joining the stamped default onto
the arms that omit the flag makes the corner value a comparable side, and

    0.005 -> 0.02 (corner)   median +0.0077   5 pairs, 5/5
    0.02  -> 0.1             median +0.0029   5 pairs, 4/5

The curve is 0.005 BAD -> 0.02 FLAT TOP -> 0.1 FLAT. Most of the +0.0106 was "0.005 is too little
decay". The step from where the corner actually sits is +0.0029, less than half the paired floor.

This also supplies the three-point curve scratchpad/tri.py found NOWHERE in 407 arms: tri.py could

Net effect on the branch: lr8e5_ship is REINFORCED, not displaced. --backbone-lr remains the only

title: sam_r01: sharpness-aware minimization at rho=0.01, the revisit knee-zqouw named
description:
PRICE: ~1.9 h of card (534 s/epoch measured on the rho=0.05 run against the control's 410 -- SAM doubles the forward+backward -- x 12 epochs). Zero submission slots.

P(clears the 0.0062 paired floor) ~0.20. P(clears the 1.5% bar) ~0.05.

CONTROL: calib_dense_hold_s2026 = 0.8634 LEDGER / 0.8949 LEDGER75 @holdout909, identical recipe, identical fp16 GradScaler path. SINGLE VARIABLE: --sharpness 0.01 (the rho=0.05 arm's only variable was the same leaf at 0.05).

WHY THIS IS NOT A RE-RUN OF A REFUTED ARM. knee-zqouw refuted rho=0.05 and diagnosed the cause as the RADIUS, not the mechanism: SAM trailed from epoch 0 (0.6921 vs 0.7515) and held ~4 points at every matched epoch, a uniform lag rather than a late-anneal shortfall. The plumbing witness fired live, so the ascent was really climbing; the ruler and the holdout were shared. rho=0.05 is the published value for from-scratch schedules on normalised weight scales, and against a pretrained trunk at --backbone-lr 4e-5 the ascent is large relative to the update. That bead names this revisit in its own closing line: 'honest revisit if ever priced: rho=0.01 or 0.005, once.' This is that once.

MECHANISM AND WHY THE AXIS IS WORTH A CARD AT ALL. Flatness is a GENERALISATION argument, and generalisation is the only axis the board gap can live on: every axis this project has closed -- scaling (depth, schedule, trunk, corpus), per-column weighting, seat and ensemble structure -- was closed IN-DOMAIN on the 909-study holdout, while the board is out-of-domain to it. The solo member now reads 0.9053 offline and 0.944 on the board. SAM is the one mechanism the project has implemented that attacks the transfer rather than the fit.

AND THE PROJECT HAS NEVER OBSERVED A CONVERGED SAM RUN. Every datum on this axis is mid-training, which is exactly where SAM is expected to look worst. That is the honest source of the 0.20: it is uncertainty, not optimism.

DELIBERATE EXCEPTION -- DO NOT ARM trajectory_check ON THIS ARM. It truncated the rho=0.05 run at e6 of 12 against a mid-training target. The hypothesis under test is that SAM lags early and pays at the anneal; gating it on an early-epoch target tests that hypothesis with a tool that presumes it false, and it is the reason no converged reading exists. This arm runs its full 12 epochs. The cost of being wrong is 1.9 h, which is the price already quoted.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS (ledger75 over 909 rows, vs the control's 0.8949; the rho=0.05 arm was written in midpoint and both rulers are quoted here so the comparison is not a cut artefact):
  >= 0.9011  (+0.0062, the paired floor)  SAM carries at a small radius; escalate to rho=0.02 and a second seed.
  0.8949-0.9011                           DIRECTIONAL only. Keep the leaf, do not plan around it, do not seat it.
  0.8887-0.8949                           flat-to-negative; the radius is still too large OR flatness is not the axis.
  <  0.8887  (-0.0062)                    CLOSE THE AXIS. Two radii an order of magnitude apart both costing
                                          is a statement about the mechanism on this stack, not about a constant.

READ THE PER-EPOCH CURVE, NOT ONLY THE FINISH. The rho=0.05 verdict turned on the SHAPE -- uniform from epoch 0 -- and that is what separates 'radius too large' from 'flatness is not the axis'. A run that lags early and closes at the anneal confirms the mechanism even if the finish is only directional; a run that lags uniformly again closes the axis at any radius.

HARNESS SUSPECTS, carried from knee-zqouw because they remain live: (1) Sharpness.climbed returns False on a non-finite gradient norm, a real path under fp16 -- grep the finished log for how often the ascent declined, and a high decline rate voids the reading rather than refuting the idea; (2) --accumulate must be 1, and sharpen() raises rather than approximating.

EINSTEIN GATE: grep -nE 'sam_dense|sam_r0|sharpness|SAM' experiments/README.md returns the rho=0.05 row written 2026-09-17 and nothing else -- no arm at any other radius exists in experiments/arms/ and no ledger row names one. medsam_dense_s2026 is Segment-Anything as a TRUNK, a different thing. GATE PASSED.
