title: GATE for knee-dz8ip: can OOF disagreement recover the gold noise ordering?
description:
knee-dz8ip wants per-column reliability weights fitted from report-label vs out-of-fold-prediction disagreement across the corpus, precisely so the weights never touch the 58 gold studies. That is only sound if the OOF estimator MEASURES THE SAME THING the gold FP/FN rates measure.

The refusal this buys: gold already states the per-column reader error rates over 58 studies (Effusion 69.6% FP, Contusion 51.3% FP, Synovitis 51.9% FN / 9.7% FP, Baker's 10.9% FP, ...). Compute the corpus-wide OOF disagreement rate per column over the 19 oof_* members (folds 0-4, 224px/8ep) and rank-correlate it against the gold ordering. If the two orderings do not agree, the estimator is not measuring label noise -- it is measuring column DIFFICULTY, which is the thing the weights must not chase -- and knee-dz8ip is dead before any card is spent.

Denominator note: the gold rates are over 58 studies with 9-35 positives per finding, so the gold ordering itself is coarse; treat a rank correlation as the read, not the individual rates.

PRICE: ~0.5 h CPU.
P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.00 -- INSTRUMENT ONLY. It scores nothing and ships nothing; it either licenses a ~6 h arm or kills it. That is the whole value.
notes:
GATE RAN 2026-09-17 12:55Z. RESULT: FAILS.

Spearman rho between per-column corpus flag rate (cleanlab confident learning over the 20-checkpoint published OOF ruler, 4406 studies) and per-column gold reader error rate (58 annotated studies, 57 cells/column) = **0.1194, p = 0.7116, n = 12 findings**.

corpus order: PF OA, Effusion, Medial Meniscus, Medial OA, Lateral OA, Contusion, Lateral Meniscus, ACL, Synovitis, Baker's, MCL, Fracture
gold   order: Contusion, Synovitis, Effusion, Lateral Meniscus, PF OA, Fracture, Medial OA, MCL, Lateral OA, ACL, Medial Meniscus, Baker's

The disagreements are the signature this bead pre-registered. Fracture is flagged LEAST of all twelve (0.0297) while the reader errs on 17.5% of it. Medial Meniscus is 3rd-highest flagged (0.1248) and 2nd-LOWEST in gold error (0.1404). Contusion and Synovitis -- the two columns where the reader is measurably worst (51.3% FP, 51.9% FN) -- sit 6th and 9th in the corpus flags. What the corpus order DOES track is prevalence and ambiguity: PF OA, Effusion, the two OA columns and Medial Meniscus at the top. That is column DIFFICULTY, which is exactly the thing a reliability weight must not chase.

POWER CAVEAT, stated so it is not read as stronger than it is: each gold rate is 6-22 errors out of 57 cells, so its own sampling sd is ~0.05 on rates spanning 0.105-0.386, and rho over n=12 has weak power. This is 'no evidence the estimator recovers the ordering', not 'proof it is orthogonal'. The point estimate is ~0 and the named disagreements go the way difficulty predicts, which is the pre-registered refusal condition.

Gate is SPENT. ~0.4 h CPU, no card.

title: Per-column reliability weighting of the loss, fitted OFF gold
description:
The per-column closure (experiments/README.md:14829) licensed only the scaling class, and that class is now measured dead end to end (interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-17_the_scaling_class_is_closed.md): depth flat-to-negative, schedule saturated at 24ep, trunk flat and adversarial at 336px, corpus negative on every SSL objective. But the closure's inference was 'lift all twelve columns at once' and it EQUATED that with scaling. Target geometry also lifts all twelve and is not a scaling knob.

Mechanism: the board metric is an unweighted mean over 12 findings; the reader's own FP rate over the 58 annotated studies runs 9.7% (Synovitis) to 69.6% (Effusion), and the model already beats its labels on 6 of 12 (labels-model -0.0470 [-0.0717, -0.0218]). Equal-weighted BCE spends its largest gradients on the noisiest column. A per-column reliability weight changes the RELATIVE gradient across findings in a way no monotone rung remap and no capacity increase can.

The blocker, from knee-vrioa: any weight fitted on the 58 gold cells is unreadable on the 58 gold cells (the raptor_solo mechanism). Fit the weights from report-label vs OUT-OF-FOLD-prediction disagreement across the full corpus instead — held-out by construction, never touches the 58 — leaving gold clean as the adjudication set.

PRICE: ~6 h (one labelwise/336/20sl/24ep arm on the card; the weight fit itself is CPU minutes).
P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.12 — reweighting redistributes gradient, it adds no information, and the closure says every one of the twelve columns has to move ~0.010. Best remaining ratio only because every scaling lever is measured dead; NOT a good ratio in absolute terms.
BLOCKED ON its own gate below: do not arm until the noise estimator is shown to recover the gold ordering.
notes:
CLOSED BY GATE knee-mmxew, 2026-09-17, before any card was spent. That is the gate paying for itself: ~6 h of card refused for ~0.4 h of CPU.

The design required the per-column weights to be fitted OFF gold, because any weight fitted on the 58 gold cells is unreadable on the 58 gold cells (the raptor_solo mechanism). The only held-out-by-construction estimator available was corpus OOF disagreement, and it does not rank-correlate with the gold noise ordering (rho 0.1194, p 0.71). So the estimator measures column DIFFICULTY, and weighting by it would UP-WEIGHT the columns the model already finds hardest rather than the ones the label is wrong on -- the same defect label_errors.py's own docstring names for reader-confidence weights: 'A weight that rises with the reader's confidence therefore UP-WEIGHTS the reader's dominant error by construction.'

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. Per-column reliability weighting itself is not refuted -- only this WAY of estimating the weights. Re-opening needs a per-column noise estimator that is neither fitted on the 58 nor confounded with difficulty. None is known. A second reader over a larger sample would be one; there is no budget for it.

title: Screen the whole shelf by TAIL OVERLAP, not solo score: the seat test seating never ran
description: knee-i97cx measured tail overlap 0.631 against a 0.100 chance on labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 over 12 members, and named the consequence: 'a new member only pays if it fails DIFFERENT studies. Member quality is not the axis; tail DECORRELATION is. Any candidate should be priced by its tail overlap against this member BEFORE it is priced by its solo score.' Nobody has run that pool-wide. knee-jy5yu, knee-lyzc1 and knee-5hbtz all call seating closed, and every one of them priced candidates on SOLO score, which is the axis i97cx says is the wrong one. study_attribution reports ONE aggregate over a sample of members and cannot surface a candidate; this ranks every member on the shelf that shares the champion seat's split, ascending by overlap. DECISIVE EITHER WAY: a member materially below 0.631 is a seat candidate the solo-score screen could not see, and a shelf whose minimum is near 0.631 closes the ensemble lane on mechanism rather than on arithmetic. PRICE: ~1 h CPU, zero card, zero slots. P(a member reads below 0.30 overlap) ~ 0.20; P(clears 1.5% if one is found) ~ 0.15. Denominator: 909 holdout studies, tail = worst 90, and only members sharing that exact study order can be compared at all.
notes: RAN 2026-09-17 10:0xZ, ~7 min CPU against the ~1h it was priced at. 391 aligned members, 51 skipped; chance 0.100, shelf mean 0.593, floor 0.022, ceiling 1.000. The printed verdict was CANDIDATE and it was wrong: the bottom decomposes into WEAK (7 members, ledger75 0.4593-0.7704, floor member below chance AUC), VOID (the whole 0.300-0.333 band, every row DINOv3/raptor, 703 or 897 of 909 in-sample, declines:730/812/877), and the reference under a second name (solobase_hold, overlap 1.000, identical 0.8679/0.9053/18/909). HONEST STRONG FLOOR 0.433 (recal_holdannot_s2026, itself already declined at declines:84) against mean 0.593 and the module CLOSED threshold 0.346 => THE ENSEMBLE/SEATING LANE CLOSES ON MECHANISM, which is what this bead was filed to get and what knee-jy5yu/knee-lyzc1/knee-5hbtz could not deliver on solo score. Second, unplanned finding: tail overlap is a LEAK DETECTOR with perfect rank separation (void band 0.300-0.333, honest floor 0.433) off two .holdout.npz files and no md5 split. Also new evidence against knee-zxm9z: mae_matched_s2026 ledger75 0.6766. Writeup: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-17_tail_overlap_closes_the_seat_lane.md; tool kneemri/evaluation/tail_screen.py.

title: A better label reader is the live lever: our champion beats the report on 12 of 12
description: supervision_gap on the champion (--hold-annotations, so the 58 annotated studies are unseen) reads labels-model -0.0616 [-0.0850,-0.0385], EXCLUDES zero; published pool reads +0.0266 and spans zero. All twelve findings are model-over-label; the reader agrees with the radiologist only 65.3% of the time where the report says YES. So the supervision, not the pixels, is the weaker half at our operating point. Recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_labels-or-pixels.md. PRICE: ~2 h CPU to re-read report_labels_v2 with a stronger extractor on the 58 annotated studies and measure the reader's own AUC move; the arm that consumes it is a refit, ~5 h. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.20 — the gap between reader and model is 0.0616 on annotation truth, which bounds what better labels could buy. Denominator: 58 studies / 696 cells, per-finding positives 9-35; only Effusion, Synovitis, Contusion exclude zero.
notes: RE-SCOPED AND CLOSED 2026-09-17 10:20Z, on the record I should have read before filing. The flip is real but it is NOT a lever, on two counts already on disk. (1) 2026-09-08 §7: colnull_v1 shows the board is an unweighted mean of twelve column AUCs (a column gaining d moves the board by d/12) and colhalf_v1 reads a 0.024 board gap against a 0.110 offline spread — every column must move ~0.010 and no per-column shortcut exists, so no per-finding plan may be priced off supervision_gap at all. (2) The reader swap was MEASURED and lost: knee-wko44 closed on v5reader, paired gold@58 -0.0112 sd 0.0122, whole-table arm not licensed. What the champion re-read DOES buy is an instrument result, recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_labels-or-pixels.md: the labels-or-pixels split is a property of the MEMBER, not of the corpus, so the published pool's ACL/Lateral-Meniscus 'vision failure' may not be carried to our model. Ranked by ACHIEVED (the 09-08 §8 rule — a baseline may not be a deterministic function of the target), our champion's floor is Lateral OA 0.8221 / Synovitis 0.8590 / Contusion 0.8799 / Lateral Meniscus 0.8919, and Lateral Meniscus is no longer the worst column.

title: Twin gate: a deployed _ff member and its validated fold-0 twin may differ ONLY on fold
description:
FIT='--fold -1 --ema' (16 arms) adds a SECOND axis to every deploy twin at a site the arm author never reads. We validate a non-EMA model and ship an EMA one, and nothing refuses.

MEASURED, so process not score. ema_dense vs band_dense is a one-variable pair (identical epochs 12 / max pooling / slices 20 / band 0.1-0.9 / rate 4e-5; --ema the only difference):
  band_dense_s2026  0.8578 midpoint  0.8877 ledger75
  ema_dense_s2026   0.8588 midpoint  0.8857 ledger75
                    +0.0010          -0.0020
Inside the 0.0062 paired floor, rulers disagree on sign. Last-epoch-vs-best (the other half of --fold -1) prices -0.0006 off the winner's flat plateau (e18 0.8679, e23 0.8673). Total drift ~0.003.

Stamped audit of the shipped pair, read off the checkpoints:
  labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_ff    fold -1 ema True  img 336 train_size 336 slices 24 epochs 24 labelwise small
  labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 fold  0 ema False img 336 train_size 336 slices 24 epochs 24 labelwise small
Only fold and ema differ. No FixRes gap: members.py:250 resolves read_size = train_size or img, member_record.py:380 stamps it.

GATE: assert an _ff checkpoint and its fold-0 twin differ on 'fold' alone across the axes member_record stamps. run_comparison.py:45 VIEW_AXES holds the diff and must be INVOKED.

PRICE: ~0.5 h, pure CPU, no card. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0 - this is a GATE, not a score lever, justified as one.
notes:
GATE LANDED: kneemri/kaggle/twin_check.py + unit mirror (6 tests). Run: python -m kneemri.kaggle.twin_check [--strict].

READING, all 11 _ff/_s2026 pairs on disk: every one differs on fold and ema and NOTHING else. The bead's audit of the shipped pair generalises to the whole shelf.

The first run did NOT read that way -- it reported 28 distinct drifting axes over the 11 pairs (layer_decay, through_plane, hold_annotations, focus_label, train_fraction, side_weight, accumulate, slice_regions, encoder_adapt_depth, ...). Every one was None against that flag's own default: the _ff half simply PREDATES the flag. That is era, not divergence, and reading it as drift would have been the denominator trap on a config axis.

The rule that separates them is mechanical and reads the trainer's OWN declared defaults off TrainConfig (108 of them), never a hand-written identity list. run_comparison.OFF_VALUES cannot do this job: it covers False/0/0.0/None/'' and cannot express layer_decay=1.0, accumulate=1, slice_regions=1.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN is only what this bead was filed on: ema rides along with fold on all 11. It is in BY_DESIGN with its measured price (+0.0010 midpoint / -0.0020 ledger75 vs band_dense, inside the 0.0062 floor, rulers disagreeing on sign), and --strict drops it -- so the check GRADUATES to blocking the day FIT stops setting --ema. Leaving this bead OPEN for that graduation, not for the comparison.
2026-09-17 09:53Z — GATE LANDED (38899138 + 189cdc0f). Lives at kneemri/experiments/twin_check.py, NOT kaggle: pyproject's layer contract names kneemri.inference/kneemri.kaggle as source modules forbidden to import training, and this check must read the trainer's declared defaults. The defaults come from DefaultDrift.declared() (new classmethod, one home, already what __init__ used) rather than a second importer of config_tree, which sat at fan-in 8 and would have tipped to a BLOCKING god-module at 9. Reading unchanged after the move: 11 deployed/validated pair(s) compared; may differ on ema, fold, out, vram_gb, witness — 0 complaints. --strict refuses all 11. Bead stays OPEN for that graduation.

title: The members fail the SAME studies: tail overlap 0.631 vs chance 0.100 -- the ensemble has nothing to vote about
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-17 on labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 (909 holdout studies, tail=worst 90) via study_attribution.

  tail overlap with 12 other members: 0.631 against a chance 0.100
  studies in this tail and no other member's: 8
  SHARED

This is the MECHANISM behind the <=0.002 ensemble premium (eightseat_v1 8 members, swapseat_v1 7, ffsolo_v1 1 -- all board 0.944). A committee averages over disagreement; on the studies that decide the score there is 6x LESS disagreement than chance. Every redistribution lever (seating, reseating, vote rules, self-distillation) is therefore capped near zero by construction, not by tuning.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the actionable half: a new member only pays if it fails DIFFERENT studies. Member quality is not the axis; tail DECORRELATION is. Any candidate should be priced by its tail overlap against this member BEFORE it is priced by its solo score -- that is a cheap CPU read off two .holdout.npz files, no card.

Also measured, both NULL:
  population_split  -- errors/positive flat 0.487-0.569 across series count and fluid-sensitive count; tail vs body series 5.467/5.457, planes 3.000/3.000. No data lane.
  study_attribution -- no report-reader error category separates tail from body at 2 sigma. No label lane.

PRICE: 0 h (closed by reading). P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0 for any reseating arm.
Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-17_one_member_equals_eight.md
notes: ANSWERED by knee-14ssw. title: Re-arm mae_unitfix: the converged in-domain SSL trunk is gone from disk
description:
PRICE: ~6.8 h of card total, 0 slots — ~65 min to rebuild the pretrain (8 epochs, measured 481 s/epoch on pretrain_matched_e8) plus ~5.7 h for the 12-epoch fit (1690/2114/1341 s measured on the killed attempt). P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.25, expected ~+0.005.

WHY IT IS THE BEST RATIO ON THE BOARD DESPITE THAT. Every redistribution axis is now priced and capped: ffsolo_v1 (ref 56296698) put ONE member on the board at 0.944, tying our own 7-seat swapseat_v1 and 8-seat eightseat_v1 at 0.944 against a 0.946 champion. The whole ensemble premium over one good member is <= 0.002, so seating, reseating and distillation-from-our-own-pool are all bounded by it. An encoder that has actually fitted in-domain knee MRI is the only lever left that produces a member knowing something the pool does not.

THE BLOCKER THIS BEAD EXISTS FOR. mae_unitfix requires $MODELS/adapt_small_e8_unitfix.pt and it is NOT on disk — the only surviving adapt/pretrain checkpoint is adapt_null_s2026.pt, the null control. That file was the one converged in-domain SSL trunk this project ever produced (pixel 0.9682 -> 0.5570, 3.2% -> 44% of hidden-patch variance explained). It vanished with every gate green, because no check asserts that a pretrain artefact a live arm REQUIRES still exists. That is why this axis sat a week: require() refuses and the refusal reads like a missing input rather than a lost asset.

UPSTREAM GATE, PRE-REGISTERED AND UNCHANGED: at epoch 2 of the rebuild, pixel MUST fall below 0.90. The broken objective sat at 0.9704 after one epoch; the fixed one reached 0.5570. A failure there kills the pretrain at ~16 min rather than after 5.7 h of fit, and the next suspects are the single nn.Linear(384,196) decoder and the 0.6 mask ratio.

NEITHER PRIOR ATTEMPT WAS A RESULT. First died 'trainer exit 127' (uv sync venv rewrite under a live arm) at epoch 3 of 12, reading 0.6637/0.6898/0.6957 RISING. Second is TRUNCATED at e1 of 2 run, 12 asked. The axis has never once been measured.

title: The offline75 board column held two rulers, and the check that guards it ignored its own --ruler flag
description:
matchpair_v1 carried offline75 0.9039, which is RECUT applied to all twelve findings. Every other cell is the mixed cut that leaves MIDPOINT_COLUMNS (Medial Meniscus, Baker's) at 0.5 — what LedgerSeventyFive.scorer() returns and what the ledger75 CLI prints. Recomputed from the stackfit_s2026 holdout record: flat 0.9039, mixed 0.8962, midpoint 0.8631; the board's midpoint cell matched to 4dp, so it was the recut alone that forked.

Two consequences, both landed.

FIRST, entry_offline.mismatched() hardcoded LabelScores() and row.offline, so --ruler ledger75 --check recomputed the MIDPOINT and compared it against the MIDPOINT column, reporting clean over an offline75 column it had never read. It now reads self.scores and self.column and exits non-zero. With the flat cell in place it named matchpair_v1 and no other row, so the corruption was one cell; after the correction to 0.8962 it reads 0 rows.

SECOND, matchpair_v1's own conclusion is retracted, and the retraction restores its pre-registration. It was shipped to measure the board's resolution floor at a matched-offline point, paired with holdsolo_v1, and it concluded it had measured the RULER instead because the two were '0.0090 apart at ledger75'. That subtracted the mixed 0.8949 from the flat 0.9039. Read on one ruler the pair is 0.0013 apart at ledger75 and 0.0003 at midpoint — matched on BOTH cuts — so the 0.005 board gap between them IS the floor reading it was shipped for, and the entry says nothing about ledger75 beating the midpoint.

board_transfer --ruler ledger75 refitted on the corrected column is UNCHANGED: +1.09 whole record, +1.02 above 0.8976, +0.99 above 0.8996, 0 of 596 resolved pairs inverted. So no arm priced off that slope moves.

title: Seating is arithmetically closed: best legit add +0.0025 vs a 0.0053 ruler floor and a +0.012 gap
description:
Board transfer read live 2026-09-17 05:28Z, --ruler ledger75, 45 ensemble entries / 844 orderable pairs.

THE THREE NUMBERS.
  slope in our band (>= 0.9012): +0.99 [+0.86, +1.13] over 24 resolved pairs. Whole record +1.08.
    So an offline75 point is a BOARD point at 1:1 in the band we ship in, and the prose constant
    +1.09 / +1.55 / +1.45 is not the number to price with here.
  holdout resolution floor: a pair is resolved only at a gap >= 0.0053. All 12 of 844 board
    inversions are pairs the holdout left UNRESOLVED; 0 of the 608 it resolved were inverted.
  board blur: median |board delta| 0.0010 over pairs the holdout could not separate.

AGAINST THE SEAT BANK.
  best LEGITIMATE seat add over 380 candidates (cleanseat_v1 base, rank-average): +0.0025
  every add above +0.0070 is VOID (competitor checkpoints / released fold weights) - see knee-lyzc1
  gap to first place: +0.012 board

The best honest seat move this project owns is LESS THAN HALF the gap our own ruler can resolve,
and would need five of itself to close the board gap. comp/board.jsonl already records twelve
distinct seatings landing at exactly 0.9440. So the flats are not a ruler failure and not a search
failure: no combination of the members on disk can reach 0.955.

CONSEQUENCE, AND THE POINT OF THIS BEAD. Six levers died in one segment - report clumping, off-axis
selection, banked sub-blur increments, the paired-floor reopening, the OOF bias argument, seat
dilution - and every one of them was a COMBINATION lever. They share a cause. The gap is a
MEMBER-QUALITY gap, and the only thing that can move it is a member above the pool's current top.
Rank every future lever by whether it produces one; a seating or vote-rule proposal needs to answer
this bead's arithmetic before it gets a card hour.
notes: INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION FROM THE BOARD'S OWN TREND, read live 2026-09-17T05:30:01Z.

title: Seat dilution is the binding mechanism: +0.0084 solo becomes +0.0018 seated, and banking sub-blur seat increments is refuted 12x
description:
WHAT THIS CLOSES, BEFORE ANY CARD IS SPENT. The empty shortlist invited an obvious strategy: the roster holds several offline-RESOLVED but board-unresolvable positive seat adds (+0.0018 warm_calib_lowlr_drop40_long, +0.0017 finding_calib_dense as a swap, +0.0015 add / +0.0013 swap at roster:333, +0.0012 at roster:119; +0.0017 merged_blend is RIJEKA and instrument-only). Nominal sum ~+0.006, which is most of the 0.010 to first place, and CLAUDE.md explicitly licenses composing sub-bar increments. It needs no training - every member is on disk.

REFUTED BY THE BOARD'S OWN RECORD. comp/board.jsonl goldseat_v1: 'Eight board rows now read exactly 0.9440 across seven distinct 7-member seatings and two 6-member ones', and it is the TWELFTH seating entry to fail to beat 0.944. A bank of seat increments composed and shipped is the thirteenth. Measured non-transfers in both directions: the blind gold ruler's +0.0970 member lead bought at most +0.0005 board; cleanseat_v1's corrected-ruler +0.0026 bought -0.002.

THE MECHANISM, WHICH IS THE PART TO CARRY. Solo-to-seat attenuation is large and repeatable: knee-rkegi +0.0084 solo -> +0.0018 seated (4.7x); stack_increments +0.0020 solo -> -0.0001 seated. This is NOT ruler failure - the paired bootstrap resolves both (paired sd of a member difference on the 909 is 0.0038 median, and the quoted 0.0070 ledger75 floor is the 95% HALF-WIDTH of exactly that, confirmed against commit 26340de0). It is redundancy: competence_axis reads 81.7-82% of what separates members as ONE latent, so a new on-axis member's gain is already in the ensemble before it is seated.

CONSEQUENCE FOR RANKING LEVERS. A member that is merely BETTER is attenuated ~5x at the seat. The only mechanism that survives both the seating saturation and the attenuation is a member that is better AND OFF-AXIS - strong on the columns where the pool is weak rather than on the mean. That is what seat_profile.py was built to see (its docstring: the 18% that is not the competence axis is per-finding, and no tool quoted it) and no arm has ever been DESIGNED against it.

AND IT DEMOTES THE 5-FOLD OOF RULER. That instrument buys a 2.2x variance cut (floor 0.0070 -> ~0.0032) at 5x training per member. But the shortlist entries it would have reopened were killed by the BOARD's 0.0020 blur (knee-cyi5v), not by our ruler: knee-rkegi's seat add is +0.0018 with CI [+0.0011, +0.0026], already resolved offline and still unshippable. The OOF refit fixes the constraint that is not binding. See knee-keg4e for the ruler's bias and its retraction.
notes:
OFF-AXIS SELECTION IS REFUTED ON DISK, and the scan that refuted it also re-derived the declines file.

Base = cleanseat_v1's six members, rank-average vote, mean 0.9035 on the canonical 909. 380 candidates
priced by seat add against that pool, each candidate's complementarity measured against the seating's
weak columns (Fracture 0.8372, Lateral OA 0.8756, PF OA 0.8890 the three weakest of twelve):

  spearman  solo  vs seat-add : +0.918
  spearman  compl vs seat-add : -0.521

Complementarity correlates NEGATIVELY with seat add; solo score predicts it. Being differently-shaped in
this pool mostly means being worse in a different shape. The 'find a better AND off-axis member' arm is
not worth a card hour, and this is the measurement that says so.

AND THE SCAN'S OWN TOP EIGHT WERE ALL VOID. The eight adds above +0.0070 - raptor_v4_swa +0.0105,
raptor_v4 +0.0100, raptor_effv2l480 +0.0088, dinov3f0_solo +0.0087, foreign_dinov3_matched +0.0079,
foreign_dinov3_band1189 +0.0077, raptor_v9 +0.0076, foreign_dinov3_band1387 +0.0070 - are every one of
them recorded as VOID in comp/members.declines. The raptor_* family is the competitor's published
checkpoints (foreign_overlap.py: 896 of our 909 holdout studies sit in their label table, 'THE DEFAULT IS
GUILT'); dinov3f0_solo and the foreign_dinov3_* family are mattiaangeli's RELEASED fold weights, 703 of
909 in-sample (declines:730-736, 884, 899, 908).

The defect was the reader, not the repo. kneemri/evaluation/member_pool.py:100-119 already filters exactly
these - its own docstring names dinov3f0_solo and raptor_v4_swa as 'the HIGHEST-scoring records there' and
states that any statistic over the default glob 'is led by exactly the rows that cannot mean anything'.
The scan globbed D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/*.holdout.npz directly instead of going through
MemberPool.at().names(). A throwaway script that bypasses the pool gate reproduces the raptor_solo defect
the gate was built to end.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY FUTURE POOL SCAN: read through MemberPool, never through glob. A raw directory sweep
of this models root will ALWAYS rank contamination first, because contamination is indistinguishable from
an excellent member by score alone.

title: Our 909 holdout is 0.0137 HARDER than the corpus and inverts two columns - the ruler is biased, not just noisy
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-17 05:07Z, zero card, zero slots. Pool held fixed (published 20-member oof, out-of-fold everywhere), corpus split into our fold-0 909 vs the other 3498.

  mean column AUC   909 0.8380   complement 0.8516   +0.0137
  Fracture          909 0.8000   complement 0.9176   +0.1176
  rank corr of the twelve columns across the two halves: rho 0.594 p=0.042

PREVALENCE IS NOT THE CAUSE. Max per-column prevalence gap between the halves is 0.0177 (MCL); ten of
twelve are under 0.016. The split stratified correctly. The holdout is unrepresentative in DIFFICULTY.

Fracture@909 bootstrap CI is 0.7564-0.8679 over 2000 resamples, so the complement's 0.9176 is OUTSIDE
it. Not a draw. Both pools agree: ours909 Fracture 0.8136, published@909 0.8000, published@4407 0.8918
- it is the STUDIES, not the members.

CONSEQUENCE 1 - FRACTURE IS A SECOND MCL. It is our 2nd-worst column and the corpus's BEST. colhalf put
it in the ablated half on the strength of our map. Same inversion shape as colmcl, now explained without
needing 'the board is a different task'.

CONSEQUENCE 2 - every offline number is ~0.014 pessimistic against the corpus, uniformly. Harmless for
ranking members (all on the same 909) but it is an unmodelled offset in every offline->board statement.

CONSEQUENCE 3 - the per-column map cannot order itself: paired bootstrap resolves 32 of 66 column pairs
(48%), median paired CI width 0.0720 against a total column spread of 0.1099. Fracture's marginal CI is
0.1115, WIDER than the whole spread, on 68 positives.

WHY colhalf READ BRANCH ONE, derivable offline before the slot was spent: changing the member pool alone
costs rho 0.748, changing the study set alone costs 0.594, and doing both lands at 0.203 p=0.527 - chance.
The board changes both at once.
notes:
MECHANISM RESOLVED, and my first hypothesis REFUTED by its own measurement.

REPORT-TEXT CLUMPING DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT. ReportFolds groups by report text so duplicate reports cannot straddle the split; I named a wholesale-cluster effect as a live candidate for the 0.0137 gap. Measured: 4407 studies, 4276 distinct reports, 46 groups of size>1 covering 177 studies (4%), design effect sum(n^2)/sum(n)=1.427. Largest groups 37,14,12,6,5,5 -> folds 2,0,2,4,0,2. The 37-study cluster is in fold 2, not ours. Too small and pointed the wrong way.

THE REAL ANSWER: WE DID NOT CHOOSE BADLY, WE CHOSE ONE. All five folds on the published 20-member OOF pool, 12 columns:
  fold 0 n=909 mean 0.8380 Fracture 0.8000  <- ours
  fold 1 n=875 mean 0.8452 Fracture 0.9168
  fold 2 n=884 mean 0.8503 Fracture 0.8831
  fold 3 n=849 mean 0.8559 Fracture 0.9575
  fold 4 n=890 mean 0.8557 Fracture 0.9171
  across folds mean 0.8490 sd 0.0076 range 0.0180 ; fold0 z=-1.46
Fold 0 is the hardest of five but NOT an outlier. That spread is what an unstratified SHA1-mod-5 draw gives at n~880 (folds.py:45-67 hashes report text with seed 2026, no label or difficulty stratification). Fracture swings 0.800-0.958 across folds on ~68 positives each.

CONSEQUENCE. The -0.0137 is a FOLD-IDENTITY OFFSET, not sampling noise around the corpus: it is fixed by which fold we picked and MORE STUDIES IN FOLD 0 CANNOT REDUCE IT. Bootstrapping fold 0 harder only measures fold 0 more precisely.

THE FIX IS NOT TO RE-PICK THE FOLD. Choosing a fold because we measured it easier is selection on the ruler - the defect that voided raptor_solo. The only clean fix is 5-fold OOF over all 4407, which averages the offset away by construction AND cuts the ledger75 floor 0.0070 -> ~0.0032. Second independent argument for that instrument, and the stronger one: it fixes a BIAS, not only a variance.
THE BIAS DOES NOT REORDER MEMBERS - I OVERSTATED THE PREVIOUS NOTE.

Test: 391 members on the canonical 909, split the studies into two random halves (454/455), score each member on each half @ledger75.
  sd across members (full 909)     0.0465   range 0.4832
  halfA vs halfB spearman 0.946 ; pearson 0.993
  per-member (A-B): sd 0.0058, mean -0.0090
  sd(A-B)/sd(across members) = 0.12
  top-40 overlap between halves 32/40 ; best-on-A is rank 1 on B and vice versa
Implied pure sampling sd of one member's score on 909 studies ~0.0029.

So changing the study pool wholesale moves a member 12% of the across-member spread and leaves the winner unchanged. The fold-0 difficulty offset is therefore LARGELY UNIFORM ACROSS MEMBERS: it shifts every absolute offline number ~-0.014 but does not change which member wins.

RETRACTION. The note above claims the 5-fold OOF refit 'fixes a BIAS, not only a variance' and calls that the stronger argument. Wrong. For seat search and member ranking - the only uses this set is put to - the bias cancels. The refit's case rests on the VARIANCE cut (ledger75 floor 0.0070 -> ~0.0032) it was already priced on. The bias remains a live caveat only for offline->board ABSOLUTE statements.

WHAT SURVIVES. 8 of the top 40 swap between halves, and the half-to-half swing 0.0058 is the same size as every effect on the dead shortlist (knee-8c8up +0.0049 solo, knee-rkegi +0.0084 solo). The ruler's NOISE is the binding constraint, now measured independently on four axes: pool (this), column (colhalf/knee-51aff), pair resolution (48% of 66 column pairs), and fold identity (sd 0.0076 across the five folds).
RESOLVED AS NOT-ACTIONABLE 2026-09-17 09:09Z. The bead's own final measurement settles it: the fold-identity offset is an OFFSET, not a reordering (spearman 0.946 between random holdout halves over 391 members, top-40 overlap 32/40, best-on-A is rank 1 on B, sd(A-B)/sd(across members)=0.12). So member SELECTION is not damaged by the bias, and the 5-fold OOF instrument cannot be justified on 'it fixes a bias that misranks us' - only on the variance argument (floor 0.0070 -> ~0.0032), which costs 5x per member on a shared card. Offset stays a documented constant on every offline->board statement, which board_transfer's slope already absorbs. Not the binding constraint.

title: Rank the member pool on GOLD and on the report ruler, and read the correlation
description:
PRICE: ~0.25 h CPU, no card, no slot. P(clears 0.002 band) ~ 0.35.

THE DEFECT, STATED AS A MECHANISM. Members are FITTED against report labels and SELECTED against report
labels on the 909-study fold-0 holdout. The competition scores against radiologist annotations. Those two
truths disagree, and supervision_gap measures WHERE: over the 58 annotated studies the reader's false
positive rate is ACL 26.5%, Lateral Meniscus 28.6%, MCL 18.4%, and those are the same three columns whose
model-side deficit is largest (ACL -0.1225, MCL -0.0964, Lateral Meniscus -0.1925, all three bands
excluding zero). Board arithmetic is settled by kneemri-colnull (constant 0.5 read exactly 0.500, so the
board is a flat mean of twelve AUCs): closing those three is +0.0343, about 3x the 0.011 gap to first.

WHY NO CHECK CAN SEE THIS. The loss and the ruler share the defect. A member that reads ACL BETTER than
the report scores WORSE on our holdout and is declined in writing; comp/members.declines holds 288 such
decisions and every one was taken with this ruler. Sixteen checks guard shipments, numbers and questions,
and not one of them asks whether the ruler agrees with the board's truth.

WHAT TO RUN, AND WHY IT IS A CORRELATION RATHER THAN A SELECTION. gold_estimators registers the pooled
per-finding rank-normalised cell AUC at paired sd 0.0096 over 696 cells. That is far too noisy to PICK a
member against our 0.002-sized seat deltas, and any attempt to reseat directly on gold repeats
l75seat_v1's failure, where the offline prediction overshot the board by about a point (it scored 0.939). The answerable question is the ORDERING: score all
442 holdout records both ways and read Spearman, with the three deficit columns read separately from the
nine.

BRANCHES, PRE-REGISTERED.
  rho >= 0.90 over the pool          the rulers agree, the pool is exhausted as measured, lane CLOSES for
                                     good and knee-2s0gp's 'designed, not picked' entry may not be a
                                     reseating of anything on disk.
  rho <= 0.70, or the three deficit  the pool has been ranked with the wrong instrument for the whole
  columns disagree while the nine    project. A declined member that leads on gold is then a REAL seat
  agree                              candidate on a mechanism rather than on scatter, and the next
                                     submission is that reseating.
  in between                         report the split by column and claim nothing.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY. 58 studies, and the gold set is the same one every label treatment was gated on, so
a high rho is evidence about the ordering and not a licence to trust either ruler at 0.002. It also
cannot price a seat: pricing stays on ledger75, which inverts 0 of 608 board pairs.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING. The 442 .holdout.npz records and the annotation table are on disk.
notes:
BLOCKED AS FILED, before anything ran. Recording the blocker instead of the arm.

Our members cannot be ranked on gold. annotated_readings states it: every member this project fits weights
the 58 annotated studies at 3.0, so scoring one there scores its own training cells, and --hold-annotations
does NOT hold them out - it withholds the annotator VALUE and the 3.0 weight while all 58 rows go on training
at their report-derived values, 45 of them inside the fold-0 training split. That is knee-x4muo 78%-in-sample
finding. What stays clean for a fold-0 member is the 13 gold studies inside its holdout: 156 cells, against a
registered estimator whose paired sd is 0.0096 over the full 696. That cannot order 442 members and could not
order four. So the reseating half of this bead is not merely unproven, it is UNMEASURABLE with the members on
disk, and stays so until a member is fitted with the annotated rows genuinely withheld - an ARM, a card, for an
instrument. This is also why supervision_gap could only ever be computed on the PUBLISHED members.

WHAT SURVIVES CLEAN, and it is an INSTRUMENT with no expected gain, not a lever. The twenty published CC0
members were fitted fold-wise over all 4,407 studies by their own authors and never saw our annotation table,
so gold is out-of-sample for them by construction. weights_gap (knee-q1pf) already scored those same twenty on
our 909-study report ruler, and supervision_gap already scored them on gold. Both orderings exist; the Spearman
between them costs one read and no card.

It answers the RULER question and not the SEAT question: whether a report-label ruler orders MODELS the way
radiologist truth does, on models neither ruler was fitted to. Disagreement would not license a reseating of
our pool - it would say the instrument behind every line of comp/members.declines mis-orders, which is a reason
to re-open declines and not a number to ship. Agreement closes the suspicion that the ruler is why the three
deficit columns (ACL, MCL, Lateral Meniscus) look the way they do. n=20 against sd 0.0096 is weak; report rho
with its interval and do not quote a point estimate.

SEE ALSO knee-51aff, which is a second, independent reason a naive 442-member ranking would have been junk:
36 members are in-sample at epoch -1 and 44 carry a MOVED ruler.
RUN 2026-09-17 04:51Z on the clean pool, no card, no slot. VERDICT: UNDERPOWERED. The lane does not close
and the suspicion is NOT retired - but it is now known that the PUBLISHED pool can never retire it either.

Both orderings were already on disk and cost nothing: every m_*.pt under processed/published carries scalar
'holdout' (report ruler, its own fold's 834-937 oof studies) and 'annot' (gold, the annotated studies inside
that fold) beside its 'oof' block. 20 members, 5 folds x 4 seeds.

THE NUMBER I ALMOST REPORTED AND DID NOT. Pooled over all 20, spearman = -0.480, p = 0.032, pearson -0.752.
A negative, significant, headline-shaped result saying our selection ruler ANTI-orders radiologist truth.
It is an artefact of the denominator. The four members topping the report ruler are all fold 2, and fold 2
is the bottom four on gold (0.7463 0.7356 0.7949 0.7375 against fold 3's 0.9164 0.8915 0.8889 0.8808).
Each fold scores on a different 870-odd oof studies AND on a different ~11 annotated studies, so the pooled
correlation is reading fold-difficulty on both axes at once and nothing about the rulers. This is the
CLAUDE.md denominator rule, and it would have been the fifth wrong constant quoted into the ledger.

WITHIN FOLD, where four seeds share both denominators exactly:
  fold 0  rho +0.40   fold 1  +0.20   fold 2  0.00   fold 3  +0.20   fold 4  +0.80
  mean within-fold spearman +0.320; concordant pairs 18 of 30 = 60.0%, binomial p ~ 0.18 against 50%.
Weakly positive, indistinguishable from unrelated. No evidence the report ruler mis-orders, and none that
it orders correctly.

WHY IT CANNOT BE RESOLVED HERE, which is the durable part. Within a fold the four seeds span only
0.0030-0.0107 on the report ruler - BELOW the project's 0.0062 noise floor in three folds of five. There is
almost no ordering to reproduce. Meanwhile the gold range is 0.0227-0.0593, three to six times larger, on
~11 annotated studies per fold, which is scatter rather than signal. An instrument whose two rulers are both
reading noise cannot detect agreement OR disagreement at any n.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY ANSWER IT: members that differ on the report ruler by more than the floor, scored on gold
over the SAME studies, and never fitted on the annotated rows. The published pool fails the first condition;
our own 442 fail the third (the 3.0 training weight above). So the ruler question needs a member fitted with
the annotations genuinely withheld - a card - and remains the one lane not closed by measurement.
DESIGN CONSTRAINT BEFORE ANYONE SPENDS TIME ON THIS -- the test as worded can only produce a wrong
verdict, and the wrong verdict is the expensive direction.

THE TRAP. Gold is 58 studies. Ranking 426 members on 58 studies gives each member a gold AUC with real
sampling error, and a rank correlation between a noisy ranking and a clean one is ATTENUATED toward
zero by the noisy side's unreliability no matter how good the clean side is. So a low Spearman here
does NOT say the report ruler is wrong. It says one of two things and cannot distinguish them without
a second measurement.

WHY THAT DIRECTION IS THE COSTLY ONE. A low number read as 'the report ruler does not track gold'
impeaches every seat decision this project has made, because they were all taken on the report ruler.
That is a conclusion large enough to redirect weeks, and the harness would have produced it by
construction. This is the faulty-TEST suspect in CLAUDE.md, arriving before the test rather than after.

THE MISSING MEASUREMENT, which has to come first. Bound what correlation is ACHIEVABLE by measuring
the gold ruler's own repeatability -- split the 58 studies in half, rank the pool on each half, and
correlate the two halves against each other (Spearman-Brown up to the full 58). That ceiling is the
denominator. Only rho_observed / rho_ceiling is interpretable; rho_observed alone is not a number about
the report ruler at all. It uses no card and no labels the project does not already hold.

CONTEXT THAT IS ALREADY ON DISK AND SHOULD NOT BE RE-DERIVED. ledger75.py's own module docstring
records researcher D25's measurement on 30 members: LEDGER~gold macro ORDERING +.59 -> +.80 at the
0.75 recut (+.25 -> +.71 on the hold split), and per-column Effusion -.17 -> +.74. So the correlation
is not unmeasured -- it is measured at n=30 members, uncorrected for the gold set's own noise. What
this bead adds over D25 is (a) the full 426-member pool rather than 30, and (b) the attenuation
ceiling D25 never computed. Framed that way it is a real instrument. Framed as 'read the correlation'
it is a number nobody can interpret.

Also note +.80 uncorrected at n=30 against a 58-study gold set is ALREADY high, which is weak prior
evidence the ruler is fine and the ceiling is the binding term.

PRICE: ~1.5 h CPU, no card. P(clears 0.0062 paired floor) ~ 0.00 -- INSTRUMENT. It buys no member. It
licenses or impeaches the ruler every seat decision is taken on, which is why it is worth running and
why it must not be run in the form that cannot fail informatively.

title: seat_weight prices the champion's own weight on the midpoint cut, the one that inverts the board
description:
PRICE: ~0.4 h CPU, no card, no slot. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.03 -- this is an INSTRUMENT, and it is justified as one: it retires the suspicion that the champion's serving weight was chosen under the wrong ruler, and it makes two seat instruments answer the same question on the same cut.

THE DEFECT. kneemri/evaluation/seat_weight.py:169 constructs SeatWeight(pool, len(pool) - 1, LabelScores()) and the CLI has NO ruler flag, so every weight this project has read is a MIDPOINT number. Its sibling seat_add.py:24 states the opposite convention in its own docstring -- 'THE RULER IS LEDGER75 BY DEFAULT, not the midpoint. Every add this project quotes is a ledger75 add' -- and offers --midpoint to ask the other question (seat_add.py:197-200). So the project runs two seat instruments on two different cuts and neither says so at the point of use. CLAUDE.md already warns this exact way: 'a number in this repo is midpoint unless it says otherwise', 47 call sites on the default, and knee-f9aao is the same error having already put a wrong coefficient in the ledger twice.

WHY THE CUT IS NOT A DETAIL HERE, measured 2026-09-17 and reproducible from comp/board.jsonl alone. board_transfer fitted both ways, then re-paired on the 39 ensemble entries carrying BOTH cuts at the same 0.0053 floor so the row set cannot explain it:
  offline   (midpoint) 414 resolved pairs, 12 inverted (2.9%)
  offline75 (ledger75) 397 resolved pairs,  0 inverted (0.0%)
Identical entries, identical boards, identical rule. The default cut is the one that orders pairs the other way from the board; ledger75 never does. Mechanism: ledger75 thresholds the soft report-derived labels at 0.75 instead of scores.py MIDPOINT = 0.5, so its truth is the confident-positive set, and the competition's labels are HARD. Midpoint counts every ambiguous report-derived positive as ground truth -- exactly the population where our labels are noise and the board is not.

WHY THIS INSTRUMENT AND NOT ANOTHER. seat_weight's own docstring says the weight is the quantity the entry actually turns on: the champion serves the foreign seat at 1/3 beside six members, about 2.4 seats, and that value was chosen ON THE BOARD at one slot per value, with raptorweight_v1 (1/7 to 1/3, +0.001) the whole record. So this is a parameter we have been paying SLOTS to tune while the offline instrument that could tune it for free was reading a different ruler.

THE WORK. Give seat_weight the same surface as seat_add: default LEDGER75, --midpoint for the other cut, and the cut named in the printed lines so a pasted number carries it. Then re-read the champion's foreign seat at weights 1,2,3 under ledger75 and compare to the midpoint reading. seat_profile.py:44,59 take the same bare default and should be checked in the same pass.

PRE-REGISTERED, BEFORE THE NUMBERS. Two outcomes and both are worth the 0.4 h. If the ledger75 weight AGREES with the served 1/3, the suspicion is retired and the board slots spent on raptorweight are confirmed as having found the right value -- a null that licenses trusting the remaining weight choices. If it DISAGREES, that is a candidate move with a named mechanism and no training, and it goes to a slot LABELLED as the instrument it is. What this may NOT do is get sold as an improvement before it is read.

title: The ruler is the binding constraint: fit a composition-aware offline statistic against the 54 scored board rows
description:
PRICE: ~0.5 h, CPU only, no card and no slot. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.02 as a SCORE - this is an INSTRUMENT and is justified as one, not sold as an improvement.

WHY THIS AND NOT A MEMBER ARM. knee-2s0gp's shortlist is empty: every axis it ranked is closed, and its own last note says the next entry 'has to be DESIGNED, not picked'. knee-xz903 prices first place at +0.0076 offline and concludes the only route is a CHAIN of three or four independent +0.002 to +0.003 moves. Our holdout noise floor is 0.0062 over 909 rows. So the chain strategy is asking us to accumulate moves that are each a THIRD of what our ruler can resolve. We cannot see them, cannot order them, and cannot tell a composing pair from an overlapping one. The ruler is therefore the binding constraint on the ONLY remaining strategy, and it is the one thing left that costs neither card nor slot.

AND THE RULER IS ALREADY KNOWN TO BE BLIND. knee-xz903, n=1 but measured: pricetop_v1 and foldseven_v1 differ by +0.0010 offline (a sixth of our floor) and by 0.006 on the board (three times the board's own 0.0020 blur). Same evening, adding a seat to an existing pool moved offline +0.0002 and the board 0.000, and an identical-entry re-ship moved the board 0.000 exactly. Read together: board movement at fixed offline tracks POOL IDENTITY, not pool quality on our ruler. That is a statement that our offline statistic is missing a term the board can see.

THE DATA EXISTS AND IS FREE. comp/board.jsonl holds 151 rows, 136 carrying their member list and 54 carrying BOTH an in-scope offline number and a board score. Those 54 are (composition -> board) observations against the real target. board_transfer today fits board on offline ALONE, one scalar per entry, and gets residual sd 0.0022 in the top band (knee-5hbtz).

THE TEST, pre-registered. Fit board against candidate offline statistics over those 54 rows and compare RESIDUAL SD against board_transfer's own 0.0022, honestly cross-validated (leave-one-out; 54 rows will happily overfit a three-term model). Candidates, each a cheap function of an already-stored pool: mean member solo; the current pooled-prediction macro-AUC; that plus a DIVERSITY term (member_distance / member_axes already compute one); pool SIZE; and family identity. A statistic that materially beats 0.0022 out-of-sample is a ruler that can certify a +0.002 move, which is exactly what the chain needs.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT A NULL, stated first. 54 rows, board quantised to 0.001, and many entries tied at 0.944 - so the ruler may simply be unfittable at this n, and the honest outcome is 'our record cannot calibrate a better ruler', which retires the chain strategy's premise rather than the chain. Either answer is worth 30 CPU-minutes, and NEITHER is worth a slot.

SCOPE. Instrument only. It ranks, it never ships, and no number it produces may be quoted as a holdout score. Every statistic carries STATISTIC@POPULATION@CUT per knee-f9aao.
notes:
2026-09-17 02:58Z — ANSWERED IN 20 CPU-MINUTES, AND THE PREMISE IT WAS FILED ON IS WRONG. No new statistic was fitted and none should be: the ruler does not need a composition term, it needs a different CUT, and the record already holds both.

THE PREMISE THAT DIED. This bead argued our ruler is BLIND to an axis worth ~0.006 board, from knee-xz903's n=1 pricetop/foldseven pair, and proposed fitting a composition-aware statistic. board_transfer already reports the test that settles it: how often the board ORDERS A PAIR THE OTHER WAY among pairs the holdout actually resolved. If the ruler were missing a term, resolved pairs would invert. Under offline75 they do not invert at all.

THE MEASUREMENT, matched rows, zero card, zero slot. board_transfer --ruler midpoint: 21/775 resolved pairs inverted. --ruler ledger75: 0/397. Those run on 50 and 39 entries, so the 39 with BOTH cuts recorded were re-paired directly from comp/board.jsonl at the same 0.0053 floor:
  offline   (midpoint) 414 resolved, 12 inverted (2.9%)
  offline75 (ledger75) 397 resolved,  0 inverted (0.0%)
IDENTICAL ENTRIES, identical boards, identical resolution rule. So it is the CUT, not the row set. Under a pooled 1.5% inversion rate, 0/397 is p ~ 0.003; pairs from 39 entries are not independent so treat that as directional, but 12 against 0 is not a scatter story.

MECHANISM, and it is not a hack. ledger75 thresholds the SOFT report-derived labels at 0.75 instead of scores.py MIDPOINT = 0.5, so its truth is the confident-positive set. The competition's labels are HARD. A 0.75 cut is therefore the closer proxy for the target the board actually scores, and a 0.5 cut counts every ambiguous report-derived positive as ground truth — which is exactly the population where our labels are noise and the board is not.

WHAT THIS COSTS US, stated because it is bad news. CLAUDE.md: 'a number in this repo is midpoint unless it says otherwise', 47 call sites take the default and three paths can recut. knee-xz903's +0.0076 offline price for first place is a MIDPOINT number, taken through the midpoint top band (+1.38 [+1.05,+1.55]). On the ruler that does not invert, board_transfer --ruler ledger75 reads the top band at +0.62 [+0.33,+0.79] over 16 resolved pairs, so the same 0.011 board gap costs roughly +0.018 ledger75 points, range +0.014 to +0.033. The climb is LARGER than the headline number, not smaller, and the chain-of-four-small-moves plan was sized against the ruler that mis-orders.

DO NOT SUBSTITUTE THE TWO (knee-f9aao). These are two slopes with two denominators; +0.62 and +1.38 are not a disagreement to reconcile, they are compression against two different rulers.

NEXT, and it is cheap: the matched-row inversion comparison belongs in board_transfer as a reported line rather than in this note, so the next reader gets it without re-deriving it. Everything above is reproducible from comp/board.jsonl alone.
EVIDENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S PREMISE, measured 2026-09-17 03:47-03:53Z, and it strengthens the case. This bead says the ruler is the binding constraint. On the 45 ensemble entries that now carry both cuts, changing ONLY the denominator's ruler on identical entries, OLS against the board reads:
  whole record: midpoint +1.11 (resid sd 0.0036) | ledger75 +1.10 (resid sd 0.0017)
  upper band:   midpoint +1.37 (resid sd 0.0019) | ledger75 +1.09 (resid sd 0.0013)
Same slope, HALF the residual scatter, and the top-band steepening the record has carried for weeks is a midpoint artefact that does not survive the swap. Inversions 0 of 608 resolved pairs at ledger75. And the recut costs only 12.5% more paired-bootstrap noise (floor 0.0062 -> about 0.0070) while lifting the base +0.033.

So a better offline statistic IS available and part of it is already built -- but note what this does to the bead as WRITTEN. It asks for a COMPOSITION-AWARE statistic fitted against the scored rows. What the ledger75 result shows is that a large part of the gap between our ruler and the board was never composition at all, it was the CUT. Re-fit the composition term against offline75 rather than offline before concluding anything about composition, or the term will absorb a cut effect that a one-line change already removes. Prerequisite done: ledger75 now covers the shipping band (entry_offline --ruler ledger75 --write, six rows, 2026-09-17 03:47Z).

title: Top band is a tight line (resid sd 0.0022): retract the pool-overlap claim; seating is closed, the member is the lever
description:
DETRENDED READ 2026-09-17 00:36Z over the 50 ensemble rows in comp/board.jsonl carrying both offline and board.

WHOLE SET: slope +1.33, residual sd 0.0070, n=50.
TOP (offline>=0.8700): slope +1.45, residual sd 0.0022, n=15.

The cohort sd of 0.0039 quoted earlier today was MOSTLY TREND, not scatter -- it came from binning peers within the 0.0062 holdout floor without removing the offline slope inside the bin. Detrended, the top band is tight.

CONSEQUENCE 1 -- RETRACTION. The claim written into CLAUDE.md and comp/SUBMISSIONS.md earlier tonight, that 'board movement at a fixed reading tracks POOL OVERLAP, not pool quality on our ruler', does not survive. It rested on one un-detrended pair (pricetop_v1 vs foldseven_v1). pricetop's residual about the top-band line is -0.0019, UNDER ONE SD. It is an ordinary point on the line, not an anomaly, and there is no pool-identity effect visible anywhere in the record. The pool-identity lever bead filed on it should be closed as unsupported.

CONSEQUENCE 2 -- THE GAP IS REAL AND CONVERTS. Leader 0.957 vs ours 0.946 = 0.011 board = 4.9 residual sd = +0.0076 offline at the top slope. Luck cannot deliver it; a genuine offline gain of that size WILL show.

CONSEQUENCE 3 -- A CLOSED AXIS RE-OPENS IN PART. comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:2450 closed offline-greedy seating with 'no further slot should be spent on an offline-greedy seating', on two readings that do not hold:
 (a) 'This is a sign flip, not a compression. +0.0050 offline became -0.004 on the board.' There is no sign flip. honest12 (offline 0.8751, board 0.937) against the twinfive shadow it beat offline (0.8705, 0.935) is +0.0046 offline -> +0.002 board, SAME SIGN. The line predicted +0.0067, so it under-delivered by 2.1 combined sd. The -0.004 came from comparing honest12 to calibsix_v1, a different entry it never claimed to beat.
 (b) 'The ordering is INVERSE to offline holdout gain', over resseat_v1 / blendseat_v1 / blendthree_v1 / pixgroup_v1 / calibsix_v1 / calibmix_v1. ALL SIX CARRY offline=None. The claim compares board values against offline numbers that are not in the record.

What SURVIVES from that closure is its independent mechanism argument: a greedy fitting on 454 of 909 studies cannot resolve a seat worth less than the 0.0062 floor. So HALF-HOLDOUT GREEDY seating stays closed. What re-opens is DESIGNED seating priced on the full 909 -- and the evidence is that our three best entries are exactly that, carrying the three HIGHEST residuals in the top band: swapseat_v1 +0.0032, foldseven_v1 +0.0026, eightseat_v1 +0.0023.

NEXT: price a designed seating search on the full-909 ledger75 cut (not half-holdout greedy) and ask whether it can find +0.0076 offline over foldseven's 0.8767. PRICE: ~0 h card (pool arithmetic over existing holdout records). P(clears +0.002 offline) ~ 0.4.

METHOD NOTE: re-derive the fit rather than quote it -- adding rows moves it, which is this file's standing failure mode.
notes:

This bead re-opened 'designed seating' on the evidence that the three highest top-band residuals are all designed pools (swapseat_v1 +0.0032, foldseven_v1 +0.0026, eightseat_v1 +0.0023). That evidence is real and the inference from it was too strong: ALL THREE OF THOSE ENTRIES READ 0.944. A residual is a position relative to the transfer line at a given offline reading; it is not a board level. The tier says so directly. The next gain has to come from what a member IS'), and 2026-08-25_the-seat-axis-is-saturated-and-the-member-is-0.028-behind.md closed the axis. Four independent roads, one destination.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THIS BEAD: nothing about seating. Its correct residue is that the top-band residual sd is 0.0022 and the gap is 4.9 sd -- the measuring rule, not the seating lever.
