title: Pool identity is worth 0.006 board and our ruler is blind to it -- lever, with an LB-overfitting hazard
description:
The three instruments of 2026-09-16 measured an axis our holdout cannot see: at a fixed offline reading,
board movement tracks POOL OVERLAP. One seat added or swapped moves the board 0.000; a near-disjoint pool
at the same reading moved it 0.006 (pricetop_v1). The identical-entry scatter is 0.000, so that 0.006 is
not noise.

THE LEVER. 0.006 board is over half the 0.011 gap to the leader, and it costs NO CARD TIME -- it is a
choice among pools we can already build from 251 members. The only instrument that can read the axis is
the board itself, at one slot per read, and slots are destroyed at 00:00Z if unspent. So the ratio looks
extraordinary: zero wall-clock, a currency that expires anyway, and a prize worth half the gap.

THE HAZARD, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT RUN. Selecting a pool because it scored well on the public
board IS leaderboard overfitting, in its textbook form: we would be choosing between candidates our own
holdout says are identical, using the public split as the ruler, and the private split is what ranks us.
The 0.000 scatter measured by leg 1 is PUBLIC-board scatter for a byte-identical entry; it says nothing
about public-to-private transfer, and a 0.006 public edge selected out of k candidates shrinks by an
amount that grows with k. This is the same in-sample-by-construction mechanism that voided raptor_solo
and l75seat_v1/cleanseat_v1 -- greedy selection scored on the thing it was selected against -- moved one
level up, from our holdout to the public board. It deserves the same suspicion.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT SAFE, AND WHAT TO DO FIRST. Two things are unknown and both are cheap to establish.
(1) The public/private split size for this competition -- a 0.006 edge on a large public split is worth
more than on a small one, and the ratio above is unpriceable without it. (2) Whether the effect is
DIRECTIONAL rather than a coin flip: pricetop is one pair, n=1, and the whole reading rests on it. A
second near-disjoint pair at equal offline, shipped as a labelled INSTRUMENT, would say whether
disjointness costs or merely scatters -- and if it scatters symmetrically, the lever is a coin flip with
an overfitting tax and should be dropped outright.

RECOMMEND: establish the split size from the competition page before spending a slot, and treat the first
disjoint entry as an INSTRUMENT testing direction, never as a rank attempt. Do not chain slots on this
without the owner, since it trades private-board safety for public-board points.
notes: 2026-09-17 00:39Z CLOSED AS UNSUPPORTED. This bead was filed on the reading that pricetop_v1 sat 0.006 below foldseven_v1 on the board at a fixed offline reading, i.e. that pool IDENTITY carries board score our ruler cannot see. A detrended fit of the 50 ensemble rows carrying both numbers kills it: over the top band (offline >= 0.8700, n=15) the line is slope +1.45 with residual sd 0.0022, and pricetop's residual about that line is -0.0019 -- UNDER ONE SD. It is an ordinary point on the transfer line. The 0.006 was never compared to the board's scatter about the line, only to its rounding. No pool-identity effect is visible anywhere in the record, so there is no lever here and no LB-overfitting hazard to gate. The gating fact this bead asked for (the public/private split size) was also chased on 2026-09-17 00:35Z and is NOT obtainable: it is absent from the Kaggle competitions API, our kernel logs see only the 3-study public stub, and the competition page is an SPA that WebFetch reads as a bare title. Superseded by knee-5hbtz.

title: First place costs +0.0076 offline, priced through the newly-priced top band
description:
The top band of board_transfer is priced for the first time (2026-09-17 00:07Z, knee-52ldh's repair plus
eightseat_v1): +1.44 board points per holdout point over SIX resolved pairs [+1.39, +1.96], where it had
read +1.45 over three marked DIRECTION ONLY. That band is the one we ship in, so the gap to first place
now converts instead of being asserted.

THE NUMBER. board_read --live 2026-09-17 00:13Z: rank 65 of 3855, ours 0.946 tied with 5, leader 0.957,
gap +0.011. Through the top band that is +0.0076 offline (interval +0.0056 to +0.0079); through the
middle band +0.0089; through the whole record +0.0102. Take +0.0076 as the working figure and +0.0102 as
the pessimistic one -- the band-specific slope is the right denominator here BY CONSTRUCTION, since the
entries being compared are in that band, but it rests on six pairs and one of them is eightseat itself.

WHAT IT REFRAMES. +0.0076 offline is ABOVE the 0.0062 holdout noise floor and far BELOW the project's
1.5% result bar. So first place is not gated on a mechanism-scale idea: it is gated on roughly 0.8
holdout points, which is a distance a CHAIN of sub-bar increments can cover and a single knob cannot.
CLAUDE.md already licenses exactly this ("increments below the bar still compose, and a chain of them
that sums past it IS a result"), and it changes what to spend slots on: the question stops being "which
lever could plausibly carry 1.5%" and becomes "which three or four independent +0.002 to +0.003 moves
compose without overlapping". Overlap is the whole risk -- seat-level gains have repeatedly failed to
add, and thirteen seating entries now read 0.944.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not price a SEAT move: eightseat measured that a sub-blur offline move
(+0.0002 midpoint) buys 0.000 board, so the curve is flat below 0.0020 board and this slope only applies
to a move large enough for the board to certify. And the frontier is moving: +0.00036/day against our
+0.00016/day, so 0.011 is today's gap and it widens at ~0.0002/day.
notes:
BLOCKER RESOLVED, and not the way it was framed. "One offline point, six board points" (pricetop_v1
0.8757 -> 0.938 vs foldseven_v1 0.8767 -> 0.944) was read as a violation of the transfer curve. It is
not. Diffed 2026-09-17 00:18Z: the two entries share exactly ONE member. pricetop is
blendhold / margin_seat / oof_teacher / warm_calib_lowlr / labelwise_drop; foldseven is
calib_dense_hold / calib_span / stack_increments / through_dense / three labelwise_*_long. They are
near-disjoint ensembles, not a seat swap, so there is no seat to blame and nothing to fix in either.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY MEASURES. Their offline gap is +0.0010, which is a SIXTH of the 0.0062 holdout noise
floor: our ruler does not distinguish these two pools at all. The board separates them by 0.006, three
times its own 0.0020 blur. Tonight's leg 1 (56288555) measured the board's identical-entry scatter at
0.000, so that 0.006 is real. Put beside leg 2 (56288513: add one seat to an existing pool, +0.0002
offline, 0.000 board) the pair of readings says something neither says alone -- board movement at fixed
offline tracks POOL IDENTITY, not pool quality on our ruler. Perturb a pool slightly and the board does
not move; replace it wholesale at the same offline and the board moves 0.006.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CONSTANT (knee-xz903). board_transfer's slope may be applied WITHIN a family and not
ACROSS one. The +1.44 top-band slope converts an offline gain into board points for a move that keeps the
pool's identity -- a better seat of the same kind, a better-trained member. It does NOT price swapping to
a different family of seats, where a 0.0010 offline difference bought 0.006 board in one direction and
could as easily buy -0.006 in the other. This is a scope limit on the number filed four minutes ago, and
it is the reason that number is filed with a family attached.

NO HEADROOM CLAIM. The champion is already in the foldseven family, which is the side that transferred
BETTER, so this explains pricetop's shortfall rather than offering us 0.006. n=1 pair, and the honest
statement is "our ruler is blind to an axis worth about 0.006 board", not "we know which side to pick" --
we know it for exactly these two pools and by construction we are already on the good one.
SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-09-17 00:22Z, same evening: the band floors are QUANTILES, so adding swapseat_v1 moved the top floor 0.8705 -> 0.8711 and re-partitioned every pair. The top band read +1.44 over six resolved pairs at 00:07Z and +1.68 over four marked DIRECTION ONLY at 00:22Z. Do not carry a pair count or a floor. Carry the stable part: top-band slope roughly +1.4 to +1.7 against a whole record of +1.1. The gap of +0.011 therefore converts to +0.0065 to +0.0080 offline, and +0.0076 stays a fair working figure inside that. Everything else in this bead stands.
2026-09-17 00:39Z: reopened. The +0.0076 offline price for first place is CONFIRMED by an independent detrended fit (knee-5hbtz: top band slope +1.45, residual sd 0.0022, gap = 4.9 sd), so this bead's number stands on better evidence than it was filed with. It stays open for its ACTIONABLE half, which knee-5hbtz does not carry: find three or four independent +0.002 to +0.003 moves that compose without overlapping, rather than hunting one 1.5% mechanism. First candidate from the detrend: designed seating on the full-909 cut.
THE CUT DOES NOT REPRICE THIS, tested 2026-09-17 03:46Z. The +0.0076 target is fitted on board_transfer's DEFAULT ruler, which is the midpoint ('--ruler midpoint', board_transfer.py:529) -- the cut that inverts 12 of 414 resolved board pairs where ledger75 inverts 0. So the number that ranks every open lever was quoted on the ruler the board disagrees with, and the seat finding an hour earlier (the midpoint roughly DOUBLES a served seat's apparent gain) predicted it would move.

IT DOES NOT MOVE. Run '--ruler ledger75' and the upper band reads +0.62 over 16 resolved pairs against the midpoint's +1.4-1.7, which would convert the +0.011 gap to +0.0177 offline and push first place back above the 1.5% bar. That reading is an ARTEFACT OF THE BAND, not of the cut. The two bands are quantiles of different distributions, so they are made of different entries -- the midpoint top band is eightseat_v1 and swapseat_v1, and NEITHER carries an offline75, so ledger75's band cannot contain them.

PAIRED TEST, which is the one to believe. 39 ensemble entries carry both rulers. Hold the entries fixed AND the pair set fixed (pairs resolved >= 0.0053 under BOTH), change only the denominator:
  whole record, 338 pairs: midpoint +1.04, ledger75 +1.08
  upper regime (offline >= 0.8678), 5 pairs: midpoint +1.51, ledger75 +1.33
Same within the scatter, both above +1.0. The rulers order 7 of those 338 pairs differently.

CONSEQUENCES. (1) +0.0076 offline for first place STANDS, and the actionable half of this bead -- three or four independent +0.002 to +0.003 moves that compose -- is unchanged. (2) 'the top band is steeper than the whole record' also stands (+1.33 to +1.51 against +1.04/+1.08), now on a paired fit rather than on a quantile. (3) The unpaired +0.62 is the THIRD spurious band-quantile reading in two segments; CLAUDE.md already says do not carry a floor or a pair count, and this is that rule earning itself again. Quote a BAND slope only from pairs held fixed across the comparison being made.
SUPERSEDES THE NOTE ABOVE, 40 minutes later and on 10x the pairs. That note concluded 'THE CUT DOES NOT REPRICE THIS' off a paired upper-band fit of FIVE pairs. Five was all that existed because the ledger75 ruler had NO COVERAGE of the band we ship in: foldseven_v1, eightseat_v1 and swapseat_v1 all read offline75 null, and ledger75's band topped out at 0.937 entries. That is the exact condition board_transfer:531 names as the reason midpoint is still its default.

FIXED, not worked around. 'entry_offline --ruler ledger75 --write' filled six rows (resnetlong 0.8764, honestsix 0.9015, pricetop 0.9065, foldseven 0.9094, swapseat 0.9095, eightseat 0.9100), 41 declined in-sample or record-less. The ledger75 fit now reads 45 entries and 844 orderable pairs, and its top band (>= 0.9012) is 24 resolved pairs at +0.99 [+0.86, +1.13] where it had been 0 pairs.

THE CUT DOES REPRICE IT. Identical entries, identical pairs, only the denominator's ruler changing:
  whole record, 523 paired: midpoint +1.11, ledger75 +1.09
  upper band,    57 paired: midpoint +1.59, ledger75 +1.07
OLS on the same entries, which is immune to the small-denominator blowup a median-of-ratios suffers:
  whole: midpoint +1.11 resid sd 0.0036 | ledger75 +1.10 resid sd 0.0017
  upper: midpoint +1.37 resid sd 0.0019 | ledger75 +1.09 resid sd 0.0013
So ledger75 is not merely the ruler that never inverts a resolved pair (0 of 608). It FITS THE BOARD TWICE AS TIGHTLY on the whole record, at the same slope. And the top-band STEEPENING that this bead and CLAUDE.md both carry is a MIDPOINT ARTEFACT: on the better ruler the slope is flat at +1.09 to +1.10 from the whole record to our own band, with no steepening anywhere.

MECHANISM, and my first guess was wrong. I proposed midpoint AUC saturating near its ceiling, which would shrink the denominator. Measured, the spread barely moves -- upper-band median |delta| is 0.0033 midpoint against 0.0035 ledger75, a ratio of 1.06, nowhere near the 1.49 the slopes differ by. What survives is pair-level: the midpoint shrinks particular pairs toward zero delta while ledger75 keeps them apart, and a near-zero denominator inflates that pair's ratio without bound. Same family as the 12-of-414 inversions. Hence the OLS reading above, which is the one to quote.

THE NUMBER, REPRICED. From eightseat_v1 (0.9100 offline75, 0.944 board) to the leader's 0.957: board_transfer --ruler ledger75 --near 0.9012 returns holdout 0.9231 needed, +0.0131 above it, off 24 resolved pairs; through the OLS slope it is +0.0119. Call it +0.012 offline75 against the +0.0076 midpoint figure this bead was filed with -- about 1.6x, and much closer to the project's 1.5% bar than the filed number suggested.

WHAT THAT DOES TO THIS BEAD. The actionable half SURVIVES but gets harder: a chain of independent increments is still the shape, and the chain is now five or six +0.002 moves rather than three or four. UNVERIFIED and the next thing to settle: the 0.0062 holdout noise floor that the +0.002 increment size is measured against is itself a MIDPOINT number, so it must be re-taken at ledger75 before the chain length is believed. Bears directly on knee-gg0la ('the ruler is the binding constraint') and on knee-yndds.
THE FLOOR IS RE-TAKEN, so the chain length is no longer UNVERIFIED. The 0.0062 this project quotes is a MIDPOINT paired-bootstrap half-width (experiments/README.md:288 says 'on this ruler' and means that one). Re-run 2026-09-17 03:53Z with LabelScores.paired_mean_interval under both scorers, on six pairs drawn from the champion's own family (calib_dense_hold_s2026, merged_span_cf, labelwise_dense_s2026, blendhold_s2026), same records, same studies:
  midpoint 0.0053 0.0048 0.0052 0.0059 0.0048 0.0061
  ledger75 0.0060 0.0054 0.0058 0.0067 0.0054 0.0067
Every pair moves the same way and the ratio is tight -- 1.10 to 1.14, median 1.125. So the ledger75 floor is about 0.0070.

WHY THAT IS A POINT FOR THE RECUT, not against it. The recut lifts the BASE by about +0.033 (0.8767 -> 0.9094 on foldseven) while widening the noise by only 12.5%. Together with the board fit halving its residual scatter at the same slope, ledger75 is the better ruler on every axis this project has measured it on: fewer inversions (0 of 608), tighter board residual (0.0017 vs 0.0036), and noise that grows far slower than the signal it is measured against.

CHAIN LENGTH, now on one ruler throughout. Target +0.012 offline75, floor 0.0070 offline75, increments of the filed +0.002-0.003 midpoint size scaling to about +0.0023-0.0034 offline75. That is FIVE increments, not three or four. Sub-floor increments still compose (CLAUDE.md), so this is a longer chain rather than a closed lane -- but it is 1.6x the work the bead was filed against, and it is the honest number to rank levers with from here.

title: reading_check: refuse an arm whose declared reading artefact ALREADY exists
description:
knee-18c5r was ranked first among all open levers on 2026-09-16 22:08Z and handed the night's card to re-run a reading that was already on disk, taken 2026-09-09 by knee-2sqyb and written up at experiments/README.md:11858. Nothing refused. Every gate was green, because every gate guards whether an arm WILL leave its artefact, never whether the artefact is already there.

The precedent for the fix is already in this repo and is one rule wide: experiments/lib.sh refuses a foreign_run whose --tag artefacts already exist, 'since he overwrites without a word and the overwritten run is usually one this project has already priced'. The identical hazard on the run_train/readout side is unguarded.

THE GATE. reading_check already resolves an arm's '# reading: <glob>' and asserts declared-and-MISSING. Add the inverse: an arm whose declared glob ALREADY matches files on disk REFUSES, naming the matched files and their mtimes, releasable with --anyway '<why>' the way the foreign_run guard is. A re-read is often legitimate (a member changed, a ruler was recut) — the point is not to forbid it but to make the re-reader say so, because the failure mode is not a bad decision, it is a decision taken without knowing the number exists.

WHY A CHECK AND NOT A HABIT. The owner's standing verdict is that only a mechanical gate that REFUSES counts; 'read the ledger first' is already written in CLAUDE.md, was already the rule after the two P0s of 2026-08-13, and did not fire here. A glob is one token and its matches are an ls — this is the cheapest refusal in the repo.

PRICE: ~40 min, no card. P(prevents a repeat) ~ high; it is the same shape that has now cost a queue slot, two P0s, and a night's card plan.
notes:
2026-09-16 23:37Z — BUILT AND LIVE.

reading_check gained --only <arm> / --anyway '<why>'. taken() is the complement of missing(): missing asserts ran => artefact exists, taken asserts not-ran => artefact must NOT exist. Same two predicates, and only the new direction can be checked before the card is spent. matches() names the hits with UTC mtimes so the refusal says how old the number that already exists is.

It keys on the '# reading:' declaration alone, never on what the arm requires — erase_own_cells require's the built g4 patches npz and declares erase_own_cells_s2026.holdout.npz, so the input/output split is what keeps the gate from refusing every arm that reads a cache. That arm was the first live test and passes.

VERIFIED on the four paths by real exit status, not by an echoed one:
  --only carve_budget_sweep            exit 1, naming all three carve_budget_*.npz with 2026-09-09 mtimes
  --only carve_budget_sweep --anyway   exit 0
  --only erase_own_cells               exit 0, 'no declared reading is on disk yet'
  whole tree (unchanged)               exit 0, 404 arms, 0 dark, 0 declared-and-missing

The whole-tree run is byte-identical to before because the rule is per-arm on demand, so it inherits no backlog and needs no advisory period. 20 unit tests pass; ruff check, ruff format --check and pyrefly clean on both files. Documented in CLAUDE.md beside the declared-and-missing rule and synced outward.

title: board.jsonl: two rows feed board_transfer with selection fields no arithmetic supports
description:
board_check names both; neither is cosmetic, because both rows are PAIR POINTS in the board_transfer fit whose constant was quoted wrong four times.

l75seat_v1 (ref 56151868, offline 0.8728, board 0.939) declares selection='greedy'. board_check accepts only {search, designed} (board_check.py:84-86), so the field is present-but-unreadable — the same shape of defect as foldseven_v1's 'named', fixed 2026-09-16. Greedy over 226 members ON THE HOLDOUT is a search. But its own offline_scope says 'NOT FITTED: ... any offline number is in-sample by construction', so relabelling it search demands an offline_raw the scope says does not exist, and the honest row may be offline=null with 0.8728 moved to offline_raw — which REMOVES a pair point from the fit.

cleanseat_v1 (ref 56168691, offline 0.8755, board 0.942) declares selection=search with no offline_raw. Its scope states the in-sample number is 0.8843. Entering that gives a correction of -0.0088, against a measured selection bias of +0.0025 to +0.0031 (selection_bias.py:30) — 3x the band, so board_check would refuse the pair rather than accept it. Where 0.8755 came from is not stated in the row and I could not source it; it is not 0.8843 minus any bias in that band.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW: the pricetop/foldseven six-point residual at one offline point is the open blocker, and it is read against strata cut on exactly these offline values. A pair point whose offline is in-sample by construction inflates the compression the fit sees — which is the same mechanism that voided raptor_solo's 0.8938 on 2026-08-29, where one cell carried the whole 'compression goes negative at the top' reading.

DO NOT fix by guessing the missing number. Either source 0.8755 from whatever produced it, or move both rows to offline=null with the in-sample figure in offline_raw and refit. Refit board_transfer after either, and state what the constant moved to.
notes:
FIXED, and the cause was not the one this bead named. Both rows already declared "EXCLUDED from board_transfer" -- in scope_reason PROSE. board_transfer.entries() (:283) filters on the scope FIELD, and both carried scope='ensemble', so the exclusion had never been enforced by anything. Census: 18 rows say EXCLUDED in prose while sitting on the ensemble scope; 16 were dropped only by a null offline, an accident rather than a mechanism, and the 2 with an offline number were in the fit.

Fixed by moving all 18 to scope='excluded' -- the value EXCLUDED at board_transfer.py:178 that is already in SCOPES and that board_check already reads. No number was invented: l75seat_v1's 0.8728 moved to offline_raw (a search's own in-sample score is what that field is for) and its selection='greedy' became 'search', which is what SEARCH's own definition says greedy is ("any argmax over a pool -- member_curve's greedy"). cleanseat_v1's unsourced 0.8755 was VOIDED in writing rather than deleted: offline_raw carries the 0.8843 its own scope names, and offline_scope records that 0.8755 is not 0.8843 minus any value in the measured band. Both gates that could have objected key on "offline is not None" (governed(), :173, and the search-bias rule, :308), so an unpriced row is outside the rule's own scope. board_check exits 0.

THE PAYLOAD, and it is bigger than the two rows. Those two were the ONLY entries above the top band's floor, so the >=0.8711 band -- the band this project actually ships in, and the one CLAUDE.md quoted at +1.71 -- was built entirely out of two offlines that are in-sample by construction. That is the raptor_solo mechanism exactly (one cell carrying a whole reading). Refit: whole record +1.09 -> +1.07, mid band +1.07/65 pairs -> +1.05/62, top band +1.71/2 pairs -> +1.45/3, and the mid band's interval tightened from [+1.00,+1.38] to [+1.00,+1.23]. Resolved inversions held at 21 across the change, so the pair removed inflated the ceiling and mis-ordered nothing. CLAUDE.md updated to the new read with the cause stated.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: the top band still prices on THREE pairs and is still marked DIRECTION ONLY, so the gap to 0.955 still cannot be priced from a single slope -- knee-f9aao's point stands unchanged.

title: board_transfer's hole is the >=0.8704 stratum (n=1), not a four-point fit — and 0.002 is the blur floor
description:
Read from the TOOL on 2026-09-16T21:44Z, not from prose. python -m kneemri.evaluation.board_transfer (it is kneemri.evaluation, NOT kneemri.kaggle) reports: 47 ensemble-scope entries, 909 orderable pairs; compression median +1.05 board points per holdout point over the whole record; among entries at or above 0.8670, 55 resolved pairs at median +1.00 [+0.97, +1.03]; among entries at or above 0.8704, ONE resolved pair at +1.13, flagged DIRECTION ONLY.

TWO CORRECTIONS THIS FORCES.

First, the framing shipped in comp/kernels/kneemri-foldseven's docstring and in commit 0c9da889 - that the curve is 'fitted on the only four entries carrying both numbers, spanning 0.002 of board' - is the wrong mechanism for the right conclusion. board_transfer is PAIRWISE over the record, not a four-point regression, and at or above 0.8670 it is tight (+1.00, interval +/-0.03 over 55 pairs). The hole is real but it is a STRATUM hole: above 0.8704 there is exactly one resolved pair, so the curve at the altitude we actually live at rests on n=1. foldseven's value stands and is sharper than written - it adds a high-offline entry with a known board number, which creates resolved pairs in the n=1 stratum rather than a fifth point in a span.

Second, and independent: board blur is median |board| 0.0020 over the pairs the holdout could not separate. A board delta under 0.002 is a move the board CANNOT CERTIFY. Consequence for the pin: tripleseat_v2 at 0.946 over noraptor_v1 at 0.945 is +0.001, BELOW that floor. The foreign raptor seat's contribution has therefore never been certified by the board, and any statement that raptor is worth +0.001 is an uncertified reading of a single pair. This does not unpin the champion - it is still the best recorded ensemble row - but it does mean the seat cannot be defended on that number.

NEXT: after 56287691 (foldseven) scores, write its row, run entry_offline --write for the offline half, then re-read board_transfer and check whether the >=0.8704 stratum has moved off n=1.
notes:
2026-09-16 22:55Z — THE TOP STRATUM IS OFF n=1, AND THAT DID NOT HELP.

foldseven_v1 landed: offline 0.8767 / board 0.944 (ref 56287691, selection=designed — the row said
'named', which board_check refuses; fixed). It is the first priceable pair near the champion band.

board_transfer, READ FROM THE TOOL:
  whole record      median +1.09
  >= 0.8679         65 pairs, median +1.07  [+1.00, +1.38]
  >= 0.8711          2 pairs, median +1.71  [+1.43, +2.00]  DIRECTION ONLY
So the top band moved n=1 -> n=2 and is still unpriceable. It also does NOT read the ~+0.8 this bead
and CLAUDE.md both believed: nothing in the tool's output says the curve saturates. The >=0.8679
stratum reads +1.07 against a whole-record +1.09 — FLAT, not saturating.

WHY THE CONSTANT KEEPS COMING OUT DIFFERENT (transfer_strata, 45 rebuildable entries):
  slope by difficulty quintile  Q1 +0.43  Q2 +0.68  Q3 +0.98  Q4 +0.86  Q5 +0.66   (r 0.71-0.92)
  sd(board) = 0.0091 in EVERY band
sd(board) is fixed because the board is one number per entry; only the denominator moves. So
'compression' is a statement about the SPREAD OF WHICHEVER RULER SITS IN THE DENOMINATOR, not a
property of the board. That is the mechanism behind three wrong quotes (+4.67, +2.14, +1.55). These
stratum slopes are compression@Qk/offline_Qk and MAY NOT be substituted into a term fitted on the
full ruler (knee-f9aao).

WHAT IS LIKE-FOR-LIKE AND CLOSES AN AXIS:
  714 resolved pairs split at the median hard-share: gain made HARD +0.75, gain made EASY +0.72.
Same pairs, same cut, flat. A gain on hard studies reaches the board exactly as well as one on easy
studies. There is NO difficulty correction to make between our holdout and the board. Suspicion
retired.

THE REAL BLOCKER, which n does not fix:
  pricetop_v1   offline 0.8757 -> board 0.938
  foldseven_v1  offline 0.8767 -> board 0.944
0.001 of offline, 0.006 of board. That residual is 3x the 0.0020 blur and WIDER THAN THE WHOLE
OFFLINE SPAN THE TOP STRATUM IS FITTED OVER. Fitting a slope through 0.006 of scatter needs ~10 more
pair points at one slot each, so buying more pairs is a bad ratio and I stopped doing it. Same
inversion survives into the hardest quintile: Q5 has foldseven 0.8167 -> 0.944 over pricetop
0.8189 -> 0.938, lower offline and six board points higher.

WHAT SEPARATES THE TWO EXPLANATIONS is whether that 0.006 belongs to the SEATS or to the BOARD, and
kneemri-eightseat (pushed 22:55Z) is the one-slot experiment that asks: foldseven's seven plus
labelwise_depth24_s2026, an eighth seat priced at +0.0005 ledger75 by seat_add (EXACT, 909 rows) —
deliberately sub-blur, so the ruler is held still and only the board may move.
2026-09-16 23:05Z — three slots spent on the decomposition of the pricetop/foldseven six-point gap. All three kernels run_check clean (eightseat 8 of 8, rerun 7 of 7, swapseat 7 of 7).

  eightseat  ref 56288513  +1 seat, +0.0005 ledger75 (EXACT, 909 rows)  -> board response to a sub-blur ruler move
  rerun      ref 56288555  byte-identical seats, submit_check --anyway  -> run-to-run scatter, never measured
  swapseat   (owed 23:17Z) different seats, +0.0001 ledger75            -> seat identity at a fixed reading

READ THE RERUN FIRST: it is the error bar and the other two are unreadable without it. Not 0.944 exactly
=> every closure in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md priced on a 0.002-0.004 board delta is retired.

Also corrected the fourth wrong quote of the transfer constant (CLAUDE.md said the curve saturates near
+0.8 in the top band; the tool reads +1.07 at >=0.8679 over 65 pairs against a whole-record +1.09 — flat —
and +1.71 at >=0.8711 over TWO pairs, DIRECTION ONLY). sd(board)=0.0091 in every stratum, so compression
is a property of the denominator ruler's spread, not of the board. Commit 9f58346b, pushed.

title: slotseat rebase is DEAD: --idea shows slot_dropout was retired twice on the board
description:
kneemri-slotseat was rebased onto the champion seven and cleared every gate -- witness_check 175 ok, mount_check --live 0 refused after declaring kneemri-members-2, run_check 'loaded 8 of 8 members', submit_check SET-new. It must still NOT be shipped.

submit_check --idea dropout reports two entries the SET comparison cannot see:
  slotseat_v1 (board 0.944): champion SIX + slot_dropout_s2026. Its own pre-registered FLAT band fired, and the recorded why says it RETIRES THE HYPOTHESIS THE SLOT WAS BOUGHT TO TEST.
  hidose_v1  (board 0.944): the same seat at the higher dose. The PAIR read fires NULL.

So the cross-site ruler's +0.0090 on this member has been offered to the board twice and the board said 0.944 both times. Rebasing onto the seven changes the BASE, not the QUESTION; a third reading buys a slot's worth of the same null. The mechanism (three AugmentConfig identity fields an offline holdout ruler is structurally blind to) is still sound and still unmeasured BY THAT RULER -- what is refuted is the board reading it, twice.

What this costs us to know: --idea is not optional garnish on submit_check. SET equality is the weak half; the idea index is the half that sees a hypothesis wearing a different member list. Every pre-flight from here passes --idea.

The kernel stays on disk, pushed at version 3, gates green -- it is the correct artefact for the day the ruler question is re-opened by a DIFFERENT mechanism, not by a new base.

title: The raptor pass is worth +0.001 — unresolvable, and it costs the seven their kernel budget
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-16 from two board rows, no new slot spent.

tripleseat_v2 (ref 56232529) = seven members + the raptor pass blended at 1/3 -> board 0.946.
noraptor (ref 56263073) = the IDENTICAL seven (final_ws_cf, calib_span_ff, stack_increments_ff, through_dense_cf, labelwise_depth24/ext/dense_drop40_long_s2026), raptor pass removed -> board 0.945.

Delta +0.001. That is BELOW kneemri-tripleseat's own pre-registered BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015 and below the board blur board_transfer measures at median |board| 0.0020 over the 172 pairs the holdout cannot separate. So the raptor seat is NOT certifiable by the board: the seven alone ARE the champion within the board's resolution.

THE LEVER, which is the reason this is P1 and not a note. kneemri-tripleseat:170-174 runs the raptor pass FIRST and hands the seven only what is left: 'the raptor pass cost %ds; the seven get what is left', Budget(seconds=max(KERNEL_SECONDS - spent, 0)). Dropping a pass that buys an unresolvable +0.001 returns the WHOLE kernel budget to the seven. Kernel compute is one of the few axes this project has not closed (calibration, seating, TTA, per-column routing and resolution >=336 are all measured shut), and it is the only one that costs no card and no training.

NEXT: price what the seven can DO with a full budget before spending a slot on it -- more studies per pass, or the overlap TTA the budget currently forbids. Do not ship a budget change as a predicted gain; it is an instrument until a reading prices it.

PRICE: ~0 h card (kernel-side only). P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.05 alone; it is an ENABLER for whatever the freed budget buys.
notes:
RAPTOR BUDGET LEVER IS MUCH SMALLER THAN FILED, and half of it is INERT. Read off tripleseat's own kernel log (kaggle kernels output dimiturnt/kneemri-tripleseat, the commit run, 3 studies):
- 'the raptor pass cost 16s; the seven get what is left' at t=45.8s -- and that 16s INCLUDES the raptor model load, so the per-study marginal is a fraction of it, not a third of the kernel.
- 'serving: ... deadline=27527s'. The whole kernel finished at t=85.8s. At commit scale the budget is not remotely binding; how binding it is on the hidden test depends on the test size, which we do not observe. So 'dropping raptor returns the whole kernel budget' (written into comp/board.jsonl for ref 56263073) OVERSTATES it: what it returns is 16s plus a marginal we cannot separate from the load without a second log.
- 'overlap=False requested, INERT -- all 7 members are whole-stack'. The overlap-TTA half of this bead's premise cannot fire for the champion seven AT ANY BUDGET -- it is refused by member shape, not by time. That half is closed; do not price it again.
What survives: more studies/views per pass, and only if a real submission log shows the seven actually hitting the deadline. No slot until that is shown.

title: Foreign corpora as an independent RULER, not a training source - the ranking instrument we do not have
description:
Owner proposal 2026-09-16: use the derivative-barred corpora (Rijeka CC BY-NC-ND, MRNet Stanford agreement, fastMRI DUA, SKM-TEA) for MEASUREMENT only, on the reading that measuring creates no adaptation and so no derivative.

LICENCE: sound, and already project policy - this is not a new permission. comp/members.roster header rules that a merged member of ANY scheme is an OFFLINE result that gets a "# licence: <corpus>" tag, and submit_check refuses on the TAGs PRESENCE rather than a corpus list. lost_fragments_census.md:81 records the owner ruling knee-vgz5b.7 as "instrument only". So the project already TRAINS on them offline and refuses at ship; measuring-only is strictly inside that envelope.

DISTRIBUTION EXPOSURE: CHECKED AND CLEAR. fastMRIs DUA forbids distributing "any subsequent variables or data files derived from the fastMRI Dataset to any person or entity", and an AUC committed to a public repo is arguably a subsequent variable. gh repo view on 2026-09-16 reads isPrivate true for dimiturtrz/rsna_knee_kaggle. If this repo is ever made public, every foreign-derived number in README, the ledger and board.jsonl becomes a distribution question. THAT IS THE TRIPWIRE - re-check before any publication.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW, and why it matters now: not a data source but a RULER. The closed-axis inventory (knee-2s0gp) plus the pricetop_v1 row show our offline holdout tops out at 0.938 priceable while EVERY board entry at or above 0.943 carries offline null by construction (--fold -1, holds nothing out). We rank members with a ruler that cannot see the regime we ship in. knee-1pgl already names SKM-TEA "the projects only external validation set" and it has never been decoded.

CHANNEL, written down rather than denied: if a foreign AUC selects WHICH member ships, foreign data has influenced the shipped artefact. Difference from training is BITS, NOT KIND - selecting 1-of-N leaks about log2(N) bits, training leaks the corpus. Not an adaptation in licence terms, but it is not zero and must not be described as zero.

WORK: the blocker is that the instrument is unbuilt (SKM-TEA never decoded). Before spending card on the decode, the cheap question is whether a foreign ruler ORDERS members differently from the 909-study holdout at all - kneemri/kaggle/ruler_swap.py and kneemri/evaluation/transfer_strata.py already exist and may answer it on the foreign readings already on disk. Do that first; a foreign ruler that agrees with ours everywhere is not worth a decode.

UNPRICED - needs PRICE and P(clears) before arm_check will accept any arm naming it.
notes:
SUPERSEDED 2026-09-16 19:13Z by owner: 'im gonig to have to make the model and the training method public'. The private-repo clearance above is VOID -- it rested on a premise the owner removed.

Re-ruled against COMPETITION_RULES.txt, four clauses:
- :119-122 winner licenses Submission + source under CC-BY-NC 4.0.
- :128-130 carve-out: input data or pretrained models with an incompatible licence need NOT be open-sourced.
- :187-196 winner must deliver training code, inference code, environment AND model weights, and 'The model weights should be provided as a public kaggle dataset.'
- :144 (Sec 6a) 'You may use data other than the Competition Data to develop and TEST your Submissions.'

RULING, unchanged in outcome, harder in reason:
1. TRAINING on Rijeka/MRNet/fastMRI/SKM-TEA stays BARRED. Publication is now compulsory for a winner, so a foreign-fitted member's weights would have to go up as a PUBLIC Kaggle dataset -- exactly the distribution of an adaptation all four licences forbid. The roster '# licence:' tag gate is correct and is now load-bearing for a rules obligation, not only for a DUA.
2. MEASUREMENT-only use is CLEAN and is named in the rules: :144 permits external data to TEST a Submission. Nothing foreign enters the weights, so the published artefact distributes nothing derived.
3. The honesty worry filed above RESOLVES. A foreign ruler in the member-SELECTION step is legal under :144, therefore fully describable under :132. No incomplete method description.

Publication exposure of the CURRENT champion: NONE. Checked 19:13Z -- all seven members (final_ws_cf, calib_span_ff, stack_increments_ff, through_dense_cf, labelwise_depth24/ext/dense_drop40_long_s2026) carry no licence tag, and members.roster:126 records every scored entry as 100% DINOv2-small (Apache-2.0). The only licence-binding trunk in the pool is dinov3_base_lora_s2026 (Meta licence, not Apache); it has never shipped. If a DINOv3 member ever enters a shipping entry, :128-130 excuses open-sourcing the TRUNK but does not excuse publishing fine-tuned weights that contain it -- re-check then.
RAN 2026-09-16 19:14Z, card-free: ruler_swap --table local_reader_annotated.csv --seats 7.

RESULT: churn 0.000. All seven seats held, 0.9577 under both rulers, 127 members over the 909 shared studies.

BUT THE NULL IS WEAK AND THAT IS THE FINDING: 'the candidate table reads 0.0143 of the 10908 cells' -- 156 cells, the partially-read gold 58. title: Board cannot certify a move under 0.0020 - stop spending slots inside the blur
description:
board_transfer over the 143-row record (run 2026-09-16 19:01Z) measures the public board blur directly: median |board| 0.0020 over the 172 pairs the holdout could not separate, and 0.0020 again restricted to pairs sharing >= 4 members. A delta smaller than that is a move the board cannot certify. Inversions: 50/909 orderable pairs ordered the other way, 21/660 of the pairs the holdout DID resolve (gap >= 0.0053) - a 3.2 percent inversion rate on cleanly-resolved pairs.

Consequence for slot policy: a slot spent to separate two entries whose OFFLINE gap is under 0.0053 buys nothing, because the board is provably unable to answer. Six reseating entries at 0.945/0.946 are one such family. Spend slots only where offline moved >= 0.005.

Second reading, on the same run: in-regime compression is +1.00 board points per holdout point among entries at or above 0.8670 (55 resolved pairs, [+0.97, +1.03]). So closing the 0.011 board gap to the leader needs +0.011 OFFLINE, about 1.1 percent absolute - just under the 1.5 percent project bar. That is the size of the real target, and it rules out every knob-sized lever as a route to first place.

Third, from comp/COMPETITION_RULES.txt: :507 public LB is a representative SAMPLE, :505 the PRIVATE LB determines final standing, :497 membership is never disclosed. So the 0.011 is a public-sample number and the shakeup is unmeasurable by anyone. The champion pin is the private-LB hedge.
notes:
QUALIFICATION, from the pricetop_v1 row (ref 56275593, comp/board.jsonl, scored today 0.938): the +1.00-per-holdout-point in-regime slope is fitted ONLY on the offline-priceable population, and that population tops out at 0.938 on the board. Every board row at or above 0.943 carries offline null BY CONSTRUCTION - tripleseat_v2 0.946 included - because those seats are fitted --fold -1 / cf and hold nothing out.

So "closing 0.011 needs +0.011 offline" EXTRAPOLATES a slope past the top of the region it was fitted in. That is the exact failure board_check documents (a kernel quoting the slope of a region it has already left), and it must not be quoted as a target. What the record supports instead: the priceable and the board-winning populations are DISJOINT, so maximising the 909-study blend cannot reach the champion from inside it.

Direct consequence for the owner question "are the people above us really better": we cannot answer it with CV, and neither can they, because the entries that occupy the top band are all-data fits with no holdout by construction. There is no CV for a --fold -1 entry. The blur number (0.0020) and the inversion rate (21/660) stand as measured; the slope-to-0.955 does not.

title: patch-occlusion maps: does the model's spatial read concentrate, or scatter?
description:
Grid-occlusion sweep producing a per-study, per-label importance map, to gate the self-distilled-locator line (owner idea: derive centre+spread from our own model's attribution, train a locator on it, delicense roi_cache.py's SKM-TEA Locator).

WHAT: Attribution.patch_importance zeroes each of grid**2 cells across all slots/slices and records the per-study probability drop. Output (studies, 12, G, G) float32 npz. Not an AUC delta - the existing region/ring sweeps already collapse to holdout AUC and that is exactly what makes them unusable as a locator target.

GATE (pre-registered): centre mass fraction = sum(inner 4 cells)/sum(all). Uniform/diffuse null = 0.25 at G=4. Well above 0.25 with per-study centroid agreement = maps carry signal, locator line is alive. At ~0.25 the line dies.

PRIOR: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-11_what-actually-moved-the-number.md:937 measured border-only 0.8006 vs centre-only 0.8021 vs whole 0.8448 on an August ~0.845 member - centre approx border, i.e. diffuse. Never re-run at 336 px or on a labelwise member. This is that finding re-asked 16-way on a current member.

PRICE: ~4 h cpu (17 forwards x 200 studies x 4.276 s/study, measured 2026-09-16 on labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026 at 336px/6 slots/20 slices). On a card the same sweep is minutes and 8x8 over the full 909 holdout becomes affordable.
P(clears gate) ~ 0.30 - our own border/centre number predicts a null.
EXPECTED SCORE: 0. INSTRUMENT: it licenses or retires the whole ROI/focal axis, the axis merged_corpus moved (focal +0.0056 vs regional -0.0031).

VALIDATION (free, exists): kneemri/evaluation/locator_audit.py measures landmark centroid distance in mm on SKM-TEA's test split - instrument use, permitted. Catches the circularity failure where a locator distilled from a periphery-reading model crops to skin, coil and air.
notes:
SMOKE (n=4, plumbing only, NOT a result) 2026-09-16 15:39Z, labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026, grid 4, cpu:
12/12 labels above the 0.25 diffuse null. Centre shares 0.322 (MCL) to 0.681 (Contusion), mean ~0.50.
Baker's centroid row 2.61 against 1.24-1.82 for every other label - a popliteal (posterior) finding sitting posterior is the one displacement a pixel-statistics confound cannot manufacture.

CONFOUND NAMED AND CONTROLLED. A centred map is NOT evidence of a learned anatomical read: blanking a middle cell removes more tissue than blanking a corner, so an untrained model would also peak in the middle. That confound is a property of the pixels and is IDENTICAL for a positive and a negative study. So the deciding reading is PatchMaps.label_contrast - the separation between the positive studies' centroid and the negative studies' centroid, in cells, read against the per-study scatter. Added, tested, wired into the report. Costs zero extra forwards (the npz already carries truth).

REVISED GATE: centre share above 0.25 is necessary, not sufficient. The line is alive only where 'moved' exceeds that label's own scatter.

RUNNING: 200 studies, grid 4, cpu, launched 15:40Z, ETA ~19:40Z, log scratchpad/patch200.log. Owner says a GPU is coming - on a card the same sweep is minutes and 8x8 over the full 909 holdout becomes affordable, so this CPU arm is the floor, not the answer.
2026-09-16 16:40Z GPU PRICED AND LAUNCHED. Card granted by owner. Labels path recovered: PROCESSED resolves through paths.yaml to D:/data/volumetric/mri/processed/rsna_knee_abnormality, so LABELS=$PROCESSED/labels/report_labels_v2.csv (experiments/lib.sh:72) — my guessed D:/data/processed/... does not exist and cost one dead smoke.

TIMING, measured: grid 8 over 32 studies = 84 s wall including ~15 s model load and decode, so ~0.034 s/study/pass on cuda against 4.276 s/study/pass on cpu — 125x. The full 909-study 8x8 (65 passes) prices at ~33 min compute, ~45 min wall. The 69 h cpu figure in patch_maps.STUDIES is a cpu fact and stays true; the card makes the full holdout the default question rather than a subset.

RUNNING: 909 studies, grid 8, labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026, launched 16:36Z, ETA ~17:20Z, log scratchpad/patch909.log, npz to scratchpad/patches/.

SUPERSEDED AND DEAD: the 200-study grid-4 cpu sweep launched 15:40Z is gone from the process table with no npz and no traceback — killed, ~56 min spent, nothing produced. Not re-run; the card answers the bigger question in less time.

DEFECT FOUND BY THE SMOKE AND FIXED (472ae18e): at --grid 2 centre_mass read 1.000 on all twelve labels and the report printed '12 of 12 labels above the diffuse null'. grid // 4 is 0 there, so the central half was the whole map — the gate was not passing, it was not being asked. Now refused at parse time (FINEST_GRID = 4) rather than after the hours. Also committed a94b13c1: patch_importance blanks each cell IN PLACE with a finally-restore instead of copying the corpus, which at 909 studies was a 12 GB memcpy 64 times.
GATE FAILED — full 909-study holdout, grid 8, labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026, 2026-09-16 17:14Z (~45 min on the card, 65 passes).

FIRST, THE NULL WAS WRONG. CENTRE_SHARE_NULL = 0.25 is the share of a FLAT field. No map over a knee is flat — a middle cell is joint, a corner is air/coil/skin — so blanking the middle removes more signal even for a model that learned nothing, and a centre share over 0.25 is the EXPECTED reading, not a finding. Measured tissue null over this holdout at grid 8 = 0.3083 (TissueNull, commit 9daecb4c, zero forward passes). Effusion moves concentrated -> DIFFUSE on the correct denominator; 12 of 12 becomes 11 of 12.

THE VERDICT DOES NOT REST ON EITHER NULL. Centroids for all twelve labels span rows 2.57-4.04 and cols 2.84-4.02 — about 1.4 cells on an 8x8 grid, all piled on the grid centre (3.5). The anatomy check, which needs no null:
  Medial OA col 3.14 vs Lateral OA col 3.20 = 0.06 cells apart. One cell = 42 px at 336. Medial and lateral compartments are opposite sides of the joint; true separation is 2-3 cells.
  Medial Meniscus 3.60 vs Lateral Meniscus 3.14 = 0.46 cells, and the SIGN is opposite to the OA pair. The same anatomical axis, two pairs, disagreeing about which way medial is.
label_contrast: 3 of 12 clear their own scatter and all three are marginal (ACL 0.40 vs 0.37, MCL 0.26 vs 0.25, Lateral Meniscus 0.54 vs 0.52) — with twelve comparisons that is what chance looks like.

So the model concentrates but does not LOCALISE, and a per-pathology locator fitted on these maps learns one crop twelve times. Step 3 is not licensed. P(clears gate) was 0.30 in this bead, revised down to 0.10 by the grid-8 32-study smoke, and the full run resolves it at 0.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT: the maps still truthfully mark what THIS model leans on, by construction — that is all occlusion-driven targeted erasing needs, so that arm survives this reading. And the tissue null is a PROXY; the exact control is the same sweep under a randomly initialised head (~45 min card), which would turn the proxy into a measurement. Neither is needed to reject the locator.

Artefacts: scratchpad/patches/labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026_g8.patches.npz (maps+studies+truth), scratchpad/patch909.log (flat-null reading), scratchpad/reread.log (tissue-null reading).
2026-09-16 18:16Z — THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION, on the TRAIN split. The g4 sweep of the train split ran in four blocks (3498 studies) and each block's own reading repeats the holdout verdict. Block 2700 (798 studies): '12 of 12 labels above the null', '1 of 12 labels separate positives from negatives by more than their scatter'.

So the kill now holds across: (a) the g8 holdout sweep, (b) the g4 holdout sweep, (c) the g4 train sweep, three different grids/splits. The maps ARE above a null — they are not noise — but they do not separate a label's positives from its negatives, which is the property a locator target needs and the property this gate asks for. Self-distilled localization stays closed.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT, and the distinction is the whole point: knee-0e2gd (occlusion-driven erasing) consumes a DIFFERENT property of the same maps — 'the cells THIS model leans on', which is true by construction of an occlusion sweep and needs no anatomical correctness. That arm stays open and is now P0.

title: Five of six slice poolings share one cache shape, so build_embeddings writes byte-identical files under different names
description:

That is 7.8 GB of duplicates and four encode passes of card time (readout_probe, 2026-09-02) that measured nothing - the arm printed 96 AUCs across two readouts and every digit matched, which reads as a perfect null and is a plumbing defect.

MECHANISM, and it is not a dropped flag. --slice-read DOES reach StudyDesign (build_embeddings.py:76) and the model does consume it (model.py:232). The collision is in the KEY. EmbeddingSpec.slice_read is in the cache filename (embedding_cache.py:140) and its own docstring says why: it 'decides the SHAPE of what is stored' - per_slice leaves a slice axis, whole-stack consumes it. Shape is a TWO-valued question. The field carries a SIX-valued name. slice_pooling.py:88-94 has channels per_slice=False and max/attend/depth/labelwise/moments/moments_wide all per_slice=True, so five names produce one array and differ only in a filename token. Both caches here are (4407, 6, 12, 3072) with the slice axis intact, which is the proof: neither pooling ran at encode time, because for a per-slice read there is nothing for it to do. The reduction those names describe happens at READ time - kneemri/evaluation/slice_readout.py, which already records this in its module docstring and is the workaround knee-n647 shipped.

AND build_embeddings NEVER CHECKS cache.exists() - it goes straight to cache.build(), so even an exact-name rebuild re-spends the hour.

THE HONEST FIX IS A RENAME and it is NOT what this bead proposes first: keying on per_slice rather than the pooling name would be correct and would break ~60 hardcoded stems (feature_probe.py:58-95, neighbour_errors.py:65-69) plus every cache on disk. FIX HERE, zero blast radius: EmbeddingSpec grows equivalent() (the specs whose bytes this one duplicates) and EmbeddingCache grows duplicate() (a finished one of those on disk), and build_embeddings refuses before encoding, naming the twin and pointing at --slice-readout. --anyway '<why>' spends it deliberately, per the foreign_run convention.

PRICE: ~0 h of card, CPU only, and it is a pure loss-avoider - it buys no score. It pays for itself the first time an arm asks for a second per-slice readout, which is a thing arms do: readout_probe did it four times in one run.
notes:
2026-09-17 02:55Z — THIS BEAD WAS PARTLY STALE WHEN READ. The fix it proposes as new is already shipped: EmbeddingSpec.equivalent() (embedding_cache.py:117) and EmbeddingCache.duplicate() (:204) exist, and build_embeddings.py refuses a byte-identical twin before encoding, naming the twin and pointing at --slice-readout. Only the SECOND half of the description was still open — 'build_embeddings NEVER CHECKS cache.exists()'.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY STILL BROKEN, and it is worse than re-spending an hour. The guard read
  twin = None if cache.exists() or arguments.anyway else cache.duplicate()
so an EXACT-NAME rebuild set twin to None and fell straight through to cache.build(). build() opens the features with open_memmap(mode='w+'), which allocates and TRUNCATES the finished array in place, and writes the mask and index only after the encode loop returns. So a rebuild of a healthy cache destroys it for the length of the encode, and a rebuild that DIES leaves exactly the prefix-with-zero-tail state exists() was written to detect — two caches on this machine are already in it (orthodiff 284/4407, large_336 504/4407, per exists()'s docstring). The rebuild path was one of the ways to manufacture that state.

FIXED. build_embeddings now refuses a cache that exists() and is complete, before the pixel cache is mapped, releasable with --anyway '<why>'. A cache whose build DIED does not reach the refusal, because exists() compares the index mtime against the features mtime and a dead build leaves the index older — so the one rebuild that must still be possible still is.

NO TEST ADDED, deliberately: the branch composes exists() and duplicate(), both already mirrored, and reaching it from main() needs a data root, a pixel cache and a card, which the 'small' gate forbids a unit test to touch.

STILL OPEN on this bead: the 7.8 GB of duplicate .npy files are still on disk and are NOT approved for deletion.

title: INSTRUMENT: a priceable blend above the record's offline maximum, to give board_transfer's top band leverage it has never had
description:
PRICE: ~0 h card (CPU kit build only; no training). P(clears 0.946) ~ 0.02 - it is NOT expected to beat the pin and must not be sold as trying to.

WHY. board_transfer's top regime reads +0.82 [+0.71, +0.93] over FOUR resolved pairs and the tool labels it DIRECTION ONLY. That reading is what prices the whole remaining project: the gap from the pinned 0.946 to the 0.955 goal converts to a +0.0092 to +0.011 OFFLINE requirement through it, and the top-band slope is the single most load-bearing unmeasured number we have. It has been quoted wrong three times (+4.67, +2.14, x1.55).

WHY IT IS DIRECTION ONLY, measured today. The whole priceable record TOPS OUT at offline 0.8751 (board 0.937). The band at or above 0.8695 holds 13 entries spanning 0.8695-0.8751 = 0.0056 offline - and the holdout's own resolution floor is 0.0053. So nearly every pair in the band is UNRESOLVED by construction, and 4 of them scrape over. The slope up there is not weakly measured, it is fitted across a span barely wider than the floor: the exact shape of the +4.67 error, which was a slope through 0.0043 of offline spread inside a 0.0062 noise floor.

WHAT THIS BUYS. priceable_blend's best all-priceable 7-member set reads offline 0.8792 - **+0.0041 above the record's maximum**. Shipping it extends the band's span 0.0056 -> 0.0097 (+73%) and resolves (gap >= 0.0053) against 8 of the band's 13 entries, taking its resolved pairs from 4 to roughly 12. That is a tripling of the evidence under the number that prices every remaining decision, bought with one slot and no card.

MEMBERS (all fold != -1, hence priceable by construction - which is the point; 42 board entries at >= 0.940 carry offline null because their seats are --fold -1, comp/champion.json:54):
  labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026, oof_teacher_s2026, labelwise_dense_drop40_long36_s2026,
  margin_seat_s2026, warm_calib_lowlr_drop40_long_s2026, labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026,
  blendhold_s2026

PRE-REGISTERED, against the tool's own interval, read BEFORE the slot is spent:
  - board 0.940-0.941: the top-band slope is confirmed at ~+0.8, and the 0.955 requirement stands at +0.0092 to +0.011 offline. The interval tightens on triple the pairs.
  - board >= 0.943: compression at the top is HIGHER than the tool reads, the offline requirement SHRINKS, and every axis closed for delivering under +0.005 offline gets re-priced. This is the outcome worth the slot.
  - board <= 0.938: compression at the top is lower or the curve has gone flat, 0.955 needs MORE than +0.011 offline than we thought, and the member problem is worse than stated.
  Any of the three is information. There is no null outcome, which is what makes it an instrument rather than a hope.

NOT A RESEATING. The board has four distinct seat sets tied at 0.946 and a byte-identical re-ship reproducing it; the pool's honest top five span 0.0009. Nothing in the pool can beat the pin, so per the pacing rule the slot goes to an instrument and the submission message says so.

Blocked on: kernel build (copy the kneemri-distinct14 shape), then submit_check --kernel, kit_check, mount_check --live, witness_check, champion_check, board_read --live.
notes:
MEMBER SET CORRECTED BEFORE THE KIT WAS BUILT (2026-09-16 07:49Z). The seven-seat 0.8792 was UNSHIPPABLE.

priceable_blend's greedy search ranges over every member with a holdout record. It does not
ask whether a member is PACKAGED or whether it has been DECLINED IN WRITING, so its headline
set is not an entry. Seat 3, labelwise_dense_drop40_long36_s2026, is on neither shelf and is
declined at comp/members.declines:1240 with an argument I cannot answer: it is the 36-epoch
horizon control for a seat already rostered, it lost to its own 24-epoch twin by -0.0018
against a pre-registered +0.003 bar, and a strictly-worse duplicate of a pool seat contributes
correlated error rather than diversity. A decline is re-opened by naming a mechanism, never by
re-quoting a number, and I have no mechanism.

SHIPPING SET, six seats, all packaged and none declined (verified per-line against both shelf
rosters, comp/members.roster and comp/members2.roster):
  shelf 1 (kneemri-members):   margin_seat_s2026, warm_calib_lowlr_drop40_long_s2026, blendhold_s2026
  shelf 2 (kneemri-members-2): labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026, oof_teacher_s2026,
                               labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026
The kernel must mount BOTH shelves, as kneemri-tripleseat does.

OFFLINE 0.8785 (priceable_blend --members, the six as a set). Losing the declined seat costs
-0.0007, which does not touch the argument:
  - record's priceable maximum      0.8751   (board 0.937)
  - this entry                      0.8785   +0.0034 over it
  - top band span 0.8695-0.8751     0.0056  ->  0.8695-0.8785 = 0.0090, +61%
  - resolves (gap >= 0.0053) against the 8 band entries at or below 0.8732, taking the band's
    resolved pairs from 4 to ~12. The tripling claim in the description SURVIVES the correction.
Predicted board 0.940 [0.940, 0.940], direction only. Pre-registration is unchanged except that
its centre moves 0.941 -> 0.940; the three branches (>=0.943 / 0.940-0.941 / <=0.938) still
partition the outcome and still each carry a consequence.

ON THE SEARCH OPTIMISM, because it would otherwise look like it eats the whole margin.
priceable_blend --optimism reads +0.0019: the blend is greedily selected on the same holdout it
is scored on. That does NOT deflate the +0.0034, because the tool's own docstring states the ten-
fold default is 'the regime every offline number in comp/board.jsonl was taken in' - the entries
this is compared against are optimistic by the same construction. The bias is common-mode and the
ORDERING, which is the only thing board_transfer reads, is what survives it.
2026-09-16 07:55-08:00Z: kernel BUILT, pre-flighted, committed c9f1e070, pushed to Kaggle as kneemri-pricetop v1 (running).

Pre-flight chain, all green:
- submit_check --kernel kneemri-pricetop --idea priceable: 'ok ... 6 members, no recorded entry carries this set'.
- mount_check: 'kneemri-pricetop: ok - declares all of metaresearch/dinov2/PyTorch/small/1'; --live same. (142 ok / 12 skipped / 0 refused of 154; pricetop is NOT among the skipped - confirmed by grep, its line sits alphabetically above the tail.)
- kit_check / --mounted: dimiturnt/kneemri-kit at c3effa61, 2 commits behind - both are roi (d6f290bd roi_native, 7c970644 roi_cache). No pricetop seat is an roi member, and champion_check reports the pinned tripleseat_v2 buildable at the SAME kit, so the lag does not touch this entry.
- witness_check --device auto --members <the six>: '6 ok, 0 unverified, 0 refused'; worst seat labelwise_depth24 at max|diff| 0.00836 of the 0.0312 bound. (The flag is --members; --only is rejected.)
- champion_check: 'tripleseat_v2 (0.946, kit c3effa61) is still buildable: 7 members named and packaged'.
- board_read --live: rank 66 of 3817, tied with 5 at 0.946; leader 0.957, gap 0.011, read 2026-09-16T07:54Z. Trend over 119 reads / 20.4 days: ours +0.00016/day, frontier +0.00037/day, closing -0.00021/day - the frontier is NOT being caught at this rate.

PRIOR THE IDEA CHECK SURFACED, and it matters for the branch reading: ceiling5_v1 (board 0.934) is the SAME construction one size down - 'five members chosen by an offline blend SEARCH over the 195 priceable members on the 909-study holdout'. So pricetop is not an untried shape; it is ceiling5 with one more seat and a higher offline point (0.8785 vs ceiling5's). That gives the instrument a second anchor rather than one: whatever pricetop scores, the ceiling5 pair is already on the record at the same population, and the two together price the curve over the band instead of at a point. It also sharpens the expectation - 0.934 is what the five-seat version of this search returned on the board.
close_reason: READ 2026-09-16 11:05Z: board 0.938 (ref 56275593, API status COMPLETE). The <=0.938 branch fired, and its written cause is wrong - the prediction was fed the RAW offline 0.8785 on a SEARCH entry. Bias-corrected at the measured +0.0028 (knee-jsgb) the offline is 0.8757, and against greedyseat_v1's 0.8740 -> 0.936 the pair gives +1.18 board points per holdout point. At the fitted +0.8 the corrected value predicts 0.937 vs the read 0.938 - inside the board's 0.001 resolution. So compression at the top is NOT flat; the instrument priced the search bias on the board a second time. Second reading, and the load-bearing one: every board row >=0.943 carries offline null by construction, so the priceable population and the board-winning population are DISJOINT and the priceable one caps at 0.938. Full entry in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md; row in comp/board.jsonl.

title: board_transfer x1.55 is a prose constant and it is wrong: the top-band compression is ~1:1
description:
2026-09-16 07:18Z. Read from the tool (python -m kneemri.evaluation.board_transfer), which comp/champion.json:55 says in as many words to do: 'Read it from the tool, never from prose, and if the two disagree the record is stale, not the tool.'

WHAT THE TOOL READS, 46 ensemble entries, 867 orderable pairs:
  whole record            median +1.05 board points per holdout point ('the wrong number to price an arm with')
  entries >= 0.8670       42 resolved pairs, median +0.98 [+0.94, +1.01]
  entries >= 0.8695        4 resolved pairs, median +0.82 [+0.71, +0.93]  DIRECTION ONLY
  board blur                                 median |board| 0.0020
  inversions              50/867 pairs the board ordered the other way; 21/624 of pairs the holdout resolved

WHAT PROSE SAYS: x1.55. experiments/README.md:14303-14370 projects the corpus lever as '+0.0201 offline
/ +0.031 board at transfer x1.55'. I repeated that figure to the owner at 07:09Z today to price the gap
to 0.955. It is the THIRD wrong value this constant has carried: +4.67 (slope through noise, five pairs
inside a 0.0062 floor), then +2.14 (computed by hand from stale prose, mis-pairing gradeswap's offline
with finalfit's board), now x1.55. Each was quoted rather than read.

CONSEQUENCE. Every board projection derived from an offline delta in the ledger is inflated ~1.6-1.9x.
The gap arithmetic: board 0.946 -> goal 0.955 is +0.009, which at +0.98 needs +0.0092 OFFLINE and at the
top-band +0.82 needs +0.011 — not the +0.0058 I stated. Against a 0.0010 seed spread that is a 9-11x
move, from a pool whose honest top five (pool.ledger) span 0.0009.

SECOND CONSEQUENCE, unrelated to the constant. Board blur is 0.0020, so a 0.001 tick is not certifiable.
noraptor_v1 0.945 vs tripleseat_v2 0.946 therefore does NOT bound the raptor seat below 0.001 — it fails
to measure it at all. Any note reading that tick as a bound should be corrected.

WHY IT PERSISTS: the tool is a PULL channel and prose is what gets read. Not proposing a check —
proposing that the three prose sites carrying a transfer number (README:14303-14370, and any
interpretation quoting x1.55) be edited to name the tool instead of a value, which is the only form that
cannot go stale. That edit is CPU work and needs no card.

FIX SCOPE: grep the tree for the literal constants, replace with a pointer to board_transfer, and re-read
any conclusion that was priced through one.
notes:
FIX SCOPE EXECUTED 2026-09-16 07:30Z, and it is SMALLER than the bead assumed.

Swept the tracked tree for the constant: 382 hits over 116 files. Triaged, near all are
CORRECT usage — the tool's NAME, which is exactly what the rule asks for. Three classes:

1. HISTORICAL RECORD, left alone deliberately. 60-odd dated interpretations under
   interpretations/kneemri/ and 30-odd shipped comp/kernels/*.py each quote the constant of
   their day (+4.67, +2.14, +1.82, +1.92, +1.72). Editing a dated log or a kernel that has
   already scored would falsify the record of what was believed when the entry shipped —
   the kernels are the primary evidence that a stale slope SHIPPED, which is board_check's
   whole case. They stay.
2. CODE, already clean. No module hardcodes a slope for USE. Every hit in kneemri/ is a
   docstring recording this defect: board_check.py:12-16 already states the curve-and-
   saturation reading and the read-from-the-tool rule, and board_claims.py:15 /
   claims_check.py:16 already carry the +1.82-vs-+1.55 prose defect as a claim. Nothing
   to fix; the check that guards this was written before I broke the rule again.
3. LIVE INSTRUCTION, two files, BOTH NOW FIXED.
   - experiments/README.md beta table — the conclusion priced through x1.55. Withdrawn
     in b942d59b, pushed.
   - CLAUDE.md:262 (-> AGENTS.md via agent_md_sync.sh) — THE SENTENCE I QUOTED FROM. It
     read '+1.82 against a complete set's +1.55', which makes the completeness argument
     correctly and leaves +1.55 standing as the right answer. It is not: a fit moves every
     time the record gains a row, so BOTH numbers are stale, and a single slope is the wrong
     SHAPE for a saturating curve whatever its value. Rewritten to say so, and to record
     that this line is where the third wrong quote came from.

THE ROOT CAUSE, which the bead title half-states: the failure is not that a wrong number was
written down, it is that a number was written down AT ALL in a place whose readers cannot tell
a fitted scalar from a curve's midpoint. All three wrong quotes (+4.67, +2.14, x1.55) came out
of prose that was accurate WHEN WRITTEN. So no amount of correcting values closes this; only
removing the value from the live surface does, which is what both edits did.
SWEEP VERIFIED 2026-09-16 13:07Z, both consequences landed; closing.

CONSEQUENCE 1 (the constant): the two LIVE-INSTRUCTION sites are fixed and pushed — experiments/README.md beta table withdrawn in b942d59b, CLAUDE.md:262 rewritten to name the tool and record that a single slope is the wrong SHAPE for a saturating curve. Historical interpretations and shipped kernels deliberately keep the constant of their day; editing them would destroy the evidence that a stale slope SHIPPED.

CONSEQUENCE 2 (the tick as a bound): comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:4253 now carries the correction inline rather than in a bead nobody greps — the noraptor entry is marked THE BOUND ABOVE IS WRONG BY 2x with the 0.0020 blur stated, and the paired per-seat reading is struck through and withdrawn on all three of its steps (additivity, scale, direction). Nothing else in the tree reads that tick as a bound: grep over *.md/*.jsonl finds noraptor only in board.jsonl (a record, no claim), SUBMISSIONS.md (corrected) and this bead family.

Live check: board_check --live at 13:06Z reads 143 recorded submissions, 100 live, exit 0.

title: Axis audit 2026-09-16: every axis but CORPUS is closed, and the corpus lever's own 224px test read NULL
description:

ARCHITECTURE IS CLOSED, by the table already on disk. interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-15_model_compute_table.md, Recommendation 1, verbatim: 'No smaller or cheaper trunk qualifies. dinov2-small at 336 is already the cheapest trunk within 0.01.' 25 trunks priced. Every larger one loses -- dinov2-base 0.8887 at 4x the FLOPs, dinov3-large 0.8525, rad-dino 0.8396, vit-base-in21k 0.8037. Bigger is worse, measured, not argued.

Depth closed at :8188 on its own re-run with the rate confound removed.

I HAD THIS WRONG AND SAID SO TO THE OWNER. I reported 336px as 'the top open lever, untested above 224'. Two separate wrong claims in one window.

README:14303 prices it -- beta = 0.22 fitted on our OWN three-point learning curve (train_fraction 0.25/0.50/1.00 = 874/1749/3498 studies, error 0.2093/0.1656/0.1422; beta 0.338 then 0.220). A doubling prices at +0.0201 offline / +0.031 board at transfer 1.55. Best knob this project ever found is +0.008 and it was a repair.
knee-g7d5i gives the mechanism: our 4407 studies occupy a 17.5-effective-dim shell (PC1-10 = 62% of between-study variance, one protocol, one population, n=4407 denominator). More of OUR studies buys density inside the shell; a SECOND SITE moves it.
knee-17hjk settles the licence axis on the HOST'S OWN WORDS -- KneeCoT was refused for GATING, not for NC. KMAR-50K (CC BY 4.0, Mendeley, open download, no agreement) is the one corpus that passes the test Kaggle actually applied.

BUT THE 224px TEST ALREADY RAN AND READ NULL. README:16255 and :16307 -- mergedk_corpus 0.8490 (+0.0039 vs base224_control), mergedk_drop40 0.8530 (+0.0079), the 2x2 closes with the two levers ADDING, and NEITHER buys an ensemble seat: as a seat mergedk_corpus is -0.0011 [-0.0018, -0.0003] and mergedk_drop40 -0.0006 [-0.0013, +0.0001]. Ledger heading: 'the gain is the SITE, not the supervision', and 'neither the sum nor the stack buys a seat'.

SO THE HONEST RANKING OF WHAT REMAINS, all card-gated:
1. mergedk at 336px / champion geometry. The 224 null was measured at the CHEAP geometry against a 224 control, on a family the compute table shows is 0.018 below the champion. Cache is PRE-STAGED and complete -- verified 2026-09-16: (5495, 6, 12, 336, 336) uint8, 5495 = 4407 + 1088, mask tail populated, 235 GB free (knee-rijuv closed today as stale).
2. knee-00zxt -- the pseudo-label student. A DIFFERENT mechanism from a corpus merge (soft cross-site targets during fine-tuning, not more rows), and pre-registered on a DIFFERENT ruler (foreign_readout decode toll vs band_dense_s2026's -0.0361), which is the one holdout909 is blind to. labels/kmar_pseudo.csv already holds 1088 rows.

ONE NUMBER NEEDS RECONCILING BEFORE EITHER IS QUOTED: knee-g7d5i's description cites 'mergedk at +0.0099 (knee-dl65h header)'. The ledger at :16276 prices mergedk at +0.0039 on holdout909 and NEGATIVE as a seat. Those are different statistics or different populations and neither bead says which -- STATISTIC/POPULATION/CUT is unstated on at least one of them. title: An arm's pre-registered band is prose, so no outcome can be compared to it
description:
arm_check enforces pre-registration with PRICE_MARKS = ('PRICE:', 'P(clears') — a SUBSTRING test (kneemri/experiments/arm_check.py:50,353). Every arm must state what it expects; that statement is prose, so nothing can ask whether an outcome DEVIATED from it.

Why: an interrupt is only worth its cost when it carries news, and news means deviation. On 2026-09-15 twenty arms finished and nineteen sat unread six hours; the first fix (posting every ARM DONE to inbox/main) was refused by the owner because a foreseeable event carries no information — 'you are guaranteed to have those logs generated. whats the point of recording a certain event at a known time?'. Deviation is the only thing worth an interrupt, and deviation is not currently computable.

The window-level version EXISTS and worked: logs/window_grand.log holds 'grand_recipe@ledger75 MISSING vs gate 0.9128' then 'gate not passed, card released'. Automatic, correct, unprompted. No per-arm equivalent.

Shape: machine-readable '# target: 0.NNNN' on the arm beside '# bead:' and '# reading:'; arm_check asserts it parses and agrees with the bead's band; _seat_value compares its ledger75 reading to it, appending the row to $LOGS/window.ledger either way and posting to inbox/main ONLY on a miss. Same shape as the window gate that already works.

PRICE: ~1.5 h CPU. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.00 — an INSTRUMENT, not a score. It earns nothing on the board; it buys spending an unattended window without reading twenty logs by hand. Justified as an instrument per the pricing rule.

Do not start during a card window.

title: roster_check's docstring claims it catches a cross-shelf duplicate; packaged() is a set, so it merges one silently
description:
ROSTERS is a pair (comp/members.roster, comp/members2.roster) and roster_check:55-62 states the rule out loud: 'A name on BOTH shelves is a duplicate the mount refuses, which is why packaged is a set and the duplicate is caught there rather than being silently merged.' The code does the opposite. packaged() (roster_check.py:163) is a set comprehension over self.patterns(), which concatenates BOTH rosters' lines; a name on both collapses to one element and the check reports it once, packaged, healthy. Nothing anywhere compares the two shelves' name sets.

WHAT IT COST, 2026-09-16. final_ws_df.pt, calib_span_df.pt and warm_calib_lowlr_drop40_long_s2026.pt were named on both rosters for as long as anyone can date, with roster_check green every run. It was harmless only because shelf 1 was STALE -- live it held 136 files and had none of the three, so the live mounts stayed disjoint by accident. The moment shelf 1 was re-pushed at its full 147 members (knee-aqppc) the duplicate went live, and MemberPackage.absorb (member_package.py:279) raises WeightsError on a name two mounts both hold. Not a dropped seat, which is the failure mode run_check exists for -- a kernel mounting both shelves DIES. mount_check is what caught it, one step before the board.

FIXED at the data level: the three are trimmed off members2.roster and shelf 2 was re-versioned, so live overlap is now empty (shelf1 148, shelf2 38, 0 .pt in common) and mount_check exits 0 across 141 kernels.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN is the guard. roster_check should name a pattern appearing on more than one shelf, in the words absorb will die in, because a roster is hand-edited and the next seat moved between shelves recreates this in one line. The fix is small -- collect patterns PER roster instead of flattening, and complain on any name in more than one -- and it belongs beside phantom(), which is the same shape of check (a roster line that cannot be served, named before the shipment tries).

PRICE: ~15 min. P(clears bar) n/a -- this is a shipping gate, not a score arm.
