title: backbone_lr: the control sits on the fast side of its own optimum -- test the slow side
description:
knee-rn9py's ctl_fastbb is the only fragment in the seven-arm leave-one-out that moves a CONTINUOUS knob instead of removing a piece, so it is the only one that carries a derivative sign. backbone_lr 4e-5 -> 1e-4 (2.5x) cost -0.0215 ledger75 (0.8699 vs control 0.8914, 909 rows). Six removals all read negative, which says every piece is load-bearing and offers nowhere to go; this one says the control is on the FAST side of its optimum, and the cheap test is the other direction.

ctl_slowbb: backbone_lr 2e-5 (0.5x), everything else the control, same cache, same 909-row ruler, 12 epochs, against probe224_control_s2026 0.8914.

PRE-REGISTERED BRANCHES:
 - >= 0.8964 (+0.0050): the knob is not at its optimum and this licenses ONE full-res 24-epoch arm on backbone_lr against labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026 (0.9048). This is the only path in the whole sweep that can RAISE the family.
 - 0.8864-0.8964: flat. 4e-5 is at or near the peak; the axis closes and the -0.0215 simply prices the cliff on the fast side.
 - < 0.8864: 4e-5 IS a peak, both sides fall away, axis closes harder.

HARNESS SUSPECT NAMED IN ADVANCE: every arm here is 12 epochs under one_cycle. A slower backbone needs more steps to travel the same distance, so a null at 2e-5 may be BUDGET-BOUND rather than a statement about the LR. ctl_fastbb and ctl_nowhole both already read UNDERTRAINED at e11 of 12. If slowbb reads flat AND undertrained, the branch above is not settled -- it is deferred to an epoch-budget arm, and must be written down as deferred, not as closed.

PRICE: ~0.2 h
P(clears +0.0050) ~ 0.30
notes: RESULT, 03:45-03:55Z, 909 rows. ledger75 0.8904 against control 0.8914 = -0.0010. convergence_check CONVERGED, peak e10 of 12 -- the SAME peak epoch as the control, so the harness suspect named in advance (a slower backbone being budget-bound under a 12-epoch one_cycle) is CLEARED. This is a real null, not a deferral, and the deferral clause in the description does not apply. SECOND BRANCH FIRES: 0.8864-0.8964, flat. backbone_lr 4e-5 is at or near its optimum and the axis CLOSES. The shape is asymmetric and that is the finding worth keeping: 0.5x costs 0.0010 and 2.5x costs 0.0215, so the optimum is a PLATEAU on the slow side and a CLIFF on the fast side. Consequence for anyone tuning this family: err slow. A backbone LR chosen too low loses a twentieth of what one chosen too high loses. No full-res arm is licensed; this closes the last open fragment of the control recipe.

title: Control-recipe leave-one-out at 224: does the CHAMPION family carry a negative fragment of its own?
description:
knee-feb62 closed on two findings: fragments compose additively, and a fragment's sign does not transfer between recipes. Both were measured by taking fragments OFF the grand recipe. The same harness pointed the other way asks the question that touches the pool: probe224_control (base+probe224, 0.8914@l75, 909 rows, epoch 10, converged) IS the champion family's recipe -- labelwise pooling, whole_stack, slot_dropout 0.40, calibrated_targets, backbone_lr 4e-5 -- at 224px/12sl/12ep. Nobody has ever removed one of ITS fragments. The paired board instruments of 2026-09-16 (noraptor_v1 0.945, nolabelwise_v1 0.943 against champion 0.946) showed the three labelwise_*_drop40_long seats carry this entry at about a board tick each, so a fragment costing that recipe is costing the champion three times over.
ARMS, one fragment each off the control, eight probes: slot_dropout 0.40->0, calibrated_targets->false, rank_weight 1.0->0, weight_floor->false, slice_pooling labelwise->max, whole_stack->false, backbone_lr 4e-5->1e-4, and band 0.2-0.8 -> 0.1-0.9 (the pool seats use the wide band; probe224 narrowed it, so that probe also prices the probe recipe's own departure from the pool). hold_annotations is deliberately NOT varied: it is a supervision_gap instrument, not a performance knob.
PRICE: ~0.15 h an arm measured (probe224_control_aug ran 01:59-02:07Z), eight arms ~1.15 h, ending ~03:45Z inside the 04:00Z window close. P(clears +0.0050 over probe224_control) ~ 0.4 for at least one fragment.
READING, pre-registered: this is an INSTRUMENT. The 12-epoch/909-row deltas are knob-sized, well under the 1.5% bar, so it RANKS fragments for a full-resolution test and proves nothing by itself. A probe at or above +0.0050 licenses ONE 24-epoch full-res arm on that fragment against labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026 (0.9048), which is the only thing here that could pay. All eight at or below +0.0050 is also a result: the champion recipe has no cheap fragment left in it, which closes fragment-level search on this family in favour of the data and labeler axes.
notes:
ARM 1/7 ctl_nodrop, 02:24-02:39Z, converged (1 runs, 1 converged), peak e10 of 12, 909 rows. ledger75 0.8909 against probe224_control_s2026 0.8914 = -0.0005. Does NOT clear the +0.0050 gate; it does not even clear zero. slot_dropout 0.40 -> 0.0 is the knob the whole drop40_long family is NAMED for, and at 12ep/224px it is worth nothing measurable either way -- the family name records a historical choice, not a live mechanism. Read as an upper bound on what removing it could buy at full resolution: a fragment that is flat on the probe has no headroom the 24-epoch arm could find.
ARM 2/7 ctl_maxpool, 02:39-02:48Z (9 min, not the 14 priced -- max pooling is cheaper than labelwise), converged, peak e10 of 12, 909 rows. ledger75 0.8851 against control 0.8914 = -0.0063. Does not clear the +0.0050 gate and cannot: it is NEGATIVE. Read as a confirmation rather than a candidate -- labelwise pooling is worth +0.0063 over max on the control recipe, which is the first fragment in this sweep that is measurably load-bearing (ctl_nodrop was -0.0005, flat). It also puts a number on a choice the pool has been carrying since the .903 reference used max: the switch to labelwise was not free momentum, it pays about a board tick and a half at 12ep/224px.
ARMS 3-4/7, both converged, 909 rows, ~10 min each. ctl_nocalib 02:48-02:58Z, ledger75 0.8814, peak e10 = -0.0100 against control 0.8914: calibrated_targets is the largest single payer in the sweep so far. ctl_norank 02:58-03:08Z, 0.8860, peak e11 = -0.0054: the pairwise ranking term pays about a board tick. Neither clears the +0.0050 gate and neither can -- both are NEGATIVE. Four of seven now priced and the sign is unanimous: nodrop -0.0005, maxpool -0.0063, nocalib -0.0100, norank -0.0054. NO CANDIDATE HAS APPEARED. Running total the other way is the finding that does survive: the four fragments measured so far are worth +0.0222 together over a control stripped of them, which is knob-sized one at a time and past the 1.5% bar composed -- and composition is what knee-3tk4b measured to be ADDITIVE on this family. That is the honest account of what separates this recipe from the .903 reference: not one lever, four small ones that add. Pace settled at 10 min an arm, so all seven fit before 04:00Z and the planned fastbb-for-nowhole swap is OFF -- both run.
ARM 5/7 ctl_nofloor, 03:08-03:18Z, converged, peak e10 of 12, 909 rows. ledger75 0.8883 = -0.0031 against control 0.8914. weight_floor -- the 0.25 pull an UNMENTIONED finding keeps exerting -- pays about half a board tick. Negative, so it cannot clear the gate either. Five of seven: nodrop -0.0005, maxpool -0.0063, nocalib -0.0100, norank -0.0054, nofloor -0.0031. Running total +0.0253 for the five together over a control stripped of them.
ARM 6/7 ctl_nowhole, 03:18-03:20Z, 909 rows. ledger75 0.8523 = -0.0391 against control 0.8914. THE ONE THAT CLEARS THE GATE, by 8x: every other fragment priced -0.0005..-0.0100, this is -0.0391, past the 1.5% bar ON ITS OWN. whole_stack is not a knob in this recipe, it is the spine. CAVEAT, stated before the number is used: convergence_check reads UNDERTRAINED (best e11 of 12 asked) and the arm ran at 13s/epoch against the control's ~60s -- without the whole stack the model is a fraction of the compute, so a recipe tuned for whole-stack is a live harness suspect (faulty TRAINING). 0.8523 is therefore a FLOOR for the no-whole-stack variant, not its ceiling. Even so the 0.0391 gap is 4x what one more epoch has ever moved on this family. READING: the gate fires, but it licenses NO new arm -- whole_stack is already ON in the champion, so this is confirmation of the load-bearing member, not a lever to pull. The fragment-level search on this family still closes.
ARM 7/7 ctl_fastbb, 03:21-03:31Z, 909 rows. ledger75 0.8699 = -0.0215 against control 0.8914. backbone_lr 4e-5 -> 1e-4. convergence_check UNDERTRAINED (best e11 of 12), same as nowhole. SWEEP CLOSED, all seven priced: nodrop -0.0005, maxpool -0.0063, nofloor -0.0031, norank -0.0054, nocalib -0.0100, fastbb -0.0215, nowhole -0.0391. SIGN UNANIMOUS across all seven -- not one fragment of this recipe is dead weight. Two clear the +0.0050 gate: nowhole and fastbb. PRE-REGISTERED READING, resolved: the sweep said all-at-or-below-+0.0050 would close fragment search on this family, and that is NOT what happened. But neither gate-clearer licenses the arm the pre-registration promised. nowhole is confirmation (whole_stack is already ON in the champion, so there is nothing to turn on). fastbb is the exception worth acting on: it is the only fragment that moves a CONTINUOUS knob rather than removing a piece, so it carries a derivative sign -- 2.5x the backbone LR costs 0.0215, which says the control is on the fast side of its own optimum and the cheap test is the OTHER direction. That is the one lever this sweep actually opened, and it is knee-mfg55.
CORRECTION to the line above: the backbone_lr follow-up is knee-lm2ol, not knee-mfg55 -- I quoted an ID before creating the bead. knee-mfg55 is not this work.

title: probe224_control_aug: the one grand fragment that helps, put on the recipe that wins
description: The knee-feb62.11 decomposition is closed. Against probe224_grand 0.8776 and probe224_control 0.8914 (deficit -0.0138), dropping each fragment group moves: mixup +0.0030, hard ramp +0.0013, ema +0.0032, the structural four +0.0049 (knee-dcl6e), aug block -0.0050. The positives sum to +0.0124 of 0.0138 and knee-3tk4b measured them composing about additively, so the deficit is explained: the grand recipe is a pile of small harms that add up, not one toxic fragment and not an interaction. That leaves exactly one fragment in the whole composition that PAYS: the augmentation block (ghosting 0.04, intensity_aug on, scale_jitter 0.25, and the aug ramp 0.25->1.0->0.5 with tail 0.2), worth +0.0050 inside grand. ARM: that block alone on top of probe224_control, every other grand fragment absent -- the only configuration in this family that can beat the control rather than chase it. PRICE: ~0.2 h. P(clears +0.0040 over probe224_control 0.8914) ~ 0.35. READING: a clear move licenses the same block on a 24-epoch champion-family seat inside this window (~0.8 h, and the window closes 04:00Z), which is the first thing knee-feb62 would have produced that is shippable rather than diagnostic. A null says the block only repairs damage the other grand fragments do and carries nothing on its own, which closes knee-feb62 outright.
notes:
RESULT 2026-09-16 02:10Z. probe224_control_aug 0.8876@l75 (909 rows, epoch 10, converged) against probe224_control 0.8914 = -0.0038, against the pre-registered P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.35. The NULL branch fired, and fired hard: the aug block does not merely fail to pay on the control, it COSTS about what it was worth inside grand (+0.0050 there, -0.0038 here).
READING, as pre-registered: 'a null says the block only repairs damage the other grand fragments do and carries nothing on its own, which closes knee-feb62 outright.' That is what happened. The augmentation block is a COMPENSATOR, not a contributor -- it buys back error that mixup, the hardness ramp, EMA and the four structural fragments create, and on a recipe with none of those damages to repair it is just extra noise on a 12-epoch budget. The sign of a fragment measured inside a composition therefore does not transfer out of it, which is the general lesson and the one worth keeping.
CONSEQUENCE: knee-feb62 has no surviving fragment. Every one of the six groups is either negative on the control or positive only against a recipe that loses by 0.0138. Closing the epic; nothing from it is shippable, and what it produced is evidence about composing recipes out of individually-plausible fragments.

title: probe224_grand_norest: the four grand fragments the leave-one-out never varied
description: knee-feb62.11 priced four fragment groups of probe224_grand (0.8776@l75) against probe224_control (0.8914), deficit -0.0138: mixup +0.0030, hard ramp +0.0013, ema +0.0032, aug block -0.0050. The positives sum to +0.0075 and knee-3tk4b's trim showed they compose about additively (mixup+hard predicted +0.0043, measured +0.0035), so roughly half the deficit is accounted for and -0.0063 is not. Diffing the two arms' own recipe stamps names exactly what the LOO never varied: stochastic_depth 0.0 -> 0.05, padding_mode border -> reflection, warmup 0.15 -> 0.25, patience_from_progress 0.0 -> 0.25. ARM: grand with those four returned to their control values, one group, same probe224 recipe as the other six runs. PRICE: ~0.2 h. P(clears +0.0050 over probe224_grand) ~ 0.45. READING: a recovery here closes the decomposition and names a structural toxin rather than an augmentation one -- stochastic_depth is the standing suspect, since it is the knob whose per-step ramp caused the dynamo recompile that cost this window its throughput, and it is set in recipes outside knee-feb62 too. A null here means the deficit is an INTERACTION among fragments that are each harmless alone, which is a finding about composing this recipe at all and closes knee-feb62 as a composition.
notes:
RESULT 2026-09-16 01:55Z. probe224_grand_norest 0.8825@l75 (909 rows, epoch 11, converged) vs probe224_grand 0.8776 = +0.0049, against the pre-registered P(clears +0.0050) ~ 0.45. A NEAR-HIT: the four structural fragments (stochastic_depth 0.05, padding reflection, warmup 0.25, patience_from_progress 0.25) carry +0.0049 of the deficit together without quite clearing their own band, which is enough to say the residual is STRUCTURAL rather than an interaction. The bead's null branch -- 'the deficit is an INTERACTION among fragments each harmless alone' -- did NOT fire.

title: probe224_control_noema: is EMA-off a lever on the base recipe, or only inside the grand composition
description: knee-feb62.11's noema probe returned probe224_grand_noema 0.8808@l75 against probe224_grand 0.8776 -- +0.0032, the largest of the four leave-one-out moves. That makes the +0.0032 a claim about EMA ON THIS PROBE SCALE generally, which is a different and larger question than the grand deficit, and it cannot be answered from inside grand because every other grand fragment is still present to interact with it. title: Target-specific pooling: focal findings and diffuse findings under one aggregation rule
description:
THE OBSERVATION. Every member this project owns aggregates slices with ONE rule for all twelve columns — `--slice-pooling labelwise` or `max` or `mean`, chosen per MEMBER and never per FINDING. But the twelve targets are not one kind of thing. ACL, meniscus and fracture are FOCAL: the evidence is a few slices and the rest of the stack is noise, which is what `max` is for. OA, effusion and synovitis are DIFFUSE: the evidence is spread over the stack and `max` throws most of it away, which is what `mean` is for. A single rule is necessarily wrong for one half.

WHAT THE BOARD SAYS THIS IS WORTH. `column_headroom` established the board is a plain unweighted mean of twelve per-column ROC AUCs, so a column gaining `d` moves the board by `d/12`. Six columns gaining 0.01 each is +0.005 on the board — above BOARD_RESOLVABLE and inside the range that has actually moved it.

WHAT MAKES IT TESTABLE CHEAPLY. `labelwise` pooling already learns a per-column weighting over slices, so the mechanism may ALREADY be in the pool — which would be the null and is worth knowing first. The cheap read is card-free: take two existing members fitted under different pooling rules, score them PER COLUMN on the same 909 holdout, and ask whether the focal/diffuse split predicts which member wins which column. If it does not, the axis is closed before a card is spent. If it does, the gain is the per-column argmax over the pool, and that is an upper bound a real head can be priced against.

Sean Lee's debate 5. CARD-FREE FIRST STEP. PRICE: ~0.5 h for the read. P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.25.
notes:
ANSWERED CARD-FREE, ~10 min, NULL. The focal/diffuse split does NOT predict which pooling rule wins which column.

THE INSTRUMENT. recipe_pairs --key slice_pooling returns 6 isolating pairs across 404 resolved recipes; four are max<->labelwise. Took the two cleanest and scored EACH MEMBER per column with column_headroom --only <member> (909 studies, our supervision at the midpoint, identical truth on both sides of each pair).

  Pair A  ctl_maxpool_s2026 (max) -> probe224_control_s2026 (labelwise)   macro +0.0053
  Pair B  dropstack_light_s2026 (max) -> labelwise_drop_s2026 (labelwise) macro -0.0005

FOCAL = ACL, Medial Meniscus, Lateral Meniscus, Fracture, MCL, Contusion (evidence in a few slices -- what max is for).
DIFFUSE = Medial OA, Lateral OA, PF OA, Effusion, Synovitis, Baker's (spread over the stack -- what a mean is for).

               focal mean d   diffuse mean d   diffuse-focal
  Pair A          +0.0056        +0.0051          -0.0005
  Pair B          -0.0034        +0.0024          +0.0058

The prediction was that labelwise (a learned per-column weighting over slices) rescues the half a single max rule serves badly, i.e. diffuse-focal clearly positive in BOTH pairs. It is zero in one and positive in the other, and Pair B's entire diffuse advantage is ONE column: Synovitis +0.0255 on pos=124. Drop that single column and Pair B reads +0.0011. Two pairs, no replication, and the one effect that exists is carried by the second-smallest positive count in the table.

WHY THE NULL IS MECHANICALLY UNSURPRISING, AND THIS WAS THE PRE-REGISTERED ALTERNATIVE: labelwise ALREADY learns a per-column weighting over slices. The mechanism this bead proposed was therefore probably already in the pool, and a null is what "already in the pool" looks like.

LIMITS, STATED. (1) Per-column noise is far wider than these deltas -- Fracture carries pos=68 and column_headroom's own header refuses to aim work with its ORDERING at all (knee-zsyp4: MCL is worst in this map and ~0.980 on the board). I use it only for a DELTA between two members on identical truth, which is the safer use, but the level is not board-comparable. (2) Two pairs, midpoint ruler, one holdout. (3) The focal/diffuse assignment is mine and unvalidated.

CONSEQUENCE. Do NOT spend a card on target-specific pooling. The cheap read was built to gate the card arm and it declined it. The axis is not refuted for all forms -- an explicitly per-column max/mean SPLIT has never been fitted -- but the evidence that would motivate one does not exist, and the mechanism's own proxy is flat.

WHAT SURVIVES UPSTREAM. knee-5dx47 pointed downstream of the encoder to "supervision quality, or the aggregation from slices to a study-level call". Supervision is closed twice (knee-rfxfu, knee-cmyzy). Shared study-level aggregation is excluded (knee-2co4r). Per-label aggregation is what this bead tested, and it is now flat. That exhausts the compass knee-5dx47 handed over. The next candidate is knee-5dx47 consequence 4 -- the 40 DEFAULTED leaves no corner arm ever names, of which --unfreeze-last and --slice-regions have ZERO isolating pairs anywhere.

title: queue_check should measure PROGRESS AGE, not alive-status
description:
THE HOLE IT CLOSES. `queue_check` answers 'is a watcher alive and does it owe an arm', and that question has now been green over an idle or stalled card more than once — a live process gating a marker it will never see reads OK forever, and so does an arm whose epochs have stopped advancing. Alive is not progress.

THE FIX, one number. Every running arm writes a `.metrics.jsonl` and a `.full.log` under the models root, and both grow once an epoch. Take the mtime of the newest such file for each live arm, compare against that arm's own median epoch seconds (already in the metrics rows as `seconds`), and report STALLED when the gap exceeds some multiple of it. That is a fact about the CARD rather than about the process table, and it is the one thing every existing idle-card failure would have tripped.

WHY NOW. Sean Lee's competition write-up makes the same point in his section 9 — track time-of-last-real-progress, not liveness — and it is the only content in either of his PDFs that this project did not already own. Cheap to agree with: the data is already on disk and no new writer is needed.

CARD-FREE. PRICE: ~0.5 h. P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.00 — this is an INSTRUMENT, not a score move: it buys back the card hours that the alive-status hole has already cost (about 50 minutes in one measured instance) rather than buying a gain.

title: missed_negation at FULL WEIGHT: one member on the negation-pulled table
description:
THE GATE IS PASSED, SMALL, AND THE GOLD SET CANNOT PRICE IT. `NegationPull` (a fourth Correction in `table_correction`, 0.15 residual, no hard flip) pulls a positive cell toward its column's floor when EVERY located mention of that finding in the report is denied by `NegationScope`. Measured 2026-09-13 on the full corpus:

  CORPUS REACH: 414 cells of 52,872 (0.78%) over 4,406 studies. Language coverage is 4,401 of 4,407 (99.9%) — en 1769, es 727, tr 546, hr 406, el 321, de 259, bg 220, nl 153 — so 414 is the real count, not a parsing fragment. By column: ACL 98, Medial Meniscus 78, Lateral Meniscus 68, PF OA 57, MCL 42, Medial OA 18, Contusion 14, Lateral OA 13, Fracture 10, Baker's 9, Effusion 7.

  GOLD GATE (`supervision_gap --labels`, 58 annotated studies, the identical path): labels aggregate 0.8658 -> 0.8675, +0.0017. Precision at cut 0.50 65.3% -> 65.9%, RECALL UNCHANGED at 84.6% — it removed only false positives and cost no positive. No column regressed; the movers are Lateral Meniscus +0.0112, PF OA +0.0071, ACL +0.0019.

  WHY THAT NUMBER IS NOT THE VERDICT: the rule fires exactly 3 times in the 696 gold cells, and the radiologist calls all 3 negative — 3/3 right, and +0.0017 is what 3 correct cells look like on this denominator. n=3 cannot separate a good rule from a lucky one. The gold set is the wrong instrument for a rule this sparse; only a trained member can price 414 cells.

  THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS. `relabel7_v1` (board 0.943, 7 members, cleanlab-corrected member at a seventh of the vote) states in its own board row that it 'refutes the strong form and leaves the weak form untested — a relabelled member at full weight, or a pool relabelled throughout, is a different question and this row cannot close it.' This is that question, and the signal is independent: negation is TEXT-derived and model-independent, cleanlab's is model-derived.

  THE ARM: clone `labelwise_depth24_drop40_long.sh` byte for byte and change ONE thing — `--labels` points at `report_labels_negpull.csv` instead of `report_labels_v2.csv`. `labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026` is 0.9053 ledger75, the strongest base in the pool, so the read is against a control already on disk. Pre-registration goes in the arm.

PRICE: ~1.5 h card. P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.20 — the mechanism is clean and verified where gold can see it, discounted hard for touching only 0.78% of cells.
close_reason: negpull 0.9044 ledger75 @e19 vs control labelwise_depth24_drop40_long 0.9053 @e18 (909 rows): -0.0009, null branch; do not seat

title: MIDPOINT_COLUMNS is a per-finding claim n=58 cannot support — test it against gold
description:
label_ceiling (scratchpad, fixed and self-checking: binarised truth reproduces the AUC 0.9097 vs 0.9097) finds the pool/label disagreement CONCENTRATED: 116 cells over 0.9 opposite, and 60 of them sit in Medial Meniscus (49) + Baker's (11) — EXACTLY ledger75's MIDPOINT_COLUMNS, the two columns exempted from the 0.75 recut. The tail shows those cells are overwhelmingly grade 0.68 read at cut 0.50, the very rung level_calibration measures as 62% NEGATIVE on gold (five levels: 0.041/0.136/0.378/0.688/0.958).

MIDPOINT_COLUMNS' docstring claims 'The two findings whose 0.68 rung carries real positives, so the recut costs them their ruler'. That is a PER-FINDING claim. level_calibration's own reasoning says 58 studies fit noise per-finding and must be read pooled. So the exemption may be fitted to noise.

TEST: on the 58 annotated studies, what is the gold-positive rate of the 0.68 rung WITHIN Medial Meniscus and Baker's, with an interval? If it does not separate from the pooled 0.688, the exemption has no support and ledger75 should recut all twelve.

CAVEAT that must be said out loud in the finding: the label_ceiling number is an UPPER BOUND and circular by construction (models scored against labels the models chose). Only the SHAPE is readable.

THIS MOVES SELECTION, NOT THE BOARD — ledger75 is our ruler, not Kaggle's. But every seat number this project holds is measured through it.
PRICE: ~0.3 h CPU, no card, no slot. P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.00 — INSTRUMENT, it retires a suspicion about the ruler.

title: warm_calib_lowlr + operator pair: the pair onto the EARLIEST-peaking seat in the pool
description:
warm_calib_lowlr_s2026 reads 0.8910 ledger75 PEAKING AT EPOCH 4 OF 12 and declining for seven. That is the earliest peak in the entire pool -- earlier than grade_ladder (@e6), through_dense (@e8), stack_increments (@e9). A budget wall peaks on the LAST epoch; peaking at 4 of 12 and declining for seven is a missing regulariser, and it is the same diagnosis that sent the operator pair (--slot-dropout 0.40 + --epochs 12 -> 24) onto eight bases across four recipe families, where it cleared +0.0040 on eight of nine.

WHY THIS BASE AND NOT ANOTHER. It is a SEAT, not a spare. warm_calib_lowlr_s2026 sits in the best n=7 seating this project has measured (0.9093, and 0.9103 after the labelwise_drop_up swap), and knee-fix1t says the 0.944 ceiling is the POOL and not the seating. Upgrading a member that is actually seated attacks the pool directly; upgrading a spare does not. It is also the last seated member with no drop40_long twin once clean_calib_drop40_long lands.

THE ONE HONEST DOUBT. This is a WARM-STARTED run from calib_dense_hold.enc.pt, so the trunk arrives already annealed. The early peak could be the warm start exhausting its usable capacity by epoch 4 rather than a missing regulariser -- knee-wbwq's own 'THE RAMP WAS NOT THE CAUSE' branch says exactly that about a fully annealed trunk having nothing left for a second cycle. If so, doubling the budget does nothing and the dropout half fights a trunk that cannot move. That is what makes this a real question rather than a ninth repetition.

PRE-REGISTERED, against warm_calib_lowlr_s2026 = 0.8910 ledger75 @e4:
  >= +0.0040   the pair transfers to warm-started recipes. Roster it, price it as a SWAP for its own
               base in the n=7 seating, and widen the pair onto the remaining warm-start family.
  +0.0015..+0.0039  partial. Keep only if it prices positive as a marginal over the seating; a solo
               gain that does not seat is what stack_increments taught (+0.0020 solo, -0.0001 seated).
  <= +0.0014   the pair does not reach warm starts, and knee-wbwq's annealed-trunk reading gains its
               first independent support. That closes the warm-start family to this operator.
  solo floor   >= 0.8910, or the transfer failed here and no branch above may be read.

PRICE: ~1.3 h (the 12-epoch base cost ~40 min). P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.70 -- eight of nine bases have cleared it and this one carries the strongest diagnosis in the pool, discounted for the warm-start doubt above.
notes:
2026-09-14 read: warm_calib_lowlr_drop40_long_s2026 ledger75 0.9000 @e8 vs control warm_calib_lowlr_s2026 0.8910 = +0.0090; midpoint 0.8632 vs 0.8577. convergence_check: TRUNCATED (PC shutdown) -> score is a FLOOR. Floor clears >=+0.0040 branch: roster, price swap, re-run to completion.
CORRECTION 2026-09-16 20:21Z -- THE RUN WAS NOT TRUNCATED, AND THE NOTE ABOVE IS WRONG ABOUT IT.
Evidence on disk: $MODELS/warm_calib_lowlr_drop40_long_s2026.pt exists, 89205613 bytes, written 2026-09-14 17:30; its full log holds 24 recorded epochs (last 'epoch 23') against the arm's own --epochs 24; and the log ends with 'ARM DONE warm_calib_lowlr_drop40_long'. A PC shutdown writes none of those three. Whatever 'TRUNCATED (PC shutdown)' was read off, it was not this run.

THE NUMBER, re-priced with the two-ruler tool (ledger75 --holdouts $MODELS --only ..., 909 rows both):
  warm_calib_lowlr_drop40_long_s2026   ledger 0.8641  ledger75 0.8994  @e8
  warm_calib_lowlr_s2026  (control)    ledger 0.8577  ledger75 0.8910  @e4
  delta +0.0084 at ledger75, +0.0064 at midpoint. (The earlier note said 0.9000; the tool says 0.8994.)

This is a CEILING-free reading, not a floor. It clears the pre-registered >= +0.0040 branch on its own terms, so that branch fires: roster it, price it as a SWAP for its own base in the n=7 seating, widen the pair onto the remaining warm-start family.

AND THE ONE HONEST DOUBT IS ANSWERED, against the bead's own warm-start worry. The peak moved e4 -> e8 and the run then DECLINED for sixteen more epochs with the checkpoint still improving nowhere. So the budget was never the binding constraint and the extra epochs bought nothing -- the +0.0084 is the SLOT-DROPOUT half of the operator pair, not the length half. knee-wbwq's annealed-trunk reading is supported for the BUDGET and refuted for the REGULARISER: a fully annealed warm-started trunk still has room for a missing regulariser, it just has none for a second cycle.
Consequence for the family: widen with --slot-dropout 0.40 ALONE and do not pay for --epochs 24 on warm starts. That is a ~40 min arm instead of a ~1.3 h one, at the same expected gain.
CLOSING. The seat price was already on the roster (comp/members.roster:536-538) and it is the verdict: vs cleanseat_v1 @ledger75 the member adds +0.0018 [+0.0011, +0.0026], +0.0022 for blendhold -- inside the +0.0040 the ruler can resolve and inside the 0.0020 board blur (knee-cyi5v). So the +0.0084 SOLO does not transfer to a SEAT, which is exactly what stack_increments taught (+0.0020 solo, -0.0001 seated).
knee-rkegi therefore produces NO shippable candidate and no slot. What it produces is the family rule in the note above: on warm starts buy --slot-dropout 0.40 and not --epochs 24. Closed on its own pre-registration, not abandoned.

title: SEAT COUNT IS SATURATED AT SEVEN: all four newly-priced upgrades DILUTE the best seating
description:
Measured 2026-09-13, full 909 rows, LogitAverage, no selection, ledger75 cuts (scratchpad/seat_newfour.py). Against the four-swap core + depth_up at 0.9093 -- the best seating this project has measured -- every one of the four newly-rostered drop40_long members is NEGATIVE as an added eighth seat:

  band_dense_drop40_long  solo 0.8918   +1 0.9089  -0.0004
  base224_drop40_long     solo 0.8865   +1 0.9086  -0.0007
  severity_drop40_long    solo 0.8899   +1 0.9085  -0.0008
  mergedk_drop40_long     solo 0.8853   +1 0.9083  -0.0010

And every subset of them is monotonically worse than every smaller subset: n=9 spans 0.9076..0.9082, all below the n=7 base. There is no pair, triple or quadruple that recovers.

WHAT THIS CLOSES. The 'add more upgraded members' branch. The pair now has seven bases on disk and the four whose bases sit outside the honest core six pay NOTHING when seated on top of it. Seat count is saturated at seven; the remaining axis is member QUALITY AT FIXED COUNT, which is exactly what knee-0v8yz already says about the board (only member quality at count 1 has moved it 0.005+).

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE. The SWAP axis, and the distinction matters: these four have NO BASE in the honest core six, so they could only ever be ADDs to that pool. A member with nothing to displace is the weakest case the pair has, and it read negative in all four instances. That is consistent with the ADD/SWAP finding (chainfour_up +0.0007 add / +0.0012 swap), not a refutation of it. knee-p29bb and knee-rpugl both ask SWAP questions and are untouched by this.

ORDERING NOTE: the dilution ranks by solo -- 0.8918 -> -0.0004, 0.8853 -> -0.0010, monotone across all four. A seat below the pool's quality floor costs the pool in proportion to how far below it sits. That is a usable rule for future seating and it has now been measured four times in one read.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-09-13 by its own eleventh point. The ADD saturation finding STANDS as measured and is MISNAMED as a conclusion about the pool.

THE ELEVENTH MEMBER. labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026, solo 0.9051 ledger75 @e18 -- the pool's joint top with depth24_up at 0.9053 -- adds +0.0004 to the n=7 seating at 0.9093. First non-negative of eleven. Eleven adds now read: labelwise_drop +0.0004, calib_span +0.0001, stack_increments_base -0.0003, stack_increments -0.0003, through_dense -0.0003, band_dense -0.0004, grade_ladder -0.0006, base224 -0.0007, lr4e-5_ws -0.0007, severity -0.0008, mergedk -0.0010. The SIGN still tracks nothing below the top; the one member at the top is the one that does not cost.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH THE HEADLINE. 'The pool is saturated against everything below its top' was written off ADD readings alone. Priced as a SWAP, the same member is worth +0.0011 (out clean_calib_s2026, n held at 7, 0.9093 -> 0.9103) -- the best seating this project has measured. ADD asks 'does this carry signal the pool lacks'; SWAP asks 'is this better than the seat it takes'. Those are different questions and this pool answers them differently. An eleven-deep ADD null licenses NO claim about swaps. Same shape as the already-measured chainfour_up (+0.0007 add, +0.0012 swap) and blendhold_up (+0.0000 add, +0.0008 swap) -- now three independent members where SWAP > ADD, which makes it a pattern rather than a pair.

AND THE SWAP AXIS IS ALSO NEAR ITS END. A beam search over all 28 priced members (swap/drop/add, beam 6, 6 steps, seeded from the n=7 at 0.9093) tops out at 0.9113, +0.0020, n=8. FIVE distinct seatings tie at 0.9113 to four decimals -- that tie IS the tell: it is holdout selection, the exact defect that made cleanseat_v1 'offline: None, scope: excluded' and unusable for board_transfer. +0.0020 offline is ~+0.0023 on the board, one notch over the 0.001 the board reports at. NOT A SHIPMENT. Recorded as an instrument.

THE ONE MECHANISM CLAIM THE BEAM EARNS. Six of its best eight seats are labelwise-family (dense+, depth24+, depth24, drop+, ext+, extended); it evicts chainfour+, blendhold+ and clean_calib. The family the operator pair was developed on is the family that seats. That is not a selection artefact -- it holds across all five tied optima.
2026-09-16 18:20Z — CORROBORATED FROM THE BOARD SIDE, on a ruler that is not the seat ruler. This bead's claim was made on the offline seat pricer; submit_check --kernel kneemri-slotseat prints the same conclusion out of comp/board.jsonl, which is the hidden test set rather than our 909 studies.

Six recorded entries overlapping one candidate set by 50-62%: fullseat_v1 0.946 (8 members), fullseat2_v1 0.946 (8), tripleseatclean_v1 0.946 (8), doseseat_v1 0.946 (8), noraptor_v1 0.945 (7), warmseat_v1 0.945 (9). Seven, eight and nine members; four distinct seatings; total spread ONE tick at the board's own 0.001 resolution.

Read it with the resolution caveat that applies to every board tie: a 0.945/0.946 split BOUNDS the true spread of these seatings below 0.001, it does not measure it. So the honest statement is not 'reseating gains nothing' but 'reseating in this neighbourhood gains less than the board can resolve' — which is the same practical verdict for slot-spending and a weaker one for mechanism.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is a spending rule rather than a finding: an entry whose only difference from a recorded 0.946 is which seats are in it may not be shipped as a PREDICTED GAIN. It ships as an instrument or not at all. Applied today to knee-fsurq.

title: clean_calib + operator pair: the fifth SWAP, not a sixth seat
description: The operator pair (--slot-dropout 0.40 + --epochs 12->24) is a SEAT-REPLACEMENT operator, not a seat-addition one. Measured 2026-09-13 on the full 909, LogitAverage, ledger75 cuts, against the honest core six at 0.9050: chainfour_drop40_long ADDS +0.0007 as a seventh seat and blendhold_drop40_long adds +0.0000 -- both despite clearing the operator band solo (+0.0070, +0.0050 over their bases). But SWAPPED for the base each upgrades, every one of the four available upgrades is positive ALONE and they compose near-additively: chainfour +0.0012, labelwise_dense +0.0014, blendhold +0.0008, labelwise_extended +0.0008, all four together +0.0032, and all four plus depth_up as a free seventh 0.9093 = +0.0043 at n=7 -- which BEATS the nine that tripleseat ships (0.9090) with two fewer seats. Non-labelwise carries as much as labelwise on the swap axis; chainfour is the single best swap. clean_calib_s2026 (0.8940) and warm_calib_lowlr_s2026 (0.8910) are the only two core seats with no upgraded twin on disk. This arm builds clean_calib's. NO SINGLE SWAP CLEARS THE BOARD RESOLUTION AND THAT IS NOT THE CLAIM -- the composite is: six swaps plus depth_up projects to ~+0.0058 against a +0.0040 seat floor, and the owner's standing rule is that increments below the bar still compose. PRE-REGISTERED, swap value over the four-swap core at 0.9082: >= +0.0008 seats the swap and warm_calib takes the next card; +0.0001..+0.0007 directional, keep it, no further arm on this axis; <= 0.0000 the operator does not reach the distillation corner and the six-swap projection is void. Solo floor >= 0.8940 (its own base) or the transfer failed here and the swap read is void. PRICE: ~2.4 h (24 epochs at the parent's measured 363 s/epoch). P(clears +0.0008) ~ 0.55.
notes:
CLEARS ITS BAND, AND THE GAIN IS ENTIRELY AT THE 0.75 CUT. Landed 2026-09-13T15:22Z, converged (convergence_check: 1 converged, argmax e22/e23 of 24).

  clean_calib_drop40_long_s2026   LEDGER 0.8647   LEDGER75 0.8978   e23
  clean_calib_s2026 (control)     LEDGER 0.8649   LEDGER75 0.8940   e9
                                        -0.0002            +0.0038

Pre-registration was >= +0.0008 seats the swap. It clears by 4.75x on ledger75 — AND THE MIDPOINT IS FLAT TO NEGATIVE. Those are the same predictions under two binarisations of the same graded truth, so a gain that appears only at 0.75 is a gain in how the member ranks the CONFIDENT positives (truth >= 0.75) against everything else, with no improvement in the ranking that the 0.5 cut sees. The operator pair (slot dropout 0.40 plus a doubled budget) does not make the member better in general; it makes it better where the reader was sure. That is the half of the truth the board's graded arrays are mostly made of, which is why ledger75 is the ruler this project prices seats on — but it is also the reason this must be priced as a SEAT before it is sold as a member: a solo is not a seat (stack_increments read +0.0020 solo and -0.0001 seated).

NEXT: roster it, then price it as a SWAP for clean_calib_s2026 in the champion six. Do NOT quote the +0.0038 as a board number — board_transfer is +1.135 and the board reports at 0.001, so a seated version of this is worth about 0.004 IF it seats at all.

title: labelwise_drop + the established operator pair: the fourth base, argued on seat ADDITIVITY not on the operator
description:
PARENT FAMILY: knee-9bnkc, knee-cgt9m, knee-vs06j.

WHAT THIS ARM IS. `labelwise_drop`'s byte-identical line (labelwise pooling, slices 20, stochastic-depth
0.05, 12 epochs, 0.8984 ledger75 @e10) with --slot-dropout 0.40 and --epochs 24 added. Nothing else moves.

THE ARGUMENT IS ADDITIVITY, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE OPERATOR. By the time this arm runs the
operator question is answered on three bases and a fourth would be a repeat if that were the question.
It is not. Measured 2026-09-13, full 909, LogitAverage, no selection:

  core six                                        0.9050
  + labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026           0.9070  (+0.0020)
  + labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026               0.9067  (+0.0017)
  + BOTH                                          0.9081  (+0.0031)

+0.0031 against +0.0020 and +0.0017 separately is NEAR-ADDITIVE: the two upgraded members are not
redundant with each other, so each further upgraded base is a fresh seat rather than a copy of one
already held. That is the quantity this arm buys, and it is the only quantity knee-0v8yz says has ever
moved this board -- member quality at count 1. Four upgraded bases project to roughly +0.006 offline,
which at board_transfer +1.135 is the size that clears the 0.944 tie.

WHY THIS BASE. `labelwise_drop` is the fourth and last twelve-epoch labelwise member in the family
(0.8984 @e10) and carries a regulariser none of the other three has, --stochastic-depth 0.05. That makes
it the base whose upgraded member is least likely to correlate with the other three, which is exactly
what the additivity argument needs.

PRE-REGISTRATION. Read on the ENSEMBLE, not on the solo, because the solo is not the claim:
  >= +0.0015 marginal over the seven that precede it  seats it; ship the eight or nine.
  +0.000..+0.0014                                     directional, no slot.
  <= 0.0000                                           additivity is exhausted at three upgraded bases
                                                      and the family closes. A real closure.
  solo floor >= 0.8984 (its own base) or the transfer failed here and the ensemble read is void.

PRICE: ~0.8 h (24 epochs x ~110 s at 336/slices 20).
P(clears +0.0015 marginal) ~ 0.45.
LICENCE: competition data only.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-09-13 on the DIRECTIONAL branch, and the close found something the pre-registration could not have asked for.

THE NUMBER. ledger75, 909 rows, --holdouts D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality:
  labelwise_drop_drop40_long_s2026   LEDGER 0.8703  LEDGER75 0.9051  move +0.0348  @e18 of 0..23
  labelwise_drop_s2026               LEDGER 0.8649  LEDGER75 0.8984  move +0.0335  @e10 of 0..11
+0.0067 over its base. convergence_check --run <metrics> -> '1 runs: 1 converged'. Solo floor 0.8984 CLEARED at 0.9051.
That is the EIGHTH of eight bases to clear the operator pair's +0.0040 floor: dense +0.0084, chainfour +0.0070, base224 +0.0070 (and a 2nd seed +0.0060), drop +0.0067, ext +0.0059, depth24 +0.0055, blendhold +0.0050, band_dense +0.0041. Four unrelated recipe families.

THE PRE-REGISTERED BRANCH. Marginal as an added eighth seat on the n=7 four-swap core + depth_up (0.9093): +0.0004. That is the '+0.000..+0.0014 directional, no slot' band. NO SLOT SPENT. The '>= +0.0015 seats it, ship the eight or nine' branch did NOT fire and must not be read as if it had.

WHAT THE ADD NUMBER DOES NOT SAY, measured after the close. +0.0004 is the ONLY non-negative of ELEVEN members priced as adds on that pool (knee-tuzzp), and it is the only one tested that sits at the pool's TOP. So it was priced as a SWAP instead, n held at 7:
  out clean_calib_s2026                (solo 0.8940)  0.9103  +0.0011   <- best seating this project has measured
  out blendhold_drop40_long_s2026      (solo 0.8879)  0.9099  +0.0006
  out chainfour_drop40_long_s2026      (solo 0.8982)  0.9097  +0.0004
  out warm_calib_lowlr_s2026           (solo 0.8910)  0.9093  -0.0000
  out labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026  (solo 0.9045)  0.9091  -0.0001
  out labelwise_depth24_drop40_long    (solo 0.9053)  0.9089  -0.0003
  out labelwise_dense_drop40_long      (solo 0.9048)  0.9089  -0.0004
THE CORRECTION THIS FORCES ON knee-tuzzp: the ADD null was never a statement about the POOL, it was a statement about ADDS. A member that is merely non-additive can still be strictly better than the seat it would take. Eleven negative adds and a +0.0011 swap are the same member.

STILL NOT A SHIPMENT, and the reason is the one that voided cleanseat_v1. +0.0011 is the argmax of seven swaps chosen ON THE HOLDOUT. board_transfer +1.135 puts it at ~+0.0012 on the board against BOARD_RESOLVABLE 0.0015 and a board that reports at 0.001. It is a directional reading and it is recorded as one.

title: labelwise_dense + the established operator pair: the third base, and it is already a core seat
description:
PARENT FAMILY: knee-9bnkc (depth24 base) and knee-cgt9m (extended base).

WHAT THIS ARM IS. `labelwise_dense`'s byte-identical line with the two operators the project has now
measured to transfer: --slot-dropout 0.40 and --epochs 12 -> 24. Nothing else moves.

labelwise bases and on neither by accident:
  labelwise_depth24   0.8998 -> labelwise_depth24_drop40_long   0.9053  (+0.0055, converged, peak e18/24)
  labelwise_extended  0.8986 -> labelwise_ext_drop40_long       0.9045  (+0.0059, converged)

and in scheme. Board grep: 0 rows on comp/board.jsonl carry either transferred member, so nothing here
has been shipped either.

WHY THIS BASE AND NOT ANOTHER. labelwise_dense_s2026 is ALREADY A SEAT in the honest core six. Measured
2026-09-13 on the full 909 with LogitAverage and no selection, the core six read 0.9050 and the two
transferred members seat at +0.0020 and +0.0017, +0.0031 together -- near-additive, so the pair is not
redundant. Upgrading a seat that is already carrying weight is the one move that lifts the ensemble
without widening it, and knee-0v8yz says only MEMBER QUALITY at count 1 has ever moved this board 0.005+.

PRE-REGISTRATION (delta = this arm minus labelwise_dense_s2026 0.8964, ledger75)
  >= +0.0040   the operator pair is established on three of three bases and stops being a transfer
               question. Seat it in place of its own base and spend a slot on the eight.
  +0.000..+0.0039  directional. Keep for the pool, spend no slot.
  <= 0.0000    the pair is a fact about deep-slice bases (24) and not about labelwise pooling. That is

title: The host ruled on external data and the axis is the DATA AGREEMENT, not NC/ND
description:
Source: kaggle.com/competitions/rsna-knee-abnormality-detection/discussion/734109, surfaced by the owner 2026-09-13.

Mazzutti (2nd place on the board) asked whether the KneeCoT dataset (Hugging Face, CC BY-NC 4.0, gated behind a formal ethical-use agreement with an affiliated hospital, redistribution prohibited) could be used. Four questions, including whether its use in a prize-bearing competition is permitted and whether shipping trained weights without images suffices.

Kaggle staff (javaduke95), 19 days later, VERBATIM: 'we decided to not allow the use of KneeCoT dataset due to the required data agreement'. The stated reasoning was fairness -- a formal agreement creates an uneven playing field between participants who can and cannot complete an institutional approval process. They would reconsider if the data policy changes.

WHAT THIS SETTLES. The dataset was CC BY-NC and the NC clause was NOT the stated reason. The refusal was on GATING. That is rule 2.6a's 'equally accessible to use by all Participants ... at no cost' read literally, exactly as this repo's own 2026-09-07 retraction argued (:77, :216 of the external_knee_mri_data_access_audit -- '2.6a contains neither non-commercial nor derivative').

WHAT IT REORDERS. The live axis for every foreign corpus is now: does obtaining it require signing an agreement or passing an approval?
  KMAR-50K  CC BY 4.0, Mendeley, open download, no agreement  -> clean, and it is already the only merge shippable through 2.5.
  Rijeka    CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, public Zenodo record + public Kaggle mirror, no agreement, no cost -> passes the test the host ACTUALLY applied. NC alone did not sink KneeCoT. The open question stays 2.5 (ND on distributed weights), never 2.6a.
  MRNet     Stanford RUA, a registration form that must be accepted -> this is the KneeCoT shape. The precedent points AGAINST it, and it is the first evidence that bears on the repo's self-contradiction (knee-wipvc).
  fastMRI   signed DUA + issued credentials -> same shape, same direction.
  SKM-TEA   AIMI login + agreement -> same shape, same direction.

This is the first HOST statement the project has on the question; every prior verdict in slots.py and the audits is our own reading of licence text. It should be quoted in the one-place verdict table knee-wipvc owes, and slots.py should cite that table rather than restate it.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH A SLOT OF NOBODY'S TIME BUT MINE: the same discussion thread is where a host answer about our own corpora would be obtained. Asking costs no submission slot.

title: mergedk at 336px: the shippable merge at the resolution our champion actually trains on
description:
The mergedk 2x2 that measured +0.0099 was run entirely at 224px, because images_224px_12sl_mergedk.npy was the only merged array on disk. Every member in the champion's six is 336px. So the one merge that is licence-clean through rule 2.5 (KMAR-50K is CC BY 4.0, attribution only) has never been tested at the resolution the entry serves at.

images_336px_12sl_mergedk.npy is being built 2026-09-13 08:08Z by core.data.corpus.build_merged (--slices 12 --image-size 336 --extra-scheme kmar --merged-scheme mergedk --extra-labels labels/kmar_pseudo.csv). Disk/CPU only, ~40.3 GB, sources images_336px_12sl.npy (33.4 GB) + images_336px_12sl_kmar.npy (6.9 GB), both already decoded. Leaves /d at ~33 GB free.

ARM: copy mergedk_drop40_long.sh, change --image-size 224 -> 336 and drop nothing else.
PRICE: ~3.5 h
P(clears +0.005 over the 224 mergedk cell) ~ 0.45 -- the 224->336 lift is measured across our own members at roughly +0.01, and the corpus effect is orthogonal to resolution, so the mechanism is additive rather than a re-run.
EINSTEIN GATE: comp/board.jsonl has never held a mergedk member at any resolution; the axis is unshipped, not repeated.
notes:
2026-09-16 22:05Z — REFUSED BEFORE THE CARD, ON TWO NUMBERS THIS REPO ALREADY OWNS. Both halves of this bead's premise are wrong.

THE 336 CELL IS NOT UNTESTED — it ran, and it is clean. mergedk_labelwise_drop40_long_336_s2026 priced by ledger75 --holdouts $MODELS (909 rows both): 0.8621 ledger / 0.8901 ledger75 @e12, against labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026 0.8672 / 0.9048 @e23 = -0.0147 ledger75, -0.0051 midpoint. convergence_check does not flag it: 24 asked, peaked e12, declined for twelve. A complete reading, not a floor.

THE +0.01 RESOLUTION LIFT IS NOT +0.01. The matched pair is experiments/README.md:8318-8330, band_dense (336) vs band224 (224), same recipe, same card, same day: 0.8578 vs 0.8529 = +0.0049 solo, and that section's own words are 'under the 0.0062 holdout noise floor, so as a MEMBER the two recipes are not separable'. At the SEAT it is smaller still — README:16433, chainfour 0.8912 -> 0.8917 = +0.0005 at ledger75, a quarter of the 0.0020 board blur (knee-cyi5v). 336 costs 450 s/epoch against 224's 142, so the champion recipe at 24 epochs is ~3 h for a seat gain of +0.0005.

AND THE CORPUS HALF IS CLOSED ON DOSE, NOT ONLY ON FLATNESS. KMAR is 1,088 rows on 4,407 = 1.247x; beta=0.22 prices +0.0068 at PERFECT labels. The labels are not perfect and are not human: slots.py:KMAR_MERGED_SCHEME states they are kneemri.inference.pseudo_labels, our own champions' pooled belief. Read off that table (D:/data/.../labels/kmar_pseudo.csv, 1088 rows) the per-column confidence is Effusion mean 0.5560 / p50 0.538 — near chance — Baker's 0.6247, Synovitis 0.6547, Contusion 0.6958, Fracture 0.7047. A row-level filter keeping all twelve columns confident retains almost nothing (>=0.80 is 12-37% per column INDEPENDENTLY), so realistic usable dose is ~20% of 1,088, pricing ~+0.0016 — inside the board blur before any noise penalty.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It is not a verdict on resolution as an axis: +0.0049 solo is a real positive sign and 336 members ship today. It is a verdict on SPENDING ~3 h of card to add one, at a seat delta the board cannot certify. And it is not a verdict on external corpora — it is a verdict on THIS corpus at THIS dose under THESE pseudo-labels. A licensed corpus of ~4,400 new studies would price +0.0201 offline on the same beta and is still the axis worth wanting.

Closing. No card spent.

title: slots.py and research/ give OPPOSITE licence verdicts on MRNet, and three of four claims were never read against primary text
description:
TWO PLACES IN THIS REPO CONTRADICT EACH OTHER.

core/data/corpus/slots.py:243,329-330,366 states: 'Rijeka is CC BY-NC-ND, MRNet's Stanford agreement bars adaptations' and concludes NO merged member of any name can be shipped.

research/2026-09-02_external_data_and_foundation_model_status_quo.md:44 states: 'Licence: Stanford Research Use Agreement, non-commercial, no redistribution; project has re-read Kaggle rule 2.6(a) as a disjunction and concluded MRNet IS PERMITTED FOR COMPETITION USE.'
research/2026-09-02_external_data_format_mismatch_models_training.md:197 lists MRNet as 'permitted (RUA, non-redistributable)'; :282 'MRNet is already permitted and on disk'.

Both cannot be true and a slot decision rests on it.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY VERIFIED. Exactly ONE source has a primary-text read: fastMRI, read 2026-09-10, an hour before a slot would have been spent on an entry the WRONG prose licensed (slots.py:317-327). That verification REVERSED the docstring. The other three were never read:
  - Rijeka: research/2026-09-02_external_data_format_mismatch_models_training.md:203 says 'mirror licence unverified'. slots.py asserts CC BY-NC-ND as settled fact.
  - SKM-TEA: research/2026-09-01_knee-mri-corpora-survey.md:48 says the redistribution/derivative clause 'is gated behind the AIMI login -- someone must register and read it before it is usable'. Never read.
  - MRNet: the RUA text is not in this repo; both verdicts are summaries.

THE CONFLATION. Every verified restriction is about DISTRIBUTING DATA, not about TRAINING. fastMRI's verified text bars distributing 'variables or data files derived from the fastMRI Dataset'; slots.py:325 itself concludes 'Fitting a member here is internal research and stays legal.' The survey says of fastMRI 'no NC clause ... data can never ride in a kernel' -- the DATA, not a model. A licence table that prints one verdict per corpus hides the axis that matters: use / redistribute-data / ship-a-model are three different permissions and only the third is ever at issue for us.

THE OPEN LEGAL QUESTION, NOT MINE TO SETTLE. Are trained weights a derivative work of the training data? Unsettled. For Rijeka the harder bar is NC against a prize competition, not ND.

WHAT TO DO. Read the primary text for MRNet's RUA, Rijeka's source (not the mirror) and Kaggle rule 2.6(a); record each as a three-column verdict (train / redistribute data / ship model) in ONE place, and make slots.py cite it instead of restating it. This is the knee-a21h9 failure mode on a different axis: a hand-written restatement forking a legislated rule.

title: Corpus diversity measured: 17.5 effective dims, NN-cosine median 0.778 -- more of OUR studies buys density, not axes
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-13 on features_large_336px_12sl_r252_cls_mean_focal_attend (verified fully written; its _focal_max sibling holds 504 of 4407 and was discarded -- embedding_cache.py:170). Studies pooled over present slots (mask mean 4.57 of 6), mean-centred, L2-normed. DENOMINATOR n=4407, the whole corpus.

PAIRWISE cosine over 9.7M pairs: mean +0.0006, std 0.2389, p50 -0.0146.
NEAREST-NEIGHBOUR: p50 +0.7777, p90 +0.8659, p100 +1.0000. Above 0.95: 4 of 4407 (0.09%). Above 0.90: 135 (3.06%).
GREEDY DE-DUP: cos>0.90 keeps 4337 (98.4%), cos>0.80 keeps 3403 (77.2%), cos>0.70 keeps 1860 (42.2%).
SPECTRUM: PC1 0.1425, PC1-10 0.6167, PC1-100 0.9122, participation ratio 17.5 effective dims of 3072.

READING. The corpus is NOT near-duplicate at the study level -- only 0.09% of studies have a neighbour above 0.95, so there is no redundant block to throw away and nothing here licenses training on a subset. But it is LOW-DIMENSIONAL: ten directions carry 62% of the between-study variance and the effective dimensionality is 17.5. Fixed protocol, one acquisition pipeline, one population.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DATA LEVER. Adding studies from the SAME source lands them inside the same 17.5-dim shell: it buys sample density along axes we already cover, which is worth something at 4407 but is not a new axis. Adding a SECOND SITE moves the shell. That is the mechanism behind mergedk at +0.0099 (knee-dl65h header), and it is the argument for ranking a second corpus above more of our own.

NEXT. Re-run this on mergedk (n=5495) and report the participation ratio with and without the KMAR rows. If KMAR lifts effective dims materially, the second-site argument is measured rather than asserted, and it prices the 336px merged build (knee-rijuv).
notes:
2026-09-16 10:27Z — THE +0.0099 THIS BEAD QUOTES AS 'corpus' IS RECONCILED, AND IT IS NOT CORPUS. experiments/README.md:14394, verbatim: 'The +0.0099 once attributed to "corpus" was corpus + slot_dropout 0.40 + 24 epochs, three changes read as one; the matched pair isolating corpus reads null.' The matched contrasts at :14387-14389, all ledger75 @909: base224_drop40_long vs mergedk_drop40_long -0.0012 (corpus alone; +0.0014 at MIDPOINT, so the sign flips with the CUT); the 2x2 seat deltas -0.0006 / -0.0011; labelwise_dense vs mergedk_labelwise_drop40_long_336 -0.0063 at 336. Three independent denominators, at or inside the 0.0010 seed spread except the third, which is negative at six times it.

So the number in this bead's description carries no STATISTIC/POPULATION/CUT and is a three-lever sum read as one lever. Do not price a mergedk arm against it. beta=0.22 predicted +0.0068 for the 1.247x and does NOT transfer across SITES — it was fitted on rows that were all RSNA knee MRI.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, same source: holdout909 is blind to the decode toll by construction (KMAR subjects are new PATIENTS, so corpus shift and decode shift are not separated). foreign_readout is the ruler that separates them and NO foreign_readout artefact exists on disk (2026-09-16 sweep). KMAR as a TRAINING corpus is spent; knee-00zxt's pre-registered ruler is untaken, and that is the only thing still standing on this axis.

Filed while settling the audit bead's own flag that this number was unreconciled. Same defect class as the withdrawn 0.949 (knee-k1d9v): a quoted number nobody re-opened.

title: the last-epoch veto is mis-specified under --one-cycle: a healthy anneal SHOULD peak last
description:
PRICE: ~0 h (analysis of runs already on disk). P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.00 -- this is an INSTRUMENT on the READING rule, not a card arm.

WHAT. Several arms carry a pre-registered clause: 'if this arm peaks ON ITS LAST EPOCH the budget is still binding at 24 and NO verdict may be read.' labelwise_ext_drop40_long (knee-cgt9m) peaked on epoch 23 of 0..23, monotone rising to the end (0.8657/0.8666/0.8667/0.8669/0.8672), so its +0.0059 over labelwise_extended was NOT quoted. Honoured.

WHY IT MAY BE WRONG. $RECIPE carries --one-cycle. The LR anneals to ~0 on the final epoch, so the last epoch is where the schedule PUTS the best weights by construction. Under one_cycle, peaking last is the EXPECTED signature of a healthy converged run, not evidence of a binding budget. The veto was written from the twelve-epoch labelwise family, whose members peak at e7-e10 -- but those are runs that DECLINE after the peak, which is the actual missing-regulariser signature. band_dense_drop40_long's e16-of-24 peak is then the ATYPICAL case, not the norm the veto assumed.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Over every one_cycle run on disk with a completed budget, histogram peak_epoch/(epochs-1). If the mass sits at 1.0, last-epoch peaking is the schedule and the veto retires (replaced by a DECLINE-based test: a budget is binding only if the tail is still rising at a rate above the epoch-to-epoch noise). If the mass is spread, the veto stands and knee-cgt9m stays unquotable.

BINDS AGAIN IMMEDIATELY. labelwise_depth24_drop40_long (knee-9bnkc, pid 71652, lands ~06:55Z) carries the identical clause and is the same recipe family. Settle this before reading it out.

DO NOT WAIVE A PRE-REGISTRATION TO RESCUE A NUMBER. If the histogram retires the veto, the RULE changes for future arms and knee-cgt9m is re-read under the NEW rule with that written down -- it is not re-read because its delta was nice.
notes:
SETTLED THE SAME HOUR, AND MY HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG WHILE THE CONCLUSION STILL CHANGES.

The one_cycle hypothesis is REFUTED by the repo's own measurement, already written down in
convergence_check.py:104-109: under one_cycle a LATE peak is ordinary (32% of finished twelve-epoch runs
peak at e9 or e10), but peaking on the very LAST epoch is RARE -- 3 of 53 finished twelve-epoch runs,
against the ~14% a flat prior over the observed e5-e11 range would give. All three carry a confirmed
recipe defect. So last-epoch peaking is NOT the expected signature of a healthy anneal. I filed this
bead on a mechanism the project had already measured against, which is the CLAUDE.md failure 'READ THE
LEDGER AND THE INTERPRETATIONS before filing a finding' for the third time.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THE ARM HEADERS. The project's veto is not argmax-alone and has not been
since 2026-08-30. convergence_check.UNDERTRAINED requires the argmax to be last AND the gain over the
final TAIL=3 epochs to clear RISING_MARGIN=0.0062, the 909-study holdout floor. The docstring records
why: argmax alone reported eleven runs, SEVEN of them plateaus that had gained 0.0004-0.0020 over their
last three epochs. The pre-registrations in labelwise_ext_drop40_long.sh and
labelwise_depth24_drop40_long.sh say only 'if this arm peaks ON ITS LAST EPOCH ... NO verdict may be
read' -- a hand-written restatement that dropped the margin. They re-introduced by prose the version the
gate retired with an argument.

MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. labelwise_ext_drop40_long_s2026 gained +0.0006 midpoint over its final three
epochs (e20 0.8666 -> e23 0.8672), a tenth of the floor. convergence_check --run on its metrics returns
CONVERGED, as does its control labelwise_extended_s2026.

THE RULE, and it is not a waiver to rescue a number: a budget verdict is read from convergence_check,
never from an argmax by hand. That binds equally on arms whose delta is bad, and it binds on
labelwise_depth24_drop40_long (knee-9bnkc) when it lands. Future arm headers cite the check instead of
restating it.

CONSEQUENCE. knee-cgt9m's delta IS readable under the legislated rule: 0.9045 vs labelwise_extended
0.8986 = +0.0059 ledger75, its pre-registered CLEAR band. See the interpretation.

title: Re-price the auxiliary-objective family at full budget with a matched control
description:
Every one of the twelve --*-weight arms was fitted at 12 epochs with no regulariser, against band_dense_s2026 0.8578. knee-kiss9 and knee-q1pp0 measured that harness to BIND: adding --slot-dropout 0.40 and --epochs 24 to the matched plain recipe moved base224_control 0.8754 -> 0.8865 at ledger75 (+0.0111), and the corpus lever's entire +0.0051 12-epoch edge evaporated once both sides converged. So the aux-objective family's numbers are facts about a wall, exactly as the corpus numbers were.

severity_weight is the arm to re-take: three non-overlapping agreement CIs (0.378 / 0.688 / 0.958 over n=98/141/72), a falsifiable concentration clause (the gain must land on graded labels and a uniform lift REFUTES it), and a stated control. It read 0.8530 mid / 0.8871 l75 against band_dense 0.8578 mid -- a -0.0048 loss on the binding harness.

TWO arms, because a single one repeats the corpus mistake of subtracting a converged arm from a truncated one:
  severity_drop40_long   = severity_weight.sh + --slot-dropout 0.40 + --epochs 24
  band_dense_drop40_long = the same line with --severity-weight OFF (the matched control)
The control is reusable as the denominator for all twelve aux arms, so it is bought once.

PRICE: ~1.0 h (two arms, ~75 s/epoch x 24 each at 224/20-slice)
P(clears +0.0040) ~ 0.25

PRE-REGISTRATION (delta = severity_drop40_long minus band_dense_drop40_long, ledger75):
  >= +0.0040  the objective earns a seat once its budget is not the control's. The aux-objective axis
              RE-OPENS and the other eleven arms are re-priceable on the same control.
  +0.000..+0.004  directional. Keep for the pool, spend no slot.
  <= 0.000    the objective is dead at full budget and the family closes on a harness that cannot be
              blamed -- the same closure shape the corpus lever just took.
  CONCENTRATION (severity_weight's own clause, inherited verbatim): the gain must concentrate on the
  graded labels (Medial/Lateral Meniscus, Medial/Lateral/PF OA). A UNIFORM lift across all twelve
  REFUTES the mechanism, and a lift concentrated in MCL refutes it too.
  holdout     expected >= 0.8530 (severity_weight's own 12-epoch peak) by the budget argument.
notes:
PRICE CORRECTED: ~2.5 h for the pair, not ~1.0 h. Measured 185 s/epoch on the card (20 slices at 224), not the ~75 s/epoch estimated from base224_drop40_long's 12-slice line. 24 epochs x 185 s = 74 min per arm. The estimate was carried over from an arm with a different slice count and that is the error. The run still stands -- the card was idle and the first slot mark is 06:10Z -- but the ratio is 2.5 h for an instrument, not 1.0 h.
READ 2026-09-18T02:14Z, FOUR DAYS AFTER THE ARMS FINISHED. Both checkpoints have sat on disk since 2026-09-13 (02:38Z and 03:53Z) with no ledger row, and the pair was still ARMED to re-run tonight behind headlr_ship_ff - reading_check --only caught it, which is the whole reason that rule exists (knee-18c5r). ledger75, population eb3ba199, 909 studies: band_dense_drop40_long_s2026 0.8918 (peak epoch 16), severity_drop40_long_s2026 0.8899 (peak epoch 18). Both ran the full 24 epochs, so neither is TRUNCATED and the budget argument held on its own terms - severity's holdout 0.8538 clears the 0.8530 it owed. DELTA = -0.0019, inside the 0.0062 paired floor and on the negative side: the <= 0.000 BRANCH. The auxiliary-objective family CLOSES at full budget, on a harness that cannot be blamed, which is the closure shape knee-kiss9's corpus lever took. CONCENTRATION was not evaluated and does not need to be: the clause governs where a GAIN lands and there is no gain. WHAT THE CONTROL DOES NOT BUY. It was bought as the reusable denominator for the other eleven --*-weight arms, but those eleven were fitted at 12 epochs with NO regulariser, so subtracting them from this converged control is the truncated-minus-converged mistake this bead was created to avoid. Re-pricing them honestly means re-running each at --slot-dropout 0.40 --epochs 24: eleven arms x ~75 min = ~13 h of card, for a family whose LEAD member - the one with three non-overlapping agreement CIs and a falsifiable clause, i.e. the best-argued of the twelve - just read null. Refused on ratio. The control keeps its value as a 24-epoch anchor at the 224/20-slice corner, which is a corner with few converged members.

title: the corpus delta has never been read with both sides at full budget - base224_drop40_long is the missing control
description:
PRICE: ~0.4 h
P(clears +0.0040 corpus delta) ~ 0.35

title: submit_check reads UNKNOWN on the whole raptor two-pass kernel family
description: submit_check --kernel dimiturnt/kneemri-hidose and --kernel dimiturnt/kneemri-slotseat BOTH return 'UNKNOWN <k>: names no members in its source, so this check did not look'.
