title: slot_dropout dose 0.55: the third point on the only monotone dose-response this project owns
description:
THE DOSE-RESPONSE IS NOW TWO POINTS AND MONOTONE THROUGH ITS LAST ONE, which is the exact condition slot_dropout_hi.sh named as re-opening the field. Measured against the matched control band_dense_s2026 in one pass each, calibration gate passed both times (the control reproduced -0.0361 exactly; slot_cost inside +/-0.0001 on every row, so the shifted path served our own pixels unchanged):

    dose        0.00      0.25      0.40
    decode_cost -0.0361   -0.0271   -0.0229
    vs control  --        +0.0090   +0.0132
    sd of pool  --        2.4       3.5      (eleven-member pool, mean -0.0336, sd 0.0038)

WHY A THIRD POINT RATHER THAN A FOURTH ENTRY BUILT ON THE SECOND. Two points on a monotone line cannot say where the line turns, and every operator this project has run has had a ceiling (fieldwide's scale-jitter died at its only dose; the ghost-spacing build died at the textbook spacing). The cheapest thing that can find this one's ceiling is one more dose, and the gain per dose is already SHRINKING -- +0.0090 for the first 0.25, +0.0042 for the next 0.15, which per unit dose is 0.036/unit then 0.028/unit. A saturating curve is the null this arm exists to separate from a still-climbing one.

ONE VARIABLE OFF slot_dropout_hi.sh: --slot-dropout 0.40 -> 0.55. Everything else byte-identical, same control, same 12 epochs, same recipe.

THE READING IS CROSS-SITE. holdout909 is drawn from the same decode as training and is blind BY CONSTRUCTION to this axis -- 0.25 read 0.8592 and 0.40 read 0.8551 against the control's 0.8578, both knob-sized and neither deciding. The deciding number is decode_cost against band_dense_s2026 MEASURED IN THE SAME PASS, never the pool mean.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS.
  OWN HOLDOUT (safety only, not the reading)
    >= 0.8480   intact, proceed to the cross-site read whatever the sign. The floor drops 0.0020 from the
                0.40 arm's 0.8500 because the 0.40 dose itself landed at 0.8551, so a 0.8500 floor would
                now refuse on a decline the previous dose already showed was affordable.
    <  0.8480   0.55 is destroying in-distribution signal faster than the axis can pay for; lane dies.
  CROSS-SITE TOLL vs band_dense_s2026's decode_cost in the same pass
    >= -0.0195  STILL CLIMBING at the per-unit rate or better. The dose axis is not the ceiling and 0.70
                becomes the next point.
    -0.0196 to -0.0229  SATURATING. The curve has flattened; 0.40 is the operating point, the axis closes
                at a KNOWN optimum rather than an assumed one, and that is the more useful of the two
                outcomes because it is what lets the dose be written into the recipe as a TERM.
    -0.0230 to -0.0300  TURNED OVER. 0.55 overshoots; the member is becoming indifferent to slots it still
                needs. 0.40 stands as the optimum and the axis closes.
    <  -0.0300  the effect does not survive at high dose at all, which retrospectively weakens the
                mechanism behind both shipped dose entries whatever the board returns for them.

PRICE: ~1.3 h (285 s/epoch measured off the live ghosting arm x 12 = 0.95 h, plus ~15 min for the two-checkpoint foreign readout, plus queue slack). P(clears >= -0.0195) ~ 0.30; P(the arm resolves the ceiling question either way, which is what it is actually bought for) ~ 0.85.

EINSTEIN GATE: grep -c slot_dropout comp/board.jsonl = 0 before today; doses 0.00/0.25/0.40 are the only ones on disk, 0.55 has never been run.

CARD: blocked until the ghosting arm and its foreign readout land (~18:45Z 2026-09-12).

title: SKM-TEA licence: governed by the Stanford Dataset Research Use Agreement, not an open licence
description:
AUDIT 2026-09-12. The last unaudited owner-supplied corpus (D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/skmtea, 19 GB: all_metadata.csv, annotations/, dicoms/, segmentation_masks/). NO licence file anywhere on disk at depth 2 - asked the host instead, as KMAR's was asked.

WHAT THE HOST SAYS. aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/skm-tea-knee-mri names no licence at all; it gives a DOI (10.71718/2ghb-nv62) and a Redivis download link. The StanfordMIMI/skm-tea DATASET.md carries access instructions and no legal terms. The governing instrument, per Stanford AIMI's own distribution language, is the STANFORD UNIVERSITY DATASET RESEARCH USE AGREEMENT - a signed DUA, NOT an open licence like KMAR's CC BY 4.0.

WHY THAT MATTERS HERE AND IS NOT A FORMALITY. This is the same shape that killed the fastMRI lane: the NYU grant covers 'or data files derived from', so a member fitted on it cannot ship. A research-use DUA raises the identical two questions and neither is answered by anything on disk - (1) does it reach DERIVED WORKS, i.e. weights fitted on the images, and (2) is a prize-bearing Kaggle entry 'research use'. Until the agreement TEXT is read, an arm on SKM-TEA is an arm that may be unshippable after it is paid for.

NOT REFUTED, UNREAD. Do not record this as a dead lane. The next step is cheap and specific: obtain the SU-DRUA text (Redivis dataset page terms tab, or the AIMI download flow's click-through) and read the derived-works clause. If it permits model weights, SKM-TEA is the BETTER-TRAINING-DATA corner's last standing candidate and goes straight into the queue.

PRICE: ~0.2 h. P(clears licence) ~ 0.35.
notes: LICENCE READ 2026-09-12 18:01Z. SKM-TEA is DEAD on licence, same shape as fastMRI. aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/skm-tea-knee-mri names NO licence instrument of its own (DOI 10.71718/2ghb-nv62 + a Redivis link, and Redivis is a JS SPA WebFetch reads as the single word 'Redivis'). The governing instrument is the Stanford University Dataset Research Use Agreement, whose text IS published verbatim on sibling AIMI dataset pages -- read off aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/lera-lower-extremity-radiographs, which is the same template AIMI applies across its shared datasets. Two clauses close the lane and either would do it alone: 'Permission is granted to view and use the ... Dataset without charge for personal, non-commercial research purposes only' and 'You must not modify, reverse engineer, decompile, or create derivative works from the ... Dataset.' A prize-bearing Kaggle entry is not personal non-commercial research, and weights fitted on the images are a derivative work -- the exact pair of questions recorded as UNREAD when this bead was filed, now both answered against us. THE ONE CAVEAT, stated rather than hidden: this is the RUA text as published for LERA, not a copy scraped from SKM-TEA's own click-through, which sits behind Redivis. It is strong evidence, not a signed instrument in hand. It does NOT need to be stronger: the lane is refused on the more permissive reading too, because 'non-commercial' alone is dispositive for a competition with a cash prize. The 19 GB at /d/data/volumetric/mri/raw/skmtea stays unused. PRICE was ~0.2 h; actual ~0.1 h; P(clears) was ~0.35 and the outcome was 0.

title: ghosting arm: motion artefact at KMAR-measured severity, cross-site read
description:
ARM: ghosting_s2026 -- one variable off band_dense_s2026, --ghosting 0.040.

MECHANISM. slot_dropout is the one shared blind spot that survived 2026-09-12 (cross-site toll -0.0271 vs its matched control band_dense_s2026 at -0.0361, +0.0090 shallower, 2.4 sd of the eleven-member pool). It is a corruption-robustness operator dialled to taste. This is the same mechanism class with the taste removed: severity CALIBRATED against KMAR-50K's measured motion residual (109 paired volumes, p50 0.040 of full scale, impulsiveness p99/mean ~9). kneemri/training/ghosting.py reproduces 7.50 impulsiveness from mechanism alone after the corpus refuted its first build at 3.39.

LICENCE: CLEAR. KMAR-50K is CC BY 4.0 (Mendeley DOI 10.17632/xw7mrg7ntg.6, data_licence.short_name 'CC BY 4.0'). No pixel of it enters a cache, a checkpoint or Kaggle regardless -- what crosses is operator parameters fitted to a published statistic. Unlike the resnet (CC BY-NC-SA) and fastMRI (derived-data clause), nothing here blocks a shipment.

READING IS CROSS-SITE. holdout909 is drawn from the same acquisition distribution as training, so it is structurally blind to a robustness lever -- a flat there refutes nothing. Comparator is decode_cost(band_dense_s2026) MEASURED IN THE SAME PASS (-0.0361 on 2026-09-12), never the pool mean.

BANDS (pre-registered):
  own holdout >= 0.8500  intact, proceed to the cross-site read whatever the sign
  own holdout <  0.8500  the operator is destroying in-distribution signal; lane dies here
  cross-site >= -0.0290  CLEARS. A calibrated artefact operator buys robustness, and the shared-field
                         axis re-opens on a term rather than a knob.
  -0.0291 to -0.0340     directional. Keep the operator, do not run a second severity.
  -0.0341 to -0.0400     NULL. The calibration bought nothing slot_dropout did not already buy.
  <  -0.0400             the operator is harmful at the measured severity.

EINSTEIN GATE: no prior submission or arm carries a motion/ghosting term -- grep of comp/board.jsonl and experiments/arms/ finds none. The three closed external-corpus arms all POOLED foreign studies into our label space; this trains on zero KMAR studies.

PRICE: ~1.2 h (12 epochs x ~280 s, plus ~10 min foreign readout). No submission slot.
P(clears >= -0.0290) ~ 0.30. Priced against the standing alternatives: a padding-only arm (partner lever already dead), a MedicalNet fine-tune (4-6 h to close 0.067 of frozen gap), and the six never-run label tables (~1 h each, recipe terms not robustness).

title: fastMRI+ localized supervision: per-slice boxes say WHICH slice and WHERE, which our labels never do
description:
PARENT: knee-keemo.

THE ASSET. D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/fastmri/labels/Annotations/knee.csv, schema 'file,slice,study_level,x,y,width,height,label' -- per-SLICE bounding boxes with pathology names, e.g. 'Cartilage - Partial Thickness loss/defect' at slice 14, box (90,173,35,10). Licence at raw/fastmri/labels/LICENSE is MIT (Microsoft), so the ANNOTATIONS are clean to ship. The fastMRI IMAGES are a separate instrument under NYU's data agreement and that must be read before a member trained on the pixels is submitted.

WHAT IT SUPERVISES THAT WE CANNOT. Our labels are STUDY-level, mined from report text by regex. Nothing in this project has ever supervised WHICH SLICE carries the finding, yet every member pools 20 slices with learned weights (labelwise / max) that receive no gradient about slice relevance at all. That pooling stage is a free parameter trained only through a study-level signal, and this file is the only thing on disk that can constrain it.

TWO USES, AND THE CHEAP ONE IS AN INSTRUMENT THAT RUNS FIRST.
  (a) INSTRUMENT, no new training: score our existing members' learned slice weights against fastMRI+-derived
      slice relevance. If our pooling already concentrates on the slices a radiologist boxed, the lane dies for
      the cost of a readout and nothing further is spent. If it does not, the size of the disagreement prices (b).
  (b) ARM: train a per-slice pathology head on fastMRI+ and use it either as an auxiliary target on our studies
      or as a slice-attention prior. Our label space is untouched; this adds a KIND, never a pooled site.

PRICE: (a) ~0.6 h, no card. (b) ~2.5 h decode of fastMRI knee h5 + ~1.2 h arm = ~3.7 h.
P(clears +0.0062 own-holdout floor | (a) shows real disagreement) ~ 0.35. P(a shows disagreement) ~ 0.6.
Unconditional P(b clears) ~ 0.21, which is why (a) is a gate and not a formality.

ORDER: run (a) before (b). It is the cheapest thing in the epic and it can close the lane without touching the card.
notes:
CLOSED WITHOUT A RUN, on an audit of code I should have read before filing it (2026-09-12 16:39Z).

I filed this bead claiming fastMRI+ per-slice boxes were an unexploited supervision KIND. Three facts on
disk say otherwise, and all three predate the bead:

1. THE ANNOTATIONS ARE ALREADY FULLY CONSUMED. core/data/corpus/fastmri_corpus.py maps the fastMRI+
   vocabulary onto our twelve findings with a three-valued verdict (positive / coarse-blocks-the-negative
   / None-leaves-it-unlabelled), and it already uses the BOX COORDINATES, not just the labels: Reading.
   compartmental straddles COMPARTMENT_TROUGH to split a side-less 'Meniscus Tear' into medial and
   lateral when its boxes fall both sides of the trough. That buys the meniscus pair 190 studies / 380
   cells in two columns that held zero. The localization I said we did not have is the load-bearing
   trick in a module that already shipped.

2. THE ARMS ALREADY RAN AND ARE DECLINED. ortho_fastmri 0.8475 vs control ortho_dense 0.8452 (+0.0023),
   ortho_fastmri_masked 0.8464 (+0.0012). Ledger README:13710 and :13767. The Einstein gate refuses this
   as a re-run.

3. IT CANNOT SHIP EVEN IF IT WON. README:13797 -- NYU's fastMRI grant covers 'data files derived from the
   fastMRI Dataset', so no member fitted on any merge of ours is shippable. The ledger already states
   'fastMRI stays PARKED, and no card is owed to it' (:15180).

WHAT THIS DOES NOT KILL. The per-SLICE axis (which slice a finding sits on, as opposed to where in the
slice) is genuinely unused -- fastmri_corpus._slot exists but nothing supervises slice weights with it.
It dies here on the LICENCE, not on the mechanism: the axis is unshippable wherever fastMRI is its only
source. Re-open it only against a corpus we may ship, never by re-quoting the +0.0023.

MY ERROR, NAMED. I priced a lane from a directory listing instead of from the repo, having written the
audit rule into CLAUDE.md myself. The same call that found kmar_corpus.py already existed would have
found fastmri_corpus.py had I grepped for the second name.

title: KMAR paired-degradation objective: the only corpus that supervises acquisition robustness directly
description:
PARENT: knee-keemo.

THE ASSET. D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/kmar50k holds ArtifactData_part1 (698 .nii) paired BY EXACT FILENAME with GroundTruthData_part1 (700), plus part2 -- e.g. 2020_103_transection_0.0.nii exists in both. Same knee, same geometry, one corrupted and one clean. Siemens 1.5T PD TSE FS (TrainingCohort.csv, 1341 rows), which is the same sequence family as RSNA knee. Views are sagittal / coronal / transection.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT TARGET TODAY. The 2026-09-12 cross-site pass measured the pool's generalisation toll at -0.0336 +/- 0.0038 and found it FLAT across eleven members -- a brittleness every member shares, which is exactly the class of defect ensembling cannot repair (knee-gcgbk: eleven distinct kernels at 0.944, reseating retired). Every attempt so far has tried to SIMULATE that shift with augmentation: intensity_augment and aug_long refuted at 12 and 24 epochs, mixup flat at two doses, and fieldwide (--scale-jitter 0.25 --padding-mode reflection) FLAT at +0.0042 on 2026-09-12. KMAR does not simulate it. It is the real corruption with the clean volume attached, which makes it supervision rather than a guess about what corruption looks like.

THE OBJECTIVE. Auxiliary consistency head: the encoder must map an artifact volume and its ground-truth twin to the same representation (cosine or L2 on pooled features), trained jointly with the RSNA task on our own corpus. Our label space is UNTOUCHED -- KMAR carries no abnormality labels and none are invented. This is why the closed site-count axis (second site +0.0043, third site -0.0024) does not apply: nothing is pooled into our labels.

FIRST STEP IS A DECODE, NOT AN ARM. KMAR is .nii and must reach our cache format before anything trains. Use arm_check --smoke to write the truncated cache (sixty studies, distinct _first60 filename) rather than hand-building one -- that step already exists and was re-discovered the hard way once (crop80_span, 2026-08-19).

READING. Cross-site decode_cost from foreign_readout against a matched control in the SAME pass, plus own holdout as the safety check. Bands to be pre-registered in the arm before the card is spent, scaled by the pool sd 0.0038.

PRICE: ~1.5 h decode (CPU/disk, no card) + ~1.2 h arm = ~2.7 h.
P(clears +0.0090 cross-site, i.e. matches the best toll-vs-control the project has measured) ~ 0.30.
P(clears own-holdout floor +0.0062) ~ 0.20 -- lower, and deliberately so: the mechanism targets transfer, and our holdout is drawn from the same field distribution as training, so it is structurally near-blind to this. A flat there refutes nothing.
LICENCE: no licence file found under raw/kmar50k at depth 2. MUST be established before any member trained on it is submitted -- the resnet-50-radimagenet member died on CC BY-NC-SA weights AFTER being built. Establish first, train second.
notes:
THE NUMBER THE OPERATOR MUST REPRODUCE, MEASURED 2026-09-12 16:40Z. 120 pairs sampled evenly through
1,339, 109 measured, 11 refused on a shape mismatch (9% -- the filenames joined and the arrays did not,
counted rather than swallowed). Report at D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/kmar_residual.json.

STATISTIC / POPULATION / CUT: per-pixel |artifact - clean| in the [0,1] space our cache holds, windowed
on the CLEAN volume's own percentiles; population = KMAR-50K parts 1+2 paired volumes, evenly spaced;
quantiles over pairs, not over pixels.

                       p10     p50     p90
  residual            0.023   0.040   0.086
  residual_p99        0.180   0.363   0.630
  background_share    0.057   0.113   0.201

  by plane (p50):  sagittal 0.0406 / coronal 0.0434 / transection 0.0367
  background_share by plane (p50): sagittal 0.106 / coronal 0.116 / transection 0.125

THREE THINGS THIS BUYS, AND EACH ONE CONSTRAINS A DIFFERENT KNOB.

1. MAGNITUDE. Mean residual 0.040 of full scale. A motion operator that moves pixels by 0.15 is not
   simulating this corpus, it is simulating a different disease.
2. IMPULSIVENESS. p99/mean = 0.363/0.040 = ~9x. Motion artifact is SPARSE and structured, not additive
   noise -- Gaussian noise has p99/mean ~2.6. Any operator whose ratio is near 2.6 is refuted on this
   number before it is ever trained with.
3. GHOSTING, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT NAMES THE MECHANISM. 11.3% of the total residual energy falls on
   pixels the CLEAN volume puts in its bottom decile -- i.e. outside the anatomy. Motion does not blur
   the knee in place; it throws replicas into empty space along the phase-encode direction. An operator
   that only blurs cannot produce a background share above ~0 and is refuted too.

THE PLANE INVARIANCE IS A RESULT, NOT A NULL. Three acquisition planes, medians 0.037-0.043 and
background shares 0.106-0.125 -- a spread far smaller than the p10-p90 spread WITHIN any one plane. The
operator therefore takes ONE parameterisation for all three, and an arm does not need a per-plane term.
That is a knob that does not have to be searched, priced at zero card.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. 109 pairs is enough for a p50 and not for a tail; residual_p99's own p10-p90 spans
0.18-0.63, so severity is to be SAMPLED per-study from this distribution, never fixed at the median.
And these are Siemens Aera 1.5T pd_tse_fs volumes (TrainingCohort.csv) -- whether RSNA's mixed vendors
ghost at the same scale is unmeasured and unmeasurable without pairs of ours.

LICENCE BLOCKER RESOLVED 2026-09-13 (forum sweep, research/2026-09-13_host_rulings_forum_sweep.md).
The bead's own gate read: 'no licence file found under raw/kmar50k at depth 2. MUST be established
before any member trained on it is submitted.' Established: KMAR-50K is CC BY 4.0 -- no access gate,
no NC clause, no ND clause. It is the ONLY external knee corpus this project holds that is clean on
every axis the competition host has ruled on:
  rule 2.6.a  public, equally accessible, no cost   -- met, ungated
  rule 2.6.b  not specifically prohibited by Host   -- met; the only by-name prohibition is KneeCoT
              (Kaggle staff, discussion 734109), refused ON THE REQUIRED DATA AGREEMENT, which KMAR
              does not have
  rule 2.5    winner licence, CC-BY-NC 4.0          -- met; BY imposes attribution only, and the host
              retired the NC objection outright in 733965 ('readily accessible datasets with
              non-commercial use restrictions are generally acceptable ... receiving prize money does
              not constitute commercial exploitation'). KMAR is not even NC.
Attribution is the ONLY obligation and it attaches to the writeup, not to the training run. TRAIN, YES.
REDISTRIBUTE, YES WITH ATTRIBUTION. SHIP WEIGHTS, YES. Nothing further needs asking -- and that is why
KMAR is deliberately NOT in the forum draft: there is no live question to put to the host about it.
Contrast Rijeka, whose ND clause against rule 2.5 is the one real open question this project holds.
The arm is unblocked on licence. It remains gated on its own decode and on card time.
LICENCE GATE CLEARED, 2026-09-20T05:25Z — and it was never open. The description's 'no licence file found under raw/kmar50k at depth 2' is a statement about our download directory, not about the dataset. Two independent confirmations:

1. PRIMARY SOURCE. The Mendeley record this corpus comes from (data.mendeley.com/datasets/xw7mrg7ntg/6 — and 'xw7mrg7ntg' is the id in our own meta_xw7mrg7ntg.json) publishes it under CC BY 4.0. Attribution only: commercial use and derivative works both permitted.
2. THIS REPO'S OWN AUDIT. knee-17hjk already carries the same verdict in its table — 'KMAR-50K  CC BY 4.0, Mendeley, open download, no agreement -> clean, and it is already the only merge shippable through 2.5' — and records the host's actual test, which is GATING, not NC: Kaggle refused KneeCoT 'due to the required data agreement', and that dataset was CC BY-NC. KMAR requires no agreement and no approval.

WHAT THE LOCAL COPY SAYS, and why it misleads. We hold the Kaggle mirror (jensvannahl/kmar-50k-1); fetch.log records 'License(s): unknown' on it. That is the MIRROR's metadata field left unset by its uploader, which is the absence of a declaration rather than the absence of a grant. The mirror's silence cannot narrow the upstream CC BY 4.0.

A WEB SEARCH RETURNED 'CC BY-NC-ND 4.0' FOR THIS DATASET AND IT IS WRONG — that is Rijeka's licence, not KMAR's. Had it been acted on, the best-argued open lever in the queue would have been killed on a snippet. The primary record is the only thing that settles a licence.

So the description's 'Establish first, train second' is satisfied and nothing here is blocked on it. What remains before the card is the decode: KMAR is .nii and must reach our cache format.
AUDIT 2026-09-20 05:30Z — the MERGE form of this lever is closed by the ledger, and the two unread KMAR builds sit on that closed axis.

experiments/README.md:16335 'mergedk reads NULL, and the two nulls together say the gain is the SITE, not the supervision'. mergedk_corpus_s2026 0.8787 vs base224_control_s2026 0.8754 = +0.0033 ledger75 at 224px under distilled labels; merged3_corpus priced the SECOND SITE at +0.0043 under SPARSE HUMAN labels. Two supervisions sharing nothing but a second hospital buy the same +0.004, so the distillation bought nothing on top of the site. At our shipping 336px/12sl, README:14427 reads labelwise_dense vs mergedk_labelwise_drop40_long_336 at -0.0063, and that is AGAINST a drop40 + double-horizon tailwind worth ~+0.0084. Seat deltas -0.0006 and -0.0011. README:16387 'the mergedk 2x2 closes: the two levers ADD, and neither the sum nor the stack buys a seat'.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TWO UNREAD BUILDS. images_336px_24sl_0.1-0.9band_mergedk.npy (89.3 GB, completed 05:53 local, its post-build labels step failed on a missing labels/mergedk_labels_check.csv) and the build_kmar336_20sl run that died at 400/1088 are both the MERGE mechanism at a new DEPTH. Depth is orthogonal to 'add another site's studies', and knee-g569k closed knobs, so neither build re-opens what 14427 closed. DO NOT arm a 24sl mergedk run because the cache now exists — that is the nearest-to-hand trap, not a lever. Neither build is worth resuming on its own account.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND ITS HONEST PRICE. This bead's actual proposal is an auxiliary CONSISTENCY head on the PAIRED artifact/clean volumes with our label space untouched. That is a different mechanism and none of the rows above tested it. But only the CLEAN side is decoded (core/data/corpus/build_kmar.py ingests the clean side alone), the head does not exist, and our holdout is near-blind to motion. ~4-5 h for P~0.2 of ~0.006 is ~0.0012 expected, about 0.00027/h. Parked on ratio, not refuted — re-open by answering the ratio, not by re-quoting the licence clearance.

LICENCE remains clear (CC BY 4.0, Mendeley xw7mrg7ntg, corroborated by knee-17hjk). That was never the blocker.
LICENCE ESTABLISHED TO THE POINT OF A CONFLICT, 2026-09-20 -- OWNER RULING NEEDED BEFORE ANY CARD IS SPENT.

The bead said 'no licence file found under raw/kmar50k at depth 2'. There is none because our copy is a
THIRD-PARTY KAGGLE RE-UPLOAD: fetch.log records 'jensvannahl/kmar-50k-1', and Kaggle's own dataset
metadata returns licenses: [{name: 'unknown'}], usability 0.118, 30 downloads, empty description. An
uploader who set no licence conveys none, so the Kaggle copy alone can never clear the gate.

The primary source IS identified, and the local filenames already carried it: meta_xw7mrg7ntg.json and
meta_95w9f5tzz8.json are the two Mendeley dataset ids.
  part1  https://doi.org/10.17632/xw7mrg7ntg.5
  part2  https://doi.org/10.17632/95w9f5tzz8.6
  paper  Wang, Y. & Shi, F., 'A Multi-view Open-access Dataset of Paired Knee MRI for Motion Artifact
         Removal', Scientific Data (2025), PMC12241304 / s41597-025-05439-1

THE TWO PRIMARY SOURCES DISAGREE, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE WHOLE RULING:
  - the Mendeley landing page for xw7mrg7ntg v6 states CC BY 4.0 (attribution only; derivatives and
    commercial use permitted -- this would CLEAR)
  - the publication's own data-availability text states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial, NO DERIVATIVES
    -- this would BLOCK, and it is STRICTER than the CC BY-NC-SA that killed the resnet-50-radimagenet
    member after it was built)

Not resolvable from here, and the two branches are opposite. Under NC-ND a trained model is plausibly a
derivative and a Kaggle competition is plausibly commercial; under CC BY the arm is clear with a citation.
So the card is NOT spent on this until the owner rules, exactly as knee-vgz5b.7 gates the SKM-TEA locator.

WHAT IS UNCHANGED AND WHY THIS IS STILL THE BEST-PRICED LEVER THE PROJECT OWNS. An independent axis sweep
today closed eleven in a row against the ledger -- label noise, corpus doubling, layer-decay ladder, patch
pooling, contrastive representation, dml_b_ff (already shipped 0.943), ROI input crop (-0.0033/-0.0067),
canonical resolution (-0.0002 at matched rate), DINOv2-base and every large trunk, through-plane, SSL-as-init
(five collapses), and mricore_corpus (0.8390). That reproduces knee-xe0aq's audit independently: every axis
but CORPUS is closed. KMAR remains the only open mechanism whose size could plausibly reach 1.5%, because
the -0.0336 +/- 0.0038 cross-site toll is FLAT across eleven members -- shared brittleness, which ensembling
cannot repair -- and it is 3x the live board gap of 0.011, while the board is itself a cross-site read and
our own holdout is same-distribution and near-blind to it.

IF THE OWNER RULES CC BY, the order stands as written: decode first (~1.5 h, CPU/disk, no card, via
arm_check --smoke for the truncated cache), pre-register bands scaled by the pool sd 0.0038, then ~1.2 h
arm. Attribution is then mandatory and the citation above is the one to carry.
LICENCE CONFLICT NARROWED THE SAME HOUR -- THE HOST SAYS CC BY 4.0 ON BOTH PARTS.

Read both Mendeley landing pages, not one: xw7mrg7ntg v6 (part1) and 95w9f5tzz8 v6 (part2) BOTH state
CC BY 4.0. The CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 line is the PAPER's data-availability text and is now the outlier, one
source against two. The licence that governs is the one attached to the artifact on the host we can
actually point at, so this leans CLEAR rather than coin-flip.

TWO CAVEATS THAT KEEP IT AN OWNER RULING RATHER THAN A GREEN LIGHT, and both are about VERSION:
  1. the paper cites part1 at v5 (10.17632/xw7mrg7ntg.5) and I read v6. A Mendeley version bump can
     change a licence, which is one way both sources are simultaneously honest.
  2. our copy did not come from Mendeley at all -- fetch.log records the Kaggle re-upload
     jensvannahl/kmar-50k-1, which declares 'unknown' and states no version. So the bytes on our disk
     are not provably the v6 the CC BY 4.0 attaches to.

The cheap fix for BOTH is to re-fetch from Mendeley v6 directly rather than argue about the Kaggle copy:
that pins the version, makes the CC BY 4.0 claim checkable against the thing we hold, and costs disk and
wall-clock but no card and no slot. Recommend that over any further reading of licence prose.

Still not started: no card spent, no decode run, awaiting the owner on whether CC BY 4.0 on the host is
accepted as governing.
PROVENANCE CAVEAT #2 IS LARGELY DISCHARGED, for zero bytes and no card (2026-09-20T10:41Z).

The recommended fix was a full Mendeley re-fetch to pin the version. PRICED AND REJECTED: the local copy is 67 GB against 291 GB free, so a re-fetch costs hours and a third of the remaining disk to answer a provenance question. There was a cheaper instrument already on disk.

f_xw7mrg7ntg.json (fetched 2026-09-01 from the Mendeley public-files API) carries Mendeley's OWN sha256 and size for part1's cohort tables. Hashed the local Kaggle-sourced copies against them:

  TestingCohort.csv    13109 B  sha256 MATCH
  TrainingCohort.csv  248681 B  sha256 MATCH

So jensvannahl/kmar-50k-1 is a FAITHFUL MIRROR of the Mendeley artifact, not a re-derivation or a re-cut. That was the substance of caveat #2 ('our bytes are not provably the thing the CC BY 4.0 attaches to') and it is now evidence rather than assumption, on the files we can check.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated so this is not over-read:
  1. It verifies the two COHORT CSVs, not the 67 GB of imaging, for which Mendeley served no file listing (meta_*.json and the part2 listing all came back empty []). It is strong evidence about the mirror's fidelity, not a hash of the pixels.
  2. It does not date the version. The listing was pulled 2026-09-01 from whatever Mendeley served as current then; the landing pages read CC BY 4.0 / v6 at that time, and the paper cites v5. Caveat #1 (a version bump could move a licence) is untouched by a hash.

NET: two independent host pages say CC BY 4.0, and our copy is now shown to be the host's bytes. The remaining question is narrower than when this was written -- not 'is our copy the real thing' but 'is v6 the governing version'. Still the owner's ruling, still no card spent, and the decode order in the plan above is unchanged if it comes back CC BY.

  corpus merge   mergedk vs base224 -0.0012 matched; the 2x2 seat deltas -0.0006 / -0.0011;

title: submit_check gives a FALSE GREEN: board.jsonl stores a member COUNT, not the member SET
description:
Measured 2026-09-12. 'python -m kneemri.kaggle.submit_check --kernel kneemri-cnnseat' printed 'ok kneemri-cnnseat: 7 members, no recorded entry carries this set'. But cnnseat_v1 HAD already shipped: ref 56147841, 2026-09-09, board 0.944, and its row is in comp/board.jsonl.

ROOT CAUSE: the check compares SET equality on members (correct, by design, since renaming is what happens between attempts), but the historical rows it compares against carry 'members' as an INT COUNT. A row with no member set cannot be set-compared, so every such row is silently skipped and the entry reads NEW. The overlap table it prints is computed from the kernels it CAN read, which is why the output looks rich and authoritative while the one row that mattered was invisible.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the only pre-flight whose job is 'is this entry NEW'. It exists because a slot went to kneemri-peak8 seven days after peak8_v1 shipped the identical eight members with every gate green (knee-1sgr). The same class of miss is still live. Today it would have cost a slot had the Einstein gate not caught it by grep.

FIX (two parts, the second is the real one): (1) submit_check must EXIT 2 (UNKNOWN) rather than 0 for any historical row whose member set is unavailable -- 'I could not compare' must not read as 'it is new', which is exactly the rule the tool already applies to run-time-ranking kernels. (2) board_check should write the member SET into the row, from the kernel's chosen tuple, so the comparison is possible at all.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-12, and the earlier int-count diagnosis in this bead was WRONG (it confused the int field `members` with the list field `members_named`, which 99 of 133 rows carry and which submit_check reads correctly).

The cause is one line in board_check.BoardCensus.rows(): `if "note" not in row`. Commentary lines were being told apart from entries by the PRESENCE OF A NOTE, so annotating a scored row deleted it from the census -- and the census is the only thing submit_check compares against. Four priced rows were invisible: cnnseat 0.944 (ref 56147841), tablepool 0.944 (56172710), honestsix 0.938 (56173554), honestfar 0.941 (56173880). Two of them sit at the board's own maximum. duplicated() could not have caught a second copy of any of them and the transfer fit dropped their points.

The symptom was a GREEN check, which is the shape that costs a slot: submit_check --kernel kneemri-cnnseat printed 'ok ... no recorded entry carries this set' while an exactly-equal row sat one filter away.

FIX: the test is the missing REF, never the present note -- `if row.get("ref") or "note" not in row`. Census 125 -> 129, named rows 99, refless 0, duplicated 0, and submit_check now REFUSES cnnseat naming ref 56147841. Mirror test test_rows_keeps_an_annotated_submission added.

TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS WERE FIXED ALONG THE WAY AND NEITHER IS THIS ONE: (a) row 56147841's members_named listed seven members the entry never held, corrected against git commit d92fd2c1 and a live kaggle kernels pull which agreed; (b) three rows carried a date one day ahead, corrected against Kaggle's own submission timestamps.

STILL OPEN, FILED SEPARATELY: nothing verifies a row's members_named against the kernel that shipped it (that is how (a) survived), and 26 priced rows name no members at all, so they are invisible to the repeat check by omission rather than by filter.

title: dropstack_dense: stochastic depth ramped over trunk depth at the dense corner
description:
MECHANISM: each residual block's branch zeroed per-sample with prob p (ramped linearly 0 at block 0 -> p at the last), survivors /(1-p) so identity in expectation. Implicit ensemble over 2^depth weight-shared subnets. Same axis as sam_dense (generalisation at fixed data + fixed architecture).

WHY BUILT AS A MODULE: transformers applies drop_path_rate FLAT at every depth; the published recipe RAMPS. And ENCODERS is a frozen registry shared with the kernel, so a per-run number cannot live in it.

EINSTEIN GATE (run before building): TimmTrunk.drop_path defaults 0.0 and no flag has ever reached it; foreign_encoders.py:297 drop_path=0.1 is the FOREIGN raptor encoder, never our trunk. No ledger row and no submission in this project has ever been measured with stochastic depth on. NOT a repeat.

CONTROL: calib_dense_hold_s2026 = 0.8634 @holdout909 midpoint. Byte-identical flag list plus --stochastic-depth 0.1.

PRICE: ~56 min (279 s/epoch MEASURED x 12 epochs at 20 slices). ZERO submission slots. ZERO extra compute over the control -- no second forward, no parameter, no buffer. A third of sam_dense's 1.9 h.
P(clears 0.005) = 0.25. P(clears 1.5% absolute) = 0.06. Published effect sizes come from long from-scratch schedules; a 12-epoch fine-tune is the regime where this is smallest.

BANDS: >= 0.8684 carries (escalate to a RATE sweep 0.05/0.2, then the span corner -- not a seed, not a fold). 0.8604-0.8683 directional only, keep the member as a diversity seat, plan nothing around it. < 0.8604 refutes THIS RATE AT THIS BUDGET, not the mechanism.
A gain concentrated on one or two labels REFUTES the mechanism while the mean reads as a win -- stochastic depth acts on the trunk, which every label reads through, so it must move the row broadly. Read the per-label row first.

HARNESS SUSPECT NAMED IN ADVANCE: StochasticDepth.applied walks by ATTRIBUTE NAME, so a trunk spelling its residual policy differently receives nothing, and the resulting run is an ordinary one under this arm's name with an identical checkpoint/score/ledger row. The walk RAISES on zero blocks, and the count is stamped as drop_path_blocks in the recipe. Assert from the LOG: "drop_path_rate": 0.1 AND nonzero "drop_path_blocks" (12 for dinov2-small).
notes: dropstack_dense relaunched 2026-09-12T07:21Z. FIRST LAUNCH DIED IN SECONDS: ValueError whole-stack reading needs per-slice pooling or a tubelet trunk, not 'channels'. My arm dropped --slice-pooling max, which the control calib_dense_hold carries, so the one-variable claim in the header was false as written. Fixed and relaunched. PLUMBING WITNESS FIRED: 'stochastic depth ramped to 0.1 across 12 blocks'. Carry the SAM rate prior into the reading: a published regularisation rate calibrated on from-scratch schedules can be far too large for a 12-epoch fine-tune of a pretrained trunk.

title: sam_dense: sharpness-aware minimization at radius 0.05 on the best dense recipe
description:
PRICE: 279 s/epoch x 2 (SAM doubles the forward+backward) x 12 epochs = ~1.9 h of card. Zero submission slots.

CONTROL: calib_dense_hold_s2026 = 0.8634 @holdout909 midpoint, the IDENTICAL recipe under the identical fp16 GradScaler path (experiments/recipe.sh:23 passes no --bf16). Single variable: --sharpness 0.05.

MECHANISM: every dense arm in the ledger descends to whatever minimum the one-cycle anneal lands in. SAM descends using the gradient taken at the WORST point of a rho-ball around the current weights, which penalises sharp minima. Published gains on ImageNet-scale classification are ~0.5-1.8% absolute; the flatness argument is a GENERALISATION argument, which is the axis the owner named (offline 0.865 vs board 0.944 means the corner is not the bottleneck the board sees).

P(clears the 0.005 board-noise bar): ~0.30. P(clears 1.5% absolute): ~0.08.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS (holdout909 midpoint, vs 0.8634):
  >= 0.8684  (+0.005)  SAM carries; escalate to a radius sweep and a second seed of the winner.
  0.8604-0.8684        within noise; DIRECTIONAL only, keep the flag, do not plan around it.
  <  0.8604  (-0.003)  the radius is too large for a 12-epoch one-cycle at backbone-lr 4e-5, OR
                       flatness is not what separates our corner from the board. Read the per-label
                       row before concluding: a uniform loss is the radius, a concentrated one is not.

HARNESS SUSPECTS NAMED IN ADVANCE: (1) the ascent must actually fire -- Sharpness.climbed returns False on a non-finite gradient, which under fp16 is a real path, so grep the run for how often it declined; (2) --accumulate must be 1, and sharpen() raises rather than approximating.

EINSTEIN GATE: grepped experiments/arms/ and experiments/README.md -- no prior arm passes --sharpness and no ledger row names SAM. medsam_dense_s2026 is Segment-Anything used as a TRUNK, a different thing. GATE PASSED.
notes:
REFUTED AT rho=0.05, truncated 2026-09-12T07:16Z by trajectory_check. sam_dense_s2026 e6 0.8213 against matched control calib_dense_hold_s2026 e6 0.8634 (its peak). Generous ceiling 0.8478, granting the largest e6-to-peak gain seen across 224 runs, sits BELOW the directional band floor 0.8604 and below the control. This refutes rho=0.05 at this budget, NOT sharpness-aware minimisation. Cost 534 s/epoch vs the control's 410 (the double forward). Honest revisit if ever priced: rho=0.01 or 0.005, once. A truncated one_cycle score is a FLOOR, not a number.

title: Weight soup across independent runs at the dense corner
description: 84 fold-0 checkpoints share the dense architecture signature exactly (small/cls_mean/max/attend/336/20sl/whole_stack/unfreeze6/band 0.1-0.9), all folds=5 split_seed=2026 (the same holdout909), all scored against report_labels_v2, all 236-key state dicts, all 12 targets. They descend from one facebook/dinov2-small init and differ only in recipe and label table - Wortsman's model-soup setting. EINSTEIN GATE RUN: experiments/arms/weight_average.sh is EMA WITHIN ONE RUN (+0.0003 over wsfold0_e6), and every README 'soup' is a LOGIT ensemble. No weight-space average across independent runs exists in this repo. Build kneemri/models/weight_soup.py: average state dicts, write a soup checkpoint carrying member-0's recipe, then read it through the existing kneemri.inference.holdout_backfill. oof_teacher_s2026 (0.8685) is VOID for leak and must never be a member.
notes: CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-09-12. Uniform weight-space souping across independent dense-corner runs is NEGATIVE and degrades MONOTONICALLY with K, at -0.0044 per doubling: best member clean_calib_s2026 0.8649 > soup_top5 0.8570 > soup_top10 0.8526 > soup_top20 0.8483 (all @holdout909 midpoint). THE HETEROGENEITY EXPLANATION IS DEAD TOO: soup_siblings_s2026, built only from runs sharing a recipe family, measured 0.8624 against the K-law's extrapolated 0.8628 -- a difference of 0.0004. Siblings land ON the same line strangers do, so what the soup loses is not diversity of recipe; the members simply do not sit in one basin, which is exactly Wortsman's precondition and it does not hold here. GREEDY SOUPING DIES ON ARITHMETIC, NOT ON A RUN: greedy's first candidate IS the K=2 case, and every K=2 measured sits below both its parents, so the search has no admissible first step. That saved ~90 min of card and ~+0.011 of holdout-selection optimism. THE WEIGHT-SPACE AXIS IS CLOSED. Logit averaging is untouched by any of this and remains the project's ensemble mechanism. What the closure does NOT rule out: a soup of checkpoints from ONE run's trajectory (weight_average.sh, EMA, +0.0003) was never the question here, and a future family genuinely trained into one basin (shared warm start, low LR, no label-table change) would be a different precondition and would have to be re-tested rather than assumed dead.

title: Attribute marginals SATURATE at ~35% pass-through -- never price a stack arm additively
description:
D380, measured on the 0%-exposure sub-pool n=290 @holdout909 midpoint-binarised v2 truth. Instrument research/scripts/marginal_additivity.py.

Base = median solo of members carrying NO positive-marginal attribute = 0.8439 (n=222). Residual of median solo against strict additivity (base + sum of that member's own 0%-pool marginals), binned by attribute count k:

  k=0  n=222  0.8439  +0.0000
  k=1  n=31   0.8545  -0.0004
  k=2  n=23   0.8575  -0.0085
  k=3  n=11   0.8607  -0.0191
  k=4  n=2    0.8609  -0.0293  (thin)
  k=5  n=1    0.8648  -0.0364  (chainfour alone)

Coarse: k<=1 n=253 residual -0.0001; k>=3 n=14 residual -0.0197.

The first attribute transfers essentially whole (+0.0106 median). Each further one realises ~+0.003 against an additive promise of ~+0.011, so pass-through at k=5 is 0.0209 realised of 0.0573 promised (~36%), and the loss per added term shows NO sign of flattening through k=5. Stacking is neither the sum nor the max: it is a strategy at roughly a third of face value, with an exchange rate of ~0.35 realised per unit of promise past the first term.

RULE: any arm stacking N positive attributes must state its pre-registered branches against base + 0.35 x (sum of marginals past the largest), never against the sum. distill_stack_max's five terms promise 0.9032 additively; the curve predicts 0.865-0.867, and its honest read band including the ~80% exposure term is 0.865-0.872.

NUANCE that the curve does NOT license (main's reading): saturation does not mean spread beats stack for SOLO score. k=5 lands 0.8648 and k=1 lands 0.8545, so stacked members still top the pool by ~0.010 -- they just do not compound. A one-attribute-each member is a weaker member whose only possible value is ensemble marginal, and D377 measured any seventh seat on the no-search six as negative in-sample. So the card should keep building stacked members at 0% exposure, varying teacher and label table for decorrelation, rather than spreading attributes across weaker members.

Caveat stated: the k=4 and k=5 bins are two members and one member deep. The tail of this curve is chainfour plus one other.

description:

title: [lesson] reindex-then-threshold silently converts absent rows into negative votes - assert row coverage before reading values
description: audit400/manifest.json records corpus_unanimous_cells 36664 / 52872 = 0.6934. Reproduced exactly: the five tables were blend_four, blend_hybrid_fx_v4, confident, local_medgemma4b_annotated, report_labels_v3. local_medgemma4b_annotated has 58 rows; reindexed to the 4406-UID corpus it is 4349 all-NaN rows, and NaN>=0.5 is False, so it casts a 0 vote on 98.7% of cells and knocks every real-unanimous 1 into the discordant stratum. The four real tables measure 0.8606 unanimous; the pack's own split is 338/402=0.8408. W_U/W_D must be 0.86/0.14, giving B=0.0487 (CONDITIONAL), not 0.0787 (REFUTED). Per-stratum rates 5/338 and 10/64 are unaffected. Builder script is gone. Corrected to the researcher in M341. GENERAL LESSON: reindex-then-threshold silently converts absent rows into negative votes - any table joined to a corpus must assert its row coverage before its values are read.
notes: PREMISE REFUTED by D334: the manifest's 0.6934 was NOT computed with a phantom voter; the five tables were ours_v2 + flight + lixin + steven v4_blend + steven full, four of which live in raw/knee_label_tables/ outside the search space I used. Filed on my own reconstruction error (M341, retracted in M342). Root cause of MY error: I treated an exact numeric collision between two 12-column definitions as identity without running a perturbation test - dropping one column separates them (35,962 vs 32,844). KEPT because the mechanical lesson is real and general regardless: a table joined to a corpus must assert its row coverage before its values are thresholded, since NaN >= 0.5 is False and an absent row becomes a silent negative vote.

title: Audit of 402 report-label cells: B=0.0787 five-way REFUTED, B'=0.0714 four-way REFUTED; error concentrates 50x into 12 cells erring at 75%
description: Blind adjudication of all 402 cells complete. Unanimous stratum 5/338 err (1.48%, u95 2.37%); discordant stratum 10/64 (15.6%, u95 20.3%). B = 0.6934*0.0237 + 0.3066*0.2031 = 0.0787 > 0.06 pre-registered REFUTED band. Point estimate 0.0582 (CONDITIONAL) recorded but the pre-registration was on the bound. 79 pct of B comes from the 30.7 pct discordant slice, whose selector (five-way extractor disagreement) is already on disk and free. Actionable route: selective re-extraction of the discordant stratum only, leaving the LICENSED-on-its-own unanimous majority untouched. Delivered as M340.
notes: D339 CORRECTS the mechanism: discordant set is 96.8% positive (n=7369), UNK set 0.0% (n=14445), corpus 30.5%. discord_mask removed 7131 positive cells = 44.2% of all 16128 v2-positives -> its -0.0417 is a class-balance result, not a label-noise one. Column concentration EXCLUDED: all 12 columns fell. Damage tracks share of each column's positives masked, Pearson -0.65 (n=12): MCL 65.1%/-0.1058, Baker's 50.1%/-0.0845, PFOA 27.7%/-0.0116. Subtraction route still closed but on confident_span ALONE (-0.0116, 0.0% positive rate, a clean test). Hardness survives second-order only (contested cells 15.6% err vs 1.48% unanimous). Ledger corrected same day. Rule taken: state class composition of a subset before acting on it.

title: confident_span: does clearing UNK label values beat weak-believing them at 0.28?
description: Single-variable arm on the LABEL axis (owner's named blocker). band_span recipe verbatim with --labels confident.csv (UNK values cleared -> weight 0.0) vs control band_span=0.8565, eval ruler pinned to report_labels_v2.csv. Pre-registered: >=0.8627 reopens label content as a live lever; 0.8503-0.8627 bounds the effect of removing 27% of supervision under a floor; <=0.8503 means silence IS weak evidence of absence and --calibrated-targets (0.28->0.136) is the lever instead. D330 supports: uncertainty-type corruption is the realistic error shape and costs 0.03-0.09, while symmetric flips are catastrophic.
notes: PRICE: ~1.0 h of card (12 epochs at band_span step time, 12 slices). GAIN if real: the arm removes 27.3% of supervision (Synovitis 84.2% UNK, Fracture 56.4%, Baker's 45.9%, Lateral OA 33.1%) — a label-content effect of that size could plausibly carry 1-2% absolute, which is the bar. P(clears the +0.0062 floor) ~ 0.30. Justified at that probability because all three branches are informative: it is an INSTRUMENT on the label axis the owner named as the blocker, and the two non-clearing branches each name the next lever (bound the supervision effect, or push --calibrated-targets 0.28->0.136 the other way). Control band_span 0.8565 already on the ledger, so this costs one run not two.
close_reason: SWEEP phase 1 (completed but not properly marked): the arm named in this bead's own title has a .full.log in $MODELS/experiments/ AND a scored row in experiments/README.md. The work ran and the ledger priced it; the bead was never marked. Reversible - bd update --status open if a reading here is still owed.

title: Foreign-family verdicts are confounded with a ViT recipe
description: radiodino_corpus 0.8214, coatnet_hybrid 0.8259, ortho_slow_trunk 0.8265, mricore_corpus all land in one narrow 0.82-0.83 band under our standard recipe, and each was written down as a fact about the family. coatnet_hybrid.sh:115-116 runs CoAtNet-2 at --batch 1 --accumulate 6, 384 px, --slices 20 (per slot, so 120 slices) and --backbone-lr 1e-4 marked '# deliberate:' as swin_supervised's. The public 0.941 blend gives its CoAtNet leg outer weight 0.55 running 62 eval windows with SWA at a rate fitted for the architecture. A cluster of families landing in one band under one recipe is more likely a fact about the recipe than about the families. cnx_own_recipe (README:3584) already names the same shape for ConvNeXt. Not a claim the families are good - a claim the verdict is unsafe. Re-test wants its own recipe, ~60 slices not 120, and a fitted rate.

title: VRAM ceiling silently removed the cap on an over-card budget
description: capped() returned max(needed()*1.15, DEFAULT_SHARE*whole) which could exceed the card (32.5 GB asked of a 31.84 GB card). select() does set_per_process_memory_fraction(min(budget/whole,1.0)), so an over-card ceiling clamps to 1.0 and removes the cap entirely; Windows answers the over-commit with WDDM sysmem fallback (paging VRAM over PCIe) instead of raising, which is the PC-freeze the owner reported. Measured live on hold_clean_distill_s2026: reserve grew 38.62->51.00 GB while allocation FELL 23.96->21.93, epoch time 1594->2681 s. Fixed in d212242d with DESKTOP_RESERVE_GB=2.0 and min(asked, whole-reserve). Verified after relaunch: 'VRAM capped at 29.8 GB of 31.8 GB', epoch 4 = 310 s, 26.24 GB reserved / 21.17 allocated. 8.6x faster. Bead is the record; fix is already in.

title: calib_hold_clean_distill ran UNCAPPED: 51 GB reserved on a 32 GB card, no --vram-gb
description: pid 58012 argv: --fold 0 --one-cycle --weight-floor --rank-weight 1.0 --epochs 12 --slice-pooling max --whole-stack --recompute-activations --backbone-lr 4e-5 --slices 20 --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9 --calibrated-targets --hold-annotations --distill-weight 0.7 --teacher-targets ... There is no --vram-gb anywhere in it. device_budget.py's capped() docstring states every accepted arm names --vram-gb (20, 26 or 28 of 31.8) and that uncapped 'was never what a measured run did'. This one is uncapped and its log confirms the consequence: 'peak memory 51.00 GB reserved, 21.51 GB allocated', 152-215 W of 575 at 100 percent utilisation, epoch 10 in 4386s, img/s swinging 58-211. Windows pages GPU memory over PCIe rather than raising OOM, so it did not fail, it crawled, and it froze the desktop when a second job joined it. Not killed: it is at epoch 11 of 12 and reads holdout 0.8635, above labelwise_dense 0.8613. Two fixes owed: (1) RECIPE in experiments/recipe.sh:23 does not carry --vram-gb so every arm that forgets it runs uncapped -- put a cap in RECIPE or make train.py refuse a run that names none; (2) note that the 51 GB reserve is for a recipe DeviceBudget prices at 28.25 (20sl, batch 12), so the distill teacher path is unpriced by the model and the 24-slice estimate of 28.03 at batch 10 may understate too. Smoke before trusting it.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THIS BEAD SAID. Fixed in d212242d.

The symptom was real; the diagnosis and BOTH proposed fixes were wrong.

WRONG (1): 'every arm that forgets --vram-gb runs uncapped'. It does not. capped() returns
max(needed()*CAP_HEADROOM, DEFAULT_SHARE*whole) when vram_gb is 0, so silence gets a derived cap.
The docstring at device_budget.py:353 argues an arm SHOULD stop naming a number -- a hand cap is a
third statement of the same fact and goes stale (13 arms already overstate by 1-12 GB). So putting
a cap in RECIPE would have been a regression, and hold_clean_distill.sh naming none is correct.

WRONG (2): 'the 51 GB reserve is for a recipe DeviceBudget prices at 28.25, so the distill teacher
path is unpriced'. The cost model is FINE. It predicts ALLOCATION and the run ALLOCATED 21.51-23.96
GB, UNDER the 28.26 prediction. Nothing about distillation is mispriced. This matters downstream:
it was the stated reason to distrust the 24sl/b10 estimate of 28.03, and that caveat is now lifted.

ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE: a ceiling above the card is not a ceiling. 20sl at batch 12 derives 28.26 GB,
CAP_HEADROOM lifts it to 32.5, and the card is 31.84. select() applies
set_per_process_memory_fraction(min(budget/whole, 1.0)) -- so an over-card budget does not widen the
cap, it clamps the fraction to 1.0 and REMOVES it. The log states it plainly and nobody read it:
'VRAM capped at 32.5 GB of 31.8 GB'. Unbounded, the caching allocator then reserved 38.62 GB against
23.96 allocated (51 GB on the earlier arm) -- the 14.7 GB gap is allocator slack, not need -- and
Windows answers an over-commit through WDDM sysmem fallback rather than raising. That is the desktop
freeze, and it is the same mechanism as the three nvlddmkm resets select() has documented since
2026-08-17. The class already states the preference (immediate OOM over a silent PCIe crawl); it was
simply not implemented, since the only guard covered free < floor().

FIX: DESKTOP_RESERVE_GB = 2.0, and capped() returns min(asked, whole - DESKTOP_RESERVE_GB). Applies
to a hand-named --vram-gb too: a typed number over the card is a typo, not a measurement. 2.0 is read
off this card (the arm logged '30.3 GB free of 31.8' with the full desktop up, so desktop plus driver
context hold ~1.5 GB). Costs no recipe, because allocation was always under the prediction.

title: Our label table is the worst of five independent extractions, and the offline ruler cannot see it
description: gold57 cell disagreement at midpoint: flight0234 v4hybrid 0.1813, lixin73 gpt56sol 0.1813, steven v4_blend 0.1827, steven full 0.1988, OURS report_labels_v2 0.2047. Paired study-clustered bootstrap 20000 resamples, 57 studies: ours - majority = +0.0219, 95% CI [+0.0044,+0.0395]. Error is one-sided: FP 108 vs FN 32, a 3.4:1 over-call; Contusion precision 16/36=0.44. experiments/lib.sh:72 puts 286 arm invocations on the losing table. NOT circular like report_labels_v3, which was fitted on these 58 and is v2 RE-CUT (dropping the 0.68 rung reproduces its 0.1696). Seven foreign tables pasted gold (exactly 0.0000) and are excluded. THE BLOCKER: our 909-study holdout labels derive from v2, so a member trained on a truer table reads worse by construction; gold@58 cannot resolve +/-0.012 (oof_band_folds). The board is the only independent ruler. Arm experiments/arms/foreign_labels_dense.sh is written and smoked. PRICE: one arm at band_dense step time, 12 epochs, no new cache (labels are not in the cache key); plus one board slot to read it. P(clears 0.005 on macro) ~0.20 offline, but offline is the rigged ruler - the board read is the deliverable.

title: Input-axis ablations were all read on a max-pooling head that suppresses real input changes
description: Matched 2x2 (M325, experiments/README.md 2026-09-11): --scheme extended reads -0.0059 under --slice-pooling max and +0.0010 under labelwise, interaction +0.0069. Per-column MCL +0.0278 and Lateral Meniscus +0.0205 under labelwise, exactly the findings COR_FLUID_NOFS is primary-plane for; -0.0150 / -0.0004 under max. So a real input change reads NEGATIVE through the max head. Consequence: extended_slots (+0.0002), resolution_420, multiscale and knee-ezz (20 slices, -0.0001) were all measured on max pooling and are downgraded REFUTED -> UNREAD. Re-open one axis at a time under --slice-pooling labelwise, each priced against its own labelwise control, never against a max number. Also refutes D184's headline: AX_T1 was called PF OA's only proper read and PF OA is -0.0141 / -0.0060. PRICE: multiscale-under-labelwise is the cheapest next test; cost is the 12-slot decode (must run alone), not the ~1h train. P(clears 0.005 on macro) ~0.25, but the per-column mechanism is already above floor.

title: submit_check's licence gate is keyed on a hand-typed roster tag, so an untagged merged member ships clean
description:
PRICE: about 1 hour, no card, no slot. P(clears the bar) n/a -- it guards a WIN, not a score. The thing it protects against costs the competition, not 0.001.

submit_check.py:110 refuses a member whose roster line carries a '# licence: <table>' comment, before the repeat question and not openable by --anyway. The refusal itself is right. What is fragile is where it gets its facts: MemberRoster.licence_refusals (package_members.py:111-124) parses the tag out of the line's own comment, so the gate knows only what a human typed.

Consequence: a member trained tomorrow on --scheme mergedf or merged3 lands on the roster untagged and passes every gate. This is structurally the SAME defect roster_check was built for -- nothing writes comp/members.roster, it is hand-edited, and on 2026-08-29 five of a sixteen-seat entry's best seats were simply not on it because nobody remembered.

THE FIX IS TO ASK THE CHECKPOINT, NOT THE COMMENT. A member's training corpus is recorded in its own recipe (the same place trajectory_check and the tissue224 row read flags like scheme, centre and image_size from), so the licence tag can be DERIVED: resolve each named member to its checkpoint, read the scheme its recipe was fitted under, and refuse any scheme that is not our own. The roster comment then becomes documentation instead of load-bearing state, which is the correct direction for a file nothing writes.

Keep the comment path as well, for members whose checkpoint is gone -- roster_check already names three such (intensity392_ws_s2026, res392_ws_s2026, tissue224_s2026) -- and make a member whose scheme cannot be determined read UNKNOWN and exit 2, never 0, exactly as submit_check already does for a kernel that names no members. 'I did not look' must not read like 'it is clean'.

Blocks nothing today: the roster is currently clean, all seven merged members are tagged (swept 2026-09-11, see knee-lsqnm). This is about the next one.

title: Foreign labelled corpora cannot ship weights — the DATA axis is closed for anything that enters a kernel
description:
PRICE: 0 hours of card, and it REMOVES a planned spend of roughly 12. P(clears the bar) n/a — this is a constraint, not an experiment. What it is worth is the arms it stops.

FINDING, from the researcher's 2026-09-11 licence survey, every licence read as primary text with the operative clause quoted. NO knee-MRI corpus carrying labels that overlap our 12 findings permits shipping trained weights. OAI is a research/education DUA with no redistribution, and everything OAI-derived inherits it. SKM-TEA carries an explicit no-derivative-works clause, the strongest in the survey. K2S is CC BY-NC-ND. Rijeka is CC BY-NC-ND confirmed on Zenodo. MRNet and fastMRI are both research-use. The only MSK-MRI corpus that permits redistributing derivatives is TCIA Soft-tissue-Sarcoma, 51 subjects, CC BY 3.0, with ZERO overlap with our findings.

THE CONSEQUENCE THE SURVEY DID NOT HAVE TO SPELL OUT, and the reason this is P1. If WEIGHTS are the blocked artefact then a self-supervised continuation trunk is blocked for the same reason as a supervised one. So the researcher's own recommendation -- continued SSL on fastMRI images as the cheapest test of organ-specific continuation -- produces something that cannot be shipped. It remains valid as an INSTRUMENT and its price changes: a roughly 6-hour card arm whose product is a reading, never a member.

WHAT THIS CLOSES. The four-corpus merge priced at +0.020 offline / +0.031 board on beta=0.22 cannot produce a shippable member, so that price is not collectable. The fastMRI+ compartment work committed today (Medial and Lateral Meniscus from zero positives to 190 each) stands as a table repair and as offline instrument material, and is not a route to the board.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, and where the remaining size is. Our own 4,407 studies carry 24,371 acquired series. Feeding more of them as input SLOTS is measured and refuted (extended_slots, 6 to 9 slots, +1,139 coronal series, +0.0002). Treating each series as its own training SAMPLE with the study's label is a DIFFERENT mechanism and is untested; it does not price off beta, since beta was fit on distinct studies and the label count stays at 4,407. Asked as M324-Q1, with test-time adaptation on the unlabelled competition test set as M324-Q3.

ALSO CHECKED AND WRONG: report_labels_v2.csv has 37 columns, which is 12 targets times value/confidence/verdict plus the UID. There are no unused label columns in our own corpus. Recorded so nobody else goes looking.
notes: DUPLICATE of knee-lsqnm, which filed the same closure on 2026-09-10 and got there first with the primary text. Filed because I did not search the beads before writing, which is the exact inversion CLAUDE.md warns about. Closing into lsqnm; the two things this bead adds that lsqnm does not say are carried over there.

title: foreign_crosswalk: map fastMRI+ box annotations onto our 12 TARGETS under partial-label confidence
description:
PRICE: doubling the corpus prices at +0.0201 offline / +0.031 board at beta=0.22 (three-point curve, experiments/README.md CORRECTION 2026-09-11). fastMRI+ is 974 studies = +22% corpus, and box+slice level so supervision is STRONGER than our study-level report labels. P(clears 1.5% bar) ~ 0.25 alone, higher once the other foreign corpora join on the same table. OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-11: 'i think maybe the blocker is actually more likely labels. and this should be worked on. and we shouldnt drop data because of it'.

MECHANISM, AND WHY NO TRAINING CODE CHANGES. The partial-label machinery already exists and is in daily use: grades.py:36 carries weights per study PER LABEL, trainer.py:634 computes elementwise*weights normalised by weights.sum(dim=1), and objective.py:429 already uses weights>0 as the idiom for 'this column is live'. A foreign study is a row whose unknown columns carry __conf=0. Nothing in the loss changes.

DESIGN DECIDED OFF MEASUREMENT (scratchpad/fmp_probe.py):
- meniscus laterality: box centre-x is BIMODAL, peaks ~90 and ~235, deep trough 145-185. But which cluster is medial depends on knee SIDE, which fastMRI+ does not give and which is near-symmetric across the corpus. So supervise only the unambiguous: boxes in BOTH clusters => both Medial and Lateral positive (208 studies); NO meniscus box => both negative (311); one cluster only => MASKED (455). Asked researcher (M323) whether side is recoverable from the HDF5/ISMRMRD header; if yes the 455 unlock.
- Effusion prevalence gap 4x (fastMRI+ 0.146 vs ours 0.605) while ACL/MCL agree closely. Mechanism: box annotator threshold is stricter than report reader. Encoding is ASYMMETRIC CONFIDENCE — a foreign POSITIVE is full weight, a foreign NEGATIVE is scaled by the per-column prevalence ratio. Never raw substitution.
- __conf=0 (NOT the 0.25 floor) wherever a corpus is silent: a corpus that never READ for a finding is not a radiologist who read and did not mention it (targets.py CONFIDENCE_FLOOR doctrine).
- Baker's <- Periarticular cysts is a PROXY, not an identity; reduced confidence, flagged in the module.
- Contusion and Fracture arrive MERGED as one fastMRI+ category; both columns get the same value at reduced confidence rather than an invented split.
- Synovitis: no fastMRI+ category. __conf=0.

Licence: fastMRI+ ANNOTATIONS are MIT (Microsoft). The PIXELS are NYU internal-research-only and that is a separate open question — the table commits cleanly either way, and is the reusable half.
notes:
SUPERSEDED BY THE AUDIT, and closed into knee-1w6t's territory. The crosswalk this bead proposed building under core/data/labels/ ALREADY EXISTS as core/data/corpus/fastmri_corpus.py, with a better-argued encoding than the one proposed here (Reading.coarse blocks the negative rather than asserting a positive, which is exactly the distinction the proposal was going to have to invent). Writing it would have rebuilt, worse, what was already there.

WHAT SURVIVED THE AUDIT AND SHIPPED. One measurement defeated one of that module's arguments. Reading.coarse blocks Meniscus Tear because 'Meniscus Tear carries no side'. Measured 2026-09-11: every one of the 973 train exams is CORPD_FBK or CORPDFS_FBK -- CORONAL, read off the acquisition attribute of all 973 and confirmed by protocolName COR in the ISMRMRD header -- so image x IS the medial-lateral axis, and the 5,658 meniscus box centres are bimodal with a trough at 165.0 of 320 (argmin of a 32-bin histogram between 100 and 220; the MEDIAN 196.5 lies inside the upper cluster and would have cut it in half).

The rule shipped is SIDE-INVARIANT and therefore needs no laterality, which is fortunate because fastMRI states none (no laterality in the ISMRMRD header, no side column in the file list, a knee coil that is the same coil either way): a term boxed in BOTH compartments is present in this column whichever compartment this column turns out to be. Medial Meniscus and Lateral Meniscus go from ZERO positives to 190 each. The corpus now has three positive columns (ACL 101, Effusion 142, Meniscus 190+190) instead of two.

WHAT THE SAME MEASUREMENT REFUSED, stated so nobody re-proposes it: the cartilage pair straddles on 15 studies and bone injury on 24, which is the n=4 MCL number one decimal place up, so neither is compartmental. Contusion/Fracture is a KIND merge, not a LOCATION merge, and no geometry can touch it. PF OA is in no COMPARTMENT_PAIRS pair and has no contralateral half to straddle.

PRICE, HONESTLY. 190 studies x 2 columns is +380 positive cells on two of twelve columns, about +11% of the meniscus supervision. At beta=0.22 that is roughly +0.003 on those two columns and well under +0.001 overall -- DIRECTIONAL, below the bar, and not a reason to spend a slot on its own. It matters as one corpus of four in the merge the owner asked for, and as the repair of a table that shipped six columns holding not one positive between them.

Written to fastmri_findings_compartment.csv, NOT over fastmri_findings.csv: build_fastmri's own --labels-out doc requires it, because the members on disk were fitted against the default name.

title: A member refit on 100% of the corpus cannot be priced, selected or witnessed by any gate we own
description:
Raised 2026-09-11 off D312. If Nixon's result carries here, the operation is refitting existing recipes on all 4407 studies. The training is not the blocker - the HARNESS is.

A full-data member has no holdout, and every gate assumes an out-of-sample record: roster_check wants a .holdout.npz; the ledger refuses an in-sample offline (raptor_solo voided 2026-08-29 at 98.6% in-sample); board_check will not price a row without one; witness_check needs reproducible predictions. Worse at the ensemble level: if every member is full-data, nothing can fit seat weights or even RANK candidate seatings offline - the SELECTION step dies before the pricing step.

Candidate answers, none measured here: (a) carve a permanent selection set nobody trains on, which costs that data from every member forever; (b) keep a fold-fit TWIN of each refit member and use the twin's OOF as the stand-in ranking signal - cheap, but nobody has measured whether a twin's OOF ranks its refit sibling correctly; (c) report the CV number for the refit model and accept the bias, which is what ESL 7.10 does without an error estimate.

M316 asks the researcher for the literature on all three plus the sign of the CV bias for a refit model (Bates/Hastie/Tibshirani arXiv:2104.00673 says CV estimates the wrong quantity - we need to know whether that changes the SIGN or only the interpretation). BLOCKS the 100%-refit axis; do not queue a refit arm before this has an answer, or the card buys a member no gate will accept.
notes:
POWER CORRECTION 2026-09-11 05:52Z, to the note above, before any card was spent on it.

The note above reads the matched board pair (lastseat_v1 0.937 -> dark7_v1 0.937, the one fold-fit ->
refit twin swap on the board) as Delta 0.000 and concludes refit alone is <= 0.000. That bound does not
hold. The swap moves ONE SEAT OF SEVEN, so a member-level effect arrives at the ensemble output diluted
roughly 7x against a board that resolves ~0.005. The test had no power to see the effect it was asked
about.

What replaced it, same morning, card-free: the three-point learning curve was already on disk and had
never been fitted. quarter_data_s2026 (874 studies, 0.7907), half_data_s2026 (1,749, 0.8344),
band_dense_s2026 (3,498, 0.8578) are matched on everything but train_fraction. Fitting error ~ N^-beta
gives beta(874->1749) = 0.338 and beta(1749->3498) = 0.220. Declining, not zero. At beta = 0.22 a 1.26x
refit (3,498 -> 4,407) predicts +0.0070 offline for the MEMBER, i.e. ~+0.001 at the ensemble - well under
what that pair could resolve. Delta 0.000 is CONSISTENT with the curve, not evidence against it.

So: refit is unpriceable but shippable (unchanged, 28 refits shipped, champion built out of them), the
matched-pair route is real but far too blunt at one seat in seven, and the axis stays OPEN with nothing
on the bench having earned an arm on it (clean_calib's own +0.008 branch missed at +0.0015;
foreign_distill_mix07_s2026 declined on licence). Full working: experiments/README.md, section headed
"CORRECTION, same morning: the corpus is NOT saturated".

title: Member error correlation vs pairwise training-set overlap - the curve nobody has published, and ours is a CPU read
description:
D312 (2026-09-11) confirms this measurement exists NOWHERE in the literature in any regime. Nixon/Lakshminarayanan/Tran (NeurIPS 2020 ICBINB) swept unique-training-point fraction per member 63.2% to 100% and reported accuracy and ECE only - never pairwise member correlation. So the curve that would tell us whether a held-out fifth buys diversity is unmeasured everywhere, and our pool can produce it with NO CARD.

WHAT: for every pair of fold-fit members on disk, plot error correlation on the shared holdout rows against the exact overlap of their training sets (known from fold assignment: two members on the same fold overlap 100%, on different folds 75%). Each member already has a .holdout.npz.

WHY IT DECIDES SOMETHING: Nixon plus Fort et al. (arXiv:1912.02757) say data partitioning contributes no diversity and random init supplies it all. If our curve is FLAT in overlap, the held-out fifth buys nothing here either and refitting the pool on 100% of the data is free - which is the operation the owner has asked for repeatedly (use more data) and the project has never run. If the curve SLOPES, the trade is real on our corpus and CIFAR does not transfer.

PRICE: 0 h of card, 0 slots, CPU only. P(clears 1.5% alone) = 0 - it is an INSTRUMENT, not a member. It licenses or kills a whole retrain axis, which is what an instrument is for.

CAUTION: this is a POOL statistic, so it carries STATISTIC, POPULATION and CUT per knee-f9aao - write corr@<pool>, never a bare corr, and midpoint unless said otherwise.

AUDITED 2026-09-11 00:35Z, BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN, AND THE 'NO CARD' PREMISE IS WRONG. The curve
cannot be read off disk, and the reason is structural rather than a gap in what we happened to save.

Measured over all 357 *.holdout.npz on disk: they hold exactly 12 distinct study sets. 309 members share
one 909-study set (fold 0's holdout), so every pair among them has 100% TRAINING overlap - one level of
the axis, 309 members deep. The fold twins are the only members at any other level: oof_fold0..4 hold
out five sets whose pairwise intersection is EXACTLY 0 and whose union is 4407, the whole corpus. Two
members that held out different folds train on 4 of 5 folds each and share 3, so their training overlap
is 75% - the second level - and they have NO evaluation row in common, by construction, because
k-fold's holdouts are disjoint.

So the observable overlap axis has two levels, 100% and 75%, and the 75% level is unmeasurable from
predictions: a pair at that level is never both out-of-sample anywhere. That is almost certainly why the
curve is absent from the literature - it is not an oversight, k-fold cannot produce it.

WHAT THE EXPERIMENT ACTUALLY COSTS. To vary overlap continuously AND keep a shared out-of-sample set,
members must be fit on RANDOM subsets rather than fold complements: draw K members at ~80% of the corpus
with independent random subsets, and any two share ~64% of their training data while their held-out
remainders intersect in ~4% of the corpus - which is the common evaluation set, and it is small. Nixon
et al. sampled exactly this way. Cost is K fits of card, not zero, and the shared-row count is what
decides K: at n=4407 and 20% held out per member, a pair shares ~176 rows, so a correlation read on one
pair is noisy and the curve needs many pairs rather than many rows.

STATUS: not runnable as scoped. Either re-scope to the random-subset arm above with its card price
stated, or close it as structurally unreadable on our fold design. Do NOT queue the read.
close_reason:
Structurally unreadable as scoped, and the audit in its own description is the finding. The overlap axis has exactly two observable levels off 357 *.holdout.npz: 100% (309 members sharing fold 0's 909-study holdout) and 75% (the oof fold twins). The 75% level cannot be read from predictions at all - two members that held out different folds share NO evaluation row, by construction, because k-fold holdouts are disjoint. That is almost certainly why the curve is absent from the literature rather than an oversight.

The decision it was raised to make - does a held-out fifth buy diversity, i.e. is refitting the pool on 100% free - has since been answered from a different direction and does not need this curve. See knee-xi3y3 notes 2026-09-11: the matched board pair lastseat_v1 0.937 -> dark7_v1 0.937 (n=7, sole swap small_batch6_s2026 -> small_batch6_ff) reads delta board 0.000 for a fold-fit -> 100%-refit swap, with an EMA confound that can only push the refit-alone figure lower. Refitting on the same 4407 studies is priced at approximately zero on our own board, which is the same answer Nixon/Fort predict and the same order as the ledger's N^-beta argument.

Re-open only with a design that MANUFACTURES the missing level - members trained on random subsets against one common permanently-held eval set - which costs card per member and is the (a) branch of knee-xi3y3, not a card-free read.

title: queue_check is blind to every bespoke watcher, and reads OK over a live queue
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 22:45Z. `queue_check` printed 'no watcher logs under logs' then 'OK: nothing is queued' while `after_fastmri.sh` (pid 62452, confirmed in the process table) was live and owed `ortho_fastmri_masked`, ~1.6 h of card. That is precisely the failure the check exists to catch, reported green.

BOTH detection paths are opt-in and a bespoke watcher opts out of both silently:
- `Watch.of` (queue_check.py:97) returns None unless the log's FIRST LINE contains the header `before running: `, which only `experiments/after.sh:47` echoes. A bespoke watcher that prints nothing until its gate opens has an empty log and is not a watch.
- `_invokes` (queue_check.py:157) tests the process line against `WATCHER = 'after.sh'` (:59) as a substring. `experiments/after_fastmri.sh` does not contain it, so `watchers()` returns nothing, so `unlogged()` — the rule written for exactly this case — cannot fire either.

SCOPE IS WIDER THAN ONE WATCHER: `head -1` over every `logs/after_*.log` on disk finds NO file carrying the header. Every watcher this project has armed recently is bespoke, so queue_check has been reporting on an empty set the whole time, and 'OK: nothing is queued' has meant 'I found no file I recognise' rather than 'the card is not owed anything'.

DONE: `after_fastmri.sh` now echoes the header verbatim before its loop (commit follows). That fixes one watcher and not the class.
PROPOSED: (1) `WATCHER` becomes a match on `after*.sh` rather than the literal `after.sh`, so `_invokes` sees bespoke chains and `unlogged()` can fire; (2) an empty-or-headerless `logs/after_*.log` whose name matches a live process REPORTS rather than being dropped — a file that exists and does not parse is a finding, not an absence; (3) the 'no watcher logs' line must not be followed by 'OK', since not looking is not the same as nothing being there. Guard (3) with a test that arms a bespoke watcher and asserts a non-zero exit.
notes: FIXED 2026-09-11 in dece77f1 with a live reproducer: a bespoke after_*.sh was never a watcher (WATCHER matched by suffix), and its log has no chain header, so both eyes were shut on the same queue. bespoke()/duplicated() now read the process side alone; lines() cannot say OK over a live bespoke watcher.
