title: arm_needs_mib overprices small recipes and underprices the one that thrashed
description:
The VRAM cost model (kneemri.experiments.vram_need, consumed by arm_needs_mib in experiments/lib.sh:286) does not predict this card's actual usage in either direction.

UNDERPRICE, which cost the run: mae_unitfix at 336px/20sl was let onto the card and reported '51 MiB free' from its FIRST step (heartbeat baseline in mae_unitfix_s2026.full.log). Actual steady state 32024 MiB of 32607. It survived epoch 0 at 510 img/s; epoch 0's holdout eval allocated on top, WDDM began paging over PCIe, and throughput collapsed to 57 img/s permanently. Epoch 1 took 5938s against epoch 0's 1314s -- 12 epochs projected ~20h against a priced 5.7h, freezing the machine throughout. Killed 2026-09-10T16:45Z.

OVERPRICE, which would deny a healthy arm: ortho_fresh_lowlr at 224px/12sl printed 'gate: this recipe reserves 32706 MiB' -- MORE than the card physically has (32607). It started only because wait_for_free_card saw no compute tenant and correctly fell through to 'the shortfall is the display driver'. Measured actual footprint after warmup: 14617 MiB. The model is off by 18 GB on this recipe.

So the gate is not conservative-but-safe; it is uncorrelated with the truth on both sides. A model that prices a 14.6 GB recipe at 32.7 GB and a 32.0 GB recipe under the card is not measuring the thing that matters.

NOT a --vram-gb fix. wait_for_free_card:339 already records why: it caps our allocator rather than the device, and set above what the card can spare it PERMITS the thrashing it was meant to prevent.

Fix direction: the eval-time peak is the number that matters and the model appears to price the TRAIN step only -- the collapse began at the first holdout eval in both the first and second mae_unitfix attempts. Calibrate against measured torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated across recipes already on disk before changing the formula.

title: card_check skipped: witness_check --device auto walked 139 members beside a live arm and froze the box
description: VRAM was 31577/32607 MiB (96.8%) with mae_unitfix live. Launching witness_check --device auto (139 members) as a submission pre-flight made WDDM evict VRAM over PCIe and stalled the whole machine; owner reported the freeze. System RAM was fine (28G free of 95G, pagefile 3.6G of 69G) so this is a VRAM-headroom failure, not a memory one. Two fixes: (1) card_check is already mandatory before any GPU op and was skipped here; (2) witness_check as a SUBMISSION pre-flight should default to the entry's own members, not the whole pool - the 139-member sweep is a maintenance job, not a pre-flight. Scoped run (--members <one> --batch 2) completed in seconds with no thrash.

title: the 0.0062 floor is a 909-study three-seed paired bar and has been quoted onto the 58-study gold ruler
description:
D295 §5. Every letter in the archive uses 0.0062 as this project's three-seed paired holdout floor over 909 studies. knee-8wa0 applied it to a 58-study gold read: 'GOLD 0.9037 vs holdannot 0.8932 = +0.0105 (above the 0.0062 floor)'. Different denominator by a factor of 15.7 in studies.

What the gold ruler actually resolves, measured (D295 §5): study bootstrap of a macro gold AUC at n=58 gives sd 0.0178; jackknife SE 0.0183; the PAIRED difference sd at the measured arm-to-arm correlation of 0.84 is 0.0101. So +0.0105 is about ONE standard deviation of its own instrument.

This is the denominator error the project rule names, on the axis that currently decides label-side arms. Consequences: knee-8wa0's +0.0105 is not a result at the bar it was read against; reader_through.sh's original +/-0.005 gold branches were written at half a sd and have been corrected in-place mid-run.

WANTED: a stated, derived bar for the gold ruler (paired 2-sd ~0.020 is the obvious candidate) written where arms will find it, and a sweep of headers/letters quoting 0.0062 against an n=58 read.

title: The report corpus is multilingual and no per-language label error rate has ever been measured
description: raw/train.csv ships a Report column of free text (mean 1097 chars, zero nulls) and its finding columns are EMPTY, so every label file this project owns is an extraction and there is no official table. Marker-token census, crude: en 2019 (45.8%), unclassified 1205 (27.3%), es 683 (15.5%), de 250 (5.7%), nl 169 (3.8%), fr 81 (1.8%), total 4407. Only the total is exact. One extraction ran over all of it, so label noise is likely stratified by language - the same shape as the age-stratified labeler error in D292 section 1, and part of why its symmetric 40% synthetic-noise evidence does not transfer to us. Checkable with no card: per-language member error rates over the 339 holdout npz. Also demotes the Impression-vs-Findings idea (D292 rank 3), which needs a per-language section grammar rather than a split on a literal token - M295 over-claimed that from one Spanish row and M296 retracts it.

title: RecordMix.narrow() cannot narrow a pool with disagreeing folds - it calls shared() mid-narrow
description: narrow() promises 'keep the LARGEST agreeing pool'. It cannot deliver that when the handed pool contains members from different FOLDS. _on_widest_split filters on each member's OWN study count, never on the intersection it causes, so five cross-fold oof_fold* members (each holding out a full-width split, just a different one) survive it. _largest_ruler_group then calls self.shared() at record_mix.py:259, which refuses on the empty intersection: 'no study is held out by all 228 members - different folds or splits'. So --largest-pool raises the exact error it exists to avoid. Hit 2026-09-10 by kneemri/evaluation/diversity_slope.py globbing all 228 seed-2026 records; worked around by grepping out ^oof_ from the arm list, which is a name-shaped workaround for a split-shaped problem and will miss the next cross-fold member that is not spelled oof_. The fix is a split-grouping pass BEFORE the ruler-grouping pass: group members by their held-out study SET, keep the largest group, then narrow the ruler inside it. record_mix's own --largest-pool carries the same defect and has not hit it only because its previous globs happened to agree on the split.

title: rank_stability: the ordering resolves at the top only, and the cut re-draws it (tau +0.6667)
description: python -m kneemri.evaluation.rank_stability resamples the 909 holdout studies and re-derives the ORDER of several arms (D281 s3(1), Maier-Hein Nat Commun 2018). Landed c5a0585c with mirror tests. Findings: (1) seat_clean_distill holds rank 1 in 96.8% of 500 resamples -- the top IS resolved; ranks 4-9 span 0.0020 with mean ranks 5.44-7.99 -- the middle is NOT, so every keep/kill inside 0.8545-0.8565 was a coin flip. (2) D281 s1.1 null: all 13 arms average over 12 of 12 columns, no denominator gap vs the board. (3) Kendall tau midpoint vs ledger75 = +0.6667 -- the cut REORDERS, calib_span 9->2 and first in 38.6% of resamples vs seat_clean_distill 38.4%. FOLLOW-UP: decide whether the project's default ruler moves to ledger75 (D27: 5 board inversions vs the midpoint's 21 over ~530 pairs), and fix the calib_span roster line which reads NEGATIVE at this operating point under the ruler now known to be the worse board predictor.

title: Separate apparent object SCALE from field CONTENT: the only explanation left for crop160_span's +0.009
description:
D269 (c) (ledger 2026-09-09) refuted the extent explanation for crop160_span's +0.0087 pooled transfer advantage over band_dense_hold: split at four cuts (130/140/150/160 mm) the advantage is flat at ~+0.009 on filled and padded studies alike, with a sign reversal at the 140 mm cut. The extra anatomy is not what pays.

What travels with a bigger nominal crop and is NOT the anatomy in it: both members resample to the SAME 336 px grid, so the 160 mm member sees the joint at 336*130/160 = 273 px equivalent -- a coarser effective in-plane resolution, occupying a smaller fraction of the frame, through a different interpolation. That is the only explanation still standing.

THE ARM: a 130 mm crop trained at image-size 272 (matching the 160 mm member's effective joint resolution while adding NO field). If it recovers the +0.009 on the same foreign readout, the mechanism is SCALE and the whole extent family is a resolution result wearing a geometry name. If it does not, scale is out too and the advantage is unexplained.

It is cheaper than its control, not dearer -- 272 px against 336. Check first whether --image-size resizes from the existing 130 mm cache or needs a new one built; the answer decides whether this is a 1 h arm or a cache build plus an arm.

M279 has gone to the researcher asking whether object-scale vs field-content has been separated in medical-image transfer, and whether a frozen trunk transfers better when the object is SMALLER in frame because that is closer to its pretraining scale statistics.
notes:
CLOSED WITHOUT RUNNING, 20 minutes after filing, against the arm's own header. crop160_span.sh:54 reads '--image-size 420' under a '# deliberate:' line saying 'carried by the flag above to hold mm/px, not an independent choice'. The wide member samples at 420/160 = 2.625 px/mm against band_dense_hold's 336/130 = 2.585 -- 1.5% apart. Apparent object scale and effective in-plane resolution were MATCHED BY DESIGN before the question was asked, so the arm this bead proposed would have measured a variable that does not differ between the two members.

The reading that stands: crop160_span's +0.0087 pooled transfer advantage is not extent (four-cut split flat at ~+0.009), not padding (the wide member tolls BETTER where it pads), and not scale (controlled by construction). It is not distinguishable from run-to-run scatter between two single runs on a readout with 0.02-0.03 intervals, and it should not be carried into another argument as a fact about geometry.

title: ortho_lora: does PEFT beat full fine-tuning on our largest trunk at 4.4k studies?
description:
D273 quotes Dutt et al. (arXiv:2305.08252): the full-FT/LoRA crossover on corpus size sits at ~3.8k images -- our scale -- below which LoRA wins by up to ~6% F1, and the gain GROWS with trunk size. Our own v3base pair points the other way (base_dense 0.8512 vs dinov3_base_lora 0.8268) but README:3040 flags it as confounded on adaptation AND geometry, and names the matched cell as never run. This arm is that cell at the capacity where Dutt predicts the largest effect: ortholarge + rank-8 adapters at ortho_dense's exact geometry, one variable.

PRICE: 1.6-1.8 h of card (ortho_dense measured 409 s/epoch, 1.36 h for 12; adapting 24 blocks keeps more activations).
GAIN AS A MEMBER: control 0.8452, seat bar 0.8521, so +0.007 needed. P(clears the seat bar) ~ 0.25. It would be an OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION architecture, the only seat type that has ever moved this board.
GAIN AS AN INSTRUMENT: prices the adaptation suspicion over all four large-trunk rows (ortho_dense 0.8452, ortho_stack 0.8417, v3large_dense 0.8258, v3large_stack 0.8277) the way band_deep_matched priced the depth suspicion over the foreign-trunk rows.

BRANCHES, pre-registered against control ortho_dense = 0.8452 with the 0.0062 paired floor:
ABOVE 0.8514 -- PEFT pays on a large trunk, Dutt transfers, the four rows are readings of OUR SCHEDULE and the family is owed a re-run under adapters.
0.8390-0.8514 -- neutral; the base pair becomes a statement about RANK, and D276's answer decides whether rank 16 follows or the axis closes.
BELOW 0.8390 -- PEFT loses on a large trunk too. The base pair's confound did not carry its delta, Dutt does not transfer to this endpoint, the adaptation lever closes on every trunk we own, and the large-trunk deficit is capacity or corpus rather than schedule.

KNOWN WEAKNESS, stated before it runs: rank 8 is a smaller relative subspace on a 1024-wide ViT-L than on base. An underfit reads exactly like a refutation. M276 asks the researcher for Dutt's own rank/alpha/injection sites; a rank-16 re-run is the follow-up and this row is its control.

The work ran and the ledger priced it; the bead was never marked. Reversible - bd update --status open if a reading here is still owed.

title: card_check passes 14s before a gated chain fires, so a manual launch lands a duplicate on the card
description:
2026-09-09 12:28:47Z card_check read OK (one job). after_carve.sh (pid 48428, armed 13:15 local) fired its control read at 12:29:01Z - fourteen seconds later. queue_check at the same instant reported 'no watcher' for it, because it greps logs/ for watcher LOGS and after_carve.sh writes none until its first arm produces output. On that pair of green readings a manual launch went out at 12:31:58Z and put a SECOND foreign_readout on the same card and the same corpus: 2x ~14.6 GB RSS, and the machine froze hard enough for the owner to notice and ask about it.

The failure is not that either check is wrong. card_check asks the DEVICE at an instant and cannot see a live shell that is about to launch; queue_check reads watcher logs and cannot see a watcher that has not written one yet. Between them sits a gap exactly as wide as the time from 'gate opens' to 'first byte of log'.

Fix candidates, cheapest first: (a) card_check also enumerates bash processes whose CommandLine names experiments/after_*.sh or experiments/arms/*.sh and reports them as PENDING - argv is only visible via Get-CimInstance, ps -W shows /usr/bin/bash for all of them; (b) after_carve-style watchers touch their log at ARM time, not at first output, so queue_check can see them; (c) both.

Cost of not fixing: the duplicate-on-card failure this file already records once (two member_curve scans, 25 minutes, one member's reading corrupted by contention). This is the second occurrence and the first to freeze the machine.

title: 52% of card time retrained a geometry already on disk; add a warm-start gate to arm_check
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-09 over 277 metrics.jsonl with per-epoch timing. Total recorded card time 307.6 h. Init breakdown: 245.3 h (223 runs) from a public encoder with a fresh head; 39.6 h (37) pre-schema, same thing; only ~21 h (13 runs) warm-started from one of OUR checkpoints; 1.0 h of LoRA in the whole project.

Fingerprinting each run on DATA+GEOMETRY (variant, image_size, slices, crop_mm, scheme, centre, band_low/high, spacing, tie, slot/slice pooling, through_plane, encoder_layer, whole_stack, labels, studies, train_fraction, fold, split_seed): 268 runs -> 128 distinct fingerprints. 140 runs retrained a geometry an earlier run had already trained, costing 161.1 h = 52% of all card time. Largest cluster is 41 runs / 53.6 h on ONE fingerprint, differing only in head/loss/optimiser (band_early, band_mid, calib_dense, certainty_ramp, band_lpft, ...). Next: 14 runs / 20.9 h.

Those clusters are where a warm start is valid -- identical pixels, only the objective moved. At 3-4 epochs from the cluster's first converged checkpoint instead of 12, ~2/3 of 161 h comes back: ~100 card-hours, about 4 days of 5090.

AGAINST MY OWN CASE: the other 146 h changed geometry or data upstream of the weights and IS a real retrain -- a checkpoint fitted at 130 mm crop is a bad init at 160 mm. And one_cycle anneals to zero, so a warm-started short arm needs its own schedule or convergence_check will correctly call its score a FLOOR. Recoverable is ~100 h of 307, not 250.

WORK: (a) a fingerprint function over the recipe's geometry+data fields, (b) arm_check reports, for each queued arm, the nearest already-trained fingerprint and whether it is IDENTICAL, (c) an identical fingerprint means the arm must either warm-start (--encoder-weights that checkpoint, own schedule) or carry a written reason, same shape as the roster decline rule. Nothing in the harness has ever asked this question: arm_check reads flags, card_check reads the device, ledger_check reads afterwards.
notes:
D267 (2026-09-09) answers M267 and it is an OBJECTION to part (c), not support: the 41-run cluster's within-cluster r is 0.8234@cluster75_pairs (2775 pairs), median 0.883, vs a seed floor of 0.9746 (n=2). The repeats bought MEASURED diversity, so a gate that DEMANDED a warm start would enforce collapsing the cheapest diversity the project owns.

Part (a) is DONE and shipped: kneemri/experiments/geometry_check.py, with GEOMETRY_KEYS, clusters() and twins(). Its docstring now carries D267.

Parts (b)/(c) are BLOCKED on one reading that needs no card at all, asked as M273: r(warm_calib_dense_s2026, calib_dense_hold_s2026) -- a warm-started member already on disk (solo 0.8562, seat 7 of the 16-seat entry, --encoder-weights encoders/calib_dense_hold.enc.pt) against its own parent (solo 0.8634), on D267's own axis and cut, plus its percentile in that 2775-pair distribution.
  r ~0.88 (cluster median) -> warm start preserves diversity; the ~100 h is live and the only remaining unknown is whether 3-4 epochs reaches the score, a ~20 min card arm.
  r ~0.97 (seat floor) -> warm start makes twins; the repeats were correct spending, ~0 h recoverable, and (c) is refuted before it is built.

Also noted while auditing: fitted_encoder.py already exports a supervised checkpoint to the .enc.pt format PretrainedEncoder reads, so the warm-start lane needs no new plumbing -- warm_calib_dense, warm_calib_lowlr and the recal_warm_* pair all already ride it.

title: arm_check executes any arm that reaches an interpreter without uv
description: arm_check's ArmInvocations._printed RUNS every arm file against a stub lib. The stub shadows `uv` only (arm_check.py:208-223, which states the rule: 'Check instead that nothing under arms/ reaches an interpreter without going through uv'). NOTHING ENFORCES THAT RULE. Eight arms call "$REPO/.venv/Scripts/python.exe" directly and are therefore EXECUTED by a lint: carve_adapt_read, depth_reserve, foreign_drop_pilot, foreign_drop_pool, foreign_oof, fovjitter160_read, merged3_tranche_one, ourtrunk44. Measured 2026-09-09: 'arm_check --only carve_adapt_read' put three foreign_readout processes (19.4 GB + 12.3 GB resident, --device cuda) on the card 16 s after it started, beside a live 12-epoch training arm, with no card_check consulted. Owner reported it as the PC slowing down. Two of the six pids SURVIVED the first Stop-Process and GREW before a second kill took them. Fix: assert in arm_check that no file under arms/ names an interpreter path, and route the eight through uv/run_train. knee-q4c3u closed this same class as 'no defect' once and was wrong.

title: Allocator fragmentation, not a co-tenant, is what thrashes an uncapped arm on this card
description:
fovjitter160 died twice in one morning at 42-206 img/s against its own peak of 944, with nvidia-smi reporting 100% utilisation and healthy clocks the whole time. Every gate was green; nothing but img/s could see it.

MECHANISM. Uncapped (vram_gb 0.0) the recipe RESERVES 31.29 GB of a 32.6 GB card while ALLOCATING only 22.41 -- 8.9 GB of allocator fragmentation slack held against the driver. That leaves ~1.3 GB free, so a ~1 GB co-tenant (a desktop window, 1197 MiB measured) is enough to tip Windows WDDM into paging GPU memory over PCIe instead of raising OOM. The co-tenant is the trigger; OUR OWN fragmentation is the cause.

FIX. --vram-gb 26. DeviceBudget.capped bounds RESERVATION while the derived fit predicts ALLOCATION, so 26 sits 3.6 GB above what the run actually allocates (cannot OOM it) and hands the driver back 6.6 GB. Held 862-914 img/s across the following epochs.

NOT THE FIX. PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True is a confirmed no-op here -- the log prints 'expandable_segments not supported on this platform'. An earlier clean relaunch was credited to it and was actually the fresh allocator.

RULE. Diagnose by img/s, never by utilisation. A paging GPU reports 100% busy.

The incident is written into experiments/arms/fovjitter160.sh above the source line. The open question is whether every uncapped arm on this card carries the same 8.9 GB of slack, i.e. whether --vram-gb should stop being per-arm and become a default.

title: LN-affine test-time adaptation on the serving path (CARVE cardinality-aware, episodic)
description:
D265 (researcher, 2026-09-09) returns the only published multi-label medical TTA number: CARVE arXiv:2607.15556 (Jul 2026) reports AUROC +0.034 to +0.036 absolute, episodic per-scan, Adam 1e-5, 2 steps, adapting LN affine gamma/beta only. That is lever-sized against a 0.010 board gap and it sits on our exact head type (per-label sigmoid, multi-label).

THE OBJECTIVE IS THE WHOLE RESULT, not a detail. Plain mean per-label Bernoulli entropy is UNPUBLISHED as a loss and is the form CARVE measures FAILING: accuracy 0.633 -> 0.605. Cross-label softmax entropy on a multi-label head provably suppresses co-occurring positives (ML-TTA Prop. 1). The published winner is CARVE Eq. 8-9: sharpen the top-khat labels, suppress the rest with lambda_neg 0.8, khat = clip(round(sum_j pbar_j), k_min, k_max) from batch prevalence.

RECIPE, tagged: LN affine only, normalization computation untouched (LN keeps no running stats). Scope all trunk LN except the last three blocks (SAR C.2) or except the first (MoETTA App. H); no paper adapts head norm or patch-embed norm. EPISODIC - snapshot affines at load, reset after every study. Adam lr 1e-5, 2 steps (CARVE 5.1) - do NOT transplant SAR's SGD 1e-3 at batch 64 into a batch-1 episodic regime. Never mix sites in one adaptation batch. Copy SAR's recovery guard: moving average of batch entropy 0.9, reset to source below e_0 = 0.2.

PLUMBING. Every serving loop here is no_grad-wrapped (holdout_predictions.py:114, study_reading.py:58, ensemble.py:460) and foreign_source.py:129 documents that lifting the decorator builds a graph and dies. So this is an ADAPT PASS before the existing no-grad forward - a strategy object, never a flag on the read. It changes the served function and may make it batch-composition-dependent, so witness_check is its gate.

CEILING, stated before the run: CARVE 5.2 measures depth/protocol shift costing -0.125 AUROC BEFORE adaptation and concludes adaptation is limited by the transferred representation. TTA tunes within what the trunk serves; it does not repair a pipeline mismatch.

UNMEASURED FOR US, in every direction (D265 silence list): no published TTA paper adapts DINOv2; every effect ships the source model raw while our head is calibrated; no TTA paper discusses 2D-slice batches of one 3D study.
notes:
2026-09-16 22:08Z — PRICED, which is what arm_check refuses this on (knee-qxse). Unblocking rather than re-filing.

PRICE: ~2.5 h, and almost none of it is card. The build is a serving-path strategy object (adapt pass before the existing no_grad forward, per the PLUMBING paragraph above), ~2 h of implementation with no GPU held. The reading is inference-only: one foreign_readout pass over an existing member, ~15 min of card. Compare against the ~3 h of card a training arm costs for a seat delta the board cannot certify — this is the cheapest lever-sized question left open.

P(clears +0.0040 on foreign_readout decode_cost vs the same member unadapted) ~ 0.35. CARVE reports +0.034 to +0.036 in its own setting, which is 8x the bar, so the discount is doing all the work and it is the bead's own silence list that justifies it: no published TTA paper adapts DINOv2; every published effect ships the source model RAW while our head is calibrated, and calibration is the most likely thing to have already absorbed the entropy the method minimises; and batch-1 episodic over 2D slices of one 3D study is unmeasured in either direction. Against those, the mechanism is a direct attack on the only gap we still have — the board is OOD to our holdout and every closed axis was closed IN-domain.

WHY IT IS RANKED FIRST NOW, stated against the alternatives rather than in the abstract. As of tonight every training lever on the ranked shortlist is spent or refused: knee-rkegi closed (+0.0084 solo, +0.0018 seated, inside the blur), knee-8c8up refused on the repo's own matched pair (336 is +0.0049 solo / +0.0005 seated, not +0.01), knee-00zxt is mergedk's mechanism at a dose that prices +0.0016. The pool axis is closed in-domain and the corpus axis has no licensed corpus large enough. What is left is the serving path, and this is the only published, lever-sized method on it.

THE GATE IS OFFLINE AND COMES FIRST. foreign_readout prices a cross-site decode toll without a board slot, so no slot is spent until the offline number clears. witness_check is the shipping gate per the PLUMBING paragraph, because the served function becomes batch-composition-dependent.

2026-09-16 23:31Z — CLOSED, and closed by a reading taken 2026-09-09, seven days before this bead was ranked first and handed a card.

THE BEAD'S OWN GATE HAD ALREADY FIRED, NEGATIVE. The gate stated above is 'offline foreign_readout decode_cost vs the same member unadapted, bar +0.0040'. That is exactly the column carve_budget_sweep (knee-2sqyb) measured on 2026-09-09 against member fovjitter160_s2026, and it is written up at experiments/README.md:11858. Recomputed tonight from the artefacts on disk with LabelScores, reproducing the ledger to the fourth decimal:

  control (unadapted, fov_perstudy.npz)   kept 0.8545  decode_cost 0.0297
  lr 1e-3 x 2   (|dtheta| ~2e-3)          kept 0.8504  decode_cost 0.0309
  lr 1e-3 x 10  (|dtheta| ~1e-2)          kept 0.8091  decode_cost 0.0355
  lr 1e-2 x 2   (|dtheta| ~2e-2)          kept 0.7570  decode_cost 0.0360

Across a ten-thousand-fold range of displacement the decode cost moves 0.0063 and moves the WRONG WAY the whole distance, while kept falls 0.0975. Adapting the norm affines per study does not trade member quality for decode: it spends the member and buys nothing. There is no budget at which the cost turns, so 'the felt budgets were destructive, try smaller' is closed too — the first point is a 0.002% perturbation and already carries the sign.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. The toll is REPRESENTATION-BOUND with the model-side lever removed rather than untested: the affines are not where the missing information is. That is a verdict on CARVE-as-implemented-here (LN affine only, episodic, our DINOv2 trunk, our calibrated head) on the DECODE axis, not on test-time adaptation as a family, and not on whatever the paper's +0.034 actually lives in — M274 ask 2 is still unanswered and is the only thing that could re-open this.

WHY IT WAS RANKED FIRST ANYWAY, since that is the reusable part. The 2026-09-16 22:08Z pricing note above says 'the build is ~2 h of implementation with no GPU held' and 'the reading is one foreign_readout pass, ~15 min of card'. Both halves were already on disk: kneemri/inference/norm_adaptation.py is dated Sep 9 14:49 with the Eq. 9 loss and the episodic Protocol, foreign_readout.py:268 already constructs it behind --adapt, and the three carve_budget_*.npz sweeps are dated Sep 9 16:20-17:37. The price was written by reading the bead and not the ledger, which is the failure CLAUDE.md names in the 'Before filing a finding, READ THE LEDGER AND THE INTERPRETATIONS' rule, on the same shape as the two P0s of 2026-08-13. A bead is the work queue; it is not evidence about what has been measured, and a bead that is a week old is evidence about a week ago.

title: card_memory.free_mib raised TimeoutExpired and killed a live arm on a loaded box
description: `free_mib` promises in its own docstring that no caller may turn a missing tool into a failed run, and then broke that promise: subprocess.run(timeout=SMI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) RAISES rather than returning None. A loaded machine is exactly the condition this diagnostic runs in. Measured 2026-09-09: a 16-way subprocess fan-out from arm_check starved nvidia-smi past ten seconds, the trainer's VRAM heartbeat raised on TimeoutExpired, and fovjitter160 died at 'ARM FAILED fovjitter160 (trainer exit 1)' at epoch 7 of 12 — two hours of card lost inside a diagnostic that is ALLOWED to say nothing. FIXED same day: the call now catches (TimeoutExpired, OSError), logs a warning, returns None. Bead kept for the class: audit every other subprocess/timeout on a heartbeat path for the same escape.

title: mm-per-pixel (resolution) jitter is unmeasured everywhere and our pool is pinned at ~0.387 by construction
description:
D258 (researcher, 2026-09-09), sub-question (c). Our whole pool holds mm/px fixed by construction: --crop-mm and --image-size are chosen together to hold 130/336 = 0.387, and fovjitter160 holds 160/420 = 0.381 for exactly that reason. No member on disk has ever seen the sampling resolution vary.

Literature position:
- nnU-Net has run resolution jitter in EVERY training for years: SimulateLowResolutionTransform(scale=(0.5,1), p=0.25), a random downsample-then-upsample. Nobody ablates it.
- Curia-MAE (Saporta et al., arXiv:2608.05844, Aug 2026) formalises 'Random Spacing' — per-volume spacing sampled between native and (1,1,1)mm — motivated EXPLICITLY as cross-site robustness. The authors are honest that they have no ablation and claim no gain.
- NO published medical-imaging paper reports a measured cross-site transfer improvement from resolution jitter. Nearest adjacent is Chen 2020's fixed-resample ablation (not jitter), which cost RV Dice 0.783 -> 0.673 — resolution HANDLING matters for transfer; jittering it is unpriced.

So this is a sibling axis to extent, run by the de-facto standard recipe, and genuinely unmeasured by anyone. It has the same shape as the extent finding that produced fovjitter160: an axis our pool has zero variance on, therefore invisible to a solo offline ruler, therefore a candidate for the flat shared decode toll (-0.0336 mean, sd 0.0038 over 11 members).

Caveat D258 flags: the literature gives NO number to pre-register against — this would be a genuine first read. Nearest analogue for an expectation is Chen 2020's extent numbers.

Sequencing: this is downstream of fovjitter160 and of the padding bead. Do not queue it until the extent arm reads, because the two axes share the same border-fabrication confound (a downsample-then-upsample stays inside the frame, so this one may actually be CLEANER than extent jitter — worth checking, it could argue for running it first).

title: Ablate padding_mode on zoom-out: border replication is the one convention the literature avoids, and nobody has measured the alternative
description:
D258 (researcher, 2026-09-09) read the extent-augmentation literature against M262. Finding: every standard recipe AVOIDS the border problem rather than solving it — RandomResizedCrop crops inside the image so no border ever appears (MAE, DINO); nnU-Net oversamples its patch by the scale envelope so zoomed-out samples come from real tissue; Chen 2020 states 'random cropping after all other image augmentations, without black borders'. torchvision/MONAI pad constant/zeros, TorchIO pads with an Otsu background estimate. Reflection is offered everywhere and NO medical-imaging paper reports it outperforming crop-inside.

So our Augmentation._warp padding_mode='border' is not a bad choice copied from practice — it is a choice practice declines to make at all. Above scale 1 the grid runs past the cached crop and edge pixels replicate, so a zoom-OUT fabricates margin. Every member on disk has a fabricated upper 8 percent.

D258 states plainly this is well-founded AND unstudied: no published result quantifies border-replication vs reflection vs zero for FOV jitter. The defensible ordering (reflection > border on zoom-out past the cached field) is inference from general-DL practice, not a medical transfer measurement. That makes it a genuine first read, and it is CHEAP — one grid_sample kwarg.

This gates the wide-jitter axis. fovjitter160's own REGRESSION branch already names padding_mode as the suspect rather than the axis. D258's closing: if fovjitter160 reads flat the literature's next width is ~0.30, with the border convention settled FIRST. So settle it before spending a wider arm.

Design: expose padding_mode as a flag (currently hardcoded in Augmentation._warp), then one matched pair on the 160mm cache at the jitter fovjitter160 used, reading decode_cost via foreign_readout on the card. The real alternative to test is crop-from-larger-field (decode a wider cache and crop inside it) since that is what the literature actually does; reflection is the cheap approximation.

title: arm_check hangs silently before its first print — 40 min of idle card, three runs, no output byte
description:
2026-09-09 05:00-05:44Z. Three separate invocations of kneemri.experiments.arm_check produced ZERO bytes of output and never terminated:

  bylj7udx6  --only fovjitter160                                  32 min, killed
  bhc95l5q7  --only fovjitter160 --smoke <dir> --smoke-studies 60 26 min, killed
  bs9xqnxm0  --only fovjitter160 --smoke <dir> --smoke-studies 60 13 min, killed, SOLE process

Measured, not inferred. Win32_Process on the live workers: 1.8 and 2.0 CPU-SECONDS after 32 and 26
minutes of wall clock, at ~606 MB resident. That is a process that imported torch and then BLOCKED. The
process tree is bash -> bash -> bash -> python.exe(4 MB, 0.00 s) with the 606 MB worker beside it, and
the smoke's --smoke output directory was never created, so it never reached training.

WHAT IS RULED OUT:
  - Contention between two arm_checks. The third run was the only arm_check on the machine and hung the
    same way.
  - The new arm. experiments/arms/fovjitter160.sh sources cleanly under the stub in under a second:
      ARM_LIB=experiments/stub_lib.sh bash experiments/arms/fovjitter160.sh
    prints its full flag line, exit 0, one flag (--scale-jitter 0.20) apart from crop160_span's.
  - A lock. No .lock files, no bd/dolt process on the machine, and arm_check's source contains no
    flock/Lock/input()/stdin read.
  - stdin. All three were launched with < /dev/null by the harness wrapper.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A SLOW TOOL: arm_check is the gate that stands between a flag typo and a spent
queue slot, and CLAUDE.md makes it mandatory before arming a queue. A gate that hangs before its first
print is worse than one that fails, because the card sits idle behind it and nothing says so -- this cost
~40 minutes of an idle RTX 5090 while the board read us LOSING ground (ours +0.00021/day, frontier
+0.00037/day, closing -0.00016/day). It also disarms the convention itself: the next agent facing a
40-minute silence will do what I did and route around the check.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM THE --scale-jitter WIRING as far as the evidence goes -- the arm sources fine and
the same hang hits the plain --only run with no smoke -- but arm_check ran to completion EARLIER in this
same session (it reported UNBEADED 99/336, UNPRICED 99/336), so something between then and 05:00Z
changed. Bisect candidates in that window: the 53e2067b wiring commit, the bd create at 05:00Z, and an
earlier kill of a duplicate arm_check pair that may have left state behind.

WORKAROUND USED: smoked the recipe directly, which is the form experiments/README.md:147 documents --
python -m kneemri.training.train --labels $LABELS --studies 60 --epochs 1 <arm flags> --out <throwaway>.
That is a strictly weaker check (it proves ONE recipe trains; it does not prove the other 335 arms parse,
which is arm_check's actual job), so this bead is not closed by the workaround.

FIRST DIAGNOSTIC WHEN PICKED UP: attach py-spy dump (or faulthandler.dump_traceback_later) to the 606 MB
worker rather than reading the source -- the block is before any print, so the stack is the only witness.
notes: MISDIAGNOSIS: it was never stuck. A faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(25) dump put it inside subprocess.communicate at arm_check.py:221 — serial over 305 arms at up to TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30 each. Fixed 2026-09-09 by mapping the spawns through a ThreadPoolExecutor (results zipped back in the commands' own order so the duplicate-flag verdict still sees one sequence). SPAWN_WORKERS=4, NOT 16: at sixteen the fan-out saturated the box, nvidia-smi stopped answering, and the live arm died (see the card_memory bead). Wall-clock at 4 workers is still UNMEASURED, and it must not be run while an arm holds the card.

title: agents.py --list showed active=1 with an 8h-dead listener and no STALE flag
description:
2026-09-09 04:53Z: no listen_for_mail.py process existed on the machine at all (Win32_Process sweep over python.exe returned none), yet 'python inbox/agents.py --list' printed:

  main        active=1 armed=2026-09-08T20:50Z delivered=259  unread=0
  researcher  active=1 armed=2026-09-08T20:48Z delivered=200  unread=11

Both lanes read GREEN. CLAUDE.md states the join's whole purpose: 'active=1 with no or a stale .status reads STALE (the dead-watcher failure wearing a green flag)'. It did not fire on a status 8 hours old with the writing process gone. Either the staleness threshold is far longer than a listener's poll interval, or .status is not being compared against wall-clock at all.

Consequence measured, not hypothetical: eleven letters to the researcher (M251-M261, oldest 2026-09-08T21:05Z) sat undelivered for eight hours while the lane reported healthy, and the main box's own listener was dead the whole time. M261 (the served-vs-source audit) is among them.

Fix: STALE must be a function of (now - armed) against the listener's poll period, not of the flag alone. A .status older than a few poll intervals is a dead watcher whatever active says.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-09 04:59Z on the EVIDENCE, not the finding. The description's line 'no listen_for_mail.py process existed on the machine at all (Win32_Process sweep over python.exe returned none)' was produced by a broken query, not by an empty process table: a subprocess.run(['powershell', ..., "-Filter \"Name=''python.exe''\""]) issued from inside python -c returns nothing while sixteen python.exe processes are running -- the doubled single-quotes do not survive the nesting. Asked properly through the PowerShell tool (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object CommandLine -match ...), six matching processes were listed.

What survives: the main box's listener WAS dead (its .status read armed=2026-09-08T20:50Z, eight hours old, and no listener commandline for --box main appeared in the corrected sweep either), and agents.py --list still printed active=1 for it with no STALE flag. The researcher's listener is likewise absent from the corrected sweep with unread=11 back to 2026-09-08T21:05Z, and also reads green.

So the defect is unchanged and the denominator claim is now taken from a query that works.

title: Field-of-view jitter arm: --scale-jitter flag + 160mm/420px recipe
description:
The 11-member readout (experiments/README.md, 2026-09-09) measured decode_cost -0.0336 +/- 0.0038 across the pool, flat, with rho(native,decode)=0.17 p=0.61 -- a better member does not generalise better. The ONE member that pays least is crop160_span at -0.0265, the only one ever fitted at a widened field (160mm/420px), and it reads NULL on our own ruler (0.8564 vs control band_span 0.8565). That is the shape a solo offline number cannot see.

Mechanism: AugmentConfig.scale_jitter=0.08 is hardcoded, so every member on disk saw the field vary by +/-8% around a 130mm crop. D206 section 5 measured his span 20-50% wider. The pool's blind spot is that the jitter is an order too narrow AND that zooming out of a 130mm crop fabricates margin (Augmentation._warp uses padding_mode='border').

Work: (1) wire --scale-jitter through the five --slot-dropout sites (flag_vocabulary, options, landed field+stamp, both run_setup replace() call sites, trainer effect report, member_record write-off) -- default 0.08 so every existing arm is unchanged; (2) arm on the 160mm/420px cache with --scale-jitter 0.20, field range 128-192mm, which CONTAINS both our historical 130mm and his wider span.

Pre-registration is on the FOREIGN number, not the native one: native expected NULL vs crop160_span 0.8564; decode_cost must beat -0.0265 or the arm is dead.

title: Cross-trunk control inheritance: a bound measured on dinov2-small was applied to v3small
description: latent_adapt.sh carries no --variant, so pretrain.py:262 default=SMALL resolved it to facebook/dinov2-small (backbone.py:167) - a trunk with NO registers. Its mask-0.6 epoch-0 refusal was then written into the ledger as the cap for v3small, and the whole masked-adaptation mask ladder was closed at 0.30 on that inherited number. Verified 2026-09-09: latent_register_deep survives all 8 pretrain epochs at mask 0.60 on v3small, on BOTH rulers (raw-axis retention min 0.447 vs floor 0.25). Same defect class as knee-j2ovn (latent_register_dense's 0.8385 prices against no same-trunk control). This is the worked example for the M258 audit: a claim whose control ran a different trunk. Fix has two halves: (a) an arm that omits --variant must be recorded with the RESOLVED variant, not a blank, so a later reader cannot inherit across families; (b) sweep the ledger for other claims whose control differs in trunk/resolution/slices/band.

title: No plain v3small control exists: the latent_register axis reads against nothing
description: latent_register_dense (v3small + latent adaptation mask 0.30, 12ep dense recipe) scored 0.8385 on holdout. Its arm header pre-registered that band_dense's 0.8578 CANNOT price it (dinov2 number, different trunk). The only v3small run at the identical supervised recipe is errors_v3small_s2026 (0.8280) and it carries --label-errors, a second difference. On dinov2 that flag costs errors_dense 0.8420 vs band_dense 0.8578 = -0.0158. Transferring that gives a plain-v3small estimate ~0.844, so 0.8385 sits INSIDE the bracket [0.828, 0.844] and the adaptation is not demonstrably doing anything either way. Fix is one arm: the same 12-epoch dense recipe on v3small with no encoder-weights and no label-errors. ~2h card, no pretrain. It makes three runs readable at once (latent_register_dense, latent_register_deep now on the card, and errors_v3small's own delta).
notes: PRICE: ~2.0 h of card, no pretrain. Instrument, not a member candidate. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.05 as a member; what it buys is that latent_register_dense (0.8385), latent_register_deep (running) and errors_v3small (0.8280) stop being unreadable. Three pre-registered branches in the arm header: ~0.844 closes the mask axis on a measured zero; ~0.828 makes the adaptation +0.010 directional and the ladder live; outside [0.820,0.850] impeaches every v3small number priced against a dinov2 control.

title: Target vs masking: the target does not change the early transient (matched smoke)
description: Three optimiser steps at 5e-5, identical masking/seed/slices, only the objective moving: pixel+spectral min retention 0.63, latent min retention 0.65. So the TARGET is not what drives the first steps. LIMIT: D252's collapse arrived at epoch 6-8, so this settles the transient and not the endpoint -- which is what the latent_adapt arm (knee-lm37v) is running to answer. Related: researcher D256 measured the published OrthoFoundation continuation (DINO self-distillation, latent target, 1.25M knee images, same v3large trunk) as CLEAN at every block, max |delta| 0.423 nats -- an existence proof that a latent-target on-domain continuation of this architecture need not destroy routing, which points the suspect list at OUR recipe (mask ratio 0.6, our lr) rather than the objective family.

title: SDPA silently hides attention maps: output_attentions=True returns Nones
description: transformers 5.15.0 defaults to attn_implementation=sdpa, whose fused kernel never materialises the attention matrix, so output_attentions=True returns a tuple of None WITHOUT error -- an attention check reads as a silent pass. Fixed in attention_health._Readable by set_attn_implementation('eager') for the read and restoring after. The read is also forced to eval() (stochastic depth/dropout would otherwise differ between two readings of one encoder by their random draws) and the probe batch is frozen. The --lr 0 control proves the combination is deterministic: every block of both epochs reads +0.00 with weights pinned, so any deviation the gate reports IS the weights.

title: Latent-target MIM continuation: data2vec-shaped sibling of SpectralMae
description: D249: DINOv2 is DINO+iBOT, so spectral_mae swapped a LATENT target for a PIXEL one. Our own ortho pair (ortholarge = v3large + 1.25M knee images) reads +0.0194 at 224/12 and +0.0140 whole-stack for in-domain continuation with a latent objective; the pixel version (mae_unitfix) is at -0.0885 and widening. Build a latent-target objective behind SpectralMae's interface: EMA teacher on the unmasked image, student through bool_masked_pos, smooth-L1 against normalised teacher patch features at masked positions. One-variable against mae_unitfix on identical corpus and schedule.

title: The patch embedding has never been trained: no flag on this project reaches the stem
description: D246 sec5: BlockWindow opens BLOCKS. The patch embedding, cls token and pos table are outside it, and encoder_drift reads stem 0.000000 on all fifteen supervised members swept - including band_dense_llrd (--unfreeze-last 12) and band_deep224 (12). So across 296 arms on single-channel MRI, not one has written a bit into the layer that reads the pixels. The stem is the modality interface: the only layer whose input is pixels rather than tokens, hence the only one where ImageNet-RGB vs 336px greyscale MRI is a difference in the DATA. This is not a knob tried and rejected; it is an axis with zero measurement. mae_unitfix's SSL trunk moves it 0.0620, which is currently the only way this project has ever moved it. M242 asks the researcher (a) whether any code path makes it trainable and what the smallest honest change would be, (b) what the pos table does at 336px/12sl - interpolated, truncated or reinit - since a frozen AND interpolated stem is a worse story, (c) whether the field freezes patch embeds under modality shift deliberately or by inherited natural-image defaults.
notes:
2026-09-17: --unfreeze-stem landed (20da10f3) and wired through ten files; BlockWindow carries the flag, stem_parameters() is the COMPLEMENT of the structurally-found block set. A gain is attributable to the rate ONLY against the stem arm's own e0-e3 curve; against the control it also carries block decay, needing a decay-without-stem arm nobody owes yet. 0.75 is the mildest published ViT-finetune LLRD value (0.65-0.75, BEiT / DINOv2 recipe), chosen for the largest stem cut per unit of trunk slowdown.

2026-09-16 23:59Z — WHAT THE STEM FLAG IMPLIES FOR THE RESOLUTION AXIS, recorded so it is not re-derived.

`stem_parameters()` (encoder_surgery.py:350-365) reads by EXCLUSION, so the set it opens is the patch embedding, the cls token AND THE POSITION TABLE. `--unfreeze-stem` is therefore the only flag in this repo that lets the position table adapt, and `git log` puts it in 20da10f3, 2026-09-16. Only two arms have ever carried it -- labelwise_dense_stem and labelwise_dense_stem_llrd -- and BOTH are 224px. So every resolution arm this project has ever run, 336 included, trained with a frozen position table while `Dinov2Embeddings.interpolate_pos_encoding` resampled it off the pretrained 37x37 grid unconditionally, every step.

THE TEMPTING INFERENCE IS WRONG AND IS WRITTEN DOWN HERE SO IT IS NOT MADE TWICE. It does NOT follow that 336's flatness (knee-8c8up: +0.0049 solo, under the 0.0062 noise floor; +0.0005 at the seat) is an artefact of the frozen table. DINOv2-S is pretrained at 518px = 37x37 patches; 224px interpolates to 16x16 and 336px to 24x24, so BOTH resolutions are handicapped and 336's grid is the CLOSER of the two to native. A frozen table predicts a penalty at every resolution, not a 336-specific one, so it cannot be the reason the 224->336 delta is small.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE: the 336+open-stem cell is unrun, but it is not independently priceable, because this arm IS that mechanism's cheap test. 336 costs 450 s/epoch against 224's 142 (3.2x, ~3 h for the champion recipe at 24 epochs), so it may only be armed if the 224 stem result says the stem carries at all. If labelwise_dense_stem_llrd_s2026 lands flat against its control, 336+stem is dead with it and no card is owed.

title: 36 of 37 watcher scripts are invisible to queue_check, and its STRANDED remedy can double-run an arm
description: queue_check keys both halves of its liveness test to a convention almost nothing in the tree follows. title: Truncated embedding caches read as healthy: two are 6% and 11% complete on disk
description: D212 measured it: features_orthodiff_336px_12sl_r256_gap256_volume holds 284 of 4407 studies (0.0644) and features_large_336px_12sl_r252_cls_mean_focal_max holds 504 (0.1144), each a contiguous prefix from study 0 with 0 interior breaks. Mechanism: EmbeddingCache.build opens features with open_memmap(mode='w+'), which allocates the full file up front, and writes mask+index only after the encode loop; a REBUILD that dies leaves the previous build's mask and index in place, so all three paths exist and exists() returned True. FIXED: exists() now also requires index mtime >= features mtime (a completed build writes the index last); healthy caches satisfy it, both broken ones fail by 108 min and by two days. REMAINING: rebuild both caches.

title: Two different files are named report_labels_v3.csv and an arm that grabs the wrong one fails silently
description:
Found by the researcher while building the consensus frame (D198 §1, 2026-09-08).

processed/labels/report_labels_v3.csv  - Aug 30, 1.34 MB - the crossing-remapped v2, and the file arms actually pass as '--labels report_labels_v3.csv'.
.agent-runtime/scratch/report_labels_v3.csv - Sep 6, 1.005 MB - the Qwen3.8 whole-corpus reader sweep, (4407, 37), written by .agent-runtime/scratch/corpus_reader.py.

Same basename, different content, different provenance, different column sets. An arm resolving the name against the wrong directory trains on a different supervision table than its header claims and nothing errors - the failure is silent and would be read as a fact about the recipe.

This is the plumbing clause of the CLAUDE.md failure taxonomy: a value recorded in a config while the consumer reads something else. It is worth a rename rather than a convention - the scratch sweep should carry a name that states its reader and its date (e.g. report_labels_qwen38_corpus_20260906.csv), since it is a distinct artefact and not a version of v3.

No arm is known to have picked the wrong one; filed before one does.
notes:
CONFIRMED 2026-09-08 by md5, both files present: labels/report_labels_v3.csv is 1339108 bytes, Aug 30 14:27, md5 44e73aa452b25260853a7bba89c07230 - this is the one the ARMS read and the one the +0.0045 (README:9638) belongs to. .agent-runtime/scratch/report_labels_v3.csv is 1005335 bytes, Sep 6 14:53, md5 e10afbc9e065f2e484a9dc0f0630692b, shape (4407, 37) - the researcher's Qwen sweep. Different md5, different size, same name. Every 'v3' in a letter is ambiguous until one is renamed. Raised to the researcher as M227 section 4.
2026-09-17: THE 'no arm is known to have picked the wrong one' LINE IS NOW FALSE. experiments/arms/v3labels_dense.sh declares its table is 'an LLM-read table (report_labels_v3.csv, Qwen over the 4,406 reports, v2 schema)' and pre-registers a labeler gate around it ('reader_agreement on the 58 must read v3 at BETTER than v2 140 net wrong'). Its path is $PROCESSED/labels/report_labels_v3.csv, which resolves to the CROSSING-REMAPPED v2 - the 1339108-byte Aug 30 file this bead already identified as the one the arms read. So the arm's header and the arm's bytes describe two different experiments.

Confirmed by content, not by name: v2's ACL takes 0.08/0.28/0.68/0.82/0.94 and the resolved v3's takes 0.040816/0.135593/0.377551/0.687943/0.958333 - the measured positive rates, i.e. level_calibration's output. core.data.labels.reader_agreement --labels <that file> REFUSES outright: 'this table's verdicts are report_labels_v2.csv's while its numbers differ on 12 of 12 findings ... score the numeric column with table_separation or supervision_gap instead'. The arm's own pre-registered GATE therefore cannot be run on the table the arm would load, which is the cleanest possible demonstration of the collision.

Every check the arm's own 'WHAT WOULD MAKE ME DISBELIEVE IT' paragraph names would have PASSED: require() finds the path, the recipe prints report_labels_v3.csv, and the row count is 4406 not 600. A name check cannot catch this; only a content check can.

The arm was NOT run. Its header is being rewritten to state the remap, and the correctly-premised version is knee-1b4zo.

description:

The SEE-axis inventory came back with exactly one flag settable-and-never-set (--tie), and it is a diagnostic its own author wrote 'not for switching on' (slots.py:100-106), with an UNMEASURED footprint (D183 withdrew the card-free computation: the shipped Fluid_Sensitive/Fat_Suppression columns are not the routing, they say SAG_FLUID_NOFS is fillable on 0 studies where the decoded mask has 2760).

title: foreign_run reports exit 0 over a child that died on import
description: after_clean_calib_chain.sh launched hisrecipe_distill at 2026-09-07T18:19:40Z. external/raptor/knee-mri-training-the-twelve-finding-model.py:68 raised ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sklearn' and the chain recorded 'hisrecipe_distill returned 0'. queue_check read OK with an idle card behind it for three minutes. kneemri/experiments/foreign_run.py:71 runs the foreign script through runpy.run_path and does not translate a failure into a non-zero exit, so a watcher gated on the exit code cannot tell a 2.4h fit from a one-second import error. Fix: ForeignRun.ran() must propagate, and an arm's success marker must be the checkpoint on disk, not the exit code. Root cause of the missing extra: uv run re-syncs a stale env and uv sync --extra X uninstalls every extra not named, so a pre-commit hook running beside a launching arm can empty the extras under it; the relaunch pins UV_NO_SYNC=1 over the whole chain.
notes: ROOT CAUSE IS THE ARM SHELL, NOT ForeignRun.ran(). foreign_run.py:64-73 already lets a runpy.run_path exception propagate (the try/finally only restores pd.read_parquet). The hole is experiments/lib.sh: it runs under 'set -u' and NOT 'set -e', so a dead trainer falls through to release_card and the script exits with THAT command's status. Fixed 2026-09-07 in both foreign arms (the only two: sweep over grep -l foreign_run experiments/arms/*.sh): hisrecipe_distill.sh and hisrecipe_distill_full.sh now capture trainer_status=$? immediately after the foreign_run call, release_card unconditionally, then exit "$trainer_status". title: No reader for the EFFICIENCY leaderboard — the one lane where we are losing to teams we outscore
description: board_read --live writes comp/leaderboard.json with leader/frontier/ours/gap/rank/field/tied, and every one of those is the ACCURACY board. There is no equivalent for the efficiency track, which is the lane where the standing is worst and the money is real: accuracy rank 41 at 0.944, efficiency rank 33 at 0.939, and 17 teams rank ABOVE us on efficiency while scoring BELOW us on accuracy. Podium pays 7k/6k/5k. The metric formula that produces that ordering is UNMEASURED by this project - we do not know how it trades accuracy against runtime, so we cannot tell whether a cheaper entry helps or hurts, and we have now spent a slot (cheapdecode_v1, board 0.925 at 3.7x cheaper decode) without being able to read what it did to the efficiency standing. WHAT IS NEEDED: find out whether the efficiency board is exposed by the Kaggle API at all (it may be a separate slug, a separate leaderboard endpoint, or published only as a page or a host notebook). If it is readable, add a reader beside board_read that records it with the same UTC-stamped discipline. If it is NOT readable by API, say so in writing and record where the rank 33 / 0.939 figure came from, because that number is currently quoted from memory with no instrument behind it - the same failure mode as the pinned gap that read 0.008 while the API said 0.015. WHY IT MATTERS: with the accuracy frontier closing at +0.00004/day (196 days to close +0.0086 at the current rate), the efficiency lane is the cheaper podium, and it is the only lane where we are demonstrably beaten by teams whose models are worse.
notes: CORRECTION, 23:45Z, and the bead was filed on a false premise - MY ERROR, found one grep later. kneemri/kaggle/efficiency_read.py ALREADY EXISTS and reads the efficiency board; interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_rank-not-gap.md is literally about the fact that the tool existed and nobody ran it. I repeated that exact failure: I probed the raw Kaggle API, saw only accuracy fields, and concluded there was no instrument instead of grepping the repo for one. THE ACTUAL READ, efficiency_read --live at 23:45Z: 3162 accuracy rows, 3132 efficiency rows, 3130 joined. Ours is accuracy rank 41 at 0.944 and efficiency rank 41 at 0.939 - NOT rank 33, so the remembered figure was wrong in the rank though right in the score, and our efficiency row is STALE because we submitted after the 21:47 snapshot. 25 teams rank above us on efficiency while scoring BELOW us, on runtime alone. THE LOAD-BEARING NUMBER: 122 teams within 0.002 of our 0.939 hold efficiency ranks 5 to 2738, median 2168. At fixed accuracy the rank spans essentially the whole field, so RUNTIME, not accuracy, is what orders this board - and being rank 41 inside that span means our runtime is already at the good end of it. Top 20 efficiency ranks score 0.927 to 0.952, median 0.940, which is the floor a cheap build must clear. cheapdecode_v1 at 0.925 is BELOW that floor, so the cheap-corner group is disqualified from the efficiency podium on accuracy, not on speed. title: Surgical fine-tuning: pick the block by SHIFT TYPE, the one recipe axis neither ortho_slow_trunk nor band_lpft touches
description:
Lee et al. ICLR 2023 (openreview APuPRxjHvZ) fine-tune a CONTIGUOUS BLOCK rather than the whole trunk, and the best block is decided by the KIND of shift: input-level (corruptions, low-level domain gap) wants EARLY layers, feature-level (subpopulation) wants MIDDLE, output-level (spurious correlation, label remapping) wants the head. WILDS Camelyon17, a histopathology SCANNER shift, is best at the earliest embedding layer; FMoW geo-shift is best at later attention blocks. Reported by Kimi in research/2026-09-05_ood-vit-finetune-schedules.md.

WHY IT IS A DISTINCT AXIS. Every unfreeze this project has run is a SUFFIX: --unfreeze-last N opens the trailing N blocks and nothing else, so early-layer-only has never been tested here. natural-image pretraining to greyscale MRI is the input-level case in Lee's taxonomy, which is the cell their own result says the trailing blocks are the WRONG choice for. That makes it a mechanism, not a knob.

WHAT IT NEEDS FIRST. train has no flag for an interior or prefix block range - --unfreeze-last only counts from the end. Cost is one small change to the trunk freezing code plus a flag, then one arm against band_dense = 0.8578 with the same everything else. Do NOT queue it before band_lpft reads: both arms move the same variable family (which parameters see gradient), and LP-FT is the cheaper and better-evidenced of the two.
design:
AUDIT 2026-09-05 05:38Z, kneemri/models/encoder_surgery.py:233-320 read in full. The flag does not exist and the shape of the change is settled, so that when band_lpft reads this is one edit rather than a design sitting.

WHAT IS THERE. open_blocks(unfreeze_last) returns blocks[len(blocks) - min(unfreeze_last, len(blocks)):] - a strict SUFFIX, with the min and the count-from-the-front both deliberate (a [-0:] read the whole encoder under a head-only name, measured at 2,592 parameters either way). Three callers: opened() -> last_blocks() freezes the complement and returns the rest; backbone_groups() calls both, and under --layer-decay emits one group per opened block anchored at the TOP so the ledger rate stays the top block's rate.

THE CHANGE, and it is a widening rather than a second path. open_blocks takes a WINDOW, not a count: the suffix is the window [depth-N, depth). One value object beside the class - BlockWindow with a last(n) constructor and a range(lo, hi) one - and open_blocks becomes blocks[window.lo:window.hi]. last_blocks, opened and backbone_groups keep their signatures by holding a window instead of an int. That keeps ONE way to say which blocks are open, rather than an --unfreeze-range flag racing --unfreeze-last through an if.

TWO THINGS THAT MUST NOT BREAK, and both are equality checks rather than opinions:
- BlockWindow.last(n) must produce byte-identical parameter sets to today's open_blocks(n) for n = 0, 1, 6, 12 and for n > depth. Every number in the ledger was measured under that shape.
- backbone_groups' layer-decay ladder anchors at the TOP OPENED block. Under an interior window the top opened block is no longer the encoder's last, and the ladder must still anchor at the top of the WINDOW - otherwise an early-block arm silently runs its blocks at backbone_lr * decay^k for a k the ledger has never seen.

NOT WRITTEN YET, on purpose. Gates cannot run while an arm holds the card (uv rewrites the venv under it), and Q-SHIFT is out with Kimi asking whether the block can be PICKED by a published diagnostic or whether it is try-all-three. The edit is ~40 lines including the mirror tests; the question decides whether it buys one arm or three.

band_early (offset 6) CLOSED the position axis: 0.8418 vs control band_dense 0.8578, -0.0160, flag verified off the WEIGHTS (blocks 0-5 drift 0.025-0.030 vs stock dinov2-small, blocks 6-11 exactly 0.00000). Trailing blocks are load-bearing on DINOv2-small knee MRI; Lee's position effect does not transfer. Ledger row committed 203d03d1.

It interpolates the SHAPE of an answer band_early already gave and cannot produce a member, so expected score gain ~0: instrument class. It was holding the card ahead of mricore_corpus, which was THIRD in the chain (band_mid -> band224 -> mricore) and the only mechanism priced >= 0.010 of holdout on its own. Chain watchers 63620 and 39336 killed with it; band224 is now unqueued and unrun.

title: Knee-continued trunk at ViT-B scale - the one unbuilt cell in the DAPT table
description: In-domain continuation is MEASURED at +0.019 and it seats nothing only because the trunk it ships on is the wrong size. Three instruments, one sign: ortho_dense 0.8452 vs v3large_dense 0.8258 = +0.0194 at matched 303M trunk and byte-identical recipe (only --variant differs); the frozen probe re-read at per-trunk ridge penalties (the knee-x4yx defect - a shared penalty is unfair when trunk feature magnitudes differ ~17x) gives ortholarge 0.8249 vs v3large 0.8046 = +0.0203, agreeing with the fitted arm to 0.001; and ortho_stack reads +0.0140 on band_dense's recipe. The decomposition against base224 (DINOv2 ViT-B, 86M, 0.8509) is DAPT +0.0194, ViT-L lane -0.0251, net -0.0057 - inside the floor, which is why ortho_dense was declined. So the lane is blocked on TRUNK SIZE, not on corpus, and the two gains have never existed in the same weights because OrthoFoundation only ships ViT-L. THE ASK: a DINOv2/v3 ViT-B or ViT-S with knee or MSK continued pretraining already published. If one exists this is a checkpoint download and one 40-minute arm for a mechanism-backed +0.019 on our best trunk size - the largest priced-and-unspent lever in the pool. Out with Kimi as Q-BASE (letter 2026-09-05T0240Z). If no such trunk exists, the fallback is distilling ortholarge into ViT-B, which is a BUILD and must be priced separately before anything is queued. Does NOT re-open trunk size (members.declines line 195 forbids that): size is held fixed on both sides of the +0.0194 and the continuation corpus is the only free term.
notes:
MRI-CORE IS A TWO-STRIKE CANDIDATE AND IT IS NOT THE RIGHT INSTANTIATION OF THIS LEVER. Audited the ledger before spending the probe gate's card, and this repo has already measured both of MRI-CORE's defining properties, separately, on controlled arms.

STRIKE 1 - MEDICAL CORPUS AT ViT-B. radiodino_corpus (Snarcy/RadioDino-b16, ViT-B/16, DINO objective, RadImageNet 1.35M medical images) was run at v3base_dense's EXACT recipe, so the pretraining corpus moved with architecture and objective held fixed. It read 0.8214 against v3base_dense 0.8455, -0.0241, and its seat priced at -0.0008 on honest12. radiodino_s16 (ViT-S) is the capacity leg: base width buys +0.0106 over small on the identical corpus, so the corpus cost is NOT a capacity artefact - a medical-corpus trunk sits 2.4 to 2.9 points behind its natural twin at BOTH widths and the gap does not close by scaling. The ledger's own words: the medical corpus transfers WORSE than natural at fixed architecture and fixed objective.

STRIKE 2 - SAM INIT. MRI-CORE initialises from SAM's ViT-B and continues with DINOv2 for four epochs. This project already ran a SAM-family ViT-B trunk as medsam_dense: 0.8137 against the same recipe's controls band_dense 0.8578 and calib_dense_hold 0.8634, so -0.044 to -0.050, seven to eight times the noise floor. comp/members.declines names the reading: a segmentation-pretrained trunk transferred to a classification stack loses to both a natural-image trunk and a domain-pretrained one, and it is re-opened only by changing the TRANSFER (promptable encoder as region proposer), not by another plain-trunk arm. MRI-CORE as a plain trunk IS another plain-trunk arm.

Note what does NOT close this: radiodino_corpus did not reach its REFUTES branch (< 0.80), so the medical-image row is open and MRI-CORE is not retired. Both strikes are priors, not measurements of MRI-CORE. But two independent controlled arms pointing the same way is a bad prior for a lane whose whole appeal was a strong one, and 20 minutes of card buys a reading that two existing readings already predict.

WHAT THE LEVER ACTUALLY NEEDS. The +0.0194 DAPT gain was measured on OrthoFoundation - DINOv2 lineage, knee/MSK-specific continuation, ViT-L. MRI-CORE changes the LINEAGE (SAM not DINOv2), the CORPUS (hospital-wide MRI, knee one of 18 locations, not knee-specific) and the SCALE all at once, which is the three-variable mistake radnet_family already made here. The clean instantiation changes ONLY scale: distil a ViT-B student from FROZEN ortholarge on unlabelled knee slices, keeping lineage and corpus fixed, then run the same per-trunk-penalty frozen probe that measured the +0.0194.

Kimi's decision rule for that, and it is a real gate: if the student probe lands within ~0.005 of ortholarge 0.8249, the DAPT gain is a property of the WEIGHTS and survives a shrink, so the build is justified. If the gap is ~0.015 or more it is a property of CAPACITY, and this lane closes for good. TinyMIM (CVPR 2023) supports the shape: ViT-L to ViT-B is a small enough capacity gap that a direct distil is not gap-limited the way ViT-L to ViT-S is.

The comparison that decides the LEVER, as opposed to the mechanism, is student-ViT-B against v3base - a distilled-from-DAPT ViT-B has to beat a plain DINOv2 ViT-B, not merely approach its ViT-L teacher.

NEXT: price the distillation build. It needs an unlabelled-slice loader we already have, a DINOv2 ViT-B student init, and a feature-matching loss - no new supervision and no labels. Do NOT spend the MRI-CORE probe gate first; it is now the weaker of the two and its result is half-predicted.

title: colmcl is a joint test of labels-vs-model for one column, not just a weight read
description: With colnull confirming the plain mean, colmcl (ref 56020054) gives MCL's board AUC as (champion - colmcl) * 12 + 0.5. Our offline pool reads MCL at 0.8104, the worst of the twelve. If the board AUC comes back materially HIGHER than 0.8104, the gap is our supervision and not the model - which is exactly the direction the 2026-09-04 four-reader measurement points, where report_labels_v2 makes 108 false positives against 32 misses. If it comes back at or below 0.8104, the model is the limiter for that column and a training-side lift is the lane. Either answer aims the next arm. Record the arithmetic in comp/board.jsonl when it lands.

title: Decompose each board pair's offline delta by difficulty band
description: transfer_strata gives a per-band slope (Q1 +0.44 rising to Q3 +0.81). That is a statement about which entries separate in which band, not yet a statement about where transfer lives. The refutation: for each already-scored board pair, split its offline delta into per-band deltas and ask which band's delta predicts the pair's BOARD delta. If a pair whose gain sits in Q5 does not out-transfer a pair whose gain sits in Q1, the per-band slopes are an artefact. Costs no slot and no card. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_transfer-is-blind-on-easy-cases.md
close_reason: Ran in the same wake it was filed. attribution() in kneemri/evaluation/transfer_strata.py splits each of the 348 resolved pairs at the median hard-share: gain made HARD transfers +0.74, gain made EASY +0.67. Seven hundredths, against a band table spanning +0.44 to +0.81 -- so most of the band spread is which entries separate where, not where the gain was made. The strong claim (easy gain worth half) is withdrawn in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_the-ruler-is-not-blind.md rather than shipped. What stands: the ruler is NOT blind above 0.870, every band transfers, pair-level +0.7.

title: twinfive_v1 board row carries a contaminated offline, and the refit constant rests on it
description:
comp/board.jsonl records twinfive_v1 with offline 0.8705 and no exclusion. It cannot be honest: the entry's five seats are calib_span_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, merged_blend_cf, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026 -- and merged_blend_cf was fitted at --fold -1, so it has seen all 909 holdout studies. This is the raptor_solo defect (an in-sample number recorded as a fact) on a row that is load-bearing.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE CELL. twinfive_v1 was built as the fold-0 half of fiveship_v1, and fiveship_v1's five seats are calib_span_ff, grade_ladder_cf, merged_blend_cf, lr4e-5_ws_cf, through_dense_cf. So the pair's reported delta of +0.006 (0.935 -> 0.941) is the price of refitting FOUR seats measured against a control that was already one-fifth refit, not five. That +0.006 is one of only two measurements of the full-corpus refit term; the other, foldfour_v1/fitfour_v1, reads +0.001 at four seats. A six-fold spread, and now one of the two halves is dirty. The constant licenses roughly thirty hours of card spent refitting a fleet and is the final term of the arithmetic path to 0.953.

FIX: (a) mark twinfive_v1's offline as excluded with the reason, the way raptor_solo was handled; (b) kneemri-twinchamp is the clean fold-0 half -- the exact fold-0 twin of every one of fiveship_v1's five seats, honest offline 0.8700 measured with record_mix before the slot -- and completes the pair properly. (c) board_check should refuse an offline on any entry seating a member fitted at --fold -1, which is the general form of the defect and would have caught raptor_solo too.
notes: WRONG PREMISE, closed on the roster's own line. comp/members.roster:387 states merged_blend_cf is 'merged_blend_s2026's flags plus --calibrated-targets; fold 0, the arm's only offline read'. It is a FOLD-0 member, not full-fit, so twinfive_v1's offline 0.8705 is honest and needs no exclusion. fiveship_v1's row agrees from the other side ('four of the five are --fold -1' = the four DARK _cf/_ff seats, merged_blend_cf being the fifth and fold-0). The board_check rule this bead asked for (refuse an offline on an entry seating a --fold -1 member) ALREADY EXISTS as BoardCheck.unpriceable, keyed on ALL_DATA_SUFFIX/_ff plus final_ws_e12, and it correctly passed this row. Nothing to fix here. What the mistake did cost: I built comp/kernels/kneemri-twinchamp on the contamination story and it is a ONE-SEAT SWAP off twinfive_v1 (merged_blend_s2026 for merged_blend_cf) -- a banned seating operation, and one seat_bonus.py:52 already prices as unresolvable at the 0.0040 single-pair floor. Not submitted.

title: Arm a scoreable non-DINO conv member — the only heterogeneity seat this project could price
description:
Pool is near-homogeneous DINOv2/DINOv3 plus one foreign CoAtNet seat (raptor_v4_swa) that is 98.6% in-sample per foreign_overlap and therefore unpriceable offline. Kimi Q-EL: add exactly ONE non-DINO member, anything more is seating theatre. Q-EM answered: CoAtNet, gated on marginal contribution rather than on solo strength.

TRUNK CHOSEN AND PLUMBED 2026-09-04. coatnet_rmlp_2_rw_384.sw_in12k_ft_in1k, 72.9M, registered as variant coatnet2 through a new TimmMapWeights (timm answers forward_features and emits a map, so the CALL and the LAYOUT are both wrong; TimmTrunk fixes one, TrunkAsTokens.from_map the other). Measured through the registry entry: 16 TransformerBlock2d blocks across stages 2 and 3, so --unfreeze-last 6 opens 35.5M params INCLUDING both stage-3 blocks. That is the mechanism: Swin and ConvNeXtV2 both hold their longest block run below the widest stage, so every arm in those families froze the top, and swin_wholetop priced fixing that at -0.0057. CoAtNet reaches its own top by its own shape. 384 is the only legal read (448 raises a 784-vs-576 rel-pos mismatch, measured). 144 final tokens is not a handicap: the ledger 224 corner reads 256 tokens for native224 0.8502 against the 336 band 0.851, so this pipeline loses almost nothing per token dropped.

PRICE: ~2.2 h of card, on a card that is otherwise idle. P(clears the 0.0062 report floor as a priced seat into honest12) = 0.15. P(solo at or above swin_supervised 0.8331, the controlled comparison) = 0.35. Priced as an INSTRUMENT and a seat candidate, never as an improvement: seven board flats closed the seating axis and this does not re-open it. What it buys is the last untried arrangement on the trunk axis plus a reading on whether the frozen-top confound was ever the story. Arm: experiments/arms/coatnet_hybrid.sh. No Kaggle mount yet (Apache-2.0, upload deferred until a seat is earned).

title: focus_mcl_s2026 reads rank 0.0445 in seat_value against its roster line's 0.5332 solo
description: The whole-pool seat sweep (logs/pool_seat_sweep.log, 2026-09-04) classifies focus_mcl_s2026.pt DISTINCT at rank 0.0445, against a roster boundary of 0.8956 and against its own roster comment, which reads '0.5332 solo - and seated deliberately at that number'. 0.0445 is not merely weak, it is far below chance on a rank ruler, which is what an INVERTED prediction array looks like. title: The trunk-family lever in the standing wake prompt is already closed by its own pre-registered gate
description:
Every wake carries a standing constraint naming the trunk-family arm (RadImageNet DenseNet first, supervised ImageNet VGG/ResNet second) as 'the only open lever that could plausibly deliver 1.5%'. The ledger refutes all three parts of that.

1. RadImageNet DenseNet-121 ALREADY RAN. 'radnet_family' peaked at 0.6716 and experiments/README.md line 6656 records it as closing the convolutional trunk lane EMPTY.
2. The BN-pinned follow-up ALREADY RAN. 'radnet_pinned' reads 0.7505 (+0.0789 over radnet_family, so the BatchNorm defect was real and is now priced) but still a full point below the incumbents.
3. The supervised-ImageNet VGG-16 / ResNet-50 arm is EXPLICITLY GATED OFF by radnet_pinned's own pre-registration: 'at < ~0.80 the supervised-ImageNet VGG-16 / ResNet-50 arm is NOT queued', on NVIDIA's IJCAI-ECAI 2022 result that a branch more than ~5 points off the incumbents measures as diverse and still ensembles worse. 0.7505 < 0.80, so the gate fired against it.

So queueing that arm would repeat a known result AND override a gate that was pre-registered precisely to stop it. Caught by auditing the ledger before re-arming the card chain, which is the rule that exists for this.

What it does license, card-free, is the per-case error correlation between radnet_pinned and the mean ViT incumbent -- the only measurement that could re-open the CNN axis. knee-cj40f.
