title: Prune by the RANKING at a small budget — cleanlab's own mask is the wrong selector for our defect (1.63x, not 4.05x)
description: errors_dense pruned all 5,360 flags (10.14% of read cells) and cost -0.0158 vs band_dense. The gate measured precision 0.640 at budget 25 (4.05x random) decaying to 2.15x by budget 200, so at a 10.14% budget the flagged set is dominated by hard-but-correct cells rather than mislabelled ones, and those carry the corpus highest gradients (the prune cost 3.4x what removing the same volume of random supervision costs). THE ARM: the same --label-errors path with the flag table truncated to the top-N by confident-joint rank, N ~500 (about 1 percent of read cells) where measured precision is still well above base rate. PRICE, and it is why this is P2: the upside is BOUNDED BY N. Removing ~500 genuinely-wrong cells out of 52,872 cannot plausibly move a mean AUC by the 0.0062 floor, let alone 1.5 percent. P(clears the floor) ~0.08. Costs ~4h card. Worth running only as an INSTRUMENT separating 'the treatment is wrong' from 'the budget is wrong', and only AFTER knee-f8hv5 (re-label) reads, because re-label subsumes it. Do not queue it ahead of f8hv5.
notes: PRICE, stated 2026-09-05 for arm rank966_hold. COST: 90 min card, twelve epochs at 336 px / 20 slices, plus ~4 min of CPU for the gold read. GAIN: 966 pruned cells are 1.8 percent of the 52,872 supervision cells; at the ranking selector precision of about 0.65 that is roughly 630 genuinely-wrong cells removed. Mechanism plausibly delivers 0.005-0.015 of gold AUC, so P(clears the 1.5 percent bar) is about 0.15. IT IS NOT SOLD AS AN IMPROVEMENT. It is an INSTRUMENT: errors_dense refuted PRUNE-at-the-confident-joint-mask-at-5360-cells, and that single point is currently carrying the whole label axis. This arm separates SELECTOR (ranking vs mask) from BUDGET (966 vs 5360) from TREATMENT (prune vs relabel, which relabel_hold tests) from RULER (gold vs the proxy that scored errors_dense). Under every branch it constrains what relabel_hold result is allowed to mean, which is the justification for the 90 minutes.

title: Re-label the flagged cells to the pool's held-out posterior, instead of pruning them (errors_dense's pair)
description:
THE PAIR TO knee-teh4, AND THE HEAD-TO-HEAD THE LITERATURE DOES NOT HAVE. A-QEB (Kimi, 2026-09-04, research/2026-09-04_qeb-label-noise-treatment-literature.md) searched for a published comparison of prune vs re-label vs down-weight under ONE detector in multi-label medical classification and returned an honest null: cleanlab (Northcutt JAIR 2021) is pruning-first and never compares the same detected set under re-labelling; BoMD (Chen, ICCV 2023) detects AND smoothly re-labels chest X-ray but is not an ablation; TLCM (Ghiassi, ACML 2023) is loss correction, not a treatment comparison. So the comparison is ours to make, and making it needs BOTH arms measured - which is why errors_dense (prune) still runs first rather than being skipped to the favourite.

WHY RE-LABEL IS THE FAVOURITE, with citations rather than taste. Meta Label Correction (Zheng, AAAI 2021) Figure 5: reweighting degrades significantly as noise rises while correction-based methods stay robust. Distilling Effective Supervision from Severe Label Noise (Zhang, CVPR 2020): meta re-labelling is very effective at high noise ratios and comparable at low ones. Nodet, Recovering by Relabelling (IAL 2021) gives the mechanism - a corrected sample contributes a full gradient, a down-weighted one contributes little. Our flag rate is 10.138% of read cells (5,360 of 52,872) with a gold-observed pooled error rate around 20.8%, which sits on the re-labelling side of that evidence. NOTE that no published CROSSOVER threshold exists; the '5-10%' rule Kimi looked for is folklore, not a cited result, and is not to be quoted as one.

AND WHY PRUNING MAY LOSE ON OUR SHAPE SPECIFICALLY. BoMD warns explicitly that sample selection under multi-label imbalance returns an extremely imbalanced clean set dominated by the no-findings class; TLCM reports corruption-matrix estimation failing on unbalanced label distributions. That is exactly errors_dense's pre-registered worst-case branch: a report-derived positive the models disbelieve may still be enriched for the finding, and Fracture, MCL and Synovitis carry 53% of holdout variance. Both arms therefore report PER-LABEL rows before any macro, those three first.

THE PLUMBING ALREADY EXISTS AND NEEDS NO TRAINING CODE. Supervision.unread (core/data/labels/targets.py:185) takes a (StudyInstanceUID, target, value) table that replaces a cell's SCORE and deliberately leaves its WEIGHT untouched, so the experiment stays one variable wide; Supervision.taught() reads it, drops rows for studies an arm's subset does not carry, and moves_the_ruler() already returns True for it. kneemri/evaluation/unread_teacher.py already writes such a table from PublishedRuler's twenty out-of-fold checkpoints. This arm is a new CELL SET for that machinery plus a table, not a new path.

THE ONE DESIGN DECISION, AND IT IS NOT INHERITED. unread_teacher is deliberately MEAN-PRESERVING inside each finding's UNK block: it adds ORDER without moving the marginal, because the UNK constant is the level the reader emits for silence and a prevalence shift is the one thing a twelve-head trunk transmits between heads. THAT PROPERTY MUST NOT BE COPIED HERE. Our flagged cells are confident FALSE POSITIVES - 108 against 32 misses on the gold 58 - so the whole content of the treatment is that their value should come DOWN. A mean-preserving override on this cell set would re-rank the cells while asserting the reader's marginal is right, which is the claim under test. The override is therefore genuinely value-lowering, and the prevalence shift it causes is a REAL second effect that has to be reported rather than designed away: state the per-finding positive-rate change the table causes before quoting any score.

READ IT ON THE PLAIN RULER. unread moves 5,360 VALUES, so a ruler read from the same file would rank against scores the member was just fitted toward. Pin --eval-labels, exactly as calib_span had to.

PRICE: ~4 h of card, 0 slots; the table costs minutes of I/O and no card, same as the flag table did. Runs only after errors_dense reads, because its value is the CONTRAST and a lone re-label arm answers a weaker question. P(clears the 0.0062 holdout floor over band_dense 0.8578, i.e. >= 0.8640) ~0.35, same as its pair - the literature moves the ORDER of the two treatments, not the size of the effect either can have here. Board transfer is UNKNOWN; no transfer number is to be invented for it.

Blocked on: knee-teh4 reading.
notes: CLOSED FLAT 2026-09-05. errors_relabel 0.8522 @ e6 vs band_dense 0.8578, MEAN -0.0056, inside its own pre-registered FLAT band (0.8578 > s >= 0.8516) by 0.0006. Twelve of twelve epochs, convergence_check clean, per-label spread -0.0250 to +0.0093 against half-widths up to +/-0.0310. Plumbing verified BEFORE the score: recipe carries unread_targets=relabel_rank1932_a06.csv and the table holds exactly 1932 rows. The null is quantitative rather than mysterious - 1932 cells is 3.65 percent of 52872 read cells, at precision 0.720 that is about 1391 corrected and 541 corrupted for a net +850 cells, and the gold panel's 140-of-684 rate puts about 10840 wrong cells in the corpus, so the arm fixed 7.8 percent of the defect. A treatment reaching under a tenth of the noise landing inside the noise floor is what the model predicts. Ledger row written, reading_check clean.
close_reason: SWEEP phase 1 (completed but not properly marked): the arm named in this bead's own title has a .full.log in $MODELS/experiments/ AND a scored row in experiments/README.md. The work ran and the ledger priced it; the bead was never marked. Reversible - bd update --status open if a reading here is still owed.

Our 909 holdout studies are RSNA competition TRAINING studies, so the overlap with a 909-study Pillar-0 read is ~100 percent and any AUC from it is in-sample. The per-label profile tracks their table label-for-label (Effusion highest 0.949 vs 0.965, MCL lowest 0.651 vs 0.630, ACL 0.756 vs 0.773, Bakers 0.846 vs 0.842), which independently confirms the PILLAR_LABELS head-permutation transcription at no extra forward. title: Pillar-0 feed shortfall is the CROP, per-label profile says so
description: pillar0 through 336px_20sl reads macro 0.6532 against a published 0.7970 (-0.1438). The per-label profile confirms the head permutation is identity -- Effusion .965->.938, Baker's .842->.851, ACL .773->.754, PF OA .758->.801 all land within noise. The collapse is confined to peripheral-compartment findings: Lateral Meniscus .781->.367, Lateral OA .774->.487, Fracture .775->.483, Synovitis .821->.520, MCL .630->.506, Medial OA .941->.767. Their adapter reads the WHOLE uncropped series; ours is a 130mm crop of 12-20 slices resampled to depth 192. The ledger corroborates the mechanism independently: crop80_span at 80mm lost MCL -0.0265 and ACL -0.0263, the same peripheral signature on our own DINOv2 members. Instrument: an uncropped 40-slice 384px cache over the gold 58 only (--only-studies, 1.7GB), re-gated. If the macro recovers toward 0.797 the feed is proven and a corpus-wide build is licensed; if it does not, the shortfall is the model or the depth interpolation and the member is not worth card.
close_reason: WRONG, and wrong because the ruler was broken. Every reading it was built on came from a member whose head was fed UNNORMALISED trunk features (norm ~72 against head weights of absmax 0.39), so every per-series sigmoid saturated to exactly 0.0/1.0 and every AUC was computed over massive ties -- which is why three feeds differing in crop, depth AND resolution returned bit-identical numbers on four findings. Fixed by L2-normalising in PillarMember.embedding. Re-gated, the claim INVERTS: uncropped 384px_40sl is the WORST feed at 0.7685, the cropped 336px feeds read 0.7810 (20sl) and 0.7853 (12sl), and MCL -- the finding the crop hypothesis rested on -- FALLS 0.651 -> 0.562 when the crop is removed. The crop helps. Superseded by knee-tl2ut.

title: Pillar-0 as a foreign seat: the only maximally-distant checkpoint that is already fine-tuned on this task
description:
A-DU (2026-09-04) found fabotelli/pillar0-knee-finetune (Kaggle Model, atlas-336-2ep/1): a Pillar-0 BreastMRI 3D foundation model FINE-TUNED ON RSNA KNEE, gold-58 macro-AUC 0.797, Educational Community License 2.0 quoted from the artefact LICENSE. Decode: uint8 [D,256,256] -> z-score -> trilinear to [192,384,384] -> channel-replicate x3 -> visual encoder -> Linear(1152->12).

WHY THIS AND NOT THE REST OF THE CENSUS. Everything else A-DU listed is already worked or already priced: dreaddevelopment/raptor-knee-arms ships TODAY as fleettwo's eighth seat (raptor_ft_effv2l480), and comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:2664 prices cnv2b336/cnn336 out explicitly. The DINOv2/DINOv3 entries are siblings of our own monoculture. MECHANISM. The champion's own pin names the plateau: the pool is an architecture monoculture. The one non-DINOv2 seat this project ever added (raptor_v4_swa) moved the board 0.941 -> 0.943. A true-3D trunk is further from a 2D per-slice reader than a CoAtNet is.

A-DS closed the 3D family on published evidence that 2D >= 3D for CLASSIFICATION, and on the ABSENCE of any measured error correlation between a volumetric and a slice-pooled reader. Neither argument touches a free, already-fitted member seated for DIVERSITY, and this checkpoint is exactly the cheap instrument A-DS named as the way to re-open the family ('a measured error correlation between a cheap 3D member and our best 2D member').

BLOCKER TO RESOLVE FIRST: like every raptor arm it is --fold -1 by construction, so it has no offline quality we can measure and its 0.797 may be in-sample. foreign_overlap is the tool. Q-DV asks Kimi for the licence text and the overlap.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM. The artefact's per-label profile is inverted relative to ours: Effusion 0.965 and Medial OA 0.941 against a 0.797 macro, with MCL 0.630 and the ligament/meniscus column weakest ('Ligament/meniscus fine structure is where the domain gap concentrates', README). A PER-LABEL seat -- weighting the foreign member only on the columns where it leads -- is not the flat-rank blend that effv2l480 was tested under, and Vote.ranks has never been given a per-label foreign weight. That is the version worth building.

CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE DROPPED: those column numbers are on 58 studies. A per-label AUC at n=58 has a CI wide enough to swallow the whole effect, so the 0.965 is a REASON TO MEASURE, never a number to plan on. The measurement is on OUR holdout, not theirs.

title: Nine members' input caches are gone from disk, the roster head among them, and nothing recorded it
description: roster_check on 2026-09-04 reports nine scoreable members whose input cache .npy is no longer on disk: res392_ws_s2026 and intensity392_ws_s2026 (images_448px_12sl.npy), extended_ws_s2026, band140_s2026, band_full_s2026, band_wide_s2026, crop80_span_s2026, crop80_tissue_s2026, adjacent224_s2026. The checkpoints survive. The caches do not, so none of those members can be re-scored, re-derived or WITNESSED offline. res392_ws_s2026 is the best single member this project has produced (0.8523) and the head of comp/members.roster; intensity392_ws_s2026 and crop80_tissue_s2026 are also rostered, and crop80_tissue is the only physically different crop in the pool. THE MECHANISM IS DISK PRESSURE, not a bug in any tool. D:/data is at 96 percent, 181G free of 3.7T. The caches are the largest deletable objects there and something reclaimed them. Nothing wrote it down, which is the actual defect: an asset was destroyed and the only record is a check that has to be re-run to notice. WHY IT IS P1 RATHER THAN HOUSEKEEPING. witness_check is a pre-submission gate and it needs the offline cache. A rostered member that cannot be witnessed cannot be shipped safely, so the roster now names members the shipping path cannot clear, and the failure surfaces at the slot rather than before it. That is the same shape as the mount_check and run_check families: green everywhere a human looks, wrong at the moment it costs a slot. It also closes off re-reading the resolution axis without rebuilding a cache the ledger prices at about 99GB, against 181G free. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. Serving on Kaggle decodes from the competition data inside the kernel and does not read our cache, so this is not evidence that any shipped entry is broken. The claim is narrower: those nine cannot be verified offline any more. WORK: 1. roster_check should FAIL on a rostered member whose cache is gone, not merely print it, since that is a shipping defect and not a note. 2. Decide per member whether to rebuild the cache or move it to declines with this as the reason. 3. Record current free space and a floor under it, so the next reclaim names what it is destroying.
notes:
RESOLVED for eight of the nine, on measurement (2026-09-04T03:50Z).

'StudyCache.witnessing()' names the same reading in a 'witness_shards/' subdirectory and
'witness_check.witnessing()' decodes the eight witnessed studies there from RAW when a member's own
cache is gone, preferring the full cache whenever it survives (commit e0a83abc). The dependency was
never on the corpus: a witness is eight named studies and the check was loading a ~99 GB array to
read about ten megabytes of it.

Live run over all nine, --device cpu (the PESSIMISTIC device: cpu has no autocast, so a half-precision
witness is compared against a float32 re-derivation and the residual inflates with trunk depth):

  8 ok, 1 unverified, 0 refused

  intensity392_ws_s2026  0.00162 of 0.00391
  extended_ws_s2026      0.0156  of 0.0312
  crop80_tissue_s2026    0.0152  of 0.0312
  band_wide_s2026        0.00863 of 0.0312
  band_full_s2026        0.00189 of 0.0312
  band140_s2026          0.00828 of 0.0312
  crop80_span_s2026      0.00153 of 0.0312
  adjacent224_s2026      0.016   of 0.0312

Every one inside its bound on the harsher device, and none anywhere near the 0.05-0.5 that every real
reading defect has produced. Eight members that could not clear the pre-submission gate this morning
can clear it now, 'crop80_tissue_s2026' - the only physically different crop the project owns - among
them.

THE NINTH IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT AND THE SHARD CANNOT TOUCH IT. 'res392_ws_s2026' returns 'no witness
(fitted before 2026-08-24)'. It is the roster head and the best single member this project has fitted,

Item (1) as filed - make roster_check FAIL on a missing cache - is SUPERSEDED and should not be built.

title: radnet_family 0.6716 is a fine-tuning failure with a 0.8197 frozen witness, and it closed a lane
description:
THE ANOMALY. radnet121 frozen probe scores 0.8197. The same trunk fine-tuned (radnet_family_s2026) peaks 0.6716 at epoch 6 of 12 and ends 0.6586. Fine-tuning cost 0.148 against its own frozen features. Every other trunk on this registry GAINS from fitting. A 12-epoch run that ends below its own linear probe is a broken fit, not a family verdict - and 0.6716 is the number written into comp/members.declines that closed the trunk-ARCHITECTURE-family lane, which the loop policy still lists as CLOSED.

IT IS NOT THE SILENCED RANKING TERM. knee-tj88y prices that term at ~+0.010 asymptotic. 0.6716 against a family floor of 0.83 is fifteen times that. Different defect.

IT IS NOT BATCH-1 BATCHNORM EITHER - checked and refuted. model.slice_features flattens b*s*g into the encoder batch, so at --whole-stack --slices 20 every BatchNorm sees ~20 samples per forward, not 1. Recorded so nobody re-derives it.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED. RadImageNet DenseNet-121 is the ONLY BatchNorm trunk this project has ever fitted; every incumbent (DINOv2/v3, ConvNeXtV2, V-JEPA2, Swin, ViT) is LayerNorm, which is batch-size and statistics invariant. There is NO BatchNorm handling anywhere in kneemri/training/ or kneemri/models/: no track_running_stats, no norm-layer eval(), no momentum override. The only .eval() on the training path is trainer.py:639, the validation switch.

SO THE ARM'S OWN NORMALIZATION ARGUMENT IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. radnet_family.sh reasons that norm0 sits inside the frozen prefix at --unfreeze-last 6 'so its running statistics cannot adapt to a wrong input scale', and picks the input scale by which candidate lands nearest the unit distribution those statistics encode. Freezing sets requires_grad=False; BatchNorm running_mean/running_var are BUFFERS and keep updating in train mode regardless. The premise the input-scale measurement rests on is contradicted by the code. That does not by itself explain -0.148, and it may even argue the wrong scale would have been absorbed - but the selection procedure was decided on a property the trunk does not have.

REMAINING CANDIDATES, unranked: learning rate inherited from a recipe tuned for 86-88M ViTs applied to a 7M DenseNet (the classic frozen-beats-fitted signature); running-stat drift across a frozen prefix whose weights cannot follow; the unfreeze depth meaning something different in a densely-connected trunk than in a block-stacked one.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT LICENCE. It re-opens the DECISION to close the lane, not the member. Frozen is 0.8197, the seat bar is 0.8459 and the best solo on disk is 0.8642; a repaired fit that gains the usual 0.02-0.04 over frozen lands near 0.85, so this is very likely correctness debt rather than a rescued member - the same shape as knee-tj88y. Do NOT spend the card on it ahead of a lever that could plausibly reach a better member. What it costs is the honesty of the CLOSED list: the medical-supervised pretraining cell is recorded as measured-and-empty when it was never measured.
notes: STRENGTHENED 2026-09-04 by the frozen-probe seat table (ledger, same date). radnet121@focal-max is not merely a good frozen witness in isolation - priced against the champion twelve it is the BEST of all ten cached trunks (+0.0016 seat, band [+0.0009,+0.0023]), ahead of ortholarge, vjepa2-large and both dinov2-large readouts. So the trunk whose FITTED member reads 0.6716 carries the most seat-relevant frozen signal we have measured. That is a fine-tuning failure with an independent witness at the ENSEMBLE level, not just the solo one, and it makes radnet_pinned (queued behind v3large_stack) a mechanism arm rather than a retry.

title: the full-fit +0.006 is not a constant: 0.953 chain needs rewriting
description:
Kimi's Q-CZ reply (outside view, Hestness 2017 power-law scaling; Mohr 2024 learning curves; Cawley-Talbot 2010 selection optimism; Breiman 1996 / Caruana 2004 on ensemble variance): the full-fit board term is the vertical gap between two points on a CONCAVE learning curve, not a portable constant. It should shrink with (i) pool quality, (ii) ensemble size - averaging has already absorbed part of the variance that more data reduces - and (iii) recipe convergence. Some of the measured +0.006 is also not data at all: _ff checkpoints differ in stopping/annealing from _s2026, and the seats were selected on the same holdout they are refit against. Planning number at an honest 0.945: +0.002 to +0.004.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE 0.953 PATH. It was: fleet moves honest ensemble 0.8751 -> 0.885, x0.97 transfer = +0.010 -> 0.947, then full-fit +0.006 -> 0.953. At +0.002-0.004 that lands 0.949-0.951 and MISSES. The fleet must carry ~0.888-0.890 honest offline rather than 0.885, or another lever must be found.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TONIGHT'S PAIR (foldfour/fitfour, 4 seats). Four seats and a weaker pool is exactly where the concave model says the term is LARGEST, so the pair's delta is an UPPER BOUND on the term at the champion's seven seats. Asymmetric instrument: only a null or small delta is decisive (it kills the chain's last step); a large delta is uninformative about the champion band and must NOT be read as licensing +0.006 there.

The measurement that would settle it directly is refitting honest12's or greedyseat_v1's seats at --fold -1 and comparing that board delta to twinfive/fiveship's - it prices the term at the 0.937 quality level where it is actually needed. Blocked on the card until ortho_stack + v3large_stack clear (~07:20Z).
close_reason: Measured +0.001 at the upper-bound seating; the last step of the 0.953 chain is dead. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_the-refit-step-is-dead-at-its-own-upper-bound.md

title: Slice index is not anatomy: the 12-slice cache is unregistered across studies
description:
Read the pixels for 4 annotated studies (2 ACL-pos, 2 ACL-neg), slot 0 (SAG_FLUID_FS), images_336px_12sl.npy.

Slices 4-7 land on: the intercondylar notch (pos2), the medial compartment (pos), the notch only on the last tile (neg), and a medial/peripheral plane with the notch nowhere in frame at all (neg2 - not in the band, not in the full 12).

So a fixed slice index does NOT name a fixed anatomic plane. The 12 slices are a fixed-count resample of a stack whose coverage, centring and FOV vary per study. For a finding that lives in ~2 planes (ACL in the notch), that means the evidence is present in some studies and absent in others, and a model cannot learn 'look at tile k'.

Also: slot 0 is not homogeneous in appearance - one study reads as bright-fat near-native contrast, another as dark low-SNR fat-suppressed. Between-study variation in sequence/window/SNR/crop exceeds within-study torn-vs-intact variation.

Discovered while explaining why four zero-shot VLMs all read AUC ~0.5 on ACL (call rates 0.931/0.483/1.000/0.034 - four different priors, no signal). It is a defect in the PRESENTATION, so it bounds trained members too, not only the VLM probe.

Open questions, in order:
1. Is the resample uniform over the acquired stack, or over a fixed physical span? Read the cache builder.
2. Does slot routing ever pick a different series for slot 0 across studies (that would explain the contrast heterogeneity)?
3. What would anatomically-registered slice selection cost, and is it a plausible 1.5%-sized lever for the trained pool rather than only for the VLM lane?

Evidence: logs/look_{pos,pos2,neg,neg2}_montage.png and logs/notch_{pos,pos2,neg,neg2}.png (logs/ is gitignored - regenerate from core.data.labels.image_probe Montage).
notes:
Q1 ANSWERED by reading the builder, no run needed.

core/data/corpus/slot_reader.py:328 band_indices(): low, high = int(band.low * (available-1)), int(band.high * (available-1)), then spacing.indices(low, high, slices). So the 12 slices are drawn as a FRACTION OF THE ACQUIRED STACK - not a physical span, not an anatomic landmark. Registration therefore holds only as far as two series cover and centre the knee identically, which is exactly what the 4-study read shows they do not.

SLICE_BAND = (0.20, 0.80) at slot_reader.py:35, the historic default every member on disk was fitted under. Its own docstring already says it is 'no longer the best one'.

The axis is MEASURED and it is not small (slot_reader.py:334): 0.00-1.00 = 0.8427, 0.20-0.80 = 0.8525, 0.10-0.90 = 0.8565. A crude fractional band change is worth +0.0138 over the worst and +0.0040 over the shipped default. That is a knob moving the pool by more than the holdout resolution floor (0.0053) at its full span - so the through-plane sampling rule is a real axis, and 'which fraction' is only the crudest possible handle on it. An anatomically-registered selection is the same axis with the confound removed.

Reframes the priority: this is not a VLM-lane defect. It bounds every trained member, and it is one of the few open levers whose mechanism could plausibly reach 1.5%.

Q2 (does slot 0 routing pick different series across studies) still open, and is the likely explanation for the contrast heterogeneity - one study reads bright-fat near-native, another dark low-SNR fat-suppressed, both nominally SAG_FLUID_FS.
Correction to my own framing, recorded before it misleads anyone: the band WIDTH knob is NOT a new lever. It is mined. experiments/README.md: band_wide (0.10-0.90, 16 slices) 0.8553, band_dense (0.10-0.90, 20 slices) 0.8578 = +0.0053 vs rate_wholestack, both on the roster, and depth_regions/depth_regions_narrow decompose it further. Caches for 0.1-0.9 at 12/20 slices and 420px/160mm already exist on disk. I quoted the +0.0138 span as if it were open; it is spent.

What survives is the narrower claim: widening the FRACTION is not the same as REGISTERING it. band_dense samples a wider fraction of each stack; index k still names a fraction, never a plane. The four-study read stands. Whether that residual is worth anything is the open part, and it is bounded by Q2 (slot-0 series heterogeneity), which is now with the peer as Q-CM.

Related: knee-wgaa (P0, log SLOT/SLICE attention and check against anatomy.py) is the same question from the model's side - it measures whether a trained member's slice attention lands on anatomy or on index. If attention is anatomically incoherent across studies, this defect bites the pool. That is the cheap test, and it should run before any cache rebuild is considered. knee-m69u (P0, name a NEW axis or stop arming) is where this lands if it survives.

title: The slice readout that wins on frozen features is not in the training vocabulary: add 'moments'
description:
MEASURED, NO CARD, 2026-09-03. feature_probe --choose-penalty --slice-readout max moments, fold-0
holdout, n=909, each trunk at the penalty chosen on a nested split inside its own training positions.
Four trunks, all four focal caches:

  trunk               max      mean     moments   moments-max
  dinov2-large      0.7936   0.8048    0.8082      +0.0146
  v3large           0.7926   0.8046    0.8042      +0.0116
  ortholarge        0.8146   0.8249    0.8279      +0.0133
  radnet121         0.8061   0.8197    0.8240      +0.0179

The ordering is moments > mean > max on every trunk, and it is `max` that every member on the roster
is fitted and served with (`--slice-pooling max --whole-stack`). `SliceMoments` is the mean along the
stack concatenated with its standard deviation, at twice the width and with no learned parameters.

WHY THIS IS A NEW AXIS AND NOT THE OLD ONE. The aggregation chapter measured `attend` at +0.0002 over
`max` and `labelwise` at the same null, and closed on that. Those are all learned pools over the SAME
first moment. `moments` adds a statistic the first moment discards — how a channel VARIES along the
stack — which is the shape a lesion occupying a few slices has and a uniform structure does not.
knee-m69u asks for a new axis rather than another knob; this is a candidate for one.

WHY IT IS NOT YET AN ARM. `SLICE_POOLINGS` in kneemri/models/slice_pooling.py has no `moments` entry,
so the readout that wins here cannot be trained. Adding one is a small change (per_slice=True plus an
aggregator that concatenates the second moment, doubling the slot width the head reads).

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME DISBELIEVE IT. A ridge over max-reduced frozen features is not the same instrument
as a learned head over a max pool — the head can in principle learn what the spread carries, in which
case the frozen gap closes to nothing at train time. That is exactly what the arm would measure, and
it is why the pre-registration has to be written before it runs. The frozen delta is also fold-0 with
penalties selected on the same 909-study holdout, so the LEVELS are inflated; the ordering, reproduced
across four independent trunks, is the finding.

DEPENDS ON THE CARD, which is the owner's. Ready to arm when it frees. Control: band_dense_hold_s2026.
notes: READ 2026-09-12: moment_wide 0.8600 @e8 of 12, converged, vs calib_dense_hold 0.8634 = -0.0034, the pre-registered FLAT band. Head width asserted off the checkpoint BEFORE the verdict: head.proj.1.weight is (256,1536), so the head was built wide. Readout axis CLOSES with the aggregation axis. +0.0084 of moment_dense's -0.0118 was the mix-down, not the statistic. Seated on the roster as a diversity seat. PRICE CORRECTION: these arms are ~56 min (279 s/epoch x 12), not the ~2.5 h this bead and the arm header both quote.

title: images_224px_12sl_adjacent.npy is gone — adjacent224_s2026 cannot be read, scored or shipped
description: label_combine over the full s2026 pool died on FileNotFoundError for D:/data/volumetric/mri/processed/rsna_knee_abnormality/images_224px_12sl_adjacent.npy. The MASK for that decode exists (mask_224px_12sl_adjacent.npy); only the images array is absent. So adjacent224_s2026.pt is a checkpoint whose predictions cannot be recomputed on a cache miss — every gate is green about it and it is silently unscoreable. Two things follow: (1) roster_check must assert every rostered member's cache key RESOLVES ON DISK, not merely that the member is named somewhere; a member whose decode is gone is exactly as unshippable as one that was never trained, and nothing currently says so. (2) Decide whether to rebuild that decode or decline the member in writing. Found 2026-09-03T08:35Z by the knee-xtpn1 label_combine instrument, which had to be relaunched excluding it.
notes:
2026-09-03 09:44Z — THE FIX, specced while gates ran so it can be written straight after the push.

WHAT ROSTER_CHECK ASSERTS TODAY: that every checkpoint with a holdout record is named in comp/members.roster or in comp/members.declines with a reason. That is a check about BOOKKEEPING, and adjacent224_s2026 passes it — it is on the roster, it has a holdout record, its decline is not needed. What it does not have is its images array: images_224px_12sl_adjacent.npy is gone from disk while the mask survives. So the member is rostered, scoreable-looking, and unbuildable, with every gate green.

WHAT TO ADD: for each member on the roster, resolve its cache key to the actual arrays and assert they EXIST. The key is already recorded per run (the recipe row of its .metrics.jsonl carries the decode parameters the cache filename is built from), so this needs no new bookkeeping — it needs the existing key put through the same path-building the loader uses, and a stat() on the result. Assert BOTH the images array and the mask, because this defect presented as exactly one of the pair surviving, and a check that looks at either alone would have stayed green.

WHY IT BELONGS IN ROSTER_CHECK AND NOT A NEW TOOL: roster_check already owns the question 'can this be shipped', and a member whose pixels are gone cannot. mount_check asks the same question one step later about encoder datasets; kit_check asks it about the packaged kit. This is the earliest point the answer is knowable.

THE FAILURE MESSAGE MUST NAME THE MISSING PATH, not just the member — the whole cost of this bug was that nothing said which file, and the mask being present made it read as a decode-parameter mismatch rather than a deletion.
LIVE RUN 2026-09-03: the defect is nine members, not one. `roster_check` over 102 packaged members names 9 complaints across 8 distinct missing arrays, with 24 image caches surviving on disk:
  adjacent224_s2026     images_224px_12sl_adjacent.npy
  band140_s2026         images_336px_20sl_140mm_0.1-0.9band.npy
  band_full_s2026       images_336px_12sl_0-1band.npy
  band_wide_s2026       images_336px_16sl_0.1-0.9band.npy
  crop80_span_s2026     images_336px_12sl_80mm_tissue_0.1-0.9band.npy
  crop80_tissue_s2026   images_336px_12sl_80mm_tissue.npy
  extended_ws_s2026     images_336px_12sl_extended.npy
  intensity392_ws_s2026 images_448px_12sl.npy
Survey: 178 scoreable of 261 checkpoints; 102 packaged, 77 declined, 1 undocumented.

REFRAMED BEFORE LANDING, twice. (1) THE CLAIM: a shipped kernel decodes Kaggle's test studies at serve time and never opens our cache, so a missing LOCAL decode does NOT stop a member shipping and does not void its recorded holdout number. What it stops is re-scoring, re-derivation, witnessing and curve-reading offline. The docstring's original 'cannot be scored, seated or shipped' was right for adjacent224_s2026's presentation and wrong as a rule. (2) THE SEVERITY: each cache is tens of GB and reclaiming old ones is ordinary housekeeping, so nine blocking findings on a check run after every run makes it permanently red and therefore skipped. The lines moved out of complaints() (SystemExit) into report() (printed, named).

IMPLEMENTATION: RosterDrift.unreadable() asks each packaged member which pixels it read — Member.from_checkpoint -> Member.reads_pixels (filters SSL encoders/teachers with no 'img') -> Member.cache(directory) -> StudyCache images_path/mask_path. A second spelling of the axis list inside the checker would BE the mismatch this check exists to catch. Both arrays are asserted because adjacent224_s2026 lost its images and kept its mask.

STILL OPEN: whether any of the eight arrays is worth re-decoding (each is a full decode), and the 1 undocumented scoreable member the survey reports.

title: CNN trunk rate ladder was already run: 4e-5 to 4e-4 is worth +0.0259, cnx trunk fair number is 0.8186
description:
THE CNN RATE LADDER WAS ALREADY RUN, AND NOTHING IN THE TREE KNEW IT. Four `cnxbase` runs sit in
D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality, every one of them at image_size 336, slices 20, variant cnxbase, and they
differ from each other in the trunk rate and almost nothing else:

    backbone_lr 4e-5    cnx_dense_s2026        0.7927   (12 epochs, the ViT adapter rate)
    backbone_lr 1e-4    cnx_warm_anneal_s2026  0.8105   (peak at epoch 3 of 6, then declining)
    backbone_lr 4e-4    cnx_own_recipe_s2026   0.8186   (12 epochs)
    backbone_lr 1.2e-3  cnx_top_rate_s2026     0.7762   (truncated at epoch 3, still rising)

THE ANSWER THE LADDER WAS BUILT TO BUY. `cnx_dense`'s 0.7927 is a statement about a ViT adapter rate on a
convolutional trunk, not about the trunk. Moving the rate an order of magnitude to 4e-4 is worth +0.0259,
which is four times the 0.0062 report-holdout noise floor and well past the 1.5% bar. The `cnx_dense`
retitle of 2026-08-24 predicted exactly this ("convolutional trunks fine-tune roughly an order of
magnitude higher") and the run that confirms it already existed when the prediction was written.

WHAT IT COSTS TO HAVE NOT KNOWN. `cnx_rate_ladder.sh` was written this morning to spend two points x three
epochs, ~1.5 h of card, on the two rates 1.2e-4 and 4e-4 - both of which are inside the range already
measured at TWELVE epochs. Its header argues the case over sixty lines and cites the ledger twice. It was
queued, and it only failed to run because of an unrelated cache miss. That is the sprawl tax stated as a
number: 1.5 h of the scarcest resource, against an answer that was on disk under four names nobody joined.
The arm is retired rather than fixed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY SETTLED, AND WHAT IS NOT. Settled: the trunk trains, the rate was the confound, and the
fair-budget number for a convolutional trunk on this task is 0.8186. Not settled: whether that member is
worth a seat. 0.8186 is 0.027 below the 0.8459 seat bar (MERIT), so it does not enter on quality. The
standing argument for it was never quality - `cnx_dense` reads nearest-neighbour 0.7941 against a seated
roster whose own spread floors at 0.8724, which is 0.078 more distant than any seated member is from its
nearest neighbour. So the open question is unchanged in shape and now has a fair number attached to it: is
a trunk 0.027 short but genuinely off-family worth a seat? That is an ENSEMBLE measurement, not another
solo arm, and it costs no card - the holdout vectors for cnx_own_recipe_s2026 are already written.

TWO SIDE FINDINGS.

1. `cnx_top_rate` at 1.2e-3 was truncated at epoch 3 and reads 0.7762 while still rising. Under one_cycle
   that number is a FLOOR and says nothing about whether 1.2e-3 beats 4e-4. It should not be quoted as a
   peak, and convergence_check will call it TRUNCATED, correctly.

2. The 352 px cache miss that stopped the ladder was a RED HERRING and points at a real defect. Every one
   of these four runs read at 336 px on cnxbase, successfully, over weeks. This morning the same variant at
   336 was refused by `encoder.py:343` with "cnxbase is patch 32, which cannot tile a 336 px read - use 320
   or 352". Either that refusal is new and wrong, or these runs used a code path that has since changed. It
   needs its own reading before any convolutional arm is queued again, because a refusal that contradicts
   four completed runs is either a bug in the check or a silent change in what the trunk does with the grid.

WHAT TO DO NEXT, IN ORDER, AND NONE OF IT NEEDS THE CARD. (a) Ensemble cnx_own_recipe_s2026 into the
champion's seat set from the holdout vectors on disk and read the delta - that answers the only live
question. (b) Put cnx_own_recipe_s2026 on the roster or decline it in writing; roster_check has been
silent about it. (c) Resolve the patch-32 contradiction in encoder.py before the next convolutional arm.
notes:
CORRECTION to the bead's own side-finding 2, same day. The patch-32 refusal is NOT a bug and does not contradict the four runs. cnxbase is stride 32 over four halving stages, so 336/32 = 10.5: the four runs read a TRUNCATED 10x10 grid, i.e. a 320 px read carrying a 336 px flag, outer 16 px dropped. encoder.py:343 is a later, correct guard against exactly that silent truncation. The rate comparison between the four is unaffected - all four are truncated identically - and 0.8186 stands as the fair-budget number at an effective 320 px. What it changes: a future cnxbase arm at the legal 352 is a DIFFERENT read, so its delta against 0.8186 would carry a resolution change on top of whatever else it moves. Item (c) of the next-steps list is withdrawn; there is nothing to resolve in encoder.py.
Ensemble question closed off the card 2026-09-03T08:18Z: member_curve over the five best s2026 seats + cnx_own_recipe reads best-5 0.8724 without it, best-6 0.8698 with it forced in, and it enters no best subset at size 2-5. -0.0026 is inside the 0.0062 floor, so: no evidence of the lift its distance predicted. Declined in comp/members.declines with the measurement; ledger appended. Re-open only via knee-uk4f (stage 3 was frozen for all four runs), never by re-quoting distance.

title: arm_read could not parse or resolve a hyphenated control; 100 of 212 arms still declare none
description:
`arm_read` is the tool that forces a PER-LABEL reading of an arm instead of a mean, and it has never
successfully read a single arm. Two independent reasons, one fixed here and one still open.

1. THE ROOT WAS WRONG (fixed 2026-09-03T07:53Z). `ArmRead.report` resolved both the arm and its control
against `root.processed()`. Every `.metrics.jsonl` this project has written lives under `root.models()` --
222 of them there, zero under processed. So every invocation died with

    ValueError: control <name>.metrics.jsonl does not exist

which reads as a MISSING RUN and not as a WRONG ROOT, and that is the whole reason the failure survived:
the obvious response to it is to go looking for the run or to blame the arm's control declaration.
`run_comparison`, which performs the same resolution one layer down, passes `root.models()` and always
did, so the two callers of one function disagreed about which root runs live in. Fixed by passing
`root.models()` and renaming the parameter, with the history written into the docstring.

2. HALF THE ARMS STILL CANNOT BE READ. `arm_read --assert` now reports 110 of 213 arms declare no
`# control <name> = <score>` line. The parser needs that exact form -- `CONTROL_LINE` requires the name to
be followed by `=` -- and the headers that do name a control mostly name it in prose: `# control  the
130 mm image-centred members on the same fold`, or `# control  band_span 0.8565` with no `=`, or the name
wrapped in backticks. So the declaration exists in the writing and not in the form the tool reads. Four
crop arms were fixed by hand while running the ROI gate (knee-f0kdy): crop80_tissue -> wholestack_s2026,
crop80_tissue_full -> crop80_tissue_s2026, crop80_span and crop160_span -> band_span_s2026.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL TOOL BUG. The mean is the wrong read for every arm whose mechanism is
supposed to trade one group of findings against another, and this project has written that sentence into
arm headers repeatedly -- crop80_tissue's own header says "Read PER LABEL, never on the mean alone". The
tool that would have enforced it could not run, so the mean is what got recorded, and crop80_tissue went
into the ledger as -0.0112 with no per-label row anywhere. When the read was finally performed it took
under a minute and produced the finding that closed a proposed multi-day build. The cost of this defect is
not the tool; it is every arm read on its mean since the tool was written.

WHAT TO DO. The fix is landed for the root. For the declarations: sweep the 110 arms and convert prose
controls to the parsed form where the header already names one, and leave genuinely uncontrolled arms
uncontrolled -- a bare `--assert` count is then a real number rather than a mix of two failures. Do it in
batches by family, verifying each converted name resolves to a metrics file that exists, because a control
that names a run nobody kept is the same dead end wearing a different message.
notes:
COUNT CORRECTED 2026-09-03T08:37Z: the uncontrolled-arm count is 62 of 212, not 110. The 110 came from a looser pattern. Measured with grep -L '^# control' experiments/arms/*.sh. Three converted this session (merged_span_cf -> merged_blend_cf = 0.8597, merged_labelwise_cf -> merged_span_cf = 0.8618, merged_blend -> lr4e-5_ws = 0.8525); the first two verified through arm_read by NAME. merged_blend's line does not resolve, because that invocation's header text comes from a different shell than merged_blend.sh — worth checking before converting any other arm whose .sh name may not be its invocation name. 59 remain.
2026-09-03 09:05Z — CORRECTION to my own earlier note in this bead, and the real defect underneath it.

MY 62 WAS WRONG. I counted FILES (grep -L '^# control' experiments/arms/*.sh) and reported the bead's 110
as an overcount. Files are not invocations: one .sh prints several run names, and some invocations come
from shells with other names. The authoritative census is arm_read --assert, which read 105 of 212. The
bead's original 110 was closer to right than my correction. My merged_blend diagnosis in that note ('that
invocation's header text comes from a different shell') was also wrong — see below.

THE DEFECT: ArmHeader.CONTROL_LINE could not match a hyphenated control name. The class was
[A-Za-z0-9_]+, which consumes 'lr4e' out of 'lr4e-5_ws' and then fails on '-' where it wants '='. So the
tool whose whole job is naming arms WITH NO DENOMINATOR was blind to the project's most-used denominator
— lr4e-5_ws = 0.8525, described in three arm headers as 'the control every other member reads' — and
reported arms that declared a control correctly as declaring none. Every rate-named control has the same
shape (lr1e-4_ws, lr2e-4_ws, res392_lr8e-6_ws). Widened to [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*; --assert went
105 -> 100. The five recovered: band_density, band_span, depth_regions_narrow, merged_blend, native224.

SECOND HALF, also fixed. Past the parse, every one of those five died on 'control
lr4e-5_ws.metrics.jsonl does not exist'. A header names an ARM; the disk holds RUNS (lr4e-5_ws_cf,
lr4e-5_ws_ff, lr4e-5_ws_s2026) and there is no lr4e-5_ws.sh to read an --out from, so produced() falls
back to the bare name. Choosing a suffix by convention was refused: _cf is a --fold -1 fit that has seen
every holdout study, so a convention would silently read a fold-0 arm against a cheating control. Fix is
ArmRead.sibling: resolve directly when a run of that name exists, else pick the split-suffixed sibling
whose best epoch matches the score THE HEADER ITSELF DECLARED (tolerance 5e-4, far inside the 0.0062
floor); ambiguity and silence both raise, naming every candidate and its auc. CONTROL_LINE now captures
the score as group 2 and ArmHeader.control_scores serves it.

VERIFIED: band_span, native224 and merged_blend now read per label against lr4e-5_ws_s2026 (mean 0.8525
at epoch 8, exactly the declared number). Three arms that had no reading at all now have one.

STILL OPEN, unchanged by this: 100 of 212 arms declare no control. That number is now measured against a
parser that works.
2026-09-03 09:09Z — the 100 SIZED, and 15 of them closed.

WHAT THE SILENCE ACTUALLY IS. Of the 100 arms declaring no control, 84 use the word 'control' in their
prose and 14 never mention one; 23 quote a 'name = 0.xxxx' pair somewhere in the header (a few of those
are my regex catching noise like 'BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015'). So this is mostly a FORMATTING problem
rather than a missing-denominator problem: the denominators exist, written in sentences no consumer can
read. That is a cheaper finding than '100 arms have no denominator' and a different one.

FIFTEEN CONVERTED, EACH VERIFIED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN. For every candidate pair the header's own prose
quoted, ArmRead.sibling was asked to resolve it first: 14 of 15 landed on a run whose best epoch equals
the declared score to four decimals, which is what makes the prose pair the true control rather than a
number that happened to sit near the word. Written into batch_teardown, cnx_dense_448, cnx_mid_rate,
final_fit, half_data, merged_corpus, ortho_dense, resolution, resolution_420, sided_pool, sided_tissue,
small_feat_fit, stack224, unfreeze_depth, v3large_dense. --assert: 100 -> 85 of 212.

THE ONE THAT FAILED FOUND A THIRD DEFECT. 'resolution' declares wsfold0_e6 = 0.8457 — the pre-convention
control knee-bot rests on, which kept PREDICTIONS rather than epoch rows. sibling tested only
RunMetrics.exists, so it fell through to a sibling search, found none, and reported a control that
resolves perfectly one layer down (RunComparison.scored reads it via HoldoutMetrics) as matching nothing.
The direct branch now accepts the checkpoint alone. 'resolution' reads 0.8457 at epoch -1.

REMAINING: 85. 63 of them name a control in a sentence with no score beside it — each needs the header
read to say which run, so this is a chore with judgement in it, not a sweep. 14 mention no control at all
and are the ones that genuinely have no denominator.

title: Competence axis is mostly trunk adaptation, not a free trade: shippable pool spans 5% of its reach; re-price per-label combining anyway
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03T06:53Z, competence_axis over every readable holdout record on disk:

  182 of 204 records became members, 909 shared studies, 182 members x 12 findings
  member quality took 81.9% of the spread and was removed before the axis was read
  component 1: 33.5% of what is left, against a null bar of 19.1%  -> ONE shared axis, real
  loading: Effusion +0.539, Synovitis +0.534, PF OA +0.158, Medial OA +0.062, Lateral OA +0.039,
           ACL -0.013, Fracture -0.066, Contusion -0.071, Lateral Meniscus -0.145, MCL -0.297,
           Medial Meniscus -0.340, Baker's -0.400
  by structure scale: focal -0.0766, regional +0.1073
  along the axis: 119 of 182 below zero holding 50% of the displacement, reach [-0.317, +0.125]
  against member quality: r = -0.01

Two readings, and they point opposite ways.

FIRST, IT CLOSES THE MEMBER AXIS BY MECHANISM rather than by the seven board flats. The pool's whole
spread is one trade — regional fluid findings against focal structures — and a permutation cannot move
the mean because the mean is what that line is orthogonal to. That is the standing argument for spending
the card on trunks, and this is the first measurement of it at pool scale.

SECOND, AND THIS IS THE OPEN PART: r = -0.01 against quality, with both ends populated. The axis is not
weak-members-versus-strong-members. It is 182 members genuinely disagreeing about WHICH findings they are
good at, independently of how good they are. A uniform rank-average maps both ends onto the middle.

WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY RE-OPENING A CLOSED LEVER. Per-label member weighting is recorded closed twice:
`member_curve` read `oracle 0.8590 vs plain average 0.8588 (headroom +0.0002)`, and the objective-side
refutation sits beside it in the ledger under "Per-label treatment is closed on both sides."

That oracle is a genuine ceiling and it is not being disputed. But it was computed over SEVEN members. A
bound over seven members bounds schemes over those seven; it cannot bound a scheme over a pool 26x larger
whose spread has now been measured and is not one-dimensional in the quality direction. The ledger's own
sentence — "the members do not disagree per label in a way any rule could exploit" — is a claim about the
seven, and the axis measurement is the first evidence that a larger pool disagrees more.

THE INSTRUMENT, and it is priced as an instrument and not as an improvement. `label_combine` already
exists and was built around exactly this trap: it fits the per-label member choice on studies it is not
scored on, and at k = every member it IS the flat rank-average, so one k curve carries both the candidate
and its matched control under the same estimator. Run it over the largest mixable pool.

COST: arithmetic over cached prediction arrays, minutes of CPU, no slot. The risk is cache misses — a
member the prediction store has not seen runs its encoder — so it needs an idle card or an explicit
--device cpu, and it must NOT be co-run with a trainer: a CPU co-run is the standing suspect for the
driver-level OOM that killed ortho_pool_read's first attempt at epoch 6.

PRE-REGISTERED BRANCHES, against the flat rank-average that the same k curve reports:
  1. gain >= +0.0062 (one arm-vs-arm floor) at some k < all, out of sample -> per-label weighting is
     re-opened AT POOL SCALE, and the seven-member oracle is re-read as a statement about seven members.
     This would be a non-seating way past the champion, which is the only kind currently permitted.
  2. gain in [0, +0.0062) -> directional only. Records that the effect has the sign the axis predicts and
     is under the floor; keep if free, never plan around it.
  3. gain <= 0 -> the closure survives 26x more members and is no longer a seven-member claim. That is
     worth the run on its own: it retires the suspicion permanently rather than leaving it re-openable
     every time the pool grows.

Branch 3 is the likely one and the run is still worth it, because what it buys is the retirement of a
question the pool will otherwise keep re-opening.
notes:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN READING, 2026-09-03T07:09Z. Same competence_axis run, positions printed for all 182
members instead of the five at each end. Two things change, and the second weakens the case for the run
this bead asks for. Recording both before the run, not after.

1. RESOLUTION DOES NOT MOVE A MEMBER ALONG THE AXIS; THE ENCODER RATE DOES.

     lr4e-5_ws_s2026          336 px, rate 4e-5   -0.022
     res392_ws_s2026          392 px, rate 4e-5   -0.027
     res392_lr8e-6_ws_s2026   392 px, rate 8e-6   +0.008

   Pixels at fixed rate move the position by -0.005. Rate at fixed pixels moves it by +0.035, SEVEN TIMES
   larger. The ledger already closed resolution on the mean ("resolution alone is nothing", knee-a8x, 392 @
   8e-6 read 0.8459 / +0.0002, the +0.0066 being the rate). The axis was the one reading on which that null

   for it in regional ones would show a flat mean and a moved position. It does not. Resolution is now

2. THE AXIS IS LARGELY TRUNK ADAPTATION, NOT A FREE COMPETENCE TRADE -- AND THE SHIPPABLE POOL OCCUPIES 5%
   OF IT.

   The reach [-0.317, +0.125] is carried entirely by members nobody would seat. Positive end: cnx_dense
   (0.7927), encoder_adapt / encoder_adapt_gentle / encoder_adapt_thawed / encoder_adapt_lower, mae_matched,

   the coarse bright regional findings with generic features. Negative end: focus_mcl -0.317 and

   That is also the honest explanation of r = -0.01 against member quality, which I read last wake as
   "182 members genuinely disagree independently of how good they are". It is not independence. It is TWO

   Every member that could hold a seat sits in a strip: res392_ws -0.027, stackfit -0.027, lr4e-5_ws -0.022,
   stack_increments -0.018, certainty_ramp -0.018, depth_regions_narrow -0.017, labelwise_dense -0.012,
   base_dense -0.012, v3base_dense -0.012, disagreed_uniform -0.010, base224 -0.009, crop80_span -0.008,
   band_dense -0.008, band_dense_hold -0.005. Span 0.022 against a pool reach of 0.442: FIVE PERCENT.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THIS BEAD. The instrument still runs and the branches still stand, but the prior moves
hard toward branch 3 (closure survives). The argument for re-opening was that a bound over seven members
cannot bound a scheme over 182; that survives. The argument that the pool's measured spread gives such a

WHAT IT DOES TO THE CARD. It removes resolution from the candidate list for an off-axis member, which was

2026-09-03 09:38Z: label_combine KILLED at 114 of 168 reads (pid 9916) to release the venv for gates+commit — 46 files had been sitting uncommitted behind it. The kill is cheap and was verified so before firing: the module takes no --out and writes nothing itself (result goes to stdout at the end), BUT each computed read caches its member's holdout predictions under processed/holdout_predictions — 48 files (24 members x .npy+.json) written in the two hours before the kill.
