title: queue_check reads OK when two watchers gate two different arms on ONE producer
description:
queue_check counts watchers PER ARM OWED, so it cannot see the opposite collision: two watchers owing two DIFFERENT arms, both gated on the SAME producer. Each arm has exactly one live watcher, which is the invariant it asserts, and it printed "OK: every arm still owed is gated by exactly one live process" over a state that would have put two arms on one card the instant ortho_pool_read exited.

Found 2026-09-03T06:43Z. after_cnx_ladder.log gated on `pid:22188` (ortho's pid) and a freshly armed after_radiodino.log gated on `ARM DONE ortho_pool_read` in ortho's own log. Different marker STRINGS, same producer, same instant. The two markers are written within a second of each other: `_mark` writes ARM DONE from the arm's shell, and the shell then exits, which is what `pid:` gates on.

This is exactly the failure card_check exists to catch AFTER the fact — two of ours on one card, which cost twenty-five minutes of contention on 2026-08 and turned one member's epoch time from three minutes into eleven. queue_check is the BEFORE check and it should have refused here.

The fix is to resolve every watcher's gate to the PRODUCER rather than comparing marker strings. A `pid:<n>` gate resolves to that process; an `ARM DONE <name>` gate resolves to the process writing <name>.full.log. Two watchers whose gates resolve to the same producer, owing arms that are not the same arm, is a collision — refuse unless the arms are declared pairable (after.sh already serialises WITHIN one watcher, and its own header records that channel-stacked small arms will pair while two max-pooling base arms drove the card to 31.5 GB of 32).

Worked around by hand for now: the radiodino watcher was killed and re-armed behind `ARM DONE cnx_rate_high`, so the pipeline is serial (ortho -> cnx_rate_ladder -> radiodino). The hand fix is not the fix; the next person to queue two arms behind one producer gets a green check over the same collision.
notes: FIXED 2026-09-04: QueuedArms.producer() resolves a gate (ARM DONE <arm> or pid:<n>) to the running process LINE, and collided() refuses when two live watchers owing DIFFERENT arms resolve to the same producer. A numeric token is matched as a FIELD, not a substring, so a pid cannot match digits inside a seed or a memory column. COLLIDED is a blocking fault, reported before DOUBLE-QUEUED (which is the opposite shape: one arm owed twice). 31 unit tests pass, mirror clean. Live queue reads no collision, which is correct.

title: Canonical corpus metadata(): the 4406 rows the merged frame cannot see
description:
Rijeka, MRNet and fastMRI now each write <processed>/metadata/<corpus>_metadata.csv and build_merged concatenates them through StudyMetadata.merged. The canonical RSNA corpus writes NONE, and it is 4406 of the 6391 merged rows -- so every axis in the frame currently reads absent for 69% of the studies, which makes the frame useless for the thing it was built for (stratified sampling, a domain column, a per-corpus score breakdown).

There is no canonical Corpus CLASS to hang a metadata() on -- the canonical decode is series-level and lives elsewhere. Two producers, and the choice is the work:

(a) train_series.csv alone. One CSV read, no DICOM sweep. Ships Anatomical_Plane, Fluid_Sensitive, Fat_Suppression per SERIES. KNOWN DEFECT, already measured in slots.py: shipped Fat_Suppression matches header-recovered on 99.3%, shipped Fluid_Sensitive on only 78.7%. Writing the shipped Fluid_Sensitive into the schema puts a column that is wrong on a fifth of the corpus next to columns read off headers, which is exactly the failure study_metadata.py's own docstring names.

(b) acquisition.Acquisition.probe over the DICOM tree. Correct on every axis and also gives TR/TE, spacing, field strength. Costs a full header sweep of 4406 studies.

AGGREGATION IS THE OTHER HALF. StudyMetadata is one row per STUDY; canonical ships several series per study with different planes. MRNet already answered this shape: plane records the SET, joined with '+'. Proposal: same join for plane and sequence; fat_suppressed/fluid_sensitive filled ONLY when every series of the study agrees, absent otherwise -- absence being a value here, not a hole.

Proposed: (b) for the flags it recovers, written once to <processed>/metadata/canonical_metadata.csv, with the shipped columns NOT written at all. Home: a canonical_metadata.py module beside study_metadata.py plus a build entrypoint, since there is no class to extend.
notes: CODE LANDED 2026-09-03T06:20Z, NOT YET RUN. Study.metadata() in core/data/corpus/study.py -- the canonical adapter already holds the acquisitions and the plane table, so no new module was needed and the bead's canonical_metadata.py proposal is withdrawn. Producer is (b): header-recovered via Acquisition, and the shipped Fluid_Sensitive/Fat_Suppression columns are NOT written at all. plane and sequence record the '+'-joined SET; fat_suppressed, fluid_sensitive, pixel_spacing_mm and slice_spacing_mm fill only on unanimity across the study's series, absent otherwise. SET_JOIN moved to study_metadata.py as the one home (mrnet_corpus.PLANE_JOIN deleted, was a second spelling of the same separator). Entrypoint: python -m core.data.corpus.build_cache --metadata-only, one header per study, no decode. 297 corpus tests pass. REMAINING: run it on an idle card (4406 header reads, disk-bound, do not co-run with an arm), then re-run build_merged so the merged frame carries all four corpora.

title: Corpora were never processed to a common format: no schema, no origin column, no sublabel, no inventory
description:
ROOT CAUSE behind the four corpus beads filed 2026-09-03 (MRNet meniscus discarded, SKM-TEA never
decoded, merged table carries no metadata, two corpora unidentified). They are not four independent
misses. They are one missing layer, and the owner named it: the working pattern at D:/work/ai is
PROCESS EVERY DATASET TO A COMMON FORMAT, THEN MERGE WITH MAXIMUM META. Only the labels half of that
was built here.

WHAT THE REFERENCE ACTUALLY DOES, read 2026-09-03 04:59Z at D:/work/ai:

  data/schema/dataset.py - a `Dataset` ABC. Required members are abstract (`name`, `path`,
  `all_audio_files_paths`). The METADATA hooks are concrete and default to unknown:
  `mic_array_for_file` returns None, `get_azimuth_for_chunk` returns (None, None),
  `get_file_label` returns Label.UNKNOWN. A dataset that cannot supply an axis SAYS SO; the axis does
  not disappear from the union. ~65 per-dataset adapters under data/raw/adapters/ implement it.

  training/sound_tracker/constants/dataframe_schemas.py - `core_dataset_metadata_fields()` declares ONE
  typed schema that is always present, with `ensure_schema` enforcing it. It carries `dataset` (origin),
  `original_filename`, `label`, `sublabel`, and nullable axes only some corpora have (`mic_array`,
  `start_azimuth_deg`, `end_azimuth_deg`). data/processed/datamix.py stamps `processed_dataset_name` per
  row on top.

  data/README.md - a DATASET INVENTORY: every corpus listed with counts, source link and caveats.

WHAT WE HAVE INSTEAD:

  - No base class. fastmri_corpus.py, rijeka_corpus.py, mrnet_corpus.py and kmar_corpus.py are four
    unrelated shapes with a build_*.py each. Adding a fifth corpus means writing a fifth from scratch,
    which is the direct reason SKM-TEA has sat undecoded beside a decoded fastMRI.
  - No declared schema. merged3_labels.csv columns are whatever pd.concat produced: 12 findings x
    (value, __conf, __verdict) and nothing else.
  - The ORIGIN COLUMN IS A DEAD WIRE. Targets.load at core/data/labels/targets.py:383 already reads
    `if "corpus" in derived.columns` into Targets.corpus. The CONSUMER EXISTS. MergedCache.labels never
    writes the column, so it is always None. This is the cheapest defect in the whole set and it has
    been sitting there through every merged member on disk.
  - No sublabel. Our label space is 12 flat columns, so a SIDE-LESS finding has nowhere to live. MRNet
    meniscus (449 positives) and the fastMRI "Meniscus Tear" term are both side-less, and BOTH WERE
    DROPPED - not for lack of data but for lack of a schema slot. fastmri_corpus.py:186 documents the
    workaround it was forced into ("these block the negative instead of asserting a positive").
  - No inventory, which is why kmar50k and knee_clinical_seq sat on disk unidentified and why fastMRI
    was priced on its own without anyone comparing it to the other three.

ORDER OF WORK, and it matters that the schema goes first: MRNet-meniscus and SKM-TEA each ADD A CORPUS
to the union, so doing them before the schema means retrofitting it three times.

  1. Declare the schema and write the corpus column. Smallest possible step, and it connects an already
     existing reader. New --labels-out name; NEVER overwrite merged3_labels.csv, every merged3 member on
     disk was fitted against it.
  2. Add the per-study metadata frame (plane, sequence, field strength, spacing, age, sex, scanner).
     SKM-TEA all_metadata.csv and the fastMRI ISMRMRD header already hold these and both discard them.
  3. Add a coarse/sublabel slot so a side-less finding has a home, then MRNet meniscus and abnormal.
  4. A corpus ABC, once there are two more adapters to justify it - not before. NO SPECULATIVE FOLDERS.
  5. docs/EXTERNAL_CORPORA.md as the inventory, with the licence reading per corpus that is already
     backlogged.

HONEST PRICING so this is not sold as a score lever. None of this is worth 1.5% by itself. The ACL
merge measured +0.0161 on its own column and +0.0063 mean, and MRNet meniscus is the same shape. What
the layer buys is that the NEXT corpus costs an adapter instead of a rewrite, and that an arm can ask
whether a transfer came from the labels or from the domain - which today is unanswerable because the
domain is not recorded anywhere.
notes: REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION READ 2026-09-03T06:00Z, at the owner's instruction, second asking. D:/work/ai: 66 per-dataset adapters under data/raw/adapters, all subclassing the Dataset ABC in data/schema/dataset.py, plus a separate data/raw/transformation layer for sources whose raw shape needs fixing before an adapter can read it, plus a human dataset inventory in data/README.md. The merge is data/processed/datamix.py and it is THIRTY-EIGHT LINES. What it does: each dataset carries its own cached meta_df; ensure_schema coerces that frame to ONE declared schema, core_dataset_metadata_fields, filling whatever the dataset lacks; two columns are stamped at mix time from the dataset object, processed_dataset_name for origin and chunk_path; and it returns a DICT KEYED BY DATASET NAME rather than a concatenation. Three findings against this repo. FIRST, we have no per-dataset metadata artifact at all - our corpora expose labels(destination) and nothing else, so the ds.meta_df half is missing at the ADAPTER, not at the merge, and fixing it at the merge is the wrong end. SECOND, MergedCache.build concatenates into one array and one table, after which the corpora are separable only by a column, which is the mechanical reason nothing can stratify or score per corpus; theirs stays keyed and mixes downstream. THIRD, the StudyMetadata schema landed this session IS ensure_schema in shape - declared columns, absent filled, shape independent of who answered - but it sits as a fortieth module in core/data/corpus rather than as the one declared schema everything coerces through. Also noted for the labels axis: they run cleanlab_diagnostic for label-noise diagnosis and semdedup for semantic dedup. We do neither.

title: Merged label table carries no metadata: no corpus, plane, field strength, age or spacing
description:
The merged label table carries LABELS AND NOTHING ELSE. merged3_labels.csv is 6390 x 37:
StudyInstanceUID plus 12 findings x (value, __conf, __verdict). There is no corpus-of-origin column, no
plane, no field strength, no sequence, no slice spacing, no age, no sex, no scanner.

This is the piece the owner named on 2026-09-03: the working pattern is process to a COMMON FORMAT and
merge with MAXIMUM META, and only the labels half of it was built here. Consequences that are already
real rather than hypothetical:

  - Nothing downstream can condition on, stratify by, or balance across the source corpus, even though
    the corpora differ in the ways that matter most: Rijeka is sagittal PD-FS, fastMRI is CORONAL, MRNet
    ships three planes, ours is its own protocol. A merged member cannot be told which distribution a
    study came from.
  - No arm can ask whether a transfer is carried by the labels or by the domain shift, because the
    domain is not recorded.
  - SKM-TEA all_metadata.csv already holds PatientAge, PatientSex, Scanner, Sequence, SliceThickness,
    SliceSpacing, MagneticFieldStrength, EchoTime, RepetitionTime, FlipAngle, ReconstructionDiameter and
    MedialDirection per exam - read, present, and thrown away at merge.
  - fastmri_corpus.py already READS per-exam geometry from the ISMRMRD header (140 mm FOV on 116 of 120
    sampled, 320 px matrix) and does not persist it either.

The fix is a schema question, not a modelling one: MergedCache.labels should carry a corpus column plus
a per-study metadata frame, written to a NEW --labels-out name so no member on disk is invalidated. Do
it once, before MRNet-meniscus and SKM-TEA add two more corpora to the union, or it gets retrofitted
three times.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-03T05:55Z: the first bullet of this description is WRONG and was filed without
checking the file it describes.

There IS a corpus-of-origin column, it is written by MergedCache._tagged, and it is correct:
  merged_tagged_labels.csv   5143 rows, 38 cols  -> canonical 4406, rijeka 736
  merged3_tagged_labels.csv  6391 rows, 38 cols  -> canonical 4406, mrnet 1248, rijeka 736
The 37-column merged_labels.csv / merged3_labels.csv this bead measured are the UNTAGGED tables written
beside them. I read the untagged pair, found no corpus column, and generalised to "the merged label
table carries labels and nothing else" without opening the two files whose names say otherwise.

THE REAL DEFECT IS ONE STEP DOWNSTREAM AND IS WORSE. Grepping every arm for the table it names:
  merged_blend_v1.csv  9 arms
  blend_three_v1.csv   6 arms
  merged_labels.csv    1 arm
  merged3_labels.csv   1 arm
  (merged_tagged_labels.csv / merged3_tagged_labels.csv: ZERO arms)
The origin axis is computed, correct, on disk, and read by nothing. Every merged member on disk was
fitted against a table with no corpus column. So the consequences this bead lists are real -- nothing
downstream can stratify by, condition on or score per corpus -- but the cause is not a missing producer,
it is a consumer that points at the wrong filename. That is a much cheaper fix than the one this bead
was about to buy, and it should be tried BEFORE anything is rebuilt.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE. Beyond origin, no acquisition metadata survives the merge: no plane, sequence, fat
suppression, field strength, spacing, echo/repetition time, age, sex or scanner. SKM-TEA's 44 columns
and fastMRI's ISMRMRD geometry are still read and dropped. That half of the bead stands.

LANDED THIS SESSION: core/data/corpus/study_metadata.py -- StudyMetadata, the flat per-study row in the
shape every corpus can answer. Fourteen axes, all defaulting to None, so a corpus overrides only what it
can say and absence is a recorded value rather than a hole (the pattern read out of the owner's
D:/work/ai reference implementation, where Dataset declares every axis and adapters return None for the
ones they lack). frame() keeps every column even for an empty corpus, joined() left-joins onto labels so
no labelled study is ever dropped. Mirror test at tests/unit/core/data/corpus/test_study_metadata.py,
8 passed, and it pins study_metadata.CORPUS == merged_cache.CORPUS so the two spellings cannot drift.
Nothing derives a field: acquisition.py's TR/TE recovery stays where it lives, because a guessed field
would be indistinguishable from a header read.

NEXT, in order: (1) point an arm at the tagged table and confirm the axis arrives -- cheap, no card;
(2) per-corpus metadata() overrides, one corpus at a time, each gate-able on its own;
(3) MergedCache writes the metadata frame to a NEW --labels-out name so no member on disk is invalidated.

title: SKM-TEA annotations never decoded: 476 boxed positives on four of our twelve columns
description:
SKM-TEA annotations were never decoded and they are the only foreign corpus on disk that asserts real
POSITIVES on our deficit findings. Measured 2026-09-03 04:56Z from
raw/skmtea/annotations/v1.0.0/{train,val,test}.json:

  images 86 / 33 / 36     annotations 242 / 104 / 130     155 distinct studies, 476 annotations
  supercategories: Cartilage Lesion 212, Effusion 117, Meniscal Tear 107, Ligament Tear 40
  Meniscal Tear is graded to SUBTYPE (Myxoid, Horizontal, Radial, Vertical/Longitudinal, Oblique,
  Complex) and each annotation carries a BOX.

This maps onto four of our twelve columns and it is the exact opposite of fastmri_findings.csv, which
asserts almost no positives at all (see the fastMRI zero-positives bead).

WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN and must be measured before any arm: whether the meniscal tears carry a SIDE
(medial/lateral) or only a subtype - if no side, this hits the same coarse-column problem as the MRNet
meniscus bead; how "Cartilage Lesion" maps to our three OA columns (compartment is probably recoverable
from the box against the segmentation masks, which ship); and how many of the 155 studies are POSITIVE
per supercategory rather than how many annotations exist, since one study can carry several.

The pixels are NOT decoded. raw/skmtea/ holds all_metadata.csv, annotations/, dicoms/ and
segmentation_masks/. Cost the decode before promising anything - 155 studies is small, and the honest
case for it is per-label positives on deficit columns plus its metadata (see the merged-metadata bead),
not volume.
notes: 2026-09-14 (knee-vgz5b.2): meniscal side and cartilage compartment are answerable from raw-data-track masks (tc-m/tc-l, men-m/men-l labels 3..6); decode lands in skmtea box table.

title: MRNet meniscus and abnormal labels were never built: 449 radiologist meniscus positives discarded
description:
MRNet ships THREE label files and we built ONE. Measured 2026-09-03 04:55Z directly on the raw CSVs at
raw/mrnet/, which are on disk and were on disk when the ACL table was built:

  train-abnormal 1130 rows, 912 positives   valid-abnormal 120 rows,  95 positives
  train-acl      1130 rows, 208 positives   valid-acl      120 rows,  54 positives
  train-meniscus 1130 rows, 397 positives   valid-meniscus 120 rows,  52 positives

Built: mrnet_acl.csv, 1248 rows, ONE column. Discarded: 449 radiologist-read MENISCUS positives and
1007 ABNORMAL positives.

WHY IT WAS DISCARDED. mrnet_labels.py:31 sets ACL_LABEL = "acl" as a module constant and both readers
close over it: ArchiveLabels.table globs f"{split}-{ACL_LABEL}.csv" and TableLabels.table globs
f"*{split}*{ACL_LABEL}*.csv". Nothing about the corpus, the download or the join is ACL-specific. The
Redivis export note in that module docstring is about PIXELS, not about which findings shipped.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ACL MERGE DID. Medial/Lateral Meniscus is a deficit finding for us and the
labels are RADIOLOGIST READS, not report-mined - so they are on the label side, which is where
knee-9198 measured the transfer to be real: the merged_corpus ACL work read +0.0161 on the ACL column
and +0.0063 mean. Meniscus gets MORE positives (449 vs 262) on a WEAKER column.

PRICE. ACL-sized is the fair prior: ~+0.006 mean, directional, BELOW the 1.5% bar on the mean and
therefore not a finding on its own - but it composes, and the cost is near zero. The PIXELS ARE ALREADY
DECODED and already in the merged3 cache, so there is no decode: it is a builder edit, a
build_merged --labels-only rerun writing a NEW --labels-out name (never overwrite merged3_labels.csv,
every merged3 member on disk was fitted against it), and one arm.

CAVEAT TO SETTLE BEFORE ARMING. MRNet meniscus labels carry NO SIDE, exactly like the fastMRI
"Meniscus Tear" term. Our schema has Medial Meniscus and Lateral Meniscus as separate columns. So
either it supervises both columns as a coarse OR (asserting a positive on a column that may be negative
- WRONG, and the opposite of what fastmri_corpus.py:186 does), or it blocks the negative only (safe,
weak, and reproduces the fastMRI outcome), or a thirteenth coarse "Any Meniscus" column is added as an
AUXILIARY head that trains but never ships. The third is the only one that uses the positives honestly.
Decide this in writing before any card time. ABNORMAL is the same shape: no column exists for it, and
it is a natural aux head.
notes:
AUX-HEAD DESIGN, audited 2026-09-03T05:11Z. Written down rather than built, and the reason is the
price, not the design.

THE HEAD WIDTH IS ONE LINE. kneemri/models/model.py:231 builds the head as
SLOT_POOLINGS[design.slot_pooling](head_width, n_slot, len(TARGETS), prior), and that is the ONLY place
a width is chosen; labelwise_attention.py:40 defaults n_out to len(TARGETS) and takes an override
already. On the labels side core/data/labels/targets.py sizes four arrays by len(TARGETS) (lines 203,
351, 352, 358). So a thirteenth column is five edits, not a refactor.

THE THIRTEENTH COLUMN MUST NOT JOIN TARGETS. core/findings.py states the order is a CONTRACT -- it is
the submission CSV's column order and every trained member's head order at once, and a member fitted
under one order and served under another is silently wrong on all twelve. TARGETS is also what the host
grades. So the aux column is APPENDED to a separate ALL_TARGETS = TARGETS + AUX_TARGETS, the head is
built to that width, and every consumer that already iterates TARGETS keeps reading the first twelve
positions unchanged. Slicing is free because the aux entries sit after, never between.

IT HAS TO BE OPT-IN OR IT INVALIDATES THE POOL. Every checkpoint on disk carries a 12-wide head, so a
width that changes unconditionally breaks the load path for the whole roster with every gate still
green -- the same failure shape as overwriting a labels table. Default AUX_TARGETS empty means width 12
and byte-identical behaviour; the flag widens both the model and Targets together, from one design
field, so the two can never disagree.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY, and this is why it is not being built today. The coarse column exists to give a
SIDE-LESS finding a home. COMPARTMENT_PAIRS already names the structure it needs -- Medial/Lateral
Meniscus is one lesion located to a side -- so the first and only aux entry worth adding is "Any
Meniscus". The positives waiting on it: MRNet meniscus 449 studies (pixels already decoded, already in
the merged3 cache) and fastMRI Meniscus Tear 663 studies (already read, currently blocking negatives).
That is roughly 1100 study-positives on one auxiliary column.

PRICED HONESTLY. targets.py:73-75 already states the mechanism: a monotone map of one head's targets
leaves that head's ranking unchanged, so whatever an aux head buys arrives through the SHARED TRUNK.
The in-house precedent for exactly that shape is the ACL merge at +0.0161 on its own column and +0.0063
on the mean, from 1984 labelled rows. This is the same size and the same mechanism, and its gain does
not even land on a graded column -- it lands on the trunk. Expect low single thousandths on the mean.
DIRECTIONAL, below the 1.5 percent bar, and it costs a multi-file change through the training path plus
a card arm to read out.

DECISION: not now. The trunk-family arm is the only open lever whose mechanism could plausibly deliver
1.5 percent, and the card is booked through it. Build this when the trunk axis closes, or when a
labels-side change is being made through the training path for another reason and this rides along.
Nothing above needs re-deriving -- it is five line numbers and a price.

title: An arm died of a driver-level CUDA OOM at 12.84 GB on a 32 GB card, and exit 127 hid it
description:
ortho_pool_read died at epoch 6 on 2026-09-03T03:58Z with 'RuntimeError: CUDA driver error: out of memory' after six epochs at a FLAT 12.84 GB reserved on a 32607 MiB card. The arm was not growing and the card was not full. The wrapper reported 'trainer exit 127', which is the same signature ortho_fresh_lowlr carried and which was filed as a candidate silent-kill; it is neither a silent kill nor gates. Exit 127 is the shell's code after a native abort, and the real error is 295 lines up the log.

MECHANISM (hypothesis, not yet measured). This recipe's gate line records that it reserves 67549 MiB on a 32607 MiB card. On Windows WDDM the allocator does not OOM, it spills to HOST memory. So the arm's true working set is partly system RAM. A CPU job launched beside it competes for that RAM, and the loser is the GPU arm, which fails at the DRIVER level rather than in the allocator.

The timing is exact. The CPU job was the gold-reading batch (supervision_gap, pids 30296/58124). It had been running through epochs 0-5 and the arm survived it. It moved onto swin_calib_dense_s2026 at 03:58:33 -- a Swin forward on CPU, the heaviest member in the batch -- and the arm died at 03:58. So the trigger is not 'a CPU job', it is a HEAVY one.

WHY NO CHECK CAUGHT IT. card_check asks the DEVICE, deliberately, so that it reads what is really on the card rather than guessing from argv. That is the right design for its own question and it makes this class invisible: neither process was a second GPU job, the card never went above 12.84 GB, and both jobs were legitimately ours. The missing assertion is about HOST memory, not the card.

WHAT IS ALSO NOT MEASURED: free host RAM at the moment of death. wmic returned nothing when asked after the fact. Until a number exists this stays a hypothesis that fits every observation rather than a demonstrated cause.

ACTIONS: (1) measure the arm's real host-RAM footprint while one runs, and the batch's; (2) if the hypothesis holds, card_check (or a sibling) grows a host-memory arm; (3) until then the operational rule is that no heavy CPU job runs beside a host-spilling arm -- which is any large trunk at 336 px.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE READING: ortho_pool_read attempt 1 is VOID. Its 0.8408 at epoch 5 must NOT be read against the pre-registered bands -- it is a truncated one_cycle score, so a FLOOR, and the truncation was my plumbing rather than the method. Relaunched 04:13Z.
notes:
AMENDMENT 04:15Z, same session, before anyone acts on this. The relaunch at batch 4 prints 'gate: this recipe reserves 25737 MiB' against a 32607 MiB card -- it FITS. The 67549 MiB figure in the description is from the arm docstring and belongs to the FIRST attempt at --batch 12, not to the configuration that died. So the WDDM host-spill story is materially weaker than the description states: the run that died was not obviously spilling, and its measured peak was 12.84 GB. The title has been changed to stop asserting a mechanism the evidence does not carry.

What survives, and it is the part worth acting on: a DRIVER-level CUDA OOM at a flat 12.84 GB on a 32 GB card is not an allocator OOM, so it is host-side or context-level, and it coincides to the minute with the heaviest CPU member of a co-running batch starting. Page-locked host allocation in the dataloader is a second host-side candidate that needs no large spill to fail.

Still unmeasured, and now unmeasurable for this incident: free host RAM at 03:58Z. It read 67.5 GB of 93.6 GB at 04:15Z with the batch already dead, which says nothing about the moment. The next deliberate co-run should sample it; that settles this far more cheaply than more reasoning from one log.

SECOND DEFECT, and it is the one with the broader reach: the wrapper reported 'trainer exit 127' while the real error sat 295 lines up the same file. That reading cost a wrong diagnosis here (I opened this bead calling it a gates kill) and it is very likely what mis-filed ortho_fresh_lowlr as a candidate silent-kill -- an arm that may never have failed on its method at all. Split out.

title: Report labels over-call: 21.1% cell disagreement vs radiologist, and the pool beats its own ruler by +0.0516
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03, card-free, from cached arrays. Full writeup: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-03_the-report-ruler-over-calls.md

Answers knee-ds2e in the LABEL-NOISE direction. Instrument: the 58 radiologist-annotated studies in raw/train.csv, read against eight members whose recipe row says hold_annotations=True, so none of them saw a gold cell. Their predictions over all 58 were already cached under processed/.../annotated_predictions/.

(1) report_labels_v2 vs radiologist at 0.5, over 58x12=696 cells: 147 disagree, rate 0.2112. ONE-DIRECTIONAL: 115 report-positive/gold-negative against 32 the other way. 323 report positives vs 240 gold. The LLM report reader OVER-CALLS by a third. Worst: Contusion 22 (20 FP), Synovitis 18, Effusion 16 (all FP), Lateral Meniscus 14. Synovitis is the single inversion (14 FN, 4 FP) and it matches its 84.2% UNK rate - the report is SILENT about it, not wrong about it.

(2) Scored against the radiologist on the same 58: eight-member pool 0.9174, report_labels_v2 used as a predictor 0.8658. Paired delta +0.0516, 95% CI [+0.0296, +0.0729] over 4000 study-level bootstrap draws, P(delta>0)=0.9998. 11 of 12 labels positive; MCL is the only negative (-0.0057) and has 9 gold positives. Every SOLO member also beats the report (0.8964-0.9189), so it is not an ensemble effect. The per-label gain ordering matches the over-call ordering (Contusion +0.1592, Effusion +0.1267) - two different quantities agreeing is what makes it a mechanism and not small-sample coincidence.

DENOMINATORS. 58 of 4407 studies = 1.3%. Nothing shows the 58 were sampled at random; if they are interesting cases the 21% is an upper bound. Only 13 of the 58 fall in the fold-0 holdout, which is why the hold_annotations members are the instrument - for them all 58 are honest.

NOT ESTABLISHED. Which ruler the hidden test uses. The argument is from PROVENANCE: train.csv is the competition's own label file, so gold is the host's convention and the report table is ours. That is an argument, not a measurement, and it is load-bearing.

WHAT IT REDIRECTS. The 909-study holdout is a report ruler, so every offline delta this project has quoted is measured against a target that over-calls by a third - orderings survive (bias shared by both arms) but an arm that REDUCES over-calling is charged for it. Label correction is a live card-free axis; knee-kabn already holds one instance (Fracture + 0.25*Contusion, +0.063 on the radiologist ruler). Any further correction must be derived from the reader's MECHANISM, never fitted on the 58 - twelve thresholds on 58 studies overfits and spends the only honest ruler the project owns.
notes: v3 comparison 2026-09-03, card-free. Both tables read against the radiologist on the same 58, tie-averaged AUC: v2 0.8658 / positive rate 0.447 / disagree 0.2083 / 108 FP / 37 FN. v3 0.8676 / 0.306 / 0.1739 / 47 FP / 74 FN. Gold positive rate 0.345. So v3 changes the ORDERING by +0.0018, under a third of the floor - it is near a monotone remap and AUC is rank-invariant - and what it actually fixes is the VALUES: over-calls 108 to 47, total disagreement down a sixth. knee-8wa0's +0.0105 is therefore a supervision-SCALE effect, not a better-ordered ruler, which is mechanistically consistent. v3 also OVERSHOOTS into under-calling (0.306 vs gold 0.345 on these 58). That is NOT a licence for a v4 shifted back up: the 58 are 1.47x enriched so the corpus rate that matches a radiologist is unknowable from them, and twelve per-label shifts fitted on 58 studies spends the only honest ruler the project has.

title: twinfive's pre-registration cannot read what it claims: peak8 already sits at offline 0.8704 -> board 0.932
description: Q-BY (Kimi, 2026-09-02) shows two things that change how the pending twinfive score must be read. (1) The board_transfer decay +1.23 -> +0.98 -> +0.80 is reproduced by a CONSTANT true slope of 1.5-1.9 once range restriction and the 0.0053 offline SE and the board's 0.001 quantization are simulated; the top cell holds 4 resolved pairs that are all honest12 differenced against four lower entries, i.e. one anchor, not four points. Price arms at the whole-record +1.16 or the 0.8670 cell's +0.98; never quote the 0.8692 cell as a local slope. (2) The kernel docstring pre-registers 0.930-0.935 as 'the slope FLATTENS at the top'. It does not. peak8 is already on the board at offline 0.8704 -> 0.932, and twinfive's offline is 0.8705 - the same point. A constant slope predicts 0.932-0.934 for twinfive, so that band distinguishes nothing. What twinfive vs peak8 actually measures, at fixed offline, is COMPOSITION (five fold-0 twins under LogitAverage vs peak8's set). The slope question needs an offline point ABOVE the record's 0.8751, which no existing pool provides. Do not write the flattening reading into board.jsonl or an interpretation when the score lands.
close_reason: twinfive scored 0.935 and the row in comp/board.jsonl records it against the mis-specified branch, not as a flattening: peak8's offline 0.8704 -> 0.932 sits 0.0001 away in offline and 0.003 away on the board, so no slope is separable. The number the slot actually bought is the twin-to-shipped gap, 0.009, which is 9x the vote-rule spread the twin-fitted combiner entries were reading.

title: Sequential cross-corpus pretraining: MRNet ACL trunk warm-started into our twelve labels
description: Owner's transfer test, and knee-ombx's untested 1.5-3% mechanism. Two arms: mrnet_acl_pretrain (scheme mrnet, 1248 exams, focus-label ACL, 8 epochs) then mrnet_warm (base224 verbatim plus --init). Control base224=0.8509. Distinct from the merged-corpus axis, which CONCATENATED foreign studies into one optimisation and closed flat at +0.006; this is two optimisations. A-BV says the transferable part is representation not head, so gain is not capped at ACL, but MRNet is far under the scale for deep feature reuse and orthofoundation-L shows knee-supervised continuation can subtract. ACL chosen over fracture as the ruler: fracture is fastMRI-only, its category is a union of three of our findings, and our holdout has 68 positives in 909.
notes:
PRICE: ~2.0 card-hours total — decode 224px_12sl_mrnet (~10 min, 1248 exams), mrnet_acl_pretrain 8 epochs (~45 min), mrnet_warm 12 epochs (~65 min, base224's own budget). Freed by killing rampsix's remaining five calls (A-BW: 4 readable deltas, 2 clear the 0.0062 floor, 0 clear 0.015, 0 board seats, 11.25 card-hours spent, and ramp_dense_gate reads -0.0055 in the champion's dense corner, which is the transfer test that family was built for). GAIN: P(clears 0.015 vs base224 0.8509) ~0.15 — A-BV says the transferable part is representation not head, so a gain is not capped at the ACL column, but MRNet's 1248 exams are far under the scale where deep features become reusable and the DINOv2 init is already strong. P(clears the 0.0062 floor) ~0.40. P(negative, the orthofoundation-L result at a thousandth of the data) ~0.25. Worth it at this ratio because it is the ONLY untried member of the external-data family, which is the largest published lever at this plateau (+0.087 ACL in Bien 2018, +3.5% cross-dataset in Liu 2024), and because a flat result is INFORMATIVE here: it localises the failure to scale, which the merged corpus can then test without a rethink.
2026-09-20T01:58Z READ, AND IT IS A NULL — the arms ran on 2026-09-03 and nobody closed the bead.

EVIDENCE, from the artefacts and not from prose:
- stage one: D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/mrnet_acl_pretrain_s2026.metrics.1.jsonl, Sep 3 00:20, 8 epochs, loss 1.1177 -> 1.0741 -> 0.9489 -> 0.8639 -> 0.7586 -> 0.6479 -> 0.5726 -> 0.5153. It LEARNED. (auc nan and per_label {} every epoch: the mrnet scheme holds out nothing scoreable in our label space, so the kept epoch is ranked by index. For a pretrain that is the right behaviour — the final trunk is what stage two wants.)
- stage two: mrnet_warm_s2026.full.log, Sep 3 05:12. The recipe line proves the mechanism FIRED rather than assuming it: "init": "D:\models\rsna_knee_abnormality\mrnet_acl_pretrain_s2026.pt", "init_scope": "trunk", "scheme": "canonical", "labels": report_labels_v2.csv, 12 epochs.
- RESULT: best holdout mean AUC 0.8487 (epoch 10 reads 0.8452, epoch 11 0.8446). Control base224 = 0.8509. DELTA -0.0022, inside the 0.0062 paired floor. Not a regression, not a gain — a null.

WHAT IT CLOSES. The SEQUENTIAL cross-corpus transfer, which was the family's last untried member and the one the merged-corpus null could not speak to. Both shapes are now read and both are flat.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE, and this is the part that keeps external data alive. The pre-registered refutation clause said a flat result 'localises the failure to scale'. It does, and the scale arithmetic is decisive against THIS corpus specifically rather than against the axis: MRNet is 1248 exams and ours is 1763, so the foreign corpus is SMALLER than the one it was meant to supplement, and it was supplied in a FOREIGN label space (one column, ACL) through the trunk alone. half_data's slope says 1763 -> 3526 studies buys ~0.020; nothing in this pair ever delivered studies in OUR label space, so it never tested that slope. A corpus that could is still the largest open lever; MRNet is simply not one.

HARNESS GAP, recorded because it cost a card and nearly cost forty minutes. reading_check --only mrnet_acl_pretrain PASSED clean today — 'no declared reading is on disk yet' — and the arm re-launched. It passed because the 355 GB cleanup deleted stage one's checkpoint and holdout artefacts, while the READING survived only inside stage two's full.log. So the --only guard asserts 'this arm's declared artefacts are absent', and a deleted artefact is indistinguishable from an unrun arm. The cheap fix is to key the guard on the arm's LEDGER ROW as well as its files.

title: fastMRI+ BOX GEOMETRY is read and discarded at fastmri_corpus.py:391
description: CORRECTED 2026-09-02 after audit. The earlier framing (fastMRI+ as a new corpus) was wrong: core/data/corpus/fastmri_corpus.py is 423 lines, already adapts this corpus, and its own docstring already states the coronal plane, the grading, and that ACL and MCL are the only two findings supervised on BOTH sides. The 89 GB is already on disk (fetch completed 2026-09-02T01:06Z, 973 train + 199 val studies extracted) and the decode is running. WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNEXPLOITED, verified in code: line 388 reads Annotations/knee.csv, line 391 does groupby(FILE_COLUMN) and keeps only the SET OF TERMS boxed per study. The x, y, width, height columns - 16,167 box coordinates - are read and thrown away. Line 211 says so outright: 'fastMRI+ boxes carry a width and height and the spacing is known, so that threshold is computable - and it is not computed here.' TWO SEPARATE USES, and they should not be confused. (a) AREA THRESHOLD: our OA criteria require a moderate/large area ~1 cm+; box w*h with known spacing makes that computable, which turns some current unlabelled rows into confident labels. Cheap, no new loss. (b) AUXILIARY SPATIAL SUPERVISION: a localization head trained on the boxes, the axis Kimi's Q-BP found in 9 of 9 top solutions and that RSNA 2023 1st quotes at +0.01-0.03 per model. (b) is the one that could clear the 0.008 gap; (a) is nearly free and should be measured first. Blocked on Q-BT (licence + which auxiliary-loss formulation carried the delta, and whether published setups had boxes on the SAME studies they were scored on - if so it does not transfer).
notes:
PARTLY ANSWERED 2026-09-11, by geometry rather than by the area threshold this bead proposed. See knee-586q2 for the full working. The box coordinates are no longer read and discarded: FastmriCorpus.straddled() uses centre-x against a measured trough at 165.0 to locate a coarse term to both compartments, which converts Medial and Lateral Meniscus from zero positives to 190 each. The AREA route this bead names is still unrun and still the only path to positives on the cartilage and bone-injury columns, where the compartment rule fires on 15 and 24 studies and is therefore declined.
2026-09-14 (knee-vgz5b.1 audit): full box geometry now decoded by overlay. knee.csv 16,167 rows = 16,154 with geometry + 13 study-level (NaN). Boxes are drawn on the UP/DOWN-FLIPPED image (README), confirmed by overlay on reconstruction_esc AND _rss (identical geometry): unflipped, a Meniscus Tear box lands inside the femoral condyle; flipped, it sits on the meniscus, and an ACL High Grade box sits in the notch. So native h5 row = matrix - y - height; x is untouched, which means straddled()/COMPARTMENT_TROUGH (x-only) was never affected by the flip. y range -1..280, height 0..228 (zero-height boxes exist). The AREA route stays unrun; knee-vgz5b.1 writes the per-box table it needs.

title: Frozen radnet121 outreads the incumbent trunk under a trained head, not just a ridge probe
description:
Cheap gate before spending card hours on radnet_frozen.sh. head_trial over the CACHED features (CPU, minutes, no card time), matched geometry 336px/12sl/r256, pool cls_mean_focal, slice-read max:

  radnet121  slot-pooling attend, 20ep -> 0.7800
  radnet121  slot-pooling mean,   30ep -> 0.7841
  v3large    slot-pooling attend, 20ep -> 0.7726   (CONTROL, identical flags)

The absolute numbers are the frozen-cache-head ceiling, ~0.06 under the ridge probe on the same features (radnet 0.8197 / v3large 0.8046) and far under the 0.8459 seat bar - a head over a cached mean-reduced feature stack is not the training pipeline. The MATCHED reading is the point: radnet121 beats the incumbent trunk by +0.007 to +0.012 here, preserving the probe ordering (+0.015). So the probe's ordering is not an artefact of ridge-on-mean-features, and radnet_frozen.sh is worth card hours.

  MCL               0.8106 -> 0.8162  +0.0056
  Medial Meniscus   0.9083 -> 0.9083  -0.0000
  Lateral Meniscus  0.8704 -> 0.8727  +0.0023
  Medial OA         0.8870 -> 0.8924  +0.0054
  Lateral OA        0.8262 -> 0.8419  +0.0158
  PF OA             0.8665 -> 0.8653  -0.0012

title: Two written conclusions rest on truncated runs (vit_in21k, stack_increments_fx)
description:
convergence_check 2026-09-02 15:00Z: vit_in21k_s2026 best e4 of 5 run, 12 asked. stack_increments_fx_s2026 best e4 of 5 run, 12 asked. Both scores are FLOORS, not the recipes' numbers.

CONSEQUENCE 1 - the supervised-ImageNet trunk lane. interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-01_q6_untried_encoder_families.md closes the lane citing ViT IN-21k 0.8274 and Swin IN-22k 0.8331. The ViT number is a 5-of-12-epoch floor. Median e3->peak gain across 12-epoch runs is +0.0210 (p90 +0.0380, n=96), so the recipe's number plausibly lands 0.848-0.865 against a non-DINOv2 seat bar of 0.8521. The lane was closed on a killed process. This is the second half of the trunk-family lever the standing brief calls the only open lever that could deliver 1.5%.

CONSEQUENCE 2 - the label lane. experiments/README.md prices stack_increments_base 0.8635 vs stack_increments_fx 0.8595 = -0.0040. The fx side ran 4 of 12 epochs, so the delta is not real; the true gap is smaller or reversed.

FIX: rerun both at full 12-epoch budget. stack_increments_fx already has a live parked watcher. vit_in21k needs queueing. Neither number may be quoted again until it converges.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-02, and HALF OF IT WAS MY ERROR.

stack_increments_fx — THE BEAD WAS WRONG. There are TWO runs on disk:
  stack_increments_fx_s2026_run1.pt + .metrics.1.jsonl  -> 13 rows, epochs 0-11, COMPLETE
  stack_increments_fx_s2026.partial + .metrics.jsonl    ->  6 rows, epochs 0-4,  DIED
run1 is the same shape as its control (stack_increments_base_s2026.metrics.jsonl, 13 rows, epochs 0-11),
which is what the ledger reports at 0.8595 vs base 0.8635. The label lane's -0.0040 rests on a COMPLETE
run and needs no re-run. What convergence_check reads as truncated is the DIED RERUN, whose .partial is
timestamped at the moment crop160_span took the card. I read the check's output without asking which run
it was describing.

Consequence beyond the bead: a watcher (pid 387827 -> 388958) was parked on the card to re-run fx when it
freed, i.e. to spend ~40 min reproducing a number already in experiments/README.md. Killed 15:24Z, reason
written into logs/after_stack_increments_fx.log.

vit_in21k — the truncation was REAL (best e4 of 5, 12 asked; vit_in21k_s2026.pt is not on disk at all, the
number survives only in metrics.jsonl) but the conclusion it supported is now closed on MECHANISM instead,
so no re-run is owed. Kimi Q-BB: Mueller-Franzes et al. 2025 (Sci Rep, arXiv:2411.15802) compare MST-DINOv2
against MST-ResNet at matched architecture and matched budget on MRNet KNEE MRI and report 0.85 vs 0.78 --
a 0.07 gap against our 0.068. And our own swin_supervised_s2026 sits at 0.8331, 0.018 off DINOv2-B, so
supervised-ImageNet pretraining is not what fails; that ViT B/16 IN-21k checkpoint is. Recorded in
interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_the-non-dino-lane-is-quality-bound.md.

STANDING LESSON, which is the part worth keeping: convergence_check names a RUN, not an ARM. When a member
has been run more than once the check can describe a different run than the ledger does, and the two will
disagree without either being wrong. Ask which file it read before treating its verdict as being about the
experiment.

title: MCL and Fracture are the floor of every member on disk — is MCL clipped by the 130mm crop?
description:
seat_profile over 15 members (logs/seat_profile_13.log, 2026-09-02): MCL is the WEAKEST label for 12 of 15 members (0.7760-0.8041) and Fracture for the other 3. Per-finding leaders: MCL 0.8253 (merged_blend), Fracture 0.8214 (calib_dense_hold) - the two lowest leaders of twelve. Lateral Meniscus has the widest spread, 0.0673.

Also refutes a hypothesis of mine cheaply: the four trade-shape members killed on their mean (focal_dense, cover_labelwise, band_density, stack224) lead NOTHING. focal_dense's Lateral Meniscus 0.856 was a gain over its own control band_dense, but the pool leader is 0.8700. So they cannot raise the per-label routing oracle; they could only pay through decorrelation, which is the axis with seven board flats.

MECHANISM UNDER TEST: crop80_span's two biggest per-label losses were MCL -0.0265* and ACL -0.0263*, and the ledger names them 'exactly the structures at the field margins'. title: Q-AW — what slice-level feature is orthogonal to our saturated competence axis?
description: Literature answer to Claude's refined question: with sequence/plane fusion and pooling already built and measured, is there any published evidence that changing what a single 2D slice encodes (resolution/receptive field, MRI-specific pretraining, or localization supervision) moves a knee-MRI multi-label AUC by >=0.010.
notes:
See knee-8ec1 (Q-AV) for the broader mechanism table. This bead focuses on the slice-representation question only.
2026-09-02T1930Z Kimi — Q-AW literature answer (refined version)

Question: with sequence/plane fusion, coverage, per-finding pooling, and trunk swaps already measured as saturated, is there published evidence that changing what a single 2D slice encodes moves a knee-MRI multi-label AUC by ≥0.010?  Claude suspects three axes: (1) resolution / lesion-scale crop, (2) MRI-specific pretraining, (3) localization supervision.

Short answer
A straight ≥0.010 gain from any one of those three, on a multi-label knee-MRI task, is **not documented in the literature I can access**.  The strongest documented effect is not in the feature vector itself but in how it is read out: patch-local / attention-based readouts can recover signal that global pooling hides.  If the single-slice representation already contains the finding, the lever is readout, not a better encoder.

1. Resolution / lesion-scale crop
- Public RSNA solutions that score 0.906–0.924 operate at whole-knee crops of 130–140 mm resized to 336–384 px (Dread Development CoAtNet: 140 mm / 336 px + 384 px backbone; prvsiyan notebook: 130 mm crop).  Those effective pitches (≈0.37–0.46 mm/pixel) already satisfy the Nyquist limit for a 1 mm meniscal tear or fracture line.
- I found no published knee-MRI classification ablation that isolates native-resolution input or a lesion-scale crop and reports a ≥0.010 multi-label AUC gain.  Most meniscal-tear papers report AUCs in the 0.84–0.97 range but vary dataset, task, and trunk together, so the resolution contribution is confounded.
- Verdict: the project is already operating at or near the literature's effective-resolution frontier.  There is no documented 0.010 bump waiting on more pixels per slice.

2. MRI-specific / knee-specific pretraining
- **OrthoFoundation-L** (knee-specific DINOv3-L continuation on 1.25M knee images) is the strongest 2D candidate.  In this project it **lost** to its own control: `ortho_dense_s2026` 0.8452 vs DINOv2-base control 0.8502; frozen probe OrthoFoundation-L 0.7387 vs DINOv2-L 0.7852 and DINOv3-L 0.7446 (`research/2026-09-02_sota_pretrained_knee_mri_models_2025_2026.md`).  That is a **negative** result for 2D knee continuation.
- **RadImageNet DenseNet** was tried and "closed the lane empty" per Claude's own ledger.
- **OrthoDiffusion** (3D diffusion on 15,948 knee MRIs, macro AUROC 0.908 on 8 labels) is a different modality — 3D, not a 2D slice feature.  It is untested in this pool and is the only remaining knee-specific pretraining candidate with a published number.
- **MRI-CORE** (general MRI SAM-based) and **Radio DINO** (radiology-domain DINOv2) exist but have no documented knee multi-label number ≥ the current pool.
- Verdict: no published 2D knee-MRI pretrained encoder shows a ≥0.010 gain over ImageNet/DINO in this competition's setting.  The only untested lever is OrthoDiffusion's 3D diffusion backbone, which is a volume-level rather than slice-level change.

3. Localization supervision changing the feature (box / mask / slice index)
- Mask R-CNN / detection frameworks for meniscus tears reach AUC ~0.90, but they are trained to localize and classify a single finding; they do not report that the localization task improves a **shared multi-label feature vector** by ≥0.010.
- CoPAS (Qiu et al., Nature Comm 2024) uses CAM/Grad-CAM++ for interpretability and finds that attention aligns with clinical plane preferences, but the gains are attributed to co-plane attention and multi-task learning, not to localization labels changing the encoder.
- OrthoDiffusion's segmentation pretraining is on unlabeled data via diffusion; the segmentation head is added at fine-tuning, and there is no ablation showing that segmentation supervision changes the classification feature vector by ≥0.010.
- Verdict: localization supervision is useful for interpretability and single-lesion detection, but I found no evidence it changes the slice-level feature vector enough to close a 0.008 gap in multi-label classification.

The real literature gap: readout, not feature
- Muthyala et al. 2026 (*Frozen Foundation-Model Embeddings Discard Small-Lesion Signal in Chest Radiography*, arXiv:2606.11606) shows that the same frozen ViT trunk goes from AUC ~0.50 (CLS) to ~1.0 (patch-local readout) on small lesions.  The feature vector already contains the signal; global pooling throws it away.
- AnyMC3D (Liu et al. 2026, arXiv:2512.12887) reports +0.016 AUC on the same frozen DINOv3 backbone by replacing max/avg pooling with query-based attention pooling over slice embeddings, and up to +0.11 AUC in an earlier setup.  Again, the trunk is unchanged; the readout is what moves.
- This project's own `trunk_vs_readout` analysis (bead knee-? / `research/2026-09-02_trunk_vs_readout_quality_medical_volumes_qal.md`) flagged the same thing: DINOv3-L underperforming DINOv2-L on a frozen max-pooled ridge probe is likely a readout mismatch, not a weaker trunk.

Implications for the 0.944→0.952 gap
- The literature does not offer a slice-level feature trick that buys 0.010.  The documented separator is readout quality (attention over slice embeddings, patch-local pooling) and, at the whole-system level, label quality + ensemble diversity.
- If the current pool's slice representations already encode the findings, the remaining move is to build a better readout that uses those representations, not to chase a magic encoder or resolution.
- The one orthogonal trunk candidate that remains untested is **OrthoDiffusion** (3D diffusion backbone).  It is a volume-level input axis, not a slice feature axis, and should be gated by the same cheap probe as any other trunk.

title: Q-AV — mechanisms separating 0.944 from 0.952 in knee MRI classification
description: Literature answer to Claude's question: in published knee-MRI work and the current RSNA Kaggle leaderboard, what mechanisms carry the last ~0.008 AUROC once ensemble construction and trunk swaps within reach appear saturated.
notes:
See research/ and Kaggle kernels pulled 2026-09-02 for primary evidence.
2026-09-02T1900Z Kimi — Q-AV literature answer

Question: once ensemble construction and trunk swaps inside our reach look saturated, what mechanisms carry the last ~0.008 AUROC from a 0.944-class ensemble to the 0.952-class leader?

Primary sources inspected
- Howard P. Chen, "Learning AI From Radiology's Messy Middle" (Aug 2026) — https://blog.howardpchen.com/2026/08/learning-ai-from-radiologys-messy-middle/
- Kaggle kernels (pulled 2026-09-02):
  - dreaddevelopment/knee-mri-twelve-findings-from-a-single-model
  - prvsiyan/rsna-knee-read-the-report-then-the-knee
  - mattiaangeli/bend-the-knee-to-dinov3-ensembled
  - romantamrazov/rsna-knee-dinosaur-v4
- Qiu et al., "Learning co-plane attention across MRI sequences for diagnosing twelve types of knee abnormalities", Nature Communications 2024 — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51888-4
- Lan et al., OrthoDiffusion, arXiv:2602.20752 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20752

Bottom line
The 0.951 public-leaderboard top is only ~0.007 above our 0.944 cluster, and the public notebooks that document their mechanics stop around 0.906–0.924.  The gap is therefore not one trick; it is the compound of (1) better report-derived targets, (2) stronger single models trained on those targets, (3) per-finding specialists, and (4) rank-aware ensembling.  Trunk identity (DINOv2/v3, CoAtNet, EfficientNet-B3, RadImageNet) is a tunable choice, not the decisive axis.

Mechanism table — documented solutions

| Source / solution | Task / corpus | Reported metric | Baseline it beat | Mechanism credited for the gain | Category |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dread Development, "twelve findings from a single model" | RSNA Knee Abnormality Detection, 12-label MRI | 0.924 public LB; 0.9054 on 58-study gate vs incumbent 0.8923 | Same CoAtNet on smaller 3,155-study corpus | Corpus expansion: LLM-derived soft labels from 4,349 reports; report confidence as sample weights; 64-slice fixed slots; physical 140 mm crop; per-finding attention over slots; laterality normalisation | EXTRA DATA + DECODE + LOSS/attention |
| prvsiyan, "read the report, then the knee" | RSNA, 12-label MRI | 0.906 verified public (rank blend) | Pilkwang 20-member DINOv2 ensemble 0.891 | Rank (not probability) averaging because metric is AUC; multi-reader soft-label fusion with per-finding reader weights; per-finding slot attention; report-hash split to avoid duplicate-report leakage | ENSEMBLE construction + LABEL quality + DECODE |
| mattiaangeli, "Bend the Knee to DinoV3" | RSNA, 12-label MRI | ~0.89–0.91 public | 20-model DINOv2 rank mean | Adding DINOv3 ViT-S/16; series-type embeddings; cross-attention over all series tokens per finding; RadImageNet ResNet-50 rank vote | TRUNK + ENSEMBLE + attention fusion |
| Yash Bishnoi reference in prvsiyan notebook | RSNA, 12-label MRI | 0.903 public | Same EfficientNet-B3 on hard labels | Locally-run Qwen3.6-35B report reader; three-source reader fusion weighted per-finding by measured accuracy; careful handling of synovitis / fracture / effusion wording | LABEL quality |
| Qiu et al. CoPAS, Nature Comm 2024 | Internal 5-center 12-label knee MRI | Mean AUC-ROC 0.812 vs MRNet/MPFuseNet/ELNet lower | MRNet-style per-plane CNN | Co-plane attention across sagittal/coronal/axial; cross-sequence attention (PDW+T1W+T2W); plane-aware probability matrix; multi-task learning; focal loss | AUXILIARY/attention + DECODE + LOSS |
| Lan et al. OrthoDiffusion 2026 | 8-label knee MRI, multi-center | 0.908 macro AUROC | 3D U-Net / 3D ResNet-18 supervised | 3D diffusion self-supervised pretraining on 15,948 knee MRIs; orientation-specific backbones; bottleneck diffusion features at task-selected timesteps; SAP pooling; multi-plane fusion | TRUNK (pretraining) + DECODE |
| Bien et al. MRNet 2018 | MRNet 3-label knee MRI | ~0.93 AUC ACL/meniscus | AlexNet-style single-plane | Three-plane CNN + max-pooling of per-plane predictions; ImageNet pretraining | DECODE/ensemble (multi-view) |

What 0.952 looks like from the inside
- Public leaderboard top was 0.951 as of 17 Aug 2026 (Chen blog).  No public writeup claims that exact number, but the visible pieces that approach it are:
  - A single strong model already scores 0.924 (Dread CoAtNet).
  - A rank-mean blend of many strong singles pushes into the 0.93s publicly.
  - The last ~0.01–0.02 therefore likely comes from (a) more models of that quality, (b) better labels feeding them, and (c) per-finding specialists for the rare labels (Fracture, Synovitis, Lateral OA, Baker's) that most easily sit near chance.
- The mechanism is therefore not "a different trunk" in isolation; it is the quality of the targets and the diversity of strong learners that consume them.

Q-AV.1 — auxiliary segmentation specifically
- CoPAS uses co-plane attention and multi-task learning, but its ablations show single-task networks sometimes beat the multi-task variant for a given finding; negative transfer is real.
- OrthoDiffusion pretrains on unlabeled knee MRI and reports 0.908 on 8 labels with 10% labels, but the gain is from self-supervised pretraining, not from an auxiliary segmentation task on top of a frozen DINO-grade trunk.
- Public RSNA solutions do not credit segmentation auxiliary tasks for their gains.  The SKM-TEA masks we hold locally are the only near-term segmentation lever, and the cross-corpus gain is unproven (see bead knee-9h0p / knee-xhhj).
- Verdict: auxiliary segmentation is not a documented separator at the 0.95 level in this competition, and most published gains are over weaker CNN trunks or in same-corpus settings.

Implications for our pool
1. Do not spend slots rearranging the same members — the ensemble axis is saturated at ~0.944.
2. The cheapest high-lever is label quality: improve the report reader, use soft targets, weight by per-finding confidence, and fuse multiple readers with per-finding weights.
3. The next lever is stronger single models trained on those improved targets, with careful input-side contracts (DICOM geometric ordering, laterality normalisation, physical crop, resolution matched to anatomy).
4. Per-finding specialists (Synovitis, Fracture, Lateral OA/Meniscus) are underpriced relative to trunk swaps.
5. External-data pretraining (OrthoDiffusion, Rijeka, MRNet) should be gated by a cheap encoder probe against our DINOv2/DINOv3 controls before any multi-day arm.

title: Implement remembered AUC-margin objective for rare labels
description: MarginObjective drops a label whenever the batch lacks both a positive and a negative (Fracture skipped ~half the steps at batch 12). Add a RememberedMargin variant that pools positive/negative statistics across the last N steps using PairMemory, gradient flowing only through the live batch. Smoke against a small dense control before spending a full arm.
notes:
2026-09-02T1750Z Kimi: implemented in kneemri/training/remembered_margin.py. RunSetup dispatches --auc-margin + --pair-memory to RememberedMargin; --auc-margin alone still uses MarginObjective. Unit tests added/updated in tests/unit/kneemri/training/remembered_margin.py and run_setup.py. Full training unit-test suite passes (308 passed). Next step is a smoked arm against calib_dense_hold or a small dense control to measure the rare-label gain.
PREMISE REFUTED ARITHMETICALLY 2026-09-20, card-free. The bead motivates RememberedMargin by 'Fracture skipped ~half the steps at batch 12'. Fracture's holdout prevalence is 0.245 (223 positives of 909), so P(a batch of 12 holds no positive) = 0.755^12 = 0.034 and P(no negative) ~ 0. MarginObjective drops it from 3.4% of steps, NOT half. No label in the set is rare: the twelve prevalences run 0.229 (MCL) to 0.514 (Effusion). The lever's ceiling is repairing 3.4% of steps for one label of twelve, which cannot approach the +0.0073 champion bar (knee-f8nwd).

The CODE is fine and stays: kneemri/training/remembered_margin.py ships, RunSetup dispatches it, 308 tests pass. What dies is the motivation, so the smoked arm this bead asks for is not worth a card slot. Re-open only if an operating point with a genuinely rare label appears (batch 2 would make the skip 57%, and some arms do run --batch 2 --accumulate 4 -- that is the one configuration where the mechanism is live, and it is worth stating before anyone re-derives it).

A fourth reading was added to study_attribution to settle which mechanism it is: the UNK rate over the same negative cells. UNK carries value 0.28 (the corpus base rate) while NO carries 0.08, and both binarise to a negative label, so the truth array cannot tell them apart. MECHANISM: the tail is the studies whose negative cells were never READ -- trained against a soft 0.28 and scored against a hard 0, so they are simultaneously under-supervised and measured on the weakest part of the ruler. This is NOT the confident-error defect knee-teh4 targets (that one is confidently-WRONG cells); it is the cells with no read at all, and the two are disjoint populations.
