title: Level 2 of the error question: WHICH studies does the champion get wrong, and is it the model or the label?
description:
Owner question 2026-09-02: 'take our best model/ensemble - what is the share of the pathologies it gets wrong? whats most wrong? why - loss or not well enough balanced data? thats level 1 - share. level 2 is which studies are those specifically and why did we get them?'

LEVEL 1 IS ANSWERED AND CLOSED - knee-q1pf, weights_gap.py, 2026-08-23. Absolute per-label AUCs of the champion on the 909 fold-0 holdout: MCL 0.7423 is the weakest column, Fracture 0.7827 second. But we BEAT the twenty published CC0 members on ten of twelve labels, so the demonstrated headroom in the weak columns is (0.0346+0.0167)/12 = +0.0043 on the mean - a quarter of the bar and a CEILING, not an estimate. focus_mcl was cancelled on that arithmetic. So 'which pathology is most wrong' does not convert into a lever, and neither of the owner's two proposed causes (loss, data balance) survives: a model that leads the field on ten of twelve columns is not mis-balanced.

LEVEL 2 HAS NEVER BEEN DONE. Nothing in kneemri/evaluation/ ranks individual holdout STUDIES by error. label_errors.py is the nearest neighbour and answers a different question - which cells the READER got wrong (confident learning over out-of-fold probabilities), not which studies the MODEL gets wrong.

WHY LEVEL 2 IS THE INTERESTING HALF, and it is a reason level 1 cannot see. The owner offers two causes; there is a third. reader_agreement.errors counts 108 confident false positives against 32 misses over the 58 radiologist-annotated studies, and the holdout truth is report-derived like the training labels. So a study we 'get wrong' may be one where the extractor is wrong and we are right. If the worst-scored studies overlap the extractor-vs-gold disagreements, the per-label numbers in knee-q1pf are measured against partly-bad truth and the weak-column reading is a fact about the RULER.

THE INSTRUMENT. Rank the 909 holdout studies by per-study contribution to the loss (and per-cell residual against the graded truth), then cross-tabulate the worst tail against covariates the repo already computes: extractor-vs-gold disagreement where the gold exists (58 studies), slot availability and sequence match (the 78.7% Fluid_Sensitive rate), laterality, band coverage, n_positives per study, and per-label residual. Read: is the tail explained by acquisition (a plumbing defect, fixable), by label disagreement (a ruler defect, feeds knee-m5jf), or by nothing measurable (genuinely hard studies, and the axis closes).

COSTS ZERO CARD AND ZERO SLOTS - the champion's holdout predictions are already on disk. Runs alongside any arm.

PRE-REGISTERED so this cannot become number-watching: state before running which covariate is expected to carry the tail. Prediction is LABEL DISAGREEMENT over acquisition, because the acquisition axis has been swept (crop, band, span, slots) and the label axis has not. If acquisition carries it instead, that is the more actionable answer and the prediction was wrong.

RELATES: knee-q1pf (level 1, closed), knee-m5jf (P1 label correction, the live consumer of a positive result), knee-teh4 (hedged-negation parser fix comes first in that thread).
notes: First reading, calib_dense_hold_s2026 e6, n=909. Mean per-study damage 0.1366 = 1 - 0.8634, the member's own AUC: the decomposition is exact, not a proxy. Tail = worst 10% (90 studies). Tail carries MORE positives (4.37 vs 3.59), so the worst studies are not the empty ones. Direction split (per-cell means, not sums -- a sum calls everyone over-ranked on the 8.4-vs-3.6 class sizes alone): tail 76/90 = 84% over-ranked vs body 492/819 = 60%. The tail is enriched +24 points in the OVER direction, which is the report extractor's known dominant error shape (108 confident false positives vs 32 misses on the 58 gold studies). PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION (label disagreement over acquisition) SURVIVES ITS FIRST TEST but is NOT confirmed: only 13 gold studies land in a fold-0 holdout, 4 in the tail, and GOLD_FLOOR=30 makes the tool refuse to quote a gold rate on that denominator. Confirming needs either the hedged-negation parser fix (knee-teh4) widening gold, or an out-of-fold prediction over all 4407 so the whole gold set is scoreable.

title: Q-AP — adjudication protocol and the 58-gold pricing
description:
Claude follow-up to Q-AO. Need three pieces of evidence to price the label-correction axis:

1. RSNA challenge adjudication protocol for this competition: how many radiologists, reading what, disagreement resolution. 'Not stated' is a valid answer.
2. Published case where training labels are report-derived and test labels are radiologist-adjudicated, with measured AUROC gain from correcting training labels.
3. Competition metric definition (macro AUC over 12 findings?) quoted from official source.

Output: research/ note with numbers, denominators and sources.
notes: 2026-09-02T0920Z: Research completed. Findings: RSNA test set annotated by expert radiologists (direct source); Kitamura 2024 gives general RSNA protocol (min 3 annotators, consensus) but no knee-specific reader count/consensus rule. Metric: macro AUC over 12 findings. Cross-standard published case: Jain 2021 is closest — better report labeler on report-derived CheXpert train labels → +0.04 AUROC on radiologist-annotated test set. No direct image-based correction case found. Output: research/2026-09-02_qap_adjudication_protocol_and_58_gold_pricing.md.

title: Image-derived label SUSPICION as a per-cell weight, never an overwrite — gated on whether test labels are report-derived
description:
OWNER'S IDEA (2026-09-02), and the design constraint is the owner's too: do NOT overwrite labels. Add a correction SUSPICION, verify it a second time, and even then keep the original. That is not a compromise, it is the correct design here for two independent reasons.

WHY NON-DESTRUCTIVE IS RIGHT, MECHANICALLY. weight_floor already implements a per-cell loss weight (0.25 + 0.75*conf), so a suspicion score enters as a weight MULTIPLIER and needs no new training path. The label survives and merely pulls less. And report_labels_v2.csv is simultaneously the EVALUATION RULER (--eval-labels pins it); overwriting it moves the scoreboard under the experiment, which is exactly what Supervision.moves_the_ruler() exists to catch. A new sidecar CSV of suspicions, joined at load, touches neither.

WHAT IS NEW HERE. Every label treatment tried so far reads the TEXT or the READER's self-report:
  blendlabels    three independent readers of the same reports   +0.0034
  confident224   drop the 14,445 UNK cells                       -0.0071
  errors_dense   prune the confident-learning flags              -0.0010 seat, pruning REFUTED
  calib_span     remap the five level values                     -0.0020, inverted
  finding_calib  per-finding offsets                             flat
Nothing has ever consulted the IMAGE. That is the virgin part of the axis, and the defect it targets is
measured and large: noise_binding finds 108 confident false positives over the 58 gold studies, ALL
verdict YES, 15.8% of every annotated cell, against 32 misses; supervision_gap reads 65.3% radiologist
agreement where the report says YES.

THE DESIGN. Not de novo labeling — 52,872 cells is out of reach and reading knee MRI from 336 px slices
is expert work. The tractable job is VERIFICATION OF PRE-FLAGGED CELLS: the confident-learning detector
(4.05x lift over a random flagger, already spent, commit f5e1f808) proposes ~5,360 candidate cells, and a
vision pass answers only the narrow binary 'is this flagged YES actually visible?'. Confirming a
candidate is a far easier task than reading blind, and it is the only shape at which the cell count is
tractable.

THE GATE THAT COMES FIRST, AND IT IS NOT A CARD GATE: knee-xxxx / Q-AO. If the COMPETITION's hidden test
labels are themselves report-extracted, then correcting a label toward what the image shows moves us
AWAY from the scored quantity — we would fix reality and lose points. experiments/README.md:2438 already
records the prediction that 'the board's labels come from the same reports ours do'. The same axis is
worth up to +0.02 or is NEGATIVE depending only on that one fact. Q-AO is with Kimi asking for the
competition's own words. Nothing is built until it returns.

FEASIBILITY CALIBRATION, cheap, runs whenever: read ~20 of the 58 gold studies as images, predict the
twelve findings, score against the radiologist annotations, and compare to the text extractor's own
accuracy on the same 20. If image reading cannot beat the extractor there, a VLM pipeline at scale will
not either and the axis closes for a few hundred images of cost. Pre-register the extractor's number on
those same 20 BEFORE looking, so the comparison is not fitted after the fact.

CHEAPER BRANCH THAT RUNS FIRST AND NEEDS NO IMAGES AND NO CARD: Q-AB found 55.9% of extractor-gold
disagreements are re-extractable CONSTRUCTION errors — 75 hedged negation ('no evidence of', 'ACL
intact'), 6 severity threshold. A parser fix for hedged negation addresses over half the known errors at
zero card and zero slots. knee-teh4's own note says the remaining branch is re-labeling / soft-relabeling
'ideally after parser fix for hedged negation (Q-AB)'. That ordering stands: parser fix, then re-read the
gap, then decide whether images are still needed.

SIZE, honestly. blendlabels bounds the text side at about +0.0034 and the ledger's verdict is that the
label lane is 'confirmed LIVE and confirmed SMALL, an order of magnitude short of the 1.5% bar'. The
image side is NOT bounded by that number, because a better reader of the same report cannot fix a report
that contradicts the picture — which is precisely why this is worth asking. But it inherits the same
suspicion, and Jain 2021 (+0.15 labeler F1 -> +0.04 AUROC on CheXpert) is the only published anchor.

Related: knee-teh4 (detector, IN_PROGRESS), knee-xhhj (segmentation as auxiliary supervision).
notes: GATE PARTLY LIFTED 2026-09-02. Q-AO answered: research/2026-09-02_test_labels_report_derived_or_radiologist_reviewed_qao.md. Hidden test labels are MOST LIKELY radiologist-adjudicated, not report-derived: RSNA's own Data-for-AI page says its ground-truth sets are 'triple-labeled by radiologists'; Kitamura 2024 (Radiology:AI) says bone-age TEST labels were averaged over six radiologist labelers; the Kaggle data tab offers report text for deriving labels for the remaining TRAINING studies only. No verbatim host statement about the test split was found, and the 'clinically adjudicated labels' phrase is a community post (discussion 733343), not a host reply. So this is preponderance, not proof. CONSEQUENCE: experiments/README.md:2438 ('the board's labels come from the same reports ours do') is an ASSUMPTION that the evidence now contradicts, and the own-goal risk that held this at P2 is reduced, not eliminated -- hence P1, not P0. The asymmetry matters: the extractor's error on the 58 gold studies is 108 confident false positives vs 32 misses, ALL verdict YES, 15.8 pct of annotated cells. Under an adjudicated test that is a systematic bias pointed AWAY from the metric on all 4349 report-labeled training studies; under a report-derived test it IS the metric. No card can separate them -- our only holdout is report-labeled too. Q-AP (sent 0910Z) asks for the adjudication PROTOCOL (how many readers, resolution rule) and for any published train-noisy/test-adjudicated experiment that MEASURES the correction gain, which is the number that prices this. Order unchanged: hedged-negation parser fix (75 of 134 disagreements, zero card, zero slot) FIRST, re-measure, then ask whether images are still needed.

title: Segmentation as AUXILIARY SUPERVISION, not as a crop: the spatial signal this model has never received
description:
THE ARGUMENT knee-t8e4 ASKED FOR, written before any disk is spent.

WHAT IS ABSENT. This project has never given the model a spatial supervision signal. All twelve targets are STUDY-LEVEL report labels: 'this knee has an ACL tear', never 'here'. experiments/README.md:1379 states the head attends over SLOTS and never a MASK, and that the feature vectors carry no localisation at all. Every localisation attempt to date was a PRIOR or a CROP, never a SIGNAL:
  - aprior_dense: the 12x6 anatomy table as an initialisation. 0.8557 vs 0.8578, washed out by epoch 0 (train loss matched to four decimals).
  - crop80_tissue: 80 mm about the TISSUE centre, i.e. point the model at the relevant pixels geometrically. 0.8345, -0.0112 vs whole_stack.
  - depth_regions, band_*: decode geometry, not supervision.
There is no seg head, no seg loss, no mask anywhere in kneemri/ or core/. Confirmed by grep 2026-09-02.

WHY THE MECHANISM IS NOT crop80's MECHANISM, and this is the whole case. crop80 REMOVED pixels on a geometric guess. An auxiliary segmentation head ADDS a gradient that forces PATCH TOKENS to encode where tissue is, changing what one slice's feature vector CONTAINS rather than which pixels reach it. attend_true's conclusion was that the slice-aggregation stage is saturated from both ends and 'the limit is upstream, in what one slice's feature vector contains'. This is a lever aimed exactly there. It also compounds with the open readout thread: our findings are 1-3 mm and --pool mean dilutes a small patch response; a trunk trained to segment has patch tokens that are spatially sharp by construction.

WHERE THE LABELS COME FROM. RSNA ships no masks, so segmentation can only enter through a foreign corpus. SKM-TEA carries expert cartilage and meniscus segmentations plus quantitative maps on knee MRI, and 19G / 154 tarballs are already on disk from the killed fetch. This is NOT the 'more external data' lever the dose curve closed (1 seat 0.944, 2 seats 0.944, 4 seats 0.943, 6 seats 0.940): the dose curve prices additional TRAINING ROWS OF THE SAME KIND. A segmentation mask is a different kind of supervision and no arm on the board prices it.

PRICING, stated before starting. Multi-day build: SKM-TEA decode adapter, seg head, multi-task arm. Published segmentation-auxiliary multi-task gains on small medical classification sets run +0.01 to +0.03; our board transfer coefficient is +0.74 to +0.83 (knee-ps8o), so +0.02 offline lands near +0.015 board against a 0.008 gap. That clears the bar, which makes it one of only two levers that plausibly can — and the trunk family just closed empty, so this being the front-runner by default is a reason for MORE scepticism, not less.

THE HONEST COUNTER-EVIDENCE, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a surprise: crop80_tissue is the nearest existing test of 'guide the model to the relevant pixels' and it lost 0.0112 on the mean (its ledger row does say the mean is the wrong read and the gate is per-label). aprior proved the head already recovers plane-level structure unaided. Four consecutive decode/head knobs returned nothing.

GATED ON Kimi's Q-AN: published numbers for segmentation-auxiliary multi-task on medical image CLASSIFICATION, with denominators, and specifically whether the gain survives when the seg masks come from a DIFFERENT corpus than the classification labels. If the literature only shows gains with same-corpus masks, this design is wrong and the axis needs a different entry point.

DISK: do not relaunch the SKM-TEA fetch until this is licensed. 91% full, 343G free, and a card arm that fills the disk dies without a traceback.
notes:
DISK BLOCKER MEASURED AND RETRACTED, 2026-09-02. This bead said '19G / 154 tarballs are already on disk' and 'do not relaunch the fetch, 91% full'. Both true of the DICOMs and neither true of the MASKS. fetch_skmtea.sh listed dicoms and segmentation_masks in one glob and the listing order puts dicoms first, so the killed run pulled 19 GB of images and ZERO masks: segmentation_masks/ was 0 bytes on this machine. The masks are 310 files at ~270 KB, ~84 MB total -- four orders of magnitude under the images. The disk objection was a fact about the image half applied to the mask half by association, and it parked a P1 for a reason that never applied to it. Script now takes a track argument (bash core/data/corpus/fetch_skmtea.sh segmentation_masks); masks fetched. THIS BEAD IS NO LONGER DATA-BLOCKED. It is blocked on Q-AN and only on Q-AN, which was itself never asked as a literature question -- restated to Kimi 2026-09-02T1235Z with the single discriminator that decides it: does the auxiliary-segmentation gain survive when the masks come from a DIFFERENT corpus than the classification labels.
2026-09-02T1630Z Kimi: Q-AN literature scan (preliminary). Direct cross-corpus auxiliary-segmentation-for-classification evidence is sparse. Same-corpus gains are strong and consistent (NeurIPS 2023 reframing paper: +2.6% to +10.0% AUROC on CANDID/ISIC/SPINE; HA-DLC 2026: segmentation loss raises tumour-classification AUC 0.623 to 0.650). Cross-corpus/cross-task evidence is indirect: SuPreM (segmentation pretrain on AbdomenAtlas 9,262 CT -> fine-grained pancreatic tumour classification) beats self-supervised init and halves annotation need; Foundation X (11 CXR datasets, some with only classification, some only segmentation) shows cross-dataset/cross-task transfer; MASS (auto-generated masks on 5K volumes -> frozen-encoder classification on unseen pathologies) matches supervised training. No paper found yet that trains one model with RSNA-like study-level labels plus SKM-TEA-like foreign masks and reports the classification gain. Conclusion so far: the axis is not refuted, but the published support is weaker than the +0.01-0.03 same-corpus number knee-xhhj used. A small cheap experiment (e.g., train a linear probe on SKM-TEA-mask-pretrained features vs. DINOv2 features) would buy more evidence than more literature. Q-AN.1 and Q-AN.2 also need answers from the same papers.
2026-09-02T1700Z Kimi Q-AN final verdict. The cross-corpus auxiliary-segmentation gain the bead priced at +0.01-0.03 is NOT well supported by direct literature. Most published gains are same-corpus. The strongest cross-corpus evidence (SuPreM, Foundation X, MASS) is pretraining-style transfer, not joint auxiliary supervision. Recommendation: do not launch the full SKM-TEA multi-day build until a cheap encoder probe shows that features pretrained on SKM-TEA masks beat the incumbent DINOv2 features on RSNA labels. If the probe is negative, decline or redesign the axis (e.g., use SKM-TEA only as pretraining data, not as a live auxiliary head). See knee-9h0p for the full table.

title: Q-Y: audit whether text/report supervision gains live in pretraining, auxiliary loss, or inference branch
description: Claude asked (2026-09-01_2250z) whether the literature's gains from report-supervised medical imaging belong to (a) contrastive image-text pretraining, (b) auxiliary text-alignment loss during supervised fine-tuning, or (c) a text branch at inference. The project's own experiment on (b) (cosine pull toward whole-report sentence embeddings) read -0.0063 monotone. Need a literature breakdown by mechanism and a recommendation on whether the axis is open, closed, or needs a different experiment.
notes:

title: Evaluate OrthoFoundation-L as a drop-in knee-MRI encoder init
description:
OrthoFoundation (arXiv:2601.18250, github.com/ytrsk/OrthoFoundation, MIT) is a 2026 DINOv3-L-based model continued with DINO-style SSL on 1.25M knee images (357k X-rays + 894k MRI slices), with released OrthoFoudation-L.pth weights. It reports ACL AUROC 0.9849, MCL 0.9334, cartilage lesion 0.9338, and is architecturally identical to the DINOv3-L backbone the project already uses. This makes it the strongest public knee-specific transfer source found so far, and a direct test of the 'strong init + in-domain SSL' mechanism.

This bead tracks whether it can be swapped in as an encoder init and whether it beats the existing DINOv3-L control. It is related to knee-ombx (external-data/supervised-pretraining), knee-vp8q (RAD-DINO control), and knee-8hn (DINOv3 licence/mount).
acceptance_criteria: A decision on whether to mount OrthoFoundation-L: (a) checkpoint loads through the existing DINOv3-L encoder path, (b) licence/Kaggle-shippability verified, (c) frozen or fine-tuned probe score compared to the current DINOv3-L baseline.
notes: PRICE (2026-09-02, required by knee-qxse): ~4 card-hours (12 epochs, 224 px x 12 slices, base224's read). EXPECTED GAIN: the pre-registered bands are >=0.8578 lane opens / >=0.8521 shippable seat / >=0.8502 matches control / below closes the in-domain trunk lane. P(clears 0.8521, the non-DINOv2 seat bar) ~ 0.3 and P(clears 0.8578) ~ 0.15, discounted because the FROZEN probe already reads ortholarge 0.7387 BELOW v3large 0.7446 and dinov2-large 0.7852 - the continuation did not help the features linearly, so the whole thesis rests on fine-tuning recovering what the probe cannot see. RATIO: 4 h for a ~30% shot at a shippable member on the one axis the pool has none of (architecture distance), plus a CLOSING reading on the low branch that retires external encoders entirely. Justified as much by the low branch as the high one: a sub-0.8502 result is worth having because it stops the project pricing external trunks, and that is an instrument value the high branch does not need to carry.

title: Q-U: does in-domain SSL continuation beat a strong init (DINOv2), not scratch?
description: Kimi's Q-T reply (2026-09-01T21:35Z) settles the knee-corpus transfer question with an honest null: no published knee->knee partial-label-overlap multi-label AUC delta exists. Evidence density is entirely form (d), external corpus as SSL substrate, which is the only form fastMRI can serve. BUT the strongest number (Zhang et al. 2024, fastMRI 10k unlabeled -> Stanford, 0.562 scratch -> 0.819 SSL) sits beside an ImageNet-init row at 0.824 - in-domain knee SSL TIED a generic supervised init and did not beat it. Our members initialise from DINOv2, a stronger init than ImageNet. Q-U asks for a measured continuation delta WITH the no-continuation control present, the corpus size at which it pays, whether the objective must match DINOv2's self-distillation, and the nearest honest negative. If the answer is no, this project has no measured route to 0.952 and that is what gets reported.
notes: Research completed: research/2026-09-02_fastmri_continuation_arithmetic.md. Key findings: (1) 35k single-coil slices sits below the 50k-300k low-data regime where in-domain SSL is shown to beat general pretraining (Konstantakos et al. 2025) and inside the regime where naive DINOv2 continuation collapses (dinov2#204). (2) OrthoFoundation shows positive continuation on 1.25M knee images incl 300k fastMRI slices, using DINOv3-L, batch 32, 4 A100s, AdamW cosine. (3) fastMRI ships RSS reconstructions; use those, not zero-filled IFFT. (4) OAI is larger and better matched than fastMRI/MRNet/SKM-TEA. Decision: do NOT arm a 35k fastMRI continuation; if ortho_dense clears, the next corpus should be OAI (or OAI+fastMRI), with forgetting safeguards.

title: Curriculum is a SCHEDULE, not a reweight — and the disagreement-schedule cell is empty
description:
Measured on our own corpus, 12 epochs each, same recipe:

  disagreed_full     static difficulty tilt      0.8471
  disagreed_uniform  matched control (bootstrap) 0.8507
  certainty_ramp     difficulty SCHEDULE         0.8584

A static tilt toward hard studies COSTS 0.0036. Ramping difficulty over training PAYS 0.0077, above
the 0.0062 holdout floor. That is the same shape Zhou et al. ISBI 2023 report on elbow-fracture X-ray
(+0.0245 binary AUC from a VoG-ordered curriculum, no human difficulty annotation), and it is the only
supervision-axis intervention with both a published AUC delta and a reproduction here.

The 2x2 has one empty cell. Difficulty has two available signals: label certainty (report confidence)
and ensemble disagreement (train_disagreement). Certainty x schedule pays. Disagreement x static costs.
Disagreement x schedule is untested, and it is the cell where the two signals disagree about WHICH
studies are hard: certainty is what the labeller felt, disagreement is what the models cannot resolve.

Both mechanisms already exist in the tree: Disagreed(spread, alpha) in kneemri/training/sampling.py
and trainer.ramp_certainty(). The arm is an alpha ramp over the disagreement weights rather than a
fixed alpha, so no new sampler is needed.

PRICE: ~1.5 h card at 12 epochs. P(clears control + floor, i.e. >= 0.8569) ~ 0.3 given the certainty
ramp cleared its own by 0.0077 and the published curriculum effect is 3x our floor. P(flat but
decorrelated, a seat on a supervision-space axis) ~ 0.4. The static arm is the control already on
disk, so no control arm runs.
notes: PRICE: ~1.5 h card, 12 epochs, no control arm (both controls on disk). P(clears disagreed_uniform + floor, >=0.8569) ~0.3: the certainty schedule cleared its own control by 0.0077 and the published curriculum effect (Zhou et al. +0.0245) is 4x our floor, but the static arm on this same signal LOST 0.0036, so the schedule has to recover that before it pays anything. P(flat-but-rescued, 0.8471-0.8569, seat candidate on error correlation) ~0.45. P(dead, <=0.8471, closes the difficulty row with a negative) ~0.25. Every branch fills a cell; the arm is a finding either way. Arm: experiments/arms/disagreed_ramp.sh

title: Explore true 3D CNN path for knee MRI (MRNet-style) vs tubelet transformers
description:
Owner flagged the MRNet project (https://stanfordmlgroup.github.io/projects/mrnet/) as a possible 3D exploration branch. The repo already ingests MRNet (1,248 ACL studies merged into merged3) and has a tubelet trunk via V-JEPA2-L, but has not tried a dedicated 3D convolutional architecture like MRNet's per-view 3D CNN + global max-pool + logistic regression ensemble.

Questions to answer:
1. What is MRNet's actual architecture and reported AUC on ACL/meniscus/abnormal?
2. Does the repo have everything needed to train an MRNet-style 3D CNN on our slices (canonical decode, labels, folds)?
3. How does a 3D CNN differ from the V-JEPA2 tubelet in terms of inductive bias, memory, and likely AUC?
4. What would a minimal arm cost (card-hours, mount feasibility)?
5. Is there a published 3D CNN result on knee MRI that beats the project's DINOv2-based 0.85x members?

Acceptance: a go/no-go decision with a cost estimate, or a concrete arm spec if go.
notes:
Initial literature pass 2026-09-01:
- MRNet (Bien et al. 2018, PLOS Med) architecture: AlexNet backbone, per-series 3D CNN treated as a volume, global max pool, logistic regression over 3 series.
- MRNet internal validation AUC: abnormal 0.937, ACL 0.965, meniscus 0.847 (1,370 exams).
- External Rijeka ACL: 0.824 zero-shot, 0.911 when trained on external data.
- Repo already has MRNet corpus (1,248 ACL studies in merged3) and a tubelet trunk (V-JEPA2-L, 0.8343 holdout), but no dedicated 3D conv CNN like MRNet.
- The user's instinct is valid: MRNet-style 3D CNN is a distinct branch from both 2D slice transformers and tubelet transformers.
- Next step: decide whether to implement an MRNet-style arm or a modern 3D CNN (3D ResNet/I3D/nnUNet encoder) on our canonical cache.
Local inventory update: MRNet, Rijeka, fastMRI, SKM-TEA, KMAR-50K are on disk at D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/. fastMRI knee has 16k bbox annotations over 974 scans. See research/2026-09-02_external_knee_mri_data_access_audit.md section 9.
SOTA pretrained model survey: research/2026-09-02_sota_pretrained_knee_mri_models_2025_2026.md. Top actionable candidate: OrthoFoundation-L (knee-specific, weights released, MIT license).
2026-09-02T0925Z: Literature sweep updated. No public, knee-specific, large-scale 3D foundation model with weights has emerged since the last pass. MR-Transformer (DeiT-Ti, TKR-specific) is the strongest actionable 3D member template; SegmentAnyBone / SAM-Med3D / VISTA3D are segmentation-only. Recommendation remains: do not pursue full 3D volumetric model as main lever; cheapest experiment is MR-Transformer-based multi-label member on downsampled volumes if diversification is desired. See research/2026-09-02_modern_3d_knee_mri_models_beyond_mrnet.md.
2026-09-02T0930Z: Added Moorthy et al. 2026 (3D CSFA-UNet on OAI-ZIB) to survey; no public weights, segmentation+KL-grade task, not multi-label abnormality classification. Conclusion unchanged.
2026-09-02T0940Z: MAJOR UPDATE — found OrthoDiffusion (Lan et al. 2026), a public 3D diffusion foundation model for knee MRI with Kaggle weights, pretrained on 15,948 knee MRIs, reporting macro AUROC 0.908 on 8 knee abnormalities. This is the first public knee-specific multi-label 3D model with weights. Filed bead knee-6hfi for smoke experiment. research/2026-09-02_modern_3d_knee_mri_models_beyond_mrnet.md updated.

title: Slot dropout: withhold a PRESENT slot during training
description: First supervision-axis regulariser here. Fill rates: AX_FLUID_FS 100%, SAG_FLUID_FS 98%, COR_FLUID_FS 93%, SAG_FLUID_NOFS 55%, COR_T1 60%, SAG_T1 57% - nearly half of all studies reach inference with slots the model has only ever seen filled. SlotScheme.presence already MASKS an absent slot rather than zero-filling, so the gap is not misrepresentation, it is that absence was never in the training distribution. Precedent at its real strength: Grovik 2021 npj Digital Medicine held AUC exactly FLAT (0.989 vs 0.989) while Dice rose 0.021 and FP/patient fell 7.0->3.6; Chrysochoou 2026 npj Precision Oncology beat zero-fill and synthesis on every missing-sequence cell. Both are segmentation and the one paper measuring AUC measured no gain, so this is armed as a diversity/supervision lever, NOT a solo-score lever. Code wired through augmentation/trainer/options/run_setup/flag_vocabulary/landed; owes unit tests and an arm with pre-registered branches.
notes: PRICE: ~1.5 h of card at 12 epochs (band_dense's recipe, dropout is a mask multiply and adds no memory). P(clears the 0.0062 floor as a SOLO) ~0.15 - the only precedent that measures AUC (Grovik 2021) measured it exactly flat, 0.989 vs 0.989, so a solo gain is not what the mechanism predicts. P(the flat-and-decorrelated branch, i.e. error correlation against champion members below every incumbent pair) ~0.4. EXPECTED VALUE IS IN THE SECOND BRANCH, and it is why the arm is worth 1.5 h: every closed axis here (seating, combiner, pooling, count, serving, decode) is a DECODE-space axis, competence_axis reads 81.7-82% of what separates 105 members as one scalar, and a member taught to survive a withheld acquisition is the first candidate for leaving that axis. Ratio: 1.5 h against a ~40% chance of the first new seat MECHANISM since seating closed, versus ~15% of a directional solo number. Priced as an INSTRUMENT on the supervision axis, not as a score improvement.
close_reason:
Slot dropout WORKS and is the best single member the project owns: 0.8592, converged (convergence_check: 1 converged, peak e9 of a 12-epoch budget, not truncated).

Against the members it has to beat: band_dense 0.8578 (+0.0014), certainty_ramp 0.8584 (+0.0008), base224 0.8502 (+0.0090). Both of the first two are inside the 0.0062 holdout noise floor, so the honest reading is DIRECTIONAL at the top of the pool rather than a new ceiling - but it is directional in the right direction, free, and mechanism-sound: withholding a PRESENT slot during training forces the head to read evidence from the slots that remain instead of leaning on the one that happens to carry the finding, which is the same argument that makes dropout work anywhere and is not a reweight of the loss.

It joins the roster at 0.8592. What it does NOT do is open a lane: the member-quality lane ceilings near 0.943 as an ensemble against a leader at 0.952, and seven board flats close reweight/add/swap/count. A better member is worth having and is not worth a slot.

title: RadImageNet DenseNet-121: a domain-supervised CNN trunk needs a non-AutoModel load path
description:
Every encoder in the registry loads through AutoModel.from_pretrained, so a trunk shipped as a bare state_dict has no load path. RadImageNet DenseNet-121 is the best-precedented candidate for the trunk-family axis (Nilay et al. report +0.031 from a cross-family ensemble containing it), and it is the empty cell on our pretraining grid: every trunk we own is either self-supervised (DINOv2/v3, ConvNeXtV2-FCMAE, V-JEPA2, RAD-DINO) or supervised on natural images (Swin IN-22k). None is supervised on medical images.

Measured 2026-09-01: the Lab-Rasool/RadImageNet HF mirror ships DenseNet121.pt as an OrderedDict of 725 keys prefixed backbone.0., which strip to a strict load into torchvision densenet121().features - 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 shape mismatch, 7.04M params, and (1,1024,14,14) out of a 448px read. Stride 32, dim 1024: the same output contract ConvNeXt-base and Swin-base already satisfy, so TrunkAsTokens.from_map applies unchanged. The Google-Drive plumbing Kimi priced at multiple hours is not needed.

Open: the input normalization RadImageNet trained under is unverified (asked as Q-L2), and the licence for a Kaggle mirror is unresolved (Q-L1) - a local arm needs neither, a submission needs both.
notes: VRAM measured 2026-09-01: at matched flags vram_need prices convnextv2-base (cnxbase) at 14443 MiB and radnet121 at 40880 MiB -- above the whole 32 GB card. arm_smoke refused the arm as written: 'NO ROOM radnet_family: card had no room: needs 40880 MiB, 30991 MiB free'. Dense connectivity concatenates every earlier feature map inside a block, so cost tracks resolution and depth, not the 7.04M parameter count. Ladder at 448 px: sl20 40880, sl14 29265, sl12 25393, sl10 21521, sl8 17649. At 336 px sl20: 23094. RESOLVED by dropping --train-size 448 -> 336 (and --vram-gb 16 -> 24) rather than cutting slices: 336 is the cache's own resolution (336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band) and cnx_own_recipe UPSAMPLES it to 448, so the deviation costs an upsampling factor, not information, where 20->12 slices would have cost eight real slices of the stack. Stated in the arm header as a deviation: a difference vs cnx_own_recipe is now pretraining AND upsampling.

title: ConvNeXt: honour cnx_own_recipe's PARTIAL branch — augmentation strength, not another rate rung
description: cnx_own_recipe scored 0.8186, landing in its own pre-registered PARTIAL band (0.80-0.83). That branch reads: 'the deficit is real but not all recipe, and the next knob is augmentation strength (never moved on this family) rather than another resolution step.' The branch binds. Do NOT run a 1.2e-3 rate rung on the strength of the ladder observation alone (see the sibling issue) — discarding a fired pre-registration is the defect that produced cnx_dense's retracted verdict. Arm = cnx_own_recipe.sh with augmentation strength raised, every other flag held. Bar context: the non-DINOv2 seat bar is 0.8521 and this family tops at 0.8186, so this is an instrument about whether our CNN numbers are under-read, not a member bet.
notes: Augmentation branch VOID (2026-09-01). The branch assumed the recipe's augmentation was off; it is not. kneemri/data/augmentation.py:60-68 declares the geometric transforms, experiments/recipe.sh:23 passes the flag that enables them, and kneemri/training/options.py:74 defaults it on. Any reading that treats the shipped members as un-augmented is wrong, and the branch that would have added augmentation is measuring a thing already present. What survives: the QUESTION of augmentation STRENGTH is untouched -- the defaults were never derived here -- but that is a knob, priced accordingly, not the branch this bead pre-registered.

description: fastMRI+ annotations carry a slice index into the ORIGINAL series. Our cache decimates ~35 slices to 12 (shape (4407,6,12,336,336) uint8). title: Rijeka knee MRI (736 labelled volumes) is on disk and unblocks supervised knee pretraining without MRNet
description:
knee-ombx wants supervised pretraining of the encoder on knee pathology, and has been blocked on obtaining MRNet. It does not need to be. D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/kneemri_rijeka/kneemridataset.zip has been on disk unextracted the whole time: 736 volumes plus a metadata.csv carrying examId, seriesNo, aclDiagnosis (0 healthy / 1 partial / 2 complete ACL tear), kneeLR (laterality), and a per-volume ROI box (roiX/Y/Z, roiHeight/Width/Depth). 3.1 GB, 737 members, one CSV and 736 .pck files.

This is the supervised knee-pathology signal the MRNet plan wanted, and it is already local. The MRNet archive the owner downloaded (now at D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/mrnet, 7.3 GB, 1250 studies x axial/coronal/sagittal) is IMAGES ONLY - it is a flattened repack with none of the six train-/valid- label CSVs, so it cannot supervise anything until those are fetched separately.

Why it matters now: five consecutive board entries have read flat on every operation over the champion pool (reweight, add, swap, count, kind, fit), and what the record leaves open is what a member IS. A trunk pretrained on knee pathology labels rather than on natural images is exactly that axis, and it is the axis raptor_feat_fit is currently probing from the foreign-checkpoint side.

Three supervision signals, in descending order of expected value:
- aclDiagnosis as a 3-class ordinal head. Directly the knee-ombx mechanism.
- kneeLR as laterality supervision. The project already audits laterality (processed/laterality_audit.csv) and has crop/centre arms that assume it.
- the ROI box as localisation supervision, which the crop_mm / crop80_span family currently approximates with a fixed millimetre box.

KNOWN COST BEFORE ANY CARD TIME: .pck is a pickle container, not npy or DICOM, so it needs a decoder before a cache can be written. Do not hand-build the truncated cache - arm_check --smoke writes a 60-study _first60 array in under a minute and that is what proves the decode. Hand-decoding crop80_span's cache on 2026-08-19 cost a session and the tool already had the step.

FIRST THING TO CHECK, before anything is trained: whether the Rijeka corpus overlaps the RSNA competition corpus. foreign_overlap put raptor at 98.6 percent in-sample here, which is what voided raptor_solo's 0.8938 and cost a whole reading. A pretraining corpus that overlaps the holdout would do the same thing one level deeper and would be much harder to see.

PRICE: decoder plus cache maybe 1-2 h of wall time and no card; the pretraining run itself prices like swin_supervised's 12 epochs. knee-ombx put the odds of the mechanism at roughly 1 in 3 and called it the best ratio on the board; that pricing was for MRNet's 1250 studies with three label heads, so 736 studies with one strong head plus two auxiliary ones is a smaller dose and the odds should be read down accordingly, not carried over unchanged.

title: Does the distilled trunk generalise better OFF-distribution? The one axis swin_distill_fit was never scored on
description:
OWNER'S QUESTION 2026-08-31: could a distilled pretrained model beat a supervised one on a NEW dataset, via better generalisation? Real mechanism -- soft teacher targets carry inter-class structure a hard label discards, and distillation is a stronger regulariser than label fitting; flatter minima and better shift behaviour are the standard reported consequence (born-again nets, self-distillation, OOD-robustness distillation).

WHAT THE EXISTING ARM DID NOT MEASURE. swin_distill_fit read -0.0077 against swin_supervised on fold-0 of OUR corpus: same reader, same decode, same population. That is in-distribution FIT. It is silent on generalisation. The interpretation written today (2026-08-31_distilling_logits_is_not_pretraining.md) names 'stage one undertrained' as its caveat and does NOT name this one, which is the larger of the two.

THIS IS knee-avzz FROM THE OTHER SIDE -- 'the offline ruler is same-distribution and blind to robustness'. Same complaint, reached from the audit rather than from an arm.

THE READ IS ALREADY AFFORDABLE, no training and no submission slot. Both checkpoints are on disk, and images_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_rijeka is built at EXACTLY the geometry both were trained at (336 px, 20 slices, band 0.1-0.9). Different hospital, scanner and population.

CONSTRAINT, stated so it is not discovered later: Rijeka labels ACL only, so this prices ONE finding, not the mean. The comparison must be stated on ACL or not at all. MRNet would add meniscus but is only built at 12sl and needs a rebuild to join the 20sl geometry.

BRANCHES, before the run:
* distilled trunk loses LESS on Rijeka than supervised does -> the write-up's scope is wrong, knee-8009 (a) reopens as a ROBUSTNESS lever rather than closing as a fit lever, and the same OOD read is owed to every arm closed on the same-distribution ruler.
* both lose the same -> the logit-target reading survives contact with the axis it was never tested on, which is worth more than the original result.
* distilled loses MORE -> the logit trunk is worse on both axes and (a) closes harder.

OWNER'S OWN CAVEAT, recorded: the hidden test is likely similar to our data, so this may not transfer to the competition. Counter-datum, not proof: board_transfer fits board = 1.37 x offline - 0.2598, and a slope of 1.37 means offline deltas AMPLIFY rather than transfer one-for-one. Prevalence and metric scaling can produce that too, so 'similar' is likely and 'identical' is not established.

PRICE: minutes of card (inference only), 0 slots.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-31T14:19Z, BEFORE planning the run. The price is not what the bead assumed.

NO TOOL RUNS THIS DIRECTION. Every foreign-corpus module in kneemri/evaluation/ serves a FOREIGN checkpoint through OUR corpus, which is the reverse of what this bead needs:
  * foreign_member.py -- serves a published checkpoint through ITS OWN decode, records it as one of our members.
  * foreign_gate.py -- the plumbing oracle scoring what foreign_member serves. Split from it by import-linter.
  * foreign_ruler.py -- joins a foreign checkpoint's PUBLISHED per-finding AUCs to our 58 radiologist-annotated studies. No inference at all.
  * foreign_overlap.py -- whether an entry trained on the studies it is being scored on.
  * board_transfer.py / ruler_transfer.py -- offline-to-board fits, not corpus transfer.

So OUR member on a FOREIGN corpus has no entrypoint. This needs a small scorer: load one of our checkpoints, run it over the Rijeka cache at its native geometry, score the labels Rijeka actually carries. That is code, not a CLI invocation, and it is the reason this bead cannot simply be 'run it when the card frees'.

WHAT IS STILL CHEAP. The cache is right: images_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_rijeka is built at EXACTLY the geometry swin_supervised and swin_distill_fit were fitted at, so no rebuild and no re-decode. Both checkpoints are on disk. The run itself is inference over one foreign corpus -- minutes of card, 0 slots. Only the scorer is new.

TWO THINGS TO VERIFY BEFORE WRITING IT:
  * whether index_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_rijeka.json carries the labels, or whether they must be joined from the raw Rijeka annotations.
  * knee-yu9k records that build_rijeka was UNCALLABLE (--spacing collided with CacheFlags --spacing). The cache on disk predates or dodges that, but whatever wrote it should be confirmed rather than assumed, because a cache built by a broken builder is the harness-suspect branch of this very arm.

title: cover_labelwise: full coverage failed under max pooling on exactly the labels it named - retest with per-label slice attention
description:
PRICE: ~50 minutes of card (12 epochs, 36 slices at 224 px; stack224 measured 257 s an epoch, labelwise attention adds a little). P(clears native224's 0.8502 on the mean) = 25%; P(recovers Lateral Meniscus and Fracture above control) = 40%.

WHAT HAPPENED. stack224 (knee-qphd) read the whole 36-slice stack for the first time and finished at 0.8476 against native224's 0.8502, -0.0026 on the mean. Its pre-registration said a flat mean with the thin findings UP was the finding. They went down hardest:

  Lateral Meniscus 0.8028 vs 0.8291  -0.0263
  Fracture         0.7929 vs 0.8109  -0.0180
  Synovitis        0.8740 vs 0.8638  +0.0101
  ACL              0.8809 vs 0.8768  +0.0041

Every thick finding rose or held; the two thin ones the mechanism named collapsed. That is not noise scatter, and it is not the coverage idea failing on its own terms - it is the shape of an AGGREGATOR failure.

THE MECHANISM. stack224 pools slices with --slice-pooling max. A maximum over 36 candidates has a strictly higher noise ceiling than a maximum over 20: the expected maximum of a set of noisy per-slice scores grows with the size of the set even when nothing in the volume changed. A finding present on two slices is exactly the case a spurious maximum drowns, and a finding present on twenty is not. So coverage and max pooling are in direct conflict, and the more slices are covered the worse the thin findings get. The measured per-label pattern is what that predicts, label for label.

THE TEST. Same arm, one flag moved: --slice-pooling labelwise (LabelwiseAttention), which gives each of the twelve findings its own attention map over the slices rather than one shared extremum. It is the mechanism-matched aggregator for a finding that lives on two slices out of thirty-six, and it is already proven at 20 slices (labelwise_dense_s2026, 0.8613). Everything else is stack224's invocation untouched, so the read is matched against BOTH stack224 (aggregator moved, coverage held) and native224 (the standing 224 control).

BRANCHES, before the number. Thin findings above native224's control and mean at or above 0.8502: the aggregator was the whole defect, coverage is real, and stack_cover_ff (knee-ujd3) un-gates with labelwise substituted for max. Thin findings recover but the mean does not: coverage is a per-finding lever, not a member lever - record it and do not ship it. Thin findings still down: coverage itself is refuted independent of the aggregator, knee-qphd closes, and knee-ujd3 closes with it.

Also drops --recompute-activations, as knee-ujd3 argues: stack224 peaked 21.9 GB of 32.6 WITH it, and the flag's 19% tax was calibrated for a 4.5x larger footprint. An OOM is itself the finding.
notes: READ 2026-08-31. cover_labelwise best holdout 0.8495, converged (12/12, best e8). Branch 3 fired: both thin findings still below native224's control (Fracture -0.0198 no recovery, Lateral Meniscus -0.0150 vs stack224's -0.0263 = about half back, inside the +/-0.0372 half-width), mean 0.8495 < 0.8502. Coverage refuted as a member lever independent of the aggregator. Seat value vs honest12: -0.0001 [-0.0006,+0.0004], 0 of 1 clears +0.0015. member_axes calls it DISTINCT (rank 0.8587 / js 0.0173 / maha 4.627 against boundaries 0.8956 / 0.0150 / 4.436) - DISTINCT is necessary for a seat, never sufficient, and both rulers declining agrees rather than adjudicating knee-iyad's gate. Only starred move: MCL +0.0247 against BOTH controls, Medial Meniscus +0.0125 against native224. Written up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_coverage_is_not_an_aggregator_bug.md

title: stack_cover_ff: full slice coverage carried into the best recipe, fit blind
description:
PRICE: ~45 minutes of card (12 epochs, 36 slices at 224 px; stack224 measures 257 s an epoch with --recompute-activations, ~215 s without). P(clears +0.0047 on a single member) = 10%, and GATED - see the gate below.

Route arithmetic, fitted this session on the 36 scored board entries that carry an honest offline number: board = 1.37 x offline - 0.2598. Board 0.946 therefore asks for an ensemble offline of 0.8815, against the best ever assembled (honest12, 0.8751) - a gap of +0.0064, one paired floor (STRONG_OF_BEST = 0.0062) wide. The ensemble tracks best-single + ~0.015, so that is +0.0047 on ONE member against the pool's best clean fold-0 run (merged_span_cf 0.8618 over 97 runs sharing its ruler). Nothing smaller is worth a seat: BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015 at the entry and a seat is diluted about 1/9 inside the champion.

Route B (blind refit, removing a seat's fit penalty) has exactly one move left and stackseat makes it: five of six champion seats are already --fold -1 --ema. After that entry scores, every further slot is paid out of member quality.

This arm is the first candidate for that: 36-slice full coverage (the cell no member has occupied, knee-qphd) carried into the blend-three corpus plus raptor-teacher distillation (the two levers worth ~+0.014 that make the pool's best members). Coverage changes which pixels are seen; the corpus and teacher change what is asked for. Independent inputs, one run.

THE GATE. stack224 is the fold-0 sibling that prices coverage on its own, and at epoch 10 it reads 0.8476 against its control native224's 0.8502 - flat to slightly negative ON THE MEAN. The mechanism never claimed the mean: it names the thin findings that live on few slices (Lateral Meniscus, Fracture). So this arm runs ONLY if stack224's final per-label read shows those two up. Flat mean with the thin findings up is the finding; flat mean with them flat kills the coverage lever and this arm with it, and the card goes to the KIND axis (knee-ombx) instead.

Fit is --fold -1 --ema by design: the destination is the champion. No holdout number exists by construction.

Also drops --recompute-activations (19% measured tax, calibrated for a 4.5x larger activation footprint). That half is unconditional and near-free: the first epoch's peak-memory line answers it either way. stack224 peaked 21.9 GB of 32.6 WITH the flag; predicted ~29 GB without, and an OOM is itself the finding that the threshold sits between 20 and 36 slices at 224.
notes:
PRICE. 12 epochs at 36 slices / 224 px. stack224 measures 257 s an epoch WITH --recompute-activations; without it, 19% less, so ~215 s -> ~45 minutes of card.

GAIN. It must clear +0.0047 on a single member for the ensemble to reach the offline 0.8815 that the board fit says 0.946 needs. Nothing smaller is worth the seat: BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015 at the entry and a seat is diluted about 1/9 inside the champion.

title: Drop --recompute-activations on 224-px arms: a 19% tax for a memory problem that no longer exists
description:
`experiments/recipe.sh:31` sets THROUGHPUT=--recompute-activations and every arm inherits it. Its own docstring (kneemri/models/encoder_surgery.py:285-300) records the cost as MEASURED: 798 img/s against 946, a 19% tax, taken 2026-08-12 at batch 6.

That measurement was taken on the 336-px geometry: 12 studies x 6 slots x 12 slices = 864 images at 577 tokens each. That footprint pinned all 32 GB and genuinely paged over PCIe, so the tax bought the run.

A 224-px arm is a different problem. stack224 runs 36 slices x 6 slots x batch 12 = 432 images at 256 tokens - about 4.5x less activation - and measures 24.3 GB reserved of 32.6, with 8 GB of headroom the whole run. It is paying a 19% throughput tax to solve a memory problem it does not have.

Do: on the next 224-px arm, drop $THROUGHPUT from the invocation and record peak reserved memory plus s/epoch against stack224's 257 s. If it fits (predicted ~29 GB, still under), 224 exploration gets ~19% cheaper for free and the standing exploration resolution (knee-s9cr) gets faster. If it OOMs, the tax is justified at 36 slices and the finding is that the threshold sits between 20 and 36 slices at 224 - which is itself worth the one arm.

Do NOT touch recipe.sh's default: the 336 arms still need it.
notes: ANSWERED BY ONE LAUNCH, 2026-08-31. cover_labelwise launched without $THROUGHPUT at 08:02Z died with torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 488.00 MiB ... 25.50 GiB allowed; 25.09 GiB is allocated, at 224 px / 36 slices — against the 21.9 GB stack224 peaked at WITH the flag at 20 slices. So the flag is dead weight at 20 slices and load-bearing at 36 at the SAME 224 px: the threshold is slice COUNT, not image size, and it sits between 20 and 36. The 19% (798 vs 946 img/s) is bought, not wasted, on any whole-stack arm. Do not drop it on a coverage arm. Cost: three minutes.

title: Read the WHOLE stack once: 36 slices at 224 px, the one decode cell no member has ever occupied
description:
THE PUBLIC FRONTIER READS 64 SLICES PER STUDY. The DINOsaur/raptor kernel (research/2026-08-23_published-per-label-auc-vs-ours.md, and the notebook pulled 2026-08-31) fills its five slots with 18+14+12+8+12 = 64 slices. Every member this project owns reads 12 or 20 (95 arms at 20, 43 at 12, 1 at 16, and NOTHING above 20 in 137 arm scripts). A sagittal knee series holds 30-40 slices, so at 12-20 we are reading a third to a half of the volume and the sampler picks which half.

WHY THE SLICE-COUNT LEDGER DOES NOT ALREADY ANSWER THIS. It measures 12 -> 20 only: +0.0080 (band_span_hold -> band_dense_hold), +0.0013 (band_span -> band_dense), -0.0001 under max pooling (knee-ezz), -0.0028 on the merged corpus. Mixed and knob-sized. But 12 -> 20 is a change of WHICH SUBSET, not of coverage; 36 of a 30-40 slice stack is the first read that cannot miss a slice. Those are different mechanisms and only the second one can answer 'is a thin finding falling between our samples'.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN RUN, AND WHY IT IS FREE NOW. VRAM is a function of slice count and nothing else (experiments/README.md:253): at 336 px, 20 slices reserve 26.92 GB of a 32 GB card, so 36 was never affordable. At 224 px native224 reserved 8124 MiB at 12 slices, so 36 lands near 24.4 GB and fits. knee-s9cr's owner directive makes 224 the standing exploration resolution, and native224 (0.8502 vs the 336 control's 0.8525, -0.0023, inside the floor) says the resolution costs nothing. band224.sh was written at 20 slices and never ran, so the 224 slice axis is entirely untested.

THE ARM. stack224: native224's invocation with --slices 36 and the band opened to 0.05-0.95. Two flags, ONE concept - read the whole stack - and they cannot be separated, because 36 slices inside a 0.2-0.8 band would resample the middle 60% at triple density rather than cover the volume. Everything else held: 224 px, max slice pooling, whole-stack, backbone-lr 4e-5, 12 epochs, fold 0, canonical scheme, report_labels_v2 ruler.

CONTROL. native224_s2026 = 0.8502, same fold-0 holdout, same ruler, same everything but the two flags.

READ IT PER LABEL, NOT ONLY ON THE MEAN. The mechanism names WHICH labels it should move: the frontier's own corpus jump reported its biggest gains on Lateral Meniscus +0.071, Fracture +0.057, Lateral OA +0.048 - the thin findings that live on few slices. A mean-AUC delta averages a two-label effect away across twelve. If the mean is flat but Meniscus and Fracture move together and the rest do not, that is the finding, and it points at per-finding slice budgeting rather than at a global count.

PRICE: ~55 min of card (94 s/epoch at 12 slices scales to ~285 s at 36; 12 epochs), zero slots, at 224 px where the queue is cheap. Plausible gain if the mechanism is real: +0.005 to +0.015 on the mean, concentrated in 2-3 labels. P(clears the 0.0062 paired holdout floor) ~ 30% - the nearest measurement (12->20 under max pooling, -0.0001) predicts a null, and this arm's claim is that the null was about subset choice and not about coverage.

BRANCHES, PRE-REGISTERED.
  * delta >= +0.0062 on the mean. Coverage is a lever, the whole 12/20 corpus was reading a third of the volume, and the next arm is 36 slices at 336 px on a smaller batch.
  * mean inside the floor but Lateral Meniscus and Fracture both up 0.02+. The effect is real and per-label; the lane becomes per-finding slice budgeting (slot_head already reads findings on particular planes), not a global count.
  * flat everywhere. Coverage is not the limit, the sampler was already picking the informative slices, and this closes the slice axis for good - knee-nj4l's axis (3) dies with it.
  * delta <= -0.0062. More slices dilute a max pool (experiments/README.md:5054 argues this for the mean pool). Then the finding is that the aggregator, not the sampler, is what cannot spend more slices.

HARNESS CHECK. The printed recipe must show image_size 224, slices 36, band [0.05, 0.95], slice_pooling max, whole_stack True, fold 0, and the log must load 4,406 studies holding out 909.

The AGGREGATOR mechanism did hold on one of the two labels it named (Lateral Meniscus -0.0263 -> -0.0150) but inside a +/-0.0372 half-width, and Fracture did not move (-0.0180 -> -0.0198). So coverage is refuted as a member lever independent of the aggregator; the aggregator argument survives as a mechanism worth under a third of one label. knee-ujd3 closes with it (it was gated on coverage surviving) and its throughput half is separately answered: --recompute-activations is load-bearing at 36 slices / 224 px (OOM without it) and dead weight at 20, so the 19% is bought. Does NOT close labelwise pooling itself, which reads 0.8613 at 20 slices. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_coverage_is_not_an_aggregator_bug.md

title: The most decorrelated member the project owns has never been in a board entry - blind-refit it for the champion lane
description:
swin_supervised_s2026 scores 0.8331 solo with a nearest-neighbour agreement of 0.8346, against a seated spread of 0.8772-0.9225. It is by a wide margin the most decorrelated member here, and it is the only non-DINO trunk that ever came close to seat-worthy. It was declined at -0.0012 seat value against greedyseat_v1.

WHY THAT DECLINE DOES NOT SETTLE IT. Every seat_value reading is taken on greedyseat_v1, a fold-0 roster scoring 0.936. The entry we actually ship is raptorweight_v1 at 0.944, five of whose six members are --fold -1 blind fits that RecordMix excludes by construction. So the ruler cannot price the champion at all, and -0.0012 is a statement about a different ensemble. Three separate candidates priced at +0.0002, +0.0005 and +0.0000 on that same ruler on 2026-08-31, which is what a saturated ruler looks like, not necessarily a saturated pool.

knee-nj4l is the standing P0 this answers: the champion is an architecture MONOCULTURE and that is the mechanical cause of the 0.937-0.941 plateau. swin_supervised is the only decorrelated non-DINO trunk available to break it, and it has never appeared in any board entry.

THE ARM. Blind full fit (--fold -1 --ema) of the swin_supervised recipe, so the member sits in the same lane as the five blind members it would join. swinbase, backbone-lr 1e-4, train-size 384, slices 20, band 0.1-0.9, max pooling, batch 1 accumulate 6 - every flag held from swin_supervised.sh, only the fold and EMA change.

PRICE: swin_supervised converged at epoch 6 of 12 and declined after, so 8 epochs at ~370 s is ~50 min of a card that is otherwise idle. It cannot be priced offline by construction, so the read is a board slot, and this arm's job is to have the shippable form READY rather than to earn the slot itself. P(clears +0.002 on the board as a champion seat) ~ 0.15 - low because three board seat operations have already come back unresolvable, but it is the only one of them that changes the ARCHITECTURE rather than the seating, and the fold-0 evidence says the member is decorrelated rather than merely weak.

HOW IT IS READ. As deltas against the control entry on the board, never absolute (knee-nh3w). No holdout number exists for it - it is --fold -1 - so nothing may be entered in the ledger as its score.
close_reason: Killed 7 minutes in, before the lane's own arithmetic was checked against the board. The arm existed to have an architecture-distant member in shippable (blind) form. vjepaseat_v1 had ALREADY run that experiment on the board on 2026-08-30: raptorweight_v1's serving with one seat added, using vjepa_warm_s2026 at nearest-neighbour 0.8119 - MORE distant than swin_supervised's 0.8346 - and it read 0.943 against the control's 0.944. Flat. Its board row sizes what the lane needs: +0.017 to +0.020 solo over the lane's current 0.8331. A blind refit buys roughly 0.008, so this arm could not have reached the bar it was aimed at, and 2h of card would have bought a member pre-refuted by its own lane's measured requirement. Arm file deleted rather than parked - it is not a plan awaiting a card, it is a plan answered. Re-open the LANE, not this arm, with a non-DINO trunk at or above the seated quality level; that is a member-quality problem, not a fit problem. Card went to knee-8ft1 (stack_increments_ff) instead.

title: Cross distillation with the merged corpus: the two things that made the best two members, never combined
description:
stack_increments_s2026 is the best solo the project owns (0.8642) and the only member that distils from raptor_teacher.npz. merged_span_cf / merged_labelwise_cf are the merged-corpus members (0.8618 / 0.8587) and none of them distils. The two quality levers have never been in the same member.

knee-urvf is why this is the arm to run: the ensemble tracks best-single + ~0.015 and that bonus has not grown in fourteen days, so member quality is the only free term left. Two readings on 2026-08-31 closed the other half from both sides - stack_increments (best quality, ordinary diversity) priced +0.0002 as a seat and merged_labelwise_cf (most decode-diverse candidate ever priced, nearest 0.8873 / mean 0.8583) priced +0.0005. Neither half buys a seat alone, so the seat is not the lever and the member is.

ONE VARIABLE against stack_increments: the corpus, blend_three_v1.csv -> merged_blend_v1.csv. Distillation weight 0.3, raptor teacher, --hold-annotations, --calibrated-targets, band 0.1-0.9, slices 20, pooling max, backbone-lr 4e-5, 12 epochs, eval ruler report_labels_v2.csv all held. So it is a matched read of what the merged corpus does to a DISTILLED member, which neither parent can answer.

--hold-annotations is carried, not introduced: it is stack_increments' own flag and dropping it would make the read two-variable. knee-9198 bans retraining the ROSTER under it, not carrying it in one matched arm.

THE EXPECTED COLLISION, stated before the number. merged_dense_cf showed the merged corpus SUBSTITUTES for a denser read (-0.0028 against merged_blend_cf), and merged_labelwise_cf repeated it on the pooling axis (0.8587 against its 0.8618 parent). A distillation teacher is a better-labelled signal by the same argument, so a third collision is the live branch.

PRICE: 12 epochs at ~430 s = ~86 min of a card that is otherwise idle. It needs 0.8704 (stack_increments 0.8642 + the 0.0062 paired floor) to be a real quality gain. P(clears 0.8704) ~ 0.2 - the two prior collisions are the reason it is not higher, and the fact that no member has ever held both levers is the reason it is not lower. 86 min at 0.2 on the ONLY free term beats an idle card and beats a fourth seat permutation, which the same day priced at zero twice.

HOW IT IS READ. Control stack_increments = 0.8642.
  * >= 0.8704: the levers are independent, the merged corpus does not eat a teacher, and the quality lane reopens.
  * 0.8580 to 0.8703: within the floor. Not a verdict; keep only if seat_value picks it over the roster.
  * <= 0.8579: THIRD collision, and that promotes 'the merged corpus substitutes for any finer signal' from an observation to a property of the corpus. Then the corpus lane is one cell wide and the next lever is a genuinely different external corpus (MRNet, knee-ombx), not another cross.
notes:
BAND RESTATED AS DELTAS against the control, per knee-nh3w - the original description names absolute scores, which is the defect that bead files. Control is stack_increments_s2026 on the same fold-0 holdout and the same report_labels_v2 ruler.

  * delta >= +0.0062: the levers are independent, the merged corpus does not eat a teacher, quality lane reopens.
  * -0.0062 < delta < +0.0062: inside the paired floor. Not a verdict; keep only if seat_value picks it.
  * delta <= -0.0062: THIRD collision, corpus lane is one cell wide, next lever is MRNet (knee-ombx).

PRICE: ~86 min on an otherwise-idle card. P(clears +0.0062) ~ 0.2.
2026-09-20 04:40Z — DISTILLATION CLOSED AS A MEMBER-QUALITY LEVER, on the only matched pair that exists, zero card.

This bead and distill_stack_max.sh both rest on a distill attribute marginal of +0.0151 (n=22). That number is
MIDPOINT. On ledger75 the term is +0.0024.

The pair was found by grouping all 397 members-with-a-recipe on every recipe key EXCEPT distill_weight /
teacher_targets / out / seed. Exactly one clean on-off pair survives, and it uses the LEAK-FREE teacher
(teacher_clean.npz, built from oof_clean_fold[1-4] only, after_clean_teacher.sh:29):

  calib_dense_s2026   distill 0.0                      LEDGER 0.8562  LEDGER75 0.8916  peak e6
  clean_calib_s2026   distill 0.7 teacher_clean.npz    LEDGER 0.8649  LEDGER75 0.8940  peak e9
  marginal                                                    +0.0087           +0.0024

+0.0024 is inside the 0.0053 paired-holdout floor and under the +0.0032 a solo needs to pass the champion.
The 3.6x gap between the two rulers is the documented midpoint inflation (knee-f9aao), and it is the same
shape as the leak warning already on record: after_clean_teacher.sh:5 says the +0.0107 distill term read on
oofsolo 'is mostly leak'. Both accounts point the same way and this is the matched measurement of what is
left once the leak is gone.

WHAT THIS KILLS. The arm designed against it tonight was the genuinely empty cell: labelwise_depth24_drop40_long
(our corner, LEDGER75 0.9053, and its recipe reads distill_weight 0.0 / teacher_targets None) plus
--distill-weight 0.7 --teacher-targets teacher_clean.npz, one variable, 1.5 h of an idle card (the corner's own
08:18Z->09:48Z on 2026-09-13). At a measured +0.0024 term it predicts 0.9077 against a 0.9085 bar: it misses
BEFORE any collision penalty, and the corner already carries --calibrated-targets and --hold-annotations, which
are two more routes to the same better-labelled-signal correction a teacher supplies. Not launched.

This bead's own arm is worse than that one on every axis (its control stack_increments 0.8642 is three weeks
stale and is no longer the corner), so it goes with it.

RE-OPEN BY a second matched on-off pair, not by re-quoting the +0.0151. One pair is one pair.

title: The fold-0 proxy ruler for BLIND champion seats -- built 2026-08-30, tested by holdswap_v1
description:
THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES. comp/champion.json pins an entry whose six members are all --fold -1. None carries a holdout record, so no seat of the best entry this project owns can be priced offline, and every seat change has had to be bought with a submission slot. That is why the champion's history is a chain of board-fitted swaps.

THE CONSTRUCTION. Five of the champion's six have fold-0 analogues that DO carry holdout records: calib_span_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, merged_blend_s2026, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026. There is no fold-0 final_ws, so the sixth seat is outside the instrument and always will be unless one is trained. Hold those five as a roster in record_mix --roster and price candidates against them; curve.swap then names which analogue each candidate would displace.

WHAT IT READ (logs/swap_champion_proxy.log, 909 shared studies, LogitAverage, roster of 5 = 0.8697). Ten strong pool members priced. TEN OF TEN named the same incumbent to displace: lr4e-5_ws, the weakest of the five at 0.8525 solo. Five of the ten cleared BOARD_RESOLVABLE = +0.0015 on that swap (labelwise_dense +0.0024, stack_increments +0.0021, finding_calib_dense +0.0019, calib_dense_hold +0.0018, merged_span_cf +0.0018). An independent earlier run had already recorded the same seat on the roster line for finding_calib_dense: '+0.0017 as a swap for lr4e-5_ws on the champion shadow'. So the sign reproduces across two runs.

WHY THE ORDERING IS NOT USED. knee-7d1 measured that only the SIGN of a member swap transfers; the ordering broke on its third point. So the table names a SEAT, not an entrant. The entrant for holdswap_v1 was picked by two independent constraints instead: BLIND (greedyseat paid 0.936 against the champion's 0.944 for shipping fold-0 members) and inside the group the proxy could not separate. calib_dense_hold_ff was the only member satisfying both.

WHAT holdswap_v1 (ref 55900461) TESTS. Whether this proxy ORDERS blind seats at all. Its pre-registration is in the kernel docstring with four disjoint bands against the champion's 0.944. A gain says the remaining five champion seats can be ranked offline without a slot each -- which would be worth far more than the tick itself. A flat says the proxy separates members the board cannot separate, and the champion six are interchangeable at this quality level.

THE STANDING LIMITS. The proxy is fold-0 and every entry it advises is blind; the sixth seat was never in the comparison; and it prices over 909 shared studies of OUR corpus while the board's test set is hidden and not ours.
notes: PRICE (2026-08-30T22:55Z, for merged_span_ff.sh and labelwise_dense_ff.sh). COST: ~45 min card each, ~90 min for both, on a card that is otherwise IDLE overnight and cannot be spent on anything competing -- cnx_warm_anneal finishes ~23:15Z and the single overnight submission slot does not open until 00:00 UTC. Opportunity cost is therefore near zero in wall-clock terms; the real cost is that neither arm can be priced offline by construction (--fold -1 has seen every holdout study). GAIN: the second champion seat is UNREACHABLE without one of them -- the step-2 swap table names four candidates and there is no blind full-fit of any of them on disk, and shipping a fold-0 member onto a champion-shaped entry is what greedyseat already paid 0.936-vs-0.944 for. Offline the swap prices at +0.0017 (merged_span_cf) and +0.0021 (labelwise_dense), both above BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015 and both inside the 0.0062 unseparable band, so the table gives the SIGN and not the ordering. P(clears +0.0015 on the board) ~= 0.30, and it is CONDITIONAL: holdswap_v1's bands A/B (>= 0.9425) keep this axis open, bands C/D close it and no further slot goes to a single-seat swap. RATIO: 90 min of free card for a ~30% shot at the one axis that has twice moved this champion (res392_ws -> band_dense, 0.925 -> 0.928; and holdswap now), plus, at worst, two blind members of greedy seats two and three that any whole-corpus roster can use. Taken as a HEDGE armed before the band is known, deliberately, the same trade calib_dense_hold_ff took against fourseat_v1.

title: Is v3's +0.0105 the re-map or the 224 corner? One dense-corner replication separates them
description:
FOLLOW-UP (2) of knee-8wa0, named in the ledger's own cost order: v3 is free (done), THEN a dense-corner
replication, and only THEN a roster rebuild.

WHAT LANDED. recal_holdannot swapped holdannot's supervision table for report_labels_v3.csv, whose six
reader levels are replaced by their measured positive rates on the 58 radiologist-read studies. Read on
both rulers per knee-9198, gold first:

  ruler                                     holdannot   recal_holdannot   delta
  GOLD (supervision_gap, 58 studies)          0.8932        0.9037        +0.0105
  proxy (ruler_check on v2, 909 studies)      0.8506        0.8515        +0.0009
  proxy, confident-only (71.0% of cells)      0.8740        0.8754        +0.0014

Gold up past the 0.0062 floor, proxy not down: the arm's LANDS branch.

THE OPEN QUESTION. n=58 is a level and not a selector (knee-kddo), and one arm at one recipe corner
(224 px, 12 slices, band 0.2-0.8) cannot separate the RE-MAP from the CORNER. This arm is the cheapest
possible separation: band_dense_hold already exists as a matched control read on BOTH rulers, so the
comparison costs nothing beyond the one 40-minute run.

PRICE: ~40 min of card. P(clears the 0.0062 gold floor) ~ 0.5 -- a replication of a single n=58 read at a
different corner, with the corner itself the named suspect. Priced as an INSTRUMENT: it produces no
seatable member (a table swap is not a quality lever, and the control is 0.8573 proxy). What it buys is
whether follow-up (3), the roster rebuild, may ever be armed -- which is many arms and is licensed by
nothing today.

PRE-REGISTERED on gold first:
  REPLICATES -- gold up 0.0062+ over band_dense_hold's gold, proxy not down by the floor. The re-map is a
    property of the table, not the corner. Licenses follow-up (3).
  CORNER -- gold within 0.0062 either way. The +0.0105 was the 224 corner. v3 stays the default table
    (free) and the label lane stops being priced as a member lane.
  REFUTES -- gold down 0.0062 or more. At the dense corner the re-map moves training away from the
    image-read process; the follow-up goes per-finding rather than pooled.

--eval-labels IS PINNED TO v2, and that is the lesson of the arm above rather than a preference.
recal_holdannot passed --labels v3 with --eval-labels unset, so its holdout truth was binarised at 0.5
against the RE-MAPPED values: the ruler moved with the arm and the log ended "best holdout mean AUC
0.8964", +0.0477 over its control, which sat there for an hour looking like the largest single-arm gain

title: Non-DINO lane inherits --unfreeze-last as a COUNT, not a fraction
description:
Every run this project has done on a non-DINOv2 trunk -- nine of them, smokes excluded -- shares one recipe skeleton transplanted from DINOv2-small: one_cycle True, layer_decay 1.0/None, unfreeze_last 6, head_lr 1e-3, patience 0, ema False. Three of the nine never converged (cnx_dense climbing at e11, vit_in21k 5 of 12 epochs climbing, vjepa_member climbing at e10), so vjepa2l 0.8343 and vitin21k 0.7847 are FLOORS quoted in this repo as those trunks' worth.

Four candidate explanations for the non-DINO deficit -- architecture, pretraining, rate, schedule -- and the project has been quoting the first while only ever testing under one setting of the other three.

THE MECHANISM, SHARPENED. The flag that does the damage is --unfreeze-last, because it is a COUNT fitted on a 12-block trunk. Read off Encoder.blocks (the real depth for a hierarchical trunk -- cnxbase states depth 12 and runs 36):

  dinov2-small  12 blocks   6 opens 50%   0.8964
  vitin21k      12 blocks   6 opens 50%   0.7847 (floor, 5 of 12 epochs)
  swinbase      24 blocks   6 opens 25%   0.8331
  vjepa2l       24 blocks   6 opens 25%   0.8343 (floor, still climbing)
  cnxbase       36 blocks   6 opens 17%   0.8186

Among the converged runs the ordering is monotone in opened fraction. Confounded with architecture and NOT offered as the explanation -- it is why this is the cheapest of the four explanations to eliminate. A block's job is set by where it sits in the trunk, not by its index from the end: the last six of a 12-block ViT are its whole second half, the last six of a 36-block ConvNeXt are the tail of one stage.

THE ARM: experiments/arms/swin_open_half.sh. Match the FRACTION rather than the count -- --unfreeze-last 12 on swinbase's 24, with --layer-decay 0.7 (the value band_dense_llrd measured) travelling with it, because opening twice as many blocks at one flat rate is how a deeper opening goes wrong. The pair is ONE mechanism. Rate held at the control's 1e-4 so the arm stays matched to swin_supervised in every other respect.

PRICE: ~2.5-3 h of card. Control swin_supervised ran 12 epochs at 384 px with six open blocks in ~90 min; twelve open blocks doubles what must be retained for the backward and the twelve include stage three at stride 16. P(clears the +0.017-0.020 seat bar over swin_supervised's 0.8331) ~= 0.15. Priced as an IMPROVEMENT this is a ~0-expected-score run.

IT IS ARMED AS AN INSTRUMENT AND MUST BE JUDGED AS ONE. What it buys is licence to re-read the lane: nine runs and three quoted floors rest on the assumption that a DINOv2 recipe transfers. P(it moves the number at all, either way, by more than 0.010) ~= 0.5, and EITHER SIGN is informative -- REFUTES closes the recipe explanation and sends the lane to knee-8009 with one arm instead of four.

Schedule (one_cycle on/off) is NOT moved by this arm. It is binary in this trainer, dropping it contradicts a measured DINOv2 result (schedule_8, -0.0028) and it would add a fourth variable to an arm already answering a joint question. It stays open as the follow-up if this one comes back FLAT.

BLOCKED ON cnx_warm_anneal, the lane's matched control.

title: queue_check: false DOUBLE-QUEUED - the launching shell is not the watcher's parent on the Windows probe
description:
FIXED 2026-08-30 in the same sitting it was found; this bead is the record, because the shape recurs.

WHAT HAPPENED. queue_check exited 2 with "DOUBLE-QUEUED: experiments/arms/recal_dense.sh" against a queue that was correct: swin_calib_dense -> recal_dense -> (warm_calib_lowlr, cnx_warm_anneal), three live watchers, exactly one owing recal_dense. Acting on the verdict as printed means killing a healthy chain and losing the card's evening.

WHY IT FIRED. doubled() counts process-table lines whose argv CONTAINS the arm path. Two live lines carried experiments/arms/recal_dense.sh: the real after.sh watcher, and the harness shell that launched it, whose own -c string embeds the whole `nohup bash experiments/after.sh ... & disown` command.

WHY THE EXISTING GUARD MISSED IT, which is the part worth keeping. watchers() already dropped the launcher, by PARENTAGE - "dropping any line that is the PARENT of another watcher line removes exactly that wrapper". That invariant holds on the POSIX probe and is FALSE on the Windows one: nohup + disown under MSYS re-parents through an intermediate, so the launcher read pid 30016 while the watcher it started read a parent of 37388. The launcher is not the watcher's parent there, nothing was dropped, and the unit test covering the drop had fixed the wrapper AS the parent - encoding the one arrangement the real failure never has. A test can hold a false invariant still.

A SECOND IMPOSTOR, found in the same dump and unrelated to parentage. Any process whose argv merely mentions after.sh matched - a grep, an editor, a checker, including the probe used to diagnose this. Those lines have no pid columns, so parentage reads blank and the drop could never have removed them either. Today they only inflated counts for arms named in their own argv; a `grep after.sh experiments/arms/recal_dense.sh` fabricates a blocking DOUBLE-QUEUED on its own.

THE FIX. A watcher is now identified by WHERE the token sits, not by whose child the process is: a shell running a -c string is a launcher and never a watcher whatever it embeds, and in a real invocation the script is the token immediately after the interpreter - the one arrangement both probe formats share. The parentage drop is kept as a second line of defence for the POSIX probe. Two tests added for the shapes that actually occur: a launcher that is NOT the parent, and an onlooker with no pids at all.

THE GENERAL LESSON, and why this is filed rather than just fixed. This is the SECOND false blocking verdict from this one check (2026-08-21 was the first). A guard that cries wolf is worse than no guard: CLAUDE.md requires queue_check at every session end and every watcher launch, so a standing false positive trains the reader to skip a check that is also the only thing standing between two watchers and one card. Every other check in this project that crosses the process table shares the exposure - card_check and misarmed() both reason over the same listing - and the Windows/POSIX parentage difference is a property of the PROBE, not of this check.

title: Feature distillation as PRETRAINING: the domain adaptation every non-DINO trunk in this project never got
description:
OWNER, 2026-08-30: 'distill is good for pretraining too if we decide we want this order.' Correct, and it is a different mechanism from what knee-for6 and knee-7ybf price - those add a teacher term to a LABELLED fine-tune. This is a pretraining STAGE before labels.
