NOTE THE ONE REAL DESIGN QUESTION: PairMemory stores what the ranking term compares (logits/scores, twelve numbers a study); a context memory stores D-dimensional vectors twelve times a study, so the memory cost is real and has to be priced before the capacity is chosen. Whether PairMemory generalises or a sibling ContextMemory is the honest structure is an implementation call, not settled here.

PRICE, STATED BEFORE ANY CARD IS SPENT. Build ~1-2 h, no card. The arm costs what contrast_dense cost: 420 s an epoch x 12 = 84 min at dense/336, or roughly a third of that at 224 (knee-s9cr). Against the control already on disk at 0.8634, so no matched baseline arm is owed.

EXPECTED GAIN, HONESTLY. This does NOT plausibly deliver 1.5% and must not be sold as if it did. It is an INSTRUMENT in the sense CLAUDE.md licenses: it retires a suspicion the ledger has carried in writing since 2026-08-27, and it licenses or closes the whole REPRESENTATION axis - the one lane knee-m69u's axis table does not list as closed, because it has never been run under conditions where its supervision was non-degenerate. Two outcomes and both are worth the card:
  - term stops costing 0.0087 -> the representation lane is live and re-opens knee-ek5s's strong form (masks, knee-2sbk)
  - term still costs -> 'shaping the representation does not work HERE' becomes sayable for the first time, and the lane closes honestly instead of on a known-broken harness

AND THE DOWNSIDE IS ALREADY BOUNDED, which is unusual. contrast_dense LOST 0.0087 solo and STILL earned a seat - greedy forward selection under record_mix --largest-pool --vote logit over 104 records / 909 shared studies seats contrast_dense_s2026.pt FIFTH at 0.8749. The contrastive term changed WHAT THE MEMBER DISAGREES ABOUT, which is the owner's standing diversity thesis measured on our own pool rather than asserted. So a flat solo result here still produces a seat candidate, and a better-supervised version of a member that already seats fifth is the cheapest diversity we can manufacture.

PRE-REGISTERED READING, so this is not scored after the fact:
  - solo within +/-0.0062 of 0.8634 = FLAT: supervision was not the binding constraint; representation lane closes on price
  - solo above +0.0062: the batch-size artefact is confirmed and the axis re-opens
  - solo below -0.0062 again: the term is harmful independent of batch size; lane closes on mechanism
  - IN ALL THREE CASES also price the seat with seat_value, because the -0.0087 version already earned one

VERIFY THE FLAG LANDED before reading any number - this bead exists because a mechanism was blocked by plumbing nobody checked. Assert the run's stored recipe carries BOTH the contrast weight and the memory capacity, and that settings() reports the pool the memory really holds (RememberedRanking.settings already asks the memory itself rather than echoing the flag - copy that).

Depends on nothing. Blocks nothing. Closes when the arm runs and its pre-registered branch is recorded.
notes: PRICE: 40 min of card for one 12-epoch fit at the dense recipe (contrast_dense's own measured 420 s/epoch says 84 min is the honest upper bound — price an arm off its control's measured epoch time, not off a prediction). Zero submission slots. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.02: this is member quality, and calibsix's measured ~23% board pass-through ceilings any such gain near 0.943, so the run is NOT sold as an improvement. It is armed as an INSTRUMENT under knee-qxse: what 40-84 min buys is which of three pre-registered readings is true — flat inside +/-0.0062 of 0.8634 closes the representation lane ON PRICE and sends topology to the strong form (masks, knee-2sbk); above contrast_dense's 0.8547 by more than 0.0062 CONFIRMS the batch-size artefact and re-opens the axis with a mechanism; below it closes the lane on MECHANISM, which is the stronger closure. P(one of the three lands cleanly) ~ 0.8, and the axis is retired or re-opened either way instead of staying open on a suspicion. Seat priced with seat_value in all three cases: contrast_dense lost 0.0087 solo and still seats fifth. WIRED 2026-08-30: RememberedContrast + PairMemory embedding + run_setup._contrastive dispatch; --pair-memory no longer refused beside --contrast-weight. Arm experiments/arms/contrast_pool.sh.
close_reason:
Built, armed, read, and it refuted the suspect it was built to test. RememberedContrast composes PairMemory with the supervised-contrastive term (the dispatch chain in run_setup.objective was the only thing that had ever blocked the pair, and _check_contrast_alone's refusal of --pair-memory beside --contrast-weight is lifted with the reason recorded). Equality oracle in the unit tests: an empty memory reproduces ContrastiveObjective exactly, so the arm is one variable against its control.

RESULT: contrast_pool_s2026 0.8515 at e5, converged. -0.0032 against contrast_dense_s2026 (0.8547, inside the 0.0062 floor) and -0.0119 against calib_dense_hold_s2026 (0.8634, outside it). Seat value 0.0000 - the honest greedy over the roster peaks at 0.8763/20 seats with or without it, identical to four decimals. Declined in comp/members.declines with the argument, not just the number.

THE MECHANISM FIRED, which is what makes this a refutation and not a null: training loss 5.859 vs the control's 3.605 at e0 and ~2.2 higher throughout, which is what widening a log-sum-exp denominator from 12 keys to 96 does. So the batch-size explanation contrast_dense offered for its own -0.0087 - 'a batch of twelve sees a 7%-prevalence finding roughly once' - is refuted on measurement. Eight times the contrastive population, no movement.

None of the three pre-registered readings applied; the fourth did. Supervised contrastive at this operating point closes on MECHANISM rather than on price. It does NOT close representation shaping generally - one formulation (SupCon over the readout, T=0.1, w=1.0), one attachment point. A re-open needs a different term, not this one at another weight.

Ledger: experiments/README.md 2026-08-30. Code shipped in 4839b5d.

title: A 3D encoder is the one named axis the ledger left untouched — price it before arming
description:
THE ARGUMENT, TAKEN FROM THE LEDGER RATHER THAN INVENTED. The `depth_true` row closes the aggregation
stage from three directions: more slices -0.0001, more slots +0.0002, and every combining rule within
0.0019 of every other (max 0.8457, order-aware gate 0.8461, mean 0.8473, permutation-blind gate 0.8476).
Its own conclusion is that the limit is UPSTREAM, in what one slice's feature vector contains. It then
names what it did NOT rule out, verbatim: "through-plane mixing at the FEATURE level is what died; a 3D
encoder that sees the volume before any per-slice feature exists is a different mechanism and untouched."

Nothing in beads and no row in experiments/README.md has touched it. Every member in the pool is a 2D
encoder run per-slice with a pooling stage bolted on.

WHY IT CLEARS knee-m69u'S BAR. m69u's standing position is that the card idling is correct until a NEW
axis is named, because every mapped axis is closed or knob-sized. This is a mechanism change, not a knob:
it alters what a feature vector can contain, which is precisely the quantity the aggregation work
identified as binding.

WHY IT IS WORTH IT EVEN IF THE MEMBER IS WEAKER. A 3D encoder is maximally decorrelated from twelve
slice-wise members. The owner's standing instruction: "even if a single model doesnt outperform our
previous models, its still worth testing if an ensemble with it have better performance - after all, its
about diversity, not averaging 7 numbers that are the same number." A 0.83 member that disagrees is worth
more here than a 0.86 member that does not.

WHAT MUST BE PRICED BEFORE ANY CARD TIME. Do not arm this on the strength of the argument above.
  1. Is there a pretrained 3D encoder available OFFLINE on this machine or fetchable, and is its licence
     compatible with the competition? Training a 3D encoder from scratch on 4406 studies is a different
     and much worse bet than fine-tuning one.
  2. Wall-clock for one arm, measured not guessed — a 3D encoder over ~20 slices is not the same cost as
     a 2D one over 20 slices.
  3. The cheap gate FIRST: the frozen-feature proxy called both signs correctly on the pooling axis at
     ~2 min against ~45 (see the depth_true row). Find out whether an equivalent proxy exists here before
     spending a full arm.

Ratio to state out loud when the answers are in: hours the arm costs, the gain the mechanism could
plausibly deliver, and the odds it clears 1.5%. Top-10 needs +0.0042 offline and no mapped axis pays it;
this is the only named candidate of that size besides a different corpus (knee-ombx, blocked on the owner).
notes:
WITHDRAWN THE SAME HOUR IT WAS FILED — the ledger had already armed this axis twice and I filed on an
incomplete grep. I searched experiments/README.md for "3d encoder|3D CNN|volume before|videomae|swin.*3d|
i3d" and none of those is the name it was run under. It is V-JEPA.

BOTH LEGS OF THE BEAD ARE FALSE, and each was measured:

1. "Untouched." False. `vjepa_probe` (2026-08-22) read V-JEPA 2 ViT-L frozen over the whole 12-slice
   stack: 0.7620 against a DINOv2-large control at 0.7669, a tie inside the 0.0062 floor with the
   capacity confound removed by construction. `vjepa_warm` (2026-08-22) then fitted it as a member at
   --whole-stack --slices 20 --train-size 256, which is exactly "sees the volume before any per-slice
   feature exists": solo holdout 0.8337 against roster members at 0.8525-0.8578.

2. "Maximally decorrelated from twelve slice-wise members, so worth a seat even if weaker." False, and
   this is the part that was actually measured rather than assumed. Residual distance to nearest
   neighbour 0.8210 (mean 0.8100), while the roster's MOST DISTANT seated member is 0.8801. The
   volumetric trunk is CLOSER to the pool than the pool's own outlier. Seat value +0.0002, 0 of 1
   clearing +0.0015.

So the diversity argument I built the bead on is the one the evidence contradicts most directly. A
different pretraining objective over a different input geometry produced a member that disagrees LESS
than the 2D members disagree with each other, which is a more interesting fact than the score is.

What the depth_true row meant by "untouched" was written before, or without reference to, these two rows.
It is not an open axis; it is a closed one under another name.

No card time to be spent here. Re-opening requires answering the residual-distance number, not re-quoting
the mechanism.

title: Does the gold ruler REORDER members, or only raise the level? Six hold-annotation members, no card cost
description:
knee-9198's last note names this and gates it: 'if the gold ruler is the one that tracks the board, member SELECTION should run on it ... Do not queue it before knee-bs4l reads; that pair is the cheapest evidence on whether the second ruler changes an ORDERING or only a level.' knee-bs4l HAS read (calibration +0.0072 proxy / +0.0129 annotation, same sign), so the gate is lifted.

WHY THIS IS NOT A KNOB. Every selection this project makes -- the greedy seat search, the 28-seat pool ceiling of 0.8753 offline, the transfer line, and the verdict in 2026-08-30_the-board-priced-an-offline-constant.md that '+0.0042 has no payer' -- is computed on the report-derived PROXY. knee-9198 measures the proxy and the objective +0.045 apart on identical weights, and argues the proxy is structurally BIASED against label-side movement because the metric is per-label rank AUC and the two label sets rank studies differently. If the gold ruler reorders these six, the shortfall is partly a FAULTY TEST rather than a missing mechanism, and the whole selection stack is being run on the wrong ruler.

THE READ COSTS NOTHING. It needs no submission slot and no training. It is 58 studies x 6 members of inference, because six --hold-annotations members already exist and only those may legally be read there (annotated_readings REFUSES the rest with TrainedOnAnnotationsError rather than scoring them).

PROXY ORDERING, all six, fold-0 honest, one label table, one sweep (logs/pool112.log, 2026-08-30):
  calib_dense_hold 0.8634 | blendhold 0.8576 | band_dense_hold 0.8573
  calib_span_hold  0.8564 | holdannot 0.8506 | band_span_hold  0.8493

PRE-REGISTRATION, written before the gold numbers are read:
 - ORDERING PRESERVED (Spearman near 1) -> the gold ruler is a LEVEL shift, selection is safe on the proxy, and the +0.0042 shortfall stays a missing-mechanism problem. This is the outcome that keeps the current plan.
 - ORDERING CHANGES at the top -> member selection is running on the wrong ruler. That does not by itself buy a point, but it re-opens the selection axis, which every audit has closed, and it prices re-training the shipping roster under --hold-annotations (~6 x 40 min of card, knee-9198) as a real option rather than a speculative one.

THE LIMIT, and it is severe: n=58, ~696 cells, and per-label standard error 0.04-0.09 (label_power). Six members spanning 0.014 of proxy will not separate pairwise on 58 studies. So the readable claim is the ORDERING PATTERN (does the proxy's best stay best), not any pairwise delta, and a reorder is a reason to measure further, never a result on its own.

SECOND LIMIT, already documented in annotated_readings' own docstring: a --calibrated-targets member's targets carry Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT, a constant FITTED on these same 696 cells, and --hold-annotations drops the cells without refitting it. So calib_* members have a structural edge on this ruler. level_agreement.stability prices it -- 4 of 5 levels under 2 sigma on disjoint halves -- but it is not zero, and calib_dense_hold being the proxy leader makes it exactly the member the caveat lands on.

Log: logs/goldrank.log
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-08-30: it raises the level and orders NOTHING. Closing.

The body above carries a PRE-FIX table read through the crossing defect (knee-bk99) — five of six rows
were under the wrong member's name. Ignore it. The corrected numbers, verified by equality against six
single-member reads:

  member                 proxy  rank    gold  rank
  calib_span_hold       0.8564     4  0.9152     1
  calib_dense_hold      0.8634     1  0.9117     2
  band_span_hold        0.8493     6  0.9023     3
  band_dense_hold       0.8573     3  0.8956     4
  blendhold             0.8576     2  0.8952     5
  holdannot             0.8506     5  0.8932     6

Spearman 0.14 — read bare, the pre-registered "ORDERING CHANGES" outcome. It does not survive its own
interval. annotated_readings now prints paired deltas against a baseline named on the command line
(--against), and against the proxy's top member five of six pairs sit inside the band:

  band_dense   -0.0161 [-0.0355, +0.0019]
  band_span    -0.0094 [-0.0277, +0.0053]
  calib_span   +0.0035 [-0.0121, +0.0187]
  blendhold    -0.0165 [-0.0362, +0.0029]
  holdannot    -0.0185 [-0.0398, -0.0019]  clears, and in the SAME direction the proxy already had

The entire gold spread best-to-worst is 0.022, narrower than the half-width of every interval on the
page. The apparent reorder is one pair moving +0.0035 inside a band twelve times its width. Spearman 0.14
is what ranking six indistinguishable members produces by construction — the statistic was measuring the
denominator, not the ruler.

Write-up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_the-gold-ruler-raises-everyone-and-orders-no-one.md

title: member_curve scores full-fit members in-sample and admits them to the greedy
description:
`member_curve` scores every checkpoint handed to it on the fold-0 holdout, including members fitted at
`--fold -1`. A full-fit member has TRAINED on those studies, so its number is in-sample and inflated.

MEASURED, 2026-08-30: `logs/curve_pool.log` printed `base_dense_ff.pt alone: 0.9035` while every
honestly-scored member in the same sweep read 0.83-0.86. That is not a good member; it is a leaked one.
The `_ff` / `_cf` families are all affected: base_dense_ff, calib_dense_hold_ff, calib_span_ff,
final_ws_cf, grade_ladder_cf, grade_ladder_ff, lr4e-5_ws_cf, lr4e-5_ws_ff, small_batch6_ff,
through_dense_cf, through_dense_ff.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE WRONG NUMBER: the greedy seats in score order, so leaked members are seated
FIRST. Any seat ordering or honest-seat count derived from a member_curve sweep over a mixed pool is
meaningless, and it fails SILENTLY — the log looks like every other sweep.

THE SISTER TOOL ALREADY HANDLES THIS. `kneemri/evaluation/record_mix.py` skips them, logging
`no holdout record, skipped` (record_mix.py:139 and :409), which is why `logs/greedy_named.log` reads
`111 of 200 records became members`. The asymmetry is the defect: two tools answering the same question,
one of which refuses leaked members and one of which averages them in.

FIX: `member_curve` should apply the same skip — a member with no holdout record cannot be scored on the
holdout. Its `seat_value` path already skips them; the `alone:` scoring loop does not. Make the skip
happen once, at pool construction, so both paths inherit it.

TEST THAT PINS IT: a pool containing one fold-0 member and one `--fold -1` member yields a curve over
the fold-0 member only, and names the skipped one.

title: greedyseat: fire a PROCEDURALLY selected fold-0 seven to buy back the offline ruler
description:
WHY, and it is not the score. comp/champion.json:53 records that two pins in a row bought board position by spending the ability to measure offline: six of the champion's seven seats are --fold -1, so the pinned entry has NO offline number by construction and board.jsonl records offline null. board_transfer confirms the damage from the other side - 29 of 31 ensemble entries are one-sided, and above 0.8691 the compression constant rests on FIVE resolved pairs. Every roster decision is now made against the board alone at five slots a day.

WHAT. The seven seats the greedy named over 111 members (logs/greedy_named.log): calib_dense_hold_s2026, merged_span_cf, labelwise_dense_s2026, blendhold_s2026, finding_calib_dense_s2026, margin_seat_s2026, warm_calib_dense_s2026. Offline 0.8768. All seven are already on comp/members.roster, so it is packageable with no new training. All seven are fold-0 and carry holdout records, so the entry IS seat-scoreable - which the champion is not.

TWO THINGS IN ONE SLOT. (1) The instrument: an anchored fold-0 point at the TOP of the offline range converts future seat decisions from a slot each into free offline reads. (2) A mechanism never tested: every entry this project has shipped was HAND-PICKED. Procedural greedy selection has never been put on the board.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS, from two fold-0 anchors in board.jsonl mapped at the top-band compression +0.89 to +0.97 board points per holdout point: 7-member anchor 0.8712 -> 0.933 gives +0.0056 * 0.89..0.97 = 0.938; top anchor 0.8751 -> 0.937 gives 0.9385. Both agree.
  >= 0.943 - procedural selection matches or beats hand-picking AND the fold-0 penalty is smaller than believed. Two results at once; re-read the all-data boundary.
  0.936-0.942 - AS PREDICTED. The ruler is bought, the anchor lands, no score claim. This is the expected outcome and it is a success for the stated purpose.
  0.930-0.935 - the anchor still lands and is still worth having, but the fold-0 all-data dose is larger at the top than the -0.004/-0.005 previously measured, which is itself a recorded finding.
  < 0.930 - procedural selection is WORSE than hand-picking by more than the fold-0 dose can explain; suspect the greedy overfits its own in-sample selection over 111 members before blaming the seats.

WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE. The greedy run is IN-SAMPLE over 111 members and seats 10 and 11 go to the pool's two worst members inside a plateau where +0.0024 buys twenty-five seats. A good board number here does not make the greedy order a ranking. And it does not touch the champion pin: raptorseat_v1 at 0.943 stays.

COST: one slot, zero card time, no training. Does NOT spend the slot held for the owner's explicit go.
notes:
LANDED. 55877491 scored 0.936 -- the bottom edge of the pre-registered 0.936-0.942 AS PREDICTED band.

THE INSTRUMENT WORKED, AND IT DID MORE THAN ANCHOR. Through the two prior fold-0 anchors
(0.8712 -> 0.933, 0.8751 -> 0.937; slope 1.026 board points per holdout point):

  raw greedy in-sample 0.8768 -> predicts 0.9387, rounds 0.939, actual 0.936, err -0.0027
  bias-corrected       0.8740 -> predicts 0.9359, rounds 0.936, actual 0.936, err +0.0001

The +0.0028 greedy selection bias was measured purely offline on 111 records. The board prices the same
correction at +0.0027 without being shown it. That is a cross-ruler confirmation of an offline constant,
and it is the real return on this slot.

IT ALSO KILLS AN APPARENT RULER INVERSION. Raw, this entry reads offline UP 0.0017 against the previous
anchor while the board went DOWN 0.001 -- the third point breaking the ordering, the same shape recorded
before. It is not an inversion: it is the greedy bias, and the correction restores the ordering exactly.
Any future entry selected by search must be entered in board.jsonl bias-corrected, never raw.

PROCEDURAL SELECTION DOES NOT BEAT HAND-PICKING. 0.936 vs raptorweight_v1's 0.944. The fold-0 all-data
dose covers ~half (-0.004/-0.005), leaving ~0.003-0.004 for the selection term itself -- above the
0.0015 board resolution by two ticks, so present but small. STATED LIMIT: no hand-picked fold-0 seven
exists, so this crosses the fold boundary and the dose is an estimate, not a matched control.

Row written to comp/board.jsonl with offline 0.8740 (corrected) and offline_scope naming the correction.
Documented in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md. board_check --live and champion_check both green; the champion pin
stays raptorweight_v1 at 0.944, as the pre-registration said it would.

title: Foreign seat WEIGHT is unmeasured: 1/7 is a convention, the mechanism says ~1/3
description:
FILED 2026-08-29 21:15Z. No bead has ever named this dial.

WHAT IS UNMEASURED. Every foreign-seat entry holds RaptorSeat.weight = 1/7. raptor_seat.py states its own
reason: "One member entering a six-member roster takes one seat of seven, which is the weight every seating
entry in this project's history has used." That is a convention about SEAT COUNT, and the premise is wrong
about what is being blended.

THE MECHANISM. The blend is two SYSTEMS, not seven members. Ours is a six-member logit-average at 0.941
board. Theirs is ONE model at 0.923 board (raptor_solo 55829913) - level with our best single by
measurement. A 0.941 system and a 0.923 system averaged at 6:1 gives the independent side a seventh of the
vote when its quality justifies nearer a third. Equal quality would say even; ours is stronger and is
itself an ensemble, so ~1/3 is the honest correction.

WHY IT SURVIVES TODAY'S CLOSURES. fleettwo_v1 closed the COUNT dimension of foreign seating (0.942, flat).
fourseat/trioseat closed our own seat count. Neither touched the weight. It is the one dial of the
foreign-seating axis with no reading at all.

IT IS ALSO AN INSTRUMENT FOR knee-uco3. That P0 reads dark6's 0.937 as the seventh seat being INERT. An
inert seat cannot care about its weight: flat here CONFIRMS knee-uco3, any move REFUTES it.

WHY ONE SLOT AND NOT A SWEEP. Board-only, because every raptor arm is --fold -1 and no offline pairing
exists - raptor_seat.py's own objection. So spend ONE at the largest step the mechanism supports:
0.143 -> 0.333, a 2.3x move. Slope shows in one slot; flat closes the axis in one instead of four.

KERNEL: comp/kernels/kneemri-raptorweight, built 2026-08-29 21:14Z. One float differs from
raptorseat_v1 - same six, same order, same overlap=False, same LogitAverage, same kit, same checkpoint.

PRE-REGISTERED (vs champion 0.943, BOARD_RESOLVABLE 0.0015):
  >=0.946        real lever AND top ten. Re-pin champion.json; next slot sweeps to 1/2.
  0.9435-0.9455  real gain. Keep 1/3; price 1/2 only on an idle slot.
  0.9405-0.943   FLAT. Foreign seating closed in both dimensions. knee-uco3 gains support.
  <=0.940        dilutes at real weight. 1/7 was at or near a maximum; stop widening the foreign side.

LIMIT IT CANNOT PASS: cannot separate "the weight is flat" from "THIS foreign member is flat". Same
--fold -1 limit fleettwo_v1 carries for the count dimension.
notes:
RESULT: raptorweight_v1 read 0.944 (ref 55875622, scored 2026-08-30). New best row; pin moved in comp/champion.json.

THE BAND LABEL AND THE ARITHMETIC DISAGREE AND THE ARITHMETIC WINS. 0.944 landed in the pre-registered 0.9435-0.9455 branch, whose text reads 'a real gain over the champion, above the resolution floor'. It is not. 0.944 - 0.943 = +0.001, UNDER this arm's own BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015, and 0.9435 was never an attainable score because the board quantises to 0.001. The band was mis-drawn: it put a clears-the-floor label on a value below the floor. Every future pre-registration on this board must snap its edges to attainable 0.001 steps and check each edge against the floor before the number arrives.

WHAT IS TRUE: this is the best board row the project owns and the pin follows it. WHAT IS NOT: the weight is not shown to be a lever. A 2.3x change in the foreign share moved one unresolvable tick, which reads closer to the FLAT branch than the gain branch. With fleettwo_v1's flat count reading, NEITHER dimension of the foreign-seating axis has produced a resolvable move, and knee-uco3's inert-seat reading gains its second support.

DO NOT sweep the weight to 1/2. That instruction was conditional on clearing the floor and the floor was not cleared.

title: Nothing writes comp/members.roster when a run finishes — 5 of 16 best seats were missing
description:
Found 2026-08-29 21:05Z while building the 16-seat entry. Five of its sixteen seats were not in comp/members.roster: merged_span_cf (greedy seat 2, solo 0.8618), labelwise_dense_s2026 (seat 3, solo 0.8613 — THIRD-BEST SOLO THE PROJECT OWNS, and the only member pooling slices labelwise), warm_calib_dense_s2026 (seat 7, a warm restart from a fitted encoder — the lane champion.json calls '0 of 131 arms have ever used'), focus_mcl_s2026 (seat 11), contrast_dense_s2026 (seat 13).

The roster is the package's ONLY definition: a member absent from it cannot be shipped no matter what any other file says. So this was five of the sixteen best available seats silently unshippable, including the third-best checkpoint in the project.

MECHANISM: a run finishing writes a checkpoint, a holdout record and (usually) a ledger section. NOTHING writes the roster. It is a hand-edited file, so every member in it is there because somebody remembered.

FIX, mechanically checkable: a check asserting the roster is the scoreable pool minus an EXPLICITLY DOCUMENTED decline. Every .pt under the processed root with a holdout record is either (a) named in members.roster, or (b) named in a declines list with a reason. Anything in neither is a finding. That would have caught all five, and it costs one pass over a directory.

NOTE the trap it must avoid: 12 checkpoints are smoke runs or scored under an older label table (record_mix --largest-pool drops them by name). Those belong in the declines list, not the roster.

Related: knee-utxq (the 16-seat entry this was found building), and the process lesson recorded in experiments/README.md — recover provenance from metrics.jsonl BEFORE declining an undocumented checkpoint, since the recipe is always there.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-30 00:05Z, and the defect was three times the size the bead recorded. kneemri.kaggle.roster_check (committed, unit-tested, 9 tests) asserts every checkpoint under the processed root that has a HoldoutRecord is named in comp/members.roster OR in the new comp/members.declines WITH A REASON; a bare name in the declines file is itself a finding, because a name alone records that somebody decided and not what. It also reports a member that is in BOTH files and a roster line matching nothing on disk.

FIRST RUN: 123 scoreable of 200 checkpoints, 47 packaged, 0 declined, 76 UNDOCUMENTED. Not five - seventy-six. And the worst of them is not labelwise_dense_s2026: stackfit_s2026 scores 0.8631 solo under LogitAverage on the 909-study fold-0 holdout, which makes it the SECOND-BEST solo checkpoint the project owns (behind calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634 and ahead of merged_span_cf 0.8618), and it was unshippable. raptor_distill_s2026 0.8613 and distill_pairs_s2026 0.8594 were too.

THE SPLIT, and the rule is not a score cut. Thirty members joined the roster: every undocumented member clearing 0.8460 solo, which is extended_ws_s2026 - the weakest member this roster has ever added on MERIT. The roster does package weaker checkpoints (lora_r8_v3small 0.8215, crop80_tissue 0.8345, focus_mcl 0.5332), but each of those is a named INSTRUMENT, which is a reason and not a number; so the way back onto the roster from a decline is to name the instrument the member would be. Forty-six were declined in writing: thirty-four below that merit level, eleven smoke/probe runs that never became members on the current label table, and confident224_s2026 - a REAL arm that falls out of the same-ruler pool and returns on a rescore (knee-8hau), written down as such so it is not mistaken for a twelfth smoke run.

AFTER: 123 scoreable, 77 packaged, 46 declined, 0 undocumented, exit 0. Wired into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as the thirteenth check, to be run after any run finishes and before building an entry out of the pool.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not push the package - the roster is the DEFINITION, and thirty new lines mean a dataset push before any of them can be mounted. That is a separate, deliberate step (package_members), and knee-0dtv was about the definition.

title: Ship the 16-seat entry: same 5 decodes as 28, +0.0045 offline, prices at ~+0.005 board
description:
From the matched seat curves (2026-08-29 20:50Z, experiments/README.md). The honest curve — greedy refit on half the studies, scored on the other half, so no selection bias — peaks at 0.8753 with 28 members. The shipped champion's five-twin shadow reads 0.8701. That is +0.0052 offline, the first delta since fourseat_v1 that is near the 0.0053 floor rather than a tenth of it, and it comes from SEAT COUNT rather than from member quality (closed, knee-07b0) or rank-space diversity (refuted, same section).

Unknown and blocking: what those 28 members cost in DECODES. The roster's 56 seats ride 27 on one decode, 19 on a second, ten singletons; if the honest 28 scatter across ten decodes it is unshippable inside the kernel's runtime, and the efficiency track (rank 16, 0.925) gets worse not better.

Next step, both free and no slot:
  1. Pull the 28 names from logs/seats_honest.log (the honest curve names its picks in order).
  2. python -m kneemri.kaggle.roster_reads --candidates <the 28> — prices them in decodes.
  3. If the read cost is one or two decodes, this is the best-argued candidate for the one spendable slot. If it is ten, ask decode_entry for the best 28-seat set CONSTRAINED to few decodes and re-read the honest number under that constraint.

Note the denominator trap decode_entry already fell into once: its search sees the SCOREABLE pool only, so a set it proposes cannot include any --fold -1 member. The honest curve has the same blind spot, which is a floor on what a shipped roster does, not a ceiling.
notes:
CLOSED WITHOUT A SLOT, 2026-08-29 21:12Z — REFUTED BY AN ENTRY THAT ALREADY SHIPPED.

comp/board.jsonl holds honest12 (ref 55817896, 2026-08-27): the SAME instrument, `record_mix --seats
honest --vote logit`, seated at its own peak of TWELVE. Offline 0.8751, board 0.937. Champion 0.943.
Its holdout said +0.0050 and the board paid -0.006: a sign flip, not a compression.

The 16-seat set here is honest12 plus six more seats from the same greedy — ten of honest12's twelve
recipes are in it. So its transfer coefficient is not unmeasured; it is measured once and negative.
Both pre-registered branches (0.945-0.950 / 0.940-0.943) omitted the only branch with evidence, ~0.937.

MY ERROR: priced this off champion.json's saturation prose (6-11 seats, ~0.941) and never opened
board.jsonl, which carries a twelve-seat entry off this exact curve with a score and a written verdict.
CLAUDE.md's rule — read the ledger and the record before filing — would have caught it in one grep.

WHAT SURVIVES: the six members surfaced by the hunt, all now rostered and documented, and knee-0dtv.
The seating dies, the members do not. honest12's own verdict sends the next slot to a better SINGLE
member (knee-wbwq, warm restarts) — and warm_calib_dense_s2026 (0.8562) is now on disk and rostered.

title: Backfill offline holdout reads for the 35 ensemble entries that have a board number and none
description:
comp/board.jsonl now holds 74 of 74 live submissions, but 35 of the 60 ensemble-scope rows carry a board number and offline: null - including the pinned champion raptorseat_v1, calibsix_v1, votefit_v1, soloseat_v1, calibsolo, onepair_v1, trioseat_v1, fleettwo_v1 and fourseat_v1. Every one of those is a pair board_transfer cannot form, which is why the regime that actually prices today's decisions is fitted on THREE resolved pairs (top cell +0.99 [+0.77, +1.18]).

This costs no card and no slot: each entry is a set of members already on disk, served through the same vote the kernel used, scored on the fold-0 holdout. The blocker is that some entries are all --fold -1 members, whose holdout sits inside their training set - those must stay null rather than be filled with an in-sample number, which is exactly the defect knee-* on raptor_solo just cost us. So the deliverable is: fill the ones that CAN be honestly filled, and record scope/reason for the ones that cannot.

Why it matters: the compression constant and the ensemble-bonus law are both quoted as planning premises, and both are currently fitted mostly on entries from before 2026-08-20.
notes:
2026-08-29 21:40Z DONE, and the deliverable was the bound rather than the numbers. kneemri.kaggle.entry_offline surveys every null offline cell and either fills it or records offline_scope naming why not. 34 rows with named members and a null: 10 filled (ratepair_v1, solotop_v1, rateviews_v1, topviews_v1, sixstrong_v1, sixfresh_v1, sevengrade_v1, sixfresh_v2, sevenplane_v1, accumseat_v1; board 0.921-0.933; scored under RankAverage because all ten shipped before kneemri-vote served LogitAverage), 24 declined - 20 in-sample (_ff / final_ws_e12), 2 foreign-in-sample (raptor_v4_swa, per foreign_overlap), 2 no-record (_cf merges wrote no holdout file).

board_transfer re-fit: whole record +1.55 -> +1.25; top regime (>=0.8668) +0.99 [+0.77,+1.18] on THREE pairs -> +0.97 [+0.94,+1.11] on FIFTEEN; a second cell now resolves at >=0.8691 (+0.89 [+0.70,+1.19], 5 pairs); inversions 0/127 -> 0/233 resolved.

The constant did not move (0.02, inside its own interval). The interval halved and the pair count went 3 -> 15. So this bought CONFIDENCE in a premise already being quoted, not a new premise. Compression above board 0.937 stays unmeasured and the file now says so per row.

title: The offline ruler resolves ~0.004; below that a submission is a coin flip
description:
Fit board on offline over the 22 scored ensemble entries in comp/board.jsonl whose offline column is our ruler on our members (raptor_solo excluded, foreign member on a different ruler):

  slope 2.099   95% CI [1.197, 3.012]   r 0.855   residual sd 0.0078
  forced slope 1.00 -> residual sd 0.0101
  forced slope 1.82 -> residual sd 0.0078

THE CONSTANT SURVIVES. board_transfer ~ +1.82 sits inside the interval and fits as well as the free slope, so nothing recorded needs changing.

THE INTERVAL AND THE RESIDUAL ARE THE FINDING. [1.20, 3.01] is not a multiplier to believe a product from. Residual sd 0.0078 is what predicting a board score from an offline score is actually worth, and it is comparable to the ENTIRE gap to first place (0.009 at the 14:00Z live read).

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both about slot spending:
1. An offline difference under ~0.004 predicts nothing about the board — the two rosters' predicted board scores overlap almost completely. This is the quantitative reason sixteen board entries sit inside 0.005 of each other despite each being chosen as an improvement: the ruler that chose them cannot resolve them.
2. It prices the honest seat plateau. Eight seats to twenty-four is +0.0005 offline, an eighth of the resolution floor. Submitting to find out which is better spends a slot on a coin flip.

So a slot buys knowledge only for a change big enough to clear ~0.004 offline. Nothing in the current pool is. This is the case FOR the raddino arm and AGAINST another reseating, in the instrument's own units, and it is why the spendable slot stayed holstered today.

A METHOD NOTE THAT COST ME A WRONG FILING. Reading the gap board-minus-offline down the TOP EIGHTEEN entries it looks like a flat OFFSET of +0.061 with no slope at all, which would contradict +1.82 outright. Those eighteen span an offline range of 0.017; range restriction flattens a slope toward zero, and eyeballing the top of a score-sorted list IS range restriction. Fit the whole set or do not fit.

ALSO SETTLED HERE (see the same interpretation): the _cf leak does NOT reach the shipped champion. honest12 carries two fold-1 members and its board-minus-offline gap is +0.0619 against a pack mean of ~+0.0613 — about +0.0006 of inflation, a third of the scatter. Two leaked members of twelve are real and unmeasurable. That does NOT clear the honest seat curve, where the leak is two of EIGHT and greedy selected them on their leaked scores; it caps how large that inflation can be.

Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-29_seats-per-decode.md
notes:
2026-08-29 15:11Z — the _cf half of this issue's description is RETRACTED; the transfer measurement is not.

The description says the _cf leak 'does NOT reach the shipped champion' and reads honest12's +0.0006
residual as an upper bound on its size. There is no leak to bound — _cf is scheme=merged, fold 0 of 5,
split_seed 2026, same split as every other member (knee-anx7). The +0.0006 is what a roster with no leaked
member looks like. An effect that is merely small when the hypothesis predicts small is not confirmation.

EVERYTHING ELSE STANDS and none of it depended on the leak: slope 2.099, CI [1.197, 3.012], r 0.855,
residual sd 0.0078, +1.82 fitting as well as the free slope, and the range-restriction trap that nearly
had me file the constant as refuted. The two consequences for slot spending are unchanged — an offline
difference under ~0.004 predicts nothing about the board, and the eight-to-twenty-four plateau (+0.0005)
is a coin flip to submit.

title: card_check exists and I skipped it, because label_combine's docstring says 'costs no card' and that is conditional on a warm cache
description:
2026-08-29 14:34Z. Cost: a 12-epoch card arm stretched ~45% on at least one epoch, and 634 MiB of headroom left on a 32 GB card.

WHAT HAPPENED. raddino_dense was training with 27.14 GB reserved (its gate reserves 29,992 MiB). I launched
two python -m kneemri.evaluation.label_combine runs beside it WITHOUT running
python -m kneemri.experiments.card_check first. Both found cold prediction caches, ran their encoders, and
put ~4.2 GB on the card: nvidia-smi read 31,973 of 32,607 MiB used. The arm survived, but its epoch 1
finished 14:12:12Z and epoch 2 had not appeared by 14:34Z against a measured 914-929 s epoch — roughly 45%
over. Same shape as the failure card_check was built for (two identical member_curve scans stretching one
member from three minutes to eleven), and the cost is the same: the READING, not the card.

WHY I SKIPPED THE CHECK, which is the part worth fixing. label_combine's class docstring opens 'No GPU:
arithmetic over the arrays HoldoutPredictions.cached returns', and I read that as a property of the tool.
It is not. The main() docstring says it correctly forty lines lower: 'IT COSTS NO CARD when the members are
already on member_curve's prediction store ... the encoder runs only for a member the store has never
seen.' The claim is conditional on CACHE WARMTH and the top line does not say so. So the tool advertises
itself as card-free, and card_check is the thing that would have contradicted it — but nothing prompts you
to run card_check for a tool you believe is offline.

WHAT IS ALREADY FIXED. label_combine now takes --device (kneemri/evaluation/label_combine.py:170), mirroring
member_curve, which had it for exactly this reason. Before today this CLI could not be told to stay off the
card at all: HoldoutPredictions(VisibleCards().device()) was hardcoded. Verified working — the rerun logs
'finding_calib_dense_s2026.pt: cache MISS, computing on cpu'.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED, and the two candidate fixes.
(1) The class docstring's opening line should carry the condition the main() docstring already states.
    Cheap, and it removes the belief that caused the skip.
(2) CPU CONTENTION IS UNGUARDED EVEN SO. --device cpu keeps the tool off the card but not out of the
    trainer's way: ten members of CPU encoder inference over ~880 studies saturates the 32 threads the
    arm's dataloader feeds from. I killed the CPU rerun for this reason at 14:34Z, so the routed pricing
    it was computing is deferred until the card frees rather than done. card_check asks the DEVICE, which
    is right for its own question and blind to this one.

DENOMINATOR HONESTY. One epoch's slowdown is one observation, and the GPU contention window (14:26-14:32Z)
overlaps epoch 2 directly, so the 45% is attributable but not isolated - I did not run a matched arm and
will not spend one on this. The claim that stands is the headroom number, 634 MiB free, which is measured.
notes:
2026-08-29 15:05Z — THE KILL AT 14:34Z NEVER HAPPENED, and the cost is now measured rather than attributed.

I recorded an hour ago that the ~45% epoch-2 slowdown was attributable to contention but not isolated,
because the GPU window overlapped it. That caveat is now moot for the wrong reason: the four CPU
label_combine processes I believed I had killed at 14:34Z were STILL RUNNING at 15:04Z. Windows pids
67364, 49268 (started 14:28Z) and 15028, 50752 (14:33Z), confirmed by CommandLine through
Get-CimInstance. They ran thirty extra minutes on top.

THE MEASURED COST. epoch 0 = 929 s, epoch 1 = 914 s, both clean. Epoch 1 ended 14:12Z. At 15:04Z epoch 2
had not landed: 52 minutes against 914, a factor of 3.4. Nothing else was on the card (28,841 MiB used,
consistent with the arm's own 27.14 GB reserved plus context) and gates had finished at 14:52Z, so the
CPU jobs are the only surviving explanation for the last twelve minutes of it and the dominant one for
the rest. This is knee-8hau's unguarded half priced: --device cpu keeps a tool off the card and does not
keep it out of the trainer's dataloader.

WHY THE KILL SILENTLY NO-OPPED — the msys-pid trap, in the direction that is worse. I used ps -W, which
prints WINPIDs, and then killed those numbers from git-bash, where kill wants MSYS pids. Every kill
no-opped with No such file or directory and I read the absence of an error as success. The liveness
direction of this trap is documented and I have been bitten by it before; the KILL direction is the one
that costs, because a failed liveness check argues back and a failed kill does not. Correct form: from
git-bash use plain ps and kill; to kill a Windows pid use PowerShell Stop-Process -Id <winpid> -Force,
and VERIFY by re-enumerating on CommandLine until the count reads 0. Never trust a kill's exit code.

AND THE ROUTED PRICING IS NOT A CHEAP MEASUREMENT AFTER ALL. logs/lc_base10.log shows it still loading
dinov2-small weights after thirty-six minutes: the ten honest12 members had COLD prediction caches, so
--device cpu was not doing arithmetic over stored arrays, it was running an encoder over 881 studies on
CPU. That is hours, not minutes. The --device flag committed in ca77bfb is still the right fix — it is
what let this run at all without OOMing the arm — but the lesson it encodes needs a second half: cpu is
the safe device for a WARM member and the wrong device for a cold one. A cold member wants the card,
after the arm, not the CPU during it.

NEXT ACTION for the routed blendlabels pricing (knee-fuhq's continuation): re-run with --device cuda once
raddino lands, so the cache misses run at card speed and populate the store for every later reader.

title: raddino_dense is gated on the HONEST eight-seat held-out delta, not on greedy position
description:
Pre-registered 2026-08-29 14:20Z, while raddino_dense is at epoch 1 of 12 and its number does not exist yet.

MATCHED-EPOCH STATE, so the read below is not made on a collapse. raddino_dense e0 0.7237 / e1 0.7377 against its
matched control base_dense_s2026 e0 0.7625 / e1 0.7759 (e2 0.8144, e3 0.8232, final 0.8512). A CONSTANT -0.038 at
both epochs, not a widening one, and nothing like the SSL-collapse family it could be mistaken for (mae_matched
-0.1505 at matched e3, encoder_adapt_thawed -0.1416). one_cycle's anneal has not run. It runs to e11.

THE QUESTION THIS ARM ACTUALLY ANSWERS. knee-nj4l names three remaining axes and this is axis (1), a trunk
pretrained OUTSIDE natural images, with the bead's own instruction: 'DO NOT close this by reseating. It is closed
by a member whose errors are somewhere else.' So the deliverable is NOT the solo AUC. Every seated member is
facebook/dinov2-small; the thing being bought is a different pixel group.

WHY THE RULER IS GREEDY POSITION AND NOT THE 0.0062 FLOOR. experiments/README.md:5361-5367 settled it on
raptor_distill: that arm read +0.0035 solo (the sign its mechanism predicted, from an architecture-distant
teacher) and was still declined, because greedy admitted it 44th of 121 records, 39 positions after the peak set
closed, while our own calib_dense_hold enters 17th. The finding was 'a student trained on our decode, our corpus
and our trunk lands back in our pixel group no matter whose ordering it was taught -- distillation moves ORDERING
and the seat ruler prices PIXEL GROUP.' raddino changes the one variable that constraint was about.

THE GATE, WRITTEN BEFORE THE NUMBER. Run the same greedy over the same record pool and read raddino_dense's ENTRY
POSITION, against base_dense_s2026's as the matched control.
  * Enters EARLIER than base_dense despite a lower solo AUC -> the trunk moved the pixel group. That is knee-nj4l
    axis (1) answered positively, and it licenses the sequel below.
  * Enters at a comparable position -> the trunk is a weaker member of the SAME group. Axis (1) closes here; a
    non-natural-image pretrain does not buy distance in this task, which is a real constraint and worth the 2.8h.
  * Enters late, like raptor_distill's 44th -> same as above, more strongly.
Read positions with raptor's fold -1 contamination in mind (README:5369-5372): positions 1, 2, 4, 7, 8 and 18 are
--fold -1 checkpoints whose holdout sits inside their training set, so only honestly-trained members are readable
against each other.

THE SEQUEL, LICENSED ONLY BY THE FIRST BRANCH. experiments/README.md:5374-5377 leaves exactly one distillation
variant open -- 'distillation onto a NON-DINOv2 trunk' -- and states it costs one student and NO teacher, because
the raptor_v4_swa teacher pass over 4,406 studies is on disk. So raddino + --distill-weight 0.3 --teacher-targets
teacher_fold0.npz is the one arm that moves BOTH things the constraint separated: the trunk (pixel group) and the
ordering. It is not queued now and must not be: if the plain trunk does not move the group, adding a teacher that
provably does not move it either cannot.

COST/GAIN. The gate itself is FREE -- greedy over existing records, no card. The sequel is ~3.1h for a mechanism
knee-ombx prices at 1.5-3%, taken only on the first branch.
notes:
2026-08-29 17:23Z — raddino_dense landed and is READ. 12/12 epochs, best 0.8155 at epoch 7, converged (convergence_check does not list it; its exit 1 is 8 pre-existing truncated runs).

Against honest12 (the pinned champion is unpriceable: 5 of its 6 members are fold -1):
  seat value -0.0007, 0 of 1 clearing +0.0015. Negative, which the board charges at ~3x, so ~-0.0020.
  distance: nearest 0.7987, mean 0.7502. The roster's own seated members sit at 0.87-0.90 nearest.
  competence axis: in the bulk, slightly below zero, not in either tail at +/-5.

Pre-registered ladder said <= +0.001 confirms head-monoculture. It reads -0.0007, so the VERDICT holds — but the distance column refutes the mechanism behind it. raddino is the most distant member ever priced against this roster by a wide margin; it is emphatically not a twin. It is simply weaker: 0.8155 against a roster around 0.86.

So the head is not what makes members interchangeable. A genuinely different encoder family, with a genuinely different ordering, still adds nothing because its quality is 0.045 short. Diversity without quality is not usable.

This does NOT contradict the repo's measured 'diversity beats member quality' (6 board entries): that was among members of COMPARABLE quality, and a 0.045 gap is far outside the range it was measured over.

Its curve peaked at epoch 7 (0.8155) and declined through the one_cycle anneal to 0.8124 — overfit at this recipe, not undertrained, so more epochs buy nothing. A raddino at competitive quality would be a strong seat given that distance, but closing 0.045 is not a knob.

title: fiveseat: does a cheap DINOv2-base trunk pay inside read A's one decode?
description:
Kernel comp/kernels/kneemri-fiveseat/ is written, metadata in place, kit at 60dbec0 clean. chosen = (final_ws_cf, grade_ladder_cf, through_dense_cf, small_batch6_ff, base_dense_ff) — fourseat plus base_dense_ff, a DINOv2-BASE trunk, all five in read A so the entry still costs ONE decode.

PRE-REGISTERED, against fourseat/trioseat 0.938 and champion raptorseat_v1 0.943:
  >=0.944  trunk swap pays inside one decode; architecture diversity is a seat axis; re-pin.
  0.941-0.943  pays, level with the three-decode champion at a third of runtime — an efficiency-track result.
  0.938-0.940  flat, so raptorseat's +0.002 was the DECODE and not the trunk; closes the cheap-architecture lane.

title: Price the VOTE axis honestly: split-half ceiling on weighted rank
description: QualityWeightedRank's own docstring says it 'has to be read on a split half, exactly as per-label selection was, and per-label selection is what failed that test' — and that split-half read was never built. So the project ships LogitAverage (votefit_v1, +1 tick over dark6, inside its pre-registered flat band) and has never measured what ANY weighting rule is worth once the fitting is paid for. PRICE: 0 card, 0 slots, CPU only over holdout records already on disk. P(clears +0.0015 offline honestly) ~ 0.3; if it clears +0.005 that is ~+0.009 on the board at board_transfer 1.82, which is the largest lever left that needs no training. DESIGN: fit weights on half the holdout studies, score on the other half, swap, average — and report the FIT-ON-SELF number beside it, because the gap between the honest and the overfit read is what says whether an apparent gain is fitting noise. Rules compared: RankAverage (flat, the ledger's rule), QualityWeightedRank (one weight per member), LabelQualityRank (new: one weight per member PER LABEL, the ceiling of the weighting family), LogitAverage, MedianLogit. The falsifiable part: if the honest per-label read does not beat flat, the vote axis closes for good and no further rule is written.
close_reason:
BUILT AND READ. kneemri/evaluation/vote_ceiling.py fits each weighted rule on one half of the holdout studies and scores it on the other, both ways, averaged, with the fit-on-self number beside it. Two independent reads agree and the falsifiable clause fires: the honest per-label read does NOT beat flat, so the vote axis is CLOSED and no further vote rule gets written.

42 members / 909 studies: RankAverage 0.8711 | QualityWeightedRank 0.8712 (+0.0000) | LabelQualityRank 0.8713 (+0.0002, overfit gap +0.0004) | LogitAverage 0.8725 (+0.0014) | MedianLogit 0.8710 (-0.0001).
Six-seat one-decode shipping shape: RankAverage 0.8738 | QualityWeightedRank 0.8738 (-0.0001) | LabelQualityRank 0.8739 (+0.0001, overfit gap +0.0006) | LogitAverage 0.8745 (+0.0006) | MedianLogit 0.8728 (-0.0010).

Everything weighted sits under the +0.0015 seat_value floor at both sizes. The overfit gap is the load-bearing detail: at +0.0004/+0.0006 the rule is not even overfitting -- a 12-parameter-per-member rule that reproduces flat when it grades its own homework has nothing to weight, which coheres with competence_axis (member quality is 81.7 pct of the pool spread, so the members are not differentiated enough per-label for a weight to find anything). LogitAverage, ALREADY SHIPPED as votefit_v1, is the family best at +0.0014, which corroborates its single board tick rather than adding a lever.

title: Distil the raptor member into OUR family: the first teacher whose ordering the pool does not already hold
description:
MECHANISM, and why today licenses it. distill_pairs (experiments/README.md:2931) read +0.0016 with a seat value of -0.0003, and the ledger names the cause exactly: 'at 0.9159 nearest, this member sits closer to a seated member than any seated member sits to its own nearest neighbour. A rank average cannot pay for an ordering it already holds.' That was a DINOv2 self-teacher. It is a statement about that teacher, not about distillation.

WHAT CHANGED TODAY. raptor_v4_swa scored 0.923 solo on the board (55829913), EXACTLY level with our own best single (calibsolo 0.923). So we now hold a teacher that is (a) equal in quality by the only ruler that counts, (b) another architecture, another decode, another training corpus — the one teacher whose ordering our pool provably does not hold. That is the precise defect distill_pairs diagnosed, removed.

AND IT IS THE ROUTE comp/champion.json NAMES. The pin's last principle: at the measured seat pass-through the member-quality lane ceilings near 0.943, 'so 0.950 is NOT reachable by making members better, and the remaining routes are external data and stacking.' A student taught by a foreign model IS the external-data route, expressed as a member we can seat — which raptorseat cannot be, since a foreign decode costs a whole second forward path inside the kernel budget.

THE BUILD IS ALMOST ALL EXISTING PARTS. Split(name='train') exists for exactly this ('lets the SAME path run over studies whose labels we hold'), RaptorEntry.run consumes it, TeacherFile.write is the format, and train already takes --distill-weight/--teacher-targets. What is new is one CLI that joins them.

PRE-REGISTRATION goes in the arm header before the number, against the control the recipe fixes. What this bead commits to now: the teacher pass is scored on the SAME fold-0 holdout our members are, so the teacher's own holdout AUC is read first and recorded — a teacher weaker than the student on our ruler is a different experiment.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY. raptor was fitted on all 4,406 studies, so its predictions on our TRAIN studies are partly memorised. That is fine for a teacher (we are copying its ordering, not validating it) and the student's fold-0 holdout stays clean because no fold-0 teacher target is ever shown. But it does mean the teacher's soft targets are sharper on train than an honest model's would be, which is a reason a large --distill-weight could hurt.

COST: ~40 min of card for the teacher pass over 4,406 studies (reused free by every later arm on this axis), then ~50 min for one dense student. ZERO submission slots.
notes: RESULT 2026-08-28: raptor_distill landed 0.8613 holdout (best at epoch 8 of 12, converged — not truncated, convergence_check clean). Pre-registered ladder: >=0.8640 transfers and earns a seat; 0.8578-0.8640 DIRECTIONAL, licenses reading DISTANCE only; <=0.8578 closes the axis. 0.8613 lands DIRECTIONAL: +0.0035 over our best own member (band_dense 0.8578), below the 1.5% bar, so it is NOT a finding and NOT a seat on this number alone. What it does establish is that a foreign teacher's ordering IS partly learnable by our family — distill_pairs read +0.0016 from a DINOv2 self-teacher, this reads +0.0035 from an architecture-distant one, which is the sign the bead predicted. Next and only licensed step: read the member's DISTANCE to the seated pool (record_mix greedy over the full holdout pool, running). A seat is licensed only if the distance is genuinely new, not by the solo number.

The bead's own gate was distance, not the solo number: greedy admits it 44th of 121, 39 positions past the peak set, while our own calib_dense_hold enters 17th. A student trained on our decode, our corpus and our trunk lands back in our pixel group whatever ordering it was taught — distillation moves ORDERING, the seat ruler prices PIXEL GROUP. Ledger row written (experiments/README.md, 2026-08-28 section); the teacher pass is on disk and free to any later arm.

title: Reimplement the raptor model (backbone + attention-MIL head) so the serving path holds no foreign code
description:
raptor_feed made the DECODE ours; this makes the FORWARD PASS ours. What is actually foreign about the member is nothing but the weights: the architecture is a timm backbone plus a forty-line attention-MIL head — LayerNorm, a two-layer gate softmaxed over the WINDOW axis, a per-finding linear read-out — and their notebook publishes it in full.

kneemri/evaluation/raptor_model.py writes it out with THEIR parameter names (backbone, norm, att, clsW, clsb), which is the whole trick: load_state_dict(..., strict=True) then either accepts their checkpoint or refuses it, with no key remapping to get subtly wrong.

ORACLE: 'python -m kneemri.evaluation.raptor_model --studies N --device cpu --checkpoint <pt>' scores the same studies through their module and ours and asserts the twelve probabilities are EQUAL, not close. raptor_feed's oracle stops at the uint8 volume; this one runs windows, backbone, head, sigmoid. Together they cover every step from a DICOM directory to a prediction, including the windowing stage neither module's own unit test can reach. Equality is claimed on cpu/fp32 only — their infer_probs runs fp16 under autocast on CUDA, which is a serving choice, not part of the spec.

CONSEQUENCE: comp/build_kit.py already packages kneemri/ and core/ wholesale and Kaggle's image already carries cv2, pydicom and timm, so the member ships with no wheel and no vendored file. external/raptor stays a measurement tool on our own disk only.

Unblocks knee-p0gk.
notes: 2026-08-28: end-to-end oracle now at 25 studies -- logs/raptor_model_equiv25.log ends '25 studies score identically'. Real raptor_ft_coatnet_v4_full_swa.pt, CPU/fp32, np.array_equal on the twelve probabilities, no tolerance. Decode oracle (knee-2olz) covers the 200-study volume half; between them every step from a DICOM directory to twelve probabilities is proven equal to theirs, windowing included.

title: Reimplement the raptor decode in our own code, proven by byte-equality against theirs
description:
knee-p0gk is blocked on one thing: their decode cannot be vendored into a Kaggle kit (external/raptor is gitignored third-party code with no LICENSE file, two Kaggle notebook exports). But the decode is ~120 lines and their notebook PUBLISHES ITS FULL SPEC IN PROSE — five fixed slots (18 sagittal-fluid / 14 sagittal-other / 12 coronal-fluid / 8 coronal-other / 12 axial), 6-94 percent span, 140mm mm-based centre crop, 336px INTER_AREA, 2/98 percentile window per series, three-slice channel stacking, 42 eval windows, imagenet normalisation.

Reimplementing from a published description is not vendoring. Our code, our repo, ships in our kit; their WEIGHTS stay a mounted Kaggle dataset, which is what datasets are for.

THE ORACLE IS EXACT, which is the reason this is worth doing rather than approximating. Both decodes produce a uint8 volume of shape (64, 336, 336) and a 64-long mask from the same DICOM files. Faithful means BYTE-IDENTICAL, not close. 'python -m kneemri.evaluation.raptor_feed' decodes the same studies through their module and ours and asserts equality element for element; anything less than equality is a bug in ours, not a tolerance to widen.

SECOND PAYOFF, LARGER THAN THE FIRST. 2026-08-27_the-feed-was-the-whole-shortfall.md measured the byte-identical checkpoint at -0.0348 through our feed and +0.030 above our best member through theirs. The shortfall was the feed. Once their feed is OUR code it stops being a serving adapter and becomes a candidate TRAINING feed for our own members — the axis that measurement says is worth the most, and the one we currently cannot test at all.

Blocks knee-p0gk.

title: Our table calls OA positive on compartments the report never names — 714 of 2604 silent cells (27.4%)
description:
FOUND while measuring knee-rwcy (the host's rubric), and it is a DIFFERENT defect from that one. The rubric
question is 'the report names cartilage, does that make OA positive'. This one is 'the report names NO OA-family
sentence for this compartment at all, and our table says positive anyway'.

MEASURED 2026-08-27 by `core/data/labels/rubric_boundary.py` on `merged_blend_v1.csv` — the table the champion's
seats were fitted on. Denominators, both stated: 1768 English reports of 4407 (40.1%); the non-English 59.9% is
unmeasured.

  osteoarthritis, bucket 'no sentence for this column': 2604 cells, our table positive on 714 — 27.4%.

The three OA columns are per-compartment (Medial OA, Lateral OA, PF OA), and the tool scopes each one to the
sentences that NAME that compartment ('medial compartment', 'lateral compartment', 'patellofemoral|retropatellar').
A silent cell is one where no sentence in the report names that compartment at the same time as any OA-family
wording. Our table calls better than one in four of those positive.

TWO MECHANISMS, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME BUG:
  (1) SPILLOVER. The reader read one compartment's osteophytes and graded all three, so a global 'tricompartmental
      degenerative change' or a single medial finding lands on the lateral and patellofemoral columns too. This
      would be a genuine attribution error and worth correcting.
  (2) IMPUTATION. The reader answered a per-compartment question the report does not answer by falling back to a
      prior. Not obviously wrong — the ledger's `confident224` result (-0.0071) already INVERTED this project's
      premise that unknown cells are noise, measuring real signal in UNK cells at 0.2875 weight. A confident
      imputation from correlated compartments could be carrying information the report withholds.

WHICH ONE IT IS DECIDES WHETHER THIS IS A FIX OR A FEATURE, and nothing measured so far separates them. The
cheapest separator costs no card: for the silent-but-positive cells, check whether ANOTHER compartment in the same
study is positive with a naming sentence. Near-total co-occurrence means spillover (1); a substantial share with no
named compartment anywhere means imputation from a prior (2).

SIZE. 714 cells is larger than knee-rwcy's whole rubric count (658 across three families) and lands on the same
three OA columns, which `supervision_gap` already measures among our worst. Both defects touch the same columns, so
a re-read that fixes only one of them will be measured against the other still in place — worth knowing before any
card arm is priced on either.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING. Costs no slot and no card. The separator above is the first step, not a re-read.
notes:
SEPARATED 2026-08-27, same session it was filed, by `RubricBoundary.attribution`. Costs no card and no slot.
The answer is neither of the two mechanisms this bead proposed — it is a THIRD, and it is the largest.

Of the 714 OA positives on columns no sentence names (1768 English reports of 4407; the non-English 59.9%
is unmeasured):

  171 SPILLOVER   (23.9%) — another column of the SAME study is named by a sentence AND positive.
   67 GLOBAL      ( 9.4%) — the report carries OA-qualifying wording localised to no compartment
                            ('tricompartmental osteoarthritis'). These positives are CORRECT.
  476 UNSUPPORTED (66.7%) — no OA-qualifying wording anywhere in the report, and no named positive column.

  meniscus  —  27 unnamed positives:  4 spillover,  6 global, 17 unsupported
  contusion —   5 unnamed positives:  0 spillover,  0 global,  5 unsupported

476 cells is 9.0% of the family's 5304 English cells. It is not spillover and it is not the compartment
regex's blind spot: the GLOBAL row exists precisely to hold the cells an unlocalised sentence explains, and
it takes only 67 of them.

WHAT 'UNSUPPORTED' MEANS EXACTLY, because the word is doing work. It means no wording matching the OA
QUALIFYING set (osteoarthr|degenerative joint|osteophyt|joint space narrow|spur) appears anywhere in the
report. A report carrying only CARTILAGE wording lands here — and under the host's stated rule that is the
right place for it, since cartilage findings do not by themselves determine the OA label. So this pile and
knee-rwcy's 615 contradicted cells are the same defect seen from two sides: the reader is producing OA
positives from something other than an OA statement.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. Not that 476 cells are wrong. The ledger's `confident224` result (-0.0071) measured
real signal in unknown cells at 0.2875 weight, so a confident prior can carry what a report withholds; and
the competition's ground truth is an IMAGE review, which can be positive on a report that says nothing.
What it does say is that for 9.0% of the OA cells our training table's value is not derived from the report
at all, while every claim this project makes about that table assumes it is.

TOGETHER WITH knee-rwcy: 615 contradicted + 476 unsupported = 1091 of 5304 English OA cells (20.6%) whose
value the report does not support under the host's rule. That is the OA supervision, not an edge of it.

title: DeviceBudget.capped uses needed() as a hard ceiling, so a recipe that matches its own prediction OOMs — the 12-slice v3base recipe does, arm and control alike
description:
MEASURED TWICE, ON BOTH SIDES OF A CONTROLLED PAIR, 2026-08-27 21:08Z and 21:13Z.

`arm_check --only warm_v3base_lora --smoke ... --smoke-studies 60` dies with:

  torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 1018.00 MiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 31.84 GiB of
  which 4.18 GiB is free. 16.27 GiB allowed; Of the allocated memory 15.14 GiB is allocated by PyTorch,
  and 1.06 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated.

`arm_check --only dinov3_base_lora` — the CONTROL, identical but for `--encoder-weights` — dies with the
SAME numbers to the digit: 15.14 GiB allocated, 1.06 reserved-unallocated, 1018.00 MiB requested,
16.27 GiB allowed. So this is the recipe, not the warm start, and `warm_v3base_lora` is not broken.

WHAT I GOT WRONG FIRST, because it is the instructive half. The first OOM landed with 3.98 GiB free and
biohub holding ~10.8 GiB, so I recorded it in knee-wbwq as co-tenant contention behaving as designed.
It is not. The re-smoke ran with 21.9 GiB FREE on the card and OOM'd at the same byte. The clue was in
the message all along and I read past it: `15.14 GiB is allocated by PyTorch` — OUR process, against a
`16.27 GiB allowed` that is OUR cap. Free VRAM was never the binding constraint. knee-wbwq is corrected.

THE MECHANISM. `DeviceBudget.capped` (device_budget.py:313-345) returns
`self.vram_gb or self.needed() or DEFAULT_SHARE * whole`, and `select()` feeds that straight into
`torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`. So when an arm names no `--vram-gb`, THE PREDICTION
BECOMES THE HARD CEILING. `needed()` derives 16.27 GB for this recipe; the recipe demands about 17.3
(15.14 allocated + 1.06 reserved-unallocated + the 1.02 it asked for). A cost model used as its own
ceiling has no room for its own error, and this recipe's error is +6%.

`needed()`'s docstring already anticipates the direction — *"An overstated ask costs `await_headroom`
polling; an understated one is an immediate OOM on a recipe that fits"* — and this is that OOM. Its one
slice of slack is slack against SLICE granularity, not against the fit's residual off the fitted point,
which is exactly where v3base sits.

THE FIX IS ALREADY LEGISLATED ONE LAYER OUT, which is the argument for the number. `experiments/lib.sh`
gates an arm at `ARM_NEEDS_MIB=18432` against the same arms' measured *"peak memory 16.24 GB reserved"*
— a ratio of 1.108 — and states why: *"the driver context plus cuDNN's kernel workspaces sit ON TOP of
the caching allocator's reservation"*. The GATE has that headroom and the CAP has none, for one cost
model. Measured need here is 1.063x the prediction, which 1.10 covers.

PROPOSED: `capped()` returns `self.vram_gb or self.needed() * CAP_HEADROOM or DEFAULT_SHARE * whole`,
CAP_HEADROOM = 1.10, derived from lib.sh's own gate ratio rather than chosen. A hand-named `--vram-gb`
is untouched — it is already a measured number and not a prediction. `set_per_process_memory_fraction`
clamps at 1.0, so a 20-slice recipe (28.3 -> 31.1 of 32.6) stays on the card, and the `floor()` refusal
and `await_headroom` wait are both unchanged.

BLAST RADIUS, and why this was not caught earlier. Every arm that NAMES `--vram-gb` is unaffected —
which is every accepted arm the ledger describes (20, 26 or 28 of 31.8). The path that breaks is the one
`capped`'s own docstring says nobody watches: *"a smoke, a bisect or a one-off"*. `arm_check --smoke`
names no cap, so the pre-flight tool that exists to catch a broken recipe before it costs forty minutes
is precisely the caller this defect blocks — and it reports the failure as `BROKEN <arm>`, blaming the
arm.

VERIFY BY RE-SMOKING BOTH: the control `dinov3_base_lora` must pass, since it is a recipe this repo has
RUN to 0.8268. That is the equality check — a fix that makes only the new arm pass has fixed nothing.
notes: FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-27. The first fix was wrong in the same way the bug was: CAP_HEADROOM=1.10 multiplied the derivation but LEFT IT A CEILING, and the re-smoke OOM'd again — at '17.90 GiB allowed ... 15.15 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 1.93 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated'. Read that: peak ALLOCATION was 16.15 GB, UNDER the 16.27 the fit derives. needed() is not wrong. It predicts ALLOCATION while set_per_process_memory_fraction bounds RESERVATION, and the caching allocator's fragmentation slack — 12.7% of its own reservation at that peak — lives in between. Two changes followed. (1) capped() now returns vram_gb or max(needed()*CAP_HEADROOM, DEFAULT_SHARE*whole): the derivation may only ever RAISE the ceiling, never lower it, because a tight self-ceiling buys nothing (the run cannot allocate more than it needs — that is needed()'s own claim) and can only convert a fitting run into an OOM. The max keeps the docstring's existing rule true: a 20-slice recipe reserving 26.92 is still never capped under its own measured demand. (2) CAP_HEADROOM re-derived 1.10 -> 1.15, the smaller step clearing the larger of two measurements: the 1.127 reserved-to-allocated ratio this smoke logged, and the 1.108 that experiments/lib.sh already gates the SAME cost model at. VERIFIED BY THE EQUALITY CHECK THIS BEAD ASKED FOR: the control dinov3_base_lora — a recipe this repo ran to 0.8268 — now smokes 'ok'. uvx nox -s gates green ('Session gates was successful in 3 minutes').

title: Slot 5 (2026-08-27, ~23:30Z): price --calibrated-targets on ONE member — final_ws_cf solo vs soloseat_v1 0.925
description:
THE DECISION, and why every scoring option was rejected first.

Four slots spent today: calibsix 0.941 (6 seats), calibmix 0.941 (11), pixgroup 0.940 (8), honest12 0.937 (12). With resseat 0.938, blendseat 0.939 and blendthree 0.939 that is SEVEN entries spanning 0.937-0.941 across seven different seatings, against a 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil floor. The seating axis is closed from both ends - count, fit-duplication, targeted pixel diversity and offline-greedy selection have each had a slot and each read flat or worse.

REJECTED, each on evidence already in the repo:
 - smallseat (knee-mq7t). An eighth point on the closed axis, and DEFECTIVE besides: it was written against the blendseat champion, and no small_batch6_cf exists (roster has only _s2026 and _ff), so against calibsix it would insert an UNCALIBRATED seat into a fully calibrated six - undoing the single treatment that produced the 0.938->0.941 climb.
 - MedianLogit (knee-brkd). This bead's own NOTES already refuted it from comp/board.jsonl: two controlled single-variable pairs (efficient_v4 0.919->vote_v2 0.919; dark6_v1 0.937->votefit_v1 0.938) bracket the whole vote axis at 0.000-0.001, under BOARD_RESOLVABLE. The note says in terms 'never as a slot of its own'.
 - Any deficit-targeted seat (knee-mvna, closed today). knee-q1pf caps the entire per-label programme at +0.0043 and we already BEAT the published members on two of the three deficit findings.
 - Any new member. The card is with biohub by the owner's instruction; nothing can be trained before the slot.

So no zero-training play has a mechanism that could plausibly deliver the +0.009 that 0.941->0.950 needs. The slot cannot buy score. It can buy the most decision-changing NUMBER we do not have, and a low read costs no rank (public LB keeps the best entry).

WHAT TO FIRE: kneemri-solo seating calib_span_ff ALONE. One member, the champion's own second seat.

WHY THIS MEMBER SPECIFICALLY. (1) It is full-fit and calibrated, so it is REGIME-MATCHED to the champion - no _s2026/_cf confound, unlike calib_dense_hold_s2026 (0.8634, our best offline solo, but fold-0 and never boarded). (2) It is a --fold -1 member, so it holds nothing out and CANNOT be scored offline by any means we own; the board is the only instrument that can put a number on it at all. (3) It is an actual champion seat, so 0.941 minus this read is exactly what the other five seats buy, measured rather than assumed.

PRE-REGISTERED BRANCHES, and both are decision-changing:
 - <=0.920 (board_transfer predicts ~0.914 for a ~0.86 solo): the six-seat ensemble buys ~+0.025. ENSEMBLING is the engine, not member quality, and the four reads today that all concluded 'card hours to better single members' (pixgroup, honest12) are pointing the wrong way. Rivals' self-reported 0.926-0.942 SINGLES then become the anomaly to explain, and knee-wbwq's warm-start lane must clear a ~0.025 gap rather than a small one.
 - >=0.932: the ensemble buys under +0.010 and MEMBER QUALITY is confirmed as the whole remaining lane. knee-wbwq (fitted_encoder, 0 of 131 arms use it) is then correctly first in the queue when the card returns, and it also converges with today's competence_axis reading that four of the top five members on our resolved deficit findings are ENCODER arms.
 - 0.921-0.931: intermediate, both levers live, no reordering.

PRE-FLIGHT, in order, none of which spends a slot: python -m kneemri.kaggle.mount_check (it has already caught kneemri-solo once - the package had gained a DINOv3 member while the kernel metadata still declared DINOv2 only, which loads every member and then cannot build one), python -m kneemri.kaggle.kit_check --mounted, python comp/witness_check.py --device cpu, and python -m kneemri.kaggle.board_read --live afterwards so board_check has a fresh read.

Fire ~23:30Z per the owner's instruction to hold the last slot until near the 00:00Z reset. Record the row in comp/board.jsonl with scope ensemble members 1 and board_check --live before quoting it.
notes:

A code submission is not a file upload: Kaggle re-runs the notebook against the hidden test set, so the

SLOT AUTHORITY. knee-pubw (P0) reads "Slot 5 of 2026-08-26 is NOT to be spent" and asks that the FIRST slot

MEMBER NAME IN THE DESCRIPTION IS STALE — read the title, not the paragraph. The description says 'seating calib_span_ff ALONE'; the pushed kernel's tuple is `chosen = ("final_ws_cf",)`, which is what the title says and what will fire.

The swap changes nothing about the argument, and I checked rather than assumed: final_ws_cf is champion seat #1 in comp/champion.json (calib_span_ff is seat #2), it is _cf so full-fit AND calibrated — regime-matched to the champion exactly as required — and NEITHER member has a .holdout.npz, so criterion (2) holds for it verbatim: the board is the only instrument that can put a number on it.
