CONSEQUENCE: this is the only composition measurement the project holds and it reads SUBSTITUTION, which lowers the prior on knee-orjq's stack route; written into experiments/README.md BEFORE stackfit's number lands so it cannot be fitted to it.

title: Contiguity, not band width: our 9 slices are linspace-spread, a rival measures +0.018 for center-adjacent
description:
FORUM EVIDENCE (topic 737597, read 2026-08-26 23:00Z, theirs and self-reported). A competitor at 0.7815 OOF / 0.870 public, EfficientNet-B0, 4 slots, 288 px, 140 mm crop, 5-fold: 'Slice geometry mattered more than resolution: center-9 ADJACENT beat 9 equal-spaced across 24 by +0.018 on fold 0.' Their negative list is a clean sweep of the training-regime axis at the same time (EMA +0.003, mixup +0.002, 60-epoch cosine +0.001, asymmetric loss -0.139) and their per-finding deficit is OURS: Baker's 0.855 / Effusion 0.843 / Fracture 0.832 against Lateral Meniscus 0.740 / PF OA 0.748 / Lateral OA 0.751 / MCL 0.758 - large-discrete-positional works, thin-small-graded does not.

WHAT WE ACTUALLY DO. core/data/corpus/slot_reader.py:252 - band_indices() takes np.linspace(low, high, slices) over the central band and de-duplicates. Every slice we feed is EQUAL-SPACED across the band. Not one arm in the ledger has varied the SPACING RULE; every one varied the band WIDTH (0.20-0.80 = 0.8525, 0.10-0.90 = 0.8565, 0.00-1.00 = 0.8427).

WHY THAT IS NOT THE SAME AXIS, AND WHY OUR BAND RESULT DOES NOT ALREADY REFUTE IT. Wider band beat narrower here, which reads as evidence FOR spread - but band width is EXTENT and adjacency is CONTIGUITY, and they carry different mechanisms. Extent buys coverage of where a finding might sit. Contiguity buys the 3D continuity a focal finding is DEFINED by: a meniscal tear is 1-3 mm of signal that has to touch an articular surface on two CONSECUTIVE slices, and equal-spacing across a wide band guarantees no two of our nine slices are consecutive in mm. Under linspace the model can never see that continuity at all, on any band width. So the two results are compatible and the axis is untested.

SIZE. +0.018 is 3x the 0.0062 three-seed floor and above the 1.5% bar - the first lever in a week whose CLAIMED size is not a knob. It is also the surviving arm of the deficit question this project has been circling from three directions (focal deficit, supervision gap, our-model-past-its-teacher), and it is a DATA change rather than a loss or a head change.

COST, AND THE ONE THING TO CHECK FIRST. This is a CACHE-shape change: slot_reader's own docstring says changing band_indices invalidates 99 GB of decoded arrays and every member fitted on them, with no fingerprint to catch it. BEFORE pricing a rebuild, check whether the cache stores more slices than a run consumes (slice_count arms ran at 12 and 20) - if it does, a contiguous CENTER-9 can be subselected from an existing 12- or 20-slice cache at zero rebuild cost, which turns a 99 GB job into one 40-minute arm.

PRE-REGISTER BEFORE RUNNING: >=+0.010 contiguity is a real lever and the cache is rebuilt on its account; +0.006 to +0.010 directional, keep as a diversity member and re-test; within +/-0.006 the axis closes and the rival's +0.018 is their 5-fold OOF ruler rather than a transferable mechanism; <=-0.006 spread is load-bearing here and our wide-band result is the reason.

Their number is self-reported and unverifiable. Read it as a claim that names a mechanism, and let our own arm settle the size.
notes:
MEASURED AND REFUTED 2026-08-27: adjacent224_s2026 0.8462 vs native224_s2026 0.8502, MEAN -0.0040, converged. The one marked delta was Medial Meniscus -0.0136*, precisely the finding contiguity was written for, with Regional -0.0073 against focal -0.0018 - the mechanism fired and it cost. Full row: experiments/README.md, 2026-08-27 section.

RE-OPEN CONDITION RETIRED 2026-09-05, WITHOUT AN ARM. The close note licensed one re-test at a denser stack where span is not the thing being spent. That condition is not reachable. Spacing docstring asserted that under SPREAD no two sampled slices are ever adjacent AT ANY WIDTH; that clause is FALSE and it is false exactly at our operating point. Series depth over a 12-study sample (68 series): min 16, p25 26, median 32, p75 38. At slices=20 the band offers ~25 indices on a median study and we take 20 of them, so consecutive pairs out of a possible 19 run spread-vs-adjacent as 12v12 at depth 16 (IDENTICAL index sets), 18v19 at p25, 14v19 at median, 8v19 at p75 - while adjacent pays full span cost at every depth (24 to 19 indices at median, 30 to 19 at p75). Contrast is large only on DEEP series, which are exactly where adjacency discards the most span, so a big contrast and a cheap span are anti-correlated by construction. A denser stack is where SPREAD CONVERGES TO ADJACENT, not where adjacency gets a fair test. DO NOT re-run this axis. The rivals +0.018 stands unchallenged for THEIR point (9 slices across 24 is the regime where the old clause is true); it does not transfer. Ledger: experiments/README.md 2026-09-05 contiguity section. Docstring now carries the table instead of the claim.

title: Score the label extractor and the image model against the same 58 gold studies
description:
Topic 735826 volunteers a diagnostic we have the parts for and have never run in this direction: score the LABEL EXTRACTOR against the 58 provided gold labels, then score the IMAGE MODEL against the same 58. If the image model does not beat its own teacher there is modelling headroom; if it beats the teacher by a large margin the labels are the ceiling. Either answer redirects the next block of card time, and it costs no submission slot and no training.

kneemri/evaluation/annotated_readings.py already scores readings against the annotated subset. What is missing is the PAIRED comparison on one denominator: teacher-vs-gold and member-vs-gold over the identical 58 studies, reported side by side. State n=58 explicitly — it is small enough that most differences will not resolve, and a rate computed over a subset that an English regex could parse is not a rate over the corpus (that error has been made three times here).

Context: research/2026-08-26_rival_single_models_and_the_label_bottleneck.md. Rivals self-report SINGLE models at 0.926-0.942 while our six-member ensemble scores 0.939, so the gap is member quality, and the field's consensus bottleneck is label quality.

title: MRNet is probably BARRED: host ruled against KneeCoT on the required-agreement mechanism
description:
Kaggle discussion topic 734109, host reply (read 2026-08-26 17:10Z via kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read --live --topic 734109):

  'After deliberation, we decided to not allow the use of KneeCoT dataset due to the required data
   agreement with dataset institution. In our interpretation of the rules, this can make the playing
   field uneven for participants who can complete the formal agreement to seek approval compared those
   that cannot. ... If the situation changes, for instance if the data use policy changes on HF, or if
   the data organizers communicate their intent differently, we may change our stance.'

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ANY ARM. External data of a different KIND is the only lever this repo has
identified whose mechanism could plausibly deliver the +0.0133 offline that 0.950 now costs (see
knee-ps8o: the transfer coefficient is +0.74-0.83 in our regime, not +1.72). Every other open lever is
a knob worth <= +0.003 board. MRNet was that lever.

THE ARGUMENT THAT LOOKED SETTLED, AND IS NOT. Topic 733652 carries a participant who pulled the actual
rule text: 2.6(a) is a DISJUNCTION - External Data must be 'either publicly available and equally
accessible ... at no cost to the other Participants, or satisfies the Reasonableness criteria as
outlined in Section 2.6.b', and 2.6.b says 'the use of external data and models is acceptable unless
specifically prohibited by the Host'. On that plain reading MRNet/fastMRI+/OAI/SKM-TEA all clear, since
all are free and not geo-restricted. The 734109 ruling is the host SPECIFICALLY PROHIBITING on exactly
the axis 2.6.b reserves to them, and their stated reason is the AGREEMENT, not the cost and not the geo.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MIGHT STILL SAVE IT, stated honestly rather than hopefully. KneeCoT requires a
'formal ethical-use agreement with the affiliated hospital' and the host's own words are 'complete the
formal agreement TO SEEK APPROVAL'. MRNet is a click-through Research Use Agreement at
stanfordmlgroup.github.io/competitions/mrnet/ - name/email/institution, immediate download link, no
approval step, no counter-signature, no institutional review. Whether the host's objection is to
'an agreement exists' or to 'approval can be withheld' decides MRNet, and nothing in the ruling settles
which.

WHAT TO DO, AND WHAT NOT TO DO.
  DO NOT accept the RUA or download the archive on the strength of the 2.6.b argument. The build path
    (build_mrnet --archive <path> --scheme mrnet, then build_merged --extra-scheme mrnet) stays unbuilt.
  DO NOT spend engineering on the MRNet ingest until a host answer exists. It is a multi-hour path whose
    permission is now actively in doubt.
  DO ask the host, in topic 733652 where the disjunction was raised, the narrow question: does a
    click-through RUA with no approval step fall under the 734109 reasoning, or only agreements where
    approval can be refused? Name MRNet, fastMRI+, OAI and SKM-TEA together - the host preferred a
    category answer over a per-dataset one in 733652 and said so.
  POSTING IS OUTWARD-FACING and needs owner sign-off; draft only.

BLOCKS: knee-w84q and every other queued arm is unaffected, but the 0.950 plan is now without a
plausibly-sized lever until this resolves. Say that plainly rather than substituting knobs for it.
notes:
DRAFT FORUM POST for topic 733652 — OWNER MUST POST IT; posting is outward-facing and I do not do that
unasked. Copy-paste as-is or edit. It deliberately asks a CATEGORY question, because the host said in
733652 they preferred that, and it cites their own 734109 ruling so they can answer inside their own
reasoning rather than re-deriving it.

---
Thanks for the KneeCoT ruling in #734109 — that answers the gated-HF case clearly. Could I ask for the
boundary, since the reasoning there seems to cover a much wider category than the one dataset?

The stated basis was "the required data agreement with dataset institution", because participants who
can "complete the formal agreement to seek approval" would be advantaged over those who cannot. That
reasoning turns on an approval step that can be refused. The other public knee-MRI corpora do not have
one:

- MRNet (Stanford) — a click-through research-use agreement: name, email, institution, and the download
  link is returned immediately. No counter-signature, no institutional review, nobody to refuse.
- fastMRI / fastMRI+ (NYU), the Osteoarthritis Initiative, and SKM-TEA — the same shape: free,
  not geo-restricted, registration and an agreement checkbox, no approval gate.

So the narrow question: does #734109's reasoning bar any dataset behind an agreement at all, or only
those where approval can be withheld? A category answer covering MRNet / fastMRI+ / OAI / SKM-TEA
together would settle #733652, #735497, #735121 and #734109 at once.

The reason it matters now rather than later: pretraining on an external corpus is a multi-hour
commitment and the deadline is 22 October, so teams are choosing whether to start on an unresolved
reading. If the answer is no, that is genuinely more useful said early than said in a winners' review.
---

WHY THIS IS WORTH A POST RATHER THAN A GUESS. The plain 2.6(a)-disjunction reading says yes; the 734109
ruling says the host reads 2.6.b restrictively on exactly this axis. Those cannot both govern MRNet.
Building the ingest on the optimistic reading risks the work; abandoning it on the pessimistic reading
discards the only lever sized for the goal (knee-ps8o prices 0.950 at +0.0133 offline; every in-repo
lever is <= +0.003 board). A forum question costs nothing and resolves the branch.

title: Residual ambiguity predicts seat value at r=+0.5 to +0.7 where distance predicts nothing
description:
A merit column that survives its own validation, and the first one here that does.

MEASURED 2026-08-26 16:26Z, zero card, zero slots. Fifteen members priced as seats against gradeswap_v1
(0.933, 7 members, fully scoreable) — experiments/logs/seat_fifteen.log. Correlated against the two
competing merit columns over the SAME TWELVE members, dropping cnx_dense (solo 0.7927) and raddino_dense
(0.8141) so that neither column is credited for spotting a member that is simply broken:

  residual ambiguity   r = +0.81
  distance (nearest)   r = -0.15

Residual ambiguity is the knee-qij2 quantity: pair-ambiguity above what the member's own solo quality
predicts, from a fit with slope -0.179 and r-squared 0.875 across fifteen members. Distance collapses the
moment the broken members leave, which is knee-bxp2 confirmed and GENERALISED — its apparent predictive
power was the weakness confound all along, across families and not merely within one.

The rankings agree end to end. Seat value, best swap, against residual:
  merged_blend        +0.0014   resid +1.63   ALREADY SEATED
  blendlabels         +0.0011   resid +1.70   NOT SEATED IN blendseat OR gradeswap
  crop80_span         +0.0004   resid +1.58   not seated
  calibrated_targets  +0.0003   resid +1.11
  vjepa_warm          +0.0001   resid +1.02
  band_span           +0.0001   resid -0.10
  depth_regions       +0.0001   resid -1.38
  band_wide           +0.0000   resid -0.41
  band140             -0.0000   resid -0.81
  severity_weight     -0.0004   resid -2.47
  v3base_dense        -0.0005   resid -0.57
  band_full           -0.0006   resid -0.67
  raddino_dense       -0.0012
  cnx_dense           -0.0025

THREE CONSEQUENCES:
1. blendlabels is the highest-value UNSEATED member we hold and it is free to add.
2. Both top-two are LABEL-TABLE members. That is independent confirmation of calibsix's bet (knee-1c00)
   from a ruler built to answer a different question.
3. The three most DISTANT candidates are the three worst seats. Buy-the-distant-member is closed with a
   named mechanism rather than a shrug.

LIMITS, BEFORE THEY ARE ASKED. n=12. Every one of the fourteen seat values sits inside +/-0.0015, the bar
under which this ruler has never been shown to pick a board tick, so the correlation runs over quantities
the ruler cannot resolve ONE AT A TIME — it is a statement about ordering, not about any single seat.
And there is PLAUSIBLE CIRCULARITY: the residual was fitted on pairs with band_dense, and band_dense sits
in the roster the seats are priced against. Different pool and different combine rule, so partial rather
than total, but real. A second anchor costs nothing and settles it, and that is the next step here.
notes: CORRECTION, second anchor completed 2026-08-26T16:36Z. The three stragglers landed (severity_weight, v3base_dense, vjepa_warm) and they move the number DOWN. Residual-ambiguity vs seat value on anchor band_span, three nestings: n=8 (pre-stragglers) slope -0.156, r=+0.82 | n=11 all comparable, slope -0.198, r=+0.66 | n=10 strict (solo >= 0.84), slope -0.091, r=+0.52. vjepa_warm is the cause: solo 0.8337, residual +14.9, seat +1 -- a big residual with no seat. It sits between the broken members (cnx_dense 0.7927, raddino_dense 0.8141) and the comparable band (0.84-0.86), so it survives the cut while behaving like a leverage point, the same pathology that dropped r to +0.35 when the broken pair was restored. severity_weight disagrees mildly (residual +2.7, seat -4); v3base_dense agrees (-5.6 vs -5). CLAIM AS CORRECTED: the merit column is positive under every nesting and merged_blend + blendlabels rank top-two in all three, so the ORDERING replicates and is what licenses calibsix. The STRENGTH does not: quote '+0.5 to +0.7, sensitive to where weak members are cut off', never '+0.82'. SECOND FINDING, against my own earlier note: on the strict band the ambiguity-on-solo slope is only -0.091 versus anchor-1's -0.179, so 'ambiguity is mostly member weakness' (experiments/README.md, commit ef80bc1) is itself carried by the weak members. Among members that work, solo quality explains much less of ambiguity than that section states. It does not overturn knee-qij2 -- no axis group separated there either, and that conclusion was drawn over the full set -- but the slope quoted there needs this caveat attached.

title: Which AXIS of member difference buys ambiguity? (pre-registered, zero card)
description:
MOTIVATION. calibsix's measurement (knee-1c00) found --calibrated-targets buys +0.0018 of AMBIGUITY, not
just quality — calibrated members disagree with each other more than their uncalibrated twins do. That is
the first diversity this ledger has obtained from a lever that was never asked for diversity. Every lever
that WAS asked (dissent_seat's negative-correlation loss, -0.0008; the architecture axis, closed three
measurements deep) returned a twin or nothing.

THE QUESTION. Is that a property of calibration, or of the LABEL TABLE AXIS? If members that differ in
what they were TAUGHT are systematically more ambiguous than members that differ in how they DECODE or in
what BACKBONE they use, then roster selection has been asking the wrong question. We have been picking by
distance (knee-bxp2: anticorrelated with seat value within a family) and by quality (23% pass-through into
a saturated pool). Neither is an axis. This would be one.

THE MEASUREMENT, free, no card, over records already on disk. Anchor band_dense (settled geometry, plain
labels). For each of ~20 members pair it with the anchor and compute

    ambiguity = pair_ensemble - mean(solo_anchor, solo_member)

grouped by which axis the member differs from the anchor on:
  LABEL       calibrated_targets blendlabels merged_blend severity_weight report03 report10
  GEOMETRY    band_span band_wide band_full band140 max12 max20 depth_regions crop80_span
  ARCHITECTURE cnx_dense dinov3_v3small v3base_dense base_dense raddino_dense vjepa_warm

PRE-REGISTRATION, written before the numbers are read:
  LABEL mean ambiguity exceeds GEOMETRY mean by >= 0.0015, with the group intervals not overlapping
      -> THE AXIS IS REAL. Roster selection should spend seats on label-table variety, and calibsix is a
         special case of a general rule rather than one lucky flag. Next arm is a roster built one member
         per TABLE at a fixed geometry.
  LABEL exceeds GEOMETRY by 0 to 0.0015, or intervals overlap
      -> DIRECTIONAL ONLY. Keep it free, do not plan around it, do not spend a slot on it. This is the
         likeliest outcome: the ambiguity deltas being compared are ~0.002 against a 0.0062 floor.
  ARCHITECTURE is the largest group
      -> THE ARCHITECTURE AXIS WAS CLOSED ON THE WRONG RULER. It was closed on seat value and board score,
         both quality rulers. That would not reopen it as a route (raddino_dense -0.0371, vjepa_warm solo
         0.8337 — the members are too weak to seat regardless), but it would say the CLOSURE ARGUMENT was
         about member quality and not about diversity, which is a different sentence than the ledger
         currently carries.
  no group separates
      -> ambiguity is a property of the member pair and not of any axis, and calibration's +0.0018 is one
         pair's scatter. That would weaken calibsix's mechanism story to a coincidence, though not the
         arm itself, whose prediction is already priced at pass-through 1.0 with ambiguity discarded.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY. Every pair here shares one anchor, so these are not independent observations — they
are 20 readings of band_dense's neighbourhood, and a group difference could be a fact about the anchor.
The honest follow-up if a group separates is a second anchor on a different geometry, which is also free.
Solo deltas in the source measurement were all inside the 0.0062 floor, and these ambiguity numbers are
smaller still.

PRICE: zero card, zero submission slots, ~4 minutes of wall-clock in a gap where the card is busy with
ema_dense. It cannot fail expensively.
P(clears the >= 0.0015 separation bar) ~ 0.3 — the quantities are a third of the noise floor, and the
only reason to expect separation at all is one measured pair plus a mechanism argument.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-26 16:2xZ. Outcome: NO GROUP SEPARATES, and the confound is the finding.

15 usable members (report03, report10, max12, max20, dinov3_v3small carry no holdout record and were
dropped — their 'pair' reads 0.8578, the anchor alone).

RAW ambiguity = pair - mean(solo_anchor, solo_member), anchor band_dense 0.8578:
  ARCHITECTURE  +0.0121  (cnx_dense .01765, raddino .01525, vjepa .01205, v3base .00835, base .00730)
  LABEL         +0.0079  (calibrated_targets .00935, blendlabels .00915, merged_blend .00815, severity .00510)
  GEOMETRY      +0.0071  (crop80_span .01030, band_full .00875, band_span .00685, band_wide .00675,
                          band140 .00630, depth_regions .00585)

Read raw, that is pre-registered outcome 3 (architecture largest). IT IS A CONFOUND, NOT AN AXIS.
Ambiguity regressed on the member's own solo over all 15: slope -0.179 ambiguity per unit solo,
**r-squared 0.875**. Eighty-eight percent of the ambiguity variance is HOW WEAK THE SECOND MEMBER IS. The
architecture group IS the weak group — cnx_dense 0.7927, raddino 0.8141, vjepa 0.8337 are the three
worst members in the whole set and they hold the three largest ambiguities.

RESIDUALS after removing the quality trend:
  LABEL        +0.00049   (blendlabels +0.0017, merged_blend +0.0016, calibrated +0.0011, severity -0.0025)
  ARCHITECTURE -0.00004
  GEOMETRY     -0.00030
LABEL over GEOMETRY is +0.00079, HALF the pre-registered 0.0015 bar, with one of four label members
strongly the wrong way. Pre-registration says DIRECTIONAL ONLY: keep it free, do not plan around it, do
not spend a slot on it. The axis is not real at this resolution.

WHAT IS REAL, AND IT IS THE GENERAL RESULT: ambiguity is not a currency that can be shopped for. It is
mostly a restatement of the candidate's weakness, which is why every 'pick the distant member' rule this
project has tried (knee-bxp2's distance column, dissent_seat's decorrelation loss) has failed on the
board — they were all buying error and calling it diversity.

IT STRENGTHENS calibsix (knee-1c00) RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. Calibrated members are BETTER solo (+0.0038),
so this fit predicts their ambiguity should FALL by 0.179 x 0.0038 = -0.00067. It ROSE +0.00184. The
calibration ambiguity gain runs AGAINST the confound, so quality-adjusted it is +0.0025, not +0.0018 —
the one lever measured here that buys disagreement without buying error. Caveat: the slope is fitted on
band_dense pairs and the trio is a different pool, so cross-applying it is approximate.

LIMIT, as pre-registered: all 20 pairs share one anchor. These are 15 readings of band_dense's
neighbourhood, not of the corpus. A second anchor is free and is the honest follow-up if this is ever
leaned on.
close_reason: Closed by its own NOTES: the verdict (REFUTED/SUPERSEDED/ANSWERED/RESOLVED/CLOSED/FIXED) was written into the bead and the status was never moved. Swept 2026-09-16 (owner: 'if we get piled upon, nothing remains important').

title: calibsix — lift five champion seats with --calibrated-targets (the uniform-lift arm)
description:
Seat pricing 2026-08-26 measured two DIFFERENT pass-through numbers, both real:

  marginal new member into a saturated pool   23%   (calib_dense_hold +0.0056 solo -> +0.0013 seat)
  uniform lift of every member                92%   (measured, three matched pairs, zero card)

The uniform-lift A/B:
  calibrated trio   (calib_dense_hold + calib_span_hold + calib_span)   0.8685
  uncalibrated twins(band_dense_hold  + band_span_hold  + band_span )   0.8629
                                                             delta     +0.0056
  mean solo delta of the same flag at the same corners                 +0.0061

No contradiction: ensemble error = mean member error - ambiguity. A uniform lift moves the first term
and leaves ambiguity alone; a single better-but-redundant member moves both and they cancel.

THE ARM: experiments/arms/calibsix.sh — the champion's five uncalibrated seats (final_ws_e12,
grade_ladder_ff, through_dense_ff, lr4e-5_ws_ff, merged_blend) each refitted with exactly one added
flag, --calibrated-targets. calib_span_ff is the sixth seat and already carries it. Each recipe copied
VERBATIM from its own arm per final_fit_six.sh's rule (a reassembly is a configuration nobody ran, and
--fold -1 leaves no holdout to catch it). Distinct _cf suffix so no seated fold-0 original is
overwritten.

--calibrated-targets and --grade-ladder compose: checked, not assumed. grade_ladder is an OBJECTIVE
policy (thresholds subtracted inside the loss); calibrated_targets is a TARGETS policy
(core/data/labels/targets.py). Different pipeline stages.

PREDICTION: 5 seats x 0.92 x +0.0061 = +0.0047 offline; x board_transfer +1.72 = +0.0081 board;
champion blendseat 0.939 -> 0.947. Not 0.950 alone. margin_calib's seat (knee-myl0) is the arm that
would carry the rest.

READOUT IS BOARD-ONLY for four of five (--fold -1 has seen every holdout study). merged_blend_cf stays
fold-0 like its original and is the ONLY offline read: score it against merged_blend_s2026 0.8587 via
convergence_check first. If that one seat reads NEGATIVE, do not ship — it is the only evidence that
the flag transfers to corners outside the two it was measured at.

RISKS, named before the card: (1) the flag was measured at two corners only; seats four and five sit at
0.2-0.8/12 slices and seat five trains on the merged corpus, so transfer there is assumed. (2)
blendthree swapped three seats for better-SUPERVISED twins and read 0.939 dead flat — nearest
precedent, returned nothing; defence is size not kind (+0.0034 at three seats vs +0.0061 at five). If
calibsix also reads flat, the uniform-lift route is refuted at the operating point and the ensemble
axis closes for good. (3) it needs a submission slot to read at all.

PRICE: ~7.1 h of otherwise-idle overnight card (five 12-epoch 336px fits, ~425 s/epoch over 4406
studies), ZERO submission slots to produce, one slot to read. Runs after margin_calib.
P(clears +0.004 offline / a board tick over 0.939) ~ 0.45 — the mechanism is measured rather than
argued, but blendthree is a flat precedent at the same operating point.

SLOT DISCIPLINE: slot 5 of 2026-08-26 is HELD by owner directive (knee-pubw). This ships no earlier
than 2026-08-27 and the owner is ASKED before it is spent.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-26 16:0xZ, before the card was spent. The 92% pass-through in this bead's
description is wrong and so is its +0.0061 mean. '+0.0061' is the DENSE pair alone, generalised to
three pairs by nobody but me — the denominator failure CLAUDE.md names. experiments/README.md:318
already recorded calib_span at -0.0020 vs band_span, which that mean silently absorbed.

All six re-scored solo over the same 909 shared studies:
  dense, hold     0.8634 / 0.8573   +0.0061
  span,  hold     0.8565 / 0.8493   +0.0072
  span,  no hold  0.8545 / 0.8565   -0.0020
                          MEAN      +0.0038

Ensembled, two nested pools:
  trio            0.8685 / 0.8629   +0.0056  vs mean solo +0.0038   pass-through 147%
  hold-only pair  0.8679 / 0.8595   +0.0084  vs mean solo +0.00665  pass-through 126%

PASS-THROUGH IS ABOVE ONE ON BOTH POOLS. A pure error-term lift predicts ~100%; 126-147% means the
calibrated members also disagree with each other MORE than their uncalibrated twins, so ambiguity moved
the helpful way rather than standing still. Calibration buys diversity as a side effect. Better result
than the one claimed, reached by being wrong about the arithmetic.

HONEST SIZE: every solo delta is inside the 0.0062 floor, the negative included; only +0.0084 clears it.

RISK 4, NEW AND UNFLATTERING: both positive pairs carry --hold-annotations, the negative does not, and
calibsix's five seats carry none. calib_span and calib_span_hold sit on the identical corner (12 slices,
0.1-0.9) differing in nothing else, yet read -0.0020 and +0.0072 — a 0.0092 spread on one flag. At n=1
per cell that is inside scatter, and the ledger's calibrated_targets row is +0.0038 with no hold at the
0.2-0.8 corner, so no-hold is not uniformly negative. Arm stays single-flag (adding --hold-annotations
would be the reassembly final_fit_six.sh forbids). If calibsix reads FLAT this confound is suspect one,
mechanism suspect two, and the follow-up is one matched no-hold pair rather than a verdict.

REPRICED at the low end (pass-through 1.0, not 1.3): 5 x 0.0038 = +0.0038 offline, x1.72 = +0.0065
board, 0.939 -> 0.946, with 0.949 the optimistic end. The earlier +0.0047/0.947 was right by
coincidence — mean solo fell and pass-through rose by nearly the same factor.

ARM STILL RUNS: cost is idle overnight card and zero slots to produce. Chained behind margin_calib.

title: margin_calib — occupy the strong-and-distant cell deliberately (AUC-margin AT the calibrated dense corner)
description:
THE MEASUREMENT THAT ASKS FOR IT (2026-08-26 15:43Z, seat_value --against gradeswap_v1, 7 scoreable members, roster 0.8694):

  +margin_seat        0.8709  (+0.0015)   best seat +0.0018   solo 0.8525   nearest 0.8628
  +calib_dense_hold   0.8704  (+0.0010)   best seat +0.0013   solo 0.8634   nearest 0.9273
  +small_batch6       0.8698  (+0.0004)
  +sided_pool         0.8698  (+0.0004)
  +vjepa_warm         0.8695  (+0.0001)
  +dissent_seat       0.8686  (-0.0008)   nearest 0.9292

margin_seat is the ONLY one of six clearing +0.0015, and its solo is 0.0109 WORSE than calib_dense_hold's.
A worse member takes a bigger seat. Measured seat pass-through from solo quality is 23%
(calib_dense_hold: +0.0056 solo -> +0.0013 seat), which is why ten board entries read 0.936-0.939 flat.

THE CONSTRUCTION. margin_seat and calib_dense_hold sit on the IDENTICAL corner (--slices 20 --band-low 0.1
--band-high 0.9 --backbone-lr 4e-5 --whole-stack, 12 epochs). Neither term has been tried with the other.
  --auc-margin 1.0 --rank-weight 0  buys DISTANCE (nearest 0.8628 against a seated spread topping 0.9248)
  --calibrated-targets              buys QUALITY (+0.0061 at this exact corner, replicated in sign at calib_span)
They are mechanically distinct: one changes what the loss RANKS, the other changes what the targets SAY.
This is the direct occupation of the empty quadrant in
interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_architecture_diversity_is_closed_and_the_empty_cell_is_strong_and_distant.md
-- strong AND distant -- which that document says nothing has ever optimised both terms of at once.

PRICE: ~85 min of card at 336 px / 20 slices, ZERO submission slots, fold-0 holdout, plus the annotation
ruler free via --hold-annotations. Plausible gain if it lands: a seat of +0.003-0.004, which at
board_transfer +1.72 is +0.005-0.007 board on a gradeswap-shaped pool.

P(clears the +0.0015 seat bar) ~ 0.45. margin_seat already cleared it once at the uncalibrated corner, so
the mechanism has fired; the risk is that calibrated targets and an AUC margin are the SAME lever wearing
two names -- both reshape which studies the loss cares about -- and the distance collapses to
calib_dense_hold's 0.9273. That failure mode is the informative one and is why the read below is the
nearest-neighbour column, not the solo.

PRE-REGISTRATION, read as SEAT first and SOLO second:
  seat >= +0.0018 and nearest <= 0.90   the cell is occupied. Both terms compose; the next arms are more
                                        members built this way, and member-quality arms stop.
  seat >= +0.0015, nearest 0.90-0.93    it seats, but on quality not distance. Directional, keep it free,
                                        do not plan around it.
  seat <  +0.0015, nearest >= 0.92      SAME LEVER. Calibration and the margin are one axis; that CLOSES
                                        the objective route the same way dissent_seat closed the
                                        decorrelation route, and it closes it for ~85 min.
  solo <  0.8525                        suspect the harness before the mechanism: both terms measured
                                        positive alone at this corner, so a fall below the weaker one is a
                                        plumbing shape. Diff the recorded recipe stamps key by key.
  Run convergence_check BEFORE quoting any of the above: under one_cycle a truncated score is a FLOOR.

SOLO CONTROLS, both at this exact corner, both already on disk:
  margin_seat        0.8525  (the margin term alone, no hold)
  calib_dense_hold   0.8634  (the calibration term alone, with hold)
  band_dense_hold    0.8573  (neither term, with hold -- the free reusable control)
  additive solo prediction = margin_seat + (calib_dense_hold - band_dense_hold) = 0.8525 + 0.0061 = 0.8586,
  less the -0.0005 hold price margin_seat does not carry = 0.8581.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY. One member. A seat measured against gradeswap_v1 (0.933, 7 members) is not a seat in
the 0.939 champion, which cannot be priced at all because five of its six members are _ff full-fit. And
knee-bxp2 stands: distance is a twin detector, never a merit column -- a distant-and-weak member is
vjepa_warm's quadrant, worth +0.0001.
notes:
RAN AND IS RECORDED (experiments/README.md, 'margin_calib — the empty quadrant is occupied, and the two terms are ANTAGONISTIC'). Solo 0.8235 @ e10/12, converged. Seat -0.0013 [-0.0021, -0.0005] against gradeswap_v1 — negative with a band excluding zero. Distance nearest 0.8298, the most distant candidate ever priced here.

The pre-registered SAME-LEVER branch is refuted: it predicted seat < +0.0015 AND nearest >= 0.92, and the distance went the other way. The terms are mechanically distinct as this bead argued, and antagonistic when combined. The harness branch was checked first as this bead demanded — recipe stamps diffed key by key against BOTH controls, both flags landed, corner exact.

Additive prediction was 0.8581; actual 0.8235; interaction -0.0346. Hypothesis for why, offered as falsifiable and not measured: an AUC-margin loss ranks across a positive/negative boundary that --calibrated-targets deliberately smears.

Closing: the cell is occupied and it is neither strong nor seatable. Do NOT re-arm this pair at another corner without first falsifying the antagonism hypothesis cheaply.

title: stack3: calib + EMA + mixup as one member, the arithmetic route to +0.010
description:
GATED on stackfit (knee-orjq) reading ADDITIVE. If it does, the next arm lays the third measured-positive term on the pair.

THE ARITHMETIC, stated before the arm:
  calib   +0.0061  (calib_dense_hold 0.8634 vs band_dense_hold 0.8573; replicated at a
                    second corner by knee-bs4l, +0.0072 proxy / +0.0129 annotated)
  EMA     +0.003   (competitor single-variable ablation, research/2026-08-26_the-ablation-
                    table-a-competitor-published.md; our own ema_dense reads it at this corner)
  mixup   +0.0015  (ours, mixup224_long 0.8505 vs 0.8490; independently confirmed at +0.002
                    by the same competitor table)
  ------------------
  sum     +0.0106  offline over band_dense 0.8578 -> ~0.8684
  x board_transfer 1.72 = +0.018 board on the member

interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_what-0950-actually-costs.md prices first place at exactly
+0.010 offline on ONE member. This sum is the only construction on the board that reaches it.

WHY THESE THREE AND NOT THE COMPETITOR'S RECIPE. Their published stack is EfficientNet-B0 /
4 slot sequences / 288 px and lands 0.870 public - BELOW our 0.925. Replicating it is a
downgrade, so 'replicate the frontier' is not available on that post. The 0.942 single at
224 px is a DIFFERENT competitor and its recipe is unnamed ('tweaks'). What we can stack is
our own measured terms plus the two of theirs that our own harness already reproduces in sign
and size (mixup +0.0015 vs +0.002).

MECHANICAL INDEPENDENCE is the precondition and it holds three ways: calib changes what the
targets say, EMA changes which weights are kept, mixup changes what the inputs are.

PRICE: ~110 min of card at 336 px / 20 slices, ZERO submission slots.
P(clears the 0.0062 floor over calib_dense_hold): ~0.35 - the two added terms sum to +0.0045,
under the floor, so a null is the modal single-seed outcome and the reading is DIRECTIONAL.
Its value is the SUM against band_dense, not the increment against its own control.

KILL CONDITION: if stackfit reads SUBSTITUTES-NOT-COMPLEMENTS, do not run this - the stack
route is dead and a three-term version of a refuted two-term result diagnoses nothing.
notes:
stackfit read 2026-08-27, converged (12/12, best e7 0.8631, convergence_check clean, both flags verified in the recipe stamp).

ARITHMETIC FIRST, as the arm's header demanded:
  predicted = calib_dense_hold + (ema_dense - band_dense) = 0.8634 + (0.8588 - 0.8578) = 0.8644
  observed  = 0.8631  ->  -0.0013 vs predicted, -0.0003 vs the control.

Nominally that is the ADDITIVE band (within 0.0062). The verdict is NOT taken, because the arm had no
power: the separation between the additive prediction and the null in which --ema contributes nothing
is +0.0010, one sixth of the decision band. The ADDITIVE region and the did-nothing region are the same
region, so no outcome of this arm could have told them apart.

WHAT IT DID SETTLE. The negative branches are far from the null and are refuted:
  substitutes-not-complements line 0.8582 -> observed is +0.0049 above it
  harness/plumbing line band_dense_hold 0.8573 -> observed is +0.0058 above it
So two levers that each measured positive alone do not cancel when stacked at this corner. The stack
route is not killed. That was the arm's own stated reason for spending the card and it is the one claim
it is entitled to make.

GATE ON stack3: OPEN, with a condition - run it only if EVERY term it stacks has a solo effect above
0.0062. Stacking sub-floor terms reproduces this failure once per term and costs a card hour each.

RULE BOUGHT: never test additivity with a term whose solo effect is below the noise floor; compute
predicted-minus-control before choosing the terms. ema_dense's +0.0010 was already on the ledger when
this arm was written.

interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_stackfit-additivity.md

title: blendlabels was priced on the ruler that cannot see it - refit with --hold-annotations and read both
description:
THE SHAPE IS knee-bs4l's, for a different flag. blendlabels trained on a three-reader blend and measured +0.0034 mean (+0.0070 on the six label-bottlenecked findings). The ledger reads that as 'the label lane is LIVE and SMALL, an order of magnitude short of the 1.5% bar'. Both numbers come from the proxy holdout, scored against report_labels_v2 - the table the blend departs from. Pinned to v2 the ruler CHARGES the arm for every cell where the blend is right and v2 is wrong; unpinned it measures disagreement with v2 and calls it quality. No pin makes that ruler able to see supervision quality, so the SIZE of this lane has never been measured.

HOW BIG THE BLIND SPOT IS, MEASURED 2026-08-26 (macro AUC against the 58 annotated studies): report_labels_v2 0.8700, blend_three_v1 0.8955, blend_four 0.8953, merged_blend_v1 0.8955, blend_nolixin 0.8935, blend_hybrid 0.8978, confident 0.8574, flatyes_v2 0.8076. The 0.8700 reproduces the public benchmark's published 0.870 for that same table exactly, which is the ruler validating itself. So the blend is +0.026 macro AUC closer to the radiologist than the table the proxy scores against, and holdannot has separately measured the ruler gap at +0.045 (0.8487 report / 0.8932 annotation).

THE ARM (experiments/arms/blendhold.sh, written): holdannot's command with --labels moved to blend_three_v1 and --eval-labels pinned to v2. Single variable. Control is holdannot_s2026 (0.8487 / 0.8932), NOT native224 and NOT blendlabels - both arms must hold the annotations or the second ruler scores training cells and annotated_readings refuses the checkpoint.

PRE-REGISTRATION:
 - better teacher -> proxy flat or slightly NEGATIVE while the supervision_gap aggregate rises above 0.8932. +0.015 or more there says the lane was mispriced by the ruler and reopens it as a path to 0.950.
 - not a better teacher -> both flat or down. The lane closes on the objective, and for every table on disk, since the blends do not separate from each other (table_blend: every pairwise interval covers zero over 58 studies).
 - both rise -> the +0.0034 understated it on its own ruler too, and the pin was what was wrong.

NON-LICENSE (knee-9198): n=58, not a random sample (ACL 41% there vs ~20% in the corpus). The claim is about WHICH RULER; documentary, not statistical. Cannot license a submission on its own.

COST: ~20 min at 224px / 12 slices, no submission slot. Queue behind the dense-hold chain.
notes:
PRICE: ~20 min of card (224 px / 12 slices, matched to holdannot), zero submission slots, no queue displacement — it runs in a gap behind the dense-hold chain.

P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.05 as an IMPROVEMENT. This is not sold as one. Read as an INSTRUMENT: P(it changes what we believe about the label lane) ~ 0.6, because the two rulers make opposite predictions and only one of them can be right. The lane is currently CLOSED on the strength of a +0.0034 reading taken through a ruler measured to be biased against exactly this kind of arm by up to +0.045. Either the arm reopens a whole axis (a +0.015 rise on the 58 is a path worth the card time it would then justify) or it closes it on the objective for every table on disk, which retires the suspicion and stops the next session re-deriving it. At 20 minutes and no slot, an instrument that settles an axis is the best ratio on the board right now.
close_reason: SWEEP phase 1 (completed but not properly marked): the arm named in this bead's own title has a .full.log in $MODELS/experiments/ AND a scored row in experiments/README.md. The work ran and the ledger priced it; the bead was never marked. Reversible - bd update --status open if a reading here is still owed.

title: Two GPU-bound jobs on one card cost >=6.6x, not 2x — serialise, never share
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-26 07:20Z, and it is the first number this project has for card sharing.

SETUP: our blend_base (blendsix member 5, ViT-B/14 at 336px, batch 6, 12 slices, compile_encoder) and biohub's hoct_finer122_converge (4x voxels, batch 4) computing simultaneously on the one RTX 5090.

CONTROL, from the same arm log, same recipe family, solo: epoch 0 at 346s / 337s / 366s / 346s across the four members that ran before the other job started (torch.compile of the encoder is INSIDE those numbers, so compile is not a confound). Steady epochs 331-335s.

READING: blend_base started 06:53Z and printed ZERO epoch lines in 27 minutes. Against a 346s solo epoch 0 that is >=4.7x, and it is a FLOOR rather than an estimate — the epoch had not landed, so the true multiple is larger than the one quotable.

nvidia-smi pmon shows both processes computing (ours 61-74% SM, theirs 24-37%), so neither is starved of the scheduler. The loss is not starvation, it is that two GPU-bound jobs do not overlap — they interleave, and each pays the other's context switches on top of its own work.

WHY >2x AND NOT 2x. Naive sharing arithmetic says each job halves. The measurement says worse than quartered. Whatever the mechanism (switch overhead, cache thrash, memory pressure at 31847/32607 MiB), the practical rule is the same and it is stronger than the intuition it replaces: SERIAL BEATS PARALLEL FOR BOTH JOBS, in either order. Ours-first finishes both sooner than sharing does; theirs-first also finishes both sooner than sharing does. Sharing is dominated.

CONSEQUENCE FOR PLANNING: every wall-clock price in this repo (the 3.3h RAD-DINO estimate at knee-fh31, the 340s/epoch scaling, member_curve timings) assumes a solo card. Any of them quoted during a shared window is wrong by a factor this bead now bounds below at 4.7. Check card_check before believing a duration, not just before launching.

NOT A CONTENTION COMPLAINT. The card is shared by arrangement and biohub owns it. Letter sent to their inbox at 0722z with the numbers and the serial proposal; the decision is theirs.

OPEN: no measurement from the biohub side. Their epoch time against their own solo baseline would turn this from half a fact into a shared one, and would say whether the 4.7x is symmetric or falls mostly on the job with the larger compiled graph.
notes:
REVISED 2026-08-26 07:32Z, upward, and the revision is the point.

The first reading quoted >=4.7x from 27 minutes with zero epoch lines. At 07:31Z blend_base had gone
38 minutes with still zero epoch lines against a 346 s solo epoch 0, which is >=6.6x and STILL a floor
— the epoch never landed, so the true multiple is unbounded from below by anything I measured.

Consequence that matters more than the constant: I wrote a letter at 07:22Z proposing the peer give us
65 more minutes, and that 65 was 11 epochs at the 335 s SOLO rate applied to a CONTENDED run. It was
the very mistake the letter existed to expose, made in the letter's own recommendation. At 6.6x the
twelve epochs were 7.6+ hours — longer than the peer's entire run, spent inside their window. Killed
our arm at 07:32Z rather than wait for a reply, and sent the correction.

RULE: when quoting time-remaining on a shared card, the rate must come from a CONTENDED epoch or the
estimate is not an estimate. If no contended epoch has landed, the honest statement is 'unknown and
larger than X', never a number.

Control (same log, same recipe family, solo): epoch 0 at 346/337/366/346 s with torch.compile inside
those numbers; steady 331-335 s. Both processes were computing, not starved — pmon had ours at 61-74%
SM and theirs at 24-37%. So the loss is interleaving, not starvation, and serial beats parallel in
EITHER order. Every wall-clock price in this repo assumes a solo card.

title: raddino_dense COLD re-run under corrected normalisation - the domain-init read, offline, no slot
description:
The 2026-08-23 raddino_dense reading of 0.8137 is void for TWO independent reasons, and neither is about radiology pretraining.

(1) NORMALISATION WAS DIFFERENTIAL, against the arm. StudyModel.forward has always normalised against buffers that defaulted to the ImageNet constants for every trunk alike. DINOv2-base declares exactly those, so base_dense_s2026 (0.8512, the control) was correct. RAD-DINO declares 0.5307/0.2583 - greyscale, repeated over three channels - so the treatment was fed inputs 0.20 std off its pretraining distribution with a 12.8 percent scale error. The arm file itself asserted the opposite ('this repository applies no ImageNet mean/std anywhere; slices are scaled per study') and concluded the mismatch cancelled between arms. That prose is now corrected in experiments/arms/raddino_dense.sh.

(2) THE PROCESS WAS KILLED at step 248/583 of epoch 7 of 12 (knee-6477). Under one_cycle the anneal never ran, so 0.8137 is a FLOOR, on a curve still decelerating upward.

PLUMBING VERIFIED BEFORE PRICING, per the CLAUDE.md rule that a value in a config with a constant at the consumer is its own failure mode. Normalization is a per-encoder frozen dataclass; both non-test construction sites now read it - kneemri/training/run_setup.py:331 (train path, already clean) and kneemri/embeddings/build_embeddings.py:72 (embeddings path, FIXED in this session, it was silently defaulting to ImageNet). Buffers are persistent, so every member already on disk keeps the constants it was fitted under and only a fresh fit moves.

NO WARM START. The e6 checkpoint carries the wrong constants in its own state dict, which makes the owner's standing ban on warm-starting it correct twice over. This is a cold run.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE CARD. It is the only unblocked instance of the encoder-KIND argument (knee-mq8x): every encoder we have fitted is natural-image or natural-video pretrained, which is several instances of ONE kind. RadImageNet fails Kaggle rule 2.6a (weights are request-gated, not freely available to every participant). MRNet and fastMRI+ are owner-blocked. RAD-DINO is MIT, already mounted at dimiturnt/rad-dino, and finetuned FROM facebook/dinov2-base - same ViT-B/14, same 768 width, same 12 blocks - so the initialisation weights are the ONLY variable against base_dense_s2026.

AND IT READS OFFLINE. Fold 0, scoreable with no submission. That is decisive with slot 5 of 2026-08-26 held under owner directive (knee-pubw) and no board reading available before the 00:00Z reset.

PRICE: ~3.3 h of card, derived from blend_through's measured 340 s/epoch at batch 12 / 12 slices, scaled to batch 6 / 20 slices - NOT the 50 min knee-vp8q guessed. Card frees ~09:20Z when blendsix member 5 lands, so it reads ~12:40Z. GAIN: +0.005-0.015 offline (partial domain match - chest radiographs, not knee MRI), which board_transfer at +1.72 puts at +0.009-0.026 board. P(clears the 1.5 percent bar) ~ 1 in 6. Accepted because the slot cost is ZERO and nothing else is queued for those hours.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS are unchanged from the arm file and were written before either defect was known: >=0.866 radiology init is the lever; 0.856-0.865 directional, keep as an ensemble seat, do not plan around it; 0.846-0.855 a tie, kills the chest-radiograph route and prices RadImageNet down without killing it, says nothing about MRNet; <=0.845 SUSPECT THE HARNESS FIRST - now doubly, since a third silent defect is more likely than a real refutation at that size.

Blocked on: blendsix member 5 (blend_base) finishing ~09:20Z, and on honouring the celltrack card-handoff offer at the member 4/5 boundary (~07:00Z) if they reply.
notes:
RATIONALE NARROWED 2026-08-26 07:37Z — an argument was REMOVED, not added.

Forum topic 737566 (posted 04:42Z today) argues everyone's Synovitis is stuck at 0.62-0.72 because the
supervision is thin (~16% of reports mention any synovitis term), and reports that a RadImageNet-pretrained
encoder reached 0.78 where all their ImageNet models sat at 0.62-0.72. That is the strongest public
argument currently available for a medically-pretrained encoder, and it DOES NOT TRANSFER HERE.

weights_gap --run small_batch6_s2026, zero card, zero slot, matched ruler (909 fold-0 studies, same graded
truth, same rank AUC, against the twenty published CC0 members):

  ours Synovitis 0.8673   their single 0.8576   their 4-seed pool 0.8661   n_pos 124
  our own MEAN   0.8598

Synovitis is ABOVE our mean and sixth of twelve, not worst. Their proposed fix reads 0.78, which is 0.089
BELOW our current number. And the 'everyone' half fails on the only matched evidence available: twenty
independent published ImageNet-family checkpoints read 0.8576 on the same studies, not 0.62-0.72. The
likeliest explanation is in their own post — they score against a label table whose Synovitis agrees with
radiologists at ~0.79, so a ceiling in the ruler reads as a ceiling in the model.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ARM: it still stands, but on knee-jk3's ground ALONE (0.044 at matched train loss,
measured on our ruler). It must be read as a general-representation test and NEVER as a Synovitis fix, and
it must not be requeued on the borrowed reason. Pre-flight remains clean (arm_check --only raddino_dense,
0 refused, 0 uncached); still waiting on the card owner's finish/fail ping.

Research page: research/2026-08-26_synovitis-is-not-our-weak-label.md

RESULT 2026-08-26 — ran, converged, and the mechanism is refuted at this corner.

12 epochs of 12. Peak 0.8141 at e7, then .8106 / .8103 / .8101 / .8102. Exact control base_dense_s2026 =
0.8512, same ViT-B/14 architecture, same 336px/20-slice/0.1-0.9 cache, same --backbone-lr 4e-5, same head
rate, same one-cycle, same fold-0 holdout. Only the initialisation weights differ. Delta -0.0371, six
times the 0.0062 paired floor.

BOTH NAMED SUSPECTS CLEARED BEFORE THE VERDICT WAS WRITTEN, which is the whole reason this bead existed.
The predecessor read 0.8137 and this reads 0.8141 - a +0.0004 move after correcting a 0.20-std input
offset is exactly the coincidence that means "check whether the fix fired" rather than "the fix did not
matter". It fired: the checkpoint's registered buffers read mean [0.5307, 0.5307, 0.5307] and std
[0.2583, 0.2583, 0.2583], RAD-DINO's own greyscale constants, not ImageNet's. Truncation cleared too -
e11 recorded, so this is not a floor under one_cycle.

Ledger entry written in experiments/README.md. Closing: the read this bead was opened to take has been
taken.

title: Encoder diversity was closed across three NATURAL-image encoders - a medically-pretrained one is a different KIND and is the last unlike-and-strong member available
description:
THE ARGUMENT, and it is the same shape as the one that reopened MRNet: KIND, not instance.

knee-jk3's notes record encoder diversity as CLOSED - 'three encoders now measured; the sign transfers member-to-member, the magnitude does not'. True, and it does not say what it is read as saying. The three are DINOv2, DINOv3 and V-JEPA2. All three are pretrained on NATURAL IMAGES. What was measured is that swapping one natural-image encoder for another natural-image encoder buys a diversity term that does not survive. That is a finding about three instances of one kind, not about the axis.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW. knee-urvf says an ensemble rises on exactly two things: raising the FLOOR of every member, or adding one that is STRONG AND UNLIKE. Slot 4 tests the floor (three champion seats swapped for blend-supervised twins). Nothing in the pool tests UNLIKE in any deep sense - six members that all read natural-image features are six samples of one representation.

THE OUTSIDE EVIDENCE, and it is the only quantified claim in the forum thread. Topic 737566 reports RadImageNet pretraining taking Synovitis from 0.62-0.72 to 0.78 where four ImageNet-pretrained architectures could not move. We DECLINED that as a Synovitis fix, correctly - our Synovitis already reads 0.8456/0.8764 (experiments/README.md:473), well above their ceiling, so the hole they patched is not ours. But the poster's own words are 'the image signal exists, but natural-image features can't see it', and that is a claim about the REPRESENTATION, not about Synovitis. Read as a representation claim it is untested here and it is testable.

WHERE IT WOULD PAY, pre-registered: the FOCAL findings. knee-lxi1's deficit set (Lateral Meniscus -0.1925, ACL -0.1225, MCL -0.0964, Medial Meniscus -0.0938, PF OA -0.0856, Lateral OA -0.0793, negative gaps summing 0.670) is where the model fails to extract from pixels what the label states clearly - today's two label instruments proved the labels there are good (ACL 4 of 58 unsure, Medial Meniscus 2). A representation that cannot resolve fine anatomy is exactly knee-am4's border result, which knee-jk3 already reads as the same finding as the starvation.

WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a resolution play. Our own native224 reads 0.8482 against band_dense's 0.8578, and knee-a8x refuted 392px at +0.0002 - our measurement and the rivals' 224-px singles AGREE that resolution is not the axis. It is not a knob inside the pilkwang family either, which is the class knee-jk3 banned.

PRICE. ~75 min of card at band_dense's 368 s/epoch x 12 epochs, against ~14 hours free after blendsix lands ~0920z. Plausible gain if the mechanism is real: a member that moves the focal half, which is the half that carries the whole deficit. Odds it clears 1.5% on the mean: low, call it 0.15 - but it is the ONLY remaining candidate that is both strong and unlike, and under knee-urvf that is the one property that raises an ensemble. Even a par-scoring member that reads differently is worth a seat, which is the owner's standing rule ('its about diversity, not averaging 7 numbers that are the same number').

REFUTATION CONDITION, written before it runs: if the focal half does not move MORE than the diffuse half, the kind-of-pretraining story is wrong and the encoder axis closes for real rather than for three instances. A mean at or below control with a flat focal/diffuse split fires it.

BLOCKER TO CHECK FIRST: RadImageNet's licence and whether Kaggle rule 2.6a permits it as external pretrained weights - the same gate MRNet sits behind (knee-ombx). Check before spending card, not after. If the licence fails, the argument survives and needs a different medically-pretrained encoder.
notes: SEQUENCING, 0645z: BiomedCLIP is licence-clean but it is NOT the next arm, and knee-fh31 (cold RAD-DINO) is. Two reasons, both structural. (1) BiomedCLIP is microsoft/BiomedCLIP-PubMedBERT_256-vit_base_patch16_224 - a CLIP image tower, ViT-B/16, contrastively trained against captions. Swapping it in moves architecture, patch size, objective AND pretraining corpus at once, which is the exact confound that made DINOv3/ConvNeXtV2/V-JEPA2 unattributable. RAD-DINO is finetuned FROM facebook/dinov2-base, so it is the only candidate where the initialisation weights are the ONLY variable against a control we already hold (base_dense_s2026, 0.8512). (2) It is a 224 px model and our own resolution reading is against it: native224 scored 0.8482 against band_dense 0.8578, so our 224 is WORSE, and knee-a8x put 392 px at +0.0002. A 224-locked trunk starts a notch down before the domain question is even asked. Also non-volumetric - PMC-15M is 2D paper figures. So BiomedCLIP is CONDITIONAL: it becomes worth its card only if RAD-DINO lands in the >=0.856 bands, i.e. only if radiology-adjacent initialisation demonstrably pays at all. If RAD-DINO ties its control (0.846-0.855), a caption-supervised 224 tower on paper figures is a worse instance of a mechanism that just failed its best instance, and this bead closes on the KIND argument rather than on a licence.

title: Dose the loss weight on hedged label cells, never the value
description:
OWNER FRAMING (2026-08-26): 'text is text but the true label might not be in the text. we extract it from there but ... and its probably hiding in the less sure diagnostics. we have to be careful not to screw them up though - we need to try to make this an improvement.'

THE CAP THIS SITS UNDER. The hosts made the gold 58 and the hidden test labels from the IMAGES (discussion 735826); every table we train on is read from report TEXT. table_separation (2026-08-26) then showed every blend recomposition lives inside the gold ruler's +/-0.008 resolution, and hybrid_v4 is separated ABOVE two blends containing it. So a better READER is a capped lever. What is not capped is how much the trainer BELIEVES each cell.

WHERE THE MISMATCH IS, MEASURED. severity_boundary over the 28 readable-English annotated studies: denial 0/5 positive, small|minimal|trace 6/12 (50%), moderate-or-larger 2/3, unqualified mention 6/7. The hedged band is a coin flip; the denial band is clean. Denominators: 28 of 58 annotated, and 58 is 1.32% of the corpus.

THE DEFECT. experiments/README.md:2430 records that UNK cells sit at the 0.28 default. A cell the reader ADMITTED it could not read is trained as a soft negative. On the findings where the image carries more than the text, that teaches against the image. confident_labels.py already clears the VALUE (Targets.load then gives weight 0) but has never been armed.

THE ACTION, AND WHY IT IS ROBUST. Two stories - hedged cells are noise, or hedged cells are where text under-describes image - give the SAME move: reduce the weight, never the value. Only a FLIP would need to know the answer, and nobody in the loop does.

RAILS (this is the 'do not screw them up' half):
- move the __conf weight only; floor it (0.3, not 0) so a hedged cell still pulls, quietly
- never flip any cell; never touch denials (0/5, the report is reliable when it says NO)
- score fold 0 with --eval-labels pinned to report_labels_v2, per table_blend's TRAINING ON THE RESULT NEEDS --eval-labels
- DOSE it: one arm at half weight on hedged cells. flat = cells were fine. down = real signal removed, stop. up = axis live.

FINDING THE HEDGED CELLS - two sources, both usable:
1. self-reported UNK, already in the tables (20% of English pairs, 34% non-English)
2. cross-reader disagreement across report_labels_v2 / steven_v4blend / lixin_gpt56 / hybrid_v4, aligned by LabelBlend (knee-uahl). Catches confidently-wrong, which UNK by construction cannot see.

GATE BEFORE ANY CARD: per-finding disagreement rate. If it is flat across the twelve findings, the mechanism story (hedging concentrates on the focal findings the model already loses) is wrong and the arm is not licensed.

COST: build is CPU-only. One dosed arm ~40 min on a free card. Plausible size: the focal deficit is 0.670 summed negative gap (knee-lxi1); this axis does not have to close it, only stop teaching against it.
notes:
REFUTED on its own pre-registered gate, 2026-08-26, card-free. Two instruments.

(1) core/data/labels/reader_disagreement.py over 4406 studies, four readers (all three foreign aligned 4406/4406). The gate said: if disagreement is flat across findings, the story is wrong. It is not flat, it is BACKWARDS. Diffuse half (Synovitis .2995, Contusion .2396, Baker's .2180, Fracture .2164, Effusion .2076, Medial OA .1755) mean 0.226. Focal half (Medial Men .2075, Lateral OA .1909, Lateral Men .1803, PF OA .1605, ACL .1496, MCL .1349) mean 0.171. Readers argue about HOW MUCH effusion, not about WHETHER the ACL is torn. Text ambiguity is a severity problem, not a detection problem.

(2) kneemri/evaluation/unsure_cost.py on the 58 annotated studies, 696 cells, 177 UNK taught at 0.28. UNK cells are 13.6% positive; decided cells 41.7%. Pooled unsure-decided -0.2806, 95% [-0.3539, -0.2042], SEPARATED (bootstrapped over STUDIES). So 'the reader could not decide' means 'the report did not mention it and there was nothing there' — 0.28 slightly OVER-states those cells rather than under-stating them. My framing of the default as a bias against the image was wrong.

Both instruments land in the same place and share no denominator: ambiguity lives on the diffuse findings, our deficit (knee-lxi1) lives on the focal ones, and they do not overlap. UNK counts on the findings we actually lose: ACL 4 of 58, Medial Meniscus 2, MCL 6, Lateral Meniscus 7 — the reader is confident there, and supervision_gap reads ACL's report label at 0.9841 against the radiologist. THE LABEL AXIS CANNOT BUY THE FOCAL DEFICIT. No confidence weighting reaches the six findings that carry the gap.

SURVIVES: Synovitis. 41 of 58 unsure, 34.1% of those positive, the only positive taught error (+0.061), and top of the disagreement ranking too. Real reader blindness, both instruments see it — but it sits on our STRONG half (+0.0508 model over labels), so it is an honest small patch, never a lever.

Cost: ~30 min CPU inside a gap where the card was busy. Retired an arm worth ~40 min and possibly a slot. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_label-ambiguity-and-our-deficit-do-not-overlap.md

title: Cross-reader DISAGREEMENT as a per-cell loss weight - the label-error route that needs no radiologist and is not a confirmation loop
description:
Owner's idea, 2026-08-26 05:35Z: find the label errors and fix or down-weight them. This is the form of it that survives audit.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this is not re-litigating it. confident_labels removes cells the reader ITSELF marked UNK (20% of English pairs, 34% of non-English) by clearing the VALUE, which Targets.load turns into weight 0. reader_agreement measures agreement with the radiologist per language on the 58. Targets already multiplies every cell's loss by a weight and reads a __conf column per target. So the PLUMBING is built and one notion of uncertainty is already wired.

WHAT IS NOT BUILT, AND IS THE GAP. confident_labels can only catch cells the reader KNEW it was unsure about. The damaging class is the opposite one - cells where the reader was CONFIDENT AND WRONG - and by construction a self-reported flag cannot see those. We hold four INDEPENDENT readings of the same reports (ours report_labels_v2, steven_v2/v4blend, lixin_gpt56, hybrid_v4 flight0234), all aligned on the same study index by LabelBlend. Where they DISAGREE the text is ambiguous; where they AGREE it is not. That is an uncertainty estimate the reader's own flag cannot produce, it costs no card and no slot to compute, and it feeds a __conf column the trainer already consumes.

WHY IT IS NOT A CONFIRMATION LOOP. The signal comes from other READERS of the text, not from the model being trained. The alternative route - confident-learning over our own held-out predictions (909-study report holdout exists) - is stronger per unit of noise but down-weights exactly what the model already disagrees with, which teaches it its own prior. If that route is run at all it must DOWN-WEIGHT and never FLIP, and it should be run second, against this as the control.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO, and the owner said it first: the text is the text. Every reader here reads the same reports, so this cleans noise INSIDE the report-derived measurement and cannot cross to the image-derived one the hidden test uses. It is orthogonal to knee-ombx (MRNet), not a substitute.

WHY IT MIGHT MATTER FOR THE LABELS THAT CARRY THE DEFICIT. knee-lxi1 puts the whole member deficit on six focal structural findings - Lateral Meniscus (model 0.6497), ACL, MCL, Medial Meniscus, PF/Lateral OA. Those are precisely the findings whose report sentences carry grade and equivocation words (possible, probable, degenerative signal reaching the surface), so they should be where four readers disagree most. That is a CHECK this bead has to run before any training: profile the disagreement rate per finding, and if it is flat across the twelve, the mechanism story is wrong and the arm is not licensed.

PRICE. The disagreement table is CPU-only, minutes, zero slots. One arm to test it is ~1.2 h of card, warm-startable since the input distribution is unchanged and only the loss weights move. P(clears the 1.5% bar alone) ~0.10 - our one previous label-content experiment read -0.0008 against a floor since measured at 0.006, so it could not have detected anything in either direction, and the axis is genuinely untested rather than refuted. Justified as a CHEAP arm on the axis that knee-lxi1 left open, not as a favourite.

PRE-REGISTER BEFORE RUNNING: the per-finding disagreement profile (does it concentrate on the six focal labels?), and a per-label read on the arm with the six diffuse findings as the control that must not fall.
notes: Closed by the same two instruments as knee-1ww2 (2026-08-26). This bead argued that the UNK default at 0.28 was a systematic bias teaching a soft NO where the image carries a YES. Measured on the 58 annotated studies: UNK cells are 13.6% positive against decided cells' 41.7%, pooled difference -0.2806 [-0.3539, -0.2042] SEPARATED. The default slightly OVER-states those cells. The mechanism this bead rests on does not exist. Do not re-open it without a NEW denominator — the 58 is the only place a radiologist and our reader both spoke, and it says no.

title: Label-table ranking now has intervals: lixin is resolvably the WORST reader and sits inside our blend; hybrid_v4 is the best and is not
description:
kneemri.evaluation.table_separation (new) puts a PAIRED bootstrap interval over the 58 gold studies on every pairwise difference between label tables. 1000 draws, StudyBootstrap, studies not cells.

Means: hybrid_v4 0.8991 > steven_v4blend 0.8927 > blend_three 0.8912 > steven_v2 0.8873 > ours 0.8658 > lixin_gpt56 0.8352.

What is RESOLVED (interval excludes zero):
- blend_three - ours +0.0254 [+0.0098, +0.0428]. The blend IS better than our v2. blendsix is not dosing noise.
- hybrid_v4 - ours +0.0333 [+0.0156, +0.0528].
- lixin_gpt56 - blend_three -0.0560 [-0.0791, -0.0343]. lixin is resolvably worse than everything here, INCLUDING our own table (-0.0306 [-0.0554, -0.0050]).

What is NOT resolved:
- steven_v4blend - blend_three +0.0015 [-0.0069, +0.0121]. table_blend's own worry ('the blend does not beat its best input') is an UNRESOLVED difference, not a deficit.
- hybrid_v4 - blend_three +0.0079 [-0.0008, +0.0180]. Nearly all positive, does not clear.

THE LEVER. blend_three_v1 = mean(ours, steven, lixin). It averages in the one reader that is separated-worse than our own table, and it omits the best reader on the board. Candidates built and being scored: blend_nolixin (ours+steven_v4+hybrid), blend_four, blend_hybrid.

CAUTION, STATED BEFORE THE ANSWER. 15 pairwise comparisons on 58 studies; choosing a blend by its gold score is fitting to the ruler. The 58 pick among a few PRE-SPECIFIED candidates; the board is the test. And blendsix is already committed to blend_three - this cannot re-dose it, it decides the NEXT table.

Also fixed here: SupervisionGap.reported now reindexes to all twelve TARGETS. It returned only the columns a table carried, and 'against' names columns BY POSITION, so a foreign table missing one finding would have scored every later finding under its neighbour's name. Ours carries twelve so it never fired.
notes:
ANSWERED, and it refutes the lever this bead proposed.

Four blends scored the same way (1000 draws, 58 gold studies):
  blend_three   0.8912   mean(ours, steven_v2-era, lixin)  -- the one blendsix is dosing
  blend_nolixin 0.8894   ours + steven_v4blend + hybrid_v4
  blend_four    0.8909   ours + steven_v4blend + hybrid_v4 + lixin
  blend_hybrid  0.8931   ours + hybrid_v4
  hybrid_v4     0.8991   the single best reader, unblended

EVERY pairwise interval among the four blends covers zero:
  blend_nolixin - blend_three -0.0019 [-0.0072, +0.0020]
  blend_four    - blend_three -0.0003 [-0.0035, +0.0019]
  blend_hybrid  - blend_three +0.0019 [-0.0055, +0.0091]

So dropping the resolvably-worst reader does NOT help, and adding the resolvably-best one does NOT help.
Recomposing the blend is unavailable as a lever on this ruler.

The one thing that DOES read: hybrid_v4 alone is separated ABOVE two blends that contain it --
  hybrid_v4 - blend_nolixin +0.0098 [+0.0016, +0.0202] SEPARATED
  hybrid_v4 - blend_four    +0.0082 [+0.0005, +0.0183] SEPARATED
  hybrid_v4 - blend_three   +0.0079 [-0.0008, +0.0180] (a hair off)
Averaging our coarser table into the best reader DILUTES it. That is the opposite of the noise-cancelling
story the blend was built on, and it is the only directional signal here.

DENOMINATOR AND LIMITS, stated because the conclusion is a null. 58 studies, 12 findings, one corpus;
this ruler resolves about +/-0.008 and every blend recipe lives inside it. 'Unresolved' is not 'equal' --
the board could still separate what the gold cannot. But we cannot buy board reads for label tables: the
slots are pinned to the blendsix harvest, and the arm-level effect is ALREADY measured at +0.0034 mean
(blendlabels, experiments/README), below the 0.0062 floor.

CONSEQUENCE: the label-TABLE axis is exhausted. A better table has to come from a better READER, not a
new weighting of the readers on hand. blendsix keeps dosing blend_three -- correctly, since blend_three
is separated above our v2 at +0.0254 [+0.0098, +0.0428] -- and no card is spent choosing among blends.

table_blend's module docstring now carries this instead of the bare pair of numbers.
close_reason: Closed by its own NOTES: the verdict (REFUTED/SUPERSEDED/ANSWERED/RESOLVED/CLOSED/FIXED) was written into the bead and the status was never moved. Swept 2026-09-16 (owner: 'if we get piled upon, nothing remains important').

title: Does the BLEND beat its best input as SUPERVISION? Our own table numbers say it does not
description:
THE SUSPICION, and it is against the arm currently on the card. blendsix puts the three-reader blend (merged_blend_v1.csv) on all six seats. But core/data/labels/table_blend.py's own measurement against the 58 radiologist studies reads mean(ours, steven, lixin) = 0.8912 while the best single foreign table reads 0.8927 — the blend does NOT beat its best input, and its docstring says so in as many words: 'which is what averaging independent readers is supposed to do'. Independently, forum topic 735304's two strongest 5-fold singles both describe themselves as 'LLM output labels only', not as a blend, and topic 737454's benchmark puts stevenleehans v4 blend at 0.893 macro AUC against radiologists — the same table we score at 0.8927. If the best single table is better SUPERVISION than the blend, blendsix is dosing the wrong table six times.

WHAT MAKES THIS CHEAP NOW. knee-1xib unblocked images_224px_12sl_merged.npy (5,143 studies, byte-identical row order to the 336 index). At ~110 s/epoch a 12-epoch fold-0 arm is ~22 minutes, so this is a method-search question, not a card block. Two arms, ~45 minutes total: one trained on merged_blend_v1.csv, one on the best foreign table alone, everything else held.

THE HARD PART, STATED BEFORE THE RUN, BECAUSE IT IS WHAT DECIDES WHETHER THE RESULT MEANS ANYTHING. Our fold-0 holdout is scored against report_labels_v2, so an unpinned comparison measures DISAGREEMENT WITH V2 and is biased toward whichever supervision is closer to v2 — which is ours, i.e. toward the blend. table_blend's docstring already raises this. The unbiased rulers are the 58 gold studies (honest but tiny: ~696 cells, no computed interval, and the numbers above must not be quoted as separated on it) and the board (a slot). So the read is: run both, report the v2-holdout delta AND the 58-gold delta, and treat the arm as informative ONLY where the two agree in SIGN. Where they disagree, the answer is that this rig cannot settle it and the question needs a slot.

NOT PRICED AS A SCORE LEVER. It is an instrument on the one axis the board evidence points at (knee-nnjb: the member deficit is 0.013 and the deficit is the member, not the ensemble). If the single table wins in both rulers, every future blend-supervised seat changes table and blendsix's dose reading has to be re-read as a dose of the WRONG table. If the blend wins, blendsix's premise is confirmed and this closes.

Run after blendsix frees the card, or in any gap. Do NOT interrupt blendsix for it.
notes:
CLOSED BY ITS OWN PRE-REGISTRATION, not by a card.

This bead's read rule was: 'run both, report the v2-holdout delta AND the 58-gold delta, and treat the
arm as informative ONLY where the two agree in SIGN. Where they disagree, the answer is that this rig
cannot settle it.'

The 58-gold ruler has now answered, with the interval this bead correctly said was missing.
kneemri.evaluation.table_separation, 1000 paired draws over studies:

  best single foreign table (steven_v4blend) - blend_three  =  +0.0015  95% [-0.0069, +0.0121]

UNRESOLVED. The premise -- 'the blend does NOT beat its best input' -- was read off a bare 0.8912 vs
0.8927 and does not survive its own error bar. One of the two rulers this bead requires has come back
with no sign at all, so by its own rule the arm cannot be informative and the 45 minutes buy nothing.

Priced anyway: two 22-min arms on an axis whose arm-level effect is already measured at +0.0034 mean
(blendlabels), below the 0.0062 floor. That is a ~0-expected-score run that is not even a good
instrument, because the instrument it would need has already run on CPU for free.

WHAT SURVIVES. blend_three is separated ABOVE our own v2 at +0.0254 [+0.0098, +0.0428], so blendsix is
dosing a table that is genuinely better than the one the champion's seats were trained on. Its premise
is confirmed, which is the outcome this bead named as 'if the blend wins, this closes'.

The wider label-table finding, including that no recomposition of the blend is available and that the
single best reader is diluted by blending, is knee-ym3z.

title: blendsix harvests TWICE: dose-3 at slot 4, dose-6 at slot 5
description:
blendsix.sh builds five all-data blend-supervised members SEQUENTIALLY at ~1.2 h each, so the roster it argues for does not exist until ~09:20Z. The owner's slot budget wants slot 4 spent inside a four-hour window from 02:15Z. Those two facts are only in conflict if the arm is read once.

HARVEST PLAN. After three members land (~05:50Z: blend_ws, blend_calib, blend_ladder) seat exactly three of them into the champion's six, replacing three non-blend seats, and spend slot 4 on DOSE 3. Let the remaining two finish and spend slot 5 (~23:30Z) on DOSE 6, the roster blendsix was written for. One arm, one card block, two board readings, and the dose variable gets a MIDPOINT instead of a single endpoint - which is worth more than either point alone, because blendseat already pinned dose 1 at 0.939.

WHY THE MIDPOINT IS NOT FREE SIGNAL AND WHAT IT COSTS. Dose 3 and dose 6 are not independent draws; they share three members, so their difference is better resolved than either against blendseat. The honest read is the SHAPE across 1/3/6, and it is only interpretable if the three seats displaced at dose 3 are the same three displaced first at dose 6.

PRE-REGISTERED for dose 3 against blendseat_v1 0.939 (dose 1), on the board:
  * >= 0.947. The dose is the lever and it is already saturating at three; slot 5 goes to dose 6 to find the knee.
  * 0.943-0.946. Real, under the 1.5% bar as a step, and the six-seat reading becomes the one that matters.
  * 0.940-0.942. Directional, inside the scatter our nine flat 6-7 member entries already span.
  * 0.936-0.939. FLAT at three. Dose 6 is still worth slot 5 - a linear dose effect would read flat at the midpoint - but the prior on it drops hard.
  * <= 0.935. Suspect the harmonised 12/0.2-0.8 geometry BEFORE the supervision, per blendsix.sh's own last band; member_distance over the three new members answers that with no card.
notes:
DOSE 3 READ 2026-08-26 06:24Z: blendthree_v1 (ref 55787345) scored 0.939 — exactly the champion blendseat_v1 0.939, i.e. DEAD FLAT. Lands in this bead's pre-registered FLAT 0.936-0.939 band.

Three of six seats carried blend supervision (blend_calib, blend_ladder, blend_ws replacing their non-blend twins); everything else — vote rule, count, kit 8243a95, serving views, member order — is blendseat's. So this is the first DIRECT board test of knee-urvf's floor-raise prescription, and at half dose it moved the board by 0.000.

That is a LOWERED PRIOR on dose 6, not a refutation: a linear dose effect reads flat at the midpoint, and only the endpoint separates 'blend supervision does nothing' from 'three seats is not enough of it'.

RULE NOT FIRED. This bead sends the FLAT band to dose 6 at slot 5. Slot 5 is HELD by owner directive (knee-pubw: 'dont spend the last slot!!' / 'at least dont spend the last one too!'). The owner beats the bead. Dose 6 waits for a slot on 2026-08-27 and is ASKED FOR before it is spent.

Champion pin unchanged — a tie does not displace a pin, and defending a pin costs no slot. Recorded in comp/board.jsonl and comp/SUBMISSIONS.md.

title: The late-training decline may be the SCHEDULE, not memorisation — one_cycle's anneal has never been varied
description:
THE EVIDENCE IS A TALLY, NOT ONE ARM. The project's standing diagnosis is that the peak-to-finish decline
(band_dense_long: peak at epoch 6 of 24, -0.0182 to the end, 2.9x the 0.0062 floor) is memorisation of the
(study,label) pair. Three independent perturbations aimed squarely at that mechanism have now left the
quantity invariant:

  half_data   halve the training studies (example COUNT)      decline -0.0169 vs control -0.0182
  aug_long    intensity block on (example APPEARANCE)          decline -0.0169 vs control -0.0182
