CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT: model.py drops well under 750, the surgery module gets its own mirror tests, and a smoke recipe (`arm_check --smoke`-sized, 60 studies 1 epoch) trains and reports the same `applied()` dict — landed.py reads that dict to assert a flag actually fired, so it is the one output that proves the surgery still runs rather than merely imports.

title: TrainingOptions is a 666-line god-config with 55 flags and six disjoint responsibilities
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25. kneemri/training/options.py: 666 lines, 55 add_argument calls, LCOM4 = 6 - the
highest in the tree by a factor of 1.5 (next is CropAlignment at 4). The cohesion detector names the six
components itself, so the seams do not need to be invented:

  {band, crop, reading} · {routing} · {cache} · {supervision} · {sampled} · {thinned}

Six groups sharing one class means every consumer of one flag imports all fifty-five, and every new arm
flag lands in the same file regardless of what it configures. It is also the reason the arm scripts pass
long undifferentiated flag strings that arm_check then has to re-parse to price.

PROPOSAL: keep TrainingOptions as the composition root, move each component to its own frozen dataclass
beside its consumer (per the repo rule that a supplementary type lives beside its producer, not in a
types bucket). The parser stays one parser - what splits is the STATE, not the CLI surface.

CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT: every arm script in experiments/arms/ must produce a byte-identical
invocation before and after, and arm_check --switches must report the same switch set. That is the
equality check; without it this is a rewrite with a chance of silently dropping a flag, and a dropped
flag is a run that reads as a fact about an architecture.
notes:
AUDITED AND PARTLY REFUSED 2026-08-25 (e2e7f7f).

The proposal in this bead - nest each cohesion component into its own dataclass - is REFUSED, and the
refusal is the finding. `TrainingOptions.parse` is `cls(**vars(parser().parse_args()))`, so argparse's
dest names and this dataclass's field names are one set. FIVE separate guards walk that set FLAT, each
against a defect that already happened:

  switch_coverage.py:80,84   - proves no flag is left unarmed by every arm
  landed.py:315,322          - proves no write-off names a flag TrainingOptions no longer has
  tests/integration/argv_to_checkpoint.py:495 - proves every declared field is READ by a run
  tests/unit/kneemri/training/options.py:103  - asserts dests == field names, exactly
  tests/unit/kneemri/runs/member_record.py:144 - a new field lands in exactly one of three places

Nesting makes all five recurse. That is MORE code guarding the same defects, which is the opposite of
what this bead wanted. And the split it asks for already exists in the shape this repo chose: crop,
band, reading, routing and supervision are each scalar fields plus a grouping property.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and is now fixed: `sampled` and `thinned`. Two numpy methods on a config
object, called from exactly one place, taking and returning exactly the tuple `ReportFolds.holdout`
produces. They are the next two steps of the SPLIT, not a statement about a recipe. Moved to
`core/data/corpus/folds.py` as `FitPositions`, together with the two disclaimers train.py spelled out
inline (`caveats`). options.py no longer imports numpy at all.

WHY LCOM4 WENT 6 -> 5 AND NOT 6 -> 4: the new `positions` property is itself a component, exactly as
crop/band/routing are. LCOM4 on this class is MEASURING THE ACCEPTED PATTERN, not a defect - it cannot
drop below about 5 while scalar-fields-plus-grouping-property stands, and driving it lower means
nesting. Do not chase that number here.

The equality constraint this bead asked for was met: the field set is byte-identical at 63 either side,
so every arm invocation and every switch the coverage walk reports are unchanged.

REMAINING, IF ANYTHING: the file is ~625 lines of which the large majority is argparse help text - i.e.
documentation, and the most valuable thing in it. Each field's default is spelled in two homes (the
dataclass and the flag), but that drift is already caught totally by options.py test_defaults, which
asserts whole-object equality. Generating the parser from the fields would remove ~55 duplicated
defaults at the cost of a reflection machine and would have to re-home the help text anyway. Not worth
it. Closing.

title: 68 CLI entrypoints hand-roll the same six-line preamble; ~300 lines of it are pure duplication
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 over kneemri/ + core/ (163 modules, 36.9k lines):

  ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)   55 modules
  logging.basicConfig(...)              60 modules
  --paths default paths.yaml            45 modules
  DataRoot.from_config(arguments.paths) 45 modules
  if __name__ == '__main__': main()     61 modules
  'for line in X.report(...): logger.info(line)'  24 modules
  add_argument calls, total             308

Three read in full (core/data/corpus/band_coverage.py, kneemri/evaluation/label_stability.py,
kneemri/evaluation/paired_floor.py) open with the SAME five statements in the same order before any
module-specific line appears. That is not a coincidence of style: it is the repo's only CLI contract,
written out 45-60 times instead of once, and it is why main() is the complexity hotspot in the tree
(arm_check.main CC 21, report_prices 14, slot_ties.main 13, mount_check.main 12).

There is NO shared CLI helper today. kneemri/commands.py is an index GENERATOR (it parses modules for a
top-level main and rewrites kneemri/README.md); it does not run anything.

PROPOSAL: core/cli.py holding the contract once - the parser seeded from __doc__, --paths declared once,
logging configured once, DataRoot resolved once, and a report(lines) sink for the 24 modules that print a
line iterator. A module then declares only its own arguments and its body.

THE RISK, stated up front so the work is judged on it: a CLI framework trades explicit lines for
indirection, and a bad one makes every entrypoint harder to read than the six lines it replaced. The bar
is that a module using it must be SHORTER and no less obvious, and that argparse stays visible rather
than being wrapped in a decorator DSL. If the first three ports do not read better, the finding stands
and the framework does not.

Do NOT port all 68 in one commit. Port three (one per package), measure the delta, then decide.
notes:
36 entrypoints ported to core.cli.Command in 519a396 (91 lines net, argparse leaves 30 modules) and 18 report loops collapsed to command.report in aa12a10. Every ported entrypoint smoked with --help and answers with --paths in its options. Three modules built their logger inside main() below where the preamble needs it; the definition moved up. STILL HAND-ROLLED, deliberately, each for a different reason worth its own read: arm_check (no --paths in the preamble block), label_probe and protocol_prior (statements between parse_args and basicConfig), run_comparison, holdout_backfill, teacher_readings (no canonical ArgumentParser line). Six left of 42.
41 of 42 ported (c7f5ca0). Only arm_check left, and DELIBERATELY: its parser has no --paths (an arm's paths travel inside TrainingOptions) and Command always adds one, so porting it would add a dead flag. That one belongs to knee-eydz.

title: Rigid test-time views on the shipping roster — the last unmeasured serving axis
description: Serving.views has never been exercised on any roster we would ship. votefit's log reads 'views=identity only (default)', and that default has held for every board entry on the all-data roster. The only three attempts (kneemri-views, topviews, rateviews) rode two- and four-member fold-0 rosters from before the all-data era, and kneemri-views came back COMPLETE with a BLANK public score from a warp OOM that WARP_CHUNK=512 has since fixed. kneemri-jitterfit (pushed 2026-08-25) serves dark6's identical six under SpatialViews(degrees=(0.0,-6.0)) with RankAverage and overlap=False held, so the single variable is the view set. Two views not three: six members at 3x forward is 18 member-passes against the 9h ceiling that 2 members at 3x once failed to clear. HAZARD: Ensemble.mitigate gives up views FIRST on a projected overrun, so a long run degrades silently into dark6 and reads 0.937 for an unrelated reason. The free run must be checked for the absence of a 'giving up test-time views' line BEFORE any slot is spent. Pre-registered against dark6 0.937: >=0.940 members are pose-brittle, license the third view and serve everything under views; 0.935-0.939 flat, both serving axes closed on board numbers and nothing serving-shaped remains; <=0.934 the warp destroys information at slice edges, retire TTA on this pool.
notes:
PRECONDITION CLEARED 2026-08-25 12:14Z, no slot and no card spent. Pulled the completed free run with `kaggle kernels output dimiturnt/kneemri-jitterfit` (note the owner is dimiturnt, not dimiturtrz - the wrong slug returns a 'Permission kernels.get was denied' that reads like a private-notebook problem and is not one).

The log answers the hazard this bead raised:

  loaded and fingerprint-checked 6 of 6 members
  overlap=False requested, INERT - all 6 members are whole-stack
  serving: vote=RankAverage (default) views=SpatialViews(degrees=(0.0, -6.0), shifts=((0.0, 0.0),)) precision=each member's own (default)

and `grep -ic 'giving up'` over the whole log returns 0. Ensemble.mitigate never fired, so this entry did NOT degrade into dark6, and a score from it would be a reading of the view set rather than of an unrelated budget event. Status is COMPLETE and the run converted its notebook normally, so it did not die late either.

The single variable against dark6 (0.937) is intact: identical six members, RankAverage held, overlap held and inert, views the only difference. The pre-registration stands as written - >=0.940 means members are pose-brittle, 0.935-0.939 means flat and both serving axes close, <=0.934 means the warp destroys information at slice edges.

What the free run CANNOT give: submission.csv holds three studies plus a header, the public stub a non-submitted run sees, so there is no score to read here. This still needs a real slot. Five were spent today and the reset is 00:00 UTC.

One observation for whoever reads the scores: every value in the stub is a twelfth (0.0833, 0.25, 0.9167), which is RankAverage over six members behaving exactly as it should on three rows - not a defect.
close_reason: jitterfit_v1 (ref 55782226) read 0.937 on the board: votefit's identical six served through SpatialViews(0,-6). Same digit as dark6's 0.937, inside the pre-registered 0.935-0.939 FLAT band. Both live directions refuted at once: >=0.940 (members pose-brittle, view averaging buys variance reduction) did not happen, and <=0.934 (the rigid warp destroys slice-edge information) did not happen either. Rigid test-time views are neither a lever nor a hazard at this amplitude. The last unmeasured serving axis is now measured and inert; remaining board levers are member quality and supervision. Recorded in comp/board.jsonl and comp/SUBMISSIONS.md.

title: [bug] witness_check reported 22 of 40 members and was silent about the 18 it skipped, all seven shipped members among them
description:
RUN 2026-08-25 02:11-02:26Z, comp/witness_check.py --device cpu over the whole package. It printed 20 'ok' and 2 'UNVERIFIED - no witness'. The manifest holds 40. The other 18 produced NO line of any kind.

The 18 unreported: aprior_dense_s2026, base_dense_ff, calib_span_ff, crop80_span_s2026, final_ws_e12, focal_dense_s2026, grade_ladder_ff, lr4e-5_ws_ff, margin_seat_s2026, severity_weight_s2026, sided_pool_s2026, small_accum_s2026, small_batch6_ff, small_batch6_s2026, through_dense_ff, through_dense_s2026, v3base_dense_s2026, vjepa_warm_s2026.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A COSMETIC GAP. That list contains ALL SEVEN all-data --fold -1 members, and those are the only members on the last four board entries (dark6, dark7, farseat, and the armed votefit). It also contains vjepa_warm_s2026, submitted in farseat 40 minutes before this run, and v3base_dense_s2026, sitting in a PENDING v3seat. CLAUDE.md names witness_check as a pre-submission gate 'which found three defects on first use'. As invoked here it was silent about 45% of the package and about 100% of what has actually shipped.

SUSPECTED CAUSE, and it is MY invocation before it is the tool's: I ran it under 'timeout 900 ... > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT 0"'. That is the exact trap CLAUDE.md documents — the echo's status is what the harness reports, so a timeout kill at member 22 reads back as a clean exit 0. The member loop is unordered with respect to importance, so a truncation lands wherever it lands. VERIFY THIS FIRST: re-run scoped and timed generously (launched 02:27Z as logs/witness_six.log over votefit's six) and see whether they verify at all.

IF THE TRUNCATION EXPLAINS IT, the tool still owns two defects: (1) it prints no per-member progress against a total, so a truncated sweep is indistinguishable from a complete one; (2) it exits without reconciling reported-vs-manifest, which is the same structural hole MountCheck.absent() just closed on mount_check — a per-item loop that cannot state what it did not reach.

IF IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT, then --fold -1 members are being dropped from the loop silently, which is worse: witness_check would be structurally unable to check the only members that ship, and knee-52mu (a --fold -1 member taking its witness from a holdout it does not have) would be only half-fixed — reporting UNVERIFIED for two members while dropping seven.

FIX EITHER WAY: reconcile the loop against the manifest and fail loudly on any member that produced no verdict, so 'checked' means 'checked all of them'.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-25 02:37Z, and it is BOTH branches, not one.

BRANCH A (my invocation) CONFIRMED. The task output's first line is `EXIT 124` — the 900 s timeout killed it at member 22 of 40, and my `; echo "EXIT $?"` reported the echo. So the 18-member silence was mine. The tool still owns the two defects that made it invisible: no progress-against-total, and no reconcile of reported-vs-manifest at exit. A cut sweep must not be indistinguishable from a complete one.

BRANCH B (the --fold -1 hole) ALSO CONFIRMED, and it is the P0 half. Re-ran scoped to votefit's six all-data members (logs/witness_six.log, 3000 s cap, ran to completion):

    final_ws_e12:     UNVERIFIED - no witness
    calib_span_ff:    UNVERIFIED - no witness
    grade_ladder_ff:  UNVERIFIED - no witness
    through_dense_ff: UNVERIFIED - no witness
    lr4e-5_ws_ff:     UNVERIFIED - no witness
    base_dense_ff:    UNVERIFIED - no witness
    0 ok, 6 unverified, 0 refused

So knee-52mu is NOT fixed, it is only DIAGNOSED. Every --fold -1 member still fails to record a witness, because the witness is taken from a holdout the member does not have. And --fold -1 members are 100 percent of what ships: dark6, dark7, allfit, lastseat, farseat and the armed votefit are all six-or-seven all-data rosters. The pre-submission gate CLAUDE.md describes as having 'found three defects on first use' is a NO-OP over every roster this project has put on the board since 2026-08-24.

THE FIX IS NOT 'skip them'. A witness only needs studies whose predictions can be compared between the fitting process and the serving process; it does not need HELD-OUT studies. Nothing about the check is a generalisation measurement. For --fold -1, take the witness from a fixed, seeded slice of the TRAIN studies. Same comparison, same tolerance, same meaning: does inference read this checkpoint the way training wrote it.

Splitting this bead: A (reconcile-and-fail-loudly) stays here; B gets its own P0.
CORRECTION 2026-08-25 02:40Z, to my own note above. Branch B is WRONGLY STATED there and the wrong version must not be the one that survives.

witness_check is NOT structurally unable to witness a --fold -1 member. The fix already landed, at kneemri/training/fitting.py:172-176: when `predicted is None` the witness is taken from `fold.training[:WITNESS_STUDIES]` and replayed through Trainer.predict. Seen studies, on purpose — the witness pins the READING (image size, slot list, decode resolution, window, precision), and a memorised study exposes a consumer-side default disagreeing with a recorded value exactly as well as an unseen one.

So the six all-data members read UNVERIFIED for a TEMPORAL reason, not a structural one: they were fitted before 2026-08-24. Re-fitting them to earn a witness costs roughly seven card-hours and buys nothing, because their reading is already proven end-to-end by a stronger instrument than the witness — dark6, dark7, allfit and lastseat are four board entries built from exactly those six members, all four reading 0.937. A member that serves wrong does not land on a plateau with three siblings; weakseven demonstrates the board resolves member quality at twenty-nine points. NOT re-fitting is the decision, and it is recorded rather than left implicit.

That leaves only branch A as a real defect, and it is FIXED in this commit. comp/witness_check.py now logs 'checking N members' before the loop and indexes every verdict '[i/N]', so a run cut by a timeout says so in its own log instead of looking like a complete one. A reconcile against the loop's own membership raises SystemExit on any member that produced no verdict — unreachable while the loop is exhaustive, kept so that 'checked' is arithmetic rather than a property a later edit is trusted to preserve.

Closing on the fix. The UNVERIFIED-for-all-data-members state is expected and documented, not open work.

title: sided_tissue: sided pooling on an anatomically centred crop, the suspect sided_pool's row named and did not clear
description:
sided_pool read 0.8561 vs band_dense 0.8578, middle band, three side-defined targets moved a mean of -0.0004 with every interval spanning zero. Its ledger row verified the mechanism FIRED (head.proj.1.weight is (256,1152)=384x3 parts) and then named one live alternative to 'the idea is wrong': the config reads centre=image, crop_mm 130, so the centre column of the patch grid is the anatomical midline only if the crop is anatomically centred.

sided_tissue is that test: sided_pool's exact recipe plus --centre tissue. Fold 0, so the per-label columns can be read.

PRICE: ~75 min card + an UNDECODED cache axis (336px_20sl_tissue_0.1-0.9band) whose build cost is being measured before the arm is queued. Zero submission slots.

THE CONFOUND IS PARTIAL AND MEASURED: crop_centre.py has tissue-centroid-vs-image-centre at median 7mm, p90 18mm, max 32mm over 60 studies. Against a 130mm crop the half-width is 65mm, so the median study is off by 11% of a half. That blurs the worst tenth, it does not destroy the median split. Honest prediction is a partial recovery of a small effect. The 0.8500-0.8579 band (flat) is pre-registered as the most likely outcome.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE CARD ANYWAY: the pot is the largest lever written down in this repo and the only one clearing the 1.5% bar. 2026-08-14_the-ruler-was-five-times-too-small measures the four weakest labels over the full corpus (Lateral Meniscus 0.7981, PF OA 0.8165, MCL 0.8166, Lateral OA 0.8215) and prices lifting them to 0.87 at +0.0189 on the twelve-label mean. Three of the four are side-defined.

AND IT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: dark6 read 0.937 with six all-data members and nothing else, tying allfit/lastseat which are those six plus a seventh, so the marginal member is inert and ensembling is saturated. Per-label profiles correlate +0.92 within a fold, so every member is weak on the same labels and no vote can fix a deficit they all share. It has to be trained out.

NOT TRIED, on policy: the small-weight side regulariser side_dense deferred to 'a head that sees position'. That is loss-engineering aimed at a named weakness.
notes:
PRICE: ~75 min of card plus a one-off cache build on the undecoded axis 336px_20sl_tissue_0.1-0.9band, and ZERO submission slots. P(clears the 1.5% bar on the twelve-label mean) ~ 0.05. P(the three side-defined columns move together by more than their intervals) ~ 0.25 — that is the reading this arm is actually bought for, and the pre-registration's most likely band is the flat one.
KILLED BEFORE RUNNING, on arithmetic over measurements the repo already had — and this is the reason to state the price out loud before starting.

The full price was not the ~75 min of training. sided_tissue lands on the undecoded reading axis 336px_20sl_tissue_0.1-0.9band, and experiments/README.md records a full cache build at about TWO HOURS. Real price ~3.25 h of card.

That forced the question of whether the suspect is even large enough to be the explanation, and it is not:

  336 px at ViT patch 14 = 24 patch columns, 12 per half, across a 130 mm crop = 5.4 mm per column.
  crop_centre.py measured the tissue centroid against the image centre over 60 studies at median 7 mm,
  p90 18 mm, max 32 mm. That is 1.3 columns at the median and 3.3 at p90.
  Contamination of each half is 1.3/12 = 11%, and a difference-of-means contrast attenuates by (1-2c),
  so about 78% of the true contrast survives for the median study and about 56% for the p90 study.

A confound that preserves 70-78% of the signal cannot flatten a real effect to -0.0004 with all three side-defined intervals spanning zero. So the image-centred crop is NOT why sided_pool read flat.

WHAT THIS PROMOTES: sided_pool's own reading stands, and it is stronger than its row claimed. Its docstring argued that a flat result is informative here in a way other pooling arms' were not, because the halves partition the grid so the head could form the patch mean and ADDITIONALLY the difference - one extra part, nothing removed. The head could have ignored the split and did. With the crop suspect now quantitatively excluded, head-sees-position is REFUTED AT HALVES on this data rather than merely unconfirmed.

WHAT IT DOES NOT KILL: the finer grid (quadrants / compartment columns) rests on the same premise that just failed at halves, so it needs a NEW argument rather than a rerun. And it says nothing about the +0.0189 four-weak-label pot itself, which stays the largest lever in the repo and now has one fewer approach.

The arm script and its cache smoke are kept - the smoke wrote the truncated cache and read ok sided_tissue, 0 refused, so the axis is proven decodable if a later argument wants it.

title: mount_check --live reads only the first page of the members dataset, so it refuses valid kernels
description:
mount_check --live refused nearly every kernel in the tree tonight, including kneemri-allfit, whose members produced a COMPLETE 0.937 board entry earlier the same day. The refusals named members the LIVE dataset supposedly does not hold.

The dataset holds them. 'kaggle datasets files dimiturnt/kneemri-members' returns ~20 entries against 38 members because 20 is the CLI default page size; with --page-size 200 all 38 appear, small_batch6_ff included. The live check is comparing kernel tuples against page one of a paginated listing, so any member sorting past the first page reads as absent.

This is the gate written after the 2026-08-19 incident specifically to be the authoritative one - the local package check was green while Kaggle held something else, so --live was added to ask Kaggle directly. It asks, and then believes a truncated answer.

Two failure directions, and the quiet one is worse. Loud: a correct kernel is refused, which costs a submission window to diagnose (it cost one tonight). Quiet: the pagination happens to include the members a bad kernel names, and the check passes a kernel that should have been refused. A gate that is wrong in both directions is worse than no gate, because it is trusted.

Fix: request the full listing (page size high, or follow the next-page token until exhausted) and assert the returned count against the number of files the local package holds before comparing anything. If the listing cannot be shown to be complete, the check must say UNKNOWN rather than REFUSED.

title: mount_check is silent about a kernel directory that has no kernel-metadata.json
description:
kneemri-dark7 held a .py and no kernel-metadata.json. mount_check walked comp/kernels/ and reported '45 ok, 4 skipped, 1 refused' — dark7 in none of the three buckets, no line at all. It was found by grepping for a kernel that should have REFUSED (its tuple names small_batch6_ff, which the package does not yet hold) and finding no mention of it whatsoever.

A metadata-less directory is not an exotic state: it is exactly the state a kernel is in between being written and being pushed, which is the moment the check is run. Silence there reads as 'nothing to say about it' when the truth is 'this cannot be pushed at all' — push.sh kernel would have failed at the reset window with the slot clock running.

Fix: a directory under comp/kernels/ with a code file and no kernel-metadata.json is a REFUSAL, not an omission. Make the totals line account for every directory walked, so ok+skipped+refused equals the directory count and a missing bucket is arithmetically visible.

title: Add a convergence check to the arm harness: refuse to record a peak that lands on the last epoch run
description:
An audit of every metrics.jsonl on disk (2026-08-24) found 21 runs whose best epoch is at or one before their LAST epoch. Two of them - raddino_dense and vjepa_member - are outright crash readings that entered the ledger as facts about their architectures. A third, cnx_dense, peaked at e11 of 11 with loss still falling and was written up as 'the first non-transformer trunk, weak'; refitting its rate returned +0.0259 and produced a curve that peaks at e6 and DECLINES, which is what convergence looks like.

So the repo has three instances of the same defect and no gate against it, while it has nine gates against shipping defects. The asymmetry is the point: we check hard that a submission will BUILD and not at all that a number is FINISHED.

WHAT THE CHECK IS. After a run, compare the best epoch against the last epoch actually recorded, and against the epochs the recipe ASKED for. Three outcomes:
  - best epoch < last recorded, and last recorded == epochs asked -> CONVERGED, record normally.
  - last recorded < epochs asked -> TRUNCATED. The arm crashed or was killed. Refuse to write the score into the ledger as the recipe's number; label it a floor.
  - best epoch == last recorded == epochs asked -> UNDERTRAINED. The budget bound the result, not the recipe. Flag for a longer run or a fitted rate before the number is quoted.

The one_cycle=True schedule is what makes TRUNCATED distinct from merely short: stopping early stops in the high-LR portion, so the anneal that does the fine convergence never runs. A truncated run is not a shorter version of the same experiment.

Fits beside the existing nine checks (kneemri/experiments/*_check.py) and follows their convention: it guards a failure that has already happened, three times.
notes:
Built and in use: kneemri/experiments/convergence_check.py, documented in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as the check that guards a NUMBER rather than a shipment.

The bead's three outcomes are all in, plus two the build found necessary. STOPPED was added because the check's own FIRST corpus run reported ten truncations, three of which (res392_lr8e-6_ws, focal_pool, calibrated_targets) carry patience=3 and stopped at exactly e10 of 12 - the stopper working, not a kill. One of those is the res392 resolution refutation, so without reading the patience key the check would have re-opened a correctly-closed family. UNSCORED was added for --fold -1 members, which hold nothing back and so have no epoch to peak on.

Only TRUNCATED exits non-zero: an undertrained run is an honest measurement of a budget and its score is real; a truncated one is a crash whose score is a floor. Smokes (a studies cap) and one-epoch throughput probes are excluded - six of the fifteen the first reading reported were timing probes that never produced a member and diluted the actual finding.

Corpus today: 83 runs, 56 converged, 8 truncated, 3 stopped, 9 undertrained, 7 unscored. The three runs this bead was filed over read as filed: raddino_dense TRUNCATED (best e6 of 7 run, 12 asked), vjepa_member TRUNCATED (e9 of 10, 12 asked), cnx_dense UNDERTRAINED (e11 of 12, 12 asked).

title: raddino_dense 0.8137 is a CRASH READING, not RadDINO's score - the run died at epoch 7 of 12
description:
logs/raddino_dense.log and the arm driver both end mid-epoch-7 with 'ARM FAILED raddino_dense (trainer exit 1)'. The full log shows step 248/583 of epoch 7 at 448 img/s with loss still falling, no traceback, no OOM (27.14 GB peak on a 32 GB card). The process was killed externally on 2026-08-23 23:29, during the card-handoff window - it did not fail on its own merits.

The recorded 0.8137 is therefore the AUC at epoch 6 of a 12-epoch schedule, and it entered experiments/README.md as a fact about the RadDINO architecture ('raddino_dense ~0.82 extrapolated', line 2682).

WHY THE TRUNCATION IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT JUST A SHORT RUN. The recipe sets one_cycle=True over 12 epochs. Stopping at 7 stops in the high-LR portion of the schedule, so the anneal - where one-cycle does its fine convergence - never ran. Contrast v3base_dense, which also peaked at e6 but then RAN its remaining five epochs and never beat that peak: that is a converged measurement. RadDINO has no such evidence.

Its own curve (0.7247 0.7439 0.7852 0.7944 0.8000 0.8119 0.8137) is decelerating, so the honest estimate of the remaining gain is modest and uncertain, NOT the naive slope extrapolation.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. RadDINO is pretrained on medical images and is the most pixel-distant trunk in the pool. The champion pin's one surviving selection rule is that a pixel-distant seventh seat did best of five tried (0.932). kneemri-farswap, queued for the 00:00Z reset, tests exactly that hypothesis with a WEAK non-DINOv2 member (lora_r8, 0.8215). If farswap pays, a STRONG RadDINO is the follow-up member and it needs to exist.

COST: kneemri/training/fitted_encoder.py exists precisely for this - it converts a member checkpoint into an encoder another arm can start from, so the finish is a warm start from the e6 .pt rather than 12 epochs from scratch. ~1.65h warm (6 x 993s) vs ~3.3h cold.

DO NOT ARM WHILE THE CARD IS BIOHUB'S. logs/YIELD_CARD is on disk by agreement; gate this on farswap's board number first.

title: Seventh dark member: is the all-data dose saturated at six?
description: Three consecutive board entries (allfit 0.937, lastseat 0.937, augseat 0.936) exchanged the ONE fold-0 seat in a six-dark-plus-one ensemble and moved at most one tick. Seat identity, seat offline quality (a -0.0076 member bought the same number) and seat regularisation are all measured flat. The variable those entries HOLD FIXED is the count of dark members: exactly six exist, so no entry has ever had a seventh to offer, and count-at-fixed-dose and dose-at-fixed-count are the same unmeasured axis. small_batch6_ff converts the best member this project owns (0.8598) - and the exact member that held that seat in lastseat at 0.937, so its fold-0 behaviour in this ensemble is a measured control. Pre-registration lives in experiments/arms/small_batch6_ff.sh against lastseat's 0.937: >=0.939 dose still pays, 0.936-0.938 flat and the full-fit axis is CLOSED with a number instead of an extrapolation, <=0.935 indicts --ema/all-data and the harness is first suspect. Cost ~95 min of otherwise-dead overnight card. NOTE band_dense_long_ff stays unrun: allfit's own board entry pre-registers it null on the sub-linear dose reading, at 24 epochs / 7.3h.
notes:
PRICE: 95 min GPU (12 epochs x ~361 s x 4406/3497), in overnight wall-clock that is otherwise dead. GAIN if the dose still pays: +0.002 to +0.003 on the board, extrapolating the finalfit->allfit step (+0.003 for one seat -> six) onto a curve that has already read sub-linear. P(clears the 0.0015 board-resolvable) = 0.3. The ratio only prices as worth running because the wall-clock is free and because the FLAT outcome is itself the deliverable: it closes the only axis that has ever moved this board with a measurement instead of an extrapolation, and it is the prerequisite checkpoint for an eight-member all-dark entry that cannot be built until a seventh dark member exists.

STILL LIVE AFTER THE 2026-08-24 22:12Z GREEDY MEASUREMENT, and it is worth saying why, because that
measurement retired two other beads and looks at first glance like it retires this one too. The greedy
curve is flat within noise from seat 4 to seat 36, so member SELECTION is not a lever. It cannot speak to
this axis at all: greedy ranks members by a HOLDOUT record, and a dark member is fitted at --fold -1 with
no holdout, so no dark member has ever appeared on that curve. Count-of-dark-members is the one variable
every board entry has held fixed, and it stays unmeasured. Arming small_batch6_ff tonight on the freed
card.
RESULT 2026-08-25: dark7 = 0.937 against dark6 0.937. FLAT, the middle band this arm pre-registered, so the all-data dose is SATURATED AT SIX and the full-fit axis closes on a measurement rather than on allfit's sub-linear extrapolation.

The arm did what it was built to do. Its whole case was that COUNT-at-fixed-dose and DOSE-at-fixed-count are the same unmeasured axis and both needed one more _ff checkpoint; the checkpoint now exists and the axis is measured and closed. small_batch6_ff is the best member this project owns and adding it as a seventh all-data member moved the board zero.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the valuable half: this arm's own pre-registration said 'queue the second conversion immediately' ONLY on >= 0.939. 0.937 is not that, so band_dense_long_ff is NOT converted and roughly three hours of card (24 epochs) is not spent. A flat result that spends its own follow-up budget correctly is worth more than the 95 minutes it cost.

WIDER: four board entries now read exactly 0.937 - dark6 (6 dark), dark7 (6+1 dark), allfit and lastseat (6 dark + 1 fold-0). Member count, member identity and the seventh member's fold status all vary across them and the number does not. Recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_the_seventh_seat_is_inert_and_four_slots_measured_it.md.

title: Run an ACTUAL multilingual reader over the reports, locally, and gate it on the 58 annotations
description:
THE ONLY UNRUN SIZED LEVER LEFT. Every other axis is closed on this repo's own measurements: member selection (0/33 append, 0/19 displacement, peak8 board 0.932 under champion 0.937), per-label weighting (oracle ceiling +0.0002), slice depth (2 of 12 clear zero, chance predicts 0.6), slot coverage (extended_slots +0.0002), pooling operator (0.0019 span), SSL-as-init (five collapses), encoder capacity (base_dense 0.8512 vs small 0.8578 at 2.5x the card time), and the cheap severity/confidence proxies (knee-mxj, closed 2026-08-24, both read out backwards).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNRUN. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the-corpus-is-not-english.md sizes it: 33.1% of the corpus carries severity vocabulary the current extraction path cannot see AT ALL, English is 40.1% of reports, and Spanish/Croatian/German/Dutch are 35.1% of reports converting at 1.5/0.0/2.7/2.6 percent. Its own closing line: 'whether better supervision on it clears the 1.5% bar is a training question, unrun.' knee-dbw states the repo runs NO language model at all - report_labels_v2.csv is a consumed rule-engine table whose __conf column is constant per verdict.

WHY IT COMPOUNDS. Our local ruler IS these labels, so a better table raises both what we train on and what we measure with. And the metric is a RANKING metric while severity is a ranking signal, which is the argument knee-mxj made and then could only test through regex proxies over the sentences the reader had already read.

NO CREDENTIAL NEEDED. There is no LLM API key on this machine. Run a multilingual instruct model LOCALLY on the 5090 instead - the HF token exists, the card is ours between arms, and 4,407 reports is a single-digit-GB pass.

THE GATE, BEFORE THE CORPUS PASS. Read only the 58 radiologist-annotated studies first. reader_agreement must beat the incumbent's 65.3%, and ordinal_signal must beat 0.741 mean over 12 labels. Both CLIs already exist and run in seconds. A candidate table is judged before anything is retrained on it.
close_reason: REFUTED before any card time, 2026-08-24. The premise was that report_labels_v2.csv is an English-pattern read leaving 33.1% of the corpus ungraded. Measured the severity spread of the three YES levels (0.68/0.82/0.94) BY REPORT LANGUAGE over all 4,407 studies: en .401/.399/.199, hr .435/.342/.223, es .331/.498/.170, tr .400/.412/.188, el .369/.404/.227, de .481/.326/.193, bg .456/.338/.207, nl .370/.379/.251. Every language grades at essentially the English rate. The table is already a multilingual read and there is no language gap in it to close. What 2026-08-17_the-corpus-is-not-english.md measured was report_language.SEVERITY - OUR English regex - not the labels we train on, so it read the TOOL's blind spot as a property of the DATA, which is the mistake its own Limits section names. Denominator discipline: the rate that matters is over the shipped label table, not over what a regex could locate.

title: Architecture diversity is a tradeoff CURVE, not a closed axis - and every non-DINOv2 trunk was trained on the DINOv2 recipe
description:
Every non-DINOv2 trunk this project has trained was trained on the DINOv2 recipe. Of 202 checkpoints on disk ~189 are DINOv2-family, one is ConvNeXt, one is V-JEPA. Read size, backbone LR, schedule, band, sampling, augmentation, batch and pooling were all tuned across those 189, so the standing recipe is a 189-run local optimum around DINOv2-small. Handing it unchanged to a convolutional trunk measures our tuning and charges the result to the architecture. See knee-zfgn for the count and for the pre-registration cnx_dense overruled.

Owns experiments/arms/cnx_own_recipe.sh: 448 px (a 14x14 grid, the retry cnx_dense itself pre-registered) and --backbone-lr 4e-4 (an order above the ViT adapter rate, and deliberately below ConvNeXtV2 published 6.25e-4 with layer decay), everything else the control.

PRICE: ~2.6 h of card for the arm, plus the smoke that writes the 448 truncated cache. P(clears 1.5% bar) 0.10-0.15. P(confirms the starvation, solo >= 0.83) 0.45-0.55. Justified as an INSTRUMENT first rather than as an improvement: either branch retires the 189:1 confound, which currently sits under every statement this repo makes about encoder diversity, including two answers already given to the owner. A refuting run licenses setting the convolutional family aside with the denominator printed next to it, which nothing today licenses.
notes:
Raised because the owner asked, for at least the second time, whether ensembling DIFFERENT ARCHITECTURES
is the better lever. Both previous answers were given from memory and quoted SOLO SCORES. This one was
measured: every non-DINOv2 trunk with a holdout record, priced against greedy7_v1's seven members on
BOTH rulers, card-free.

  member                trunk                 nearest   solo
  mae_matched           MAE pretraining       0.4333    0.6735
  cnx_dense             ConvNeXt (CNN)        0.7941    0.7927
  vjepa_warm            V-JEPA 3D tubelet     0.8212    0.8337
  lora_r8_v3small       DINOv3 + LoRA         0.8455    0.8217
  dinov3_base_lora      DINOv3 + LoRA         0.8467    0.8268
  v3base_dense          DINOv3 full fine-tune 0.8829    0.8512
  distill_pairs         DINOv2 self-distill   0.9159    0.8594

  roster of 7, its own nearest-neighbour spread: 0.8724 .. 0.8893

THE FINDING. Distance orders EXACTLY by architectural distance from DINOv2, across seven points with no
exception: a different pretraining objective is farthest, then a different inductive bias, then a
different input geometry, then a frozen base of the same family, then a fine-tuned base of the same
family, then the same family distilled from itself. That is not scatter around a mean; it is a curve, and
it is the owner's thesis measured rather than asserted. Architecture diversity does produce genuinely
different orderings here, and the amount scales with how different the architecture is.

THE OTHER HALF, on the SAME seven points. Solo score is monotone in the opposite direction. Farther trunk,
weaker member. Distance and strength are anti-correlated across the entire axis, which is why every
individual arm read as a refutation: each one bought its distance with quality and was judged on quality
alone.

WHAT NOBODY TESTED, and why the axis is not closed. Every non-DINOv2 trunk in that table was trained on
the recipe tuned for DINOv2 - dense sampling, 336, the same schedule and the same learning rate. A CNN
trunk and a tubelet trunk have different optimal read sizes, different LR scales, and in the tubelet case
a different token geometry (prefix_tokens = 0, no class token, no registers). The measured weakness is
therefore confounded with recipe transfer and cannot be charged to the architecture. Faulty TRAINING is
a live suspect and it has never been eliminated on this axis.

So the correct statement is NOT "architecture diversity does not pay" - it is "architecture diversity has
only ever been measured at points where the recipe was wrong for the trunk". No arm has tried to move the
curve; every arm sampled a point on it.

WHAT MOVES IT. Pick the trunk whose distance is largest among those still worth rescuing, and give it its
own recipe rather than DINOv2's. cnx_dense at nearest 0.7941 is 0.078 more distant than any seated member
is from its own nearest neighbour, and it is a CNN, so the knobs that are wrong for it are nameable in
advance rather than searched: read size, LR scale, and the pooling that assumes patch tokens.

BANDS, pre-registered before any number exists:
  solo >= 0.85 with nearest still under 0.82  -> the distant-and-strong member knee-053z asked for, and
      the recipe was the confound all along. Ship it and re-open every trunk in the table.
  solo >= 0.85 with nearest risen above 0.87  -> the recipe bought quality by making it a DINOv2 twin.
      Distance and strength are genuinely exclusive here. Axis closes, correctly this time.
  solo 0.83-0.85                              -> recipe transfer was part of it but not all of it; needs
      a slot, not another offline reading.
  solo still under 0.82                       -> recipe was not the confound. Charge it to the trunk.

Depends on knee-u0my only in ordering, not in logic - u0my tests the same confound one step milder (same
family, different adaptation). This one tests it at the far end of the curve.

CAVEAT that must travel with any use of the distance ruler: it has ONE paired board observation behind it
(the 2026-08-21 split). It is quoted as a RANKING, never as a price.

CORRECTION, same hour, after reading the rows this was filed against (experiments/README.md 1607-1664 and
2532-2544) rather than recalling them.

1. The recipe confound was NOT unnoticed. `raddino_dense` raised it on 2026-08-23: "a new trunk plugged into
   a recipe that was fitted around DINOv3 ... every trunk swap needs its own tuning pass before it can be
   read at all." It was set aside on cost, not refuted. This bead's contribution is the distance measurement,
   not the confound.

2. The knobs named above are wrong for cnx_dense. Read size is dead on three independent readings (equal
   focal/regional deltas to four decimals; `resolution` at 392 scored +0.0002; the 448 retry was explicitly
   killed). Schedule and LR are dead too - the underfit claim was refuted hard enough to retitle knee-9otf.

3. What survives, from the arm's own trajectory: at MATCHED TRAIN LOSS cnx_dense holds 0.7927 at loss 0.8332
   where base_dense holds 0.8371 at loss 0.8456. A 0.044 generalisation gap at EQUAL FIT - it fits better and
   generalises worse. That rules out an under-driven trunk and points at REGULARISATION, which is the one
   knob on this arm nothing has tested. DINOv2's recipe carries generalisation in the pretrained
   representation and so needs little augmentation; a CNN fine-tuned end-to-end from ImageNet weights on
   ~1.5k studies is a different regime.

4. What today's number refutes is a SENTENCE, not a knob: cnx_dense's entry closes with "a different
   inductive bias is not a different error structure. The axis closes." Nearest 0.7941 against a spread
   bottoming at 0.8724 says a different inductive bias produced the MOST different error structure this
   project has. The entry showed it was a WORSE one, which stands; it never showed it was a SIMILAR one, and
   the quality ruler could not have.

REVISED BANDS for the cnx retry - augmentation strength only, everything else at the arm's own settings:
  solo >= 0.84 with nearest still under 0.82 -> regularisation was the confound. Distant-and-strong exists.
  solo >= 0.84 with nearest above 0.87       -> quality was bought by becoming a DINOv2 twin. Axis closes.
  solo 0.80-0.84                             -> partial; needs a slot, not another offline reading.
  solo still under 0.80                      -> charge it to the trunk. Axis closes on the right evidence.
PRICE, added 2026-08-24 because arm_check refused cnx_own_recipe as UNPRICED and it was right to.

COST: ~2.5 h of card for the 12-epoch arm, plus a two-minute 60-study smoke to write the 448 px truncated
cache and price the memory. The seat measurement afterwards is card-free (record_mix over holdout records).
Call it 2.6 h of card, one arm, zero submission slots.

GAIN IF IT LANDS: cnx_dense is the most distant member this project owns — nearest 0.7941 against a seated
roster whose own spread floors at 0.8724, i.e. 0.078 beyond anything seated. The strong-and-distant
quadrant has been empty since the project began and is the only unexhausted cell on the ensemble axis
(seat, vote and count are all measured flat; three board entries on 2026-08-24 read 0.936/0.937/0.936
across single-seat exchanges). A seatable convolutional member is worth more than its own seat value,
because it reopens a FAMILY that currently has one run in it against DINOv2's ~189 (knee-zfgn) — an LR
sweep, augmentation strength and schedule all become live, each decomposed against a member that works.

P(clears the 1.5% bar) — LOW ON THIS ARM ALONE, call it 0.10-0.15, and the arm is not justified on that
number. One seat at seven has never moved the board more than a tick here. What it is justified on is the
OPTION it buys: P(solo clears 0.83, i.e. the starvation is confirmed and the family earns a budget) is
much higher, call it 0.45-0.55 — two corrections argued from the architecture, against a baseline that ran
at a fifth of the slot head's fitted spatial support and at a ViT adapter's learning rate.

SO IT IS AN INSTRUMENT FIRST AND A MEMBER SECOND, and it must be read that way. It retires a suspicion —
that 'encoder diversity is closed' was a measurement of our own tuning — and it either licenses re-running
the whole trunk axis at a fair budget or closes it with the denominator finally printed. A refutation here
is worth nearly as much as a confirmation, which is what makes 2.6 h the right price: the alternative is
carrying an unfalsified 189:1 confound through every future ensemble decision.

RATIO AGAINST THE STANDING ALTERNATIVE. NCL (knee-2f0q) is ~1.3 h and attacks the same empty quadrant from
the strong side. It ranks BELOW this one now, not on expected member quality but because it inherits the
same recipe and therefore cannot test the confound. Fixing the measurement comes before adding to it.
2026-08-24, EXTERNAL EVIDENCE FOR THE TRUNK HALF, gathered after the 189:1 count.

Three consecutive RSNA Kaggle first-place solutions on 3D volumes name their backbone, and none of them is a ViT:
  2022 cervical spine - EfficientNet-V2-S or ConvNeXt.
  2023 abdominal trauma - CoaT Lite or EfficientNet-V2-S.
  2024 lumbar spine - ConvNeXt-S or EfficientNet-V2-S.
Convolutional or hybrid trunks win this competition series three years running, on volumetric medical data, at Kaggle scale. That is not proof they beat DINOv2 here, but it removes the reading that our one 0.7927 ConvNeXt run reflects the family. It is the same trunk family that took three of these, run once, on a recipe fitted to something else.

EfficientNet-V2-S has NEVER been tried in this repo - it is not in backbone.py's variant table at all, despite appearing in all three winning solutions. That is a second starved trunk sitting behind the first, and it is CHEAP relative to ConvNeXtV2-base (87.7M): V2-S is ~21M and gradient-checkpointable, so it prices in well under cnx_own_recipe's memory bill.

Both winners' solutions also pair the trunk with a SEQUENCE head over slices, which is knee-blvm. The two are independent - do not confound them in one arm. cnx_own_recipe tests the recipe confound on the trunk axis alone and should finish before a trunk-plus-head arm is designed.
PRICE (2026-08-24 17:45Z) — WALL-CLOCK / EXPECTED GAIN

COST: ~3.0-3.5 h card. cnx_dense measured 519-727 s/epoch at train-size 352; this arm runs 448
(1.62x the pixels) for 12 epochs. The earlier '~2.5 h' estimate did not scale for resolution.
CHEAP KILL AT ~1.2 h: cnx_dense read 0.7659 / 0.7681 at epochs 3 / 4. With a 10x backbone LR the
curve must be clearly above that by epoch 4 or the mechanism did not fire; kill there, not at 12.

MECHANISM (corrected today — the ledger's stated suspect was wrong):
The architecture section names augmentation strength as 'the one knob on this arm that nothing has
tested', reasoning from a 0.044 generalisation gap at matched train loss (cnx_dense 0.7927 at loss
0.8332 vs base_dense 0.8371 at loss 0.8456) — read as a regularisation regime that does not transfer.
logs/cnx_dense.log refutes that reading. Its holdout is MONOTONE RISING to the final epoch:
  e0 0.7050 -> e6 0.7858 -> e8 0.7921 -> e10 0.7927 -> e11 0.7927, train loss still falling steeply.
No turnover in 12 epochs. That is an UNDER-TRAINED curve, not an over-fitted one. The matched-loss
comparison holds two different points on two different trajectories side by side; it shows ConvNeXt
converts loss into AUC more slowly, not that it overfits. Adding --intensity-aug would slow a model
that never finished climbing. The arm is therefore left EXACTLY as written: backbone-lr 4e-5 -> 4e-4
is the standard fix for a monotone-rising fine-tune, and it is the one this arm already carries.

GAIN: the prize is the strong-and-distant cell, which margin_seat just proved pays. cnx_dense sits at
nearest-neighbour 0.7941 against a roster whose most distant SEATED member reads 0.8724 — 0.078
outside the spread, the largest of any member that did not collapse, i.e. the most different error
structure in this project. It is unseated only because it is weak (solo 0.7927, greedy 63rd of 65).
margin_seat took 2nd of 65 from nearest 0.8628. A member 0.06-0.08 MORE distant at comparable quality
is plausibly worth more than margin_seat's seat, and no other live lever offers that much distance.

ODDS: ~40% it reaches usable quality (0.84+). The trajectory says the headroom exists and the LR is
the conventional lever, but 10x is a large step and may destabilise instead. ~50% that a usable
member then takes a seat, given the distance it starts from. So ~20% for a seat-grade member at
~3 h, with the kill at 1.2 h capping the loss on the other 80%.

VERDICT: run it. Best available ratio, our own data, no licence blocker, and it is the unrun
architecture plan rather than a fourth exchange of an already-null axis.

ATTRIBUTION LIMIT, stated up front: this arm varies THREE things against cnx_dense (LR 10x,
352->448, batch 2/accum 3 -> batch 1/accum 6 at equal effective batch 6). If it works we will not
know which knob did it without an ablation. That is deliberate stage-gating — at the finding stage
the question is whether ConvNeXt reaches usable quality AT ALL, and isolating three knobs costs
~9 h to answer a question worth asking only after the answer is yes.

BAR REPLACED 2026-08-24 18:15Z, by knee-98y2. The pre-registered test written yesterday was
"~0.85 solo to be a candidate, then peak8 + it > 0.8731". That bar is now known to be a test
NOTHING passes: 33 candidates spanning solo 0.79-0.857 and nearest 0.769-0.951 all land below
0.8731, and 12 of them also fail an exhaustive single-swap against the peak. A bar with a 0/33
pass rate prices no member.

REPLACEMENT - DISPLACEMENT TEST. When cnx_own_recipe finishes, put its holdout record into the
FULL pool and re-run the greedy from scratch:
  record_mix --records <full pool + cnx_own_recipe> --seats greedy
KEEP if the new peak > 0.8731. Solo AUC is no longer a gate at any value - a member that cannot
append can still rebuild the set around itself, and that is the only remaining way in.

This also retires the epoch-4 solo-AUC kill checkpoint. There is nothing a mid-run solo number can
decide any more; the run goes to completion (~21:05Z) or dies on a failure signature.

TRAJECTORY SO FAR. epoch 0: loss 0.6218 / holdout 0.7314 / 970s, against cnx_dense's epoch 0
loss 1.2612 / 0.7050 / 519s. The 10x LR fired: half the loss, +0.026 AUC, and NOT collapsed to the
prior (that would read ~0.5). But half the loss for a quarter of the gain is the same conversion
pathology cnx_dense showed, now at higher fit. 970s/epoch x 12 = 3.2h.
epoch 1: loss 0.6132 holdout 0.7394 (922s). Loss essentially flat from epoch 0 (-0.0086) while AUC gains 0.008 - near its loss floor at epoch 1 with AUC at 0.739, where cnx_dense still had 0.43 of loss headroom. One-cycle anneal can still produce a late jump. No mid-run kill under the displacement bar; runs to ~21:05Z.
2026-08-25, discussion topic 735826 via kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read - an OUTSIDE controlled comparison on the same competition data, and it points the same way this bead does.

A competitor froze their CPU preprocessing as a control (all 4,407 studies to a fixed (4407, 6, 9, 224, 224) uint8 cache) and changed ONLY the representation side:
  - pretrained ResNet34 pipeline: OOF BCE ~0.664
  - pretrained DINOv2-Small with diagnosis-specific slot attention, same cache and same labels: OOF BCE ~0.674 (rank correlation ~0.391)
i.e. moving to DINOv2 made it WORSE on their harness. Their conclusion: 'compute cost and model size are poor proxies for useful information; a more expensive model can simply process the same imperfect input more expensively.' The thread's opening post reports the same pattern from several people - single DINO models reach ~0.91-0.92, and increasing encoder size does not improve CV (which is knee-7u5's finding from outside, and knee-155's +0.0011 scaling result from outside).

CAVEATS BEFORE THIS IS USED AS EVIDENCE FOR A TRUNK SWAP: their DINOv2 arm carries a slot-attention head we do not run, so trunk and head moved together; BCE is not our metric; and their ResNet34 recipe is presumably the one they tuned. It does NOT show ResNet34 beats DINOv2. What it does show is that a serious competitor got a NON-DINOv2 trunk to a competitive number on this exact corpus, which is the premise this bead was blocked on - our own non-DINOv2 trunks were starved 189:1 (knee-zfgn), so we have never made that comparison at parity either.

title: LoRA-v3 at the dense recipe and 336 — the distant-and-strong cell nobody ran, and the v3 axis was closed on the wrong member
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-24, card-free, against the CURRENT roster of seven (greedy7_v1, 0.933):

  roster's own nearest-neighbour spread: 0.8724 (most distant seated, calib_span) .. 0.8893 (worst)

  candidate            seat      nearest   solo
  lora_r8_v3small_224  -0.0013   0.8455    0.8217
  dinov3_base_lora     -0.0009   0.8467    0.8268
  v3base_dense         -0.0006   0.8829    0.8512

THE TWO LoRA-v3 MEMBERS ARE MORE DISTANT FROM THIS ROSTER THAN ANY SEATED MEMBER IS FROM ITS OWN NEAREST NEIGHBOUR, by 0.027. By member_distance.py's own stated rule that is 'genuinely new information'.

WHY THIS WAS MISSED, and it is a reasoning error not a measurement one. The v3 axis was closed on 2026-08-21 with the verdict 'a second ViT of a different family does not buy a second diversity seat'. That verdict was reached: (a) on v3base_dense, which this reading shows is the ONE v3 member that is NOT distant — 0.8829 sits inside the roster's own spread; (b) against a roster of FIVE (basedense_v1, 0.8690) that no longer exists, now seven with two members changed; (c) using the QUALITY ruler alone, on the same day MemberDistance was built to answer exactly this question, and never re-read with it. The ledger's own text already warned about (b)/(c): 'The -0.0007 is not evidence that a v3base seat would cost a tick; it is evidence that this ruler cannot tell.' The caveat was written and then the verdict was quoted without it.

THE MECHANISM FOR THE DISTANCE. LoRA freezes the base, so the member keeps DINOv3's representation instead of being fine-tuned toward the solution every other member converges on. That is a reason for a member to disagree, and it predicts exactly the ordering measured: both LoRA members distant, the full fine-tune ordinary. The ledger read the same pair as an ADAPTATION finding ('DINOv3 is weak was an adaptation finding wearing an encoder name', v3base_dense +0.0187 over its LoRA sibling) and was right about quality — but the adaptation that scores WORSE is the one that is DISTANT, and nothing charged that to diversity.

THE UNISOLATED VARIABLE, which is what makes this runnable. v3base_dense and dinov3_base_lora differ on TWO things: LoRA-vs-full-FT, AND 224 -> 336 plus the dense recipe. The +0.0244 was charged entirely to adaptation. base_dense -> v3base_dense shows what the dense recipe alone is worth on this trunk. NOBODY HAS RUN LoRA + DENSE RECIPE + 336.

THE ARM: dinov3_base_lora's LoRA config at v3base_dense's read, slices, band and schedule. Cheaper than full FT (base frozen, no backbone grads) against v3base_dense's 680 s/epoch; budget ~1.5 h for 12 epochs.

PRE-REGISTERED, before any number exists:
 - solo >= 0.85 AND nearest < 0.88 -> the distant-and-strong member knee-053z asked for. This is the seat. Ship it.
 - solo >= 0.85 AND nearest >= 0.88 -> the recipe bought quality by making it a twin. That is the whole trade and it fails; the v3 axis really is closed and this time on the right member.
 - solo < 0.84 with nearest still ~0.85 -> distant-and-weak, same as vjepa_warm. LoRA's distance is real and unusable; stop paying for it.
 - solo 0.84-0.85 -> the split is genuine and the seat needs a slot to settle, not another offline reading.

BLOCKED ON THE CARD ONLY: margin_seat then dissent_seat own it to ~17:30Z. Ranks above knee-3ped (V-JEPA larger read): same distance argument, cheaper arm, and the weakness here has a NAMED cause rather than a suspected ceiling.
notes:
PRICE (2026-08-24, required by arm_check's UNPRICED clause and by CLAUDE.md's wall-clock-over-gain rule).

COST: ~2.2-2.6 h of card. `v3base_dense` ran ~750-850 s/epoch over 12 epochs on this exact recipe and
encoder; LoRA removes the optimiser state and the weight gradients but the backward still traverses the
whole trunk to reach the early adapters, so expect a modest step-time saving, not a large one. Note this
CORRECTS an earlier verbal estimate of ~40 min, which came from `dinov3_base_lora`'s 224 px / 12 slices /
batch 12 shape. This arm runs the DENSE recipe - 336 px, 20 slices, batch 6 - which is where the cost is.

GAIN IF IT LANDS: a member 0.027 outside the roster's own nearest-neighbour spread that is also strong
enough to seat. No member the project holds is both. `raddino_dense`'s entry states why that is the thing
worth buying: the greedy curve peaks at seats 8-10 and declines after, so the ensemble does not want
another member - it wants one that does something none of the existing ones can. Plausible board size is
one to two ticks, i.e. roughly +0.001 to +0.004. That is UNDER the owner's 1.5% bar on its own and is not
sold as clearing it; it composes against the original baseline and, more importantly, it is an INSTRUMENT
- it decides whether distance and strength can coexist on this data at all, which licenses or retires the
entire architecture axis (knee-y59c, knee-053z, the cnx retry) behind one reading.

P(CLEARS +0.0015 SEAT VALUE): call it 0.25-0.35. The anti-correlation between distance and strength held
across all seven measured points, which is the honest reason to price it low. What argues the other way is
that no point on that curve was ever measured with the recipe matched to the trunk, and this is the
cheapest place to test that - same encoder family, same recipe, one regime moved.

RATIO: ~2.4 h for a ~30% shot at a small board gain plus a near-certain axis verdict either way. The axis
verdict is what justifies it, not the tick. Ranked ABOVE the cnx regularisation retry (knee-y59c, similar
2-3 h) because it is a strict single-variable isolation against a control we already hold at 0.8512,
whereas the cnx retry has to search an augmentation setting with no matched control at the new setting.
Both were mispriced relative to each other in conversation when this one was quoted at 40 min; on the
corrected numbers the ordering survives on MERIT rather than on cost.

PRICE: ~2.4 h of card (12 epochs at ~750-850 s, LoRA trims the backward modestly) for a seat that no
existing member can occupy - distant AND strong - plus a near-certain verdict on whether those two can
coexist on this data at all, which licenses or retires knee-y59c, knee-053z and the cnx retry behind one
reading. P(clears +0.0015 seat value) ~ 0.30: low because distance and strength were anti-correlated
across all seven measured trunks, and not lower because no point on that curve was ever measured with the
recipe matched to the trunk, which is exactly what this arm moves. The axis verdict is what buys the card,
not the tick.
2026-08-25 14:24Z — ARM LAUNCHED AND KILLED AT STEP 85, NOT RUN. The number does not exist and this bead stays open as untried.

Two real defects were found and FIXED before it ever started, and both are worth keeping: the arm's VRAM paragraph was wrong (LoRA does not cut activation memory — the backward still traverses all 72 layers to reach the early adapters, so every trunk activation is held and the adapters add their own; memory here is bought by token count, not parameter count), and it OOMed at the default cap. --eager-encoder took allocated 25.75 -> 22.53 GiB and --vram-gb 29.5 made it fit. The smoke then passed clean (0.5269 over 11 of 12 labels, 189 s). Those edits are committed in 54c7530 and the arm is launchable.

WHY IT DIED, and it is not the recipe: the card was BIOHUB'S, granted by me in writing at 12:12Z ('take it for as long as you want it'). I launched onto it at 14:09Z having checked only nvidia-smi, which read momentarily free. With both of us resident the device sat at 31964 of 32607 MiB and Windows paged over PCIe rather than failing: throughput 198 -> 27 -> 13 img/s across fifteen minutes. Killed 14:24Z, fault letter sent to their inbox, device released (10067 MiB at 95% = them alone).

CONSEQUENCE FOR --vram-gb 29.5: it is correct ONLY on an idle card. 30208 MiB against 31045 free leaves ~800 MiB of device slack, which is not slack when anyone else is resident. The next launch of this arm must be on a card that is ours, and lib.sh:256's physics is symmetric — the 20-slice recipe derives 28.3 GB, so a co-tenant of any size denies it AND it denies any co-tenant.

RE-PRICED AGAINST knee-uco3 BEFORE IT IS RE-LAUNCHED. dark6 (six all-data members, no seventh) reads 0.937, the same plateau every seventh-seat entry read. So this arm's PREDICTION branch — 'ship it' — is a seventh seat and is worth ~0 board points on that measurement. What survives is its INSTRUMENT value: it is the only test of whether distance and strength can coexist on one member, and the REFUTATION branch (strong AND near) retires the v3 axis honestly. It also trains at fold 0 while the champion is six --fold -1 members, so shipping it would need a second ~3 h all-data refit on top. Re-price that chain against the card's real availability before spending ~6 h on it.

FAILURE READ, 2026-08-25 15:30Z. The arm died at 14:14Z and it was NOT contention. The run's own
heartbeat says so in its log: `STALLED: 5 img/s against this run's own peak of 230 - 213 MiB free
against 755 at the start, so no foreign process arrived - this is our own footprint against this card`.
It reached step 86 of 583, then Windows began paging GPU memory over PCIe and the trainer exited 1.

THE FIRST OOM AND THIS STALL ARE DIFFERENT FAILURES AND THE SECOND ONE IS FRAGMENTATION, NOT VOLUME.
The header's fix for the first (`--eager-encoder --vram-gb 29.5`) worked on the axis it named: the
inductor buffer is gone. The numbers the eager smoke then reported:

    v3lora_dense smoke   28.77 GB reserved   24.38 GB allocated     (LoRA r8, eager)
    v3base_dense         ~27.85 GB reserved  25.38 GB allocated     (full FT, same shape, RAN FINE)

Allocated is LOWER than the control that fits. What is higher is RESERVED - 4.39 GB held by the
allocator and not handed to a tensor. So this arm is not asking for more memory than its control; it is
asking for it in a shape the caching allocator cannot pack. `--vram-gb 29.5` then left only ~800 MiB of
DEVICE slack, and the residual grew into it until the card had 213 MiB and started paging.

Gradient checkpointing is ALREADY ON (`recompute_activations: True` in the failing run's own recipe
line), so the memory-for-compute trade is already spent and is not the lever.

THE NEXT LAUNCH IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A GUESS, AND THE SMOKE IS THE ORACLE. The 60-study smoke runs the
same batch, slice count and token count as the arm, so it reproduces the peak exactly - it is where the
28.77 above was measured - and it costs 189 s. Two smokes, ~7 min of card:

  1. as-is, to confirm the peak is stable rather than a one-off;
  2. with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`.

lib.sh records expandable_segments as unhelpful on this machine, but all three arms it records were
short of ALLOCATED memory, which that setting does not create. This one is short of PACKING, which is
the case it exists for. If the reserved-minus-allocated gap closes, the arm runs at the recipe the
single-variable argument requires and nothing about the arithmetic moves. If it does not close, the arm
does not fit on this card at this recipe and that has to be said plainly rather than worked around with
a batch change - `--batch 3 --accumulate 2` is still refused for the reason the header gives (it halves
the ranking term's pair population, which is a second variable in a one-variable arm).

title: arm_check cannot see a flag an arm OMITS relative to its declared control
description:
distill_pairs.sh declared 'the control is band_dense byte-for-byte' and 'ONE VARIABLE: --distill-weight', then omitted --backbone-lr and silently trained at the trainer default 8e-6 against a control at 4e-5. It passed arm_check ('1 arms checked, 0 refused, 0 uncached'), smoked clean, and burned ~75 min of card producing an uninterpretable number. arm_check validates that the flags PRESENT are real; it has no notion of the flags that should be present.

The control is already declared machine-readably: every arm carries a '# control  <name> = <score>' line near the bottom (distill_pairs.sh, distill_v3base.sh both do). So the check is buildable: parse the arm's control line, read that control arm's run_train flag set, diff the two, and REFUSE on any flag that differs or is absent without an explicit '# deliberate: <flag>' waiver in the arm. An arm that legitimately moves two things then has to say so in writing, which is the point.

Prior art for the detector already exists downstream: kneemri.evaluation.run_comparison prints exactly this diff ('vs control: backbone_lr 4e-05->8e-06') — but AFTER the card is spent. This bead is about moving that diff to BEFORE.

Audit note: a sweep of all 90 arms shows ~30 with no --backbone-lr at all. Most are analysis tools (build_cache, attribution, diversity_curve, vjepa_probe) or pre-date the 4e-5 era, so MISSING is not by itself a defect — it is a defect only where the arm names a 4e-5 control. That distinction is precisely what the proposed check encodes and what a human eye does not reliably do.
notes:
2026-08-24: BUILT. arm_check now parses the arm's own '# control  <name> = <score>' line, resolves that control's run_train flag set out of the same stub-lib sweep, and diffs the two — reporting every flag that differs or is ABSENT relative to the control.

An arm is supposed to differ, so the diff alone is not the defect; an UNDECLARED diff is. Each moved flag needs one '# deliberate: <flag>' line in the arm's header. That is the check, and it costs the author one line per variable — which is also the moment they notice the arm moves three things.

Asymmetry copied from report_prices, and for the same reason: 32 of 100 arms differ from a named control without declaring it, and nearly all of them already ran. The full sweep prints the COUNT and passes; '--only <arm>' names the flags and REFUSES. The defect only costs a card at the moment an arm is armed, and the run that arms one is the run that names it.

Details: values compare numerically where both parse as float (4e-5 == 4e-05, which would otherwise be a diff nobody reads twice). --out/--labels/--paths are INCIDENTAL and excluded. A control the sweep cannot resolve to an arm (wsfold0_e6 and friends are CHECKPOINT names, 15 arms) is skipped rather than reported — a missing comparison, not a wrong one. CONTROL_LINE requires the '=' because five headers open prose with 'control is the same recipe...'.

Verified on the three live arms: distill_pairs now reports only its two real variables (its --backbone-lr was fixed by hand after the incident, so the check correctly no longer flags it), dissent_seat three, margin_seat two; all three now carry their '# deliberate:' lines and pass.

title: Volumetric encoder: the one through-plane mechanism the aggregation sweep did NOT test
description:
Carried out of knee-yuqf's closure rather than folded into it, per the standing rule that a refuting experiment kills a USE of an asset and not the asset. What depth_true refuted is through-plane mixing at the FEATURE level: the encoder sees one slice at a time, emits a per-slice vector, and only then does an order-aware aggregator get to mix across depth. Four combining rules on the settled recipe now span 0.0019 (max 0.8457, depth gate 0.8461, mean 0.8473, permutation-blind gate 0.8476), more slices moves -0.0001 and more slots +0.0002. Three directions, all flat: the aggregation STAGE is saturated and the limit sits UPSTREAM, in what a single slice's feature vector contains.

A volumetric encoder is a different mechanism and is untested here. It sees the stack before any per-slice feature exists, so through-plane structure can shape the representation rather than being reconstructed from vectors that already discarded it. MRI is 3D and every arm this project has ever run treats it as a bag of 2D pictures.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE OF LEVER. It is a data/architecture change, not a knob, and it is the only member type that would be structurally unlike the seven-member pool along an axis the offline ruler is known to under-price (knee-avzz, 2.4x). It is also the honest reading of the member-population exhaustion result: 11/11 arms negative on the mean says the tuning is done, not that the encoder is.

WHAT MUST BE ANSWERED BEFORE ANY CARD IS SPENT (audit first, per the standing order):
  1. Which volumetric encoder, and does a pretrained one exist that is worth more than a randomly-initialised 3D net on 3,526 studies? Candidates to READ on, not assume: video ViT / VideoMAE with the depth axis as time, a 3D ResNet on medical pretraining, or 2.5D (slice triplets into the 3-channel input) which is the CHEAPEST probe of the same mechanism and may be runnable inside the current recipe with almost no new code.
  2. VRAM. The settled 20-slice 2D recipe already derives 28.3 GB of a 32.6 GB card. A volumetric encoder at the same slice count will not fit; the arm has to be priced at a slice count and batch that does, and that reduction is itself a confound against every 2D control.
  3. What the matched control is. v3base_dense and base_dense are 2D full-adaptation numbers at the settled point; a 3D arm at a different slice count is not matched to them and the delta cannot be read straight.

Start with 2.5D as the gate: it costs the least, it uses the existing trainer, and if the depth axis carries nothing even when handed to the encoder directly, a full 3D encoder is not licensed. Reference row: experiments/README.md line 283.
notes:
2026-08-24: CLOSING AS DUPLICATE, filed before the audit finished and refuted by it within four minutes. Everything this bead proposed as unbuilt already exists:
  * The 2.5D gate it recommended STARTING with has run and is SEATED. through_dense channel-stacks a 3-slice window and reads -0.0020 against its control. volume_read.py's own docstring proves why that is not a 3D probe at all: Conv2d(3,D,k=14,s=14) over slices (i-1,i,i+1) is mathematically IDENTICAL to Conv3d(1,D,k=(3,14,14),s=(1,14,14)), so channel stacking at window 3 collapses to one linear projection and ONE depth position. The recommendation was wrong, not merely redundant.
  * The encoder-family seam exists: Backbone.load already wraps a non-ViT family (MapAsTokens for CONVNEXT), so a volumetric trunk costs no branch per consumer.
  * VRAM was answered and the answer inverts this bead's worry. knee-2nxh had the tubelet direction BACKWARDS - units is PER-SLICE, so a token spanning two slices HALVES it. The read prices at 21.7 GB, not the 38.3 GB the uncorrected cap claimed, and fits the card at 20 slices batch 6.
  * The matched-control worry is answered better than this bead framed it: there IS no matched control, by construction, because the trunk refuses band_dense's reading (crop, pooling and trunk all differ and have to). vjepa_member prices itself as an INSTRUMENT and by seat DISTANCE, not by a delta of means.
  * knee-rpkw and experiments/arms/vjepa_member.sh carry the whole thing, smoked and CPU-precleared 2026-08-22.
The one thing worth carrying over is the saturation framing, appended to knee-rpkw.

title: DINOv3 student taught the fold-0 ensemble's order — the distillation axis on a DIFFERENT encoder family
description:
GATED ON distill_pairs (knee-1xsu). Do not launch until that arm reads.

WHAT IT IS. v3base_dense's invocation with the teacher term added: --distill-weight 0.3 --teacher-targets teacher_fold0.npz. Everything else held, so v3base_dense's own measured 0.8455 (2026-08-21, peak e6) is the matched control and it costs ZERO extra card — it is already in the ledger.

WHY THIS ONE RATHER THAN A SECOND DINOv2 STUDENT. A teacher's ORDER is architecture-agnostic, which is the entire reason distillation is worth more here than a knob. The champion pool is seven members of one family; the board's only live mechanism at the top is the seventh member's TYPE OF DISTANCE (allfit's seat principle, and augseat is testing the regularisation axis on it right now). A DINOv3 student carries encoder-family distance AND is taught the pool's own ordering, which is the only construction this project has that could produce a member that is both strong and structurally unlike the pool.

WHAT THE LEDGER ALREADY SETTLED, so this is not re-litigating it: the FAMILY by itself is worth nothing (v3base_dense 0.8455 vs base_dense 0.8512, inside the 0.0062 floor), and the two weak DINOv3 members in the roster were mis-attributed — that was a LoRA-over-frozen-trunk penalty of ~0.019, not the encoder. So the family is a live axis at full adaptation and only at full adaptation.

PRICE, out loud. ~2.3 h of card (680 s/epoch x 12), teacher already written and reusable at zero. Zero submission slots. P(clears the 1.5% bar alone) ~0.05. It is worth 2.3 h ONLY in the branch where distill_pairs shows the teacher term transfers at all — otherwise this is 2.3 h buying a second measurement of a null.

THE GATE, from distill_pairs' own pre-registration:
  distill_pairs >= 0.860 — LICENSED, run it. The term transfers, and the question becomes whether it transfers ACROSS families.
  distill_pairs 0.850-0.860 with a RARITY-ORDERED per-label profile — licensed, because the mechanism is alive at a wrong operating point and the family swap is a cheaper next move than a weight sweep.
  distill_pairs <= its control with a FLAT profile — NOT licensed. File the profile and leave this bead open with the reason.

PRE-REGISTERED against v3base_dense's 0.8455:
  >= 0.8598 — the student beats the best solo member this project has, on the far encoder. Seat it, and the pool stops being one family.
  0.8455-0.8598 — the term transfers across families by whatever distill_pairs measured on its own. Read the DELTA against distill_pairs' delta, not against the absolute: two students, two families, one teacher is a transfer measurement.
  <= 0.8455 — the term is family-specific, which would be the interesting negative: it would say what the teacher carries is not order but something the student's own family already had.
notes: PRICE: ~2.3 h of card (~680 s/epoch x 12), teacher file already written and reused at zero, ZERO submission slots. P(clears the owner's 1.5% bar alone) ~= 0.05. Justified as the TRANSFER half of a pair rather than as an improvement: distill_pairs measures whether the teacher's order transfers at all, this measures whether it is a property of the ORDER or of the student's own family — and only the second answer licenses a member the champion pool does not already contain. Gated: not launched until distill_pairs reads inside its licensing bands.

title: Mount aug_long_s2026: the regularisation member the same-distribution ruler structurally under-prices
description:
THE OWNER'S OVERFIT ARGUMENT REPRICES A MEMBER WE ALREADY OWN, AND IT COSTS ZERO CARD.

He said, on 2026-08-24: "the real kaggle test dataset is NOT our dataset - meaning part of the data is unknown and unknowable and we shouldnt chase just a perfect fit (overfit) - because we dont know the final test". That is not a general caution here, it is a specific indictment of our ruler. The 909-study holdout is drawn from the SAME distribution as the training side, so a mechanism whose whole purpose is to trade in-distribution fit for robustness to shift reads FLAT or NEGATIVE on it BY CONSTRUCTION. The ruler cannot see the axis.

aug_long_s2026 is the member that argument lands on hardest, and it is already trained and sitting on disk.
  It scores 0.8511 solo, which is level with base_dense at 0.8512 - and base_dense CARRIED the 0.931 board entry.
  Its arm read -0.0076 offline, which is outside the 0.0062 noise floor, so it was read as a kill.
  It is the REGULARISATION axis. Regularisation degrades training-distribution fit on purpose. That is the exact shape the ruler punishes and a shifted test rewards.
  It has NEVER BEEN MOUNTED. Not once, in any entry.

THE LEDGER ALREADY SHOWS THE RULER MISSING THIS, three times, in the same direction:
  calib_span read -0.0020 offline and the board went UP past 0.928.
  base_dense read -0.0066 offline, outside the floor and at 2.5x the card cost, and the board went up a tick.
  through_dense read flat in its own arm and bought a board tick as the seventh seat.
