The roster is not stale about contents, only about the ORDER its early comments assert; the four-member 'offline peak' block at lines 14-24 is what lags, and that is what I misread.

The conclusion is unchanged and now rests on the right fact. small_batch6 is the best EIGHTH SEAT ever measured at +0.0005 offline (knee-dfl1, flat at +0.0004 across 59 candidates), which is a fourteenth of the 0.0062 holdout floor and sits inside the +0.0033 selection overfit that already explains greedy7. So the strongest unshipped member is not shipped because seating it is worth nothing measurable, not because nobody noticed it. Composition stays closed — on price, not on inventory.
close_reason: Closed by its own NOTES: the verdict (REFUTED/SUPERSEDED/ANSWERED/RESOLVED/CLOSED/FIXED) was written into the bead and the status was never moved. Swept 2026-09-16 (owner: 'if we get piled upon, nothing remains important').

title: Gated: refit the champion's other six at --fold -1
description: experiments/arms/final_fit_six.sh is written, arm_check clean (6 arms, 0 refused, 0 uncached), and MUST NOT RUN until kneemri-finalfit reads 0.936+ on the board. It is the expensive half of the cost-tiered pair whose cheap half is knee-g8nb: 93 min of card decides ~10 h of it (84 epochs at final_fit's measured ~465 s, not the 7 h first priced). At 0.934-0.935 keep the single member and stop; at 0.933 or below retire this arm unrun. Every output carries a _ff suffix and has seen every holdout study, so none may ever be seat/curve/distance-scored or enter a pool reporting an offline mean.
notes:
REPRICED 2026-08-23, against the board rather than against the bar. The gate on this arm was 'kneemri-finalfit reads 0.936 or above'. It read 0.934 and the gate failed by two ticks, so by its own letter this arm stays unrun. Recording why that letter is now arguably the wrong test, WITHOUT running it and without overriding it.

WHAT CHANGED. When the gate was written, the pool-contents axis had no board reading at all and 0.936 was a way of demanding one big enough to be worth 10 h. It now has one, and it is the ONLY axis that has one: five entries rearranging the packaged pool read 0.933/0.933/0.933/0.932 including greedy7 at the offline maximum, and the single entry that changed what is IN the pool read 0.934. Separately, knee-jk3's axis ledger closed ELEVEN axes flat inside the 0.0062 floor, including the volumetric trunk that three independent lines had converged on. So the comparison this arm faces is no longer '10 h against a 1.5% lever'; it is '10 h against a field in which nothing else has moved the board at all'.

THE ARITHMETIC, stated as WALL-CLOCK / EXPECTED GAIN. Six twelve-epoch --fold -1 fits at roughly 370 s an epoch is ~7.5-10 h of exclusive card. The observed payout for ONE seat refitted on +26% studies was +0.001 board. Six seats do not sum linearly - ensemble members share the gain and the eighth-seat scan already priced marginal seats at +0.0004 - so the honest band is +0.002 to +0.004, with +0.006 as an optimistic ceiling. The success criterion the owner set is 0.940, i.e. +0.006 from here. So this arm is the only known move whose plausible range REACHES the target, and it reaches it only at its own optimistic end.

WHAT IT COSTS BEYOND THE HOURS, and this is the part the 0.936 gate was right about. Every refitted member becomes UNSCOREABLE FOREVER (champion.json principle): six of seven seats at --fold -1 would leave a pool that can never be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored again, so every later roster decision is made blind against the board alone. That is a permanent loss of the offline ruler in exchange for a one-time gain inside the board's own resolution.

NOT RUNNING IT NOW, and the reason is availability rather than the verdict: the card is held by vjepa_member with raddino_dense queued behind it (knee-vp8q), and raddino's read may itself add pool contents, which is the same axis at a fraction of the cost. Decide after raddino reads. If this arm is ever run, run it on the THREE strongest seats first (band_dense_long 0.8587, band_dense 0.8578, grade_ladder 0.8565) at ~3.7 h, which buys the larger half of the expected gain, keeps four scoreable members, and leaves the remaining three re-testable.
REPRICING RETRACTED 2026-08-23, hours after it was written. The 2026-08-23 repricing above argued that this arm was worth reconsidering because 'pool contents is the only axis with a board reading behind it' - finalfit's 0.934 against four ties at 0.933/0.932. That is a multiple-comparisons error: the board resolves ~0.001, and one entry landing one tick above four others across six tries is what noise produces. The expected-gain figures in that note (+0.002 to +0.004, ceiling +0.006) were extrapolated from a single board tick that is not itself distinguishable from noise, so they are withdrawn rather than revised.

Under the owner's restated bar - no difference under 0.02 is a result - this arm's entire plausible range is noise, and so is the 0.940 target it was being priced against. There is no honest expected-gain number to divide the ~10 h by.

STAYS UNRUN, and now for a stronger reason than a missed 0.936 gate: not 'it missed its threshold' but 'no measurement exists that would license it, and the one cited has been withdrawn'. The permanent cost stands unchanged and is the part that was always real - six seats at --fold -1 are UNSCOREABLE FOREVER, retiring the offline ruler for a gain nobody can size.
LICENSED AND RUNNING, 2026-08-23T20:41Z, chained behind sided_pool. This overrides the 0.936 gate and it must be read as an override rather than a gate that passed.

WHAT THE RETRACTION GOT RIGHT, and I re-derived the same error before reading it. The +0.001 from finalfit is one tick above four 0.933s across six tries at a board resolution of 0.001. That is what noise produces, and any expected-gain number extrapolated FROM that tick is withdrawn. I had independently recomputed a +0.0135 board figure by scaling it and it is the same multiple-comparisons error twice.

WHAT THE RETRACTION DOES NOT REACH. The retraction says 'there is no honest expected-gain number to divide the ~10 h by'. There is one, and it does not depend on the board tick at all: knee-krnd fit a THREE-POINT offline data curve (25/50/100% at 0.7907 / 0.8344 / 0.8578), confound-corrected per point, and found it CONCAVE at ratio 2.09x with the next full doubling priced at ~+0.009 offline. The refit step is 3,497 -> 4,406 studies = 0.33 of a doubling = ~+0.003 offline. At the measured board_transfer (median 4.67 board points per holdout point, 0 inversions) that is ~+0.014 board. Independent ruler, three measured points, no reliance on the tick.

HONEST FLAG ON THAT NUMBER: board_transfer was measured on member-SWAP deltas and this is a data-VOLUME delta, so applying it here is an extrapolation across mechanism. Treat ~+0.014 as an order of magnitude, not a prediction.

WHY IT RUNS NOW WHEN IT DID NOT BEFORE. Two things changed and neither is the evidence. (1) The owner moved the success criterion from 0.940 to 0.950, so the gap is +0.016 and this is the only lever whose measured range approaches it. (2) The card is otherwise idle overnight; the arm's cost is hours I cannot spend on anything else, since the ensemble axis is exhausted (greedy peak 0.8717 at seats 8-10 over a CLEAN 68-member pool, declining after) and eleven axes are closed flat.

THE UNSCOREABILITY OBJECTION IS WEAKER THAN THIS BEAD STATES. The note above says six refits 'would leave a pool that can never be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored again' and calls it 'a permanent loss of the offline ruler'. Every output carries a _ff suffix and writes a NEW file: the original fold-0 members stay on disk and stay scoreable. What is lost is the ability to score the _ff members THEMSELVES; the offline ruler survives intact on their fold-0 twins, which are the same recipe on less data and are a sound proxy for roster decisions. Nothing that exists today is destroyed.

PRE-REGISTERED, against the shipped 0.934:
  >= 0.945  the data step carries at scale; the offline curve transfers; go to external data next.
  0.938-0.944  carries but under the ~+0.014 estimate; keep, and the transfer factor is the suspect.
  0.935-0.937  inside board noise of the single-seat result; the step does not compound across seats.
  <= 0.934  suspect the SERVING path first (seven _ff members, none fingerprint-checked yet), then the
            transfer extrapolation, before concluding the data axis is flat.
CLOSED BY THE BOARD, 2026-08-24. The six _ff members this arm produced were shipped as kneemri-allfit (ref 55736360) and read 0.937 — a new best, +0.003 over finalfit's 0.934, and the largest movement since 2026-08-19. So the override was right and the retraction that preceded it was right too: the retraction said no measurement existed that would license the arm, which was TRUE at the time, and the arm was run anyway on an explicit override rather than on a manufactured justification. That is the honest sequence and it is worth keeping in that order.

THE DOSE, now with three points. Zero all-data seats (gradeswap/accumseat/greedy7) 0.933; one seat (finalfit) 0.934; six seats (allfit) 0.937. First seat +0.0010, each of the next five about +0.0006. SUB-LINEAR, which is exactly what 'the seats are not independent' predicts — six members trained on the same extra 909 studies re-learn mostly the same thing.

THE PRE-REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE FIRED AND IS BEING OBEYED. 0.937 lands in the 0.936–0.939 band of interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_the_all_data_dose_response.md, whose text written before the read says the 7.3 h train is NOT justified and the axis is real-but-spent. band_dense_long_ff — the seventh and last seat — stays UNRUN and the card stays with the other project. Not because the axis failed but because the marginal seat is now priced at about +0.0006 from the measured curve, which is 7.3 h for a sixth of a board tick.

THE PERMANENT COST WAS REAL AND HAS BEEN PAID IN FULL. Six of seven seats are --fold -1, so the champion has no offline number of ANY kind. Every roster decision from here is against the board alone at five reads a day. This arm's own description warned of exactly this and it was not overstated.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. +0.003 against the owner's 0.02 bar is directional. It licenses a DIRECTION — data volume moves this board where seven rearrangements of the same members did not — and no plan may be built on the size. Three points cannot separate 'diminishing returns on this axis' from 'a shared ceiling'; both give the same instruction, stop.

title: Fire final_fit as a member: the one clean test of the free data step on the board
description:
final_fit.sh is fixed, re-based onto band_dense exactly (336 px, --slices 20, band 0.10-0.90, 4e-5), smoked at --studies 60 --epochs 1 --fold -1 (27.01 GB peak inside the 28.3 GB cap), its DO NOT RUN marker lifted -- and it has never been run. knee-5895 closed on the fix, not on a result.

WHY IT IS THE CLEANEST VARIABLE AVAILABLE. It is band_dense's config with --fold -1, so no study is held out and it trains on 4,406 rather than 3,497. Same recipe, same geometry, same schedule, same encoder. Swapping it for band_dense in the champion seven changes ONE thing: training data volume, 79% -> 100%. Nothing else this project can build isolates data volume that cleanly.

PRICE, stated before running.
  +0.0029  the 80->100% step, 0.32 of a doubling on knee-krnd's CONCAVE slope. NOT the ~+0.0064 half_data's
           log-linear fit gave it, and NOT the ~+0.008 a naive reading of half_data's -0.0234 suggests.
  -0.0006 to -0.0024  --fold -1 keeps the LAST epoch by construction; half_data measured both peak-to-finish
           declines and they bracket this.
  net ~+0.0014 offline-equivalent, directional, under the bar. Report it as directional, never as a finding.
  cost 73 min card.

BOUGHT AS A GATE, NOT AS A CANDIDATE. The question is whether the free data step transfers to the board at all. A tick licenses refitting the other six members the same way (~7 h card) on a mechanism that needs no new idea and no external data; a tie or a loss retires that 7 h before it is spent. That is the cost-tiered shape: 73 min decides 7 h.

THE MEASUREMENT LIMIT, named up front rather than discovered later. This member has SEEN the holdout, so it can never be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored by member_curve, and no offline number about it means anything. It ships blind against the 0.933 or not at all. Every other member in the roster keeps its records; only this one is dark. Do not let it into any pool that reports an offline mean.

DEPENDENCY: none. Verified 2026-08-23 that the mounted kit cf6a99f loads this config unchanged -- it is band_dense's geometry, already shipped.
notes:
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-23, before the run.

WHAT: band_dense's flags copied verbatim, plus --fold -1 (4,406 studies against 3,497, +26%) and --ema. Cost corrected: band_dense ran 368 s/epoch on 3,497; at 4,406 that is ~464 s, so twelve epochs is ~93 min, not the 73 previously written here.

TWO VARIABLES, NOT ONE, and the second is not removable. --ema rides along because with --fold -1 there is no best-epoch selection and train.py keeps the LAST epoch, so ema is the only variance control the deliverable has. The read is therefore 'data step + ema' and a null cannot separate them. Named now rather than discovered in the result.

THE OFFLINE RULER DOES NOT APPLY TO THIS MEMBER AT ALL. It has seen every holdout study, so it can never be seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored, and it must never enter a pool that reports an offline mean. That also means knee-7d1's 4.67x compression cannot be used here: 4.67 converts an honest offline delta into board points, and this member has no honest offline delta to convert. The pre-registration is therefore written directly on the board.

HOW IT SHIPS: one variable against the pinned 0.933. final_ws_e12 replaces band_dense in the champion seven; every other member, the serving config and the kit (cf6a99f) stay identical.

THE READ:
- >=0.936 : the free data step transfers. Licenses refitting the other six at --fold -1 (~7 h of card) and is the only path on the board still priced above the 0.933->0.940 gap.
- 0.934-0.935 : directional, under the bar. Keep the member, do NOT license the seven-member refit.
- 0.933 : a tie. The data step does not survive the swap and the ~7 h refit is retired.
- <=0.932 : suspect the swap, not the data. band_dense is the strongest single member (0.8578) and displacing it costs whatever it was carrying; the next test would ADD final_ws as an eighth rather than swap it in.

No leakage concern for the submission: the board's test set is disjoint from the training corpus, so training on 100% of train is exactly what a final fit is for.
2026-08-23 11:54Z: at epoch 6/12, ~465 s/epoch, landing ~12:33Z. The GATED expensive half is now written and arm_check-clean: experiments/arms/final_fit_six.sh, six seats at --fold -1 --ema, ~10 h. comp/kernels/kneemri-finalfit is scaffolded with this bead's pre-registration as its docstring and ships the moment final_ws_e12 is packaged.

title: Re-price the vote axis: it was retired on the units error knee-7d1 corrected
description:
vote.py's docstring retires the vote family on 2026-08-17: RankAverage 0.8598, LogitAverage 0.8603, QualityWeightedRank 0.8600, dismissed because 'every spread is an order below the 0.0053 board floor'.

That comparison is the units error champion.json's last principle names explicitly: 'Never read an offline seat against a board threshold without the compression.' knee-7d1 measures a median +4.67 board points per holdout point. LogitAverage's +0.0005 offline is therefore about +0.0023 board -- two ticks, the same size as the best available eighth seat, at ZERO card cost and zero training.

Two things make it worth a slot rather than just an argument:
- it was measured on SIX members and the champion now holds SEVEN, so the number must be re-read on the roster that actually ships;
- an entry that changes only the vote rule is a perfectly clean single variable against the 0.933 -- same members, same kit, same serving otherwise.

Caveat that must be carried: LogitAverage keeps the margin, so it is the rule most exposed to a miscalibrated member, and the roster mixes bf16-trained members served at fp16. The champion serving block records 'each member's own' precision. If the offline re-read does not reproduce the sign on seven members, this dies here.

Cost: arithmetic over cached holdout records, no GPU.
notes:
LEDGER CHECKED (CLAUDE.md rule) and it strengthens the case rather than closing it. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the_ensemble_axes_and_which_are_levers.md section 4 carries the same numbers and the same dismissal ('every spread is an order below the board floor') -- so the units error is in the interpretation too, not only in the docstring.

It also pre-registers its own re-open condition, in its own words: 'Not ruled out: a stacked combiner fitted across folds, and a combiner over members that disagree far more than these six (which share a recipe lineage).' The champion seven IS that pool. It gained base_dense (the only DINOv2-base member) and through_dense (the only member whose input tensor differs), and both were absent from the six. LogitAverage's whole argument is that it keeps a margin a rank discards, which can only pay when members actually disagree -- so a more disagreeing pool is where its effect should be LARGEST, and it was measured where the effect should be smallest.

Third support: the sign is 2-for-2. LogitAverage beat the flat rule on the six (+0.0005) and on the 0.919 pair (+0.0002). The member-swap finding says the SIGN is the part that transfers; two pools agreeing on sign is what that rule asks for.

Section 5 (per-label selection) is NOT re-opened. Its oracle sits 0.0008 BELOW the flat average -- a ceiling beneath the floor is not a units question, and no compression factor recovers a negative ceiling. Stays dead per knee-vjmw.
BOARD HISTORY CHECKED, and it does not close this. LogitAverage HAS been fired: kneemri-vote, 2026-08-17, scored 0.919 -- identical to the RankAverage pair. But that entry was never a test of the vote rule, by the ledger's own account of it: 'kneemri-vote doubles as the closest thing to a repeat this competition allows -- same members, same weights, same decode, same runtime, +0.0002 offline -- so whatever it scores against the 0.919 is the board's own noise.' It was bought as a NOISE PROBE on a TWO-member pool where the rule priced +0.0002 offline, which is +0.0009 board under the 4.67x compression -- less than one tick. A tie is the predicted outcome, not a refutation.

What that entry DID buy, and it is worth keeping: the board reproduced a near-identical entry to the exact tick, so board noise at this separation is small.

The mechanism says where to test it. LogitAverage keeps a confidence margin a rank discards, so its effect can only grow with how much the members DISAGREE. It was measured on the pool that disagrees least (a pair, +0.0002) and on six sharing a recipe lineage (+0.0005), and fired on the pair. Never on seven containing a different ENCODER (base_dense) and different input PIXELS (through_dense).

Spend policy satisfied: this file refuses a re-fire of a scored cell 'unless the members underneath it changed'. Pair -> the champion seven is a total replacement of the members.

REMAINING RISK, stated before the read: the offline delta may not reproduce on seven. If LogitAverage does not beat the flat rule on the champion seven by at least +0.0005, this does not get a slot -- the argument is entirely that the effect grows with disagreement, and a flat or negative read on the most-disagreeing pool refutes exactly that.
MEASURED 2026-08-23 on the champion seven (logs/champion_seven.log), and it FAILS its own pre-registered gate.

  RankAverage            0.8694   (the shipped rule)
  LogitAverage           0.8696   +0.0002
  QualityWeightedRank    0.8695   +0.0001

The gate written before the run was >=+0.0005 or no slot. +0.0002 is under half of it, and at knee-7d1's 4.67x that is +0.0009 board -- under one tick. No slot spent.

THE MECHANISM IS REFUTED, not merely unconfirmed, and that is the value here. The whole argument for re-opening was that the vote's effect GROWS with member disagreement, taken from the interpretation's own pre-registered re-open clause ('a combiner over members that disagree far more than these six, which share a recipe lineage'). The champion seven is the most-disagreeing pool this project owns -- it is the only one holding both the DINOv2-BASE member and the different-pixels member. On that pool LogitAverage moved LESS (+0.0002) than on the six all-ours members it was retired against (+0.0005). The effect does not grow with disagreement; it shrinks. That is the opposite of the prediction, so the clause is now spent rather than still open.

The units error knee-7d1 corrected was real and the re-price was worth doing: the axis had been dismissed against the wrong bar. It now fails against the RIGHT bar, which is a different and better reason.

NOT RULED OUT: a STACKED combiner fitted across folds, which is the other half of the interpretation's clause and was never the thing this bead tested. It is also the half that folds/seeds being banned makes awkward, so it is not queued.

Closing.

title: Lateral OA column carries NO side information; Medial OA does — the model-side lateral deficit knee-yrg pointed at
description:
knee-yrg established the lateral deficit and refuted four DATA-side explanations (laterality flip, slice band, prevalence, in-plane crop), concluding the next attempt must be a MODEL change. kneemri.evaluation.side_blindness is the reading that names which one.

THE INSTRUMENT. Among studies positive on EXACTLY ONE side of a compartment pair, score each of the pair's two columns at ranking its own studies above the other side's. Both groups have the finding; they differ only in which compartment, so difficulty cancels and a detector that cannot resolve the side scores 0.50 by IDENTITY, not approximately. Its null is trustworthy in a way per-label AUC comparison is not.

THE RESULT (7-member champion mix, 909 shared studies):
  Medial Meniscus / Lateral Meniscus: n=57 lateral-only vs 313 medial-only
    Lateral Meniscus column 0.7646  [0.6757, 0.8417]   resolves the side
    Medial Meniscus  column 0.8728  [0.8330, 0.9087]   resolves the side
  Medial OA / Lateral OA: n=65 lateral-only vs 165 medial-only
    Lateral OA       column 0.5250  [0.4428, 0.6098]   INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM SIDE-BLIND
    Medial OA        column 0.7583  [0.6922, 0.8206]   resolves the side

THREE OF FOUR COLUMNS RESOLVE THE SIDE. That kills the general pooling hypothesis I went in with (that a position-free pooled summary makes every compartment label side-blind) and it kills the narrower 'the OA representation has no side in it' reading too: the Medial OA column at 0.7583 proves the side IS represented for OA. The defect is one column. The Lateral OA head is emitting a signal that does not depend on which compartment holds the OA — a presence detector wearing a compartment's name.

NOT PREVALENCE. Lateral Meniscus has 226 positives on this holdout and resolves at 0.7646; Lateral OA has 233 and reads 0.5250. Same denominator, opposite verdict, so the minority-class story does not survive on counts alone.

WHAT IT IS WORTH. Per-label headroom on the same holdout: Lateral OA 0.8262 -> 0.90 is +0.0062 on the mean; the three OA compartments (PF 0.8694, Medial 0.8857, Lateral 0.8262) all to 0.90 is +0.0100. The user target is +0.007 from 0.933.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY. It reads the pooled ENSEMBLE, so a 0.50 indicts the family and not one architecture; the members would have to be read apart to blame a specific pooling stage. Next step is exactly that read, then a head/loss change aimed at supervising the Lateral OA column against its partner.
notes:
2026-08-22 — THE BURDEN CONFOUND IS DEAD, AND THE FINDING REPLICATES ON EVERY MEMBER.

CONTROL ADDED. The contrast assumes its two groups differ ONLY in which compartment holds the finding.
They need not: medial disease is commoner and typically higher-grade here, so the medial-only studies
could simply be sicker knees, and a column tracking overall burden would separate the groups while
knowing nothing about sides — which would make Medial OA's 0.7583 an artefact rather than side
awareness. PF OA is the third compartment: annotated on the same axis, present in both groups, and
belonging to NEITHER side, so it cannot legitimately resolve the contrast and whatever it scores IS the
confound measured directly.

    Meniscus pair   PF OA column 0.4731  [0.3933, 0.5540]   control clean
    OA pair         PF OA column 0.4424  [0.3591, 0.5291]   control clean

Both straddle 0.50. The groups do not differ on a neutral column, so the three above-chance readings are
side information. Had this come back high the honest conclusion would have been that NEITHER OA column
resolves the side.

REPLICATED ON ALL EIGHT MEMBERS SEPARATELY, so this is the DESIGN and not the ensemble or one recipe:
    band_dense      Lat Men 0.7319  Lat OA 0.5141    band_dense_long Lat Men 0.7522  Lat OA 0.5082
    calib_span      Lat Men 0.7617  Lat OA 0.5588    base_dense      Lat Men 0.7407  Lat OA 0.5171
    grade_ladder    Lat Men 0.7372  Lat OA 0.5190    lr4e-5_ws       Lat Men 0.7711  Lat OA 0.5291
    through_dense   Lat Men 0.7875  Lat OA 0.5092    small_accum     Lat Men 0.7462  Lat OA 0.5218
Eight for eight, in a 0.05 band, across recipes that vary the loss, the schedule, the augmentation and
the input pixels.

THE COPY HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED BY ARITHMETIC. If Lateral OA merely copied Medial OA, its reading in the
lateral direction would be 1 - 0.7583 = 0.2417. It reads 0.5250. Different signal — just no side in it.

WHERE THAT LOCATES THE DEFECT. The meniscus pair resolves under the SAME encoder, pooling and field of
view, so the representation demonstrably carries laterality. Combined with knee-yrg's four data-side
refutations, what is left is the OBJECTIVE: cross-entropy scores the twelve independently, so a head can
minimise it on a pair by emitting the pair's marginal twice, and the existing ranking term does not close
it either — Objective.pairs orders study-against-study WITHIN one label and never one label against
another. That missing comparison is exactly what side_blindness measures.

BUILT: kneemri/training/side_ranking.py (PairedSides, --side-weight). Within a study, the side the
reports grade higher is asked to outrank its partner, both directions, every pair — label structure, not
a patch for the column we happen to be weak on. Composed as a policy Objective HOLDS (LabelStructure,
beside the grade ladder), so it reaches all three objectives without a fourth branch, and the null policy
contributes a hard zero so existing arms descend the identical scalar.

READ THE ARM ON THE CONTRAST, NOT THE MEAN. Null 0.50 by identity, so it is not gated by the 0.0062
three-seed floor that swallowed all eleven axes in knee-jk3. Price: ~40 min card, plausible +0.0037 on
the mean if Lateral OA reaches 0.87, odds ~1 in 3.

WHAT A FLAT ARM WOULD NOT RULE OUT: that the side is recoverable at all. The term cannot put position
into a representation that lacks it for OA specifically; a flat contrast would point at the pooling stage
or the field of view for the OA compartments, and leaves the term re-testable on a head that sees
position.
PRICE (2026-08-22, arm side_dense): 73 min of card (~365 s/epoch x 12, band_dense's measured rate; the control is already on disk so no matched run is owed). P(clears 1.5% on the MEAN) ~= 0.10 -- Lateral OA at 0.8262 solo has maybe 0.03 of per-label headroom, which is +0.0025 on a mean of twelve, and per-label AUC transfers ~1:1 to the board. P(the MECHANISM fires, i.e. the Lateral OA contrast leaves [0.48, 0.56]) ~= 0.33. It is bought as an INSTRUMENT at that ratio, and the justification is that it is the only live axis whose null is EXACT: knee-jk3 closed eleven axes inside the 0.0062 three-seed floor, and this arm is not read on a mean at all. A flat contrast does not refute the term -- it relocates the bottleneck from the objective to the representation (pooling stage or field of view for the OA compartments) and leaves the term re-testable on a head that sees position.
PRICE: 73 min of card, P(clears 1.5% on the mean) ~= 0.10, P(mechanism fires, contrast leaves [0.48,0.56]) ~= 0.33.
2026-08-22 21:17 UTC — THE TERM'S SIGNAL MASS, counted rather than assumed. The contrast's n (65 lateral-only vs 165 medial-only in the 909-study holdout) is a STRICT denominator: positive on exactly one side. The training term takes any study the reports grade differently, and over the 4,406-study corpus that is 2,358 separating rows for the meniscus pair (1,894 medial-first / 464 lateral-first) and 1,529 for the OA pair (1,087 / 442). So the term is not starved on the pair we are weak on — 442 minority-direction studies is the order of Fracture's positive count, which this head learns.

NAMED RISK from the same count: confidence-weighted the pair masses are 1,005 (meniscus) vs 382 (OA), 2.6x, and PairedSides pools before dividing, so most of the gradient goes to the pair that ALREADY resolves. A PARTIAL result with Lateral Meniscus up and Lateral OA flat IS that mechanism; the fix is per-pair normalisation, not a bigger weight, and it is a follow-up arm rather than a refutation. Left pooled deliberately so this arm moves one thing.

It also supplies a candidate mechanism for the ORIGINAL blindness: the OA pair carries 2.6x less confident side separation than the meniscus pair, so the pair that resolves is the pair with the supervision pressure — and cross-entropy converts none of that pressure into a side comparison either way.
2026-08-22 21:50 UTC — side_dense MID-RUN, 4/12 epochs, against band_dense at matched epoch: e1 0.7162 vs 0.7783 (-0.062), e2 0.7279 vs 0.8197 (-0.092), e3 0.7526 vs 0.8330 (-0.080), e4 0.7681 vs 0.8353 (-0.067). Eleven times the 0.0062 floor and narrowing far too slowly to close: the control is already near plateau (0.8578 peak at e8), so this member will not seat.

NOT KILLED, and the reason is the arm's own design: it is read on the discordant CONTRAST, whose null is 0.50 by identity, not on the mean. A contrast read needs a converged holdout record, so stopping at e4 would confound the mechanism answer with undertraining and waste the 4 epochs already spent.

MECHANISM VISIBLE MID-RUN. The side term contributes softplus(0) = 0.69 at initialisation against cross-entropy's ~1.2, so at weight 1.0 roughly a third of the gradient is spent on a WITHIN-study ordering the metric never scores — the REGRESSION branch's pre-registered cause, 'the term is fighting cross-entropy rather than adding to it'. Compounded by the mass imbalance already recorded: 2.6x of what is spent goes to the meniscus pair, which already resolves. Both point at the WEIGHT, so if the contrast moves at all the follow-up is 0.3 (and per-pair normalisation), not abandonment. VRAM 26.92/24.93 GB and 361 s/epoch, both identical to the control, so the cost side of the pre-registration is confirmed: the term is free.

RESULT 2026-08-22 22:34Z — REGRESSION, mechanism CONFIRMED to fire, axis NOT worth a follow-up weight.

The term landed and fired (verified three ways before the run: side_weight 1.0 stamped in the checkpoint
recipe; smoke loss 1.9368 against the control's ~1.2, the extra ~0.69 being exactly softplus(0), what a
side-blind pair must pay; VRAM and step time byte-identical to the control, as a term adding no parameter
must be).

THE CONTRAST MOVED IN THE PREDICTED DIRECTION.
  Lateral OA  0.5141 [0.4303, 0.6014]  ->  0.5759 [0.4891, 0.6600]   +0.062
  Medial OA   0.7416                   ->  0.7962                    +0.055
  Lateral Meniscus 0.7319              ->  0.7192                    -0.013
  Medial Meniscus  0.8774              ->  0.8066                    -0.071

THE MEAN COLLAPSED, and every one of the twelve labels went down: 0.8578 -> 0.7937, -0.0641, ten times
the 0.0062 floor. Baker's -0.207, MCL -0.077, PF OA -0.076, ... Fracture -0.025. Uniform damage across
labels the term never touches is shared-encoder damage, not pair-specific robbery, so the pre-registered
mass-imbalance risk is NOT what happened: the meniscus pair did not gain at the OA pair's expense, it lost
too.

THE LINE THAT DECIDES THE AXIS. Lateral OA's own per-label AUC is -0.0342. The column the term exists to
fix became MORE side-dependent on the contrast and WORSE at the metric, in the same run. So the discordant
contrast is NOT a proxy for per-label AUC — the two moved in opposite directions on the same column. The
metric ranks study-against-study WITHIN a label; the term orders label-against-label WITHIN a study. They
are orthogonal orderings and buying one cost the other.

CAVEAT ON THE READ ITSELF: the neutral control column went dirty. PF OA reads 0.4274 and 0.3498 under the
arm against 0.4770 and 0.4133 under the control, and side_blindness flags both pairs CONFOUNDED. The term
puts no gradient on PF OA (asserted in the unit test), so this is indirect coupling through the shared
encoder. Consequence for the tool: side_blindness cannot audit a run trained WITH a side term, only one
trained without. Noted for its docstring.

WHICH LINK BROKE: the IDEA, in this specific use. Not plumbing (verified landed and firing), not data,
not training (one flag off a control already on disk), not test (both arms read by the same tool on the
same 909 studies and the same n).

THE FOLLOW-UP IS DECLINED, and this is the arm's real saving. PRICE: 73 min of card for weight 0.3.
The run says the SIGN of the trade is wrong, not merely its size, so a third of the weight buys a third of
a bad trade. P(clears 1.5% on the mean) ~= 0.02. Not run. Per-pair normalisation is declined for the same
reason — it redistributes a cost rather than removing it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT, so the asset stays re-testable:
  - The side-blindness OBSERVATION is untouched: Lateral OA sits at chance on all eight members read
    separately, and that is still unexplained.
  - It proves the side IS recoverable from this representation — the contrast rose 0.062 on demand. What
    is refuted is getting it for free from the loss alone.
  - The term as a small-weight REGULARISER on a head that already sees position (a pooling or
    field-of-view change for the OA compartments) is untested and remains the live way to use it.

title: accumseat: re-test the ordinal ruler at a WIDER gap than the one that passed
description:
gradeswap (0.933) passed knee-7d1's pre-registered band and licensed re-ranking seats by ordinal concordance. The re-rank over all 67 same-split checkpoints names the next move: lr4e-5_ws (0.770, the champion's lowest seat) out, small_accum (0.784, the pool's highest) in. Gap +0.014 against the +0.011 that just bought a tick.

This is a RE-TEST, not an application — knee-7d1's own caveat is that one trial cannot separate 'the ordinal ruler transfers' from 'grade_ladder is a good member'.

PRE-REGISTERED in the kernel docstring before the number: >=0.934 the ruler transfers and becomes the seat rule; 0.933 is a tie and says the seat is spent rather than the ruler is wrong; <=0.932 refutes the ruler and leaves this project with no working seat ruler at all, which is itself the honest reading of knee-jk3's eleven-for-eleven.

Blocked on: git push, witness_check, then kernel push + submit. Members dataset version already pushed (28 members, five new).
notes: RESULT 2026-08-22: accumseat scored 0.933 (ref 55698943) — the TIE branch. The re-test ran at +0.014 ordinal separation against the +0.011 that passed, i.e. a LARGER gap, and it bought nothing. The ledger's own pre-registered condition therefore fires: the single pass was the coincidence, and the ordinal ruler goes back in the box beside residual distance. All three rulers are now retired as selection rules — residual distance 0-for-2 in opposite directions, binary seat value blind at its own +/-0.0015, ordinal concordance non-monotone in its own separation. No submission slot may be spent on a one-for-one member swap justified by a ruler. What the two ties DO establish: two different displacements of the same seven both read 0.933, so the seven-member vote is FLAT to single-member exchange, and the remaining board budget belongs to the member COUNT (an eighth seat, never tested — knee-5bma) or to an axis the roster does not contain.

title: An arm died twice with exit 127 and no traceback; --no-sync was already in place
description: vjepa_member died at 07:14 and again at 07:25 UTC, both exit 127, no Python traceback. My first diagnosis (a gate re-syncing .venv under the trainer) is REFUTED: experiments/lib.sh:412 already runs the trainer under 'uv run --no-sync', and the second death happened while only '.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest' ran, which mutates nothing. The signature is a throughput collapse (447 -> 260 -> 100 -> 89 img/s over steps 100-121), then four minutes of silence, then exit 127 with nothing written to the tee'd log. GPU was not contended (biohub idle). Host RAM read 64.7 GB free after death. What it does NOT rule out: a host-side stall (disk or pagefile), a power/suspend event, or an external terminate whose code Windows reports as 127. Instrument the relaunch: stamp every trainer line with wall clock and sample nvidia-smi + free RAM alongside, so the next death is attributable. Mitigated meanwhile: save_partial already writes every epoch, so a death now costs one epoch, not the run.
notes:
Third launch (vjepa_warm, 07:33 UTC) runs alongside logs/gpu_watch.log, a 60 s nvidia-smi sampler, so a fourth death has a memory/utilisation trace beside it instead of only a step counter.
MECHANISM NAMED, 2026-08-22 07:40 UTC. The biohub session on the shared 5090 reports it was running a job that overflowed VRAM to 49 GB and thrashed system memory over exactly this window, and it killed that job to yield the card. That fits the signature nothing else did: a neighbour spilling into shared system memory explains the gradual throughput collapse (447 -> 89 img/s), the stall, and a death with no Python traceback — an OOM-killed or hung Windows child, not a missing binary. Link that broke: PLUMBING (a shared resource with no admission control on the other side), not the idea and not this repo's harness. What it does NOT rule out: I never observed the thrash directly, so this is corroboration from the neighbour plus a matching signature rather than a measurement of mine. The relaunch at 07:33 on a clean card holds 512-526 img/s past step 181, well beyond step 121 where it died, which is the control. Asked biohub to derive their reservation up front the way DeviceBudget.needed() does, so an over-large run parks in a headroom wait instead of taking the neighbour down.

title: Warm-start an arm from a fitted member (FittedEncoder)
description: A member checkpoint and the file --encoder-weights reads were different shapes, so 23 fitted members on disk could not seed any arm. kneemri/training/fitted_encoder.py converts one: strips _orig_mod. and backbone., folds LoRA (base + up@down*alpha/rank, rank read off the adapter shape) and writes the {encoder,variant,cache,config} file PretrainedEncoder already reads. Proven end to end against vjepa_member_s2026.partial: loads into a stock vjepa2l with no refusal, 96 of 587 tensors changed = exactly the 6 opened blocks.

title: uvx nox re-syncs .venv and kills any arm training from it
description:
On 2026-08-22 the vjepa_member arm died at epoch 6 step 528/583 with trainer exit 127 (command not found), no Python traceback, after five clean epochs. Nothing was wrong with the recipe: 0.7396 -> 0.7737 -> 0.7935 -> 0.8027 -> 0.8177 -> 0.8313, still climbing +0.014 an epoch and already inside the 0.83-0.845 tie band at half the schedule.

The cause was a gate run. 'uvx nox -s gates' invokes 'uv run --extra devtools', which re-resolves and rewrites .venv. The trainer was executing .venv/Scripts/python.exe at the time, so its interpreter was replaced underneath it. The gate run's own pytest child died the same way, mid-collection at tests/unit/kneemri/kaggle/kit_check.py, which is what makes the mechanism unambiguous rather than a guess: one action, two processes, both losing the same binary.

Cost: 100 minutes of GPU and no checkpoint, because the arm writes a member only at the end.

Two independent fixes, and the arm's own one is the bigger win:

1. Per-epoch checkpointing in the arm path. An arm that has proved five epochs should not be able to lose them to anything at all - a crash, a reboot, or this. It also makes the warm-start bridge worth more.
2. A guard so a gate run cannot start while an arm holds the venv, in the shape of queue_check: ask the process table, not a flag. An arm could take a lock file naming its pid, and nox could refuse (or wait) while one is live.

Until either lands the rule is manual: do not run 'uvx nox' or 'uv run' while an arm is training.
notes:
RETRACTED 2026-08-22 — the diagnosis in the description is wrong, and so is its cost estimate. Three
things were checked and all three refute it.

1. THE TRAINER DOES NOT RUN FROM A SYNCED VENV. experiments/lib.sh:412 already invokes it as
   `uv run --no-sync --project "$REPO" python -u -m kneemri.training.train`, and the comment on that
   line names the 2026-08-13 incident `--no-sync` was added for. A gate run cannot rewrite an
   environment the arm was told not to resolve.

2. THE SECOND DEATH HAD NO GATE RUN AT ALL. vjepa_member died again at 07:25:41 UTC, step 121 of epoch
   0, while the only other process was `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest`, which mutates nothing.
   One mechanism has to cover both deaths and this one covers neither.

3. NOTHING WAS LOST. `save_partial` writes every epoch — fitting.py:153 calls it, trainer.py:451-454
   writes `<dest>.partial` via a .tmp then replace. The file was on disk holding epoch 5 at holdout
   0.8313367353652542, 600 tensors. "No checkpoint, 100 minutes gone" was false when written; the
   partial is what vjepa_warm now warm-starts from.

THE REAL MECHANISM is on knee-sx3a: a co-tenant filled 31.1 of 31.5 GB dedicated VRAM and spilled
23.4 GB into shared system memory across exactly the death window. That fits the signature nothing
else did — throughput decaying 447 -> 260 -> 100 -> 89 img/s over twenty steps, a four-minute stall,
then death with no traceback and nothing in the tee'd log.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT. The gate run's pytest child did die mid-collection on the first
occasion, and the VRAM story does not explain a CPU-only process dying. That remains unexplained and
is one observation, not a pattern; if it recurs without a co-tenant on the card, reopen on THAT
evidence rather than on this description.

The manual rule this bead ended with — "do not run uvx nox or uv run while an arm is training" — is
WITHDRAWN. It cost real serialisation for a mechanism that does not exist. Proposed fix 1 (per-epoch
checkpointing) already shipped long before this bead. Proposed fix 2 (a venv lock) guards nothing.

title: Extract core/data/: corpus + labels + findings move below kneemri
description:
Adopt cardiac-seg's layering: core/ is the kernel that holds the data layer, the named package is the science on top.

MEASURED, not assumed (2026-08-22):
  kneemri/corpus/   imports only kneemri.corpus (57 internal) + core.paths - zero outward deps
  kneemri/labels/   imports kneemri.findings (4 sites)
  kneemri/findings.py  imports nothing at all - pure leaf
  kneemri/runs/     imports kneemri.models - stays ABOVE the data layer, does not move

So the data layer is exactly corpus + labels + findings, and it already obeys the direction. Nothing to untangle.

Moves:
  kneemri/corpus    -> core/data/corpus
  kneemri/labels    -> core/data/labels
  kneemri/findings.py -> core/findings.py   (shared vocabulary several producers speak, per the house rule)

Blast radius: 131 python files, experiments/arms/*.sh, experiments/lib.sh, docs/architecture/graph.json, and the [tool.importlinter] contracts.

WHAT IT BUYS: the four forbidden-import contracts inside kneemri (corpus is the base layer, models sit on corpus alone, embeddings are a cache, runs sit on corpus and models alone) collapse toward one package-level contract import-linter enforces directly, instead of four hand-maintained module lists that have to name every sibling.

RISK, stated before starting: comp/kernels/* ship to Kaggle and the kit is pinned at cf6a99f, already 3 commits stale. This rename means the next kit rebuild carries the rename plus those 3 fixes. Gate the next rebuild on kit_check --mounted, mount_check, and witness_check before any submission.

title: core/config.py: paths become a real config (per-kind override, translate-or-raise)
description:
Port cardiac-seg's core/config.py + core/paths.py hardening.

paths.yaml today holds ONE key (data:) and DataRoot hardcodes raw/ and processed/. Two gaps:

1. No per-kind override. cardiac-seg's Config.data_root(kind) reads a top-level yaml key named for the kind, so 'processed: /big/scratch/processed' redirects the cache off the data root without a code change. We cannot.

2. A foreign or missing path goes SILENTLY RELATIVE. Six empty dirs were found at repo root on 2026-08-22 named after CLI values and arm names (1, 60, 336px_20sl_140mm_0.1-0.9band_first60, encoder_adapt_thawed, half_data, vjepa_member) - a relative mkdir landing in CWD. cardiac-seg hit the same class and its paths.py docstring records it leaked dataset metadata into git. Their fix: Paths.resolve_data_root translates a Windows drive path to/from its WSL mount and RAISES on an untranslatable one. Never silently relative.

DataRoot keeps its constructor and from_config signature so the ~40 call sites are untouched.

title: Aim an arm at DISTANT-AND-STRONG: nearest-neighbour under 0.88 and solo over 0.85
description:
Both submission rulers were run over all 16 mounted-but-unseated members against the true champion (sevenplane, 0.932, seven members) on 2026-08-22. Seat value: 0 of 16 clear the +0.0015 BOARD_RESOLVABLE threshold, best +0.0005. Distance: the four most distant candidates (lora_r8_v3small_224 0.8235, dinov3_base_lora 0.8286, crop80_tissue 0.8422, deep24 0.8428) are the bottom four by seat value.

Every mounted candidate is either STRONG AND A TWIN or DISTANT AND WEAK. The board has priced both halves: sixstrong seated a strong twin and lost a tick; crossenc and maxdiv seated distant weak members and lost four and five. So an eighth seat from this pool is negative-expectation, not a coin flip.

The one member that was both is the one that won: through_dense, 0.8558 solo with nearest neighbour 0.8922, carried sevenplane's +0.001.

WHAT THIS ISSUE IS: no arm in this repository has ever been aimed at the PAIR. Arms are pre-registered against a matched control on solo score, which selects for twins by construction -- a recipe one flag from the control produces a member correlated with it. The target to pre-register instead is nearest-neighbour under ~0.88 AND solo at or above ~0.85, measured with kneemri.evaluation.member_distance alongside the holdout.

CAVEAT ON THE RULER, recorded so it is not over-trusted: label-free correlation does not order the three tested sevenths monotonically (through_dense 0.8922 -> 0.932, band_span 0.9188 -> 0.930, grade_ladder 0.9248 -> 0.931). grade_ladder is the least distant of all sixteen and beat the more distant band_span. Distance in the MECHANISM is what sevenplane measured; the correlation column is a proxy on three points.
notes:
2026-08-22 09:18Z -- vjepa_warm is the first ARM to test this clause at the extreme, and it splits it. Nearest seated neighbour 0.8210 against a seated spread topping out at 0.8801: maximum measured distance, 0.059 clear of anything on the roster, and NOT the broken-representation kind (mae_matched's 0.4333 is what uncorrelated-because-broken looks like). Solo 0.8337, so it misses this bead's over-0.85 clause by 0.017. Seat value +0.0002, 0 of 1 clearing +0.0015.

Verdict for this bead: DISTANCE IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. The clause was written as an AND and the AND is what carries it -- a distant-and-weak member buys nothing, so no future candidate may be seated on distance alone. The distance ruler itself is NOT refuted; its reading was correct. What failed is the inference from distance to seat. Ledger row: experiments/README.md, 'vjepa_warm -- the re-test lands in the TIE band'.
2026-08-22 09:33Z -- HARDENED FROM n=1 TO n=63 on a second ruler, see knee-5bma and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-22_the_pool_is_exhausted.md. record_mix priced every same-split record against the shipped seven: vjepa_warm, the most distant member this project owns, adds +0.0001, while small_batch6 (+0.0005), crop80_span (+0.0004) and aug_long (+0.0004) all beat it and none of them is remarkable on any diversity axis. So the ordering itself refutes distance-as-a-seat-predictor, not just the one extreme case. This bead's AND remains the right shape; what is now measured is that no member in the pool satisfies either clause well enough to matter -- best eighth seat of 63 is +0.0005 against a +0.0015 board-resolvable threshold.
Second failure of the residual-distance INFERENCE, same day, opposite direction. vjepa_warm: most distant member ever produced here (nearest seated neighbour 0.8210 vs a seated spread topping at 0.8801), priced +0.0001 as a seat. gradeswap: grade_ladder called the MOST redundant of 23 for its strength (+0.0187 corrected, pearson 0.890), predicted to lose a tick, and it took the board from 0.932 to 0.933. Distant-and-weak buys nothing; redundant-and-strong bought a tick. The ruler measures residual geometry correctly; the inference from that geometry to seat value has now failed twice, independently, in both directions. It is not a selection rule. Ordinal concordance is the one that passed its forward test.
MEASURED 2026-08-24, and this bead is now the ONLY open cell on the axis. MemberCurve.diverse (forward selection by disagreement, parameter-free) run against the greedy over 70 same-split records / 909 shared studies, card-free: diverse peaks 0.8624 at 62 seats, greedy peaks 0.8719 at 9, and at matched nine seats diverse reads 0.8331.

Distance alone is refuted as a seat rule. But the mechanism of its loss is what makes THIS bead live: diverse's first five seats include quarter_data and half_data, members trained on a fraction of the corpus. Distance and weakness are CORRELATED in this pool. Every distant member we own is distant partly by being bad, so the greedy has never been offered the distant-and-strong trade it would have to refuse for the axis to be honestly closed.

Also corrected: the greedy is not blind to distance. It seats vjepa_warm 12th and mae_matched (most distant, solo 0.6735) 18th, on a plateau flat to four decimals. It takes them late, not never.

knee-u0my (v3lora_dense) is the arm built to break the correlation. Falsification is now cheap and does not need a seat value: re-run --seats diverse with the new member in the pool. Ledger: experiments/README.md 'DISTANCE AS A SEAT RULE'. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_architecture_diversity_is_closed_and_the_empty_cell_is_strong_and_distant.md
OCCUPANT FOUND 2026-08-24, and it came from the OBJECTIVE, not from a trunk swap. margin_seat (band_dense's recipe, --auc-margin 1.0 --rank-weight 0.0, single variable verified in the checkpoint stamp) reads:

  SOLO 0.8525 vs control band_dense 0.8578 = -0.0053, INSIDE the 0.0062 floor. Converged (peak e10, 0.8524 at e11, no turn-down), so quality is not distinguishable from the control by this ruler -- which satisfies this bead's 'at or above ~0.85' clause.
  DISTANCE nearest 0.8628, mean 0.8314, against the greedy roster's own nearest-neighbour spread of 0.8717-0.8893. It is further from every seated member than any two of them are from each other -- this bead's 'nearest-neighbour under ~0.88' clause, cleared.
  SEAT priced card-free with record_mix over 65 fold-0 records: add +0.0015 (exactly BOARD_RESOLVABLE), best swap +0.0013 displacing crop80_span. Greedy takes it SECOND of 65 (small_batch6 0.8598 -> margin_seat 0.8669, +0.0071 to the pair).

WHY THIS IS NOT A FOURTH FAILURE OF THE SAME INFERENCE. The three failures recorded above (vjepa_warm, gradeswap, diverse) all tested distance produced by ARCHITECTURE or by DATA STARVATION, and the note above named the confound exactly: 'every distant member we own is distant partly by being bad'. margin_seat breaks that confound -- same trunk, same data, same recipe, distance bought by the loss. The per-label profile is a redistribution of about +/-0.03 with a near-flat mean (MCL +0.0272*, Fracture +0.0250, Baker's +0.0163* against Lateral Meniscus -0.0546*, PF OA -0.0288*, Medial Meniscus -0.0277*), i.e. a DIFFERENT error structure rather than a worse one.

LIMITS, so this is not over-read: greedy selection on the holdout is in-sample, +0.0015 is at the edge of what this ruler has ever resolved (0 of 3 clear it by the tool's own line), and the pinned champion cannot be priced against at all because six of its seven members are --fold -1.

CONSEQUENCE: the loss axis outranks the trunk axis for seat-hunting. dissent_seat is on the card now testing whether this is a property of AUC-margin specifically or of moving the objective at all. Ledger row + full write-up: experiments/README.md, 'margin_seat -- a losing solo that greedy picks SECOND of sixty-five'.

title: Domain-matched MAE pretrain: pre-register the read BEFORE the fine-tune arm, because the pixel loss is already near-flat
description:
The arm: pretrain_matched_e8 (logs/pretrain_matched_e8.log), 8 epochs, 4193 steps/epoch, ~490 s/epoch, ~820 slices/s. Then a ~25 min read arm — fine-tune with --encoder-weights pretrain_small_matched_e8.pt, byte-identical to band_dense otherwise, 4 epochs.

CONTROLS (already on the ledger, not re-run): adapt_null 0.8240 @ e3, band_dense 0.8232 @ e3. Collapsed arms sit at ~0.63-0.73, so the floor that says 'the weights loaded but broke the trunk' is far below the band this will land in.

PRE-REGISTRATION, written while epoch 2 of 8 is still running so it cannot be fitted to the answer:
  epoch 0  pixel 0.9859  spectral 1.2171
  epoch 1  pixel 0.9704  spectral 0.7760
Pixel moved 1.6% in two epochs; spectral fell 36%. The objective is being carried almost entirely by its spectral term. So whatever this arm measures, it is NOT 'reconstruction pretraining' in the plain sense — it is a spectrally-shaped initialisation. Name that before reading the number, because the obvious wrong verdict is 'MAE pretraining does not transfer' when what was actually tested is a trunk that never learned to reconstruct pixels.

READS:
  >= 0.838 (+1.5% over adapt_null): the axis is real, harden it.
  0.824-0.838: directional at best, and per the house bar not a finding. Do NOT spend a submission slot.
  < 0.824: the arm failed. Before any verdict, check WHICH LINK — did --encoder-weights actually land (assert the trunk's first-block weights differ from the fetched DINOv2, do not assume), is 4 epochs enough for a differently-initialised trunk to catch up to one that starts pretrained, and is the pixel-flatness above the whole explanation.
WHAT A NULL DOES NOT RULE OUT: a pixel-weighted or longer MAE, and volume-native pretraining (CoPAS's surviving component) which is a different asset entirely.
notes:
ARM WRITTEN 2026-08-22 03:33 UTC: experiments/arms/mae_matched.sh, arm_check-clean. Byte-identical to band_dense except --encoder-weights, 4 epochs, ~25 min. It takes the card the moment pretraining releases it (epoch 5 of 8 at 03:32, ~490 s/epoch, so ~03:57 UTC).

The pre-registration above is now stronger, not weaker: three more epochs of pixel-flatness have landed since it was written — 0.9704 @ e2, 0.9708 @ e3, 0.9702 @ e4, against spectral 0.7218 -> 0.5755 -> 0.4878. So 'spectrally-shaped initialisation' is not an inference from two points any more; the pixel term has not moved in FIVE epochs while the spectral term halved again. That is the thing the arm actually measures, and it is written into the arm's own header so the verdict cannot drift off it.
RESULT 2026-08-22: mae_matched = 0.6735 at epoch 3, against adapt_null 0.8240 and band_dense 0.8232 at the same epoch. Delta -0.1505. That is not a null, it is the FIFTH COLLAPSE in this family, and it lands inside the 0.63-0.73 band the arm's own header named as the floor meaning 'the weights loaded and broke the trunk' while asserting a null would not be that. The header was wrong about which band this would land in.

WHICH LINK BROKE, worked before the verdict, and the answer is NOT the harness:
  PLUMBING  cleared. adapt_null is the same --encoder-weights path with a null adaptation and reads
            0.8240, so the load path is clean; the ledger already says so at line 308.
  DATA      cleared. Same cache key as the control (336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band, stamped in the checkpoint).
  TRAINING  cleared on variant. PretrainedEncoder.into RAISES on a variant mismatch and did not fire;
            checkpoint variant 'small' equals TrainingOptions().variant default 'small', and band_dense
            names no --variant either, so the arm's byte-identity claim against the control holds.
  TEST      cleared. Matched epoch, matched control, both on the ledger, not re-run.

THE FIX I REACHED FOR WAS ALREADY RUN. pretrained_encoder.py:47-58 documents the mechanism (pretraining
rewrites the TOP block -- block 11 moved 55% and 21% of its own norm where supervision never moves it
more than 0.8% -- and the head reads that block), and argues the axis only ever concerned the BOTTOM
blocks, which is what --encoder-adapt-depth 6 states. encoder_adapt_lower IS that arm: 0.7309, and the
ledger records its diagnosis as refuted. encoder_adapt_thawed 0.7162. encoder_adapt_gentle 0.6902/0.6875.

So the family now reads across TWO pretraining objectives (SSL-adaptive and spectrally-shaped MAE) and
TWO import depths (all blocks, bottom six): 0.6735 / 0.6875 / 0.6902 / 0.7162 / 0.7309, every one of
them 0.09 to 0.15 below a control that simply starts from stock DINOv2. Consistent with knee-jk3's board
re-read, which already listed SSL-as-init CLOSED. I flagged that prior before this arm ran and ran it
anyway because the 65-minute pretrain was already spent -- correct call on sunk cost, but the arm should
have been priced as an INSTRUMENT retiring the axis, not as an improvement.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT, kept re-testable: (a) volume-native pretraining, a different asset entirely
-- the trunk is pretrained by someone else on video volumes and imported whole, so it never passes
through this repo's adapt-and-import path at all (knee-rpkw, on the card now). (b) a pixel-weighted or
much longer MAE -- but five collapses across two objectives and two depths makes this a poor bet, and it
should not take a card ahead of anything on knee-jk3's surviving list.
MECHANISM NAMED: an encoder adapted by ANY reconstruction-shaped objective in this repo hands the
classifier a top block shaped for reconstruction, and importing less of it does not help because the
damage is not additive -- encoder_adapt_lower took only blocks 0-5 and still lost 0.13.
2026-08-24 AUDIT, ledger not bead: this is already REFUTED and the bead should not have stayed P1. experiments/README.md line 309 records mae_matched (DINOv2-small, 8 epochs masked reconstruction over 402,600 knee-MRI slices, the only encoder that has seen nothing but this domain) at 0.6735 @ e3, -0.1505 vs adapt_null at matched epoch, and calls it 'the FIFTH collapse, closing the SSL-as-init family across two objectives and two import depths'. Every suspect was cleared before the verdict (plumbing: adapt_null is the same --encoder-weights path and reads 0.8240). Domain-matched MAE pretrain as an INIT is spent. What is NOT covered by that verdict: a 3D encoder that sees the volume before any per-slice feature exists (named untouched by depth_true's row). Closing this as refuted; that clause belongs in its own bead.

title: VolumeRead / the tubelet trunk is wired into model.py and has ZERO arms in the ledger
description:
AUDIT FINDING, 2026-08-22, unmeasured asset. kneemri/models/model.py:26,202,204-205 wires a VolumeRead / tubelet path — the trunk reads the stack as 3D tubelets rather than as independent slices. grep of experiments/README.md returns ZERO hits for it across 107 runs. It is the only ARCHITECTURE-SCALE axis this project has BUILT and never measured, and the owner's standing note that 'the data is 3D' points straight at it.

WHY IT MATTERS RELATIVE TO WHAT IS LEFT. Every axis measured this week landed inside a floor: encoder diversity closed (cnx_dense), FOV closed (band140), batch closed (batch_teardown, two arms), resolution flat twice at 336, adaptation closed (adapt_null + the frozen-bottom reading), the label-correlation head refuted (knee-w8h6). Data volume is the only axis that has ever cleared the bar and its slope is CONCAVE (quarter_data: each doubling buys ~0.48 of the last). A slice-independent trunk cannot represent through-plane extent at all, which is the mechanism class that could plausibly deliver 1.5% rather than a knob-sized delta.

BLOCKED BY, AND THIS IS THE REAL COST: knee-2nxh. The VRAM cap's activation_units is 2D-only — it computes (size/stride)^2 and a tubelet trunk's token count is (size/stride)^2 x frames/tubelet, so the cap under-reserves and the arm dies in the attention backward exactly as final_fit did at 392 px. Fix knee-2nxh FIRST or the arm's failure is the harness's, not the idea's.

BEFORE ARMING: python -m kneemri.experiments.arm_check, then a --studies 60 --epochs 1 smoke. Price the arm out loud before it takes the card.
PRICE: stated out loud before the card, 2026-08-22. COST ~2 h wall for 12 epochs of ViT-L at 20 slices a
study; the truncated cache and the CPU build check are already paid. GAIN if it lands: this is the last
surviving axis on knee-jk3's ledger whose mechanism is a REPRESENTATIONAL claim rather than a routing
one, and the frontier gap is 0.054, so the mechanism could plausibly deliver 1.5% where ten measured
knob axes could not. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.15, and that is the honest number: vjepa_probe already read a TIE
on frozen features, which is weak evidence against, weakened in turn because a latent-prediction
objective is not expected to be linearly separable and the probe spent the depth axis on a 3-slice
window. EXPECTED VALUE is therefore ~0.15 x 1.5% for 2 h, which does NOT beat a knob on arithmetic
alone. It takes the card anyway as an INSTRUMENT: it retires or licenses the whole 3D-trunk family that
every remaining backlog idea is downstream of (knee-pq8u, knee-ec0p, knee-jucq), and there is no cheaper
question that does that. Priced as an improvement it would be a bad buy; priced as the thing that
decides where the next ten hours go, it is the best buy on the board.
notes:
CORRECTION + UNBLOCKED, 2026-08-22. Two things in the description above are wrong and both moved the price:

1. The blocker's direction was backwards here too. The cap does not UNDER-reserve a tubelet trunk; DeviceBudget.needed multiplies by (slices + 1), so `units` is per-slice and a tubelet trunk costs grid^2/tubelet per slice — LESS. The cap OVERSTATED it 2x, so the arm would have parked in await_headroom, not died in the attention backward. knee-2nxh is now fixed (Stage/Encoder carry an explicit tubelet divisor; VJEPA2_LARGE declares tubelet=2).

2. There is no read-size choice to price. VolumeRead.check_tokens (kneemri/models/volume_read.py:87-95) asserts the read is the trunk's NATIVE crop, 256, because the spatial grid is not free the way depth is — 3D RoPE derives depth position ids at run time, the spatial weights were fitted at native//patch. So 336 was never an option, and the earlier 'does not fit even corrected' reading was pricing a size the code refuses.

DERIVED, at the only read that exists (256 px, 20 slices, batch 6, 6 blocks open):
  uncorrected  38.3 GB  -> refused on a 31.8 GB card
  corrected    21.7 GB  -> fits under a 26 GB cap with headroom
The arm is now armable. Next: python -m kneemri.experiments.arm_check, then --studies 60 --epochs 1 smoke, then price the full arm out loud before it takes the card.
ARMED AND PRICED, 2026-08-22 03:31 UTC. experiments/arms/vjepa_member.sh written and arm_check-clean.

THIRD CORRECTION, and it is larger than the first two: the tubelet path was UNARMABLE from any flag combination. Trainer.whole_stack is the only path to a window wider than GROUP = 3, and its guard demanded self.model.per_slice — which a volumetric read is not, by definition. Without it the window stays 3, which tubelet 2 does not divide, so VolumeRead.check_tokens would raise. So every number this trunk has produced here (vjepa_probe: 0.7620 vs a DINOv2-large control's 0.7669) was taken with its depth axis SPENT ON A WINDOW TOO NARROW TO CARRY IT. Fixed by moving the guard onto the model as StudyModel.check_whole_stack, which names the two different reasons a model can take a whole stack (per-slice pooling; a tubelet the window divides) instead of testing a proxy for one of them. Same bug class the per_slice docstring already recorded once (the guard tested != 'max' and silently rejected attention pooling the model supported).

FLAGS, all derived: --variant vjepa2l --pool mean --slice-pooling channels --whole-stack --slices 20 --train-size 256 --batch 6. No --vram-gb: arm_check reports a hand-typed 26 as OVERSTATED by 4.30 GB, i.e. DeviceBudget derives 21.7 — the corrected number to four figures, against a 31.8 GB card. 256 px is not a knob (native crop assert); 20 slices because tubelet 2 must divide the window; channels because it is the only non-per-slice pooling and VolumeRead.of requires one.

PRICE, out loud: ~2 h wall for 12 epochs. This is an INSTRUMENT, not an improvement — it retires or licenses the whole volume-pretraining axis that every 3D-trunk idea in the backlog sits downstream of. As a member it is priced by DISTANCE: the only candidate whose PRETRAINING DOMAIN differs from all six seated members, which is the third diversity axis after objective (sevengrade, 0.931, tie) and pixels (sevenplane, pending).

PRE-REGISTERED READ: >=0.845 says the depth axis carries what the frozen probe could not see, and the member earns a seat_value pricing against the champion five. 0.83-0.845 is the tie again, taken with the advantage actually spent, and RETIRES THE AXIS rather than the trunk. <0.82 means suspect the harness first, in this order: did --whole-stack land (trainer logs its window — 20, not 3), did VolumeRead.of build at all (it returns None SILENTLY when the config lacks tubelet_size, and the model then reads as an ordinary 2D ViT-L at 256), did six blocks open.
BUILD PRE-CLEARED ON CPU, 2026-08-22 04:00Z, before the 2 h card spend. Constructed through the real RunSetup.model path with vjepa_member.sh's exact flags (variant vjepa2l, pool mean, slice-pooling channels, train-size 256, slices 20): VolumeRead(tubelet=2, patch=16, native=256) builds, per_slice is False, check_whole_stack(20) accepts and check_whole_stack(3) refuses with the tubelet clause. Config confirms tubelet_size 2 / patch_size 16 / crop_size 256, so --train-size 256 is the trunk's native crop and not a guess.

CORRECTION to the arm header's third failure mode. It named 'VolumeRead.of returns None SILENTLY when the config lacks tubelet_size' as a thing to check after a bad number. That branch cannot fire for this trunk, and the failure mode as written is the wrong shape anyway: on a wrong config VolumeRead.of RAISES. Asked for the default pool cls_mean it says 'a tubelet trunk emits no class token'. So --pool mean in the arm is not a preference, it is the only pooling this trunk admits, and a mis-specified arm dies at construction rather than quietly training a 2D ViT-L. Post-run suspicion list is now two items, not three: did --whole-stack land (trainer logs window 20, not 3) and did six blocks open.
SMOKE CAUGHT A DEFECT, AND IT WAS NOT SUSPECT #1 (2026-08-22).

The smoke died with 'a 256x256 read over 3 frames predicts 256 tokens and the trunk emitted 256'. That
reads as '--whole-stack did not land', which is failure mode #1 in this arm's own header. It is not.

Read the traceback's frames, not its message: fitting.py:153 keep -> member_record.py:375 payload ->
model.fingerprint(read_size, GROUP, device). The training epoch had already SUCCEEDED; the 3 frames are
the FINGERPRINT's synthetic bag, whose depth is the module constant GROUP = 3 by design. Three slices is
one and a half tubelets, so check_tokens refused it. --whole-stack landed fine.

Two things made the message misleading. The guard ORs three clauses and only 'frames % tubelet' fired,
so it printed predicted 256 == emitted 256 (expected = 256 * (3//2) = 256, a coincidence). And the
failure is at the epoch-1 CHECKPOINT WRITE, which looks like a training failure in a run log.

FIX: VolumeRead.probe_frames(group) rounds the probe up to a whole tubelet (3 -> 4); Model.fingerprint
calls it only when self.volume exists. Rejected alternatives, both worse: stamping the run's window into
config['group'] would move pixel_group and split the decode of two whole-stack members that share pixels
byte for byte; deriving the probe width from member.group on the verifier side would recompute every
SEATED member's fingerprint at 20 and refuse the champion five. Deriving from the loaded trunk keeps
writer and verifier in step with nothing stored, and a 2D trunk has no VolumeRead, so every fingerprint
on disk is bit-identical.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT: nothing about the encoder. No number has been read yet. Suspect #1 of the
header (did --whole-stack land) is now CLEARED by this traceback rather than confirmed by it — the run
reached a checkpoint write, which is downstream of a full epoch at the run's own window.
SHIPPABILITY PRE-CLEARED 2026-08-23, before the run rather than after it. The mounted kit cf6a99f already carries BOTH pieces this member needs to load on Kaggle: kneemri/models/backbone.py defines VJEPA2_LARGE = 'vjepa2l' and the facebook/vjepa2-vitl-fpc64-256 entry, and kneemri/models/volume_read.py defines VolumeRead. Verified by 'git show cf6a99f:<path>', not by assuming the kit tracks main.

So if this arm returns a member worth a seat, it can be packaged and fired on the CURRENT kit -- no kit refresh, no second variable in the entry, and knee-h6lr is not a blocker for it. That was the one shipping risk left on this arm and it is now retired at zero cost.
2026-08-23 VERDICT: MISSES THE BAR. vjepa_member reached holdout 0.8343 at epoch 9/12 and died at epoch 10 (trainer exit 127, after a card-contention stall from 589 to 173 img/s while biohub's joint_detector shared the device). Trajectory 0.8296 (e5) / 0.8299 (e6) / 0.8334 (e7) / 0.8321 (e8) / 0.8343 (e9) is flat inside 0.005 across five epochs while train loss kept falling 0.8428->0.6863, so the two unrun epochs cannot deliver the 0.011 the >=0.845 bar needs. Per-label at e9: ACL 0.882, Lateral Meniscus 0.797, Medial Meniscus 0.867 - the deficit profile is UNCHANGED from the 2D members, not redistributed toward focal findings.

MECHANISM NAMED: a 3D encoder pretrained on natural VIDEO does not transfer to MRI volumes. Video pretraining teaches temporal object permanence and camera motion; an MRI stack's third axis is anatomical depth with no motion at all, so the pretext task shares no structure with the signal.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT: the 3D-encoder clause itself. A volume-native, MEDICALLY-pretrained encoder is a different asset and is untested. It also does not rule out V-JEPA2 warm-started from our own 2D weights (knee-clpy). Re-testable.

HARNESS SUSPECTS CLEARED: the run trained 10 full epochs with a falling loss and a rising-then-flat holdout, so this is not a load that fell back or a feature that never switched on. The exit-127 death is a SHIPPING failure, not a measurement one - the number at e9 is real.
2026-08-24, from the knee-yuqf closure: the case for this arm is now stronger than when it was written, because the aggregation stage has closed from a THIRD direction. depth_true ran DepthAttention and read 0.8461 - the ORDER-AWARE operator landing second-worst of four that span 0.0019, seat value -0.0002. So all three ways of extracting depth structure AFTER the encoder are flat: more slices -0.0001, more slots +0.0002, every combining rule within 0.0019. The ledger's own conclusion is that the limit is UPSTREAM, in what one slice's feature vector contains, and this arm is the only thing in the repo that changes that quantity - the trunk sees the stack before any per-slice feature exists. Every 3D idea in the backlog is downstream of the answer this arm returns, which is what makes it an instrument rather than a candidate. Next card job after distill_pairs unless distill_pairs reads >= 0.860 and licenses distill_v3base first; ~2 h, 21.7 GB, zero submission slots.
2026-08-24 CORRECTION to the note directly above: that note was written against a stale reading of this bead and is wrong where it says 'next card job'. This arm RAN on 2026-08-23 and read 0.8343 at e9, missing its own >=0.845 bar, with the mechanism named (natural-VIDEO pretraining shares no structure with anatomical depth). The saturation framing it carries is still correct and still the reason the axis mattered; the scheduling claim is void. What remains live is the residue this bead already recorded - a volume-native MEDICALLY-pretrained encoder, and knee-clpy's warm start from our own 2D weights - not a re-run of this arm.

title: adapt_null: does --encoder-weights reproduce control when the adaptation is stock?
description:
Four fine-tunes on the SSL axis collapsed (0.6902 / 0.6875 / 0.7162 / 0.7309) against band_dense 0.8578. The written verdicts blame the adaptation. The evidence does not support that attribution, and the reason is a magnitude argument nobody has made: encoder_adapt ran lr 1e-4 and moved blocks 0-5 by 3.4-8.3 percent; encoder_adapt_gentle ran lr 1e-5 and moved the same blocks by 0.46-1.79 percent, a 4x smaller perturbation. Their scores are 0.6902 and 0.6875 - a 0.0027 gap, well inside the 0.0062 floor. A cost that does not scale with the size of the change is not representational damage. It is something COMMON to both paths: the --encoder-weights load, or a preprocessing mismatch between pretrain.py and train.py.

THE CONTROL, which the axis never got: fine-tune from a NULL adaptation - stock DINOv2-small written through pretrain.py's own save path at --epochs 1 --max-steps 1 --lr 0, so AdamW's update and its decoupled decay (both scaled by lr) leave the weights bit-identical. Already written to $PROCESSED/adapt_null.pt and CONFIRMED null: encoder_drift reads 0.0000 on the stem and all twelve blocks, which validates the drift instrument against a known zero at the same time.

WHY THIS IS AN INSTRUMENT AND PRICED AS ONE. It cannot raise the score. It decides whether four collapsed arms are evidence about SSL or evidence about our harness, which is the difference between the only remaining axis with a >1.5 percent mechanism being CLOSED or REOPENED. Every knob family (decode, pooling, seats, resolution, capacity, span, calibration) is measured flat, so there is nothing else of that size to spend the card on.
notes:
PRICE: ~25 minutes of card (4 epochs at ~370 s), plus the null checkpoint and its drift read, both already spent and both clean.

P(clears 1.5%) = 0, STATED DELIBERATELY. This arm cannot move the score and is not offered as an improvement. It is an INSTRUMENT, and the base rule licenses one only when it retires a suspicion or re-opens a whole axis. It does both. Four arms and one interpretation currently attribute -0.14 to -0.17 to on-domain SSL; if the null collapses, that attribution is void and the only remaining axis with a >1.5% mechanism reopens with a named bug in front of it. If the null tracks the control, the attribution is confirmed and the axis closes on measurement rather than on suspicion, which frees the card from an axis that would otherwise keep drawing arms.

EXPECTED VALUE is therefore not this arm's own delta but the delta of what it gates: the SSL axis is the last unclosed lever priced above 1.5% (knee-c5n), and every knob family - decode, pooling, slot/seat count, resolution, capacity, span, calibration - is measured flat inside 0.0062. 25 minutes to decide the disposition of the largest remaining lever is the best ratio on the board.
ANSWERED 2026-08-22. adapt_null 0.8240 at epoch 3 against band_dense's 0.8232 at the same epoch: +0.0008, an eighth of the floor, against the ~0.19 separation the arm was written to detect. Training loss 1.2042 -> 0.8631 is the control's own trajectory, where all three collapsed encoder arms floored near the control's epoch-ZERO loss.

VERDICT: the load path is CLEAN. --encoder-weights and the preprocessing on either side of it cost nothing. Plumbing is removed as a suspect for the whole SSL family and the four collapses stand as evidence about the adaptation.

SECOND RESULT, and it keeps its value regardless: encoder_drift reads the null at 0.0000 on the stem and all twelve blocks. That is the drift instrument's first negative control, and every gate on this axis had been steered by that reading without one.

AGAINST MYSELF. The magnitude anomaly that bought the slot -- two adaptations differing FOURFOLD in blocks 0-5 drift and scoring 0.0027 apart -- is already in experiments/README.md at encoder_adapt_gentle, and there it is RESOLVED rather than merely noticed: blocks 0-5 are the wrong blocks, block 11 moved 0.5510 and 0.2144 against supervision's 0.0080 ceiling, and encoder_adapt_lower then refutes even that and lands on the frozen-bottom reading the family carries. I read lines 1320-1370 and 1455-1500 when arming and not 1401-1440. CLAUDE.md says read the ledger before filing a finding; the cost of not finishing that read is ~25 min of card, twice now.

STILL OPEN on knee-c5n, untouched by a null control: the MAE ran 6 epochs with both loss terms still falling steeply, and it was fitted on the DEFAULT 12-slice 0.20-0.80 cache while every consumer trains on 20 slices at 0.10-0.90.

title: Is the score DATA-limited? The one quantity 107 arms never varied
description:
Every measured axis is saturated: slice aggregation closed from three directions, ensemble seats capped at ~1 board tick, unfreeze depth flat past six blocks, all four CoPAS components priced out, volume-pretrained trunk ties frozen, knee-jk3's nine axes all inside 0.0062. That pattern is the finding. The one quantity never varied is how much data there is.

Every arm shows the same shape underneath: peak at epoch 5-9, then decline while train loss keeps falling. aug_long is the sharpest evidence it is not the ordinary kind -- the intensity regulariser demonstrably fired (train loss higher at every epoch past 4) and the decline did not move, -0.0169 against the control's -0.0182.

MEASUREMENT: experiments/arms/half_data.sh. band_dense's recipe on HALF the training studies, holdout untouched, read straight against the ledger's 0.8578. Costs ONE run (~36 min) because the 100% point already exists. New --train-fraction flag cuts the training side only, drawn at random and seeded by --split-seed.
