     resnet_224_short_s2026  resnet50d   0.8527
     base224                 DINOv2-B    0.8509
     native224               DINOv2-S    0.8502
   DINOv2-B over DINOv2-S is +0.0007 at matched resolution -- an eighth of the 0.0062 seed spread, i.e. indistinguishable. This is the same conclusion the bead reached by ARGUMENT (ViT-S/14 is distilled from ViT-g/14, so S is a compression of the giant and the RadioDino +0.0106 width gain does not transfer inside the DINOv2 family), now with a number behind it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RANKING. P(clears 0.0062) drops from the stated 0.08 to ~0.04, and PRICE stays ~7.7 h. At an expected gain under +0.0006 for 7.7 h of card this is the worst ratio among open levers and must not be armed on 'the trunk is the obvious next thing' -- which is exactly the instinct the bead was written to serve.

NOT CLOSED, and the residual is honest: the 224 reading is at a resolution nobody ships (the stack runs 336), and the width term could in principle turn where the recipe actually lives. Re-opening it needs that argument made explicitly against these three numbers, not a re-quote of the +0.0106.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It is not evidence that trunk capacity is irrelevant -- knee-fvzvm's close reason calls the decode toll REPRESENTATION-BOUND, which points AT the representation. It says the DINOv2 S->B step is not the way to buy more of it.

title: Confident-wrong residual: view, clustering, compartment-confusion and co-occurrence smear all null
description:
Four hypotheses about the champion's 53 confidently-wrong cells, all closed on CPU with no card and no slot (2026-09-17).

1. VIEW. PF OA read as 5 of the top 10 confident FNs; PF OA is patellofemoral, the crop is centred on the joint, so crop_mm/centre (VIEW_AXES) were the suspect. study_render draws the trainer's own cache: the patella is plainly present in both confident FNs (pred 0.018, 0.026) and in the TP control, whole in anterior sagittals and centred in the axial stack. Field of view is NOT the mechanism. Caveat: the render samples 5 evenly-spaced slices per slot, so it proves presence, not lesion absence.

2. CLUSTERING. 5-of-10 was a top-ten count, not a rate. Over each label's own positives against the pooled 0.0486: PF OA 12/168 = 0.0714, p=0.1189 (NOT significant; it is simply the most common positive label). Lateral OA 9/48 = 0.1875, p=0.000451, survives Bonferroni at 12 labels. Medial OA 0/103. Denominator error, fourth occurrence.

3. COMPARTMENT CONFUSION. Hypothesis: model detects tibiofemoral OA and assigns the compartment by prior. Refuted: on the 9 confident Lateral OA FNs the medial prediction averages 0.231, exceeds 0.5 in 1 of 9, and 1 of 9 is medial-positive in truth. It calls the knee clean, it does not misfile the side.

4. CO-OCCURRENCE SMEAR. Lateral OA AUC 0.8067 medial-negative (n=576) vs 0.7267 medial-positive (n=333), gap +0.0799, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0020,+0.1628], P(gap<=0)=0.0295 - marginal. Oracle ceiling for PERFECT lateral ranking in that stratum: macro 0.8679 -> 0.8790, i.e. +0.0111, under the bar before discounting. Swept over all 12 labels against their most co-occurring partner: 8 of 12 degrade, coin null p=0.194, four IMPROVE, median gap +0.0150. The 0.9249 aggregate oracle is IN-SAMPLE (strata selected by the sign of their own gap on this holdout) and must not be quoted.

All AUCs midpoint cut. Holdout ReportFolds(folds=5, seed=2026), n=909. Write-up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-17_one_member_equals_eight.md, section 'Looking at the pixels kills the view hypothesis'.

title: MEASURED: no train/deploy divergence — the two paths agree to 0.00004 macro AUC
description:
Owner's standing MUST-FIX axis ('if you find divergence between what we validate and what we deploy, we MUST fix it'). Measured 2026-09-17, not argued.

METHOD: copied labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026.pt + its .metrics.jsonl to a probe dir, ran holdout_backfill --device cuda there (it reads through Member, the type the submission path uses), and diffed the derived .holdout.npz against the array the trainer itself wrote. 909 of 909 studies joined by name; truth arrays byte-identical.

per-cell |delta|   max 0.016822   mean 0.000964   p99 0.006409   (fp16 eps 9.77e-04)
macro AUC          trained 0.867917   derived 0.867955   delta +0.000038
worst label        Lateral OA +0.0004, against the 0.0062 paired floor

VERDICT: no divergence on this member. Offline-to-board gap is the ruler and the truth, not the inference path. board_transfer's slope already prices that.

DEFECT FIXED IN PASSING: holdout_backfill's docstring asserted 'roughly 4x eps' and called it 'WIDER than the +/-0.016 half-widths a paired floor quotes'. Two different UNITS read as one number — a per-cell prediction delta is not a score half-width, and the per-cell max happens to be ~0.016 which is what made the confusion invisible. Real figures: 17x eps per cell, 0.00004 on the score. Docstring now carries the measurement.

SCOPE: one member, one device. witness_check reads 1.6-2.4x eps on four members and 5.8x on the project's largest trunk, so a deeper member may diverge further. The DERIVED stamp stays — it records provenance, not a tolerance.

Probe dir D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/backfill_probe/ can be deleted; log at logs/backfill_probe.log.

within-study cross-label ordering    side_dense     0.7937  -0.0641 vs band_dense 0.8578 (README:2754)

side_dense is a CONFIRMED-MECHANISM negative, not a null: recipe stamp side_weight=1.0; smoke loss 1.9368 vs control ~1.2, excess exactly softplus(0); VRAM and s/epoch byte-identical as a no-parameter term must be. The contrast then moved as predicted (Lateral OA 0.5141->0.5759, Medial OA 0.7416->0.7962) and ALL TWELVE labels fell, ten of them past the 0.0062 floor.

THE LAW, and it prices every future loss idea for free: the metric ranks study-against-study WITHIN a label; a within-study term orders label-against-label. Two orthogonal orderings over the same logits — buying one COSTS the other rather than composing. A loss term is worth arming here only if its ordering is the metric's own.

Weight sweep DECLINED: PRICE ~1.2 h for weight 0.3, P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.02 — the result says the SIGN of the trade is wrong, not its size.

NOT ruled out: the side-blindness OBSERVATION (Lateral OA at chance on all eight members; knee-yrg refuted four data-side explanations) and the fact that side IS recoverable from this representation. What is refuted is getting it out of the loss for free. Term survives as a small-weight regulariser on a head that SEES position, read on per-label AUC not on the contrast.

ALSO: side_blindness is now a CONFOUNDED tool on any run trained WITH a side term — its neutral control column (PF OA 0.4274/0.3498 under the arm vs 0.4770/0.4133 under control) moves although the term puts zero gradient there. Indirect coupling through the shared encoder. It can audit a run trained WITHOUT a side term only.

ALSO, self-correction: the 13:1 confident-FN:FP asymmetry is calibration, not ranking. AUC is rank-only, so where a column places its threshold cannot move the score. Worth zero on this competition.

title: pricetop/foldseven is a pool-identity effect, not a transfer-curve violation
description:
BLOCKER RESOLVED, and not the way it was framed. "One offline point, six board points" (pricetop_v1
0.8757 -> 0.938 vs foldseven_v1 0.8767 -> 0.944) was read as a violation of the transfer curve. It is
not. Diffed 2026-09-17 00:18Z: the two entries share exactly ONE member. pricetop is
blendhold / margin_seat / oof_teacher / warm_calib_lowlr / labelwise_drop; foldseven is
calib_dense_hold / calib_span / stack_increments / through_dense / three labelwise_*_long. They are
near-disjoint ensembles, not a seat swap, so there is no seat to blame and nothing to fix in either.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY MEASURES. Their offline gap is +0.0010, which is a SIXTH of the 0.0062 holdout noise
floor: our ruler does not distinguish these two pools at all. The board separates them by 0.006, three
times its own 0.0020 blur. Tonight's leg 1 (56288555) measured the board's identical-entry scatter at
0.000, so that 0.006 is real. Put beside leg 2 (56288513: add one seat to an existing pool, +0.0002
offline, 0.000 board) the pair of readings says something neither says alone -- board movement at fixed
offline tracks POOL IDENTITY, not pool quality on our ruler. Perturb a pool slightly and the board does
not move; replace it wholesale at the same offline and the board moves 0.006.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CONSTANT (knee-xz903). board_transfer's slope may be applied WITHIN a family and not
ACROSS one. The +1.44 top-band slope converts an offline gain into board points for a move that keeps the
pool's identity -- a better seat of the same kind, a better-trained member. It does NOT price swapping to
a different family of seats, where a 0.0010 offline difference bought 0.006 board in one direction and
could as easily buy -0.006 in the other. This is a scope limit on the number filed four minutes ago, and
it is the reason that number is filed with a family attached.

NO HEADROOM CLAIM. The champion is already in the foldseven family, which is the side that transferred
BETTER, so this explains pricetop's shortfall rather than offering us 0.006. n=1 pair, and the honest
statement is "our ruler is blind to an axis worth about 0.006 board", not "we know which side to pick" --
we know it for exactly these two pools and by construction we are already on the good one.

title: band_coverage: --band-low/--band-high never reached the worker
description:
PRE-EXISTING, found during the audit dedup 2026-09-16 and FIXED by it.

core/data/corpus/band_coverage.py accepted --band-low/--band-high on its parser, recorded them in the report header, and then built its SlotReader inside the worker from the module default FULL_BAND. So every run of that tool measured the DEFAULT band while printing the band the flag asked for -- the plumbing failure CLAUDE.md names: 'a value recorded in a config while the consumer reads a constant'. Any coverage number quoted from a non-default --band invocation is a number about the default band.

FIX (in this refactor): BandCoverage is now a frozen dataclass carrying its Band, and measure_study is a BOUND METHOD rather than a staticmethod, so the flag travels to the worker through the pickled instance. CorpusAudit.drawn also takes a reading= override for exactly this class of flag. Same pattern applied to CropLaterality(crop_mm).

STILL OPEN: nothing checks that a flag LANDED. Every audit that grows a geometry flag can re-introduce this silently. A cheap guard would be for Reading.line -- which now prints the geometry under the denominator sentence -- to be asserted against the parsed arguments in each main, or for drawn() to refuse an argparse namespace carrying a geometry key the Reading does not match.

title: priceable_blend recommends members that are declined or on no shelf, so its headline blend is not a shippable entry
description:
Caught 2026-09-16 while building the knee-hr499 instrument, one step before a kit was built on it.

priceable_blend's greedy forward selection ranges over every member carrying a holdout record. Two properties it never consults:
  - PACKAGED: is the member on comp/members.roster or comp/members2.roster? A kernel names members out of what is MOUNTED, and KernelRun DROPS one it cannot mount and keeps going - the farseat_v1 defect, which shipped six of seven named members and read the sixth-member entry's exact score for five days.
  - DECLINED: is it argued against in comp/members.declines? That file is where seat decisions are recorded, and a decline is a standing argument.

Measured on today's run: the printed 7-member blend at offline 0.8792 includes labelwise_dense_drop40_long36_s2026, which is on NEITHER shelf and IS declined (declines:1240, as a strictly-worse duplicate of its own rostered 24-epoch twin). So the tool's headline number describes an entry that cannot be built, and the failure is silent in the direction that costs a slot: had the kit been built on that list, KernelRun would have dropped the seat, produced a valid submission.csv, scored it, and written a board row under a name for a 7-seat entry that was really 6.

WHY THIS IS NOT roster_check's JOB. roster_check guards the POOL (every scoreable checkpoint is rostered or declined in writing) and it passes clean - 0 undocumented. The hole is one step later: nothing checks that a member a TOOL PROPOSES is shippable. run_check catches it only AFTER the slot is spent, from the kernel log.

FIX SCOPE: priceable_blend filters its candidate pool to packaged-and-not-declined by default, and takes a flag to range wider when the question is about the pool rather than about an entry. Where a declined member would have been selected, PRINT the decline's reason rather than dropping it silently - the reason is the argument a re-opening has to answer, and it is the most useful thing the tool could say at that moment.

Note --members is NOT a candidate-pool filter: it evaluates the given set as one blend. That is how the six-seat replacement was priced (0.8785), and it is also why this is a real defect rather than an operator error - there is no flag that asks the question correctly.

title: Does the control LOO sweep's +0.0253 actually compose? Strip all five knobs at once
description:
knee-rn9py priced five fragments of probe224_control one at a time: nodrop -0.0005, maxpool -0.0063, nocalib -0.0100, norank -0.0054, nofloor -0.0031, running total +0.0253. That total is an ARITHMETIC claim, not a measurement -- it assumes the five are additive, which knee-3tk4b measured on this family but not for THIS set. I have already written the +0.0253 account into the knee-rn9py bead, so the claim is load-bearing and untested.

ctl_stripall removes all five in one arm, same cache (224px/12sl/0.2-0.8), same ruler (909 rows, report_labels_v2), same 12 epochs, against probe224_control_s2026 0.8914.

PRE-REGISTERED BRANCHES, written before the run:
 - lands 0.8630-0.8690 (i.e. 0.8661 +/- ~0.003): additive composition HOLDS, the +0.0253 account stands as written.
 - lands above 0.8750: the fragments OVERLAP, +0.0253 double-counts, and the knee-rn9py note must be corrected.
 - lands below 0.8570: the fragments INTERACT super-additively; the recipe is more than the sum of its knobs, which is a different and larger claim than the one I made.

This is an INSTRUMENT. It cannot raise a score -- it strips a recipe. Its whole value is that it can FALSIFY a number I already wrote down, and it is the only arm in the sweep that can.

PRICE: ~0.2 h
P(clears 0.8630-0.8690) ~ 0.60
notes: RESULT, 03:35-03:45Z, 909 rows, convergence_check CONVERGED (peak e9 of 12 -- the only arm in this family tonight that is not undertrained, which makes sense: a stripped recipe has less to learn). ledger75 0.8645 against control 0.8914. Additive prediction was 0.8914 - 0.0253 = 0.8661; measured lands 0.0016 BELOW that, inside the pre-registered 0.8630-0.8690 band. FIRST BRANCH FIRES: additive composition HOLDS. The five knobs measured together remove +0.0269, against +0.0253 predicted by summing the five separate arms -- a hair super-additive, well inside the band and far inside noise. CONSEQUENCE: the +0.0253 running total in knee-rn9py is no longer arithmetic over five arms, it is a measured quantity, and the account of what separates this recipe from the .903 reference stands as written. This was the only arm in the sweep that could have falsified a number already written down, and it did not.

title: arm_check TWIN misses a twin that lives in a default the other arm never spells
description: knee-eduxz queued probe224_control with --set optim.ema=false. That is probe224_control flag for flag -- the control never sets ema, and the default is False -- so it was a card slot for a second name for one recipe, exactly what the TWIN rule exists to refuse (knee-7uoq). arm_check passed it clean. The rule compares the arms' SPELLED flags and config layers; this twin is only visible in the RESOLVED recipe, where an explicit --set lands on the value a default already held. It caught the same arm earlier for a different reason (a malformed multi-pair --set left only mixup, which made it a literal twin of probe224_grand_nomixup) -- so the check works when the duplication is spelled and misses it when it is resolved. FIX: resolve each arm's config stack plus its --set overrides into the same dict the trainer stamps, and compare THOSE, not the argv. The trainer already writes exactly that dict as the 'recipe:' line of every full log, so the shape is proven and the comparison is a dict equality. PRICE: ~0.7 h, no card. P(clears) n/a -- this is a check defect, priced as the card it protects: a twin costs a full arm slot, and this is the second time one has reached the card in a week.

title: Full-depth study cache + processed dir layout: replace band/slice-count cache copies
description:
Owner 2026-09-14: processed/rsna_knee_abnormality is 528 GB, flat, and misstructured.

PROBLEM
1. Every Band x slices x size x scheme choice writes its own decoded array (18 images_*.npy = 485 GB). Slice picks are linspace(low, high, n).astype(int) over the band (core/data/corpus/slot_reader.py:126), so 12sl is NOT a subset of 20sl and 0.2-0.8 is NOT cuttable from a 0.1-0.9 file: each cache stores the picks already applied.
2. The dir mixes caches, features, subsets, predictions, kaggle build output (wheels, kit, kernel_logs, leaderboard, dry_run) and foreign models (rad-dino + raddino-hf) at one level, because every producer names its own path under DataRoot.processed().

DESIGN
- Store each routed series ONCE at full depth, cropped + resized, per (image_size, crop, scheme). Select slices (band, count, spacing incl. Spread dedupe/pad) at LOAD time. Byte-identical to the old caches iff the resize is per-slice (verify first).
- Size variants stay separate: 336->224 at load is not byte-identical to 224 from source.
- One layout object in core/paths owns every subdir name; consumers never spell paths. Layout: processed/.../cache/images, cache/features, subsets, predictions; models/.../foreign, models/.../kaggle.
- Migration: move script + path change in one commit.

PROOF
Equality check: for every existing images_* cache, load-time selection from the full-depth file reproduces the array bit-for-bit on all studies (or on a 60-study sample, then full). A member's holdout re-read matches its recorded .holdout.npz.

FIRST STEP
Measure in-band series depth distribution -> real full-depth size (estimate unverified: ~80-90 GB for 336 canonical vs ~233 GB of variants). Time one full-depth decode (owner expects decode is cheap relative to training).

  KMAR-50K (raw/kmar50k) -- ArtifactData_part1 (698 files) PAIRED BY EXACT FILENAME with GroundTruthData_part1

  (file_prostate_AXT2_001.h5, PIRADS). Not knee. Lane dropped before a bead was spent on it.

(merged_corpus, merged3_corpus) POOLED foreign studies into OUR label space and trained one head on the union.
None of the three uses below does that. They add a supervision KIND our corpus does not contain -- where a
finding is, which slice it is on, and what the same anatomy looks like corrupted -- and our label space is
untouched. The concave data-volume slope prices VOLUME; none of this is volume.

WHY NOW. The cross-site pass of 2026-09-12 measured the pool's generalisation toll at -0.0336 +/- 0.0038 and
found the board unreachable by better solos (board_transfer +0.74 in-regime, no pair resolving above 0.8679).

shares, and the two candidates are brittleness to acquisition shift (KMAR is that shift WITH ground truth
attached) and a pooling stage that is learned with zero supervision on which slice matters (fastMRI+ says which).

title: MedicalNet/Med3D 3D-ResNet50: the only clean distant PRETRAINING, and the only lane left aimed at the 0.8696 needle
description:
ASSET ON DISK 2026-09-12T13:36Z at D:/data/raw/medicalnet (353 MB, from royceplayz/rsna-medicalnet-resnet50-weights). Licence MIT per the README shipped inside it (Kaggle tags the dataset Apache 2.0; either way permissive, no NC, no share-alike). Files: resnet_50_23dataset.pth (the 23-dataset aggregate, the distant one) and resnet_50.pth.

CHECKPOINT SHAPE, read with weights_only=True. 318 tensors, DataParallel 'module.' prefix, no wrapper keys, NO classifier head -- a pure trunk. 53 five-dimensional tensors; conv1.weight is (64, 1, 7, 7, 7), i.e. genuine single-channel 3D volumetric convolution, full ResNet-50 depth through layer4 to 2048 channels.

WHY THIS AND NOTHING ELSE. Three P0s converge. knee-gcgbk: eleven distinct seatings -- six, seven and eight seats, different member sets -- all land on exactly 0.944, so our two-thirds of the blend cannot move the sum and reseating is retired as a submission category. knee-0v8yz: only solo-level member quality at count 1 has ever moved this board 0.005+. knee-iw21t: the solo required to reach the leader is ~0.8696 while our ceiling over 296 honest members is 0.8685 -- the target sits PAST the max of everything ever trained, and everything ever trained shares one feature space.

WHY IT IS NOT THE CLOSED FOREIGN LANE. knee-zkfin's notes close foreign MOUNTS on three independent rulers: pilkwang's 20-checkpoint system blends NEGATIVE at every weight with fitted optimum w=0, and a foreign ENSEMBLE is less distant than its own members because averaging contracts them. This is not a mount. It is a PRETRAINING: we fine-tune it on our own train split and hold out our own 909, so its offline score is HONEST and may enter the ledger -- the one thing no raptor, pilkwang or coat number can ever be, all of which are in-sample on our holdout by construction (raptor_v4_swa reads 0.9484 offline against 0.923 on the board, ~+0.025 of inflation).

DISTANCE ARGUMENT. Volumetric 3D conv on a single grayscale channel versus our entire pool's 2D-per-slice DINOv2/v3 plus slice-pooling. Every RadImageNet route is NC-SA blocked upstream, so after that exclusion this is the only distant pretraining we are permitted to use at all.

OPEN QUESTION BEFORE ANY CARD TIME: our trainer is built around a 2D per-slice encoder plus a slice-pooling stage, and a 3D trunk consumes the whole stack at once, replacing BOTH. The integration cost is the thing to price first -- a recon of the encoder abstraction is in flight.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-12T14:23Z, FROZEN READOUT ONLY. Cache (4407, 6, 1, 2048) built end to end; probe on fold-0 holdout909, own ridge penalty per trunk.

  medicalnet@mean  (layer4, dim 2048)  0.7348
  medicalnet3@mean (layer3, dim 1024)  0.7499
  ortholarge@mean  (dinov3-vitl16)     0.8170   <- CONTROL, reproduced its ledger value EXACTLY in the same run

ALL FOUR PRE-REGISTERED HARNESS SUSPECTS CLEARED before the verdict was written:
1. penalty at the grid edge -- re-swept 1e-5..100, still 0.001, an INTERIOR optimum.
2. mean/max/moments byte-identical -- degenerate BY CONSTRUCTION on a depth-1 volumetric cache (mean==max, the moments std half is all zeros). Not a bug.
3. read depth / segmentation dilations -- layer4 runs dilation 4 and layer3 dilation 2, so the stage was the one suspect that could reopen the axis. Built a second cache off layer3: +0.0151, real and directional, and nowhere near the 0.8170 needed.
4. intensity preparation / depth resample -- prepared() dumped on REAL studies (not random pixels): unit z-score per slot (mean -0.0000, std 1.0000), ranges -2.5..5.8, frac_nonzero 0.985..0.250 falling with slot as slot presence does. Sound.

SEAT VALUE, ledger75, against cleanseat_v1 (0.942, 6 members):
  +ortholarge   -0.0001  [-0.0014, +0.0012]
  +medicalnet3  -0.0025  [-0.0041, -0.0006]
  +medicalnet   -0.0028  [-0.0047, -0.0010]
All three read DISTINCT on the member axes (maha 3.72-3.80 against a roster boundary of 3.36) -- so the distance argument in the description SURVIVES; distance is real and it does not pay. 0 of 3 clear the +0.0040 bar.

WHAT IS CLOSED: the FROZEN-READOUT use of this asset, on both rulers. The capacity confound ortho_diffusion pre-registered is REMOVED FROM THE OTHER SIDE -- 2048 is wider than dinov2-large's 1024 and it still loses by 0.067 -- so the volumetric loss is closed on MECHANISM, not on width.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, and why this is P2 rather than closed: a frozen probe prices a FEATURE SPACE, not a fine-tune. The control is the proof -- ortholarge frozen reads 0.8170 while our fine-tuned dinov3 members read 0.85-0.868, so the frozen reading under-prices a fine-tune substantially. The fine-tune lane is DEFERRED ON PRICE, not refuted: a 3D ResNet-50 fine-tune is ~4-6 h of card, it would have to close 0.067 of frozen gap AND then clear +0.0040 of seat bar from a position that currently prices -0.0028. Re-open it by answering that ratio, never by re-quoting the distance.

title: The public foreign-weights ecosystem is unmounted: seven+ authors, none but dreaddevelopment ever tried
description:
FOUND 2026-09-12 by pulling six top public kernels (kaggle kernels pull, zero slot). Every leading public kernel mounts the SAME set of foreign weight datasets, from at least seven distinct authors, and this project has only ever mounted dreaddevelopment's raptor checkpoints.

THE SET: marwanmath/resnet-50-radimagenet-marwan (RadImageNet ResNet-50 -- almost certainly the owner's 'resnet that allegedly gets 0.936'); antoinegg1/rsna-knee-e9-radimagenet-heads-v15 and e11-diverse-heads-v20; prvsiyan/rsna-knee-v52-radimagenet-heads-20260812; pilkwang/rsna-knee-weights; mattiaangeli/knee-mri-fold-weights and rsna-knee-coat-resgated-ep10-top3; royceplayz/rsna-medicalnet-resnet50-weights; tonylica/rsna-knee-bend-dinov3-0917-repro-assets.

WHY THIS IS THE LEVER AND NOT ANOTHER SEAT. Two measurements landed today. (1) Averaging is a CONTRACTION: six-member ensembles of our pool are 0.9725 correlated with each other, a seat built to MINIMISE internal correlation lands 0.9799 correlated with the by-score seat, so reseating our own pool is retired on both objectives. (2) External DATA did not buy decorrelation: fastMRI, MRNet and the merged corpora all sit INSIDE the pool's ordinary correlation spread and all lose at 1/3. What made raptor pay (+0.003 on the board despite being WORSE solo, 0.923 vs 0.941) is a foreign PIPELINE, not a foreign dataset. RadImageNet pretraining is a different feature space from DINOv2/v3 -- the largest pipeline distance available.

IT ALSO EXPLAINS fleettwo. That entry read 0.942 against 0.944 with a SECOND foreign seat -- but the second seat was another dreaddevelopment checkpoint, same author, same pipeline, so it bought weight without distance. A second foreign seat from a DIFFERENT author has never been tried and is not priced by fleettwo's null.

CONSTRAINTS BEFORE ANY OF THIS SHIPS. (a) LICENCE. The owner's standing gate is licence-clean; each dataset's licence must be read before mounting, and package_members.py:111-124 has a known licence-tag-gate hole. (b) IN-SAMPLE. Every one of these is trained on the competition train set, which contains our 909 holdout, so NO offline score from them may enter the ledger -- raptor_v4_swa reads 0.9484 offline and 0.923 on the board, about +0.025 of inflation. title: card_check is blind to our INFERENCE jobs: two of ours held the card and it said one
description: 2026-09-11 10:02Z the PC froze. Win32_Process showed TWO rsna_knee GPU jobs: pid 58012 (kneemri.training.train, calib_hold_clean_distill, 20.2 GB RSS) and pid 58416 (kneemri.inference.holdout_backfill, 19.1 GB RSS, plus child 22604). Combined RSS left 2.6 GB of 98 GB physical free and Windows paged. card_check ran at 10:00:37Z and printed 'OK: at most one of our jobs holds this card', listing only 58012 and the LibreOffice co-tenant. It asks the device for compute PIDs but classifies ours by an argv pattern that matches the trainer only, so every inference entrypoint (holdout_backfill, foreign_gate, member sweeps) is counted as not-ours or not at all. The check whose entire purpose is to block two of ours on one card cannot see half our GPU entrypoints. Fix: classify by the venv path / repo root in CommandLine, not by the training module name. Note the cost is exactly what the docstring predicts: card at 32041 MiB and 212 W of 575 at '100 percent utilisation', and the arm's own log reads 'peak memory 51.00 GB reserved, 21.51 GB allocated' with epoch 10 at 4386s.
notes:
DIAGNOSIS WRONG, EVIDENCE RIGHT, AND THE FREEZE HAD A DIFFERENT CAUSE. Re-priced 2026-09-11 12:04Z.

(1) The proposed fix is ALREADY the implementation. 'classifies ours by an argv pattern that matches the
trainer only' is not true: Holder.ours (card_check.py:123-131) returns
normalised(repo) in normalised(command) -- the repo root in the command line, exactly what this bead
asks for. card_check.py:43 records that the venv-path variant was considered and rejected on purpose
(it is the wrong check on a second checkout). holdout_backfill launched from this tree matches
identically to a trainer. So no misclassification could have occurred, and the fix as written is a no-op.

(2) THE REAL HOLE IS SINGLE-SOURCE ENUMERATION. holders() (:198) builds its list from
report.compute_pids() ALONE. A job the driver omits from its process table is not misclassified -- it is
never constructed, so ours() cannot see it and the count cannot reach two. That matches this bead's own
evidence better than misclassification does: the output listed 58012 and LibreOffice and did not mention
58416 in any category, not even as shared. nvidia-smi's WDDM process table is the unreliable component.

(3) AND THE FREEZE ITSELF WAS THE VRAM CEILING DEFECT, now fixed in d212242d (see knee-88s24). This
bead quotes 'peak memory 51.00 GB reserved, 21.51 GB allocated' as a symptom; that 30 GB of unbacked
reservation IS the sysmem spill, it lands in the process's RSS, and it is why two jobs whose real
allocation was ~21 GB each could exhaust 98 GB of physical RAM. The cap now lands at 29.8 GB of 31.8
(verified in the relaunched arm's log), so the spill no longer happens and the same two jobs would not
page. card_check's blindness made it unable to WARN; it did not cause the freeze.

(4) THE FIX NEEDS A DISCRIMINATOR, AND A NAIVE ONE BREAKS EVERY ARM. Measured just now off
Win32_Process: an arm runs TWO python.exe out of .venv-arm -- pid 60480 at 0.00 GB RSS (the launcher)
and 56612 at 3.03 GB (the trainer). Sourcing holders from the process table without a filter would
therefore report OVERSUBSCRIBED on every single normal arm, which is the false refusal card_check.py:126
names as the worst failure mode this tool has. A resident-set floor separates them cleanly: the two
jobs in this bead held 20.2 and 19.1 GB, a loaded CUDA context pins GB host-side, and every non-GPU
repo process measured here (listeners, gates, card_check itself) sits under 0.05 GB.

REMAINING WORK, and it is smaller than this bead as filed: add a SECOND source to holders() -- our own
processes from the process table above an RSS floor, merged by pid with the driver's list so a job in
both is counted once -- and derive the floor from a measurement rather than picking it. Do NOT change
ours(). Do not do it mid-arm: it cannot be tested without deliberately reproducing a driver omission,
and a regression here blocks launches.

title: The 24,371 series are NOT 5.5x more views — they are the slots, underfilled. Only 3,037 are spare
description:
PRICE: 20 seconds of pandas, no card. It retires a lever I was about to price at a full rebuild, and it explains a measured null that has been sitting unexplained.

THE CLAIM I WAS ABOUT TO BUILD ON. Our own corpus holds 24,371 acquired series over 4,407 studies, 5.53 per study, against the one volume per study we train on. That reads as a 5.5x view budget sitting unused inside the competition's own licence -- the last data-shaped lever after the foreign corpora closed on licence (knee-lsqnm). It is wrong, and the arithmetic is one groupby.

MEASURED 2026-09-11 off raw/rsna_knee_abnormality/train_series.csv. A slot keys on the acquisition TYPE -- Anatomical_Plane, Fat_Suppression, Fluid_Sensitive -- so the question is how many series a study has BEYOND one per distinct type:

  series per study        mean 5.53   median 5   p90 7   max 14
  distinct type combos    mean 4.84   median 5   p90 6   max 6
  SPARE (same type twice) mean 0.69   median 0   p90 2   max 8

Studies with at least one spare: 1,936 of 4,407. Total spare series: 3,037.

SO THE EXTRA SERIES ARE THE SLOTS. 4.84 distinct types against a six-slot stack means the stack is UNDERFILLED, not overfilled. The genuine surplus is 3,037 acquisitions over 44% of studies -- about +12% of view budget, unevenly spread -- and not +450%.

THIS EXPLAINS A NULL THAT WAS RECORDED WITHOUT ONE. extended_slots took routing from 6 to 9 slots, added 1,139 coronal series, and scored +0.0002 (README:324, filed REFUTED). The ledger reads that as refuting the physics of showing the model more coronal series. On these numbers it refutes less than that: there was very little to add, because a median study has ZERO spare acquisitions and the sixth slot is already empty for most of the corpus. The null is real; its scope is narrower than written.

CONSEQUENCE FOR M324-Q1, which I asked the researcher this morning. The question -- multi-view as CHANNELS versus multi-view as SAMPLES -- is still a fair mechanism question, but its SIZE here is not 5.5x. Treating each series as its own labelled sample would multiply gradient steps by about 5.5 while multiplying distinct VIEWS by about 1.12, and most of that 5.5 is re-presenting the same six acquisitions the slot stack already stacks. Do not price it as a corpus multiplication.

WHAT THIS LEAVES OPEN, and it is a different axis from slot COUNT. The slots are underfilled (4.84 of 6) and slots.py:87 records that 9.9% of acquired series match no canonical slot at all. Filling the stack is a ROUTING repair, and routing repair has never been tested -- extended_slots tested adding slots on top, which is the opposite move. Whether the unrouted 9.9% can be mapped onto the six existing slots is a question about the canonical-type vocabulary, costs no card to answer, and is the only remaining in-licence data lever I can still name.

title: TrainerRecord.instead_of gates on slab.corpus.slices, the SOURCE depth — knee-kcvma's family, latent
description:
M261 audit, done inline because the researcher lane is down. Sweep of every consumer of a source shape attribute and every HoldoutSlab subclass.

(a) SAME DEFECT, latent: kneemri/inference/trainer_record.py:63

    if window != member.window(slab.corpus.slices, overlap=False):
        return None

The method takes a SLAB and asks its source corpus how deep it is, while the caller sized its window against what the slab SERVES. That is knee-kcvma's exact shape: a value taken from an object's source where the consumer needs what the object serves, with nothing asserting the two agree. MappedSlab is the subclass where they differ (his 44 against our 12 or 20).

WHY IT IS NOT BITING TODAY, stated so the re-test is possible rather than assumed:
  - ForeignReadout.scored (foreign_readout.py:144) deliberately calls predict, not cached, so no reshaping slab reaches this line. The reason is written at the call site: cached keys on the checkpoint and the studies and NOT on the pixels, so it would answer a shifted pass with the native probabilities and report exactly zero.
  - Were one to reach it, the foreign leg carries HIS study names, so the rows lookup two lines below would return None anyway.
Both are accidents of the current callers, not properties of this method. The failure mode when it does bite is the dangerous direction: instead_of decides 'the record answers this reading' from member + window + studies and NEVER from what the slab serves, so a slab whose pixels differ from the trainer's while its names and depth match would be handed the trainer's own array and score exactly native by construction.

(b) SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: kneemri/evaluation/foreign_slots.py:17 SlotsKept. It overrides batch only, blanking slots in place; the shape is untouched, so the inherited depth == corpus.slices is correct. Note it is safe on the DEPTH axis only -- it is the slab whose pixels differ from the trainer's while its names and depth match exactly, i.e. the precise input that would expose the line above if the readout ever routed it through cached.

(b) SAFE: the four attribution/attention/oof callers (attention_readout.py:271, attribution.py:461, attribution_faithfulness.py:280, oof_oracle.py:280) pass member.window(corpus.slices) with a base HoldoutSlab, where served and source are the same object's number.

Fix: instead_of should take the depth from slab.depth, the property added for knee-kcvma, and the mirror test should build a MappedSlab whose corpus.slices differs from its depth and assert the record is refused.

title: encoder_drift's relative column was read across blocks and the shape was the stock norms
description: blocks() divides by each block's own stock norm, and on dinov2-small those norms run 69.8 (b4) to 204.6 (b11) with a 167.5 spike at b3 - 2.9x, not flat. So a constant absolute change prints as a falling curve. Reading adapt_small_e8_unitfix off the ratio alone gave a '4.7x monotone early-heavy slope' that is 1.8x and non-monotone in absolute terms (b11 above b9 and b10; b3's dip was entirely its own norm). That profile was written into a letter as a mechanism for a live arm's -0.0885 gap before the denominator was checked. FIXED: pairs() yields the squared norms both columns are built from, changes() returns the undivided one, and report() prints both on every line. The relative column remains the only honest one ACROSS encoders and the absolute the only honest one WITHIN one. Same family as knee-f9aao: a number quoted without the population it was computed over.

title: Ledger75Row carries between_cut, so a recut-blind pair cannot read as a measured zero
description: D245's recommendation, implemented 2026-09-08. Ledger75Row gained between_cut (truth cells in [MIDPOINT, RECUT)) and recut_blind(); LedgerSeventyFive.between() computes it in row(). The refusal lives on the ROW and not on macro()/scorer(), because a pool's combined score stays legitimate when one member in it is blind and a scorer-layer refusal would void the whole pool for one probe. Criterion is truth MASS, never a level count - verified from the other side on the real pool: 260 members with records, 0 recut-blind, and the eight lowest absolute counts are all 12-study smokes whose FRACTION is 0.1528 against the 909-study median of 0.121, i.e. more recut-sensitive per cell, not less. A level count would have refused exactly that set. The guard is therefore prospective: nothing in the pool today is blind, and a future probe record cannot enter the ledger with a moved() of 0.0000 that is construction wearing a measurement's clothes.

title: [bug] encoder_drift CONCENTRATION_BLOCKS is legislated at 4 and justified by a flag the trainer does not define
description: D246 sec6. encoder_drift.py:44-49 sets CONCENTRATION_BLOCKS = 4 with the docstring reason 'that is what --unfreeze-depth opens by default'. There is no --unfreeze-depth in the trainer: the string appears in two docstrings (encoder_drift.py:47, spectral_mae.py:4) and in three encoder_adapt arms that pass it to the ADAPTATION loader, never to run_train. The real boundary is --unfreeze-last, default 6 (trainer.py:87, encoder_flags.py:61-63). So the concentration ratio is read over the top FOUR of twelve while supervision opens the top SIX, and the ':140-141' spread-evenly reference is 4/12=0.333 against a boundary of 6/12=0.5. Fix: derive CONCENTRATION_BLOCKS from Adaptation().unfreeze_last rather than legislating it, and correct the docstring. Note the top-SIX share of any default supervised member is identically 1.000 by construction - a statistic that restates the flag - so the top-4 share is the only version that varies, and it varies because blocks 6-7 are inside the open window and outside the ratio.

title: Ledger75Row silently prints a midpoint number in the ledger75 column for two-level-truth probes
description: D242 §4: three records shift EXACTLY 0.0000 under the recut — ortholarge@focal-attend_mean_probe, radnet121@focal-max_mean_probe, v3large@focal-attend_mean_probe. Cause: their truth is already binarised (2 levels, [0,1]) so there is no mass between the cuts, against a member's 7 levels ([0,.08,.28,.68,.82,.94,1], between-cut mass 0.1209). A probe's midpoint number IS comparable to a member's — its hard labels match the midpoint binarisation on 10,876 of 10,908 cells against wsfold0_e6, and the 32 that differ are a different label snapshot, not a different cut. But its 'ledger75' number is not a ledger75 number at all: it is the midpoint number printed in an L75 column, so anything ranking probes beside members under L75 reads them ~0.027 low BY CONSTRUCTION. Fix: Ledger75Row refuses, or flags, a reading whose truth has two levels. Blast radius requested from the researcher before writing it.

title: report_labels_v3.csv +0.0045 is measured and UNSPENT: no W8 seat carries it
description:
experiments/README.md:9638 - 'report_labels_v3.csv is the one priced knob no W8 seat carries: +0.0045 (band_dense_hold -> recal_holdannot)'. v3 is the recalibration of v2's six confidence levels onto their measured positive rates (README:7023).

Knob-sized, so directional by the standing bar and not a finding on its own. But it is MEASURED, it is FREE (a label table swap, no new mechanism), and it composes with the running total against the original baseline. Every champion seat is still supervised by raw v2.

Do not confuse the table with the scratch one - see knee-ibfrw, two different files share the name.
notes:
THE +0.0045 IS WRONG AND THE HONEST NUMBER IS +0.0009. Corrected 2026-09-17 13:22Z by re-reading the ledger section the bead cites (experiments/README.md, the 2026-08-30 'recal_holdannot LANDS' entry) rather than the one-line quote.

The bead names the control wrongly too: it says 'band_dense_hold -> recal_holdannot'. The arm's control is holdannot_s2026, its own recipe twin. Measured now:

  holdannot_s2026          LEDGER 0.8506   LEDGER75 0.8782   move +0.0276   e7
  recal_holdannot_s2026    LEDGER 0.8964   LEDGER75 0.9004   move +0.0040   e8

That apparent +0.0222 ledger75 is NOT a result, and the ledger already says why in bold: the arm passed --labels report_labels_v3.csv with --eval-labels UNSET, so its stored holdout truth was binarised at 0.5 against the RE-MAPPED values. The ruler moved with the arm. run_comparison refuses the pair outright ('the two runs were scored by different label tables over their 909 shared studies'). The matched proxy, re-scored against v2, is holdannot 0.8506 -> recal_holdannot 0.8515 = +0.0009. FLAT, an order of magnitude inside the 0.0062 paired floor.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PREMISE: the bead's claim is 'the one priced knob no W8 seat carries'. At +0.0009 it is not a priced knob, it is a null, and no seat is missing anything. The v3 axis has now been closed twice from different directions on the same day -- interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-17_the_v3_remap_is_a_table_property.md closed the composition arm (recal_calib DOES NOT COMPOSE, 0.8945 against parent 0.8949) and voided the gold gain as in-sample, and this closes the original standalone claim. CLOSING.

AND ledger75 IS NOT SAFE ON A LABEL-VALUE ARM, which is the transferable half. It reads <stem>.holdout.npz, whose stored truth is whatever --labels that arm trained against. Any member trained on a re-mapped table without --eval-labels pinned is priced by ledger75 against a different ruler than every sibling, silently and with no warning.

THE DEFECT IS SCREENABLE, and the screen is one line over output the tool already prints. The 'move' column (ledger75 minus midpoint) is ~+0.030 to +0.038 for honest members across the whole shelf -- our best solo labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026 moves +0.0374 at 0.9053, so a small move is NOT a property of a high score. Screening 446 rows for move < 0.015 in the top band returns exactly three members, and all three read 0.90+ on the ruler they contaminated:

  foreign_oof_corpus       0.8929 / 0.9051   move +0.0122   (would rank 2nd of all solos)
  dinov3f0_solo            0.8874 / 0.9021   move +0.0147
  recal_holdannot_s2026    0.8964 / 0.9004   move +0.0040

ALL THREE ARE ALREADY IN comp/members.declines AND NONE IS ON comp/members.roster. So the trap is already defused for anything shippable, and roster_check's rule -- every scoreable member is either rostered or declined IN WRITING -- is what defused it, without anyone knowing this particular contamination existed. That is the check paying for itself on a failure mode it was not designed for, and it is why no --move flag is being added to ledger75: a screen whose every hit is already declined would be a second lock on a door that is shut.

title: EmbeddedCorpus mask docstring was backwards: an absent slot is a blank IMAGE, not a zero feature
description: The docstring asserted 'a feature vector for a slot that was never acquired is zeros, and only the mask can say so'. Measurably false: across the healthy caches the mask reports 20130 slot-instances present while the features are non-zero at 26442 of 26442. An unacquired slot's PIXELS are blank, and a blank image is the encoder's perfectly ordinary non-zero response. Consequence, and why this is a bug rather than a wording fix: the mask is MORE load-bearing than the wording implied - an unmasked mean over slots silently ingests blank-image features for 24% of slot-instances and no inspection of the features would reveal it. Docstring corrected 2026-09-08 in kneemri/embeddings/embedding_cache.py and in its unit test. OPEN: audit every consumer that means over the slot axis (head_trial.py, feature_probe.py, transduction.py) for whether it applies the mask.

title: Is the offline seat ADD monotone in the board delta?
description: 16 candidates priced into honest12 across every axis we own returned 16 negative ADDs, while the only two seats that ever moved the board (base_dense -0.0066 offline; raptor_v4_swa ~-0.079 solo vs ours) were both offline NEGATIVE. THAT IS NOT AN ANTI-CORRELATION - an inverted wrong ruler is a right ruler. The offline ADD and the board measure DIFFERENT DISTRIBUTIONS: our holdout is 909 studies from our corpus, our pixel path, our labels, i.e. the same three things every candidate was fitted under, so an ADD is an IN-DISTRIBUTION REDUNDANCY measure and 16 negatives is what a saturated pool looks like. Both board winners were out-of-distribution members and paid where the ruler is BLIND. Job: scatter (offline ADD, board delta) over one-seat steps in comp/board.jsonl (123 rows); state the denominator BEFORE any coefficient; two branches only - slope~1 = ruler transfers and pool is saturated, answer is external data; slope~0 = ruler measures in-distribution redundancy only and every screening decision since the plateau was made with an instrument blind to the paying axis. If n cannot separate them, say so and stop. Zero card, zero slots. Delegated M207 3, rescoped M208 3.

title: Spread dedupes then pads, which skews attention-pooled members on thin series
description: core/data/corpus/slot_reader.py:123 Spread.indices runs dict.fromkeys over linspace(low, high, slices), so truncated duplicate indices collapse; band_indices (:405-422) then repeats the last index to refill. Its own docstring measures 8.3% of series as holding fewer than twelve planes in the band, where the read becomes an exhausted band plus repeats rather than a stride. Documented and deliberate - the result is identical under max pooling, which is duplicate-invariant, and changing it invalidates 99 GB of cache and every member fitted on it. But it SKEWS attention pooling, and no bead names it. Filed by researcher D119 1b. Not a lever: on that 8.3% the band is already exhausted, which is half of why phase-TTA is closed.

title: vjepa_cold: the volumetric family has never had a fair draw
description: D118 §3. The family's four arms are two crashes, one TRUNCATED 12-epoch run (best e9 of 10, 12 asked - a FLOOR under one_cycle) and one 6-epoch arm warm-started off its own e5 encoder. Effective independent n is ~2, where the order-statistic p goes 0.0126 -> 0.112 and the family stops rejecting; it is also the only family in the table drawn at half the epoch budget, and it reached the highest non-default best doing it. So the rejection prices an unfair draw, not the trunk. A cold 12-epoch matched arm settles it. ~3.2 h of card, queued as an INSTRUMENT with a low honest prior on clearing the seat bar; the buy is that it retires the suspicion the family was closed on an artefact. Pre-registration in the arm header (vjepa_member's bands, unchanged).
notes:
PRICE: ~3.2 h of card (12 epochs at ~16 min, vjepa_warm's measured rate at 20 slices / train-size 256 / batch 6). P(clears >= 0.845, the re-open branch) ~ 0.25 - the TRUNCATED cold arm's floor and the half-budget warm arm both landed near it, and the family holds the highest non-default best in the project. GAIN if it clears: the volumetric read is a family rather than an artefact, and the trunk census (orthodiff, dinov2, ortholarge) becomes worth its card time - a READ change is the only thing that has ever paid above the floor here (whole_stack, +0.0103). GAIN if it does not: the family is retired on a FAIR draw, and D118 2's 'trunk-swap under a default-fitted recipe is closed' extends to it. Sold as an INSTRUMENT, not an improvement: the honest prior on clearing the +0.007 seat bar is low, and the buy is retiring the suspicion that p=0.0126 measured an unfair draw (n=4 warm chain at half budget; at effective n=2, p=0.112).
READING PRE-DETERMINED 2026-09-17T18:13Z, before the arm lands. trajectory_check --target 0.82 exits 1: e5 0.7383, generous ceiling 0.7753 over 256 corpus trajectories - the arm CANNOT reach even the bottom of the lowest pre-registered band. So the verdict is the <0.82 branch: SUSPECT THE HARNESS FIRST.
THE SUSPECT IS NAMED, AND THE CORPUS ALREADY CONVICTS IT. The same V-JEPA2 ViT-L trunk has been run here twice before: vjepa_member 0.8343 and vjepa_warm 0.8337 (experiments/README.md:3356, :3237), both at the encoder's NATIVE 256 px over a 12-slice stack. vjepa_cold runs the same trunk at image_size 336 and slices 20. A 0.09 shortfall against our own prior run of the same weights is not a fact about volume pretraining; it is a fact about feeding a 256-native tubelet ViT at 1.31x its resolution.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PRE-REGISTERED BANDS. None of the three may be read as written: >=0.845 re-opens the depth axis, 0.83-0.845 retires volume pretraining at this data scale, <0.82 suspect the harness. The arm landed in the third, so it says nothing about volume pretraining either way and the 0.83-0.845 retirement is NOT triggered.
WHAT THE AXIS ACTUALLY READS, from the corpus rather than this arm. Frozen V-JEPA2 features 0.7620 against a capacity-matched 0.7669 - a tie (vjepa_probe, 2026-08-22). Best fitted V-JEPA2 member ever: 0.8343, against the cold corner's 0.9053. Volume pretraining is 0.07 behind on its own best configuration, so no resolution fix reaches the corner. DO NOT queue a 256 px re-run to chase this - the number it would land near is already on disk.
The member still needs its roster line or decline when the checkpoint closes (roster_check currently reports vjepa_cold_s2026 as the single undocumented member).
RULER CORRECTION 2026-09-17T18:15Z, to the note above. The 0.8343/0.8337 quoted from experiments/README.md are MIDPOINT and were compared against the corner's 0.9053 ledger75 - a cross-ruler comparison, the same defect knee-wbwq was corrected for this hour. On ledger75, population 66c6f231, 909 studies: vjepa_warm_s2026 0.8673 @e3 and vjepa_member_s2026 0.8640 @e9. So the best V-JEPA2 member this project owns sits 0.0380 under the cold corner, not 0.07. The verdict is unchanged - 0.038 is six times the 0.0062 paired floor and no resolution fix closes it - but the number quoted in the previous note is wrong and this line supersedes it.
LANDED AND PRICED. vjepa_cold_s2026 reads 0.7499 midpoint / 0.7614 ledger75 @holdout909, peak epoch
9 of 12, flat across e9-e11 (0.7499 0.7496 0.7495) — converged, NOT budget-bound, so the delta is
readable and the escalation caveat does not apply.

THE PRE-REGISTERED <0.82 BRANCH IS CONFIRMED and trajectory_check called it before the run finished
(CANNOT REACH, generous ceiling 0.7753; the run landed 0.7499, below even that).

THE NAMED SUSPECT IS THE HARNESS, AND IT IS NOT SPECULATION. The same V-JEPA2 ViT-L trunk read 0.8640
(vjepa_member) and 0.8673 (vjepa_warm) ledger75 at its NATIVE 256 px over a 12-slice stack. This arm
ran it at 336 px over 20 slices and lost 0.10. One trunk, two harnesses, a gap ten times the paired
floor: that is a fact about the harness, not about the architecture. Recorded exactly that way in the
decline so the asset is re-testable rather than assumed dead.

DECLINED IN WRITING at comp/members.declines; roster_check clean on this member. Re-open by running
the trunk at 256 px / 12 slices under the current recipe and beating its own 0.8673 — never by
re-quoting either number.
