title: targets.py silently remaps a foreign label value that collides with one of our five levels
description: core/data/labels/targets.py:332-343 Supervision.applied remaps any cell np.isclose to one of our five supervision levels: applied[np.isclose(value, level)] = rate. A foreign label table is not written against our levels, so a collision is an accident. Measured on raptor's labels_llm_soft.csv: Lateral OA has 1176 cells at exactly 0.08, which our level table remaps to 0.041 -- BELOW his own 0.05 negatives, an order inversion inside the one column the his-labels arm was built to test. Second behaviour in the same file, :439-443: a table with no __conf column trains every cell at weight 1.0 (raw = derived[confidence].to_numpy() if confidence in derived.columns else ones), so the his-labels arm moved VALUES and WEIGHTS in one step and never isolated the labels. Fix: refuse or warn when a non-v2 table hits a level, and make the __conf default explicit at the call site. Any future foreign-label arm nudges colliding values off the levels and states what it did with __conf. From D58 (researcher) via mastermind 18:50Z; both regions verified by main in the file itself (the letter cited kneemri/data/targets.py, which does not exist).

title: targets.py: warn or refuse when a foreign labels table collides with our calibration levels
description: core/data/labels/targets.py Supervision.applied (:332-343) remaps any cell np.isclose to one of our five levels. A foreign table on a different scale can collide: raptor's LatOA has 1176 cells at exactly 0.08, rewritten to 0.041, BELOW his own 0.05 negatives - an order inversion inside the column the arm was for. The docstring promises untouched pass-through for values the reader never emits; the collision case is silent. Add a guard that refuses or warns when a non-v2 table hits a level. Related: :439-443, a table with no __conf column trains every cell at weight 1.0, so a foreign-labels arm moves values AND weights in one step.

title: foreign_run swallows the foreign script's failure (runpy.run_path, no status)
description: kneemri/experiments/foreign_run.py:71 runs the foreign script via runpy.run_path and does not translate a failure into a non-zero exit status. hisrecipe_distill died on ModuleNotFoundError twice on 2026-09-07 and both deaths were logged by the chain as 'returned 0'; queue_check read OK with an idle card behind it. Propagate a non-zero status (and assert the checkpoint) so a dead arm cannot look like a finished one.

title: mail_check: exactly one live listener per box, and no unread letter older than ten minutes
description: The mailbox listener is a ONE-SHOT: it prints, archives into read/ and EXITS the moment a letter lands. So every letter kills the watcher, and the next letter is invisible until somebody re-arms. On 2026-09-07 that left 15 letters unread in inbox/main from 16:25Z to 17:56Z and the mastermind had to notice from outside. The opposite hole exists too: while re-arming I found TWO listeners on box main at once, which is the mail version of the two-watchers-one-arm case queue_check already closes for card arms - one of them archives the letter into read/ where the other never sees it, and both look perfectly healthy. So: a mail_check beside queue_check, asserting exactly one live listener process per box (ask the process table, not the directory) and that no letter in a box is unread for more than ten minutes. The box LOOKS armed either way and only the process table knows, which is queue_check's own sentence. Whether the listener should re-arm itself is the owner's call; the CHECK is ours either way.

title: convergence_check is blind on every --fold -1 member
description: convergence_check reads '1 runs: 1 unscored' and returns NO verdict for a member fitted at --fold -1, because it scores a run by comparing its best epoch to its last, and a full-fit run has no holdout to have a best epoch on. So the gate that exists to separate TRUNCATED from STOPPED from UNDERTRAINED is silent on exactly the class of member that ships blind. Found 2026-09-07 on labelwise_dense_ff, which the mastermind ordered convergence-checked before it took a seat in kneemri-stack; the tool could not answer and the seat was decided by reading metrics.jsonl by hand (13 rows = recipe + epochs 0..11 = 12 of 12, COMPLETE). A guess would have fallen back to labelwise_dense_s2026 and lost about 0.0002 of block delta for no reason. Rule to add: for a fold -1 run, take the verdict from the EPOCH COUNT against the recipe budget - rows-1 == epochs means COMPLETE, fewer means TRUNCATED - and a truncated full-fit under one_cycle never annealed, so refuse to ship it. This is the only check available on that class.

title: Instrument entry: his DINOv3 OOF beside raptor, pre-reg <= +0.001 board
description: D47: his five-fold OOF table reads corr 0.731 to raptor / 0.748 to our block and +0.0063 [+0.0052,+0.0073] offline as a sixth ours-member with raptor 1/3 untouched. Board has priced this family's complementarity twice: bend_v1 (56076290) 0.941 = ~+0.001 over the midpoint with a STRONGER version of the same object, and foreignsolo_v1 (56063670) 0.882 board vs 0.8812 offline. D35 (b) at lift -0.06 / corr 0.75 gives ~-0.002 board. So this is an instrument, not a champion attempt: does OOF-beside-raptor beat program-instead-of-raptor. Entry shape: champion six as mean-of-six with his five folds as the sixth member at 2/3, raptor 1/3 untouched; mount mattiaangeli/knee-mri-fold-weights, bend_entry.py already mounts it. Spare-slot class, TOMORROW at the earliest. Pre-reg <= +0.001 board.

title: queue_check: refuse a live watcher gating an arm whose checkpoint is already on disk
description: after_clean_calib.sh sat alive as pid 1733548 waiting for 'ARM DONE effv2l_f0' and gated to launch clean_calib.sh — the arm that was on the card at that moment (pid 60360, 29.6 GB). Its gate was the repo logs/ spelling, which is never written, so it would have waited forever; had the marker landed it launches a SECOND clean_calib on a busy card, which is the card_check incident (two identical member_curve scans, one member stretched 3 min to 11 min). queue_check cannot see this class: a live process gating an owed arm is all it reads, and OK is what it says. Fix: for each owed arm, if the arm's --out checkpoint already exists on disk, the watcher owing it is STALE — refuse and name the pid.

title: foreign_run writes no metrics.jsonl, so three checks are blind to every raptor fine-tune
description: trajectory_check, convergence_check and ledger_check all read a run's <name>.metrics.jsonl. run_train writes one; foreign_run does not - a finished raptor fine-tune leaves only raptor_ft_<tag>.holdout.npz and _swa.holdout.npz (verified against raptor_ft_repl2x2_c on disk). Consequence, measured on 2026-09-07: the mastermind ordered trajectory_check against effv2l_f0's pre-registered target while it was running, and the tool had no input to read. The only progress record was the training log's GOLD macro-AUC line, which is a DIFFERENT ruler from the arm's pre-registration (solo OOF-896 under LEDGER, after_effv2l.sh:31-35), so no truncate decision was available at all. Fix: foreign_run writes a metrics.jsonl with a recipe row 0 and a per-epoch row, in run_train's format, so a foreign arm is readable by the same checks as a native one. Zero card.

title: three @focal-* probe npz predate the ProbeCorpus.graded fix and carry binarised truth
description: ortholarge@focal-attend, radnet121@focal-max, v3large@focal-attend _mean_probe records written 2026-09-02T18:15Z with 0/1 truth; c8d248f8 (2026-09-04) made the writer emit Targets.load(...).scores. Re-emit, no card needed (cached features + ridge).

title: submit_check is blind to foreign members: cross-family blend reads as a reseating
description: submit_check compares SET equality over OUR member vocabulary only. kneemri-bend is our champion six PLUS mattiaangeli's entire 24-member published program, rank-averaged at 0.5 in rank space; the foreign half is invisible, so the entry REFUSES as 'SAME 6 members as calibsix_v1 ...'. That is a false positive for the reseating ban and forces --anyway on a genuinely new entry, which is exactly the mode where --anyway stops being a signal. Fix: an entry that runs a foreign program as a subprocess must contribute a member identity to the set (parse the kernel's RaptorSeat.combined arguments, or a declared foreign-block manifest).

title: train --help crashes: TypeError %o format in a flag's help string
description: python -m kneemri.training.train --help raises TypeError: %o format: an integer is required, not dict, from argparse._expand_help. A literal % in one help string (--vram-gb's help contains '80%%' which is escaped, so it is another flag) is read as a format spec. Effect: the ONE command that documents the flag vocabulary cannot run, so every arm author reads flags out of other arms instead. Found 2026-09-07 while writing resnet_224_short; worked around with FlagVocabulary.parser()._actions.

title: final_ws_wf: price the warm start so retrains can run at 4 epochs
description: Warm twin of final_ws_df (same seat, same teacher_oof5, same distill weight) started from final_ws_cf on a complete 4-epoch one_cycle. If the two land inside the 0.0062 floor on the canonical-holdout witness, every retrain from here runs 3x faster. Prior is against it: warm_calib_dense lost 0.0072, and every distillation arm on the ledger peaks late. Instrument, not an improvement.

title: Pre-register gen-2 teacher on SHARPNESS, not only AUC: a sharper same-family teacher may be a better one
description: The oof_teacher --fill witness found band_dense's fold-0 block outside the 224px/12-slice twins' spread scatter on 9/12 labels, always SHARPER. That was read as heterogeneity and the block was refused for round one, correctly — but sharper-and-same-family is a candidate for a BETTER teacher, not just a different one. teacher_gen2 runs the 224/12 geometry; oof_teacher's own recipe is already the 336/20 geometry band_dense has. So pre-register the gen-2 read against gen-1 on SPREAD as well as on AUC: if gen-2's blocks are sharper than gen-1's and the student improves, sharpness is a lever on the teacher term, which is the term the six-seat retrain multiplies. Costs nothing extra to read - BlockStats.axes() already reports it.

title: package_members can leave the local manifest ahead of the pushed dataset
description: The local all_ours manifest listed oof_teacher_s2026 while dimiturnt/kneemri-members does not hold it, so MemberPackage.shipped raised WeightsError: [all_ours] and members_2 both hold ['oof_teacher_s2026']. The duplicate refusal was correct; the state that produced it was silent. Whatever writes the manifest should record what was PUSHED, or a check should compare the manifest against the live dataset listing before a kernel is built on it. Worked around by trimming the local manifest to 126 (backup at .json.bak).

title: aprior_fixed: the anatomical prior held as a buffer, not a warm start
description: aprior_dense_s2026 read 0.8557 vs band_dense 0.8578 and the ledger closed the anatomical-prior family. Its own explanation was WASHOUT: train loss tracked the control to the fourth decimal, so 72 numbers of initialisation on an nn.Parameter the data may overrule were gone before the fit mattered. That is a claim about the HOLDING, not the anatomy. FixedPriorSlotHead register_buffers the same prior, so a gradient step cannot erase it - the published form (SLOT_PRIOR_STRENGTH 0.55, added to the attention logits every forward pass). Two controls on one axis: gain over both 0.8578 and 0.8557 is the constraint, between them is noise, at aprior_dense says the holding was never the mechanism. 73 min card, zero slots, +0.000 to +0.005 expected, P(clears +0.010) ~0.15. An INSTRUMENT: it decides whether the family closed on the idea or only on our warm-start form.
notes: PRICE: 73 min of card, zero slots. Expected +0.000 to +0.005 on holdout mean. P(clears +0.010) = 0.15. Justified as an INSTRUMENT, not an improvement: it separates 'the anatomical prior does not help this head' from 'our warm-start holding of it does not survive a gradient step'.

title: run_check refuses a zero-of-ours entry instead of reporting NOT-APPLICABLE
description: run_check asserts a census of N-of-M our members. An entry that names none of ours (a foreign-solo instrument) has M=0 and the check refuses rather than reporting not-applicable, which makes the pre-flight unrunnable for exactly the entries whose identity is most at risk.

title: foreign_entry.SOURCE: one declaration read by both build_kit and kit_check
description: A foreign-fold entry declares its source in two places today, so a kit can be built from one spelling and checked against another. Make it a single SOURCE constant on foreign_entry that both build_kit and kit_check read, so a mismatch is impossible rather than merely caught.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-09-15 P0->P2: foreign dinov3 fold family not in champion (knee-uhyas inversion); refactor not score-bearing

title: A kit rebuild without --extra silently unships every foreign kernel
description: comp/build_kit.py copies extra files only when handed --extra <path>. The 18:18:55Z rebuild on 2026-09-06 omitted external/dinov3folds/bend_the_knee_to_dinov3_ensembled.py, so kneemri-foreignsolo died with FileNotFoundError: no their serving program, carried in our kit under /kaggle/input. Every foreign kernel mounts that same file through foreign_entry.mounts.one(SOURCE), so kneemri-foreignlogit (the registered 21:41Z fallback) was equally dead and would have spent a slot to discover it. Fixed by rebuilding with the flag and pushing a kit version at 20:19:48Z. The defect class: a kernel dependency declared in a hand-typed build flag, invisible to kit_check and to the kernel that needs it. Fix is for foreign_entry.SOURCE to be the single declaration, read by build_kit AND by kit_check, so a kit that cannot serve a foreign kernel refuses to push.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-09-15 P0->P2: rebuild fixed 2026-09-06; only foreign seat shipped now is raptor via Kaggle mount, not --extra; class defect remains

title: foreign_distill_calib: distant DINOv3 teacher on the calibrated champion recipe
description: calib_dense's invocation plus --teacher-targets teacher_foreign_corpus.npz and --distill-weight 0.3. Control: calib_dense (seated) and foreign_distill_s2026 (same teacher, uncalibrated). Reading is seat_value + nearest distance, not the solo.
close_reason: SWEEP phase 1 (completed but not properly marked): the arm named in this bead's own title has a .full.log in $MODELS/experiments/ AND a scored row in experiments/README.md. The work ran and the ledger priced it; the bead was never marked. Reversible - bd update --status open if a reading here is still owed.

title: foreign_recipe reproduced at 0.8087 — their recipe is not what carries their family
description: foreign_recipe_v3small_336_20sl_s2026 finished 12/12 epochs, peak epoch 11, holdout mean AUC 0.8087 (logs/foreign_recipe_launch.log). Not truncated. Against 0.8545-0.8670 for champion-seat members and 0.8812 for mattiaangeli's own released folds under the same nominal recipe. A ~0.07 gap between their recipe as transcribed here and their released weights: what carries their family is not the recipe. Header branches VOID (written against a different question). Owed: ledger row in experiments/README.md; a decision on whether the checkpoint joins the roster or gets a written decline.

title: mattiaangeli's kernel bands 0.2-0.8 when training and 0.12-0.88 when serving the same checkpoints
description: Their released folds (m_f0..4.pt) are served at SLICE_BAND (0.12, 0.88) at :1622 but their training program bands (0.2, 0.8) at :411. Either their own kernel has a train/serve mismatch - in which case serving OUR port at 0.2-0.8 may be free AUC on their weights, a two-minute rerun of foreign_folds - or the two sections are different generations and their published training code is not the recipe that produced these weights. Asked of Kimi as a source-reading question 2026-09-06. Cheap to test either way: rerun foreign_folds with the band overridden and re-price.

title: Port slot-token trunk conditioning (their cond: token) into our recipes
description: Their cond:token injects the SERIES SLOT TYPE as a token into the trunk: ViTSlotToken(enc, N_SLOT_TYPES), forward_features(im, slot) at bend_the_knee_to_dinov3_ensembled.py:2095/2118. It is NOT site conditioning - n_sites:109 is a dead cfg key on that path, and my site reading was wrong. We already carry slot identity through the pipeline, so the port needs no new metadata and nothing derived at test time. Cheapest form: a learned nn.Embedding over our six slots added into the trunk tokens, gated by a StudyDesign flag so no published member's state dict moves. Warm-start from a champion twin - the input distribution is unchanged. Unpriced: nothing says this term carries score, since the 0.8874 gap it was argued from was a label-table number (retracted).

title: A read group whose members are all dropped still decodes
description: Ensemble.afford can drop every member of a read group mid-run, but the group itself stays in the schedule and its decode still runs - paying the full decode cost for a group that will contribute no logits. The drop should collapse an empty group out of the schedule.

title: record_mix orders foreign and dead runs ahead of live ones
description: record_mix's ordering puts foreign-split and dead (no-longer-on-disk) runs ahead of live ones in the mix, so a reader of the top of that listing sees entries that cannot be rebuilt or cannot be priced. Ordering should demote anything whose checkpoint is absent or whose split is foreign, and label the reason inline.

title: TrainerRecord resize guard: a record written at a different read size is accepted silently
description: A holdout record carries the predictions for the read size it was served at. Nothing asserts that a record being blended was produced at the same read size as its checkpoint's recipe, so a regrouped record and a native record can be mixed into one vote with no complaint. It did not bite in the read-group work because the queue writes distinct suffixed filenames, but the guard is absent rather than satisfied.

title: Kaggle kernel: elapsed == decode is the SERIAL path, not the budget
description: The budget argument written down earlier equated a group's elapsed wall-clock with its decode cost. On Kaggle the two are the same number only because decode and forward run SERIALLY in the kernel - there is no prefetch overlap - so elapsed happens to equal decode plus forward with forward small. That is a property of the serving path, not of the budget model, and it stops holding the moment any overlap is introduced. Anything that reasons about afford() or worth from measured elapsed must say which of the two it means.

title: read_group_queue.sh pointed MODELS at all_ours/, which holds no holdout records
description: all_ours/ holds a packaging COPY of each .pt and no .holdout.npz; records live beside their checkpoint in the models ROOT (core/paths.py:50). Every seat read 'no holdout record, skipped' and the run died with 'none of the 5 named records carries a holdout array' - the --fold -1 refusal message, which would have been blamed on the fold line rather than on the path. Fixed in the script; the failure MODE is the finding, since any tool given an all_ours path will fail the same way and say the same misleading thing.

title: Read-group diversity is self-correlated: three free points, all at or below 0.8706
description: twinfive native five reproduce 0.8706 exactly. Ten-seat blends with already-on-disk regroups: +_r224 0.8693 (-0.0013), +_r280 0.8707 (+0.0001), +_n12b0.1-0.9 0.8698 (-0.0008). Pre-registered bar was 0.8751. Mechanism: a twin of yourself under unweighted LogitAverage is the most correlated seat the pool can hold, so diversity gained is smaller than dilution paid. Reweighting is a seating operation, closed. read_group_queue.sh cut to the single r392 candidate (an UPSCALE - r224/r280 are downscales from the 336 native, and res392_ws_s2026 is our best solo, so it is a different sign of the knob). Four depth/band candidates parked. Full write-up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_read-group-diversity-is-self-correlated.md

title: DataRoot.checkpoints mangles any bare name containing a dot
description: core/paths.py:121-139 resolves a bare checkpoint name through Path.stem: self.models() / f'{path.stem}{CHECKPOINT_SUFFIX}'. A regrouped holdout record is spelled ..._n16b0.1-0.9.pt, whose stem is ..._n16b0.1-0 because .9 reads as the suffix - so the file silently resolves to one that does not exist. read_group_queue.sh works around it by passing full paths (a path with a parent is taken as written), but the resolver should refuse or handle a dotted name rather than truncate it.

title: members.py sits ON the 750-line god-file ceiling
description: Adding one TypedDict key and its docstring pushed kneemri/inference/members.py from 749 to 756; it was brought back under only by compressing two unrelated docstrings. The next feature that touches it pays the same tax. Split: MemberConfig + the manifest constants are one concern, Member/MemberPackage/Window another.

title: Decode is headers(all files) + pixels(slices): depth cuts only 81% of the bill
description: Acquisition.ordered_files header-parses EVERY file in every series to sort them; only then does SlotReader.cropped decode the slices the band selects. Measured 96 studies: headers-only 0.09 s/study serial vs 0.48 s/study at 12 slices = headers are 19% of a 12-slice decode, and that term is invariant to depth. So a slice-count lever is priced wrong unless the header term is held out of it. A per-series single-header parse (or filename ordering) is the lever that moves the other term. NOTE also that the committed bench table reads 0.27 s/study at 12 slices and this run read 0.48 with identical code - the box was loaded, so ratios are honest and absolutes are not.

title: members.py is at the god-file ceiling - split MemberPackage out
description: kneemri/inference/members.py sits at 750 lines against [tool.structure] file_max=750, and arch-fitness counts one line MORE than wc -l, so any addition blocks. Two docstrings were trimmed on 2026-09-06 purely to land Serving.read_size. MemberPackage is ~220 lines and has 35 consumers including shipped comp/kernels/*, so the split is a real refactor with a kernel-compat surface, not a move. Do it before the next member-side change, not during one.

title: Vote.ranks breaks ties by array position, the defect area_under_curve already fixed
description:
core scoring fixed this once: LabelScores.area_under_curve used argsort().argsort()+1, which are ORDINAL ranks, so tied predictions are ordered by their position in the corpus and a CONSTANT predictor scored 1.0 or 0.0 instead of 0.5. It now takes midranks and says so at length in its own docstring.

Vote.ranks (kneemri/inference/vote.py) still does exactly what was fixed there: member[:, label].argsort().argsort() / (studies-1). Every rank-space rule in the module builds on it - RankAverage, QualityWeightedRank, LabelQualityRank, SharpenedRank - so a member whose column carries ties votes by ARRAY ORDER inside each tie group.

How much it matters, honestly: raw sigmoids are float64 and effectively never tie, so single-member and ordinary-ensemble numbers are unaffected. It bites where predictions are coarse or quantised - a member served at low precision, a member whose head saturates, a re-ranked or thresholded input, and any future rule that feeds an already-combined table back through ranks(). It surfaced while testing SharpenedRank, where a flat rank-average of three members ties by construction and the near-flat squash agreed with the flat rule at 0.998 rather than 1.0.

Fix: the midrank loop area_under_curve already carries, lifted to Vote.ranks. Assert the constant-column case (a member with one repeated value must vote flat, contributing the same midrank everywhere) - that is the test the scoring fix wanted and did not get here.

PRICE: under an hour, zero card, zero slots. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0 - this is correctness, not score. P(it has silently moved a recorded ensemble number) ~ 0.1, and that is the reason to do it: the failure is invisible and the same failure has already been paid for once.

title: Label-table directory priced on CPU: blend_four dead, v4 corrections at ~+0.002, four filenames are duplicates
description: Distance map of all 20 label tables against blend_three_v1 over 4406x12 cells. blend_four: mean|d| 0.0114, corr 0.99915, ZERO of 52872 verdict flips - the step that bought +0.0073 (report_v2 to blend_three) is 8.3x larger, so a fourth reader is worth ~+0.0009. Dead without a card. merged_blend_v1 == blend_three_v1 exactly; merged_labels == merged3_labels == report_labels_v2; merged_tagged == merged3_tagged == report_labels_v3; confident_v2 == confident - four filenames that cannot be experiments. Only report_labels_v4 / blend_hybrid_fx_v4 / _v4b flip verdicts (~510 cells); gold ruler puts hybrid_v4 at +0.0079 over blend_three and the measured ruler-to-supervision ratio is 0.29, so they price at +0.0023, under the 0.0062 floor. Not refuted - take a cheap ride if one appears, no dedicated arm. Reading: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_the-untested-label-tables-priced-without-card.md

title: recal_holdannot_s2026 records its holdout against a re-mapped truth table and outranks every member
description: Its holdout truth differs from the corpus label table in 10752 of 10908 cells, because the arm was fitted on a supervision table whose values were re-mapped from the 58 annotated studies and it records its holdout against that table. It reads 0.8964 where the best comparable member reads 0.8642, so it sorts first in any AUC ranking of the pool while answering a different question. RecordMix.narrow drops the minority ruler only once a second member joins, so a single-member read never triggers the guard, and a forward selection seeded on it picks it first and then cannot add a seat. Same failure mode as raptor_solo. priceable_blend.on_the_corpus_ruler now drops non-majority truth tables. Open question this bead carries: whether any shipped entry or roster read has ranked members across mixed rulers.
notes: NOT A DISCOVERY - comp/members.declines line 84 already records this in full, including DO NOT QUOTE 0.8964 and the reason (--labels v3 with --eval-labels unset, so the holdout truth was binarised against the re-mapped values and the ruler moved with the arm). run_comparison already refuses the pair. I filed this without reading the declines file first, which is the rule in CLAUDE.md. What is actually new and is all this bead now carries: the RANKING path had no such guard. A bare AUC sort over the pool puts this member first, and RecordMix.narrow only drops a minority ruler once a second member joins, so a single-member read never triggers it. priceable_blend.on_the_corpus_ruler now takes the majority truth table, by majority rather than by name.

title: annotated_readings writes no artefact, so a gold reading lives only in scrollback
description: The tool prints its table to stdout and has no --out. Three arms (relabel_hold, rank966_hold, band224_hold) declared readings of the shape <name>_annotated*.json and NOTHING in the tree can produce that file: grep for a writer returns empty. reading_check caught relabel_hold the moment it finished, and the other two would have followed at 21:35Z and 22:05Z. Repointed all three to logs/<name>_ledger.log for now, which is what the other eleven declaring arms already use, and wrote logs/relabel_hold_ledger.log by hand. THE HAND-WRITTEN LEDGER IS THE WEAKNESS: the reading exists because somebody remembered, which is the same failure shape as the roster. Fix: give annotated_readings an --out that writes the per-checkpoint gold AUC, the paired deltas with their intervals, the study count and the gold_fitted route per member, then let the arms declare that file again. Then a gold reading is an artefact by construction. Note while doing it: the 58-cell ruler carries a 95 percent half-width near 0.014 against effects of 0.010, so the json should record the interval prominently enough that no reader quotes the point estimate alone.

title: reading_check accepts prose in a reading line, so one arm declares a ruler nobody can resolve
description: experiments/arms/cover_labelwise.sh line 3 reads: # reading: a flat mean with the thin findings UP is the finding. They went down hardest, and everything ... That is prose, not a glob. reading_check treats the token after the colon as a filename pattern, so this arm declares a ruler that can never resolve and the declared-and-missing rule can never fire on it. The check survived its own first run precisely because prose has spaces and a glob is ONE token, which is the accident that keeps it from being a false positive rather than a rule it enforces. Fix: refuse a reading line whose payload is more than one whitespace-delimited token, with the arm name in the message. Then fix cover_labelwise to name the artefact it actually leaves, and move the prose to a normal comment line. Scope: 15 of 232 arms carry a reading line at all, so the convention is young and this is the moment to make it exact.

title: 224 px control so the label axis costs 28 minutes a point, not 90
description: band224 measured 142 s an epoch against 450 for the same recipe at 336 px on this card, for 0.0049 of solo AUC (0.8529 vs band_dense 0.8578) - under the 0.0062 holdout noise floor. A twelve-epoch arm goes from 90 minutes to 28. PRICE for arm band224_hold: COST 28 minutes of card plus ~4 minutes CPU for the gold read. GAIN as a score: ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION - it is a control, not a hypothesis, and no number it returns is a finding on its own. Its value is that it unblocks the dose curve on the supervision axis at a third of the price; that axis currently holds one refuted point (errors_dense) and two running arms, each costing 90 minutes because each is matched to band_dense_hold at 336. P(clears the bar) is not defined for a control. JUSTIFICATION: three dose points at 28 minutes cost less than one at 90, and the axis cannot be PRICED at one point per ninety minutes - only sampled. It cannot be base224_s2026: that fit is not --hold-annotations, so annotated_readings refuses it and the gold ruler cannot score anything against it.

title: annotated_readings --against takes a stem and crashes with a KeyError on a Path
description: Passing --against band_dense_hold_s2026 (the name the tool PRINTS in its own score table) reads all nine members, then dies at annotated_readings.py:193 with KeyError: WindowsPath(band_dense_hold_s2026), because per_member is keyed by the full checkpoint path while the printed table shows the stem. The whole read is thrown away at the last step, which on cpu is the expensive part. Two fixes, either is enough: resolve --against against the stems the table prints, or validate it against the per_member keys BEFORE the members are read so the failure costs a second instead of a full pass.

title: Vendor-robust seat selection: re-run greedy on worst-vendor rather than pooled holdout
description: Card-free, and it attacks the seven board flats directly rather than reseating. Greedy seat selection has always maximised mean AUC over the pooled 909-study holdout, which is a random split over our scanner mix and therefore in-distribution by construction. Alternative objectives, computable from the HoldoutRecords already on disk: (a) mean AUC on the WORST vendor subset, (b) the mean across per-vendor AUCs rather than the AUC of the pooled set, (c) minimise rank disagreement across vendor subsets. If those pick a different seat set than the champion, the difference is a mechanism (selection was fitted to our mix) and not a reseating, which is the distinction the submission rules turn on. Gated on knee-v9m5z (the ruler) and knee-m4jkz (the reader fix). Grep comp/board.jsonl for the OPERATION before any slot is spent on the result.

title: Crop-skip census: how many of 4407 studies train at a different mm/pixel than the rest
description: SlotReader.window returns None when PixelSpacing is absent, when the computed box is under MIN_CROP_PIXELS, or when it is wider than the frame (slot_reader.py:376-400) — and _crop then hands back the FULL frame uncropped. That is honest (no guessed spacing constant) but it means crop_mm=130 holds mm/pixel constant only on the SUBSET where the window applies, and nobody has measured that subset. Every study outside it enters training at whatever scale its acquisition happened to have. Two card-free readings wanted: (1) the skip rate over all 4407, split by which of the three conditions fired; (2) whether the skip rate is vendor- or field-strength-correlated, which would make it a confound in the vendor-grouped ruler rather than an independent axis. NOT answered by crop_coverage, which asks which CENTRE keeps more tissue, not how often the crop applies at all. Related: canonical_metadata.csv holds pixel_spacing_mm for only 344 of 4407 and slice_spacing_mm for 855, though that table is not what the reader consumes.

title: fastMRI+ merge: 974 image-read knee studies, ten of our twelve columns, on disk and unused
description: AUDIT 2026-09-05. Board flat six days at 0.944; best member flat six days at 0.8642. quarter_data priced every known lever under 1.5% and the project kept running arms pre-registered to produce nothing. But 1.5% is the bar for a FINDING; knee-urvf says first place needs +0.010 on ONE member, and the external-data programme is priced at +0.009 - the same number. It was dismissed for being too small to write up. It is the right size to win. merged_corpus is the only arm on this axis: 736 Rijeka studies, ONE label column (ACL), mean +0.0020 but deficit findings +0.0061 and Lateral Meniscus +0.0196 star - a structure Rijeka never labels, so the gain is the ENCODER learning focal structure from expert image reads, not supervision. Transfer by KIND. fastMRI+ is on disk at raw/fastmri/labels/Annotations/knee.csv, never processed: 16167 radiologist bounding-box annotations over 974 studies, 1172 volumes local. Label space covers TEN of our twelve columns - Meniscus Tear 5658, Cartilage partial 2985 and full 615, Effusion 1311, Fracture/Contusion 1060, Subchondral edema 986, Periarticular cysts 864 (Bakers), ACL 1443, MCL 296. Same size class as merged_corpus, ten times the supervision. BLOCKERS before any card: (1) licence - NYU fastMRI DUA plus fastMRI+ licence, does it permit a Kaggle submission, MRNet is already blocked here on exactly this; (2) singlecoil is raw k-space and needs IFFT plus root-sum-square reconstruction; (3) sagittal single-plane against our 4-14 series multi-plane slot machinery. Q-CORPUS sent to Kimi 2026-09-05T1545Z asks all three. DO NOT propose SSL/MAE - closed five ways, 0.6735 to 0.7309 against a 0.8578 control. DO NOT propose foreign trunks - about 25 arms, all below the natural-image control.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-05 15:55Z by the cheapest possible test, card-free. Two things in the original filing were wrong. (1) NOT UNBUILT: core/data/corpus/fastmri_corpus.py and build_fastmri.py already exist, wired through slots.FASTMRI_SCHEME, never run. The reader also answers questions I had opened as unknowns: plane is CORONAL not sagittal, and there is no k-space reconstruction problem because the h5 files carry reconstruction_esc and fastMRI+ boxes were drawn on exactly that array via the corpus own fastmri_to_dicom.py. (2) NOT PRICED: experiments/README.md:332 merged3_corpus already answered the site-count form of this operation and answered it negative. Second site +0.0043, third site -0.0024, and the shape was a rotation not an addition, with the argued column ranking last of twelve. That row names fastMRI-as-a-fourth-site explicitly as priced before any card is spent on it. THE CENSUS, run with build_fastmri --scheme fastmri --labels-only over 1173 read studies: the positive contribution to our twelve columns is ACL 101, Effusion 142, MCL 4, and ZERO everywhere else. Medial and Lateral Meniscus take 509 rows each, all negative. The three OA columns take 1050 each, all negative. Baker cyst 1011, Contusion 875, Fracture 1053, all negative. Structural, not a bug: a fastMRI+ Meniscus Tear is not sided and Cartilage Full Thickness names no compartment, so a positive of that kind cannot fill a sided column while an unboxed read study is a confident negative in both. WHAT THIS LEAVES. The corpus is a class-prior shift toward absence on nine of twelve columns, bought for a multi-hour decode plus a 12-epoch arm, on an operation the ledger already prices negative. That is a bad ratio and this bead is NOT ready to become an arm. It becomes one only if the supervision corner is argued first (merged_blend_cf 0.8597 and merged_span_cf 0.8618 are the corner still paying at a fixed two-site cache), i.e. whether an ASSERTED foreign negative should be masked like an absent one, which Targets.pair already supports. description:

Underneath: SlotHead over cls_mean-pooled ViT with window pooling - structurally ours.

All three named mechanisms are already priced here. Target-wise fusion IS the per-finding learned combiner: stack_combiner on honest12 over 909 holdout studies reads +0.0013 own-finding at best, -0.0053 to -0.0081 crossed. Raptor is already mounted by our entries. RadImageNet-for-diversity is the closed convolutional trunk lane.

Consequence: the public frontier is 0.007 BELOW us and carries no axis we have not read, so the 0.010 to the leader is not recoverable by reading public kernels harder. Combiner side is closed by measurement across every question asked (seat count, seating, weighting, re-lensing, calibration, level-2 fit). The remaining lever is a better MEMBER. Q-TOP is with Kimi for the discussion tab and method notes.

Related: the labelled-external-data lane is dead on LICENCE not mechanism - NYU fastMRI DUA covers derived variables, so fastMRI-trained weights cannot ship in a public kernel (Q-BT).

title: CCN de-bias of per-column AUC is out of range - the cheap ruler fix is dead
description:
Derived the closed-form class-conditional-noise inversion (affine, invertible) and applied it to the flip rates measured over the 57 annotated studies. Every column's implied clean AUC exceeds 1.000 (MCL 1.086, Contusion 1.561, macro 1.142 against a measured 0.8578).

Two readings, not separated: flip rates overestimated on 57 studies (study-bootstrapped ceiling CI is +/-0.11, and only Synovitis and Contusion clear the upper bound), or the noise is instance-dependent rather than class-conditional (the reader and the model read the same report vocabulary, so the reader's over-calls land where the model scores high, which inflates measured AUC). Point estimates favour the second unanimously; intervals support it in 2 of 12.

CONSEQUENCE: no per-column correction can be applied to the ledger. The cheap fix for knee-zsyp4 is dead and fixing the LABELS (knee-wko44) is the only route to an honest per-column number.

Full derivation and table: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-05_the-offline-ruler-cannot-be-arithmetically-de-biased.md

The DEFAULT sweep still skips it - it holds one package at a time by design. So an entry shipping its own package needs TWO invocations before a slot: the default sweep (everything on kneemri-members) and --root against its own. kneemri-relabel7 and kneemri-orthorehearse are the two that exist. description:
Kimi's Q-CEIL reply (research/2026-09-05_knee-mri-column-ceilings.md) supplies the prior the two ablation slots were buying, at zero slots, with the caveat that it is a BORROWED ordering from other corpora and the same note proves those orderings do not transfer.

Label-limited, so card time cannot buy them: overall abnormality (MRNet Fleiss kappa 0.508), meniscus (0.745), any partial-tear distinction (one paper reads partial ACL at AUC 0.58 externally). title: queue_check MISARMED hint names the wrong naming rule
description: The MISARMED line tells the operator to re-arm on '<arm>_s<seed>.full.log'. That is not the rule. lib.sh:689 _arm_log names the log after the CHECKPOINT - basename of --out minus .pt - falling back to the arm name only when a run has no --out (knee-tkyy). So ortho_slow_trunk (--out ortho_slow_trunk.pt) writes ortho_slow_trunk.full.log with no seed, and mricore_corpus (--out mricore_corpus_s2026.pt) writes mricore_corpus_s2026.full.log with one. Following the hint cost two wakes on 2026-09-05: it disarmed a correctly-armed watcher, then the check flagged the corrected one, and only reading _arm_log settled it. Fix the hint to say: the log is named for the arm's --out, so grep the arm for --out and take the basename.
notes: 2026-09-06: found the SECOND half of this defect, and it is worse than the hint. The arm LOG carries the checkpoint spelling (_arm_log -> ARM_LOG_NAME, lib.sh:580,685) while the MARKER TEXT carries the run_train name (_mark, lib.sh:642, writes 'ARM DONE $name'). So foreign_distill_mix30 writes foreign_distill_mix30_s2026.full.log containing 'ARM DONE foreign_distill_mix30'. after_mix30.sh was armed grepping the checkpoint spelling in the marker and would have waited forever with the card idle behind it; queue_check reported OK throughout, because a live process gating an owed arm is all it can see and it cannot read the string that process is blocked on. Killed and re-armed at 21:23Z against 'ARM DONE foreign_distill_mix30' over both after_dissent2.log and the arm log. CLAUDE.md now states the two-variable rule; queue_check's MISARMED hint still needs to print the marker format, not just the log name.

title: Label axis closed at TWO detectors: neighbour vote and the rank-average both lose at the paying budget
description: python -m kneemri.evaluation.neighbour_errors --against-confident, no card, no slot. Similarity-weighted 10-NN vote over six frozen 336px trunks, read on the same gate/census/budgets as confident learning. Separation AUC, all disagreements / confident false positives / misses: CL 0.7628 / 0.7580 / 0.6903; vote 0.6830 / 0.7714 / 0.3588; rank-average 0.7511 / 0.8020 / 0.5161. The rank-average is the best false-positive ranking the project has, by 0.0440 over CL on the stratum that is 77 percent of the census. It still does not pay: net benefit is B(2p-1) in the PRECISION at the budget, not the area under the curve, and precision at budget 25 on all disagreements is 0.720 for CL against 0.480 combined and 0.200 for the vote alone. Both are below the 0.5 break-even at every budget read, so the net-benefit peak moves off the table rather than to a larger budget. The vote is structurally blind to misses (a false negative agrees with the negatives around it by construction) and its own majority mask flags 22.363 percent of read cells against cleanlab 6.523 percent, which is the shared-neighbourhood multi-label cost stated in the module docstring, now measured. Reopening needs precision above 0.5 at a budget reaching a material share of the corpus wrong cells; neither detector nor their average is near it. Do not spend a card arm on a relabel from this ranking. Ledger: experiments/README.md section neighbour_errors 2026-09-05.

title: Budget curve before alpha on the label axis - and the headroom is at SMALLER budget, not larger
description:
CONDITIONAL on errors_relabel clearing 0.8578. If it lands flat or costs, the axis closes and this does not run.

errors_relabel.sh pre-registered its follow-through as 'the alpha curve (0.4/0.6/0.8), then a budget curve'. Q-BUDGET (Kimi, 2026-09-05T0250Z) says that ordering is backwards and gives the mechanism. Recorded here so the pre-registration is overridden in writing rather than quietly.

WHY BUDGET FIRST. Alpha and budget are NOT SEPARABLE. In BoMD's smooth re-labelling, lambda controls how far the noisy label moves toward the corrected target: at high precision (small budget) the detected cells are almost certainly wrong so a strong correction is safe, and at low precision (large budget) many detected cells are actually correct so the same strength corrupts good labels. Reed et al's bootstrapping makes the same point - the optimal alpha depends on how much you trust the detector. So alpha-then-budget yields a CONDITIONAL optimum, not a joint one: if budget changes, the alpha chosen at the old budget is no longer best. Running alpha first also mostly re-measures BoMD's published ablation (0.2/0.6/1.0 on a fixed detected set, 0.6 winning) on our corpus, which is a knob, not a mechanism.

THE CURVE SHAPE IS RISING THEN FALLING, not saturating. Rising from correcting real errors, falling as false corrections overwhelm them. BoMD's own benchmark (Table 4) shows the collapse and the authors state outright that at the most aggressive setting their re-labelling 'may be injecting too much noise into the training set'. Northcutt's Confident Learning formalises it: lowering the threshold to expand the detected set raises recall and drops precision, and past a point the corrected labels are worse than the original noisy ones.

THE REORDERING KIMI DID NOT STATE, AND IT IS THE ACTIONABLE PART. The literature's useful-precision band is roughly 0.6-0.7, below which correction stops being clearly beneficial. Our ranking's precision at the current 1,932-cell cut is 0.640 - the BOTTOM of that band, not the middle. The asymmetry is why it matters: a false correction ADDS a new error to training, while a missed error merely leaves an old one in place. So the expansions (1.5x, 2x) sit on the predicted-falling side of the curve and are the LOW-expected-value points, while 0.5x - 966 cells at materially higher precision - is the only point with predicted headroom.

RUN ORDER, therefore: 0.5x FIRST at alpha 0.6, against errors_relabel's own 1x as the control. That is one arm, roughly two hours, and it tests the mechanism at the point the mechanism predicts a gain. Expand to 1.5x ONLY if 0.5x comes back at or below 1x, because that ordering would mean we are on the rising side after all and the precision estimate is wrong. Alpha refinement (0.4/0.6/0.8) comes last and only at the winning budget.

MECHANICS. kneemri.evaluation.suspect_teacher has --labels/--flags/--alpha/--out and NO budget flag: budget is set by the --flags file, so a 0.5x arm needs a flags file holding the top 966 ranked cells rather than 1,932. Find the ranking that produced relabel_rank1932_a06.csv before writing the table. Kimi's cheaper alternative if card is tight: a 3 budgets x 3 alphas grid at ONE epoch each to read the trend, then commit full runs to the best corner - but one-epoch reads on this corpus are far below the 0.0062 floor, so treat that as direction-finding only, never as a result.

title: seat_value crashes on mean_probe holdout records: KeyError epoch
description: kneemri/runs/holdout_record.py:195 reads stored['epoch'] unconditionally, but the *_mean_probe.holdout.npz records written by the probe path carry no epoch key. So seat_value dies with KeyError: 'epoch is not a file in the archive' the moment a probe is named as a candidate, and it takes the whole run down rather than skipping the one record. Four probe records are affected on disk: radnet121@focal-max (0.8197), ortholarge@focal-attend (0.8249), ortholarge@focal-max (0.8249), v3large@focal-attend (0.8046), plus orthodiff_mean_probe and dinov2-large@focal-max. These score fine under column_headroom and count as scoreable in roster_check, so they look shippable everywhere a human looks and are unpriceable by the only tool that decides a seat. radnet121 is the RadImageNet DenseNet trunk the trunk-family lever was named for, so the hole sits exactly on the axis that was called the only open 1.5% lever. Fix: make epoch optional in HoldoutRecord.read, or have RecordMix.readings drop an unreadable record by name the way it already drops a checkpoint-less one.
notes: Fixed. read() now branches on stored.files: a missing epoch defaults to UNKNOWN_EPOCH and a missing source to PROBE, which is exactly what those two constants were declared to say — the PROBE docstring already stated 'Its epoch is UNKNOWN_EPOCH'. Arrays still raise, because a missing array is a truncated file and has no reading. Unit test test_read_without_stamps covers both halves. CORRECTION to this bead's original P1 framing: radnet121 was called the RadImageNet DenseNet trunk on the 1.5% lever, but the PROBE docstring records that the same trunk FITTED reads 0.6716 against the probe's 0.8197 — a probe is a property of frozen features and was never a shippable member, so no lane was blocked. The bug was a crash that took three other candidates down with it, which is a tooling defect and not a score one.

title: uv sync partial-extra runs damaged the venv mid-session
description: Two syncs with partial --extra lists (dev/devtools/labelnoise, then +attribution) uninstalled captum, nibabel and kaggle, and left h5py without a RECORD file and psutil with a locked .pyd. Symptoms were four pyrefly missing-attribute/missing-import errors and three cleanlab test failures reading 'module psutil has no attribute cpu_count' — all of which look like code regressions and none of which were. The kaggle CLI was also gone, which would have cost a submission slot had a mark been due. FIX THAT WORKED: uv sync --all-extras (never a partial extra list), plus --reinstall-package psutil for the file that was locked by a live .venv python at sync time. The lock came from stale .venv processes (a scratchpad script, a hung pytest, two duplicate mail listeners); stop those before syncing. Update the global memory note 'uv sync extras are exclusive' to name --all-extras as the invocation.

title: Nested hyperparameter selection is unusable at this holdout size

Recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_serve-time-column-mixing-is-a-null.md. Carry it to stack_fit and to any future selector.

title: DeviceBudget under-prices global attention on a large grid by 25 to 60 percent
description: DeviceBudget.needed() models activation as TRAINABLE_FLOOR * units + RETAINED_WEIGHT * retained, where units is summed tokens x width over blocks - LINEAR in tokens, with no term for attention being quadratic in them. Measured on coatnet2 at 384 px: units 10,321,920 against swinbase's 9,142,272, i.e. 13 percent more, yet Swin runs at an 8 GB cap and CoAtNet OOMs there. Reason: Swin's attention is confined to a 12x12 window and CoAtNet runs 14 blocks of GLOBAL attention over 576 tokens. Derived needed() = 8.358 GB; measured on the first real epoch, vram_alloc_gb 10.45 and vram_peak_gb 13.39. So the model understates allocation by about 25 percent and reservation by about 60 percent for a globally-attending trunk on a large grid. CONSEQUENCE TODAY IS SMALL because the fix is to name no cap at all - capped() returns max(needed() * CAP_HEADROOM, DEFAULT_SHARE * whole) and the co-tenant share (0.8 x 31.84 = 25.5 GB) swamps the error. It bites when an arm hand-names --vram-gb, which is taken EXACTLY as typed; coatnet_hybrid inherited swin_supervised's 8 and died twice on it. knee-ylp0 already says the flag should be dropped from every arm, which is the real fix. This bead records the cost model's blind spot so the number is not re-derived: a global-attention term wants to scale with tokens squared, not tokens.

title: Combiner axis CLOSED: a level-2 ridge loses to the flat vote by 8-18 thousandths
description: stack_combiner.py fits a ridge per finding over member ranks, blocked estimate, penalty chosen inside the kept rows. On honest12's twelve scoreable members over 909 holdout studies: flat vote 0.8750 (matches board's recorded 0.8751, harness validated), ridge own-finding -0.0179, ten blocks -0.0110, cross-finding -0.0076. Every variant loses. Pre-registered as a null by Kimi's Q-EL (Muller et al. 2022: mean equals or beats SVM/LR stacking in medical-image ensembles) with a >0.001 bar; missed in the wrong direction. Nothing that reduces our existing pool differently is worth a card or a slot. Does NOT say the ensemble is at its ceiling: Q-EL also says +0.016 over best single is normal, so the mix is not under-combining and the remaining distance lives in the MEMBERS. Recorded in experiments/README.md 2026-09-04.

title: seat_value prints two different quantities under the word 'rank' in one report
description: In the member-axes block the column reads 'rank 0.8970' and is a SCORE against a 'boundaries rank 0.8956'. In the candidates block the same word labels 'nearest 0.0445  mean 0.0319', which are rank DISTANCES, where small means most distinct. Both blocks print in a single seat_value report, and the batched sweep output interleaves them. Reading the distance column as the score column produced a P1 (knee-hmxko) claiming a roster member had inverted predictions, on a member whose solo AUC the same line printed as 0.5332. It took two follow-up runs to unwind. The distance columns want a name that cannot be read as a score -- 'nearest_dist'/'mean_dist', or a units suffix the way the neighbouring block already writes '0.0153 bits'. AUDIT the report's own vocabulary before renaming anything; the fix is in the report text, not in the measurement.

title: Prune at a SMALL budget, where the detector's precision is 0.640 rather than near base rate
description:
errors_dense pruned all 5,360 flags (10.14% of read cells) and cost -0.0158 vs band_dense. The gate measured precision 0.640 at budget 25 (4.05x random) decaying to 2.15x by budget 200, so at a 10.14% budget the flagged set is dominated by hard-but-correct cells rather than mislabelled ones, and those carry the corpus's highest gradients (the prune cost 3.4x what removing the same volume of random supervision costs).

THE ARM: the same --label-errors path with the flag table truncated to the top-N by confident-joint rank. N ~500 (about 1% of read cells) is where measured precision is still well above base rate.

PRICE, stated honestly and it is why this is P2 not P1: the upside is BOUNDED BY N. Removing ~500 genuinely-wrong cells out of 52,872 cannot plausibly move a mean AUC by the 0.0062 floor, let alone 1.5%. P(clears the floor) ~0.08. It costs ~4h of card. It is worth running only as an INSTRUMENT that separates 'the treatment is wrong' from 'the budget is wrong' — and only AFTER knee-f8hv5 (re-label) reads, because re-label subsumes it: if re-labelling at full budget works, the budget question is moot. Do not queue it ahead of f8hv5.

title: queue_check DOUBLE-QUEUED counts dead watchers, so it fires on a correctly-queued arm
description:
queue_check reports DOUBLE-QUEUED for experiments/arms/radiodino_corpus.sh saying 'more than one live after.sh will start each of these'. Three logs name that arm, but only ONE is live:

  after_band_pairmem.log      waits 'ARM DONE band_pairmem'   live
  after_radiodino_corpus.log  waits 'ARM DONE v3large_stack'  no watcher (dead)
  after_radnet_pinned.log     waits 'ARM DONE v3large_stack'  2/2 started, no watcher (dead)

The per-log liveness is computed correctly and PRINTED correctly in the listing directly above the warning, so the double-queue rule is joining on the log set rather than on the live subset it already has.

Cost: the warning is the one queue_check exists to raise (two arms of one geometry on one card), so a false positive trains the reader to ignore the true one. It fired on a chain that was armed correctly, in the same run that correctly flagged nothing else.

Fix: filter to watchers whose liveness check passed before counting owners. Also consider not counting an arm a dead watcher already STARTED (after_radnet_pinned.log is 2/2) — that is a finished obligation, not a pending one.

Same run also reports STRANDED for medsam_dense while medsam_dense is the process holding the card, which looks like the same class of defect on the opposite rule.

title: bd dolt push hangs past 10 minutes — session-close protocol cannot complete as written
description: Twice on 2026-09-04, 'bd dolt push' ran past the tool timeout (7m then 10m) with no output, in a PowerShell foreground call. Both times the surrounding git commit and git push completed fine once dolt push was dropped from the chain, so the Dolt remote is the thing that blocks, not git. Effect: the mandated close protocol (git pull --rebase; bd dolt push; git push) cannot be run as one chain, and chaining it costs a full tool timeout each time. Workaround in use: commit .beads/issues.jsonl and git push, skip dolt push. That still versions the issue set, since issues.jsonl is the git-tracked export. Needs a look at whether the Dolt remote is reachable at all from this machine.

title: Listener prints the WRONG re-arm command — .claude copy tells you to arm .agent-runtime
description: Both copies of listen_for_mail.py resolve their box from their own directory, which is correct. But the docstring and all three printed re-arm lines hardcode '.agent-runtime/listen_for_mail.py'. The .claude copy therefore ends every notification by telling the reader to arm the OTHER SIDE'S listener, which watches Kimi's box and delivers nothing while looking healthy. CLAUDE.md already records that this failure happened once. Fix: derive the printed path from __file__ (relpath against the repo root, forward slashes) so the message names the copy that is running. .claude/ is edit-protected for me, so this needs the owner or a different route.

title: RadioDino s16/s8 rows landed; patch-size pair is queued work, not yet run
description:
backbone.py now carries radiodinos16 (vit_small_patch16_224, 384) and radiodinos8 (vit_small_patch8_224, 384) alongside radiodinob16, all three through TimmHubWeights. load_check reads 18 entries, every one built from its own weights. The pair exists to read PATCH SIZE at constant width (Dehghan et al. arXiv:2602.18614, smaller patches beat 14/28 across twelve medical datasets, up to +12.78% balanced accuracy 2D).

PRICE: radiodino_s16 ~18 min (196 tokens/slice, cheaper than its own native224 control at 256); radiodino_s8 ~60-80 min (784 tokens, 4x MLP, up to 16x attention), gated on s16 clearing 0.80. Pair cost ~1.6 h of card.

GAIN. Patch size is a property of EVERY trunk in the table, not of this one. Dehghan et al. measured smaller patches beating 14/28 on twelve medical datasets, up to +12.78% balanced accuracy 2D. Our worst finding is Lateral Meniscus 0.7981 - focal, small-structure, the exact class that argument is about. A win reopens the whole trunk row rather than adding one member, which is the only class of finding that clears the 1.5% bar. Board read 2026-09-04T12:23Z: rank 36/3046, tied with 8 at 0.944, leader 0.953, gap 0.009 board = about +0.009 offline at the +0.98 top-band compression (knee-j4jog). This line previously quoted +0.0163 against a 0.937 champion and was stale by one champion.

P(clears the bar) ~= 0.15. Modal outcome is a flat, which closes the axis for 1.6 h - that is the reason to run it even at 0.15: the alternative is leaving a property of every trunk unmeasured. Ratio: 1.6 h for a 15% shot at reopening the trunk row, against the same card-hours buying one more member on a closed axis.

The marker arm_check matches is the literal 'PRICE:' WITH A COLON (PRICE_MARKS at kneemri/experiments/arm_check.py:49), and it greps the whole 'bd show' output, NOTES included. Both arms refused as UNPRICED on 2026-09-04 while this bead carried a full price block written as 'PRICE.' - a period, not a colon.
