title: Text supervision as an AUXILIARY LOSS is declined; the literature-backed form is contrastive PRETRAINING, gated on ortho_dense
description:
Two decisions in one bead, because they are the same axis split by mechanism. Kimi's Q-Y audit (research/2026-09-01_text_supervision_mechanism_audit.md, knee-iem6) separates the published record into (a) contrastive image-report PRETRAINING, (b) an auxiliary text-alignment loss during supervised fine-tuning, (c) a text branch at inference.

DECLINED: mechanism (b), the form this project already ran. experiments/arms/report_supervision.sh measured control rank24_s2026 0.8272, report term at 0.3 -> 0.8219 (-0.0053), at 1.0 -> 0.8209 (-0.0063), MONOTONE in the weight. I asked whether that refuted the axis or only its weakest member, naming three repairs: a Findings/Impression-only target, a stronger trunk control, and distilling a text teacher rather than adding a cosine pull.

The audit answers all three against me, and this is the part worth keeping. ConVIRT, CheXzero, MedCLIP, GLoRIA and BioViL/BioViL-T all place their gains in the PRETRAINED VISION ENCODER; the text encoder is discarded at fine-tuning or reduced to class-name prompts at inference. MedCLIP is the cleanest: CheXpert-5x200 ACC 0.596 against 0.320 for an ImageNet init, MIMIC 0.565 against 0.283 - all of it pretraining. Mechanism (b) has NO published medical gain at all; the nearest positive is TeS+CLIP (ICCV 2023, +4.4% on fine-grained sets) which uses class-name prompts, is not medical, and is not free-text reports. So repair 1 is still mechanism (b), repair 2 changes the baseline without changing the mechanism, and repair 3's teacher would itself have to be a mechanism-(a) model we do not have.

My suspicion was right that an explanation naming its own fix is the shape of a rationalisation, and the fix it named was inside the mechanism that does not work. Declined. It is re-opened by a published medical (b) result, not by another weight.

OPEN, AND GATED: mechanism (a). Continue a trunk with an image-report contrastive objective on this project's ~4,400 report-labelled studies, then fine-tune the 12-label task. Direct precedent, and the only literature-backed form of the axis.

WHY IT IS NOT ARMED TONIGHT. It must not run before ortho_dense reads. The whole argument for continuing a trunk on 4,400 studies is that the continuation is CHEAP relative to what it inherits - so it has to inherit from the right trunk, and which trunk that is (v3large or OrthoFoundation-L) is the question ortho_dense answers in ~3 h. Pretraining a trunk we have not shown is the right trunk spends the expensive half first. Second constraint: 4,400 unique reports is far below MedCLIP's corpus, and the same below-threshold arithmetic that priced our own DINO continuation as a likely loss (knee-440m: ~72k slices against a ~100k threshold) applies here and needs its own count before this is armed.

title: Post-ensemble readout axis is closed: threshold calibration cannot move a mean-AUC score
description:
Kimi's Q-M answer (2026-09-01, research/2026-09-01_past_ensemble_plateau_mechanisms.md) surveyed what carried the last 0.5-1% past an ensemble plateau in published work. The strongest item -- per-source/per-label threshold calibration, Nilay et al. +0.14 F1 over their own nine-model ensemble -- is INAPPLICABLE here and the reason is arithmetic, not judgement: our score is a mean of per-label AUCs, and AUC is invariant to any monotone per-column transform. A threshold choice cannot move it by any amount. F1 is exactly the metric where a threshold is the whole game, which is why the delta is so large there and identically zero here.

The rest of the axis was already closed by our own numbers: rank-vs-logit-vs-median averaging (record_mix --vote; whole pool RankAverage 0.8697 / LogitAverage 0.8702 / MedianLogit 0.8664, and the champion kernel has served LogitAverage since kneemri-vote), per-label member selection (label_combine 2026-08-26, the flat rank-average is the optimum of its own family), and overlap TTA (five whole-stack members, no gain above the 0.0062 floor). Mueller et al. arXiv 2201.11440 compared 12 pooling functions on medical data and found mean/median equal or better than learned stacking, which agrees with our measurement.

WHAT THIS BUYS: the last 0.5-1% is not hiding in how the ensemble is combined or read out. Combined with the seven board flats that closed the seating axis, the open levers are exactly two -- what a member IS (trunk family/supervision; knee-jyb6, knee-nj4l, knee-nz34) and what it is FED (input representation: localization/crop, in-plane resolution, slice sampling in mm rather than fraction, plane fusion, sequence weighting). The second has never been priced here; Q-O asks for it. Pseudo-labeling and confident learning stay live but are training-time, not readout.

title: The ConvNeXt backbone-lr ladder is monotone and never turned over
description: Three finished 12-epoch runs on ConvNeXtV2-base, same trunk: backbone-lr 4e-5 -> 0.7927 (cnx_dense, 352px), 1.2e-4 -> 0.7993 (cnx_mid_rate, 448px), 4e-4 -> 0.8186 (cnx_own_recipe, 448px). +0.0259 across the ladder and the LARGEST step is the last one (+0.0193), so the curve is still climbing at the top rung nobody has passed. cnx_dense's ledger entry predicted this in August ('4e-5 is a ViT ADAPTER rate ... convolutional trunks fine-tune roughly an order of magnitude higher') and the prediction is three-quarters confirmed. This does NOT license a 1.2e-3 arm on its own — cnx_own_recipe's PARTIAL branch names augmentation as the next knob. It licenses asking for an external prior first: Q-J1/Q-J2 were sent to Kimi 2026-09-01 19:00Z asking what LR ratio published cross-family medical ensembles give a CNN branch versus a ViT branch. A paper saying 'conv trunks want 10-30x the ViT rate' buys the right rung in one arm instead of walking the ladder.

title: arm_check --only does not match certainty_ramp; --smoke was a silent no-op

title: fastMRI+ knee labels are 974 studies of BOX annotations, not 1172 study-level

Measured on the cloned MIT repo (D:/data/raw/fastmri/labels/Annotations/knee.csv): 974 distinct studies, 16,167 annotation rows, and study_level='No' on 16,154 of them. The annotations are per-slice bounding boxes (x,y,width,height), which is a DIFFERENT KIND of supervision from our study-level labels - localized, not just more studies. That is the lever, and the survey undersells it. title: KMAR-50K: 1,444 free CC-BY knee scans, unlabelled — needs a mechanism before it needs a download
description: data.mendeley.com/datasets/xw7mrg7ntg + /95w9f5tzz8, CC BY 4.0, ~20.7 GB, no registration (Kimi Q-D, research/2026-09-01_knee-mri-corpora-survey.md). NO finding labels — motion-artifact pairs — so a supervised merge weights every one of the twelve columns at 0.0 and the block contributes exactly zero gradient. Rijeka and MRNet both carry at least ACL; this does not. It is therefore NOT a merged4 arm. The mechanism has to come first, and there are two candidates: pseudo-labelling by the champion ensemble (self-distillation, cannot exceed the teacher on axes it knows, gains only encoder robustness) or SSL pretraining (a separate build). PRICE: 20.7 GB download + ~11 GB cache against 98 GB free tonight, plus a mechanism that does not exist yet, against a card already committed to merged3. P(clears the bar without a mechanism) ~ 0. Blocked on merged3_corpus reading, which prices the corpus axis on data we already own and already label.

Q-AE 2026-09-02: kmar50k is motion-artifact/clean PAIRS, not a labelled corpus. No published precedent found for using real motion artifacts as train-time augmentation to improve classification on a clean same-distribution test set. Literature focuses on artifact detection/correction. Unless hidden test contains motion artifacts, this is not a useful augmentation corpus for the competition.
KMAR-50K has no finding labels, so it only enters Scheme A (merged unlabeled SSL continuation). Without OAI the merged unlabeled pool is ~122k slices, near the low end of the positive SSL regime; expected mean-AUC gain +0.002-0.005. Not a priority until Scheme B reads positive.

title: Audit: no single source of truth for run configuration
description: Adding one training flag (the disagreement sampler, knee-nyqc) required edits in SIX places that all restate the same fact: flag_vocabulary.py (argparse), options.py (TrainingOptions field), landed.py (Request field + wanted() entry), run_setup.py (requested() mapping + attach), trainer.py (policy key + policies() entry), member_record.py (config stamp or NOT_IN_CONFIG write-off). AUDIT SCOPE: (1) enumerate every option and count how many files name it; (2) decide whether one declaration site (a per-option descriptor carrying flag spec, default, request name, policy key, and config disposition) can generate the other five; (3) price the migration against the ~60 existing options and say whether the gates survive as generated checks or retire. title: SupervisionGap.reported scores findings under their neighbour's name on a short table
description: Named in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_the-label-table-axis-is-exhausted.md and never filed. SupervisionGap.reported returns only the columns a table actually carries, while 'against' names the columns BY POSITION. A foreign table missing one finding therefore scores every later finding under its neighbour's name — silently, with plausible numbers. It has never fired here because our own tables carry all twelve findings, so this is latent, not active. It becomes live the moment any foreign or partial label table is read, which knee-ombx (MRNet) and any Rijeka-side table would do. Fix: join on column NAME, and refuse a table whose finding set is not the expected one rather than aligning what is left.

title: README:3896 attributes calib_span's 0.8545 to band_span

On disk band_span_s2026 = 0.8565; 0.8545 is calib_span_s2026's exact score. res392's 0.8523 is correct (held by res392_ws_s2026). The table four lines above reads 'five, without | best single 0.8565', which IS band_span's real number, so the same passage carries both values. Two readings and I cannot pick between them from the text: either the sentence means calib_span and misnames it, or it means band_span and miscopied a neighbour's score. The ranking claim ('best single member in the pool') survives either way only if the subject beats 0.8565 rather than 0.8545. Adjudicate against member_curve's own output for that pool, then fix the number or the name. Do NOT guess: the house rule is that a number nothing stands behind gets bracketed, not corrected on a hunch.

title: Slot-4 candidate champ8 (champion + an eighth dark seat) was killed BY the board record before it cost a slot
description:
Built comp/kernels/kneemri-champ8 -- raptorweight's seating plus small_batch6_ff -- then ran the check the peak8 repeat proved was missing: grep comp/board.jsonl for the operation, not the kernel name. It came back with three rows that already answer it. vjepaseat_v1 ADDED an eighth seat to this exact champion shape and read 0.943 against 0.944. dark7_v1 added THIS EXACT MEMBER, small_batch6_ff, as a seventh dark seat on dark6 and read 0.937 flat, with its own text saying 'the all-data dose is spent at six, measured rather than extrapolated'. holdswap_v1 exchanged a champion seat for the best-priced alternative and read exactly 0.000. Together with raptorweight_v1's own +0.001 for a 2.3x weight move, that is four operations on WHO SITS and four flats, which is knee-uco3's inert-seat reading with four supports.

The kernel was deleted rather than shipped. Recorded because the NEAR-MISS is the finding: the entry passed every existing gate (kit_check, mount_check, roster_check would all have been green) and was stopped only by a grep of the record, which is exactly the gate the peak8 P0 asks for. This is the second candidate in one hour that the record killed and the tooling would not have.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SLOT SELECTION: no further slot goes to a seating operation on this pool. What the record leaves open is the levers that change what a member SEES (decode, corpus) or WHAT IT IS (trunk). kneemri-champviews is the first of those -- the champion's exact seating served under SpatialViews, nothing reseated.

title: Re-extract the negation slice corpus-wide: 12 of 108 over-calls are missed negations
description:
knee-deo5 measured it: missed_negation fires on 12 of 108 confident false positives (11.1%) against 3 of 203 confident true positives (1.5%), difference +9.6% [+4.4,+15.3] study-clustered. That is the ONLY one of four extractor categories that separates from the control; laterality, hedge_dropped and historical all fire MORE on cells the radiologist agreed with and are report style, not extraction error.

SIZE, STATED HONESTLY SO THIS IS NOT OVERSOLD. Clean extractor failure is 16 of 108 (14.8%) and that is an UPPER bound (see below). 15% of a 15.8% supervision hole is ~2.3% of annotated cells. This will NOT clear 1.5% absolute on its own. It is worth doing because it is corpus-wide (4,407 studies), upstream of every member, and cheap — not because it is the lane. The lane question is closed the other way: 84 of 108 (77.8%) is rubric mismatch plus real disagreement.

WHAT TO DO. core.data.labels.negation_scope already holds the eight-language rule that found these (forward-scoping DENIALS bounded at the next clause boundary, clause-scoping NORMALITY predicates, a lesion-family test for what the denial must land on). Run it over all 4,407 reports, not the 57, and flip the verdict where it fires on a report-YES cell. Measure the flip rate before flipping anything.

WHY THE 14.8% IS AN UPPER BOUND. The 3 surviving control negations are LOCATION errors, not vocabulary errors: the report denies the finding in one sentence and asserts it in another, and the locator hands over the first. Not fixable without a parse. So a corpus-wide flip WILL flip some cells the radiologist would have agreed with, and the flip needs the same true-positive control before it is trusted.

See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_the-overcalls-are-mostly-not-the-extractor.md

title: Second head predicting P(label is wrong), supervised externally — blocked on the confident-learning detector
description:
OWNER QUESTION 2026-08-31: would heads returning label score AND confidence separately help, and how would they collapse?

WHY THE NAIVE FORM IS REDUNDANT. For a Bernoulli the score already IS the confidence — p=0.5 means 'not sure'. A second head is non-redundant only if it separates first-order from second-order uncertainty (evidence balanced vs no evidence), i.e. the evidential/Beta form: output (alpha, beta), score alpha/(alpha+beta), confidence alpha+beta. No heteroscedastic, evidential or log-variance head exists anywhere in kneemri/models, kneemri/training or core (grepped 2026-08-31); 'dissent' is member decorrelation, unrelated.

THE THREE COLLAPSES, and what each is worth.
(1) Discard c at inference (Kendall & Gal's standard use): c becomes a pure training-time loss-attenuation device, ranking comes from the score head. This is the SAME lever as confident learning, but self-referential — the model decides which labels to distrust from its own fit on data it trained on. Degenerate solution is real (raise sigma on everything hard), and with rarer positives it collapses toward ignoring the minority class, which is where AUC lives. OOF disagreement is the identified version of the same signal and costs no card.
(2) Shrink the score by c: changes the ranking so it CAN move AUC, but only if c predicts CORRECTNESS rather than DIFFICULTY, and nothing in this formulation supervises the first.
(3) Confidence-weighted ensembling, sum(c_k p_k)/sum(c_k): the only genuinely new use, and its ceiling is already measured. knee-qrtx puts member disagreement at 0.0565 bits in a 0.6807-bit pool (8.3%, and FALLING as members are added). Same wall as a better seat.

Compare to grade_ladder's post-mortem, which is the same shape of answer one axis over: 'the labels are already a severity encoding; laddering them re-expresses the same supervision rather than adding any.' Here: the probability is already a confidence.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WORTH BUILDING, and the blocker. A head predicting P(this label is wrong), supervised EXTERNALLY — by the 58 gold radiologist studies and by the confident-learning detector's flags — not by the model's own fit. That is second-order and identified, and it is a distillation of the detector into the model so it can act on studies with no gold annotation.

BLOCKED ON: the confident-learning detector (CPU, running 2026-08-31T15:25Z) beating a prevalence-matched random baseline on the 108 known radiologist disagreements over the gold 58. If the detector cannot find known label errors from OOF disagreement, a self-referential head has no reason to find them either, and this bead closes unbuilt.

COST IF UNBLOCKED: ~4.5 h card for one arm, plus the cost that every existing member becomes non-comparable on the head axis. Do not spend it before the detector reads.
notes:
PUBLISHED EVIDENCE, found 2026-08-31 (research/2026-08-31_report_label_noise_and_uncertainty_heads.md). The field has already benchmarked this and it loses. 'Benchmarking Uncertainty and its Disentanglement in multi-label Chest X-Ray Classification' (arXiv 2508.04457) runs 13 UQ methods on MIMIC-CXR-JPG over ResNet and ViT, extending Evidential Deep Learning, HetClass NNs and Deep Deterministic Uncertainty to the MULTI-LABEL setting — our setting exactly. Findings: ensemble methods (D-Ens, S-Ens) 'consistently perform best across architectures'; EDL sits at ECE ~0.4, 'strongly ill-calibrated for both models'; and decisively for the second-order argument, 'almost all methods show significant correlations between EU and AU', with many methods failing to disentangle the two at all — the authors advise applying the information-theoretic framework 'with caution'. They also never report whether an uncertainty head moves AUROC/AUPRC against a plain BCE baseline; the entire evaluation is calibration, OOD and correctness prediction. So there is no published claim of a classification gain to replicate.

This does NOT close the bead as written. What it closes is the EVIDENTIAL/heteroscedastic form — a head that estimates its own second-order uncertainty from its own fit. The bead's actual proposal, a head predicting P(this label is wrong) supervised EXTERNALLY by the gold 58 and by the confident-learning detector's flags, is not what that benchmark tested: it is supervised regression onto an external target, not self-estimated uncertainty, and it is therefore not subject to the EU/AU degeneracy they measure. Keep the bead, narrow it to the externally-supervised form, and treat the evidential form as retired on published evidence rather than on our own card time.

SEPARATE CONSEQUENCE, for knee-qrtx. Our 12.7%/8.3% reducible-uncertainty read uses the same information-theoretic decomposition this paper cautions about. It stands better than a single-model split would — ours is computed over a deep ensemble of separately trained members, the method class that won their benchmark, and it is used as an UPPER BOUND on what another member can buy rather than as a per-cell signal. But the caveat is real: '87.3% aleatoric' should be read as 'at most 12.7% is addressable by more members', not as a clean partition into ambiguity and ignorance. That belongs in the interpretation, which currently states it without the caveat.

title: Systole's negatives: five axes NOT to queue card time on here, and the one lever that transferred OOD
description:
Read of D:/personal_projects/cardiac-seg on 2026-08-31, for its NEGATIVES. Same owner, different modality, same wall (a generalisation gap that would not close). Recording so this project does not re-buy them. Each is evidence about cardiac MRI segmentation, not proof about knee — but each cost real card time there, and none has a mechanism that obviously stops at the modality boundary.

WHAT FAILED THERE, all measured, all with matched controls:
 * Intensity harmonization is FLAT across the whole design space, 0.86 +/- 0.01. Nyul null (0.857 vs 0.864). N4 bias correction REGRESSED both unseen test vendors. Bias-field augmentation REGRESSED (Canon 0.839 -> 0.827, ECE 0.172 -> 0.192, AUPRC 0.600 -> 0.563). Five separate confirmations.
 * SAME-RECIPE DEEP ENSEMBLING bought nothing on unseen vendors: Canon +0.000, GE +0.006. The 4-seed ensemble's own uncertainty decomposition showed only 15-18% reducible headroom, i.e. the members agreed. THIS IS OUR SHAPE — see knee-qrtx, which runs that decomposition here, and knee-nj4l, which reached the monoculture verdict from the entry side.
 * MC-dropout regressed EF by 2pp and was killed.
 * Directed spectral domain adaptation closed the PSD distance 2.88 -> 0.19 and STILL LOST. A method can hit its own stated objective perfectly and buy nothing on the task.

Its conclusion, in its own words: the gap is not reducible by augmentation, same-recipe ensembling or normalization — the reducible lever is a STRONGER MODEL CLASS, and a same-recipe ensemble is structurally blind to it.

ITS ONE OOD-TRANSFERRING LEVER: a linear calibration of the EF bias, FITTED ON VAL, transferred to both unseen vendors (val 7.1 -> 5.4, Canon 9.9 -> 5.4, GE 11.0 -> 7.4) while temperature scaling did NOT. NOTE FOR US, and it is probably fatal: our competition metric is ranking-based, and any MONOTONE recalibration leaves AUC unchanged. So this transfers only if the metric is not pure AUC — check comp/ before spending anything on it. Written down here so the check happens once instead of the idea resurfacing.

METHODOLOGY WORTH IMPORTING, cheap and general:
 * 'Per factor, pick ONE direction' — stripping a nuisance factor and augmenting it are opposite bets on the same axis, and running both cancels. We have no such rule written down.
 * Always run the MATCHED default baseline in the same harness before calling anything a mover.
 * Compare arms at equal GRADIENT-STEP budget, not equal epochs, when the data size differs — this confound invalidated systole's own data-scarcity curve.
 * A negative on a finite test set says the test lacks that axis, not that the method is wrong. Systole states this about its own N4 result rather than about someone else's.

title: 38 of 164 arms never ran - speculative files in the directory every census sweeps
description:
Measured 2026-08-31: experiments/arms/ holds 164 shells, 126 with a run on disk and 38 with none. Speculative files, which the project rule forbids in the same words it forbids speculative folders.

The cost is not disk. arm_read --assert, arm_check and the control-line census all enumerate the directory, so every 'N of M arms declare no control' number this project quotes as a harness fact is computed over a denominator that includes arms nobody will ever run. That is the same denominator defect that CLAUDE.md already records twice.

Several are dead on arrival rather than merely unfunded: stack_cover_ff closed today with knee-qphd, v3base_own_recipe is on the do-not-arm list.

DISPOSAL RULE, same discipline as comp/members.declines: delete outright where a bead closed the idea (the closed bead already holds the reasoning and the arm adds nothing); keep the file with a one-line decline header where the idea is live but unfunded. Never bulk-delete - an arm header is a pre-registration, and a live one is the only place some of these arguments are written down.

DO NOT touch the 126 that ran. They are the experiment record: today's stack224 decline cites that arm's per-label shape as the evidence that named the aggregator mechanism.

title: Reorganisation: move every module into the pipeline that owns it
description: The cheap half, and the one that must come LAST. Execute the taxonomy: move modules into their pipeline packages, update imports, add the import-linter contracts that make the direction one-way, and regenerate docs/architecture/graph.json in the same commit. Blocked by the taxonomy decision and by the hook-point work, because moving a module that is about to gain a scheduled caller means moving it twice. A folder reshuffle done before the map is drawn rebuilds the confusion at a new path, which is exactly what the epic exists to stop.

title: DECIDE: experiment tracking - mlflow, or an argued alternative
description: The owner named mlflow. The honest counter is that this repo already has a ledger (experiments/README.md), a per-run metrics file, comp/board.jsonl and a set of checks that read them, so a tracker added beside those is a second home for the same facts - the DRY violation the project's own rules forbid. The decision is therefore not 'mlflow yes/no' but 'what does a tracker give that the ledger cannot, and does the ledger move INTO it or does the tracker read FROM it'. Concrete criteria to answer against: does it survive an arm dying mid-run, does it work with the existing arm shell scripts without a wrapper, does it cost card time, and can convergence_check/trajectory_check read its store. Depends on the audit; independent of the hook points.

description: arm_read --assert census, 2026-08-31: 86 of 162 arms in experiments/arms declare no control line, so no reading of them has a mechanical denominator. The urgent subset is the arms that are themselves QUOTED as controls by other arms - stack224, native224, calib_dense_hold, band_dense, merged_span_cf - because an arm read against them inherits their silence. title: merged_labelwise_cf: external corpus x labelwise pooling, the one cell where both greedy diversities meet
description:
The route statement (experiments/README.md:4783) says 0.950 needs a seat that is BOTH high-quality and in a pixel group nothing else occupies - external data AND a different decode path in the same member. merged_span_cf answered that on the slice/band square. The POOLING axis has never been varied on the merged corpus.

Greedy seat two is merged_span_cf (merged corpus, 0.8618, largest single jump in the 111-member curve). Greedy seat three is labelwise_dense_s2026 (--slice-pooling labelwise, 0.8613). Separately seated, never combined. If the two diversities are independent the combination occupies a cell no member does; if they are the same diversity wearing two names it collapses onto one of them.

One variable against merged_span_cf: pooling max -> labelwise. Corpus, eval ruler, fold, slices 20, band 0.2-0.8, rate, epochs, calibrated-targets all held.

Fold 0 deliberately, not a blind refit, unlike the two arms queued ahead of it. A --fold -1 member is only readable on the board and the board costs a slot. This cell has no fold-0 evidence behind it at all, so a blind arm would carry two unknowns for the same card time as one. The cheap proxy gates the expensive commit; the blind refit is a later arm if it earns a seat.

Read (pre-registered, control merged_span_cf = 0.8618):
  >= 0.8618 - diversities independent, cell is free, take the seat.
  0.8556-0.8617 (inside the 0.0062 unseparable band) - expected, NOT a verdict. Keep iff greedy over the roster picks it.
  <= 0.8555 - labelwise pooling and the merged corpus substitute. Third instance of the merged corpus colliding with a finer decode (slices, band, now pooling), which promotes that from an observation to a property of the corpus, and the merged lane's seat is one cell wide.
notes: PRICE: ~100 min of card that is otherwise idle after 02:35 UTC (the two _ff arms ahead of it finish then), plus zero submission slots - fold 0 is readable offline. GAIN: the ONE cell where the curve's two independent diversity axes meet; the pixel-group axis is also the axis with amplified board transfer (0.0059 offline read +0.014 on the board, 2.4x), so a seat here is worth more than its holdout delta says. P(clears the 0.0015 seat bar as a greedy pick over the roster) ~ 0.35 - merged_dense_cf already showed the merged corpus substituting for a finer decode (-0.0028), and labelwise pooling is a finer decode by the same argument, so the modal landing is inside the 0.0062 unseparable band with the seat decided by greedy rather than by the member number. RATIO: ~100 min of idle card for a pre-registered three-way read that closes the merged lane's width either way - a null here is not a null result, it is the third point that turns 'the merged corpus collides with finer decodes' into a property and sends the route statement at a different EXTERNAL CORPUS (MRNet, knee-ombx) rather than at another path. NOT CONDITIONAL on holdswap_v1's bands: this is a member for the pool, not a single-seat swap, so bands C/D do not retire it.

The work ran and the ledger priced it; the bead was never marked. Reversible - bd update --status open if a reading here is still owed.

title: trajectory_check is blind to short warm-restart budgets, which is now a lane we run
description:
Found 2026-08-30 22:18Z while cnx_warm_anneal was running.

python -m kneemri.experiments.trajectory_check --run <cnx_warm_anneal metrics> --target 0.8186 returns:
'REFUSED: no run under <processed root> reached epoch 3 with 10 recorded. A check that measured nothing has not passed.'

That is the tool WORKING -- it refuses rather than inventing a gain from a corpus it does not have, which is exactly the discipline it was built with after lora_r8_v3small_224 lifted its ceiling two and a half times. The defect is the CORPUS, not the logic.

CAUSE. trajectory_check measures the epoch-3-to-peak gain across runs matched to the arm's OWN epoch budget. The corpus it was calibrated on is twelve-epoch runs (n=96: median +0.0210, p90 +0.0380, max +0.0529). cnx_warm_anneal asks for six (recipe epochs '6', confirmed in its metrics header), and essentially nothing on disk is a six-epoch run, so the match set is empty.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW rather than as a curiosity. Warm restarts are a lane this project has just committed to: warm_calib_lowlr closed branch A of knee-wbwq by showing warm starting is a TIME mechanism (one warm epoch is worth about twelve cold ones), and the whole POINT of that result is that the next arms are SHORT. Branch B -- a LoRA parent warm-started with a fresh --lora-rank -- will be short for the same reason. So the instrument that can end a bad job is blind to precisely the lane the ledger just recommended, and it will stay blind for as long as the lane's runs are the only short ones.

CONSEQUENCE, measured on this arm. cnx_warm_anneal priced itself at '~20 min at 6 epochs'. Its epochs are running 756-770s, so six is ~76 min -- a 3.8x underestimate of the card cost, and no instrument was able to arbitrate it mid-run. It was allowed to continue on judgment alone, which is the state trajectory_check exists to remove.

FIX, in cost order. (1) Cheapest and probably right: let the budget match be a BAND rather than equality, and report the band it used, so a six-epoch arm is priced against the eight-to-twelve corpus with the mismatch stated. The gain-to-peak curve is unlikely to be discontinuous in budget. (2) Better but slower: build a short-budget corpus as the warm lane produces one, and keep the strict match. (3) Do NOT widen it silently -- the refusal text is currently honest and a wrong number here TRUNCATES A JOB, which is the one action that cannot be undone by re-reading.

Do not fix by loosening the refusal into a pass.

title: Jensen-Shannon between members: the confidence axis a rank average throws away
description:
OWNER, 2026-08-30, named KL divergence as an analysis instrument. Synthesis: research/2026-08-30_analysis-instruments-distance-divergence-attribution.md.

THE INCUMBENT is that there is no single one, which is itself the finding. Distribution questions are answered today by narrow tools that each read one moment: prevalence_match (base rates), foreign_overlap (study overlap), level_calibration and --calibrated-targets (target sharpness), paired_floor (noise bands).

THE THREE USES, ranked.
1. MEMBER DISAGREEMENT AS DIVERGENCE, NOT CORRELATION. Two members can rank studies identically and still be confidently different: one saturated near 0/1, the other hedged. Rank correlation is blind to that by construction. Symmetric KL, or better Jensen-Shannon (bounded, a proper metric), sees it. This matters because a rank-average ensemble DISCARDS exactly the confidence a divergence term would read. NEARLY FREE: consumes prediction arrays already on disk, zero card.
2. DISTRIBUTION SHIFT BETWEEN CORPORA. The Kaggle test set is hidden, so no divergence to it is computable and any claim that our holdout matches the test distribution is unknowable. Say that rather than reaching for it. What IS computable: divergence between our own splits, and between our corpus and any external corpus (MRNet, knee-ombx) BEFORE it is trusted as extra data. That is the honest version of the question.
3. TEACHER/STUDENT DIVERGENCE for the knee-8009 distillation lane, where a score-distribution matching loss is needed and the pair-based imitation term currently stands in for one.

THE HONEST COUNTER. KL is asymmetric and unbounded, and it explodes wherever the reference has near-zero mass, which is exactly the rare-finding regime (MCL, synovitis) where our per-label scores are already weakest. Use Jensen-Shannon or smoothed KL, and never report one on a thin label without its support count beside it.

PRICE: ~2 hours of code for use 1, zero card, 0 slots. Cheapest instrument of the three the owner named.
notes: AUDITED 2026-08-31 and it is ALREADY BUILT: kneemri/evaluation/member_divergence.py implements Jensen-Shannon divergence in bits between two members' predictions read as Bernoulli beliefs (per study, per label, then mean), and it is already printed by 'python -m kneemri.kaggle.seat_value' directly beneath MemberDistance. It chooses JS over KL for exactly the reason this bead names: KL is asymmetric and unbounded and explodes where the reference has near-zero mass, which is the rare-finding regime our weakest per-label scores live in; JS is symmetric, bounded in [0,1] bits, and a proper metric under its square root. Its honest counter, also written down: high divergence with high rank correlation is a member that is only differently SCALED, so the pair worth hunting is high divergence AND low rank correlation. Nothing left to build; closing.

title: Mahalanobis on embeddings: the seat ruler runs on a proxy for the quantity that actually transfers
description:
OWNER, 2026-08-30, named Mahalanobis distance as an analysis instrument worth having. Synthesis: research/2026-08-30_analysis-instruments-distance-divergence-attribution.md.

THE INCUMBENT. member_distance.py prices diversity as per-label Spearman RANK CORRELATION over the twelve predictions, averaged, reported as NEAREST (twin detector) and MEAN. record_mix greedy consumes it. It is the most decision-heavy tool in the repo: it declined raptor_distill (admitted 44th of 121) and distill_pairs before it, and knee-for6 was closed on its verdict.

THE GAP. It measures distance in PREDICTION space. The quantity measured to transfer to the board is DECODE PATH / PIXEL GROUP (knee-nas5, ~2.4x the board slope), and knee-for6 closed with the words "distillation moves ORDERING, the seat ruler prices PIXEL GROUP". Prediction-space rank correlation is a PROXY for that, and a whole axis has already been closed on the proxy. Mahalanobis over EMBEDDINGS measures representation distance directly and divides out the pool covariance, so a member counts as far only along an axis the pool does not already span. It also separates a genuinely distinct member from a merely NOISY one, which rank correlation cannot do by construction, since both decorrelate.

THE HONEST COUNTER. With ~121 candidates and embedding width in the hundreds the covariance is rank-deficient. It needs shrinkage (Ledoit-Wolf) or a projection, and that choice is a knob that can quietly fit the answer. ADOPTION GATE, non-negotiable: the new ruler must first REPRODUCE the seat decisions the board has already validated before it is trusted to overturn one. A ruler that disagrees with the board on day one is a bug, not a finding.

PRICE: no card for the ruler itself (embeddings dump in the same pass that writes predictions). Half a day of code. 0 slots. It scores no points. It is bought as an INSTRUMENT that could re-open knee-for6 and re-rank the whole candidate pool.
notes:
BUILT 2026-08-31, NOT ADOPTED. Three modules land: kneemri/evaluation/member_space.py (the members as points - per-label rank-normalised predictions, centred on the pool mean; its own module because the coordinates are a separate subject from the rulers, and because an embedding dump replaces it without touching a ruler), kneemri/evaluation/member_mahalanobis.py (the whitened distance, taken IN THE SPAN via the SVD of the centred matrix rather than by inverting a features-by-features covariance that is catastrophically rank-deficient at ~121 members; eigenvalues shrunk Ledoit-Wolf style, (1-a)*lambda + a*mean(lambda), with sensitivity/unstable reporting the ordering at several a so a verdict surviving only one shrinkage is named as no verdict), and kneemri/evaluation/member_axes.py (the JOIN, which is the actual instrument).

THE JOIN, because three columns printed side by side would have been the tool-dump the owner objected to. Rank correlation, Jensen-Shannon and whitened separation place a candidate in one of four cells: TWIN (or SCALED when JS is far - same opinion, different confidence, which a temperature knob buys more cheaply than a seat), NOISY (decorrelates along an axis the pool is already wide in - the cell a rank ruler alone most flatters), DISTINCT (the only cell that is a seat), PUZZLE (reported, never acted on). Cell boundaries are the ROSTER'S OWN median nearest reading on each ruler, so they move when the roster moves and no cell can be defined without a roster that has neighbours. Wired into kneemri/kaggle/seat_value.py, which already printed the other two rulers - no fourth unowned CLI.

WHAT IS STILL OWED, AND IT IS THE WHOLE ADOPTION GATE. The Mahalanobis column has not been run against the board-validated seat decisions. Until it reproduces them in writing on this bead, it may not overturn one: a ruler that disagrees with the board on day one is a bug, not a finding. Nothing in record_mix consumes these modules and nothing should until that is answered. Both reports print an ADOPTION GATE line saying so. The gate is deliberately NOT automated - a check that scored the ruler against the board would be the ruler grading its own homework.

THE OTHER STANDING GAP: the features are prediction space, not embeddings. The bead names embeddings as the ideal and they are - representation distance is nearer the decode-path quantity measured to transfer at ~2.4x. An embedding dump costs a forward pass per member over the holdout. MemberSpace is the seam it plugs into.
2026-09-17 01:36Z — THE GATE SHOULD COVER rank AND js, NOT maha ALONE. Two members tonight were called DISTINCT by member_axes and both priced NEGATIVE as seats:
  ortho_dense_s2026     rank 0.8809  js 0.0286  maha 3.674  -> seat_add -0.0006
  erase_own_cells_s2026 rank 0.9037  js 0.0092  maha 2.469  -> seat_add -0.0004
against roster boundaries rank 0.9216 / js 0.0092 / maha 3.540. The first is distinct on all three axes and js 3x the boundary; the second sits AT the js boundary and is distinct on rank alone. Neither bought a seat.

So the tool's own headline -- 'DISTINCT is the only cell that is a seat' -- is falsified on two cases in one night, and the failure is not specific to the maha column this gate was written about. rank and js were equally unpredictive here. Widen the gate: NO axis in member_axes licenses a seat until that axis reproduces board-validated seats; only seat_add prices one. n=2 is a small n, and this is not a claim that the axes are worthless -- it is a claim that they have not yet earned the sentence the tool prints.

title: 84% of the scored pool is ONE encoder: every non-DINOv2-S trunk was judged on 1-4 runs against a recipe tuned over 113
description:
Census over all 191 runs with a holdout record, best peak AUC per trunk variant:

  trunk      runs   best     run
  small      113    0.8964   recal_holdannot_s2026      <- DINOv2 ViT-S
  base         4    0.8512   base_dense_s2026
  v3base       4    0.8455   v3base_dense_s2026
  vjepa2l      2    0.8343   vjepa_member_s2026
  swinbase     3    0.8331   swin_supervised_s2026
  v3small      3    0.8217   lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026
  cnxbase      4    0.8186   cnx_own_recipe_s2026
  raddino      2    0.8155   raddino_normfix_s2026
  v3splus      1    0.8012   dinov3_v3splus_224_lr8e-6_s2026
  vitin21k     1    0.7847   vit_in21k_s2026

113 of 191 runs are one encoder; adding the DINOv3 variants makes it 84% one FAMILY. Every other trunk has
had between one and four attempts, and each was scored against a recipe (band, slices, pooling, lr,
train-size, calibrated targets) that 113 runs of search tuned for DINOv2 ViT-S. That is an unmatched
comparison, not a measurement of the trunk.

WHY THIS IS THE OPEN LEVER RATHER THAN A COMPLAINT. Every closed axis in knee-m69u was measured INSIDE that
113: ensemble count, spread, per-label weighting, combiner, decode geometry, slice order, composition,
recalibration, distillation. knee-uco3's seat-saturation law is stated in its own text as measured only over
near-duplicate DINO seats. A pool that is 84% one encoder saturating at six seats is the expected result and
says nothing about what a genuinely uncorrelated member would add. The label lane just closed at +0.0003
(knee-fuhq) and the knob axes are closed; trunk diversity is what is left that could plausibly clear 1.5%.

THE FAILURES SO FAR ARE MOSTLY PLUMBING, NOT TRUNKS. vjepa2l's history is a weights mirror that did not
exist, a mount leaf that was wrong, and a member silently dropped by KernelRun while its entry scored under
a name it never had (knee-nbk3, farseat_v1). raddino needed a norm fix before it read at all. None of those
measured an encoder. Recorded experience is not a verdict on the asset.

NEVER RUN AT ALL, though backbone.py supports them: convnext, vit, vitb16, vits16, vits16plus, swin, large.

WHAT THE ARM IS. Not another one-shot. Pick ONE non-DINO trunk and give it the same courtesy the 113 gave
DINOv2-S: a short recipe search over the two or three knobs the trunk actually changes (lr, train-size,
pooling), then judge it BOTH solo and as a seat via seat_value against the champion. The seat number is the
one that matters - the user's standing direction is that a member that does not outperform is still worth
testing in the ensemble, because the object is diversity, not averaging seven copies of one number.

Pre-register per attempt before it runs, against the roster merit level, not the control.
close_reason: Folded into knee-nj4l as a note - the census belongs on the monoculture bead, not beside it as a rival P0.

title: Band mm-normalisation is not worth arming: the same fraction reads as the same distance (p90/p10 1.27-1.52)
description:
The through-plane band stays a FRACTION of the acquired stack while in-plane is already mm-normalised (crop_mm=130.0 through pixel_spacing). The case for normalising the band to millimetres needs the same fraction to read as materially different extents across studies.

Measured, card-free, 200 studies / 923 series at band 0.2-0.8 (core/data/corpus/band_coverage.py now reports the per-study span spread the mean was hiding):

  slot            mean   p10    p90   p90/p10   n
  AX_FLUID_FS    126.3   99.0  150.8   1.52    197
  COR_FLUID_FS   108.3   93.7  126.0   1.34    193
  COR_T1         108.1   94.5  126.0   1.33    133
  SAG_FLUID_FS   103.0   87.3  117.6   1.35    190
  SAG_FLUID_NOFS 104.9   93.5  118.5   1.27    123
  SAG_T1         100.8   84.9  115.5   1.36     87

The premise is false. Sagittal - where every band arm was decided - spans 1.27-1.36 p10 to p90, not the ~2x
the axis assumed. A fixed-mm band would move the field of view ~15% on each tail and nothing in the middle,
inside the region the band fraction sweep already measured FLAT (0.20-0.80 = 0.8525, 0.10-0.90 = 0.8565,
0.00-1.00 = 0.8427 - an INTERIOR optimum, so the band is a filter on uninformative end slices, not a budget
buying a fixed anatomical extent; a filter does not care about millimetres).

NOT armed. AX_FLUID_FS at 1.52 is the one slot with real spread and the largest mean span - if this is ever
re-opened it is for the axial slot alone, priced against that slot's own contribution, never as a global
decode change.

Re-open by answering the measurement, not by re-stating the premise.
See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_band_span_spread.md
close_reason: Measured and recorded; the axis is priced as not-worth-arming rather than left open.
