title: ConvNeXt declines are facts about the knee-94ec handicap, not about the trunk
description:
encoder_surgery.blocks() docstring names ConvNeXt explicitly as sharing Swin's staged shape (27 of 36 blocks in the longest ModuleList), so --unfreeze-last 6 opened only the middle stage and left the top stage frozen for the whole run. Every ConvNeXt member in comp/members.declines was measured that way: cnx_own_recipe_s2026 at 0.8186, cnx_dense_s2026 at 0.7927. Their decline lines say only 'below the 0.8460 merit level; re-open by naming the instrument it would be', which is silent about the handicap - the same silence swin_supervised's line carried until knee-94ec was found.

DO NOT ARM A cnx_wholetop YET. swin_wholetop is the direct measurement of what the discovery fix is worth on a staged trunk: it re-runs swin_supervised (0.8331 handicapped) byte-identical on the fixed discovery. That delta prices this one. If the fix is worth +0.023 (the ask that takes swin to its own LANDS branch of 0.8560), the same delta puts cnx_own_recipe at 0.8416 - still below the 0.8460 merit level, and not worth 4h of card. Only a substantially larger delta makes the ConvNeXt family worth re-opening.

The action now is the record, not an arm: when swin_wholetop's number lands, annotate the two cnx decline lines with the handicap and the priced re-open condition, so the next reader is not told these are facts about ConvNeXt.
notes: Both decline lines annotated in 7b10553 with the handicap and with what the re-open costs. Nothing armed: swin_wholetop is the identical correction on the identical $RECIPE at the identical --unfreeze-last 6, and its delta prices the ConvNeXt re-run. Through e3 that delta is ~zero (e0 0.7444/0.7441, e1 0.7816/0.7803, e2 0.8109/0.8110, e3 0.8164/0.8192 against swin_supervised), so on current evidence the ConvNeXt re-run buys nothing either — decide on swin's peak, not on this.
close_reason: PRICED AND CLOSED 2026-09-03. This bead's own decision rule was 'decide on swin's peak, not on the partial curve'. The peak landed. swin_wholetop finished 12 of 12, CONVERGED, and its delta against swin_supervised is NEGATIVE at every epoch of the finished curve — the thaw correction is worth <= 0 on a staged trunk, not the +0.023 that would have been needed. By this bead's own arithmetic the ConvNeXt re-run therefore buys nothing: it was priced off swin's delta, and that delta is not positive. cnx_own_recipe stays at 0.8186 and cnx_dense at 0.7927 against a 0.8459 merit bar, and those numbers are now facts about the trunk rather than about the knee-94ec handicap. Both decline lines were already annotated with the handicap and the re-open condition in 7b10553, so the record this bead asked for exists. The ConvNeXt family is closed on a PRICED argument, and re-opening it needs a mechanism, never a re-quote.

title: RunMetrics.rows() merges runs when the recipe is back-filled (3 of 142 files)
description:
RunMetrics.rows() is documented (convergence_check.verdict) as returning the LAST run's group, because a re-run to the same --out appends. On lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026 it returns 16 rows against a recipe that asked for 12, so the grouping did not hold: the series stitches two runs, and its e3 belongs to one while its peak belongs to the other.

Read as one trajectory it contributes a gate-to-peak gain of +0.1350 against a real twelve-epoch maximum of +0.0529 - two and a half times the largest genuine gain in the corpus. trajectory_check decides on the MAXIMUM, so that one series alone lifted the ceiling enough to leave the gate barely able to fire. It is worked around there by refusing any run with more recorded epochs than its recipe asked for, which is a sound guard on its own terms but hides the underlying grouping bug rather than fixing it.

Also worth checking what else reads this run's rows: its holdout number (0.8217, on the roster as a member) is the max over a stitched series, so it may not be one run's peak either.

Found 2026-08-30 building trajectory_check (knee-gnzx). RunMetrics.begin's rotation is the account that would settle which rows belong to which run.
notes:
CAUSE, and it is not the grouping rule in general. rows() splits on RECIPE lines. The recipe in
lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026.metrics.jsonl is BACK-FILLED - appended after the run finished, at line 16 -
so the only split point in the file is at the END and every run lands in one group. The file is four
epochs of an aborted run (e0-e3, peak 0.6867), then the real twelve (e0-e11, peak 0.8217 at e8), then
the recipe.

FIX: the boundary was in the data the whole time - a run's epoch counts up, so a value that does not
increase starts a new group. That subsumes the recipe rule and is strictly more information; the
back-filled-recipe test (test_rows_reads_a_run_whose_recipe_was_back_filled) still passes.

DENOMINATOR: 3 of 142 metrics files on disk merge more than one run - dinov3_v3small_s2026 (15 rows,
restart at index 12), lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026 (16 rows, restart at 4), throughput_plain (2 rows,
restart at 1).

NO SHIPPED NUMBER MOVES. lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026.pt is on the roster at 0.8215 and its clean last-run
peak is 0.8217 - the same epoch either way, because the aborted run peaked well below it.
dinov3_v3small_s2026 has no holdout record (roster_check passes, 0 undocumented). What moves is every
TRAJECTORY read across such a file, which is what trajectory_check does.

The gate is unchanged by the fix: the corpus goes 96 -> 102 runs (lora_r8_v3small_224 now ENTERS it at
+0.0165 rather than being refused), median +0.0210 -> +0.0216, and the max stays +0.0529. The
more-rows-than-asked guard in trajectory_check.gain stays anyway - it caught this before the reader was
fixed, and a series stitched by a shape the reader does not know about would arrive the same way.

title: mount_check widens to the whole package silently when a member name is not a literal
description: mount_check resolves a kernel's KernelRun member names by static parse. A name it cannot reduce to a string literal makes the tuple read as the WHOLE package instead — documented behaviour (mount_check.py:11) but INVISIBLE in the output. kneemri-swinseat was REFUSED for an undeclared dimiturnt/vjepa2-hf that none of its seven members use, purely because the entering seat was written as the SWIN_SEAT constant. The failure mode is the expensive direction only by luck: here it over-demanded and refused loudly, but a kernel whose literal names happen to cover the widened set passes while the check silently proved something else. Fix: print which names resolved and which did not, and say 'read as the whole package (N names unresolved)' on the fallback, so the widening is on the transcript. Found 2026-08-30 during the swinseat pre-flight; worked around by inlining the literal (commit a8fa900).

title: card_check calls a smoke OVERSUBSCRIBED — arm_check and the trainer it spawned are one job
description:
card_check counts CUDA contexts on the device and blocks on TWO OF OURS. During a smoke that is always two, and they are not two jobs:

  OURS  pid 26608  ...venv-arm...  smokes/swin_wholetop_smoke/swin_wholetop/swin_wholetop.pt
  OURS  pid 58644  ...venv-arm...  --smoke smokes/swin_wholetop_smoke/swin_wholetop --smoke-studies 60
  OVERSUBSCRIBED: 2 of our own processes compute on this card (pids 26608 58644)

58644 is kneemri.experiments.arm_check and 26608 is the trainer it launched as a subprocess. The parent initialises CUDA itself, so both hold a context, but there is exactly one piece of work and the advice the check prints - 'kill all but one before trusting any timing' - would kill half of one smoke.

Observed 2026-08-30 when the swin_wholetop pid gate fired and ran its smoke.

Why it matters rather than being cosmetic: card_check is the gate consulted BEFORE putting anything on the GPU, and it earned its place on a real 25-minute collision. A gate that cries wolf on every single smoke is a gate that gets read past, and the next real double-booking is the one that gets waved through. This is the same failure shape as the queue_check MISARMED false positive (knee-j0gu) - a correct check whose signal is being diluted by a state it should recognise as legal.

Fix direction, not yet chosen: card_check already reads each process's argv (it prints it). A candidate is to collapse a parent/child pair into one job when one process's argv names a --smoke directory that the other's output path sits inside, which is exactly the relationship above and needs no process-tree walk. A more general fix walks the parent chain and counts process TREES rather than pids. Prefer whichever does not add a new liveness probe - the existing ones (kill -0 vs tasklist, knee namespace mismatch) are already a documented hazard here.

Do not fix by raising the threshold to three: two genuinely independent arms is the exact condition the check exists to catch.

title: Epoch-3 holdout AUC is a cheap kill-gate for 12-epoch one_cycle arms
description:
A 12-epoch one_cycle arm can be judged at epoch 3 against a matched trajectory instead of at epoch 11, which is 2+ hours of card per arm.

The measurement that licenses it, from swin_supervised_s2026.full.log (12 epochs, one_cycle, whole_stack, slices 20, band 0.1-0.9, slice_pooling max, fold 0):

  e0 0.7441  e1 0.7803  e2 0.8110  e3 0.8192  e4 0.8209  e5 0.8239
  e6 0.8331 (peak)  e7 0.8261  e8 0.8255  e9 0.8269  e10 0.8268  e11 0.8256

Two facts fall out. The late-one_cycle anneal in THIS harness is worth about +0.014 from epoch 3 to the peak, not the large late jump one_cycle is usually credited with. And the peak lands at epoch 6, with epochs 7-11 flat-to-decaying - so the last five epochs of a 12-epoch arm bought nothing here.

That makes epoch 3 a usable gate: e3 + 0.014 approximates the peak, and doubling the gain gives a generous ceiling. An arm whose generous ceiling misses its own pre-registered SEAT branch can be truncated at epoch 4 without changing the branch it lands in.

First use, same session: vit_in21k_s2026 read 0.7755 at epoch 3 - 0.044 BELOW the trunk this same recipe family had already declined as too weak - so its generous ceiling was ~0.80 against a SEAT branch of 0.8393. It was truncated rather than run 8 more epochs (2.3h) to confirm a determined branch.

Limits worth stating. This is ONE reference trajectory, and swin_supervised is itself a handicapped run (knee-94ec froze stage 3). The gate is only sound where the comparison arm is matched on epochs/schedule/pooling, and it may only TRUNCATE an arm whose generous ceiling misses its branch - it must never be used to promote or to rank two arms, and never to close a family. A truncated one_cycle score is a FLOOR (convergence_check calls it TRUNCATED), so the record must carry it as a floor and not as the trunk's number.

Follow-up: collect e3-to-peak deltas across the other completed 12-epoch one_cycle logs to replace this single-reference gate with a distribution.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-30, and the single-reference gate in the description is SUPERSEDED. The follow-up asked for a distribution; it exists, and it is now a check: python -m kneemri.experiments.trajectory_check.

Matched to a twelve-epoch schedule the gain from e3 to peak reads median +0.0210, p90 +0.0380, max +0.0529 over n=96 - so the +0.014 single-reference figure in the description understated the median and badly understated the tail. The gate now decides on the MAXIMUM, never the p90: firing at p90 is wrong one run in ten and what it costs when wrong is a member, against two hours of a card that is not otherwise scarce.

Matching on the epoch BUDGET turned out to be required, not a refinement. A 24-epoch run has twice the anneal left after the gate and reads median +0.0339; pooling the schedules lets a long run's headroom excuse a short arm.

THE CORPUS DEFECT the hand reading missed. Before runs recording more epochs than they asked for were refused, the twelve-epoch maximum read +0.1350 rather than +0.0529: lora_r8_v3small_224 holds 16 rows against a 12-epoch recipe, so its gate value and its peak belong to different runs. RunMetrics.rows() is documented as returning the last run's group and here it does not. One stitched series lifts a maximum-decided ceiling two and a half times, which would have left the gate barely able to fire. Worth a separate look at rows() grouping.

The vit_in21k truncation was re-derived by the tool independently of the hand reading and lands in the same place: e4 0.7847, needs +0.0546, generous ceiling 0.8376, CANNOT REACH.

title: queue_check reports MISARMED for a watcher whose producer has not started yet
description:
queue_check flags a watcher as MISARMED when the file it watches does not exist, on the reasoning that 'the watched file does not exist while the arm named in the marker is running'. But a THREE-deep chain is the normal shape here: vit_in21k running, swin_wholetop owed behind it, recal_holdannot owed behind that. The third watcher's file cannot exist yet, because the arm that writes it has not started. The verdict is a false positive, and it fired twice in one session on a correctly-armed queue.

It is a false ALARM and not a harmless one: wait_for is 'until grep -q $marker $file 2>/dev/null; do sleep 60; done' (experiments/lib.sh:680), which tolerates a missing file and will pick it up the moment it appears. So the chain is fine and the check says it is broken — which is the failure mode that teaches you to ignore the check.

THE FIX is the distinction the message already assumes and does not test: is the arm named in the marker RUNNING? If it is, a missing watched file is a real misarming (wrong path, wrong seed). If it is instead OWED by another live watcher — which queue_check already enumerates — the missing file is the expected state of a queued third rung, and the right verdict is OK.

Guard: a two-deep chain whose second file path is genuinely wrong must still report MISARMED.

title: convergence_check calls a PLATEAU undertrained: peaking last is an argmax, being budget-bound is a slope
description:
Measured 2026-08-30 11:09Z, card-free, over the whole processed root: 135 runs, 11 UNDERTRAINED. Seven of the eleven are plateaus, not budget binds.

mixup_dense   tail 0.8548 0.8541 0.8546 0.8552  gain over three epochs 0.0004
mixup224      tail 0.8510 0.8514 0.8515 0.8516  gain 0.0006
cnx_dense     tail 0.7921 0.7909 0.7927 0.7927  gain 0.0006
encoder_adapt tail 0.6887 0.6888 0.6902 0.6902  gain 0.0015
crop80_tissue gain 0.0020 · schedule_8 gain 0.0020 · wholestack_fold2 similar

The rule is 'peak >= done - 1', an ARGMAX over a flat tail. A run that gained 0.0004 across its last
three epochs is not bound by its budget; its highest point merely happened to be the final one. The
verdict argues for a longer schedule, and the 24-epoch arm already measured a longer schedule as
HARMFUL under one_cycle (ledger lines 1004-1005, 4204): an oversized budget stretches the anneal and
leaves the rate far from annealed where the model converges. So the false verdict points at the one
fix the repo has already refuted.

FIX: undertrained requires a GAIN over the tail that clears the paired holdout floor (0.0062), the
smallest difference this holdout resolves. Under that rule the four that survive are lora_r8_small_336
(+0.0784), mae_matched (+0.0901), adapt_null (+0.0789) and encoder_adapt_lower (+0.0073) - and the
first three are FOUR-epoch runs, where a budget genuinely binds. That coherence is the check on the fix.

PRICE: ~20 min, card-free. P(the seven flip to CONVERGED) ~0.95 - the arithmetic is already done above.
It guards a NUMBER (which runs may be quoted as their recipe's own), which is what this tool is for.

title: Vote rule is the third combiner axis: rank vs logit vs median on one pool, pre-registered
description:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE NUMBERS LANDED (the runs are in flight as this is written; logs/vote_{rank,median,logit}.log).

WHY ASK. Two combiner axes are closed on this pool — seat COUNT (knee-m69u, 0.4 of a floor across 1-24)
and seat CHOICE (knee-ymek, per-label routing lands 0.0003 under global greedy). The vote RULE is the
third and last one the ruler can price card-free, and unlike the other two it is not hypothetical: the
shipped champion serves LogitAverage while every number in the ledger was measured under RankAverage.
So this axis is already live in production and has never been read head-to-head.

THE COMMAND, identical but for one flag, all three on the same pool (113 of 202 records, 909 shared
studies), all --seats honest:

    record_mix --records <processed root>/*.pt --largest-pool --seats honest --vote {rank,median,logit}

PREDICTION, and it is a null. Rank and logit differ only in the monotone transform applied before
averaging, and AUC is itself rank-based, so the two can only diverge where members disagree about the
ORDER of studies they score close together. Median is the robust centre of the same space and should
help only if some member is an outlier on a subset of studies — which knee-ymek's routing curve argues
against, since top-1-per-label was the worst point on it and nothing in this pool behaves specially on
any subset. Expect all three inside the 0.0062 floor of each other.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT NOT A NULL, stated now so it cannot be invented afterwards: any pair separated by
more than the floor. If median were to win by that much, the pool contains an outlier the seat curve is
averaging in, and the fix is a ship-side vote swap costing no card and no training. If logit were to
LOSE to rank by that much, the shipped champion is serving the worse of the two and every ledger number
(all taken under rank) overstates what ships.

EITHER WAY IT IS CHEAP AND IT IS NOT A SUBMISSION. Nothing here gets a slot: a vote swap on the shipped
entry would be evidence-free without a board reading, and the board reading is worth a slot only if the
offline gap clears the floor first.
notes:
RESULT: NULL, exactly as pre-registered, and both trip-wires stayed down.

Honest peaks, one pool (113 of 202 records, 909 shared studies), --seats honest, one flag apart:

    rank    0.8752 at 23 seats   greedy bias +0.0013   (in-sample peak 0.8768 at 12)
    median  0.8756 at 23 seats   greedy bias +0.0015   (in-sample peak 0.8778 at 19)
    logit   0.8763 at 19 seats   greedy bias +0.0012   (in-sample peak 0.8778 at 15)

SPREAD 0.0011 ACROSS ALL THREE, against a 0.0062 floor — 0.18 of a floor. The rule you vote under does
not matter on this pool.

NEITHER TRIP-WIRE FIRED. Median did not beat the others by more than the floor, so nothing in the pool
behaves as an outlier the mean is absorbing — which independently confirms knee-ymek's reading from the
opposite direction: routing said no member is special on a subset of LABELS, median says no member is
special on a subset of STUDIES. And logit did not lose to rank, so the ledger's rank-measured numbers do
not overstate what the champion ships.

TWO DIRECTIONAL NOTES, kept because they are free and mechanism-sound, and reported as directional
because each is a fifth of a floor. Logit is nominally the best of the three AND it is what already
ships — so there is nothing to change, which is the most useful form a null can take. It also carries
the LOWEST selection bias (+0.0012 against +0.0015 and +0.0013 at their own peaks, and +0.0010 at 24
seats against +0.0014 and +0.0017): under logit the greedy overfits its own choice least, so the same
ruler is steadier there. That is an argument for reading FUTURE seat work under logit rather than rank,
which is a change to the INSTRUMENT and costs nothing, not a change to the entry.

THIRD AXIS CLOSED. Count (knee-m69u), choice (knee-ymek) and now rule: three combiner axes, measured on
one pool inside one day, none of them delivering as much as a fifth of what a result needs. The ceiling
is the members. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_the-combiner-is-closed.md.

title: TrunkAsTokens dropped transformers' checkpointing hook — every non-ViT trunk died on --recompute-activations
description:
FOUND 2026-08-30 by the swin_supervised smoke, which reported BROKEN with the last line of stderr — an HTTP 302 from the HF fetch, which is not the failure at all. The failure was eighteen lines above:

  AttributeError: 'TrunkAsTokens' object has no attribute 'gradient_checkpointing_enable'
  encoder_surgery.py:301 in recompute_activations

EncoderSurgery.recompute_activations calls gradient_checkpointing_enable on whatever it holds as a backbone, and until TrunkAsTokens existed that was always an HF model directly. nn.Module.__getattr__ raises for any name that is not a submodule, so a WRAPPED trunk — ConvNeXtV2 (from_map) and Swin (from_sequence) — died at model construction, before a single batch.

LATENT SINCE THE WRAPPER EXISTED. The only non-ViT arm that has ever run, cnx_own_recipe, predates $THROUGHPUT and so never passed --recompute-activations. So the first arm to combine a wrapped trunk with checkpointing was the first to hit it, and it hit it after the card had already been handed over by after.sh.

FIXED: TrunkAsTokens.gradient_checkpointing_enable delegates to self.trunk. Delegation rather than a family test in the surgery — the point of the wrapper is that anything callable as backbone(pixel_values=) substitutes, and a caller that must know which of the two it holds puts back the dispatch the wrapper removes. Unit test test_gradient_checkpointing_enable asserts the kwargs travel intact.

THE SECOND DEFECT, NOT FIXED HERE. ArmSmoke._subprocess reports lines[-1] of stderr as the arm's complaint. transformers logs HTTP requests to stderr at INFO and keeps doing so after the traceback, so the last line is routinely a 200/302 and the traceback is invisible. Two smoke runs were spent before the real cause was read, and only by re-running the recipe by hand outside the tool. A smoke that reports the wrong line is worse than one that reports nothing: it invites the repair of a fetch that was never broken. Candidate fix: report the last line matching an exception shape (^\w+Error:|^Traceback) if there is one, else lines[-1].

title: queue_check is blind to any watcher that is not after.sh
description: queue_check globs logs/after_*.log and parses the 'waits on ARM DONE X' line that after.sh writes. A gate armed any other way - e.g. a nohup'd bash -c that sources lib.sh and calls wait_for directly, which is what a SMOKE-THEN-RUN chain has to be, since after.sh only takes arm scripts - is not in that glob, so queue_check reports 'every arm still owed is gated by exactly one live process' while owing an arm it cannot see. That is the exact hole the tool exists to close, inverted: a false OK instead of a false alarm. Two fixes worth weighing: (a) teach after.sh to gate an arm on a preceding smoke, so every queue goes through the one path queue_check understands; (b) have queue_check enumerate live processes owing arms rather than inferring them from log filenames. (a) is smaller and keeps one entrypoint. Found 2026-08-30 while queueing swin_supervised behind stack_increments.
close_reason: after.sh grew --smoke <dir>, so a smoke-gated queue goes through the one entrypoint queue_check parses. Fix (a) of the two weighed; (b) - queue_check enumerating live processes instead of inferring from log filenames - stays unbuilt, since with (a) landed there is no longer a reason to arm a queue any other way. Verified: queue_check now reports 'after_swin_supervised.log waits on ARM DONE stack_increments 0/1 started live' and OK. Commit 72f1506.

title: loadcheck built trunks raw, bypassing the registry adapter
description:
`comp/kernels/kneemri-loadcheck` resolved `ENCODERS[member.variant]` and then built the trunk with `AutoModel.from_pretrained(weights)` directly, discarding the `adapter` the entry names. For DINOv2/DINOv3 the two are identical, which is why it never showed. For ConvNeXtV2 the trunk arrives as a feature map (n, dim, h, w) and for Swin as a sequence with no prefix token, so the head's `tokens[:, 1:]` eats the grid's first cell with no shape error. A load probe that loads a member differently from the way `kernel_run` ships it can only certify the families it happens not to differ on.

FIXED in the same commit: the call is now `encoder.load(weights)`, which is what `kneemri/kaggle/kernel_run.py:223` does.

STILL OPEN, and the reason this is filed rather than just closed: `kneemri-graft` and `kneemri-graft-verify` carry the same spelling. Both are DINOv2-only historical entries and both hardcode DINOV2_DIM, so neither is wrong today — they are latent, and they are the record of what was submitted, so they are not edited on spec. Decide whether a shipped kernel's source is frozen evidence or live code before touching them.

title: ledger_check attribution is line-scoped, so its 15 crossed quotes are all false positives
description:
`ledger_check` reports '42 unattributed (15 of those quote a number another run owns)'. Three cases audited 2026-08-30, all three benign, by three distinct mechanisms:

- through_dense_s2026 / 0.8558: the prose IS correct. The run name ends README line 5402 and '(0.8558' opens 5403, which also names calib_dense_hold_s2026. A markdown hard wrap, nothing more.
- band140_s2026 / 0.8556: that value is a cell in band_dense's epoch-curve table. A coincidental four-decimal collision between two unrelated runs.
- schedule_8_s2026 / 0.8429: the ledger names the run by its KNOB (a 'schedule_length' table row), not by its run id, and 0.8429 also collides with nocycle224_long.

None is a wrong number in the ledger. The consequence is not cosmetic: a check whose crossed-attribution class is ~100% false positive is a check nobody reads, and a REAL crossed attribution would sit in that list unnoticed — which is exactly the failure that AnnotatedReadings.readings shipped (knee-bk99, five of six rows under another member's name).

Fix direction: attribute over a sentence/paragraph window rather than a physical line; require the number to be adjacent to a name (or in the same table row) rather than merely co-resident; and treat a number that already has an owner elsewhere in the ledger as owned, not as crossed. Knob-named table rows want an explicit run-id column or an alias map.

Do NOT chase the 42-unattributed list until this lands — it is the same heuristic.

title: member_curve recomputes on GPU what HoldoutRecord reads free
description:
member_curve scores every member by running inference over the fold-0 holdout on the card (PredictionCache, 'cache MISS, computing on cuda'). Measured 2026-08-30: one uncached member (cnx_dense_s2026, ConvNeXtV2-base) took over 15 minutes. A 149-member sweep at that rate is ~24 hours and cannot finish inside its 2h timeout; the run that was killed had done 10 cached members and one uncached one in 17 minutes.

The trainer already writes .holdout.npz on every improving epoch. 142 of the 200 checkpoints under the processed root carry one. record_mix reads exactly those through HoldoutRecord and answered the SAME question -- per-member alone scores, greedy and honest seat curves, over 111 of 200 records and 909 shared studies -- in five seconds on the CPU.

This is the same asymmetry as knee-vq46 (two tools answering one question, one of them wrong): there the fold leak, here the cost. It is also structurally safer, because a --fold -1 member writes no .holdout.npz, so the leak knee-vq46 fixed by hand cannot occur in record_mix at all.

What member_curve is still FOR: the 38 members that have a checkpoint but no record (dinov3_v3small_s2026, ema24_s2026, adapt_null and others), and scoring an arbitrary reading axis / TTA / vote rule rather than the axis the trainer happened to save. That capability is real and should not be removed.

The fix is to make member_curve READ the record when one exists and matches, and fall back to the card only when it does not -- so a pool sweep costs the card only for the members that genuinely need it. Until then: for a plain fold-0 pool seating, use record_mix, not member_curve.
notes:
RULER IDENTIFIED, and the ruler axis measured on FIXED predictions.

The killed curve_pool3 sweep scored against labels/local_reader_annotated.csv. Proof: re-running
member_curve over the same ten cached members with --labels local_reader_annotated reproduces the
sweep's numbers exactly (adapt_null 0.8208, best-of-ten 0.8543). Nothing else varied: one cache MISS
line in the whole log, so its first ten were HITS on the same arrays record_mix read.

Sweep of all ten label tables on disk over those same ten members (identical predictions, identical
909 studies, only the truth vector changes). Alone-score mean / best:

  blend_nolixin           0.8587 / 0.8683
  blend_hybrid            0.8570 / 0.8672
  blend_four              0.8568 / 0.8649
  blend_three_v1          0.8568 / 0.8649
  merged_blend_v1         0.8568 / 0.8649
  confident_v2            0.8524 / 0.8634
  flatyes_v2              0.8524 / 0.8634
  merged_labels           0.8524 / 0.8634
  report_labels_v2        0.8524 / 0.8634   <-- what the arms use (experiments/lib.sh:61)
  local_reader_annotated  0.8428 / 0.8543   <-- what curve_pool3 used

Rank agreement against report_labels_v2 (Spearman over the ten, max rank move):

  confident_v2 / flatyes_v2 / merged_labels   1.000   0 places
  blend_hybrid / blend_nolixin                0.988   1 place
  blend_three_v1 / merged_blend_v1            0.964   2 places
  blend_four                                  0.915   3 places
  local_reader_annotated                      0.552   6 places

Two separate readings, and only the second is alarming:

1. The reader-BLEND family is a stable ruler. Nine of ten tables sit inside 0.0063 of mean score and
   inside 3 rank places of each other. That is consistent with knee-m69u's "+/-0.008 envelope" and
   confirms it on a fixed prediction set rather than across retrainings.

2. local_reader_annotated is NOT in that family and must not be treated as a substitutable ruler.
   -0.0096 mean, and it reshuffles seat order by up to SIX places out of ten. Seat order is what
   decides which members ship. Scoring a seat search against it and shipping the result is a live
   trap of knee-vq46's shape, and there is no default on member_curve's --labels to catch it: the
   flag is required, so a hand-run picks whatever is typed.

The three identical-scoring tables (confident_v2 / merged_labels / report_labels_v2) are genuinely
different files -- distinct md5, 4407 / 5143 / 4407 rows, all 4407 rows differing between the two
same-sized ones. They score identically because the metric is a per-label rank AUC over a binarised
truth and they differ only in confidence values that binarise the same way on this holdout.
CONSEQUENCE for knee-m69u: its "+0.0034 label TABLE swap" cannot be a scoring effect between those
three, so it is a TRAINING effect -- the table changed what the model learned, not how it was graded.

Logs: logs/ruler_<table>.log, one per table.
close_reason:
Landed. HoldoutPredictions.cached now reads three sources in cost order: PredictionCache, then the run's own .holdout.npz via the new TrainerRecord, and only then the encoder.

THE SUBSTITUTION IS AN EQUALITY AND IT WAS CHECKED TWICE. member_curve --refresh over the ten cached members fired the record path 10/10; nine scored identically to the prior cached-GPU run and aprior_dense_s2026 moved 0.8558 -> 0.8557, which is exactly what record_mix reports. So the record path matches record_mix EXACTLY and the old GPU path was the one off by 0.0001 (float32 record storage vs fp16 inference). The change makes the ruler more exact, not less.

SPEED, measured: 45 members alone-scored on the CPU, no card at all, in about ten minutes including corpus load. Through the encoder the same 45 is roughly eleven hours at the fifteen minutes a member measured on cnx_dense_s2026. That is what killed the 95-member curve_pool3 sweep.

THE GUARDS ARE THE DESIGN. instead_of returns None - falling back to the card - when the record is absent, FOREIGN, the views are not the identity, the window is not the member's own no-overlap window, or the record does not cover every requested study. A record computed under another reading would score a member as a function it was never read as, which is the knee-y8y defect in the tool that chooses what we submit.

Fitness gates forced two structural improvements: TrainerRecord is its own module beside its siblings, and the key-read-else-produce-write dance moved onto PredictionCache.remembered where it belongs - the caller had begun to be about the cache rather than about members.

title: member_curve crashes on SSL encoder checkpoints with KeyError: 'img'
description:
Passing every *.pt under processed/ to member_curve dies before it reads anything:

  File kneemri/inference/members.py, line 121, in image_size
    return int(self.config['img'])
  KeyError: 'img'

Seven checkpoints in the pool are SSL ENCODER artifacts, not members — they were produced by the pretraining runs and have never had a classifier head, so their config carries the pretraining knobs instead of a reading policy:

  adapt_null.pt, adapt_small_e6.pt, adapt_small_e6_lr1e5.pt, pretrain_small_matched_e8.pt,
  probe_adapt.pt, smoke_adapt.pt   -> config keys: epochs, highpass, mask_ratio, patch,
                                      slices_per_step, spectral_weight
  vjepa_member_e5.encoder.pt       -> config keys: from_member, holdout, merged_lora

None of them is a member and none could ever be scored or seated, so the right behaviour is to SKIP them with a logged line, the way the tool already skips 'no holdout record'. Instead it raises inside a list comprehension at member_curve.py:657, before the first member is read, so a pool sweep over the directory cannot be started at all without the caller hand-filtering first.

Why this matters beyond the inconvenience: member_curve's own comment at line 650 says it 'is the tool that decides WHICH members to submit, so a wrong number here chooses the wrong ensemble'. A tool with that job should not be un-runnable over its own data directory, and hand-filtering is exactly where a member gets silently dropped from a pool and never considered for a seat — the same class of hole roster_check was built to close.

Fix: give Member.from_checkpoint a way to say 'this is not a member' (config lacking 'img' is a sufficient and honest test, since every real member records its read size), and have MemberReadings skip and log rather than the caller pre-filtering. A unit test with one member-shaped config and one encoder-shaped config covers it.

Worked around for now by filtering to logs/ckpt_members.txt (182 of 200 files: 200 minus 7 encoders minus 11 probe/smoke throwaways).

title: trioseat's docstring claims LogitAverage and its code served the RankAverage default
description:
comp/kernels/kneemri-trioseat/kneemri-trioseat.py says under WHAT IS HELD: 'These are the champion's OWN seats, unmodified: same checkpoints, same --calibrated-targets refit, same LogitAverage, same overlap=False.' The code is KernelRun(names=chosen, overlap=False) with no serving argument, so Serving.vote falls to its RankAverage default. The champion kneemri-raptorseat DOES pass Serving(vote=LogitAverage()), so trioseat differs from the champion on a variable its own docstring names as held.

FOUND by pushing kneemri-greedyseat, which was copied from trioseat and inherited the omission: its version-1 kernel log reads 'serving: vote=RankAverage (default)'. Caught before a slot was spent, and only because kernel_run logs the served rule - the line added after 'The first kneemri-vote run logged the kit, the members and the studies and said nothing about the vote'. That logging is what made this visible.

CONSEQUENCE for the record, which is the reason this is filed rather than just fixed. trioseat_v1 scored 0.938 on the board and comp/board.jsonl:76 carries its why. If that row or the docstring is read later as 'three champion seats under the champion's vote', it is wrong: it is three champion seats under a DIFFERENT vote. vote_ceiling1.log prices the two rules 0.8720 LogitAverage against 0.8710 RankAverage honest, so the difference is about one tick and under the floor - the 0.938 is not invalidated, but what it is a measurement OF must be stated correctly.

Also stale: votefit's inline comment 'no kernel that produced a board number has ever overridden it [RankAverage]'. raptorseat overrides it and scored 0.943.

FIX: correct trioseat's docstring to say it served RankAverage, and correct votefit's comment. Do NOT re-run trioseat - the entry scored and the rule difference is under the floor. Decide separately whether a LogitAverage trioseat is worth a slot on the efficiency track.

title: Kernel logs cannot price the efficiency track: the public rerun scores THREE studies
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 23:05Z, free -- kaggle kernels output on six shipped entries, no slot, no card.

THE LEAD. knee-7lyz cannot price the efficiency lane because the efficiency board's snapshot
(2026-08-28 22:37) predates trioseat_v1. Kernel logs looked like a way around the wait: Kaggle's
kernel log is a JSON list of {stream_name, time, data} with per-record elapsed seconds, so the last
record's `time` is the run's wall clock.

  soloseat     (1 member,  1 decode)  63.6 s   board 0.925
  calibsix     (6 members, 3 decodes) 73.4 s   board 0.941   <- holds our efficiency row
  trioseat     (3 members, 1 decode)  93.5 s   board 0.938   <- built AS the cheap entry
  fourseat     (4 members, 1 decode)  98.4 s   board 0.937
  raptorseat   (7 seats,   3 decodes) 96.5 s   board 0.943   <- champion
  raptorweight (7 seats,   3 decodes) 89.0 s   scoring

THE LEAD IS DEAD, AND THE REASON IS ONE LOG LINE. Every kernel prints `studies 1-3`. The public
rerun scores THREE studies. Gap analysis puts 20-35 s in imports and 15-35 s in weight loading, and
4-8 s in all decode-and-forward work combined -- so the 63-98 s spread is startup jitter and the
inversion above (the "cheap" trioseat 20 s SLOWER than the six-member calibsix) is noise about
nothing. No runtime ordering may be read from these numbers, and the ordering they appear to give is
backwards from the design intent, which is exactly how a bad instrument does damage.

A SECOND READING I NEARLY FILED, CAUGHT BY READING THE SOURCE. calibsix and raptorseat print
`projecting 0.0h of 7.7h` and `0.0h of 7.6h`. I read those as projected full-test runtimes and had
derived a hidden test set of ~8300 studies from them. kneemri/inference/budget.py:81 says otherwise:
the format is `projecting {projected}h of {seconds}h` where `seconds` is the CEILING. The projection
is 0.0h. There is no projected runtime in any log we hold.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT, and it is small: the private rerun over the full hidden test is where the
efficiency metric's runtime is measured, and we cannot observe it. The efficiency board snapshot
remains the only instrument, and waiting for it to refresh past trioseat_v1 remains the move.

THE INSTRUMENTATION GAP, worth fixing on its own. Budget.report() (kneemri/inference/budget.py)
returns "" until measured() is true, and measured() needs index + fraction > 0. A SINGLE-decode entry
running a single chunk therefore prints no projection on the only chunk line it has. So the entries
built for the efficiency track -- one decode, by design -- are precisely the ones that can never
self-report a projection, on a private run where nothing else can either. Not urgent (the guard's
real job is to stop a 9 h overrun, and a one-group entry is the case least at risk), but it is the
wrong way round.

title: Member-count axis is SATURATED: 111-member honest greedy peaks 0.8753, +0.0002 over honest12
description:
First honest greedy ever run over the whole pool, enabled by the knee-0dtv roster fix. 200 checkpoints on disk, 111 survive --largest-pool narrowing (11 smoke runs + confident224_s2026 drop as a group). --vote logit --seats honest.

CURVE: 1 seat 0.8624, 3 seats 0.8729, 12 seats 0.8743, 20 seats 0.8750, best honest count 28 at 0.8753. In-sample peak 0.8777 at 13.

Against the previous unrestricted honest12 at 0.8751 this is +0.0002. Thirty members that were unshippable until tonight -- stackfit_s2026 0.8631, the project's second-best solo, among them -- entered the pool and the honest curve did not move.

WHAT IT CLOSES. 'Add more members of the kind we already build' is now closed on our own honest ruler at full pool size. It was already narrowed by the 23% quality pass-through; saturation is stronger, because pass-through says gains arrive small while saturation says there are none left to pass through. The 28-vs-13 peak disagreement is the estimator wandering on a plateau, not two real optima.

WHAT IT SUPPORTS. knee-nj4l / knee-ombx: a saturated pool of one architecture is exactly what predicts that the remaining lever is a different decode or corpus. And the efficiency lane -- three seats deliver 99.7% of twenty-eight -- bought free by a run aimed at score.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ANSWER. Seating, not weighting. A weighted fit over the same 111 is a different question. Also offline on 909 fold-0 studies, so the board mapping is through the compression constant, not direct.

title: The honest seating and the full-fit dose are separable terms nobody has combined
description:
entry_offline (knee-awxb) filled the fold-0 family end to end, and it changes what honest12 means. honest12 is the TOP of its own family on BOTH rulers (offline 0.8751 / board 0.937, against peak8 0.8731/0.932, greedy7 0.8712/0.933, accumseat 0.8695/0.933), and board_transfer now reports 0 inversions in 233 resolved pairs. The earlier verdict - 'offline-greedy seat selection picks a seating that LOSES on the board, its rankings do not transfer' - was computed against the champion's 0.943, an _ff entry whose offline is unmeasurable. That pairs a fold-0 offline with an _ff board score: the same contamination class that voided raptor_solo, one level up. The two entries differ in TRAINING DATA DOSE, not in seating.

THE CANDIDATE: seats chosen by the offline greedy (which demonstrably transfers inside its family), served from _ff refits of those same recipes. Neither term has been combined with the other. Measured sizes: the dose term is ~+0.003 and saturates (finalfit_v1 0.934 -> allfit_v1 0.937; converting the seventh member bought nothing, lastseat_v1 vs dark7_v1 both 0.937); the seating term is +0.004 to +0.006 inside the fold-0 family (basedense 0.931 -> honest12 0.937).

WHY IT IS NOT YET A PLAN. Both terms are below the 1.5% bar alone and their sum is not obviously above the pinned 0.943. The cost is one training run per member that has no _ff twin, and honest12's twelve seats mostly do not have one. Price the ratio before arming anything: which of the twelve already have an _ff refit on the roster, and what does record_mix say the honest curve peaks at when restricted to members that DO. If that restricted peak is at or below the six the champion already serves, this closes for free.
notes: PRE-TEST RAN, AXIS CLOSES FOR FREE (2026-08-29 21:44Z). Four of honest12's twelve have an _ff twin; seven roster recipes have one at all (base_dense, calib_dense_hold, calib_span, grade_ladder, lr4e-5_ws, small_batch6, through_dense). record_mix --seats honest --vote logit restricted to those seven, on the 909 shared studies: honest peak 0.8705 at SEVEN members (in-sample peak 0.8711 at four, bias +0.0004 at six). Against the unrestricted honest12 at 0.8751 that is -0.0046 - restricting the pool to twinned recipes gives up HALF AGAIN the whole dose term (~+0.003) before the dose term is even paid. Under board_transfer's +0.97 top-regime slope, 0.8705 predicts board ~0.932-0.933 (it sits between basedense 0.8690/0.931 and peak8 0.8731/0.932), and adding the saturating dose term lands ~0.936. The pinned champion is 0.943. So the combination is not a candidate: the seating term that made honest12 top of its family lives in the FIVE members with no _ff twin, and buying it costs five training runs to land below what is already shipped. Closing without arming anything - the bead's own stated stop condition ('if that restricted peak is at or below the six the champion already serves, this closes for free') is met.

title: The READER is the weaker half on OUR members, bracketed for the first time — the label side is where a member's ceiling is
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 17:30Z, via kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap --records over our six --hold-annotations members (band_dense_hold, band_span_hold, calib_dense_hold, calib_span_hold, blendhold, holdannot), 58 annotated studies, none of which any of them trained on.

  aggregate: labels 0.8658   model 0.9156
  labels - model: -0.0498  [-0.0742, -0.0255]  over 58 studies
    the interval EXCLUDES zero: the model beats its own labels, so the READER is the weaker half
  2 of 12 per-finding bands exclude zero: Effusion, Contusion

Our model beats the report label on 10 of 12 findings. Only ACL (-0.0025) and MCL (-0.0249) sit the
other way, and both are inside the noise.

WHY THIS IS NEW. The published-pool reading of the same tool has been on record since 2026-08-25 and
was ABOUT A STRANGER'S MODEL; the module's own docstring says so. This is the first read on models we
fitted, and it was suppressed by a one-sided verdict branch (fixed in 99276c2) that printed a decisive
negative interval as 'SPANS zero'.

DENOMINATOR. 58 studies, 696 cells — the whole gold set, not a subset of it. The radiologist calls
34.5% of cells positive. At the 0.5 cut our reader calls 44.7%, agreeing 79.2%, precision 65.3%,
recall 84.6%; at 0.75 precision rises to 77.9% for recall 69.2%. The reader OVER-CALLS, and the mild
band is where it does it.

WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT LICENSE. It does NOT license re-blending the tables on disk: blendlabels
closed that axis at MEAN +0.0034 against 0.8502, inside its own +/-0.006 band, and table_separation's
docstring records that the +0.025 blend-over-v2 gap is TIE MASS rather than quality. It does not by
itself license distillation either: distill_pairs read +0.0016 and raptor_distill diagnosed the lane as
'a rank average cannot pay for an ordering it already holds'.

What it does say is that the member's ceiling is on the LABEL side rather than the vision side for ten
of twelve findings, which is the opposite of where the queue has been spending. Before an arm is
chosen the ledger has to be read for what the label-side lever space already contains — the band_*
family and unsure_cost look like prior work on exactly the over-call this measurement names.
notes:
LEDGER READ, 17:38Z, BEFORE ANY ARM WAS PROPOSED — and it closes most of what this finding looks like it licenses. Dropping P1 -> P2 for that reason: the measurement is sound and the lane is largely spent.

1. RECALIBRATION IS WORTH EXACTLY 0.000, BY CONSTRUCTION. experiments/README.md 'Per-label reader
   agreement' (2026-08-25): the error census is lopsided 3.4:1, 108 false positives against 32 misses,
   which reads as a calibration lever and is not one — the metric is a per-label RANK AUC and a monotone
   per-label recalibration cannot change it. That retires the arm this finding most obviously suggests
   (down-weight the mild band, where precision goes 65.3% -> 77.9% between the 0.5 and 0.75 cuts).
   Consistent with calibrated_targets at +0.0038, inside the floor.

2. A BETTER LLM READER IS CLOSED ON THIS RULER. 'The reader gate fired NOT DISTINGUISHABLE': Qwen3-8B
   speaks on 45.8% of the pairs the lexicon left blank and scores 0.840 against a majority class of
   0.840, interval [0.737, 0.911], while REGRESSING to 0.812 on the 463 pairs the lexicon already
   answered. Both cached 35B readers fail to load under transformers 5.15 and vLLM is Linux-only here.
   The per-label narrow route was retired as unmeasurable: blank-cell denominators of 7 to 24 on 57
   studies cannot resolve anything at any reader size.

3. SWAPPING TABLES IS CLOSED. blendlabels trained the control recipe on blend_three_v1 with the ruler
   pinned to v2 and read MEAN +0.0034 against 0.8502, inside its pre-registered +/-0.006 band, which its
   own header called the axis closing. table_separation's docstring adds that the +0.025 blend-over-v2
   gap is TIE MASS, not quality: quantise the public table to our five levels and it falls to 0.8445,
   BELOW ours.

4. DISTILLATION IS NOT LICENSED BY THIS EITHER. distill_pairs read +0.0016 and diagnosed its own null as
   'a rank average cannot pay for an ordering it already holds'; raptor_distill found the sign and not
   the size. And a teacher over the TRAINING corpus is not buildable without folds, which are banned.

WHAT SURVIVES AS OPEN. The reader's RECALL — the 32-miss column — is a different axis from the precision
this and the 2026-08-25 census both measure, and no arm has priced it. And the blocker named there is
still the real one and is not a modelling problem: a truth set larger than 58 annotated studies. Every
per-label statement in this lane is being asked of denominators between 7 and 50.

THE VALUE OF THIS FINDING IS THEREFORE A NEGATIVE ONE, and it is worth having: it says the member's
ceiling is on the label side for ten of twelve findings, which means the vision-side knob queue is
pointed at the smaller half — without licensing a label-side arm, because those are priced and closed.

title: The vote axis is closed: fitted weights buy +0.0003 at champion pool size, and LogitAverage has no parameters
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29, ZERO CARD, ZERO SLOT, while raddino_dense held the GPU. This is the split-half read QualityWeightedRank asked for in its own docstring and never got, and which vote_ceiling.py was written for and had not been run over a pool.

python -m kneemri.evaluation.vote_ceiling, weights fitted on one half of the 909 studies and scored on the other, both directions, with the fit-on-self number printed beside it so the overfit is visible rather than assumed.

OVER ALL 109 SCOREABLE MEMBERS (four dropped as unmixable: smoke_loop, smoke_v3base, v3lora_smoke, confident224_s2026):
  RankAverage          honest 0.8661   flat baseline
  QualityWeightedRank  honest 0.8670  +0.0009  overfit gap +0.0001
  LabelQualityRank     honest 0.8672  +0.0011  overfit gap +0.0007
  MedianLogit          honest 0.8677  +0.0015  overfit gap +0.0000
  LogitAverage         honest 0.8688  +0.0027  overfit gap +0.0000

OVER FOUR MEMBERS, the greedy top of the whole-stack pool and the shape we actually ship:
  RankAverage          honest 0.8616
  QualityWeightedRank  honest 0.8616  -0.0000
  LabelQualityRank     honest 0.8617  +0.0000  overfit gap +0.0003
  LogitAverage         honest 0.8619  +0.0003
  MedianLogit          honest 0.8611  -0.0005

THE READING. At the pool size that ships, all five rules lie inside 0.0005 against a 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil floor - the vote is not a lever. The winner at both sizes is the one rule with ZERO fitted parameters, so nothing here is bought by fitting. The two fitted rules have overfit gaps of +0.0001 and +0.0007, which is small in the good sense and worthless in the useful one: they do not overfit because there is nothing for them to fit.

WHAT THE +0.0027 AT 109 MEMBERS IS, and it is not a weighting gain. It is LogitAverage tolerating a pool that is mostly junk better than RankAverage does; it collapses to +0.0003 the moment the pool is four good members. Do not quote the large number - it is a statement about the junk, not about the rule.

CONSEQUENCE. This is the FOURTH aggregation strategy to land on the same ceiling. Routed top-k per label, honest greedy seats, and a flat rank-average of a curated eight came within 0.0018 of one another at ~0.876 earlier today; learned weights now join them. The ceiling is a property of the members and no arithmetic over them moves it. Stop pricing vote rules; the champion already serves LogitAverage, which is the honest maximum.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY. Fold-0 holdout only, so every _cf and _ff member is excluded by RecordMix rather than by judgement, and the all-data boundary rule forbids comparing across it. Halving the studies doubles each per-label sampling error, which is why a separation under the floor on a half corpus is a separation by nothing - the flat rule is scored on the identical halves so that inflation cancels where it can.

title: Per-finding routing measured for the first time: +0.0008 split-half, and the ORACLE is negative
description:
Ran the per-label routing curve over the eight honest seats (calib_dense_hold, merged_span_cf, labelwise_dense, margin_seat, finding_calib_dense, blendhold, through_dense, merged_blend_cf), 909 shared studies, from their .holdout.npz — no encoder, no card, ~60 s CPU beside a live arm. Log: logs/route_seats8.log.

NO NEW CODE WAS NEEDED. record_mix with no reading flag runs MemberCurve.logged, which already calls LabelCombine.curve on the pool. I had started adding a --records mode to label_combine and hit an import cycle (label_combine -> record_mix -> member_curve -> label_combine); the cycle was the gate telling me the feature already had a home. Reverted.

THE NUMBERS (split-half column, the only quotable one):
  top- 1 per label:  in-sample 0.8736   split-half 0.8669
  top- 2 per label:  in-sample 0.8796   split-half 0.8737
  top- 3 per label:  in-sample 0.8808   split-half 0.8767
  top- 4 per label:  in-sample 0.8806   split-half 0.8770
  top- 5 per label:  in-sample 0.8798   split-half 0.8774   <- best routed
  top- 6 per label:  in-sample 0.8789   split-half 0.8772
  top- 7 per label:  in-sample 0.8775   split-half 0.8772
  top- 8 per label:  in-sample 0.8764   split-half 0.8766   (= the flat rank-average, the matched control)

Routing buys +0.0008 over its own matched control, under one estimator. That is an eighth of the 0.0062 holdout noise floor and a fifth of the ~0.004 the board can resolve (knee-b6sn). Directional at best; nothing to ship.

THE MECHANISM, which is the part worth keeping: oracle 0.8736 vs plain average 0.8764 -- headroom MINUS 0.0029. The oracle picks the best member per label USING THE ANSWERS and still loses to the flat average of eight. Strictly it compares a single member per label against an eight-member average, so correlation alone would favour the average; but the top-k curve is the fair read and it agrees, peaking at k=5 for +0.0008 and returning to the control by k=8. Both say the same thing: there is no per-label specialism in this pool to route on. That is head-monoculture measured on the LABEL axis, and it is the same prediction knee-fzpy gates raddino against.

Also read off the same run: LogitAverage 0.8769 vs RankAverage 0.8764 (+0.0005). The champion already serves LogitAverage, so this is consistent rather than new.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT: routing over a pool that CONTAINS a specialist. Every member here is the same head on near-identical backbones. If raddino (or any genuinely different encoder) lands with a per-label profile unlike the pool's, this curve is worth re-running -- it costs a minute and no card. Re-run condition, not a dead axis.
notes:
FOLLOW-UP, same day 15:26Z: ran the routing curve over the FULL 109-member pool, which needed the one piece of code the eight-seat run did not — the default reading prints the routing curve but enumerates every subset first, so past a dozen members it was unreachable. Added MemberCurve.routing (extracted from the inline call in logged, so no duplication) and a --routing flag on record_mix. Log: logs/route_pool109.log.

  top-  1 per label:  in-sample 0.8760   split-half 0.8652
  top-  9 per label:  in-sample 0.8827   split-half 0.8761   <- best
  top-109 per label:  in-sample 0.8663   split-half 0.8664   (= the flat rank-average of all 109)

+0.0097 over its own last row — and that number must NOT be quoted as routing's value. The control here
is the flat average of 109 members, most of them weak; nearly all of the gap is ordinary member
SELECTION, which the mean-based greedy scan already does. The fair contrasts, all split-half honest over
the same 909 studies:

  routed top-9 over 109 members      0.8761
  honest greedy seats over 109       0.8748  (peak at 21 seats, logs/honest_pool_20260829.log)
  flat average of the curated 8      0.8766  (logs/route_seats8.log)

Routing beats mean-greedy by +0.0013 and loses to a hand-curated flat eight by -0.0005. Three
independent aggregation strategies over the same pool land inside 0.0018 of each other, all at ~0.876.
That is the finding: THE POOL HAS AN AGGREGATION CEILING NEAR 0.876 AND THE METHOD DOES NOT MATTER.
It is the strongest form of the head-monoculture result — not just that the members carry the same
information in the mean and in the same places, but that no way of combining them found anything the
others missed. Only a member of a different KIND moves this number.
close_reason: Measured; the axis is answered for this pool and the re-run condition is written into the description.

title: Honest seat curve saturates at eight — and the leak I reported in it does not exist
description:
record_mix --seats honest --largest-pool over the ~110-record pool returned held-out 0.8743 at eight members and 0.8748 at twenty-one: +0.0005 over thirteen extra seats, an eighth of the 0.0062 holdout floor. The SHAPE is the finding (the roster saturates at eight); 'best honest count 21' is the argmax of a flat line and is not a recommendation.

THIS IS THE THIRD RULER TO SAY THE POOL IS SPENT and the first entitled to say it. seat_value priced marginal contribution to the holdout MEAN over 41 candidates (null). Full-pool greedy priced ENTRY POSITION (plateau at 10-11 of ~110). This one prices the whole roster under a choice fitted on studies it is not scored on. Three blind spots, one sign.

SELECTION OPTIMISM IS SMALL, which licenses reading greedy for position without an honest re-run each time: in-sample sits +0.0010 to +0.0032 above held-out and the gap SHRINKS with seats (+0.0032 at ten, +0.0010 at twenty-four). greedy's 0.8767 peak is ~+0.0023 optimistic, not manufactured. knee-fzpy gates raddino on greedy POSITION and this is what makes that legitimate.

THE DEFECT. Three members in the pool end in _cf — fold -1, trained on every study including the fold-0 holdout these numbers score on. Their holdout AUC is a training-set AUC. Two are seated inside the first eight:
  greedy  2: merged_span_cf
  greedy  8: merged_blend_cf
  greedy 18: merged_dense_cf
A split-half estimator does NOT remove this. It removes optimism from the CHOICE by fitting elsewhere; it cannot remove leakage from a MEMBER, because both halves lie inside that member's training set. So the honest column is fitted-elsewhere and still contaminated, and 0.8743-0.8748 is not a held-out number.

I ALREADY KNEW THIS RULE AND DID NOT CARRY IT ACROSS. The routed blendlabels pricing launched an hour earlier dropped exactly these two from honest12's roster for exactly this reason. The denominator discipline is not applied once per session.

WHAT SURVIVES. The shape probably does, the level does not: two leaked members inflate every row from the second onward by roughly the same amount, and leakage shifts a level rather than manufacturing a plateau. Whether saturation sits at eight or ten after removal is the same claim about a spent pool.

THE FIX, and it is one flag: re-run --seats honest --largest-pool with the three _cf paths excluded from --records. Offline arithmetic over cached predictions, no card — but CPU-heavy enough to have already cost the running arm a measurable epoch (knee-8hau's unguarded half), so it waits for the arm.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE AUDIT. Eight seats scoring what twenty-four score is a score-lane null and an EFFICIENCY-lane result: the shipped champion seats twelve. A third fewer members for +0.0005 held-out is the shape of an efficiency-prize entry. Not worth a slot alone today; if raddino enters the peak set under knee-fzpy, the eight-seat roster rebuilt around it is ONE submission serving both prizes.
notes:
2026-08-29 15:10Z — RETRACTION. The leak in this issue's original description is not real, and the curve is quotable as it stands.

_cf DOES NOT MEAN FOLD -1. IT MEANS THE MERGED CORPUS. The checkpoints' own options say so:
  merged_blend_cf   fold=0 folds=5 split_seed=2026 scheme=merged train_fraction=1.0
  merged_span_cf    fold=0 folds=5 split_seed=2026 scheme=merged train_fraction=1.0
  merged_dense_cf   fold=0 folds=5 split_seed=2026 scheme=merged train_fraction=1.0
Fold 0 of 5 on split seed 2026 — the same split every other member in the pool holds out. merged is a
FOREIGN_SCHEME, so the training corpus carries foreign studies beside the RSNA ones while the fold
assignment still holds out RSNA fold 0. No member in this pool trains on its own holdout.

CONSEQUENCES:
 - held-out 0.8743 at eight seats and 0.8748 at twenty-one are QUOTABLE. So is the bias column.
 - the _cf-free re-run named as this issue's fix is CANCELLED. There is nothing to correct.
 - the saturation finding is unchanged and now unqualified: the roster saturates at eight, and the
   thirteen seats past it are worth +0.0005 — an eighth of the 0.0062 holdout floor.
 - the reasoning about split-half estimators stands on its own: fitting the choice elsewhere removes
   optimism from the CHOICE and could not remove leakage from a MEMBER. It just had nothing to apply to.

WHAT WENT WRONG, and the counter-evidence was already in the same session. RecordMix raises 'a whole-corpus
member (--fold -1) writes no .holdout.npz'. The existence of merged_*_cf.holdout.npz was therefore proof,
on disk AND in the source I had read, that these are not fold -1. I asserted a claim about training data
from TWO SUFFIX LETTERS that one torch.load of the checkpoint's options refutes in nine seconds.

The tell I ignored: I 'remembered' that the routed blendlabels pricing had dropped these two for exactly
this reason. It had — and that earlier drop was the same unverified inference. Repetition is how a guess
becomes a fact about the repo. A belief that arrives already carrying its own justification is the one to
check, because the justification is what makes it feel checked.

SECOND ONE THIS HOUR: knee-b6sn records nearly filing board_transfer +1.82 as refuted off a range-restricted
eyeball of a score-sorted top-eighteen. Neither was caught by a gate; both by re-deriving a premise that had
only ever been asserted. This one had already produced an interpretation section and a P2 bead before the
nine-second check was run.

title: An 8B reader adds no supervision on the blank pairs; the lane is blocked on a loadable 35B, not refuted
description:
Qwen3-8B on the 57 annotated studies, scored by reader_upgrade: speaks on 81 of 177 blank pairs (45.8%) at accuracy 0.840 against a majority class of 0.840, interval [0.737, 0.911] - it matches 'absent everywhere' and adds nothing. It also regresses on the 463 pairs the lexicon answered (0.812 vs the lexicon's own 0.8705 macro against the same annotations).

Gate verdict: NOT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE MAJORITY CLASS. Do not spend card on the 4,406-report sweep with this reader.

What stays open: knee-fuhq's label-noise ceiling is untouched by this - it rests on our labels reading 0.8705 while a published coatnet reads 0.9167 on the same studies. The reader route to it is blocked on LOADING, not on evidence: both cached 35B checkpoints fail under transformers 5.15 (gptqmodel imports the removed no_init_weights; the NVFP4 twin's modelopt is not in AUTO_QUANTIZER_MAPPING) and vLLM is Linux-only on this machine. Reopening needs a 35B-class reader that loads, or a different route to the labels entirely.
notes:
Per-label check of the narrow surviving claim (knee-07wb/knee-pju4), on the annotated-58 truth: Synovitis 11 spoken of 41 blank, 0.727 vs majority 0.659; Baker's 7 of 29, 0.857 vs 0.966 (a loss); Fracture 24 of 26, 0.875 vs 0.846.

The denominators are 7 to 24 asserted cells. One flipped cell moves Synovitis by 0.09, larger than its whole lead. The limit is the RULER - 57 annotated studies - not the reader, so a loadable 35B would not settle it either. The narrow claim is unmeasurable on the truth we have; it needs more annotated studies, which we do not have.

title: Neither cached 35B reader loads under transformers 5.15
description:
core.data.labels.report_reader's DEFAULT_MODEL is Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4. Loading it needs a GPTQ backend; gptqmodel 4.2.5 (the latest) imports 'no_init_weights' from transformers.modeling_utils, which transformers 5.15 removed, so the import fails before any weight is read. The other cached 35B, mmangkad/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, declares quant_method 'modelopt', which is not in transformers 5.15's AUTO_QUANTIZER_MAPPING at all. vLLM would serve both and is Linux-only.

So the reader lane runs on a bf16 checkpoint under plain transformers: Qwen3-8B. Revisit if the reader's quality turns out to bound the label table rather than the mechanism.

title: HF cache entries written from WSL are unreadable by native Windows Python
description:
models--Qwen--Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 (and any snapshot fetched from WSL) stores its snapshot entries as WSL-style symlinks (IO_REPARSE_TAG_LX_SYMLINK). git-bash resolves them; native Windows Python sees a 0-byte file and open() raises OSError errno 22 while os.path.exists returns False. The blobs themselves are intact.

Recipe that fixes a snapshot without copying bytes (same NTFS volume, so hardlinks cost nothing): read each entry's target with 'readlink' under git-bash, then New-Item -ItemType HardLink from the blob into a sibling directory, and point --model at that directory. Done for the Qwen GPTQ snapshot at C:/Users/User/.cache/huggingface/local/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 (24 files, 22.8 GB, zero 0-byte entries).

The symptom reads as a corrupt or incomplete download, which is what cost the time: the index and every shard are present and the sizes are right.

title: Per-study reader over-call is not over-dispersed — label lane's per-study branch closes
description: Instrument core/data/labels/overcall_clustering.py, 0 card / 0 slots. Per-study over-call dispersion 1.24 [0.83, 1.65] against 1.00 for independent cells, over 56 annotated studies / 311 positive calls / 108 over-called (34.7%). The interval brackets independence, so the per-study latent a target shrinkage would grip is not measurable at this size and a per-study weight would fit the same noise twelve per-finding scalars fit. Pre-registered branch three fired. What stays open is the ledger's other clause: supervision that is not the reader at all. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-29_the-over-call-is-not-a-property-of-the-study.md.

title: decode_entry: the best roster a decode budget can buy
description: Joins roster_reads (cost in decodes) to RecordMix/Pool (score) with a greedy forward search under a decode ceiling. First measurement 2026-08-29: budget 1 -> 0.8736, budget 2 -> 0.8744, budget 3 -> 0.8746 over 37 members / 8 decodes; honest12 is 0.8750 on 12 seats across 3 decodes. The second and third decode buy +0.0008 and +0.0002, both inside the 0.0062 floor. Board agrees independently: trioseat_v1 (1 decode) 0.938 > honest12 (3 decodes) 0.937. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-29_one-decode-is-enough.md.

title: Efficiency Track: a second $7k/$6k/$5k podium whose metric we cannot measure offline
description:
FOUND 2026-08-29 by reading comp/ rather than by measuring anything. Two facts the working plan did not
contain.

ONE. The Efficiency Track pays its own prizes. comp/COMPETITION_RULES.txt lines 61-64:
First Efficiency Prize $7,000 / Second $6,000 / Third $5,000, out of $77,000 total. The third
efficiency prize EQUALS the tenth main prize ($5,000) and beats fifth through ninth on rank distance.

TWO. We are much closer to that podium than to the main one. Live read
(uv run --extra submit python -m kneemri.kaggle.efficiency_read --live), 2026-08-29 07:40Z:

  accuracy rank 28 of 2623 at 0.943 (read 2026-08-29)
  efficiency rank 16 of 2516 at 0.925 (read 2026-08-29)
  top 20 efficiency ranks score 0.925 to 0.948, median 0.935
  0 teams rank above us on efficiency while scoring BELOW us

Rank 16 needs to pass 13 teams. Rank 28 needs to pass 18, against a field whose top is 0.952.

THE LEVER IS MEASURED AND IT IS STEEP. comp/README.md recorded our efficiency row on 2026-08-25 as
rank 95 at 0.933. It is now rank 16 at 0.925. We LOST 0.008 of accuracy and GAINED 79 ranks, because
the entry driving the row changed from a mid-size roster to soloseat (ONE member, 0.925). Runtime is
weighted far harder than the main board's ruler and a cheap entry is not a compromise there, it is the
product.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE DIAGNOSIS, and it inverts the README's prescription. On 2026-08-25 the note read
"68 teams rank above us on efficiency while scoring below us. Accuracy is not what holds us at 95." At
rank 16 that number is ZERO. Every team above us outscores us. Runtime has stopped being the binding
constraint; SCORE AT THIS RUNTIME is. The cheap-build advice in comp/README.md is now aimed at a
constraint we already cleared.

THE FREE MOVE FIRST, BEFORE ANY SLOT. The efficiency board is a SNAPSHOT (2026-08-27 22:11) and
efficiency_read says our own row is stale. onepair scored 0.936 on TWO members on 2026-08-28 - after
the snapshot. A 0.936 two-member entry against a top-20 band of 0.925-0.948 could move us several ranks
for nothing already spent. Re-read the board before pricing any new entry; we may hold a rank we have
not seen.

THE PAID MOVE, IF THE FREE ONE IS NOT ENOUGH. A ONE-member entry scoring above 0.925 is the direct
attack, and it is the same object knee-rh4t is about (rivals reach 0.938-0.942 on a single model). The
efficiency track converts a better single model into prize money on a board where our rank is already
16, which is a materially better ratio than the same member buying a seat in a saturated ensemble
(knee-va22, knee-xuj5, knee-urvf all say the seat is worth ~0).

ADDITIVITY IS MEASURED, so an efficiency entry costs a slot and nothing else: 472 of 2097 settled teams
carry an efficiency entry BELOW their public best and 0 carry a better one. Holding both is normal and
the accurate entry is not displaced.

NOT YET KNOWN: the metric's formula. The evaluation page is JS-only and the API does not carry it, so
nothing here predicts a rank - only the direction, which the 95 -> 16 move measures at our own operating
point.
notes:
2026-08-30 03:28Z. THE FORMULA IS NOT REACHABLE, and that is the finding — this bead can stop trying.

Tried and closed off: the evaluation overview page 404s on the efficiency-prize path; the public LB kernel (ryanholbrook/rsna-knee-abnormalities-efficiency-lb) is a thin reader that only merges an upstream CSV; the upstream data kernel is 403 (private); the kernel's OUTPUT (comp/efficiency_lb/full_leaderboard.csv, 2584 rows) carries only EfficiencyRank,TeamName,PublicScore,DateSubmitted; and 'kaggle competitions submissions -v' carries ref,fileName,date,description,status,publicScore,privateScore. NO RUNTIME COLUMN EXISTS ANYWHERE WE CAN REACH, for us or for anyone. The metric is a function of a variable nothing available reports, so it cannot be fitted, and rank cannot be predicted for a candidate entry.

What the pull DID settle, and these are worth keeping:

1. KAGGLE PICKS OUR EFFICIENCY ROW; WE DO NOT. Our row is 245,Dimitar Terziev,0.941,Thu Aug 27 08:05:42 2026 — that timestamp is calibsix_v1 (ref 55810756, 6 members, board 0.941). It is NOT our best submission: raptorweight_v1 reads 0.944. One row per team, joined on team name.

2. THE METRIC REWARDS SCORE SUBSTANTIALLY. Our row previously sat on a one-member 0.925 entry and has since moved to a six-member 0.941 one. Whatever the weighting is, +0.016 of score outweighed six times the members. That kills the assumption behind the cheap-resubmission play: a deliberately small entry does not automatically take the row back.

3. THE ADDITIVITY STAT IN THIS BEAD'S EARLIER NOTES IS TAUTOLOGICAL. '462 of 2126 settled teams carry an efficiency entry BELOW their public best and 0 carry a better one' — 0 is not evidence of anything. The efficiency entry is drawn from the team's own submissions, so its score cannot exceed the maximum over those submissions, which is the public best by definition. Do not quote it as a finding again.

4. THE 16 -> 245 COLLAPSE IS REAL BUT ITS CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The rank-16 read described a 2516-team field; the current one is 2584 teams. Our row also changed submissions between the two reads. Two things moved at once and this file cannot separate them.

WHY DOWNGRADED P0 -> P2. Every reading on this axis now costs a SUBMISSION SLOT, because fire-and-observe is the only instrument left. Five slots a day, one held for the owner, and the live goal is a top-10 main-board place from rank 48. An axis that cannot be measured offline should not be spending the scarcest resource we have against the axis that can. Re-open to P0 if any of these appear: a runtime column in any Kaggle surface, a public write-up of the formula, or a spare slot on a day the score track has nothing queued.

DO NOT re-run efficiency_read --live to 'check' — it reads the same kernel this CSV came from and will return the same 245.
STALE RANKS 2026-09-01 (board_claims). The efficiency and accuracy standings quoted in the notes (accuracy 28 of 2623 at 0.943, efficiency 16 of 2516 at 0.925) predate the current board; the live accuracy read at 2026-09-01T07:33:16Z is rank 30 of 2814 at 0.944. The efficiency board has still never been read by any tool we own - that unread state, not the numbers, is what this bead is for.

title: Every non-DINOv2 trunk was trained at a rate fitted for DINOv2, and the suspect has never been cleared
description:
cnx_dense (4e-5) peaked at e11 of 11 with the training loss still falling - never converged. cnx_own_recipe (4e-4) peaked at e6 of 12 and then declined - converged and overfitted. An undertrained point and an overfitted point do not bracket a fitted rate; they bracket an interval nobody sampled.

The same 4e-5 was handed to raddino (0.8141) and vjepa (0.8343). It was fitted over ~189 DINOv2-family runs. So the conclusion 'foreign trunks are worse than our family' rests on a knob that was never fitted for any of them - a FAULTY TRAINING suspect standing behind a whole lane.

ARM: cnx_mid_rate, 1.2e-4 (geometric mean of the bracket), every other flag byte-identical to cnx_own_recipe so the delta is the rate alone and cnx_own_recipe is a matched control that already exists.

EXPECTED SCORE ~0 AND IT RUNS ANYWAY. Even a clean win lands the trunk near 0.83 against base_dense 0.8512, and forty displacement tests (experiments/README.md:3086) say a member at that quality cannot move the peak set. It is an INSTRUMENT: it either downgrades every foreign-trunk number on record to 'measured at a rate never fitted for it', or it clears the suspect so no future foreign arm owes a rate sweep. Both are worth having; only one is good news.

Pre-registration is in the arm header. Cost ~70 min of card, zero slots.
notes:
2026-08-29 07:51Z — ARM KILLED AT EPOCH 1 OF 12. NO NUMBER. Do not read anything from it.

WHAT HAPPENED. The arm was priced at ~70 minutes. Its first epoch measured 815 s, so twelve epochs is
2.7 HOURS - 2.3x the price it was armed at. Its own `timeout 7200` would then have killed it around
epoch 8, and under `one_cycle` the anneal never runs, so the recorded score would have been a TRUNCATED
floor rather than a reading against the pre-registration. An instrument that costs 2.7h and returns an
unreadable number is not an instrument.

THE ONE DATA POINT, recorded so the epoch cost is not re-discovered: epoch 0, loss 0.6246, holdout mean
AUC 0.7177, 815 s, 8.48 GB peak reserved against a 14 GB reservation. That last figure says the arm was
ALSO over-reserving by ~5.5 GB, which is worth carrying into the next cnxbase arm.

THE RATE QUESTION IS STILL OPEN and this bead stays open with it. Nothing was learned about 1.2e-4.

WHY IT WAS KILLED RATHER THAN LET RUN. The owner named two higher-ratio uses of the card in the same

title: kneemri-blendall names two members that were never trained
description:
