This is the ONLY refusal in the tree: 58 ok, 5 skipped, 1 refused of 64 kernel directories. It has been failing since before the raptor work and is unrelated to it.

Two honest ends: train the two arms, or delete the kernel. Deleting is the cheaper one unless the dose-at-six curve is still wanted — the kernel's own docstring is the argument for it. Until one of them happens, mount_check exits 1 for everybody, which is how a real refusal gets read as background noise.
notes:
Resolved by deleting the kernel, and the deletion is argued from the CURVE rather than from the missing weights.

blend_through and blend_base were blendsix's last two outputs; blendsix is cancelled and do-not-requeue, so the roster was unbuildable and mount_check exited 1 for every shipment on its account.

The reason not to train them instead: blendall was the far end of a dose curve over how many seats saw the three-reader blend supervision, count/vote/serving held fixed. dose 1 blendseat_v1 0.939, dose 4 blendthree_v1 0.939. FLAT -- four blend-supervised seats score what one does. The entry existed to read a SHAPE, and a third point at the far end of an axis whose first two lie on top of each other buys nothing worth a slot.

Not a verdict on the supervision axis (still the only axis on this board with external corroboration -- forum 735304/735826). A verdict on measuring a saturated curve a third time.

mount_check now reads 59 ok, 5 skipped, 0 refused of 64.

title: Five more foreign checkpoints exist; only one has a declared arch
description:
`kneemri.evaluation.foreign_member` serves `module.ARMS[0]`, and their published inference script declares exactly one arm: raptor_ft_coatnet_v4_full.pt / coatnet_rmlp_2_rw_384.sw_in12k_ft_in1k / res 384.

But the fetch pulled THREE datasets, six checkpoints:
  raptor-knee-widedense/raptor_ft_coatnet_v4_full.pt        <- the declared one
  raptor-knee-widedense/raptor_ft_coatnet_v4_full_swa.pt
  raptor-knee-finespacing/raptor_ft_coatnet_v9_full.pt
  raptor-knee-arms/raptor_ft_cnv2b336.pt
  raptor-knee-arms/raptor_ft_coatnet384.pt
  raptor-knee-arms/raptor_ft_effv2l480.pt

The last three are DIFFERENT TRUNKS (a ConvNeXt-V2 and an EfficientNetV2-L beside the CoAtNet), which is
the axis 2026-08-27_the-pool-is-82-percent-one-number.md says our 105-member pool has almost none of. Their
arch strings and resolutions are not declared in the script we have — the filenames imply them and a timm
name is not a thing to guess, since build_backbone routes on substrings ('convnext' hybrid, 'vit' path) and
a wrong route loads silently and scores as a weak member.

RECOVERABLE WITHOUT GUESSING: the state_dict key prefixes and the first conv's shape name the backbone, and
the positional/pooling shapes pin the resolution. A CPU-only torch.load of each file answers it in seconds.

DO NOT BUILD THE --arch/--res FLAG BEFORE THE BASE PATH HAS RUN ONCE (knee-9g28). The declared arm is the
gate: if their decode does not reproduce ~0.9167 on our holdout through this adapter, a flag that serves
five more checkpoints through the same seam serves five more wrong numbers.
notes:
Blocked on knee-9g28's first run — see its notes for why the declared arm is the gate.
2026-08-27 23:46Z — ALL FIVE RUN, AND THE ADAPTER VALIDATES ITSELF.

The five remaining checkpoints went through the same path as raptor_v4, 909-study fold-0 holdout, and
every one of the six wrote at 0.0% fallback. Absolute means, our best member calib_dense_hold_s2026 =
0.8634 for scale:

  member              our 909    vs ours    their published gold (58)
  raptor_v4_swa        0.8938    +0.0304                     0.9150
  raptor_v4            0.8915    +0.0281                     0.9167
  raptor_v9            0.8769    +0.0135                     0.9031
  raptor_effv2l480     0.8703    +0.0069                     0.8716
  raptor_cnv2b336      0.8550    -0.0084                     0.8901
  raptor_coat384       0.8508    -0.0126                     0.9025

FOUR OF SIX BEAT OUR BEST MEMBER; three clear the 0.0062 paired floor by a wide margin and the fourth
(effv2l480, +0.0069) only just.

THE ADAPTER IS NOW SELF-VALIDATING, which no single checkpoint could show. Their published ordering and
ours agree on the top three, in order, on two different rulers fifteen times apart in size — v4 and its
SWA twin first and second, v9 third. A plumbing bug does not preserve a rival's own ranking of six
checkpoints it knows nothing about. This is the check knee-9g28's pre-registered near-0.9167 test was
reaching for and could not make, because that test compared across denominators.

WHERE THE TWO RULERS DISAGREE, stated rather than smoothed: coat384 and cnv2b336 invert. Their gold puts
coat384 at 0.9025 and effv2l480 last at 0.8716; our 909 puts effv2l480 fourth and coat384 last. At n=58
with Hanley-McNeil SE 0.031-0.072 per label those three are one indistinguishable clump on their ruler,
so the inversion is what small-sample noise looks like, not a contradiction. It is also the direction that
matters least: it is entirely among the checkpoints not worth seating.

THE FAMILY HAS ONE SIGNATURE, and it is a seat's worth of complementarity. All six are WORSE than our
member at Synovitis (-0.052 to -0.094) and five of six worse at Effusion. All six are better at Fracture.
The two large fluid collections are ours and the focal findings are theirs, on every checkpoint
independently — that is a structural trade, not one member's scatter.

CONSEQUENCE: knee-tlba is done as scoping. The seating question is now which ONE, and the answer is
raptor_v4_swa (0.8938) unless mixing v4 with its SWA twin buys something, which record_mix can price
offline for no slot. Recommend closing this and opening the seating work against raptor_v4_swa.

title: band_dense_llrd's refutation is confounded: layer decay was never tested, only a 0.41x rate cut
description:
band_dense_llrd read 0.8483 against band_dense 0.8578 (-0.0095) and the family reads as refuted. It is not: the arm moved TWO variables.

encoder_surgery.backbone_groups (kneemri/models/encoder_surgery.py:230) anchors the ladder at the TOP opened block — deliberately, and the comment at :227 states the argument: 'the rate in the ledger is the rate the top block was measured at'. That argument holds while depth is fixed. band_dense_llrd also moved depth (--unfreeze-last 12 against the default 6), and the anchor then reprices the CONTROL'S OWN SIX BLOCKS.

With opened=12 and decay 0.7, blocks 6-11 take exponents 5,4,3,2,1,0, so their geometric-mean rate is 0.7^2.5 = 0.410 x the control's flat 4e-5 (verified: 4e-5 -> 1.6e-5, 2.3e-5, 3.3e-5, 4.8e-5, 6.8e-5, 9.8e-5 read bottom-up from the matched anchor below). The arm's training loss floored ~0.13 high while still falling — underfit, not damaged blocks. So the reading is 'the control's own six blocks trained at 0.41x rate and lost 0.0095', which says nothing about depth-scaled rates and nothing about depth.

THE CLEAN ONE-VARIABLE ARM NEEDS NO CODE. Raise backbone_lr so the ladder's geometric mean over the control's six blocks lands back on 4e-5:

    --unfreeze-last 12 --layer-decay 0.7 --backbone-lr 9.8e-5

Then blocks 6-11 run 1.6e-5 .. 9.8e-5 (geometric mean 4e-5, the control's rate) and blocks 0-5 run 1.9e-6 .. 1.1e-5. The only thing that changed against the control is six deeper blocks opening at a tenth the rate — which is the mechanism the family was supposed to test.

STATED RISK, so it is not discovered as a surprise: geometric-mean matching is not the only matching, and it puts the TOP block at 9.8e-5, 2.4x the rate the ledger measured. If this arm regresses, the top block is the first suspect, not the mechanism — and the alternative anchor (hold the top block at 4e-5 and scale only the six NEW blocks down) is a code change to backbone_groups, an explicit anchor argument rather than the implicit len(opened)-1.

PRICE, unchanged from the ledger: ~2.2 h, ceiling ~+0.005, roughly one-in-five odds. DECLINED while better arms exist; filed so the family is not treated as closed. The card is with the peer project as of 2026-08-27, so nothing is queueable now.
close_reason: SWEEP phase 1 (completed but not properly marked): the arm named in this bead's own title has a .full.log in $MODELS/experiments/ AND a scored row in experiments/README.md. The work ran and the ledger priced it; the bead was never marked. Reversible - bd update --status open if a reading here is still owed.

title: Our training labels read 0.8705 against the radiologists; a published model beats them on ten of twelve findings, so LABEL NOISE outranks architecture as the ceiling
description:
Measured 2026-08-27T15:44Z. No card, no slot.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. train.csv carries 58 radiologist-annotated studies. 57 of them appear in our
report_labels_v2.csv, so our LLM labels can be scored as if they were a model:

  ACL 1.0000 | MCL 0.9722 | Medial Meniscus 0.9516 | Lateral Meniscus 0.8440
  Medial OA 0.9127 | Lateral OA 0.7984 | PF OA 0.8946 | Effusion 0.8517
  Synovitis 0.6951 | Baker's 0.9537 | Contusion 0.7564 | Fracture 0.8162
  macro 0.8705  (n=57)

OUR TARGETS ARE A 0.8705 RULER. Our best members read ~0.873 holdout mean AUC against those same
targets, i.e. they have already fitted the labels about as far as the labels go. The published Raptor
coatnet reads 0.9167 on the same 58 studies, and beats OUR LABELS on ten of twelve findings:

  finding      their MODEL   our LABELS
  Effusion        0.9789       0.8517
  Contusion       0.9150       0.7564
  Fracture        0.9125       0.8162
  Lateral OA      0.8685       0.7984
  Synovitis       0.7575       0.6951
  Baker's         0.9873       0.9537
  Lateral Men     0.8807       0.8440
  Medial OA       0.9860       0.9127
  PF OA           0.8288       0.8946  (ours wins)
  Medial Men      0.9483       0.9516  (ours wins)
  MCL             0.9705       0.9722  (ours wins, ties)
  ACL             0.9669       1.0000  (ours wins)

Sign test on 8-9 of 12 in their favour is p ~ 0.05; the four we win are the four EASY findings where
our labels are already near 1.0. Every finding we are weak on is a finding they are strong on.

A SECOND INDEPENDENT LABEL SET IS ON DISK AND IS CC0. D:/data/external/raptor/labels/labels_llm_soft.csv,
4349 studies, the same twelve columns, soft in [0,1], keyed by StudyInstanceUID. It covers 4349 of our
4406 and DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES ALL 58 GOLD STUDIES - which is why their gold_auc is a clean oracle, and
is also why the two label sets cannot be compared head to head on the gold.

THE TWO LLM READINGS OF THE SAME REPORTS DISAGREE A LOT. Pearson over the 4349 shared studies:
  Medial Men 0.898 | Lateral Men 0.884 | PF OA 0.881 | Medial OA 0.850 | ACL 0.822 | Baker's 0.803
  Lateral OA 0.799 | Fracture 0.786 | MCL 0.766 | Contusion 0.747 | Effusion 0.725 | SYNOVITIS 0.389
Their soft prevalence is LOWER than ours on eleven of twelve (e.g. Effusion 0.325 vs 0.499, Baker's
0.170 vs 0.345, Fracture 0.115 vs 0.240). Synovitis is the single inversion and also the single worst
correlation - the two readers do not agree on what the word means.

WHY THIS IS THE BIGGEST OPEN LEVER. Sixteen scored board entries built from our members span
0.936-0.941 regardless of seat count; knee-97ib priced the marginal seat at 0.000. That is the
signature of a pool that has saturated its own targets. Averaging two independent noisy labellings is
the standard treatment for exactly this, it is mechanically sound, and the disagreement measured above
says there is real noise to average out - unlike a knob, this could plausibly clear the 1.5% bar.

THE ARM IS ONE FLAG. train already takes --labels (the recipe records it), so a consensus CSV is a
drop-in. Build ours-and-theirs averaged, falling back to ours where they have no row (the 57 gold
studies among them, which the _hold members withhold anyway), and run it against a matched control.
Rule 2.6a clears the data: CC0-1.0, publicly available at no cost.

DO NOT SKIP THE CONTROL. The two label sets differ in PREVALENCE as well as in noise, so an averaged
target is also a re-calibrated one, and a gain could be either. The control is the same recipe on
report_labels_v2.csv.
notes:
2026-08-29 14:23Z — DEMOTED P0->P2, and the one live continuation named.

Its own two notes already price the lane out as a TARGET rewrite: blendlabels reads +0.0034 on the mean
with the ledger's verdict 'confirmed LIVE and confirmed SMALL ... do not refit the roster on it', and the
fourth reader (labels_llm_soft.csv) cannot be scored on the gold 58 at all because their corpus is exactly
our 4,406 minus those 58 — a broken denominator, not a null. Nothing here licenses an arm or a slot, so it
should not have been sitting at the top of `bd ready` as a P0 pointing the next session at a rewrite.

WHAT IS NOT SPENT, and is running now with no card. The bead's SPLIT is the part that survived: label noise
is the ceiling on six findings (Effusion +0.1304, Contusion +0.0891, Synovitis +0.0508, Medial OA +0.0419,
Baker's +0.0226, Fracture +0.0160) and the MODEL is the ceiling on the other six. blendlabels reads +0.0034
on the mean but +0.0070 on exactly those six. `seat_value` priced blendlabels_s2026 at +0.0001 marginal and
that is not a contradiction — seat_value prices a MEAN contribution, so a member that helps on half the
findings and dilutes on the other half reads as nothing. That is the dilution the mechanism predicts, and
per-finding routing is the instrument that does not average it away (knee-q1pf, +0.0043 matched;
kneemri/evaluation/label_combine.py).

THE PRICING, launched 14:22Z, zero card, arithmetic over cached holdout arrays. label_combine over
honest12's TEN fold-0 members, then the same ten plus blendlabels_s2026. The two _cf members
(merged_blend_cf, merged_dense_cf) are dropped from both arms: fold -1 holdouts sit inside their training
set and would inflate a split-half estimator. label_combine carries its own matched control — selecting
top-k per label at k=every member IS the flat rank-average — so one k curve holds candidate and baseline
under the SAME estimator, which is the only way to avoid comparing a split-half number to a whole-holdout
one. Logs: logs/labelcombine_base10.log, logs/labelcombine_plus_blendlabels.log.

HOW IT IS READ, before the number. A rise in the honest split-half peak when blendlabels is added, with
blendlabels selected on the label-bottlenecked findings, means two directional gains COMPOSED — which is
knee-orjq's open question ('nothing has ever tested whether directional gains ADD') answered on a free
instance. Flat or lower means the +0.0070 was inside the selection optimism the module is built around,
and the label lane closes for good rather than being demoted.
close_reason:
The pre-registered read came back FLAT, so the lane closes rather than being demoted again.

Ran the bead's own instrument under its own matched estimator (label_combine, fold 0, cpu, arithmetic over
cached holdout arrays; logs/labelcombine_base10.log and logs/labelcombine_plus_blendlabels.log). The
2026-08-29 note said this was launched at 14:22Z; no logs of it existed on disk, so it was re-run.

  arm                      split-half peak      flat control (k = every member)
  honest12 ten fold-0      0.8751 (k=6)         0.8742
  the same ten + blend     0.8754 (k=6,8)       0.8745

blendlabels_s2026 is worth +0.0003 on the peak and +0.0003 on the flat. The bead pre-registered: 'Flat or
lower means the +0.0070 was inside the selection optimism the module is built around, and the label lane
closes for good rather than being demoted.' It is flat, at 1/50th of the significance bar and consistent
with seat_value's independent +0.0001 marginal.

Two things settle with it. knee-orjq asked whether directional gains ADD; on this free instance they did
not - a +0.0034 mean and a +0.0070 six-finding subset composed into +0.0003. And per-label ROUTING itself
is worth only +0.0009 over the flat rank-average in BOTH arms, the same order as knee-m69u's +0.0002
per-label weighting oracle headroom, so routing is not the instrument that rescues a diluted member either.

What is NOT closed by this: the label-noise SPLIT measurement itself (six findings where the labels are the
ceiling, six where the model is) stands as a description. What is refuted is that averaging a second LLM
reading into the targets converts that split into score.

title: Mount the hold-annotations corner: four best unmounted members are staged but the kit is stale
description:
calib_dense_hold_s2026 (0.8634) and stackfit_s2026 (0.8631) are the two best solo checkpoints in the pool and neither is mounted; distill_pairs_s2026 (0.8594) and ema_dense_s2026 (0.8588) are next. All four are copied into <processed>/all_ours already (55 files, 6.5 GB) and NOT pushed.

Rebuilding the kit means build_kit.py --wheels <dir> plus verify_kit.py plus a kit dataset version, and that was judged too large a change to make twenty minutes before a submission decision on a 0.941 champion whose kit is pinned at fec94e7 in comp/champion.json.

TO FINISH: rebuild the kit, verify it, push the kit, then push all_ours, then re-run mount_check and champion_check. The staged .pt files can sit in all_ours indefinitely - extra members in the package break nothing (mount_check only refuses a kernel that asks for a member the package LACKS).

VALUE, priced honestly: mounting costs no slot and buys OPTIONALITY, not board points. The 23% pass-through measured on calibsix says a member-quality gain of +0.004 on one seat is not a board tick. Name these only if something makes the hold-annotations family look like a DIVERSITY axis rather than a quality one.

title: Seat lane closed on the offline ruler: honest count plateaus at +0.0018, diverse peak is -0.0088 behind
description:
record_mix over 103 records / 909 shared studies, 2026-08-27.

HONEST: six 0.8720, nine 0.8729, peak 0.8738 at twenty-four. Six to twenty-four buys +0.0018, under a third of the 0.0062 floor, against an in-sample/held-out bias of +0.0017 - the selection bias is the size of the whole gain. Count is exhausted from ~nine.

DIVERSE: peak 0.8650 at ninety-nine, -0.0088 behind honest, 1.4 floors. Flat-distance selection elects the worst members first (seat 2, focus_latmen, drops 0.8634 to 0.7501) and needs twenty-five seats to reach what one member does alone.

So an ensemble built for spread does NOT beat one built for quality, which is the question record_mix's docstring has carried unanswered since it was written.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE. Both selectors are offline rulers, and knee-nas5 measured the offline ruler as under-pricing decode-path diversity 2.4x (0.0059 offline / 0.014 board). A TARGETED pixel-group add is not covered by either result. Everything else in the seat lane is.

title: Roster claims of the form 'never tried on the board' go stale and nearly buy slots
description:
comp/members.roster line 119 read 'the encoder SIZE axis, never varied on the board' from 2026-08-20 until 2026-08-27. By 08-27 twenty-three kernels named a base member and the axis was priced: base-seated board entries span 0.934-0.939, while the two best entries this competition has produced (calibsix 0.941, and the 0.939 above it) seat none. The claim was not merely stale, it had inverted.

It nearly bought slot 3 of 5 on 2026-08-27. The pre-registration being drafted was 'add base_dense_ff as a seventh seat because the encoder SIZE axis has never been on the board' - a slot spent on an axis already measured flat-to-down at the top of the board. The check that caught it was one loop over comp/kernels/*/*.py grepping for the member name, which is cheap enough to be a gate.

WHAT TO DO. Sweep the roster for every claim of the form 'never mounted' / 'never varied' / 'never on the board' / 'the only X' and resolve each against comp/kernels/ and comp/board.jsonl as of today. Then decide whether kit_check or mount_check should assert it: a roster line that says NEVER and a kernel that names the member is a contradiction a script can find.

This is the second time a roster claim outlived its measurement (the first was the board_transfer slope quoted from prose).

title: normalise_by_count is the LAST unmeasured recipe key - close the knob space or find the one that moved
description:
PRICE: ~19 min of card at 224 px (8124 MiB, native224's corner), zero slots. P(clears the 0.0062 floor) ~0.10.

WHY IT IS WORTH 19 MINUTES ANYWAY, AS AN INSTRUMENT AND NOT AS AN IMPROVEMENT. knee-s9cr's 2026-08-26 survey walked all 61 keys of a recorded recipe stamp against the ledger and against the 110 files in experiments/arms/. Exactly ONE key is neither in the ledger nor behind an arm file: --normalise-by-count, which takes the loss .mean() instead of dividing by the weight sum. Running it converts 'the knob space is enumerated' from a survey claim into a measured fact, and that claim is currently load-bearing: it is the reason knee-s9cr redirected away from a 224 px knob sweep, and the reason the schedule points at members rather than at recipes.

THE PRIOR IS WEAK AND STATED UP FRONT. The nearest relative, per_label_loss, is refuted at -0.0043 with its falsifiable clause resolving the wrong way. So the expected score movement is ~0, and this must be justified as an instrument or not run.

THE SINGLE VARIABLE. native224's recipe verbatim - 12 slices, band 0.2-0.8, --image-size 224, 12 epochs, backbone-lr 4e-5, max pooling, whole-stack, fold 0 - plus --normalise-by-count. Control native224 = 0.8502, already on the ledger, so this costs ONE run.

THE LADDER, against the 0.0062 three-seed paired floor:
  * >= 0.8564 - the weight-sum denominator was costing us, and the whole weighted-loss family reopens.
  * 0.8440-0.8564 - within the floor. The knob space is CLOSED, measured rather than surveyed.
  * <= 0.8440 - dividing by the weight sum is load-bearing; keep it, and note that the UNK down-weighting it interacts with is doing real work.

WHEN. In a card gap after the queued instruments (confident224, finding_calib_dense). Not before them - both answer larger questions.
notes: card is free 2026-08-27 10:33Z — this is the arm to run in the gap
close_reason: FLAT, as pre-registered. Peak 0.8498 @ e6 (12/12 epochs, converged) against native224's 0.8502 @ e7 — a delta of -0.0004, mid-band of the 0.8440-0.8564 FLAT ladder. The knob is retired and the knob space is now closed BY MEASUREMENT rather than by survey: 61 keys, every one varied at least once. The instrument paid for itself — the schedule's pointing at members and ensembles no longer rests on a survey claim. Ledger: experiments/README.md, 'normcount224'.

title: mount_check refuses kneemri-blendall: it names blend_through/blend_base, which the roster no longer holds
description: `python -m kneemri.kaggle.mount_check` exits 1 on a REFUSED row for `comp/kernels/kneemri-blendall`: it asks for ['blend_through', 'blend_base'] while all_ours holds blend_calib / blend_ladder / blend_ws. title: build_rijeka was uncallable: --spacing collided with CacheFlags --spacing
description:
core.data.corpus.build_rijeka added its own --spacing (float, mm per pixel) and CacheFlags later added --spacing (choice, how slices sit inside the band). argparse raised ArgumentError at parser construction, so the CLI could not run AT ALL - every invocation died before reading argv. Undetected because the rijeka cache on disk predates the CacheFlags flag and nothing re-decoded it until 2026-08-27.

FIXED in the same session: the rijeka flag is now --pixel-spacing, with a docstring naming the collision. The 336px/20sl rijeka cache built clean afterwards (736 studies, 1 slot).

REMAINING: nothing tests that these CLIs can be CONSTRUCTED. A smoke that builds every core.data.corpus entrypoint's parser would have caught this the day CacheFlags gained the flag, and costs milliseconds.

title: Raptor inference half read: our preprocessing is at parity or ahead; only band width and resolution differ
description:
Read external/raptor/knee-mri-twelve-findings-from-a-single-model.py end to end (the 0.924 public inference notebook). Recording what it does that we do not, and what we already do better, so no future session re-reads 459 lines to find out.

MATCHES OUR NEW BUILD EXACTLY. Their head is Linear(768,256) -> Tanh -> Dropout -> Linear(256,12), softmaxed over the K window axis, then einsum('bkn,bkf->bnf') and a per-class readout (pooled*clsW).sum(-1)+clsb. That is our LabelwiseAttention plus SlotHead's readout, operator for operator. The one difference is initialisation: their 256->12 score layer is default-initialised, ours is zeroed so the pooling starts as the mean for all twelve at once. Ours is the better choice — an arm's delta is then entirely something training chose, with no part of it paid for by an opinion the module held before it saw a study. Their prose ranks this operator above every other design choice they made.

THEIR WINDOWING IS OUR adjacent224. Three physically-consecutive slices stacked as the three channels of one image, passed through the backbone; 'most of the benefit of a 3D model at the cost of a 2D one'. K_EVAL=42 windows per study at inference, chosen as every window position the volume holds rather than an evenly spaced subset.

WHERE WE ARE AHEAD. They crop a 140 mm box around the CENTRE OF THE IMAGE. We crop 130 mm around a TISSUE CENTRE found by Otsu (core/data/corpus/crop_centre.py) — same scale normalisation, better centring, and the docstring already argues why a fixed percentile would get the field of view wrong.

WHERE WE DIFFER AND IT IS NOT A GAP. They fill five fixed slots for 64 slices total (18/14/12/8/12); we sample 12 per slot across five slots, so the sampling density is the same regime, not a 5x deficit as the raw '64 vs 12' suggests.

THE TWO REAL DIFFERENCES. (1) Slice band: they span 6-94 percent of each series and say cutting the outer slices was measurably costing them MCL and lateral meniscus — our two worst per-label deltas. We measured 0.10-0.90 as band_wide (+0.0028, and it sits in the champion family), but the 224 control arms still run 0.20-0.80. The remaining 0.10->0.06 is a sliver and does not justify its own arm; the point is that the axis is already ours. (2) Resolution 336 and a CoAtNet backbone.

THEIR OWN ENSEMBLE NUMBER, worth keeping: on the live leaderboard CoAtNet alone scored 0.914 and every blend scored 0.914-0.915, so ensembling bought them ~+0.001 there against the ~+0.010 it showed on their 45-study gold set. They call the gold-set figure noise. That is a direct external confirmation of our own small-holdout caution.

NOTHING TO QUEUE FROM THIS. The two mechanisms they credit are the two arms already in flight (adjacent224, labelwise224).

title: queue_check cannot see a live watcher whose log it did not name
description:
On 2026-08-26 23:42Z two after.sh watchers were live and correctly paired (831801 owes adjacent224, gating on 'ARM DONE merged_blend_cf'; 794482 owes calibsix). queue_check reported UNLOGGED for BOTH — 'a live after.sh owes these and has no watcher log under logs' — even though experiments/logs/after_adjacent224.log existed, was under the searched directory, and held the waiting line. So its whole verdict was reached blind, which is its own stated failure mode and the reason it exists.

The invariant had to be checked by hand instead: ps -ef | grep after.sh, read the argv, confirm one live watcher per owed arm. That is the manual step queue_check was written to remove.

Suspect: the log-to-watcher join. Both watchers write a log named for the arm they OWE while gating on a marker in a log named for a DIFFERENT arm, and queue_check appears to join on the watched file rather than on the redirect target — the same class of defect board_check fixed by joining on the Kaggle ref instead of on a name. Fix by joining on the watcher PROCESS (argv already carries both the marker, the watch path and the arm list) rather than on any filename.

title: Keep a leader-score series: one board_read a day, appended not overwritten
description:
comp/leaderboard.json is OVERWRITTEN on every read, so the project holds exactly one board snapshot at a time. The leader has read 0.952 on both 2026-08-25 and 2026-08-26 - flat across the only two points we have, and two points is not a slope.

Our own running-best climbs +0.0016/day (9-day fit, interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_the-horizon-is-56-days-not-4-hours.md). The gap is 0.013, so our rate covers it in ~8 days against 56 days of runway - IF the leader stays still. That is the single unevidenced assumption in the whole plan, and it is free to measure: board_read costs no submission slot.

Change board_read to APPEND a row to comp/leaderboard.jsonl (leader, ours, rank, field, tied, taken) while still writing the current-state leaderboard.json champion_check reads. Within a week the leader's slope becomes a measurement instead of an assumption, and the top-5 series says whether the frontier is climbing or plateaued.

title: calib_dense_hold_s2026 is our best solo member and cannot ship
description:
calib_dense_hold_s2026 reads 0.8634 solo on the 909-study shared holdout — the best single member this project has, ahead of small_batch6_s2026 (0.8598) and merged_blend_s2026 (0.8589). It is ABSENT from comp/members.roster, so package_members.py never packs it and it is not mounted in dimiturnt/kneemri-members. Any kernel naming it fails to build a member at serving time.

Shipping it needs a manual members dataset push, which was not affordable inside the 2026-08-26 slot window. Offline it did not clear the bar as a swap (0.8702 vs 0.8704 base) and read +0.0009 as a seventh seat, both inside the 0.0062 noise floor — so this is not urgent on evidence, it is a gap in what the roster can express. Add the line, push the members dataset, then re-run record_mix so the honest ladder is measured over a shippable pool rather than a superset of one.
close_reason: SWEEP phase 1 (completed but not properly marked): the arm named in this bead's own title has a .full.log in $MODELS/experiments/ AND a scored row in experiments/README.md. The work ran and the ledger priced it; the bead was never marked. Reversible - bd update --status open if a reading here is still owed.

title: Kaggle GPU session cap is shared with biohub and no gate looks at it
description:
One Kaggle account serves both kneemri and biohub_kaggle. Kaggle caps batch GPU sessions at TWO across the account, so a kernel push fails outright with 'Maximum batch GPU session count of 2 reached' when the other project has two live runs. On 2026-08-26 22:06Z this refused the resseat push while three celltrack kernels were live (21:49/22:00/22:01Z), costing the authorised slot ~50 minutes of a ~110 minute window before the 00:00Z reset.

Neither project's pre-push gate asks. kit_check, mount_check and champion_check all pass a push that cannot land. Fix: ask 'kaggle kernels status' (or kernels list --mine --sort-by dateRun) for live runs before pushing, and report 'slot busy, N live' as a message rather than letting the CLI refuse. Letter sent to biohub inbox 2026-08-26_kneemri-needs-one-gpu-slot.md proposing they mirror it.

title: the report silence is the REPORT's, not the reader's — reader survives only as a 58-study probe
description:
27.3% of our supervision is a CONSTANT, not a read. Filling it with a locally-run open-weights
multilingual reader is permitted, is a uniform lift by construction, and is the only lever found
that is plausibly sized for the +0.0133 offline that 0.950 now costs (knee-ps8o).

THE MEASUREMENT. report_labels_v2.csv, denominator 4406 studies x 12 findings = 52,872
(study,finding) pairs. UNK verdicts:

  Synovitis  3712  84.2%      Baker's     2023  45.9%      Lateral OA 1457  33.1%
  Fracture   2486  56.4%      PF OA        815  18.5%      Contusion   916  20.8%
  Medial OA  1125  25.5%      Lat Menisc   442  10.0%      MCL         430   9.8%
  Effusion    434   9.9%      ACL          355   8.1%      Med Menisc  250   5.7%

  TOTAL 14,445 / 52,872 = 27.3% of all pairs.

An UNK is filled with a base-rate prior (0.28), not with a read. Synovitis is effectively
unsupervised: 84% prior, 580 YES, 114 NO.

IT PROPAGATES INTO THE CHAMPION. Cell-value census of the derived tables:
  merged_labels.csv    14,445 cells at exactly 0.28   -- identical count, silence passed through
  confident.csv        14,445 cells BLANK             -- identical count, silence masked out
  blend_three_v1.csv   578 distinct values, top 0.035 (12,609) and 0.17667 (9,049)
      the champion's own table (blendhold recipe). The UNK cells were averaged with two other
      readers, so they are diluted rather than resolved -- 0.17667 is a prior-derived average,
      and it is the second most common value in the entire table.

WHY IT IS A LEXICON, AND WHY THAT MATTERS. report_labels_v2.csv carries 8 distinct confidence
values in the whole file and 5 distinct (value,conf,verdict) triples on ACL. That is a
deterministic rule fingerprint. The lexicon's failure mode is SILENCE, and per api_labeler.py's
docstring the silence is concentrated in a few languages (Greek, Bulgarian, Turkish, Croatian,
Dutch, German, Spanish, French) rather than spread evenly -- so the 27.3% is not random
missingness, it is a systematic hole with a known cause.

THE LEVER. train.csv carries a `Report` column, so the raw text is in hand. A local open-weights
multilingual reader (Qwen-class) over the 14,445 blank pairs:
  * PERMITTED -- local weights, no hosted API, no transmission of competition data, no external
    dataset. Distinct from the MRNet route (knee-2sbk), which is blocked on a host answer.
  * UNIFORM BY CONSTRUCTION -- a new label table retrains EVERY seat, which is the only mechanism
    measured above 100% pass-through (126-147%). The "better label table ~13%" figure was a
    single-seat swap and does not apply.
  * SIZED FOR THE GOAL -- replacing a constant on 27.3% of pairs is not a knob. Every other lever
    in the census (knee-s3cd) is settled, closed, or below the noise floor.

VALIDATION INSTRUMENT ALREADY EXISTS. `kneemri/evaluation/annotated_readings.py` scores a member
against the annotated subset and REFUSES any checkpoint not trained with `--hold-annotations`.
So a new reader can be scored against human annotations on the UNK pairs specifically, before any
seat is retrained. That is the gate: the new table must beat the lexicon ON THE PAIRS THE LEXICON
LEFT BLANK, measured on annotations, before it costs a single training hour.

PLAN. CPU now: build the reader + prompt, reuse api_labeler.py's SYSTEM block and twelve-finding
schema (it is a stranded draft -- see knee-sajo note -- but the prompt is sound and already
multilingual). Card frees ~21:03Z per celltrack's letter. Then: read -> score against annotations
-> only if it clears, write the table and retrain seats.

THIS DISPLACES calibsix (knee-1c00) FOR THE NIGHT. calibsix prices 7.1 h for ~+0.003 board with
its only unconfounded pair reading negative. This targets 27.3% of the supervision. Owner's call,
but the ratio is not close.
notes:
2026-08-27 12:32Z — THE PREMISE IS REFUTED, measured on CPU before any card hour was spent.

This bead said 27.3% of supervision is a constant because an English-pattern lexicon goes silent on the
seven other report languages, and proposed a local multilingual reader to recover it. Two measurements
kill that diagnosis.

1. UNK RATE BY LANGUAGE (report_language classification joined to report_labels_v2):
     en 20.7% (1768 studies)  es 42.3% (727)  tr 33.6% (546)  hr 22.2% (406)
     el 27.0% (321)  de 22.7% (259)  bg 23.8% (220)  nl 37.5% (153)
   English — the language the lexicon was BUILT for — is a fifth unread, 4,384 cells. A translation gap
   does not explain that.

2. THE UNK CELLS DO NOT NAME THE STRUCTURE AT ALL. Over nine findings, in each language's own words:
     en 24 of 3550 (0.7%)   es 29 of 2414 (1.2%)   tr 41 of 1277 (3.2%)
     nl  7 of  428 (1.6%)   el 11 of  750 (1.5%)
   The silence is the REPORT's, not the reader's. A knee report discusses what was asked about; there is
   nothing in the text for any reader, lexicon or model, to mine for a finding never mentioned.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT — the refutation is finding-shaped, not global. Broadening the English patterns
moves exactly two findings: Baker's names a cyst in 236 of its 765 UNK cells (30.8%), Contusion in 55 of
342 (16.1%). Synovitis manages 25 of 1424 (1.8%), Effusion 0 of 84. A global normality statement that
could license an absent call covers 84 of 1768 English studies (4.8%). Total recoverable: roughly 5-10%
of UNK cells, i.e. 1-3% of the label matrix moving ONE rung. Cannot plausibly deliver 1.5%. The full
sweep (3-6 card hours) is NOT armed.

WHAT REPLACES IT. core/data/labels/report_reader.py is built, tested and gate-clean, and it is a PROBE
rather than a pipeline. The open question the sweep could not answer cheaply is whether a model reads the
72.7% of cells the lexicon DID read any better — finding_calibration already measures the lexicon
over-calling Contusion (44.4% agreement on its positives) and missing Synovitis. `--annotated` grades only
the 58 image-annotated studies, which is minutes of card, not hours, and is the only place a reader can be
checked against pixels. If the model beats the lexicon on those 696 cells, the sweep earns its hours; if
not, the label-reading axis closes for the price of a coffee.

Also corrected here: the 0.28 rung is NOT an unpriced guess. Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT prices it at
13.6% positive over 177 annotated cells, and --calibrated-targets already trains those cells there. The
champion's own 0.938->0.941 came through that path.
UNK-MASKING VARIANT IS DEAD — 2026-09-20, 0 card, 0 slots. I proposed masking the 14,445 UNK cells out of the LOSS (not filling them), on the reading that the 0.28 rung binarises to NEGATIVE in ruler and loss, and that class B carries 2.7x class C's UNK mass (36.8% vs 13.4%). Masking them out of the RULER lifted six class-B columns: MCL +0.0125, Lateral OA +0.0188, PF OA +0.0170, Baker's +0.0193, Fracture +0.0179, Medial OA +0.0055.

THAT LIFT WAS A DENOMINATOR ARTEFACT AND THE RUNG IS CORRECT. ReaderAgreement.silence on the 684 annotated cells: 177 silent (25.9%), the radiologist calls 13.6% of them positive. Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT prices the 0.28 rung at exactly 13.6%. The rung was FITTED to this number; 0.28 is a calibrated soft negative, not an assertion-free placeholder. Per column the three class-B holes I claimed would lift carry ZERO recoverable positives: MCL 6 silent / 0 hidden, Lateral OA 22 / 0, Medial OA 14 / 0. Dropping mostly-negative cells shrinks the population and moves AUC without revealing skill.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT: the silence bound itself is unchanged (a perfect filler fixes at most 24 cells against 108 over-calls), and Synovitis/Fracture still hold 14/4 of those 24. Nothing here touches the over-call lane or the aggregation lane.

title: Risk register: our label table is third-party LLM-derived, and a host verdict on that is pending
description:
AUDITED 2026-08-26 17:10Z after Kaggle topic 733652 surfaced the question. Result: WE ARE CLEAN ON THE
ACT, exposed only second-hand, and the exposure is shared with much of the field.

WHAT THE RULE SAYS AND WHO IS ARGUING ABOUT IT. Topic 733652 asks whether sending competition report
text to a commercial LLM API (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google) to derive labels is permitted. Two participants
read Section 4.b Data Security as forbidding it: participants agree not to "transmit, duplicate,
publish, redistribute or otherwise provide or make available the Competition Data to any party not
participating in the Competition", and a commercial API provider is such a party. Their reading does
not depend on submission-time behaviour - the transmission itself is the violation. A third participant
notes the obvious consequence: "label datasets derived using GPT have been publicly shared on the
platform ... I don't see how the competition hosts or Kaggle staff could realistically make that
determination for any given dataset." NO HOST VERDICT YET; the thread's last line is "any verdict on
any of this? :)".

WHAT WE ACTUALLY DID, verified rather than assumed. A grep over the whole tree for openai / anthropic. /
api.openai / generativelanguage / rsna_llm_key / requests.post / httpx returns ZERO hits in core/ and
kneemri/ - the only matches are string constants inside external/sdlc-scaffold's own network-detector
(devtools/hygiene/small.py NETWORK_CHAINS). There is no LLM-calling code in this repo and there never
was. The path ~/.config/rsna_llm_key was documented once and verified NOT to exist.

Our supervision is the file report_labels_v2.csv, fetched by the step in comp/README.md:

    kaggle datasets download pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels -p "<processed>/labels" --unzip

i.e. a PUBLIC KAGGLE DATASET published by another participant. We consumed a shared artifact; we did not
transmit competition data anywhere. The blended tables (blend_three_v1, merged_blend_v1) are built by
core/data/labels/table_blend.py from public tables, and that module already tracks a LEAKED tuple
(report_labels_v5, train_labels_final, train_targets_soft) for a different hazard.

THE RESIDUAL RISK, not zero. If the host rules that datasets derived via commercial LLM APIs are
tainted, every table in the field is affected including ours, and a winners' review could reach it.
Mitigations if that lands, in cost order:
  1. table_blend already composes multiple public tables; drop any table the host names and refit.
  2. The 58 studies carrying train.csv annotations are untainted ground truth, and --hold-annotations
     already exercises that ruler - it is a fallback ruler, not a fallback trainer.
  3. A locally-run open-weights multilingual labeller (Qwen-class) over the reports is explicitly the
     branch BOTH participants agree is permitted: "(b) looks fine ... internet-off only applies to the
     submission notebook, so offline label generation during development isn't restricted". We have a
     5090 and the reports are in nine languages. That is a real, permitted, in-house route to a label
     table we OWN - and it is the only one that would survive any ruling. It is also, separately from
     the compliance question, the only untried supervision lever of a different KIND left on the board.

ACTION NOW: none required for compliance. Watch topic 733652 for a host verdict via discussion_read. Do
NOT rebuild labels speculatively - our tables are permitted under every reading currently on the record.

title: blend labels and hold-annotations are SUPERADDITIVE: +0.0034 and +0.0004 alone, +0.0073 together
description:
Measured 2026-08-26T16:53Z from blendhold, which finished at 16:52 and so postdates 'the label-table axis is exhausted' (2026-08-26). One ruler, run_comparison against native224_s2026 = 0.8502 at e9, a clean 2x2:

                 default labels    blend_three_v1
  no hold-annot      0.8502          +0.0034
  hold-annot         +0.0004         +0.0073

blendlabels vs native224 is 'matched on every option both runs recorded' -- fully clean. blendhold vs holdannot is a pure READER contrast (+0.0069 mean, focal +0.0090, MCL +0.0291* Lateral Meniscus +0.0235* Lateral OA +0.0137*).

THE POINT. Additive prediction is 0.0038; actual is 0.0073. Interaction +0.0035. The blend-label effect is measured TWICE with the same sign (+0.0034 without hold, +0.0069 with), which is the replication the interpretation did not have -- it bounded the lane on blendlabels' +0.0034 alone and called it 'below the 0.0062 floor'. The BEST CELL is +0.0073, which is above the floor. That does not overturn its conclusion (recomposing the blend is still not a lever, and the gold-ruler ranking still stands); it says the lane is bigger than the one cell it was bounded on.

THE UNTRIED ARM. blendsix dosed '--scheme merged --labels $MERGED_BLEND' onto six seats with NO --hold-annotations. The superadditive cell has never been run at seat scale.

PRICE, stated before anyone runs it. ~7h wall behind calibsix (which owns the card to ~01:25Z), so it would land ~08:30Z 2026-08-27, zero slots. Gain if the +0.0039 hold-on-blend increment transfers, at uniform pass-through 1.26-1.47: +0.0049 to +0.0057 offline ensemble = +0.008 to +0.010 board at transfer 1.72, i.e. 0.939 -> 0.947-0.949. Odds it transfers: ~0.3, because the +0.0039 is single-seed at 224px/12-slices/canonical while blendsix's seats are merged-scheme 336, and a label-side INTERACTION transferring across geometry is a stronger assumption than a main effect transferring. Expected value ~+0.003 board for 7h.

THIS IS A KNOB, NOT THE ROUTE TO 0.950. 0.939 -> 0.950 needs +0.011 board = +0.0064 offline. Even the optimistic end of this arm lands short, and its central estimate is a third of the way. It should be argued for on ratio against whatever else wants the card after calibsix, not sold as the target.

Related: knee-ym3z (label-table intervals), knee-9vgx (closed), interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_the-label-table-axis-is-exhausted.md

title: Geometry axis is closed on our data: neither resolution nor slice depth is a lever
description:
The forum names 'crop geometry, resolution and slice selection' as the paying axis. Both halves read closed here, measured 2026-08-26T16:49Z at zero slots and zero GPU.

RESOLUTION. run_comparison --control base224_s2026 --arms base_dense_s2026: MEAN +0.0003, by structure scale focal -0.0027 regional +0.0046. CAVEAT and it is the important one: that pair moves five knobs at once (batch 12->6, slices 12->20, image_size 224->336, band_low 0.2->0.1, band_high 0.8->0.9), so it is NOT a clean resolution contrast. What it does establish is a JOINT bound: a 2.25x pixel budget plus a wider band plus more slices, together, moved the mean by +0.0003. A clean 336->448 arm inherits that prior, so it is not worth a 32-minute slot-free arm ahead of anything else on the queue.

SLICE DEPTH. grep over experiments/arms/*.sh: 66x --slices 20, 36x --slices 12, 1x --slices 16. We have never gone above 20. But core/data/corpus/cache_flags.py declares --slices as 'slices per slot the cache holds' and it names the cache file, so >20 is a full cache rebuild (~26 GB, the band224 cache is the size reference), not a free flag. Price: 12->20 bought +0.0036 focal / -0.0013 mean, so 20->28 extrapolates to about +0.002 for a rebuild. Below the 1.5% bar and below the 0.0062 three-seed noise floor.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO ARMS. The forum sweep bead argues the next NEW arm should be model-side rather than label-side, because we do not beat our teacher (labels 0.8658 vs model 0.8392 over 696 cells). Geometry was the obvious model-side candidate. It is now priced and it is small. The remaining model-side candidates are architecture and objective, not input geometry.

Does NOT close: crop_mm. crop80_span is a real member and crop geometry was not tested here.

title: reader_agreement --labels is blind to a blended table: it reads __verdict, which blending never writes
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-26. Ran `core.data.labels.reader_agreement --labels X` over all nine tables in processed/labels/. Every one printed BYTE-IDENTICAL output: '684 annotated cells, 311 called positive', '140 wrong of 684 cells over 57 studies', the same per-language rates, the same graded/hedged block.

The flag DOES land (a nonexistent path raises FileNotFoundError). The cause is that `cells()` merges only the `__verdict` columns (YES/NO/UNK strings), while `table_blend` blends the NUMERIC column and carries `__conf` and the verdicts over from the base untouched. So a blend is, to this tool, its base table.

The tables are NOT the same over those studies: against report_labels_v2 on the 57 annotated studies, blend_three_v1 / blend_four / merged_blend_v1 flip 33 of 684 cells across 0.5, blend_nolixin 13, blend_hybrid 7; and macro AUC against the radiologist gold moves 0.8700 -> 0.8955 / 0.8953 / 0.8955 / 0.8935 / 0.8978. (report_labels_v2 at 0.8700 reproduces the public benchmark's published 0.870 for that table exactly, which is the ruler validating itself.)

THE TRAP IS THAT IT READS AS A RESULT: 'every blend agrees with the radiologist exactly as well as v2 does' is what the output says, and it is false. Nothing is wrong with the number it prints — it is a true statement about VERDICTS — the defect is that the flag invites a question the tool cannot answer.

FIX: refuse a table whose `__verdict` columns are identical to the default's while its numeric columns are not, naming table_separation / supervision_gap as the tool that scores a table's numeric column. A docstring line alone is weaker but is the minimum.

NOT A NEW FINDING ABOUT LABELS: the lane is already settled and small — see the blendlabels ledger row (+0.0034 mean, +0.0070 on the six label-bottlenecked findings, both at or under the 0.0062 floor) and table_blend's own docstring, which prices this ruler at +/-0.008 over 58 studies and shows every pairwise blend interval covering zero.

title: 224 px is FREE and we never used it as one - it buys 3x the arms per hour, which is what an unknown-tweak search needs
description:
THE MEASUREMENT IS ALREADY OURS, from the ledger, 2026-08-25 'native224: the resolution axis is flat, and
that is a THROUGHPUT result':

  lr4e-5_ws (control, 336 px)   0.8525   ~290 s/epoch   17997 MiB
  native224                     0.8502     94 s/epoch    8124 MiB

-0.0023 against a 0.0062 floor - flat - and convergence_check does not flag it (best epoch 7, 8-11
declining), so it is the arm's real number, not a truncation floor.

WHAT WE DID WITH THAT. Nothing. Every arm since has run at 336 or 392. The ledger wrote 'THROUGHPUT
result' in its own title and then the queue kept paying 3.1x per epoch for a number inside the noise.

WHY IT MATTERS TODAY AND NOT AS A CURIOSITY. knee-rh4t read ten self-reported single-model scores off
forum topic 735304: the two best, 0.942 and 0.938, are both at 224 px and one is a SINGLE FOLD. The
poster who reached 0.942 got there from 0.934 with unnamed 'tweaks' and stayed at 224 throughout. So the
lever is a recipe/training tweak nobody has named, and the only way to find an unnamed tweak is to try
many. At 336 a 12-epoch arm is ~40 min; at 224 it is ~19. Over the ~11.5 h of card left after
raddino_dense ends (~12:25Z) that is roughly 35 attempts instead of 17.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. Not a proposal to run arms concurrently. card_check blocks on TWO OF OURS for a
measured reason - contention once stretched one member from 3 min to 11 and cost the READING, not just
the time. The card stays serial; 224 buys attempts through speed alone.

WHAT STAYS AT 336. The four queued arms - band_dense_hold, calib_dense_hold, ema_dense, stack_dense - are
single-variable measurements against band_dense_hold at the dense corner, each with a pre-registered
prediction. Moving them to 224 breaks the control and throws away the pre-registration. They run as
written. This is about everything AFTER them.

WHAT SHOULD RUN AT 224. Every exploratory arm whose question is 'does this recipe change move the
number' - the search for the unnamed tweak, and the tissue-centre cache test (knee-b96p), which needs a
cache rebuild and should rebuild the cheap one.

title: Free-VRAM gate parked a 20-slice arm for an hour on an IDLE card
description:
wait_for_free_card compared the recipe's derived reservation against nvidia-smi memory.free. Measured 2026-08-26 08:41Z: free 29981 MiB against a derived 29992 for the shipped 20-slice recipe — 11 MiB short — with ZERO compute processes on the device. This card keeps ~2.6 GB in window-manager and browser clients that show up in memory.free and never release, so for the shipped recipe the free-VRAM test cannot pass on an idle card; the arm parks the full FOREIGN_WAITS hour and then starts anyway, having prevented no paging and spent an hour of a granted day.

Fix (landed): compute_tenants() parses the driver's plain report for Type == C exactly, the same field and the same exactness kneemri.experiments.card_check documents (--query-compute-apps enumerates 31 clients here and answers [N/A] for every memory figure). The gate returns immediately when no process computes, and keeps the free-VRAM wait for when one does. Mechanism match: PCIe paging comes from another TRAINER holding gigabytes, not from a compositor's framebuffer.

Cost of the defect before the fix: one hour per launch of the shipped recipe, silent unless the log was read within the first minute.
close_reason: fixed in experiments/lib.sh: compute_tenants() short-circuits the free-VRAM wait on an idle card

title: 224px buys 2.25x the experiments and rivals score their best singles there
description: Forum topic 735304: the two highest self-reported 5-fold singles are 0.929 @224px and 0.926 @336px, and the single best reported is 0.942 @224px. We train everything at 336. Our own 224 arms on the plateau read holdout 0.8490 (native224_long) and 0.8505 (mixup224_long) against 336 members at 0.8525-0.8598, so 224 is SLIGHTLY WORSE on our ruler - about 0.005, inside the 0.0062 paired floor. That is not a score lever and this bead does not claim one. It is a THROUGHPUT lever: 224 is 2.25x fewer pixels, and our measured 224 epoch time is ~91s against ~297-361s for a 336 merged epoch. At a fixed card budget that is roughly 2.25-3x the experiments per hour on an axis where four 224 arms have now read flat against each other, i.e. where the recipe is insensitive. PROPOSAL, not yet a plan: run METHOD SEARCH at 224 and only the final fit at 336. Blocked on one thing - the merged corpus is decoded at 336 only (images_336px_12sl_merged.npy, 41.8GB); a 224 merged cache would cost ~19GB and an unmeasured decode over 5,143 studies, against 425GB free. Price that before adopting.
notes:
UNBLOCKED 2026-08-26 02:06Z, and the blocker was mispriced. The bead said a 224 merged cache needs ~19 GB plus an unmeasured decode over 5,143 studies. Actual cost: 90 seconds. images_224px_12sl.npy already existed (15.9 GB, 2026-08-25), so only rijeka needed decoding at 224 (736 studies, <60 s) and build_merged is a concatenation. images_224px_12sl_merged.npy is on disk, (5143, 6, 12, 224, 224) uint8, 18.6 GB, 0 studies with no slot. Re-verified 02:47Z: its index holds 5,143 studies in byte-identical order to the 336 index, and the 336 array is exactly (336/224)^2 = 2.25x its size, so it is the same geometry at lower resolution and not a partial decode.

WHAT IT IS FOR, unchanged and worth restating because the cheap price invites the wrong use: EXPERIMENTS, not members. 224 is for the arms that decide WHERE to look, at ~110 s/epoch against ~361. blendsix stays at 336.

CORRECTED 02:50Z. The previous note closed with 'the point estimate is ~0.005 offline WORSE and board_transfer turns that into ~0.009 board. A 224 roster would ship ~0.009 below a 336 one.' Both halves are unsound and the same error appears in 2026-08-26_the-deficit-is-the-member.md, where it is now corrected. The slope used was +1.82, quoted from prose; board_transfer fits +1.72 over the complete entry set board_check recovered on 2026-08-25. And the fit is built entirely on entries at or below 0.933, so applying it to a 0.939 champion is an extrapolation outside its own support. The defensible statement is the offline one and only it: 224 is 0.005 worse on our ruler, inside the 0.0062 paired floor, and UNTESTED AT SERVING. It is not shown to be safe there and it is not shown to cost 0.009 either. Three of the four strongest singles on forum topic 735304 are at 224, which is a reason to keep the question open rather than to reopen it with a card.

title: Forum consensus 2026-08-25: labels are the bottleneck, and a public benchmark now prices every report-label table
description:
Two threads read live 2026-08-26T01:17Z. Recording the NUMBERS, not the mood.

TOPIC 737454 — the first public benchmark of report-label tables against the 58 radiologist-annotated studies (notebook: kaggle.com/code/starkhushi/rsna-knee-which-report-labels-should-you-train-on):
  macro AUC vs radiologists — stevenleehans v4 blend 0.893, stevenleehans v2 0.887, pilkwang report_labels_v2 0.870
  'Averaging two independent tables beats either alone on several labels'
  per-label spread is huge: ACL ~0.99, Synovitis ~0.79, and only ~16% of reports mention synovitis in ANY of the nine languages, so that label is largely inferred

WHAT THAT CONFIRMS FOR US. blendlabels already composes tables and measured +0.0034 mean / +0.0070 on its own label-bottlenecked six, with MCL +0.0239. The forum arrived at the same mechanism independently and prices the ceiling: a table at 0.87-0.89 against gold is the TEACHER, and a per-label score at or above it is label-limited rather than model-limited. Synovitis at 0.79 is the clearest case.

TOPIC 735826 — 'what is the real bottleneck', 9 replies from active participants. The consensus is A (report-derived label quality) with B (crop geometry / slice selection) second, and explicitly NOT C (backbone capacity). One participant reports DINOv2-small with diagnosis-specific slot attention scoring WORSE than a ResNet34 control on OOF BCE (0.674 vs 0.664) with the CPU cache and labels held fixed. Another: 'the entire competition is the label making'; the hosts have said the test labels were NOT derived from the reports.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE. Our own board says the same thing from the other side: seven entries at 0.936-0.937 with count, member identity, fold status, regularisation, encoder family and architecture family each moved alone. We have been reading that as 'the ensemble axis is closed'; the forum's independent read is that the axis was never where the headroom is. The remaining lever above the 1.5% bar is the four weak labels (Lateral Meniscus 0.7981, PF OA 0.8165, MCL 0.8166, Lateral OA 0.8215; lifting them to 0.87 is +0.0189), and this says to attack them through SUPERVISION, not through the trunk.

CAUTION ON THE DENOMINATOR: 58 studies, and our own severity_boundary tool found 59.9% of the corpus is not English, so any per-label number quoted from that benchmark rests on a few dozen pairs at most. Treat the ORDERING as the finding and not the values.

RELATED: knee-twtr (merged_blend), the severity_boundary interpretation 2026-08-25_effusion-threshold-ruler.md, which measured the same label-noise mechanism on our own copy of the 58.
notes:
SECOND READ 2026-08-26 12:0xZ — discussion_read --live, 60 topics, three dumped in full. The 2026-08-25
consensus is unchanged and now has numbers attached. What is NEW:

RIVAL SINGLE-MODEL NUMBERS, and they beat our best member by a wide margin. A poster reports a single
model moving 0.934 -> 0.942 at 224 px. Our best SINGLE member on the board is soloseat 0.925; our
champion 0.939 is a SIX-member blend. So the frontier's ONE model is at our blend's score. That reframes
the ensemble lane: we are buying with diversity what they get from one fit, which means our per-member
ceiling is the gap, not our combining rule (which the ledger already shows saturated within 0.0019).

224 > 336 CONFIRMED EXTERNALLY. The same poster reports 0.929 @ 224 beating 0.926 @ 336. That is an
independent reproduction of our native224 (0.8502) vs 336 (0.8525) read, which we called flat inside the
0.0062 floor. Two independent corpora agreeing that the resolution axis is flat closes it harder than our
own paired arm did, and the 3x throughput refund is now safe to spend anywhere.

THEIR TRANSFER IS ~ZERO AND OURS IS +0.075. One poster: "OOF AUC = LB AUC within noise, 0.92". Ours is
proxy 0.85 -> board 0.925+, a +1.72 compression fit over 58 submissions. That is not a contradiction to
resolve by adjusting our constant — it means their holdout denominator is not ours. Their OOF is scored
on the SAME label kind the board uses; ours is scored on report-derived labels while the board is
image-read consensus. The transfer constant IS the ruler gap, which is exactly the +0.045 that
holdannot_s2026 measured directly (0.8487 report vs 0.8932 annotated). Do not "fix" the transfer; it is
carrying real information about the label mismatch.

BACKBONE CAPACITY IS NOT THE LEVER, measured by a rival. A ResNet34 control (OOF BCE 0.664) BEAT
DINOv2-small (0.674). Consistent with our own raddino -0.040 and vjepa 0.8343: this task does not reward
a bigger or fancier encoder. Stop pricing backbone swaps as improvements.

THE HOSTS DID NOT START FROM THE REPORTS. Sharpest post in 735826: "the entire competition is the label
making... According to comments from the hosts those folks did not use the reports as a starting point."
If true this is the single most load-bearing external fact of the window, because it says the target is
NOT a denoised version of our report table — it is an independently produced image read. Treat as a
claim from a forum post, not a host statement; but it is the same conclusion our own +0.045 ruler gap
reaches from measurement, and two independent routes to it is why the label-side lane (band_dense_hold ->
calib_dense_hold, dual-ruler) is the right thing on the card.

~7 TRAINING STUDIES CARRY BOTH KNEES IN ONE DICOM (topic 735639, posted today). Small enough to be a
curiosity at 7/4406, but it is a data DEFECT we have never checked for on our side, and a both-knees
volume feeds the model a contralateral joint as if it were the target. Worth one CPU pass over the
corpus, never a card.
PRICE, written 2026-08-27T16:50Z, before the arm runs.

COST. Five members at --fold -1 over the 12sl/0.2-0.8 merged cache, ~1.2 h each on the measured 361 s/epoch x 12 = ~6 h of card that is otherwise IDLE (contrast_dense frees it ~17:16Z and nothing is queued behind it), plus the LAST submission slot of the day, plus a kit rebuild. Realistic finish: four members by ~22:05Z, the fifth ~23:15Z against a ~23:30Z submission. The arm runs blend_base LAST deliberately - it is the slowest (batch 6, variant base) and the least seat-matched, so a four-member finish drops the right one.

GAIN, by precedent and by arithmetic. The uniform-lift move has been run once on this board and it worked: calibsix took blendseat's six seats and applied ONE flag (--calibrated-targets) to five of them, 0.939 -> 0.941, +0.002. This is the identical move on the other flag with a measured positive. The two flags are the same SIZE offline - calibration +0.0038 mean solo, blend +0.0034 mean solo - so the calibsix realisation is the honest predictor, not the 1.0-pass-through arithmetic (+0.0034 x board_transfer 2.14 = +0.007) which calibsix already over-predicted by 3x.

P(clears the 1.5% house bar, i.e. >= 0.956): ~2%.
P(a real tick, >= +0.002, i.e. >= 0.943): ~35%.
P(flat or down, 0.936-0.942): ~65%. That is the arm's own modal band and its pre-registration says so.

WHY IT IS STILL THE RIGHT SLOT. An unspent slot scores 0 and expires at 00:00 UTC. The alternative use is a re-submit of a known 0.941, which returns exactly 0.941 - expected gain zero, with certainty. Any bet with positive probability of a tick beats holding, and this is the only untried move whose PRECEDENT on this exact board is positive. It is also the only axis our board and the forum consensus (topic 735826, 9 replies: labels first, geometry second, explicitly NOT backbone) point at from opposite directions.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED TODAY, independently. supervision_gap on the gold 58 splits the twelve findings six-and-six: the LABELS are the weak half on Lateral Meniscus, ACL, MCL, Medial Meniscus, PF OA and Lateral OA. Those are exactly the findings blendlabels lifted by +0.0070. This arm is aimed at a bottleneck that has now been measured on our own copy of the gold studies, not inferred from a forum thread.

RISK THE ARM NAMES ITSELF, unchanged: the harmonised 12sl/0.2-0.8 geometry loses the champion's 12/20-slice spread. If this reads <= 0.935, member_distance over the five answers that with no card before the blend supervision is indicted.

arm_check 2026-08-27T16:48Z: 5 arms checked, 0 refused, 0 uncached. The only finding was this missing price.
PRICE: ~6 h of otherwise-idle card (five members at ~1.2 h) plus the day's last submission slot, against a precedent of +0.002 board for the identical uniform-flag move (blendseat 0.939 -> calibsix 0.941). P(clears 1.5%) ~2%. P(>= +0.002) ~35%. P(flat or down) ~65%, which is the arm's own modal band. Justified because an unspent slot scores 0 with certainty and the card is free; see the full pricing note above.
ARM RETRACTED 2026-08-27T16:56Z, BEFORE IT RAN, and the price above is void.

WHAT I MISSED AND HOW. I priced blendsix as an untried uniform-flag lift by precedent against calibsix. It is not untried. FOUR of its five members already exist on disk - blend_ws.pt, blend_calib.pt, blend_ladder.pt, blend_through.pt, all written 2026-08-26 - and comp/members.roster has carried them since, at lines 435-437, annotated 'dose-3 seat'. The arm's own header says 'this arm builds five more of them' because it was written before they were built; the header is a plan, not a state, and I read it as a state.

AND THE DOSE IS ALREADY MEASURED FLAT. blendthree_v1 served final_ws_e12 / blend_calib / blend_ladder / merged_blend_s2026 / blend_ws / through_dense_ff - FOUR blend seats out of six - and scored 0.939. blendseat_v1 served ONE blend seat and scored 0.939. Dose one to dose four is +0.000. The arm's own pre-registration named 0.936-0.939 as 'FLAT: six blend seats buy what one bought, which is nothing measurable', and that band has already been read at dose four.

WHAT RUNNING IT WOULD HAVE COST. Not just six idle card-hours and the day's last slot on a measured null - run_train writes to $PROCESSED/blend_*.pt, so it would have OVERWRITTEN four members that blendthree_v1's 0.939 board row depends on being reproducible. champion_check guards the pinned entry's members; nothing guards a non-champion entry's.

THE RULE THIS BREAKS is the repo's own: audit -> file -> plan -> work, where AUDIT means reading the actual files rather than greps about them. I read the arm's header and the bead, and neither knew about a build that happened after both were written. The one artefact that DID know was the roster, and an  would have answered it in one call. Before any arm is queued from now on: list the checkpoints it declares as --out, not just the arm text.

WHAT THE DOSE CURVE ACTUALLY LEAVES OPEN. Blend and calibration have never been composed on the same seat at roster scale. Only two members carry both flags (blend_calib, merged_blend_cf); blendthree's other blend seats are uncalibrated and calibsix's other calibrated seats are unblended. That cross is untried - but both flags reshape the same soft-target distribution, so the prior is that they are one lever rather than two, and the compose is sub-additive. Not priced as worth the slot on that reading; recorded so it is not re-discovered as novel a third time.

title: Every member of the pinned champion is UNVERIFIED by witness_check, and cannot be made otherwise
description:
witness_check swept all 41 roster members on CPU (logs/witness_full.log, 2026-08-26). Result:

  38 ok
  1  REFUSED - vjepa_warm_s2026, max|diff| 0.0456 against a 0.0312 tolerance, 3 of 12 labels carry it: inference reads that member differently than training did. It is seated in kneemri-farseat (already scored 0.936) and nowhere else; it is under a standing do-not-rebuild instruction, so this is a record, not a live risk.
  6  UNVERIFIED - final_ws_e12, calib_span_ff, grade_ladder_ff, through_dense_ff, lr4e-5_ws_ff, base_dense_ff.

Those six UNVERIFIED members are EXACTLY the six in comp/champion.json - the votefit entry that scored 0.938 and held rank 51 of 2410 (read 2026-08-26). So the check written to catch 'inference reads this member differently than training did', which found three defects on its first use, has never been able to speak about the entry we actually ship.

WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE FIXED. A witness is recorded DURING training; these members predate the 2026-08-24 witness or were published, so there is no stored tensor to compare against. Producing one means refitting all six at --fold -1, which is the ~7 h all-data train the ledger already declined on dose-response grounds, for zero expected board movement. The honest position is that the champion's serving path is unverified by this instrument and will stay that way.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, and it is cheap: every member fitted from now on carries a witness, so the gap closes by succession rather than by a refit. This bead exists so nobody spends a card on the refit believing it is the cheap option, and so the champion's 'EVERY SHIPPED MEMBER IS FINGERPRINT-CHECKED AND WITNESS-CHECKED' principle is read with the correction that its own six are not.
notes:
RE-COUNTED AGAINST THE CURRENT PIN 2026-09-04T04:06Z, which this bead's own stale-premise note asked for. THE FINDING SHRANK BY FIVE SIXTHS.

raptorweight_v1's six seats are final_ws_cf, calib_span_ff, grade_ladder_cf, merged_blend_cf,
lr4e-5_ws_cf, through_dense_cf. Of those, exactly ONE - calib_span_ff - is witnessless. The other five
are _cf members and carry witnesses. So the headline 'every member of the pinned champion is
UNVERIFIED' was true of votefit_v1 and is 1-of-6 true of raptorweight_v1: the pin moved from an
all-fold--1 six to five fold-0 members plus one all-data seat, and it carried the coverage with it.

Package-wide the count is 8 witnessless of 120 members (93% coverage): res392_ws_s2026 and
deep24_s2026 (fold-0, predate the 2026-08-24 witness) plus final_ws_e12, calib_span_ff,
grade_ladder_ff, through_dense_ff, lr4e-5_ws_ff, base_dense_ff (all --fold -1).

AND THE 'CANNOT BE MADE OTHERWISE' IN THE TITLE IS WRONG, which matters more than the count. This bead
argues a witness needs a holdout and therefore a --fold -1 member can never carry one, so the only
route is a ~7 h refit that the ledger already declined. Both halves of that follow from treating the
witness as a SCORE. It is not one. It is a fingerprint that the serving path re-derives the training
path's predictions to within a precision-derived bound, and no label is consulted anywhere in it -
witness_check compares recorded predictions against re-derived predictions, never against truth. Eight
studies from an all-data member's own TRAIN set fingerprint it exactly as well, leak nothing, and cost
one forward pass at fit time.

So the succession fix this bead recommends is right but incomplete: as written, every future --fold -1
member reproduces the hole. The change is in 'Fitting.witnessed' - take the witness studies from the
holdout when there is one and from train when there is not - and it would have covered the champion
seat that is open today. Note what it does NOT recover: res392_ws_s2026 and deep24_s2026 predate the
witness entirely, so nothing exists to compare against at any cost, and only a refit produces one.

Related: the eight cache-less members were closed separately in knee-wbhjw (witness shards, commit
e0a83abc, 8 ok / 0 refused on cpu). knee-mz9r0 was filed this morning re-discovering this bead and is
closed as a duplicate; its one novel item is the train-set-witness argument above.

title: board_check refuses a submission that is still scoring
description: board_check --live counted every live ref absent from comp/board.jsonl as 'scored and is recorded NOWHERE', including one Kaggle had not finished scoring. Such an entry CANNOT be recorded (it carries no board number), so the gate went red for ~40 minutes after every submission for a reason nobody could act on - which is how a gate teaches its reader to ignore it. Split: unrecorded() now covers only refs with a score (still a refusal); pending() covers refs still scoring and is logged as a warning that does not exit 1.

title: kaggle datasets version mangles an absolute Windows path, and the workaround bypassed push.sh
description:
Hit twice at 23:35Z and 23:37Z pushing the kit.

FAILURE. 'kaggle datasets version -p D:/data/volumetric/mri/processed/rsna_knee_abnormality/kit' dies with

  [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
  'C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Temp\.kaggle/uploads\D_/data/volumetric/.../kit_<file>.json'

The CLI builds a per-file temp descriptor by pasting the SOURCE path under its uploads directory, and
the drive letter becomes the directory component 'D_'. That parent is never created, so every file's
descriptor write fails. It fails per FILE, after printing 'Starting upload for file ...', so the log
reads as a partial upload rather than as a path bug.

WORKAROUND THAT WORKS: cd to the dataset's parent and pass a RELATIVE path ('-p ./kit'). No drive
letter, no mangling. Pushed successfully on the retry.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE BUG. comp/push.sh says of itself: 'the ONE way anything reaches
Kaggle from here', and it exists because a kernel run was once lost to a members version pushed while
the kit lagged the repo -- the guarded path was the one nobody ran. I then ran the raw CLI twice
instead of push.sh, which is the same mistake the script was written to prevent. No damage this time
only because kit_check had been run clean immediately before, by hand.

FIX, in push.sh rather than in a habit: resolve the target to a path relative to the cd it already
does (it already resolves TARGET before the cd, for a related reason), so the drive letter never
reaches the CLI. Then the guarded path is also the only one that works on this machine, and the
temptation to reach past it disappears.

title: arm_check --smoke does not reap the trainer it starts when the smoke times out
description:
THE HALF OF 2026-08-25's SMOKE DEFECT THAT IS NOT FIXED. The memory gate is now in (`ArmSmoke.room` /
`ArmSmoke.reserves` refuse an arm whose derived reservation exceeds what the driver reports free, and
report it as NO ROOM rather than BROKEN). That prevents the situation. It does not fix the second thing
that went wrong once the situation existed.

WHAT HAPPENED. The 28.26 GB smoke could not allocate, sat the full 600 s bound, and `_subprocess` returned
TIMED_OUT — and the trainer stayed RESIDENT at 16.4 GB until it was killed by hand. `subprocess.run(timeout=)`
does kill on expiry, so the direct child should have died; the resident process was therefore either a
grandchild (dataloader workers, or the CUDA context's own) or a child that TerminateProcess did not reach
through the tree. THIS IS A WINDOWS-SHAPED BUG and the guess above is a guess — nobody has looked.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS WITH THE GATE IN. The gate only refuses arms it can PRICE. `reserves` derives 0 for a
recipe whose slices are unknown and for flags the parser rejects, and those arms are deliberately let
through; a timeout on one of them leaves the same orphan. And a timeout has causes other than memory.

BEFORE FIXING, MEASURE RATHER THAN ASSUME: run one smoke with a deliberately tiny bound, and check the
process table AND `nvidia-smi` after `_subprocess` returns. If a grandchild survives, the fix is a process
GROUP (`CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` on Windows / `start_new_session` on POSIX) plus a group kill in the
except branch, which belongs in `Spawn` rather than in `ArmSmoke` — `Spawn` is the one place that knows
how a child is started here.

Cost: ~20 min, no card, no slot. Priority is P2 and not P1 because the gate removes the common trigger and
the failure is loud (a resident 16 GB process is visible in `card_check`), but it left someone else's run
sharing a card with a dead job for several minutes and that is the kind of cost this project has agreed to
stop paying.

title: Stochastic depth (drop-path) is the second never-run regulariser, and only ONE of mixup's outcomes calls for it
description:
GREP, 2026-08-25: `drop_path|droppath|stochastic_depth|label_smooth` returns ZERO hits across `core/` and
`kneemri/`. Mixup was the first never-run regulariser and is being run tonight (knee-x580). Drop-path is
the second, and label smoothing the third; none has ever been in this repo.

WHY IT IS A CANDIDATE AT ALL. The diagnosis is memorisation: band_dense_long peaked at epoch 6 and slid
-0.0182 to epoch 23 while train loss halved, and knee-jk3 reads a 0.044 generalisation gap at MATCHED train
loss. Stochastic depth is the standard ViT-side answer to exactly that, it is one constructor argument on a
timm trunk, and at 224 px an arm costs 19 min and 8 GB (see the native224 row).

WHY IT IS NOT BEING BUILT TONIGHT, and the rule that decides it. Adding it is a new `TrainingOptions`
field, which fires the same four totality gates mixup did (NOT_IN_CONFIG write-off, an armed recipe,
run_setup's pinned count, trainer's policies dict) — about 30 min of CPU work that the card being busy
would make free. The reason to hold is not cost, it is that THREE OF MIXUP'S FOUR OUTCOMES MAKE IT THE
WRONG FOLLOW-UP:

  mixup peak RISES with dose  -> scale mixup, do not switch regulariser. Drop-path is a distraction.
  mixup peak FLAT, train loss ROSE (aug_long's outcome) -> the perturbation fired and the memorisation did
        not care. Drop-path is ANOTHER perturbation regulariser and has no reason to do better; the
        remaining suspects are supervision volume (knee-ombx) and representation (knee-jk3).
  mixup points SCATTER -> the axis closes on two points; nothing licenses a third perturbation.
  mixup peak FALLS      -> THE ONE CASE THAT CALLS FOR IT. A falling peak says blending the INPUT destroyed
        focal signal, which is a fact about this corpus rather than about regularisation. Drop-path
        perturbs the NETWORK and never touches the pixels or the target, so it attacks the same
        memorisation without the failure mode that just fired. This is the only branch where it is the
        indicated next arm rather than momentum.

PRICE: ~30 min CPU to implement and gate, then 19 min of card, 8124 MiB, control native224 = 0.8502.
P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.10 on its own; its value is as the second independent attack on a diagnosis three runs
agree on. DO NOT START before mixup224 and mixup224_strong have read.

Label smoothing is deliberately NOT proposed alongside it: our targets are already weighted confidences in
[0, 1] rather than binary labels (see objective.py), so smoothing would be smoothing something already
soft, and `calib_span` is the ledger's record of what happens when we remap soft targets without a
per-finding argument (-0.0020, with the prediction inverting).

title: Manifold mixup: the same convex combination at the pooled embedding, and the successor both of mixup_dense's failure modes name
description:
FOLLOW-UP TO knee-x580, filed before its arm ran so the branch is not chosen after seeing the number.

WHAT. Blend at a hidden representation instead of at the pixels — the pooled study embedding, or a random layer as in ROAM. The target blends by the same draw, exactly as in the pixel version. Blend already takes the draw as a VALUE, so the seam is a fourth method on it and the policy object does not change.

WHY IT IS NOT SPECULATIVE. mixup_dense's two failure modes each name this as the successor, for OPPOSITE reasons, which is why the pixel arm runs first and is decisive:
  - peak FALLS -> a convex combination of two knees is not a knee, and the findings here are focal and few-voxel. Manifold mixup never shows the encoder an impossible anatomy.
  - peak FLAT while train loss ROSE (aug_long's outcome) -> the blend fired and the memorisation did not care, i.e. the perturbation never reached the representation that memorises. Manifold mixup applies it there.
Only a CONFIRMED pixel arm makes this unnecessary, and even then alpha and layer are the follow-ups.

PRIOR ART, read 2026-08-25 22:51Z.
