title: KMAR-50K as TRAINING DATA, not as a statistic: ~1100 cross-site knee subjects pseudo-labelled by the champion
description:
THE OWNER'S OWN COMPLAINT, ANSWERED WITH THE ONE CORPUS THAT CLEARS ITS LICENCE. 'not just labels - more, better training data, additional objectives' and 'i would be glad if you could use more data - ive always been all for that and dont know why it never happened.' Every audited corpus has died on licence -- fastMRI on 'or data files derived from', SKM-TEA on the Stanford RUA's 'personal, non-commercial research purposes only' plus 'must not ... create derivative works' (knee-355vh, closed 2026-09-12). KMAR-50K is CC BY 4.0 (Mendeley, DOI 10.17632/xw7mrg7ntg.6): derivatives and commercial use both permitted with attribution. It is the ONLY corpus on this machine that clears, and so far this project has used it for ONE floating-point number (the 0.040 motion residual the ghosting arm is calibrated on). Its pixels have never entered a cache.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON DISK, measured 2026-09-12 18:04Z, not assumed. /d/data/volumetric/mri/raw/kmar50k holds two parts. GroundTruthData_part1 = 700 .nii volumes / 575 distinct subjects / 14 GB; GroundTruthData_part2 = 642 volumes. Planes in part1: sagittal 267, coronal 231, transection (axial) 202 -- MULTI-PLANE, the same three the RSNA competition carries. Geometry read off three headers: (640, 640, 22) and (640, 520, 23) at 0.25-0.27 mm in-plane and 3.5-4.2 mm through-plane, float32. Slab depth 22-23 slices against this project's 12/20-slice cache: compatible without resampling through-plane.

THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS NOT 'MORE DATA' IN THE ABSTRACT. The thing this project measures and cannot move is the DECODE TOLL: a member loses 0.023-0.036 macro AUC when served a second site's decode geometry, and the whole slot_dropout dose-response exists to shave that. Pseudo-labelled cross-site data attacks it at the source rather than through an operator: the champion ensemble labels ~1100 subjects whose decode is NOT ours, and a student trained on 4407 real + ~1100 soft cross-site targets is fitted, for the first time, to a second site's pixels. That is a different lever from every knob in the ledger, which all re-weight the same 4407 studies.

WHY IT IS NOT A LABEL-LAUNDERING NULL. The soft targets carry no information our ensemble does not already have -- what they carry is the ensemble's function EVALUATED ON PIXELS IT WAS NEVER FITTED ON, which is exactly what a distillation gains from and exactly what holdout909 is blind to. The pre-registered ruler is therefore the FOREIGN DECODE (foreign_readout against band_dense_s2026's -0.0361), the same ruler slot_dropout and ghosting are read on, with holdout909 reported alongside as a non-deciding sanity number.

PRICE: ~3.5 h (decode+cache ~1 h CPU, parallel, off-card; one pseudo-label inference pass with the champion six ~0.7 h card; one 12-epoch student ~1.8 h card at 1.25x epoch cost for the enlarged corpus). P(clears +0.0040 on decode_cost vs matched control) ~ 0.35.

FALSIFIABLE BEFORE IT RUNS. >= +0.0040 shallower toll than band_dense_s2026 and the cross-site data lane opens (part2, and then the plane axis). -0.0040..+0.0040 is FLAT and says pseudo-labels carry no cross-site signal our operators do not already synthesise, which retires the lane cheaply. <= -0.0040 says the champion's labels on foreign pixels are WORSE than no labels, which would be a finding about the champion, not about the corpus.

EINSTEIN GATE: grep -ci kmar over experiments/ returns three files and all three are the ghosting operator's calibration (arms/ghosting.sh, after_ghosting.sh, the 2026-09-12 ledger section). No arm has ever trained on these pixels. No board row names them.

BLOCKED ON THE CARD until the ghosting arm lands (~20:55Z). The decode+cache step is CPU-only and can start now.
notes:
EINSTEIN GATE, ANSWERED AGAINST THE SECTION THAT LOOKS LIKE IT CLOSES THIS. experiments/README.md:7411 'The DATA axis closes before it costs a card week -- in-domain knee-MRI pretraining is published as a wash' retires SSL/in-domain PRETRAINING on Zhang et al. (MedIA 2024): the in-domain-over-ImageNet gain runs +0.073 at 80 labelled subjects and -0.005 at 800, and our labelled corpus is ~4,400, five times past the crossing. core/data/corpus/kmar_corpus.py says the same thing in its own header -- 'Using its clean volumes as unlabelled pretraining data is the SSL-as-init path, which this project has now watched collapse five separate times.' THIS LANE IS NOT THAT LANE, and the closing section says so itself in its own What-it-does-NOT-say paragraph: 'It is also not a verdict on external data as LABELLED augmentation, which is a different mechanism and untested here.' Pseudo-labelling is labelled augmentation -- the supervision comes from the champion ensemble, not from a pretext task, and it enters as training targets rather than as an initialisation. The five collapses and Zhang's table are both about what an ENCODER INIT buys before fine-tuning; neither measures what cross-site targets buy during it.

ALSO ON DISK ALREADY, so the build is smaller than the bead priced: core/data/corpus/ carries build_rijeka.py, build_mrnet.py, build_merged.py and merged_cache.py -- a second corpus has been decoded into the trainer's own cache shape before, twice, and kmar_corpus.py already pairs the KMAR volumes and normalises the filename join (disk writes 2020_1_transection_0.0.nii, the cohort table writes ..._0.nii.gz, and a naive stem join matches nothing). So the decode step is a third instance of an existing pattern rather than new machinery. Re-price the decode leg DOWN once build_rijeka.py has been read end to end.

ONE THING THE BEAD GOT WRONG AND IT MATTERS FOR THE RULER: core.data.corpus.foreign_cache is NOT a corpus of new patients. raptor-corpus covers ALL 4,407 of OUR studies and no others -- a different pixel path over the same studies under the same labels, which is what makes decode_cost a clean one-variable shift. KMAR subjects are new PATIENTS, so an arm trained on them is not read by the same instrument in the same sense: foreign_readout still prices its decode toll, but the corpus shift and the decode shift are no longer separated. Say that in the arm's header rather than letting the reading carry an unstated second variable.
2026-09-16 06:58Z — THE 336 MERGED ARM ALREADY RAN. mergedk_labelwise_drop40_long_336_s2026, on disk since 2026-09-13 12:11, 24 epochs complete (metrics.jsonl e0-23, auc flat 0.8591-0.8593 over e21-23, peak e12 — converged, not truncated). Cache images_336px_12sl_mergedk.npy, so 12 slices at 336, labelwise head.

READING, all ledger75 @909 rows:
  labelwise_dense_s2026                    0.8964  e7   12sl/336, OUR corpus, no drop40, short horizon
  mergedk_labelwise_drop40_long_336_s2026  0.8901  e12  12sl/336, +KMAR corpus, +drop40, 24 epochs
  labelwise_dense_drop40_long_s2026        0.9048  e23  20sl/336 champion geometry (NOT matched - depth differs)

The matched pair is the first two: same geometry, same head, same rows. The merged arm carries drop40
AND double the horizon, worth ~+0.0084 together at 224, and still reads -0.0063 BELOW the plain-corpus
control that had neither. Corpus is negative at 336 once the two levers riding with it are credited.

Third independent null on corpus: -0.0012 (224 matched, corpus alone), -0.0006/-0.0011 (mergedk 2x2 seat
deltas, README:16255/:16307), -0.0063 here at 336/labelwise. beta=0.22 predicted +0.0068 for the 1.247x.
beta does not transfer across SITES.

NOT killed: this bead's own mechanism. Its pre-registered ruler is foreign_readout's decode toll and
holdout909 is blind to it by construction. No foreign_readout artefacts exist on disk (find -iname
'*foreign*readout*' at maxdepth 2 returns nothing), so that reading has never been taken. The bead stands
on that axis alone; the training-corpus use of KMAR is spent.

SCHEDULE CONSEQUENCE: 'build the mergedk_336 arm' is cancelled. It was not an arm to write, it was a
result to read, and it sat unpriced for three days.
2026-09-16 22:06Z — THIS IS mergedk's MECHANISM, NOT A NEW ONE, AND IT IS CLOSED ON DOSE. The bead reads as though KMAR-as-pseudo-labelled-training-data is untried. It is not: core/data/corpus/slots.py:KMAR_MERGED_SCHEME is exactly this lane and says so — 'its rows are supervised by kneemri.inference.pseudo_labels — our own champions' pooled belief over all twelve columns, weighted by how much those champions agree'. Three arms have already trained on it (mergedk_corpus, mergedk_drop40_long, mergedk_labelwise_drop40_long_336), and all three read null or negative: corpus alone at 224 is -0.0012 ledger75 / +0.0014 midpoint (the sign flips with the CUT, i.e. null), and the 336 cell is -0.0147 ledger75 against its matched control on a complete 24-epoch run.

THE DOSE ARITHMETIC CLOSES IT WITHOUT ANY RULER. 1,088 rows on 4,407 is 1.247x. beta=0.22 prices +0.0068 at PERFECT labels. The per-column confidences in the pseudo table are Effusion 0.5560 mean / 0.538 p50 (near chance), Baker's 0.6247, Synovitis 0.6547, Contusion 0.6958, Fracture 0.7047; >=0.80 retains 12-37% per column independently, so a row usable across twelve columns is rare. Realistic dose ~20% -> ~+0.0016, inside the 0.0020 board blur, before charging anything for label noise. No ruler recovers a gain the dose cannot contain.

WHAT SURVIVES. The bead's ruler argument is still right and still unspent: foreign_readout prices a decode toll that holdout909 is blind to, and no board row is needed to read it. That is worth keeping as an INSTRUMENT question. It is not worth 3.5 h of card at P 0.35 for a score lever whose mechanism has read null three times on our own holdout and whose ceiling is +0.0016.

WHAT WOULD RE-OPEN IT. Not a re-quote of +0.0099 (knee-g7d5i reconciled that to corpus + slot_dropout 0.40 + 24 epochs, three levers read as one). Either a licensed corpus large enough to matter (~4,400 new studies, which prices +0.0201 offline on the same beta), or pseudo-labels from a source materially more confident than 0.65 mean agreement. Downgrading to P3 rather than closing, because the instrument half is real.

title: transfer_strata prints a ratio with no spread or correlation beside it
description: compression() at transfer_strata.py:233 reports a median board-per-holdout pair ratio per band. Both it and an OLS slope divide by that band's own offline spread, which is the quantity that actually varies across bands (sd 0.0145 Q1 to 0.0079 Q4 while sd(board) is constant at 0.0080 by construction). The reported 1.8x easy-band compression is the 1.84x spread ratio. OLS r is flat-to-noisy at 0.75-0.91 with its minimum at Q4, in the middle. This published a wrong mechanism (SATURATION) in an interpretation file and an experiments/README row on 2026-09-08 09:20Z; retracted 09:37Z. Fix: lines() emits sd(offline), sd(board) and pearson r beside every band's ratio, so a spread ordering can never again be read as a transfer ordering. title: recal_holdannot.sh still lacked --eval-labels; the 0.8964 defect was already ledgered 2026-08-30
description: D189 6 flagged recal_holdannot_s2026 = 0.8964@n909, +0.0279 above the next-best trained solo, as either the best member the project owns or a leak. It is neither: it is a CUT change. recal_holdannot.sh passes --labels report_labels_v3.csv and no --eval-labels, so its holdout truth is the recalibrated table, while every comparable member is scored against LABELS. The v3 re-map sends level 0.68 to 0.378, which crosses the 0.5 midpoint, so cells positive for every other member are negative for this one: 2017 positives across the 12 columns against the canonical 3336. Fewer, more extreme positives is an easier problem. Rescoring the SAME predictions against the canonical holdout truth (studies verified identical to holdannot_s2026): 0.8515, against control holdannot 0.8506. Plus 0.0009 - flat, and squarely in the arms own pre-registered FLAT band (the models were already inverting the miscalibration unsupervised). A sweep of every arm training on a non-canonical table with no --eval-labels found four candidates; only this one is affected. confident224_s2026 truth differs in float values but not in positive set, so its AUC is identical on both (0.8431). confident_span_s2026 and v3labels_dense_s2026 have no holdout npz on disk. FIX: recal_holdannot.sh must carry --eval-labels LABELS like merged3_corpus.sh does; the ledger row must read 0.8515 with the canonical cut named.
notes:
DOWNGRADED P1->P3 ON READING THE LEDGER. The 0.8964-is-an-artefact finding is NOT new: experiments/README.md:6417 records it on 2026-08-30, names the cause (--eval-labels unset so the holdout truth was binarised against the re-mapped values), and already carries the corrected proxy pair 0.8515 vs control 0.8506 = +0.0009. This is the CLAUDE.md rule I skipped: read the ledger and the interpretations before filing a finding.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW AND STAYS OPEN:
1. FIXED HERE - the ledger wrote the rule (any future label-VALUE arm must pin --eval-labels) and nobody applied it to the file. recal_holdannot.sh still passed --labels RECAL with no --eval-labels as of 2026-09-08. Now explicit, with the defect written into the header beside the rank-AUC-invariance argument that hid it.
2. NEW - the existing arms had never been swept for the same defect. Every arm whose run_train block carries a non-canonical --labels and no --eval-labels: confident224.sh, confident_span.sh, recal_holdannot.sh, v3labels_dense.sh. Only recal_holdannot is affected. confident224_s2026 truth differs in float VALUES but not in positive SET, so it reads 0.8431 on both rulers. confident_span_s2026 and v3labels_dense_s2026 have no holdout npz on disk.
3. NEW - the mechanism stated as a positive-SET change rather than a truth-values change: the v3 re-map sends level 0.68 to 0.378, crossing the 0.5 midpoint, so 2017 positives across the twelve columns against the canonical 3336. That is why confident224 is unaffected and recal_holdannot moves 0.0449, and it is the test any future sweep should apply (positive set at midpoint, not float equality).

SCREEN 2026-09-18 00:41Z — THE CUT IS NOT THE PROBLEM; the exhausted ruler is the CORPUS.
research/scripts/cut_sweep.py recomputes every solo entry's macro under a grid of FLAT cuts and regresses
it on that entry's board, over all ten single-member rows in comp/board.jsonl. Residual sd IS the error
you make ranking two members with that ruler, so a better ruler is a smaller one.
  incumbent ledger75 (mixed 0.75 / midpoint)  slope +1.072  resid sd 0.0021
  flat 0.50 / 0.60                            slope +1.312  resid sd 0.0031  span 0.0250
  flat 0.68 / 0.75 / 0.80                     slope +1.084  resid sd 0.0021  span 0.0302
  flat 0.82 / 0.90                            slope +1.048  resid sd 0.0040  span 0.0292
NOTHING BEATS THE INCUMBENT. The best flat cut TIES it at 0.0021 — inside its own scatter, so no winner
(the script says so in its own docstring). Recutting the ruler cannot rescue the top-three tie, so that
tie is a property of the 909-study corpus, not of where the cut sits.
AND THE GRID COLLAPSES TO THREE RULERS, not seven: 0.50==0.60, 0.68==0.75==0.80, 0.82==0.90. The label
reader has five rungs, so a cut can only ever land in one of three gaps between them. That is a hard
bound on this whole axis and it means the incumbent had at most two alternatives to lose to.
CONSEQUENCE: retire every plan of the form 'recut the holdout and the top members will separate'. The
lever that remains is the CORPUS (more held-out studies), not the threshold.
CEILING 2026-09-18 00:52Z — research/scripts/ruler_ceiling.py. The corpus is not the lever either.
Bootstrapped paired delta, headlr_ship_s2026 vs labelwise_depth24_drop40_long_s2026, 400 draws a rung:

Scaling exponent -0.525 against -0.500 for a clean sqrt-n law, so the extrapolation is honest.
To resolve the 0.0014 spread at the top of the solo line needs 8,246 held-out studies. The project owns
4,406 labelled studies IN TOTAL; holding out every one of them lands at 0.0019, still above 0.0014.
THE RULER CEILING IS STRUCTURAL. Above offline75 ~0.904 no holdout cuttable from this corpus separates the
members we choose between, under any threshold. Consequences: an offline delta under ~0.004 between two of
our best is NO evidence; the board is the only instrument up there, so a slot is now the ranking resource

title: A finished arm can be relaunched by a stale watcher, and queue_check cannot see it
description: Cell D (ourtrunk44) completed ~02:57Z 2026-09-08 and wrote 'ARM DONE ourtrunk44'. title: Chain steps exit non-zero without stopping the queue, and two watchers may gate one marker
description: At 04:56Z the teacher pass in after_oof5_student.sh exited 1 (FileNotFoundError on images_224px_12sl_merged3.npy) and the chain went on to run noisy_student anyway, which also exited 1. Nothing stopped. The failure was invisible because after_retrain.sh was gated on the SAME marker (ARM DONE seat_oof5_distill), fired 45s earlier, and put final_ws_df on the card - so the card never went idle and queue_check reported OK throughout: a live process gating an owed arm is all it can see. Two defects. (1) Watcher scripts run their steps unconditionally; a step that fails must stop the chain, not hand the card to the next step. after_seats_done.sh now does this with an explicit stop-and-exit after every step; the other watcher scripts do not. title: Price every remaining route against one denominator before it takes card time
description:
The gap to first place is +0.0117 offline and NO single route reaches it. Measured, not argued: seat_requirement closed selection over 206 members; the member axis has seven board flats; and column_lift caps the weak-column route at +0.0041 achievable (+0.0074 at a degenerate oracle). So first place has to come from two or three routes SUMMING, which is the project's own standing rule about sub-bar increments against the ORIGINAL baseline.

What is missing is a common denominator. Each candidate route must be priced in ENSEMBLE POINTS against the greedy-optimal seven at 0.8764, the same way column_lift prices the column route, BEFORE it takes card time.

1. LABEL DENOISING / confident learning on the consensus-graded panel - what does the offline score do if the noisiest label-study pairs are dropped from the ruler? Zero card, data already on disk. OPEN, and now the cheapest thing on this list.

2. TIE STRUCTURE / prediction granularity - CLOSED 2026-09-06, zero card. SharpenedRank(k) bends each member's ranks through a logistic before averaging; the flat rule is its k->0 limit so there is no null to fit. Monotone NEGATIVE at both pool sizes: over 109 members -0.0001 / -0.0002 / -0.0009 / -0.0038 at k = 2/4/8/16, and over the greedy seven -0.0001 / -0.0003 / -0.0010 / -0.0024. Mechanism: binarising a column pays only when the column is RIGHT - the oracle case in column_lift - and a 0.83 column loses the within-class ordering that is the only thing separating it from a coin. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_the-two-column-route-has-a-measured-ceiling.md, addendum.

3. VOTE RULE - STRICKEN, it was never open. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_every-no-card-axis-is-priced-and-flat.md lines 22-24 record it BOARD-measured twice: efficient_v4 0.919 -> vote_v2 0.919 flat, and dark6_v1 0.937 -> votefit_v1 0.938 flat. That same document also records that a P1 was already filed once claiming this axis had never been measured. This is the second time; the fix is the standing rule - read the ledger and the interpretations before filing. The only live residue is a correctness bug, not a score route: Vote.ranks still uses ordinal ranks where area_under_curve was fixed to midranks.

4. TEST-TIME / scanner-shift adaptation - card, unpriced. Note the scanner axis was already found to exist in the data and NOT in the member ordering (commit e3f69d19), which lowers the prior.

title: Learned slice SELECTION at a fixed budget - the one upstream knob never turned
description:
knee-m69u asks for a new axis; the 2026-09-05 input-geometry re-audit (experiments/README.md, final section) closed multi-plane input, in-plane registration and the through-plane band, and left exactly two legs open. This is the live one.

CLAIM. Our aggregation stage is saturated from three directions: more slices -0.0001, more slots +0.0002, every combining rule within 0.0019. The ledger reads that as the limit sitting upstream, in what a single slice feature vector contains. Every arm this project has run samples slices UNIFORMLY across a fractional band. Which slices are taken, at a fixed budget, has never been varied.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY DONE BY MAX POOLING. Max pooling selects at READ time, over features the encoder computed from a uniformly chosen set. It cannot recover a slice that was never sampled. Selection here means changing which slices reach the encoder at all, which changes the gradient the encoder sees.

CHEAPEST FORM THAT WOULD SHOW SIGNAL. Two-pass. Run an existing trained whole-stack member over a dense slice grid, record per study which slices carried the argmax under max pooling, then train a fresh member at the SAME budget on those slices instead of the uniform ones. No new architecture, no new loss. The control already exists at every budget we use.

MEASURED HEADWIND to price against, not to ignore. The pooling-by-slice-count interaction says max wins short stacks and loses long ones, so a selection built from max argmax at a long stack is reading the operator that is worst there. The selector should be built at the budget it will serve.

PRICE. Not yet priced; do not arm until Q-SINGLE-B comes back from Kimi with an isolated published delta, or until the two-pass proxy is run card-free on existing checkpoints. Blocked on that, deliberately - the audit rule is plan before arm.

NOT the other surviving leg: a localiser crop is knee-tracked separately and carries crop80_span at -0.0099 against it.

Measured 2026-09-05 over the 57 annotated studies / 684 cells (ReaderAgreement.cells, the only non-reader ground truth).

Per-column reader precision on YES calls vs band_dense_s2026 best-epoch per-label AUC:

  finding                gold+  TP  FP MISS   prec    AUC
  Contusion                 18  16  20    2  0.444  0.871
  MCL                        9   9   9    0  0.500  0.793
  Lateral OA                11   9   7    2  0.562  0.816
  Medial OA                 15  14   8    1  0.636  0.880
  Lateral Meniscus          23  20  10    3  0.667  0.846
  PF OA                     20  16   8    4  0.667  0.858
  Effusion                  34  34  16    0  0.680  0.860
  Fracture                  17  13   6    4  0.684  0.809
  Bakers                    12  11   5    1  0.688  0.907
  ACL                       23  23   9    0  0.719  0.874
  Medial Meniscus           26  25   7    1  0.781  0.905
  Synovitis                 27  13   3   14  0.812  0.876

  spearman precision vs AUC: rho=+0.529 p=0.077 (n=12)
  spearman recall    vs AUC: rho=+0.162 p=0.615

DIRECTIONAL, not a finding: n=12 columns, p=0.077, and Contusion is the counterexample (worst precision, mid AUC). Do not plan around the correlation itself.

THE SPECIFIC CELL THAT IS NOT DIRECTIONAL: MCL has 9 gold positives, 9 true positives and 9 FALSE positives. The reader DOUBLES the MCL positive rate - half of every MCL positive our members train on and are scored against is wrong. MCL is our worst offline column at 0.793, and knee-zsyp4 measured the boards implied MCL column at 0.980 (colmcl ref 56020054). The column where the board says the task is nearly solved is the column where our supervision is half wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS: our offline holdout is scored against the SAME lexicon table the members train on, so a column with noisy labels is deflated on BOTH sides. Member selection has been ranking on that ruler. This is a named mechanism for knee-zsyp4 (biased-ruler) and independent evidence for knee-wko44 (labeler axis).

NEXT: ask whether noisy-label AUC can be de-biased to clean-label AUC per column without new annotations (letter out to Kimi 2026-09-05). If it can, every ledger number gets a per-column correction and the reseat decisions get re-read.

title: The label detector is the ceiling, and confident learning is the measured floor - build a SimiFeat-style kNN detector over the cached features
description:
THE BUDGET AND ALPHA KNOBS ARE BOTH SPENT AND BOTH WERE KNOBS ON A CEILING. knee-jom26 priced the budget curve out in both directions: our confident-learning detector separates radiologist disagreements at AUC 0.7628, its precision at the operating point is 0.720, and its recall there is 0.129 - so it can reach 13 percent of the corpus's real label errors before precision collapses. Corrected-minus-corrupted peaks exactly at the cut errors_relabel already trains on. Nothing on this axis moves again until the DETECTOR moves.

THE LITERATURE SAYS CL IS NOT THE CEILING - IT IS THE FLOOR. Kimi's Q-DET reply, 2026-09-05:

  AQuA (Goswami et al., NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2306.09467), a benchmark over 17 datasets, 4 noise types and
  4 noise rates evaluating AUM, Confident Learning, CINCER and SimiFeat, concludes verbatim: 'Overall, we
  found SimiFeat (SIM) to be the best cleaning method ... closely followed by CINCER (CIN) ... Confident
  learning (CON) consistently performed the worst among all the evaluated methods.'

  SEMD (Srikanth et al., arXiv:2312.02200) measures CL underperforming by -0.206 F1 on CIFAR-10 symmetric
  and -0.156 F1 on CIFAR-100 symmetric, and notes CL underperforms across all synthetic settings.

  SimiFeat (Zhu, Dong and Liu, ICML 2022, arXiv:2110.06283) is TRAINING-FREE: kNN over pretrained
  embeddings with test-time augmentation. On HUMAN-annotated noise it beats CL by about 20 percent F1 on
  CIFAR-10 and 10 percent on CIFAR-100 - human noise, which is the regime we are actually in.

WHY THIS ONE IS CHEAP HERE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT. SimiFeat needs embeddings and a neighbour search, not a training run. The processed root already holds full-corpus 336 px feature arrays for SIX trunks - ortholarge, v3large, large, radnet121, vjepa2l and small - each with its index json and mask. So the strongest published detector runs on arrays this project already paid for. ZERO CARD, ZERO SLOT. That is a far better ratio than any arm currently queued.

MEASURE IT THROUGH THE GATE THAT ALREADY EXISTS, so the number is comparable rather than merely new. kneemri.evaluation.label_errors already reports, against the 58-study radiologist panel: separation AUC over all 140 disagreements, precision and recall and lift at budgets 25/50/100/150/200 in gold-scaled units, and the same split for the 108 confident false positives and the 32 misses. The new detector must be scored by exactly that reporting path. Our CL numbers to beat:

  all disagreements (n=140)   separation AUC 0.7628   precision 0.720 at gold budget 25   recall 0.129
  confident false positives   separation AUC 0.7580   precision 0.640 at gold budget 25
  misses (n=32)               separation AUC 0.6903   precision 0.08-0.11 at every budget
  cleanlab's own mask         precision 0.484 all-disagreements, 0.258 on false positives (lift 1.63x)

NOTE WHERE THE HEADROOM ACTUALLY IS. Our detector is nearly blind to MISSES - 0.6903 separation and precision under 0.11 at every budget, against 0.7628 and 0.720 on the same panel for disagreements overall. The 32 misses are the cells where the lexicon said absent and the radiologist said present, and they are the half a report-derived label table should be worst at. A detector that only matches CL on false positives but reads misses at all would change the shape of the corrected corpus, not just its size.

WHAT A RESULT LOOKS LIKE. Separation AUC materially above 0.7628 on the same panel. Then re-run the net-benefit arithmetic from knee-jom26: a higher precision curve moves the corrected-minus-corrupted peak to a LARGER budget, which is the only thing that reopens the budget axis - and it does so with more corrected cells, not fewer. If the kNN detector ties CL, the label axis is closed on this corpus and should be written up as closed.

WHAT IT IS NOT. Not a member, not a submission, and it must not be sold as one. It is an instrument that decides whether an axis reopens.

SECOND CANDIDATE, CHEAPER STILL IF THE ARTEFACT EXISTS: AUM (Pleiss et al., NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:2001.10528) ranks by area under the margin across epochs and needs only per-epoch per-sample logits. Checked - our metrics.jsonl stores per-epoch aggregates (loss, auc, ece, loss quantiles) and no per-sample margins, so AUM would need the runs re-instrumented and re-run. That makes it CARD, not free, and it goes behind SimiFeat.

DO NOT REACH FOR: Li et al. NeurIPS 2022 trains an LSTM meta-detector on synthetic noise; strongest reported transfer, but it is a build on top of a build and the training dynamics we would feed it do not exist either.

REFS: knee-jom26 (the budget closure and the net-benefit arithmetic), knee-v78o1 (reading_check), kimi letter 20260905T0615Z.

title: Train an arm on table_correction — the +0.0632 Fracture rule has never reached a training run
description:
core/data/labels/table_correction.py implements the cross-column TRAINING-LABEL rule Fracture := rescale(Fracture + 0.25*Contusion), measured at +0.0632 on the gold Fracture column with p=0.0022. Grep shows its only importer is kneemri/evaluation/column_mixing.py. NO ARM HAS EVER TRAINED ON IT.

The serve-time null (2026-09-04) does NOT cover this. Its own text scopes itself out: mixing at the OUTPUT is dead because the members' columns already carry each other's information by then; a training-label rule changes what the model is FITTED on, which is a different operation and the interpretation says so at line 63.

PRICE. One 12-epoch arm on band_dense's recipe, ~70 min of card. Fracture is one of our two worst columns (control 0.8088). Full transfer of +0.0632 would be +0.0053 of board; the label lane's measured transfer rate (blendlabels: +0.0034 mean, +0.0174 on Fracture) says expect +0.002 to +0.003. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.02. DIRECTIONAL, and it is worth running only because increments below the bar still compose against the original baseline, and because the card has no better-priced occupant after the knee-fqit7 re-open arm.

QUEUE POSITION: third. errors_relabel is on the card to ~04:00Z; knee-fqit7's re-open arm (ortho on the DENSE recipe against a ViT-L control, 2h) has the better ratio because its effect size is already measured at +0.014.
notes: PRICED NEGATIVE BEFORE IT RAN, by Kimi Q-XFER (letter 2026-09-05T0230Z). The serve-time null bounds the training-time rule, because THE IMAGE IS THE SHARED CHANNEL. If the model already sees the contusion evidence, a Fracture target carrying 0.25*Contusion is redundant and adds label noise on a coefficient nobody calibrated. If it does NOT see it, serve-time mixing should have paid, because the same proxy is equally available at inference - and it did not: dense ridge ceiling -0.0022, sparse Label-Graph Refinement -0.0019, two estimators landing 0.0003 apart, which is a statement about the mechanism rather than about ridges. Kong et al 2014's label-enrichment gains are on INCOMPLETE labels (recovering positives an annotator omitted), not on enriching labels already present, so they do not transfer. The only escape is a CURRICULUM effect rather than an information one, and there is no medical-imaging demonstration of that at the +0.01 level. DO NOT SPEND THE 70 MINUTES. If ever revisited: a few-epoch ablation on the transformed Fracture target, read validation Fracture AUC against baseline, kill early absent a clear gain.

title: The refit constant is +0.001, not +0.006 -- the difference is --calibrated-targets
description: Two board pairs measure fold-0 twins -> full-fit at four seats: foldfour_v1 0.936 -> fitfour_v1 0.937 (+0.001) and twinfive_v1 0.935 -> fiveship_v1 0.941 (+0.006). title: coatnet2 registry entry ran under IMAGENET normalization while timm publishes 0.5/0.5
description:
FIXED, and filed for the class rather than the instance. The COATNET_2 entry declared no normalization, so it took Encoder's default, IMAGENET (0.485/0.456/0.406, 0.229/0.224/0.225). timm publishes (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) for coatnet_rmlp_2_rw_384.sw_in12k_ft_in1k inside config.json's pretrained_cfg — the AugReg convention, HALF here. The arm ran 25 minutes of card on inputs centred a third of a standard deviation off in every channel.

WHAT IT WOULD HAVE COST. coatnet_hybrid is pre-registered with four branches and its FLAT branch closes the hierarchical row of the registry with three families measured. A mis-normalized trunk lands low, so the arm would very likely have read FLAT or REFUTES, and that reading would have been written into the ledger as a fact about a convolutional-prior-feeding-global-attention ARRANGEMENT when it was a fact about preprocessing. That is the faulty-PLUMBING row of the CLAUDE.md list exactly: a value recorded in a config while the consumer reads a constant.

WHAT CAUGHT IT. tests/integration/registry_to_checkpoints.py::test_every_encoder_states_its_own_constants, which refuses an entry that neither matches a published preprocessing document nor carries normalization_evidence prose. It did not run for two days because gates were red earlier in the chain (a god-file and a method mirror), so pytest was never reached. THAT is the real lesson: a blocking gate early in the session order hides every gate after it, and the arm was launched in that window.

THE CLASS. Encoder.normalization has a DEFAULT, and a default is what let this entry say nothing and be wrong. Every natural-image trunk here is ImageNet-normalized so the default was right eleven times, which is precisely how a twelfth silently inherits it. timm repositories are the exposed surface: they ship no preprocessor_config.json, so the published-document check cannot fire at all and only the evidence-prose rule stands between an entry and a default.

FIX SHIPPED: normalization=HALF plus normalization_evidence quoting the file, attempt 1's artefacts renamed _voidnorm (never deleted, never stitched — knee-gnzx), the arm relaunched 20:24Z, and the arm header now carries the void.

FOLLOW-ON WORTH DOING: make Encoder.normalization mandatory for any entry whose repository is a timm one, or drop the default entirely and make all twelve say ImageNet out loud. The second is more churn and strictly safer.

title: Continued in-domain pretraining (DAPT) of the DINOv2 trunk on knee-MRI volumes
description:
The trunk-FAMILY axis is closed (Swin, ConvNeXtV2, MedSAM -0.044, RadioDino x3, OrthoFoundation; RadImageNet void on a BatchNorm defect; coatnet_hybrid is the last arrangement, on the card now). The CORPUS axis closed tonight too, and it closed with a mechanism rather than a shrug: radiodino_corpus priced its seat at -0.0008 into honest12, and Juodelyte (TMLR 2023) measures exactly that shape - ImageNet and RadImageNet representations diverge after finetuning while their PREDICTIONS stay similar. Krones (2026) adds the condition under which in-domain pretraining does pay: the modality has to MATCH. RadioDino's corpus is 2D radiology, not knee MRI, which is why it seats at zero.

What that leaves open is not which trunk, but what the trunk was TAUGHT. Continued self-supervised pretraining (Gururangan DAPT/TAPT) of an existing DINOv2 ViT-B/14 on our own unlabeled knee-MRI corpus - the competition volumes, fastMRI knee (231 presigned URLs already held), SKM-TEA - is the only corpus direction the literature still predicts a gain for, and it is the largest lever this project can still name.

BLOCKED ON Q-EP (sent to Kimi 2026-09-04T20:15Z), which prices it before it takes 6-12 h of card: (1) is there measured gain from continuation at under ~12 GPU-hours, or is every published number an 8-A100 run; (2) which objective survives continuation on a DINO-INITIALISED trunk - a reduced single-GPU DINO recipe, or MAE, whose reconstruction loss may destroy the features that make the frozen representation good; (3) does 'modality-matched' mean MRI slices of anything, or knee-specific volumetric acquisition. Answer (1) can price the lever OUT, which is a useful answer.

Do not arm before Q-EP returns.
notes:
PRICED OUT ON EVIDENCE THE REPO ALREADY HELD, within an hour of filing. Q-EP came back fast and its own citations kill it, together with two ledger rows nobody had put next to them.

Kimi's Q-EP-3 names OrthoFoundation as the SOTA instance of exactly this lever: 1.2M unlabeled knee X-ray + MRI images, DINOv2/DINOv3-L backbone, 2D slice encoder, SOTA on 14 musculoskeletal tasks. That is somebody else's DAPT on our own modality and our own joint, at a corpus and compute scale we cannot approach - and it is ALREADY A MEMBER HERE, as variant ortholarge. So the lever does not need building to be priced; it needs reading.

What the ledger says it bought:
  ortho_dense  0.8452 at 224 px / 12 slices, against native224 0.8502 and tissue224 0.8491 - the
    DAPT trunk is -0.005 under a natural-image trunk at a matched read.
  ortho_stack  0.8417 against v3large_stack 0.8277 - at MATCHED trunk size the DAPT trunk is +0.0140,
    which is the effect size, and it is below the 0.0062 floor's big brother, the 1.5% bar.
Those two are not in conflict: DAPT is worth about +0.014 at matched ViT-L, and the ViT-L lane itself
costs about that much against ViT-B here, so the net against base_dense 0.8512 is a wash.

Then the compute. Kimi's curve: DIET-CP gains at <10 min but under a DIFFERENT objective (datum-index
classification) on 2D MedMNIST; the DINO-objective positives are ExPLoRA at 80-100 GPU-h (+1.2% on
satellite, ablated down to 24 h) and BrainFound at ~104 GPU-h on 1.5M brain-MRI slices. There is NO
published DINO-objective medical gain at a 12 GPU-hour budget. So our version would spend 12 h of card
plus a DINO self-distillation training loop that does not exist in this repo, to chase an effect whose
best-case measured size here is +0.014, at a fraction of the corpus that produced it.

PRICE: ~12 h card + roughly a day of build. P(clears 1.5%) = 0.08. That is the worst ratio of any lever
currently named, and it is worse than it looks because the 0.08 assumes we match a 1.2M-image run.

RE-OPEN BY: not by a bigger budget. By a reading that the ortho rows are confounded - the honest one is
that both were run against ViT-L controls and the trunk-size handicap was measured only later
(band_pairmem, knee-710gi). An ortho arm on the DENSE recipe against a ViT-L control at the same read
would separate DAPT from trunk size properly, and that is 2 h, not 12. If DAPT then reads well above
+0.014 at matched everything, this bead comes back.

title: The rank loss was inert in sixteen arms - every batch-1 arm ran the plain recipe under a rank-loss name
description: experiments/recipe.sh sets RECIPE with --rank-weight 1.0. A pairwise term needs pairs, and --batch 1 forms none: --accumulate cannot repair it because it sums the gradients of micro-batch losses each computed alone. --pair-memory N is what supplies pairs across steps, and sixteen arms set --batch 1 without it: cnx_dense_448, cnx_distill_warm, cnx_mid_rate, cnx_own_recipe, cnx_top_rate, cnx_warm_anneal, radnet_family, raptor_feat_fit, raptor_feat_pre, swin_calib_dense, swin_distill_fit, swin_distill_pre, swin_open_half, swin_supervised, swin_toprate, swin_wholetop. That is the ENTIRE hierarchical-trunk family plus both raptor feature arms. Found because the trainer now REFUSES the combination outright and coatnet_hybrid died on it at smoke; fixed there with --pair-memory 15 = C(6,2) at --accumulate 6, by band_pairmem's own rule that 66 = C(12,2) matched --accumulate 12. WHAT THIS DOES NOT INVALIDATE: comparisons WITHIN the sixteen. They are mutually consistent - all sixteen ran the same plain recipe, so swin_supervised 0.8331 vs cnx_own_recipe 0.8186 vs swin_wholetop 0.8274 still order correctly against each other. WHAT IT DOES PUT IN DOUBT: the non-DINO deficit reading, which compares these sixteen against DINO arms run at batch 2 or higher where the term was at least partly live, and recipe.sh's own comment claiming --rank-weight is 'the only loss change positive in 3 of 3 matched arms' - name those three arms and check their batch size, because if any was batch 1 the claim is about nothing. Also check coatnet_hybrid's reading when it lands: it is the FIRST hierarchical arm with a live rank term, so it differs from swin_supervised in two variables, not one, and that is already stated in its header.

title: The champion's seats cannot be priced: 5 of raptorweight_v1's 6 members are fold -1
description:
seat_value refuses on our own champion:

  unscoreable (fold -1, they have seen every holdout study): calib_span_ff, final_ws_cf, grade_ladder_cf, lr4e-5_ws_cf, through_dense_cf

So the seven board flats that closed the member axis were measured on scoreable entries, and the champion sits outside that evidence rather than inside it. We do not know which of its seats carry it.

It also means the fallback seat_value itself suggests -- --against honest12 (0.937, 12 members) -- prices seats in a DIFFERENT entry 0.007 below the champion, and any conclusion transferred from there to the champion is an assumption, not a measurement.

NOT PROPOSING A FIX YET. Retraining five members on a real fold is 10+ hours of card and would produce different checkpoints, not the champion's. The cheaper question is whether a held-out slice exists that none of the five saw, or whether the champion has to be re-derived from scoreable members before any seat claim about it is allowed. Audit first.

title: arm_check does not refuse an arm that has ALREADY RUN — it cost a window and nearly 4h of card
description:
On 2026-09-04 a whole session armed, priced, pre-registered, smoked and QUEUED errors_dense on the belief that it had never run. It ran 2026-09-02 07:57 and completed twelve of twelve epochs: D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/experiments/errors_dense_s2026.full.log, checkpoint errors_dense_s2026.pt, metrics jsonl, and the log ends with 'ARM DONE errors_dense'. The watcher chain had it queued behind band_pairmem and would have re-run it for ~4h. It was caught only because a routine ls of the experiments directory happened to show the log, minutes before band_pairmem finished.

EVERY GATE WAS GREEN. arm_check --only errors_dense reported '1 checked, 0 refused, 0 uncached' and even ran a 60-study smoke. arm_check asks whether an arm CAN run; nothing asks whether it ALREADY DID. ledger_check does see unrecorded runs, but it runs AFTER arms finish and nothing chains it to arming. queue_check reports what a watcher owes, not whether the owed thing is already done.

WHY THE HUMAN CHECK FAILED TOO: CLAUDE.md says 'Folds and seeds are banned. Do not repeat experiments whose result is known' and 'READ THE LEDGER before filing a finding' — and errors_dense has NO ledger row, so reading the ledger actively CONFIRMED the wrong belief. The absence of a row was read as evidence the arm had not run, when it was evidence the arm was unrecorded. That is the same shape as the ledger_check finding it was built for.

THE FIX: arm_check refuses (or at minimum loudly warns) when an arm's --out checkpoint, its metrics jsonl, or a '<arm>.full.log' containing 'ARM DONE <arm>' already exists on disk. A deliberate re-run needs an --anyway '<why>' the way submit_check does, and that why belongs in the arm's header. The disk is the authority here, exactly as card_check asks the DEVICE rather than argv and mount_check --live asks Kaggle.

SECOND-ORDER COST: the belief was carried into a letter to Kimi (2026-09-04T1535Z) that CORRECTED their correct statement that pruning loses. That letter has to be retracted.

continuation lands near 0.873 against the 0.8578 incumbent. The target needs +0.0175 offline on the best

title: MedSAM read-out point: neck (256d) or raw ViT tokens (768d)
description: sam_trunk returns SamModel.vision_encoder, whose forward ends in the 256-channel neck built for the mask decoder. Three published results argue the neck is the wrong read-out for classification: SAMantics (arXiv:2411.15288) linear-probes SAM's neck output at 11.1 percent ImageNet top-1 against DINOv2's 77.4; FODA-PG (arXiv:2409.03947) drops the MedSAM neck explicitly to read patch embeddings for a medical task; the neck is a 3x compression with no decoder here to serve. Against that, MedSAM's paper says the fine-tune updated ALL image-encoder parameters and publishes no layer-wise breakdown, so a neck-concentrated adaptation would make raw tokens discard what makes the checkpoint medical. kneemri.models.sam_drift measures that directly against facebook/sam-vit-base, card-free. Decide the read-out on its ratio before any medsam arm is queued. See research/2026-09-04_sam-neck-vs-raw-tokens-for-classification.md

title: Slice-pooling 'transformer': the MST operator our attend deliberately is not
description:
MECHANISM. kneemri/models/slice_attention.py:15-37 states our attend pooling is DELIBERATELY TINY - one gate of width 64, a single shared query, a few thousand parameters, 'rather than a transformer' - and its own docstring names Medical Slice Transformer (2025, same DINOv2 backbone we use) as the published knee-MRI work that replaces the elementwise max with exactly this attention. MST does NOT use a gated-MIL pool. It uses a slice TRANSFORMER, and Kimi's Q-CR reply carries its numbers: DINOv2 + slice Transformer reads 0.85 AUC on MRNet meniscus, frozen DINOv2 with plain slice AGGREGATION reads 0.79 on the same task and the same trunk. The published attribution of the operator upgrade on this exact axis is +0.06.

WHY IT PRICES ABOVE THE BAR. attend itself measured +0.0059 (experiments/README.md:5050) once the gate-never-learned defect (knee-7gyw) was fixed - the parameter_groups bug that had made attend_dense secretly compare MEAN vs MAX. So the operator family works here; the question is whether the tiny gate is leaving the rest on the table. This is the only architectural lever left with a published number attributing gain to it, on our anatomy, our modality and our trunk.

WHAT TO BUILD. A new SLICE_POOLINGS entry: multi-head self-attention ACROSS slice tokens, positional encoding along the slice axis (the depth pooling already establishes the axis carries ORDER), CLS-query read. Register it beside attend/depth/labelwise; it is the fourth member of a vocabulary that already exists, not a new subsystem.

COST AND ODDS, stated before building. ~1h to build, one 12-epoch fit at measured 380 s/epoch = ~76 min. Total ~2.5h. Odds of clearing 1.5%: maybe 25%, and the honest counter-evidence is in the same docstring - this model is supervision-limited (58 of 4,407 studies carry an image-read label) and forcing better attention measured NEUTRAL once, when the anatomical prior supplied correct slot attention and bought nothing.

MUST VERIFY THE FLAG LANDED. knee-7gyw is the precedent: assert the new module's parameters appear in a param group and are non-zero after one epoch, in the CHECKPOINT config, before quoting any number. A silently untrained transformer would repeat the exact defect this axis already produced once.

RELATED: knee-46g9p (MST/MRNet replication, blocked on Kimi Q-CS). This bead is the part that needs no reply - the operator can be built and measured on OUR task without knowing their split.
notes:
KILLED 2026-09-03 BEFORE IT COST A CARD HOUR, by the ledger. Three reasons, and the third is the one that matters.

(1) kneemri/models/slice_pooling.py:38-41 records that attend, depth AND labelwise 'all select among slices and measured within +0.0002 of the elementwise maximum'. A slice transformer is the FOURTH selector on an axis measured null three times.

(2) experiments/README.md:5131 - fuse_attend ALREADY RAN. Stacking --through-plane + attend + --pool sided reads 0.8509 against its control calib_dense_hold's 0.8634: -0.0125, OUTSIDE the 0.0062 paired floor in the wrong direction. The ledger's own reading is that these are 'not independent mechanisms adding up but three spellings of one'. A transformer over slices is a fourth spelling.

(3) MST's +0.06 IS CONFOUNDED AND I READ IT TOO FAST. Their comparison is 0.85 (DINOv2 + slice Transformer) against 0.79 (FROZEN DINOv2 + slice aggregation). That contrast moves TWO variables - frozen vs fitted, and aggregation vs transformer - so it cannot attribute the gain to the operator. Their other number, 0.69, is a 3D ResNet, which is not our baseline either. We already fine-tune the trunk. The most likely reading of their +0.06 is the fine-tuning we already do, not the transformer we do not have.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT: the slice-order axis specifically (depth is the only pooling that sees ORDER and it is one arm), and MST's actual protocol, which Q-CS still asks for. If Kimi's reply carries an ablation that separates trunk from pooling and the pooling half is large, this reopens - by answering (3), not by re-quoting the headline.

title: Continued SSL pretraining at 4.4k volumes: killed on literature, do not queue
description:
Q-CR reply from Kimi, 2026-09-03T2220Z. Asked whether continued self-supervised pretraining of the trunk on our own knee MRI pays at ~4.4k volumes, since it is the one lever with no code path and no arm in this repo.

ANSWER: no published crossover exists at that scale for CONTINUED SSL of a strong general trunk. The largest fully-3D medical SSL effort (SPECTRE, arXiv 2511.17209) pretrains on 229,619 CT volumes. Konstantakos 2024 (arXiv 2404.17202) finds in-domain low-data SSL beats general pretraining, but its low-data regime is 50k-300k images, an order of magnitude above us. El-Nouby 2021 (arXiv 2112.10740) does show gains at ~1k images, but training FROM SCRATCH with masked reconstruction, not continuing a strong init - and reports DINO specifically DEGRADES as pretraining data shrinks. Lee 2022 (arXiv 2210.02871) reports naive further-pretraining of ViT on target unlabeled data OVERFITS and underperforms plain fine-tuning.

DECISION: the 6-12h arm is NOT queued. Killed before the card, on literature, which is the cheapest kill this project has made.

WHAT SURVIVES if it is ever re-opened: the objective would have to be MAE/iBOT-style masked reconstruction, never DINO-style self-distillation, and it would be a SLICE-level MAE over ~50k slices rather than a volume-level objective over 4.4k volumes.

OPEN QUESTION, unresolved and worth recording: whether SSL effective-N for MRI scales with SLICE count rather than VOLUME count. Kimi found no paper that tests it either way. If we ever ran it we would be producing new evidence, not replicating.

SUPERSEDED IN PRIORITY BY knee-46g9p (MST/MRNet replication), which has a published number on a dataset we hold.

title: Replicate MST on MRNet: DINOv2 + slice transformer, published 0.85 AUC meniscus
description:
Kimi Q-CR reply (2026-09-03T2220Z) surfaced Muller-Franzes et al. 2025 (Sci Rep), Medical Slice Transformer: DINOv2 on MRNet knee MRI slices + slice Transformer reads 0.85 AUC on meniscus-tear vs 0.69 for a 3D ResNet; FROZEN DINOv2 with slice aggregation reads 0.79 on the same task.

WHY THIS RANKS P1. It is the only lever on the desk with a PUBLISHED NUMBER ON A DATASET WE ALREADY HOLD, same anatomy, same modality. The project's stated order is gather -> replicate -> merge -> build past; every recent arm skipped to build because nothing had an external number to stand on. This does.

WHAT IT IS NOT. Not a seating operation, not a slot. The first deliverable is a replication of 0.85 under our own harness on their split and their task. If our harness cannot reproduce it, that is a harness finding and worth more than the arm.

title: The vote tracks the member MEAN, not the member BEST: +0.0147 over average, +0.0040 over best
description:
Zero-card, 2026-09-03T17:29Z. LogitAverage over the twinfive fold-0 five, 909 studies, per-column.

label              ens   bestsolo  meansolo   e-best   e-mean
Fracture         0.8337   0.8440   0.8188   -0.0103  +0.0149
MCL              0.8114   0.8195   0.7939   -0.0081  +0.0175

Bakers           0.9205   0.9174   0.9089   +0.0031  +0.0116
Lateral OA       0.8249   0.8218   0.8135   +0.0031  +0.0114
ACL              0.9011   0.8952   0.8793   +0.0059  +0.0218
PF OA            0.8653   0.8590   0.8460   +0.0064  +0.0194
Medial Meniscus  0.9083   0.9012   0.8971   +0.0071  +0.0112
Medial OA        0.8881   0.8808   0.8775   +0.0073  +0.0105
Effusion         0.8647   0.8572   0.8525   +0.0075  +0.0121
Contusion        0.8817   0.8734   0.8667   +0.0083  +0.0151
Lateral Meniscus 0.8716   0.8557   0.8525   +0.0159  +0.0191
MEAN             0.8706   0.8666   0.8558   +0.0040  +0.0147

READING. The vote sits +0.0147 above the AVERAGE member and only +0.0040 above the BEST. So the ensemble tracks the pool MEAN, roughly 1:1 -- consistent with Krogh-Vedelsby ambiguity decomposition (ensemble error = average member error - average disagreement) and with the calibsix pass-through of >1.0 measured earlier. Raising the mean member by X raises the vote by about X. That is the quantified form of the reframe: our board 0.944 comes from a 0.923 solo, the +0.021 is saturated, and the leader at 0.952 has a better SINGLE model.

NOT ACTIONABLE, stated so it is not mis-read later: e-best is a HINDSIGHT column (best member chosen per label on the same holdout), and the two negative cells sit inside their own Hanley-McNeil SEs (Fracture 0.0316, MCL 0.0215). This does not license per-label member selection -- that axis is already closed on the board.

CONSEQUENCE. No further combination-side arm. Every card hour goes to solo quality. unread_dense_s2026 (knee-s6s9r) is the one running, and it is a solo-quality arm.

Reproduce: LogitAverage over calib_span_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, merged_blend_cf, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026 via VoteCeiling.over + LabelScores.per_label.
notes:
DOWNGRADED P1->P3 2026-09-03T17:35Z, by owner challenge. This is NOT a finding and NOT a reframe. 'Ensemble beats single model' has been known for a month, and the ~1:1 pass-through from member mean to vote was already measured on calibsix (+0.0038 pooled solo -> +0.0056/+0.0084 ensemble). 'Focus on solo quality' is not a change of direction either -- every arm this project has run trains a solo; it is the only thing the card has ever done.

What survives as useful, and it is one line: the vote sits only +0.0040 above the BEST member, so no combiner over this pool reaches the leader's 0.952 from our 0.944. That is a BOUND on combination, consistent with the seven board flats, not a direction to work in.

Keep the per-column table as a reference reading. Do not cite this bead as licensing anything.
THE NUMBER THE 0.008 GAP DEMANDS, from holdfive_v1's fitted compression: at pool positions above 0.8694 the slope is +0.71 board per offline point. Closing 0.008 board therefore needs 0.008/0.71 = +0.0113 OFFLINE over the champion's shadow. Best ensemble offline this project owns is 0.8754 (strong-and-distant five, today); the champion twins read 0.8700. So the target is a pool reading ~0.8813 on the 909 shared studies. Best solo on disk is 0.8642. That is the size any solo-quality arm has to be priced against — a +0.005 member does not get there and should not be queued as if it might.
CORRECTION, same day, to the +0.0113 figure I appended above. That used board_transfer's +0.71 slope. Refitting on the full record (2026-09-03 18:50Z, logs in-band) shows the +0.71 rests on THREE resolved pairs, and its printed '[+0.70, +0.89]' is a median over three non-independent pairs sharing entries, not an interval. Better-supported bands: +0.97 over 13 pairs at >=0.8678, +1.25 over the whole record (which the tool itself labels the wrong number to price an arm with). So the offline gain needed to close 0.008 board is +0.0064 (at 1.25) to +0.0082 (at 0.97) to +0.0113 (at 0.71), and the tightest-sounding of those is the least supported. Quote the RANGE.
SECOND, structural: board_transfer reports 43 entries ONE-SIDED, which is every --fold -1 entry including the champion. The fit therefore sees only the fold-0 half of the board, which is systematically the 0.932-0.938 half. Any statement about how compression behaves 'at the top' is a statement about the top of the FOLD-0 range, not the top of the board. Filed separately.
THE CLOSURE OF THE STRONG-AND-DISTANT POOL DOES NOT DEPEND ON ANY OF THIS. honest12 measured the operation directly: +0.0050 offline over the same five champion twins, 0.937 board against the champion's 0.944. That is a measurement, not an extrapolation through a slope.

title: Architecture distance buys nothing BELOW parity: two measured zeros, and the axis restates
description:
Measured 2026-09-03 17:12Z with vote_ceiling over the twinfive_v1 fold-0 five (calib_span_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, merged_blend_cf, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026), 909 studies, honest split-half, no card time.

  five members                                   LogitAverage 0.8706
  + ortho_pool_read   (FITTED DINOv3-L ortho)    0.8705   -0.0001
  + ortho_lpft_head   (FROZEN trunk + head only) 0.8697   -0.0009

Both under BOARD_RESOLVABLE 0.0040 and under the 0.0062 floor, so these are nulls rather than refutations of magnitude. They join mrnet_warm_s2026's measured 0.0000 (corpus distance).

THIS ANSWERS AN UNPUBLISHED QUESTION. Kimi Q-CP (2026-09-03) searched for whether a frozen foreign trunk plus a trained head retains the ensemble diversity benefit of a fully fine-tuned foreign member and found the experiment absent from the literature. For this pool the answer is no: the frozen member is WORSE in the pool than the fitted one, -0.0009 against -0.0001.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW, and this is the reading. Both members are far weaker solo than the pool (0.8464 and 0.7537 against 0.8635), so a rank or logit average dilutes with either. Distance is confounded with weakness in every architecture-distant member this project has BUILT. The single distant member that ever paid was mounted, not trained: a public CoAtNet at solo PARITY (0.923 against our 0.923) that took the pair to 0.936, +0.013, the largest one-seat move in 99 board rows.

SO THE AXIS RESTATES: distance pays at parity, and parity is unreachable by fitting because there is no published cross-family recipe-transfer rule (Kimi Q-CO: muP is within-family; LLRD and linear LR scaling are heuristics) and sweeps are banned at the finding stage. The affordable route is MOUNTING another competitive public checkpoint, which costs licence review rather than card hours.

ALSO CLOSED BY THE SAME LETTER: diversity-promoting losses. Abe et al. 2024 ICLR (arXiv 2302.00704, ~600 ensembles) find diversity interventions help small ensembles and HARM large deep ones. No arm goes there.

ALSO: CKA is NOT a published screen for ensemble gain. What is published is forward-pass transferability metrics for source-model ensemble selection (Agostinelli et al. 2022, arXiv 2111.13011; SoftIoU-EEP, weighted Kendall tau 69.3%, selected ensemble +6.0% relative over the best single source). That is a candidate screen for ranking mountable checkpoints without fitting any of them, and it is the follow-up worth scoping.

title: holdfive_v1's offline gap is mostly --calibrated-targets, not --hold-annotations
description:
holdfive_v1 (shipped 2026-09-03 13:00Z, ref 55981507) reads offline 0.8729 against twinfive_v1's 0.8706, a +0.0023 gap its own docstring attributes to the --hold-annotations supervision family, while admitting the two supervision flags are fused: all five seated members carry --calibrated-targets as well.

A calib-only five de-confounds it at zero cost. vote_ceiling over calib_span_s2026, calibrated_targets_s2026, merged_dense_cf, merged_labelwise_cf, merged_span_cf -- the fold-0 members carrying --calibrated-targets and NOT --hold-annotations -- reads the same 909 shared studies and the same rule:

  LogitAverage honest 0.8724 (+0.0005 vs flat, overfit gap +0.0000)
  RankAverage 0.8719, QualityWeightedRank 0.8718, LabelQualityRank 0.8719, MedianLogit 0.8692

Decomposition: ordinary 0.8706 -> calib-only 0.8724 is +0.0018; calib-only 0.8724 -> hold+calib 0.8729 is +0.0005. The flag the entry is named after carries about a fifth of the gap the entry is priced on.

WHY IT MATTERS BEFORE THE BOARD NUMBER LANDS. The docstring's >= 0.941 branch commits card hours to a full re-fit of the champion seats under --hold-annotations --calibrated-targets, reading a high board number as the hold flag transferring. This says the calibration flag is the bigger half, so that branch should be read as licensing --calibrated-targets and NOT the hold flag, and any follow-up arm should move one flag at a time.

CAVEAT, and it bounds rather than isolates. The calib-only five is matched on FLAGS, not on members: different recipes sit in those seats, so member identity is confounded with the flag. Both terms are also under the 0.0062 report-holdout noise floor individually -- the split is the reading, not either number.

Also note calib_dense_s2026 has neither a checkpoint nor a holdout record on disk, so the calib-only pool is five and not six.

title: A trained SlotHead scores 0.061 BELOW a ridge on the same frozen features, and that gap is 85% of what was read as a trunk result
description:
MEASURED, not suspected. On the frozen ortholarge cache, fold-0, n=909: ridge on max-pooled features 0.8146; the project's own trained SlotHead on the SAME max-pooled features 0.7537 (ortho_lpft_head @e11). The head is 0.0609 WORSE than a linear ridge fitted on identical inputs.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN NUMBER. The 0.071 gap between ridge+moments (0.8279) and SlotHead+max (0.7537) was read here as evidence about the SECOND MOMENT and about the ortho trunk. It decomposes as roughly 15% missing second moment and 85% the head being worse than a ridge. So ortho_lpft_head is evidence about OUR READOUT, not about that trunk, and any decline that cited it as a trunk verdict is mispriced the same way knee-x4yx describes for the shared ridge penalty.

FOUR CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, none tested (Kimi's Q-CK answer, research/2026-09-03_second_moment_pooling_and_lpft_literature.md): (a) the 1024->256 projection discards directions a ridge keeps; (b) the anatomy prior fights the data on a FROZEN trunk, where it cannot be absorbed; (c) optimisation mismatch -- head LR/schedule tuned for the fine-tuning regime, not the frozen one; (d) unearned inductive bias. Named literature: Kumar et al. ICLR 2022 (arXiv:2202.10054) on LP-FT; Knott/Marks arXiv:2407.12210, which says explicitly DO NOT rank trunks for fine-tuning by frozen linear probe alone.

THE CHEAP DIAGNOSTIC, NO TRAINING: fit a ridge on raw frozen features, then fit a ridge on the same features passed through the head's FROZEN 1024->256 projection. If the second collapses toward 0.7537 the projection is the bottleneck (a) and the fix is width; if it stays near 0.8146 the bottleneck is downstream and (b)/(c) are live. One matrix multiply and two ridge fits over a cache that already exists.

FOURTH CELL STILL MISSING for the 2x2: ridge+max 0.8146, ridge+moments 0.8279, SlotHead+max 0.7537, SlotHead+moments unmeasured. That one needs card.

Blocks nothing, but it re-prices every frozen-probe reading this project has made.

title: card_check is blind to Docker/WSL GPU holders and its blind spot reads as absence
description: card_check reported '1 process, 31841 MiB, other pid LibreOffice' while the real holder was a Docker vLLM container (vllm-qwen-128k, 31832 MiB, device 0). nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps returns [Insufficient Permissions] for the elevated holder and [N/A] for desktop processes, so the tool fell back to naming the largest process it COULD see. LibreOffice holding 31.8GB on a 5090 was never plausible. Consequence: two written, smoked, pre-registered arms (moment_dense, unread_dense) were parked for a window that was not contested, on an attribution one 'docker ps' away. Fix: when the compute-apps query is refused or the named processes cannot account for the resident bytes, card_check must SAY the holder is unidentified-and-elevated and check docker ps, rather than attributing the memory to the largest nameable process. A diagnostic that cannot see something has made a finding, not a null observation.

title: Qwen3.8 reader: point it at the OVER-CALLED cells, not the UNK ones
description:
research/2026-09-03_label_audit_protocol_with_qwen38.md proposes gating the local Qwen3.8-27B endpoint on filling UNK, and calls a targeted UNK-only sweep 'the cheapest way to fill the silence'. The repo already measured that and it does not hold: report_reader.py:19-27 shows the silence is the REPORT's, not the reader's - a knee report discusses what was asked about, and on UNK cells the report does not name the structure at all (Synovitis 25 of 1,424 = 1.8%, Effusion 0 of 84). No reader, however strong, reads text that is absent.

The refutation is FINDING-SHAPED, not global, and that is the part worth keeping. Broadening the patterns moves two findings: Baker's names a cyst in 236 of 765 UNK cells (30.8%) and Contusion 55 of 342 (16.1%). That was measured against an ENGLISH LEXICON, so a stronger multilingual LLM is a genuinely different instrument there and its ceiling is not known - but the ceiling of the AXIS is: roughly 5-10% of UNK cells in two findings, 1-3% of the label matrix moving one rung, which report_reader:27 already declines to arm as a full sweep because it cannot deliver 1.5%.

WHERE THE ENDPOINT IS ACTUALLY LIVE: the cells the reader DID read and got wrong. reader_agreement measures 108 confident false positives over 58 annotated studies - 15.8% of every annotated cell, all verdict YES - against 32 misses of which only 8 are a confident NO. That is a measured defect on cells where the text EXISTS, so a better reader can act on it. The protocol's own steps 3 and 4 (reader_agreement, overcall_audit) already test exactly that; only the step-2 gate (reader_upgrade, which scores ONLY on the blanks) points at the closed axis.

ACTION: re-gate the protocol on reader_agreement's false-positive count rather than on reader_upgrade's blank-fill, and scope any sweep to Baker's + Contusion UNK plus the full read-cell set. Also prices out the 40-70h estimate: the card is the owner's, and a sweep over 1,200 silent studies buys the smaller half.

Separately: knee-s6s9r (unread_teacher) is the OTHER half of the same defect and does not compete with this - it gives the never-read cells an ORDER from the published out-of-fold pool rather than trying to read them, which is the only route left once the text is known to be absent.

title: OrthoFoundation-L is derived from fastMRI, which our own licence reading closed for shipping
description:
Kimi Q-CD (2026-09-03T05:19Z) names OrthoFoundation-L's pretraining corpus: OAI (100k X-ray + 200k MRI slices), fastMRI (300k knee MRI slices), and a PUTH internal cohort. That answers the leakage question well — RSNA is not a pretraining source, the private cohort is Peking University Third Hospital, wrong institutions and wrong collection window — so the seat is licensed for development.

But it creates a licence conflict nobody has adjudicated, and it lands on the trunk we are about to build a shippable member from.

This project's own reading is that fastMRI is CLOSED for shipping under NYU DSA section 5(c): weights DERIVED from it cannot go in a Kaggle kernel, though it is fine as an internal instrument. OrthoFoundation-L is derived from fastMRI, among two other corpora. So two facts now point opposite ways: Kimi quotes the repo as MIT, which would permit re-hosting, and our fastMRI reading would forbid exactly this derivative.

The question is whose obligation is whose. The MIT grant is the OrthoFoundation authors releasing THEIR weights. Our NYU DSA obligation arises from OUR acceptance when we downloaded fastMRI. It is not obvious that section 5(c) reaches weights a third party derived and released, and it is equally not obvious that it does not, given we are a DSA acceptor re-hosting the derivative.

This must be settled BEFORE ortho_pool_read's number is treated as a seat rather than a probe, because the whole reason the read matters is that MIT appeared to give it a shipping path. If the answer is no, the trunk stays an internal instrument and its number is worth only what an unshippable probe is worth.

Blocks any Kaggle re-host of OrthoFoundation-L weights. Does NOT block the running read, which is internal.

title: listen_for_mail prints a re-arm command its own parser rejects
description:
On exit the listener prints: python .agent-runtime/listen_for_mail.py --name claude 86000. The parser takes a POSITIONAL timeout only, so that exact line dies with 'invalid timeout: --name', exit 2. Cost one wasted re-arm this session, and the failure mode is the bad one: the harness reports a background task that failed, but a less careful re-arm would leave the mailbox unwatched while everything looks healthy.

Two defects in one line. The flag does not exist, and the PATH names the peer's script rather than this side's, which is the exact mistake CLAUDE.md warns arms a watcher on the wrong directory. Correct line for this side: python .claude/listen_for_mail.py 86000.

Fix the printed hint to be the command that actually works, resolved from the script's own directory so each side prints its own path.

title: fastmri_findings.csv asserts almost no positives: Fracture, Effusion, Meniscus and OA are 100% negative, MCL has 4
description:
Measured 2026-09-03 04:49Z directly on the built table at processed/.../labels/fastmri_findings.csv, 1172 rows, before arming anything against it.

VALUE COUNTS, per column, over the rows that are not NaN:
  ACL              1071 at 0.28, 101 at 0.82
  MCL              1168 at 0.28, 4 at 0.82
  Fracture         1053 at 0.28, ZERO positives
  Effusion         1030 at 0.28, ZERO positives
  Medial Meniscus   509 at 0.28, ZERO positives
  (Lateral Meniscus, the three OA columns and Contusion are the same shape.)

This is not a defect in the builder - it is the documented design arriving at its logical end, and it is
recorded here because the CONSEQUENCE was being got wrong in conversation. fastmri_corpus.py:186 states
that a coarse term BLOCKS THE NEGATIVE rather than asserting a positive: a "Meniscus Tear" carries no
side so it is unknown on both meniscus columns, and BONE_INJURY is the single merged term
"Bone-Fracture/Contusion/dislocation" which cannot separate our Fracture from our Contusion. So every
coarse-term positive becomes NaN (that is exactly why Fracture holds 1053 of 1172 rows and Medial
Meniscus only 509) and what survives in the column is the confident NEGATIVE.

ACL and MCL are the only two findings fastMRI+ grades finely enough to assert on both sides, and MCL
turns out to assert 4 times in 1172 studies.

WHAT THIS KILLS. The pitch that fastMRI supplies CORONAL MCL supervision - MCL being our weakest finding
per knee-ii0q - is dead on arrival at n=4. Any arm built to collect it would have measured its own
sampling noise. Equally the owner's fracture-transfer idea (train on the foreign corpora for Fracture,
test on ours) cannot be run on this corpus at all: there are zero Fracture positives to train on.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is worth stating rather than discarding the corpus:
  (a) 101 coronal ACL positives. Rijeka already supervises ACL sagittally, so this is the same finding in
      the other plane - a real cross-plane test, but ACL is not one of our deficit findings.
  (b) ~1000 confident NEGATIVES per column on findings where our own table is text-mined and over-calls
      (knee-ds2e: the report ruler over-calls by 108 to 37). Negative supervision against an over-calling
      target is mechanistically the right direction. It is also, under a per-label rank AUC, the weak
      direction - adding negatives moves prevalence, not the positive ordering.

PRICE, so nobody arms it on enthusiasm: 1,172 studies is a quarter-doubling on our own concave dose
curve, ~+0.002, and this corpus was explicitly built for what its labels ARE rather than for volume.
With the KIND argument now measured down to 101 ACL positives plus negatives, there is no path here to
the 1.5% bar. DO NOT give it card time ahead of the ConvNeXt ladder or the ortho arm.

WHERE THE REMAINING VALUE ACTUALLY IS: knee-1w6t. The 16,167 box coordinates are read and discarded at
fastmri_corpus.py:391, and the AREA THRESHOLD use is precisely what would convert some of these 0.28
cells into confident labels - box w*h against the per-exam spacing read from the ISMRMRD header. That is
the only route by which this table gains positives. It is cheap and it should be measured before any arm
is written against the corpus as it stands.

title: Make --hold-annotations the default for every new arm: 1.3% of the data buys an honest ruler
description:
The 58 radiologist-annotated studies in raw/train.csv are the ONLY labels this project owns that are not LLM-read report text. 2026-09-03 measured what that ruler is worth: report_labels_v2 disagrees with the radiologist on 20.8% of cells, one-directionally (108 over-calls to 37 under-calls), and the pool beats its own training target by +0.0516 against the radiologist, CI [+0.0296,+0.0729].

But that ruler is unusable for almost every member on disk. A member trained normally has seen the 58, so its gold read is contaminated; only 13 of the 58 fall in the fold-0 holdout, and n=13 reads nothing. TODAY EXACTLY EIGHT MEMBERS of 177 scoreable can be read on gold, all of them because somebody passed --hold-annotations for a different reason.

PROPOSAL: --hold-annotations becomes the default for every new arm, opt-OUT rather than opt-in.

COST: 58 of 4406 training studies, 1.3%. Every member weights annotated studies at 3.0, so the effective loss is larger than 1.3% but still small, and it is a CONSTANT across arms, so it costs nothing in any comparison - which is what arms are for.

BUY: every future member gets a read against a ruler that is not the report reader. That is the only defence this project has against the whole ledger being an internally-consistent fit to a target that over-calls by a third. It also makes the 58 usable as a CHECK on any label-side change, which is the axis knee-8wa0 opened and knee-5oxzo widened.

WHAT IT IS NOT. The 58 are 1.47x finding-enriched and n=58 with 9-35 positives a label, so gold is a LEVEL and never a SELECTOR - it can say a member is better than its target, it cannot rank two members. Nothing here proposes seating on a gold number.

DECIDE BEFORE THE NEXT ARM IS WRITTEN: this is a default in experiments/lib.sh, so it costs one line and only applies going forward.

Do not guess - the next time an arm is on the card, run the pre-push pytest with the card already full and watch whether the arm survives.

title: BOARD_RESOLVABLE raised 0.0015 -> 0.0040: the old value sat inside the measured inversion band
description:
Kimi's Q-CA sweep (2026-09-02T23:16Z) over comp/board.jsonl: 34 rows carry both an honest offline number and a board number = 561 ordered pairs. 35 of them (6.2 pct) INVERT - the entry with the higher offline scored lower on the board. The largest offline separation at which the record still inverts is 0.0037 (gradeswap_v1 0.8694 -> board 0.933 against peak8_v1 0.8731 -> board 0.932). Above ~0.004 the ordering is stable.

BOARD_RESOLVABLE was 0.0015, fitted on SIX pairs (knee-825t) as 'the plateau longseat's +0.0012 tie sits above'. That is not a conservative floor - it sits squarely inside the band where the ruler is now measured to get the SIGN wrong. Raised to 0.0040 in kneemri/evaluation/member_curve.py with the argument in the docstring.

WHAT THIS RE-OPENS: every decision taken on an offline delta between 0.0015 and 0.0037 was made by a ruler that inverts there. Both directions - arms killed for a small negative and seats taken for a small positive. The prose in ten kernel docstrings still quotes 0.0015 in pre-registrations already scored; those are history and are left as written, but no NEW pre-registration may use 0.0015.

TWO LIMITS, stated: the board quantises to 0.001 and its own sampling SE is several times that (Q-BX), so an inversion of one quantum is one rounding step and 6.2 pct is an upper bound on real disagreement. What 0.0037 bounds is the separation at which disagreement stops appearing at all. Checked against the single-cell trap: crossenc_v1 is the most-involved row at 5 of 35, so no one cell carries the count.

title: Fair-penalty probe reverses the trunk ordering: ortholarge +0.020 over dinov2-large, radnet121 +0.015, on BOTH readouts
description: Run 2026-09-02 22:22Z, feature_probe --choose-penalty (nested split inside the training positions, holdout untouched), 909 fold-0 studies. At each trunk's OWN penalty: ortholarge@focal-max 0.8249 (p=1.0), radnet121@focal-max 0.8197 (p=0.003), dinov2-large@focal-max 0.8048 (p=30), v3large@focal-max 0.8046 (p=3), vjepa2-large 0.7985 (p=10), dinov2-small 0.7896 (p=100), orthodiff@gap256 0.7435 (p=0.3). On the mean_max caches the same ordering holds: ortholarge 0.8170 (p=0.1) vs v3large 0.7968 (p=0.3) vs dinov2-large 0.7996 (p=10). THE CONTROLLED READING: ortholarge is v3large continued on 1.25M knee images and identical otherwise, so its +0.0203 (focal-max) and +0.0202 (mean_max) over v3large is in-domain SSL continuation measured on the only controlled pair the project can build - and the SAME delta on two readouts makes it a trunk property, not a pooling artefact.
