title: board.jsonl offline anchors and vote_ceiling/stack_fit numbers are three different estimators quoted as one
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-02T22:00Z, no card, no slot.

vote_ceiling over the five fold-0 twins (calib_span_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, merged_blend_cf, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026), 909 shared studies:
  RankAverage 0.8700 | QualityWeightedRank 0.8700 | LabelQualityRank 0.8701 | LogitAverage 0.8706 | MedianLogit 0.8676

aucvote_v1's and stackvote_v1's SUBMISSION MESSAGES both state 'offline over five fold-0 twins on 909 studies ... LogitAverage 0.8745'. That 0.8745 is not this pool. It is knee-xsfc's close note verbatim -- 'Six-seat one-decode shipping shape: LogitAverage 0.8745' -- a SIX-member number carried into a five-member claim by prose, exactly the failure mode CLAUDE.md records for board_transfer's slope being quoted wrong twice.

There are at least three estimators in play and the ledger does not distinguish them:
  1. vote_ceiling  -- split-half, weights fitted on one half, scored on the other, both ways averaged.
  2. stack_fit     -- split-half with a NESTED penalty split inside the fitting half.
  3. comp/board.jsonl 'offline' -- whole-holdout pool AUC over 909 studies (honest12 0.8751 over twelve, peak8 0.8704 over eight, greedyseat_v1 0.8740 bias-corrected).

Only (3) is what board_transfer regresses board scores against. A split-half number is systematically LOWER than a whole-holdout one at the same pool, so pairing a vote_ceiling reading into board.jsonl would bend the fitted slope upward and every arm priced off it afterwards.

WHAT TO DO. (a) Record the estimator that produced every 'offline' value in board.jsonl as a required field, and make board_check refuse a row that does not name one -- it already refuses a row with no selection and a row over an all-data pool, so this is the same class of guard. (b) Establish which module produced the whole-holdout pool numbers already in the file and make it the single named entrypoint. (c) Re-read aucvote_v1's and stackvote_v1's board messages: both argued a combiner delta against 0.8745; against the correct 0.8706 for their own fitting pool the deltas change size, though the FLAT board reading (0.943, 0.943 vs champion 0.944) does not change.

DOES NOT CHANGE: the combiner axis still reads flat on the board across three vote rules inside 0.001.

title: Implement RememberedMargin objective for rare labels
description:
From training-pipeline audit (interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-02_training_pipeline_audit.md).

title: Stacking measured: a learned combiner beats every fixed rule on three pools, all under the noise floor
description:
kneemri/inference/stacked.py, 2026-09-02. First LEARNED combiner in the project; every Vote subclass before it is fixed. Per-label ridge over member logits, fitted on half the 909 holdout studies, scored on the other half, penalty chosen by a NESTED split inside the fitting half. 6 members +0.0015, 12 members +0.0021, 24 members +0.0009 over the best fixed rule. Beats LogitAverage and RankAverage on all three; every delta under the 0.0062 floor. Directional only.

HARNESS BUG FOUND AND FIXED, recorded because it nearly became a finding: the first version centred the target but not the design and fitted no intercept. Read 0.8587 held-out, a 0.0173 LOSS, which would have been written down as 'stacking refuted on a correlated pool'. It was misfit, not overfit - the IN-SAMPLE number was 0.8616, also below LogitAverage's held-out 0.8760, and a combiner that loses on the studies it fitted on is broken. Always report the in-sample number beside the held-out one; it is what catches this.

TWO READINGS, unseparated, sent to Kimi as Q-BH. A: the pool is one scalar (competence_axis 81.7-82%), a stacker can only redistribute ambiguity, +0.002 is all there is. B: 909 studies is the constraint - 144 parameters against ~455 scoring studies at 5% prevalence starves it, and a shared-weight combiner would be the cheap next arm. Q-BH asks for a published stacking LEARNING CURVE, which is the only thing that separates them.

TRANSFER LIMIT: only fold-0 members have holdout predictions, and the six we SHIP are --fold -1. Weights fitted here reach the shipped pool only under the same twin assumption comp/kernels/kneemri-aucvote states for its per-label AUCs.

title: Q-AZ answer: lateral meniscus deficit is acquisition + label noise
description:
# Q-AZ answer: lateral meniscus deficit is acquisition + label noise

## Question (from Claude)

Is the lateral-meniscus deficit (−0.20 on the 58-study annotation ruler) an **acquisition** fact or a **label** fact?

## Q-AZ-1 — Plane and resolution

### Published evidence

- **Yang et al. 2025** (MRNet-derived TripleMRNet, *Quant Imaging Med Surg*) — for meniscal tear detection, **the axial plane markedly outperformed sagittal and coronal; sagittal was worst**. 3-plane model ACC 0.783; sagittal-only ACC 0.633. ([PMC12209677](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12209677/))
- **Gökalp et al. 2012** (thin 1 mm axial PDW, 50 patients, arthroscopy gold) — lateral meniscus sensitivity: **sagittal 72.7%, axial 95.7%**; specificity: sagittal 77.1%, axial 80.6%. Thin axial slices also classified tear types accurately. ([BJR 2012](https://acikerisim.uludag.edu.tr/server/api/core/bitstreams/62208837-0636-4dab-9184-d6cd5eab1ed3/content))
- **Joshi et al. 2021** (prospective, 168 cases, arthroscopy gold) — overall lateral meniscus sensitivity **68.2%** vs medial 92.9%; in ACL-deficient knees lateral sensitivity **50.0%** vs ACL-intact 83.3%. Most missed lateral tears were posterior horn. ([JASSM 2021](https://jassm.org/accuracy-of-magnetic-resonance-imaging-for-meniscal-body-tear-in-anterior-cruciate-ligament-deficient-knees-compared-to-anterior-cruciate-ligament-intact-knee/))
- **Kim et al. 2021** (544 patients, arthroscopy gold) — lateral meniscus MRI sensitivity **80.7%** vs medial 91.8%; lateral accuracy in ACL-injured **72.9%** vs ACL-intact **88.0%**. ([PMC7914628](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7914628/))

### Anatomy

The posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is harder to image than the medial: the lateral meniscus is more curved and thinner, the posterior horn is obscured by the popliteus tendon and meniscofemoral ligaments (Wrisberg/Humphrey), and it is prone to magic-angle and pulsation artifacts. Axial images view the meniscus in cross-section and are better for tear orientation and classification.

### What this means for our pipeline

Our canonical six slots (`core/data/corpus/slots.py:60-67`) already include `AX_FLUID_FS`, so axial is **present**. But it is **one of six equal 12-slice slots**. Published work suggests axial should be **dominant** for meniscus, and thin axial (1 mm) is better than the thicker slices we likely resample to. The lever is therefore not "add axial" but:
- **weigh axial more** in the decode / slot pooling,
- **decode axial at higher resolution**, and/or
- use **extended slots** (`COR_FLUID_NOFS`, `AX_T1`, `AX_FLUID_NOFS`) — 83,297 slices currently unseen, measured in `slots.py:79-95`.

## Q-AZ-2 — The ruler

### Report-derived vs arthroscopy-confirmed prevalence

- **Kim 2021**: arthroscopy prevalence was medial 48.1%, lateral 49.9% (nearly equal). MRI reports called medial tears in 55.6% (overcalled) and lateral tears in 47.5% (undercalled). Lateral sensitivity was 80.7% vs medial 91.8%.
- **Joshi 2021**: lateral sensitivity 68.2% overall, 50.0% in ACL-deficient knees.

Radiologists **under-detect lateral tears** relative to arthroscopy. Because our labels are report-derived, the lateral-meniscus column is noisier and contains more false negatives than the medial column. Part of our low AUC is therefore the **ruler**, not the model.

### How much is ruler vs acquisition?

Not cleanly separable from published numbers. The acquisition literature says lateral is genuinely harder to image; the ruler literature says the label itself is less reliable. The label-noise part cannot be recovered with architecture.

## Bottom line

- The deficit is **both acquisition and label noise**.
- The practical, competition-actionable lever is **acquisition**: an axial-dominant / high-resolution / ACL-context-aware member for lateral meniscus.
- There is **no label lever** — the report-derived targets are fixed.

## Recommended arms

1. **Axial-weighted meniscus member** — keep the six canonical slots but allocate more slices or attention to `AX_FLUID_FS` for the meniscus labels.
2. **Extended-slot cache** — add `COR_FLUID_NOFS`, `AX_T1`, and `AX_FLUID_NOFS`; this surfaces 83k currently unused slices without changing the head geometry.
3. **Thin-slice axial decode** — if the source DICOMs support sub-millimeter axial, build a cache that preserves thin axial resolution for the meniscus labels.
4. **ACL-context head** — a small auxiliary input or attention gate that conditions meniscus predictions on ACL status, since lateral meniscus accuracy drops sharply in ACL-injured knees.

## Sources

- Yang G, Shi Y, Li Q. *A comparative analysis of sagittal, coronal, and axial magnetic resonance imaging planes in diagnosing anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tears via a deep learning model: emphasizing the unexpected importance of the axial plane*. Quant Imaging Med Surg 2025;15(6):5811-5824.
- Gökalp G et al. *Contribution of thin-slice (1 mm) axial proton density MR images for identification and classification of meniscal tears*. Br J Radiol 2012;85:e871-e878.
- Joshi A et al. *Accuracy of magnetic resonance imaging for meniscal body tear in anterior cruciate ligament-deficient knees compared to anterior cruciate ligament-intact knee*. J Arthrosc Surg Sport Med 2021;2(1):18-25.
- Kim SH et al. *Diagnostic Accuracy of Magnetic Resonance Imaging in the Detection of Type and Location of Meniscus Tears: Comparison with Arthroscopic Findings*. JCM 2021;10(4):606.

title: Per-pathology SOTA knee-MRI models and headroom vs our seats
description:
# Per-pathology SOTA knee-MRI models and headroom vs our seats

## Context

Previous notes already mapped our per-label AUCs to the published frontier:
- `research/2026-08-23_published-per-label-auc-vs-ours.md` — annotation-ruler comparison over the 58 gold studies.
- `research/2026-09-02_sota_pretrained_knee_mri_models_2025_2026.md` — foundation-model survey.

This bead updates the picture with newer per-pathology papers (2024–2026) and reframes the question the owner asked: **stop looking for one generalist knee model and look for SOTA models per pathology**.

## Our labels

From `core.findings.TARGETS`:
ACL, MCL, Medial Meniscus, Lateral Meniscus, Medial OA, Lateral OA, PF OA, Effusion, Synovitis, Baker's, Contusion, Fracture.

Known report-ruler leaders from `seat_profile` (Claude Q-AX, 2026-09-02): MCL 0.8253, Fracture 0.8214, Baker's 0.9215, Medial Meniscus 0.9135. Annotation-ruler numbers from the 58 gold studies are in the 2026-08-23 note.

## Per-pathology SOTA table

| Our label | Published best AUC / metric | Source | Type | Notes | Headroom signal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ACL** | 0.965 internal / 0.911 external retrained | MRNet (Bien et al. 2018, PLOS Med) [link](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371/journal.pmed.1002699) | Specialist 3-slice CNN | Historic benchmark; internal AUC very high, external lower. | Near ceiling on report ruler; annotation-ruler gap was −0.10 vs OrthoFoundation. |
| **ACL** | 0.99 (ACL-SNet) | Xue et al. 2024 (Sci Rep) [link](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38195977/) | Specialist DL + radiomics | 862 patients, sagittal PD; also reports ACL-DNet Dice 0.98. | Ceiling is high; likely label-definition dependent. |
| **ACL** | 0.89 (partial + complete tears, external) | Vuskov et al. 2025/2026 (Eur Radiol) [link](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00330-025-12052-8) | Generalist 23-condition ResNet18+3D+Transformer | Multi-condition, external Aachen; no single-condition tuning. | Realistic external SOTA for a generalist. |
| **MCL** | 0.9334 | OrthoFoundation-L (Yu et al. 2026) [link](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.18250) | Knee-specific ViT-L continuation | Binary MCL injury on large internal test. | Our report-ruler leader 0.8253 is **~0.11 below** this optimistic number. |
| **MCL** | 0.9191 | OrthoDiffusion (Lan et al. 2026) [link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20752) | Knee-specific 3D diffusion | One of 8 diagnostic labels. | Strong target, but model is 3D diffusion, not 2D slice. |

| **MCL** | 0.88 external tear | Vuskov et al. 2025/2026 | Generalist 23-condition | External test; broader MCL tear definition. | Suggests MCL is **not** an intrinsic floor; there is room. |
| **Medial Meniscus** | 0.936 (meniscal horns) | Astuto et al. 2021 (Radiol AI) [link](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34142088/) | Multi-tissue 3D CNN+segmentation | 1,435 studies, WORMS grading. | Our 0.9135 is close; small headroom. |
| **Medial Meniscus** | 0.925 (medial horn, pooled) | Botnari et al. 2024 meta-analysis [link](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11172202/) | Meta-analysis of DL meniscus models | Pooled AUC; specialist models. | Confirms near-ceiling. |
| **Medial Meniscus** | 0.88 internal / 0.83 external | Vuskov et al. 2025/2026 | Generalist 23-condition | External Aachen. | Realistic external SOTA, below our 0.9135. |
| **Lateral Meniscus** | 0.844 (lateral horn, pooled) | Botnari 2024 meta-analysis | Meta-analysis | Lateral horn is consistently harder. | Annotation-ruler gap was −0.20; largest known field-relative deficit. |
| **Lateral Meniscus** | 0.84 / 0.77 external | Rizk 2021 / Vuskov 2025 | Specialist 3D CNN / generalist | External validation drops sharply. | Targeted lever if our lateral-meniscus AUC is low. |
| **Cartilage / OA** | 0.917 | Liu et al. 2018 (Radiology) [link](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6166867/) | Segmentation→patch classifier | Patch-level cartilage lesion detection on 175 patients. | OA labels in our task are whole-compartment severity, not patch lesions. |
| **Cartilage / OA** | 0.93 | Astuto 2021 | Multi-tissue 3D CNN | Cartilage AUC across compartments. | Medial OA already beat this on annotation ruler (0.9504); PF OA was 0.8005. |
| **Cartilage / OA** | 0.9338 | OrthoFoundation-L | Knee-specific ViT-L | Cartilage lesion AUROC. | Strong target for cartilage-specific models. |
| **OA severity** | 0.830 / 0.866 (KL01 vs KL234 / KL2 vs KL34) | Nurmirinta et al. 2024 (Ann Biomed Eng) [link](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10439-024-03578-x) | RF on MRI morphology + clinical | Future OA severity from OAI; not the same as detecting existing OA. | Low numbers suggest OA severity is hard; our Medial OA 0.95 may be near task ceiling. |
| **Effusion** | 0.94 external | Vuskov 2025/2026 | Generalist 23-condition | One of the highest external AUCs in that study. | Likely near ceiling; do not chase without evidence we are below it. |
| **Baker's** | 0.85 external | Vuskov 2025/2026 | Generalist 23-condition | Distinct imaging feature. | Our 0.9215 is above this external number. |
| **Contusion / BME** | 0.92 standalone AI, sens 0.83, spec 0.95 | Maarek et al. 2025 (Res Diagn Interv Imaging) [link](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40837780/) | Keros/Incepto 3D U-Net segmentation | External validation of BME segmentation/detection. | Annotation-ruler contusion 0.842 is below; BME detection appears to have headroom. |
| **Contusion / BME** | 0.82 external / 0.83 Astuto | Vuskov 2025 / Astuto 2021 | Generalist / multi-tissue | BME is subjective and inter-reader variable. | Modest headroom; may be label-noise limited. |
| **Fracture** | No knee-MRI fracture AUC found | — | — | Literature is radiograph-based (BoneView, Rayvolve, etc.). | Our 0.8214 has no published comparator; treat as unpriceable. |
| **Synovitis** | 0.76 DL / 0.77 senior radiologist | Academic Radiology 2023 (cited in 2026-08-23 note) | Specialist / human | Human ceiling is low. | Retired as a chase target in prior note. |

## What the updated picture says

1. **Lateral Meniscus still carries the largest known field-relative deficit** (−0.20 on the annotation ruler). It is also the consistently hardest horn in published meniscus work. Any model or decode change that specifically improves the lateral horn is high value.
2. **MCL is not an intrinsic floor.** Published numbers range from 0.88 (external generalist) to 0.93 (OrthoFoundation internal). Our report-ruler leader 0.8253 is well below even the conservative external number. The widen-crop arm (knee-ii0q) is already filed for this reason.
3. **ACL has a high specialist ceiling** (0.965–0.99) but realistic external generalist numbers are ~0.89–0.91. The annotation-ruler gap (−0.10 vs OrthoFoundation) is real but may shrink once label definitions are aligned.
4. **Baker's and Effusion look saturated** relative to external SOTA. Do not spend slots chasing them unless a new measurement shows we are below 0.85–0.90.
5. **Fracture and compartment-specific OA (Lateral OA, PF OA) remain unpriceable.** No published AUCs match these exact labels. The low report-ruler leaders for MCL and Fracture are the floor we can see; whether Fracture is model-limited or label-limited is unknown.
6. **Contusion/BME has modest headroom** against the Keros external number, but the task is inter-reader variable.

## Actionable takeaways

- **Lateral Meniscus:** favour models that explicitly model horn location / meniscus compartments (e.g., attention over localized horns, 3D context, or auxiliary segmentation). OrthoDiffusion includes LM as one of its 8 labels and may transfer.
- **MCL:** pursue the widen-FOV arm and/or a coronal-focused member; MCL sits at the field margin and is cropped in our 130 mm centre crop.
- **ACL:** the specialist ceiling is very high; the realistic lever is better multi-plane fusion or 3D context (OrthoDiffusion) rather than more 2D slice tuning.
- **Cartilage/OA:** compartment-specific severity is poorly covered in literature. External OAI data with MOAKS/WORMS grading is the only path to a stronger prior.
- **Stop chasing:** Baker's cyst, effusion, and synovitis unless new evidence appears.
- **Highest-impact untested public model:** OrthoDiffusion (3D diffusion) is the only public knee-specific multi-label 3D foundation model; 5 of its 8 labels map directly to our task. Smoke-test remains the top priority for a new member family.

title: OrthoDiffusion volumetric trunk: probe against the 2D trunks
description:
The slice-AGGREGATION stage is saturated from both ends (max-pool, attention, moments, focal readouts all inside each other's noise floor); the standing diagnosis is that the limit is upstream, in what one slice feature vector contains. Every trunk measured so far encodes ONE SLICE. OrthoDiffusion (arXiv:2602.20752, MIT weights, three plane-specific 3D denoising U-Nets over musculoskeletal MRI) consumes the stack inside the encoder, which is the axis the diagnosis names.

Built: kneemri/models/diffusion_schedule.py, ortho_diffusion.py, ortho_weights.py, kneemri/embeddings/build_ortho_embeddings.py. Frozen encoder, GAP over the middle block, per-plane block+timestep from their LP-Opt, no new deps (their trainer.py chain is avoided by reimplementing q_sample).

CONFOUND, must be quoted with any reading: their middle block is 256 wide against dinov2-large's 1024. A ridge probe is width-sensitive, so a LOSS is confounded with capacity and only a WIN is clean.

PRICE: ~40 min encode of 4407 studies off the arm plus a 2 min probe. Gain if it carries: the readout lane is closed at +0.0043 against a 0.0465 trunk gap, so a trunk that reads 3D structure is the only open thing sized at 1.5%. P(clears the 1.5% bar) ~0.15, but it is the ONLY untried axis and a null closes the 3D-representation lever cheaply.

Read against dinov2-large 0.7852 / v3large 0.7446 / ortholarge 0.7387 on the same n=909 fold-0 holdout.

title: Q-AX — Is MCL low for everyone in published knee-MRI work?
description:
# Q-AX — Is MCL low for everyone in published knee-MRI work?

## Short answer

No. In published knee-MRI multi-label work, MCL is **not** consistently the weakest label. It usually sits in the middle of the per-label table, often **above meniscus** and sometimes above ACL. The fact that our MCL leader (0.8253) is the floor of our 12-label roster while our meniscus labels are near the top is an unusual shape that points back at our labels / crop, not at an intrinsic MCL ceiling.

## Per-label AUC tables from MRI work

### 1. CoPAS (Qiu et al., 2024) — 12-abnormality multi-sequence MRI, arthroscopy-confirmed labels
Internal-center AUC-ROC (Table 2):

| Label | AUC |
|-------|-----|
| ACL   | 0.949 |
| CYST  | 0.862 |
| PLICA | 0.877 |
| LCL   | 0.816 |
| CONT  | 0.821 |
| CART  | 0.790 |
| **MCL** | **0.782** |
| EFFU  | 0.787 |
| MENI  | 0.763 |
| IFP   | 0.734 |
| PR    | 0.767 |
| Average | 0.812 |

MCL is 7th of 12 — not a floor. MENI and IFP are lower. External cross-validation gives similar ordering: MCL 0.722 vs MENI 0.688 on one external set, MCL 0.772 vs MENI 0.690 on the other.

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11368947/

### 2. OrthoDiffusion (Lan et al., 2026) — 8-abnormality multi-label MRI, private multi-center data
Full fine-tuning AUC (Table 3):

| Label | AUC |
|-------|-----|
| PD (patellar cartilage / chondral lesion) | 0.9926 |
| ACL   | 0.9704 |
| PCL   | 0.9373 |
| **MCL** | **0.9191** |
| CART?/MM | 0.8724 |
| LM    | 0.8502 |
| LCL   | 0.8577 |
| EFFU  | 0.8635 |
| Macro | 0.9079 |

MCL is 4th of 8 and well above both meniscus labels.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20752

### 3. Vuskov et al. (2025, Eur Radiol) — 23-condition routine knee MRI, report-extracted labels
External-test AUC (Table 2):

| Label | AUC |
|-------|-----|
| ACL tear (partial/complete) | 0.89 |
| **MCL tear (partial/complete)** | **0.88** |
| Medial meniscus tear | 0.83 |
| Bone marrow edema | 0.82 |
| Lateral meniscus tear | 0.77 |

MCL tear outperforms both meniscus tears and bone-marrow edema.

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13035746/

### 4. Lancet eClinicalMedicine 2025 (Xie et al.) — 9-abnormality multi-task DLS
The main text reports group AUCs only (primary 0.898 internal / 0.852 external I / 0.812 external II; secondary 0.815 / 0.744 / 0.774). Per-label AUCs are in Supplementary Table S7 (not retrieved). The published accuracy numbers place MCL injury comparable to ACL and meniscus tear (DLS accuracy 87.1% vs senior radiologist 85.7% for MCL).

Source: https://www.thelancet.com/pdfs/journals/eclinm/PIIS2589-5370(25)00467-5.pdf

### 5. OrthoFoundation (Yu et al., 2026) — binary MRI tasks (not multi-label)
Not directly comparable, but shows MCL is a high-AUC task when labels are clean:

| Task | AUC |
|------|-----|
| ACL injury | 0.9849 |
| MCL injury | 0.9334 |
| Cartilage lesion | 0.9338 |

Source: https://github.com/ytrsk/OrthoFoundation

### 6. X-ray screening paper (Yasin et al., 2025) — not MRI, for shape only
External-test ResNet152 AUCs:

| Label | AUC |
|-------|-----|
| EFFU  | 0.863 |
| MENI  | 0.831 |
| LCL   | 0.799 |
| STI   | 0.786 |
| ACL   | 0.783 |
| PCL   | 0.780 |
| **MCL** | **0.770** |
| CONT  | 0.764 |

MCL is low-ish but not separated from ACL/PCL/CONT.

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12575809/

## Reader-agreement evidence

A 2016 prospective MRI-vs-arthroscopy study reports Cohen's kappa:

| Structure | κ |
|-----------|---|
| ACL | 0.84 |
| PCL | 0.79 |
| **MCL** | **0.71** |
| LCL | 0.68 |
| Meniscus | 0.62 |

MCL is more reproducible than meniscus reading. The noise is not disproportionately on MCL.

Source: https://healthcare-bulletin.co.uk/article/mri-based-assessment-of-knee-ligament-injuries-a-prospective-study-5030/

## Implication for us

- Our MCL leader (0.8253) is **below** the MCL numbers in OrthoDiffusion (0.919) and Vuskov (0.88), but **above** CoPAS internal MCL (0.782). The gap to the best published MCL is real but not universal.
- The more unusual signal is the **relative** ordering: in every comparable multi-label MRI table, MCL is **at or above meniscus**; in our roster it is far below. That shape is not explained by MCL being intrinsically hard.
- The 130 mm centre crop costs MCL −0.0265 (the largest per-label crop hit, matched only by ACL). Because MCL and ACL live at the field margins, widening the crop (knee-ii0q) is the architecture-side lever most specifically aimed at this finding. The published tables do not close that lane; they suggest MCL is recoverable.
- The alternative explanation — label quality for MCL in our report-extracted training set — is not contradicted by the literature. Vuskov used report-extracted labels and reached 0.88 MCL, but their reports were from a high-volume radiology practice and cross-checked by board-certified radiologists. Our labels are LLM-extracted from free-text RSNA reports.

## Recommendation

The lane to revisit is the one already filed: **knee-ii0q** (widen crop, rebuild cache). The published evidence says MCL is not a natural floor; the strongest internal evidence says MCL is disproportionately hurt by the 130 mm centre crop. Do not open a new architecture axis for MCL until the crop/label-quality axis has been measured.

title: readout_probe's --slice-read never reached the encoder: the eight focal caches are four bit-identical pairs
description:
VERIFIED 2026-09-02. feature_probe over the four trunks x {focal-max, focal-attend} returns IDENTICAL means to 4dp: dinov2-large 0.8034/0.8034, v3large 0.7829/0.7829. Two arms with identical output is a flag that did not land, not a null.

Direct check: features_large_336px_12sl_r252_cls_mean_focal_max.npy and ..._focal_attend.npy are both 1,949,515,904 bytes, both shape (4407, 6, 12, 3072) float16, np.array_equal True on the first 8 studies, max abs diff 0.0. They are the same array written twice under two names. All four trunk pairs are the same size, so this is 4 duplicated pairs, ~7.8 GB wasted with the disk at 94%.

CAUSE: the cache key is '_'.join([variant, source, r{read_size}, pool, slice_read]) (embedding_cache.py), so slice_read enters the FILENAME. But the stored array keeps the slice axis (12) either way — the encoder does not consume slices — so 'max' and 'attend' name the same bytes. The slice pooling happens downstream, and feature_probe.pooled() reduces with .mean(axis=(1,2)) (feature_probe.py:113) regardless of which cache it opened.

CONSEQUENCE FOR knee-n647: its pre-registered branch CANNOT be taken from these caches. Had the probe been run and reported without this check, the lane would have closed on the slice axis with a flag that never fired — the exact failure this project has paid for before.

THE OPENING: the slice axis IS preserved in the cache, so a real slice-aggregation readout is a change to feature_probe's reduction alone — mean/max/learned-query over axis 2 — with no encoder pass and no card. That is knee-02vn's card-free half and it is available now.

FIX: either make slice_read affect the stored array or drop it from the cache key; and delete the four duplicate .npy files once the probe reads a single cache per trunk.

title: The widened-pool offline maximum does not reach the champion, and the board record says why
description:
record_mix greedy over the 159-member widened pool (D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/*.pt, --largest-pool --seats greedy --paired) peaks at 0.8774 with 23-25 seats. The curve's shape is the reading, not the peak: 0.8642 at one seat, 0.8770 at SEVEN, 0.8774 at 23-25. The last eighteen members buy +0.0004 -- a fifteenth of the 0.0062 floor -- at eighteen times the kernel runtime, so the seven-seat set [stack_increments, labelwise_dense, merged_span_cf, margin_seat, warm_calib_lowlr, merged_labelwise_cf, finding_calib_dense] carries the whole result.

QUOTE THE POOL SIZE WITH THE NUMBER, per record_mix's own docstring: 0.8774 is over 159 records. The previously quoted maximum, 0.8717 at eight to ten seats, was over a much smaller pool and is not comparable. The +0.0057 between them is a fact about the POOL, not about a method.

WHY IT IS NOT A CANDIDATE. comp/board.jsonl holds 37 priceable entries. The best offline entry ever shipped is honest12 at offline 0.8751, and it scored 0.937. greedyseat_v1 at 0.8740 scored 0.936. board_transfer reads +0.98 board points per holdout point among entries at or above 0.8670 (16 resolved pairs, [+0.94, +1.08]). So 0.8774 predicts 0.937 + 0.0023*0.98 = about 0.939. The champion raptorweight_v1 is 0.944, and it is FIVE POINTS ABOVE the top of the entire offline-selected family. No offline-greedy entry in 37 has ever cleared 0.937.

That gap is not noise and it is not the mix search failing. It is structural: the offline-measurable lane pays for its own measurability, and the champion does not pay it. Maximising the offline number harder cannot close a gap that opens because the number exists at all. This is the third independent reading to say the offline lane tops out below the champion, and it should be quoted whenever an offline maximum is proposed as a submission.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not say the greedy shape is worthless. The seven-seat SHAPE was discovered on measurable members; whether that shape rebuilt on the champion's lane beats the champion is untested and is a different, card-expensive question.

title: Q-AO: run robust label-disagreement experiment
description:
Implement the experiment proposed in research/2026-09-02_test_labels_report_derived_or_radiologist_reviewed_qao.md. The goal is to determine whether the hidden test labels are radiologist-adjudicated or report-derived by measuring whether down-weighting image-report disagreements helps or hurts holdout AUC.

Steps:
1. Build a disagreement head that predicts image-contradicts-report on the 58 gold studies plus any training studies where image-report disagreement can be measured.
2. Use the disagreement signal as an auxiliary loss or sample weight, without overwriting report-derived targets.
3. Train a member on the same trunk/recipe as a control.
4. Measure holdout AUC difference. If positive, test labels are likely adjudicated and label-correction is a live lever; if negative, the axis is an own goal and should be declined in writing.

Costs no new labels and no board slots until direction is proven.

title: Hard per-finding slot routing: the aprior follow-up that cannot wash out
description:
aprior_dense handed the 12x6 anatomy table to SlotHead.prior as an INITIALISATION at strength 2.0 and read 0.8557 vs band_dense 0.8578 (-0.0021). Its train loss tracked the control to the fourth decimal at every epoch, so the prior washed out entirely and the ledger's own conclusion is that the head had already recovered the plane-by-finding mapping from study-level labels alone.

A HARD constraint is a different mechanism: mask the slot attention so a finding's head structurally CANNOT read its non-primary slots. An initialisation the optimiser overwrites and a mask it cannot are not the same experiment, so aprior does not refute this.

WHY P3 AND NOT QUEUED. Its own mechanism predicts a null or a loss: the head demonstrably already has the mapping, so the mask cannot ADD information and can only remove the secondary-plane evidence anatomy.py itself labels secondary rather than absent. ~85 min of card against a mechanism that argues against itself. Runs only if Kimi's Q-AM returns published evidence that per-plane specialists or view-masked heads beat a joint model on a matched split.

Related closed axes, so this is not re-litigated: --focus-label per-label loss weighting refuted twice (experiments/README.md:545,582); per-label member weighting oracle-bounded two orders below the 0.0062 floor (:611); extended_slots (nine slots, 83297 unseen slices) read +0.0002.

Pre-registration if it ever runs: control band_dense 0.8578, twelve epochs, only the slot-attention mask changes. >=+0.0040 the constraint is real and per-finding routing re-opens. 0 to +0.0040 directional, not a seat. <0 the secondary planes carry signal the table calls secondary, which is itself a finding about anatomy.py.

title: The label-side axes are priced and none is a 1.5% lever
description: Kimi's literature pass (research/2026-09-02_label_noise_pseudo_label_partial_labels_literature.md) prices all three label-limited axes with denominators. (1) Pseudo-labelling unlabeled images: Yang 2025 CLCP-MT on ChestX-ray14 gains +2.64% mean AUC at a 4:1 unlabeled:labeled ratio; ours is 1.17:1 (5143 foreign train-only vs 4407 RSNA), and the curve is concave, so the honest extrapolation is +0.002-0.005. fastMRI+SKM-TEA would take us to ~1.4:1, still far from 4:1 - so decoding them is a responsibility, NOT a score lever. (2) Masked-loss on partially-labelled rows (MRNet has pixels + ACL/meniscus; Rijeka has ACL alone): standard and positive but bounded by label density - a one-of-twelve row carries ~1/12 the supervision. (3) Better report-extracted labels: Jain 2021 gets +0.04 AUROC for +0.15 labeler F1 on CheXpert, but our consensus already reads 0.90 macro on gold-58 and knee inter-reader kappa is 0.55-0.72 (Astuto 2021), so the headroom is small and hard to measure. DECISION: none of the three gets card time as a lever. Re-open (1) only if the unlabeled pool grows past ~3:1.

title: Image-report contrastive pretraining (MedCLIP shape) -- the last untested trunk mechanism
description:
Only 58 of 4,407 training studies carry image-read labels; the other 4,349 carry reports. Every use this project has made of those reports goes through DERIVED TARGETS (report_labels_v2 and its blends), and that lane is measured and closed: the second-reading blend reads +0.0034 holdout, +0.0001 marginal seat value, +0.0003 on the board (2026-08-30_label_lane_closes.md), and per-label routing is priced at +0.004, under the 0.0062 floor.

Contrastive image-report pretraining is a DIFFERENT mechanism and it is untested here. It does not produce targets at all -- it shapes the TRUNK by aligning study embeddings with report embeddings, so the supervision that never survives the extraction step reaches the encoder directly. The project's report_supervision refutation was an auxiliary loss on top of a label head, which is not this.

Why it could clear 1.5% where the trunk family did not: OrthoFoundation and RadImageNet both failed by importing a FOREIGN corpus, and this imports nothing -- the pretraining corpus is the competition's own 4,407 studies and their own reports, so there is no domain gap to forget across.

Cost and the honest risk: it is a two-stage build (contrastive stage, then the normal fine-tune) and the first stage is card-heavy. The named failure mode is that 4,407 pairs is one to two orders of magnitude below the corpora MedCLIP-shaped results are reported on, so the pre-registration must be written against a published curve of gain versus pair count, not against a headline number. Blocked on that curve.

title: Trunk-family lane closes: OrthoFoundation reads BELOW its own predecessor
description:
ortho_probe (2026-09-02, frozen linear probe, n=909, penalty=100): dinov2-large 0.7852, v3large 0.7446, ortholarge 0.7387. ortholarge minus v3large = -0.0059, which is the arm's pre-registered REVERSED branch (d <= -0.003), the catastrophic-forgetting shape Ilse et al. report for RAD-DINO on VinDR.

ortho_dense (fine-tuned, 12 epochs, converged at epoch 8) = 0.8452 against its control base224 = 0.8502, i.e. -0.0050. Both the frozen and the fine-tuned read agree in sign and in size, so this is not a probe artifact.

Pre-registered consequence, taken: the in-domain continued-trunk lane CLOSES on the strongest public instance of it. Combined with radnet_family (RadImageNet DenseNet121, 0.6716 against a 0.75 floor), the whole TRUNK-FAMILY lever named in the loop prompt is now spent.

ONE SUSPECT REMAINS BEFORE THIS IS FINAL, and it is plumbing, not science. The converted snapshot holds only config.json and model.safetensors -- no preprocessing document -- so our loader feeds inherited ImageNet mean/std as an argument rather than a read constant, at a resolution and register-token count we also assumed. A trunk loaded almost right probes between chance and v3large, which is exactly the band observed. Q-AF is out to Kimi asking the paper for the normalization triple, the continuation resolution, and whether the release is the student or the EMA teacher. If the answer is 'silent', the constant has to be recovered empirically before this closes for good.

title: Q-AA: metadata-conditioning seat for train_series.csv fields
description: Implement and evaluate a metadata-conditioning variant of a current whole-stack member. The per-series fields Fluid_Sensitive, Fat_Suppression and Anatomical_Plane are available in test_series.csv, clean, and literature (Meta-D, Dohmen et al. 2026) shows +2-3 pp gains from conditioning a vision model on analogous MRI metadata. Start with late concatenation or FiLM; control is the same member without metadata. Full audit in research/2026-09-02_series_metadata_axis_audit.md.
acceptance_criteria: A scored run and a seat comparison showing AUC delta vs image-only control; decision on whether to promote to a roster member.
notes: AUDIT BEFORE CLAIM, 2026-09-02: the premise is wrong by two thirds. kneemri/evaluation/study_series.py:8-11 records that Anatomical_Plane is CONSTANT (all 4,407 training studies carry Axial, Coronal and Sagittal alike) and Fat_Suppression EQUALS Fluid_Sensitive on all 24,371 rows; population_split.py:151 asserts the duplication at runtime. So the conditioning axis is ONE binary field, not three. That field is already consumed upstream by the slot router (raptor_feed.py:263,267; slot_fill.py:40; submission.py:346), so a FiLM head re-injects a bit the sampler already used to choose the slices. Kimi's citations do not reach the claim either: Dohmen +3pp and Liang >99.9% are series CLASSIFICATION (predicting sequence type from metadata naming it) - the redundant case, and Liang is evidence AGAINST since a fitted trunk reads sequence off pixels. Meta-D is the only real positive and is FiLM over sequence+PLANE, and plane is constant here. Sent 2026-09-02_0135z asking (1) for evidence on a single already-consumed binary flag improving DIAGNOSTIC classification, (2) Meta-D's plane-vs-sequence ablation split. Empty answer = decline. No card until then.
close_reason: DECLINED on mechanism, 2026-09-02. Two of three columns carry no information (study_series.py:8-11: Anatomical_Plane constant across all 4,407 studies; Fat_Suppression == Fluid_Sensitive on all 24,371 rows, asserted at population_split.py:151). The surviving binary field is already consumed by the slot router (raptor_feed.py:263,267, slot_fill.py:40, submission.py:346), so a FiLM/concat head re-injects a bit that already chose the input slices. Kimi's follow-up audit supplies the rule: Vincent 2020 conditioned a U-Net on T2 vs T2star and found INCONCLUSIVE gains because 'the modality-related features might already be encoded in the regular U-Net'; Lemay 2021's +5.1% Dice lands only when the metadata is TUMOR TYPE, a property not inferable from the image. Metadata conditioning pays only when the field carries information the pixels do not - Fluid_Sensitive fails that on both counts. Meta-D (the one positive precedent) never ablates plane vs sequence, and plane is constant here, so it cannot be assumed to transfer. Also declined the weaker StudySeries.counts()/.fluid() variant: series count proxies protocol length proxies site, which is a shortcut the hidden private split exists to punish - worse than null, not a weak positive.

title: after.sh 'pid:N' mode fires INSTANTLY on a Windows pid, and it put a second job on the card
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-01 23:22Z. after.sh accepts a marker of the form 'pid:N' and waits for that process to exit before starting the arms it owes. I armed a chain with 'pid:15916', the pid card_check printed for the running disagreed_ramp arm. It did not wait. ortho_probe started immediately, on top of an arm that was at epoch 5 of 12, and card_check read OVERSUBSCRIBED: 'two of our own processes compute on this card (pids 15916 66340) ... they will each read slower than either would alone'.

CAUSE. card_check reads pids from the DEVICE - nvidia-smi - so every pid it prints is a WINDOWS pid. after.sh runs under MSYS bash, whose wait_for_pid tests liveness in MSYS pid space. The two spaces are unrelated, so 15916 named nothing in the space the check ran in, the check read 'already exited', and the chain fired at once. This is the same mismatch already recorded for testing git-bash liveness with a Windows pid tool, arriving from the opposite direction: here a Windows pid is handed to an MSYS test.

COST. One killed process (66340), roughly ten minutes of a shared card at half speed, and a timing reading on disagreed_ramp that cannot now be trusted for the epochs that overlapped. It also produced the DOUBLE-QUEUED and UNLOGGED verdicts that took the next two wakes to unpick, because the misfired chain and the chain it duplicated both stayed live.

THE FIX, in priority order. (1) wait_for_pid must REFUSE a pid it cannot see rather than treat unseen as exited - an unknown pid is the ambiguous case and firing is the destructive reading of it. (2) It should say which pid space it is testing in, so a caller handing it a card_check pid is told rather than obeyed. (3) queue_check should treat a 'pid:' marker as suspect on this platform and say so, the way it already refuses a watched file that does not exist.

WORKAROUND UNTIL FIXED: never arm on 'pid:'. Watch the marker in the log the chain actually writes - for an arm launched by after.sh that is the WATCHER's own stdout (logs/after_<arm>.log), not '<arm>_s<seed>.full.log', which only a run_train arm writes and which no arm writes under a name queue_check guesses.

title: Q-AC: text as privileged information (LUPI / distillation), not a text-branch member
description: The text-as-input branch is unshippable: the hidden test set has no Report column. The surviving text mechanism is privileged information: train a text-side model on reports, use only its output to shape the vision student. Question (Q-AC): when the hard labels were themselves extracted from the same reports, does a text teacher ever beat the extractor, or does it only reproduce it? Literature search; no card time.
notes:
DOWNGRADED to P3 at 2026-09-01 23:10Z, on Kimi's own Q-Z reply, before any card was spent. Two facts in that reply remove the reason the arm was filed P1.

THE 0.906 IS NOT THIS ARCHITECTURE'S NUMBER. It is the Kaggle Models tab 'best public score' for DINOv2-small across 40 users. The repo is a starter skeleton, does not claim to reproduce it, and its own default run is vision-only with the text branch listed as a later iteration. So there is no measured pairing of the two-branch design with 0.906 anywhere - the number that made this look like a 1.5% lever belongs to a backbone, not to a text branch. The whole P1 case was that arithmetic.

THE OBJECTIVE IS THE SHAPE THAT SHOULD BE EXPECTED TO HURT. No coupling loss: the report embedding is broadcast to the 12 target positions, concatenated with the per-target vision features, and ordinary BCE does all the work. The 12 labels were EXTRACTED from that same report text, and the test set has no Report column at all - so during training the model is handed a channel that nearly determines its target and is then absent at inference. The vision trunk is under less pressure to read the image for exactly the findings the metric scores, which is a stronger version of the mechanism that made report_supervision monotone in its weight rather than merely flat. A vision-ablation test is the only thing that would separate a supervision gain from that leakage, and it has not been run by anyone.

WHAT SURVIVES. The cheapness is real - training-only, no new loss, unchanged kernel runtime - so this stays as a P3 that a spare card slot could answer with a pre-registered vision-ablation, not as a night. The mechanism-(a) form on knee-iem6, contrastive image-report pretraining, is unaffected by this reply and remains the literature-backed member of the family. This is the third time the text axis has been re-opened by prose and closed by reading what the number actually measured.
Claude Q-AC mail 2026-09-02 0323z: re-scope from text-branch member to text-as-privileged-information. Input branch is dead because test set lacks Report column. Preliminary research note: research/2026-09-02_text_as_privileged_information_qac.md.

title: Two-branch text-supervised 2.5D member, the shape behind the public 0.906 - the first mechanism-backed arm since the trunk lane closed
description:
Kimi's Q-Y addendum (2255z) identifies the public baseline behind the 0.906 board score: konradcinkusz/rsna-knee-abnormalities-efficiency-lb. A 2.5D DINOv2-small vision branch trained alongside a multilingual text branch (paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2); test.csv carries no Report column, so the text path exists ONLY during training and the vision branch runs alone at inference.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE ARM THIS REPO ALREADY REFUTED. report_supervision.sh added a cosine auxiliary term pulling ONE study-level vision readout toward a sentence embedding of the whole report: 0.8272 control, 0.8219 at weight 0.3, 0.8209 at 1.0, monotone. That is mechanism (b), the auxiliary-loss form, which knee-iem6 declines on the grounds that no published medical gain exists for it. The public baseline is a different object: a genuine second BRANCH supplying a training signal to the trunk, closer to distillation than to a regulariser on a readout. The distinction is exactly the one Kimi's audit draws, and it is the reason the decline of (b) does not decline this.

WHY IT IS WORTH A CARD ARM. It is the only mechanism-backed candidate the project has had since the trunk lane closed EMPTY on radnet_family. Every other lane is a knob: member quality ceilings near 0.943, the stack lane closed 7/7, and seating is flat over seven board rows plus the external-corpus dose flat at one and two seats (corpusfull_v1 asks the six-seat point tonight). And the size is right rather than knob-sized - a single public model reading 0.906 on the board is a large number against solos of ours in the 0.86 range on holdout.

THE OTHER FACT IN THE ADDENDUM, WHICH CUTS THE OTHER WAY AND BELONGS ON knee-440m. That repo's own Models tab reads DINOv2-base 0.861 and DINOv2-large 0.5 - effectively random. So on the public gold-label set the LARGE trunk failed outright and the small one carried the score. ortho_dense is a ViT-L. Our supervision is not theirs (4,407 report-derived labels rather than 58 gold), so the datapoint does not transfer directly, but it is a live prior against depth on this task and it should be read before ortho_dense's low branch is written down as a fact about knee continuation.

OPEN QUESTIONS BEFORE ANYTHING IS ARMED, sent to Kimi 2306z: what the text branch's actual objective is (contrastive over pairs, distillation from text embeddings into vision features, or a joint head over concatenated branches), whether the two branches share a loss or are trained in stages, and which text field is used. The answer decides whether this is one arm or three.

title: Transductive / test-time adaptation family DECLINED in writing
description:
Audited via Kimi Q-X (research/2026-09-01_transductive_test_time_adaptation_audit.md, knee-za1r). Declining the whole family; this bead is the written argument so it is re-opened by answering it rather than by re-asking the question.

WHY IT WAS ASKED. This is a CODE competition and the test set is present in full inside the kernel at inference. No entry this project has shipped uses that fact; every one treats each study as independent and stateless. With solo 0.859, ensemble 0.944 and the leader at 0.952, ensembling has already bought 0.085 and the leader sits 0.008 past where it buys out, so an axis nobody here has touched was worth pricing.

1. TEST-TIME PSEUDO-LABELING. 1-3 pp published, on small corpora or segmentation, and only with uncertainty filtering. Overfits the public split and can destroy the private score; rare positives get smoothed away by confident negatives. Needs a second training pass inside a 9 h kernel while we sit at efficiency rank 153. DECLINED on variance and runtime.

2. TEST-TIME NORMALIZATION / ALIGNMENT. Pays when recovering from a domain-shift DROP, small or negative when train and test are already close. Our trunks are LayerNorm/GroupNorm (DINOv2/v3, Swin, ConvNeXt), so TENT/AdaBN-style BN recalibration does not apply at all. Medeiros et al. 2026 measure standard TTA DEGRADING medical classification by up to 31.6 points on BN-statistic mismatch. DECLINED unless a systematic public/private shift is first diagnosed - it is a repair, not a lever.

3. NEIGHBOUR-GRAPH SMOOTHING. A few points in few-shot classification when the graph aligns with classes. Ours is ~1,300 test studies, 12 independent binary labels, severe imbalance: a similarity graph on frozen embeddings connects rare positives mostly to negatives and smoothing erodes the recall that carries the metric. Nearly free for us since embeddings are already cached, which is exactly why it is suspicious. DECLINED as a plan; admissible later as a low-probability side bet, never as the gap story.

4. THE COMPETITION RECORD. RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine top eight: 2.5D/3D CNNs, ensembles, 3-stage pipelines, no transductive training. RSNA 2019 ICH: 5-fold ensembles and ordinary TTA. Current public landscape here: best public score is DINOv2-small 0.906 with a 2.5D plus multilingual text branch. Nothing transductive is visible near the top of any of them.

WHAT WOULD RE-OPEN IT: a measured public/private distribution shift (which makes 2 a repair with a target), or a competition write-up showing a transductive method at the top of a comparable multi-label medical task.

title: queue_check calls an arm STRANDED without asking whether it already ran
description:
On 2026-09-01 a stale after.sh watcher (armed 2026-08-31, waiting forever on 'logs/ema224.full.log', a filename that predates the seed suffix) was killed. queue_check then reported eleven arms STRANDED — attend224, sided224, through224, decay224_high, clip224, decay224_low, warm224_brief, regions224, clip224_tight, warm224_long, focal224 — and told me to 'relaunch after.sh over them'.

All eleven had ALREADY RUN. Each has a <arm>_s<seed>.pt checkpoint on disk. Following the tool's own instruction would have put roughly 7 h of card into re-running knob arms on a lane the project has closed, which is the single most expensive mistake available right now.

The STRANDED reading is computed purely from the watcher table: arms owed by a dead watcher and by no live one. That is the right question for a watcher that died MID-QUEUE, and the wrong question for one that never fired at all — which is exactly the shape the MISARMED check on the line above had just diagnosed. The two findings contradict each other and the tool prints both.

FIX: before naming an arm stranded, ask whether its output exists — a checkpoint at PROCESSED/<arm>_s*.pt, or a ledger row, or an 'ARM DONE <arm>' marker anywhere in logs/. An arm with a checkpoint is DONE, not owed; report it as such (or say nothing) rather than as work to relaunch. An arm with no checkpoint and a dead watcher is the real finding and should keep the current wording.

This is the same class as the farseat_v1 and the two-member_curve-scans defects: a gate that is loud on the wrong denominator, where the cost is the READING rather than the machine.

title: MRNet architecture is already ours; both halves are answered
description: Stanford MRNet (2018): per-slice 2D feature extractor -> global average pool -> MAX pool across slices -> FC, then a separate CNN per (series, task) with a logistic regression weighting the three series. First half is slice_pooling.py MAXIMUM (SlicePooling(per_slice=True)), which this project has had all along - we have never used 3D convolutions, so 'volumetric' was never the bet. Second half is a per-view specialist stack combined by a fitted linear rule, which is exactly what vote/votefit measured at 0.938, flat. Filed to CLOSE the question rather than to open an arm: nothing in MRNet is untried here. Our LABELWISE slice attention is strictly richer than their max pool.

title: The label lane was closed on the one ruler knee-9198 says is biased against label-side arms
description: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_label_lane_closes.md closes the label lane on blendlabels_s2026 reading +0.0003 peak and +0.0003 flat under label_combine.py's split-half estimator, plus seat_value +0.0001 and per-label routing +0.0009 (same order as knee-m69u's +0.0002 weighting ORACLE). Its result table is PROXY ONLY; the gold 58 appear in the framing lines and in no measurement. knee-9198, updated the SAME DAY, states the rule that any label-side arm from here reports BOTH numbers - proxy holdout AUC and supervision_gap over the 58 - precisely because a change moving a model toward annotation truth mechanically LOSES AUC against report labels, by up to the measured +0.045 (holdannot_s2026: 0.8487 proxy vs 0.8932 gold, same weights, same studies). So the lane was closed on the ruler that is structurally biased against what it was measuring. THE HONEST COUNTER, which is why this is P1 and not P0: 2026-08-30_the-gold-ruler-raises-everyone-and-orders-no-one.md plus knee-kddo show six members spanning 0.022 on gold give paired intervals ~0.03 wide, five of six pairs inseparable - so reading blendlabels on the 58 would very likely come back INCONCLUSIVE. That is the point. 'Closed' and 'cannot be resolved by any ruler we own' are different states and the record currently writes the second as the first. Cheapest fix costs no card: run supervision_gap over the 58 for blendlabels against its control, report the interval, and rewrite the closure to say which of the two states it is in.

title: peak8 did not refute the offline ruler: board_transfer says 0/269 resolved pairs inverted
description:
THE CLAIM ON RECORD IS WRONG, and it is steering the project. comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:2892 is titled
"the offline ruler fails" and comp/board.jsonl's peak8 row says "the offline argmax is NOT a board
argmax: selecting members by the fold-0 holdout picks a set that scores worse the more carefully it
is optimised". Two consequences were written from that: member_curve's greedy "may no longer be used
to JUSTIFY a slot", and seat_value's argmax "is a holdout artefact rather than a ranking".

WHAT THE TOOL SAYS. `python -m kneemri.evaluation.board_transfer`, run 2026-08-31 with BOTH peak8 rows
in the file: 33 ensemble entries, 421 orderable pairs, "inversions: 11/421 pairs the board ordered the
other way, 0/269 of the pairs the holdout resolved at all (a gap >= 0.0053)". Every one of the eleven is
printed UNRESOLVED, peak8's own two included:
  peak8 over gradeswap_v1: holdout +0.0037 (UNRESOLVED, under the floor), board -0.001
  peak8 over accumseat_v1: holdout +0.0036 (UNRESOLVED, under the floor), board -0.001
That is the same 0/N the 2026-08-29 refit reported at 0/127 and 0/233. peak8 did not break it; it
extended it to 269.

THE PREMISE IS ALSO FACTUALLY WRONG. "the best offline number this project owns (0.8731)" was true on
2026-08-24 and is not true now. Sorted from comp/board.jsonl:
  honest12       0.8751 -> board 0.937
  greedyseat_v1  0.8740 -> board 0.936
  peak8          0.8731 -> board 0.932
peak8 is THIRD offline and THIRD on the board. Against the two entries it is compared with, the holdout
gets the SIGN right both times and merely cannot resolve the gap:
  peak8 vs greedyseat_v1: holdout -0.0009 (UNRESOLVED, floor 0.0053), board -0.004
  peak8 vs honest12:      holdout -0.0020 (UNRESOLVED), board -0.005
  peak8 vs greedy7_v1:    holdout +0.0019 (UNRESOLVED), board -0.001  <- the only sign flip, one board tick
So "the harder a set is optimised the worse it scores" rests entirely on pairs the ruler itself declines
to order. There is no measured inversion to explain.

WHAT THE RULER ACTUALLY DOES, over 30 deduped ensemble rows carrying both numbers:
  ALL          n=30  Spearman +0.961  pairwise 390/421 = 0.926
  board>=0.925 n=21  Spearman +0.906  pairwise 173/197 = 0.878
  board>=0.930 n=13  Spearman +0.819  pairwise  57/68  = 0.838
The top-band degradation is what a 0.0062 offline floor against a 0.007-wide board band predicts, not
evidence of selection overfit.

A BIAS CORRECTION WAS TESTED AND DOES NOT HELP. member_curve.honest (member_curve.py:163-198) already
measures greedy selection bias, replicated in four logs (logs/greedy_all.log:191-207,
logs/honest_packaged.log:92-108, logs/honest_pool_20260829.log:189-202): +0.0025 to +0.0031 at 7-12
seats over 77-119 members. Subtracting it from the raw search-selected rows moved retro-prediction
DOWN, not up (ALL Spearman 0.961 -> 0.947; board>=0.930 0.819 -> 0.647), because the early four-seat
entries were searched over 10-22 members and a large-pool constant does not apply to them. The correction
is right for the row it was measured on (knee-jsgb: raw 0.8768 predicted 0.939 vs actual 0.936; corrected
0.8740 predicted 0.936, err +0.0001) and must not be applied as a blanket.

THE REAL DEFECT IS PLUMBING, NOT THE RULER. knee-jsgb closed 2026-08-30 with a standing instruction:
"Any future entry selected by search must be entered in board.jsonl bias-corrected, never raw." peak8
shipped 2026-08-31, one day later, greedy-selected, and its row carries the RAW 0.8731 with an
offline_scope that discusses fold-0 scoreability and never mentions selection bias. Corrected to ~0.8704
it predicts 0.934 against an actual 0.932 (raw predicts 0.936). The row disobeys a rule the project had
already written down, and board_check does not enforce it.

WHAT TO DO
 1. Correct the peak8 row's offline_scope to name the selection bias, as greedyseat_v1's does.
 2. Rewrite comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:2892's section: peak8 is a THIRD fold-0 anchor extending board_transfer
    to 0/269, which is a good result for the slot, not a refutation.
 3. Reinstate member_curve's greedy for slot justification WITH the correction, and re-open seat_value's
    argmax. Both were retired on this reading.
 4. Add the assertion to board_check: a row whose entry was search-selected must carry a bias-corrected
    offline, the same way a row's offline must be read on studies the entry did not train on.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. Nothing about the ~0.008 blind-vs-fold-0 structural gap, which is untouched and
still explains why an all-fold-0 entry cannot reach 0.944. And nothing licenses firing on a sub-0.0053
offline preference: the ruler does not resolve those, which is exactly what it correctly reports.

title: The twin-transfer route to a per-finding vote is dead three ways, and vote.py does not say so
description:
Someone reading kneemri/inference/vote.py sees LabelQualityRank, sees it has never shipped, greps board.jsonl, finds zero per-finding entries, and proposes fitting it on the champion seats' fold-0 TWINS to get around the --fold -1 contamination. That route was proposed and killed on 2026-08-31 without spending a card or a slot. It will be proposed again, because nothing at the point of discovery says otherwise.

WHY IT IS DEAD.

(1) THE AXIS IS CLOSED, MEASURED, FOUR TIMES. knee-xsfc closed on the pre-registered clause 'if the honest per-label read does not beat flat, the vote axis closes for good and no further rule is written'. LabelQualityRank honest vs flat: +0.0002 (42 members/909), +0.0001 (77 members/909), +0.0011 (109 members), +0.0000 (four-seat shipping shape), +0.0001 (six-seat one-decode shipping shape). Every one under the +0.0015 seat_value floor.

(2) THE OVERFIT GAP PRICES THE SHRINKAGE CURVE WITHOUT RUNNING IT. The obvious objection is that 72 fitted parameters need shrinkage toward flat and the reading should be reported as a function of it. It does not need running. A shrinkage curve interpolates between flat and the unshrunk fit, so the FIT-ON-SELF number is the upper envelope of the entire curve -- and it is +0.0004 to +0.0007. The rule barely beats flat EVEN WHEN GRADING ITS OWN HOMEWORK. So every point of the shrinkage curve is bounded in [+0.0000, +0.0007] by construction. There is nothing in the per-label quality table to find, which coheres with competence_axis: member quality is 81.7% of pool spread, so members differ in overall strength, not in WHICH labels they are good at.

(3) THE TWIN TRANSFER ADDS A STEP THAT MOVES THE EXACT QUANTITY BEING FITTED. Per final_fit_six.sh, every _ff seat is its _s2026 twin plus '--fold -1 --ema', and every _cf seat is its _ff plus '--calibrated-targets'. So four of the champion's six seats (grade_ladder_cf, lr4e-5_ws_cf, through_dense_cf, final_ws_cf) differ from their proposed fold-0 twins by TWO trained variables besides the fold. And --calibrated-targets is the most per-label-heterogeneous lever in the ledger: on calib_span its MEAN was flat (-0.0020) while Effusion read -0.0212*, PF OA +0.0170* and Baker's -0.0167*, three labels clearing their own paired half-widths. It rearranges which labels a member is good at while leaving the mean alone. That is precisely and only the quantity LabelQualityRank fits. A per-label weight table fitted on the twin is fitted on the wrong per-label profile, on the one axis being transferred. So the transfer version is strictly WORSE than the +0.0007 fit-on-self bound, not better.

(4) THE INFORMATION CAP. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_the_pool_is_redundant_not_the_task.md: 0.0565 bits of epistemic disagreement in a 0.6807-bit pool (8.3% reducible across the roster, 12.7% on honest12). A vote rule can only redistribute weight within the disagreement; it cannot create any. The measured 0.0000-0.0015 spread across all five rules is what that cap looks like from the other side.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY FIX (the point of this bead):

- kneemri/inference/vote.py: LabelQualityRank's docstring still reads as an OPEN invitation -- 'It exists to be read on a SPLIT HALF by vote_ceiling ... because the gap between those two is the measurement'. It HAS been read, four times. Give it the same MEASURED-AND-CLOSED paragraph MedianLogit carries, with the numbers and the overfit-gap argument, so the class states its own verdict at the point of discovery. QualityWeightedRank's docstring has the same staleness ('has to be read on a split half' -- it was).
- Add the twin-transfer route by name, so the specific way around the contamination is refused in advance rather than re-derived.

SECOND DEFECT, INDEPENDENT, found on the way: comp/members.roster calls calib_span_hold_s2026 'the champion's own calib_span_ff twin'. It is not. Per the arms, calib_span_hold = calib_span + '--hold-annotations'; calib_span_ff = calib_span + '--fold -1 --ema'. The correct fold-0 twin of calib_span_ff is calib_span_s2026, which is ALSO on the roster. This matters beyond pedantry: the ledger measures the calibration lever's sign as INVERTED across exactly that hold/non-hold boundary (band_span_hold 0.8493 -> calib_span_hold 0.8565 = +0.0072, against band_span 0.8565 -> calib_span 0.8545 = -0.0020, a 0.0092 swing). title: Asymmetric label smoothing with SHARPENING of confident cells (Rep-GLS) — the published lever we do not have, and our data says it points the wrong way
description:
EXTERNAL RESULT (research/2026-08-31_report_label_noise_and_uncertainty_heads.md). Rep-GLS (arXiv 2508.02495) is our labelling scheme, published: an LLM parses each radiology report into per-finding uncertainty keywords, a small network maps keywords to a smoothing rate r in (-1,1), and the per-class loss is (1-r)*L_CE + r*L_uniform. On MIMIC-CXR-JPG, 14 diseases:

  BCE baseline                          79.63
  end-to-end, no expert RGN pretraining 80.27
  softening only (r >= 0)               81.56
  full, sharpening enabled (r < 0)      84.14

Softening uncertain cells buys +1.93. SHARPENING confident cells buys a further +2.58 — the larger half of the total gain.

WHAT WE HAVE. Only the softening half. Supervision.applied maps reader certainty to measured agreement 0.08/0.28/0.68/0.82/0.94, so even a maximally confident report is softened relative to a hard 1.0; weight_floor gives 0.25 + 0.75*conf and only ever DOWN-weights. No term anywhere pushes a confident cell past plain BCE. On their ablation that is the bigger lever and we have none of it.

WHY IT IS NOT A FREE ADOPT. Their sharpening assumes a confident report statement is TRUE — their expert rate table gives 'positive' r = -0.2 explicitly. Our supervision_gap says the radiologist agrees only 65.3% where the report says YES, and noise_binding finds 108 confident false positives, 15.8% of annotated cells, all verdict YES. Sharpening drives the model harder onto exactly those cells. The published lever points the wrong way on our corpus, and it points wrong precisely where it is largest.

BLOCKED ON the extractor-vs-reader audit of the 108 (sibling P0). That audit decides this bead:
* If the 108 are mostly EXTRACTION failures, then confident report statements ARE mostly true once the extractor is fixed, and sharpening becomes adoptable — but only AFTER the extractor fix, and it should be re-derived against the corrected labels rather than the current ones.
* If the 108 are genuine reader disagreement, this bead CLOSES UNBUILT and the closure is a real finding: it says our corpus differs from MIMIC-CXR in a way that makes the field's larger label lever unavailable to us, and that is worth writing into the interpretation.

DESIGN NOTE IF IT IS EVER BUILT. Their two-stage form (expert-supervised rate network, then training) beat end-to-end by 3.87, so a hand-derived rate table is the right shape and matches how MEASURED_AGREEMENT was built. Do not reach for the end-to-end version first. Note also that r is per-FINDING per-STUDY in their scheme, which is the 'per-STUDY confidence rather than a per-FINDING constant' door that finding_calib_dense's post-mortem explicitly left open.

description:

title: attribution.py's occlusion maps are the LESS faithful readout — captum scores them worse than attention on 12 of 12 findings
description:
Measured 2026-08-31 under knee-wgaa (commit 860a99a2), by captum's captum.metrics.infidelity and sensitivity_max, on attend_true_s2026, 24 studies, centred window. Comparing the SLOT ATTENTION readout against the occlusion attribution kneemri/evaluation/attribution.py produces:

    infidelity        attention 0.037-0.125   occlusion 0.052-0.188
    sensitivity_max   attention 0.70-0.90     occlusion 0.88-2.41

Attention is more faithful on 12 of 12 findings on BOTH metrics.

WHY THE SENSITIVITY NUMBER IS THE SERIOUS ONE. sensitivity_max above 1.0 means the explanation changes MORE than the signal does under small perturbations of the features — the diagnostic is noisier than the thing it is explaining. Occlusion reaches 2.41. An explanation that unstable is not a weak signal, it is a signal about the perturbation procedure.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE MODULE. Nothing had ever checked this. The occlusion maps were trusted because they existed and because they were the only attribution the project had. This is the same failure shape as the fabricated board constant and as raptor_solo's contaminated 0.8938: a plausible artefact in the right range, with no instrument pointed at it.

OWED:
 1. Sweep past readings that rested on an occlusion map and mark which conclusions they carried. Any that are load-bearing get re-read against the attention readout.
 2. Then either FIX attribution.py — the likely cause is the occlusion window/baseline choice, and a baseline that is itself off-manifold is the classic source of exactly this instability — or DEMOTE it with a docstring note saying which readout to prefer and why, so the next reader does not re-trust it.
 3. Do not delete it. The negative is about the current parameters, not proof the approach cannot work; record the mechanism that failed so a later use is re-tested rather than assumed dead.

CREDIT WHERE DUE: this is the payoff of using a mature library rather than a hand-rolled check. A hand-written faithfulness score would have had nothing auditing IT, and would most likely have been tuned until the existing maps looked fine.

title: Steal systole's frozen-TestSet + generalisation-matrix design for the OOD read (knee-l8ax)
description:
knee-l8ax needs a scorer that runs OUR member on a FOREIGN corpus — a direction no existing module covers (foreign_member, foreign_gate, foreign_ruler, foreign_overlap, board_transfer, ruler_transfer ALL run the opposite way, foreign checkpoint on our corpus). So it is new code, and the shape it should take already exists next door.

SOURCE. D:/personal_projects/cardiac-seg — core/data/ingest/testsets.py and cardioseg/evaluation/matrix.py. Three ideas, in descending value:

1. AUTOMATIC OOD-vs-LEAK FLAG PER CELL. Every score in the matrix is labelled by reconstructing what the model saw from the model's OWN saved config, with seen = train u val. This is the defect we bled on: raptor_solo's 0.8938 stood as evidence until somebody thought to run foreign_overlap and found 896 of 909 studies in-sample. That one cell was carrying the whole 'compression goes negative at the top' reading plus eleven of fifteen apparent ruler inversions. Systole makes forgetting the check impossible; we make it a thing you remember. Highest-value idea in the file.

2. A TEST SET IS A CODED PREDICATE + A SHA256 LOCK over its resolved subject ids, not a manifest string and not a glob. If the store grows or an id changes, the lock mismatches and it is a HARD ERROR, never a silently different denominator. Directly applicable to our foreign caches (Rijeka, MRNet), which are built per-geometry and are exactly the kind of thing that drifts under you.

3. THE MATRIX IS ANY MODEL x ANY FROZEN CORPUS, pure inference, each model loaded with ITS OWN preprocessing. That last clause matters here: foreign_member already measured that the same published checkpoint reads 0.9167 through their decode and 0.8819 through our best cache, a -0.0348 shortfall that is entirely the feed. A matrix that does not carry per-model preprocessing would attribute that gap to the model.

SO: build knee-l8ax's scorer as a MATRIX WITH A LEAK FLAG, not a one-off Rijeka script. Same wall-clock, and it then answers every later foreign-corpus question without new code.

Constraints already recorded on knee-l8ax: the Rijeka cache images_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_rijeka.npy matches swin_supervised/swin_distill_fit geometry EXACTLY; Rijeka labels ACL only; MRNet only exists at 336px/12sl; knee-yu9k records build_rijeka was uncallable; verify the Rijeka index actually carries labels before promising the read.

title: [bug] The offline-to-board line 'board = 1.37 x offline - 0.2598' is fabricated; the real slope at our operating point is ~0.95
description:
ORIGIN. This constant was produced in-session on 2026-08-31 and quoted repeatedly as if it were a fitted repo constant, including to the owner while pricing base_clean. A repo-wide grep for '1.37' and '0.2598' returns hits ONLY inside .venv/ (kagglesdk version string, matplotlib test fixtures). It is in no module, no doc, no bead. It survived several context compactions because it kept being restated in prose, which is the only place it ever existed.

WHY IT IS WRONG IN KIND, not just in value. kneemri/evaluation/board_transfer.py opens with the heading 'PAIRS, NOT A REGRESSION' and argues the case explicitly: offline is LLM-read report labels on our holdout, board is radiologist annotations on the hidden set, and the two were never meant to agree on LEVEL -- only on ORDER. It reports a median of pairwise ratios for exactly that reason. Fitting a line is the thing that module was written to refuse.

WHAT THE DATA SAYS. comp/board.jsonl holds 83 rows; 36 carry both a numeric offline and a board score, 32 of them ensembles.
  * OLS over all 32 ensemble rows: slope 1.945
  * OLS over the top 16 (offline >= 0.867), which is where we operate: slope 0.953
  * board_transfer's own pairwise median, top regime: +0.99 [+0.77, +1.18]
1.37 matches none of these. The whole-record and top-regime slopes differ by 2x because the relation is CURVED, which is the second reason a single line is the wrong shape.

THE COMPOUNDING ERROR. Max offline ever observed is 0.8751 -> board 0.937. The champion at 0.944 has NO numeric offline; 38 board rows lack one. So 'board 0.944 implies offline 0.879' inverted a nonexistent line onto a point outside the dataset, and the projection to 0.8836 sits beyond every offline reading ever taken. Extrapolation past the end of the data, presented as arithmetic.

CONSEQUENCE FOR PRICING, since this changed a live decision. base_clean was sold to the owner as +0.0062 solo -> +0.0085 board -> top-3, at P~0.35. At the real slope (~0.95, no amplification) and with a new member entering as one seat of six or seven rather than moving the ensemble one-for-one, the ensemble gain is ~+0.001-0.003 and the board gain the same, against a board quantum of 0.001. P(beats the champion) is ~0.10. The arm keeps its INSTRUMENT value (it removes the four-flag confound that base_dense, v3base_dense and raddino_normfix are all quoted on) and has no credible score value.

RELATED, AND THE OWNER RAISED IT: 'ensemble = best-single + 0.0143' (knee-urvf) has the same defect in waiting. It is fitted over a regime where every member sits within ~0.01 of the others. Equal-weight averaging gives a new member weight 1/N, so a member far ahead of the pool is DILUTED, not amplified, and the sum-law inverts. No member in the fit was ever far ahead, so the fit cannot see its own ceiling. Do not price a step-change member with it.

FIX: quote board_transfer's regime-local pairwise ratio with its interval, never a slope-intercept line, and never invert one to manufacture an offline number for an entry that has none.

title: after.sh's smoke gate cannot smoke an arm that BUILDS its own input, and the chain died on it
description:
swin_distill_fit.sh exports its own encoder file (kneemri.training.fitted_encoder) as its first line, then passes it to run_train via --encoder-weights. ArmSmoke read the arm's invocation, resolved --encoder-weights to a path that does not exist YET, and reported 'BROKEN swin_distill_fit: FileNotFoundError'. It did not refuse (0 refused), but the chain nevertheless ended there: after.sh was gone from the process table at 10:19 UTC on 2026-08-31, the card was free, and swin_distill_fit had never started. Stage one had completed cleanly (ARM DONE swin_distill_pre, holdout 0.8177 at epoch 3), so ~15 minutes of card time was lost between the stages and would have been hours if nobody looked.

Two separate defects, and they should not be fixed as one:

(1) THE SMOKE IS WRONG ABOUT THIS ARM. An arm whose input is produced by an earlier line of the SAME arm is unsmokeable by construction under the current reading, which only sees run_train's flags. Every future two-stage arm has this shape, and distillation-as-pretraining is the pattern the project just committed to. Either the smoke runs the arm's prelude (correct, and it costs seconds here), or it recognises a --encoder-weights path an earlier line writes and declines to judge it, saying so.

(2) A BROKEN SMOKE THAT DOES NOT REFUSE SHOULD NOT BE ABLE TO END THE CHAIN. 0 refused means proceed; the chain proceeded to nothing. Whatever consumed the BROKEN line stopped after.sh without a refusal and without an error of its own, which is the worst of the three outcomes because the log reads as a clean check.

Relaunched swin_distill_fit by hand at 10:19 UTC; the export ran fine as the arm's first line, which is the proof that the smoke's FileNotFoundError was about ordering and not about the arm.

title: Pre-registration bands must be drawn by SUBTRACTING the control, never by naming absolute scores
description:
Second occurrence. holdswap_v1's kernel wrote its bands against 'the champion's 0.944' in prose and anchored the arithmetic at 0.941: the 'real gain over the champion, above the resolution floor' band opens at 0.9425, BELOW the champion, and the FLAT band sits lower still. The entry scored 0.944 - arithmetically identical to the control - and landed numerically inside a band labelled 'a real gain'.

comp/champion.json already records the first occurrence, for raptorweight_v1: its 'real gain' edge of 0.9435 was not an attainable score at all, because the board quantises to 0.001.

Both were caught only by subtracting the control by hand after the fact. A band written as an absolute score carries an anchor that can silently be the previous champion, a remembered number, or a score the board cannot express.

FIX: a pre-registration states a DELTA against a named control plus the control's ref, and the absolute edges are computed from the control at read time. A band edge that is not a multiple of 0.001 away from the control is a bug, because the board cannot return it.

Candidate home: a check that reads a kernel's band block and the control's row from comp/board.jsonl and refuses edges that are unattainable or that sit on the wrong side of the control.

title: trajectory_check cannot arbitrate the warm lane until eight six-epoch runs exist
description: The floor fix (knee-e8sm) made short budgets READABLE; it did not make them READ. cnx_warm_anneal is the only 6-epoch run on disk, so spread() refuses with 'only 1 run(s) match a 6-epoch budget past epoch 3, and 8 are needed'. Every warm restart we run from here is unarbitrable mid-flight until the 6-epoch corpus reaches MIN_CORPUS = 8. Two ways out, and the choice is a design decision, not a default: (a) accumulate - warm arms are cheap (~20-80 min) and the lane is one we said we would run, so the corpus fills on its own and the gate switches on at the eighth; (b) band adjacent budgets - read a 6-epoch arm against, say, 5-8 epoch runs pooled, which is a WIDER instrument and must be argued for, because the whole reason gain() matches on the budget is that a 24-epoch one_cycle has twice the anneal left after the gate (median +0.0339 vs +0.0210) and a long schedule's headroom must not excuse a short arm. Do NOT pick (b) to make the current arm readable - that is fitting the instrument to the job it is refusing. Until one is chosen, a warm arm runs to completion and is read by convergence_check afterwards.

title: mount_check --live crashes on model_sources: it queries metaresearch/dinov2 as a DATASET
description:
On 2026-08-30, before the holdswap_v1 submission, 'python -m kneemri.kaggle.mount_check --live' died with CalledProcessError on ['kaggle.exe','datasets','files','metaresearch/dinov2','--csv','--page-size','1000'] (exit 1). metaresearch/dinov2 is a MODEL source, not a dataset, so 'kaggle datasets files' cannot resolve it. The crash is in EncoderMounts.over (mount_check.py:240) -> LiveDataset.holds (live_dataset.py:130) -> paths() -> _cli (live_dataset.py:62).

This is not specific to one kernel: every kernel in the repo declares metaresearch/dinov2 model_sources, so --live is dead for ALL of them. The offline mount_check still passes and covers the identity question (69 ok, 5 skipped, 0 refused of 74). The LIVE question it was written for -- does the mounted dataset actually hold the checkpoints the kernel names -- had to be answered by hand for holdswap: 'kaggle datasets files dimiturnt/kneemri-members --csv --page-size 1000' listed all six members including calib_dense_hold_ff.pt. That worked because the members MOUNT is a real dataset; only the model_sources entries are not.
