title: Captum for per-STUDY failure triage, and the standing argument in attribution.py it must answer first
description:
OWNER, 2026-08-30, named attribution (captum) as an analysis instrument. Synthesis: research/2026-08-30_analysis-instruments-distance-divergence-attribution.md.

THIS IS NOT A GAP, IT IS A POSITION ALREADY TAKEN. kneemri/evaluation/attribution.py already does attribution, by OCCLUSION, and its docstring argues against the gradient/saliency family by name: nothing in the supervision ever says WHERE a finding is, so a saliency map has no reason to look right and cannot be checked against anything, whereas an occlusion produces a NUMBER on the held-out score. It closes with: saliency is deliberately not here, the sibling cardiac project keeps captum behind an optional extra for the same reason, the always-on diagnostic has to be the one that yields a measurement. Three occlusion diagnostics exist and each returns a delta: slot importance, border-vs-centre, depth profile. That argument is correct and this bead does not discard it.

WHERE CAPTUM STILL ADDS SOMETHING. Occlusion is COARSE BY DESIGN (a whole acquisition slot, a border ring, a depth window) because it costs a forward pass per occlusion, so its resolution is bounded by card time. Integrated Gradients and GradientSHAP cost a fixed multiple of one backward pass regardless of spatial resolution, so they are cheaper PER UNIT OF DETAIL. The framings that survive the incumbent argument:
  - VALIDATE SALIENCY AGAINST OCCLUSION FIRST, then use it where occlusion is unaffordable. The three occlusion measurements are ground truth a saliency method can be SCORED against. Reproducing border-vs-centre and the depth profile is what licenses it to answer finer questions. This is the only framing in which a picture becomes a measurement.
  - ATTRIBUTE OVER SLOT ATTENTION rather than pixels. SlotHead per-diagnosis attention is small and checkable directly against the slot-importance occlusion.
  - PER-STUDY FAILURE TRIAGE, which is the owner actual framing: why a model does bad somewhere. Corpus-level attribution is what occlusion already does well. The unmet need is the individual failure: take the studies the ensemble is most wrong on and ask what the model looked at. Occlusion is too coarse and too slow for that.

THE HONEST COUNTER. The saliency reliability literature is unkind. Adebayo et al. sanity checks (randomise weights, randomise labels) show several popular methods produce near-identical maps for a trained and an untrained network. ADOPTION GATE: run that sanity check on OUR model first and report it, before any map is read as evidence. captum arrives as an OPTIONAL EXTRA matching the sibling cardiac project, never a declared dependency, never in the serving path or the kernel budget.

PRICE: ~half a day plus the sanity check. Zero card of consequence, 0 slots. Ranked LAST of the three instruments the owner named, because the incumbent argument is sound and this clears it only in the narrow per-study framing.
notes: Do not build before the sanity check is specified. Optional extra only; must not enter serving or the nine-hour kernel budget.

Five of them sit at e11 of a 12-epoch budget: cnx_dense, encoder_adapt, encoder_adapt_lower, mixup224_strong, mixup_dense.

Priced 2026-08-30 before running anything. Best holdout among the whole undertrained set:

description:

The roster is the DEFINITION; the Kaggle dataset is the ARTEFACT, and the mounted one predates all thirty. So every one of them is still unseatable in a kernel today, for a different reason than yesterday: yesterday the roster did not name them, today the package does not carry them.

Until this is pushed, mount_check will read a roster the package cannot satisfy, and any entry chosen from a greedy over the full 123-member pool is unbuildable on Kaggle.

STEPS: python -m kneemri.kaggle.package_members (builds from the roster), then the manual upload, then python -m kneemri.kaggle.mount_check to assert Kaggle will actually serve what the roster names. Uploading is manual, so mount_check is the only thing that can tell us the artefact matches.

WATCH THE SIZE. Thirty more checkpoints is a materially bigger dataset; if it does not fit or the upload is too slow, the answer is a second package, not a silently trimmed roster.
notes:
DEMOTED P1 -> P3 the same evening, by the measurement that the roster fix made possible. This bead was filed on the assumption that thirty unshippable members meant thirty missing seats. The honest greedy over the full 111-member pool then read best honest count 28 at 0.8753, which is +0.0002 over the previous unrestricted honest12 at 0.8751. The thirty members buy nothing on the honest curve. So pushing a materially bigger dataset -- on a disk that is 95% full -- to seat them is paying a real cost for a measured null.

WHAT STAYS TRUE. The roster is still the definition and the artefact still lags it, so mount_check will report the divergence and should. This is now a hygiene item, not a lever.

WHAT WOULD RE-PROMOTE IT. Not a bigger pool. A member that is genuinely OFF this architecture -- a different decode or corpus (knee-ombx) -- would need packaging to be seated, and that is the case where the push buys something. Push then, with that member in it, rather than pushing thirty members that a measurement says are interchangeable with what is already mounted.

title: Foreign checkpoints trained on 896 of our 909 holdout studies; the +0.030 member gap is contamination and is retired
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29T17:44Z. No card, no slot. One set intersection against two files already on disk.

THE ANOMALY. Two readings of one checkpoint, raptor_v4_swa, disagree by ~0.05 and both were already in the repo. knee-9g28 (closed 2026-08-27) scored it at 0.8938 on our 909-study fold-0 holdout against our best member 0.8634 — +0.0304 at 0.0% fallback. knee-rh4t (2026-08-28) records the same checkpoint scoring 0.923 solo on the board, exactly level with our own best single. board_transfer fits +1.72 to +1.82x, so +0.0304 offline predicts ~+0.05 on the board. It delivered 0.000, and the two numbers were never put beside each other.

THE MEASUREMENT. Their published label table D:/data/external/raptor/labels/labels_llm_soft.csv against our own ReportFolds assignment:
  corpus 4407 | fold0 holdout 909 | their labels 4349
  holdout in their label file: 896 / 909
  gold in their label file:      0 / 58
  holdout that is gold:         13
The arithmetic closes exactly (909 = 896 + 13). Their row set is the corpus MINUS the 58 gold and nothing else, and our holdout is 98.6% inside it. That is the signature of train-on-everything-hold-out-the-oracle, corroborated from their side by the fact that the metric their checkpoints self-report is gold_auc on those same 58.

THE THREE RULERS. gold 58, both held out: 0.9167 vs 0.9152, NULL. Our fold-0 909, theirs 98.6% in-sample: +0.0304. Board hidden test, both held out: 0.923 vs 0.923, NULL. Two clean rulers agree at zero; the single contaminated one carries the whole gap.

WHAT IT KILLS. The member gap as a quantity. Its four supports are now: a forum self-report of 0.938-0.942 (single, unreproduced, already flagged on knee-rh4t), the +0.030 offline lead (contaminated), the board (null), the gold 58 (null). On every ruler where both models are honest, the best published member of this field and ours are level. Six open P0s rest on member quality being the free term and that premise now has no measurement behind it.

WHAT IT DOES NOT KILL. The foreign member as a SEAT. Its seat values were priced on the same contaminated ruler, so raptor solo 0.8928 and champion-six-plus-raptor 0.8910 are unreadable in BOTH directions. The pricing is void, not the seat. Re-pricing needs a ruler it did not train on: the gold 58 (too small to seat on) or the board (a slot). Also untouched: the 224px throughput argument (knee-s9cr) rests on our own ledger, and every purely-internal comparison is unaffected — this is contamination in one foreign checkpoint family, not in our fold.

THE CORRECTION OWED, AND IT IS FILED. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_the-feed-was-the-whole-shortfall.md has a section 'A ruler that disagrees with itself' that spots this exact contradiction and pins it on OUR selection over 105 arms, concluding the member gap is NOT retired. The selection effect is real and secondary; it cannot explain the board null. Correction appended to that page; full reading in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-29_the-foreign-member-trained-on-our-holdout.md.

THE GUARD. python -m kneemri.evaluation.foreign_overlap --foreign <table> [--fold N] [--assert-clean], committed with four unit tests. Default is GUILT: a competitor's model has seen our holdout unless their own artefacts prove otherwise, since our fold assignment is a hash of report text that no external party has any reason to respect. Costs no card and no slot, and runs BEFORE the number is read rather than two days after it has driven six P0s.

WHERE IT POINTS. knee-fuhq. Two independently built models — different architecture, decode, corpus and label reader — landing on the same 0.923 on a hidden test is what a shared supervision ceiling looks like, and it is the only reading left standing.

    Synovitis -0.454, Effusion -0.389, Medial OA -0.199, Lateral OA -0.181, Contusion -0.057,
    PF OA -0.003, ACL +0.015, Lateral Meniscus +0.032, MCL +0.060, Medial Meniscus +0.214,
    Fracture +0.313, Baker's +0.647
  by structure scale: focal -0.0086  regional +0.0121
  ends: depth_regions_span_run1 -0.158, mae_matched -0.137, encoder_adapt -0.117
        ... merged_blend +0.037, normcount224 +0.040, contrast_dense +0.041

WHAT IT MEANS. A member better at Synovitis and Effusion is measurably WORSE at Baker's, Fracture and Medial Meniscus. That is not noise: after member quality is removed the first component takes 45.7% of the remaining spread against a 27.4% null. The pool is NOT a flat monoculture on the competence axis, whatever it is on the architecture axis.

IT RESOLVES TODAY'S CONTRADICTION. Routed top-k per label measured NEGATIVE this morning, and a flat rank average, honest greedy seats and (knee-669u) learned weights all tie at the same ceiling. If a real per-label trade exists, routing should win. It does not, and the reason is the DENOMINATOR: the routing choice is made on 909 studies with as few as 62 Fracture positives, so the per-label ordering that the axis proves exists in aggregate cannot be recovered per label at this sample size. The axis is real AND our ruler cannot pick along it.

IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE CEILING MECHANISM. Averaging members that sit at opposite ends of a trade cancels the trade. That is why four aggregation strategies sharing nothing but the pool land within 0.003 of each other: they are all averaging along an axis whose ends subtract.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT LICENSE. Not a per-label loss and not a focus-label member: the house rule is to keep the objective general and fix needs with balanced data, not loss-engineering, and per_label_loss and focus_label are both already flags this project has. Nor does it license a diversity-seeking seat search - that is what has already been measured flat, four ways.

WHAT IT DOES LICENSE, and it needs its own pre-registration before anything is armed: a member deliberately placed OFF this axis rather than at an end of it. The ends are populated (depth_regions_span at -0.158, contrast_dense at +0.041); what the pool has never held is a member whose competence profile is orthogonal to the trade.

IMMEDIATE USE: this is a THIRD read for raddino_dense when it lands, and a better one than the two on knee-fzpy. Re-run competence_axis with the new checkpoint present and read WHERE IT SITS. At an end of the existing axis it is another draw from the pool whatever its solo score. Off the axis - a member whose loading is small on component 1 while its own quality is high - is the first genuinely new competence profile this pool has held, and that is the finding the seat and distance rulers cannot report.
notes:
2026-08-29 17:20Z — RETRACTED, by an instrument added one tick after the finding.

AxisReading.maturity correlates each member's axis position with its own holdout mean. Over the same 109-member pool: r = +0.90.

The axis is very largely MEMBER QUALITY. Row-centring removes each member's LEVEL — that is the 81.7% the reading already reported — but it cannot remove the SHAPE of being under-fitted, and that shape is a direction in this matrix: the high-prevalence large-signal findings (Synovitis, Effusion) come first in training and the rare focal ones (Baker's, Fracture, Medial Meniscus) come last. So the first component is mostly the FITTING GRADIENT read back as pool structure. The tail widened to 15 a side put lr2e-4_ws (a learning-rate knob) and quarter_data (a data fraction) at the diffuse end, which is what prompted the check.

Retracted: (1) the pool spans one competence trade; (2) the aggregation ceiling is that trade cancelling under averaging; (3) the pre-registered target of a member at +0.15 toward the focal end. A focal-end member is just a better member; seating the opposite end seats a worse one.

Survives, and duller: the ceiling still has an explanation — the pool is ONE QUALITY LADDER with a long weak tail, so every strategy that averages it averages strong with weak and they land together. The four-strategy tie (knee-669u) and the closed vote axis are untouched; those were measured on held-out score, not on this decomposition.

Priority dropped P1 -> P3: the module and its guard are worth keeping, the finding is not. General lesson now in the module docstring: removing a confound's LEVEL is not removing the confound, and a decomposition that reports how much quality it stripped can still be reporting quality afterwards. Any future reading of a resolved axis quotes maturity beside it or means nothing.

title: Forty-four packaged free seats: the entry that ships with a kernel edit and no push
description:
MEASURED, by `python -m kneemri.kaggle.roster_reads --max-decodes 1` over the packaged roster (which
groups checkpoints by the same `Member.decode_key` the kernel serves under, so it cannot disagree with a
submission):

  read B  canonical / 12sl / 0.2-0.8 / 224+336+448 — 17 packaged and UNSEATED, one decode, asserted
  read A  canonical / 20sl / 0.1-0.9 / 336         — 24 packaged and UNSEATED, one decode, asserted
  span    canonical / 12sl / 0.1-0.9 / 336         —  3 packaged and UNSEATED, one decode, asserted

The pinned champion `raptorseat_v1` already pays for all three (final_ws_cf + grade_ladder_cf +
through_dense_cf on A, merged_blend_cf + lr4e-5_ws_cf on B, calib_span_ff on span, plus the foreign
raptor's own read = four decodes). So forty-four packaged members sit on decodes ALREADY BOUGHT.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEAD FROM knee-z652, which prices the same axis over what is on DISK. The
difference is what a positive costs to act on: a positive there needs a dataset push (upload minutes to
hours) plus a kernel edit plus a slot; a positive here needs a kernel edit plus a slot, today. Five slots
a day reset at 00:00 UTC and a push is the step that has repeatedly made a slot unusable in the window it
was planned for. A ranked list of seats needing no push is the list a slot can actually be spent from.

Read B is the interesting one twice over: largest pool AND the only read carrying three resolutions, so
its unseated members bring resolution diversity as well as treatment diversity on a decode already paid.
The span read is the thinnest — one seat on a whole decode — so it is the cheapest place to look for a
second seat if reads hold several seats at all.

THE ARM: experiments/arms/packaged_seats.sh, queued behind trio_seat_value (itself behind merged_span_cf).
It asserts the one-decode cost claim FIRST (--max-decodes 1 on each list), then prices each list with
`seat_value` against the pinned champion. Bar is the 0.0062 holdout floor and nothing else: there is no
decode budget to trade against.

HOW IT IS READ, pre-registered:
  * any candidate at or above the floor -> kernel edit off the champion's `chosen` tuple, one slot, no
    push, no fit.
  * all inside the floor, positive -> the reads are saturated at what the champion already holds; the
    free-seat lane is a COST result only and the next slot goes to a genuinely NEW read (decode
    distance) rather than a wider one.
  * all negative -> seats on a paid read actively harm, which sits against trioseat_v1 (three seats,
    one decode, 0.938 vs a 0.925 single). Read as a question, not a verdict.

vjepa_warm_s2026 (0.8337) and mae_matched_s2026 (0.6735) are deliberately IN the read-A pool: a member
far below the seated ones is exactly where alone-quality and seat-value have disagreed here before
(calib_span, base_dense), and excluding them on their own control would repeat an error the champion's
own principles record.

Offline is not the board: knee-nas5 measured this axis transferring at 2.4x (0.0059 offline -> 0.014
board), the only ensemble axis here that amplifies. Inside the floor offline is not dead, but it is not
evidence and no slot is spent on one.

title: Log every constant that entered the model at run start (normalization, loss weights, off-by-default flags)
description:
celltrack found an entire head family trained with the InfoNCE weight at 0.0 -- the trainer's own default -- because the launch scripts omitted the flag. Their tell was the loss breakdown printing 'nce 0.0000' every step: the feature announcing it never switched on.

We have no equivalent. The normalization constants are a registered torch buffer set at construction (kneemri/models/model.py:228) and nothing logs them at run start. Normalization.assert_declared is an INTEGRATION TEST against the HuggingFace snapshot -- it guards the registry, never the run -- and in the broken era it could not have fired at all, because there was one global IMAGENET constant and nothing to disagree with it. The raddino defect was found from DATES (run 2026-08-23, fix 2026-08-25), not from any log.

Rule: a feature whose OFF state is also its DEFAULT must announce itself at startup, because that is exactly the class where an omitted flag and a deliberate choice are indistinguishable afterwards. Both bugs are in that class -- their --contrastive-weight defaulting to 0.0, our normalization defaulting to IMAGENET for every encoder.

Do: one log line at the top of a training run naming the encoder variant, its normalization mean/std as the model actually holds them (read the BUFFER, not the config), every loss term weight, and every flag whose default is falsy. Read from the constructed object so it asserts the value LANDED rather than that the config carried it.

title: Graduate ledger_check's unattributed advisory: 13 runs quote a number another run provably owns
description:

The philosophy is graduated gates: a check starts advisory and becomes enforced once the code is clean. The 13 collided rows are the clean-able subset. Fix them (give each run a same-line row of its own), then the collided count is the thing to enforce — `if collided: raise SystemExit(1)` — while the plain 46-loose count stays advisory, because a gate failing on a third of a correct-enough ledger is one the reader learns to skip.

The 46 are printed as one line, the 13 individually, so the actionable subset is already separated in the output. Blocked on nothing; it is bounded reading work.

title: Arm a band_wide twin at the champion fit regime — a seat covering the resolved deficit axis
description:
First card arm when the GPU returns; better argued than the calibrated-blend cross (knee-brkd's neighbour) because it aims at a BOUNDED weakness.

MECHANISM, measured today at zero cost from records already on disk. The supervision gap resolves three deficit findings (ACL, MCL, Lateral Meniscus) whose paired bands exclude zero while the aggregate does not (knee-yx0n). In-plane resolution does not reach them: lr4e-5 vs res392 reads ACL +0.0109, MCL -0.0088, LatMen -0.0001, nothing marked. THROUGH-PLANE DOES, and in the wrong direction for us: band_wide_s2026 (16 slices) vs band_dense_s2026 (20), the only diff 'slices 16->20', reads PF OA +0.0194*, Medial OA +0.0122*, Synovitis +0.0135 against MCL -0.0111, ACL -0.0037, LatMen -0.0007. All three deficit findings move negative TOGETHER, MCL the largest negative on the table, against a +/-0.0315 band.

So band_dense's +0.0025 is a TRADE (centre bought with collaterals and cruciates), and the champion family is dense - it holds the losing side of exactly the three findings the gap resolves as its deficit. band_wide is a diversity seat with a mechanism: worse on the mean, better where the roster is measurably weak.

WHY IT IS NOT A SLOT. band_wide_s2026 is _s2026 and the champion's seats are _cf/_ff; swapping across fit regimes gives back the +0.004 the regime is worth, more than this axis could pay. It needs a TWIN trained at the champion's regime.

DISCOUNT, pre-registered: every seat permutation on this board prices between -0.004 and +0.001 (see 2026-08-27_every-no-card-axis-is-priced-and-flat.md). What is new is the selection RULE - a resolved per-finding deficit rather than the offline mean - which is a different die, not a better roll. Three same-sign moves on three findings named in advance by an unrelated measurement is a pattern; no single one of them is marked.

See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_the-supervision-gap-is-four-findings-not-an-average.md.
notes:
REFUTED ON ITS CONTENT, 2026-08-27, by the instrument this bead asked for. kneemri/evaluation/competence_axis.py reads 105 members x 12 findings over 909 shared studies: double-centred (by finding, then by member), first component against a column-shuffle null.

READING. Member QUALITY takes 81.7% of the spread and is removed before the axis is read. Component 1 then takes 45.9% of what is left against a null bar of 27.7% - so a shared axis exists, but it carries about 8% of the total member-to-member variation.

The axis is NOT centre-vs-periphery. Loadings: Synovitis -0.451, Effusion -0.388, Medial OA -0.198, Lateral OA -0.181 at one end; Baker's +0.649, Fracture +0.316, Medial Meniscus +0.215 at the other. A fluid-and-inflammation axis. The centre/periphery hypothesis in this bead was generalised from ONE controlled pair (band_wide vs band_dense) and 105 members disagree with it.

WHAT REPLACES IT, and it is better. The flat seat search is explained by the 81.7%: a pool that differs almost entirely by uniform quality has nothing to trade, so no selector can extract diversity from it. And the three resolved deficit findings - ACL, MCL, Lateral Meniscus - load +0.014, +0.053, +0.028 (near zero) while their own spreads read 0.0141, 0.0165, 0.0183 (ordinary, above Contusion's 0.0097). They vary across members as much as anything else, ORTHOGONALLY to the shared axis. Idiosyncratic variation is exactly what a flat rank-average destroys and exactly what a targeted selector could keep.

Full reading: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_the-pool-is-82-percent-one-number.md

title: Cross the two treatments that actually paid: calibrated targets ON a blend-supervised twin
description:
The board's own lesson, read across 58 submissions on 2026-08-27: the only two changes worth more than one tick are TREATMENTS APPLIED TO EVERY SEAT AT ONCE, never seat permutations.

  votefit 0.938 -> calibsix 0.941   --calibrated-targets on all six      +0.003
  fit regime                        --fold -1 on every seat              +0.004 (ema_dense separates EMA at +0.0010)

Every seat permutation tried since is worth between -0.004 and +0.001.

Blend supervision is the ONLY other treatment of the all-seats shape - it changes the label SOURCE (external expert reads, Rijeka) where calibration re-scales the label VALUES. Different mechanisms on different parts of the pipeline is the standard precondition for two effects to add rather than overlap. The cross has never been built: no calibrated blend twin exists.

Honest discount, pre-registered: the blend DOSE curve is flat from one seat to three (votefit 0.938 -> blendseat 0.939 -> blendthree 0.939), so blend's own axis may be saturated and the cross may inherit that. What licenses arming it anyway is that dose was measured as seat REPLACEMENT while calibration was measured as an all-seat TREATMENT, and the board says only the second shape pays. The cross has not been measured in the shape that works.

Card question, not a slot question - needs a blend-supervised twin trained with --calibrated-targets. First thing to arm when the card returns from the peer project. Smoke it with arm_check --only <arm> --smoke <throwaway dir> --smoke-studies 60 before queueing.

title: The vote rule is the one ensemble axis never measured offline, and the champion disagrees with the ruler
description:
Every offline reading in experiments/README.md was taken under RankAverage - the Pool.vote default - while the shipped champion kneemri-calibsix combines with LogitAverage, and has since kneemri-vote. So the ruler and the entry have never agreed on the combination rule, which makes every offline->board transfer this project quotes carry an unmeasured rule change on top of the population mismatch already recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_seat-count-is-flat-both-rulers.md.

record_mix --vote now offers rank, logit and median (MedianLogit has never been submitted at all). The axis is zero-training and zero-upload: it changes one line of the kernel's combine step, not a member. Price all three on the largest agreeing pool with LabelScores.paired_mean_interval, which can now bound a named pair on the competition metric directly.

Caveat that bounds what it buys: the offline pool is the _s2026 family and the champion is _cf/_ff, so a rule result transfers only if the rule is family-independent. A combination rule is far more plausibly family-independent than member identity is, but that is an argument, not a measurement.
notes:
CORRECTED before any compute was spent. The central claim - that the vote axis was never measured - is WRONG, and comp/board.jsonl says so in two CONTROLLED single-variable pairs:

  2 seats:  efficient_v4 0.919 -> vote_v2    0.919  ( 0.000)
  6 seats:  dark6_v1     0.937 -> votefit_v1 0.938  (+0.001)

Both are the same six/two members with LogitAverage swapped for RankAverage and every other variable held. Rank->logit buys zero to one board tick, at or under BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015, and the champion already serves the better side of it. So the offline ruler defaulting to RankAverage while the champion serves LogitAverage is a documentation discrepancy worth one line, NOT the unmeasured axis this bead claimed, and it does not license a submission slot.

What survives, much smaller: MedianLogit has never been submitted and appears in no board row, so it is the only untried member of VOTE_RULES. Given the two measured points bracket the axis at ~0.001, its prior is a null too - price it offline on the pool with paired_mean_interval if the pool is being read anyway, never as a slot of its own.

Third false start this session caught by reading the record before spending. The first two were the fit-regime 'discovery' and the seat-count transfer; the rule that catches them is CLAUDE.md's read-the-ledger-and-the-board-first, and it has now paid three times in one window.

title: board_transfer slope must not be applied to a seat-count delta
description:
The fitted slope of +2.14 board points per holdout point was fitted on member QUALITY changes — a better member measured solo, then seated. It is not a general exchange rate between the offline ruler and the board.

On 2026-08-27 it was nearly used to price a seat-count delta: the honest curve reads 12 seats +0.0030 over 6, which at +2.14 predicts +0.0064 board, i.e. 0.941 -> 0.947 for zero training. Both halves of that are wrong. The 0.0030 span is inside the 0.0062 paired holdout floor, and the board had ALREADY run the experiment: honest12 is that exact twelve-member roster and scored 0.937 against calibsix's 0.941. The sign flipped, not just the magnitude.

Same class as the compression constant being quoted from prose twice (board_check). Action: board_transfer's docstring/report must state the axis it was fitted on and refuse — or at minimum warn — when asked to price a delta that is not a member-quality change. title: Harness checks keyed by parameter name must resolve on a known-good checkpoint first
description:
labelwise_dense pre-registered 'slices.pool.gate.3.weight' to assert its per-diagnosis attention gate had trained. That key does not exist; the real one is 'slices.gate.3.weight'. The dump came back an EMPTY key list, which is indistinguishable from the dead-gate failure the check was written to catch — on a run whose gate was in fact healthy (absmax 0.171, std 0.059, whole stack trained off its zero init).

A mechanism-fired check that names a key must first be shown to resolve on a checkpoint known to have the mechanism. Otherwise the check reports its own typo as the result, and it does so in the direction that kills a working idea. Same class as the CLAUDE.md 'faulty PLUMBING' bullet: assert the flag LANDED.

Fix: a small helper that raises on an unresolved key pattern instead of returning an empty list, used by every arm header that greps a state dict.

title: A new member costs a 7 GB package push before it can take a seat — the last-slot plan has to start it early
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-27T17:57Z, while de-risking the 23:30Z slot with five hours of margin rather than five minutes.

kneemri-calibsix mounts dimiturnt/kneemri-members, which is the all_ours directory: 58 files, 7.0 GB. A member is small — calib_dense_hold_s2026.pt is 86 MB, and a labelwise member would be the same — but the Kaggle dataset CLI versions a DIRECTORY, not a delta, so putting one 86 MB member in front of a kernel re-uploads all 7 GB.

THE SECOND-MOUNT SHORTCUT IS REFUSED, and not for lack of imagination. Adding a small kneemri-member-<name> dataset to dataset_sources would upload 86 MB instead of 7 GB, but MemberPackage.shipped_root (kneemri/inference/members.py:474) exists specifically to keep ONE directory carrying that dataset id: a second home aged silently on 2026-08-18 and made mount_check refuse a valid kernel. Manifest, fingerprints and the tie rule are all package-scoped. Inventing a two-package mount hours before a submission is the kind of unforced change that loses the slot, not the kind that wins it.

SO THE PLAN IS TIMING, NOT ARCHITECTURE. Any last-slot play that needs a member not already in all_ours must start its push as soon as the member lands, not when the slot is fired. Note that all_ours is ALREADY behind the members on disk — blend_through.pt was written 2026-08-26 and is not in the package, which is why mount_check refuses kneemri-blendall for blend_through and blend_base.

AND THE CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE IS REAL, so it must be priced against the swap rather than skipped. A last slot spent on a new COMBINATION over members already packaged costs zero upload and zero risk of a half-pushed dataset. It is only worth less if the new member's seat value beats what re-weighting the existing 58 can buy. Decide that with numbers when the member has a holdout record — do not default to the swap because the member is new.

UNMEASURED, and it gates the timing: nothing here records how long a 7 GB push actually takes. The first one that runs should be timed and the number written into this issue.

title: queue_check counts the Bash-tool nohup wrapper shell as a second watcher and reports DOUBLE-QUEUED
description:
FALSE POSITIVE, 2026-08-27. queue_check reported DOUBLE-QUEUED: experiments/arms/contrast_dense.sh. The process table held two matches: pid 919283, the real watcher (bash experiments/after.sh ...), and pid 919281, the nohup wrapper shell the Bash tool launches, whose argv QUOTES THE ENTIRE COMMAND. A substring match over argv therefore counts one chain twice. Only one after_*.log names the arm.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC MISCOUNT. The documented response to DOUBLE-QUEUED is to kill all but one chain. Following it here would have killed the only live watcher and left the card idle after fuse_regions finished - which is the EXACT hole queue_check exists to close, opened by queue_check itself.

FIX, either of: (a) match argv[0..1] == (bash, experiments/after.sh) rather than a substring anywhere in the command line; or (b) drop any matching process that is the PARENT of another match, since a wrapper always is. (b) is cheaper and also covers whatever the next harness wraps things in.

VERIFY WITH: launch a watcher through the Bash tool nohup path, then run queue_check --directory experiments/logs; it must report OK with one live process, not DOUBLE-QUEUED.

title: queue_check counts the nohup wrapper shell as a second watcher, so one armed chain reads DOUBLE-QUEUED
description:

title: Raptor's published label table cannot be scored on the 58, because its author removed them
description:
dreaddevelopment/rsna-knee-labels (labels_llm_soft.csv, 4349 studies x 12, published 2026-08-14, pulled to D:/data/external/raptor/labels/) is a SECOND INDEPENDENT LLM read of the same 4407 reports we read. It is the only foreign reader whose author states its provenance and whose model weights are also published.

IT CANNOT BE PLACED ON OUR RULER. 4349 = 4407 - 58. The 58 radiologist-annotated studies are exactly the ones the author held out, so `kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap --labels <their csv>` returns labels 0.5000 for all twelve findings - an empty join, not a score. Our own table reads 0.8658 on that ruler and the best public foreign table reads 0.8927; theirs reads NOTHING. Any claim that their labels are better or worse than ours is unmeasurable with the instruments this repo has.

WHAT IS MEASURABLE, AND THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS. rubric_gap over both tables, same eight rules, same reports: ours 502 contradicted cells over the rules the annotations BACK, theirs 34 - a 93% reduction, and 1600 vs 157 over all eight. That looks like a better reader and IS NOT SHOWN TO BE ONE. The control: their macro positive rate is 0.187 against our 0.303, lower on 11 of 12 columns. A reader that says negative more often contradicts a negative-class rule less often for free. rubric_gap cannot separate a better threshold from a more negative one, and this is the confound to state whenever that tool is pointed at a foreign table.

BASE RATE AGAINST THE 58 AS REFEREE (the annotated positive rate per column, the one truth available). Mean absolute error of the corpus positive rate against it: OURS 0.109, THEIRS 0.158. Ours is closer on 7 of 12. The readable gaps - the referee's own SE at n=58 is ~0.06, so only large ones count - are Effusion (ours off by 0.001, theirs by 0.347), ACL (0.139 vs 0.284), Lateral Meniscus (0.146 vs 0.262) and Contusion (0.038 vs 0.176) in OUR favour; Synovitis (0.336 vs 0.221) and Medial OA (0.108 vs 0.013) in theirs. Both tables sit far below the annotated rate on Fracture (0.068 and 0.037 vs 0.310), which is the known report-vs-image gap, not a reader defect.

THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING. Inter-reader correlation per column is 0.72-0.90 on eleven findings and 0.389 ON SYNOVITIS. Two independent LLM readers of the SAME reports barely agree there. Corroboration from two directions: their own model's worst label is Synovitis at 0.7575 (read from the checkpoint's own aucs dict), and forum topic 737566 is titled 'Why everyone Synovitis AUC is stuck around 0.6-0.7'. Synovitis being label-limited has been suspected here; this is the first evidence that is INDEPENDENT of our reader.

DO NOT spend a card arm on adopting or blending this table. table_blend already measured that blending readers on this ruler moves +0.0015 [-0.0069, +0.0121] - unresolved - and that averaging our coarser table into a stronger reader DILUTES it. A fourth reader that cannot be scored on the ruler adds an unauditable input to a blend the ruler already cannot resolve.

title: An arm snapshots the WORKING TREE at launch, so an uncommitted half-edit kills a queued arm hours later
description:
fuse_regions died at 12:44Z, eight seconds in, with 'TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable Readout object' at trainer.py:392 — inside experiments/fuse_regions.src, the snapshot lib.sh takes at launch.

The tree was NOT broken. It was MID-EDIT: model.py already returned the new Readout dataclass and trainer.py had not yet been rewritten to read it when fuse_attend finished and the chained fuse_regions started. The snapshot froze that torn instant. Every gate would have passed minutes later, and did.

The cost was a card window, not a file: fuse_regions had been chained behind fuse_attend precisely so no wall-clock was lost, and instead the card sat idle from 12:44Z.

The rule this wants: while ANY arm is queued or chained, edits to shared training code land as a COMMIT or not at all — a queued arm reads the tree at ITS start time, not at the time you last thought about it. Options worth pricing: (a) lib.sh snapshots from 'git stash create'/HEAD rather than the dirty tree, which makes the snapshot reproducible as well as safe; (b) a launch-time refusal when 'git status --porcelain' touches kneemri/training or kneemri/models; (c) nothing but this note, on the argument that arms are usually launched from a clean tree.

title: Per-finding label calibration: arm on the dense-hold corner, pre-registered
description:
core/data/labels/finding_calibration.py fits one empirical-Bayes-shrunk logit offset per finding on top of the pooled MEASURED_AGREEMENT map. tau=0.294 (sd 0.543 logits) survives the moment subtraction, so the twelve findings do not share one scale. Shipped as FINDING_OFFSETS in core/data/labels/targets.py behind --finding-calibration (REQUIRES --calibrated-targets; UncalibratedFindingShiftError otherwise).

WHY: noise_binding (2026-08-27) shows every --hold-annotations member tracks the reader's 108 confident false positives at +0.54 to +0.70, and that --calibrated-targets cuts that by ~0.15 at two independent corners. The pooled map flattens a 37-point per-finding spread (Contusion 44.4% vs Synovitis 81.2% agreement on positive calls) and the two fail in OPPOSITE directions, so one pooled number cannot carry both.

PRICE: ~40 min of card, no submission slot. Expected offline +0.002-0.004 - DIRECTIONAL, under the house bar. Justified as an INSTRUMENT: it licenses or kills a whole family (per-finding loss weighting, per-finding thresholds, per-finding heads), and a label-table change is the 126-147% pass-through class because it retrains every seat.

PRE-REGISTERED against calib_dense_hold 0.8634 (paired three-seed floor 0.0062):
  >= 0.8696  the lever is real, open the per-finding family
  0.8572-0.8696  FLAT on this ruler - but see the caveat, do not kill on this alone
  <= 0.8572  it hurts; the pooled map is right and the family closes

HARNESS CAVEAT, stated before the run: the offline holdout is scored against the REPORT labels, which carry the very defect these offsets correct. The offline ruler is biased AGAINST this table, so its number is a FLOOR. The primary rulers are kneemri.evaluation.annotated_readings (the radiologist read) and kneemri.evaluation.noise_binding (does the binding to the lexicon drop below --calibrated-targets alone?).

SELF-CRITIQUE, priced in: a per-finding MONOTONE map leaves each head's own ranking unchanged, so in the well-specified limit per-head AUC is untouched. Whatever this buys comes through the SHARED TRUNK and cross-head gradient balance - the same indirect route the pooled calibration must already be working through. That caps the expected size at second-order relative to the pooled +0.0061.

title: convergence_check is blind to any run not in the ledger, and epochs_done reads like a truncation when it is not
description:
Today the four 2x2 hold checkpoints (band_span_hold, calib_span_hold, band_dense_hold, calib_dense_hold) each stamp epoch=6..9, epochs_done=7..10, epochs=12, patience=0. Read straight off the checkpoint that is the exact TRUNCATED signature the check defines: died short of the budget it asked for, no stopper armed, so the score is a FLOOR. I was one step from recording all four scores as floors and hedging the additivity finding on it.

They are not truncated. The .metrics.jsonl files carry e0..e11 for all four - every run completed its full 12 epochs and peaked mid-run on the one_cycle tail. So epochs_done does NOT mean epochs completed, and nothing in the checkpoint says what it does mean.

TWO HOLES, both live:

1. convergence_check --run <name> answers '1 runs: 1 unscored' for every one of these, because it reads the LEDGER and these runs were never scored into it. The check that exists to stop a floor being quoted as a fact is silent on exactly the runs most likely to be quoted from a checkpoint - the ones no arm recorded.

2. The truncation verdict is derived from epochs_done when .metrics.jsonl is the ground truth and is sitting next to the checkpoint. A run's own per-epoch curve says whether it finished; a counter of ambiguous meaning should not outrank it.

FIX: convergence_check should fall back to the metrics file when a run is absent from the ledger, and should prefer the metrics line count over epochs_done wherever both exist. Either rename epochs_done to what it actually counts or drop it from the stamp.

COST OF NOT FIXING: the same misread in the other direction - a genuinely truncated run whose epochs_done happens to read full - would quote a floor as a converged score, which is the failure this check was built for.

title: The deadline is 2026-10-22: ~280 slots remain, and the ratchet reaches 0.950 without a step change
description:
Read from the Kaggle API 2026-08-26 22:45Z: deadline 2026-10-22 23:59, 2469 teams, our rank 46. 56 days remain, ~5 slots a day, so roughly 280 submissions - not five. The deadline appeared in no doc, bead, kernel or interpretation before today; every plan was made against the recurring prompt's four-hour horizon.

Our running-best climbs +0.0016/day over 9 days (+0.0010 over the last 3). 0.950 needs +0.011, i.e. 7-11 days, inside the window with 45 days to spare. Of 57 scored submissions 18 set a new best (31.6%), but every one of the last eleven was +0.003 or smaller - individually knobs, together +0.014 since 08-18. The project is running a working RATCHET, not failing to find a lever.

Consequences to hold to:
1. Slots are not the scarce resource; card hours and ideas are. 'Spread the slots' is a DAILY rule and correct as one - it must not be read as a global scarcity that argues against firing an informative arm.
2. Do not abandon the ratchet for a step change. Pursue a step change in PARALLEL - that is what closes on first place rather than on 0.950.
3. Seating is the ratchet's cheapest fuel and nearly spent: nine six-member entries span 0.014 total, and the last two gains came from a vote rule (votefit) and better label supervision (blendseat), not a seat swap.

title: The reader over-calls 108 cells and hides 24 - a replacement must be built for PRECISION, not coverage
description:
Displaces the sizing argument in knee-pju4 (see its notes, measured 2026-08-26 22:33Z).

THE MEASUREMENT. core.data.labels.reader_agreement --> silence/silence_report, over 684 annotated cells / 57 studies:
  177 silent cells (25.9%, matching the corpus 27.3%)
  radiologist positive rate 13.6% among SILENT cells, 41.6% among spoken ones
  perfect silence-filler ceiling: 24 cells. Over-calling: 108 cells.

So the reader's dominant defect is saying YES where the radiologist says no - 108 of 684 cells, 15.8% of everything annotated, and errors() reports every one of them as a confident YES rather than an abstention. Per-finding net over-calling: Contusion +18, Effusion +16, ACL +9, MCL +9, Medial OA +7, Lateral Meniscus +7. Synovitis is the sole inversion at -11.

WHY THE CONFIDENCE COLUMN CANNOT HELP. __conf takes one value per verdict level (std 0.0 over all 52,872 cells), so it is a deterministic function of the verdict and cannot downweight a confident error. This is the same defect knee-b8g9 names from the forum side: LLM self-reported confidence measures certainty in APPLYING A HEURISTIC TO TEXT, not diagnostic uncertainty.

WHAT TO BUILD, in order of size:
1. A precision-tuned second pass over the cells the lexicon calls YES (311 of 684 annotated; corpus-wide the YES cells, not the blank ones). The acceptance test is reader_agreement's own per-language and per-finding agreement table, run before and after - it exists and it refuses tables it cannot read.
2. A targeted Synovitis pass. 84.2% UNK corpus-wide, 41 silent of 58 annotated, 14 hidden positives - the only finding where silence is the larger failure, and the finding whose labels predict the radiologist worst (0.6870, supervision_gap).
3. Only then the general blank-filling of knee-pju4, which is now priced at <=3.5% of cells.

CONSTRAINT WORTH STATING: our member already scores 0.8932 against the radiologist while its teacher scores 0.8658 (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_our-model-is-past-its-teacher.md). The model is ALREADY discounting the teacher's over-calls to some degree. A better table has to beat what the model has learned to ignore, which is a higher bar than beating the table.

DENOMINATOR: 684 cells / 57 studies / 1.3% of the corpus. 108 and 24 are small integers with no intervals - read the RATIO, not the rates.

title: The efficiency board says the leaders are not ensembles - price seating against member quality accordingly
description:
Topic 736678, read 2026-08-26 22:20Z, written up in research/2026-08-26_rival_single_models_and_the_label_bottleneck.md.

Two competitor statements that together make the reading: (a) only ~32% of the public LB top 50 also appear in the efficiency LB top 50, and (b) the top TWO public LB submissions do appear on the efficiency board. The broad plateau is slow; the very top is fast. A third poster is efficiency-LB #1 with no ensemble at all, and a fourth sits at Efficiency 22 / Public 78 with 0.926 on a ~20-minute single-model 5-fold pipeline.

Read together: ensembling is what the 0.936-0.940 plateau is MADE of, and the leaders are above it without one. We reached 0.939 through six members. Eleven of our entries now sit in 0.936-0.939 across count, member identity, fold status, regularisation, encoder family, architecture family, vote rule, serving views, corpus and supervision.

What this is NOT: a licence to drop the ensemble. 0.939 is our best result and decode-path diversity is the only axis with a measured board transfer (knee-nas5, 2.4x). It is a PRICE: another seating variation is a knob on a plateau the field says tops out near 0.94; a better member is the axis the leaders are on.

Note the disagreement worth keeping rather than merging: the forum says the lever is a better MODEL; our own gold-label reading (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_our-model-is-past-its-teacher.md) says our model is already 0.027 ABOVE its teacher and the lever is better LABELS. Both point away from seating. knee-pju4 (P0, the local relabeller) is the one that satisfies both readings, since better labels are how a better member gets built here.

No slot and no card needed to act on this - it is a ranking of the open levers, not an experiment.

description:

resseat (fired 2026-08-26) enters res392_ws_s2026: quality-NEUTRAL by construction (twin solos 0.8523 vs the outgoing 0.8525) so only the decode path changes, but it introduces a SECOND fold-0 seat into a six that otherwise runs full-fit.

title: LLM confidence measures heuristic-application certainty, not diagnostic uncertainty
description:
A competitor states the defect our calibrated-target arms inherit (topic 735826): asking an LLM for its confidence in a finding returns its confidence in APPLYING THE HEURISTIC TO THE TEXT, not the uncertainty in the diagnosis. It will be very confident that 'small effusion' means Effusion=0, because the rule is clear and the words are clear — while the process that produced the word 'small' rather than 'moderate' was itself noisy and is where the real uncertainty lives.

Evidence it is not merely an argument: filter reports whose effusion sentence carries a small-size qualifier (small/minimal/trace) and the group contains BOTH Effusion=0 and Effusion=1; two reports with the same English template and the same sentence carry opposite labels, and at least one 'moderate effusion' report is labelled 0.

Consequence for us: every calibrated/soft-target arm treats reader disagreement as if it were model uncertainty, with the confidence pointing the wrong way exactly where the labels are least reliable. Cross-check against core/data/labels/severity_boundary.py and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_effusion-threshold-ruler.md, which found the boundary independently. A soft target derived from AGREEMENT BETWEEN READERS is the mechanism-correct replacement; a soft target derived from LLM self-reported confidence is not.

title: Uniform-lift census over 85 matched pairs: no second candidate exists
description:
The "stack three independent uniform lifts" plan for +0.0133 offline is NOT executable: the disk
record contains exactly one uniform-lift candidate, and its evidence is confounded.

METHOD. 175 .pt records, 155 carry a recipe. Matched pairs = differ in exactly one recipe key,
ignoring non-semantic keys (out/labels/paths/eval_labels/vram_gb/compile_encoder/
recompute_activations/accumulate/batch/cache_studies) and the banned axis (seed/split_seed).
Ignoring those took the count from 56 pairs / 27 switches to 85 pairs / 22 switches. Each pair
scored by RunMetrics.best(); a switch is a uniform lift only if the sign holds across DISTINCT
seats and the magnitude clears the 0.0062 three-seed noise floor.

RESULT, every switch with >= 2 scored pairs:

  calibrated_targets  +0.0072 (band_span_hold -> calib_span_hold)
                      +0.0061 (band_dense_hold -> calib_dense_hold)
                      -0.0020 (band_span      -> calib_span)
      NOT uniform. Both positives carry --hold-annotations; the one seat without it reads
      NEGATIVE. This independently reproduces the confound calibsix.sh already names at its
      lines 75-82 and deliberately declines to resolve. No new information, but it is now
      measured from the record rather than argued from three quoted pairs.

  intensity_aug off   +0.0077 (aug_long -> band_dense_long, 336px/20sl/24ep)
                      +0.0064 (intensity392_ws -> res392_ws, 448px/12sl/12ep)
      Uniform in sign, both above the noise floor, two genuinely distant seats. And worth
      ZERO: only 2 records in the whole corpus ever set intensity_aug=True, and both ARE this
      experiment. Every production seat already trains with it off. A closed negative, not an
      available lever.

  bf16 off            +0.0024 +0.0017 +0.0016 +0.0013 (4/4 positive)
      All four share one base seat (throughput_*), all four below the noise floor, and the
      owner has standing direction for bf16 training / fp16 serving. Not a lever.

  unfreeze_last 6->4  0/5 positive (-0.0062 .. -0.0073); 6->12 -0.0148. Settled at 6.
  slice_regions       0/4 positive. regions=4 loses to None/1 uniformly. Closed negative.
  slices 20->12/16    0/3 positive. Settled at 20.
  hold_annotations    2 pairs, both small and opposite-signed. Unresolved on its own.
  variant             7 pairs, 3 positive, mixed. v3base loses to both base and small.
  mixup               7 pairs, 2 positive, all |d| < 0.0070. Scatter.
  epochs, backbone_lr, encoder_weights  dominated by one huge pair each (a 1-epoch throughput
      probe, a 2e-4 divergence, a null-adapter). Not comparisons of settings.

CONSEQUENCE. There is no second uniform-lift flag on disk to stack. Every remaining candidate
would need a fresh matched pair ON CARD to price, which is the resource we do not have. The
+0.0133 offline that 0.950 now costs (see knee-ps8o: transfer is +0.83, not +1.72) has no
in-repo lever sized for it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR calibsix (knee-1c00). Priced honestly: 7.1 h for a pooled solo +0.0038 whose
only unconfounded pair reads -0.0020, times ~0.83 transfer = ~+0.003 board, against a 0.0062
noise floor. Odds of clearing the 1.5% bar: ~0. The arm that the RECORD supports is
--calibrated-targets WITH --hold-annotations (+0.0072 / +0.0061); calibsix declines that as
reassembly, which is a defensible choice about seat identity but leaves it running the one
configuration the data reads negative on. Not changing a 7.1 h arm unilaterally - flagged for
the owner.

Probe script was throwaway (job tmp). Not building uniform_lift.py: the record it would read
has now been read, and it says no.

title: Forum sweep 2026-08-26: single models reach 0.942, and our model does not beat its teacher
description:
Zero-slot research sweep of the competition forum plus three of our own instruments, run while the card was busy with blendhold.

WHAT STANDS.

1. SINGLE-MODEL FRONTIER. Topic 735304 carries several independent single-model claims: 0.942 at 224px ('single model 0.934 @ 224px, update: 0.942 with some tweaks'), 0.938 single-model single-fold, 0.934, plus a cluster at 0.915-0.929. Our board single is 0.925 and our SIX-MEMBER ensemble is 0.939 -- so a claimed single model beats our whole ensemble. Unverified claims, per the owner's standing warning about notebook claims, but the efficiency-leaderboard argument underneath is structural rather than honesty-dependent: high-scoring entries have short runtimes, so they are not 20-model ensembles. This corroborates our own seat pricing (23% pass-through of a new member into a saturated pool) from the opposite direction: MEMBER QUALITY is the bottleneck and the combiner never was.

2. WE DO NOT BEAT OUR TEACHER. kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap on report_labels_v2 over 58 annotated studies / 696 cells: labels 0.8658, model 0.8392. A forum reply proposes exactly this diagnostic ('if your image model is not beating the label extractor teacher, there is likely modeling headroom'). By that rule the binding constraint for US is MODELING, not labels -- which is the opposite of the forum's own majority answer (most replies vote label quality). Per-finding the split is clean by structure type: the model beats the reader on the diffuse findings (Effusion +0.130, Contusion +0.089, Synovitis +0.051, Medial OA +0.042, Baker's +0.023, Fracture +0.016) and loses on the thin focal ones (Lateral Meniscus -0.193, ACL -0.123, MCL -0.096, Medial Meniscus -0.094, PF OA -0.086, Lateral OA -0.079). CAVEAT ON THE DENOMINATOR: the per-finding numbers rest on 58 studies where our own severity_boundary work prices the per-label standard error at 0.04-0.09, so the RANKING is weak evidence and only the aggregate and the coarse diffuse-vs-focal split should be quoted.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE. calibsix and margin_calib are both label/target-side flags, aimed at the term this measurement says is not binding. It does NOT refute them -- their case is direct measurement (+0.0038 pooled solo, +0.0056 and +0.0084 ensembled on two nested pools), not a theory about which term binds -- but it lowers the prior on any FURTHER label-reader work, and it argues the next NEW arm should be model-side.

WHAT DIED, and all of it died on evidence already on disk at zero card cost.

3. BAND GEOMETRY, re-read on the right ruler. The band axis was closed on the 12-label macro, where a fix recovering all of Lateral Meniscus's headroom would show as +0.016 -- inside the 0.0062 floor, the 'metric averaging the effect away' failure. run_comparison prices band members per-label AND by structure scale, so the question was already answerable: Lateral Meniscus moves -0.0058 / +0.0007 / -0.0035 / +0.0036 across band_span, band_wide, band_full, band140 against half-widths of +/-0.03. band_full restores the ENTIRE band and Lateral Meniscus still reads -0.0035, so 'the 0.2-0.8 band deletes the lateral compartment' is refuted from the one direction that could refute it. Band axis stays closed, now on a ruler that could have seen the effect.

4. SIDE-BLINDNESS, rediscovered and already retired. side_blindness reads Lateral OA at 0.5184 [0.4364, 0.6014] -- indistinguishable from side-blind -- while Medial OA resolves at 0.7328 and both menisci resolve, with PF OA clean as a control. Both positional members are equally blind (through_dense 0.5092, depth_regions 0.5261), so no mechanism we own touches it. But interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-23_side_resolution_is_not_score.md settled this on 2026-08-22: side_dense moved the Lateral OA contrast +0.062 and the holdout mean -0.0641, with the term verified landed three ways. An AUC orders study-against-study within a label; the side term orders label-against-label within a study; the orderings are orthogonal and buying one costs the other. That doc explicitly retires the contrast as a selection instrument. My rediscovery adds nothing and cost twenty minutes that reading the interpretation first would have saved -- the second time in one session the ledger has caught a finding I was about to file.

5. TWO KNEES IN ONE DICOM (topic 735639, posted today). 7 studies of 4,407 = 0.16%. Not a lever. The laterality question underneath it is already handled: core/data/corpus/laterality.py normalises to a left-knee convention using a geometric rule covering 100% of the corpus where the DICOM tag covers 49.3%, it is consumed through study.py, and augmentation.py forbids horizontal flips precisely to protect it.

title: crop_alignment.dump writes spread, not the centroid offset magnitude — the clipping claim is unmeasurable
description:
tissue224 (knee-2zbi) came out flat and refuted the COMMON-MODE mechanism, leaving CLIPPING alive but untested. Clipping is a subpopulation claim: only studies whose tissue centroid sits further than the ~15 mm margin from the image centre actually lose anatomy to the image-centred crop, which crop_coverage puts at roughly the worst tenth (p90 offset 18 mm, max 32 mm). An effect confined to 10% of the corpus moves the mean by about a tenth of its own size, so it produces a flat mean BY CONSTRUCTION and can only be read in an offset split.

THE GAP: crop_alignment.dump() writes `spread` — the disagreement BETWEEN slots — not the centroid's offset MAGNITUDE from the image centre. Those are different quantities: a study whose joint sits 25 mm off-centre in every slot identically has a large offset and zero spread. So the decile the split needs does not exist on disk.

THE FIX IS A DUMP COLUMN, NOT A FIT. tissue224 and native224 both read the SAME studies and both kept per-study predictions, so the split is a re-read of two existing checkpoints once the offset column exists. No card time for the fit; the dump is CPU.

PRICE HONESTLY BEFORE ANYONE SPENDS ON IT: the mean is flat and the surviving claim is worth at most a tenth of its own size on the corpus mean, i.e. below the 0.0062 floor even if the mechanism is entirely real. This is an INSTRUMENT that closes the crop/centre axis cleanly, never an improvement. It is P3 for exactly that reason. Do not promote it on the strength of the mechanism being sound.

title: The recipe line records 40+ flags but NOT the encoder normalization - the one value that already invalidated an arm
description:
WHAT IS MISSING. Every arm prints a `recipe:` line carrying every training flag - accumulate, band_low,
layer_decay, tie, weight_floor, forty-odd of them. It does NOT carry the encoder's normalization
constants. Those come from `ENCODERS[...].normalization` in kneemri/models/backbone.py and are registered
as buffers in `StudyModel` (kneemri/models/model.py:227-228, fed at kneemri/training/run_setup.py:331).
They are a property of the ENCODER REGISTRY, not of the argv, so nothing in the run's own record names
them.

WHY THAT IS A BUG AND NOT A COSMETIC GAP. This is precisely the "faulty PLUMBING" failure mode - a value
that decides the result living somewhere the record cannot see. It has already cost one arm. Until
2026-08-25 every trunk was fed the ImageNet constants regardless, so RAD-DINO - pretrained on greyscale
radiographs at 0.5307 / 0.2583 - was seeing a 0.20-std offset with a 12.8% scale error. `raddino_dense`
scored 0.8137 and that number is a reading of the mismatch as much as of the domain (backbone.py:620-628).
The defect was found by reading `preprocessor_config.json`, NOT by reading the run's log, because the run's
log could not have shown it.

THE COST RIGHT NOW, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS P1 RATHER THAN A TIDY-UP. The cold re-run finished today and
peaked at 0.8141 (e7 of 12; e0 0.7237 rising to e7 then declining 0.8106 / 0.8103 / 0.8101). The
truncated, mismatched predecessor peaked 0.8137 at e6, and the fixed run reads 0.8111 at that same e6.
So correcting a 0.20-std input offset moved the number by +0.0004 - inside any noise floor this project
has. Two readings fit that: the fix landed and radiology initialisation genuinely loses ~0.040 to
ImageNet at this rate, or the fix did not reach this process and we have now run the same broken arm
twice. THE RUN'S OWN LOG CANNOT DISTINGUISH THEM. That is the whole defect: a 20-hour experiment whose
headline suspect is unfalsifiable from its own record.

THE CHECK THAT WORKS TODAY, and it is a workaround rather than the fix: the constants are saved as
buffers, so `torch.load(ckpt, weights_only=True)` and print any key ending in `mean` / `std` - 0.5307
means the fix fired, 0.485/0.456/0.406 means it did not. That only works AFTER a run finishes, which is
too late to stop a wrong one, and it needs someone to already suspect the axis.

THE FIX. Record the normalization in the recipe line beside every other flag, so it appears in the log at
model construction and in the saved options. Cheap, and it makes the axis falsifiable from the record
instead of from a hunch. Consider the same for any other registry-sourced value that reaches the model
without passing through argv (encoder repository, dim, family, leaf) - the recipe should describe the
EXPERIMENT, and an encoder identity is part of the experiment.

title: The day's card is uncontested: run the two instruments, then STACK what survives into one seatable member
description:
CELLTRACK GRANTED THE WHOLE DAY, 2026-08-26 08:44Z, in writing: 'card is yours today, no contention from me, I'm on a card-free day... take the follow-up arm after it too.' Their side is CPU/git consolidation. So the card is free from raddino_dense's finish (~12:25Z) to 00:00Z — about 11.5 hours, against the ~2 hours the queue was planned for.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS RATHER THAN JUST A LONGER QUEUE. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_what-0950-actually-costs.md prices first place at +0.010 OFFLINE ON ONE MEMBER, and states the consequence explicitly: 'First place does not require a finding. It requires a STACK of directional gains,' and 'no single arm in that stack will be individually believable.' Ten flat board entries in 0.936-0.939 have now closed the ensemble axis as the source. This is the first day with enough card to actually BUILD the stack rather than measure one term of it.

THE ARITHMETIC, and it is why the queue order is what it is:

  calibration, held pair (knee-ep74)   +0.0072 proxy / +0.0129 annotated at the span corner (knee-bs4l)
  EMA (knee-56w5)                      +0.003 by an outside ablation, against its own +0.0062 bar
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  sum, IF the two terms are additive    ~+0.010 offline = +0.017 board at board_transfer 1.72

+0.010 offline is exactly the distance to a 0.942 single, which is what the rivals in knee-rh4t report and what puts the ensemble at ~0.954 — above the current leader — with the SAME six seats and the SAME vote rule. The target is not a coincidence; it is the same number read from two directions.

QUEUE, in order, all zero submission slots:
  1. band_dense_hold      ~40 min  the held control the dense corner does not own; reusable infrastructure
  2. calib_dense_hold     ~40 min  the calibration term, read on BOTH rulers (knee-9198 P0)
  3. ema_dense            ~72 min  the EMA term, and the instrument splitting allfit's +0.004 into DATA vs EMA
  4. stack_dense          ~45 min  UNHELD, seatable: band_dense recipe + every term that landed in 1-3
  Total ~3.3 h of an 11.5 h day. The remainder is deliberately unallocated — arms 1-3 are instruments and their results decide arm 4's flags.

WHY arm 4 IS NOT WRITTEN YET. Its flag list is the OUTPUT of arms 1-3. Writing it now would be a speculative arm carrying flags for terms that may not land, and the repo's rule is that a piece is added when it is real. It gets written when the instruments read.

THE ASSUMPTION, NAMED. Additivity of calibration and EMA is assumed, not measured. The precedent is good but narrow: span (+0.0039) and density (+0.0014) are additive on this exact control with an interaction of ~0.0001 (band_dense carries both). Calibration is a LABEL-side term and EMA is an OPTIMISER-side term, which is further apart than span and density were, so the prior for additivity is decent on mechanism. stack_dense IS the test of it: if the stack reads materially below the sum of its parts, the interaction is the finding and it is a new fact about this recipe, not a failed arm.

THE OTHER ASSUMPTION, ALSO NAMED. Both terms are BELOW the 0.0062 paired noise floor individually. CLAUDE.md licenses exactly this — 'increments below the bar still compose, and a chain of them that sums past it IS a result' — but it also forbids calling either one a finding. Neither gets a confirmation seed. The stack's own number, against band_dense, is the one that is read.

PRICE: ~3.3 h of a card that is free and otherwise idle, zero submission slots, zero new preprocessing (all four arms cached). The alternative use of that card is nothing — celltrack is not using it and slot 5 is held by owner directive (knee-pubw), so there is no submission to feed today regardless. P(clears the 0.0062 floor on stack_dense vs band_dense) ~ 0.45; P(the stack reaches +0.010 and therefore the 0.942-single target) ~ 0.2; P(at least one of the two terms lands and is worth keeping as a free directional gain) ~ 0.7.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS THE WRONG PLAN. If calibration's held gain does not survive the move from the span corner to the dense corner, arm 4 loses its large term and the stack is EMA alone at +0.003 — a quarter-floor arm not worth 45 minutes. Arms 1-2 gate arm 4, and the gate is read before it is queued.

title: Ensemble is saturated: 37 members, honest peak 0.8721, flat from six seats — no slot can be spent on this pool
description:
record_mix --seats honest over the fold-0 proxy pool, card-free, slot-free, ~40 s.

CHASED a real-looking lead and killed it. The 2026-08-25 ledger read the best honest seat COUNT as twelve
at 0.8720 against a shipped six or seven, priced widening at +0.0023, and named three members the package
does not hold (blendlabels, base224, attend_dense). All three are on disk; mounting is a dataset push, no
slot, no card. So it read as a free gain.

  34 members, MOUNTED ONLY        best honest count  9   peak 0.8720   (6 seats 0.8711, 7 seats 0.8710)
  37 members, + the three unmounted best honest count 15  peak 0.8721   (6 seats 0.8707, 7 seats 0.8713)

Widening from seven to the honest peak: +0.0010, a sixth of the 0.0062 floor. Adding three new members to
a 34-member pool: +0.0001.

The +0.0023 was NEITHER a count effect NOR a member effect. It was two different pools compared as though
count were the variable — the same denominator error this repo keeps making. Compare curves only over one
pool.

Both curves are flat from six seats to twenty within 0.0015, which is smaller than the bias term the
estimator reports for itself. No peak; a plateau, occupied since the fourth seat.

TWELFTH flat-or-negative reading on ensemble construction, and it now covers every axis this pool admits:
count, membership, per-label selection (label_combine, same day), vote, overlap TTA, external corpus.

CONSEQUENCE: 0.8720 is the ceiling of arithmetic over members we already have. No entry from this pool —
any count, subset, per-label roster or vote — beats the pinned 0.939 by more than noise. Holding slot 5 is
what the measurement recommends, not only what the owner directed. The next real number costs a CARD.

LIMITS: fold-0 proxy pool only; six champion members are --fold -1 and cannot appear, so this is the SHAPE
of the axis, not the shipped level. Says nothing about a member from an axis the pool does not vary at all
(different encoder, image-derived supervision).

Logs: experiments/logs/mix_mounted_honest.log, experiments/logs/mix_plus3_honest.log

title: Per-label member selection is refuted — the flat rank-average is optimal in its own family
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-26 07:23Z. Card-free, slot-free, ~1 minute of arithmetic over prediction arrays already on disk.

THE AXIS. The competition metric is the unweighted mean of twelve INDEPENDENT per-label ROC AUCs, so the combine that matches the metric is per-label: let each of the twelve findings pick its own subset of members instead of every label sharing one flat rank-average. That is the most metric-aligned ensemble idea available and it had never been read.

kneemri/evaluation/label_combine.py had implemented it on 2026-08-20 and was cited twice as prior art — once at experiments/README.md:539 and once in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_per_label_reread.md — while producing NO NUMBER, because it had no main(). A library with no entrypoint is a claim, not a measurement. Wired it (this session) and ran it.

ROSTER: gradeswap_v1's seven, all fold-0 scoreable, all already in member_curve's holdout_predictions store — so the encoder never ran. band_dense_s2026, calib_span_s2026, base_dense_s2026, band_dense_long_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026. Truth: report_labels_v2.csv on the fold-0 holdout.

  top- 1 per label:  in-sample 0.8643   split-half 0.8538
  top- 2 per label:  in-sample 0.8708   split-half 0.8637
  top- 3 per label:  in-sample 0.8714   split-half 0.8663
  top- 4 per label:  in-sample 0.8714   split-half 0.8674
  top- 5 per label:  in-sample 0.8710   split-half 0.8686
  top- 6 per label:  in-sample 0.8705   split-half 0.8688
  top- 7 per label:  in-sample 0.8694   split-half 0.8696  (= the flat rank-average)

READ THE SPLIT-HALF COLUMN ONLY. It is MONOTONE INCREASING in k and its maximum is at k=7, which IS the flat rank-average already shipped. Every per-label subset is worse out of sample. Best candidate (k=3) is 0.8663 against 0.8696, i.e. -0.0033.

THE CONTROL IS INSIDE THE CURVE, which is why this is a verdict and not a shrug. Selecting the top k per label at k = every member IS the flat average, so the candidate and its matched baseline are estimated by the SAME split-half estimator on the SAME studies. No cross-ruler comparison, no separately-run control arm.

AND THE OPTIMISM IS VISIBLE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. In-sample peaks at k=3-4 (0.8714) — a +0.0020 'gain' over the flat average that is entirely the selection choosing its own noise. The two columns diverge by 0.0051 at k=3, LARGER than any candidate gain in the table, which is exactly the failure the module's docstring pre-registered: 'if the two columns diverge by more than the gain, the gain is the divergence'. Anyone who had run this without the split-half estimator would have shipped a per-label roster and reported +0.002.

MECHANISM, so this is not just a number. Twelve choices are fitted on 881 holdout studies with as few as 62 Fracture positives. A per-label AUC over 62 positives has a standard error near 0.04, so the ranking it induces is mostly noise, and selecting on it discards real members to chase it. Averaging more members is the variance reduction; selecting fewer is the opposite of what the small-positive labels need.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. (1) One roster, seven members, one fold. (2) Selection was by per-label AUC ranking; a per-label WEIGHTING that shrinks toward the flat average rather than hard-selecting is a different estimator and is not tested here — though this result lowers its prior, since the optimum of the hard version sits exactly at 'do not select at all'. (3) It says nothing about per-label supervision, which was refuted separately from the training side (per_label_loss, 2026-08-19).

CONSEQUENCE. This is the eleventh flat-or-negative reading on the ensemble-construction axis and the first one that is metric-aligned by construction. It strengthens knee-uj15's arithmetic rather than merely agreeing with it: the remaining distance is inside one member, not in how members are combined, and now the most favourable combine rule anyone could propose has been measured at the same place the ledger already stood.

title: The public Synovitis hole is not our hole - RadImageNet declined, and the read is evidence our reader is ahead of the floor
description:
Forum topic 737566, posted 2026-08-26 0442z, four hours before this was written: 'Why everyone's Synovitis AUC is stuck around 0.6-0.7 (its not your model)'. The poster measures 0.62-0.72 on Synovitis across FOUR architectures, finds only ~16% of the 4407 reports mention any synovitis term across the nine report languages, prices the public label tables at ~0.79 AUC on Synovitis against ~0.99 on ACL, and reports that a RadImageNet-pretrained encoder took them to 0.78 where every ImageNet-pretrained model sat at 0.62-0.72.

TWO THINGS, AND THEY POINT OPPOSITE WAYS.

(1) The DIAGNOSIS confirms ours, by a route that shares no denominator. Our unsure_cost run on the 58 annotated studies found Synovitis is the most-unsure finding by a distance (41 of 58 cells UNK, 34.1% of those actually positive, the only POSITIVE taught error at +0.061), and reader_disagreement over 4406 studies ranked Synovitis top of twelve on cross-reader spread (0.2995, split rate 0.175). They counted report TERMS across nine languages; we counted reader VERDICTS and cross-reader SPREAD. Three instruments, same finding: the reports genuinely do not say much about synovitis. That is now externally confirmed and can be quoted as such.

(2) The PRESCRIPTION does not transfer, because we do not have their number. experiments/README.md:473 puts our Synovitis holdout AUC at 0.8456/0.8764 depending on the member. That is not 0.62-0.72; it is above our corpus mean and roughly a fifth of a point above the ceiling they reached WITH RadImageNet. Our two worst labels are MCL 0.7745 and Fracture 0.7922 — Synovitis is not close to the bottom for us.

CONSEQUENCE: DECLINE the RadImageNet member on this evidence. It is offered as a fix for a hole we do not have, and the price would be a fresh encoder family plus a pretrain-weights dependency for a label already 0.10-0.15 above the number that motivates it. Revisit only if a medically-pretrained encoder is argued on the FOCAL findings (knee-lxi1) instead, where our deficit actually lives — and note that is a different argument needing its own evidence, not this thread's.

SECOND CONSEQUENCE, and it is the more useful one: this is the first outside measurement of the PUBLIC label floor on a finding where we can compare directly. Their tables read Synovitis at ~0.79 against the annotated studies; ours trains a model to 0.85-0.88 on it. Our reader pipeline is ahead of the public floor on the hardest-to-read finding in the set, which is a concrete answer to 'are the public tables better than ours' — on this finding, no. Related: table_separation (recomposing the blend is not a lever, every recipe inside the gold ruler's +/-0.008), knee-1ww2 and knee-uahl (both closed 2026-08-26).

title: The gold/test labels are IMAGE-derived and every table we train on is REPORT-derived - that bounds the supervision axis
description:
MECHANISM, read out of interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_effusion-threshold-ruler.md on 2026-08-26 03:08Z. Not a new measurement - a consequence of one we already made and did not price.

THE FACT. Per the hosts (discussion topic 735826) the gold 58 and the hidden test labels were made by radiologists FROM THE IMAGES. Every label table this project trains on - ours, steven, lixin, hybrid_v4, and the blend blendsix is dosing - is derived from the REPORT TEXT. Those are two different measurements of the same knee, and severity_boundary measured how far apart they sit at the threshold: of 28 readable English annotated studies, SEVEN contradict the competition's own stated moderate-or-above rule, and the size qualifier is not even monotone in the gold class (small 50% positive, moderate-or-larger 67%, unqualified mention 86%). The denominators are 7/28 of the readable English subset and 7/58 as a floor over all annotated studies; neither is a rate over the corpus and neither has an interval.

WHAT IT BOUNDS. A better REPORT READER converges on the report-derived measurement, and at the threshold that measurement disagrees with the test's roughly half the time in the buckets that hold both classes. So the supervision axis has a ceiling that is not 1.0 and is not reachable by reading reports harder. table_separation already showed the recomposition half of that axis is dead (four blends span 0.8894-0.8931, every pairwise interval covers zero); this says the REPLACEMENT half - a genuinely better reader - is bounded too, in a way no amount of reader quality removes.

WHAT IT LICENSES, and this is the point. A teacher built from IMAGE predictions targets the measurement the test actually uses. That is a different argument for distillation than knee-1x4j makes (there the teacher is fold-0 order, and the case is encoder-family diversity); here the case is TARGET CORRECTNESS - the only construction we have whose supervision is image-derived rather than report-derived. It also predicts WHERE the gain would land: on the borderline cases the report grades and the radiologist re-graded, i.e. a per-label profile concentrated on findings with a size or grade word (Effusion, Meniscus, Cartilage), not a flat lift.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. Report and image are strongly correlated - the report is written from the image - so this is a THRESHOLD effect, not a claim that report supervision is wrong. blendsix is not indicted: blend_three is separated above our v2 at +0.0254 [+0.0098, +0.0428] on the gold set, so it is a better reader and the arm is sound. This bounds how much further that road goes, it does not close it.

NOT PRICED AS AN ARM HERE. No card is free (blendsix holds it until ~09:00Z) and both remaining slots are committed. This is the ARGUMENT, to be spent when a card window opens - most cheaply as a per-label profile read on an existing distillation arm rather than a new one.
