title: STUDY_RESAMPLES=1000 has never had the measurement RESAMPLES=1500 got
description:
core/bootstrap.py now holds two draw counts. RESAMPLES=1500 is MEASURED: its docstring records that at 300 draws the Lateral Meniscus lower bound moved 0.0063 across three resample seeds - enough to flip whether it cleared zero - and that 1500 brings that spread to 0.0015. STUDY_RESAMPLES=1000, the count behind the paired 0.0062 floor, the +/-0.0106 absolute band and every per-label interval in the ledger, has had no such check. Its old docstring asserted 1000 was 'stable to about a thousandth', which is the SAME claim 300 made and lost.

The test is cheap and spends no card: run paired_interval and mean_interval at three different resample SEEDS on a recorded pair of arms and read how far each bound moves. If the Monte Carlo spread is near 0.0015 the count is fine and the docstring can say so with evidence. If it is nearer 0.006 then the floor this project quotes everywhere is partly a seed.

DO NOT simply raise it to 1500. Changing the count moves every interval already published in experiments/README.md and interpretations/, so the measurement comes first and any change is a separate, deliberate re-read of those numbers.

title: CoPAS correlation-mining head: inter-label co-occurrence term, the surviving half of knee-0a9c
description:
Split out of knee-0a9c when its cross-plane-attention half was killed on the paper's own supplementary table (the CPA row is built on the no-crop baseline, so no clean step exists, and the whole stack over the ROI-cropped baseline is +0.031 against +0.038 for the two clean modules - the crop and the attention substitute for each other, and we already crop to 130mm).

WHAT SURVIVES. Correlation mining (CRM) is a clean +0.013 step in their Table 10: a 12-channel conv plus SENet-style attention over the per-label logits, modelling which abnormalities co-occur. Our head emits twelve INDEPENDENT logits with no inter-label term, and knee MRI has strong real co-occurrence (ACL tear / bone contusion / effusion is the classic triad).

WHY IT IS CHEAP. Head-only: it changes the readout, not the input distribution, so a member can be WARM-STARTED rather than refit. And the co-occurrence structure can be read off the 4,349 report-derived targets rather than the 58 annotations, so it is not blocked behind the 58-study ruler the rest of the label-side family sits behind.

WHY IT IS P3 ANYWAY. +0.013 is on THEIR corpus and THEIR ruler, before any transfer to ours, and it is under the 1.5 pct house bar. Directional at best. Take it only if something else opens the head anyway - never as its own arm, and never as a reason to spend a submission slot.

Source table and arithmetic: research/2026-08-24_published_knee_mri_multilabel_sota.md.

title: We have no usable single-model board transfer, and the two solo entries disagree by a factor of five
description:
FOUND WHILE PRICING THE MEMBER GAP (see the P0 on the seat axis and
interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_the-seat-axis-is-saturated-and-the-member-is-0.028-behind.md).

`board_transfer` = +1.82 board points per holdout point, and it is fitted on ENSEMBLE submissions. The
record holds exactly TWO single-member entries and only one of them carries an offline number:

  solo_v1  ref 55450174  2026-08-12  board 0.868  offline 0.8518  "one model, no ensemble"
  solo_v4  ref 55582892  2026-08-17  board 0.914  offline NONE    "ONE whole-stack member, overlap=False"

Run the constant between them and solo_v4's member prices at ~0.877 holdout — above every member
holdout we have ever recorded (best: band_dense_long 0.8587 at epoch 6). Run it the other way, assuming
solo_v4 sits in our whole-stack members' actual range (~0.855-0.859), and the implied slope is ~8.8
board points per holdout point, nearly five times the fitted constant. Both readings cannot hold, and
neither is checkable, because solo_v4 records no members_named and no kernel — so we cannot even say
which member it was.

WHY IT MATTERS RIGHT NOW. It is why the seat-axis interpretation quotes the member deficit as "about one
bar's worth" rather than as 0.0154 holdout. The ORDERING survives without any constant (their reported
single 0.942 beats our best six 0.938), but the SIZE does not, and a target holdout number derived from
+1.82 for a single model would be a number with no support. This is the same denominator failure the
project has now made three times in one session, caught before it was planned against.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT, cheaply and with no slot: run one CURRENT member alone through a kernel (a kernel RUN
costs no slot; only `kaggle competitions submit` does) and pair its known holdout with the board score.
One such pair, taken with today's recipe and today's serving, is worth more than both existing rows —
solo_v1 predates whole-stack and solo_v4 is unidentified. It does cost ONE SLOT for the board score, so
it is only worth doing if a member lane is live enough to need the calibration.

DO NOT quote a single-model holdout target until this exists.

title: Distance is anticorrelated with seat value WITHIN a family - it is a twin detector, never a merit column
description:
Measured 2026-08-25 18:35Z, pricing the whole 224 family against gradeswap_v1 (0.933, 7/7 scoreable) in one call.

  candidate                     seat value   nearest
  dinov3_v3small_224_s2026        -0.0017     0.7936
  lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026       -0.0010     0.8159
  base224_s2026                   +0.0007     0.8679
  native224_s2026                 +0.0002     0.8946

Monotone, and in the WRONG direction for anyone reading distance as merit: across four candidates the
more distant the member, the more it COSTS the mix. Four points, one family, so it is a lean rather
than a law - but the mechanism is not subtle and it is the one that generalises.

WHY: distance is confounded with quality. A weak member is distant BECAUSE its predictions are noisy,
and noise is maximally uncorrelated with everything. A rank-distance column cannot tell orthogonal
SIGNAL from orthogonal NOISE, and those two have opposite value. The seated members' own spread says
the same thing from the other side: every seat sits at 0.88-0.92 to its nearest, i.e. the board's best
roster is built from members that are neither twins nor strangers.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is a correction to what I had already written into the slot plan (knee-5clp).
I had argued slot 1 as a DISTANCE bet - base224's 0.8679 being below every seated member's nearest.
That argument is void. Distance's real job is the one seat_value's own doc gives it: a TWIN DETECTOR,
which is how the 2026-08-22 split was called (band_span priced +0.0002 and cost a tick because it was a
near-twin of a seated member, and a rank average cannot charge for contributing one ordering twice).
It vetoes a candidate that is too CLOSE. It does not endorse one that is far.

So the usable rule is a BAND, not a maximum: a candidate wants positive seat value AND a nearest inside
roughly 0.86-0.92. base224 is the only member of the 224 family that satisfies both, which is why it
stays the slot-1 candidate - on being best on both columns at once, not on being far.

This also retires an idea worth naming before it comes back: shipping dinov3_v3small_224 for its 0.7936
would have been the single most distant member we have ever measured and the worst seat value in the
family.

title: CoPAS (Nat Commun 2024) fuses planes at FEATURE level; we fuse at context level only
description:
Frontier gather, 2026-08-25, no GPU spent. CoPAS - 'Learning co-plane attention across MRI sequences for diagnosing twelve types of knee abnormalities', Nat Commun 15 (2024), HKUST, PMC11368947. Same task shape as ours: twelve knee abnormalities, multi-sequence MRI, 1748 subjects. Their headline is 0.812 mean AUC on THEIR OWN dataset and is NOT comparable to our 0.938 board or our holdout - different corpus, different label definitions, different denominator. Read for MECHANISM only.

WHAT THEY DO THAT WE ALREADY DO, and arguably better: 'each knee abnormality has its optimal diagnostic MRI plane' is their motivating claim, and they cash it as a plane-aware matrix built by element-wise multiplication of three branch predictions. SlotHead already gives every diagnosis its own query over the acquisition slots AND seeds those logits with an anatomical prior (slot_head.py:60-72). That axis is closed here; do not re-open it.

THE GENUINE GAP - WHERE THE FUSION HAPPENS. CoPAS enhances one plane's FEATURES using another plane's features: the main plane supplies queries, synthetic volumes rotated into the orthogonal orientations supply keys and values, through weight-shared ResNet3D-18 encoders, before any readout. Our slot embeddings are each computed independently by the encoder and only ever meet inside SlotHead's attention - which combines CONTEXTS, not features. No slot's representation is ever conditioned on another slot's. through_plane is not this: it gives a slice its two DEPTH neighbours in the RGB channels (model.py:85-89), which is within-plane, not cross-plane.

Note their reason for SYNTHESISING the orthogonal volumes does not apply to us. They rotate the high-res PDW volume because they want its in-plane detail expressed in other orientations; our slots are the planes the study actually acquired, so we already hold real orthogonal information and would attend across acquired slots rather than rendered ones. That makes our version CHEAPER than theirs, not more expensive - no rotation, no synthetic volume, no second encoder pass.

SECOND, CHEAPER LEVER - inter-label correlation. Their correlation mining module (12-channel conv + SENet-style attention over the plane-aware matrix) explicitly models which abnormalities co-occur. Our head emits twelve INDEPENDENT logits with no inter-label term, and knee MRI has strong real co-occurrence (ACL tear with bone contusion with effusion is the classic triad). Head-only, no encoder change. It is a LABEL-side mechanism, which interpretations/kneemri record as blocked behind the 58-study ruler - but co-occurrence structure can be read off the 4,349 report-derived targets rather than the 58 annotations, which is what makes it worth pricing separately from the rest of that family.

NEITHER IS PRICED YET and neither is armed - the card is biohub's and the owner has ruled out GPU work. Cross-plane feature attention is an ENCODER change and therefore a full refit of every member that would use it, so it must be priced as wall-clock-per-member before anything is queued. The correlation head is cheap enough to warm-start, since it changes the readout and not the input distribution. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11368947/ and https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51888-4
notes:
PRICED AND LARGELY KILLED, 2026-08-25, from the supplementary ablation (Table 10) rather than the article - the article defers it and never shows it.

The cross-plane-attention lever this bead filed CANNOT be priced at all from their own table: the paper builds the CPA row on the NO-crop baseline while comparing its multitask row against the CROPPED one, so every subtraction reaching CPA also crosses the ROI crop or the single-to-multitask change. There is no clean CPA step. The +0.049 that has been quoted here twice is (iv)-(ii), which skips (iii).

What the table does say, and it goes against this bead: the two CLEAN steps sum to +0.038 (CSA +0.025, CRM +0.013) while the WHOLE stack over the ROI-cropped baseline is +0.031. The crop and the attention modules substitute for each other, which their own text states outright - 'cropping along ROI can align the spatial position across sequences'. We already crop to 130mm, so we sit at their row (i) and the residual for cross-plane feature attention is near zero BY THEIR NUMBERS. An encoder change plus a refit of every member for that is a bad ratio; do not queue it.

Note the reasoning correction in both directions: the earlier kill ('our slots are already orthogonal within 87.3 deg, so it does not transfer') was also invalid. Orthogonality is the PRECONDITION their module operates on, not a substitute for it. The table kills this, the geometry does not.

SURVIVING HALF, kept and downgraded: correlation mining (CRM) is a clean +0.013 step, head-only, warm-startable, readable off the 4349 report-derived targets. Under the 1.5 pct bar on their own ruler before any corpus transfer, so it is directional at best - worth taking only if something else opens the head anyway, never as its own arm.

Full table and the arithmetic: research/2026-08-24_published_knee_mri_multilabel_sota.md, which had already argued the plane axis was spent on 2026-08-24. This bead re-opened it a day later without reading that note - the failure CLAUDE.md names.

title: Code-reduction axis measured across the whole tree: nothing to reduce
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-25, run under the standing refactor instruction (lower the amount of code, make it easier to keep in order). Three instruments over kneemri + core, and all three come back clean. Recording it so the next session does not pay for the same scan.

DUPLICATION. jscpd at min-tokens 35 - BELOW the gate own 50 - over 160 files, 29918 lines: 25 clones, 167 duplicated lines, 0.56 percent. Read every clone. They fall into three kinds and none is a reduction target:

  IMPORT BLOCKS. band_coverage/crop_coverage/crop_alignment/crop_laterality share 5 clones that are
  literally the same import run plus the logger line. Deduplicating imports is not a thing.

  STRATEGY SIBLINGS. token_pooling has two self-clones which are the @override decorator, the
  signature and the patch-slice line shared by ClassAndPatchMeanAndTail and ClassAndSidedMean. That
  boilerplate IS the strategy pattern the house style mandates; collapsing it collapses the pattern.

  THE CORPUS-WALKING CLI PREAMBLE. slot_ties and tie_divergence share three clones, the largest single
  one in the tree at 92 tokens, and they are the same idiom: --split/--workers/--studies, rooted().raw(),
  StudyCache.planes_of, sorted directories, an optional head, then a ProcessPoolExecutor over
  ((directory, planes) for directory in directories). Twelve modules use a pool and ten of them are in
  corpus. This is the ONE case with a real shared responsibility, and it is still not worth a type: only
  three modules call planes_of at all, and the rest differ in what the worker returns and how the flags
  are named. A CorpusScan value type would buy ~15 lines and pay an import edge in ten modules.

COHESION. cohesion.lcom reports 44 low-cohesion classes, 41 of them at LCOM4=2 which is one method
touching one other field - noise. The one real outlier, TrainingOptions at 6, is correct by design and
now says so in its own docstring (commit 19da8be): the fields are flat because parse builds the
dataclass from argparse dest names, so the grouping is properties over disjoint scalars, which is
exactly what LCOM4 counts as six responsibilities.

DATA CLUMPS. One, {batch, start, width} across study_cache and window_reader, already argued as
deliberate at window_reader.py:37.

COMPLEXITY. radon ranks 15 at the top but the fixed gate is ruff C901 at >10, and the two count
differently by design - ruff counts branches, radon also counts boolean operators and comprehensions.
No pyproject max-complexity override, so ruff is at its default 10 and passes. Nothing is over.

FILE SIZE. Largest module is arm_check at 701 against file_max 750; see knee-0ox0, whose own
measurement already refused the split.

WHAT THIS MEANS. The tree is not carrying redundant code. If the amount of code is to come down it has
to come down by deleting a CAPABILITY nobody uses, not by deduplicating - and the only such candidate on
record is knee-xh96 layer three, the 17 board-less kernels, which is the owner call.

title: arm_check is 701 of 750 lines and holds three responsibilities behind one class
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-25. kneemri/experiments/arm_check.py is 701 lines against the [tool.structure] file_max of 750 - 3.5x the next-largest module in the package (queue_check at 280) and the only one anywhere near the ceiling. It passes every gate today, including god-file, so this is pressure and not a failure.

ArmCheck itself is ~480 lines over ~20 methods, and reading them they fall into three groups that do not talk to each other much:

  READING what the arms declare - _environment, queued, invocations, _printed, selected, _parsed,
  carriage_returns. Runs the shell arms under git-bash, captures the invocation each prints, parses
  the flags into TrainingOptions.

  JUDGING what was declared - refused, mismatched, _flag_values, _same, unpriced, _descriptions,
  prices, verdicts, overstated, unstated. Every one of these takes an invocations mapping and
  returns complaints; none of them needs to know how the invocation was obtained.

  SMOKING - readings, uncached, decode_smoke_caches, plus the ArmReading dataclass.

THE PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN THE TREE: arm_smoke.py exists as a 195-line module carved out of exactly
this file, so the seam has been cut once before and held.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST, which is why this is a bead and not a commit: LCOM reports the class cohesive,
and a split that just relocates methods LOWERS no code - it buys a smaller file and pays an import
edge plus a second mirror test file. The standing instruction is to lower the amount of code, not to
redistribute it. So the split is only worth doing if the READING half can take the shell-running
machinery with it whole (GIT_BASH, TIMEOUT_SECONDS, STUB, SHELLS, _environment, _printed) and leave
the judging half a pure function of a mapping - that is a genuine interface, and it would also make
the judging half testable without git-bash on the machine.

NEXT STEP is measurement, not editing: count what actually moves and what each half would still
import from the other. If the two halves share more than the ArmVerdict type, leave it alone.
notes:
MEASURED the same day, and the measurement REFUSES the split on this bead's own stated criterion.

Per-method audit of what each half reaches for through self:

  verdicts (JUDGE, 76 lines) calls carriage_returns (READ).
  refused, overstated (JUDGE) and readings (SMOKE) all call _parsed (READ).
  self.headers is read by both halves - _printed and queued on the READ side, mismatched, prices and
  verdicts on the JUDGE side.

So the two halves share three things, not one type: the flag parser, the CR scan, and the headers
path. A split would either duplicate _parsed, or leave the JUDGE module importing the READ module for
it - which is the import edge this bead already said is the cost, bought for nothing. LEAVE THE CLASS
WHOLE. Its stated pre-condition ('only if the judging half becomes a pure function of a mapping') is
measurably false.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT DID FIND, and the reason this stays open at P3 rather than closing: SIX methods
touch no self at all - selected, _parsed, _flag_values, _same, unpriced, _descriptions, unstated (and
_parsed only fails the count because it is called as self._parsed). That is ~105 lines of pure
function sitting inside a class as staticmethods. Moving them to module level, or onto a small value
type that owns a flag string, takes the CLASS well under 400 lines and costs no import edge, because
they already depend on nothing. It shrinks the file honestly; it does not lower the amount of code, so
it is worth doing only alongside a change that already touches them.

title: uv cannot build the devtools git dep while the git-shim blocks reset --hard
description:
Every devtools_ref bump (copier update) makes uv re-fetch sdlc-devtools from git. uv builds a git dependency by checking it out into its own cache and running 'git reset --hard <sha>'. The global git-shim blocks reset-hard, so 'nox -s gates' dies at the first devtools-using session with:

  BLOCKED by git-shim [reset-hard] in global scope

The failure names the shim but reads like a repo problem, and it lands mid-gate-run (after ruff/vulture/import-linter pass), so it is easy to misread as a gate regression. It is neither - the target is uv's cache checkout, never this tree.

WORKAROUND that works: install the dep once with the shim in log-only mode, then run gates normally (the build is cached, no further git op):

  GIT_SHIM_LOG_ONLY=1 uv sync --extra dev --extra devtools
  uvx nox -s gates

Log-only rather than GIT_SHIM=off so the operation is still recorded. Decide whether this belongs in the shim as a scoped allowance for uv's cache path, or in the repo README as the documented step after a copier update.
notes:
Hit for real 2026-08-25 during the v1.28.0 update; workaround applied and it works.
DECIDED 2026-08-25: documented in the repo, not fixed in the shim. The scoped allowance is the better permanent fix and loses no protection - uv only ever resets its OWN cache checkout, never a work tree - but the shim is machine-global and lives outside this repo, so changing it is the owner s call rather than something a session edits blind. What landed: the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md Scaffolding section now carries the mechanism, the misreading it causes (dies mid-gate-run after three gates print clean, so it reads as a gate regression), and the two-command workaround with GIT_SHIM_LOG_ONLY=1 rather than GIT_SHIM=off so the op is still recorded. Closing as documented; re-open only to take the shim-side allowance.

title: board.jsonl: 26 older rows still carry no members_named, so unpriceable() stays inert on them
description: Follow-up to knee-zc70, which repaired only the five at the top of the board (dark6_v1, dark7_v1, v3seat_v1, farseat_v1, votefit_v1). 26 rows remain half-written, from trained_v1 through sixfresh_v2. Consequence is the same one zc70 named: BoardCensus.unpriceable() reads members_named to catch an offline number recorded over a pool that has seen its own holdout, so it cannot fire on those rows. Lower priority than the five because the older entries are not what anything prices against today, and because their kernel logs may no longer exist -- v3seat_v1's did not, which is why its kit is recorded null rather than guessed. Repair the ones whose kernel dir and log survive; for the rest, record members_named from the kernel's chosen tuple alone and leave kit null rather than inventing one.

title: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md quote the champion pin's score in prose and name basedense_v1, two generations stale
description: Both files (which must stay in sync) describe champion_check as asserting 'the 0.925 entry pinned in comp/champion.json', and both name basedense_v1 as the entry the pin holds. The file itself pins allfit at 0.937. The number went stale because it was copied into prose at all -- comp/champion.json is its one home. title: run_setup's two exclusivity guards are one loop written twice
description:
_check_margin_alone and _check_dissent_alone differ only in which flag is being refused, its value, the flags it conflicts with, and the trailing clause of the message. The body of each is the same three steps: name the given conflicts, and if any, raise a ValueError spelling the flag, its value, the conflicting flags with their values, and why they do not compose.

THE MOVE: extract _check_alone(flag, value, conflicts, reason) holding the loop and the raise. Both callers keep their own method and their own docstring - those carry the MECHANISM (why the margin objective replaces cross-entropy, why the dissent term is the label ranking at a re-weighted pair mass) and are the reason the guards exist at all; only the plumbing is shared. conflicts is typed Mapping[str, float], not dict, because a literal mixing int and float values is not assignable to an invariant dict.

WHY IT MATTERS beyond line count: a third exclusive objective flag is the obvious next one, and today that means a third copy of the loop. The message FORMAT is the thing that would drift - one guard listing values and another not, one saying 'is not composed with' and another 'cannot be used with', in errors a reader hits at queue time with the card already held.
close_reason:
Tried it and MEASURED it: run_setup.py went 393 -> 403. The extraction is a net LOSS of ten lines and I am closing it as not worth doing, not deferring it.

THE ARITHMETIC, so nobody re-opens this on the same reasoning I did. The shared body is five lines standing twice, so ten lines are available. Against that: the helper signature and its four-line body, a docstring that has to say why a private helper exists at all, and two call sites that grow because the conflicts dict and the trailing message clause become spelled-out arguments where they used to be locals. The duplication is real and the removal still costs more than it saves - two instances of a five-line loop is under the size where extraction pays.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: a THIRD exclusive objective flag. At three instances the arithmetic flips, and the drift risk the original description named (one guard listing values and another not, in an error read at queue time) becomes worth paying for. Until then the two guards stay as they are.

Filed and closed inside one sitting under a refactoring directive that says lower the amount of code; a change that adds ten lines does not clear that bar on a P3 drift risk.

title: batch/start/width travel together through study_cache and window_reader as three loose ints
description:
AUDIT (2026-08-25, cohesion.data_clumps): the triple `batch, start, width` is passed as three separate arguments across core/data/corpus/study_cache.py and core/data/corpus/window_reader.py. Three ints in a fixed order is the shape that lets a caller swap start and width silently - both are non-negative, both index the same axis, and neither a type checker nor a shape contract can see the swap.

DESIGN: one frozen value beside its producer (a window's placement in a cached array), constructed once where the arithmetic that derives it lives, passed whole thereafter.

CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT: no call site passes the three as positionals any more, the existing window_reader tests pass unchanged, and a swapped-argument test that used to read as a valid call no longer type-checks or no longer constructs.
close_reason: Fixed by keyword-only start/width rather than the value object: window_reader.WindowReader.read, MappedReader.read, FileReader.read/_fill, study_cache.CachedCorpus.window. The reader's own docstring already argued against a request type (nothing stores/returns/decides from the triple) and the call-site audit backed it - two read() sites, four window() sites. Keyword-only kills the swap-silence, which was the whole risk, and adds no type on the inner loop. Constraint met: pyrefly rejects a positional extent (it found comp/witness_check.py, a caller outside core/kneemri/tests the greps missed), a negative test asserts TypeError, and the pre-existing window_reader/prefetch/study_cache tests pass unchanged. 195 tests green, uvx nox -s gates successful. Commit e39ec3d.

title: Sixteen vulture findings sit under the enforced gate's confidence floor
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 with vulture 2.16 at --min-confidence 60 over kneemri/ + core/ (the gate itself
runs at the same floor, so these are AT the boundary, not below it):

  oof_oracle.py:71,72,83   unused variables ids / pred / oof
  switch_coverage.py:82    unused method unaccounted
  members.py:47,116        unused variables img / annot
  members.py:431           unused property pixel_group
  kernel_run.py:34         unused class KernelRun
  kit_wheels.py:30         unused class KitWheels
  backbone.py:30,31        unused DINOV2 / DINOV3
  member_record.py:19,33   unused RECORDED_AS / NOT_IN_CONFIG
  run_metrics.py:78,79     unused vram_peak_gb / vram_alloc_gb
  landed.py:66             unused NOT_A_SWITCH

AT LEAST THREE ARE FALSE, and knowing which is the point of the task rather than a reason to skip it:
KernelRun and KitWheels are instantiated by the Kaggle kernel scripts under comp/kernels/, which live
outside the analysed packages, so vulture cannot see the call. The vram_* fields are written into a JSON
record and read back by tooling. DINOV2/DINOV3 are almost certainly string constants selected by name.

Triage each into: genuinely dead (delete), read across a package boundary vulture cannot follow (add to
the whitelist WITH the reason), or a real unused binding masking a bug (oof_oracle's three unpacked-and-
discarded names are the ones to read first - a discarded 'pred' in an oracle is worth a look before it is
worth a deletion).
notes:
TRIAGED THREE OF SIXTEEN, 2026-08-25, by reading rather than by deleting:

oof_oracle.py:71,72,83 are NOT discarded bindings and there is no bug behind them. They are TypedDict
FIELDS - OutOfFoldBlock declares ids/pred and PublishedPayload declares oof - so vulture is reporting a
declared key it cannot see indexed. Whitelist with that reason; do not delete, since deleting them
deletes the only written record of the published checkpoint's layout.

kernel_run.py:34 KernelRun and kit_wheels.py:30 KitWheels stay for the reason already stated: their only
callers live in comp/kernels/*, outside the analysed packages.

That leaves eleven to triage. The remaining ones worth reading before whitelisting are backbone.py's
DINOV2/DINOV3 (string constants selected by name, so a rename would be silent) and members.py:431
pixel_group (a property on the shipping Member - if nothing reads it, a member's pixel grouping is
recorded and never applied).
close_reason: Triaged all sixteen in ad979d0. ONE was real: DINOV2/DINOV3 had no readers because six encoder rows in backbone.py wrote family="dinov2"/"dinov3" as literals while CONVNEXT/VJEPA2/RADDINO all used their constants — a rename would have silently missed the six. They now use the constants. The other thirteen are whitelisted in [tool.vulture] ignore_names WITH the path vulture cannot follow, in three groups: TypedDict/dataclass fields read by subscript (ids, pred, oof, img, annot, vram_peak_gb, vram_alloc_gb); symbols whose only callers are outside the scanned packages, in comp/ (pixel_group is read by comp/verify_members.py:81, KernelRun and KitWheels by comp/kernels/*); and the four written-off sets a unit gate differences against TrainingOptions to keep a wire total (RECORDED_AS, NOT_IN_CONFIG, NOT_A_SWITCH, unaccounted) — being unused in the package IS what those are for. members.py:431 pixel_group was the one flagged as worth reading first for a real bug and it is not one: verify_members groups a package by it. FOLLOW-UP: the tree now reports nothing at min-confidence 60, so the ENFORCED vulture run should graduate from 80 to 60 — but that invocation lives in the template-owned noxfile, so it belongs upstream in sdlc-scaffold.

title: Per-label reader agreement measured: rho=+0.53 vs per-label AUC, and per-label recalibration is worth 0.000
description:
core.data.labels.reader_agreement.by_label was in the tool and never in the ledger. Ran it card-free 2026-08-25 (logs/reader_agreement_20260825.log).

Agreement on the reader's POSITIVE calls, per finding: Synovitis 81.2 (16 calls), Medial Meniscus 78.1 (32), ACL 71.9 (32), Fracture 68.4 (19), Baker's 68.8 (16), Effusion 68.0 (50), PF OA 66.7 (24), Lateral Meniscus 66.7 (30), Medial OA 63.6 (22), Lateral OA 56.2 (16), MCL 50.0 (18), Contusion 44.4 (36). DENOMINATOR: 311 positive calls over 57 annotated studies, 684 cells. Per-label n is 16-50, so each rate carries roughly +/-20pp and no PAIR of labels is separated.

Paired against band_dense's per-label AUC table (experiments/README.md:411), Spearman rho = +0.53 (sum d2 = 134.5, n=12, p~0.08). Moderate, NOT established. The residual is two trauma findings pulling opposite ways: Contusion is 6th by AUC and LAST by agreement; Fracture is 11th by AUC and 5th by agreement.

TWO CONSEQUENCES.

(1) FREE KILL, and it needs no resolution at all. The error census is lopsided 3.4:1 - 108 false positives against 32 misses, Synovitis the only inversion at -11 - which looks like a calibration lever. It is not one. The metric is a per-label rank AUC, so a monotone per-label recalibration cannot change it by construction. Any arm that corrects the reader's over-call rate is worth exactly 0.000 on this board. Retired before proposal. Consistent with calibrated_targets at +0.0038, inside the floor.

(2) The twelve-label deficit target is OVER-PRICED. farseat's FLAT branch hands off to 'lifting Lateral Meniscus 0.7981, PF OA 0.8165, MCL 0.8166, Lateral OA 0.8215 to 0.87 is +0.0189'. MCL at 50.0 and Lateral OA at 56.2 are the worst reader precision after Contusion, so that arithmetic prices headroom the label table may not contain. NOT refuted - Contusion scores 0.8705 on 44.4 precision, which proves a label can - but not licensed as a target either. Anything built against the label deficit must state which labels it targets and what their agreement is.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. Agreement here is precision on the reader's positives only, not full agreement; recall is the separate 32-miss column. And the board scores radiologist annotations while we train on report-read labels - experiments/README.md:2356 and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-11 line 644 do not agree on how far those two diverge, and this measurement does not settle it.
notes: SWEEP phase 2, 2026-09-16: demoted P1 -> P3. Open, filed more than 7 days ago, and NEVER touched since creation. 190 beads met all three tests, which is why P1 had stopped carrying information - owner: 'if we get piled upon, nothing remains importnat'. This is a demotion, not a verdict: promote it back the moment somebody argues its mechanism against comp/champion.json.

title: Buy the denominator: score our own members on all 58 annotated studies, not 13
description:
The only ruler that measures the truth the competition scores (radiologist annotations) covers 58 studies, giving per-label 95% halfwidths of 0.14-0.21 - about half the entire spread across the twelve findings. The only ruler large enough to rank findings (our holdout) scores LLM-read report labels, a proxy that agrees with the radiologist on ~65% of positives. So no measurement this project owns is both the right truth and large enough to resolve a per-label gap, and that single missing denominator has now surfaced as three separate puzzles: the crop80 per-label gate, the 2026-08-20 per-label re-read, and the retracted per-label section of 2026-08-24_the_goal_priced_against_the_inventory.md.

See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_no_denominator_resolves_a_per_label_deficit.md.

Why our members cannot use the 58 today: they are fitted with the annotated studies upweighted, so scoring them against those annotations scores their own training data. supervision_gap works around it by scoring PUBLISHED members instead - somebody else's models, which is why its table cannot be quoted as ours.

The infrastructure is already partly built and that is what makes this cheap. Two commits already landed: 'a member can now be fitted without the 58 radiologist annotations' and '13 of 58 annotated studies are held out'. So the current path measures on 13 studies. Fitting a member that excludes ALL 58 makes every one of them scorable and roughly quadruples the annotation denominator, taking a per-label halfwidth from about 0.30 (n=13) to about 0.15 (n=58).

Note honestly what that does and does not buy. It does NOT make per-label targeting sound - 0.15 is still half the observed spread. It buys the ability to score OUR members on the competition's own truth at all, which today we cannot do, and it is the prerequisite for any per-label decision rather than the decision itself. Price it as instrument work.

Cost is one member fit, and the axis is not seeds or folds - it is a held-out annotation set, which is a different object.

Open question worth answering before spending the card: is 58 studies enough to be worth the fit at all, or does this need more annotation than exists? If the answer is 'not enough', that is itself the finding, and it says every per-label argument this project has made is unresolvable and should stop being made.
notes:
REFRAMED 2026-08-24 22:00Z, and the reframing raises it, by measuring what n=58 can and cannot do.

The per-label case is now closed NEGATIVE and should not be the justification. Even with all 58 studies
scorable, the per-label 95% halfwidths are 0.14-0.21 against a total across-label spread of 0.305. The
instrument would still not resolve a per-label ordering, so 'fit a member without the 58 so we can target
Lateral Meniscus' is not a reason to spend anything.

What n=58 CAN do is aggregate, and that is the open problem this project actually has. The competition
metric is the unweighted mean of twelve per-label AUCs. Averaging twelve labels over 58 studies is far
better conditioned than any one of them - not 12x better, since labels are correlated within a study, but
enough - and it would be measured against RADIOLOGIST truth rather than against LLM-read report labels.

That gives the one thing missing everywhere else in this repo: an offline number in the units the
leaderboard scores, computable without spending a submission slot.

Why that is worth more than it sounds. board_transfer (+1.82 board points per holdout point) is fitted
ENTIRELY on entries at or below 0.933, and our four best entries are one-sided and enter no pair. Every
decision at the top of our range is therefore an extrapolation, and the one direct probe we have says the
transfer SATURATES there: 0.8712 offline scored 0.933, then 0.8731 offline - our best ever - scored 0.932.
An offline ruler on the competition's own truth is how that question gets answered without burning five
slots a day discovering it.

So the pitch is not 'resolve the labels'. It is: we currently choose what to submit using a proxy truth
and a transfer constant fitted where we no longer live. This is the cheapest path to choosing on the real
truth. Still instrument work, still one member fit, but the thing it instruments is the submission
decision rather than a per-label build.

Sequencing note: this is CPU-cheap to specify and GPU-cheap to run (one fit), and it does not compete with
the raddino_dense warm start for the same slot of evidence - that one buys a member, this one buys a
ruler. If the card frees and only one can run, the warm start is the one with a measured floor under it
(mean +0.0035, 90th +0.0113 for a kill at 7 of 12); this one has no size estimate yet, which is itself an
argument for specifying it before running it.
PRICED 2026-08-24 22:02Z, and the aggregate pitch above is now REFUTED by a measurement the repo already contained. Read this note before acting on either of the two above it.

kneemri.evaluation.ruler_transfer already builds the instrument this bead proposes, for the PUBLISHED
members, and it runs on all 58 annotated studies - not 13. Its output tonight:

  58 annotated studies, 58 of them with a held-out prediction; 1000 paired resamples
    arms 1->2   report +0.0021 [-0.0087,+0.0142]   annot +0.0041 [-0.0072,+0.0153]   ratio +1.97 [-2.03,+3.31]
    arms 2->4   report +0.0043 [-0.0037,+0.0124]   annot +0.0054 [-0.0025,+0.0139]   ratio +1.27 [-1.24,+3.38]
    perm 0.40   report +0.0430 [+0.0183,+0.0692]   annot +0.0730 [+0.0501,+0.0996]   ratio +1.70 [+1.07,+3.48]

The delta halfwidth on the annotation ruler is about 0.011. So 58 studies CAN resolve a delta at this
house's own bar (0.015) and CANNOT resolve anything smaller. Both real arm deltas measured here - adding
members, the axis this project spends most of its slots on - are +0.002 to +0.005 and their intervals
span zero on BOTH rulers. The instrument is fit to gate 'is this a result at all', not to rank knobs.

That is the argument against fitting a member to unlock it, and it is quantitative: the offline gain first
place costs is +0.0082, which is BELOW this instrument's resolution. The ruler cannot see the thing the
goal is made of. Dropping P1 -> P3.

Two findings from the same run that are worth more than the bead and should not be lost with it:

1. The ratio is ABOVE 1 wherever it resolves. At a large perturbation it is +1.70 [+1.07, +3.48], an
   interval excluding 1, and the share sweep runs 0.97 / 0.98 / 1.17 / 1.15 as the perturbation grows.
   The report ruler UNDERSTATES deltas relative to radiologist truth rather than overstating them. If that
   holds for real gains, our offline numbers are a conservative floor on what the board sees - which is
   the same direction as board_transfer's +1.82 and an independent route to it.
2. It is a permutation perturbation, not a quality improvement, so read 1 as a direction and not as a
   transfer constant. Do not put 1.70 in a document; it would go stale exactly the way 4.67 did.

What is still worth doing, at P3, is the cheap half: this ran on published members and needed no GPU. If
a member is ever fitted without the 58 for another reason, run ruler_transfer on OUR arms too - the
comparison costs arithmetic. Do not fit one FOR this.

title: dissent_seat retracted the objective-axis family on a run killed at 8 of 12 epochs, so the family is closed on a FLOOR
description:
convergence_check (new, this session) reads dissent_seat_s2026 as TRUNCATED: 9 rows recorded, recipe asked 12, patience=0 so no stopper existed, and logs carry 'ARM FAILED dissent_seat (trainer exit 1)'. The ledger IS honest about this - its row says '0.8509 (killed at epoch 8 of 12)'. The defect is what was concluded anyway: that row 'Retracts the "loss axis buys seats" rule this table stated one row up', and interpretations/2026-08-24_the_goal_priced_against_the_inventory.md carries the consequence forward as 'loss / objective | seat-positive once, retracted by dissent_seat | closed'.

A killed run's score is a FLOOR. Under one_cycle the anneal never ran, so 0.8509 is not 'what this objective scores', it is 'at least what it scores with three twelfths of its schedule missing, none of it the fine-convergence part'. The -0.0069 vs band_dense that carries the retraction is smaller than the anneal is worth on every finished curve in the ledger (base_dense gains ~0.004 from e8 to its e8 peak region; cnx_own_recipe's whole shape is anneal).

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: margin_seat read POSITIVE on the same axis. So the objective family has one positive finished reading and one negative killed reading, and it was closed on the killed one. With decode geometry, pooling, resolution, SSL-init and seat swaps all closed on finished evidence, an objective axis reopened by a harness defect is one of the few levers left that is not already measured at a tenth of what the goal costs.

NOT A CLAIM THAT THE OBJECTIVE WORKS. It is a claim that we do not know, and that we recorded that we did. Re-run dissent_seat to 12 epochs before the family stays closed; ~3h on the card, and it is gated behind the goal-sized threads (raddino warm start) rather than ahead of them.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-24, by measurement, against my own claim in this bead.

I wrote that dissent_seat's -0.0069 is 'smaller than the anneal is worth on every finished curve in the
ledger'. That is FALSE, and the check I built is what refutes it. Measured on all 54 CONVERGED 12-epoch
runs: for each, the gain from best-through-epoch-N to best-overall — what a run killed at N rows would
under-report by.

  killed at  7 rows: median +0.0011  mean +0.0035  90th +0.0113  max +0.0336  over noise floor 7/54
  killed at  9 rows: median +0.0000  mean +0.0006  90th +0.0023  max +0.0099  over noise floor 2/54
  killed at 10 rows: median +0.0000  mean +0.0001  90th +0.0004  max +0.0028  over noise floor 0/54

54 runs. So the missing anneal does not explain its -0.0069, and the quantitative case in this bead is

What survives is only the qualitative half, and it is weak on its own: a killed run's score is a bound
rather than a measurement, and margin_seat read positive on the same axis. That is a reason not to call

What the same measurement makes STRONGER, and it is the finding worth keeping: truncation depth decides

0.8137 is the one genuine floor of the three and the warm start is the one worth the 1.65h.

Note the shape of my own error: I priced a general claim ('a truncated run is a floor') at exactly one
depth and then quoted it at every depth. The check reports the depth. I did not read it.

title: Sequence head over depth: three consecutive RSNA winners use one, we use MRNet's 2018 max-pool
description:
Every member this project has ever trained reads a study as 2D slice -> per-slice features -> elementwise max over slices -> head. That aggregation is order-blind by construction: a finding continuous across five adjacent slices and a single bright artefact slice produce the same pooled vector. MRI is 3D and our reader is not.

WHAT THE FIELD DOES WITH 3D VOLUMES. Three consecutive RSNA Kaggle first places, all on 3D volumes, all the same shape - a 2D backbone per slice plus a SEQUENCE head over the slice axis:
  2022 cervical spine - EfficientNet-V2-S or ConvNeXt, 15 slices per vertebra, neighbour-concatenated multi-channel 2D inputs, LSTM.
  2023 abdominal trauma - CoaT Lite or EfficientNet-V2-S, 96 slices reduced to 32 adjacent-slice triplets, GRU.
  2024 lumbar spine - ConvNeXt-S or EfficientNet-V2-S, localize-then-classify, 2.5D multiview crops, bidirectional LSTM plus attention MIL.
Two axes, and we match neither: their trunk family is the one this repo starved 189:1 (knee-zfgn), and their aggregator is a sequence model where ours is amax.

MRNet, the canonical knee-MRI model, is AlexNet per slice plus max pooling across slices. Our aggregation is literally the 2018 baseline for this exact anatomy.

WE ALREADY BUILD THE INPUT AND THROW IT AWAY. depth_window.py sets NEIGHBOURS = (-1, 0, 1) - the same 2.5D neighbour triplet the 2023 winner feeds its GRU. We build the triplet, encode it, and then amax over the slice axis, at which point the ordering is gone. The information the winners' sequence heads consume is present in our tensors up to the pooling line.

WHERE IT PLUGS IN. SLICE_POOLINGS in kneemri/models/slice_pooling.py is already a strategy dict mapping a name to (per_slice, aggregator); ATTEND and DEPTH already register modules there. A GRU over the slice axis is a fifth entry and a new --slice-pooling choice, not a fork. per_slice=True, aggregator=<bidirectional GRU + pooled state>. The slice axis must reach the aggregator in ANATOMICAL ORDER for this to mean anything - assert that before believing any number, because a shuffled sequence would train to roughly the mean-pool result and read as a null.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER. The MIL benchmark at arXiv 2604.26807 finds simple MEAN pooling matches or outperforms recent MIL and 3D-CNN alternatives on 4 of 6 moderate-sized tasks at 25x lower cost, and that attention-MIL variants never provide an absolute AUROC gain above 0.025. That is a real argument against learned aggregation. It is not an argument for max: our pooling is max, and the cheap control this bead depends on is max->mean (separate bead).

PRICE: ~2.5 h card for one arm at the standing recipe with the pooling swapped. Plausible gain: this is the only axis in the stack that three independent winning solutions agree on and we have never tested, so a 1.5% mechanism is credible rather than hoped-for - unlike a knob. P(clears the 1.5% bar) 0.20-0.30; P(solo beats band_dense 0.8578 at all) 0.45. Ranked above knee-y59c because it is a mechanism change rather than a recipe correction, and the two are independent: a sequence head helps a ViT trunk and a CNN trunk alike.

PRE-REGISTER BEFORE RUNNING. Bands, the noise floor 0.0062, and the DENOMINATOR (solo vs band_dense on the same split), in an arm script under experiments/arms/, checked by arm_check.
CORRECTED 2026-08-24, HOURS AFTER FILING, BY THE LEDGER THIS BEAD SHOULD HAVE BEEN GREPPED AGAINST FIRST.
Two of the three claims above are false against measurements this repo already holds, and the correction
is what makes the remaining one worth keeping.

FALSE: "the aggregation is order-blind". DepthAttention has existed since knee-tqn and mixes each slice
with its through-plane neighbours (a depthwise conv of span 3) BEFORE the gate. It was run as depth_true
from the fixed snapshot: 0.8461, which is -0.0015 against attend_true and second-WORST of four operators.
Order-aware aggregation at the feature level is not untested; it is tested and slightly costly.

FALSE: "our aggregation is MRNet's max". StudyModel.over_depth takes an amax within depth REGIONS and
then a MEAN across the regions, and the four operators measured on one recipe span 0.0019 in total -
max 0.8457, order-aware gate 0.8461, unweighted mean 0.8473, trained gate 0.8476. Every gap is under a
third of the 0.0062 floor. The aggregation stage is saturated from three directions at once: more slices
-0.0001, more slots +0.0002, every combining rule within 0.0019.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF. The winners' pattern has two axes and only one of them is
closed here. The aggregator is closed. The TRUNK is not - it is knee-y59c's 189:1, and all three winning
solutions run convolutional or hybrid trunks. And both attend_true and depth_true wrote the same
conclusion independently: the limit is UPSTREAM, in what a single slice's feature vector contains. That
is an argument for the trunk arm and against another pooling arm, which is the opposite of what this
bead was filed to say.

STILL GENUINELY UNTOUCHED, per depth_true's own exclusion clause: a trunk that sees the VOLUME before any
per-slice feature exists. Feature-level through-plane mixing died; encoder-level 3D reading is a
different mechanism and has one run in this repo (V-JEPA, n=1, on the DINOv2 recipe - the other starved
family). That is where this bead's remaining value points, and it merges with knee-3ped and knee-ec0p
rather than standing as a sequence-head bead.

DEMOTED to P3, kept open only as the record of the external evidence and of the correction. Do not spend
a card slot on a slice-sequence head on the strength of the RSNA-winner pattern alone: this repo measured
that axis four ways and it spans 0.0019.

title: Non-DINOv2 trunks were starved 189:1, and cnx_dense's own pre-registration was overruled by its write-up
description:
THE OWNER ASKED FOR THE DISTRIBUTION OF EFFORT ACROSS ARCHITECTURES. Counted 2026-08-24 over the 202 trained checkpoints on disk, by the variant stamped in each checkpoint's own options blob:

  131  small     DINOv2-small
   45  <unstamped, early; every filename reads adapt_small_* / *_small_*>  DINOv2-small
   11  base      DINOv2-base
    2  large     DINOv2-large
   10  v3small / v3base / v3splus   DINOv3   (9 real, 1 smoke)
    2  cnxbase   ConvNeXtV2   (ONE real run, cnx_dense_s2026; the other is cnx_smoke)
    1  vjepa2l   V-JEPA-2-large   (one run)

DINOv2 family ~189. ConvNeXt 1. V-JEPA 1. Ratio 189:1.

Arm scripts agree: 93 arms, 70 of which never set --variant at all and inherit the default .

WHY THE RATIO IS THE FINDING AND NOT A CURIOSITY. The 189 DINOv2 runs are where every recipe knob in this
project was tuned: read size, backbone LR, schedule, slice band, sampling, augmentation, batch, pooling.
The standing recipe is therefore a 189-run local optimum around DINOv2-small. It was then handed unchanged
to ConvNeXt once and to V-JEPA once, and their scores were written up as properties of those
architectures. They are not. They are measurements of our own tuning, charged to the trunk. Any trunk
would fail that test, DINOv2 included had the recipe been fitted to a CNN.

THE SPECIFIC OVERRULING, which is worse than the count. experiments/arms/cnx_dense.sh pre-registered four
outcomes before it ran. Verbatim:

  THE EXPENSIVE NEGATIVE - solo below 0.80. The head, the band and the slice pooling were all settled on
  token sequences from a patch-14 ViT; a 121-token grid may simply be too coarse for the slot head's
  spatial pooling, in which case the reading is about RESOLUTION and the retry is 448 px (a 14x14 grid)
  BEFORE THE TRUNK IS JUDGED.

cnx_dense scored 0.7927. That is below 0.80. The arm's own protocol fired the branch that says the result
is about resolution and the trunk is NOT yet judged. The 448 retry was never run. Instead
experiments/README.md:1607 titles the entry 'the first non-transformer trunk, and it closes encoder
diversity as an axis', and that sentence has since been quoted forward into an interpretation and into two
answers given to the owner. A pre-registration that is discarded when it fires is not a pre-registration.

SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME ARM: --backbone-lr 4e-5 is DINOv2's adapter rate handed unchanged to a
convolutional trunk. Convolutional trunks fine-tune at rates roughly an order of magnitude higher. LR was
never varied on this family - one point, one rate, chosen for a different architecture.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED ABOUT NON-DINOv2 TRUNKS: that they are FAR. knee-y59c measured distance
ordering exactly by architectural distance from DINOv2 across seven points with zero exceptions, and
cnx_dense is the most distant thing we own (nearest 0.7941 against a seated roster whose own spread floors
at 0.8724). The distance half of the owner's thesis is measured and holds. The quality half has never been
tested at a fair budget.

ACTIONS:
  1. Correct experiments/README.md:1607 - the title claims a closed axis on n=1 against n=189, and the
     entry must print that denominator and its own unrun retry branch.
  2. Run the pre-registered 448 px retry (knee-y59c).
  3. Run a CNN learning rate, which nothing has ever done.
  4. Do not quote 'encoder diversity is closed' anywhere until 2 and 3 have run.

title: evaluation/ has 28 modules and no retirement policy — settled questions still pay quality tax
description:
RELAYED BY PEER SESSION sdlc-scaffold-b4, 2026-08-24. This is the one finding of the three with real substance, and it is a POLICY DECISION for the owner, not a refactor to schedule.

THE FINDING. kneemri/evaluation/ holds 28 modules. Many were built to settle ONE question, settled it, and then stayed: the question is closed in experiments/README.md or an interpretation, the module still costs a test mirror, a coverage share, a shape-contract, a ruff pass and a line in graph.json on every commit forever. vote.py's own docstring says the axis it explores is 'closed instead of re-openable' and the family 'stays because the question recurs' — which is the right call THERE and cannot be the right call 28 times.

THE TENSION, which is why this needs a decision rather than a cleanup. Deleting a diagnostic destroys the ability to re-ask its question cheaply, and this project has already been burned by re-litigating settled numbers (2026-08-13: two P0s filed against results the repo had already measured). A module that answers a closed question is also the artifact that PROVES it closed. So 'delete when settled' is wrong.

THE THREE POLICIES WORTH CHOOSING BETWEEN:
  A. KEEP EVERYTHING. Status quo. Cost is a slowly rising per-commit gate tax and a package nobody can hold in their head.
  B. RETIRE TO A NAMED SHELF. A settled diagnostic moves to evaluation/settled/ with a header naming the question, the answer, and the ledger entry — excluded from the test mirror and coverage floor, still runnable, still readable, no longer paying. Reversible in one git mv.
  C. RETIRE TO GIT HISTORY. Delete, with the ledger entry carrying the commit hash that holds the module. Cheapest steady state, highest cost to re-ask.

RECOMMENDATION IF ASKED: B. It preserves the proof, which is the thing this repo actually needs, and stops the tax. But this is a taste call about what the portfolio should look like and it belongs to the owner.

NOTHING SHOULD BE MOVED UNTIL A POLICY IS PICKED. A one-off tidy of evaluation/ without a rule is how the bucket re-forms.

title: core/ is a leftovers bucket: seven platform-plumbing modules filed by nothing
description:
RELAYED BY PEER SESSION sdlc-scaffold-b4, 2026-08-24, from an architecture audit of this repo. Filed because an audit finding that is not written down is a finding paid for and thrown away; NOT claimed, and not scheduled ahead of board work.

THE FINDING. core/ holds sleep_policy.py (98), wakelock.py (36), mounts.py (73), native_path.py (107), bootstrap.py (59), and kneemri/ holds process_table.py (144), spawn.py (77). None of these is data, model, or evaluation. They are host-platform plumbing — power state, Windows path shapes, drive mounts, process liveness — and they sit at package roots because nothing named them. 594 lines, seven modules, no cohesive owner. This is the shape the global rules forbid for TYPES (never bucket by kind) applied to modules: a package root accumulating whatever had no home.

THE PROPOSED MOVE: one platform/ package, in core/ (the kernel imports none of the others, and this is the most kernel-ish material in the repo). core/platform/{power,paths,mounts,process}.py or one module each, moved verbatim.

WHAT IT BUYS, HONESTLY: findability and a name that refuses the NEXT stray module. It does not fix a bug. No defect in this repo has been traced to these modules' location, and the move is import-rewrites over code whose behaviour does not change — a class of refactor whose own risk is small but nonzero and whose payoff is zero board points.

WHAT IT COSTS: ~7 module moves, ~15 import rewrites, a docs/architecture/graph.json regeneration, and an import-linter contract update. Roughly an hour, card-free, so it fits in a gap between arms. It must NOT displace a queued arm.

DO NOT DO THIS WHILE A SUBMISSION PATH IS BEING EDITED. mounts.py and native_path.py are on the Kaggle kit path; a rename that lands mid-kit is a slot spent on an ImportError. Gate it behind kit_check and mount_check both green.

title: Negative-correlation training: buy ambiguity without paying member error
description:
THE EMPTY CELL. Sort every member this project has built by (solo strength, distance from the seated pool) and three of the four quadrants are occupied:
  strong + near   — every DINOv2 member. Seats saturate at seven.
  distant + weak  — vjepa_warm 0.8337, nearest seated neighbour 0.059 beyond the seated spread. Seat value +0.0002.
  distant + broken— mae_matched, nearest neighbour 0.4333. Seat value -0.0041.
  STRONG + DISTANT— has never existed here.
knee-053z asked for distant-and-strong and the repo answered the distance clause by a mile and missed the solo clause by 0.017. Distance is necessary and demonstrably not sufficient.

WHY SWAPPING THE TRUNK CANNOT FILL IT, already measured three ways and closed 2026-08-21: v3base_dense seat value -0.0007 / -0.0005 (a tie), cnx_dense -0.0042 (a CNN trunk, outside the transformer family entirely), against base_dense's one paying seat. 'A different inductive bias is not a different error structure.' The reason is visible in what those arms hold FIXED: identical slice sampling, identical 2D-slice-then-pool architecture, identical five-level targets, identical BCE objective, identical head. Only the trunk weights move. The error structure is set by the shared pipeline, and a trunk swap cannot reach it.

THE THEORY THAT SAYS WHAT TO DO INSTEAD. Ambiguity decomposition: ensemble error = mean member error - ambiguity. Every arm above moves ONE term. vjepa raised ambiguity and raised mean error at least as much (net +0.0002). A trunk swap left ambiguity flat (net -0.0007). The quadrant is empty because nothing here has ever optimised BOTH terms at once — and the decomposition says that is exactly what an ensemble member's objective should do.

Negative Correlation Learning does it directly: a correlation penalty in the member's own loss, so it is trained to be accurate AND to disagree with the existing pool, jointly rather than in sequence. See 'Generalized Negative Correlation Learning for Deep Ensembling' (arXiv 2011.02952) for the deep-ensemble formulation, and 'Composing Diverse Ensembles of CNNs by Penalization' (MDPI Mathematics 11(23):4730) for the penalty-term form.

WHY THIS REPO CAN BUILD IT CHEAPLY, which is the real argument for doing it now. The plumbing already exists and points the wrong way. DistilledObjective (kneemri/training/objective.py:271) already loads the pool's per-study predictions through teacher_targets.py and adds a term that pulls the student TOWARD the ensemble's ordering. A negative-correlation term is the same loader, the same batch alignment, and the opposite sign: penalise the residual correlation between this member's errors and the pool's, with the BCE term holding accuracy. It is a fourth sibling in the Objective hierarchy beside the AUC-margin one (knee-bdhb), not a fork.

WHAT IT PREDICTS, so it is falsifiable. A member whose SOLO score is at or slightly below its control (the penalty costs some fit) but whose nearest-seated-neighbour correlation drops well below the seated spread's floor, and whose SEAT VALUE clears +0.0015 where vjepa_warm's +0.0002 did not. The refutation is a member that is distant and weak AGAIN — same quadrant as vjepa, which would say ambiguity cannot be bought at this pool's operating point by any means and would close the seat axis for good rather than just for trunks.

READ SEAT VALUE, NOT SOLO SCORE. base_dense is the standing proof that solo does not predict seat: it lost its own control outside the floor and then took the board. This arm is expected to lose solo. Judging it on solo would kill it for doing exactly what it is designed to do.

COST. One 12-epoch arm, ~76 min of card, plus a record_mix seat measurement against the champion roster. Zero submission slots. The pool predictions it needs are already on disk (teacher_fold0.npz, and 87 holdout npz files).

DEPENDS ON: knee-bdhb landing first is NOT required, but the two compose - an AUC-margin member that is also decorrelated is the strong-and-distant construction stated in one sentence.
notes:
PRICE: ~45 min card (teacher cache already SPENT and on disk from knee-1xsu), ZERO submission
slots. P(the member seats at >= +0.0015, the board-resolvable bar) ~= 0.30. Plausible gain if it
seats: +0.002 to +0.005 seat, which is +0.004 to +0.010 board at the 1.92 transfer slope — below the
1.5% bar on its own, and it is priced as a SEAT rather than as a member: seats compose against the
original baseline and the champion is seven of them.

WHY 0.30 AND NOT LOWER, given the encoder axis closed three ways. Those three arms were all attempts
to buy ambiguity as a SIDE EFFECT — pick a different trunk, then measure afterwards whether the errors
happened to decorrelate. None of them put the ensemble into the member's loss. That does not make this
likely; it makes it a genuinely untried mechanism rather than a fourth run of a settled one, and the
quadrant it targets (strong AND distant) has never been occupied by anything here.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE SLOT EVEN ON A NULL. It is an INSTRUMENT for the whole seat axis. If a member
trained explicitly to be right where the pool is wrong still lands distant-and-weak, then ambiguity
cannot be bought at this pool's operating point by any means, and the seat axis closes for good rather
than only for trunks — which retires a line this project has now spent four arms on. That is the
justification for the run, not the +0.004.

ARM: experiments/arms/dissent_seat.sh, control band_dense = 0.8578, one variable (the pair mass; total
ranking strength held at 1.0). Code landed: DecorrelatedObjective + Objective.pairs(emphasis=...),

P(clears 1.5% on its own) ~= 0.05 — a single seat has never moved the board that far here; the 1.5%
is reached by seats composing, and the number this arm is priced against is the +0.0015 seat bar.

ANSWERED 2026-08-24 BY ITS OWN ARM, and left open for a day. This bead's NOTES already name experiments/arms/dissent_seat.sh as its arm with the code landed (DecorrelatedObjective, --dissent-weight). It did not land in the pre-registered refutation quadrant (distant and weak); it landed somewhere the pre-registration did not anticipate and which is worse for the mechanism. The per-label table is the finding: nine of twelve labels DOWN against its control, widest swing -0.0307, and every swing in the same direction. Set beside margin_seat, whose swings ran +0.0272 MCL and -0.0546 Lateral Meniscus, dissent_seat reads the SAME WAY as its control, slightly worse everywhere. A member that is uniformly a little worse is not distant — it is just worse, and a greedy selecting on complementarity has no reason to reach for it. Putting the ensemble into the member's loss did not buy ambiguity; it bought a small uniform accuracy loss.

WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT CLOSE. It closes THIS construction of negative correlation at this pool's operating point — the pair-mass reweighting form. It does not license the stronger claim the bead pre-registered ('ambiguity cannot be bought by any means'), because the arm was stopped at epoch 8 of 12 on a 6/7/8 plateau, and because a penalty on the RANKING pairs is not the same object as a penalty on the error CORRELATION that arXiv 2011.02952 states. That distinction is worth one paragraph in an interpretation, not another 45 minutes of card while a genuinely untried axis (v3lora_dense) is unrun.

RE-PRICED P0 -> P3. The P0 rested on 'a genuinely untried mechanism'; it had been tried before the bead was read.

  0.8509, killed at epoch 8 of 12 = -0.0069 vs band_dense
  NO SEAT: greedy picks it 38th of 66 and the ensemble peak is unchanged
  nine of twelve labels down, widest swing -0.0307

AND THE READING IS THE REFUTATION THIS BEAD PRE-REGISTERED, not a null. The prediction was 'solo at or slightly below control, but nearest-seated correlation well below the seated floor'. What happened instead is that it reads the SAME as its control and slightly worse — where margin_seat, the other objective-axis member, at least read DIFFERENTLY. A member trained explicitly to spend capacity where the pool is wrong did not end up distant. That is the stated refutation clause: ambiguity cannot be bought at this pool's operating point by moving the objective, and it closes the objective axis as a seat lever rather than leaving it open.

This bead sat at P3/open with a PRICE note quoting P=0.30 and '~45 min card' for an arm that had already run and failed. That is the failure mode CLAUDE.md names — beads lag the ledger, and bd search will not find a result recorded only in experiments/README.md. The price note is void; the entry above is the record.

THE SEAT, WHICH IS WHAT THE ARM WAS BOUGHT FOR AND NOBODY HAD READ. member_curve, fold 0, the five champion holdout twins plus a sixth seat, LogitAverage:
  6th = dissent_seat_s2026 (solo 0.8509)  ->  0.8694
  6th = holdannot_s2026    (solo 0.8506)  ->  0.8701
Solo held to 0.0003, so the seats are matched on member strength and differ only in construction. The dissent seat is -0.0007 against an ordinary pool member. It buys nothing.
