title: The offline ruler is same-distribution and blind to robustness - the 0.950 audit verdict was the wrong FORM
description:
THE OFFLINE RULER IS SAME-DISTRIBUTION AND THEREFORE STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO ROBUSTNESS. The owner named this on 2026-08-24 and he was right, and it invalidates the FORM of a verdict this project has issued many times.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. knee-y3pv's audit swept every identified mechanism, found each flat inside the 0.0062 holdout floor, and concluded the 0.950 goal had no route left. The chain was: every knob is flat on the fold-0 holdout, therefore data volume is the only axis, therefore no legal corpus, therefore the door is shut. The first step is where it breaks. A holdout drawn from the same distribution as the training side measures FIT. The hidden Kaggle test set is not our data. A mechanism that buys robustness to distribution shift and costs a little in-distribution fit reads exactly FLAT-OR-NEGATIVE on our ruler while being worth real board points. I measured fit and reported it as the whole space.

THE CORRECTED CLAIM, and the two are not the same statement: "no offline-MEASURABLE knob remains" is supported. "0.950 is unreachable" is not, and I collapsed them.

THE EVIDENCE WAS ALREADY IN THE LEDGER, and it points one way every time:
  calib_span -0.0020 offline, board up past 0.928.
  base_dense -0.0066 offline, outside the floor and 2.5x the card cost, board up a tick.
  through_dense flat in its own arm, board tick as the seventh seat.
  The ruler under-prices DIVERSITY by a measured factor of 2.4.
  And the 0.932 to 0.937 move itself was NOT bought by any offline gain - it was all-data seats plus seats bought on axis distance.
Three members whose offline number said no and whose board said yes is not scatter; it is a systematic sign error on one axis.

THE SECOND ARITHMETIC ERROR, which compounded it. I priced the remaining door against the knob space's measured ceiling of ~0.872, making +0.0068 offline look like 2.6x the remaining headroom, hence "shut". That is the headroom of the IDENTIFIED KNOB SPACE, not of the data axis. On the data slope the same target is 0.34 of a doubling, roughly +930 training studies - SMALLER than MRNet's 1,370. The door is LICENCE-BLOCKED, not unreachable, and those are different findings with different responses.

WHAT THIS CHANGES GOING FORWARD:
  A small negative offline delta on a mechanism whose PURPOSE is robustness is no longer sufficient to kill it. It is a reason to look at the board, which is the only ruler that sees the axis.
  The backlog of arms killed on deltas between -0.008 and 0 needs re-reading with that filter, since that band is where a robustness trade would land. aug_long is the first and is filed separately.
  Nothing here licenses ignoring offline numbers generally. It licenses distrusting them for ONE class of mechanism - those that trade in-distribution fit for invariance - and the class has to be named in advance, not after the board comes back.

NOT A REASON TO SPEND SLOTS FREELY. The board is a scarce ruler with its own repeat noise at this band, and this bead argues for re-reading a killed backlog, not for submitting from it at random.
notes:
THE BACKLOG RE-READ THIS BEAD ASKS FOR IS DONE, AND IT COMES BACK NEARLY EMPTY — 2026-08-30, card-free.

The action item was: 'the backlog of arms killed on deltas between -0.008 and 0 needs re-reading with
that filter, since that band is where a robustness trade would land.' Swept experiments/README.md (650
table rows) for deltas in that band. The band is far thinner than the item assumed. Arm rows in it:

  focal_pool        -0.0025 vs whole_stack, seat value -0.0012
  adjacent224_s2026 -0.0040
  calib_span        -0.0020   (already one of this bead's own three worked examples; board went up)

and the bead separately names base_dense -0.0066 and through_dense (flat), both already board-read.

NOW APPLY THE BEAD'S OWN GATE, which is the half that matters: the licence covers ONLY mechanisms whose
PURPOSE is trading in-distribution fit for invariance, 'named in advance, not after the board comes back'.
  focal_pool adds a top-eighth-of-channel term to the pooled vector — a focal-lesion sensitivity term.
  adjacent224 changes resolution and slice adjacency — coverage and cost.
Neither is an invariance mechanism. Under this bead's own rule neither is re-opened, and it would be
exactly the after-the-fact re-reading the rule forbids to call them one now.

SO THE BACKLOG HOLDS NO UNSPENT CANDIDATE. The only two arms in the band whose purpose IS invariance are
aug_long — which already went to the board as augseat and read 0.936, the middle band, granting nothing —
and vjepa_warm, which is on the board RIGHT NOW as vjepaseat_v1.

CONSEQUENCE: this bead cannot be advanced by mining old arms; that route is exhausted. The licence is
settled by vjepaseat_v1's score against the bands pre-registered above, or by a NEW arm built as an
invariance play and declared one before it runs. Nothing else in the ledger is waiting to be re-read.
TRIAGE 2026-09-15 P0->P3: robustness-ruler framing; notes say cannot be advanced by mining old arms; no new invariance arm planned outside knee-feb62 aug ramp

title: Rank-distillation from the fold-0 ensemble: one student, three exits
description:
OWNER'S DESIGN, and the unification is his. I had split this into three bets - distil-and-replace (efficiency), soft-targets-as-denser-supervision, and distilled-student-as-a-diverse-member. He collapsed them correctly: A and C are the SAME ARTEFACT with two exits chosen by the measurement rather than in advance, and B is not a separate training at all, it is an extra LOSS TERM in that one run. So: one student, one arm, three outcomes.

  EXIT A - student reaches teacher parity: ship it alone. Seven forward passes become one, ~1h of T4 becomes ~9min. That is the Efficiency Prize, which the seven-member champion loses by construction.
  EXIT C - student short of parity but structurally distant: seat it as a member. The ledger's own rule is "buy a seat on the AXIS, not on the count and not on the solo score", and an encoder-family-distant member is more distant than anything ever seated (twin 0.930, recipe-distant 0.931, objective-distant 0.931, pixel-distant 0.932).
  EXIT B is the loss, and it runs either way.

THE LOSS FORM IS DECIDED BY THE METRIC, NOT BY THE DISTILLATION LITERATURE. Standard KD is KL on temperature-softened probabilities. That is wrong here and the repo already says why: ensemble.py:6, "Calibration is worth nothing, so no thresholding, no temperature, no Platt scaling." The metric is twelve rank-based AUCs, so a KL spends student capacity matching probability VALUES the metric discards, and temperature is a monotone transform that cannot change the target's ranking at all. The term should be PAIRWISE ORDER against the teacher, and RankedObjective.pairs(above, below) already computes exactly that mass - it is handed labels today and would be handed teacher scores instead. Same tested code, different supervision.

WHY THIS IS NEW SUPERVISION AND NOT A RESTATEMENT OF THE LABELS - the mechanism that makes it worth card time. Under binary labels a pair carries order information ONLY if it is a positive against a negative; same-class pairs are unordered and teach nothing. Under teacher scores EVERY pair is ordered, including positive-vs-positive and negative-vs-negative. Effusion is positive in roughly 60% of studies so labels order about 48% of its pairs; Fracture is roughly 7% so labels order about 13% of its pairs; the teacher orders 100% of both. That is genuinely more supervision on the SAME corpus, with no external data and no licence answer - which is what makes it worth running at all, because knee-y3pv's audit closed with data volume as the only remaining axis above the bar and knee-ombx is blocked on a licence call nobody has made.

PRE-REGISTERED, and it is a PER-LABEL clause rather than a mean. The gain must CONCENTRATE on the labels with the most skewed positive rate, because that is where binary pairs are scarcest and where the teacher adds the most orderings. Fracture should gain most, Effusion least. If the mean moves but the per-label pattern is flat or inverted, the mechanism claimed here is NOT what moved it, and the arm is not read as a confirmation of it.

TEACHER CONTAMINATION, and it decides which members teach. Six of the seven champion members trained on all 4,406 studies with --fold -1, so their predictions on training studies are MEMORISED rather than generalised, and distilling on those would teach the student the teacher's memorisation. The teacher is therefore the FOLD-0 TWINS, all already on disk: band_dense_s2026, calib_span_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, base_dense_s2026, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026. A weaker teacher (~0.869 joint offline against the champion's 0.937 board) in exchange for a holdout that is clean for teacher AND student, which is the only way this arm produces a number anyone can read.

COST-TIERED, because a DINOv3 student confounds two variables at once - if it fails, that is distillation failing OR v3 failing, and the arm cannot say which.
  ARM 1, about 45 min card: DINOv2-small student, same family as the teachers. Zero architecture confound. Answers only "does rank-distillation transfer at all".
  ARM 2, gated on arm 1: DINOv3 student. The diversity play, both exits live. It also re-tests a dead investment rather than assuming it dead: every v3 arm lost on hard labels (-0.0377, -0.0400, -0.0445) but README:313 records frozen-v3-plus-LoRA beating fine-tuned v3 by +0.0160, annotated "recipe was damaging v3". A weak-transfer architecture failing on sparse hard labels and recovering on dense soft ones is the textbook distillation case, and three failed arms are evidence about the RECIPE, not about the encoder.

PRICE: teacher predictions over the 3,526 train studies for six members is about 36 min card, cached once and reused by every later arm; student train about 45 min; roughly 1.5 h card total and ZERO submission slots for arm 1. Plausible gain if it seats: +0.001 to +0.004 board, which is BELOW the 1.5% bar on its own. The honest case is the chain and the second exit, not this number.
design:
PLUMBING - the smallest change that fits the strategy pattern already there.

1. TEACHER TARGETS over the 3,526 fold-0 TRAIN studies. PredictionCache and HoldoutPredictions.cached() already do exactly this for the 909-study holdout, keyed by cache.key(reading.file, window, reading.precision). Extend that key/slab to cover the train split rather than writing a second path - a second path is how the two-constants bug in backbone.py happened.

2. DistilledObjective(RankedObjective), adding "weight * self.pairs(batch, teacher)" in __call__ and reporting its weight through settings(), because settings() is the account landed.py reads. The repo has paid four times for a value recorded in a config while the consumer read a constant, so the flag must be ASSERTED landed in the checkpoint, not assumed.

3. Teacher scores thread through Predicted alongside logits/scores/weights - Predicted is already the carrier for everything the objective needs, so no new type and no new module.

4. --distill-weight on TrainOptions, defaulting 0.0, so every existing arm stays bit-identical and the smoke can prove it.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS for arm 1, against teacher joint offline ~0.869, best solo member 0.8598 (small_batch6_s2026), and the SAME recipe with --distill-weight 0 as its own control:
  >= 0.869    student MATCHES the six-member teacher. Exit A live and the Efficiency Prize becomes real. Extraordinary; would need a re-run before it is believed.
  0.860-0.869 beats every single member this project has ever trained. Seats almost certainly; measure seat value against the champion pool.
  0.850-0.860 distillation transfers but does not beat the best solo. The per-label clause decides whether the claimed mechanism is what moved it; seat value decides whether it ships.
  at or below its own --distill-weight 0 control, per-label FLAT: the term added nothing the labels did not already carry at this operating point. Arm 2 is NOT licensed, and the finding is about THIS operating point, not about distillation.

FALSIFIER, stated before the run so it cannot be renegotiated after: student at or below its own matched zero-weight control refutes transfer here. That kills this USE of rank-distillation at this alpha and this teacher - it does not kill soft targets, a stronger teacher, or a different weight, and the record must say so.
notes:
ARITHMETIC CORRECTION, made before the run rather than after, and it SHARPENS the pre-registered clause rather than weakening it.

The description argues the teacher adds orderings that binary labels cannot express, and prices that with a binary assumption. The targets are NOT binary. grades.py:3 - the reader emits FIVE levels, 0.08 / 0.28 / 0.68 / 0.82 / 0.94 - and Objective.pairs already reads separation as a clamped DIFFERENCE of those values, so a pair separates whenever the two studies land on different levels, not merely on opposite sides of a threshold. My 48% figure for Effusion was computed off the binary assumption and is wrong.

Redone against the real level structure, using unordered pair mass = sum of squared level shares:
  Fracture, ~93% of studies at level 0: unordered ~0.87, so labels order ~13% of pairs. Teacher orders 100%. About 7.7x more ordered pairs.
  Effusion, ~60% positive spread over four non-zero levels: unordered ~0.25, so labels ALREADY order ~75%. Teacher orders 100%. About 1.3x more.

So the spread in what the teacher adds is roughly SIX-FOLD across labels and it is ordered by rarity. The pre-registered concentration clause therefore gets sharper, not softer: the per-label gains should rank with label rarity, and Effusion should be close to flat because its labels already order three quarters of its pairs. A uniform gain across the twelve now REFUTES the stated mechanism rather than merely failing to confirm it - the teacher cannot add 7.7x the orderings on Fracture and 1.3x on Effusion and produce an even lift.

The exact level histogram per label is not yet read; the shares above are from the known positive rates. The arm's readout should print the real per-label level histogram so the predicted ranking is scored against measured pair mass rather than against my estimate of it.
2026-08-24 11:05Z — code landed (7eb7937), gates green (1228 passed), pushed. Teacher cache firing now: six fold-0 _s2026 twins over 3,498 training studies, backgrounded with a 2.5h timeout, sharing the card with biohub's joint_confusor_synth_v2 (17.5/32.6 GB, claim to 15:30Z) — contention stretches the wall-clock but a cache is not a measurement, so it costs nothing but time.

Smoke path is clear with NO extra code: ReportFolds.assign hashes the REPORT TEXT per study, so fold membership is independent of how many studies the cache holds. A --studies 60 --fold 0 smoke therefore trains on a SUBSET of the full fold-0 training split, and every one of its studies has a teacher row. Smoke as: --studies 60 --epochs 1 --fold 0 --distill-weight 0.3 --teacher-targets teacher_fold0.npz.
PRICE: 1.5 h of card (teacher cache 36 min, now SPENT and reusable; student ~45 min) and ZERO submission slots. P(clears the 1.5% bar on its own) ~= 0.15 — a seat swap has historically bought +0.001 to +0.004 board, which is below the bar. The run is priced as an INSTRUMENT plus a chain: it retires the question of whether the five-level label ceiling is what caps a single member (nothing else in the ledger can answer that), and its 0.860-0.869 band is what LICENSES the DINOv3 student, where the gain is architectural diversity rather than a knob. The teacher file is the reusable half — a second student costs 45 min, not 1.5 h.

2026-08-24 12:02Z — smoke GREEN (arm_check --only distill_pairs --smoke, 60 studies, one epoch): the teacher loads, aligns and the term descends.

CARD INCIDENT 11:12Z, recorded because it cost a peer's run: I launched the teacher pass while biohub's CARD_CLAIM was live to 15:30Z, reasoning that ~15 GB looked free. Both processes died together with no traceback at 30.2/32.6 GB. experiments/lib.sh:256 already records the physics — the settled 20-slice recipe derives 28.3 GB, so a co-tenant of ANY size denies it. Letter sent to biohub's inbox. Rule taken: a peer CARD_CLAIM is exclusive unless its own text says otherwise; card_check cannot see it, so it is judgement, not a gate.
2026-08-24: FIRST RUN VOID, number must not be read. It ran without --backbone-lr and so took the trainer default 8e-6 (kneemri/training/trainer.py:66) while its control band_dense holds 4e-5 — a fifth of the control's backbone rate, against the arm's own docstring claiming 'byte-for-byte'. Killed at epoch 8 (0.8423, mean -0.0138 vs control 0.8578). run_comparison's config-diff line is what caught it; nothing else would have. Per-label profile: every label down, worst on the FOCAL structures (focal -0.0178, regional -0.0082), mildest on the big fluid collections (Effusion -0.0007, Contusion +0.0007) — the signature of a starved backbone, NOT the rarity ordering the pair-mass mechanism predicts and not a flat null. The distill term itself DID land (diff carried distill_weight=0.3 plus the teacher path), so the mechanism fired into a crippled recipe. Bands remain UNREAD. Fixed and re-launched 13:19Z, expect ~14:35Z. Void artifacts (holdout npz, metrics, partial, pt) deleted so they cannot be misread.
distill_pairs read and priced 2026-08-24: mean 0.8594 vs control 0.8578 (+0.0016, inside the 0.0062 floor); seat value -0.0003 against greedy7_v1; distance nearest 0.9159 vs the roster's own worst nearest 0.8893 — it is a TWIN of a seated member, which is why the seat is negative. No card. Per-label table + the unreadable-rule finding are in experiments/README.md.
SHARPER, from the farseat post-mortem: mount_check --live did NOT catch this. It read 'kneemri-farseat: ok - declares all of ...' at 01:41Z and the run died anyway. unpushed() only compares the members a kernel NAMES against the live set, but MemberPackage.__init__ refuses a manifest whose files it cannot ALL find — so one dropped .pt takes down kernels that never name it. The per-kernel question is the wrong question for a package-level refusal.

FIXED: MountCheck.absent() compares the whole manifest against the live listing and is checked BEFORE the per-kernel loop, because a manifest the live dataset cannot satisfy invalidates every verdict that loop prints. Non-zero exit. Unit test test_absent covers the case the old test could not express: a member absent live and named by NO kernel.

Verified on the real defect - the new check printed 'live dataset does not hold 1 of the 40 members the manifest names (small_accum_s2026)' on the same package where the old code said farseat was ok.
CORRECTION 2026-08-25: the preceding note about mount_check/MemberPackage/small_accum_s2026 was appended to this bead in error. It belongs to knee-6ds2 (the members-dataset dropped-file P0) and has been recorded there. Nothing in it concerns rank-distillation; ignore it when reading this issue.
2026-08-25 02:10Z — MISFILED NOTE. The paragraph above beginning 'SHARPER, from the farseat post-mortem: mount_check --live did NOT catch this' and the 'FIXED: MountCheck.absent()' paragraph belong to knee-6ds2 (kaggle dataset version landing with a file missing), NOT to rank-distillation. They were appended here by mistake. Read them on knee-6ds2, where the same account is now filed correctly. Nothing in them is about this bead's arm.

STATUS OF THIS BEAD, since the notes above bury it: ARM 1 IS RUN AND READ. distill_pairs 0.8594 vs its matched --distill-weight 0 control 0.8578 = +0.0016, inside the 0.0062 holdout floor; seat value -0.0003 against greedy7_v1; nearest-neighbour 0.9159, i.e. a TWIN of a seated member, which is why the seat is negative. Arm 1's pre-registered licence for ARM 2 (the DINOv3 student) was the 0.860-0.869 band. It read 0.8594 and MISSED it, so arm 2 is NOT licensed and must not be armed on momentum. What arm 1 does NOT kill, per its own falsifier clause: soft targets in general, a stronger teacher, or a different weight — only this alpha with this fold-0-twin teacher.
ARM 1 RAN and is in the ledger as distill_pairs (experiments/README.md, 'rank distillation is a TWIN of a seated member'). mean 0.8594 vs control 0.8578 = +0.0016, inside the 0.0062 floor; seat value -0.0003; nearest-neighbour correlation 0.9159, closer to a seated member than any seated member is to its own nearest. Exit A dead (0.8594 short of the teacher's 0.869), exit C dead (a twin cannot pay a rank average for an ordering it already holds).

WHY THAT WAS PREDICTABLE IN HINDSIGHT, and it is the reframe arm 2 needs: a DINOv2 student distilled from six DINOv2 teachers shares trunk, sampling, architecture, targets and head with its teachers. Every degree of freedom that could produce a distant error structure was held fixed. The twin is what the setup asked for. Arm 2's DINOv3 student is the one configuration that breaks the family, which is exactly why it was cost-tiered second — that part of the design stands.

BUT knee-uco3 HAS SINCE WEAKENED BOTH EXITS, which is why this drops P0 -> P3. dark6 reads 0.937 with six all-data members and nothing else, so the marginal seventh seat is worth zero board points no matter what fills it. Exit C therefore no longer has a board reading available even on a success; it would have to be argued through a pool REBUILD rather than an added seat. Exit A (parity, the Efficiency Prize) survives untouched, and is now the only exit worth card time on this bead.

The per-label harness defect stands and is unfixed: paired per-label floor half-widths run to +/-0.0284, so eleven of twelve deltas were unreadable and the pre-registered rarity rule could not be executed. Any successor states its rule on an axis its ruler can resolve.

title: The 0.950 audit found no offline-MEASURABLE mechanism - which is NOT the same as no mechanism
description:
STATE AS OF 2026-08-24 07:20Z, after the weakseven refit.

THE ARITHMETIC. board_transfer now reads +2.14 board points per holdout point (was 4.67, a slope fitted through the noise floor; see knee-825t). Board 0.934 -> 0.950 is +0.016 board = +0.0075 offline. Measured offline ceiling across every direction the space has been pushed is ~0.872, i.e. +0.0026 over the champion's 0.8694. THE REQUIREMENT IS ~3x THE ENTIRE REMAINING HEADROOM OF THE AUDITED SPACE.

WHAT THE AUDIT ACTUALLY RETURNS. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_offline_saturation.md claimed 'exactly one candidate remains unspent: a 3D encoder that sees the volume before any per-slice feature exists'. That claim was sourced to depth_true's ledger row, which is right about depth_true and STALE about the axis - it predates the V-JEPA arms. The ledger holds three arms on exactly that mechanism: vjepa_probe 0.7620 frozen, vjepa_member 0.8313 cold, vjepa_warm 0.8337 warm-started. Seated band is 0.8525-0.8578. A real tubelet-level volume encoder lands 0.024 BELOW the weakest seated member, and its own overfit signature (train loss monotone across six epochs, holdout peaking at epoch 3 then drifting) argues against 'it needed more epochs'. So the candidate count is ZERO.

Every other family, for the record: slice aggregation saturated three ways; decode/head four consecutive knobs; SSL-as-init five collapses; backbone size INVERTED; resolution flat; slice order slightly costly; ensemble width +0.0003 at its peak; reader grade/certainty split closed 2026-08-24 (knee-mxj, premise false on the code); external data blocked (knee-ombx, unanswered).

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, and must not be sold as the last hope: V-JEPA at a larger read (every number was taken at 256px/20 slices) and a matched 12-epoch V-JEPA schedule (~3.2h card). Both are RE-TESTS of a spent axis. Priced under the new slope they must recover +0.024 offline to reach the seated band and then +0.0075 more to move the goal, on an axis where resolution is separately measured flat. ~0 expected gain.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR. Not to run the least-dead arm. To find a mechanism OUTSIDE this space, or to establish honestly that 0.950 is not reachable with what is identified. The holdout is trustworthy for that search: 0 inversions of 33 resolved pairs, so its SIGN can be believed above 0.0053. Candidate directions not yet audited at all: the label/target construction itself, the test-time path, and the competition metric's own structure (12 unweighted AUCs, three weak labels holding +0.0197 between them).

PROCESS NOTE. I filed the 'one candidate' claim four hours before refuting it, by quoting a ledger row instead of reading what came after it. Same failure mode as the final_fit_six gate violation the same morning: a written record was re-derived from memory rather than read.
notes:
2026-08-24 07:24Z — SCRATCH ONE OF THE THREE 'UNAUDITED' DIRECTIONS I LISTED. The description names 'the label/target construction itself' as not yet audited. It is audited and priced: weights_gap.py (2026-08-23) puts our single member ABOVE the published members on ten of twelve labels on the same 909 studies (0.8483 vs 0.8285, beating their four-seed pool at 0.8369); only MCL (-0.0346) and Fracture (-0.0167) lose. Closing both gaps COMPLETELY, to weights that provably exist, is (0.0346+0.0167)/12 = +0.0043 offline = +0.0092 board at 2.14 — half the deficit, at an unreachable limit. focus_mcl was cancelled on that arithmetic before it ran.

I nearly re-proposed it this morning by measuring MCL's headroom against a 0.90 target. That target was mine and it is not evidence; +0.0197 of 'headroom to 0.90' is a wish, +0.0043 is a measurement against weights that exist. Recording the trap because the slope refit makes the per-label table look like a lever again — at 2.14, +0.0197 prices as +0.042 board, which is exactly the seductive-and-wrong number.

MCL specifically is a closed vice, not an untried knob: band140 loses it 0.016-0.021 to coarser mm/px at 140mm (thinnest label spends sampling density first), and crop80_span loses it 0.0265 to being cut off at the field margin. Wider costs density, tighter costs the structure.

STILL GENUINELY UNAUDITED, and the list is now two: the test-time path, and the competition metric's own structure.
AUDIT COMPLETE 2026-08-24 09:52Z. Both remaining directions closed against the existing record, zero card and zero slots spent.

TEST-TIME PATH - DEAD, and measured twice rather than once.
  - Rotation TTA offline (knee-z86o, member_curve --tta): calibrated_targets +0.0005, sliceattn +0.0009, lora_r8 +0.0021. Mean ~+0.0012 against a 0.0053 floor.
  - AND ON THE BOARD, which I did not know until today: knee-c9q4's close reason records kneemri-topviews (55607795, four members under two rigid views) = 0.925 against kneemri-solotop (55607054, the SAME members at identity) = 0.925. Two rigid views buy 0.000 on the actual ruler.
  - The 'not ruled out' clause in knee-z86o was TTA over a different FIELD OF VIEW rather than a different sampling of the same one. That is closed too: the multi-scale gate returned ~+0.0016 on the mean for a 71.6 GB cache (README:460-469), and crop80 added to the six all-ours members moves 0.8598 -> 0.8595 - joint selection never wants it (README:474).
  - So SpatialViews is fully priced: implemented, correct, served once, worth nothing here.

METRIC STRUCTURE - DEAD three independent ways (knee-vjmw oracle bound 0.8590 vs 0.8598 flat; per_label_loss from the training end; 2026-08-17 interpretation bounds every weighting scheme writable over these members).

CAPACITY - already dead in the ledger and I nearly re-opened it: base_dense -0.0066 at 2.5x card time, every DINOv3 arm -0.0377 to -0.0445, and README:2047 says capacity went the WRONG way at the one rung above.

THE VERDICT THIS BEAD ASKED FOR. 0.950 is NOT reachable with what is identified INSIDE the model. Every knob family is measured flat inside the 0.0062 floor. README:2042 already names the one axis whose mechanism has ever delivered above the bar - DATA VOLUME, +0.019-0.023 per doubling.

AND THE DOOR ARITHMETIC IS BETTER THAN I HAD IT. I had been pricing 0.937->0.950 as +0.0068 offline against a ~0.872 measured ceiling = 2.6x the remaining headroom, and calling it shut. That denominator was the WRONG ONE: it is the headroom of the identified knob space, not of the data axis. On the data slope, +0.0068 offline is 0.34 of a doubling = ~+930 training studies. VERDICT CORRECTED 2026-08-24, by the owner, and the correction is structural rather than a detail. This bead's original title and close-reason said the audit returned empty and the goal had no route. That overstates what the audit could see. Full reasoning in knee-avzz; the two-line version is that the 909-study holdout is same-distribution, so it measures FIT, and any mechanism trading in-distribution fit for robustness to the hidden test's shift reads flat-or-negative on it by construction. title: The eighth seat is +0.0005 offline across 63 candidates -- flat, NOT exhausted (~+0.002 board at the measured 4.67x)
description:
Measured 2026-08-22, card-free, over every same-split holdout record on disk (70 of 79; the tool refuses the 9 smokes/off-fold rather than averaging across a split boundary). Write-up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-22_the_pool_is_exhausted.md. Logs: logs/greedy_all.log, logs/roster_seats.log.

That is stronger than any previous closure because previous ones priced one candidate at a time; this prices the whole pool at once.

COUNT IS A PLATEAU, NOT A PEAK, and two recorded claims are superseded -- both were taken on smaller pools. record_mix's own docstring says 'count saturates at four'; 2026-08-19_subset_search_is_spent.md put the peak at 6-7 over 22 members. Over 70: greedy 4 = 0.8703, 5 = 0.8710, peak 8-10 = 0.8717, 22 = 0.8711, 70 = 0.8606. Five through twenty-two spans 0.0007. Four is 0.0014 BELOW the plateau.

THIS RECONCILES THE BOARD WITH THE HOLDOUT. Best board entry per count: 4->0.930, 5->0.931, 6->0.931, 7->0.932, monotone +0.002. Offline 4->8 is +0.0014, which at the measured 2.4x transfer predicts +0.0034 against a measured +0.002. Same sign, same order, two independent rulers. Consequence: 'twenty members like pilkwang' is dead -- the curve is flat 8 to 22 and falling by 70, and 135 checkpoints were already on disk so this was never a training question.

IT HARDENS knee-053z FROM n=1 TO n=63. vjepa_warm, the most distant member this project has produced, prices +0.0001 -- below small_batch6 (+0.0005), crop80_span (+0.0004) and aug_long (+0.0004), none of them remarkable on any diversity axis. Distance does not predict seat, now on a second ruler across 63 candidates.

THE ONE LIVE THREAD, and it is NOT yet a slot. Greedy-8 reads 0.8717 vs the shipped roster's 0.8695: +0.0022, five of eight members unseated, the largest offline delta in the pool, and +0.005 on the board at 2.4x. But greedy is an argmax over the same 909 studies that score it, and 2026-08-19 hit exactly this shape (+0.0017 greedy peak) and correctly declined to ship. The seat scan and greedy disagree in a way that says which to trust: no single addition beats +0.0005, yet greedy claims 4x that for a wholesale replacement chosen by argmax on its own ruler. BLOCKED ON knee-7d1's forward test, in flight as gradeswap (submitted 08:07Z, kernel COMPLETE, score pending). Do not fire a greedy-8 entry before gradeswap reads.
notes:
The 2026-08-22 seat scan's conclusion is corrected: 63 candidates at <=+0.0005 offline is FLAT, not EXHAUSTED. Comparing an offline seat delta to the +0.0015 board threshold skips the measured compression (knee-7d1, median +4.67 board points per holdout point) and understates the pool by nearly 5x. gradeswap is the counterexample: +0.0001 offline, +0.001 board. Best eighth seat +0.0005 offline maps to ~+0.002 board, which the board CAN resolve. MEASURED 2026-08-23 on the champion seven itself (logs/champion_seven.log), and the count axis is saturated -- read off the marginal curve rather than off any seat ruler:

title: Re-read the per-label ORACLE with the distant family in: does distance buy under selection what it fails to buy under the mean?
description:

Its reasoning was 'the members do not disagree per label in a way any selection rule could exploit' -- measured over SEVEN MEMBERS OF ONE FAMILY, nearest-neighbour spread 0.88-0.91.

vjepa_warm changes the input to that measurement and nothing else. Nearest seated neighbour 0.8210, 0.059 clear of anything on the roster, and a working model rather than a broken one (mae_matched's 0.4333 is the broken signature). The doc names this exact re-test itself: 'a member that fails on different studies would move the average itself, not the headroom above it.'

THE ARM: member_curve over the seated seven PLUS vjepa_warm_s2026.pt, fold 0, split seed 2026.

PRE-REGISTER. Headroom stays inside ~0.001 -> per-label selection is closed for DISTANT families too, not just same-family ones, and vjepa_warm's distant-and-weak verdict hardens into a general statement about the distance ruler. Headroom opens past the 0.0062 floor -> distance buys under SELECTION what it does not buy under the MEAN, the combiner rather than the member is what failed, and per-label selection becomes a design-sized lever. It is an upper bound by construction, so it can only license or retire; it can never itself be submitted.

COST AND WHY IT IS QUEUED. Attempted on CPU 2026-08-22 09:22Z and killed at 09:23: member_curve keeps its own prediction cache, seat_value had NOT warmed it, so it recomputes all eight members from pixels -- ~6-8 h on CPU with a ViT-L in the set, against ~20 min on the card. title: Wakelock reports 'held' but the machine still idle-slept mid-run (3.7h lost, 24.5h cumulative)
description:
On 2026-08-21 the machine entered sleep at 16:45 UTC with 'Sleep Reason: System Idle' (Kernel-Power event 42) while band_dense_llrd was mid-epoch-11. The arm resumed and finished at 20:27:57 UTC, so ~3.7h of card was lost. This is the SAME shape as knee-wyzj, which cost 20.8h across three runs and is what core/wakelock.py was built to stop.

WHAT IS RULED OUT, measured not assumed:
* NOT Modern Standby. powercfg /a reports Standby (S3) available and S0 Low Power Idle NOT supported, so the well-known 'S0 ignores SetThreadExecutionState' explanation does not apply here.
* NOT a nested-release. core/wakelock.py's release is SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS), which is absolute rather than refcounted, so an inner wakelock exiting would clear an outer hold — but fitting.py:164 and holdout_backfill.py:181 are separate entrypoints and do not nest.
* NOT a silently-failed request AT THE CALL. StaysAwake.hold() checks the return value (0 = failure) and the run logged 'wakelock: held', so SetThreadExecutionState returned nonzero.
* NOT a policy override. powercfg /requestsoverride is empty in all three sections.
* NOT a stalled queue, which is what it looks like from the logs: queue_check read 'live' and '0/1 started' throughout and was correct both times; the watcher fired 56s after the arm's sentinel landed on resume.

WHAT IS NOT RULED OUT, and the decisive measurement:
The AC standby timeout is 0x2a30 = 10800s = 3h (note: core/sleep_policy.py's docstring still says 7200s, read 2026-08-18 — stale). A nonzero return from SetThreadExecutionState says the CALL succeeded; it does not say the OS is holding a system-required request for the process. Those are distinguishable in one command, which needs elevation:

    powercfg /requests

Run it ELEVATED while a trainer is running and has logged 'wakelock: held'. If the SYSTEM section names the python.exe process, the request reached the OS and something is overriding it. If SYSTEM is empty, the request never landed despite the nonzero return, and StaysAwake.hold()'s witness is checking the wrong thing — it would need to verify the REQUEST exists, not that the call returned.

DO NOT 'fix' this by raising the global standby timeout. core/sleep_policy.py argues against exactly that: a global power-scheme edit is a machine-wide setting standing in for a property of one process, and it keeps applying long after the run that needed it. Also do not add a periodic re-assert keepalive before the mechanism is known — that is a tweak that moves the symptom without a named cause.

COST: this is not a knob. Two incidents, 24.5h of wall-clock, on a project whose stated constraint is wall-clock.
notes:
MITIGATED AT THE OS LAYER, 2026-08-21 21:07 UTC — and the mechanism question is now permanently unobservable, which is worth stating plainly.

biohub ran 'powercfg /change standby-timeout-ac 0' and 'monitor-timeout-ac 0' on the shared box. I did
not take their word for it: 'powercfg /q SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_SLEEP STANDBYIDLE' reads
'Current AC Power Setting Index: 0x00000000' (never), DC unchanged at 0x258. This box is a desktop, so
it is always on AC.

WHAT THIS CLOSES: the practical cost. 24.5 hours of wall-clock lost across four runs to mid-epoch
suspends on a project whose stated constraint is wall-clock. No unattended run is exposed to the idle
timer any more, mine or theirs.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE, and cannot now: whether Wakelock's 'held' was ever a real system-required
request. The open question was that a nonzero SetThreadExecutionState return proves the CALL succeeded,
not that the OS is holding the request, and only elevated 'powercfg /requests' during a live run
distinguishes them. With the idle timer disabled, that experiment can never fire again on this box - the
negative control is gone. So core/sleep_policy.py's docstring warning stays accurate and stays in place:
'held' is still not proof, it is just no longer load-bearing here. Anyone porting Wakelock to a machine
with a live idle timer inherits the unresolved question, not a fix.

Downgrading from P1. Not closing: the code claim is unverified, only the exposure is gone.

title: Focal loss + per-branch deep supervision: CoPAS's smallest component, and the one our live severity chapter already half-owns
description:
CoPAS child (D) of knee-pq8u. Their objective is L = alpha * sum_over_branches sum_over_12_labels BCE + sum_over_12_labels FL, alpha = 0.3: every intermediate branch is supervised with BCE against the same twelve labels, and the fused head additionally carries a focal term.

TWO SEPARABLE CLAIMS, AND ONLY ONE IS NEW HERE.
(1) FOCAL on the fused head. This is the same family as the live severity-weighting chapter (grade_ladder, band_dense and the severity ladder arms) - a per-example reweighting that spends capacity on the hard, rare positives. We are already measuring this axis under our own parameterisation. Do NOT open a second front on it; read grade_ladder first and let that chapter own the loss-shape question.
(2) PER-BRANCH DEEP SUPERVISION. This one we have never run. Our slots feed an aggregator and only the fused output sees a gradient from the labels; CoPAS puts a full twelve-label BCE on each branch at alpha = 0.3 so every plane learns to predict all twelve on its own before fusion. That is a different mechanism from a loss reweighting: it is a gradient-path change, and it is the standard fix for an aggregator that collapses onto one strong member.

WHY IT MIGHT MATTER MORE THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS. Nine slot-aggregation axes have landed inside the 0.0062 floor (knee-jk3). One reading of that is that the aggregator never had to work because the fused gradient is happy as soon as the best slot is good. Deep supervision removes that escape.

PRICE. Their own ablation puts the whole loss/CRM tail at +0.013, UNDER our 1.5% bar - so this is not sold as an improvement. It is an INSTRUMENT: it tests whether the aggregation axis is dead or merely untrained, which is the question gating knee-vigl, knee-jucq and the rest of the slot chapter. ~2h dev (an auxiliary head per slot plus one alpha), one ~40 min arm warm-started off band_dense. Ratio is what justifies it, not size.

GATE. After grade_ladder is read, so the loss chapter's verdict is in hand and claim (1) is not re-run by accident.

title: Label error is 20.5% and it is an OVER-CALL on GRADED findings, not a language problem
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 by kneemri.labels.reader_agreement against the 58 radiologist-annotated studies — the only ground truth in this project that is not the reader's own output. Log: logs/reader_agreement.log.

THE NUMBER: 140 of 684 cells wrong over 57 studies. 20.5% label error. Thirteen times the 1.5% bar, and larger than every modelling lever measured to date COMBINED.

THE SHAPE, which is what makes it actionable:
- 108 of 140 errors are FALSE POSITIVES. The reader over-calls. Missed: 32 (UNK 24, NO 8).
- Net over-call by finding: Contusion +18, Effusion +16, ACL +9, MCL +9, Medial OA +7, Lateral Meniscus +7, Medial Meniscus +6, Lateral OA +5, Baker's +4, PF OA +4, Fracture +2. Synovitis is the only under-caller at -11.
- Worst per-call agreement: Contusion 44.4%, MCL 50.0%, Lateral OA 56.2%.

LANGUAGE IS REFUTED AS THE CAUSE. English 66.7% against non-English 64.2%: +0.025 [-0.076, +0.126] bootstrapped over studies. Flat. This kills branch (a) of knee-mxj — the multilingual-encoder premise — on direct measurement rather than argument.

THE CAUSE IS THE GRADE. Positive calls on reports that GRADE the finding agree 63.2%; plain statements agree 77.8%. -0.146 [-0.277, +0.005]. The reader promotes mild / grade-1 findings to YES where the radiologist does not. That is a THRESHOLD defect in the reader, and it is fixable without re-reading a single report if the grade tier is already recorded — which it is, as the <target>__verdict column (YES 1 / YES 2 / YES 3).

STATE THE DENOMINATOR: 58 studies, 1.32% of the corpus, all-or-nothing annotated. Cells inside a study share a report and a radiologist so they are not independent draws; the intervals above are bootstrapped over STUDIES and are about twice a cell-wise width. This is a small ground truth and every number here inherits that.

THE CAVEAT THAT GATES ACTING ON IT: the leaderboard's ground truth is not ours. A reader agreeing better with OUR radiologist need not agree better with THEIRS. Circumstantial support that it would — champion scores 0.931 board against 0.869 holdout; a board built from the same noisy process should score about the same, not 0.06 higher, and cleaner board labels would explain the gap. That is an INFERENCE, not a measurement, and must not be written up as one.

FIRST ARM, and it is free (no API, no re-read): the YES 1 tier is already isolated in the verdict column. Demote or down-weight it and retrain. Note calib_span (-0.0020) is NOT this experiment — it rescaled all soft targets; this moves one tier. Note also grade_ladder, on the card 2026-08-21, subtracts thresholds inside the loss and is the closest existing probe of the same tier; read it first.

ACCEPTANCE TEST for any replacement reader is this module, run before and after — it says so in its own docstring.
notes:
DEMOTED P1->P3 the same hour it was filed, by 2026-08-20_label_contest_pilot.md, which I had not read when I filed it — the rule I keep breaking.

The pilot prices this whole axis at +0.006, AT the 0.0062 noise floor, by the metric's own arithmetic (unweighted mean of twelve AUCs; 58% of contested cells are Fracture+Contusion = 17% of cells; a GENEROUS fix of Fracture 0.80->0.85 and Contusion +0.02 gives (0.05+0.02)/12 = +0.006). And correcting label VALUES has been tried once and lost: calib_span -0.0020 with every pre-registered clause inverting.

The 20.5% here is NOT a contradiction of the pilot's 93%, and must not be written up as one. They are different rulers and the pilot says so itself: the pilot measures conformance to the RULEBOOK (a re-read can fix that), reader_agreement measures conformance to the IMAGE (a re-read cannot). The reports themselves disagree with the radiologist about a third of the time on positive calls. Since the leaderboard is scored against report-derived labels too, that third is the same noise on both sides of the comparison and is not recoverable by any reader.

WHAT SURVIVES AND IS STILL WORTH DOING, both free:
1. The graded-vs-plain split (63.2% vs 77.8%, -0.146 [-0.277, +0.005]) is a NEW observation not in the pilot, and it names the reader's threshold on mild findings as the mechanism behind the over-call. It is an interval that touches zero, so it is directional. grade_ladder (on the card 2026-08-21) is the closest existing probe.
2. The language refutation is now measured twice from two directions and can be treated as settled: reader_agreement +0.025 [-0.076, +0.126] English vs non-English, and the pilot's 2.7% vs 4.9% localised to ONE sentence shape rather than a language deficit.

The rulebook fix the pilot recommends (unmentioned = UNK, never NO; and a stable rule for what a normal-bone sentence denies) stays worth doing if a re-read ever happens for another reason. It is not worth a pass on its own.

title: Training-regimen axis is closed by mechanism: holdout selection already absorbs the decline
description:
Do not arm longer schedules, mixup, cutmix, stochastic depth, or any further regulariser as a SCORE arm without first defeating this argument.

Chain:
- Every arm saves the best epoch by holdout, so the peak-to-finish decline (band_dense_long -0.0182) costs the shipped model NOTHING. We ship the peak.
- Therefore a regulariser can only pay by raising the PEAK.
- aug_long ran exactly that test: intensity aug on the 24-epoch schedule. The regulariser demonstrably FIRED (train loss higher at every epoch past 4, 0.463 vs 0.454) and the peak moved later (6 -> 9) but the peak VALUE fell, 0.8511 vs 0.8587 (-0.0076).
- weight_average (EMA) is the same verdict from the other side: 0.8460, +0.0003 vs wsfold0_e6, flat, because a holdout already picks the epoch an EMA would have smoothed toward. Ledger README:409.

Read: the model is not memorisation-limited. It peaks at epoch 6-9 and no schedule or regulariser lifts that peak. That is a SIGNAL ceiling.

What this does NOT rule out: a regulariser that changes what the model can REPRESENT rather than how hard the fit is (the peak could move if the input or the target changes). It rules out the training regimen as a free lever on the current input/target pair.

Where the ceiling then lives: not the encoder (v3base_dense -0.0005, cnx_dense -0.0042, DINOv2-large +0.0021 at 3.7x cost), not decode/head (four levers all under a seventh of the 0.0062 floor), not crop/FOV (closed on availability 2026-08-21). Remaining: label accuracy (knee-dtk says 6 of 12 labels are label-bottlenecked) and self-supervision. Both held on an explicit go-ahead.

title: Synovitis is 84.2% UNK and Fracture 56.4% — the biggest supervision hole in the corpus, and it does NOT predict our scores
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-20, zero GPU, over ALL 4,406 corpus rows. Every one of the twelve columns is populated
on every row, so these are rates over the corpus, not over a subset that happened to parse.

  label              UNK%    NO%   YES%
  Synovitis          84.2    2.6   13.2
  Fracture           56.4   36.5    7.1
  Lateral OA         33.1   42.3   24.7
  Medial OA          25.5   37.7   36.7
  Contusion          20.8   49.8   29.4
  PF OA              18.5   36.3   45.2
  Lateral Meniscus   10.0   64.5   25.4
  Effusion            9.9   29.6   60.5
  MCL                 9.8   72.8   17.4
  ACL                 8.1   64.1   27.8
  Medial Meniscus     5.7   41.1   53.3
  (Baker's Cyst absent on a column-name mismatch, not a missing measurement.)

WHERE THIS CAME FROM. The user challenged the label-contest pilot's headline — MCL is our worst label
and had 0/100 contested cells — with "that's unknown, if our worst labels were just not found in the
reports". Agreement on ABSENCE is not evidence of correctness, and it is failure mode 2 of that very
pilot. So it was measured rather than argued.

THE OBJECTION FAILS FOR MCL AND ACL, at the sharpest point. They are the two labels with zero contested
cells and they carry the LOWEST UNK rates of all eleven, 9.8% and 8.1%. MCL's 72.8% NO rate is the
highest in the corpus: the reports address the medial collateral ligament and call it intact. The reader
agreeing with that is agreeing with a real statement, not with a silence. So the pilot's conclusion
holds — supervision is not what bounds MCL.

IT RELOCATES AND LANDS HARDER. 3,710 studies carry no synovitis information and 2,485 carry no fracture
information. Over half the corpus is silent on fracture. That is a supervision hole far larger than the
pilot's 4.0% contest rate, and a contest cannot see it — a contest only scores cells where the reader
made a call.

AND IT DECLINES TO EXPLAIN OUR SCORES, which is the part worth keeping. If missingness capped
performance the ordering would show it. It inverts:
  Synovitis  worst coverage in the corpus (84.2% UNK)  ->  0.873, mid-pack, above seven other labels
  MCL        third-best coverage (9.8% UNK)            ->  0.788-0.793, worst of the twelve
So the hole is real, it is much bigger than the contest rate, and it is NOT the current bound.

MECHANISM FOR WHY IT COSTS LESS THAN IT LOOKS. Under --weight-floor (shipped in RECIPE) an UNK cell is
not dropped: it trains at value 0.28, weight 0.2875 — a soft negative. Synovitis's 13.2% positives are
learnable against a quiet negative background, which is what 0.873 on 84% missing data looks like.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY PRICE IT, and it is not a re-read — the reports genuinely do not contain the
information, so a better reader cannot recover it:
  (a) the AUC ceiling per label given its UNK share, computed on the 57 image-read annotations, which
      are the only cells where the truth is known independently of the report;
  (b) whether the soft-negative treatment of UNK is better or worse than dropping those cells, which is
      a matched arm and NOT one this bead should assume the sign of;
  (c) whether the ~0.87 Synovitis number survives on the annotation ruler or is an artefact of scoring
      against a holdout that inherits the same 84.2% silence — this is the one that could invert the
      whole reading above, and it is the FIRST thing to run.

Recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_label_contest_pilot.md, section "The objection that
'0 contested' might just mean 'never mentioned' — measured".

P3 rather than higher: it is a ceiling question, not a floor question, and (c) is cheap enough that it
should gate any further work here.
notes:
ITEM (c) RUN 2026-08-20, and it CORRECTS THE EVIDENCE IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION while leaving the conclusion standing. Tool already existed: kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap, on report_labels_v2.csv, 58 annotated studies / 696 cells.

THE TWO POINTS I ARGUED FROM BOTH FLIP ON THE ANNOTATION RULER:
  Synovitis  report holdout 0.873  ->  annotation ruler 0.7378  (2nd worst of twelve)
  MCL        report holdout 0.788  ->  annotation ruler 0.8798  (4th best of twelve)
So the ~0.87 Synovitis number does NOT survive -- it falls 0.135 -- and it was in part an artefact of
scoring against a holdout that inherits the same 84.2% silence, exactly as (c) suspected. The specific
inversion this bead's description leans on ('worst coverage scores mid-pack, best coverage scores
worst') is a property of the REPORT ruler and must not be quoted again.

BUT THE CONCLUSION HOLDS, on twelve points instead of two. UNK share against annotation-ruler AUC:
  Synovitis 84.2% -> 0.7378 | Fracture 56.4% -> 0.8861 | Baker's 45.9% -> 0.9547 | Lateral OA 33.1% ->
  0.7099 | Medial OA 25.5% -> 0.9504 | Contusion 20.8% -> 0.8421 | PF OA 18.5% -> 0.8005 |
  Lateral Meniscus 10.0% -> 0.6497 | Effusion 9.9% -> 0.9453 | MCL 9.8% -> 0.8798 | ACL 8.1% -> 0.8640 |
  Medial Meniscus 5.7% -> 0.8498
  spearman rho = 0.014 (t = 0.04, df 10), pearson r = -0.111.
The best-scoring label carries 45.9% silence; the worst carries 10.0%. Missingness does not order the
findings on the ruler that counts either.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. rho = 0.014 over TWELVE points with each AUC drawn from ~58 studies cannot exclude a
moderate relation -- it fails to detect one, which is weaker than showing none. Per-label SE here is
~0.04-0.06 (label_power), so no single row above should be read to better than a few points, and the
2nd-worst / 4th-best ranks for Synovitis and MCL are themselves inside that noise. What survives is the
absence of an ORDERING, which is a claim about all twelve together and is the only thing twelve points
of this quality can support.

ITEM (a) IS NOW LARGELY ANSWERED TOO by the same run: supervision_gap's 'labels' column IS the report
label used as a predictor of the radiologist. Synovitis 0.6870 labels vs 0.7378 model -- the model
BEATS its own supervision by +0.0508 despite 84.2% silence, which is the mechanism this bead proposed
(an UNK cell trains as a soft negative, not a dropped one) confirmed on the annotation ruler.
ITEM (b) is untouched and is still a matched arm.

title: The labeler rulebook has three undecided conventions that produce 36 of 48 known label errors
description:
FOUND 2026-08-20 by the 100-report contest pilot (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_label_contest_pilot.md).
Filed separately from knee-mxj because this is a RULEBOOK defect, not a reader defect: none of the three
needs a better model, a re-read, or a GPU. They need a decision written down.

THE PILOT'S NUMBERS: 1,200 cells, 48 contested. 36 of the 48 trace to just two of the conventions below,
and a further 9 cells were parked as UNCERTAIN by the third.

(1) NO STABLE RULE FOR WHAT A NORMAL-BONE SENTENCE DENIES — the largest single source.
    The same template gets opposite answers across studies:
      tr, signal-only:   'sinyal intensiteleri dogaldir'  -> Fracture NO in 008/037, UNK in 032/046
      bg, structural:    'normalna forma'                 -> Fracture NO in 054/085, UNK in 007/036
    A signal statement and a structural statement deny different things, and the rulebook does not say
    which. This is also where the entire multilingual excess lives (bg 12.5%, tr 7.7%, hr 6.3% against
    en 2.7%) — those three languages compress bone and cartilage into one boilerplate clause, so the
    ambiguity fires more often there. It is a SENTENCE SHAPE, not a language deficit.

(2) A FINDING THE REPORT NEVER NAMES, ANSWERED NO — 23 cells, almost all Fracture / Contusion / Baker's,
    the findings a normal knee report simply does not mention. The bias is ONE-WAY: the reader fabricates
    denials, never positives. And the damage is a WEIGHT error, not a sign error: such a cell trains at
    value 0.08 / weight 0.85 where the rulebook puts it at 0.28 / weight 0.05. A cell that should be
    nearly switched off is trained at near-full confidence. PROPOSED RULE: unmentioned = UNK, never NO.

(3) OSTEOCHONDRAL LESION -> COMPARTMENT OA IS UNDECIDED — UNK in 018/022/052, YES in 015/044/054/061.
    9 cells parked as uncertain purely because the convention does not exist. Pick one and write it.

ALSO OBSERVED, smaller and worth recording before it is lost: BILATERAL OR COMPARTMENT-UNSPECIFIED SPANS
ANSWERED FOR ONE SIDE ONLY, 6 cells. Study 037's 'Medial ve lateral menisküste grade II dejenerasyon'
scored the medial and left the lateral UNK — the lateral is named in the very sentence used for the
medial. A span that names both compartments should answer both.

WHAT THIS IS WORTH, stated honestly so nobody plans around it. The pilot priced the WHOLE label axis at
+0.006 on the unweighted mean of twelve — at the 0.0062 holdout noise floor, a twentieth of the project
bar — and correcting label VALUES has been tried once and lost 0.0020 (calib_span). So this is P3 and it
is NOT a scoring lever. It is filed because the diagnosis was paid for, because a rulebook decision is
cheap and permanent, and because any future reader work would otherwise rediscover the same three
questions from scratch.

ACCEPTANCE: the three conventions written into the labeler rulebook as explicit rules. NOT a re-read of
the corpus — see the interpretation for why that pass is not worth taking.

title: Some commits fail once on 'files were modified by this hook' while every gate reports clean
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-20, twice in one session. A commit fails with three hooks marked Failed — importlinter-gate, arch-fitness, astgrep-gate — each with the SAME reason line, '- files were modified by this hook', and each with its own output reporting CLEAN:

  Contracts: 11 kept, 0 broken.
  INFO devtools.graph.fitness: architecture fitness: clean (0 god-modules / cycles / god-files; 0 advisory)
  INFO devtools.astgrep: ast-grep: clean (module shape)

So nothing is actually wrong with the code. Re-running the identical commit immediately afterwards succeeds first try, both times.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD AT P3 RATHER THAN IGNORING: this is the exact failure shape CLAUDE.md warns about — the twenty-odd Passed lines scroll past and the Failed lines are hundreds of lines up, so a commit verified by the tail of its own output reads as landed when it is not. It has already cost three silent no-op commits in an earlier session. The cost here is small (one retry) but the FAILURE MODE is the expensive one, and a recurring benign red makes the gate less likely to be read when it goes genuinely red.

DIAGNOSIS IS UNCONFIRMED. .beads/issues.jsonl shows as modified during the failing runs, including one where no bd command had been issued since the previous commit, which points at a beads daemon rewriting the jsonl while pre-commit is running — a race, which would explain why it is intermittent (one of three commits in this session passed first try with bd mutations staged). Not verified. .grimp_cache/ is gitignored so it is not the cache.

NEXT STEP: run the three hooks manually with the jsonl untouched and see whether the modification reappears; if it is the beads daemon, the fix is either an exclude in the hook config or ordering, and the pre-commit config is TEMPLATE-OWNED by sdlc-scaffold, so the change goes upstream and comes back through copier update rather than being hand-edited here.
notes:
NEXT STEP RUN 2026-08-25 — it does NOT reproduce standalone, and that is itself the finding.

Ran each of the three named hooks ALONE against the whole tree, no bd command in flight:
  importlinter-gate ... Passed
  arch-fitness ... Passed
  astgrep-gate ... Passed
.beads/issues.jsonl md5 IDENTICAL before and after all three (435b2a7c500e5ece2eec4dc7513fe8e8), and
git status came back empty. So none of these hooks writes the jsonl.
(NOTE: pre-commit run takes ONE hook id. Passing three exits 2 with unrecognized arguments — not a
failure of the hooks. Run them separately.)

WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE DIAGNOSIS. The three are not the agents of the modification; they are the
three SLOWEST, so they are the ones still running when something ELSE writes the file. bd --help shows
an auto-sync — there is a --sandbox flag whose whole description is "Sandbox mode: disables auto-sync",
plus --dolt-auto-commit (off|on|batch) — so a bd write exports to the jsonl asynchronously. If that
export lands while pre-commit is mid-run over a STAGED jsonl, pre-commit sees the file modified and
attributes it to whichever hook was running: all three at once, each with clean output, exactly the
observed shape. A retry then passes because the export has already landed. Grepping .pre-commit-config.yaml
and .git/hooks/pre-commit for beads/issues.jsonl returns NOTHING — no hook references the file at all,
which is the same conclusion from the other side.

EVIDENCE THIS SESSION, consistent though not decisive: three commits, each with beads mutations staged,
all landed first try — and in each the last bd command was more than a minute before the commit.

PROPOSED FIX, and it needs no template change: run bd export BEFORE git add, so the jsonl is final by
the time pre-commit reads it. That is a session-protocol line, not a hook edit, so nothing goes upstream
to sdlc-scaffold. It also predicts its own test: the failure should follow a bd write in the SECONDS
before a commit and never follow a quiet gap.
MECHANISM FOUND 2026-08-25, and it is bd itself, not a hook.

A bd WRITE does two things at the end of the command: it exports the whole working set to
.beads/issues.jsonl AND it git-adds the file. Measured just now — one bd update took the jsonl from
435b2a7c... to f8b1909a..., and git status came back "M " (STAGED, index ahead of HEAD, worktree equal
to index) on a tree that had been clean at 388c1b2. Nothing else ran. So bd stages on its own.

READS ARE INNOCENT: bd list --status=open, bd show and bd ready run back to back left the md5 identical.
Only writes rewrite.

That closes the shape exactly. If a bd WRITE lands while a commit is in flight — between git add and
the end of the hook phase — the staged jsonl changes underneath pre-commit, which reports "files were
modified by this hook" and blames whichever hook was running. The three named hooks are simply the
three slowest, which is why they were always the accused and always clean, and why a retry passes: the
export has already landed. It also explains the earlier finding from the other side, that no hook
config references .beads/issues.jsonl at all.

THE FIX IS AN ORDERING, not a hook change and not an upstream one: finish every bd write BEFORE git
add, and run no bd write until the commit returns. bd export before git add is the belt-and-braces
version. Nothing goes to sdlc-scaffold.

Closing: the failure is explained, reproducible in mechanism, and the fix is a protocol line. Re-open
if it ever fires with no bd command anywhere near the commit — that would refute this.

title: The intensity augmentation block costs at most 0.8% of an arm, not the 15% first measured
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-20 from the two arms' own metrics files, which record per-epoch `seconds`. aug_long and band_dense_long are a matched pair differing only in `intensity_aug`, so the epoch-time delta IS the block's cost.

  band_dense_long  median 363 s/epoch  (n=24, range 363-376, very tight)
  aug_long         median 417 s/epoch  (n=5,  range 389-429)
  delta            +54 s/epoch, +14.9%, +21.6 min over a 24-epoch arm

WHERE IT GOES. kneemri/training/augmentation.py is already vectorised and on-device — every transform draws from one torch.rand(n,...) and probabilistic ones are applied by MASK (out = do*transformed + (1-do)*original) rather than a Python branch. That is the documented, correct choice for batch throughput, and its price is that a blur with blur_probability=0.2 is COMPUTED on 100% of the batch and then thrown away for 80% of it. Same for gamma at 0.3. So the 15% is real GPU work, not a data-loading stall.

CONTENTION HYPOTHESIS CHECKED AND NOT SUPPORTED. aug_long's epoch times scatter over 40 s where band_dense_long's sit inside 13 s, which looked like CPU contention from other work on the machine during the arm. The wall-clock windows refute it: the fastest epoch (1, 389 s) and a slow one (2, 421 s) both ran while the machine was otherwise idle, and the two epochs that overlapped a nox gates run (3 and 4, 429/417) bracket that same range. Read the scatter as natural variance, not as a cost I am imposing.

IS IT WORTH FIXING. Not obviously. Gating blur/gamma on whether the mask has ANY true entries would recover most of it only when a whole batch draws below threshold, which at batch size n is rare; genuinely skipping per-sample means a Python branch per image, which is the thing the vectorisation exists to avoid. The honest options are (a) accept 15% as the price of the block, (b) index-select the subset the mask selects, run the transform on that subset, and scatter back — one gather/scatter against a full-batch conv, which is a real win at p=0.2 and a loss at p=1.0. (b) is the only one worth measuring and it must not change the RNG draw ORDER, which augmentation.py's docstring says is what makes a member's pixels reproducible.

FILED NOT CLAIMED: no fix attempted, no arm gated on this. It is a number to have before anyone argues about whether the intensity block earns its time.
notes:
THE PRICE THIS BEAD WAS FILED ON WAS MOSTLY SOMEBODY ELSE CPU. Re-measured 2026-08-20 over 13 aug_long epochs against all 24 of band_dense_long, a pair whose recorded recipes differ in exactly one field (intensity_aug True/False, every other key byte-identical):

    aug_long          n=13  median 392  min 366  max 429
    band_dense_long   n=24  median 363  min 363  max 376

MEDIAN gap +29 s (+8.0%), not the +54 s (+14.9%) this bead was filed on - that figure came from a handful of early epochs and did not survive more of them. But the medians are the wrong statistic and the SPREADS say why: the control varies over 13 s across 24 epochs, aug_long over 63 s across 13. A constant-work vectorised block cannot produce five times the variance; a contended machine can. ps -ef shows two celltrack proxy_eval CPU jobs at 7-8 CPU-hours each plus a dozen biohub_kaggle log watchers, all from other projects, competing with the dataloader.

MIN AGAINST MIN is the least-contended estimate available: 366 against 363, +3 s an epoch, +0.8% - and that comparison is BIASED AGAINST the block, since the control has 24 draws to find a low minimum and aug_long only 13. So the true cost is at most 3 s an epoch.

WHICH VINDICATES THE DOCSTRING I WAS IMPLICITLY DOUBTING. Augmentation._intensity records 18.7 ms against 19.0 ms a step for the enabled path against a guard, on a ~1.15 s step - about 1.7%. This bead +14.9% contradicted it by an order of magnitude, and I treated the docstring as the unrepresentative number (different shape) rather than treating my own measurement as the contaminated one. The docstring was right.

CONSEQUENCE, and the point of closing rather than re-scoping: the optimisation this bead proposed - index-select the masked subset, transform, scatter back, preserving RNG draw order - targets a share of 0.8%, on the ENABLED path only, which today is one arm whose own result is still undecided. Not worth the risk it carries: the whole ledger matched controls depend on identical augmentation, and a scatter/gather rewrite is exactly the kind of change that silently perturbs a draw. Reopen only if intensity augmentation earns a permanent place in the recipe AND the block is re-measured on an idle machine at a real training shape.

STANDING LESSON, bigger than the bead: an epoch-time delta measured while other projects hold the CPU is not a measurement of the flag. Take mins, not medians, or take the measurement when the machine is ours.

(This reason replaces an earlier one in which unescaped backticks were command-substituted by the shell and pasted a ps -ef dump into the ledger. Never put backticks in a bd reason written from bash.)
close_reason: Re-measured 2026-08-20: the intensity block costs AT MOST 3 s an epoch (+0.8%), not the 54 s (+14.9%) this bead was filed on. aug_long n=13 median 392 min 366; band_dense_long n=24 median 363 min 363, recipes differing in exactly one field. The medians are contaminated - control spread 13 s, aug_long spread 63 s, and ps -ef shows two celltrack CPU jobs at 7-8 CPU-hours plus a dozen biohub_kaggle watchers competing with the dataloader. Min against min is the least-contended estimate and is biased AGAINST the block (24 draws to find a low minimum against 13). That vindicates Augmentation._intensity own docstring (18.7 ms against 19.0 ms a step, ~1.7%), which I had implicitly doubted. The proposed index-select/scatter optimisation therefore targets a share of 0.8% on the enabled path only, against a real risk of perturbing an RNG draw the whole ledger matched controls depend on - not worth it. Reopen only if intensity augmentation earns a permanent place in the recipe AND is re-measured on an idle machine. STANDING LESSON: an epoch-time delta measured while other projects hold the CPU is not a measurement of the flag; take mins, not medians. Full working is in this issue notes.

title: final_ws_e12 recorded its epoch index into the auc field; the run has no score and no predictions
description:
FOUND 2026-08-19 while auditing runs-on-disk against the ledger.

D:/data/.../final_ws_e12.metrics.jsonl has twelve epoch rows in which auc == epoch exactly (0.0, 1.0, ... 11.0) and no per_label key at all. The loss column is healthy and monotone (1.1992 -> 0.5774 over the twelve), so the run TRAINED; what failed is the recorder, which wrote the epoch index into the score field.

IT CANNOT BE RECONSTRUCTED FROM DISK. Every other run of that era kept a .holdout.npz that HoldoutMetrics.of can rescore from - this one did not (only .metrics.jsonl, .partial and .pt). So the only path to its number is re-scoring final_ws_e12.pt against the holdout on the card, which is GPU work and therefore queued behind arms, not done inline.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE RUN: a metrics file whose auc field is well-formed nonsense passes every reader we have. RunMetrics.best would happily return auc=11.0 as this run's best epoch, and any comparison against it would quote 11.0 as a score. The ledger never named this run so nothing downstream was corrupted, but nothing DETECTED it either - it surfaced only because a name-matching audit went looking. Worth an assert in the recorder or a range check where scores are read (an AUC outside [0,1] is not a number any reader should accept).

SCOPE NOTE: this is one file and a pre-existing era's bug, not a live defect - current runs record correctly (band_span's rows this hour are well-formed). Priority is the range check, not the historical run.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-19: the filing claimed `RunMetrics.best` would return auc=11.0 for final_ws_e12 and that every reader accepts it. Both halves are wrong, checked against the code rather than assumed. run_metrics.py:274 already guards it — the run recorded fold -1, a run that held nothing back cannot have a best epoch, and best() returns None for final_ws_e12 AND final_fit_e12 today. The other three readers of auc are guarded too, two by that same best(), and LabelStability by requiring per_label, which the corrupt rows do not carry.

What the audit DID find in the same sweep is a different defect and it is now fixed: LabelStability.best parsed the metrics file itself and took a maximum over every line, missing the last-run-group rule RunMetrics.rows() exists for. pair_memory_s2026 is the case on disk (12 epochs peaking 0.8353, then 4 peaking 0.8155) and it contributed the profile of an overwritten checkpoint to the stability correlation. Delegated to RunMetrics.rows(); the across-holdout median rank correlation is unchanged at +0.51, so the recorded conclusion survives the fix.

Remaining scope of this bead is therefore SMALLER than filed: not 'readers accept a nonsense AUC' but 'the guard is a recipe lookup, so a corrupt file whose recipe does NOT record fold<0 would pass'. final_fit_e12 is that shape (no fold in its recipe) and returns None only because it recorded no rows at all. A range check on auc in [0,1] would close it by value rather than by provenance. Downgrading to P3 — no reader is wrong today.

title: An EMA of the weights is kept for the FINAL FIT only: +0.0013 directional, free
description:
weight_average scored 0.8460 vs control 0.8457 — flat, and its pre-registration says that is the EXPECTED result, not a disappointment: keeping the best epoch by holdout score is itself an average over the trajectory, so an EMA was predicted to help LEAST here and MOST in the final fit, where no holdout ranks epochs and the last one is kept by construction.

The mean is therefore the wrong read. Its own stated targets were the best-to-last gap and the last-epoch value:
  control          best 0.8457  last 0.8394  gap 0.0063
  weight_average   best 0.8460  last 0.8407  gap 0.0053
Gap shrinks 0.0010, last epoch +0.0013. Both far under the 0.0062 floor, so NEITHER IS A RESULT.

VERDICT (the significance bar applied literally): directional, mechanism-sound and free — one extra weight copy, no extra step time, no measured throughput cost. So KEEP IT for the final fit, where there is no holdout to select on, and do NOT spend a slot on it, rebuild a member for it, or plan around it.

It does not rescue the banned seed/fold axis it was scouting for: damping the last few hundred steps recovers about a fifth of the 0.0062 three-seed spread — a knob-sized piece of a floor-sized problem.

ACTION when a final fit is next built: pass --ema. Nothing to do before then. Ledger: experiments/README.md, 'An EMA buys nothing where a holdout picks the epoch'.

title: Report length as a free auxiliary target (rho ~0.5 with finding count, model never sees it)
description:
Measured 2026-08-19 (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-19_report-length-is-severity.md): report length predicts the number of positive findings inside EVERY language, rank corr +0.42 (en) to +0.85 (tr), Q4-Q1 of +2.2 to +5.5 findings a study. Verified on the 57 annotated studies to be real severity rather than reader harvesting: calls per study rise with length (+0.506) while precision does not fall with it (67.6/63.9/64.3 by tercile, a spread under one binomial SE).

So it is a cheap, language-independent, reader-independent severity proxy that the IMAGE model never sees. Candidate: regress log length as an auxiliary head. One scalar per study, reuses the ReportSupervision plumbing already in the trainer (--report-weight / --report-vectors path).

NOT a finding and not priced. Nothing measured says it moves the score; what is measured is that the signal exists and is free to construct. Gate it behind a smoke plus one short arm against rate_wholestack (0.8525) before it takes a queue slot.

title: READERS=4 buys ~9% of a 448px epoch — measured in step time, not just GB/s
description:
knee fetch follow-up, MEASURED 2026-08-18. fetch_bench said the trainer's narrow-window read peaks at four handles (1.39 vs 1.06 GB/s). Open question was whether Prefetch hides that. It does not.

448 px, batch 12, 600 studies (476 train), 1 epoch, --recompute-activations --vram-gb 26, narrow window (no --whole-stack). Handle counts INTERLEAVED 2,4,2,4,2,4 so cache warming cannot name a winner:

    READERS=2 : 22, 23, 21 s   (mean 22.0)
    READERS=4 : 20, 20, 20 s   (mean 20.0)

Round one (4,2,2,4) agrees on its warm arms: 22/21 at two vs 19 at four; its first arm was 47 s cold.
Loss identical to four decimals in all ten runs — the reader changes how bytes arrive, not what is computed (the equality oracle in tests/unit/kneemri/corpus already asserts this).

DENOMINATOR: 9% is of a WARM epoch — 600 studies fit in RAM. A full-corpus epoch reads colder, where the fetch term is larger, so 9% is a floor on the saving, not a ceiling.

Constant already shipped at 4 (commit d8b52e4). This bead records the step-time confirmation.

title: Fetch throughput: the windowed read peaks at 4 handles (measured), whole-stack at 2
description: MEASURED 2026-08-18 with the new kneemri.corpus.fetch_bench on the 336px_12sl cache. Windowed read (3 of 12 slices, one seek per slot): 0.72 / 1.06 / 1.39 / 1.31 GB/s at 1/2/4/8 handles; reproduced with arms reversed over different rows at 0.77 / 1.25 / 1.43 / 0.92. Whole stack (one seek per study): 0.67 mapped, then 1.06 / 1.35 / 1.35 / 1.38. READERS raised 2 -> 4 in commit d8b52e4; the equality oracle against MappedReader still passes and the 60-study smoke returns the same loss 1.3441, so no number the trainer produces changed. OPEN QUESTION, not measured: what fraction of a real step the fetch is at 448 px and batch 12 - the win is on the host-side term only, so its size in STEP time is unknown until a full-size arm is timed with and without. Re-run the bench on any new cache before trusting the constant: --width for the branch, --offset for fresh rows, --reverse against arm-order effects.

title: Five training switches no committed arm exercises: --pool, --anatomical-prior, --normalise-by-count, --tie, --head-lr
description:
Measured 2026-08-18 by diffing TrainingOptions' 48 flags against every --flag appearing under experiments/**.sh: 13 are never passed by any arm or script. Eight of those are legitimately unarmed (--paths, --seed, --split-seed, --folds, --cache-studies, --bf16 and --band-low/--band-high are defaults, smoke plumbing, or set by the cache builder rather than the trainer). Five are real switches with no coverage on the card: --pool (cls_mean vs focal — the ledger records that before its wiring no arm could select focal AT ALL, and none does now), --anatomical-prior (last used in LEGACY_COMMANDS.md, not in any live arm), --normalise-by-count, --tie (the router; every arm takes the default first-maximal) and --head-lr.

Consequence: arm_check --smoke proves 'every committed recipe survives a real epoch', which is only true of the paths the arms take. These five are landed-checked and stamped but never RUN, so a break in them surfaces at the queue, not at the smoke. Either an arm exercises each (which also answers whether the knob is worth anything) or the knob is dead weight the vulture gate cannot see, because it is reachable Python that argparse references.

Repro: python - <<'EOF'
import pathlib, re
from kneemri.training.train import TrainingOptions
flags = {f"--{n.replace('_','-')}" for n in vars(TrainingOptions())}
text = chr(10).join(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8') for p in pathlib.Path('experiments').rglob('*.sh'))
print(sorted(flags - set(re.findall(r'--[a-z0-9-]+', text))))
EOF
notes: Answered by execution 2026-08-18 and closed off mechanically: all five never-run switches (--pool focal, --anatomical-prior, --normalise-by-count, --tie last, --head-lr) reach a written checkpoint at 60 studies / 1 epoch. The defect was that nothing was watching, so switch_coverage.py now partitions every TrainingOptions field into armed / covered / written-off, a unit test asserts the partition is total, and arm_check --switches runs the recipes. Commit fd26930.

title: --unfreeze-last has no landed-check because LoRA legitimately ignores it
description: StudyModel.parameter_groups honours unfreeze_last only when no adapters are present -- under LoRA every block carries one and the depth argument does not apply. So a naive observed-vs-asked check on open blocks false-positives on every LoRA arm. Wanted: model reports the count of blocks holding a trainable parameter, and Request maps the ask through the adaptation mode rather than through the flag. Deferred because the ambiguity is a design question, not plumbing.

title: KernelRun logs the overlap it was ASKED for, not the one any member used
description: 2026-08-17. FILED ON A REFUTED PREMISE, corrected here. Original claim: solo ran overlap=True while trio ran False, so solo confounded the member-count curve. WRONG. Member.window (kneemri/inference/members.py:385) gives a whole_stack member ONE centred window and never reads the flag at all. Every member in the current pool is whole_stack, so solo v3 and v4 predict identically and the count curve was never at risk. The proposed fix was worse than the bug: flipping the default to False silently disables overlap for WINDOWED members, where tests/integration/mounts_to_kernel.py:130 asserts it is worth +0.0156 — the strongest number in the repo, and the 20 CC0 members in the fusion entry are windowed. Reverted; the default stays True. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is small: kernel_run.py:148 logs 'serving: ... overlap=%s' from self.overlap, i.e. the REQUEST. No member reports what it did. That log line is the entire reason a non-difference read as a confound and cost a re-push.
